entries.definition_en: a remark made spontaneously without prior preparation
entries.example_cn: 这位演员忘词了，不得不依靠即兴发挥来完成这场戏。
entries.example_en: The actor forgot his lines and had to rely on an ad-lib to finish the scene.

entries.definition_en: done with little or no preparation or forethought
entries.example_cn: 由于会议被意外召集，团队不得不做出一个未经充分准备的决定。
entries.example_en: The team had to make an ad-lib decision because the meeting was called unexpectedly.

entries.definition_en: said or done without being planned or written in advance
entries.example_cn: 导演要求演员以即兴的方式念出台词，以使对话听起来更自然。
entries.example_en: The director asked the actors to deliver their lines in an ad-lib style to make the dialogue feel more natural.

entries.definition_en: congenital absence of fingers and/or toes
entries.example_cn: 缺指（趾）症是一种罕见的疾病，患者出生时没有手指或脚趾。
entries.example_en: Adactylia is a rare condition where a person is born without fingers or toes.

entries.definition_en: congenital absence of fingers and/or toes
entries.example_cn: 医学术语 adactylism 描述了手指和/或脚趾先天性缺失的情况。
entries.example_en: The medical term adactylism describes the congenital absence of fingers and/or toes.

entries.definition_en: having no fingers and/or toes
entries.example_cn: 这种无指的生物用手掌和脚底爬行。
entries.example_en: The adactylous creature moved by crawling on its palms and soles.

entries.definition_en: without claws on the feet, as in some crustaceans
entries.example_cn: 这种足部无爪的甲壳动物用光滑的足挖入沙中。
entries.example_en: The adactylous crustacean used its smooth feet to burrow into the sand.

entries.definition_en: the congenital absence of fingers and/or toes
entries.example_cn: 先天性缺指（趾）是一种罕见的病症，患者出生时没有手指或脚趾。
entries.example_en: Adactyly is a rare condition where a person is born without fingers or toes.

entries.definition_en: a short, memorable saying that expresses a general truth or piece of wisdom
entries.example_cn: 这句古老的格言“熟能生巧”指导着许多学生。
entries.example_en: The old adage 'practice makes perfect' guides many students.

entries.definition_en: having a leisurely or slow tempo
entries.example_cn: 指挥示意演奏交响曲的慢板部分。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled for the adagio section of the symphony.

entries.definition_en: a piece of music written to be played slowly and gracefully
entries.example_cn: 管弦乐团以柔和流畅的旋律开始了慢板乐曲。
entries.example_en: The orchestra began the adagio with a soft, flowing melody.

entries.definition_cn: 展示高难度平衡、旋转和托举动作的芭蕾双人舞或混合三人舞
entries.definition_en: a ballet duet or mixed trio displaying demanding balance, spins, and lifts
entries.example_cn: 这部芭蕾舞剧的双人舞展示了高难度的平衡、旋转和托举动作。
entries.example_en: The ballet's adagio featured demanding balances, spins, and lifts.

entries.definition_en: in a slow and graceful manner
entries.example_cn: 舞者在舞台上缓慢优雅地移动。
entries.example_en: The dancer moved adagio across the stage.

entries.definition_cn: 一种北美兰花，单叶，花黄褐色
entries.definition_en: a type of North American orchid with a single leaf and yellowish-brown flowers
entries.example_cn: 园丁在温室里发现了一株罕见的亚当夏娃兰花正在开花。
entries.example_en: The gardener spotted a rare adam-and-eve orchid blooming in the greenhouse.

entries.definition_en: resoluteness resulting from being unyielding and inflexible
entries.example_cn: 她在谈判中拒绝妥协的坚定不移令人印象深刻。
entries.example_en: Her adamance in refusing to compromise impressed everyone in the negotiation.

entries.definition_en: impervious to pleas, persuasion, requests, reason
entries.example_cn: 她对于辞职的决定依然坚决。
entries.example_en: She remained adamant about her decision to quit.

entries.definition_cn: 坚硬无比的传说中的物质或岩石；有时指金刚石
entries.definition_en: an imaginary substance or rock of extreme hardness; sometimes identified with diamond
entries.example_cn: 在古代文献中，adamant 被想象成比任何已知岩石都坚硬的物质。
entries.example_en: In older writings, adamant was imagined as a substance harder than any known rock.

entries.definition_en: unmoved by pleas, persuasion, or requests
entries.example_cn: 尽管我们坚决拒绝，他们继续索要更多的钱。
entries.example_en: Despite our adamantine refusal, they continued to ask for more money.

entries.definition_en: having the hardness of the mythical metal adamant
entries.example_cn: 这颗钻石正如传说中所说的那样坚硬如金刚石。
entries.example_en: The diamond was as adamantine as the legends claimed.

entries.definition_en: having the hardness of a diamond
entries.example_cn: 这颗宝石坚硬的表面抵抗了所有的划痕。
entries.example_en: The adamantine surface of the gemstone resisted all scratches.

entries.definition_en: inflexibly; unshakably
entries.example_cn: 她坚决拒绝签署合同。
entries.example_en: She adamantly refused to sign the contract.

entries.definition_en: to change something to suit a new purpose
entries.example_cn: 这部电影改编自一部著名小说。
entries.example_en: The movie was adapted from a famous novel.

entries.definition_en: to change oneself to fit new conditions
entries.example_cn: 她花了一段时间才适应新的气候。
entries.example_en: It took her a while to adapt to the new climate.

entries.definition_en: the ability to change or be changed to fit new circumstances
entries.example_cn: 该公司的适应性使其能够熬过经济衰退。
entries.example_en: The company's adaptability allowed it to survive the economic downturn.

entries.definition_en: capable of adapting (of becoming or being made suitable) to a particular situation or use
entries.example_cn: 儿童非常能适应新环境。
entries.example_en: Children are highly adaptable to new environments.

entries.definition_en: the process of changing to fit new conditions
entries.example_cn: 适应新气候花了几个月的时间。
entries.example_en: The adaptation to the new climate took several months.

entries.definition_en: a version of a written work that has been changed for a new form, like a movie
entries.example_cn: 这部电影是那部著名小说的改编作品。
entries.example_en: The movie is an adaptation of the famous novel.

entries.definition_en: the way a body part adjusts to different conditions
entries.example_cn: 眼睛适应黑暗的过程发生得很快。
entries.example_en: The adaptation of the eye to darkness happens quickly.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involving adaptation
entries.example_cn: 该物种的适应性策略使其能够在极端气候中生存。
entries.example_en: The adaptational strategies of the species allow it to survive in extreme climates.

entries.definition_en: having the ability to adapt to new conditions
entries.example_cn: 该物种的适应性策略使其得以在干旱中生存。
entries.example_en: The adaptative strategies of the species allowed it to survive the drought.

entries.definition_cn: 改编的；为适应不同情境或媒介而改动的
entries.definition_en: changed in order to improve or made more fit for a particular purpose
entries.example_cn: 这部电影改编自一部成功的小说。
entries.example_en: The film was adapted from a successful novel.

entries.definition_en: a device that allows something to be used in a different way or connects different equipment
entries.example_cn: 你需要一个特殊的适配器才能在这个国家使用你的手机充电器。
entries.example_en: You need a special adapter to use your phone charger in this country.

entries.definition_en: a person who changes a piece of music to suit different voices or instruments
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的作曲家聘请了一位改编者将他的交响乐改编为合唱曲。
entries.example_en: The famous composer hired an adapter to rewrite his symphony for a choir.

entries.definition_en: the process of changing to fit new conditions
entries.example_cn: 该物种适应恶劣气候花了数千年时间。
entries.example_en: The adaption of the species to the harsh climate took thousands of years.

entries.definition_en: having the ability to adjust to new conditions
entries.example_cn: 该软件适应性的特点使其能在旧电脑上运行。
entries.example_en: The adaptive nature of the software allows it to run on old computers.

entries.definition_en: a device that allows two different pieces of equipment to be connected and used together
entries.example_cn: 你需要一个特殊的适配器才能在欧洲使用你的手机充电器。
entries.example_en: You need a special adaptor to use your phone charger in Europe.

entries.definition_en: located nearest to or facing the axis of an organ or organism.
entries.example_cn: 叶片的近轴面朝向茎。
entries.example_en: The adaxial surface of the leaf faces the stem.

entries.definition_en: in an adaxial manner
entries.example_cn: 维管束在叶片中呈向轴排列。
entries.example_en: The vascular bundles are arranged adaxially within the leaf blade.

entries.definition_en: to join or combine things together; to increase the amount or quality of something
entries.example_cn: 请在咖啡里加点糖。
entries.example_en: Please add some sugar to the coffee.

entries.definition_en: to calculate the sum of numbers
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把这两个数加起来。
entries.example_en: We need to add these two numbers together.

entries.definition_en: to say something more to what has already been said
entries.example_cn: 他补充说会议将延期。
entries.example_en: He added that the meeting would be postponed.

entries.definition_en: to find the total of numbers
entries.example_cn: 你能算出所有物品的总价吗？
entries.example_en: Can you add up the cost of all the items?

entries.definition_en: to give or bestow a quality on something
entries.example_cn: 新设计为大楼增添了优雅。
entries.example_en: The new design adds elegance to the building.

entries.definition_en: to constitute an addition; to be an extra part
entries.example_cn: 新章节增加了书的篇幅。
entries.example_en: The new chapter adds to the book's length.

entries.definition_cn: （可插入计算机扩展槽以增加其功能的）扩展卡
entries.definition_en: a printed circuit that can be inserted into expansion slots in a computer to increase the computer's capabilities
entries.example_cn: 他买了一块图形扩展卡来提高游戏性能。
entries.example_en: He bought a graphics add-in to improve his gaming performance.

entries.definition_en: a piece of software that makes an existing program work better or have more features
entries.example_cn: 这个新附加组件允许你在应用程序中直接编辑照片。
entries.example_en: The new add-on allows you to edit photos directly in the app.

entries.definition_cn: 为设备或系统增加功能的外接部件
entries.definition_en: a physical component added to a device or system to provide extra functions
entries.example_cn: 这台相机有一个在弱光下拍照用的外接镜头。
entries.example_en: The camera has an add-on lens for taking pictures in low light.

entries.definition_en: an extra part that improves the ability of something to do a job
entries.example_cn: 这台相机有一个用于在光线不足时拍照的增强组件。
entries.example_en: The camera has an add-on lens for taking pictures in low light.

entries.definition_en: able to be added or added to something
entries.example_cn: 电子表格允许你添加新行，使数据可以添加到报告中。
entries.example_en: The spreadsheet allows you to add new rows, making the data addable to the report.

entries.definition_cn: 可添加到基本模型或配方中的附加项；附加组件或增强功能
entries.definition_en: Something that can be added to a basic model or formulation, such as an add-on or enhancement
entries.example_cn: 该软件支持多种可添加组件，包括额外的控件和查看选项。
entries.example_en: The software supports several addables, including extra controls and viewing options.

entries.definition_en: a large antelope with lightly spiraled horns found in the deserts of northern Africa
entries.example_cn: 大羚羊非常适应炎热沙漠的生活。
entries.example_en: The addax is well adapted to life in the hot desert.

entries.definition_en: a number that is added to another number
entries.example_cn: 在等式 5 + 3 = 8 中，3 是加数。
entries.example_en: In the equation 5 + 3 = 8, 3 is the addend.

entries.definition_en: extra information added to the end of a document
entries.example_cn: 合同包含了一份关于付款条款的附录。
entries.example_en: The contract included an addendum regarding the payment terms.

entries.definition_en: a small terrestrial viper common in northern Eurasia
entries.example_cn: 徒步者在穿越荒原时被一条有毒的蝰蛇咬伤。
entries.example_en: The hiker was bitten by a venomous adder while walking through the heathland.

entries.definition_en: a machine that adds numbers
entries.example_cn: 电子加法器将输入值相加并得出总和。
entries.example_en: The electronic adder combined the input values and produced their sum.

entries.definition_cn: 进行加法运算的人或事物
entries.definition_en: a person or thing that performs arithmetic addition
entries.example_cn: 这个计算机程序充当财务计算的加法器。
entries.example_en: The computer program acts as an adder for the financial calculations.

entries.definition_en: capable of being added or added to
entries.example_cn: 总成本可以加到上个月的支出中。
entries.example_en: The total cost is addible to the previous month's expenses.

entries.definition_en: someone who is extremely devoted to something
entries.example_cn: 他是个十足的电子游戏迷。
entries.example_en: He is a total video-game addict.

entries.definition_en: someone who is physiologically dependent on a substance
entries.example_cn: 这位瘾君子需要专业帮助才能康复。
entries.example_en: The addict needs professional help to recover.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to become dependent on something
entries.example_cn: 这种药物能迅速使用户成瘾。
entries.example_en: The drug can quickly addict a user.

entries.definition_cn: 对容易成瘾的事物产生身心依赖的；沉迷于某事物的
entries.definition_en: physically or psychologically dependent on something habit-forming; very devoted to or obsessed with something
entries.example_cn: 他每晚都沉迷于玩电子游戏。
entries.example_en: He is addicted to playing video games every night.

entries.definition_cn: 对习惯成癖之物（如毒品或酒精）的病态依赖
entries.definition_en: an abnormal dependence on something habit-forming, such as drugs or alcohol
entries.example_cn: 他正与严重的赌博成瘾作斗争。
entries.example_en: He struggled with a severe addiction to gambling.

entries.definition_cn: 对某物的异常强烈的渴望
entries.definition_en: an abnormally strong craving for something
entries.example_cn: 她突然对甜食产生了强烈的渴望。
entries.example_en: She felt a sudden addiction to sweet food.

entries.definition_cn: （罗马法）将人或物正式判给或移交给他人
entries.definition_en: in Roman law, the formal award or surrender of a person or thing to another
entries.example_cn: 在罗马法中，债务人可能被正式移交给债权人。
entries.example_en: In Roman law, a debtor could be formally surrendered to a creditor.

entries.definition_en: causing a strong desire to keep using something
entries.example_cn: 电子游戏对青少年来说可能非常令人上瘾。
entries.example_en: Video games can be very addictive for teenagers.

entries.definition_cn: 容易上瘾的；有成瘾倾向的
entries.definition_en: having a tendency to become addicted
entries.example_cn: 他有成瘾倾向，很难停止赌博。
entries.example_en: He has an addictive personality and finds it hard to stop gambling.

entries.definition_en: the act of performing addition
entries.example_cn: 老师解释了不用计算器进行加法运算的概念。
entries.example_en: The teacher explained the concept of adding without using a calculator.

entries.definition_cn: add 的现在分词和动名词
entries.definition_en: present participle and gerund of add
entries.example_cn: 把这两个数相加，总和是十。
entries.example_en: Adding the two numbers gives a total of ten.

entries.definition_en: the mathematical operation of finding the total of numbers
entries.example_cn: 加法是孩子们在学校学习的第一种运算。
entries.example_en: Addition is the first operation children learn in school.

entries.definition_en: the action of putting one thing together with another
entries.example_cn: 加糖使茶的味道更甜。
entries.example_en: The addition of sugar makes the tea taste sweeter.

entries.definition_en: a part added to something to make it better
entries.example_cn: 新扩建的侧翼是博物馆最近的增添物。
entries.example_en: The new wing is a recent addition to the museum.

entries.definition_en: something extra added to what you already have
entries.example_cn: 他们提供了一件免费礼物作为购买的附加物。
entries.example_en: They offered a free gift as an addition to the purchase.

entries.definition_en: a quantity added to something
entries.example_cn: 加一点盐后，酱汁的味道更好了。
entries.example_en: A small addition of salt improved the sauce.

entries.definition_en: a planned area for houses that is being built outside a town
entries.example_cn: 城市的新建郊区住宅区仍在建设中。
entries.example_en: The new addition to the city is still under construction.

entries.definition_en: further or added
entries.example_cn: 我们需要额外的信息来完成报告。
entries.example_en: We need additional information to finish the report.

entries.definition_en: in addition; furthermore
entries.example_cn: 此外，该项目还需要详细的预算分析。
entries.example_en: Additionally, the project requires a detailed budget analysis.

entries.definition_en: a substance added to enhance food, gasoline, paint, or medicine
entries.example_cn: 人工色素通常作为添加剂用于加工食品中。
entries.example_en: Artificial colors are often used as an additive in processed foods.

entries.definition_en: characterized or produced by addition
entries.example_cn: 加法过程将两个数字相加以求和。
entries.example_en: The additive process combines two numbers to find their sum.

entries.definition_en: designating an equation whose terms are of the first degree
entries.example_cn: 这位数学家迅速解出了一次方程。
entries.example_en: The mathematician solved the additive equation quickly.

entries.definition_en: to mix up or confuse
entries.example_cn: 复杂的指令完全弄乱了我的思路。
entries.example_en: The complex instructions addled my mind completely.

entries.definition_en: to become rotten
entries.example_cn: 高温导致鸡蛋迅速变质。
entries.example_en: The heat caused the eggs to addle quickly.

entries.definition_en: stupid and confused
entries.example_cn: 这个愚蠢而混乱的计划未能考虑到基本的安全措施。
entries.example_en: The addlebrained plan failed to account for basic safety measures.

entries.definition_en: confused and vague, especially regarding one's thinking or mental state.
entries.example_cn: 在那场复杂的争论之后，他的思维完全混乱了。
entries.example_en: After the complex argument, his mind felt completely addled.

entries.definition_en: (of eggs) no longer edible because the yolk has become loose or the white has run.
entries.example_cn: 鸡蛋在阳光下放得太久，已经变质了。
entries.example_en: The eggs were left in the sun too long and became addled.

entries.definition_en: a person with confused ideas; incapable of serious thought
entries.example_cn: 别再像个糊涂蛋一样行事，仔细听指示。
entries.example_en: Stop acting like an addlehead and listen to the instructions carefully.

entries.definition_en: stupid and confused
entries.example_cn: 这个糊涂的证人对事情经过作了混乱的叙述。
entries.example_en: The addlepated witness gave a confused account of what had happened.

entries.definition_en: the place where someone lives or works, used for sending mail
entries.example_cn: 请在信封上写清楚你的详细地址。
entries.example_en: Please write your full address on the envelope.

entries.definition_en: a code that identifies the location of data in a computer system
entries.example_cn: 计算机程序使用内存地址来存储数据。
entries.example_en: The computer program uses a memory address to store data.

entries.definition_en: a formal speech given to an audience
entries.example_cn: 总统向全国发表了一次有力的演说。
entries.example_en: The president delivered a powerful address to the nation.

entries.definition_en: to speak to someone formally or publicly
entries.example_cn: 市长将在中午向人群致辞。
entries.example_en: The mayor will address the crowd at noon.

entries.definition_en: to give a speech to an audience
entries.example_cn: 她就学生的未来职业发表了演讲。
entries.example_en: She addressed the students about their future careers.

entries.definition_en: to write an address on an envelope or package
entries.example_cn: 他把信放进邮箱前忘了填写地址。
entries.example_en: He forgot to address the letter before putting it in the mailbox.

entries.definition_en: to ask a question directly to someone
entries.example_cn: 老师向全班提出了一个难题。
entries.example_en: The teacher addressed a difficult question to the class.

usage.label: address a question to someone
usage.pattern: address a question to the class

entries.definition_en: the way someone speaks to another person
entries.example_cn: 你应该以尊重的态度与他交谈。
entries.example_en: You should address him with respect.

entries.definition_cn: （计算机中）可通过特定地址访问的
entries.definition_en: in computing, accessible through a particular address
entries.example_cn: 该计算机系统需要一个可通过地址访问的存储单元。
entries.example_en: The computer system requires an addressable memory unit.

entries.definition_en: (of mail) having a destination written on it
entries.example_cn: 这封已贴好地址的信函随时可以寄出。
entries.example_en: The addressed envelope was ready to be mailed immediately.

entries.definition_en: the person to whom something is addressed
entries.example_cn: 这封信的收件人是公司的经理。
entries.example_en: The addressee of the letter was the manager of the company.

entries.definition_en: to present evidence or reasons to support a claim or argument
entries.example_cn: 律师提出几项证据以证明被告无罪。
entries.example_en: The lawyer adduced several pieces of evidence to prove the defendant's innocence.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指肌肉）使向身体中线或相邻部位靠拢的
entries.definition_en: especially of muscles; bringing together or drawing toward the midline of the body or toward an adjacent part
entries.example_cn: 内收肌有助于在运动时稳定肩关节。
entries.example_en: The adducent muscles help stabilize the shoulder joint during movement.

entries.definition_en: a person who presents evidence or arguments to support a claim
entries.example_cn: 举证者提供了几项统计研究来证明该假设。
entries.example_en: The adducer provided several statistical studies to prove the hypothesis.

entries.definition_en: to move a limb towards the midline of the body
entries.example_cn: 外科医生让患者将手臂内收。
entries.example_en: The surgeon asked the patient to adduct the arm.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound created by an addition reaction
entries.example_cn: 该反应生成了稳定的加成物。
entries.example_en: The reaction produced a stable adduct.

entries.definition_en: the movement of a body part toward the central axis of the body
entries.example_cn: 物理治疗师指导患者进行肩关节内收练习。
entries.example_en: The physical therapist instructed the patient to perform adduction exercises for the shoulder.

entries.definition_en: causing muscles to move toward the midline of the body
entries.example_cn: 手臂的内收运动使其更靠近躯干。
entries.example_en: The adductive movement of the arm brings it closer to the torso.

entries.definition_en: a muscle that pulls a body part toward the midline of the body
entries.example_cn: 内收肌有助于将双腿并拢。
entries.example_en: The adductor muscles help bring the legs together.

entries.definition_en: a sweetened beverage of diluted fruit juice
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喜欢用稀释的橙汁制成的清凉橙味饮料。
entries.example_en: The children enjoyed the refreshing orangeade made with diluted orange juice.

entries.definition_en: an insect of the genus Adelges
entries.example_cn: 园丁注意到松树枝上有一群球蚜属昆虫。
entries.example_en: The gardener noticed a cluster of adelgids on the pine branches.

entries.definition_en: a purine base found in DNA and RNA that pairs with thymine in DNA and with uracil in RNA
entries.example_cn: 腺嘌呤是 DNA 中的四种含氮碱基之一。
entries.example_en: Adenine is one of the four nucleobases in DNA.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of a gland or lymph node
entries.example_cn: 医生在检查肿大的淋巴结后，诊断该患者患有急性腺炎。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the patient with acute adenitis after examining the swollen lymph nodes.

entries.definition_en: a cancer that starts in the gland cells of an organ
entries.example_cn: 该患者被诊断为肺癌（腺癌）。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with an adenocarcinoma of the lung.

entries.definition_cn: 腺癌性的；与腺癌有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to or characterized by adenocarcinoma
entries.example_cn: 该肿瘤被确定为腺癌性肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The tumor was identified as adenocarcinomatous.

entries.definition_en: the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland
entries.example_cn: 由垂体前叶产生的激素调节生长和代谢。
entries.example_en: Hormones produced by the adenohypophysis regulate growth and metabolism.

entries.definition_en: a mass of lymphatic tissue located in the throat behind the uvula
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了孩子肿胀的腺样体。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the child's swollen adenoid.

entries.definition_en: relating to or resembling lymphatic glands or lymphoid tissue
entries.example_cn: 外科医生从病人的喉咙里切除了淋巴腺组织。
entries.example_en: The surgeon removed the adenoid tissue from the patient's throat.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of the adenoids
entries.example_cn: 这孩子患有慢性的腺样体充血。
entries.example_en: The child suffered from chronic adenoidal congestion.

entries.definition_en: having a nasal quality as if the nose were pinched
entries.example_cn: 他生病时声音听起来像是捏着鼻子发出的。
entries.example_en: His voice sounded adenoidal when he was sick.

entries.definition_en: surgery to remove the adenoids, often performed together with tonsil removal
entries.example_cn: 腺样体切除术后，这名儿童慢性呼吸困难的症状得到了显著缓解。
entries.example_en: After the adenoidectomy, the child experienced significant relief from chronic breathing difficulties.

entries.definition_en: a non-cancerous tumor that develops from glandular tissue
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出患者甲状腺有一个良性腺瘤。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the patient with a benign adenoma in the thyroid gland.

entries.definition_en: the condition of having enlarged glands
entries.example_cn: 医生在发现淋巴结肿大后，诊断该患者患有腺肿大。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the patient with adenomegaly after noticing swollen lymph nodes.

entries.definition_cn: 含有横纹肌细胞的肌肉肉瘤
entries.definition_en: a myosarcoma containing striated muscle cells
entries.example_cn: 由于肿瘤含有横纹肌细胞，病理学家将其确定为含横纹肌细胞的肌肉肉瘤。
entries.example_en: The pathologist identified the tumor as an adenomyosarcoma because it contained striated muscle cells.

entries.definition_en: a condition in which endometrial tissue grows into the muscular wall of the uterus
entries.example_cn: 患者在经历严重的经前疼痛后被诊断为子宫腺肌病。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with adenomyosis after experiencing severe premenstrual pain.

entries.definition_en: a disease or swelling of glandular tissue, especially the lymph glands
entries.example_cn: 医生在检查到肿大的淋巴结后，诊断该患者患有腺病。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the patient with adenopathy after examining the swollen lymph nodes.

entries.definition_en: a nucleoside consisting of adenine and ribose, found in RNA and in molecules such as ATP
entries.example_cn: 腺苷是身体能量携带分子的关键组成部分。
entries.example_en: Adenosine is a key component of the body's energy-carrying molecules.

entries.definition_en: a medical disorder affecting the glands of the body
entries.example_cn: 专科医生正在调查该患者的腺病，以确定最佳治疗方案。
entries.example_en: The specialist is investigating the patient's adenosis to determine the best treatment plan.

entries.definition_en: a virus that can cause upper respiratory infections or infectious pinkeye in humans
entries.example_cn: 腺病毒是引起类似感冒症状的常见原因。
entries.example_en: The adenovirus is a common cause of cold-like symptoms.

entries.definition_en: having or showing knowledge, skill, and aptitude
entries.example_cn: 他是一位熟练的厨师，能很快做出美味的饭菜。
entries.example_en: He is an adept cook who can prepare a delicious meal quickly.

entries.definition_en: a person who is extremely skilled in a particular field
entries.example_cn: 她擅长解决复杂的数学问题。
entries.example_en: She is an adept at solving complex mathematical problems.

entries.definition_en: the quality of performing tasks with great skill and ease
entries.example_cn: 她解决复杂问题的熟练程度给整个团队留下了深刻印象。
entries.example_en: Her adeptness at solving complex problems impressed the entire team.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being able to meet a need satisfactorily
entries.example_cn: 救援队质疑了避难所的充足性。
entries.example_en: The adequacy of the shelter was questioned by the rescue team.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being sufficient for a specific purpose
entries.example_cn: 证据的足够性对于法院的判决至关重要。
entries.example_en: The adequacy of the evidence was crucial for the court's decision.

entries.definition_en: having the necessary qualities or resources to meet a requirement
entries.example_cn: 这个房间对于小型会议来说足够了。
entries.example_en: The room is adequate for a small meeting.

entries.definition_en: sufficient for a particular purpose
entries.example_cn: 我们有一周的足够食物供应。
entries.example_en: We have adequate food supplies for the week.

entries.definition_en: acceptable or average in quality
entries.example_cn: 他的表现尚可，但令人印象深刻。
entries.example_en: His performance was adequate but not impressive.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is sufficient or good enough
entries.example_cn: 冬天这个房间供暖不足。
entries.example_en: The room was not adequately heated during the winter.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being sufficient to meet a need or requirement satisfactorily
entries.example_cn: 救援人员质疑应急物资的充足性。
entries.example_en: The adequateness of the emergency supplies was questioned by the relief workers.

entries.definition_en: a B vitamin essential for the metabolism of amino acids and starch
entries.example_cn: 研究人员正在研究吡哆醇如何影响氨基酸和淀粉的代谢过程。
entries.example_en: Researchers are studying how adermin influences the metabolic processes of amino acids and starch.

entries.definition_en: to come into close contact with; to stick or hold together firmly
entries.example_cn: 胶水帮助这两块木头紧密粘合。
entries.example_en: The glue helps the two pieces of wood adhere tightly.

entries.definition_en: to be compatible with or in accordance with something
entries.example_cn: 新政策必须符合公司的道德准则。
entries.example_en: The new policy must adhere to the company's ethical guidelines.

entries.definition_en: to follow through or carry out a plan without deviation
entries.example_cn: 尽管有延误，我们必须坚持原定的时间表。
entries.example_en: We must adhere to our original schedule despite the delays.

entries.definition_en: to be a devoted follower or supporter of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 许多粉丝忠诚地支持球队为球迷而战的哲学。
entries.example_en: Many fans adhere to the team's philosophy of playing for the fans.

entries.definition_en: to be loyal to a person, group, or cause
entries.example_cn: 士兵们宣誓效忠国家的宪法。
entries.example_en: The soldiers swore to adhere to their country's constitution.

entries.definition_en: to fasten something by adhesion
entries.example_cn: 用力按压，使标签粘牢在瓶子上。
entries.example_en: Press firmly to adhere the label to the bottle.

entries.definition_en: the act of supporting a cause, party, or religion faithfully
entries.example_cn: 她对党的原则的忠诚从未动摇。
entries.example_en: Her adherence to the party's principles never wavered.

entries.definition_en: the property of sticking together or the joining of different surfaces
entries.example_cn: 胶水强大的粘合性确保了木材保持在一起。
entries.example_en: The strong adherence of the glue ensured the wood stayed together.

entries.definition_en: someone who believes and helps to spread the doctrine of another
entries.example_cn: 他成为了新哲学的忠实信徒。
entries.example_en: He became a devoted adherent of the new philosophy.

entries.definition_en: sticking fast
entries.example_cn: 标签牢牢粘附在玻璃表面上。
entries.example_en: The label was adherent to the glass surface.

entries.definition_en: the property of sticking together or the act of joining different surfaces
entries.example_cn: 胶水粘在木头上的粘附力非常强。
entries.example_en: The adhesion of the glue to the wood was very strong.

entries.definition_en: an abnormal joining of body tissues, often occurring in the abdomen
entries.example_cn: 外科医生切除了阻塞肠道的粘连组织。
entries.example_en: The surgeon removed the adhesion that was blocking the intestine.

entries.definition_cn: 连接通常分离的解剖结构的瘢痕组织条带
entries.definition_en: a band of scar tissue that connects normally separate body parts
entries.example_cn: 该患者在手术后遭受了严重的瘢痕索困扰。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered from severe adhesions following the operation.

entries.definition_cn: 对事业、政党或宗教的忠诚拥护
entries.definition_en: loyal support for a cause, party, or religion
entries.example_cn: 他对政党的忠诚支持从未动摇。
entries.example_en: His adhesion to the political party never wavered.

entries.definition_en: a substance that unites or bonds surfaces together
entries.example_cn: 她用粘合剂修好了那个破碎的花瓶。
entries.example_en: She used an adhesive to fix the broken vase.

entries.definition_en: sticky or tending to adhere
entries.example_cn: 胶带牢牢黏在墙上。
entries.example_en: The adhesive tape stuck firmly to the wall.

entries.definition_en: the quality of sticking together, such as glue adhering to wood, or the joining of different surfaces
entries.example_cn: 这种新胶水的粘附性使其能有效粘合木材和金属。
entries.example_en: The adhesiveness of the new glue allows it to bond wood and metal effectively.

entries.definition_en: an organization that operates with very little formal structure or hierarchy
entries.example_cn: 这家初创公司采用无结构组织模式，以促进团队间的快速创新。
entries.example_en: The startup adopted an adhocracy to foster rapid innovation among its teams.

entries.definition_en: occurring without loss or gain of heat
entries.example_cn: 气体的绝热膨胀导致温度下降。
entries.example_en: The adiabatic expansion of the gas caused a drop in temperature.

entries.definition_en: the condition of a process occurring without any exchange of heat with the surroundings
entries.example_cn: 气体的迅速膨胀展示了该系统的绝热性。
entries.example_en: The rapid expansion of the gas demonstrated the adiabaticity of the system.

entries.definition_en: a religious ritual considered a matter of personal conscience rather than a scriptural command
entries.example_cn: 教众们争论这项新仪式究竟是属于个人良心的中性礼仪，还是必须遵守的教规。
entries.example_en: The congregation debated whether the new ceremony was an adiaphoron or a required practice.

entries.definition_en: in Stoic philosophy, a matter that has neither moral value nor disvalue
entries.example_cn: 斯多葛学派教导说吃肉是一件道德无关之事，将选择权留给个人判断。
entries.example_en: The Stoics taught that eating meat was an adiaphoron, leaving the choice to individual judgment.

entries.definition_en: a formal farewell
entries.example_cn: 他转向人群，在离开前说了最后的再见。
entries.example_en: He turned to the crowd and said a final adieu before leaving.

entries.definition_cn: 告别语；再见（尤用于西班牙语语境）
entries.definition_en: a word or expression used to say goodbye, especially in Spanish-speaking contexts
entries.example_cn: 她挥手告别，并在离开派对时喊道：“再见！”
entries.example_en: She waved goodbye and shouted adios as she left the party.

entries.definition_en: composed of or consisting of animal fat
entries.example_cn: 动物尾巴中的脂肪组织储存能量以供过冬。
entries.example_en: The adipose tissue in the animal's tail stores energy for winter.

entries.definition_cn: 含脂状态；脂肪多的状态
entries.definition_en: the quality or state of containing fat
entries.example_cn: 实验室测量了该组织的含脂状态。
entries.example_en: The adiposeness of the tissue was measured in the laboratory.

entries.definition_en: the condition of having excessive fat in the body
entries.example_cn: 医学研究正在调查早发性肥胖症的遗传成因。
entries.example_en: Medical research is investigating the genetic causes of early-onset adiposis.

entries.definition_en: the state of being excessively fat; obesity
entries.example_cn: 这名患者的肥胖增加了他患心血管疾病的风险。
entries.example_en: The patient's adiposity increased his risk of cardiovascular disease.

entries.definition_cn: 矿井平巷；从地表通入矿井的近水平巷道
entries.definition_en: a nearly horizontal passage from the surface into a mine
entries.example_cn: 矿工们利用这个矿井入口进入矿井的深层区域。
entries.example_en: Miners used the adit to access the deep levels of the mine.

entries.definition_en: the state of being next to or touching something
entries.example_cn: 这两个房间的邻近使得它们之间的交流变得很容易。
entries.example_en: The adjacency of the two rooms allows for easy communication between them.

entries.definition_en: nearest in space or position; immediately next to something
entries.example_cn: 隔壁的房间被用作储藏室。
entries.example_en: The adjacent room is used for storage.

entries.definition_en: sharing a common boundary or edge
entries.example_cn: 这两个接壤的国家有很长的边界。
entries.example_en: The two adjacent countries have a long border.

entries.definition_en: near or close to but not necessarily touching
entries.example_cn: 我们住在邻近的街区。
entries.example_en: We live in an adjacent neighborhood.

entries.definition_en: relating to or functioning as an adjective
entries.example_cn: 该短语的形容词性质使其易于修饰。
entries.example_en: The adjectival nature of the phrase makes it easy to modify.

entries.definition_en: an adjective-like phrase or clause
entries.example_cn: 这个句子包含一个形容词性成分，用来描述迟到的人。
entries.example_en: The sentence contains an adjectival describing the person who arrived late.

entries.definition_en: in the manner of an adjective
entries.example_cn: 这个短语作为形容词修饰名词'decision'。
entries.example_en: The phrase functions adjectivally to modify the noun 'decision'.

entries.definition_en: A word that modifies a noun or noun phrase or describes its referent.
entries.example_cn: 在短语“红苹果”中，单词“red”是一个形容词。
entries.example_en: In the phrase 'red apple', the word 'red' is an adjective.

entries.definition_en: the word class that qualifies nouns
entries.example_cn: 被称为形容词的词类修饰名词。
entries.example_en: The part of speech known as an adjective modifies nouns.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or functioning as an adjective
entries.example_cn: 形容词“happy”描述一种感觉。
entries.example_en: The adjective 'happy' describes a feeling.

entries.definition_cn: 与法律执行方式和程序规则有关的，而非与实体法律原则有关的
entries.definition_en: Relating to methods of enforcing law and rules of procedure, rather than to substantive legal principles.
entries.example_cn: 法官裁决了一个涉及程序法的事项。
entries.example_en: The judge ruled on a matter of adjective law concerning court procedure.

entries.definition_en: in the manner of an adjective
entries.example_cn: 这个短语以形容词的方式修饰名词'decision'。
entries.example_en: The phrase functions adjectively to modify the noun 'decision'.

entries.definition_en: to lie adjacent to another or share a boundary
entries.example_cn: 花园与公园毗邻。
entries.example_en: The garden adjoins the park.

entries.definition_en: to be in direct physical contact with
entries.example_cn: 两国在北部边界接壤。
entries.example_en: The two countries adjoin at the northern border.

entries.definition_en: to attach or add something to something else
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在博物馆旁增建一个新翼楼。
entries.example_en: They decided to adjoin a new wing to the museum.

entries.definition_en: to close a meeting or session at the end of it
entries.example_cn: 所有议程完成后，主席宣布会议结束。
entries.example_en: The chair adjourned the meeting after all the business had been completed.

entries.definition_en: to take a break from a meeting or gathering
entries.example_cn: 法官暂停法庭审理去吃午饭。
entries.example_en: The judge adjourned the court for lunch.

entries.definition_en: the official ending of a meeting or session
entries.example_cn: 议会于中午宣布休会。
entries.example_en: The adjournment of the parliament was announced at noon.

entries.definition_en: the act of postponing a meeting to a later time or place
entries.example_cn: 法院批准延期，以便证人能够赶到。
entries.example_en: The court granted an adjournment to allow the witnesses to travel.

entries.definition_en: to officially declare or determine that something is true or valid
entries.example_cn: 法院将裁定该合同因欺诈而无效。
entries.example_en: The court will adjudge the contract void due to fraud.

entries.definition_en: to award or assign something by judicial decision
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定将这份遗产判给遗孀。
entries.example_en: The court adjudged the estate to the widow.

entries.definition_en: to sentence or condemn someone
entries.example_cn: 法官判处被告五年监禁。
entries.example_en: The judge adjudged the defendant to five years in prison.

entries.definition_en: to act as a judge in a legal case
entries.example_cn: 法院将审理这两家公司之间的纠纷。
entries.example_en: The court will adjudicate the dispute between the two companies.

entries.definition_cn: 正式裁决或解决某件事，尤指以法官身份
entries.definition_en: to decide or settle a matter officially, especially as a judge
entries.example_cn: 委员会受邀裁决比赛并宣布获胜者。
entries.example_en: The committee was asked to adjudicate the competition and declare a winner.

entries.definition_cn: 裁决过程；法律程序中作出的裁决或判决
entries.definition_en: the act or process of adjudicating; a judgment or decision reached in a legal proceeding
entries.example_cn: 该案件的最终裁决将于下周公布。
entries.example_en: The final adjudication of the case will be announced next week.

entries.definition_en: relating to or concerned with the act of making a formal judgment or decision.
entries.example_cn: 法院行使裁决权来解决争端。
entries.example_en: The court's adjudicative powers were exercised to resolve the dispute.

entries.definition_en: a person who adjudicates or settles a dispute
entries.example_cn: 独立的仲裁者裁定支持租户。
entries.example_en: The independent adjudicator ruled in favor of the tenant.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involving the process of making a formal judgment or decision
entries.example_cn: 裁决委员会在做出最终裁决前审查了证据。
entries.example_en: The adjudicatory committee reviewed the evidence before making a final ruling.

entries.definition_cn: 附加在另一事物上的、但并非其必要组成部分的东西
entries.definition_en: something added to another thing but not an essential part of it
entries.example_cn: 这门在线课程作为大学主学位课程的附加内容开设。
entries.example_en: The online course was offered as an adjunct to the university’s main degree program.

entries.definition_en: a person who is an assistant or subordinate to another
entries.example_cn: 她担任主编的副手。
entries.example_en: She works as an adjunct to the chief editor.

entries.definition_en: a construction that can be used to extend the meaning of a word or phrase but is not one of the main constituents of a sentence
entries.example_cn: 在这个句子中，短语“在某种程度上”充当附加成分。
entries.example_en: The phrase 'in a way' acts as an adjunct in this sentence.

entries.definition_cn: 提供额外支持的；处于附属或次要职能的
entries.definition_en: providing additional support or serving in a subordinate capacity
entries.example_cn: 这位兼任教授帮助学生进行研究。
entries.example_en: The adjunct professor helped the students with their research.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to a person who is subordinate to another
entries.example_cn: 这位副手职员参加了会议。
entries.example_en: The adjunct staff member attended the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the act of joining or adjoining things together
entries.example_cn: 新翼的扩建增加了博物馆的容量。
entries.example_en: The adjunction of the new wing expanded the museum's capacity.

entries.definition_cn: （数学）向代数结构（如环或域）中添加一个或多个元素的过程；以及由此产生的结构
entries.definition_en: the process of adding one or more elements to an algebraic structure, such as a ring or field, and the structure produced by this process
entries.example_cn: 将元素 a、b 和 y 添加到环 R 后得到的环记作 R[a,b,y]。
entries.example_en: The ring obtained after adjoining the elements a, b, and y to the ring R is denoted R[a,b,y].

entries.definition_en: serving as an addition or supplement to something else
entries.example_cn: 这种辅助疗法有助于减轻主要药物的副作用。
entries.example_en: The adjunctive therapy helped reduce the side effects of the main medication.

entries.definition_en: a solemn and earnest appeal to someone to do something
entries.example_cn: 法官正式恳求证人说出真相。
entries.example_en: The judge issued a formal adjuration to the witness to tell the truth.

entries.definition_en: earnestly or solemnly entreating
entries.example_cn: 这封信恳切的语气旨在促使收件人采取行动。
entries.example_en: The adjuratory tone of the letter was intended to move the recipient to action.

entries.definition_en: containing a solemn charge or command
entries.example_cn: 该文件包含一个要求立即遵守的庄严命令条款。
entries.example_en: The document contained an adjuratory clause requiring immediate compliance.

entries.definition_en: to ask for or request something very earnestly
entries.example_cn: 他恳求朋友们保守秘密。
entries.example_en: He adjured his friends to keep the secret.

entries.definition_en: to command someone solemnly, often by appealing to a higher power
entries.example_cn: 法官庄严地命令陪审团作出公正的裁决。
entries.example_en: The judge adjured the jury to return a fair verdict.

entries.definition_en: to change something slightly so that it is correct or fits properly
entries.example_cn: 你需要调整镜子以便看得清楚。
entries.example_en: You need to adjust the mirror so you can see clearly.

entries.definition_en: to change your behavior or feelings to fit new conditions
entries.example_cn: 他花了一段时间才适应新的气候。
entries.example_en: It took him a while to adjust to the new climate.

entries.definition_en: to make two things match or correspond with each other
entries.example_cn: 我们必须调整计划以符合新的时间表。
entries.example_en: We must adjust our plans to match the new schedule.

entries.definition_en: to arrange things in a straight line or parallel to each other
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生把课桌排成一排。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the students to adjust their desks in a row.

entries.definition_en: to decide the amount of money to pay for an insurance claim
entries.example_cn: 保险公司将在几天内核定赔款。
entries.example_en: The insurance company will adjust the claim within a few days.

entries.definition_en: capable of being changed so as to match or fit
entries.example_cn: 这把椅子的高度可调节，你可以将其调整到合适的水平。
entries.example_en: The chair has an adjustable height so you can set it to the right level.

entries.definition_en: capable of being regulated
entries.example_cn: 恒温器允许设置可调节的温度。
entries.example_en: The thermostat allows for an adjustable temperature setting.

entries.definition_cn: 已调整以适应特定需求或使事物协调运作
entries.definition_en: changed to fit specific needs or to make things work together properly
entries.example_cn: 时间表已调整以适应新的会议。
entries.example_en: The schedule was adjusted to accommodate the new meeting.

entries.definition_cn: 已与周围环境建立舒适关系
entries.definition_en: having achieved a comfortable relationship with your surroundings
entries.example_cn: 这名新学生很好地适应了学校环境。
entries.example_en: The new student adjusted well to the school environment.

entries.definition_cn: 能适应日常生活需求；情绪稳定
entries.definition_en: able to cope with the demands of daily life; emotionally stable
entries.example_cn: 搬家后，她很快适应了新的生活。
entries.example_en: After the move, she quickly adjusted to her new life.

entries.definition_cn: (衣物) 已调整尺寸或款式以更适合
entries.definition_en: (of clothes) having the fit or style changed to be more suitable
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙被改过尺寸，穿在她身上非常合身。
entries.example_en: The dress was adjusted to fit her perfectly.

entries.definition_en: a person who investigates insurance claims and recommends settlements
entries.example_cn: 保险理赔员查看了受损的房屋。
entries.example_en: The insurance adjuster visited the damaged house.

entries.definition_en: helping to make something fit or work properly
entries.example_cn: 该调整机制使设备能够适应不同的温度。
entries.example_en: The adjustive mechanism allows the device to adapt to different temperatures.

entries.definition_en: the act of making something suitable or adapting to circumstances
entries.example_cn: 他迅速调整了相机设置。
entries.example_en: He made a quick adjustment to the camera settings.

entries.definition_en: a change made to the size, shape, or fit of something
entries.example_cn: 裁缝对裙子的下摆进行了改制。
entries.example_en: The tailor made an adjustment to the hem of the dress.

entries.definition_en: the process of adapting to new conditions
entries.example_cn: 适应新的气候花了她几周时间。
entries.example_en: The adjustment to the new climate took her a few weeks.

entries.definition_en: the act of changing something to match a standard
entries.example_cn: 这台机器需要定期校准以保持精度。
entries.example_en: The machine requires a regular adjustment to maintain accuracy.

entries.definition_en: an amount added or deducted based on specific circumstances
entries.example_cn: 他的最终账单上有一笔税务调整额。
entries.example_en: There was a tax adjustment on his final bill.

entries.definition_cn: 财务账户的结算或调账
entries.definition_en: the settling or balancing of a financial account
entries.example_cn: 信用卡公司对我的账户作了调整，免除了滞纳金。
entries.example_en: The credit card company made an adjustment to my account to waive the late fee.

entries.definition_cn: 保险公司对保险索赔的评估和理赔
entries.definition_en: the assessment and settlement of an insurance claim by an insurance company
entries.example_cn: 由于损失严重，保险理赔花了几周时间。
entries.example_en: The insurance adjustment took several weeks because the damage was extensive.

entries.definition_en: a person who investigates insurance claims or damage claims and recommends a settlement.
entries.example_cn: 理赔员在定损前前往现场评估损失。
entries.example_en: The adjustor visited the scene to assess the damage before settling the claim.

entries.definition_en: an officer who assists a senior military officer
entries.example_cn: 副官为将军的视察安排了日程。
entries.example_en: The adjutant organized the schedule for the general's inspection.

entries.definition_cn: 印度和东南亚特有的两种大型鹳之一
entries.definition_en: either of two large stork species native to India and Southeast Asia
entries.example_cn: 那只副官鹳静静地站在高草丛中。
entries.example_en: The adjutant stood motionless in the tall grass.

entries.definition_en: a substance added to a medical treatment to increase its effectiveness
entries.example_cn: 该疫苗含有辅助剂，以帮助免疫系统对抗原产生更强的反应。
entries.example_en: The vaccine contains an adjuvant to help the immune system respond more strongly to the antigen.

entries.definition_en: providing additional support or assistance
entries.example_cn: 辅助疗法为患者康复过程提供了额外支持。
entries.example_en: The adjuvant therapy provided extra support to the patient's recovery process.

entries.definition_en: enhancing the action or effectiveness of a medical treatment
entries.example_cn: 医生通常使用增效药物来增强主要化疗的作用。
entries.example_en: Doctors often use an adjuvant drug to enhance the action of the primary chemotherapy.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to create or manage advertising campaigns
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的广告人设计了一场改变品牌形象的活动。
entries.example_en: The famous adman designed a campaign that changed the brand's image.

entries.definition_cn: 易受大众媒体影响的公众群体
entries.definition_en: the segment of the public that is easily influenced by mass media (chiefly British)
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家调整了他的演讲，以吸引易受大众媒体影响的公众群体，而非知识分子。
entries.example_en: The politician tailored his speech to appeal to the admass rather than the intellectuals.

entries.definition_en: to measure out or apportion something
entries.example_cn: 法院在分配遗产前按份额确定了每位继承人应得的遗产。
entries.example_en: The court admeasured each heir’s share of the estate before distributing it.

entries.definition_en: to work in an administrative role; to supervise or be in charge of something
entries.example_cn: 她被任命管理这家新慈善机构。
entries.example_en: She was appointed to administer the new charity.

entries.definition_en: to give or apply medications
entries.example_cn: 护士小心地注射了药物。
entries.example_en: The nurse administered the injection carefully.

entries.definition_en: to perform a church sacrament ritually
entries.example_cn: 牧师为婴儿施行了洗礼圣礼。
entries.example_en: The priest administered the sacrament of baptism to the infant.

entries.definition_en: to distribute or apportion something
entries.example_cn: 慈善机构向这些家庭发放了紧急援助。
entries.example_en: The charity administered emergency aid to the families.

entries.definition_en: to cause a patient to ingest a drug, openly or deceptively
entries.example_cn: 护理人员把药混在食物里让病人服下。
entries.example_en: The caregiver administered the medicine by mixing it into the patient's food.

entries.definition_en: able to be administered or managed
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策可以由这个小团队进行管理。
entries.example_en: The new policy is administrable by the small team.

entries.definition_en: to work in an administrative capacity or to supervise an organization
entries.example_cn: 她被聘来管理新部门。
entries.example_en: She was hired to administrate the new department.

entries.definition_en: the way in which a group of people manages its business or affairs
entries.example_cn: 新政府承诺减税。
entries.example_en: The new administration has promised to reduce taxes.

entries.definition_en: the group of people responsible for managing an organization or system
entries.example_cn: 大学的管理部门包括校长和几个委员会。
entries.example_en: The administration of the university includes the president and several committees.

entries.definition_cn: 某位总统或领导人执政期间的政府；政府当局
entries.definition_en: the government or administration under a particular president or leader
entries.example_cn: 奥巴马政府推出了几项重大政策。
entries.example_en: The Obama administration introduced several major policies.

entries.definition_en: the act of governing or exercising authority
entries.example_cn: 治理国家需要强有力的领导。
entries.example_en: The administration of the country requires strong leadership.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving medicine to someone
entries.example_cn: 护士负责给药。
entries.example_en: The nurse is responsible for the administration of the drug.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving punishment according to the law
entries.example_cn: 司法是法院的职责。
entries.example_en: The administration of justice is the duty of the courts.

entries.definition_en: relating to or responsible for the management of an organization or government
entries.example_cn: 她在大学的行政部门工作。
entries.example_en: She works in the administrative department of the university.

entries.definition_en: by or for an administrator
entries.example_cn: 该决定是行政上做出的，未咨询员工意见。
entries.example_en: The decision was made administratively without consulting the staff.

entries.definition_en: someone who administers a business
entries.example_cn: 这位新管理员重组了公司的财务。
entries.example_en: The new administrator reorganized the company's finances.

entries.definition_cn: 管理政府机构或部门的人
entries.definition_en: someone who manages a government agency or department
entries.example_cn: 该部门的管理员宣布了新安全规定。
entries.example_en: The administrator of the department announced new safety regulations.

entries.definition_cn: 被遗嘱认证法院指定分配无遗嘱死者遗产的人
entries.definition_en: the party appointed by a probate court to distribute the estate of someone who dies without a will or without naming an executor
entries.example_cn: 法院指定了一位管理员来处理死者的遗产。
entries.example_en: The court appointed an administrator to handle the deceased's estate.

entries.definition_en: tiresome but essential details and tasks required to run an organization
entries.example_cn: 我们整个上午都在处理没完没了的行政琐事。
entries.example_en: We spent the morning dealing with endless administrivia.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being admirable; excellent worthiness
entries.example_cn: 他牺牲的令人钦佩的品质鼓舞了整个社区。
entries.example_en: The admirability of his sacrifice inspired the whole community.

entries.definition_en: worthy of admiration
entries.example_cn: 她帮助他人的奉献精神确实令人钦佩。
entries.example_en: Her dedication to helping others is truly admirable.

entries.definition_en: worthy of respect
entries.example_cn: 尽管困难重重，他仍信守诺言，这值得尊敬。
entries.example_en: It is admirable that he kept his promise despite the difficulties.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being admirable; excellent worthiness
entries.example_cn: 她品格的令人钦佩之处显而易见。
entries.example_en: The admirableness of her character was evident to all.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is worthy of admiration; very well
entries.example_cn: 她出色地处理了这场危机。
entries.example_en: She handled the crisis admirably.

entries.definition_cn: 达到令人钦佩的程度；非常出色地
entries.definition_en: to an admirable or impressively high degree
entries.example_cn: 他们的质量有了令人钦佩的巨大提升。
entries.example_en: They have made admirably great improvements in quality.

entries.definition_cn: 海军上将；海军上将军衔
entries.definition_en: a high naval rank, or a person holding that rank
entries.example_cn: 海军上将命令舰队准备战斗。
entries.example_en: The admiral ordered the fleet to prepare for battle.

entries.definition_cn: Admiral butterfly (一种色彩鲜艳的蝴蝶)
entries.definition_en: a butterfly with bright colors
entries.example_cn: 我们在花园里看到了一只美丽的 Admiral 蝴蝶。
entries.example_en: We saw a beautiful admiral butterfly in the garden.

entries.definition_en: the government department responsible for the navy
entries.example_cn: 海军部下令建造新舰船。
entries.example_en: The Admiralty ordered the construction of new ships.

entries.definition_en: the office or position of an admiral
entries.example_cn: 他在战役成功后被任命为海军上将。
entries.example_en: He was appointed to the Admiralty after his successful campaign.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of pleasure and approval for someone or something
entries.example_cn: 她满怀钦佩地注视着那幅画。
entries.example_en: She looked at the painting with great admiration.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of wonder caused by something strange
entries.example_cn: 孩子们惊奇地看着这场魔术表演。
entries.example_en: The children watched the magic show with admiration.

entries.definition_en: a positive opinion or judgment
entries.example_cn: 这本书受到了评论界的广泛好评。
entries.example_en: The book received widespread admiration from critics.

entries.definition_en: to feel deep respect and warm approval for someone or something
entries.example_cn: 我钦佩你面对如此困难时的勇气。
entries.example_en: I admire your courage in facing such difficulties.

entries.definition_en: to look at something with pleasure and approval
entries.example_cn: 她停下来欣赏美丽的日落。
entries.example_en: She stopped to admire the beautiful sunset.

entries.definition_en: a person who admires or respects someone
entries.example_cn: 她是那位著名作家作品的仰慕者。
entries.example_en: She is a great admirer of the famous author's work.

entries.definition_cn: 支持政治人物或球队的人
entries.definition_en: a person who supports a politician or team
entries.example_cn: 这位球队的支持者在比赛期间从看台上挥舞着旗帜。
entries.example_en: An admirer of the team waved a flag from the stands during the game.

entries.definition_en: a person who admires a young woman
entries.example_cn: 这位追求者每周都送花给她。
entries.example_en: The admirer sent her flowers every week.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows admiration
entries.example_cn: 她钦佩地看着他。
entries.example_en: She looked at him admiringly.

entries.definition_cn: 可采纳性；（尤指证据在法庭上的）可采性
entries.definition_en: the quality of being admissible or allowable, especially as evidence in court
entries.example_cn: 辩护律师质疑了该证据的可采性。
entries.example_en: The admissibility of the evidence was questioned by the defense lawyer.

entries.definition_en: worthy of being allowed or accepted
entries.example_cn: 提出的证据在法庭上是可以被采纳的。
entries.example_en: The evidence presented was admissible in court.

entries.definition_cn: （启发式算法）不高估达到目标所需成本的
entries.definition_en: describing a heuristic that never overestimates the cost of reaching a goal
entries.example_cn: 可采纳的启发式函数能保证 A* 找到最优路径。
entries.example_en: An admissible heuristic guarantees that A* can find an optimal path.

entries.definition_en: the act of admitting someone, especially to an institution
entries.example_cn: 他昨天被通知已被大学录取。
entries.example_en: His admission to the university was announced yesterday.

entries.definition_en: the act of acknowledging that something is true
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上完全承认了自己的错误。
entries.example_en: He made a full admission of his mistakes during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the money paid to gain entry to a place
entries.example_cn: 博物馆对学生免收入场费。
entries.example_en: Admission to the museum is free for students.

entries.definition_en: the right or permission to enter a place
entries.example_cn: 凭这张票，您可以进入所有展厅。
entries.example_en: With this ticket, you have admission to all the exhibits.

entries.definition_en: tending to admit or allow
entries.example_cn: 这项准许进入的政策允许访客自由进入。
entries.example_en: The admissive policy allowed visitors to enter freely.

entries.definition_en: to declare that something is true
entries.example_cn: 他不得不承认自己错了。
entries.example_en: He had to admit that he was wrong.

entries.definition_en: to allow someone to enter a place
entries.example_cn: 守卫不许可无票者入内。
entries.example_en: The guard will not admit anyone without a ticket.

entries.definition_en: to allow someone to participate or exercise rights
entries.example_cn: 俱乐部上周接纳了新成员。
entries.example_en: The club admitted new members last week.

entries.definition_en: to allow someone to join a group or community
entries.example_cn: 他们让他进入了那所大学。
entries.example_en: They admitted him to the university.

entries.definition_en: to have room for; to hold without crowding
entries.example_cn: 这个小房间容纳不了十个人。
entries.example_en: The small room cannot admit more than ten people.

entries.definition_en: to make something possible
entries.example_cn: 证据不容许有其他结论。
entries.example_en: The evidence admits of no other conclusion.

entries.definition_en: to give access or entrance to
entries.example_cn: 这把钥匙可以打开保险箱。
entries.example_en: The key admits access to the safe.

entries.definition_en: to serve as a means of entrance
entries.example_cn: 门让光线进入房间。
entries.example_en: The door admits light into the room.

entries.definition_en: able or permitted to be admitted
entries.example_cn: 那名获准接纳的乘客被允许进入限制区域。
entries.example_en: The admittable passenger was allowed into the restricted zone.

entries.definition_en: the act of allowing someone to enter
entries.example_cn: 保安在准许进入之前检查了身份证件。
entries.example_en: The security guard checked the ID before granting admittance.

entries.definition_en: the right to enter a place
entries.example_cn: 您的门票赋予您参加音乐会的准入权。
entries.example_en: Your ticket grants you admittance to the concert.

entries.definition_cn: 诚然；不可否认（常用于承认事实后引出转折）
entries.definition_en: used to acknowledge a fact, often before contrasting it with another point
entries.example_cn: 诚然，这个项目比我们预期的要困难得多。
entries.example_en: Admittedly, the project was more difficult than we had expected.

usage.label: conjunctive
usage.pattern: Often followed by but to introduce a counterpoint; source w12059r1.

entries.definition_en: to mix or mingle substances together
entries.example_cn: 科学家在受控环境中混合这些化学物质以研究它们的反应。
entries.example_en: Scientists admix the chemicals in a controlled environment to study their reaction.

entries.definition_cn: 混合物质的行为或过程
entries.definition_en: The act or process of admixing substances.
entries.example_cn: 混合后形成均匀的混合物。
entries.example_en: The admix results in a uniform mixture.

entries.definition_cn: 混合后形成的混合物，尤指加入另一种材料中的合金
entries.definition_en: A mixture produced by admixing, especially an alloy added to another material.
entries.example_cn: 这种玻璃离聚物含有银合金混合物，以增强强度。
entries.example_en: The glass ionomer contains a silver alloy admix for added strength.

entries.definition_en: an additional ingredient that is added by mixing with the base substance
entries.example_cn: 厨师添加了少量香料作为添加剂以增强汤的味道。
entries.example_en: The chef added a small admixture of spices to enhance the flavor of the soup.

entries.definition_en: the act of mixing two or more substances together
entries.example_cn: 油和水的混合需要特殊的乳化剂才能发生。
entries.example_en: The admixture of oil and water requires a special emulsifier to occur.

entries.definition_en: the state of impairing the quality or reducing the value of something by mixing it with inferior elements
entries.example_cn: 掺入廉价材料显著降低了产品的耐用性。
entries.example_en: The admixture of cheap materials significantly reduced the durability of the product.

entries.definition_en: to advise someone to improve their conduct
entries.example_cn: 老师劝告学生在课堂上更专心。
entries.example_en: The teacher admonished the student to pay more attention in class.

entries.definition_en: to warn someone firmly against wrongdoing or danger
entries.example_cn: 船长严厉警告船员在暴风雨期间要保持警惕。
entries.example_en: The captain admonished the crew to be vigilant during the storm.

entries.definition_en: to rebuke or reprimand someone for wrongdoing
entries.example_cn: 她因他无正当理由违反规定而责备了他。
entries.example_en: She admonished him for breaking the rules without a valid reason.

entries.definition_en: a person who gives a warning to prevent a mistake
entries.example_cn: 老师充当了告诫者的角色，在考试前提醒学生们注意规则。
entries.example_en: The teacher acted as an admonisher, reminding the students of the rules before the exam.

entries.definition_en: expressing reproof or reproach as a corrective measure
entries.example_cn: 老师向那个说话的学生投去训诫的目光。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave an admonishing look to the student who was talking.

entries.definition_en: a firm rebuke or scolding.
entries.example_cn: 老师的责备对于纠正学生的行为是必要的。
entries.example_en: The teacher's admonishment was necessary to correct the student's behavior.

entries.definition_en: cautionary advice given about something that is about to happen, especially danger
entries.example_cn: 老师关于小心化学品的警告是有根据的。
entries.example_en: The teacher's admonition to be careful with the chemicals was well-founded.

entries.definition_en: a firm rebuke or scolding
entries.example_cn: 他因错过截止日期而受到了经理的严厉训斥。
entries.example_en: He received a stern admonition from his manager for missing the deadline.

entries.definition_en: serving to warn someone of danger or trouble
entries.example_cn: 闪烁的红灯是提醒人停下来的警告信号。
entries.example_en: The flashing red light was an admonitory signal to stop.

entries.definition_en: expressing reproof or reproach intended to correct behavior
entries.example_cn: 老师向那个说话的学生投去训诫的目光。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave an admonitory look to the student who was talking.

entries.definition_cn: 与不同类型结构合生或贴生的
entries.definition_en: attached or fused to a structure of a different kind
entries.example_cn: 在这朵花中，花瓣与萼片合生，形成一个连续的管状结构。
entries.example_en: In this flower, the petals are adnate to the sepals, forming a continuous tube.

entries.definition_en: accessory or adjoining anatomical parts or appendages to an organ
entries.example_cn: 外科医生仔细检查了卵巢的附属器官。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the adnexa of the ovary carefully.

entries.definition_en: of or pertaining to adnexa
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了卵巢的附属结构。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the adnexal structures of the ovary.

entries.definition_en: an adjective that functions as a noun
entries.example_cn: 在短语“穷人”中，单词“poor”作为一个名词化的形容词，指代人。
entries.example_en: In the phrase 'the poor', the word 'poor' acts as an adnoun referring to people.

entries.definition_en: a fuss or commotion
entries.example_cn: 火警响起时引起了一阵骚动。
entries.example_en: There was an ado when the fire alarm went off.

entries.definition_en: a brick made of clay and dried by the sun
entries.example_cn: 沙漠中的房屋通常用土坯砖建造。
entries.example_en: Houses in the desert are often constructed using adobe.

entries.definition_en: the clay used to make adobe bricks
entries.example_cn: 古老的墙壁是用晒干的土坯建成的。
entries.example_en: The ancient walls were built from sun-dried adobe.

entries.definition_cn: 一种菲律宾菜肴，通常将猪肉或鸡肉在含酱油、醋和蒜的酱汁中慢炖
entries.definition_en: a Philippine dish of meat, usually pork or chicken, slowly cooked in a sauce containing soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐点了阿多波。
entries.example_en: We ordered adobo for dinner.

entries.definition_en: a marinade
entries.example_cn: 这个食谱要求将鸡肉放在腌料中腌一夜。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for chicken to be left in adobo overnight.

entries.definition_en: to become an adolescent or pass through the period of adolescence
entries.example_cn: 这个男孩在十几岁初期开始进入青春期。
entries.example_en: The boy began to adolesce during his early teenage years.

entries.definition_en: the time period between the beginning of puberty and adulthood
entries.example_cn: 许多青少年在青春期挣扎。
entries.example_en: Many teenagers struggle during adolescence.

entries.definition_en: the state of being between puberty and adulthood
entries.example_cn: 他仍处于青春期。
entries.example_en: He is still in adolescence.

entries.definition_en: a young person who has started puberty but is not yet fully grown
entries.example_cn: 该校有一个针对青少年健康的特别项目。
entries.example_en: The school has a special program for adolescent health.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of an adolescent
entries.example_cn: 青少年的行为可能难以预测。
entries.example_en: Adolescent behavior can be unpredictable.

entries.definition_en: between the ages of 13 and 19
entries.example_cn: 该调查重点关注十三至十九岁的人群。
entries.example_en: The survey focused on the adolescent population.

entries.definition_en: showing a lack of maturity
entries.example_cn: 他那不成熟的态度让人很难与他合作。
entries.example_en: His adolescent attitude made it hard to work with him.

entries.definition_cn: 处于青春期发育阶段的
entries.definition_en: in the stage of development between puberty and maturity
entries.example_cn: 处于青春期发育阶段的身体会发生显著变化。
entries.example_en: The adolescent body undergoes significant changes.

entries.definition_en: to choose and start using a method, idea, or policy
entries.example_cn: 政府决定采纳新的安全法规。
entries.example_en: The government decided to adopt new safety regulations.

entries.definition_en: to take up and practice as one's own
entries.example_cn: 她采用了一种更高效的工作方式。
entries.example_en: She adopted a more efficient way of working.

entries.definition_en: to take a child into one's family and raise as one's own
entries.example_cn: 他们去年收养了一个女婴。
entries.example_en: They adopted a baby girl last year.

entries.definition_cn: 接受（某种主张或意识形态）
entries.definition_en: to take up the cause or ideology of someone and use it as one's own
entries.example_cn: 该党接受了环保主义者的观点。
entries.example_en: The party adopted the environmentalist's views.

entries.definition_en: to take on titles, offices, or duties
entries.example_cn: 他接受了团队领导者的角色。
entries.example_en: He adopted the role of team leader.

entries.definition_en: to take on a certain form, attribute, or aspect
entries.example_cn: 该项目呈现出更灵活的结构。
entries.example_en: The project adopted a more flexible structure.

entries.definition_en: to change a story so that it can be performed as a play
entries.example_cn: 这部戏剧改编自一部著名小说。
entries.example_en: The play was adapted from a famous novel.

entries.definition_en: suitable for adoption
entries.example_cn: 收容所有几只可收养的小狗在等待新家。
entries.example_en: The shelter has several adoptable puppies waiting for new homes.

entries.definition_en: a person who has been adopted
entries.example_cn: 这名被收养者在多年后与亲生父母团聚。
entries.example_en: The adoptee was reunited with their biological parents after many years.

entries.definition_en: a person who legally takes a child of other parents and raises them as their own
entries.example_cn: 收养人和被收养的孩子多年来建立了深厚的感情纽带。
entries.example_en: The adopter and the adopted child have formed a loving bond over the years.

entries.definition_en: the legal process of making someone a child of another family
entries.example_cn: 他们去年办理了收养手续。
entries.example_en: They went through the adoption process last year.

entries.definition_cn: 采用或挪用其他来源的观点或文字
entries.definition_en: the act of taking and using ideas or words from another source
entries.example_cn: 作者因采用其他来源的观点而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The author was criticized for adopting ideas from another source.

entries.definition_en: accepting something with approval; receiving it favorably
entries.example_cn: 该提议得到了广泛的接受。
entries.example_en: The proposal met with widespread adoption.

entries.definition_en: relating to parents or children who are connected through adoption
entries.example_cn: 养父母非常爱他们的女儿。
entries.example_en: The adoptive parents loved their daughter very much.

entries.definition_en: acquired as your own by free choice
entries.example_cn: 她自愿决定改变自己的职业道路。
entries.example_en: She made an adoptive decision to change her career path.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being extremely attractive or charming
entries.example_cn: 这只小狗的可爱模样让人无法抗拒。
entries.example_en: The adorability of the puppy made it impossible for anyone to resist.

entries.definition_en: lovable especially in a childlike or naive way
entries.example_cn: 那只可爱的小狗开心地摇着尾巴。
entries.example_en: The adorable puppy wagged its tail happily.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being adorable
entries.example_cn: 小狗的可爱让每个人都笑了。
entries.example_en: The adorableness of the puppy made everyone smile.

entries.definition_en: in an adorable manner
entries.example_cn: 那只小狗用一种可爱的眼神看着她。
entries.example_en: The puppy looked at her adorably.

entries.definition_en: deep love and respect for someone
entries.example_cn: 她满怀爱意地注视着孩子。
entries.example_en: She looked at her child with pure adoration.

entries.definition_en: the act of admiring someone very much
entries.example_cn: 人群向歌手表达了极大的钦佩。
entries.example_en: The crowd gave the singer their adoration.

entries.definition_en: worship given to God
entries.example_cn: 大教堂是崇拜上帝的地方。
entries.example_en: The cathedral is a place of adoration.

entries.definition_en: love intensely
entries.example_cn: 孩子们非常爱他们的父母。
entries.example_en: Children adore their parents.

entries.definition_en: someone who deeply admires, is fond of, or loves someone or something
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻人以那位著名女演员的狂热爱慕者而闻名。
entries.example_en: The young man was known as an ardent adorer of the famous actress.

entries.definition_en: showing adoration
entries.example_cn: 人群用爱慕的眼神注视着那位名人。
entries.example_en: The crowd watched the celebrity with adoring eyes.

entries.definition_en: extravagantly or foolishly loving and indulgent
entries.example_cn: 她溺爱着她那个被宠坏的孩子。
entries.example_en: She was adoring of her spoiled child.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows deep love and admiration
entries.example_cn: 她深情地看着他。
entries.example_en: She looked at him adoringly.

entries.definition_en: to make something more attractive by adding decorations or ornaments.
entries.example_cn: 她用美丽的花朵装饰了她的裙子。
entries.example_en: She adorned her dress with beautiful flowers.

entries.definition_en: to be beautiful to look at.
entries.example_cn: 花园里种满了五颜六色的花，看起来很美。
entries.example_en: The garden is adorned with colorful flowers.

entries.definition_en: to furnish with power or authority, especially of kings or emperors.
entries.example_cn: 国王授予他的儿子王子头衔。
entries.example_en: The king adorned his son with the title of prince.

entries.definition_en: provided with something intended to increase its beauty or distinction
entries.example_cn: 大厅装饰着鲜花。
entries.example_en: The hall was adorned with flowers.

entries.definition_en: a decoration added to make something look more interesting
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙很简单，但胸针是一个美丽的装饰物。
entries.example_en: The dress was simple, but the brooch was a beautiful adornment.

entries.definition_en: The act of decorating.
entries.example_cn: 她佩戴金饰的行为反映了她的富有。
entries.example_en: Her adornment with gold jewelry reflected her wealth.

entries.definition_cn: 颂扬琐碎或卑鄙事物的写作
entries.definition_en: the art or practice of writing in praise of trivial or base subjects
entries.example_cn: 作者的作品是颂扬琐碎事物的写作的经典范例，赞美了日常生活的平凡方面。
entries.example_en: The author's work is a classic example of adoxography, celebrating the mundane aspects of daily life.

entries.definition_cn: 紧贴或平贴于某物表面
entries.definition_en: pressed close to or lying flat against a surface
entries.example_cn: 叶子紧贴着茎，从远处很难看见。
entries.example_en: The leaves were adpressed to the stem, making them difficult to see from a distance.

entries.definition_en: of or pertaining to the adrenal glands or their secretions
entries.example_cn: 肾上腺疲劳是替代医学中经常讨论的一种状况。
entries.example_en: Adrenal fatigue is a condition often discussed in alternative medicine.

entries.definition_en: near the kidneys
entries.example_cn: 肾上腺位于肾脏附近。
entries.example_en: The adrenal glands are located near the kidneys.

entries.definition_en: either of a pair of complex endocrine glands situated near the kidney
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了病人的肾上腺。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the patient's adrenal glands.

entries.definition_en: surgical removal of one or both adrenal glands
entries.example_cn: 患者接受了肾上腺切除术以治疗肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The patient underwent an adrenalectomy to treat the tumor.

entries.definition_en: a hormone secreted by the adrenal glands in response to stress
entries.example_cn: 过山车的刺激让他感到肾上腺素飙升。
entries.example_en: The thrill of the roller coaster gave him a rush of adrenaline.

entries.definition_en: excitement or a thrill
entries.example_cn: 她喜欢沿山路飞驰时的刺激感。
entries.example_en: She loves the adrenaline of racing down a mountain trail.

entries.definition_cn: 肾上腺皮质成熟的一个阶段，通常发生在六至十岁，与青春期相关
entries.definition_en: a stage of adrenal-cortex maturation associated with puberty, typically occurring between ages six and ten
entries.example_cn: 应将肾上腺皮质功能初现过早与阴毛过早出现区分开来，尽管肾上腺皮质功能初现通常会导致阴毛出现。
entries.example_en: Premature adrenarche should be distinguished from premature pubarche (early onset of sexual hair), even though adrenarche commonly causes pubarche.

entries.definition_cn: 肾上腺素能的；与肾上腺素的释放或作用有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to epinephrine (its release or action)
entries.example_cn: 肾上腺素反应有助于身体对抗压力。
entries.example_en: The adrenergic response helps the body fight stress.

entries.definition_cn: 肾上腺素能化合物或药物
entries.definition_en: an adrenergic compound or drug
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种具有肾上腺素效应的药物来治疗休克。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed an adrenergic to treat the shock.

entries.definition_en: relating to or produced by the outer layer (cortex) of the adrenal glands
entries.example_cn: 肾上腺皮质激素在调节身体对压力的反应方面起着至关重要的作用。
entries.example_en: Adrenocortical hormones play a vital role in regulating the body's response to stress.

entries.definition_cn: 刺激或作用于肾上腺皮质的
entries.definition_en: stimulating or acting on the adrenal cortex
entries.example_cn: 促肾上腺皮质激素在调节身体的应激反应中起着至关重要的作用。
entries.example_en: The adrenocorticotrophic hormone plays a crucial role in regulating the body's stress response.

entries.definition_cn: 由垂体前叶产生并刺激肾上腺皮质的激素
entries.definition_en: a hormone produced by the anterior pituitary gland that stimulates the adrenal cortex
entries.example_cn: 当身体暴露于严重压力时，促肾上腺皮质激素的水平会显著上升。
entries.example_en: Levels of adrenocorticotrophin rise significantly when the body is exposed to severe stress.

entries.definition_cn: 促肾上腺皮质的；刺激肾上腺皮质的
entries.definition_en: stimulating or acting on the adrenal cortex
entries.example_cn: 这种激素会刺激肾上腺皮质。
entries.example_en: The hormone is adrenocorticotropic in its effect on the adrenal glands.

entries.definition_en: a hormone made by the front part of the pituitary gland that triggers the adrenal cortex to produce hormones
entries.example_cn: 医生解释说，促肾上腺皮质激素调节身体的压力反应。
entries.example_en: The doctor explained that adrenocorticotropin regulates the body's stress response.

entries.definition_en: a type of steroid with male hormone activity that is found in the outer layer of the adrenal gland
entries.example_cn: 研究人员正在研究肾上腺雄酮，以了解其在激素平衡中的作用。
entries.example_en: Researchers are studying adrenosterone to understand its role in hormonal balance.

entries.definition_en: moving aimlessly without a clear direction or purpose
entries.example_cn: 失业后，他感到完全漫无目的地漂泊。
entries.example_en: After losing his job, he felt completely adrift.

entries.definition_en: afloat on the surface of a body of water
entries.example_cn: 船沉没后，救生筏仍漂浮在水面上。
entries.example_en: The life raft remained adrift after the ship sank.

entries.definition_cn: 落后于对手，或低于规定的分数、数量或名次
entries.definition_en: behind one's opponents or below a required score, number, or position
entries.example_cn: 这支球队落后对手六分。
entries.example_en: The team were six points adrift of their rivals.

entries.definition_en: off course; wandering aimlessly
entries.example_cn: 由于风暴，船只偏离了航向。
entries.example_en: The ship was adrift due to a storm.

entries.definition_en: floating freely; not anchored
entries.example_cn: 那艘小船随波逐流地漂在湖中央。
entries.example_en: The small boat was adrift in the middle of the lake.

entries.definition_en: skillful and quick in action or thought
entries.example_cn: 她擅长解决复杂的问题。
entries.example_en: She is adroit at solving complex problems.

entries.definition_en: in a skillful and clever way
entries.example_cn: 他巧妙地避开了那个棘手的问题。
entries.example_en: He adroitly avoided the difficult question.

entries.definition_en: skillful performance or ability without difficulty
entries.example_cn: 这位舞者的灵巧令观众惊叹。
entries.example_en: The adroitness of the dancer amazed the audience.

entries.definition_en: added or coming from something outside; not part of the original nature
entries.example_cn: 建筑工地的外加噪音让人难以集中注意力。
entries.example_en: The adscititious noise from the construction site made it difficult to concentrate.

entries.definition_en: supplemental; not essential to the true nature of something
entries.example_cn: 该软件的非本质功能对于基本任务来说是不需要的。
entries.example_en: The adscititious features of the software were not needed for the basic task.

entries.definition_en: written or printed right after another character and aligned with it
entries.example_cn: 在公式中，附标数字表示元素的顺序。
entries.example_en: In the formula, the adscript number indicates the order of the element.

entries.definition_cn: 隶属于土地的；依附于土地的
entries.definition_en: bound to a piece of land so that their service follows the land's owner
entries.example_cn: 历史上，隶属于土地的人不能离开他们依附的土地。
entries.example_en: Historically, an adscript person could not leave the land they were attached to.

entries.definition_en: to cause a liquid or gas to collect on the surface of a solid or liquid.
entries.example_cn: 活性炭过滤器会吸附水中的杂质。
entries.example_en: The charcoal filter will adsorb impurities from the water.

entries.definition_en: able to be taken up and held on the surface of a solid material
entries.example_cn: 这种毒素很容易被吸附，可用活性炭从水中去除。
entries.example_en: The toxin is highly adsorbable and can be removed from water by activated carbon.

entries.definition_en: a substance that has been or can be adsorbed onto a surface
entries.example_cn: 吸附质积聚在过滤器的表面上。
entries.example_en: The adsorbate accumulated on the surface of the filter.

entries.definition_cn: 可被固体表面吸附或在其上聚集的
entries.definition_en: capable of being adsorbed onto or accumulating on a solid surface
entries.example_cn: 这种可吸附材料可以被固体表面吸附。
entries.example_en: The adsorbate material can be adsorbed onto a solid surface.

entries.definition_en: a solid or liquid that adsorbs another substance onto its surface
