entries.example_en: We saw a chaffinch hopping on the garden fence.

entries.definition_en: covered with or full of chaff
entries.example_cn: 风吹着满是谷壳的种子飘过田野。
entries.example_en: The wind blew the chaffy seeds across the field.

entries.definition_en: of little value or importance
entries.example_cn: 委员会忽略了他那些无价值的评论。
entries.example_en: His chaffy remarks were ignored by the committee.

entries.definition_cn: 因摩擦造成的皮肤疼痛或刺激
entries.definition_en: painful soreness or irritation of the skin caused by rubbing or friction
entries.example_cn: 那条紧腰带让他的腰部有些磨擦疼痛。
entries.example_en: The tight belt caused some chafing on his waist.

entries.definition_en: strong feelings of embarrassment
entries.example_cn: 他因忘记她的生日而感到深深的懊恼。
entries.example_en: He felt deep chagrin after forgetting her birthday.

entries.definition_en: cause to feel shame; hurt the pride of
entries.example_cn: 这个坏消息让团队成员们感到懊恼。
entries.example_en: The bad news chagrined the team members.

entries.definition_en: feeling or caused to feel ill at ease, self-conscious, or ashamed
entries.example_cn: 她意识到自己忘了他的生日，感到十分懊恼。
entries.example_en: She was chagrined to realize she had forgotten his birthday.

entries.definition_en: a series of metal rings fitted together to make a flexible ligament
entries.example_cn: 自行车链条需要上油。
entries.example_en: The bicycle chain needs oiling.

entries.definition_en: a series of things that depend on each other
entries.example_cn: 经济处于一连串向下的事件中。
entries.example_en: The economy is in a downward chain of events.

entries.definition_en: a group of similar businesses owned by one company
entries.example_cn: 我们去了同一家连锁集团的几家餐厅。
entries.example_en: We visited several restaurants in the same chain.

entries.definition_en: anything that acts as a restraint
entries.example_cn: 繁重的工作量束缚了他的创造力。
entries.example_en: The heavy workload was a chain on his creativity.

entries.definition_en: to connect or arrange things into a chain by linking them
entries.example_cn: 该软件自动将文件链接在一起。
entries.example_en: The software chains the files together automatically.

entries.definition_en: to fasten or secure something with chains
entries.example_cn: 他们把狗锁在柱子上。
entries.example_en: They chained the dog to the post.

entries.definition_en: a series of linked atoms in a molecule
entries.example_cn: 碳链构成了有机分子的骨架。
entries.example_en: The carbon chain forms the backbone of the organic molecule.

entries.definition_en: a unit of length equal to 66 feet
entries.example_cn: 这块地有两链长。
entries.example_en: The field is two chains long.

entries.definition_cn: 连续不断地吸烟，常把一支烟接在上一支烟上点燃
entries.definition_en: to smoke cigarettes continuously, often lighting each cigarette from the previous one
entries.example_cn: 他压力大时倾向于连续吸烟。
entries.example_en: He tends to chain-smoke when he is stressed.

entries.definition_en: a heavy smoker who lights one cigarette off of another
entries.example_cn: 作为一个老烟枪，他每天早上都需要买一包烟。
entries.example_en: As a chain-smoker, he needs to buy a pack of cigarettes every morning.

entries.definition_en: held fast by chains
entries.example_cn: 囚犯们被锁链拴在墙上。
entries.example_en: The prisoners were chained to the wall.

entries.definition_en: a portable power saw with teeth linked to form an endless chain
entries.example_cn: 伐木工人用链锯砍倒了那棵老橡树。
entries.example_en: The logger used a chainsaw to cut down the old oak tree.

entries.definition_en: a seat for one person with a support for the back
entries.example_cn: 请把椅子拉开坐下。
entries.example_en: Please pull out the chair and sit down.

entries.definition_en: the person who presides at the meetings of an organization
entries.example_cn: 主席以演讲开场。
entries.example_en: The chair opened the meeting with a speech.

entries.definition_en: the position of a professor in a university department
entries.example_cn: 他被任命为历史学教授。
entries.example_en: He was appointed to the chair of history.

entries.definition_cn: （管弦乐队中音乐家的）席位；声部职位
entries.definition_en: a musician’s assigned position or place in an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 她获得了小提琴首席席位。
entries.example_en: She won the first-chair violin position.

entries.definition_en: to preside over a meeting or event
entries.example_cn: 经理将在上午十点钟主持会议。
entries.example_en: The manager will chair the meeting at 10 AM.

entries.definition_en: to act as the leader of an academic department in a university
entries.example_cn: 她明年将担任语言学系主任。
entries.example_en: She will chair the department of linguistics next year.

entries.definition_en: an instrument of execution by electrocution that looks like a seat
entries.example_cn: 该囚犯被判处电椅死刑。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was sentenced to die by the chair.

entries.definition_cn: 吊椅式索道（座椅悬挂在循环运行的架空钢缆上，载人上下山）
entries.definition_en: a ski lift on which riders are seated and carried up or down a mountainside; seats are hung from an endless overhead cable
entries.example_cn: 我们乘坐吊椅式索道到了山顶欣赏风景。
entries.example_en: We took the chairlift to the top of the mountain to enjoy the view.

entries.definition_cn: 主持组织会议的人；主席；会长
entries.definition_en: a person who presides over meetings of an organization; also chair or chairperson
entries.example_cn: 主席以演讲开场。
entries.example_en: The chairman opened the meeting with a speech.

entries.definition_en: to act as the leader of a meeting or department
entries.example_cn: 她明年将担任该委员会的主席。
entries.example_en: She will chairman the committee next year.

entries.definition_en: the position or role of being the chairman
entries.example_cn: 她非常热情地接受了委员会主席一职。
entries.example_en: She accepted the chairmanship of the committee with great enthusiasm.

entries.definition_en: the person who presides at the meetings of an organization
entries.example_cn: 主席以简短的介绍开启了会议。
entries.example_en: The chairperson opened the meeting with a brief introduction.

entries.definition_en: a woman who leads a group or organization and presides over its meetings
entries.example_cn: 女主席以简短的发言开启了会议。
entries.example_en: The chairwoman opened the meeting with a brief statement.

entries.definition_en: a long chair designed for reclining
entries.example_cn: 客人们在壁炉旁的躺椅上放松。
entries.example_en: The guests relaxed on the chaise by the fireplace.

entries.definition_en: a two-wheeled carriage with a folding top, drawn by a single horse
entries.example_cn: 马车夫拉着那辆单马双轮敞篷马车穿过狭窄的街道。
entries.example_en: The carriage driver pulled the chaise through the narrow streets.

entries.definition_en: a small, painless lump on the eyelid caused by a blocked oil gland
entries.example_cn: 医生从病人的眼睑上摘除了霰粒肿。
entries.example_en: The doctor removed the chalazion from the patient's eyelid.

entries.definition_en: a type of quartz that is milky, greyish, and translucent or transparent
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商为项链挑选了一块蓝玉髓。
entries.example_en: The jeweler selected a piece of blue chalcedony for the necklace.

entries.definition_en: a small wasp whose larvae are parasitoids of other insects’ eggs or larvae
entries.example_cn: 生物学家利用小蜂来控制有害害虫的种群数量。
entries.example_en: Biologists use chalcids to control populations of harmful pests.

entries.definition_en: a heavy grey mineral that is an ore of copper
entries.example_cn: 矿工们在安第斯山脉的辉铜矿矿藏中开采铜。
entries.example_en: Miners extracted copper from the chalcocite deposits in the Andes.

entries.definition_en: a yellow copper ore made up of copper and iron sulfide
entries.example_cn: 矿工们常在岩石山丘中发现黄铜矿。
entries.example_en: Miners often find chalcopyrite in the rocky hills.

entries.definition_en: a house in the Swiss style with a sloping roof and wide eaves
entries.example_cn: 他们在阿尔卑斯山租了一栋瑞士式小屋过冬。
entries.example_en: They rented a chalet in the Alps for their winter vacation.

entries.definition_en: a bowl-shaped drinking vessel, especially the Eucharistic cup
entries.example_cn: 牧师在仪式中将圣杯高高举起。
entries.example_en: The priest held the chalice high during the ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 一块方解石或类似物质制成的、形状像蜡笔的粉笔，用于在黑板上写字或画画
entries.definition_en: a piece of calcite or similar substance shaped like a crayon used for writing or drawing on blackboards
entries.example_cn: 他伸手拿了一块粉笔在黑板上写方程。
entries.example_en: He reached for a piece of chalk to write the equation on the board.

entries.definition_cn: 一种柔软的白色方解石
entries.definition_en: a soft whitish calcite
entries.example_cn: 地质学家从悬崖上采集了白垩样本。
entries.example_en: Geologists collected samples of chalk from the cliff face.

entries.definition_cn: 一种无光泽、低反射的纯白色
entries.definition_en: a flat, nonreflective white color
entries.example_cn: 艺术家用无光泽的纯白色作为背景色。
entries.example_en: The artist used chalk white for the background.

entries.definition_cn: （俚语）甲基苯丙胺，一种苯丙胺类兴奋剂
entries.definition_en: (slang) methamphetamine, an amphetamine stimulant
entries.example_cn: 报告中，“chalk”指的是甲基苯丙胺。
entries.example_en: In the report, “chalk” referred to methamphetamine.

entries.definition_cn: 用粉笔写字、画画或描摹
entries.definition_en: to write, draw, or trace with chalk
entries.example_cn: 老师在黑板上用粉笔写下新的词汇。
entries.example_en: The teacher chalked the new vocabulary words on the blackboard.

entries.definition_en: a board made of slate, enamel, or another material for writing on with chalk
entries.example_cn: 老师在黑板上写了新的词汇。
entries.example_en: The teacher wrote the new vocabulary words on the chalkboard.

entries.definition_en: of something having the color of chalk
entries.example_cn: 旧墙上覆盖着一层白垩色的白色灰尘。
entries.example_en: The old wall was covered in a chalky white dust.

entries.definition_cn: 由碳酸钙或方解石或白垩组成或含有或类似白垩的
entries.definition_en: composed of or containing or resembling calcium carbonate or calcite or chalk
entries.example_cn: 石灰岩悬崖具有白垩般的质地。
entries.example_en: The limestone cliffs have a chalky texture.

entries.definition_cn: （美国，体育）指比赛中大多数场次由热门选手获胜或预计获胜的
entries.definition_en: US sports: characterized by the favorites winning, or being expected to win, most games in a tournament
entries.example_cn: 这场比赛走势很符合预期，几乎所有热门选手都晋级了。
entries.example_en: The tournament has been chalky, with nearly all the favorites advancing.

entries.definition_cn: 一种含蛋且用酵母发酵的白色面包，通常编成辫状并用蛋液刷面
entries.definition_en: a loaf of white bread containing eggs and leavened with yeast, often braided and glazed with eggs
entries.example_cn: 一家人在星期六早晨聚在一起掰开哈拉面包。
entries.example_en: The family gathered on Saturday morning to break the challah.

entries.definition_en: a situation that is difficult but helps you improve
entries.example_cn: 学习一门新语言是一项巨大的挑战。
entries.example_en: Learning a new language is a great challenge.

entries.definition_en: an invitation to fight or compete
entries.example_cn: 他向冠军拳手发出了挑战书。
entries.example_en: He sent a challenge to the champion boxer.

entries.definition_en: asking someone to explain why they said something
entries.example_cn: 律师质疑了证人的证词。
entries.example_en: The lawyer challenged the witness's statement.

entries.definition_en: to disagree with something and say it is wrong
entries.example_cn: 她质疑了“金钱是唯一重要的东西”这一观点。
entries.example_en: She challenged the idea that money is the only thing that matters.

entries.definition_en: to invite someone to compete or fight
entries.example_cn: 球队向客队发起了比赛挑战。
entries.example_en: The team challenged the visitors to a match.

entries.definition_en: to ask someone to prove who they are
entries.example_cn: 警卫要求司机出示驾照。
entries.example_en: The guard challenged the driver to show his license.

entries.definition_en: a formal objection to choosing a specific person as a juror
entries.example_cn: 辩护方提出正式异议，要求剔除有偏见的陪审员。
entries.example_en: The defense made a challenge to remove the biased juror.

entries.definition_cn: 在法庭上提出正式异议
entries.definition_en: to make a formal objection in a court of law
entries.example_cn: 法官驳回了律师提出的正式异议。
entries.example_en: The judge overruled the challenge made by the lawyer.

entries.definition_en: able to be questioned or disputed
entries.example_cn: 辩护律师可以对提出的证据提出质疑。
entries.example_en: The evidence presented was challengeable by the defense lawyer.

entries.definition_en: a person or group that you hope to defeat in a competition or contest
entries.example_cn: 挑战者在决赛中对阵卫冕冠军。
entries.example_en: The challenger faced the defending champion in the final match.

entries.definition_en: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
entries.example_cn: 这次攀登探险具有挑战性但很有回报。
entries.example_en: The climbing expedition was challenging but rewarding.

entries.definition_en: stimulating interest or thought
entries.example_cn: 这本书提供了关于历史的发人深省的观点。
entries.example_en: The book provided a challenging perspective on history.

entries.definition_en: disturbingly provocative
entries.example_cn: 这次演讲在批评政府方面令人不安地具有挑衅性。
entries.example_en: The speech was challenging in its criticism of the government.

entries.definition_en: a soft lightweight fabric (usually printed)
entries.example_cn: 她买了一件柔软的卡利什布连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She bought a dress made of soft challis.

entries.definition_en: containing dissolved iron salts or tasting of iron
entries.example_cn: 这处含铁的泉水以其疗效而闻名。
entries.example_en: The chalybeate spring was famous for its healing properties.

entries.definition_cn: 天然或人造的封闭空间或腔室
entries.definition_en: a natural or artificial enclosed space
entries.example_cn: 蜜蜂住在蜂巢里的小隔间中。
entries.example_en: The bee lives in a small chamber inside the hive.

entries.definition_en: a room used primarily for sleeping
entries.example_cn: 客房非常舒适。
entries.example_en: The guest chamber was very comfortable.

entries.definition_cn: 审议、立法、行政或司法机构
entries.definition_en: a deliberative or legislative or administrative or judicial assembly
entries.example_cn: 该议会经过长时间辩论后通过了这项法案。
entries.example_en: The chamber passed the bill after a lengthy debate.

entries.definition_cn: 法官处理公务的私人办公室或审议室
entries.definition_en: a private room or office where a judge conducts official business
entries.example_cn: 法官去了办公室审阅案件。
entries.example_en: The judge went to chambers to review the case.

entries.definition_en: an enclosed volume in the body
entries.example_cn: 心脏有四个泵血的腔室。
entries.example_en: The heart has four chambers that pump blood.

entries.definition_en: to place in a chamber
entries.example_cn: 技术人员将子弹装入枪膛。
entries.example_en: The technician chambered the bullet into the gun.

entries.definition_en: having compartmental chambers
entries.example_cn: 有隔间的鹦鹉螺有一个带有许多内部隔间的壳。
entries.example_en: The chambered nautilus has a shell with many internal chambers.

entries.definition_en: an officer who manages a king's or nobleman's household
entries.example_cn: 宫廷总管宣布皇家客人到了。
entries.example_en: The chamberlain announced the arrival of the royal guests.

entries.definition_en: the treasurer of a city or town
entries.example_cn: 市政长官管理着城市的财政。
entries.example_en: The chamberlain managed the city's finances.

entries.definition_en: a maid employed to clean and care for bedrooms, especially in hotels
entries.example_cn: 客房女服务员在早餐前早早到达整理客人的房间。
entries.example_en: The chambermaid arrived early to tidy the guest's room before breakfast.

entries.definition_en: a container used for urination or defecation that is kept in a bedroom
entries.example_cn: 在18世纪，人们睡觉时通常在床边放一个便壶。
entries.example_en: In the 18th century, it was common for people to sleep with a chamberpot beside their bed.

entries.definition_en: a lightweight fabric woven with white threads across a colored warp
entries.example_cn: 她买了一件青年布衬衫准备夏天穿。
entries.example_en: She bought a chambray shirt for the summer.

entries.definition_en: a lizard from Africa and Madagascar that changes skin color and shoots its tongue
entries.example_cn: 这只变色龙改变了颜色以匹配树叶。
entries.example_en: The chameleon changed its color to match the leaves.

entries.definition_cn: 变色龙（喻指见风使舵的人）
entries.definition_en: a person who changes their opinions or behavior to suit others
entries.example_cn: 他是个变色龙，根据谈话对象的不同而改变自己的政治观点。
entries.example_en: He is a chameleon who changes his political views depending on who he is talking to.

entries.definition_en: cut a bevel on; shape to a bevel
entries.example_cn: 他们给玻璃边缘切出了倒角。
entries.example_en: They chamfered the edges of the glass.

entries.definition_en: to cut a groove in something
entries.example_cn: 石匠在那根古柱上切出了凹槽。
entries.example_en: The mason chamfered the ancient column.

entries.definition_cn: 以非90度角相交的两个表面
entries.definition_en: two surfaces meeting at an angle different from 90 degrees
entries.example_cn: 桌子的角落有一个倒角。
entries.example_en: The corner of the table has a chamfer.

entries.definition_en: a soft suede leather made from sheepskin, formerly made from the skin of the chamois antelope
entries.example_cn: 设计师选择了一件麂皮夹克，因为它的质地柔软。
entries.example_en: The designer chose a chamois jacket for its soft texture.

entries.definition_en: a hoofed mammal found in the mountains of Eurasia that has upright horns with backward-hooked tips
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者看到一只岩羚羊在高山的岩架上吃草。
entries.example_en: The hikers spotted a chamois grazing on a high mountain ledge.

entries.definition_en: a Eurasian plant with apple-scented foliage and white-rayed flowers used for medicine
entries.example_cn: 她在茶中加入了一勺洋甘菊。
entries.example_en: She added a spoonful of chamomile to the tea.

entries.definition_en: a person who has won first place in a competition
entries.example_cn: 冠军用奖杯庆祝了他的胜利。
entries.example_en: The champ celebrated his victory with a trophy.

entries.definition_en: to chew noisily or vigorously
entries.example_cn: 狗开始大声用力地咀嚼食物。
entries.example_en: The dog started to champ its food loudly.

entries.definition_en: to chafe at the bit, like horses
entries.example_cn: 马开始在马厩里不安地嚼嚼嚼。
entries.example_en: The horse began to champ in its stall.

entries.definition_en: a white sparkling wine from the Champagne region
entries.example_cn: 他们打开一瓶香槟来庆祝。
entries.example_en: They opened a bottle of champagne to celebrate.

entries.definition_en: a vast area of flat open land
entries.example_cn: 农民们在平原上种植小麦。
entries.example_en: The farmers planted wheat across the champaign.

entries.definition_en: someone who has won first place in a competition
entries.example_cn: 她是游泳世界冠军。
entries.example_en: She is the world champion in swimming.

entries.definition_en: someone who fights for a cause
entries.example_cn: 他是环境保护的倡导者。
entries.example_en: He is a champion of environmental protection.

entries.definition_en: someone who is extremely skilled in any field
entries.example_cn: 她擅长解决难题，是个高手。
entries.example_en: She is a champion at solving difficult puzzles.

entries.definition_en: a person who supports a politician or team
entries.example_cn: 这位候选人有许多忠诚的支持者。
entries.example_en: The candidate has many loyal champions.

entries.definition_en: to protect or fight for a cause or group
entries.example_cn: 他们捍卫了工人的权利。
entries.example_en: They championed the rights of workers.

entries.definition_en: holding first place in a contest
entries.example_cn: 冠军队与弱队进行了比赛。
entries.example_en: The champion team played against the underdogs.

entries.definition_en: a competition to decide the best player or team
entries.example_cn: 网球锦标赛将于下个月举行。
entries.example_en: The tennis championship will be held next month.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being the best player or team in a competition
entries.example_cn: 赢得冠军是每个队伍的目标。
entries.example_en: Winning the championship is the goal of every team.

entries.definition_en: the act of supporting and approving someone's actions
entries.example_cn: 他对民权事业的支持赢得了广泛尊重。
entries.example_en: His championship of civil rights earned widespread respect.

entries.definition_en: a possibility that something might happen
entries.example_cn: 你赢的机会很大。
entries.example_en: You have a good chance of winning.

entries.definition_en: a number showing how likely an event is to happen
entries.example_cn: 下雨的几率是百分之五十。
entries.example_en: The chance of rain is fifty percent.

entries.definition_en: a risk that involves danger
entries.example_cn: 她冒险驾车穿过了暴风雨。
entries.example_en: She took a chance by driving through the storm.

entries.definition_en: happening by luck or accident
entries.example_cn: 这是一次偶遇。
entries.example_en: It was a chance meeting.

entries.definition_en: to happen by luck or accident
entries.example_cn: 我碰巧遇到了老朋友。
entries.example_en: I chanced to meet my old friend.

entries.definition_en: to find or meet by accident
entries.example_cn: 我偶然发现了一本好书。
entries.example_en: I chanced upon a beautiful book.

entries.definition_en: an unpredictable event that changes the outcome
entries.example_cn: 偶然性在他的成功中起了作用。
entries.example_en: Chance played a role in his success.

entries.definition_en: take a risk in the hope of a favorable outcome
entries.example_cn: 他冒险进行了一次危险的攀登。
entries.example_en: He chanced a dangerous climb.

entries.definition_cn: 【历史】在突然且无预谋的自卫冲突中杀死他人这一行为
entries.definition_en: (historical) the killing of another person in a sudden, unpremeditated self-defense encounter
entries.example_cn: 在历史法律用语中，突然且无预谋的自卫冲突中杀死他人被称为 chance-medley。
entries.example_en: In historical legal usage, a killing in a sudden, unpremeditated self-defense encounter was called chance-medley.

entries.definition_cn: 教堂内的圣坛区，通常与教堂其余部分以屏风或栏杆隔开
entries.definition_en: the part of a church containing the altar, usually separated from the rest of the building by a screen or railing
entries.example_cn: 唱诗班站在唱诗班席上，在晨祷期间演唱赞美诗。
entries.example_en: The choir stood in the chancel, singing hymns during the morning service.

entries.definition_cn: 大臣或大法官的办公楼；总理府
entries.definition_en: a building housing the office of a chancellor
entries.example_cn: 代表团访问了总理府，讨论新的贸易协定。
entries.example_en: The delegation visited the chancellery to discuss the new trade agreement.

entries.definition_en: the person who is head of government in several countries
entries.example_cn: 总理昨天宣布了新的经济政策。
entries.example_en: The chancellor announced new economic policies yesterday.

entries.definition_cn: 负责财政的英国内阁大臣
entries.definition_en: the British cabinet minister responsible for finance
entries.example_cn: 财政大臣向议会提交了预算案。
entries.example_en: The chancellor presented the budget to parliament.

entries.definition_cn: 大学的荣誉或名义上的校长
entries.definition_en: the honorary or titular head of a university
entries.example_cn: 校长主持了大学的年度典礼。
entries.example_en: The chancellor opened the university's annual ceremony.

entries.definition_en: the office of chancellor
entries.example_cn: 她去年被任命为大学校长。
entries.example_en: She was appointed to the chancellorship of the university last year.

entries.definition_en: a court with jurisdiction in equity
entries.example_cn: 该案被移交给衡平法院以求公正解决。
entries.example_en: The case was transferred to the chancery for a fair resolution.

entries.definition_cn: 公共或教会档案办公室
entries.definition_en: an office of archives for public or ecclesiastic records
entries.example_cn: 历史学家前往档案办公室查阅旧的土地契约。
entries.example_en: Historians visited the chancery to examine old land deeds.

entries.definition_en: a small, hard, painless lump that forms where a disease-causing germ enters the body, such as syphilis
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了他腿上的硬下疳以诊断感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the chancre on his leg to diagnose the infection.

entries.definition_cn: 由杜克雷嗜血杆菌引起的性传播感染
entries.definition_en: a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Haemophilus ducreyi
entries.example_cn: 软下疳是一种会导致生殖器疼痛性溃疡的性传播感染。
entries.example_en: Chancroid is a sexually transmitted infection that causes painful genital sores.

entries.definition_en: a painful ulcer caused by a sexually transmitted infection
entries.example_cn: 确诊后，该患者接受了软下疳的治疗。
entries.example_en: The patient was treated for a chancroid after the diagnosis.

entries.definition_cn: 结果不确定的；尤指充满风险的
entries.definition_en: having an uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk
entries.example_cn: 这项投资结果不确定的性质让许多人犹豫不决。
entries.example_en: The chancy nature of the investment made many people hesitate.

entries.definition_cn: 受偶然因素影响的；不可预测的
entries.definition_en: subject to chance; unpredictable
entries.example_cn: 多变的天气迫使户外活动取消。
entries.example_en: The chancy weather forced the cancellation of the outdoor event.

entries.definition_en: an ornate branched lighting fixture that hangs from the ceiling
entries.example_cn: 大厅由一盏水晶枝形吊灯照亮。
entries.example_en: The grand hall was illuminated by a crystal chandelier.

entries.definition_en: a steep climbing turn in aviation used to gain altitude while changing direction
entries.example_cn: 飞行员做了一个完美的钟形机动以避开前方的障碍物。
entries.example_en: The pilot performed a perfect chandelle to clear the obstacle ahead.

entries.definition_en: to climb suddenly and steeply
entries.example_cn: 气球遇到上升气流后开始急剧爬升。
entries.example_en: The balloon began to chandelle rapidly as it caught the updraft.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes or sells candles
entries.example_cn: 在老城，蜡烛商出售高质量的蜡烛。
entries.example_en: In the old town, the chandler sold high-quality candles.

entries.definition_en: a person who sells food and supplies to ships
entries.example_cn: 船舶供应商为船只装上了新鲜水和补给品。
entries.example_en: The chandler loaded the ship with fresh water and provisions.

entries.definition_en: goods such as candles and other supplies sold by a chandler
entries.example_cn: 船上的杂货铺备齐了长途航行所需的一切物品。
entries.example_en: The ship's chandlery stocked everything needed for the long voyage.

entries.definition_en: a room where candles are stored
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员将蜡烛移到蜡烛储藏室。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to move the candles to the chandlery.

entries.definition_cn: 引起变化；使不同；导致转变
entries.definition_en: cause to change; make different; cause a transformation
entries.example_cn: 新政策将改变我们的工作方式。
entries.example_en: The new policy will change the way we work.

entries.definition_cn: 经历变化；本质上变得不同；失去原有的性质
entries.definition_en: undergo a change; become different in essence; losing one's or its original nature
entries.example_cn: 洪水后河流改道了。
entries.example_en: The river changed course after the flood.

entries.definition_cn: 以某种特定方式变得不同，但不永久失去原有的特征或本质
entries.definition_en: become different in some particular way, without permanently losing one's or its former characteristics or essence
entries.example_cn: 树叶在秋天变色了。
entries.example_en: The leaves changed color in autumn.

entries.definition_cn: 事物从一种状态或阶段转变为另一种状态或阶段的事件
entries.definition_en: an event that occurs when something passes from one state or phase to another
entries.example_cn: 从冬天到春天的变化是渐进的。
entries.example_en: The change from winter to spring was gradual.

entries.definition_cn: 状态间的关系差异；特别是某事件前后的状态差异
entries.definition_en: a relational difference between states; especially between states before and after some event
entries.example_cn: 他的外貌有很大的变化。
entries.example_en: There is a big change in his appearance.

entries.definition_en: the result of alteration or modification
entries.example_cn: 设计的改进提升了产品。
entries.example_en: The change in the design improved the product.

entries.definition_cn: 搁置、放弃或换成另一个
entries.definition_en: lay aside, abandon, or leave for another
entries.example_cn: 我用新鞋替换了旧鞋。
entries.example_en: I changed my old shoes for new ones.

entries.definition_cn: 付款金额超过价格后退回的钱
entries.definition_en: Money returned after a purchase when the amount paid is more than the price.
entries.example_cn: 收银员找给我三美元。
entries.example_en: The cashier gave me three dollars in change.

entries.definition_cn: 用大面额货币兑换的小面额零钱
entries.definition_en: Small denominations of money given in exchange for a larger denomination.
entries.example_cn: 我可以把这张二十美元的钞票换成零钱吗？
entries.example_en: Could I have some change for this twenty-dollar bill?

entries.definition_en: the action of changing something
entries.example_cn: 改变计划花费了太长时间。
entries.example_en: Changing the plan took too long.

entries.definition_en: a type of baseball pitch thrown slowly to surprise the batter
entries.example_cn: 投手投出一个变速球来迷惑击球手。
entries.example_en: The pitcher threw a change-up to fool the batter.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being changeable; having a marked tendency to change
entries.example_cn: 春季天气的多变性使得打包行李变得困难。
entries.example_en: The changeability of the weather in spring makes packing difficult.

entries.definition_en: capable of or tending to change in form or quality or nature
entries.example_cn: 这个地区的天气变化无常。
entries.example_en: The weather in this region is very changeable.

entries.definition_en: such that alteration is possible; having a marked tendency to change
entries.example_cn: 合同条款经双方同意可以更改。
entries.example_en: The terms of the contract are changeable by mutual agreement.

entries.definition_en: subject to change
entries.example_cn: 活动价格在最终日期前可能会变动。
entries.example_en: Prices for the event are changeable until the final date.

entries.definition_cn: 变色（随光线或角度变化）的
entries.definition_en: varying in color when seen in different lights or from different angles
entries.example_cn: 蝴蝶的翅膀会变色，在阳光下从蓝色变为绿色。
entries.example_en: The butterfly's wings are changeable, shifting from blue to green in the sunlight.

entries.definition_en: different in nature or form
entries.example_cn: 这片改变后的景观看起来与旧照片完全不同。
entries.example_en: The changed landscape looked completely different from the old photos.

entries.definition_en: different in some respect
entries.example_cn: 这些修改后的规则适用于所有新成员。
entries.example_en: The changed rules apply to all new members.

entries.definition_en: likely to change; subject to alteration
entries.example_cn: 沿海地区多变的天气使得打包行李变得困难。
entries.example_en: The changeful weather of the coast made packing difficult.

entries.definition_en: not subject to change or variation in form, quality, or nature
entries.example_cn: 山峦上空的不变天空提供了宁静的背景。
entries.example_en: The changeless sky above the mountains offered a serene backdrop.

entries.definition_en: unvarying in nature
entries.example_cn: 尽管岁月流逝，他们的友谊依然性质恒定。
entries.example_en: Their friendship remained changeless despite the years that passed.

entries.definition_en: remaining the same for indefinitely long times
entries.example_cn: 海洋波浪长久不变的节奏安抚了疲惫的旅行者。
entries.example_en: The changeless rhythm of the ocean waves soothed the weary traveler.

entries.definition_cn: 婴儿时被秘密调换的孩子
entries.definition_en: a child secretly exchanged for another in infancy
entries.example_cn: 在民间传说中，一个被偷走的孩子会被用一个调换的孩子代替。
entries.example_en: In folklore, a changeling was left in place of a stolen baby.

entries.definition_cn: （过时）被认为是白痴或傻瓜的人
entries.definition_en: a person regarded as an idiot or simpleton (obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 这部旧文本用 changeling 作为“傻瓜”的侮辱性称呼。
entries.example_en: The old text used changeling as an insult meaning a simpleton.

entries.definition_en: a conversion or transition from one thing, system, or state to another
entries.example_cn: 新软件系统的切换将于下周进行。
entries.example_en: The changeover to the new software system will take place next week.

entries.definition_en: a person or device that changes or exchanges something
entries.example_cn: 机场的货币兑换员非常乐于助人。
entries.example_en: The currency changer at the airport was very helpful.

entries.definition_en: an automatic mechanical device on a record player that causes new records to be played without manual intervention
entries.example_cn: 那台老唱机有一个内置的自动换盘器，可以自动播放下一首歌。
entries.example_en: The old record player had a built-in changer that played the next song automatically.

entries.definition_en: becoming different or undergoing change
entries.example_cn: 不断变化的气候正在影响沿海城市。
entries.example_en: The changing climate is affecting coastal cities.

entries.definition_en: a means of communication or access
entries.example_cn: 社交媒体为政治讨论提供了新的渠道。
entries.example_en: Social media provides a new channel for political discussion.

entries.definition_en: a passage for water or other fluids to flow through
entries.example_cn: 河流穿过山脉中的狭窄水道。
entries.example_en: The river flows through a narrow channel in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: a path for electrical signals to travel
entries.example_cn: 数据通过数字信道传输。
entries.example_en: The data travels through the digital channel.

entries.definition_en: to transmit or act as a medium for transmission
entries.example_cn: 这个卫星频道传送来自世界各地的音乐。
entries.example_en: The satellite channel transmits music from around the world.

entries.definition_en: to direct the flow of something
entries.example_cn: 工程师设计了一个系统来将水从房子旁引开。
entries.example_en: The engineer designed a system to channel the water away from the house.

entries.definition_en: to send from one person or place to another
entries.example_cn: 请立即将此消息传递给经理。
entries.example_en: Please channel this message to the manager immediately.

entries.definition_en: a deep narrow body of water allowing vessels to pass
entries.example_cn: 船只穿过海峡驶向大海。
entries.example_en: The ship sailed through the channel to reach the open sea.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow furrow cut by nature or a tool
entries.example_cn: 那张旧的黑胶唱片上有深深的沟槽来承载声音。
entries.example_en: The old phonograph record has deep channels that hold the sound.

entries.definition_en: to switch between television channels quickly
entries.example_cn: 他整个晚上都在换台，却找不到任何有趣的东西。
entries.example_en: He spent the whole evening channel-surfing without finding anything interesting.

entries.definition_en: the management of communication through specified channels
entries.example_cn: 公司实施了严格的渠道化管理，以确保所有营销信息的一致性。
entries.example_en: The company implemented strict channelization to ensure all marketing messages were consistent.

entries.definition_cn: 将宽带通信信道分成多个窄带信道
entries.definition_en: The division of a wide-band communications channel into multiple narrow-band channels.
entries.example_cn: 信道化使多个窄带服务能够共享一个宽带通信信道。
entries.example_en: Channelization allows several narrow-band services to share one wide-band communications channel.

entries.definition_en: to direct the course or determine the direction of travelling
entries.example_cn: 道路施工开始前，车辆被引导进入不同车道。
entries.example_en: Traffic was channelized into separate lanes before the roadworks began.

entries.definition_en: to make a channel for something or provide it with a channel
entries.example_cn: 工程师为排水系统开渠以应对大雨。
entries.example_en: Engineers channelized the drainage system to handle the heavy rainfall.

entries.definition_en: to send information or messages from one person or place to another
entries.example_cn: 办公软件可以将电子邮件直接传递到经理的收件箱。
entries.example_en: The office software can channelize emails directly to the manager's inbox.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to form a channel
entries.example_cn: 河岸的侵蚀使溪流形成了渠道。
entries.example_en: The erosion of the riverbank has channelized the flow of the stream.

entries.definition_en: official routes or methods of communication
entries.example_cn: 我们需要通过官方渠道进行沟通。
entries.example_en: We need to communicate through official channels.

entries.definition_en: a traditional Japanese ritual involving the preparation, serving, and drinking of tea
entries.example_cn: 在仪式上，主人以极大的精准和优雅主持了茶道仪式。
entries.example_en: During the ceremony, the host conducted a chanoyu ceremony with great precision and grace.

entries.definition_en: to recite with musical intonation or as a psalm
entries.example_cn: 僧侣们每天早上吟诵经文。
entries.example_en: The monks chant the scriptures every morning.

entries.definition_en: to utter something monotonously, repetitively, and rhythmically
entries.example_cn: 工人们一遍又一遍地反复喊同一个口号。
entries.example_en: The workers chant the same slogan over and over.

entries.definition_cn: 用于歌唱或吟诵歌词的简短、简单的旋律
entries.definition_en: a short, simple melody to which words are sung or recited
entries.example_cn: 合唱团用一段简单的旋律吟唱这首诗篇。
entries.example_en: The choir sang the psalm to a simple chant.

entries.definition_en: a reed pipe with finger holes used to play melodies
entries.example_cn: 音乐家调整吹管以发出更高的音调。
entries.example_en: The musician adjusted the chanter to produce a higher pitch.

entries.definition_cn: 鸡油菌属的一种黄色喇叭形食用蘑菇
entries.definition_en: a yellow, trumpet-shaped edible mushroom of the genus Cantharellus
entries.example_cn: 我们在松树下发现了一株鸡油菌。
entries.example_en: We found a chanterelle growing under the pine trees.

entries.definition_en: a rhythmic work song originally sung by sailors
entries.example_cn: 船员们唱着一首传统的海员号子，以便在拉粗绳索时保持节奏。
entries.example_en: The crew sang a traditional chantey to keep time while hauling the heavy ropes.

entries.definition_en: the act of singing or reciting words in a repeated, rhythmic way
entries.example_cn: 人群齐声高呼口号。
entries.example_en: The crowd was chanting slogans in unison.

entries.definition_cn: （用于支付宗教仪式的）捐赠基金
entries.definition_en: a fund of money set aside to pay for religious services
entries.example_cn: 该捐赠基金被设立以确保每日举行弥撒。
entries.example_en: The chantry was established to ensure daily Masses were sung.

entries.definition_cn: （为捐赠者灵魂而设的）小教堂
entries.definition_en: a chapel built to hold Masses for the soul of the person who paid for it
entries.example_cn: 那座小教堂位于旧大教堂的一角。
entries.example_en: The chantry stood in the corner of the old cathedral.

entries.definition_en: a rhythmic song sung by sailors to coordinate work
entries.example_cn: 船员们唱起海员号子，以便在拉绳索时保持节奏。
entries.example_en: The crew sang a chanty to keep the rhythm while pulling the ropes.

entries.definition_en: a state of extreme confusion and disorder
entries.example_cn: 派对结束后，房间一片混乱。
entries.example_en: The room was in total chaos after the party.

entries.definition_en: the formless state of matter before creation
entries.example_cn: 根据神话，世界最初是混沌状态。
entries.example_en: According to the myth, the world began as chaos.

entries.definition_cn: 对初始条件极度敏感的动态系统
entries.definition_en: a dynamical system sensitive to initial conditions
entries.example_cn: 由于大气中的混沌现象，天气预报变得很困难。
entries.example_en: The weather forecast is difficult because of chaos in the atmosphere.

entries.definition_en: lacking a visible order or organization
entries.example_cn: 混乱的场面让人难以找到出口。
entries.example_en: The chaotic scene made it hard to find the exit.

entries.definition_cn: 完全无序且不可预测的
entries.definition_en: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.example_cn: 混乱的交通造成了严重延误。
entries.example_en: The chaotic traffic caused a major delay.

entries.definition_cn: 对初始条件敏感依赖的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to a sensitive dependence on initial conditions
entries.example_cn: 这个混沌系统对微小的变化高度敏感。
entries.example_en: The chaotic system is highly sensitive to small changes.

entries.definition_en: in a wild and confused manner
entries.example_cn: 人群在狭窄的街道上混乱地移动。
entries.example_en: The crowd moved chaotically through the narrow streets.

entries.definition_en: in a manner suggestive of chaos
entries.example_cn: 文件杂乱无章地堆在桌子上。
entries.example_en: The files were stored chaotically on the desk.

entries.definition_en: a boy or man
entries.example_cn: 那边的那个家伙是这家店的经理。
entries.example_en: That chap over there is the manager of the shop.

entries.definition_en: a crack in a lip caused usually by cold
entries.example_cn: 她的下唇有一道因寒冷引起的裂口，很疼。
entries.example_en: She had a painful chap on her lower lip.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow depression in a surface
entries.example_cn: 一道深深的裂缝横贯结冰的湖面。
entries.example_en: A deep chap ran across the frozen lake.

entries.definition_en: leather leggings worn by cowboys to protect their legs
entries.example_cn: 这位牛仔骑马时，在裤子外面穿了护腿。
entries.example_en: The cowboy wore chaps over his trousers while riding.

entries.definition_cn: 使皮肤因寒冷或干燥而干裂
entries.definition_en: to cause skin to become cracked or rough through cold or dryness
entries.example_cn: 寒冷的风吹得他的嘴唇干裂。
entries.example_en: The cold wind chapped his lips.

entries.definition_cn: 灌木丛生的地区，通常夏季干燥、冬季多雨
entries.definition_en: a region of shrubs, typically dry in summer and rainy in winter
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者们在烈日下穿过干燥的灌木丛。
entries.example_en: The hikers walked through the dry chaparral under the hot sun.

entries.definition_en: a flat, pancake-like bread cooked on a hot griddle
entries.example_cn: 我们用餐时搭配了新鲜的恰巴提饼和辛辣的咖喱。
entries.example_en: We served the meal with fresh chapati and spicy curry.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: Used both for individual breads and bread as food.

entries.definition_cn: 恰巴提，一种在烤盘上烤制的无酵薄饼
entries.definition_en: an unleavened flatbread cooked on a griddle
entries.example_cn: 他们晚餐吃了热的恰巴提薄饼，配咖喱。
entries.example_en: They served hot chapattis with curry for dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 一种有造型帽冠和通常有帽檐的帽子，用于在恶劣天气中保护头部
entries.definition_en: a hat with a shaped crown and usually a brim, worn to protect the head from bad weather
entries.example_cn: 他出门前戴上了他的帽子。
entries.example_en: He put on his chapeau before stepping out into the rain.

entries.definition_en: a place of worship that has its own altar
entries.example_cn: 他们参观了建在山边的那座小教堂。
entries.example_en: They visited the small chapel built into the side of the mountain.

entries.definition_cn: 殡仪馆，或其中举行葬礼的房间
entries.definition_en: a funeral home, or a room in one for holding funeral services
entries.example_cn: 家人聚集在殡仪馆的礼堂参加葬礼。
entries.example_en: The family gathered in the funeral chapel for the service.

entries.definition_en: a person who accompanies and supervises a young woman or a group of young people
entries.example_cn: 老师担任了学生们实地考察的监护人。
entries.example_en: The teacher acted as a chaperon for the students on the field trip.

entries.definition_en: to accompany someone as a chaperone
entries.example_cn: 家长被要求在学校舞会上陪同他们的孩子。
entries.example_en: Parents are required to chaperon their children at the school dance.

entries.definition_cn: 陪同并监督年轻人的成年人；陪护人
entries.definition_en: an older person who accompanies and supervises younger people, especially to ensure proper behavior
entries.example_cn: 老师担任了学校旅行的监护人。
entries.example_en: The teacher acted as a chaperone for the school trip.

entries.definition_cn: 帮助其他蛋白质和分子结构折叠、展开及组装，但本身不成为其组成部分的蛋白质
entries.definition_en: a protein that helps other proteins and molecular structures fold, unfold, and assemble, without becoming part of them
entries.example_cn: 分子伴侣帮助新合成的蛋白质折叠成正确的形状。
entries.example_en: Molecular chaperones help newly made proteins fold into their proper shapes.

entries.definition_en: to accompany and supervise young people
entries.example_cn: 父母被要求陪同孩子参加舞会。
entries.example_en: Parents were asked to chaperone their children at the dance.

entries.definition_cn: 为特定机构或团体提供牧灵或精神关怀的人员，通常为牧师
entries.definition_en: a person assigned to provide pastoral or spiritual care to a particular institution or group, often a member of the clergy
entries.example_cn: 船上的牧师去慰问船员。
entries.example_en: The ship's chaplain visited the crew to offer comfort.

entries.definition_en: the position of chaplain
entries.example_cn: 她接受了大学医院的牧师职位。
entries.example_en: She accepted the chaplaincy at the university hospital.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指大学校园内）提供宗教服务和支持的建筑或设施。
entries.definition_en: A building or facility, especially on a university campus, where religious services and support are provided.
entries.example_cn: 这所大学建了一座宗教服务中心，供所有信仰的学生祈祷并寻求帮助。
entries.example_en: The university built a chaplaincy where students of all faiths could pray and seek support.

entries.definition_en: a circular wreath of flowers or leaves worn as an ornament
entries.example_cn: 她头上戴着一圈精致的白玫瑰花环。
entries.example_en: She wore a delicate chaplet of white roses in her hair.

entries.definition_en: an obsolete term for an itinerant dealer or merchant
entries.example_cn: 这个小贩穿过市场兜售他的商品。
entries.example_en: The chapman walked through the market selling his wares.

entries.definition_cn: 因寒冷或暴露而干燥粗糙、常有皲裂的
entries.definition_en: dry, rough, and often cracked from cold or exposure
entries.example_cn: 她的手因寒风而皲裂。
entries.example_en: Her hands were chapped from the freezing wind.

entries.definition_en: a subdivision of a written work; usually numbered and titled
entries.example_cn: 这本书的第三章讨论了战争的历史。
entries.example_en: The third chapter of the book discusses the history of the war.

entries.definition_cn: （历史或人生的）一个阶段；时期
entries.definition_en: any distinct period in history or in a person's life
entries.example_cn: 战争是这个国家历史上黑暗的一页。
entries.example_en: The war was a dark chapter in the country's history.

entries.definition_cn: 一系列相关事件构成的插曲
entries.definition_en: a series of related events forming an episode
entries.example_cn: 他们在巴黎的时光是他们关系中快乐的插曲。
entries.example_en: Their time in Paris was a happy chapter in their relationship.

entries.definition_en: a local branch of some fraternity or association
entries.example_cn: 他加入了当地的学生组织分会。
entries.example_en: He joined the local chapter of the student organization.

entries.definition_en: an ecclesiastical assembly of the monks in a monastery or even of the canons of a church
entries.example_cn: 僧侣们召开会议讨论修道院的新规。
entries.example_en: The chapter met to discuss the new rules for the monastery.

entries.definition_en: a building attached to a monastery or cathedral used as a meeting place for the chapter
entries.example_cn: 僧侣们在会堂聚集，讨论他们修会的规章。
entries.example_en: The monks gathered in the chapterhouse to discuss the rules of their order.

entries.definition_en: a house used as a residence by a chapter of a fraternity
entries.example_cn: 新成员搬进了兄弟会会所开始他们的训练。
entries.example_en: The new members moved into the chapterhouse to begin their training.

entries.definition_en: to burn something until it turns to black ash
entries.example_cn: 强烈的热量瞬间将肉烧成了焦炭。
entries.example_en: The intense heat charred the meat instantly.

entries.definition_en: to burn the surface of something slightly
entries.example_cn: 烤面包时要小心别把它烤焦了。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to char the bread while toasting it.

entries.definition_en: a black, burnt substance
entries.example_cn: 大火在木头上留下了一层焦痕。
entries.example_en: The fire left a layer of char on the wood.

entries.definition_en: dated, chiefly British: a woman employed to do housework
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子雇了一名女佣打扫房间。
entries.example_en: The old house had a char to clean the rooms.

entries.definition_en: a type of small trout-like fish
entries.example_cn: 渔民们在冰冷的河里钓到了几条似鳟鱼的小鱼。
entries.example_en: The fishermen caught several char in the cold river.

entries.definition_en: a vehicle carrying many passengers; used for public transport
entries.example_cn: 我们乘坐大型公共客车前往乡村。
entries.example_en: We traveled to the countryside in a charabanc.

entries.definition_en: a person in a story, play, or movie
entries.example_cn: 书中的主要角色是一位勇敢的侦探。
entries.example_en: The main character in the book is a brave detective.

entries.definition_en: the distinctive nature or character of something
entries.example_cn: 古老的建筑是这座城市特色的一部分。
entries.example_en: The old architecture is part of the character of this city.

entries.definition_en: the moral qualities that make a person who they are
entries.example_cn: 诚实是一个重要的品格特征。
entries.example_en: Honesty is an important character trait.

entries.definition_en: the way an actor plays a role
entries.example_cn: 她对女王这一角色的塑造非常有趣。
entries.example_en: Her portrayal of the queen was very funny.

entries.definition_en: a person with strange or unusual habits
entries.example_cn: 那个独自居住的老人是个奇怪的怪人。
entries.example_en: The old man is a strange character who lives alone.

entries.definition_en: obsolete: to write using characters; to describe
entries.example_cn: 诗人在树皮上刻下了自己的想法。
entries.example_en: The poet charactered his thoughts on the tree bark.

entries.definition_en: a good reputation
entries.example_cn: 他被发现偷窃后名誉扫地。
entries.example_en: He lost his character after being caught stealing.

entries.definition_en: a letter of recommendation from a former employer
entries.example_cn: 她需要前老板的推荐信才能找到这份工作。
entries.example_en: She needs a character from her previous boss to get the job.

entries.definition_en: a graphic or vivid verbal description
entries.example_cn: 这部小说对反派人物的刻画十分鲜明。
entries.example_en: The novel offers a striking characterisation of the villain.

entries.definition_en: the act of describing distinctive characteristics or essential features
entries.example_cn: 对主角动机的刻画很复杂。
entries.example_en: The characterisation of the protagonist's motivations is complex.

entries.definition_en: to describe or portray the specific qualities of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 这部小说将主人公描绘成一位勇敢无私的英雄。
entries.example_en: The novel characterises the protagonist as a brave and selfless hero.

entries.definition_en: to be typical of or show the qualities of
entries.example_cn: 该地区的特点是丘陵起伏，气候温和。
entries.example_en: The region is characterised by its rolling hills and mild climate.

entries.definition_en: a prominent attribute or aspect of something
entries.example_cn: 耐心是这个工作的一项显著特征。
entries.example_en: Patience is a characteristic of this job.

entries.definition_en: a distinguishing quality; a feature that can be used to identify something
entries.example_cn: 叶子独特的形状有助于识别这种植物。
entries.example_en: The characteristic shape of the leaf helps identify the plant.

entries.definition_cn: 在严格规定的条件下测量的设备的任何可测量属性
entries.definition_en: any measurable property of a device measured under closely specified conditions
entries.example_cn: 传感器的特性是在受控条件下进行测试的。
entries.example_en: The characteristic of the sensor was tested under controlled conditions.

entries.definition_en: the integer part (positive or negative) of the representation of a logarithm
entries.example_cn: 在表达式“log 643 = 2.808”中，特征值是 2。
entries.example_en: In the expression 'log 643 = 2.808', the characteristic is 2.

entries.definition_en: typical or distinctive
entries.example_cn: 松树特有的气味充满了空气。
entries.example_en: The characteristic smell of pine trees filled the air.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is typical of a particular person or thing
entries.example_cn: 他一如往常地迟到了会议。
entries.example_en: He characteristically arrived late to the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the process of describing the essential features of something
entries.example_cn: 这本书详细刻画了经济危机。
entries.example_en: The book provides a detailed characterization of the economic crisis.

entries.definition_en: a vivid or detailed description of a person or thing
entries.example_cn: 作者对反派的描写既令人恐惧又令人同情。
entries.example_en: The author's characterization of the villain was both terrifying and sympathetic.

entries.definition_en: the act of portraying a character through speech, action, and gesture
entries.example_cn: 她对主角的扮演赢得了起立鼓掌。
entries.example_en: Her characterization of the lead role earned her a standing ovation.

entries.definition_en: to describe the qualities or nature of something
entries.example_cn: 该报告将经济描述为稳定但增长缓慢。
entries.example_en: The report characterizes the economy as stable but slow-growing.

entries.definition_en: to be typical of or show the nature of
entries.example_cn: 频繁的降雨是这个地区气候的典型特征。
entries.example_en: Frequent rain characterizes the climate in this region.

entries.definition_en: lacking distinct or individual characteristics; dull and uninteresting
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因缺乏特色且可预测而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The movie was criticized for being characterless and predictable.

entries.definition_en: a word acted out in an episode of the game of charades
entries.example_cn: 这个团队很难猜出“大象”这个猜词游戏中的词。
entries.example_en: The team struggled to guess the charade for 'elephant'.

entries.definition_en: making a false outward show
entries.example_cn: 那位政治家的道歉不过是虚伪的做作。
entries.example_en: The politician's apology was nothing but a charade.

entries.definition_en: a game where one person acts out a word or phrase without speaking for others to guess
entries.example_cn: 我们在聚会上玩哑剧猜词游戏，猜电影标题时玩得很开心。
entries.example_en: We played charades at the party and had a lot of fun guessing the movie titles.

entries.definition_en: black material made by heating wood without air
entries.example_cn: 他们用木炭在火上烤肉。
entries.example_en: They used charcoal to cook the meat over the fire.

entries.definition_en: a very dark grey color
entries.example_cn: 日落前天空变成了深炭灰色。
entries.example_en: The sky turned a deep charcoal color just before sunset.

entries.definition_en: a stick of black carbon used for drawing
entries.example_cn: 她拿起一支炭笔来素描肖像。
entries.example_en: She picked up a charcoal to sketch the portrait.

entries.definition_en: a drawing made with a stick of black carbon
entries.example_cn: 画廊展出了一幅著名雕像的炭笔画。
entries.example_en: The gallery displayed a charcoal of the famous statue.

entries.definition_en: to draw or trace using charcoal
entries.example_cn: 艺术家在添加细节之前用炭笔画出了山的轮廓。
entries.example_en: The artist charcoaled the outline of the mountain before adding details.

entries.definition_en: of a very dark grey color
entries.example_cn: 那套炭灰色的西装在舞台灯光下看起来很优雅。
entries.example_en: The charcoal suit looked elegant under the stage lights.

entries.definition_cn: 可直接食用的腌肉，尤指猪肉
entries.definition_en: cured meat that is ready to eat, especially pork
entries.example_cn: 拼盘里有几种腌肉。
entries.example_en: The platter included several kinds of charcuterie.

entries.definition_cn: 腌肉熟食店；熟食店中专营腌肉的柜台
entries.definition_en: a shop or section of a shop specializing in cured meat
entries.example_cn: 我们在熟食店买了一些萨拉米香肠和奶酪。
entries.example_en: We bought some salami and cheese from the charcuterie.

entries.definition_cn: 烹制和加工即食肉制品的做法，尤指猪肉制品
entries.definition_en: the practice of cooking and preparing ready-to-eat meat products, especially pork
entries.example_cn: 她学习了法国南部的传统肉制品加工技艺。
entries.example_en: She trained in the traditional charcuterie of southern France.

entries.definition_en: a beet lacking a swollen root, grown as a vegetable for its edible leaves and stalks
entries.example_cn: 我们在汤里加了些甜菜以增加风味。
entries.example_en: We added some chard to the soup for extra flavor.

entries.definition_cn: 叶用甜菜的长而多汁的白色茎
entries.definition_en: long succulent whitish stalks with large green leaves
entries.example_cn: 厨师挑选了嫩绿的甜菜茎来做沙拉。
entries.example_en: The chef selected the tender chard stalks for the salad.

entries.definition_en: the price asked for an article or service
entries.example_cn: 停车收费是多少？
entries.example_en: What is the charge for parking?

entries.definition_en: a formal statement of a crime or offense
entries.example_cn: 警方对他提出了指控。
entries.example_en: The police filed a charge against him.

entries.definition_en: an excess or deficiency of electricity
entries.example_cn: 这个气球带有正电荷。
entries.example_en: The balloon has a positive charge.

entries.definition_en: to demand payment
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店早餐额外收费。
entries.example_en: The hotel charges extra for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: to blame someone for wrongdoing
entries.example_cn: 她被指控偷钱。
entries.example_en: She was charged with stealing the money.

entries.definition_en: to make a sudden attack upon
entries.example_cn: 那只狗冲向入侵者。
entries.example_en: The dog charged at the intruder.

entries.definition_en: to assign someone a duty or responsibility, or give them an order
entries.example_cn: 主管委派他负责这个项目。
entries.example_en: The supervisor charged him with leading the project.

entries.definition_en: an impetuous rush toward someone or something
entries.example_cn: 士兵们向敌人发起冲锋。
entries.example_en: The soldiers made a charge at the enemy.

entries.definition_en: to move quickly and violently
entries.example_cn: 汽车疾驰下山。
entries.example_en: The car charged down the hill.

entries.definition_en: capable of being charged
entries.example_cn: 这个设备是一个可充电的电池组。
entries.example_en: This device is a chargeable battery pack.

entries.definition_cn: 可记入账户的；可由账户支付的
entries.definition_en: able to be charged to an account
entries.example_cn: 维修费用可以记入公司的账户。
entries.example_en: The repair costs are chargeable to the company's account.

entries.definition_cn: 可能被指控或依法控告的（罕见，指人）
entries.definition_en: liable to be accused or legally charged with an offence
entries.example_cn: 根据该法，这名嫌疑人可被指控犯有欺诈罪。
entries.example_en: The suspect was chargeable with fraud under the statute.

entries.definition_en: having a net amount of positive or negative electric charge
entries.example_cn: 气球在羊毛毛衣上摩擦后带电了。
entries.example_en: The balloon became charged after rubbing against the wool sweater.

entries.definition_en: full of strong emotion
entries.example_cn: 比赛开始前，人群情绪激昂。
entries.example_en: The crowd was charged with excitement before the game started.

entries.definition_cn: 引起强烈情绪或争议的
entries.definition_en: likely to cause strong emotion or controversy
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家就经济问题发表了一场引起强烈反响的演讲。
entries.example_en: The politician made a charged speech about the economy.

entries.definition_en: supplied with carbon dioxide
entries.example_cn: 苏打水充有二氧化碳以产生气泡。
entries.example_en: The soda is charged with carbon dioxide to give it fizz.

entries.definition_en: a device used to charge or recharge a battery
entries.example_cn: 我把手机充电器留在了桌子上。
entries.example_en: I left my phone charger on the desk.

entries.definition_en: a strong and fast horse used in ancient battles
entries.example_cn: 那匹战马在战场上飞奔。
entries.example_en: The charger galloped across the battlefield.

entries.definition_cn: 一种由马牵引的轻便四轮马车，通常用于仪式
entries.definition_en: a light four-wheeled carriage pulled by horses, often used for ceremonies
entries.example_cn: 国王乘坐金色马车前往神庙。
entries.example_en: The king rode in a golden chariot to the temple.

entries.definition_cn: 古代文明中用于战争或赛车的双轮马战车
entries.definition_en: a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used for war or racing in ancient civilizations
entries.example_cn: 古希腊战士从他们的战车上作战。
entries.example_en: Ancient Greek warriors fought from their chariots.

entries.definition_en: to transport someone in a chariot
entries.example_cn: 众神用战车将英雄们运送到战场。
entries.example_en: The gods charioted the heroes to the battlefield.

entries.definition_en: to ride in a chariot
entries.example_cn: 他们乘坐战车穿越沙漠沙丘。
entries.example_en: They charioted across the desert sands.

entries.definition_en: a person who drives a chariot
entries.example_cn: 这位古代战车御者熟练地驾驭战车队绕场奔驰。
entries.example_en: The ancient charioteer guided his team around the track with skill.

entries.definition_en: a personal attractiveness that enables you to influence others
entries.example_cn: 这位领导人的个人魅力激励团队更加努力工作。
entries.example_en: The leader's charisma inspired the team to work harder.

entries.definition_en: having a special ability to attract and influence people
entries.example_cn: 这位有魅力的领袖用他的演讲赢得了人群的拥护。
entries.example_en: The charismatic leader won over the crowd with his speech.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characterized by charity
entries.example_cn: 他们向一个慈善机构捐款。
entries.example_en: They donated money to a charitable organization.

entries.definition_en: full of love and generosity
entries.example_cn: 她向陌生人露出了充满爱意的微笑。
entries.example_en: She gave a charitable smile to the stranger.

entries.definition_cn: 富有同情心和理解力的
entries.definition_en: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.example_cn: 法官对他的行为做出了富有同情心的解释。
entries.example_en: The judge made a charitable interpretation of his actions.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows kindness and generosity
entries.example_cn: 她宽厚地解读了他粗鲁的评论，认为他只是压力太大。
entries.example_en: She interpreted his rude comment charitably, assuming he was just stressed.

entries.definition_en: an activity or gift that benefits the public at large
entries.example_cn: 在食物银行做志愿者是一种美好的慈善行为。
entries.example_en: Volunteering at the food bank is a wonderful form of charity.

entries.definition_en: an institution set up to provide help to the needy
entries.example_cn: 当地的慈善机构为无家可归的家庭提供庇护。
entries.example_en: The local charity provides shelter for homeless families.

entries.definition_en: a kindly and lenient attitude toward people
entries.example_cn: 他在冲突中对敌人表现出了极大的仁慈。
entries.example_en: He showed great charity toward his enemies during the conflict.

entries.definition_en: a foundation created to promote the public good (not for assistance to any particular individuals)
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构组织年度活动以筹集教育资金。
entries.example_en: The charity organizes annual events to raise funds for education.

entries.definition_cn: 基督教之爱（古语）；上帝对人的爱、人与上帝的爱或人与同胞之间的爱
entries.definition_en: Christian love (archaic); love of God, humanity, or one's fellow people
entries.example_cn: 在基督教神学中，charity 包括对上帝和同胞的爱。
entries.example_en: In Christian theology, charity includes love of God and one's fellow people.

entries.definition_cn: （广义）任何响亮刺耳的噪声或喧闹声
entries.definition_en: (broadly) Any loud, cacophonous noise or hubbub.
entries.example_cn: 拥挤街道上传来的喧闹声让我们无法入睡。
entries.example_en: The charivari from the crowded street kept us awake.

entries.definition_cn: 为新婚夫妇举行的喧闹恶作剧式祝贺（敲打锅碗瓢盆）
entries.definition_en: a noisy mock serenade made by banging pans and kettles to a newly married couple
entries.example_cn: 邻居们加入这场喧闹的恶作剧，取笑这对新婚夫妇。
entries.example_en: The neighbors joined in the charivari to tease the newlyweds.

entries.definition_cn: 冒充具有特殊知识或技能并以此骗取钱财的人；江湖骗子
entries.definition_en: a person who falsely claims special knowledge or skill, especially to deceive people for personal profit
entries.example_cn: 观众意识到那位魔术师是个江湖骗子。
entries.example_en: The audience realized the magician was a charlatan.

entries.definition_en: dishonest behavior by someone who pretends to have special knowledge or skills
entries.example_cn: 观众对这位所谓专家的江湖骗术感到震惊。
entries.example_en: The audience was horrified by the charlatanism of the so-called expert.

entries.definition_cn: 肌肉痉挛（通常在大腿或小腿）
entries.definition_en: a muscular cramp (especially in the thigh or calf) following vigorous exercise
entries.example_cn: 跑完马拉松后，我的小腿抽筋了。
entries.example_en: I got a charley-horse in my calf after running the marathon.

entries.definition_en: a weedy Eurasian plant that is often a pest in grain fields
entries.example_cn: 农民试图在野芥蔓延到麦田之前将其清除。
entries.example_en: Farmers try to remove charlock before it spreads in the wheat fields.

entries.definition_en: a mold lined with cake or crumbs and filled with fruit or whipped cream or custard
entries.example_cn: 她为聚会烤了一个美味的夏洛特蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She baked a delicious charlotte for the party.

entries.definition_en: a quality that makes people like or admire you
entries.example_cn: 她有一种天生的魅力，让每个人都感到放松。
entries.example_en: She has a natural charm that puts everyone at ease.

entries.definition_en: an object believed to bring good luck
entries.example_cn: 他在钥匙扣上戴了一个幸运护身符。
entries.example_en: He wore a lucky charm on his keychain.

entries.definition_en: a spell or incantation used in magic
entries.example_cn: 那本古书中包含许多古老的咒语。
entries.example_en: The old book contained many ancient charms.

entries.definition_en: to make someone feel attracted or enchanted
entries.example_cn: 魔术师试图用他的戏法使观众着迷。
entries.example_en: The magician tried to charm the audience with his tricks.

entries.definition_en: to persuade someone to do something using charm
entries.example_cn: 他用魅力诱使服务员多给他一份甜点。
entries.example_en: He charmed the waiter into giving him an extra dessert.

entries.definition_en: to control someone using magic
entries.example_cn: 女巫试图用魔法让龙屈服。
entries.example_en: The witch tried to charm the dragon into submission.

entries.definition_en: to protect someone using magic
entries.example_cn: 牧师给房子施了法，以驱赶邪恶的灵魂。
entries.example_en: The priest charmed the house to keep evil spirits away.

entries.definition_en: a type of quark in particle physics
entries.example_cn: 粲夸克是六种夸克风味之一。
entries.example_en: The charm quark is one of the six flavors of quarks.

entries.definition_en: a man employed to do housework
entries.example_cn: 在那古老的故事里，男佣每天打扫整个房子。
entries.example_en: In the old story, the charman cleaned the entire house every day.

entries.definition_cn: 因某人或某物令人愉悦的特质而喜欢或着迷的
entries.definition_en: pleased and attracted by someone’s or something’s pleasant qualities
entries.example_cn: 她被他温和的态度迷住了。
entries.example_en: She was charmed by his gentle manner.

entries.definition_en: full of wonder and delight
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被魔术表演迷住了。
entries.example_en: The children were charmed by the magic show.

entries.definition_en: a person who charms others by personal attractiveness
entries.example_cn: 她是个天生的魅力人物，笑容灿烂。
entries.example_en: She is a natural charmer with a bright smile.

entries.definition_en: someone with an assured and ingratiating manner
entries.example_cn: 新经理真是个讨人喜欢者，让每个人都感到受欢迎。
entries.example_en: The new manager is a real charmer who makes everyone feel welcome.

entries.definition_en: very pleasant and attractive
entries.example_cn: 那座迷人的小茅屋有一个舒适的壁炉。
entries.example_en: The charming little cottage had a cozy fireplace.

entries.definition_en: having or using magical powers
entries.example_cn: 故事里有一位会飞的巫师。
entries.example_en: The story features a charming wizard who can fly.

entries.definition_en: in a charming manner
entries.example_cn: 她亲切动人地对那个紧张的孩子说话。
entries.example_en: She spoke charmingly to the nervous child.

entries.definition_cn: 存放尸体或遗骨的墓室、建筑或其他场所
entries.definition_en: a vault, building, or other repository for corpses or bones
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的修道院被改造成停尸堂，用来存放死者的遗骸。
entries.example_en: The old abbey was converted into a charnel house to hold the remains of the dead.

entries.definition_cn: 与死亡或死者有关且令人毛骨悚然的
entries.definition_en: gruesomely indicative of death or the dead
entries.example_cn: 废弃医院里那种令人毛骨悚然的死亡气息让访客感到不安。
entries.example_en: The charnel atmosphere of the abandoned hospital made the visitors feel uneasy.

entries.definition_cn: 红点鲑属的一种似鳟鱼的小鱼
entries.definition_en: a small fish that looks like a trout
entries.example_cn: 红点鲑在寒冷的山涧中快速游动。
entries.example_en: The charr swam quickly in the cold mountain stream.

entries.definition_en: a visual display of information
entries.example_cn: 该公司使用图表来展示销售增长。
entries.example_en: The company used a chart to show the sales growth.

entries.definition_en: a map designed to assist navigation by air or sea
entries.example_cn: 船长在起航前查阅了航海图。
entries.example_en: The captain consulted the chart before setting sail.

entries.definition_en: a listing of best-selling recorded music
entries.example_cn: 这首新歌登上了排行榜榜首。
entries.example_en: The new song climbed to the top of the chart.

entries.definition_en: make a chart of
entries.example_cn: 我们需要绘制项目进展的图表。
entries.example_en: We need to chart the progress of the project.

entries.definition_en: plan in detail
entries.example_cn: 他们规划了一条路线以确保安全到达目的地。
entries.example_en: They charted a course to reach the destination safely.

entries.definition_en: represent by means of a graph
entries.example_cn: 科学家用图表表示了全年的气温变化。
entries.example_en: The scientist charted the temperature changes over the year.

entries.definition_en: having the texture or appearance of paper
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子是纸质的，摸起来又干又脆。
entries.example_en: The leaves of the plant were chartaceous, feeling dry and brittle to the touch.

entries.definition_en: a document that establishes an institution and specifies its rights
entries.example_cn: 该公司是根据皇家宪章成立的。
entries.example_en: The company was founded under a royal charter.

entries.definition_en: a contract to hire or lease transportation
entries.example_cn: 他们签署了一份包租私人飞机的合同。
entries.example_en: They signed a charter for a private jet.

entries.definition_en: to hold under a lease or rental agreement
entries.example_cn: 我们租了一艘船进行周末旅行。
entries.example_en: We chartered a boat for the weekend trip.

entries.definition_en: to engage for service under a term of contract
entries.example_cn: 航空公司包机用于该活动。
entries.example_en: The airline chartered a fleet of planes for the event.

entries.definition_en: to grant a charter to an organization
entries.example_cn: 政府授予了那所新大学特许状。
entries.example_en: The government chartered the new university.

entries.definition_en: leased or hired for a particular purpose
entries.example_cn: 我们乘坐包机前往那座岛。
entries.example_en: We took a charter flight to the island.

entries.definition_en: hired for the exclusive temporary use of a group of travelers
entries.example_cn: 我们包了一辆巴士去参观历史遗迹。
entries.example_en: We took a chartered bus to visit the historical sites.

entries.definition_en: a Carthusian monastery
entries.example_cn: 这座加尔都西会修道院建于14世纪。
entries.example_en: The charterhouse was founded in the 14th century.

entries.definition_en: a woman employed to do housework
entries.example_cn: 这所老房子需要一名女佣每天打扫地板。
entries.example_en: The old house needed a charwoman to clean the floors every day.

entries.definition_en: showing great caution and wariness
entries.example_cn: 她对于在网上分享个人信息很谨慎。
entries.example_en: She was chary about sharing her personal information online.

entries.definition_en: go after someone or something with the intent to catch them
entries.example_cn: 那只狗追着球跑过田野。
entries.example_en: The dog chased the ball across the field.

entries.definition_en: pursue someone sexually or romantically
entries.example_cn: 他在聚会上见到她后，决定追求她。
entries.example_en: He decided to chase her after seeing her at the party.

entries.definition_en: cut a groove into a surface
entries.example_cn: 机器在金属杆上刻出一道槽。
entries.example_en: The machine chases a groove into the metal rod.

entries.definition_en: cut a furrow into a column of type
entries.example_cn: 排字工在字排中刻出一道沟以分隔各部分。
entries.example_en: The compositor chases a furrow into the column to separate sections.

entries.definition_en: the act of pursuing someone or something in an effort to overtake or capture them
entries.example_cn: 警方展开追捕以抓获小偷。
entries.example_en: The police launched a chase to catch the thief.

entries.definition_en: a rectangular metal frame used in letterpress printing to hold together the pages or columns of composed type
entries.example_cn: 印刷机在运行前锁紧了活字框。
entries.example_en: The printer locked the chase before running the press.

entries.definition_en: a person who is being chased
entries.example_cn: 那个小偷是拥挤街道上的被追逐者。
entries.example_en: The thief was the chased in the crowded street.

entries.definition_cn: 在另一种饮料之后饮用的饮料
entries.definition_en: a drink taken after another drink, typically of a different kind
entries.example_cn: 他点了一杯威士忌和一杯青柠饮料作为续饮，结束了这个夜晚。
entries.example_en: He ordered a whiskey and a lime chaser to finish the night.

entries.definition_en: a person who is pursuing and trying to overtake or capture
entries.example_cn: 追捕者终于在桥边抓住了嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police chaser finally caught the suspect near the bridge.

entries.definition_en: a deep crack or opening in the ground
entries.example_cn: 一道深深的峡谷将山的两侧隔开。
entries.example_en: A deep chasm separated the two sides of the mountain.

entries.definition_en: a large difference of opinion
entries.example_cn: 两党在这个问题上的分歧越来越大。
entries.example_en: There is a growing chasm between the two parties over the issue.

entries.definition_cn: 芭蕾舞中的追步（一脚追随或领先另一脚的快速滑步）
entries.definition_en: a quick gliding step in ballet in which one foot chases or leads the other
entries.example_cn: 舞者在舞台上优雅地做了一个滑步。
entries.example_en: The dancer executed a graceful chasse across the stage.

entries.definition_en: to perform a chasse step in ballet
entries.example_cn: 她练习滑步，直到动作流畅精准。
entries.example_en: She practiced the chasse until her movements were smooth and precise.

entries.definition_en: the skeleton of a motor vehicle consisting of a steel frame supported on springs that holds the body and motor
entries.example_cn: 这辆汽车的底盘设计用于吸收崎岖路面的冲击。
entries.example_en: The car's chassis was designed to absorb shock from rough roads.

entries.definition_en: a metal mounting for the circuit components of an electronic device
entries.example_cn: 技术员将新芯片焊接到了电路板的金属底座上。
entries.example_en: The technician soldered the new chip onto the circuit board's chassis.

entries.definition_en: (slang) a woman's buttocks
entries.example_cn: 他欣赏她曲线优美的臀部。
entries.example_en: He admired her shapely chassis.

entries.definition_en: sexually pure, especially refraining from sexual intercourse
entries.example_cn: 她直到结婚前都保持贞洁。
entries.example_en: She remained chaste until her marriage.

entries.definition_en: pure and simple in design or style
entries.example_cn: 这座建筑具有简洁朴素的风格。
entries.example_en: The building has a chaste architectural style.

entries.definition_cn: 不发生被视为不正当的性关系的；守贞的
entries.definition_en: abstaining from sexual intercourse considered unlawful
entries.example_cn: 那部宗教文献称他守贞，因为他不发生文献所认定的不正当性关系。
entries.example_en: The religious text called him chaste because he abstained from sex it considered unlawful.

entries.definition_en: in a chaste and virtuous manner
entries.example_cn: 她过着贞洁的生活，将一生奉献给慈善事业和服务。
entries.example_en: She lived chastely, dedicating her life to charity and service.

entries.definition_cn: 惩罚或训诫以使其改正
entries.definition_en: punish or reprimand someone, especially to improve their behavior
entries.example_cn: 严格的规则旨在纠正新兵的缺点。
entries.example_en: The strict rules were meant to chasten the new recruits.

entries.definition_en: to make something less extreme or excessive; to moderate it
entries.example_cn: 严冬使他鲁莽的驾驶习惯有所收敛。
entries.example_en: The harsh winter chastened his reckless driving habits.

entries.definition_en: rebuke or censure someone severely
entries.example_cn: 老师不得不严厉斥责那个学生粗鲁的行为。
entries.example_en: The teacher had to chasten the student for his rude behavior.

entries.definition_en: the quality of lacking ornamentation
entries.example_cn: 建筑师赞赏这座建筑设计风格的朴素。
entries.example_en: The architect admired the chasteness of the building's design.

entries.definition_en: the act or experience of chastening; a lesson that corrects or disciplines
entries.example_cn: 失去那份合同对团队来说是一次深刻的教训。
entries.example_en: The loss of the contract served as a chastening experience for the team.

entries.definition_en: to criticize or reprimand someone severely
entries.example_cn: 老师不得不严厉斥责那些扰乱课堂秩序的学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher had to chastise the students for their disruptive behavior.

entries.definition_en: punishment, especially physical punishment, for wrongdoing
entries.example_cn: 那名违法者因屡次违抗命令而受到体罚。
entries.example_en: The offender received physical chastisement for his repeated disobedience.

entries.definition_en: a sharp rebuke for making a mistake
entries.example_cn: 她因计算错误受到了老板的斥责。
entries.example_en: She received a chastisement from her boss for the calculation error.

entries.definition_cn: 戒绝性行为，尤指出于宗教或道德原因
entries.definition_en: abstention from sexual activity, especially for religious or moral reasons
entries.example_cn: 她进入修道院前立下了禁欲誓言。
entries.example_en: She took a vow of chastity before entering the convent.

entries.definition_en: morality concerning sexual relations
entries.example_cn: 这个故事强调了传统文化中贞操的重要性。
entries.example_en: The story emphasizes the importance of chastity in traditional culture.

entries.definition_en: a long sleeveless vestment worn by a priest when celebrating Mass
entries.example_cn: 牧师在服务开始前穿上了祭披。
entries.example_en: The priest put on the chasuble before the service began.

entries.definition_en: talk socially without exchanging too much information
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在门廊上闲聊。
entries.example_en: They sat on the porch and chatted.

entries.definition_en: an informal conversation
entries.example_cn: 我们就计划闲聊了一会儿。
entries.example_en: We had a chat about our plans.

entries.definition_en: a small potato, especially one fed to pigs
entries.example_cn: 农夫把小土豆喂给了猪。
entries.example_en: The farmer fed the chats to the pigs.

entries.definition_en: (regional) mining waste from lead and zinc mines
entries.example_cn: 矿工们在铅锌矿废料中发现了晶体。
entries.example_en: The miners found crystals among the chats.

entries.definition_en: a large and impressive country house or castle in France
entries.example_cn: 他们住在卢瓦尔河谷的一座美丽城堡里。
entries.example_en: They stayed in a beautiful chateau in the Loire Valley.

entries.definition_en: a chain formerly worn at the waist by women; for carrying a purse or bunch of keys etc.
entries.example_cn: 她腰间戴着一条装饰性的腰链用来挂钥匙。
entries.example_en: She wore a decorative chatelaine on her belt to hold her keys.

entries.definition_en: the mistress of a chateau or large country house
entries.example_cn: 这位庄园女主人以极高的效率管理着家务。
entries.example_en: The chatelaine managed the household with great efficiency.

entries.definition_cn: 具有猫眼效应的；呈丝绢光泽的
entries.definition_en: having a silky or cat's-eye optical reflectance effect
entries.example_cn: 这块具有猫眼效应的宝石表面呈现出一条丝绢般的光带。
entries.example_en: The chatoyant gemstone displayed a silky band of light across its surface.

entries.definition_en: a site on the internet where a number of users can communicate in real time
entries.example_cn: 他们在一个专门讨论摄影的聊天室里相遇了。
entries.example_en: They met in a chatroom dedicated to photography.

entries.definition_en: personal property that can be moved, such as furniture, domestic animals, or a car
entries.example_cn: 合同规定，所有动产，包括家具和汽车，都包含在出售范围内。
entries.example_en: The contract specified that all chattels, including the furniture and the car, were included in the sale.

entries.definition_en: to talk socially without exchanging too much information
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在门廊上闲聊天气。
entries.example_en: They sat on the porch and chattered about the weather.

entries.definition_en: to speak (about unimportant matters) rapidly and incessantly
entries.example_cn: 她喋喋不休地谈论她的度假计划长达数小时。
entries.example_en: She chattered on about her vacation plans for hours.

entries.definition_en: to make noise as if chattering away
entries.example_cn: 鸟儿在树枝上叽叽喳喳地叫。
entries.example_en: The birds chattered in the branches.

entries.definition_en: noisy talk
entries.example_cn: 人群的嘈杂声淹没了演讲者的声音。
entries.example_en: The chatter of the crowd drowned out the speaker.

entries.definition_cn: 动物（鸟类或猴子）发出的高音持续噪音
entries.definition_en: the high-pitched continuing noise made by animals (birds or monkeys)
entries.example_cn: 我们听到了树上猴子的叫声。
entries.example_en: We heard the chatter of the monkeys in the trees.

entries.definition_en: the rapid series of noises made by the parts of a machine
entries.example_cn: 引擎里传来巨大的噪音。
entries.example_en: There was a loud chatter coming from the engine.

entries.definition_en: to click repeatedly or uncontrollably
entries.example_cn: 随着齿轮磨损，机器开始咔哒作响。
entries.example_en: The machine began to chatter as the gears wore down.

entries.definition_en: to cut unevenly with a chattering tool
entries.example_cn: 木材被故障的锯子切得参差不齐。
entries.example_en: The wood was chattered by the faulty saw.

entries.definition_en: a person who talks excessively
entries.example_cn: 别总是这么喋喋不休的，听我说！
entries.example_en: Stop being such a chatterbox and listen to what I am saying!

entries.definition_cn: 一种生长在北美西部溪流或池塘旁的兰花（Epipactis gigantea），有叶状茎，上部每片叶的叶腋处有一朵绿褐色和粉色的花
entries.definition_en: an orchid growing along streams or ponds of western North America having leafy stems and 1 greenish-brown and pinkish flower in the axil of each upper leaf
entries.example_cn: 这种名为 chatterbox 的稀有兰花在春天于溪流旁开花了。
entries.example_en: The rare orchid known as chatterbox bloomed near the stream in spring.

entries.definition_en: a person who chatters; a chatterbox
entries.example_cn: 别这么喋喋不休了，听我说。
entries.example_en: Stop being such a chatterer and listen to what I am saying.

entries.definition_en: a type of passerine bird found in the New World tropics
entries.example_cn: 美洲热带鸣禽在新世界热带茂密的森林中很常见。
entries.example_en: The chatterer is a common sight in the dense forests of the New World tropics.

entries.definition_cn: 鸟、猴子等动物发出的快速连续叫声
entries.definition_en: a rapid series of high-pitched sounds made by animals such as birds or monkeys
entries.example_cn: 我们听到了头顶树上猴子叽叽喳喳的叫声。
entries.example_en: We heard the chattering of monkeys in the trees above us.

entries.definition_cn: 机器零件发出的咔哒声
entries.definition_en: the rapid series of noises made by the parts of a machine
entries.example_cn: 齿轮发出的咔哒声警告我们引擎过热了。
entries.example_en: The chattering of the gears warned us that the engine was overheating.

entries.definition_cn: 充满非正式或琐碎谈话的
entries.definition_en: characterized by a lot of informal or trivial conversation
entries.example_cn: 聚会上闲聊的氛围让人难以专注于严肃的讨论。
entries.example_en: The chatty atmosphere at the party made it hard to focus on the serious discussion.

entries.definition_en: inclined to talk in a friendly and informal way
entries.example_cn: 我的邻居非常健谈，喝咖啡时总有故事分享。
entries.example_en: My neighbor is very chatty and always has a story to share over coffee.

usage.label: informal
usage.pattern: of a person, fond of chatting

entries.definition_en: a person paid to drive a privately owned car
entries.example_cn: 酒店提供司机将客人送往机场。
entries.example_en: The hotel provides a chauffeur to drive guests to the airport.

entries.definition_en: to drive someone in a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 一名司机开车送这位名流参加红毯活动。
entries.example_en: A chauffeur drove the celebrity to the red-carpet event.

entries.definition_en: extreme and blind patriotism
