entries.definition_en: sexual intercourse
entries.example_cn: 这对夫妇在晚餐后进行了性交。
entries.example_en: The couple engaged in coition after dinner.

entries.definition_en: sexual intercourse, especially penile–vaginal intercourse
entries.example_cn: 术语“性交”常用于医学或科学语境中来描述性活动。
entries.example_en: The term coitus is often used in medical or scientific contexts to describe sexual activity.

entries.definition_en: a low point between two mountain peaks
entries.example_cn: 登山者从两座山峰之间的山口向下行进。
entries.example_en: The climbers descended into the col between the two peaks.

entries.definition_cn: 位于两个反气旋和两个低压区之间的鞍形气压区，在反气旋之间相对较低、在低压区之间相对较高
entries.definition_en: a saddle-shaped pressure region between two anticyclones and two areas of low pressure, relatively low between the anticyclones and relatively high between the lows
entries.example_cn: 天气图显示两个反气旋和两个低压区之间有一个鞍形气压区。
entries.example_en: The weather map showed a col between two anticyclones and two low-pressure areas.

entries.definition_en: carbonated drink flavored with extract from kola nuts
entries.example_cn: 他在酒吧点了一杯冰可乐。
entries.example_en: He ordered a cold cola at the bar.

entries.definition_en: a bowl-shaped strainer used to wash or drain foods
entries.example_cn: 她把意大利面倒入漏勺中以沥干多余的水分。
entries.example_en: She poured the pasta into the colander to drain the excess water.

entries.definition_cn: 最初从秋水仙属植物中提取、主要用于治疗痛风的生物碱药物
entries.definition_en: an alkaloid drug originally extracted from plants of the genus Colchicum and used mainly to treat gout
entries.example_cn: 医生开了秋水仙碱治疗他的痛风。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed colchicine to treat his gout.

entries.definition_en: having a low or inadequate temperature or feeling a sensation of coldness
entries.example_cn: 汤太冷了，没法吃。
entries.example_en: The soup is too cold to eat.

entries.definition_en: without human warmth or emotion
entries.example_cn: 他对我的问题给出了冷漠的回应。
entries.example_en: He gave a cold response to my question.

entries.definition_en: giving no sensation of warmth
entries.example_cn: 房间被漆成了冷色调。
entries.example_en: The room is painted in cold colors.

entries.definition_en: a mild viral infection involving the nose and respiratory passages
entries.example_cn: 我上周感冒了。
entries.example_en: I caught a cold last week.

entries.definition_en: the absence of heat
entries.example_cn: 冬天带来了寒冷。
entries.example_en: Winter brings the cold.

entries.definition_en: the sensation produced by low temperatures
entries.example_cn: 她因感到寒冷而发抖。
entries.example_en: She shivered from the cold.

entries.definition_cn: 不再新鲜的；失去时效的
entries.definition_en: having lost freshness through the passage of time
entries.example_cn: 几周过去后，警方追踪的是一条已经失去时效的线索。
entries.example_en: After several weeks, the police were following a cold trail.

entries.definition_en: marked by errorless familiarity
entries.example_cn: 他熟练地弹起了钢琴。
entries.example_en: He played the piano cold.

entries.definition_en: lacking human feelings or conscience
entries.example_cn: 这名罪犯被描述为一名冷血的杀人犯。
entries.example_en: The criminal was described as a cold-blooded murderer.

entries.definition_en: having a body temperature that depends on the environment
entries.example_cn: 蛇是变温动物，需要阳光来取暖。
entries.example_en: Snakes are cold-blooded animals that need the sun to warm up.

entries.definition_en: emotionlessly and heartlessly; with deliberate cruelty or callousness
entries.example_cn: 他冷酷地毫不犹豫地杀死了他的对手。
entries.example_en: He cold-bloodedly killed his rival without any hesitation.

entries.definition_cn: 冷静而不带偏见的；冷峻的
entries.definition_en: showing no strong emotion or prejudice
entries.example_cn: 法官冷静而客观地评估了证据。
entries.example_en: The judge made a cold-eyed assessment of the evidence.

entries.definition_en: to pay no attention to or show disrespect to someone
entries.example_cn: 争吵后，他决定冷落他的老朋友。
entries.example_en: He decided to cold-shoulder his old friend after the argument.

entries.definition_en: lacking in sympathy or feeling
entries.example_cn: 那位冷酷无情的经理在没有警告的情况下解雇了全体员工。
entries.example_en: The coldhearted manager fired the entire staff without warning.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows no warmth or emotion
entries.example_cn: 她冷漠地拒绝了他的提议。
entries.example_en: She rejected his proposal coldly.

entries.definition_en: the sensation produced by low temperatures
entries.example_cn: 冷风让她打了个寒颤。
entries.example_en: The coldness of the wind made her shiver.

entries.definition_en: a lack of affection or enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 他对家人冷漠的态度让朋友们很担心。
entries.example_en: His coldness towards his family worried his friends.

entries.definition_en: a relative lack of heat
entries.example_cn: 深海中的寒冷是由洋流维持的。
entries.example_en: The coldness of the deep ocean is maintained by currents.

entries.definition_cn: 甘蓝类蔬菜；芸薹属植物
entries.definition_en: a cabbage or other plant of the genus Brassica, especially a cole crop
entries.example_cn: 甘蓝类蔬菜在凉爽的天气里生长良好。
entries.example_en: Cole crops grow well in cool weather.

entries.definition_en: coarse curly-leafed cabbage
entries.example_cn: 农夫种植了一种在寒冷气候下茁壮成长的羽衣甘蓝品种。
entries.example_en: The farmer grew a variety of cole that thrived in the cold climate.

entries.definition_en: shredded cabbage mixed with dressing
entries.example_cn: 我们搭配炸鸡上了凉拌卷心菜。
entries.example_en: We served coleslaw with the fried chicken.

entries.definition_en: a tropical plant with multicolored decorative leaves and blue flower spikes
entries.example_cn: 园丁种了几株彩叶草，为花园的阴凉角落增添了鲜艳的色彩。
entries.example_en: The gardener planted several coleus to add vibrant color to the shaded garden corner.

entries.definition_en: severe abdominal pain, especially affecting infants
entries.example_cn: 宝宝因为肠绞痛在哭。
entries.example_en: The baby was crying because of colic.

entries.definition_cn: 患绞痛的；（尤指婴儿）因肠绞痛哭闹的
entries.definition_en: suffering from colic, especially abdominal pain and crying in infants
entries.example_cn: 那个婴儿患有肠绞痛，每天晚上哭几个小时。
entries.example_en: The baby was colicky and cried for hours every evening.

entries.definition_cn: 大型剧场、电影院或体育场；竞技场
entries.definition_en: a large theatre, cinema, or stadium, especially an arena for events
entries.example_cn: 游客参观了古老的圆形竞技场，看到了废墟。
entries.example_en: Visitors toured the ancient coliseum to see the ruins.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the colon
entries.example_cn: 患者在经历剧烈腹痛后被诊断为急性结肠炎。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with acute colitis after experiencing severe abdominal pain.

entries.definition_en: to work jointly with others on a common project or enterprise
entries.example_cn: 来自不同国家的科学家合作解决了这个问题。
entries.example_en: Scientists from different countries collaborated to solve the problem.

entries.definition_en: to cooperate with an enemy or oppressive regime as a traitor
entries.example_cn: 他因勾结占领军而被捕。
entries.example_en: He was arrested for collaborating with the occupying forces.

entries.definition_en: the act of working together with others
entries.example_cn: 这个项目的成功归功于两个团队之间的紧密合作。
entries.example_en: The success of the project was due to close collaboration between the two teams.

entries.definition_en: the act of working with an enemy that is occupying your country
entries.example_cn: 他在战争期间与占领军勾结，因此被捕。
entries.example_en: He was arrested for collaboration with the occupying forces during the war.

entries.definition_cn: 通敌者；与占领本国的敌军合作的人
entries.definition_en: someone who collaborates with an enemy occupying force
entries.example_cn: 抵抗战士追捕那个背叛村庄的通敌者。
entries.example_en: The resistance fighters hunted down the collaborationist who had betrayed their village.

entries.definition_en: done by people working together
entries.example_cn: 团队合作完成了设计新软件的项目。
entries.example_en: The team worked on a collaborative project to design the new software.

entries.definition_cn: 为实现特定目标而合作的个人或组织团体
entries.definition_en: an organized group of people or organizations working together toward a particular goal
entries.example_cn: 这个合作团体召集了艺术家和工程师共同开发该项目。
entries.example_en: The collaborative brought artists and engineers together to develop the project.

entries.definition_en: a person who works together with someone else on a project or activity
entries.example_cn: 她是新研究项目中一位宝贵的合作者。
entries.example_en: She is a valued collaborator on the new research project.

entries.definition_en: a person who works with an enemy occupying force
entries.example_cn: 战争期间，这位叛徒向入侵者出卖了自己的国家。
entries.example_en: During the war, the collaborator betrayed his country to the invaders.

entries.definition_en: a person who helps in a secret plan or plot
entries.example_cn: 警方逮捕了协助策划抢劫的同谋者。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the collaborator who helped plan the robbery.

entries.definition_cn: 用纸张或照片拼贴而成的艺术品
entries.definition_en: a paste-up made by sticking together pieces of paper or photographs to form an artistic image
entries.example_cn: 她用旧杂志剪报制作了一幅美丽的拼贴画。
entries.example_en: She created a beautiful collage from old magazine cutouts.

entries.definition_en: any collection of diverse things
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了来自不同文化的各种文物的集合。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a collage of artifacts from different cultures.

entries.definition_en: a fibrous protein found in bone, cartilage, and connective tissue
entries.example_cn: 胶原蛋白有助于保持皮肤和关节的强健与灵活。
entries.example_en: Collagen helps keep skin and joints strong and flexible.

entries.definition_cn: 分解胶原蛋白肽键的酶
entries.definition_en: an enzyme that breaks peptide bonds in collagen
entries.example_cn: 研究人员使用胶原酶分解结缔组织。
entries.example_en: Researchers used collagenase to break down the connective tissue.

entries.definition_en: relating to or consisting of collagen
entries.example_cn: 皮肤中的胶原质组织提供了强度和弹性。
entries.example_en: The collagenous tissue in the skin provides strength and elasticity.

entries.definition_en: able to collapse or be collapsed
entries.example_cn: 这把可折叠的椅子很容易携带去露营。
entries.example_en: The collapsable chair is easy to carry on a camping trip.

entries.definition_cn: （因生病、疲劳或突发状况而）倒下
entries.definition_en: to fall down suddenly because of illness, fatigue, or a sudden attack
entries.example_cn: 她因精疲力竭而倒在地上。
entries.example_en: She collapsed on the floor from exhaustion.

entries.definition_en: to break down or fail completely, either physically or metaphorically
entries.example_cn: 这座旧桥在卡车的重量下开始坍塌。
entries.example_en: The old bridge began to collapse under the weight of the trucks.

entries.definition_en: to cease functioning or fail suddenly and completely
entries.example_cn: 该组织因内部腐败而瓦解。
entries.example_en: The organization collapsed due to internal corruption.

entries.definition_en: a sudden act of collapsing or falling down
entries.example_cn: 他突然瘫倒在沙发上，家人很担心。
entries.example_en: His sudden collapse onto the sofa worried his family.

entries.definition_en: an event where a structure suddenly falls down or caves in
entries.example_cn: 矿难发生后，矿工们被困住了。
entries.example_en: The miners were trapped after the mine collapse.

entries.definition_en: a sudden and severe drop in business activity or stock prices
entries.example_cn: 股市上周经历了重大崩盘。
entries.example_en: The stock market experienced a major collapse last week.

entries.definition_cn: （因体力或精神耗尽而）虚脱；昏倒
entries.definition_en: a sudden failure of health or strength, or complete exhaustion
entries.example_cn: 跑完马拉松后，他彻底虚脱了。
entries.example_en: After running the marathon, he suffered a total collapse.

entries.definition_en: to fold into a compact form
entries.example_cn: 请把雨伞折叠好再放进包里。
entries.example_en: Please collapse the umbrella before putting it in the bag.

entries.definition_en: designed to be collapsed, especially to take up less space when not in use
entries.example_cn: 我们把露营椅收起来，因为它们可折叠且易于携带。
entries.example_en: We packed our camping chairs because they are collapsible and easy to carry.

entries.definition_en: a band of fabric around the neck of a shirt
entries.example_cn: 他穿着一件硬领衬衫。
entries.example_en: He wore a shirt with a stiff collar.

entries.definition_en: a band of color around an animal's neck
entries.example_cn: 老虎脖子上有一圈黑色的颈圈。
entries.example_en: The tiger has a black collar.

entries.definition_en: anything worn around the neck
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一条围巾作为颈饰。
entries.example_en: She wore a scarf as a collar.

entries.definition_en: the upper edge or opening of a shoe or boot
entries.example_cn: 这双靴子的靴口已经磨破了。
entries.example_en: The collar of the boot is worn out.

entries.definition_en: a ring on a machine part to limit movement
entries.example_cn: 工程师在轴上安装了新的挡圈，以限制部件移动。
entries.example_en: The engineer installed a new collar on the shaft to limit movement.

entries.definition_en: to arrest or take into custody
entries.example_cn: 警官逮捕了嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police officer collared the suspect.

entries.definition_en: to grab someone by the neck
entries.example_cn: 那只狗试图揪住猫的脖子。
entries.example_en: The dog tried to collar the cat.

entries.definition_en: to put a collar on something
entries.example_cn: 裁缝会给你把衬衫装上领子。
entries.example_en: The tailor will collar the shirt for you.

entries.definition_en: the long bone that connects the shoulder blade to the breastbone
entries.example_cn: 她在滑雪事故中摔断了锁骨。
entries.example_en: She broke her collarbone in a skiing accident.

entries.definition_en: a type of kale with smooth leaves
entries.example_cn: 厨师用新鲜的羽衣甘蓝叶做了一道沙拉。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a salad with fresh collard leaves.

entries.definition_en: having a shirt or jacket without a stiff neckband
entries.example_cn: 他夏天野餐时穿了一件休闲的无领衬衫。
entries.example_en: He wore a casual, collarless shirt for the summer picnic.

entries.definition_en: to arrange items in a proper sequence or order
entries.example_cn: 请在装订书籍前将页面按顺序整理好。
entries.example_en: Please collate the pages before binding the book.

entries.definition_en: to compare texts critically to check for accuracy or differences
entries.example_cn: 学者们校勘了这些古代手稿以找出原文。
entries.example_en: Scholars collated the ancient manuscripts to find the original text.

entries.definition_en: a security pledged for the repayment of a loan
entries.example_cn: 他们用汽车作为商业贷款的抵押品。
entries.example_en: They used their car as collateral for the business loan.

entries.definition_en: additional but secondary; auxiliary
entries.example_cn: 该报告包含了关于该地区经济的辅助信息。
entries.example_en: The report included collateral information about the region's economy.

entries.definition_en: serving to support or corroborate
entries.example_cn: 证人提供了佐证嫌疑人不在场证明的旁证。
entries.example_en: The witness provided collateral evidence for the suspect's alibi.

entries.definition_en: occurring with or following as a consequence
entries.example_cn: 新政策对当地企业产生了伴随发生的影响。
entries.example_en: There were collateral effects of the new policy on local businesses.

entries.definition_en: situated or running side by side
entries.example_cn: 这两条河并行流淌了好几英里。
entries.example_en: The two rivers run collateral for several miles.

entries.definition_en: descended from a common ancestor but through different lines
entries.example_cn: 这两位兄弟是旁系亲属。
entries.example_en: The two brothers are collateral relatives.

entries.definition_en: to pledge something as security for a loan or other obligation
entries.example_cn: 银行要求公司在批准合并之前对其资产提供抵押。
entries.example_en: The bank required the company to collateralize its assets before approving the merger.

entries.definition_cn: 按正确顺序整理书页或物品
entries.definition_en: the act of assembling pages or items in the correct order
entries.example_cn: 印刷工检查了书页的顺序。
entries.example_en: The printer checked the collation of the book's pages.

entries.definition_en: careful examination and comparison to note points of disagreement
entries.example_cn: 编辑们对两个手稿版本进行了彻底的核对。
entries.example_en: The editors performed a thorough collation of the two manuscript versions.

entries.definition_en: a light informal meal
entries.example_cn: 会议结束后，我们享用了一顿简单的奶酪和水果便餐。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a simple collation of cheese and fruit after the meeting.

entries.definition_en: a historical machine designed to sort, combine, and match decks of punch cards
entries.example_cn: 那间旧计算机房里有一台用于处理数据卡片的大型卡片整理机。
entries.example_en: The old computer room contained a large collator for processing data cards.

entries.definition_en: a person you work with
entries.example_cn: 我的同事帮我完成了报告。
entries.example_en: My colleague helped me finish the report.

entries.definition_en: a person who belongs to the same profession or class
entries.example_cn: 她是医学界受人尊敬的同行。
entries.example_en: She is a respected colleague in the medical field.

entries.definition_en: get or gather together
entries.example_cn: 请把桌子上所有的文件收集起来。
entries.example_en: Please collect all the papers from the desks.

entries.definition_cn: 收藏；收集（尤指作为爱好）
entries.definition_en: accumulate similar objects, especially as a hobby
entries.example_cn: 她喜欢收集来自不同国家的邮票。
entries.example_en: She likes to collect stamps from different countries.

entries.definition_en: call for and obtain payment of
entries.example_cn: 司机在您到达时将收取车费。
entries.example_en: The driver will collect the fare when you arrive.

entries.definition_en: payable by the recipient on delivery
entries.example_cn: 我订购了一本到付的书。
entries.example_en: I ordered a book on collect.

entries.definition_en: make a telephone call or mail a package so that the recipient pays
entries.example_cn: 她以到付的方式寄出了包裹。
entries.example_en: She mailed the package collect.

entries.definition_en: a short prayer generally preceding the lesson in the Church of Rome or the Church of England
entries.example_cn: 牧师在布道前宣读了集祷文。
entries.example_en: The priest read the collect before the sermon.

entries.definition_en: assemble or get together
entries.example_cn: 经理召集团队开会。
entries.example_en: The manager collected the team for a meeting.

entries.definition_en: get or bring together
entries.example_cn: 他们在公园聚集了朋友们。
entries.example_en: They collected their friends at the park.

entries.definition_en: things considered to be worth collecting
entries.example_cn: 这枚稀有邮票是许多收藏爱好者珍视的藏品。
entries.example_en: This rare stamp is a valuable collectable for many enthusiasts.

entries.definition_en: suitable or intended for collecting
entries.example_cn: 这些限量版卡片很值得收藏。
entries.example_en: The limited-edition cards are highly collectable.

entries.definition_en: brought together in one place
entries.example_cn: 她收藏了一套来自欧洲每个国家的邮票。
entries.example_en: She has a collected set of stamps from every country in Europe.

entries.definition_en: in full control of your faculties
entries.example_cn: 尽管周围一片混乱，他依然保持镇定。
entries.example_en: He remained collected despite the chaos around him.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being collectible
entries.example_cn: 近年来，古邮票的可收藏性显著提高了。
entries.example_en: The collectibility of vintage stamps has increased significantly in recent years.

entries.definition_en: items considered worth collecting, which may not necessarily be valuable or antique
entries.example_cn: 他周末花时间去购买稀有的收藏品硬币。
entries.example_en: He spends his weekends buying rare collectible coins.

entries.definition_en: subject to or requiring payment as specified
entries.example_cn: 游戏中的需付费内容需要单独购买。
entries.example_en: The collectible content in the game requires a separate purchase.

entries.definition_en: the hobby of seeking, acquiring, organizing, cataloging, displaying, and preserving items of interest
entries.example_cn: 他喜欢收集世界各地的复古邮票。
entries.example_en: He enjoys collecting vintage stamps from around the world.

entries.definition_en: a group of similar items kept together
entries.example_cn: 他有一大套旧邮票收藏品。
entries.example_en: He has a large collection of old stamps.

entries.definition_en: a book containing various short stories or poems
entries.example_cn: 她买了一本著名作家的短篇小说集。
entries.example_en: She bought a collection of short stories by the famous author.

entries.definition_en: the action of gathering things together
entries.example_cn: 博物馆正在对古代文物进行收集工作。
entries.example_en: The museum is working on the collection of ancient artifacts.

entries.definition_en: a request for money
entries.example_cn: 慈善机构为洪水受害者举行了募捐活动。
entries.example_en: The charity held a collection for flood victims.

entries.definition_en: done by or characteristic of individuals acting together
entries.example_cn: 集体的努力挽救了这个项目。
entries.example_en: The collective effort saved the project.

entries.definition_en: forming a whole or aggregate
entries.example_cn: 该群体的集合意见是一致的。
entries.example_en: The collective opinion of the group was unanimous.

entries.definition_cn: 集体主义的；集体所有制的
entries.definition_en: set up on the principle of collectivism or ownership and production by the workers involved
entries.example_cn: 他们在集体农庄工作。
entries.example_en: They worked in a collective farm.

entries.definition_en: members of a cooperative enterprise
entries.example_cn: 集体成员决定投资购买新机器。
entries.example_en: The collective decided to invest in new machinery.

entries.definition_en: as a group or whole; considered together rather than separately
entries.example_cn: 团队集体合作解决了这个问题。
entries.example_en: The team worked collectively to solve the problem.

entries.definition_en: the organization of a nation or economy on the basis of collectivism
entries.example_cn: 农业集体化彻底改变了乡村的面貌。
entries.example_en: The collectivisation of agriculture changed the rural landscape entirely.

entries.definition_en: to bring under collective control, especially regarding farms and industrial enterprises
entries.example_cn: 政府决定对农业部门实行集体化。
entries.example_en: The government decided to collectivise the agricultural sector.

entries.definition_cn: 生产资料和分配手段由人民共同拥有和控制的一种经济制度
entries.definition_en: an economic system in which the means of production and distribution are owned and controlled collectively by the people
entries.example_cn: 新宪法强调集体主义，生产资料和分配手段由人民共同拥有和控制，而非私人所有。
entries.example_en: The new constitution emphasized collectivism, with the means of production and distribution owned and controlled collectively rather than privately.

entries.definition_cn: 集体主义；优先考虑集体而非其中个人的原则
entries.definition_en: the practice or principle of giving a group priority over each individual in it
entries.example_cn: 该政权的政策根植于一种严格的集体主义形式。
entries.example_en: The regime's policies were rooted in a strict form of collectivism.

entries.definition_cn: 集体主义的；主张集体所有的
entries.definition_en: relating to collectivism or advocating collective ownership
entries.example_cn: 这种集体主义经济学方法强调社区所有而非私人企业。
entries.example_en: The collectivist approach to economics emphasizes community ownership over private enterprise.

entries.definition_en: an advocate of collectivism
entries.example_cn: 这位集体主义者主张资源应由社会共同拥有。
entries.example_en: The collectivist argued that resources should be owned collectively.

entries.definition_cn: 集体主义的；强调集体而非个人的
entries.definition_en: Relating to collectivism or emphasizing the group over the individual.
entries.example_cn: 这个集体主义社会优先考虑群体的需求而非个人的欲望。
entries.example_en: The collectivistic society prioritized the needs of the group over individual desires.

entries.definition_en: the process of organizing a nation or economy based on collective ownership
entries.example_cn: 集体化政策改变了该国的农业结构。
entries.example_en: The policy of collectivization changed the agricultural structure of the country.

entries.definition_en: to bring farms or industrial enterprises under collective control
entries.example_cn: 政府决定对农业部门实行集体化。
entries.example_en: The government decided to collectivize the agricultural sector.

entries.definition_en: a person who gathers and keeps items of interest
entries.example_cn: 博物馆收藏了一位著名收藏家的邮票。
entries.example_en: The museum has a large collection of stamps from a famous collector.

entries.definition_en: a person employed to collect money or payments
entries.example_cn: 大楼经理雇佣了一名收债人来追讨未付的租金。
entries.example_en: The building manager hired a collector to recover unpaid rent.

entries.definition_en: the electrode in a transistor where carriers leave the region
entries.example_cn: 集电极电流是晶体管电路设计中的一个关键参数。
entries.example_en: The collector current is a key parameter in transistor circuit design.

entries.definition_en: a major sewer that collects sewage from several smaller branch sewers
entries.example_cn: 总下水道收集几条较小下水道的污水。
entries.example_en: The collector carries sewage from several smaller sewers.

entries.definition_en: an Irish girl
entries.example_cn: 那位爱尔兰姑娘对陌生人露出了温暖的笑容。
entries.example_en: The colleen smiled warmly at the stranger.

entries.definition_cn: 授予学位的高等教育机构；有时是大学的一部分
entries.definition_en: an institution of higher education that grants degrees; sometimes part of a university
entries.example_cn: 她决定上大学学习工程学。
entries.example_en: She decided to attend college to study engineering.

entries.definition_cn: 高等教育机构所在的建筑群
entries.definition_en: a group of buildings where a higher education institution is located
entries.example_cn: 新图书馆是该学院建筑群的一部分。
entries.example_en: The new library is part of the college complex.

entries.definition_en: the body of faculty and students of a college
entries.example_cn: 学院的师生欢迎这项新政策。
entries.example_en: The college's faculty and students welcomed the new policy.

entries.definition_en: of, relating to, or involving colleagues; characterized by shared authority among colleagues
entries.example_cn: 该决定是通过涉及所有部门主管的同事共权程序做出的。
entries.example_en: The decision was made through a collegial process involving all department heads.

entries.definition_cn: 学院的；大学生的；大学式的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to a college or its students; collegiate
entries.example_cn: 这所大学的学院式传统体现了各学院和学生的习俗。
entries.example_en: The university's collegial traditions reflected the customs of its colleges and students.

entries.definition_en: a current or former student at a college or university
entries.example_cn: 作为一名大学生，他大部分晚上都在图书馆度过。
entries.example_en: As a collegian, he spent most of his evenings in the library.

entries.definition_cn: 大学的；学院的；大学生的
entries.definition_en: relating to a college or typical of college students
entries.example_cn: 这所大学有着浓厚的学院精神。
entries.example_en: The university has a strong collegiate spirit.

entries.definition_en: showing cooperation and shared responsibility among colleagues
entries.example_cn: 团队采取了协作的方式来解决这个问题。
entries.example_en: The team adopted a collegiate approach to solving the problem.

entries.definition_cn: 夹头；用于夹持工具或圆柱形工件的套筒
entries.definition_en: a sleeve or chuck used to grip and hold a tool or cylindrical workpiece
entries.example_cn: 车工拧紧夹头，以固定金属杆进行车削。
entries.example_en: The machinist tightened the collet to secure the metal rod for turning.

entries.definition_en: a band or collar that holds an individual stone in a jewelry setting
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商仔细调整镶石圈，以确保钻石被牢固地固定住。
entries.example_en: The jeweler carefully adjusted the collet to ensure the diamond was held firmly.

entries.definition_en: a metal cap or band placed on a wooden pole to prevent it from splitting
entries.example_cn: 木匠在木杆的一端钉上了一个木杆箍。
entries.example_en: The carpenter hammered a collet onto the end of the wooden pole.

entries.definition_en: to crash together with violent impact
entries.example_cn: 两艘船在风暴中猛烈相撞。
entries.example_en: The two ships collided in the storm.

entries.definition_en: to be incompatible or to come into conflict
entries.example_cn: 这两个政党在税收问题上发生了冲突。
entries.example_en: The two political parties collided over the issue of taxation.

entries.definition_en: to cause to collide
entries.example_cn: 粒子加速器使两束粒子迎头相撞。
entries.example_en: The particle accelerator collided two beams of particles head-on.

entries.definition_en: a machine that accelerates two beams of particles to collide head-on
entries.example_cn: 科学家利用对撞机来研究宇宙的基本粒子。
entries.example_en: Scientists use a collider to study the fundamental particles of the universe.

entries.definition_cn: 用于碰撞检测的物体形状模型
entries.definition_en: a model of an object's shape used for collision detection
entries.example_cn: 这款游戏在角色周围使用一个简单的碰撞体来检测是否碰到墙壁。
entries.example_en: The game uses a simple collider around the character to detect contact with walls.

entries.definition_cn: 因果图中至少有两条入边的节点
entries.definition_en: a node in a causal graph with at least two incoming edges
entries.example_cn: 在因果图中，该疾病是一个碰撞节点，因为有两个相互独立的原因指向它。
entries.example_en: In the causal graph, the disease is a collider because two independent causes point to it.

entries.definition_en: a breed of sheepdog with a long silky coat
entries.example_cn: 这只苏格兰牧羊犬把羊群赶过了山坡。
entries.example_en: The collie herded the sheep across the hill.

entries.definition_en: a person who works in a coal mine
entries.example_cn: 这位矿工在地下工作了二十年。
entries.example_en: The collier worked deep underground for twenty years.

entries.definition_en: A vessel that carries a bulk cargo of coal.
entries.example_cn: 这艘运煤船把数千吨煤运到了港口。
entries.example_en: The collier carried thousands of tons of coal to the port.

entries.definition_cn: 煤矿及其相关建筑和设备的总称
entries.definition_en: a workplace consisting of a coal mine plus all the buildings and equipment connected with it
entries.example_cn: 该煤矿的工人们在那里工作了五十多年。
entries.example_en: The workers at the colliery had been employed there for over fifty years.

entries.definition_cn: 调整光学仪器的准直线
entries.definition_en: to adjust the line of sight of an optical instrument
entries.example_cn: 观测前，技术员调整了望远镜的准直线。
entries.example_en: Before observing, the technician collimated the telescope.

entries.definition_en: to make rays or lines parallel to each other
entries.example_cn: 这台望远镜被设计用来使来自遥远恒星的光线平行。
entries.example_en: The telescope was designed to collimate light from distant stars.

entries.definition_en: the process of aligning the optical axis of a telescope or instrument
entries.example_cn: 天文学家在观测前花了几个小时对新望远镜进行准直。
entries.example_en: The astronomer spent hours performing collimation on the new telescope before the observation.

entries.definition_en: an optical device with a lens and a slit that produces a parallel beam of light
entries.example_cn: 该实验需要一个准直器来为探测器产生平行光束。
entries.example_en: The experiment required a collimator to create a parallel beam of light for the detector.

entries.definition_en: a small telescope attached to a large telescope to help align it
entries.example_cn: 天文学家调整准直望远镜，以确保主望远镜完全对准。
entries.example_en: The astronomer adjusted the collimator to ensure the main telescope was perfectly aligned.

entries.definition_en: lying on the same straight line
entries.example_cn: 这三个点共线，形成一条单一的线段。
entries.example_en: The three points are collinear and form a single line segment.

entries.definition_cn: 一种通常加杜松子酒、柠檬汁、糖和苏打水的酒精饮料
entries.definition_en: an alcoholic drink made with lemon juice, sugar, and carbonated water, usually with gin
entries.example_cn: 徒步回来后，我们要了一杯柯林斯鸡尾酒来降温。
entries.example_en: We ordered a collins to cool down after the hike.

entries.definition_cn: 物体相撞的事件，常造成损坏
entries.definition_en: an instance in which two or more objects collide, often causing damage
entries.example_cn: 司机通过急刹车避免了交通事故。
entries.example_en: The driver avoided a collision by braking suddenly.

entries.definition_en: a situation where different ideas or goals conflict with each other
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司之间存在利益冲突。
entries.example_en: There was a collision of interests between the two companies.

entries.definition_en: a brief event where two or more objects come together and hit each other
entries.example_cn: 两颗卫星之间的碰撞被天文学家探测到了。
entries.example_en: The collision between the two satellites was detected by astronomers.

entries.definition_en: to have a strong tendency to occur side by side
entries.example_cn: 在英语中，单词“strong”和“coffee”经常搭配出现。
entries.example_en: The words 'strong' and 'coffee' often collocate in English.

entries.definition_en: to group or chunk together in a certain order or place side by side
entries.example_cn: 图书管理员将按主题把这些书排列在一起。
entries.example_en: The librarian will collocate the books by subject.

entries.definition_en: a grouping of words in a sentence
entries.example_cn: 短语“做出决定”是一个常见的词语搭配。
entries.example_en: The phrase 'make a decision' is a common collocation.

entries.definition_en: the act of positioning close together (or side by side)
entries.example_cn: 两座雕塑的并列摆放形成了协调的展示效果。
entries.example_en: The collocation of the two sculptures created a balanced display.

entries.definition_en: a syrupy solution used to coat wounds or photographic films
entries.example_cn: 医生在病人的伤口上涂了一层薄薄的火棉胶以保护它。
entries.example_en: The doctor applied a thin layer of collodion to the patient's wound to protect it.

entries.definition_en: a mixture with properties between those of a solution and fine suspension
entries.example_cn: 牛奶是胶体的一个常见例子。
entries.example_en: Milk is a common example of a colloid.

entries.definition_en: having the properties of a colloid, a mixture where tiny particles are suspended in a fluid
entries.example_cn: 科学家研究了这种新油漆混合物的胶体特性。
entries.example_en: The scientist studied the colloidal properties of the new paint mixture.

entries.definition_en: used in informal spoken language or conversation
entries.example_cn: 这部电影使用了非常自然的口语。
entries.example_en: The movie features colloquial language that sounds very natural.

entries.definition_en: a word or phrase characteristic of informal spoken language
entries.example_cn: 他使用的俚语是典型的口语表达。
entries.example_en: His use of slang was a typical colloquialism.

entries.definition_en: with the use of colloquial expressions
entries.example_cn: 他的朋友们在口语中称他为“老板”。
entries.example_en: He was colloquially referred to as 'the boss' by his friends.

entries.definition_en: an academic meeting or seminar where different topics are discussed by different lecturers
entries.example_cn: 上周大学举办了一场关于现代物理的学术研讨会。
entries.example_en: The university hosted a colloquium on modern physics last week.

entries.definition_en: a speech or address given at an academic meeting or seminar
entries.example_cn: 她为国际会议准备了一场详细的学术演讲。
entries.example_en: She prepared a detailed colloquium for the international conference.

entries.definition_en: a conversation or dialogue
entries.example_cn: 两位领导人举行了一次私下会谈以讨论条约。
entries.example_en: The two leaders held a private colloquy to discuss the treaty.

entries.definition_cn: 审判期间为确保被告理解诉讼程序及其权利而进行的讨论
entries.definition_en: a discussion during a trial to ensure that the defendant understands the proceedings and their rights
entries.example_cn: 在庭审讨论中，法官询问被告是否理解指控内容及其权利。
entries.example_en: During the colloquy, the judge asked the defendant whether he understood the charges and his rights.

entries.definition_cn: 正式会议或讨论（已废弃）
entries.definition_en: a formal conference or discussion (obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 这次外交会谈让两个代表团聚在一起举行正式会议。
entries.example_en: The diplomatic colloquy brought the two delegations together for a formal conference.

entries.definition_en: a photomechanical printing process using a glass plate with a gelatin surface to reproduce images
entries.example_cn: 这本珍本书是使用珂罗版印刷法印制的。
entries.example_en: The rare book was printed using the collotype process.

entries.definition_cn: 通过珂罗版印刷法制成的图像
entries.definition_en: An image produced by the collotype printing process.
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展出了一幅细节精美的历史建筑珂罗版印刷图像。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a finely detailed collotype of the historic building.

entries.definition_en: to secretly cooperate with someone for an illegal or dishonest purpose
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司串通起来操纵产品价格。
entries.example_en: The two companies colluded to fix the prices of the products.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: Source w30108r0 explicitly labels collude intransitive.

entries.definition_en: secret agreement
entries.example_cn: 调查揭露了两家公司之间的密谋。
entries.example_en: The investigation revealed collusion between the two companies.

entries.definition_en: agreement on a secret plot
entries.example_cn: 他们因共谋欺诈政府而被起诉。
entries.example_en: They were charged with collusion to defraud the government.

entries.definition_en: acting together in secret to achieve a fraudulent or illegal purpose
entries.example_cn: 调查显示，这两家公司串通操纵价格。
entries.example_en: The investigation revealed that the two companies were collusive in fixing prices.

entries.definition_cn: 【古】用煤或煤烟等把……染黑；弄脏
entries.definition_en: archaic: to make black, as with coal or soot
entries.example_cn: 煤烟把烟囱砖熏黑了。
entries.example_en: The soot collied the chimney bricks.

usage.label: archaic; transitive
usage.pattern: to make black, as with coal

entries.definition_cn: 胃痛或肠胃不适；焦虑、恐惧或不安
entries.definition_en: a stomachache or upset stomach; anxiety, fear, or uneasiness
entries.example_cn: 吃了奇怪的食物后，他开始感到肠胃不适。
entries.example_en: After eating the strange food, he started to get the collywobbles.

entries.definition_cn: 疣猴（包括疣猴属、红疣猴属和黑疣猴属等非洲猴类）
entries.definition_en: an African monkey of the genera Colobus, Piliocolobus, or Procolobus
entries.example_cn: 疣猴大部分时间都在树间活动。
entries.example_en: The colobus monkey spends most of its time moving through the trees.

entries.definition_en: a perfumed liquid made of essential oils and alcohol
entries.example_cn: 他出门前喷了点古龙水。
entries.example_en: He sprayed some cologne before going out.

entries.definition_en: the part of the large intestine between the cecum and the rectum
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了患者的大肠。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the patient's colon.

entries.definition_en: a punctuation mark used after a word introducing a series or explanation
entries.example_cn: 她写道：“冒号在这里使用。”
entries.example_en: She wrote: 'The colon is used here.'

entries.definition_en: the former basic monetary unit of El Salvador, equal to 100 centavos
entries.example_cn: 在采用美元之前，这件商品的价格是五萨尔瓦多科朗。
entries.example_en: Before the US dollar was adopted, the price was five Salvadoran colones.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Costa Rica, equal to 100 centimos
entries.example_cn: 他用哥斯达黎加科朗付了咖啡钱。
entries.example_en: He paid for the coffee with Costa Rican colones.

entries.definition_en: a high-ranking officer in the US Army, Air Force, or Marines, ranking above a lieutenant colonel and below a brigadier general
entries.example_cn: 上校在阅兵前检阅了部队。
entries.example_en: The colonel inspected the troops before the parade.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of a colony
entries.example_cn: 那种殖民风格的建筑在该地区非常流行。
entries.example_en: The colonial style of architecture is very popular in that region.

entries.definition_en: living in a colony, such as ants
entries.example_cn: 蜜蜂是群居动物，它们共同生活在蜂巢里。
entries.example_en: Bees are colonial animals that live together in a hive.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指生物或细胞）由许多个体联合组成群体的
entries.definition_en: composed of many distinct individuals united to form a colony, especially of organisms or cells
entries.example_cn: 群体生物由许多个体共同生活组成。
entries.example_en: A colonial organism is made up of many individual organisms living together.

entries.definition_cn: 殖民地居民；殖民地出身的人
entries.definition_en: a person from a country or territory that is or was controlled by another
entries.example_cn: 博物馆保存着殖民地居民在外国统治下写的信件。
entries.example_en: The museum preserves letters written by colonials living under foreign rule.

entries.definition_cn: 殖民主义（通过控制其他民族或领土来扩张或维持统治，常为经济或政治支配）
entries.definition_en: a policy or practice by which a country extends or maintains control over other peoples or territories, often for economic or political dominance
entries.example_cn: 许多历史学家认为，殖民主义给被殖民国家造成了长期的经济损害。
entries.example_en: Many historians argue that colonialism caused long-term economic damage to the colonized nations.

entries.definition_en: a person who believes in or supports the policy of colonialism
entries.example_cn: 这位殖民主义者认为帝国负有教化殖民地的责任。
entries.example_en: The colonialist argued that the empire had a duty to civilize the colonies.

entries.definition_en: relating to the large intestine
entries.example_cn: 医生开具了结肠检查，以排查息肉。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a colonic examination to check for polyps.

entries.definition_en: a treatment to clean the large intestine with water
entries.example_cn: 她决定做一次结肠灌洗，为体检做准备。
entries.example_en: She decided to try a colonic to prepare for her health checkup.

entries.definition_en: the process of establishing colonies in a new territory
entries.example_cn: 这本书详细介绍了太平洋岛屿的殖民历史。
entries.example_en: The book details the history of colonisation in the Pacific islands.

entries.definition_en: to settle in a new area and establish a community there
entries.example_cn: 拓荒者在该山谷定居并建立了农场和学校。
entries.example_en: The pioneers colonised the valley, building farms and schools.

usage.label: British spelling
usage.pattern: colonise is the British spelling of colonize.

entries.definition_en: to establish a colony in a foreign country, typically by settling there
entries.example_cn: 欧洲列强于十九世纪开始殖民非洲。
entries.example_en: European powers began to colonise Africa in the nineteenth century.

entries.definition_en: a person who establishes or settles a colony
entries.example_cn: 这本书详细讲述了一位英国殖民者在非洲的生活。
entries.example_en: The book details the life of a British coloniser in Africa.

entries.definition_en: a member of a colony, especially a person who settles in a new colony
entries.example_cn: 第一位殖民者抵达新领土以建立农场。
entries.example_en: The first colonist arrived in the new territory to establish a farm.

entries.definition_en: the act of colonizing; the establishment of colonies
entries.example_cn: 这本书详细讲述了欧洲在非洲的殖民历史。
entries.example_en: The book details the history of European colonization in Africa.

entries.definition_en: to settle in a new place and establish a colony there
entries.example_cn: 他们决定定居在偏远的山谷以逃离城市。
entries.example_en: They decided to colonize the remote valley to escape the city.

entries.definition_en: to establish a colony in a new area, especially by a country in the past
entries.example_cn: 大英帝国在18世纪殖民了许多加勒比岛屿。
entries.example_en: The British colonized many islands in the Caribbean during the 18th century.

entries.definition_en: a person who establishes or helps establish a colony
entries.example_cn: 第一批殖民者带着一个小团体到达了新领土。
entries.example_en: The first colonizer arrived in the new territory with a small group.

entries.definition_cn: 在新地区建立种群的物种
entries.definition_en: a species that establishes a population in a new area
entries.example_cn: 这种先驱物种迅速扩散到新形成的池塘中。
entries.example_en: The colonizer quickly spread through the newly formed pond.

entries.definition_en: a structure consisting of a row of evenly spaced columns
entries.example_cn: 博物馆入口处矗立着一座宏伟的柱廊。
entries.example_en: The museum entrance is marked by a grand colonnade.

entries.definition_cn: 环绕开放空间（尤指庭院）的柱廊；列柱中庭
entries.definition_en: a colonnade surrounding an open space, especially a courtyard; a peristyle
entries.example_cn: 他们穿过拱廊来到了花园。
entries.example_en: They walked through the colonnade to reach the garden.

entries.definition_en: having a series of columns arranged at regular intervals
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的寺庙是一座宏伟的有柱廊建筑。
entries.example_en: The ancient temple was a magnificent colonnaded structure.

entries.definition_en: visual examination of the colon with a colonoscope, from the cecum to the rectum
entries.example_cn: 医生建议做结肠镜检查以排查息肉。
entries.example_en: The doctor recommended a colonoscopy to check for polyps.

entries.definition_en: a group of people who live in a foreign country but keep ties with their home country
entries.example_cn: 该侨民社区拥有自己的学校和报纸。
entries.example_en: The colony maintained its own schools and newspapers.

entries.definition_en: a group of the same kind of organism living together
entries.example_cn: 科学家观察到培养皿上有一个细菌菌落正在生长。
entries.example_en: The scientist observed a bacterial colony growing on the petri dish.

entries.definition_en: a place where people with similar interests gather
entries.example_cn: 该市老城区有一个庞大的艺术家聚居地。
entries.example_en: The city has a large artist colony in the old district.

entries.definition_en: a territory controlled by a distant country
entries.example_cn: 许多国家曾经是欧洲列强的殖民地。
entries.example_en: Many countries were once colonies of European powers.

entries.definition_en: a group of microorganisms grown from a single cell
entries.example_cn: 实验室技术员计数菌落以确定细菌数量。
entries.example_en: The lab technician counted the colonies to determine the bacteria count.

entries.definition_cn: 成为美国最初各州的十三个英国殖民地之一
entries.definition_en: one of the thirteen British colonies that became the original states of the United States
entries.example_cn: 弗吉尼亚是后来成为美国最初各州的十三个英国殖民地之一。
entries.example_en: Virginia was one of the thirteen British colonies that became the original states.

entries.definition_cn: 书籍中的题记或出版者标志
entries.definition_en: a printer's or publisher's identifying inscription or logo in or on a book
entries.example_cn: 这本珍本书的最后一页上有一个精美的版记。
entries.example_en: The rare book contained a beautiful colophon on its final page.

entries.definition_en: the visual quality of an object caused by the light it reflects, emits, or transmits.
entries.example_cn: 日落将天空染成了美丽的色彩。
entries.example_en: The sunset painted the sky in beautiful colors.

entries.definition_en: interest, variety, and intensity.
entries.example_cn: 这场聚会缺乏情趣和活力。
entries.example_en: The party lacked color and excitement.

entries.definition_en: to add color to something.
entries.example_cn: 她用画笔给图画着色。
entries.example_en: She used a brush to color the picture.

entries.definition_en: to affect someone's thoughts or feelings.
entries.example_cn: 他的话影响了我对这件事的看法。
entries.example_en: His words colored my opinion of the event.

entries.definition_en: to modify or bias something.
entries.example_cn: 新闻报道歪曲了事实以迎合故事。
entries.example_en: The news report colored the facts to suit the story.

entries.definition_en: having or capable of producing colors.
entries.example_cn: 彩色玻璃窗透进柔和的光线。
entries.example_en: The colored glass window let in soft light.

entries.definition_en: the quality of a musical sound that distinguishes it from other sounds of the same pitch and loudness.
entries.example_cn: 小提琴的音色温暖。
entries.example_en: The violin has a warm color.

entries.definition_cn: （正式，尤用于法律语境）假象；幌子
entries.definition_en: a deliberately misleading outward appearance or pretense (formal, especially legal)
entries.example_cn: 他们打着权力的幌子行事，实际上并没有这种权力。
entries.example_en: They acted under color of authority, although they had no such power.

entries.definition_cn: 不带种族偏见的；不因种族而歧视的
entries.definition_en: not showing prejudice or discrimination based on race
entries.example_cn: 该校力求在招聘中不带种族偏见。
entries.example_en: The school aims to make its hiring practices color-blind.

entries.definition_en: unable to distinguish one or more chromatic colors
entries.example_cn: 他是色盲，经常分不清红色和绿色。
entries.example_en: He is color-blind and often confuses red and green.

entries.definition_en: the appearance of something in terms of its color
entries.example_cn: 蝴蝶翅膀的颜色外观随季节而变化。
entries.example_en: The coloration of the butterfly's wings changes with the seasons.

entries.definition_en: the selection and use of colors by an artist
entries.example_cn: 艺术家独特的用色赋予了画作一种独特的氛围。
entries.example_en: The artist's unique coloration gives the painting a distinct mood.

entries.definition_en: the quality of a musical sound that distinguishes it from others of the same pitch and loudness
entries.example_cn: 小提琴的音色温暖，与大提琴融合得很好。
entries.example_en: The violin has a warm coloration that blends well with the cello.

entries.definition_en: singing with florid ornamentation
entries.example_cn: 这首咏叹调以其困难的花腔段落而闻名。
entries.example_en: The aria is famous for its difficult coloratura passages.

entries.definition_cn: 花腔歌手，尤指花腔女高音
entries.definition_en: a singer, especially a soprano, who specializes in coloratura
entries.example_cn: 这部歌剧的主角是一位才华横溢的花腔女高音，她能毫不费力地唱出高音。
entries.example_en: The opera featured a brilliant coloratura who could hit high notes effortlessly.

entries.definition_en: relating to the colon and the rectum
entries.example_cn: 医生正在为五十岁以上的人群筛查结肠直肠癌。
entries.example_en: Doctors are screening for colorectal cancer in people over fifty.

entries.definition_cn: 有颜色的；有时用于组合词中
entries.definition_en: having color or a certain color; sometimes used in combination
entries.example_cn: 彩色的灯光照亮了舞池。
entries.example_en: The colored lights illuminated the dance floor.

entries.definition_cn: （过时且冒犯）非白人肤色的，尤指黑人的
entries.definition_en: of a skin color other than white, especially Black; dated and offensive
entries.example_cn: 在美国，历史上曾使用“colored”一词来形容皮肤黝黑的人。
entries.example_en: In the United States, the term 'colored' was historically used to describe people with dark skin.

entries.definition_en: favoring one person or side over another
entries.example_cn: 法官对案件的陈述带有偏见，偏袒富有的被告。
entries.example_en: The judge gave a colored account of the case that favored the wealthy defendant.

entries.definition_cn: （指颜色）人工产生的；非天然的
entries.definition_en: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.example_cn: 窗户里的彩色玻璃是用人工染料制成的。
entries.example_en: The colored glass in the window was made from artificial dyes.

entries.definition_cn: （过时且冒犯）非白人，尤指黑人
entries.definition_en: a nonwhite person, especially a Black person; dated and offensive
entries.example_cn: 在现代社会语境中，'colored' 一词被视为冒犯性用语。
entries.example_en: The term 'colored' is considered offensive in modern contexts.

entries.definition_en: having color that does not fade or run when washed or exposed to light
entries.example_cn: 这种面料色牢，洗涤时不用担心染料会褪色或渗色。
entries.example_en: This fabric is colorfast, so you can wash it without worrying about the dye bleeding.

entries.definition_en: having a lot of different colors
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了色彩斑斓的花朵。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with colorful flowers.

entries.definition_en: interesting and varied
entries.example_cn: 节日提供了丰富多彩的文化表演。
entries.example_en: The festival offered a colorful array of cultural performances.

entries.definition_en: having a specific color
entries.example_cn: 彩旗在风中飘扬。
entries.example_en: The colorful flag waved in the wind.

entries.definition_en: an instrument used to measure the quantity of a substance based on the color it produces with specific reagents
entries.example_cn: 科学家使用比色计分析了水样。
entries.example_en: The scientist used a colorimeter to analyze the water sample.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to colorimetry
entries.example_cn: 该实验室使用比色法来分析水质。
entries.example_en: The laboratory uses colorimetric methods to analyze water quality.

entries.definition_en: the measurement and quantitative analysis of color
entries.example_cn: 实验室利用比色法测定了溶液的浓度。
entries.example_en: The laboratory used colorimetry to determine the concentration of the solution.

entries.definition_cn: 物体因发射、透射或反射光线而产生的视觉属性
entries.definition_en: a visual attribute of things that results from the light they emit or transmit or reflect
entries.example_cn: 日落的色彩令人叹为观止。
entries.example_en: The coloring of the sunset was breathtaking.

entries.definition_cn: 改变某物颜色的行为或过程
entries.definition_en: the act or process of changing the color of something
entries.example_cn: 她正在尝试不同的染发技巧。
entries.example_en: She is experimenting with different coloring techniques for her hair.

entries.definition_cn: 用于着色的物质，尤其是食用色素
entries.definition_en: a substance used to give color, especially to food
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕鲜艳的红色来自天然果汁。
entries.example_en: The cake's bright red coloring is made from natural fruit juice.

entries.definition_cn: 专门给头发染色和调色的美发师
entries.definition_en: a hairdresser who specializes in coloring and tinting hair
entries.example_cn: 她去找染发师补染发根，并选择一种新发色。
entries.example_en: She visited her colorist to touch up her roots and choose a new shade.

entries.definition_en: an artist skilled at using color to create special effects
entries.example_cn: 电影海报由一位才华横溢的色彩大师设计。
entries.example_en: The movie poster was designed by a talented colorist.

entries.definition_en: to add color to something
entries.example_cn: 该软件允许您为旧的黑白照片上色。
entries.example_en: The software allows you to colorize old black-and-white photographs.

usage.label: US spelling
usage.pattern: Source w44649r0 and w44649r1 explicitly mark the verb US.

entries.definition_en: having very little or no color
entries.example_cn: 那种无色的液体被倒入试管中。
entries.example_en: The colorless liquid was poured into the test tube.

entries.definition_en: lacking variety, excitement, or interest
entries.example_cn: 这部电影是一次平淡无奇且无聊的经历。
entries.example_en: The movie was a colorless and boring experience.

entries.definition_en: so great in size or force or extent as to elicit awe
entries.example_cn: 那座巨大的雕像矗立在广场中央。
entries.example_en: The colossal statue stood in the center of the square.

entries.definition_cn: （比喻）受人敬仰的重要人物或事物；巨头
entries.definition_en: figuratively, a person or thing greatly admired and respected
entries.example_cn: 他是科技界的巨头。
entries.example_en: He is a colossus in the world of technology.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that is extremely large and powerful
entries.example_cn: 这座新摩天大楼是城市天际线中的巨人。
entries.example_en: The new skyscraper is a colossus in the city's skyline.

entries.definition_en: a surgical operation that creates an opening from the colon to the surface of the body to function as an anus
entries.example_cn: 手术后，病人接受了结肠造口术。
entries.example_en: The patient underwent a colostomy after the surgery.

entries.definition_cn: 结肠造口术中将结肠引至腹壁表面形成的开口
entries.definition_en: the opening in the abdominal wall created when the colon is brought to the surface in a colostomy
entries.example_cn: 护士清洁了结肠造口术中在腹壁形成的开口。
entries.example_en: The nurse cleaned the opening in the abdominal wall created during the colostomy.

entries.definition_en: milky fluid secreted for the first day or two after giving birth
entries.example_cn: 鼓励新妈妈在分娩后立即给婴儿喂初乳。
entries.example_en: New mothers are encouraged to feed their babies colostrum immediately after birth.

entries.definition_en: a material used for its color
entries.example_cn: 她买了一管蓝色颜料。
entries.example_en: She bought a tube of blue colour.

entries.definition_en: interest and variety and intensity
entries.example_cn: 这个节日为小镇增添了趣味和活力。
entries.example_en: The festival brought colour and excitement to the town.

entries.definition_en: the timbre of a musical sound
entries.example_cn: 小提琴的音色温暖。
entries.example_en: The violin has a warm colour.

entries.definition_en: having or capable of producing colors
entries.example_cn: 日落时彩色的天空很美。
entries.example_en: The coloured sky at sunset was beautiful.

entries.definition_en: to decorate with colors
entries.example_cn: 他们为复活节庆祝活动给鸡蛋着色。
entries.example_en: They coloured the eggs for the Easter celebration.

entries.definition_en: to modify or bias
entries.example_cn: 这份报告因他个人的偏见而有所歪曲。
entries.example_en: The report was coloured by his personal prejudices.

entries.definition_en: the characteristic of quarks that determines their role in the strong interaction
entries.example_cn: 物理学家研究夸克的色荷以理解粒子相互作用。
entries.example_en: Physicists study the colour of quarks to understand particle interactions.

entries.definition_en: to give a deceptive explanation or excuse for
entries.example_cn: 他借口生病来掩饰自己的缺席。
entries.example_en: He coloured his absence by claiming he was ill.

entries.definition_en: unable to distinguish between certain colors
entries.example_cn: 他是色盲，分不清红色和绿色。
entries.example_en: He is colour-blind and cannot tell red from green.

entries.definition_cn: 不因种族而有偏见的；不歧视种族的
entries.definition_en: not prejudiced or discriminatory on racial grounds
entries.example_cn: 该校旨在在招生过程中做到不歧视种族。
entries.example_en: The school aims to be colour-blind in its admissions process.

entries.definition_en: the way something looks in terms of its color
entries.example_cn: 日落的色泽令人叹为观止。
entries.example_en: The colouration of the sunset was breathtaking.

entries.definition_en: the selection and use of colors by an artist
entries.example_cn: 这幅画的用色非常大胆。
entries.example_en: The artist's colouration in this painting is very bold.

entries.definition_en: the quality of sound that distinguishes different voices or instruments
entries.example_cn: 小提琴家独特的音色使她的表演脱颖而出。
entries.example_en: The violinist's unique colouration made her performance stand out.

entries.definition_cn: 有颜色的；有时用于复合词中
entries.definition_en: having color or a certain color; sometimes used in combination
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了五颜六色的花朵。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with coloured flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 受到影响的；有偏见的，尤指偏袒某一方或某人
entries.definition_en: influenced or biased, especially in favor of one side or person
entries.example_cn: 这份报告受作者政治观点的影响。
entries.example_en: The report was coloured by the author's political views.

entries.definition_cn: （指颜色）人工产生的；非天然的
entries.definition_en: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.example_cn: 彩虹是用彩色灯光制造出来的。
entries.example_en: The rainbow was created using coloured lights.

entries.definition_cn: 有色人种的；指人时可能过时或冒犯
entries.definition_en: having a skin colour other than white; dated or potentially offensive when referring to people
entries.example_cn: 许多有色人种因黑色素含量高而拥有深色皮肤。
entries.example_en: Many coloured people have dark skin due to high melanin levels.

entries.definition_en: a United States term for Blacks that is now considered offensive
entries.example_cn: 在现代社会语境中，'coloured' 一词被视为冒犯性用语。
entries.example_en: The term 'coloured' is considered offensive in modern contexts.

entries.definition_en: striking in variety and interest
entries.example_cn: 这场节日是当地传统的一场丰富多彩的庆祝活动。
entries.example_en: The festival was a colourful celebration of local traditions.

entries.definition_en: having much or varied color
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了色彩斑斓的花朵。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with colourful flowers in full bloom.

entries.definition_en: having color or a certain color; sometimes used in combination
entries.example_cn: 她戴了一条彩色的围巾来搭配她的衣服。
entries.example_en: She wore a colourful scarf to match her outfit.

entries.definition_en: the act or process of changing the color of something
entries.example_cn: 给旧墙壁着色花了几天时间才完成。
entries.example_en: The colouring of the old walls took several days to complete.

entries.definition_en: the visual attribute of things resulting from light they emit, transmit, or reflect
entries.example_cn: 艺术家对日落微妙的色泽着迷。
entries.example_en: The artist was fascinated by the subtle colouring of the sunset.

entries.definition_en: a substance added to food to give it color
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕使用了人工色素使其看起来色彩鲜艳。
entries.example_en: The cake was made with artificial colouring to make it look bright.

entries.definition_en: having little or no color; not colorful
entries.example_cn: 大雾期间，天空呈现出灰蒙蒙的颜色。
entries.example_en: The sky was a colourless grey during the heavy fog.

entries.definition_en: lacking in variety and interest; dull
entries.example_cn: 那次讲座是对日常行政工作的平淡无奇的描述。
entries.example_en: The lecture was a colourless account of routine administrative tasks.

entries.definition_en: a piece of cloth with a design representing a country
entries.example_cn: 仪式在升起国旗时开始。
entries.example_en: The ceremony began with the raising of the colours.

entries.definition_en: a symbol used to represent a group, country, or organization
entries.example_cn: 球队在决赛中穿上了国家队的队服。
entries.example_en: The team wore their national colours in the final match.

entries.definition_en: a metallic ore from which niobium and tantalum are extracted
entries.example_cn: 钶钽铁矿的开采给该地区造成了严重的环境破坏。
entries.example_en: The mining of coltan has caused significant environmental damage in the region.

entries.definition_en: a sharp steel wedge placed in front of a plow to cut through the soil vertically
entries.example_cn: 农民调整犁刀以确保它能切透土壤。
entries.example_en: The farmer adjusted the colter to ensure it cut the soil deeply enough.

entries.definition_cn: 活泼顽皮且不守规矩的
entries.definition_en: playful, lively, and undisciplined
entries.example_cn: 这些小男孩顽皮的行为让老师笑了起来。
entries.example_en: The coltish behavior of the young boys made the teacher laugh.

entries.definition_cn: 款冬：一种多年生草本植物，叶片大而圆，形似马蹄，黄花先于叶片开放，原产欧洲，曾用作药材。
entries.definition_en: a perennial herb with large rounded leaves resembling a colt's foot and yellow flowers that appear before the leaves; native to Europe and used medicinally.
entries.example_cn: 她在早春黄花先于叶片开放时采集了款冬。
entries.example_en: She collected the coltsfoot early in spring when the yellow flowers bloomed before the leaves.

entries.definition_cn: 一种常绿多年生草本植物，花序为小白花，叶片有光泽，秋季变铜色或紫色。
entries.definition_en: a tufted evergreen perennial herb with spikes of tiny white flowers and glossy green leaves that turn coppery or purple in autumn.
entries.example_cn: 花园里的千里光随着秋天的到来变成了美丽的紫红色。
entries.example_en: The coltsfoot in the garden has turned a beautiful maroon color with the fall weather.

entries.definition_cn: 游蛇科的一种蛇，通常无毒
entries.definition_en: a snake of the family Colubridae, usually nonvenomous
entries.example_cn: 这条游蛇在高草中悄悄爬行。
entries.example_en: The colubrid slithered quietly through the tall grass.

entries.definition_cn: 设有存放骨灰瓮壁龛的墓室或建筑
entries.definition_en: a vault or structure with recesses in the walls to receive urns for ashes
entries.example_cn: 访客们在整齐排列着骨灰瓮的骨灰堂里表达了敬意。
entries.example_en: Visitors paid their respects at the columbarium where the urns were neatly arranged.

entries.definition_en: a niche for holding an urn with the ashes of a cremated person
entries.example_cn: 教堂墙壁上的骨灰堂里存放着许多装有逝者骨灰的骨灰瓮。
entries.example_en: The columbarium in the church wall holds many urns containing the ashes of the deceased.

entries.definition_en: a house for keeping pigeons
entries.example_cn: 这座旧花园里有一个供当地鸽子居住的小鸽舍。
entries.example_en: The old garden contained a small columbarium for the local pigeons.

entries.definition_en: a plant with irregular, showy flowers that have spurs; found in temperate regions and mountains
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者发现岩石山坡上生长着一株罕见的耧斗菜。
entries.example_en: The hikers spotted a rare columbine growing on the rocky mountain slope.

entries.definition_en: a black mineral that serves as an ore of niobium and tantalum
entries.example_cn: 地质学家在偏远地区发现了一处铌钽铁矿矿藏。
entries.example_en: Geologists discovered a deposit of columbite in the remote region.

entries.definition_cn: 一种高大的多年生草本植物
entries.definition_en: a tall perennial herb found in the western United States
entries.example_cn: 这位植物学家从俄勒冈州的干燥山丘上采集了一种稀有的columbo。
entries.example_en: The botanist collected a rare columbo from the dry hills of Oregon.

entries.definition_en: a small column-like structure that is part of a plant or animal
entries.example_cn: 在青蛙体内，耳柱将振动从鼓膜传到内耳。
entries.example_en: In a frog, the columella transmits vibrations from the eardrum to the inner ear.

entries.definition_en: a vertical arrangement of numbers or information
entries.example_cn: 请检查表格最后一列的数字。
entries.example_en: Please check the figures in the last column of the table.

entries.definition_en: a line of things arranged one after another
entries.example_cn: 一列士兵沿着道路行进。
entries.example_en: A column of soldiers marched along the road.

entries.definition_en: a section of a page divided vertically
entries.example_cn: 报纸每页有四栏。
entries.example_en: The newspaper has four columns on each page.

entries.definition_en: a tall round structure used to support a building
entries.example_cn: 这座古庙有许多巨大的支撑柱支撑着屋顶。
entries.example_en: The ancient temple has many large columns supporting the roof.

entries.definition_en: an object that looks like a tall, round tower
entries.example_cn: 这座纪念碑呈石柱状。
entries.example_en: The monument was shaped like a stone column.

entries.definition_en: an article expressing opinions or views
entries.example_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的专栏文章。
entries.example_en: The newspaper published a column on climate change.

entries.definition_en: a tall, round structure standing alone
entries.example_cn: 广场中央矗立着一根高大的石柱。
entries.example_en: A tall column stood in the center of the square.

entries.definition_en: a vertical glass tube used in chemistry to separate mixtures
entries.example_cn: 科学家将混合物倒入色谱柱进行分析。
entries.example_en: The scientist poured the mixture into the column for analysis.

entries.definition_en: having the shape or form of a column
entries.example_cn: 由于树木高大笔直，森林呈现出柱状的外观。
entries.example_en: The forest has a columnar appearance due to the tall, straight trees.

entries.definition_cn: 有柱子的；由柱子构成的
entries.definition_en: characterized by or arranged in columns
entries.example_cn: 该建筑具有柱状设计，排列着一排排柱子。
entries.example_en: The building features a columnar design with rows of pillars.

entries.definition_en: having or resembling columns; having columns of a specified kind
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的庙宇由巨大的大理石柱子支撑。
entries.example_en: The ancient temple was columned with massive marble pillars.

entries.definition_en: a regular writer of a column in a newspaper or magazine
entries.example_cn: 该报的政治专栏作家对这项政策进行了尖锐的批评。
entries.example_en: The newspaper's political columnist wrote a sharp critique of the policy.

entries.definition_cn: 甘蓝型油菜（油菜），因其可榨油的种子而种植
entries.definition_en: oilseed rape (Brassica napus), cultivated for its seeds, which yield oil
entries.example_cn: 油菜在欧亚大陆许多地区被种植，以获取富含油脂的种子。
entries.example_en: Colza is cultivated in many parts of Eurasia for its oil-rich seeds.

entries.definition_en: a state of deep and often prolonged unconsciousness; usually the result of disease or injury
entries.example_cn: 事故后，病人陷入了昏迷。
entries.example_en: The patient fell into a coma after the accident.

entries.definition_en: (astronomy) the luminous cloud of particles surrounding the frozen nucleus of a comet
entries.example_cn: 彗星的彗发在天空中明亮地发光。
entries.example_en: The coma of the comet glowed brightly in the sky.

entries.definition_en: (botany) a usually terminal tuft of bracts or tuft of hairs
entries.example_cn: 菠萝的顶部有一簇苞片。
entries.example_en: The pineapple has a coma at its top.

entries.definition_cn: 用于烹制玉米饼或其他食物的扁平盘状陶制或金属煎盘
entries.definition_en: a flat, pan-like clay or metal griddle used to cook tortillas or other foods
entries.example_cn: 玉米饼在煎盘上烹制时散发出烘烤玉米的香味。
entries.example_en: The tortilla cooked on the comal developed a toasted corn aroma.

entries.definition_cn: 昏迷的；处于深度且通常持久的无意识状态
entries.definition_en: in a state of deep and usually prolonged unconsciousness; unable to respond to external stimuli
entries.example_cn: 这位昏迷的病人对任何声音或触摸都没有反应。
entries.example_en: The comatose patient did not respond to any sounds or touch.

entries.definition_en: relating to or associated with a coma
entries.example_cn: 事故后，病人处于昏迷状态。
entries.example_en: The neurologist discussed the patient's comatose condition with the family.

entries.definition_en: a flat device with narrow pointed teeth used to disentangle or arrange hair

entries.example_cn: 她知道家人安全，感到很安心。
entries.example_en: She felt comfortable knowing her family was safe.

entries.definition_en: having enough money to live well
entries.example_cn: 他们在经济上很富裕。
entries.example_en: They are comfortable financially.

entries.definition_en: sufficient to provide comfort
entries.example_cn: 这个房间对两个人来说很舒适。
entries.example_en: The room was comfortable for two people.

entries.definition_en: having a wide margin or allowance
entries.example_cn: 我们有充裕的时间来完成。
entries.example_en: We have a comfortable margin of time to finish.

entries.definition_en: a state of being relaxed and free from pain
entries.example_cn: 长途旅行后，她唯一想要的就是自己床铺的舒适感。
entries.example_en: After the long journey, the only thing she wanted was the comfortableness of her own bed.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: Source w53336r0 labels the noun “usually” uncountable.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of being at ease in a relationship
entries.example_cn: 他们的友谊以深厚的融洽感为特征，使他们可以自由地分享秘密。
entries.example_en: Their friendship was characterized by a deep comfortableness that allowed them to share secrets freely.

entries.definition_en: in a way that provides physical ease and relaxation
entries.example_cn: 沙发足够大，我们可以舒适地坐下。
entries.example_en: The sofa is large enough for us to sit comfortably.

entries.definition_en: in a state of mental ease and without stress
entries.example_cn: 得知家人安全，她感到十分安心。
entries.example_en: She felt comfortably secure knowing her family was safe.

entries.definition_en: in a state of having enough money to live without worry
entries.example_cn: 他们靠养老金过着富裕的生活。
entries.example_en: They live comfortably on their pension.

entries.definition_en: feeling less worried or sad because someone has given you support
entries.example_cn: 在听到坏消息后，她因朋友的安慰而感到宽慰。
entries.example_en: She felt comforted by her friend's kind words after the bad news.

entries.definition_en: bedding made of two layers of cloth filled with stuffing and stitched together
entries.example_cn: 她为冬天的床买了一条新被子。
entries.example_en: She bought a new comforter for her winter bed.

entries.definition_en: a person who reduces the intensity of fears and calms and pacifies
entries.example_cn: 老师充当了那位紧张学生的安抚者。
entries.example_en: The teacher acted as a comforter for the nervous student.

entries.definition_en: a person who commiserates with someone who has had misfortune
entries.example_cn: 慰问者与哀悼的家庭坐在一起好几个小时。
entries.example_en: The comforter sat with the grieving family for hours.

entries.definition_en: a device used for an infant to suck or bite on
entries.example_cn: 婴儿把安抚奶嘴掉在了地上。
entries.example_en: The baby dropped the comforter on the floor.

entries.definition_en: making you feel less worried or anxious
entries.example_cn: 在等待了这么久之后，听到这个消息让人安心。
entries.example_en: The news was comforting to hear after such a long wait.

entries.definition_en: giving you comfort or solace
entries.example_cn: 她温柔的话语让那个受惊的孩子感到非常慰藉。
entries.example_en: Her gentle words were very comforting to the frightened child.

entries.definition_cn: 以安慰或宽慰的方式；安慰地
entries.definition_en: in a way that provides emotional reassurance or consolation
entries.example_cn: 护士安慰地对受惊的孩子说话。
entries.example_en: The nurse spoke comfortingly to the frightened child.

entries.definition_en: lacking comfort or consolation
entries.example_cn: 他们在寒冷的船舱里度过了一个不舒适的夜晚。
entries.example_en: They spent a comfortless night in the cold cabin.

entries.definition_en: a perennial herb that grows rapidly and is suitable for shaded areas
entries.example_cn: 她在花园北侧种了筋骨草，那里阴凉，非常适合它生长。
entries.example_en: She planted comfrey in the north side of the garden where it could thrive in the shade.

entries.definition_en: a plant whose leaves are used to make herbal tea or eaten in salads
entries.example_cn: 年轻的筋骨草叶子常被采摘用来制作舒缓的草本茶。
entries.example_en: Young comfrey leaves are often harvested to make a soothing tisane.

entries.definition_en: providing or experiencing physical comfort and well-being
entries.example_cn: 这把舒适的扶手椅非常适合读书。
entries.example_en: The comfy armchair was perfect for reading a book.

entries.definition_en: arousing or provoking laughter
entries.example_cn: 电影中的滑稽场景让每个人都笑了起来。
entries.example_en: The comic scene in the movie made everyone laugh.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or characteristic of comedy
entries.example_cn: 他们正在大学学习喜剧文学。
entries.example_en: They are studying comic literature at the university.

entries.definition_en: a professional performer who tells jokes and performs comical acts
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员用他有趣的故事逗乐了观众。
entries.example_en: The comic entertained the crowd with his funny stories.

entries.definition_en: funny or amusing in a way that makes people laugh
entries.example_cn: 这位演员滑稽的表演引得观众哄堂大笑。
entries.example_en: The actor's comical performance made the audience roar with laughter.

entries.definition_en: in a funny way
entries.example_cn: 他滑稽地摔倒了，大家都笑了。
entries.example_en: He fell down comically and everyone laughed.

entries.definition_en: of the relatively near future
entries.example_cn: 即将举行的选举将决定这个国家的未来。
entries.example_en: The coming election will determine the country's future.

entries.definition_en: the arrival of something important that people have been waiting for
entries.example_cn: 新总统的就职在全国范围内受到了庆祝。
entries.example_en: The coming of the new president was celebrated all over the country.

entries.definition_en: the act or process of drawing spatially closer to something
entries.example_cn: 敌军向村庄的逼近引起了恐慌。
entries.example_en: The enemy's coming toward the village caused panic.

entries.definition_en: the state of becoming nearer in time
entries.example_cn: 随着冬天的临近，白天变得越来越短。
entries.example_en: With the coming of winter, the days get shorter.

entries.definition_cn: 性交过程中达到性高潮的时刻（非正式）
entries.definition_en: the moment of orgasm during sexual intercourse (informal)
entries.example_cn: 在这个非正式义项中，coming 指达到性高潮的时刻。
entries.example_en: In this informal sense, coming refers to the moment of orgasm.

entries.definition_en: a state or atmosphere of harmony and mutual respect
entries.example_cn: 外交官努力维持国家间的和睦。
entries.example_en: Diplomats strive to maintain comity between nations.

entries.definition_en: a punctuation mark used to separate elements within a sentence
entries.example_cn: 她在停顿片刻后加了一个逗号来分隔两个分句。
entries.example_en: She paused for a moment before adding a comma to separate the two clauses.

entries.definition_en: a type of butterfly with a comma-shaped mark on its wings
entries.example_cn: 这种罕见的逗号蝶常栖息在叶子的背面。
entries.example_en: The rare comma butterfly is often found resting on the underside of leaves.

entries.definition_en: an authoritative direction or instruction to do something
entries.example_cn: 将军下达了进攻的命令。
entries.example_en: The general gave the command to advance.

entries.definition_en: the power or authority to command
entries.example_cn: 他被赋予了全面指挥这次行动的权利。
entries.example_en: He was given full command of the operation.

entries.definition_cn: 对某物使用或操作的控制权；掌握
entries.definition_en: power or control over the use or operation of something
entries.example_cn: 她熟练掌握这款软件。
entries.example_en: She has excellent command of the software.

entries.definition_en: be in command of
entries.example_cn: 她在战斗中指挥军队。
entries.example_en: She commanded the troops during the battle.

entries.definition_en: make someone do something
entries.example_cn: 老师命令学生们保持安静。
entries.example_en: The teacher commanded the students to be quiet.

entries.definition_en: demand as one's due
entries.example_cn: 她赢得了房间里每个人的尊敬。
entries.example_en: She commanded respect from everyone in the room.

entries.definition_en: a military unit or region under the control of a single officer
entries.example_cn: 整个省份都是他的辖区。
entries.example_en: The entire province was his command.

entries.definition_en: to overlook or dominate from a position of height or strategic advantage
entries.example_cn: 这座城堡俯瞰着下面的山谷。
entries.example_en: The castle commands the valley below.

entries.definition_en: an officer who has command of a military unit
entries.example_cn: 指挥官在阅兵前检阅了部队。
entries.example_en: The commandant inspected the troops before the parade.

entries.definition_en: to take something arbitrarily or by force, especially for official use
entries.example_cn: 军队征用了几辆卡车来运输物资。
entries.example_en: The army commandeered several trucks to transport the supplies.

entries.definition_en: an officer in command of a military unit
entries.example_cn: 指挥官命令部队前进。
entries.example_en: The commander ordered the troops to advance.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有官方权威并能控制他人的职位人员
entries.definition_en: someone in an official position of authority who can control others
entries.example_cn: 作为项目负责人，她对预算拥有最终决定权。
entries.example_en: As the project commander, she has the final say on the budget.

entries.definition_cn: 军衔高于海军少校、低于海军上校的海军军官
entries.definition_en: a commissioned naval officer whose rank is above lieutenant commander and below captain
entries.example_cn: 他从海军少校晋升为海军中校。
entries.example_en: After serving as a lieutenant commander, he was promoted to commander.

entries.definition_en: an officer in the airforce
entries.example_cn: 指挥官驾驶战斗机飞向目标。
entries.example_en: The commander flew the fighter jet to the target.

entries.definition_en: the person who has the highest authority and control over an army or navy
entries.example_cn: 总统担任武装部队的最高统帅。
entries.example_en: The president serves as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces.

entries.definition_en: the position or office of commander
entries.example_cn: 他怀着极大的荣誉感接受了指挥官的职位。
entries.example_en: He accepted the commandery with great honor.

entries.definition_en: impressively dominant or exceptionally good
entries.example_cn: 她在最后一场辩论中表现得非常出色。
entries.example_en: She gave a commanding performance in the final debate.

entries.definition_cn: 喜欢发号施令的；专横的
entries.definition_en: tending to give commands; authoritarian
entries.example_cn: 他专横的态度让别人很难质疑他。
entries.example_en: His commanding manner made it difficult for others to question him.

entries.definition_en: providing a clear view of a large area, usually because it is high up
entries.example_cn: 我们坐在居高临下的山顶，俯瞰着下面的山谷。
entries.example_en: We sat on the commanding hilltop and watched the valley below.

entries.definition_en: a command, especially one believed to be divinely ordained
entries.example_cn: 十诫是许多宗教传统的核心内容。
entries.example_en: The Ten Commandments are fundamental to many religious traditions.

entries.definition_cn: 神授的命令，尤指十诫中的一条
entries.definition_en: a divinely ordained command, especially one of the Ten Commandments
entries.example_cn: 爱邻如己的诫命是基督教教义的核心。
entries.example_en: The commandment to love one's neighbor is central to Christian teaching.

entries.definition_en: a soldier who is part of a special military group trained for quick surprise attacks
entries.example_cn: 突击队成功地在夜间渗透进敌方基地。
entries.example_en: The commando team successfully infiltrated the enemy base at night.

entries.definition_en: a military unit trained to conduct raids from the sea onto enemy land
entries.example_cn: 两栖突击队对沿海城镇发起了突袭。
entries.example_en: The amphibious commando launched a surprise attack on the coastal town.

entries.definition_en: to celebrate an important event or person with a ceremony
entries.example_cn: 该镇将举行游行来纪念战争的周年纪念日。
entries.example_en: The town will commemorate the anniversary of the war with a parade.

entries.definition_en: to keep the memory of someone or something alive
entries.example_cn: 我们聚集在这里缅怀那些牺牲生命的英雄。
entries.example_en: We gather here to commemorate the heroes who sacrificed their lives.

entries.definition_cn: 作为某人或某事的纪念物
entries.definition_en: to serve as a memorial for a person or event
entries.example_cn: 这座雕像纪念了这座城市的建立。
entries.example_en: This statue commemorates the founding of the city.

entries.definition_en: a ceremony held to honor the memory of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 该镇为阵亡士兵举行了庄重的纪念活动。
entries.example_en: The town held a solemn commemoration for the fallen soldiers.

entries.definition_en: something that serves to commemorate; a memorial
entries.example_cn: 博物馆建造了一座纪念碑来纪念遇难者。
entries.example_en: The museum erected a memorial as a commemoration of the victims.

entries.definition_en: intended as a commemoration
entries.example_cn: 市政厅是一座建于1920年的纪念性建筑。
entries.example_en: The town hall is a commemorative building constructed in 1920.

entries.definition_cn: 为纪念某人或某事件制作的物品；纪念物
entries.definition_en: an object made to mark an event or honor a person
entries.example_cn: 他们买了一枚纪念币来庆祝战争一百周年。
entries.example_en: They bought a commemorative coin to celebrate the centenary of the war.

entries.definition_en: to begin or start an action or process
entries.example_cn: 典礼将于中午开始。
entries.example_en: The ceremony will commence at noon.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to start or begin
entries.example_cn: 委员会将于下个月开始实施这项新政策。
entries.example_en: The committee will commence the implementation of the new policy next month.

entries.definition_en: to start operating or functioning successfully
entries.example_cn: 火箭开始了它的太空之旅。
entries.example_en: The rocket commenced its journey into space.

entries.definition_en: the time when something is scheduled to start
entries.example_cn: 项目的开始时间定在下周一。
entries.example_en: The commencement of the project is set for next Monday.

entries.definition_en: a formal ceremony at a university where degrees are awarded
entries.example_cn: 她将参加毕业典礼以领取文凭。
entries.example_en: She will attend the commencement ceremony to receive her diploma.

entries.definition_en: the act of beginning or starting something
entries.example_cn: 会议的开始因技术问题而推迟了。
entries.example_en: The commencement of the meeting was delayed due to technical issues.

entries.definition_en: to express approval or praise for someone or something
entries.example_cn: 经理赞扬了团队的努力工作。
