entries.definition_en: having the characteristics of country music
entries.example_cn: 这位歌手的新专辑具有乡村音乐风格，深受乡村音乐老歌迷喜爱。
entries.example_en: The singer's new album has a countrified sound that appeals to longtime country fans.

entries.definition_en: a nation with its own government
entries.example_cn: 法国是欧洲的一个国家。
entries.example_en: France is a country in Europe.

entries.definition_en: the land and area where a nation lives
entries.example_cn: 这个国家很大，有很多山脉。
entries.example_en: The country is very large and has many mountains.

entries.definition_en: an area outside of cities and towns
entries.example_cn: 我们去乡下过周末假期。
entries.example_en: We went to the country for a weekend holiday.

entries.definition_en: the people who live in a nation
entries.example_cn: 这个国家的人口超过一千万。
entries.example_en: The country has a population of over ten million people.

entries.definition_en: a particular geographical region with special features
entries.example_cn: 这种葡萄酒产自一个多山的地区。
entries.example_en: The wine comes from a mountainous country.

entries.definition_cn: 乡村舞（尤指英国乡村舞）
entries.definition_en: a traditional folk dance where couples are arranged in lines or sets facing each other
entries.example_cn: 村民们在大丰收节上表演了热闹的乡村舞。
entries.example_en: The villagers performed a lively country-dance at the harvest festival.

entries.definition_en: to perform a type of folk dance where couples dance in lines or sets
entries.example_cn: 游客们向当地人学习如何跳乡村舞。
entries.example_en: The tourists learned how to country-dance with the locals.

entries.definition_en: people raised in or living in a rural environment; rustics
entries.example_cn: 城里人觉得乡民的习俗大不相同。
entries.example_en: The city dwellers found the countryfolk's customs quite different.

entries.definition_en: people who live in the same country; compatriots
entries.example_cn: 同胞们张开双臂欢迎访客。
entries.example_en: The countryfolk welcomed the visitors with open arms.

entries.definition_en: a man who is from the same country as you
entries.example_cn: 这位同乡帮我修好了汽车。
entries.example_en: The countryman helped me fix my car.

entries.definition_en: a man who lives in the countryside and has a rural lifestyle
entries.example_cn: 这位乡下人在花园里自己种菜。
entries.example_en: The countryman grew his own vegetables in the garden.

entries.definition_en: rural regions
entries.example_cn: 他们搬到乡村去过更安静的生活。
entries.example_en: They moved to the countryside to live a quieter life.

entries.definition_en: occurring or extending throughout a whole country
entries.example_cn: 全国大选在周二举行。
entries.example_en: The countrywide election took place on a Tuesday.

entries.definition_en: a woman who is a native of the same country as the speaker
entries.example_cn: 作为同胞，她完全理解当地的习俗。
entries.example_en: As a countrywoman, she understood the local customs perfectly.

entries.definition_en: a woman who lives in the countryside and has a rural lifestyle
entries.example_cn: 那位乡下妇女用新鲜的面包和牛奶迎接了访客。
entries.example_en: The countrywoman greeted the visitors with fresh bread and milk.

entries.definition_en: an administrative division of a U.S. state
entries.example_cn: 洛杉矶县是加利福尼亚州的一个大县。
entries.example_en: Los Angeles County is a large county in California.

entries.definition_en: a region in the UK for local government
entries.example_cn: 她住在英格兰的一个小郡。
entries.example_en: She lives in a small county in England.

entries.definition_en: occurring or extending throughout an entire county
entries.example_cn: 全县范围的选举结果于周五公布。
entries.example_en: The countywide election results were announced on Friday.

entries.definition_en: throughout a county
entries.example_cn: 该项目在全县范围内开展。
entries.example_en: The program operates countywide.

entries.definition_en: a sudden and decisive change of government illegally or by force
entries.example_cn: 军队发动政变推翻了总统。
entries.example_en: The military staged a coup to overthrow the president.

entries.definition_en: a brilliant and notable success
entries.example_cn: 赢得冠军对这个年轻队伍来说确实是一次巨大的成功。
entries.example_en: Winning the championship was a real coup for the young team.

entries.definition_en: a car with two doors and front seats and a luggage compartment
entries.example_cn: 他买了一辆红色的轿跑车供周末使用。
entries.example_en: He bought a red coupe for the weekend.

entries.definition_cn: 用于盛起泡酒或甜点的浅口高脚杯或浅盘
entries.definition_en: a shallow stemmed glass or dish used to serve sparkling wine or desserts
entries.example_cn: 香槟用精美的浅口高脚杯盛上来。
entries.example_en: The champagne was served in elegant coupes.

entries.definition_cn: 用浅口高脚杯盛装的冰淇淋甜点
entries.definition_en: an ice-cream dessert served in a coupe glass
entries.example_cn: 我们点了一份巧克力冰淇淋杯作为甜点。
entries.example_en: We ordered a chocolate coupe for dessert.

entries.definition_cn: 一对互相熟识并经常在一起的人
entries.definition_en: a pair of people who know each other well and spend time together
entries.example_cn: 他们是一对交往了十年的伴侣。
entries.example_en: They have been a couple for ten years.

entries.definition_en: a small number of people or things, usually two or three
entries.example_cn: 有几位朋友来拜访我们。
entries.example_en: A couple of friends came to visit us.

entries.definition_en: two things of the same kind
entries.example_cn: 我需要买一双新鞋。
entries.example_en: I need to buy a couple of new shoes.

entries.definition_en: two people who live together as partners
entries.example_cn: 他们是一对没有结婚但同居的伴侣。
entries.example_en: They are a couple living together without being married.

entries.definition_en: to connect or join two things together
entries.example_cn: 这两根管子被连接在一起。
entries.example_en: The two pipes are coupled together.

entries.definition_en: to bring two things or people together
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策将教育与医疗保健结合起来。
entries.example_en: The new policy couples education with health care.

entries.definition_en: to form pairs
entries.example_cn: 舞伴们为华尔兹舞配对。
entries.example_en: The dancers couple up for the waltz.

entries.definition_en: to have sexual intercourse
entries.example_cn: 他们在卧室的私密空间里性交。
entries.example_en: They couple in the privacy of their bedroom.

entries.definition_en: a mechanical device used to connect the ends of two adjacent objects
entries.example_cn: 火车车厢通过沉重的钢制连接器连接在一起。
entries.example_en: The train cars are linked together by a heavy steel coupler.

entries.definition_cn: 由两行连续诗句组成的诗节
entries.definition_en: a stanza consisting of two successive lines of verse
entries.example_cn: 这首诗以一首押韵的对句开头。
entries.example_en: The poem begins with a rhyming couplet.

entries.definition_cn: 一对方向相反的单行街道
entries.definition_en: a pair of one-way streets carrying opposing directions of traffic
entries.example_cn: 这两条单行街道在市中心构成一对相反方向的街道。
entries.example_en: The two one-way streets form a couplet through downtown.

entries.definition_en: a device connecting two objects so they move together
entries.example_cn: 火车车厢之间的连接装置受损了。
entries.example_en: The coupling between the train cars was damaged.

entries.definition_en: a mechanical device connecting adjacent objects
entries.example_cn: 工程师检查了管道上的机械连接件。
entries.example_en: The engineer inspected the coupling on the pipeline.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: A coupling can mean a device; coupling can also name the connection generally. Source: w13224r1.

entries.definition_en: an act of sexual intercourse
entries.example_cn: 小说描述了他们的第一次性交。
entries.example_en: The novel describes their first coupling.

entries.definition_en: a certificate that can be detached and redeemed as needed
entries.example_cn: 我用了一张优惠券在杂货上获得了折扣。
entries.example_en: I used a coupon to get a discount on my groceries.

entries.definition_en: a small representative sample of a bulk material prepared for testing
entries.example_cn: 实验室分析了这种新混凝土的样本。
entries.example_en: The laboratory analyzed a coupon of the new concrete.

entries.definition_en: the ability to face danger or pain without showing fear
entries.example_cn: 面对危险局势时，她表现出了极大的勇气。
entries.example_en: She showed great courage when she faced the dangerous situation.

entries.definition_en: having the strength to face danger or fear without showing worry or hesitation.
entries.example_cn: 那位勇敢的消防员冲进着火的建筑去救那只猫。
entries.example_en: The courageous firefighter ran into the burning building to save the cat.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing great bravery and fearlessness
entries.example_cn: 尽管敌军火力猛烈，那名士兵还是勇敢地冲了上去。
entries.example_en: The soldier courageously charged forward despite the heavy enemy fire.

entries.definition_en: a quality of spirit that enables you to face danger or pain without showing fear
entries.example_cn: 消防员冲进燃烧的大楼，他的勇敢显而易见。
entries.example_en: The courageousness of the firefighter was evident as he entered the burning building.

entries.definition_en: a court dance from the 16th century that involved short steps forward and backward
entries.example_cn: 舞者们以精准的进退动作表演了优雅的库朗特舞。
entries.example_en: The dancers performed the elegant courante with precise advances and retreats.

entries.definition_en: the edible immature fruit of a marrow or squash plant
entries.example_cn: 这道食谱要求用擦碎的西葫芦代替奶酪。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for grated courgette instead of cheese.

entries.definition_en: a marrow or squash plant whose immature fruit is eaten
entries.example_cn: 这株西葫芦结出了几个可食用的果实。
entries.example_en: The courgette plant produced several edible fruits.

entries.definition_cn: 传递消息或包裹的人；快递员
entries.definition_en: a person who delivers messages or packages
entries.example_cn: 信使将包裹送到了前门。
entries.example_en: The courier delivered the package to the front door.

entries.definition_en: education given in a series of lessons
entries.example_cn: 我正在上一门烹饪课。
entries.example_en: I am taking a cooking course.

entries.definition_en: a connected series of events or actions
entries.example_cn: 历史的发展过程是不可预测的。
entries.example_en: The course of history is unpredictable.

entries.definition_en: a general line of orientation
entries.example_cn: 我们需要找到正确的方向。
entries.example_en: We need to find the right course.

entries.definition_en: a mode of action
entries.example_cn: 我们必须选择最好的行动方案。
entries.example_en: We must choose the best course of action.

entries.definition_en: to move along, especially of liquids
entries.example_cn: 水流下山坡。
entries.example_en: The water courses down the hill.

entries.definition_en: as might be expected
entries.example_cn: 他理所当然地得出了这个结论。
entries.example_en: He naturally course to the conclusion.

entries.definition_en: to move swiftly through or over something
entries.example_cn: 血液在他的血管中迅速流动。
entries.example_en: The blood coursed swiftly through his veins.

entries.definition_en: to hunt with hounds
entries.example_cn: 猎犬正在追踪鹿。
entries.example_en: The hounds are coursing the deer.

entries.definition_en: a dog trained for coursing
entries.example_cn: 这只猎犬以极快的速度追逐野兔。
entries.example_en: The courser chased the hare with great speed.

entries.definition_en: a huntsman who hunts small animals with fast dogs that use sight rather than scent to follow their prey
entries.example_cn: 这位猎手带领着一群灵缇犬穿过田野。
entries.example_en: The courser led the pack of greyhounds across the field.

entries.definition_en: formerly, a swift horse, especially a racehorse or charger
entries.example_cn: 历史记录将战马描述为中世纪战争中的重要资产。
entries.example_en: Historical records describe the courser as a vital asset in medieval warfare.

entries.definition_en: swift-footed terrestrial plover-like bird of southern Asia and Africa; related to the pratincoles
entries.example_cn: 有人在沙质海岸边发现了游鸻。
entries.example_en: The courser was spotted running along the sandy shore.

entries.definition_en: assignments and work done by students during a course that are used to calculate their grades
entries.example_cn: 学生必须在学期末前提交课程作业。
entries.example_en: Students must submit their coursework by the end of the semester.

entries.definition_en: hunting with dogs trained to chase game by sight
entries.example_cn: 传统的猎犬追逐运动涉及灵缇犬追逐野兔。
entries.example_en: The traditional sport of coursing involves greyhounds chasing hares.

entries.definition_en: a group of judges and officials who hear legal cases
entries.example_cn: 法官走进法庭并坐下。
entries.example_en: The judge entered the court and took her seat.

entries.definition_en: a marked area on the ground for playing a sport
entries.example_cn: 这个网球场是泥地做的。
entries.example_en: The tennis court is made of clay.

entries.definition_en: a room where judges sit to hear cases
entries.example_cn: 律师站起来在审判庭发言。
entries.example_en: The lawyer stood up to speak in the court.

entries.definition_en: the ruler and their advisors who govern a country
entries.example_cn: 国王的朝廷决定修改法律。
entries.example_en: The king’s court decided to change the law.

entries.definition_en: to show romantic interest in someone
entries.example_cn: 他已经追求她三个月了。
entries.example_en: He has been courting her for three months.

entries.definition_en: to try to gain someone's approval or favor
entries.example_cn: 她正试图讨好新经理。
entries.example_en: She is courting the favor of the new manager.

entries.definition_en: the family and servants of a king or prince
entries.example_cn: 宫廷里充满了贵族和音乐家。
entries.example_en: The court was full of nobles and musicians.

entries.definition_en: to go out with someone with the intention of marrying them
entries.example_cn: 他们从去年夏天开始约会。
entries.example_en: They have been courting since last summer.

entries.definition_cn: 审判涉嫌严重违反军法军人的军事法庭
entries.definition_en: a military court to try members of the armed services accused of serious breaches of martial law
entries.example_cn: 将军被军事法庭判处终身监禁。
entries.example_en: The general was sentenced to life imprisonment by a court-martial.

entries.definition_cn: 由军事法庭进行的审判
entries.definition_en: a trial conducted by a military court
entries.example_cn: 军事法庭进行了三周才宣布判决。
entries.example_en: The court-martial lasted for three weeks before delivering its verdict.

entries.definition_cn: 将某人提交军事法庭审判
entries.definition_en: to subject someone to trial by a military court
entries.example_cn: 该军官因不服从命令而被军事法庭审判。
entries.example_en: The officer was court-martialed for insubordination.

entries.definition_en: to order someone to do something by a court order
entries.example_cn: 法官下令该公司支付赔偿金。
entries.example_en: The judge court-ordered the company to pay damages.

entries.definition_en: showing politeness and good manners
entries.example_cn: 为提着沉重袋子的人开门是一种礼貌的行为。
entries.example_en: It is courteous to hold the door open for someone carrying heavy bags.

entries.definition_en: characterized by gracious and polite behavior
entries.example_cn: 主人整晚对每位客人都彬彬有礼。
entries.example_en: The host was courteous to all the guests throughout the dinner.

entries.definition_en: in a polite and respectful manner
entries.example_cn: 接待员礼貌地迎接了每一位客人。
entries.example_en: The receptionist greeted every guest courteously.

entries.definition_en: a high-status female prostitute or mistress, especially of a wealthy or powerful man
entries.example_cn: 在17世纪，交际花通常是艺术的赞助人。
entries.example_en: In the 17th century, the courtesan was often a patron of the arts.

entries.definition_en: an act that is polite and respectful
entries.example_cn: 他特意去拜访了以前的老板。
entries.example_en: He made a courtesy call to his old boss.

entries.definition_en: a polite and respectful way of behaving
entries.example_cn: 她以礼貌和善良而闻名。
entries.example_en: She was known for her courtesy and kindness.

entries.definition_cn: 非出于义务而自愿作出的礼貌表示或话语
entries.definition_en: a polite gesture or remark offered voluntarily rather than as an obligation
entries.example_cn: 作为礼貌，我们将免费寄给您一个样品。
entries.example_en: As a courtesy, we will send you a free sample.

entries.definition_en: a building that houses judicial courts
entries.example_cn: 审判将在市中心的主法院大楼进行。
entries.example_en: The trial will take place in the main courthouse downtown.

entries.definition_cn: （美国）容纳县政府办公室的政府大楼
entries.definition_en: (US) a government building that houses the offices of a county government
entries.example_cn: 县书记官办公室位于新政府大楼内。
entries.example_en: The county clerk's office is located in the new courthouse.

entries.definition_en: a person who attends the court of a king or queen
entries.example_cn: 这位宫廷侍臣在君主面前深深鞠躬。
entries.example_en: The courtier bowed deeply before the sovereign.

entries.definition_cn: 通过奉承他人来博取好感的人
entries.definition_en: a person who flatters others to gain their favor
entries.example_cn: 这位逢迎者不断赞美国王，以博取他的好感。
entries.example_en: The courtier praised the king constantly to win his favor.

entries.definition_cn: 求爱；为结婚而进行的追求
entries.definition_en: the act of courting; romantic advances, especially with a view to marriage
entries.example_cn: 他追求她持续了几个月。
entries.example_en: His courting of her lasted for several months.

entries.definition_en: elegance suggestive of a royal court
entries.example_cn: 舞厅里充满了贵族们的宫廷式优雅。
entries.example_en: The ballroom was filled with the courtliness of the aristocracy.

entries.definition_cn: 优雅的；符合宫廷礼仪的
entries.definition_en: refined or imposing in manner or appearance; befitting a royal court
entries.example_cn: 大使以优雅的宫廷礼仪接待了客人。
entries.example_en: The ambassador received the guests with courtly grace.

entries.definition_en: a room in which a law court sits
entries.example_cn: 律师为法庭辩论做准备。
entries.example_en: The lawyer prepared for the courtroom battle.

entries.definition_en: the act or period of wooing someone in preparation for a romantic relationship or marriage
entries.example_cn: 他们的求爱持续了两年，之后他们订婚了。
entries.example_en: Their courtship lasted for two years before they got engaged.

entries.definition_cn: 动物为吸引配偶而表现出的求偶行为
entries.definition_en: the behavior of an animal when it tries to attract a mate
entries.example_cn: 雄鸟通过复杂的求偶动作来吸引配偶。
entries.example_en: The male bird performs an elaborate courtship display to attract a mate.

entries.definition_en: an area wholly or partly surrounded by walls or buildings
entries.example_cn: 午餐休息时，孩子们在庭院里玩耍。
entries.example_en: The children played in the courtyard during the lunch break.

entries.definition_en: a pasta made in northern Africa of crushed and steamed semolina
entries.example_cn: 粗麦粉蒸面是许多北非国家的主食。
entries.example_en: Couscous is a staple food in many North African countries.

entries.definition_cn: 以粗麦粉蒸面为主料的菜肴，常配肉和蔬菜
entries.definition_en: a dish made with couscous, often served with meat and vegetables
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐享用了一道传统的北非辣味炖菜。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a traditional couscous for dinner.

entries.definition_en: the child of your aunt or uncle
entries.example_cn: 我的表亲住在伦敦。
entries.example_en: My cousin lives in London.

entries.definition_en: the child of your aunt or uncle
entries.example_cn: 我的表亲从另一个城市来看我。
entries.example_en: My cousin-german is visiting from another city.

entries.definition_en: resembling or characteristic of a cousin
entries.example_cn: 尽管以前从未见过面，他们之间却有着表亲般的情谊。
entries.example_en: They shared a cousinly bond despite never meeting before.

entries.definition_cn: 文雅有教养的（用于讽刺）
entries.definition_en: refined and well-mannered (used facetiously)
entries.example_cn: 她对待仆人的方式显示出她的文雅有教养。
entries.example_en: Her couth was evident in the way she addressed the servants.

entries.definition_en: refinement (used facetiously)
entries.example_cn: 他以雅致著称，尽管这常遭到同辈的嘲笑。
entries.example_en: He was known for his couth, though it was often mocked by his peers.

entries.definition_en: the art of designing and making high-fashion clothing
entries.example_cn: 她在著名的时装学校学习高级时装设计。
entries.example_en: She studied couture at the prestigious fashion school.

entries.definition_en: a designer of high-fashion clothing
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的时装设计师在巴黎时装周上展示了她的新系列。
entries.example_en: The famous couturier presented her new collection at the Paris Fashion Week.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有高级定制服装设计师或雇用此类设计师的时装公司（或时装屋）。
entries.definition_en: A fashion house that is owned by or employs a designer of haute couture.
entries.example_cn: 这家时装公司在巴黎时装周上发布了秋季系列。
entries.example_en: The couturier unveiled its autumn collection at Paris Fashion Week.

entries.definition_cn: 男性妊娠共感症；男子出现类似孕妇的症状，如体重增加或晨吐
entries.definition_en: a condition in which a man experiences symptoms similar to those of his pregnant partner, such as weight gain or morning sickness
entries.example_cn: 伴侣怀孕期间，他出现了男性妊娠共感症，包括晨吐和体重增加。
entries.example_en: During his partner's pregnancy, he experienced couvade, including morning sickness and weight gain.

entries.definition_en: a custom where a husband lies in bed during his wife's pregnancy and childbirth
entries.example_cn: 这位人类学家研究了几个土著部落中古老的伴产习俗。
entries.example_en: The anthropologist studied the ancient custom of couvade in several indigenous tribes.

entries.definition_cn: 含至少 32% 可可脂的巧克力
entries.definition_en: chocolate containing at least 32 percent cocoa butter
entries.example_cn: 厨师使用优质 couverture 制作巧克力甘纳许。
entries.example_en: The chef used high-quality couverture to make the chocolate ganache.

entries.definition_en: containing or characterized by covalent bonds
entries.example_cn: 碳原子与四个氢原子形成共价键。
entries.example_en: The carbon atom forms covalent bonds with four hydrogen atoms.

entries.definition_en: a statistical measure of how two variables change together
entries.example_cn: 这两个变量之间的协方差表明存在强烈的正相关关系。
entries.example_en: The covariance between the two variables indicates a strong positive relationship.

entries.definition_en: changing in a way that keeps the relationship with other variables unchanged
entries.example_cn: 在物理学中，运动定律必须在参考系变换下保持协变性。
entries.example_en: In physics, the laws of motion must remain covariant under a change of reference frame.

entries.definition_en: a situation where two variables change together in a correlated way
entries.example_cn: 这项研究考察了降雨量与作物产量之间的共变关系。
entries.example_en: The study examined the covariation between rainfall and crop yield.

entries.definition_en: a small bay or inlet along a coastline
entries.example_cn: 他们将船停泊在一个宁静的海湾里。
entries.example_en: They anchored their boat in a quiet cove.

entries.definition_en: a small cave in the side of a cliff
entries.example_cn: 探险者在山崖边发现了一个小岩洞。
entries.example_en: The explorers found a small cove in the mountain side.

entries.definition_en: a formal group or assembly of witches
entries.example_cn: 传说中提到一个女巫团在满月下集会。
entries.example_en: The legend spoke of a coven meeting under the full moon.

entries.definition_cn: 为做或不做某事而订立的正式协议或作出的有约束力的承诺
entries.definition_en: a formal agreement or binding promise to do or refrain from doing something
entries.example_cn: 两国签署了和平契约以结束冲突。
entries.example_en: The two nations signed a peace covenant to end the conflict.

entries.definition_en: an agreement between God and his people involving promises and required behavior
entries.example_cn: 在圣经中，圣约代表了上帝与人类之间的特殊关系。
entries.example_en: In the Bible, the covenant represents the special relationship between God and humanity.

entries.definition_en: enter into a covenant
entries.example_cn: 领导人发誓相互缔结契约以提供保护。
entries.example_en: The leaders vowed to covenant with each other for mutual protection.

entries.definition_en: to bind oneself by contract
entries.example_cn: 他们立约承诺维护这座建筑十年。
entries.example_en: They covenanted to maintain the building for ten years.

entries.definition_en: to put a covering over something
entries.example_cn: 请用盖子把食物盖好。
entries.example_en: Please cover the food with a lid.

entries.definition_en: to form a layer over something
entries.example_cn: 雪覆盖了地面。
entries.example_en: Snow covered the ground.

entries.definition_en: to extend over a period of time or distance
entries.example_cn: 这本书涵盖了战争的历史。
entries.example_en: The book covers the history of the war.

entries.definition_en: to pay for or provide enough money for something
entries.example_cn: 她的工资足以支付全家的月度开支。
entries.example_en: Her salary covers the family's monthly expenses.

entries.definition_en: something used to conceal or shelter
entries.example_cn: 沙发有一个防护罩。
entries.example_en: The sofa has a protective cover.

entries.definition_en: the protective outer part of a book
entries.example_cn: 这本小说的封面是红色的。
entries.example_en: The cover of the novel is red.

entries.definition_en: the act of hiding something by blocking the view
entries.example_cn: 树木为士兵提供了掩护。
entries.example_en: The trees provided cover for the soldiers.

entries.definition_en: bedding used to keep warm in bed
entries.example_cn: 这条被子很柔软。
entries.example_en: The quilt is a soft cover.

entries.definition_cn: 掩盖或隐瞒某事（尤其是错误或不当行为）的行为
entries.definition_en: an attempt to conceal or disguise something, especially wrongdoing or a mistake
entries.example_cn: 警方调查了掩盖丑闻的行为。
entries.example_en: The police investigated the cover-up of the scandal.

entries.definition_cn: 不下水时穿在泳衣外面的衣物
entries.definition_en: a garment worn over a swimsuit when not in the water
entries.example_cn: 她穿上泳衣外罩，然后走去餐馆。
entries.example_en: She put on a cover-up before walking to the restaurant.

entries.definition_en: the extent to which something is covered
entries.example_cn: 这颗卫星覆盖了很大的区域。
entries.example_en: The satellite provides coverage over a wide area.

entries.definition_en: the total amount and type of insurance carried
entries.example_cn: 该保单不包括洪水损害的保险范围。
entries.example_en: The policy does not include coverage for flood damage.

entries.definition_en: the news as presented by reporters for newspapers or radio or television
entries.example_cn: 该事件的电视新闻报道吸引了数百万观众。
entries.example_en: The television coverage of the event reached millions of viewers.

entries.definition_cn: 移动电话或其他无线电网络可以使用的区域
entries.definition_en: the area in which a mobile phone or other radio network is available
entries.example_cn: 这个山谷里没有手机信号覆盖。
entries.example_en: There is no mobile coverage in the mountain valley.

entries.definition_en: a loose-fitting protective garment worn over other clothes
entries.example_cn: 这位机械师穿着一件黄色的连体工作服，以保护衣服不被油污弄脏。
entries.example_en: The mechanic wore a yellow coverall to protect his clothes from oil.

entries.definition_cn: 被覆盖的；被包围或包含的
entries.definition_en: overlaid with, covered by, or enclosed within something
entries.example_cn: 桌子上铺着一块白布。
entries.example_en: The table was covered with a white cloth.

entries.definition_en: an artifact that covers something else (usually to protect or shelter or conceal it)
entries.example_cn: 她在油漆家具前用保护罩将其盖住。
entries.example_en: She put a protective covering over the furniture before painting.

entries.definition_en: a natural object that covers or envelops
entries.example_cn: 积雪为森林地面提供了厚厚的覆盖物。
entries.example_en: The snow provided a thick covering for the forest floor.

entries.definition_cn: 通过覆盖来保护某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of protecting something by covering it
entries.example_cn: 仔细覆盖家具使其免受油漆污染。
entries.example_en: The careful covering of the furniture kept it free of paint.

entries.definition_en: the act of concealing the existence of something by obstructing the view of it
entries.example_cn: 浓雾形成了一层遮蔽，隐藏了远处的群山。
entries.example_en: The heavy fog created a covering that hid the distant mountains.

entries.definition_en: the work of applying something
entries.example_cn: 艺术家花了几个小时在画框上涂抹金箔。
entries.example_en: The artist spent hours on the covering of gold leaf on the frame.

entries.definition_en: a decorative bedspread, often quilted
entries.example_cn: 她把绣花的床罩铺在床上。
entries.example_en: She spread the embroidered coverlet over the bed.

entries.definition_cn: 秘密的；隐藏的；不公开进行的
entries.definition_en: secret or hidden; not openly practiced or shown
entries.example_cn: 他们对此事进行了秘密调查。
entries.example_en: They conducted a covert investigation into the matter.

entries.definition_en: (of a wife) being under the protection of her husband
entries.example_cn: 在那个时代，受丈夫保护的妻子很少在外工作。
entries.example_en: In that era, a covert wife rarely worked outside the home.

entries.definition_en: a covering that conceals or shelters something
entries.example_cn: 士兵们躲在灌木丛的掩护物后面。
entries.example_en: The soldiers hid behind a covert of bushes.

entries.definition_en: a flock of coots (water birds)
entries.example_cn: 那群鸊鷉在湖面上游动。
entries.example_en: The covert of coots moved across the lake.

entries.definition_en: in a secret or hidden way
entries.example_cn: 间谍秘密地将数据传输给他的联络人。
entries.example_en: The spy covertly transmitted the data to his contact.

entries.definition_cn: 渴望；垂涎（尤指他人的财产）
entries.definition_en: wish, long, or crave for (something, especially the property of another person)
entries.example_cn: 他从不觊觎他人的财富。
entries.example_en: He never covets the wealth of others.

usage.label: 及物动词：covet something
usage.pattern: Source w20866r0 labels this sense transitive.

entries.definition_en: desired or wanted by many people
entries.example_cn: 这款限量版手表深受收藏家追捧。
entries.example_en: The limited edition watch was highly coveted by collectors.

entries.definition_en: immoderately desirous of acquiring wealth
entries.example_cn: 那位贪财的商人不惜一切代价追求利润。
entries.example_en: The covetous merchant sought profit at any cost.

entries.definition_en: showing extreme greed; painfully desirous of another's advantages
entries.example_cn: 他贪婪地觊觎邻居的财富和地位。
entries.example_en: He was covetous of his neighbor's wealth and status.

entries.definition_en: an intense and envious desire to possess something that belongs to someone else
entries.example_cn: 他对邻居财产的觊觎之心导致了他偷窃。
entries.example_en: His covetousness for his neighbor's property led him to steal it.

entries.definition_en: extreme greed for material wealth
entries.example_cn: 这个故事警告人们要警惕在追求金钱时产生的贪婪。
entries.example_en: The story warns against the dangers of covetousness in the pursuit of money.

entries.definition_en: an insatiable desire for wealth, considered one of the deadly sins
entries.example_cn: 在这个寓言中，贪欲被描绘为人心中的破坏性力量。
entries.example_en: In the parable, covetousness is depicted as a destructive force within the human heart.

entries.definition_en: a small flock of grouse or partridge
entries.example_cn: 我们在田野里发现了一丛鹧鸪。
entries.example_en: We spotted a covey of partridges in the field.

entries.definition_en: a small group of people
entries.example_cn: 这群志愿者在社区中心聚集。
entries.example_en: The covey of volunteers gathered at the community center.

entries.definition_en: a desert shrub found in the southwestern United States and New Mexico with aromatic foliage and small yellow flowers
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者经常发现这种稀有的科维尔灌木生长在沙漠岩石之间。
entries.example_en: Hikers often spot the rare coville growing among the desert rocks.

entries.definition_en: a female domestic cattle
entries.example_cn: 农民每天早上挤母牛的奶。
entries.example_en: The farmer milked the cow every morning.

entries.definition_cn: 雌性哺乳动物（雄性称为公牛）
entries.definition_en: a mature female of mammals whose male is called bull
entries.example_cn: 这头母牛是田野里吃草的牛群的一部分。
entries.example_en: The cow was part of the herd grazing in the field.

entries.definition_cn: （英国、爱尔兰，非正式，贬义）讨厌的女人；泼妇
entries.definition_en: an informal, derogatory term in Britain and Ireland for an unpleasant woman
entries.example_cn: 别让那个泼妇欺负你。
entries.example_en: Don't let that cow bully you around.

entries.definition_en: to subdue or frighten someone
entries.example_cn: 巨大的噪音让狗畏缩而保持沉默。
entries.example_en: The loud noise cowed the dog into silence.

entries.definition_en: a person who shows fear or timidity
entries.example_cn: 他因拒绝战斗而被称作懦夫。
entries.example_en: He was called a coward for refusing to fight.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being lacking in courage
entries.example_cn: 他的懦弱使他不敢在会议上发言。
entries.example_en: His cowardice prevented him from speaking up during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being afraid to take risks or face danger
entries.example_cn: 他的懦弱使他不敢在会议上发言。
entries.example_en: His cowardliness prevented him from speaking up during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: lacking courage; showing ignoble timidity and faint-heartedness
entries.example_cn: 临阵脱逃是懦弱的行为。
entries.example_en: It was cowardly to run away from the fight.

entries.definition_en: a bell worn around a cow's neck to help locate it
entries.example_cn: 农夫摇动牛铃把走失的牲畜叫回来。
entries.example_en: The farmer shook the cowbell to call the stray animal back.

entries.definition_cn: 一种通常没有铃舌的金属打击乐器
entries.definition_en: a metal percussion instrument, typically without a clapper
entries.example_cn: 副歌部分，鼓手加入了牛铃来加强节奏。
entries.example_en: The drummer added a cowbell to the rhythm during the chorus.

entries.definition_en: a blackbird native to North America that follows cattle and lays its eggs in the nests of other birds
entries.example_cn: 牛鹂跟着牛群穿过草原。
entries.example_en: The cowbird followed the herd of cattle across the prairie.

entries.definition_en: a male hired hand who tends cattle and performs other duties on horseback
entries.example_cn: 牧牛工骑着马穿过广阔的平原放牧牛群。
entries.example_en: The cowboy rode his horse across the vast plains to herd the cattle.

entries.definition_en: someone who acts recklessly or irresponsibly, especially when driving a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 那个鲁莽的人开车闯红灯，看都没看一眼。
entries.example_en: The cowboy drove the car through the red light without looking.

usage.label: informal
usage.pattern: reckless person, especially one showing off

entries.definition_en: a male performer who gives exhibitions of riding and roping and bulldogging
entries.example_cn: 这位牛仔表演者给观众展示了惊险的套绳技巧。
entries.example_en: The cowboy performed thrilling roping tricks for the audience.

entries.definition_en: a metal frame at the front of a train engine designed to push obstacles off the tracks
entries.example_cn: 那台旧蒸汽机车有一个巨大的排障器，用于清理铁轨。
entries.example_en: The old steam locomotive had a large cowcatcher to clear the rails.

entries.definition_en: to crouch or cringe in fear
entries.example_cn: 打雷时，那只狗蜷缩在桌子底下。
entries.example_en: The dog cowered under the table when the thunder started.

entries.definition_en: to show submission or fear
entries.example_cn: 他畏缩在愤怒的老板面前。
entries.example_en: He cowered before the angry boss.

entries.definition_en: a type of trunkfish that has horn-like spines over its eyes
entries.example_cn: 潜水员发现一条牛角鱼躲在珊瑚丛中。
entries.example_en: The diver spotted a cowfish hiding among the coral.

entries.definition_en: a woman who tends cattle, especially on a ranch
entries.example_cn: 她像真正的女牛仔一样骑马穿过平原。
entries.example_en: She rode her horse across the plains like a true cowgirl.

entries.definition_en: a female performer who demonstrates riding and roping skills
entries.example_cn: 牛仔竞技表演中有一位才华横溢的女表演牛仔赢得了套索比赛。
entries.example_en: The rodeo featured a talented cowgirl who won the roping competition.

entries.definition_en: a hired worker who takes care of cattle and does other jobs while riding a horse
entries.example_cn: 这位牧牛工骑马穿过平原去检查牛群。
entries.example_en: The cowhand rode his horse across the plains to check on the herd.

entries.definition_en: a hired worker who tends cattle and performs other duties on horseback
entries.example_cn: 那位老牧牛人骑着马穿过田野去检查牛群。
entries.example_en: The old cowherd rode his horse across the fields to check on the herd.

entries.definition_en: leather made from the hide of a cow
entries.example_cn: 工匠用牛皮制作了一个结实的包。
entries.example_en: The artisan crafted a sturdy bag from cowhide.

entries.definition_en: the hide of a cow
entries.example_cn: 制革商从农场购买了一张新鲜的牛皮。
entries.example_en: The tanner purchased a fresh cowhide from the farm.

entries.definition_en: a heavy flexible whip braided from leather made from the hide of a cow
entries.example_cn: 牛仔用牛皮鞭抽打马鞍。
entries.example_en: The cowboy cracked his cowhide against the saddle.

entries.definition_en: to flog with a cowhide
entries.example_cn: 这名囚犯因犯罪被用牛皮鞭打。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was cowhided for his crimes.

entries.definition_en: a metal cover for an engine
entries.example_cn: 机械师拆下发动机罩以检查引擎。
entries.example_en: The mechanic removed the cowl to inspect the engine.

entries.definition_en: a loose hooded robe worn by monks
entries.example_cn: 修士将兜帽拉下来遮住了脸。
entries.example_en: The monk pulled his cowl over his face.

entries.definition_en: to cover with a cowl
entries.example_cn: 他们用罩子盖住引擎以防雨淋。
entries.example_en: They cowl the engine to protect it from the rain.

entries.definition_en: having the head enclosed in a cowl or hood
entries.example_cn: 一个戴兜帽的身影从阴影中走出。
entries.example_en: A cowled figure emerged from the shadows.

entries.definition_en: fitted with a cowl, especially of a chimney
entries.example_cn: 那座老农舍有一根装有烟罩的烟囱。
entries.example_en: The old farmhouse had a cowled chimney.

entries.definition_cn: 头发旋；翘起的一绺头发
entries.definition_en: a tuft of hair that grows in a different direction and will not lie flat
entries.example_cn: 拍照前她试图抚平那撮乱发。
entries.example_en: She tried to smooth down her cowlick before the photo.

entries.definition_en: a metal cover that protects an engine
entries.example_cn: 机械师拆下发动机罩以检查发动机。
entries.example_en: The mechanic removed the cowling to inspect the engine.

entries.definition_en: a man who works with cattle, especially on a ranch, farm, or feedlot
entries.example_cn: 牧牛工骑马穿过田野去检查牛群。
entries.example_en: The cowman rode his horse across the field to check on the herd.

entries.definition_en: the fruit or seed of the cowpea plant
entries.example_cn: 豇豆是一种常出现在汤中的营养豆类。
entries.example_en: The cowpea is a nutritious legume often found in soups.

entries.definition_cn: 一种蔓生的一年生豇豆植物，用于食用、饲料和绿肥
entries.definition_en: a sprawling annual cowpea plant cultivated for food, forage, and green manure
entries.example_cn: 美国南部的农民种植豇豆以获取其饲料价值。
entries.example_en: Farmers in the southern United States grow the cowpea for its forage value.

entries.definition_cn: 作为鲜荚豆或干豆食用的菜豆
entries.definition_en: cowpeas that are eaten fresh as shell beans or dried
entries.example_cn: 我们把菜豆煮熟，作为鲜荚豆食用。
entries.example_en: We boiled the cowpea to eat them fresh as shell beans.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to herd cattle
entries.example_cn: 这位老牧牛人熟悉农场的每一寸土地，能找到任何走失的牛。
entries.example_en: The old cowpoke knew every inch of the ranch and could find any lost steer.

usage.label: US slang
usage.pattern: cowpoke is a US slang term for a cowhand

entries.definition_en: a viral disease of cattle causing a mild skin disease affecting the udder; formerly used to inoculate humans against smallpox
entries.example_cn: 历史上，牛痘曾被用来让人对天花产生免疫力。
entries.example_en: Historically, cowpox was used to create immunity to smallpox.

entries.definition_en: a hired hand who tends cattle and performs other duties on horseback
entries.example_cn: 那位老赶牛工骑着马穿过广阔的平原去放牧牛群。
entries.example_en: The old cowpuncher rode his horse across the vast plains to herd the cattle.

entries.definition_en: a tropical sea snail with a highly polished, brightly colored shell
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在沙滩上收集了漂亮的货贝。
entries.example_en: The children collected beautiful cowrie shells on the beach.

entries.definition_en: a tropical sea snail with a highly polished, brightly marked shell often used as currency
entries.example_cn: 收藏家花了几个小时在海滩上寻找稀有的宝贝螺。
entries.example_en: The collector spent hours searching the beach for rare cowries.

entries.definition_en: domesticated bovine animals kept for milk, meat, or labor
entries.example_cn: 农民们在清晨给牛挤奶。
entries.example_en: The farmers milked the cows early in the morning.

entries.definition_en: a barn used for housing cows
entries.example_cn: 农民在冬天到来之前修理了牛棚的屋顶。
entries.example_en: The farmer repaired the roof of the cowshed before winter.

entries.definition_en: leather produced from the hide of a cow
entries.example_cn: 那副旧马鞍是用厚实耐用的牛皮制成的。
entries.example_en: The old saddle was made of thick, durable cowskin.

entries.definition_en: a common early spring flower in the British Isles with fragrant yellow or sometimes purple blooms
entries.example_cn: 我们在田野里发现了一丛盛开的报春花。
entries.example_en: We found a patch of cowslips blooming in the meadow.

entries.definition_en: a swamp plant found in Europe and North America that has bright yellow flowers resembling buttercups
entries.example_cn: 植物学家识别出湿地中生长的沼委陵菜。
entries.example_en: The botanist identified the cowslip growing in the wetland.

entries.definition_en: a town or city associated with the cattle industry
entries.example_cn: 他们搬到了德克萨斯州一个宁静的养牛业小镇，开始新的生活。
entries.example_en: They moved to a quiet cowtown in Texas to start their new life.

entries.definition_en: the ball-and-socket joint connecting the head of the femur to the acetabulum
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了患者的髋臼关节以评估损伤情况。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the patient's coxa to assess the damage.

entries.definition_en: the red fleshy crest on the head of a rooster or similar bird
entries.example_cn: 公鸡鲜红的鸡冠在灰暗的天空下格外显眼。
entries.example_en: The rooster's bright red coxcomb stood out against the grey sky.

entries.definition_cn: 自命不凡的人；爱慕虚荣的人
entries.definition_en: a vain person who is overly proud of their own achievements
entries.example_cn: 他表现得像个自命不凡的人，吹嘘自己微不足道的成功。
entries.example_en: He acted like a coxcomb, boasting about his minor success.

entries.definition_en: a cap worn by court jesters, decorated with a red strip
entries.example_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位戴着宫廷弄臣帽子的国王。
entries.example_en: The painting depicts a king wearing a coxcomb.

entries.definition_cn: 柯萨奇病毒（一类主要引起儿童疾病的肠道病毒）
entries.definition_en: any of several enteroviruses that cause various illnesses, mostly in children
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出孩子感染了柯萨奇病毒。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the child with a coxsackievirus infection.

entries.definition_en: the person who steers a racing boat or a ship's small boat
entries.example_cn: 舵手发出精确的指令，引导船只穿过狭窄的航道。
entries.example_en: The coxswain gave precise commands to steer the boat through the narrow channel.

entries.definition_en: affectedly modest or shy, especially in a playful or provocative way
entries.example_cn: 他称赞她时，她报以故作矜持的微笑。
entries.example_en: She gave a coy smile when he complimented her.

entries.definition_en: showing marked and often playful or irritating evasiveness or reluctance to make a definite or committing statement
entries.example_cn: 他对周末的计划故意含糊其辞。
entries.example_en: He was being coy about his plans for the weekend.

entries.definition_cn: 对追求或邀约表现得矜持而不愿接受的
entries.definition_en: modestly or warily reluctant to accept an approach or overture
entries.example_cn: 她对接受他的晚餐邀请显得矜持而犹豫。
entries.example_en: She was coy about accepting his invitation to dinner.

entries.definition_en: in an affectedly shy or modest manner
entries.example_cn: 她故作羞怯地避开了他的目光。
entries.example_en: She coyly avoided looking him in the eye.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being coy, especially affected shyness or modesty
entries.example_cn: 她表现出的故作矜持让人难以忽视。
entries.example_en: She displayed a coyness that was hard to ignore.

entries.definition_en: a small wild dog native to western North America
entries.example_cn: 郊狼对着月亮嚎叫。
entries.example_en: The coyote howled at the moon.

entries.definition_cn: 把非法移民偷运进美国的人
entries.definition_en: a person who smuggles illegal immigrants into the United States
entries.example_cn: 这名人口走私者带领那群人越过了边境。
entries.example_en: The coyote led the group across the border.

usage.label: US informal
usage.pattern: a person who smuggles undocumented immigrants

entries.definition_en: a firefighter who battles remote and severe forest fires
entries.example_cn: 这名森林消防员工作了数天以扑灭大火。
entries.example_en: The coyote worked for days to put out the fire.

entries.definition_cn: 一种形似大型鼠类、产于南美洲并因毛皮而饲养的水生啮齿动物；海狸鼠
entries.definition_en: a South American rodent that looks like a small beaver and is raised for its fur
entries.example_cn: 农民饲养海狸鼠以获取其珍贵的皮毛。
entries.example_en: Farmers raise the coypu for its valuable fur.

entries.definition_en: to act with artful deceit; to trick someone cleverly
entries.example_cn: 魔术师用巧妙的诡计让观众相信他瞬移了。
entries.example_en: The magician cozened the audience into believing he had teleported.

entries.definition_en: to cheat or trick someone
entries.example_cn: 他们被骗签了一份欺诈性合同。
entries.example_en: They were cozened into signing a fraudulent contract.

usage.label: archaic
usage.pattern: to cozen someone out of something

entries.definition_en: to be false to someone; to be dishonest with them
entries.example_cn: 他试图欺骗他的朋友，骗取他们的积蓄。
entries.example_en: He tried to cozen his friends out of their savings.

entries.definition_en: in a comfortable and warm manner
entries.example_cn: 他们舒适地坐在火炉旁读书。
entries.example_en: They sat cozily by the fire reading.

entries.definition_cn: 温暖而舒适惬意的状态
entries.definition_en: a state of warm snug comfort
entries.example_cn: 壁炉增添了客厅的舒适感。
entries.example_en: The fireplace added to the coziness of the living room.

entries.definition_en: comfortable and warm, especially in a small space
entries.example_cn: 我们坐在壁炉旁舒适的角落里。
entries.example_en: We sat in a cozy corner by the fire.

entries.definition_en: friendly and informal in atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅的氛围非常友好且非正式。
entries.example_en: The restaurant has a very cozy atmosphere.

entries.definition_cn: 暗示秘密勾结的；涉嫌串通的
entries.definition_en: suggesting secret agreement or collusion
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司之间亲密的关系引起了怀疑。
entries.example_en: The cozy relationship between the two companies raised suspicions.

entries.definition_en: a cloth cover to keep a teapot warm
entries.example_cn: 她在茶壶上盖了一个茶壶套。
entries.example_en: She put a cozy on the teapot.

entries.definition_cn: 频率单位，等于每秒一个周期；现通常称为赫兹
entries.definition_en: a unit of frequency equal to one cycle per second, now usually called a hertz
entries.example_cn: 信号频率以周/秒为单位进行测量。
entries.example_en: The signal frequency was measured in cps.

entries.definition_en: a small, sour apple suitable for preserving
entries.example_cn: 这些酸苹果非常适合做派，因为它们的味道很酸。
entries.example_en: These crabapples are perfect for making pies because of their tart flavor.

entries.definition_en: a wild apple tree that typically bears small, sour fruit
entries.example_cn: 花园里那棵老野苹果树结着小红果，味道非常酸。
entries.example_en: The old crabapple tree in the garden has small, red fruit that tastes very sour.

entries.definition_cn: 栽培的海棠品种，因其小而酸的果实或观赏性花朵而种植
entries.definition_en: a cultivated crabapple variety grown for its small acidic fruit or ornamental blossoms
entries.example_cn: 这个海棠品种因其小而酸的果实和美丽的花朵而栽培。
entries.example_en: This crabapple variety is cultivated for its small acidic fruit and attractive blossoms.

entries.definition_en: annoyed and irritable
entries.example_cn: 他在交通拥堵中待了太久，心情变得十分暴躁。
entries.example_en: He was feeling crabbed after spending too much time in traffic.

entries.definition_en: annoyed and easily irritated
entries.example_cn: 他太易怒了，不愿和邻居说话。
entries.example_en: He was too crabby to talk to his neighbors.

entries.definition_cn: 马唐（一类匍匐茎易生根、常见于草坪的禾本科杂草）
entries.definition_en: a type of grass with creeping stems that roots easily, often considered a weed in lawns
entries.example_cn: 园丁花了整个周末从草坪上拔除马唐。
entries.example_en: The gardener spent the weekend pulling up crabgrass from the lawn.

entries.definition_en: the edible flesh of various crabs
entries.example_cn: 我们午餐点了一份配有新鲜蟹肉的沙拉。
entries.example_en: We ordered a salad with fresh crabmeat for lunch.

entries.definition_en: an infestation of pubic hair by lice
entries.example_cn: 医生开了药来治疗阴虱病。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed medication to treat the crabs.

usage.label: plural-only slang
usage.pattern: Crabs is a slang plural-only noun for pubic lice.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow cleft in a surface
entries.example_cn: 墙上有一条裂缝。
entries.example_en: There was a crack in the wall.

entries.definition_en: a narrow opening
entries.example_cn: 光线从门缝中透进来。
entries.example_en: Light came through the crack in the door.

entries.definition_en: to become fractured or break on the surface only
entries.example_cn: 滑冰者的体重使冰面开裂。
entries.example_en: The ice cracked under the weight of the skater.

entries.definition_en: to make a sharp sound
entries.example_cn: 鞭子经过时发出了尖锐的声音。
entries.example_en: The whip cracked as it passed by.

entries.definition_en: to make a very sharp explosive sound
entries.example_cn: 枪声在寂静中爆裂作响。
entries.example_en: The gun cracked loudly in the silence.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 这是一支一流的运动员队伍。
entries.example_en: This is a crack team of athletes.

entries.definition_en: a sudden sharp noise
entries.example_cn: 我们听到树上突然传来一声爆裂声。
entries.example_en: We heard a sudden crack from the tree.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow depression in a surface
entries.example_cn: 这条路上有一条深深的沟槽。
entries.example_en: The road has a deep crack running through it.

entries.definition_en: a sudden mental or physical collapse
entries.example_cn: 在几周的压力之后，他彻底崩溃了。
entries.example_en: After weeks of stress, he had a complete crack-up.

entries.definition_cn: 严厉打击；加强执法或纪律处分
entries.definition_en: a sudden increase in strict enforcement or disciplinary action
entries.example_cn: 政府宣布严厉打击非法毒品交易。
entries.example_en: The government announced a crackdown on illegal drug trade.

entries.definition_cn: 形容精神不正常的（非正式或俚语）
entries.definition_en: informal or slang terms for mentally irregular
entries.example_cn: 别叫他精神失常，他只是累了。
entries.example_en: Don't call him cracked; he is just tired.

entries.definition_cn: 因寒冷或暴露而皮肤粗糙的
entries.definition_en: having skin that is rough and dry from cold or exposure
entries.example_cn: 他的脸被冻风刮得粗糙开裂。
entries.example_en: His face was cracked from the freezing wind.

entries.definition_cn: 油漆或清漆的；呈鳄鱼皮状的
entries.definition_en: of paint or varnish; having the appearance of alligator hide
entries.example_cn: 旧清漆呈现出鳄鱼皮般的开裂外观。
entries.example_en: The old varnish had a cracked, alligator-skin appearance.

entries.definition_cn: 由面粉和水制成的薄脆饼干，常配奶酪食用
entries.definition_en: a thin, crisp wafer made of flour and water, often eaten with cheese
entries.example_cn: 她端上了饼干和奶酪作为开胃菜。
entries.example_en: She served crackers and cheese as an appetizer.

entries.definition_cn: 一种带有引信的小型烟花，装在纸壳内
entries.definition_en: a small firework with a fuse inside a paper casing
entries.example_cn: 孩子们点燃了烟花，迅速跑开了。
entries.example_en: The children lit the cracker and ran away quickly.

entries.definition_cn: 破解计算机系统或软件、通常为绕过安全限制或获取未经授权访问权限的人
entries.definition_en: a person who cracks computer systems or software, typically to bypass security restrictions or gain unauthorized access
entries.example_cn: 安全团队抓获了一名试图从服务器窃取数据的破解者。
entries.example_en: The security team caught a cracker trying to steal data from the server.

entries.definition_cn: 一种派对小礼物，两端一拉就会弹出，通常装有糖果
entries.definition_en: a party favor that pops when pulled at both ends, usually containing candy
entries.example_cn: 每位客人都收到一个装满巧克力硬币的派对小礼物。
entries.example_en: Each guest received a cracker filled with chocolate coins.

entries.definition_cn: 对美国南部贫穷白人的贬义词
entries.definition_en: a derogatory term for a poor White person in the southern United States
entries.example_cn: 这部小说用“cracker”作为对美国南部贫穷白人的贬义称呼。
entries.example_en: The novel uses “cracker” as a derogatory term for a poor White person in the southern United States.

entries.definition_cn: 质朴的；带有小镇居民特色的
entries.definition_en: characteristic of simple, small-town people or their informal wisdom
entries.example_cn: 他们喜欢围着篝火进行那种质朴的闲聊。
entries.example_en: They enjoyed the cracker-barrel conversation around the campfire.

entries.definition_en: exceptionally fine or excellent; top-notch
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅以一流的服务而闻名。
entries.example_en: The restaurant is known for its crackerjack service.

entries.definition_en: a person who is extremely good at something
entries.example_cn: 她是个解决复杂谜题的高手。
entries.example_en: She is a real crackerjack at solving complex puzzles.

entries.definition_en: something that is extremely good
entries.example_cn: 最后的演出真是一场精彩的表演。
entries.example_en: The final performance was a real crackerjack.

entries.definition_cn: （英国，口语）疯狂的；精神失常的
entries.definition_en: crazy or insane (UK, colloquial)
entries.example_cn: 那听起来像是个疯狂的主意。
entries.example_en: That sounds like a crackers idea.

entries.definition_en: excellent
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛中表现出色。
entries.example_en: The team put in a cracking performance in the final match.

entries.definition_en: a sudden sharp noise
entries.example_cn: 木头爆裂的声音在森林中回荡。
entries.example_en: The sound of cracking wood echoed through the forest.

entries.definition_en: the act of cracking something
entries.example_cn: 他正被当场发现撬保险箱。
entries.example_en: He was caught in the act of cracking the safe.

entries.definition_en: the process whereby heavy molecules of naphtha or petroleum are broken down into hydrocarbons of lower molecular weight (especially in the oil-refining process)
entries.example_cn: 炼油厂利用裂解工艺将重油转化为汽油。
entries.example_en: The refinery uses cracking to convert heavy oil into gasoline.

entries.definition_en: to make a crackling sound
entries.example_cn: 树叶在我们脚下发出噼啪声。
entries.example_en: The leaves crackled under our feet.

entries.definition_en: to make a crushing noise
entries.example_cn: 冰碎裂时发出咔嚓声。
entries.example_en: The ice crackled as it broke.

entries.definition_en: to become, or to cause to become, covered with a network of small cracks
entries.example_cn: 旧油漆在冬天后开始出现裂纹。
entries.example_en: The old paint began to crackle after the winter.

entries.definition_en: the sharp sound of snapping noises
entries.example_cn: 我们听到了壁炉里火焰的噼啪声。
entries.example_en: We heard the crackle of the fire in the hearth.

entries.definition_cn: 裂纹釉；形成细小表面裂纹的釉料
entries.definition_en: a style of glaze producing a network of fine surface cracks
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展出了一只饰有裂纹釉的花瓶。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a vase decorated with crackle glaze.

entries.definition_en: having the surface decorated with a network of fine cracks
entries.example_cn: 她买了一个表面有裂纹装饰的花瓶。
entries.example_en: She bought a vase with a crackle glaze.

entries.definition_en: a sharp, snapping sound
entries.example_cn: 炉火发出令人舒适的噼啪声。
entries.example_en: The fire produced a comforting crackling sound.

entries.definition_en: the hard, crispy residue left after animal fat is melted
entries.example_cn: 我们把炸油渣和烤猪肉一起吃。
entries.example_en: We ate the crackling with our roast pork.

entries.definition_en: a whimsically eccentric person
entries.example_cn: 这位科学家被同事们视为古怪离奇的人而遭到排斥。
entries.example_en: The scientist was dismissed as a crackpot by his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: a baby bed with sides and rockers
entries.example_cn: 婴儿在木制摇篮里睡得香甜。
entries.example_en: The baby slept soundly in the wooden cradle.

entries.definition_en: where something originated or was nurtured in its early existence
entries.example_cn: 这所大学是现代科学的发源地。
entries.example_en: The university is the cradle of modern science.

entries.definition_en: infancy or very early life
entries.example_cn: 从出生到死亡，她始终对世界充满好奇。
entries.example_en: From the cradle to the grave, she remained curious about the world.

entries.definition_en: hold gently and carefully
entries.example_cn: 她双手轻轻抱着那只受伤的鸟。
entries.example_en: She cradled the injured bird in her hands.

entries.definition_cn: 像放在摇篮里一样放置
entries.definition_en: hold or place in or as if in a cradle
entries.example_cn: 摄影师像抱着婴儿一样抱着相机，以获取完美的角度。
entries.example_en: The photographer cradled the camera to get the perfect angle.

entries.definition_en: to nurse, raise, or train during infancy
entries.example_cn: 他在一个小村庄由祖母抚养长大。
entries.example_en: He was cradled by his grandmother in a small village.

entries.definition_en: a trough that can be rocked back and forth; used by gold miners to shake auriferous earth in water in order to separate the gold
entries.example_cn: 矿工们使用一个巨大的木制淘金槽从河床中提取黄金。
entries.example_en: The miners used a large wooden cradle to extract gold from the riverbed.

entries.definition_en: cut grain with a cradle scythe
entries.example_cn: 农民在金色的田野里用割谷镰刀收割成熟的小麦。
entries.example_en: The farmer cradled the ripe wheat in the golden fields.

entries.definition_en: the skilled practice of a practical occupation
entries.example_cn: 她对陶艺这门手艺有着深厚的热爱。
entries.example_en: She has a deep love for the craft of pottery.

entries.definition_cn: 用于在水上、空中或太空中航行的交通工具
entries.definition_en: a vehicle designed for navigation in or on water or air or through outer space
entries.example_cn: 飞行员在起飞前检查了飞行器的导航系统。
entries.example_en: The pilot checked the navigation systems of the craft before takeoff.

entries.definition_en: skill in an occupation or trade
entries.example_cn: 她在编织方面的技艺在村里无人能及。
entries.example_en: Her craft in weaving is unmatched in the village.

entries.definition_cn: 某类熟练工作的从业者；工匠
entries.definition_en: people who perform a particular kind of skilled work
entries.example_cn: 当地工匠们为成员组织了一场节日庆典。
entries.example_en: The local craft organized a festival for its members.

entries.definition_en: shrewdness as demonstrated by being skilled in deception
entries.example_cn: 这位政客操纵舆论的能力显示了他的狡诈。
entries.example_en: The politician's craft was evident in his ability to manipulate public opinion.

entries.definition_en: make by hand and with much skill
entries.example_cn: 他花了几个小时精心制作了一个木制鸟屋。
entries.example_en: He spent hours crafting a wooden birdhouse.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes things by hand as a hobby or business
entries.example_cn: 这位工匠花了数小时在毯子上编织复杂的花纹。
entries.example_en: The crafter spent hours weaving intricate patterns into the rug.

entries.definition_en: in a subtle and cunning manner
entries.example_cn: 他狡诈地避开了那个棘手的问题。
entries.example_en: He craftily avoided answering the difficult question.

entries.definition_en: the skill of deceiving others cleverly
entries.example_cn: 当这位政客在纳税申报单上撒谎时，他的狡诈被揭露了。
entries.example_en: The politician's craftiness was revealed when he lied about his tax returns.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being crafty
entries.example_cn: 她的狡猾使她能够成功地应对复杂的办公室政治。
entries.example_en: Her craftiness allowed her to navigate the complex office politics successfully.

entries.definition_en: a man skilled in making things by hand
entries.example_cn: 这位工匠技艺高超地雕刻了木头。
entries.example_en: The craftsman carved the wood with great skill.

entries.definition_en: a highly skilled person in a craft or profession
entries.example_cn: 他是工程领域的真正专家。
entries.example_en: He is a true craftsman in his field of engineering.

entries.definition_en: the skill and quality demonstrated in making things by hand
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了19世纪精湛工艺的作品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed examples of fine craftsmanship from the 19th century.

entries.definition_en: a person highly skilled in a trade or in producing arts and crafts
entries.example_cn: 每一位工匠都以自己作品的耐用性为荣。
entries.example_en: Every craftsperson takes pride in the durability of their creations.

entries.definition_en: a woman who creates things with great skill using her hands
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件由技艺精湛的女工匠制作的精美花瓶。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a beautiful vase made by a skilled craftswoman.

entries.definition_en: a female professional whose work is consistently of high quality
entries.example_cn: 她是建筑领域一位备受赞誉的优秀女专业人士。
entries.example_en: She is a renowned craftswoman in the field of architectural design.

entries.definition_en: marked by skill in deception
entries.example_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸设法逃出了猎人的陷阱。
entries.example_en: The crafty fox managed to escape the hunter's trap.

entries.definition_en: a steep, rugged rock or cliff
entries.example_cn: 登山者攀登了峡谷边缘的陡峭峭壁。
entries.example_en: The climbers scaled the sheer crag at the edge of the canyon.

entries.definition_cn: 多山丘和峭壁的；崎岖多岩的
entries.definition_en: having hills and crags
entries.example_cn: 徒步者攀登了多峭壁的山脉。
entries.example_en: The hikers climbed the craggy mountain range.

entries.definition_en: a bird belonging to a group of short-billed rails found in the Old World
entries.example_cn: 人们发现一只稀有的秧鸡正在浅水沼泽中涉水。
entries.example_en: The rare crake was spotted wading through the shallow marsh water.

entries.definition_en: to study very hard and quickly in preparation for an exam
entries.example_cn: 我不得不通宵突击复习期末考试。
entries.example_en: I had to cram for the final exam all night.

entries.definition_en: to fill a space with so many people or things that there is no room left
entries.example_cn: 那个小房间里挤满了家具。
entries.example_en: The small room was crammed with furniture.

entries.definition_en: to put something into a place until it is completely full
entries.example_cn: 离开前他把书塞进了包里。
entries.example_en: He crammed his bag with books before leaving.

entries.definition_en: to prepare students hastily for an upcoming test
entries.example_cn: 老师试图在一周内把整个教学大纲塞给学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher tried to cram the whole syllabus into one week.

entries.definition_en: a teacher who is paid to cram students for examinations
entries.example_cn: 许多学生聘请应试补习教师帮助他们准备期末考试。
entries.example_en: Many students hire a crammer to help them prepare for the final exams.

entries.definition_en: a student who crams
entries.example_cn: 那个突击学习者熬夜背诵历史日期。
entries.example_en: The crammer stayed up all night to memorize the history dates.

entries.definition_en: a special school where students are crammed
entries.example_cn: 这所突击补习学校以高强度的学习日程而闻名。
entries.example_en: The crammer was known for its intense study schedule.

entries.definition_en: a textbook designed for cramming
entries.example_cn: 她买了一本突击复习教材来准备驾照考试。
entries.example_en: She bought a crammer to review for her driving test.

entries.definition_en: a painful and involuntary muscular contraction
entries.example_cn: 跑步时我的小腿抽筋了。
entries.example_en: I got a cramp in my calf while running.

entries.definition_en: a clamp for holding pieces of wood together while they are glued
entries.example_cn: 他用一个木工夹具将木块固定到位。
entries.example_en: He used a cramp to hold the wood pieces in place.

entries.definition_en: suffer from sudden painful contraction of a muscle
entries.example_cn: 她在马拉松比赛中抽筋了。
entries.example_en: She cramped during the marathon.

entries.definition_en: prevent the progress or free movement of
entries.example_cn: 大雪阻碍了高速公路上的交通。
entries.example_en: The heavy snow cramps the traffic on the highway.

entries.definition_en: affect with or as if with a cramp
entries.example_cn: 寒冷的风吹得他双腿痉挛。
entries.example_en: The cold wind cramped his legs.

entries.definition_en: secure with a cramp
entries.example_cn: 木匠在粘合木板前用夹具将它们固定在一起。
entries.example_en: The carpenter cramps the boards together before gluing them.

entries.definition_en: a strip of metal with ends bent at right angles; used to hold masonry together
entries.example_cn: 石匠用金属角铁将砖块绑在一起。
entries.example_en: The mason used a cramp to bind the bricks.

entries.definition_en: constricted in size; having very little space
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不坐在拥挤公交车的狭窄座位上。
entries.example_en: We had to sit in a cramped seat on the crowded bus.

entries.definition_cn: 固定在鞋上以防在冰上滑倒的铁钉
entries.definition_en: an iron spike attached to a shoe to prevent slipping on ice
entries.example_cn: 登山者在下山前将冰爪固定在靴子上。
entries.example_en: The mountaineer clipped his crampon onto his boots before descending.

entries.definition_cn: 一对用于抬起重物的铰接弯曲铁条
entries.definition_en: a hinged pair of curved iron bars used to raise heavy objects
entries.example_cn: 工人们用一个大撬棍抬起发动机。
entries.example_en: The workers used a large crampon to lift the engine.

entries.definition_en: a unit of measurement used for fresh herring
entries.example_cn: 渔民们用“克兰”为单位计算了他们在每周市场上的渔获量。
entries.example_en: The fishermen calculated their catch in crans for the weekly market.

entries.definition_en: a very tart red berry used for sauce or juice
entries.example_cn: 她端上了配蔓越莓酱的火鸡。
entries.example_en: She served turkey with cranberry sauce.

entries.definition_en: a shrub of the genus Vaccinium that bears cranberries
entries.example_cn: 蔓越莓灌木生长在潮湿、酸性的土壤中。
entries.example_en: The cranberry grows in wet, acidic soil.

entries.definition_en: (archaic) to press or grind with a crushing noise
entries.example_cn: 这台机器开始碾碎那些旧金属管。
entries.example_en: The machine began to cranch the old metal pipes.

entries.definition_en: a machine with a long pivoted arm used for lifting and moving heavy objects
entries.example_cn: 他们使用起重机吊起沉重的钢梁。
entries.example_en: They used a crane to lift the heavy steel beams.

entries.definition_en: a large bird with a long neck that lives in marshes and plains
entries.example_cn: 一只白鹤优雅地站在湿地里。
entries.example_en: A white crane stood gracefully in the wetland.

entries.definition_en: to stretch your neck to see something more clearly
entries.example_cn: 她伸长脖子越过人群看去。
entries.example_en: She craned her neck to see over the crowd.

entries.definition_en: any of numerous geraniums of the genus Geranium
entries.example_cn: 花园里点缀着红色的老鹳草花。
entries.example_en: The garden was dotted with red cranesbill flowers.

entries.definition_en: relating to the cranium, the part of the skull that encloses the brain
entries.example_cn: 颅神经将大脑与身体的其余部分连接起来。
entries.example_en: The cranial nerves connect the brain to the rest of the body.

entries.definition_cn: 切除部分颅骨（骨瓣）的外科手术，通常术后复位
entries.definition_en: a surgical procedure in which part of the skull is removed as a bone flap, usually temporarily
entries.example_cn: 医生进行了开颅手术以切除肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The doctor performed a craniotomy to remove the tumor.

entries.definition_cn: 颅骨（包围脑部的头骨部分）
entries.definition_en: the part of the skull that encloses the brain
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查头骨是否有受伤迹象。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the cranium for signs of injury.

entries.definition_cn: 连接在轴上的弯曲臂或手柄，用于传递旋转运动
entries.definition_en: a bent arm or handle attached to a shaft, used to impart rotary motion
entries.example_cn: 转动曲柄使机器旋转。
entries.example_en: Turn the crank to rotate the machine.

entries.definition_en: a person who is bad-tempered and difficult to deal with
entries.example_cn: 别让那个脾气暴躁的人毁了你的心情。
entries.example_en: Don't let that crank ruin your day.

entries.definition_en: a person who is whimsically eccentric
entries.example_cn: 他是一个古怪离奇的人，相信月亮是由奶酪制成的。
entries.example_en: He is a crank who believes the moon is made of cheese.

entries.definition_en: to rotate using a crank
entries.example_cn: 她转动把手打开窗户。
entries.example_en: She cranks the handle to open the window.

entries.definition_en: to start an engine by cranking
entries.example_cn: 你必须摇动那辆旧车才能发动它。
entries.example_en: You have to crank the old car to start it.

entries.definition_en: (of boats) inclined to heel over easily under sail
entries.example_cn: 那艘小船船身不稳，在强风中很容易侧倾。
entries.example_en: The small boat is crank and heels over easily in a strong breeze.

entries.definition_cn: 一种苯丙胺衍生物（甲基苯丙胺），用作中枢神经系统兴奋剂和食欲抑制剂
entries.definition_en: an amphetamine derivative used as a stimulant and appetite suppressant
entries.example_cn: Crank是甲基苯丙胺的俚语名称。
entries.example_en: Crank is a slang term for methamphetamine.

entries.definition_en: to travel along a zigzag path
entries.example_cn: 这条路蜿蜒穿过群山。
entries.example_en: The road cranks through the mountains.

entries.definition_en: the housing that contains a crankshaft in an engine
entries.example_cn: 机械师检查了曲轴箱内的油位。
entries.example_en: The mechanic checked the oil level in the crankcase.

entries.definition_en: a disposition that is fussy, irritable, and eccentric
entries.example_cn: 他脾气古怪，很难与邻居和睦相处。
entries.example_en: His crankiness made it difficult for him to get along with his neighbors.

entries.definition_en: a rotating shaft that is driven by or drives a crank
entries.example_cn: 发动机的曲轴将活塞的直线运动转化为旋转运动。
entries.example_en: The engine's crankshaft converts the linear motion of the pistons into rotational motion.

entries.definition_en: easily irritated or annoyed
entries.example_cn: 他今天早上很易怒，因为他没睡好。
entries.example_en: He was cranky this morning because he didn't sleep well.

entries.definition_cn: （船因压载不足等）容易倾侧或倾覆的
entries.definition_en: (of a boat) liable to heel or capsize easily, especially because of insufficient ballast
entries.example_cn: 这艘小船在强风中显得非常不稳定，容易倾侧。
entries.example_en: The small boat felt very cranky in the strong wind.

entries.definition_en: a small opening or crevice (especially in a rock face or wall)
entries.example_cn: 光线透过岩石壁上的缝隙透进来。
entries.example_en: Light filtered through the cranny in the rock face.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow depression in a surface
entries.example_cn: 老鼠躲进了墙壁的一个阴暗凹陷处。
entries.example_en: The mouse hid in a dark cranny of the wall.

entries.definition_cn: （轻度粗俗俚语）无价值或质量很差的东西；废话
entries.definition_en: mildly vulgar slang for something worthless or of very poor quality; nonsense
entries.example_cn: 那档节目纯粹是垃圾。
entries.example_en: The show was pure crap.

entries.definition_en: mildly vulgar slang for feces
entries.example_cn: 我踩到了人行道上的一些狗屎。
entries.example_en: I stepped in some dog crap on the sidewalk.

entries.definition_en: to have a bowel movement
entries.example_cn: 我需要找个厕所排便。
entries.example_en: I need to find a bathroom to crap.

entries.definition_en: a small, very thin pancake
entries.example_cn: 她吃了一个上面放着新鲜草莓的薄煎饼。
entries.example_en: She ate a warm crape topped with fresh strawberries.

entries.definition_en: a soft, thin, light fabric with a crinkled surface
entries.example_cn: 这条裙子是用优雅的黑色皱纱制成的。
entries.example_en: The dress was made of elegant black crape.

entries.definition_en: to cover or drape something with crape fabric
entries.example_cn: 哀悼者用黑纱覆盖窗户以纪念逝者。
entries.example_en: The mourners crape the windows of the house in memory of the deceased.

entries.definition_en: to curl tightly
entries.example_cn: 热量使金属卷曲成紧密的螺旋状。
entries.example_en: The heat caused the metal to crape into tight spirals.

entries.definition_en: a plumbing fixture for defecation and urination
entries.example_cn: 地下室里的那个旧厕所需要更换了。
entries.example_en: The old crapper in the basement needs to be replaced.

entries.definition_en: small sunfishes of the genus Pomoxis found in central United States rivers
entries.example_cn: 垂钓者在密西西比河中钓到了一条黑鲈。
entries.example_en: The angler caught a crappie while fishing in the Mississippi River.

entries.definition_en: small sunfishes found in central United States rivers
entries.example_cn: 我们花了一下午在当地湖泊里尝试钓太阳鱼。
entries.example_en: We spent the afternoon trying to catch crappie in the local lake.

entries.definition_en: very bad
entries.example_cn: 我们度过了糟糕的一天，整个上午都在下雨。
entries.example_en: We had a crappy day with rain all morning.

entries.definition_cn: 双骰赌博游戏（克拉普斯）：首掷为7或11赢，2、3或12输；其他点数定为目标点，须在掷出7前再次掷出该点才赢。
entries.definition_en: a gambling game played with two dice: a come-out roll of 7 or 11 wins, 2, 3, or 12 loses, and any other number establishes a point that must be rolled again before a 7
entries.example_cn: 他们晚上在赌场玩骰子赌博游戏。
entries.example_en: They spent the evening playing craps at the casino.

usage.label: 仅复数
usage.pattern: 游戏名称通常使用复数形式。

entries.definition_cn: （克拉普斯中）输的首掷：掷出2、3或12
entries.definition_en: a losing come-out roll of 2, 3, or 12 in the game of craps
entries.example_cn: 掷骰者在首掷时掷出了输骰（2、3或12）。
entries.example_en: The shooter rolled craps on the come-out roll.

entries.definition_en: diarrhea (slang, vulgar)
entries.example_cn: 吃了变质食物后，他整晚都在拉肚子。
entries.example_en: After eating spoiled food, he had the craps all night.

entries.definition_en: a venture that involves great risk and uncertainty
entries.example_cn: 把所有积蓄都投进那个初创公司完全是个冒险。
entries.example_en: Investing all your savings in that startup is a total crapshoot.

usage.label: US, idiomatic
usage.pattern: Risky or unpredictable venture; source w38349r1.

entries.definition_en: the game of craps
entries.example_cn: 赌场里充满了掷骰子游戏的喧闹声。
entries.example_en: The casino floor was filled with the noise of a crapshoot.

entries.definition_en: to fall or come down violently
entries.example_cn: 飞机猛烈坠入群山之中。
entries.example_en: The plane crashed into the mountains.

entries.definition_en: to move with a loud crashing noise
entries.example_cn: 海浪猛烈地拍打着岩石。
entries.example_en: The waves crashed against the rocks.

entries.definition_en: to be damaged or destroyed upon impact
entries.example_cn: 汽车撞上了墙壁并彻底损毁。

entries.definition_en: the act of making something new
entries.example_cn: 这座雕塑的创作花了几个月的时间。
entries.example_en: The creating of the sculpture took months of hard work.

entries.definition_en: something that has been made by someone
entries.example_cn: 这幅画是这位艺术家的精美创作。
entries.example_en: This painting is a beautiful creation of the artist.

entries.definition_en: the act of making something new
entries.example_cn: 新软件的创造需要时间和努力。
entries.example_en: The creation of new software takes time and effort.

entries.definition_en: the act of starting something new
entries.example_cn: 新公司的创立取得了巨大成功。
entries.example_en: The creation of the new company was a big success.

entries.definition_en: the event when something begins to exist
entries.example_cn: 宇宙的创生是一个谜。
entries.example_en: The creation of the universe is a mystery.

entries.definition_en: everything that exists
entries.example_cn: 上帝是万物的创造者。
entries.example_en: God is the creator of all creation.

entries.definition_cn: 相信神创造了世界的教义，尤其指《创世记》等宗教文本所描述的创世观
entries.definition_en: the belief that a deity created the world, especially as described in a religious text such as Genesis
entries.example_cn: 辩论集中在创世论的科学有效性上。
entries.example_en: The debate focused on the scientific validity of creationism.

entries.definition_en: having the ability or power to create
entries.example_cn: 她是一位非常有创造力的作家。
entries.example_en: She is a very creative writer.

entries.definition_en: original, expressive, and imaginative
entries.example_cn: 政府推出了一项促进城市建设的计划。
entries.example_en: The government launched a creative plan to improve the city.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows imagination and originality
entries.example_cn: 她创造性地解决了这个问题。
entries.example_en: She solved the problem creatively.

entries.definition_en: the ability to create new things or ideas
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家的作品展现了非凡的创造力。
entries.example_en: The artist's work demonstrates a remarkable creativeness.

entries.definition_en: the ability to create new ideas or things
entries.example_cn: 老师鼓励学生在艺术课上发挥创造力。
entries.example_en: The teacher encouraged the students' creativity in art class.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that creates or makes something
entries.example_cn: 这位软件的创造者是一位杰出的工程师。
entries.example_en: The creator of the software is a brilliant engineer.

entries.definition_en: an animal, especially a nonhuman one
entries.example_cn: 那个动物从水里爬了出来。
entries.example_en: The creature crawled out of the water.

entries.definition_en: a living being
entries.example_cn: 地球上的每种生物都需要水来生存。
entries.example_en: Every creature on Earth needs water to survive.

entries.definition_cn: 受人操纵或支配的人；傀儡
entries.definition_en: a person controlled by or subservient to someone else
entries.example_cn: 他只是老板的傀儡，老板让他做什么他就做什么。
entries.example_en: He was just a creature of his boss, doing whatever was asked.

entries.definition_en: a model showing the birth of Jesus in a stable
entries.example_cn: 教堂在圣诞节期间展示耶稣降生场景模型。
entries.example_en: The church displays a creche during Christmas.

entries.definition_en: a hospital that cares for babies whose parents are unknown
entries.example_cn: 这家医院为弃婴运营一个收容所。
entries.example_en: The hospital operates a creche for foundlings.

entries.definition_cn: 信誉；社会认可度，尤指在特定群体中的认可度
entries.definition_en: credibility or social standing, especially among a particular group
entries.example_cn: 这位新设计师立刻在城市青年中获得了信誉。
entries.example_en: The new designer gained instant cred with the urban youth.

entries.definition_en: relating to a creed or system of beliefs
entries.example_cn: 这个新宗教团体的信条声明引起了争议。
entries.example_en: The credal statements of the new religious group were controversial.

entries.definition_en: the mental attitude that something is believable and should be accepted as true
entries.example_cn: 她相信她听到的那些谣言。
entries.example_en: She gave credence to the rumors she had heard.

entries.definition_en: a kind of sideboard or buffet
entries.example_cn: 他们把银器陈列在餐具柜上。
entries.example_en: They displayed the silverware on the credence.

entries.definition_cn: 证明身份或资格的正式文件
entries.definition_en: an official document that proves a person's identity or qualifications
entries.example_cn: 他出示了大学学历证明，以证明自己的学位。
entries.example_en: He showed his university credential to prove his degree.

entries.definition_cn: 登录凭据；用于登录账户或系统的信息（如用户名和密码）
entries.definition_en: the information, such as a username and password, used to log in to an account or system
entries.example_cn: 千万不要把你的登录凭据告诉任何人。
entries.example_en: Never share your login credentials with anyone.

entries.definition_en: official documents that prove a person's qualifications or authority
entries.example_cn: 她出示了证明文件以进入安全区域。
entries.example_en: She showed her credentials to gain access to the secure area.

entries.definition_en: a kind of sideboard or buffet
entries.example_cn: 他们将银器放在木制餐边柜上。
entries.example_en: They placed the silverware on the wooden credenza.

entries.definition_cn: 横式文件柜，通常放在书桌后面
entries.definition_en: a horizontal filing cabinet, typically placed behind a desk
entries.example_cn: 经理把合同放在书桌后面的横式文件柜里。
entries.example_en: The manager kept the contracts in the credenza behind her desk.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being believable or trustworthy
entries.example_cn: 律师质疑了证人的可信度。
entries.example_en: The witness's credibility was questioned by the lawyer.

entries.definition_en: capable of being believed
entries.example_cn: 证人提供了关于该事件的可靠证词。
entries.example_en: The witness gave a credible account of the event.

entries.definition_en: appearing to merit belief or acceptance
entries.example_cn: 这个计划看起来在纸面上是可行的，但在实践中可能会失败。
entries.example_en: The plan looks credible on paper, but it may fail in practice.

entries.definition_en: credulous
entries.example_cn: 他太轻信了，相信听到的每一个谣言。
entries.example_en: He is too credible to believe every rumor he hears.

entries.definition_en: easy to believe on the basis of available evidence
entries.example_cn: 证人可信地陈述了他所看到的事情。
entries.example_en: The witness testified credibly about what he saw.

entries.definition_en: recognition or praise for an achievement or contribution
entries.example_cn: 委员会认可了团队的努力工作。
entries.example_en: The committee gave credit to the team for their hard work.

entries.definition_cn: 银行允许客户借出的款项
entries.definition_en: money that a bank allows a customer to borrow
entries.example_cn: 他申请了一笔高信用额度的贷款。
entries.example_en: He applied for a loan with a high credit limit.

entries.definition_cn: 电影或电视节目开头或结尾显示的演职员等信息
entries.definition_en: written information about the people who made a film or television program, shown at the beginning or end
entries.example_cn: 他们接吻后，演职员表开始滚动播放。
entries.example_en: They kissed, and then the credits rolled.

entries.definition_cn: 会计账目中记录收入或资本的条目
entries.definition_en: a record in accounting showing income or capital
entries.example_cn: 会计师在账簿中将这笔付款记为贷方条目。
entries.example_en: The accountant entered the payment as a credit in the ledger.

entries.definition_en: acknowledge that someone deserves praise for something
entries.example_cn: 我们必须承认这个新项目的想法是她提出的。
entries.example_en: We must credit her with the idea of the new project.

entries.definition_cn: 将成就或品质归因于某人
entries.definition_en: attribute an achievement or quality to someone
entries.example_cn: 这次活动的成功归功于熟练的市场营销团队。
entries.example_en: The success of the campaign is credited to the skilled marketing team.

entries.definition_en: to record an amount as a credit in an account
entries.example_cn: 收到存款时，系统会自动将账户记为贷方。
entries.example_en: The system automatically credits the account when the deposit is received.

entries.definition_en: an achievement that deserves praise
entries.example_cn: 你能按时完成这项任务，这值得称赞。
entries.example_en: It is to your credit that you finished the task on time.

entries.definition_en: to have trust in someone or something
entries.example_cn: 我不相信他的故事，我认为他在撒谎。
entries.example_en: I do not credit his story; I think he is lying.

entries.definition_en: worthy of some praise or commendation, though perhaps not excellent
entries.example_cn: 他的表现值得称赞，尽管没有赢得比赛。
entries.example_en: His performance was creditable, even if it did not win the competition.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows a reasonable level of worthiness or achievement
entries.example_cn: 这名学生在困难的考试中表现值得赞许。
entries.example_en: The student performed creditably on the difficult exam.

entries.definition_cn: 被归因于某人或某事；被认为是……造成的
entries.definition_en: attributed to someone or something as a cause or source
entries.example_cn: 项目的成功应归功于团队的辛勤工作。
entries.example_en: The success of the project was credited to the team's hard work.
