entries.definition_cn: 什么也没有；毫无价值的一点东西
entries.definition_en: nothing at all; no amount or value whatsoever
entries.example_cn: 我从彩票中一无所获。
entries.example_en: I didn't get diddly-squat from the lottery.

entries.definition_en: to stop living; to cease to exist as a living being
entries.example_cn: 那棵老树最终在冬天死了。
entries.example_en: The old tree finally died in the winter.

entries.definition_en: to stop working or functioning
entries.example_cn: 我们在高速公路上行驶时，引擎熄火了。
entries.example_en: The engine died while we were driving on the highway.

entries.definition_en: to die, especially as a result of a specified cause or for a purpose
entries.example_cn: 士兵们为祖国英勇牺牲。
entries.example_en: The soldiers died bravely for their country.

entries.definition_en: to be so embarrassed, amused, or ashamed that one feels as if they will die
entries.example_cn: 那个笑话太好笑了，我笑死了。
entries.example_en: I died laughing at that funny joke.

entries.definition_en: a small cube with numbers on its faces, used in games of chance
entries.example_cn: 他掷骰子得到了六点。
entries.example_en: He rolled the die and got a six.

entries.definition_en: a tool used to shape metal by cutting it
entries.example_cn: 工厂使用冲模来冲压汽车零件。
entries.example_en: The factory uses a die to stamp out car parts.

entries.definition_en: a cutting tool fitted into a holder to cut screw threads
entries.example_cn: 机械师为螺栓选择了正确的丝锥。
entries.example_en: The machinist selected the correct die for the bolt.

entries.definition_en: to feel indifferent or unconcerned towards something
entries.example_cn: 她对周围的苦难漠不关心。
entries.example_en: She died of indifference to the suffering around her.

entries.definition_en: formed by forcing molten metal into a die
entries.example_cn: 这辆玩具车是金属压铸模型。
entries.example_en: The toy car is a die-cast model made of metal.

entries.definition_en: stubbornly holding onto old traditions or opinions
entries.example_cn: 那些顽固守旧的球迷拒绝接受比赛的新规则。
entries.example_en: The die-hard fans refused to accept the new rules for the game.

entries.definition_en: a plant disease where young shoots die starting from the tips
entries.example_cn: 园丁注意到枯梢病正从玫瑰灌木的顶端蔓延开来。
entries.example_en: The gardener noticed the dieback spreading from the tips of the rose bushes.

entries.definition_cn: 顽固地拒绝改变的；狂热支持某项事业的
entries.definition_en: stubbornly resistant to change or fanatically devoted to a cause
entries.example_cn: 这名顽固的传统主义者反对所有提出的改革。
entries.example_en: The diehard traditionalist opposed every proposed reform.

entries.definition_en: a person who stubbornly resists change or remains fanatically devoted to a cause
entries.example_cn: 他是那个旧政党的顽固支持者。
entries.example_en: He is a diehard supporter of the old political party.

entries.definition_cn: 能隔绝电流并可在电场中极化的材料；介电材料
entries.definition_en: a material that is electrically insulating and can be polarized by an electric field
entries.example_cn: 电容器使用陶瓷绝缘体来储存电能。
entries.example_en: The capacitor uses a ceramic dielectric to store electrical energy.

entries.definition_en: the posterior part of the forebrain that connects the cerebral hemispheres with the midbrain
entries.example_cn: 间脑在调节身体内部环境中起着至关重要的作用。
entries.example_en: The diencephalon plays a crucial role in regulating the body's internal environment.

entries.definition_en: an engine that runs on heavy oil
entries.example_cn: 这辆卡车有一个强大的柴油发动机。
entries.example_en: The truck has a powerful diesel engine.

entries.definition_en: a locomotive driven by the electric current generated by a diesel engine
entries.example_cn: 柴油电力机车轰鸣着驶入车站。
entries.example_en: The diesel-electric train pulled into the station with a loud roar.

entries.definition_cn: 由柴油发动机驱动发电机供电的
entries.definition_en: powered by a diesel engine that drives an electrical generator
entries.example_cn: 这台柴油电力机车牵引货运列车爬上陡坡。
entries.example_en: The diesel-electric locomotive hauled the freight train up the steep grade.

entries.definition_en: a locomotive powered by a diesel engine and driven by a hydraulic transmission system
entries.example_cn: 那台柴油液力传动机车拉着沉重的货运列车爬上了山坡。
entries.example_en: The diesel-hydraulic locomotive pulled the heavy freight train up the mountain.

entries.definition_en: a controlled selection of foods and drinks prescribed or chosen for health or another purpose
entries.example_cn: 医生给他制定了严格的饮食计划以降低胆固醇。
entries.example_en: The doctor put him on a strict diet to lower his cholesterol.

entries.definition_en: the usual food and drink consumed by an organism
entries.example_cn: 狮子的日常饮食主要由肉类组成。
entries.example_en: The lion's diet consists mainly of meat.

entries.definition_en: the act of restricting your food intake
entries.example_cn: 节食是减肥的一种常见方式。
entries.example_en: Going on a diet is a common way to lose weight.

entries.definition_en: a legislative assembly in certain countries
entries.example_cn: 日本国会昨天通过了这项新法律。
entries.example_en: Japan's National Diet passed the new law yesterday.

entries.definition_en: to follow a controlled regimen of food and drink, usually for health or weight reasons
entries.example_cn: 她节食三个月了，目的是减肥。
entries.example_en: She has been dieting for three months to lose weight.

entries.definition_en: to eat sparingly in order to lose weight or improve health
entries.example_cn: 他想健身，所以正在节食。
entries.example_en: He is dieting because he wants to get fit.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the diet
entries.example_cn: 她正在遵循严格的饮食计划以减肥。
entries.example_en: She is following a strict dietary plan to lose weight.

entries.definition_en: a regulated diet
entries.example_cn: 在较早的英国用法中，dietary 可指规定的饮食。
entries.example_en: In older British usage, a dietary meant a regulated diet.

entries.definition_en: a person who is trying to lose weight by eating less food
entries.example_cn: 作为一名节食者，她避免喝任何含糖饮料。
entries.example_en: As a dieter, she avoids all sugary drinks.

entries.definition_cn: 饮食的；与饮食疗法或限制性饮食有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to diet, especially a restricted or therapeutic diet
entries.example_cn: 她选择了一份饮食计划来改善她的整体健康。
entries.example_en: She chose a dietetic meal plan to improve her overall health.

entries.definition_en: the scientific study of food preparation and intake
entries.example_cn: 她在大学学习营养学，以便成为一名营养师。
entries.example_en: She studied dietetics at university to become a nutritionist.

entries.definition_en: a potent estrogen used in medicine and in feed for livestock and poultry
entries.example_cn: 兽医给患激素失衡的牛开了己烯雌酚。
entries.example_en: The veterinarian prescribed diethylstilbestrol to treat the hormonal imbalance in the cattle.

entries.definition_en: a professional who specializes in studying diet and nutrition to promote health
entries.example_cn: 医院聘请了一名营养师来帮助患者制定健康的饮食计划。
entries.example_en: The hospital hired a dietician to help patients develop healthy eating plans.

entries.definition_en: the practice of following a diet, especially by restricting food intake
entries.example_cn: 她节食三周以减轻体重。
entries.example_en: She has been dieting for three weeks to lose weight.

entries.definition_en: a professional who specializes in food and nutrition
entries.example_cn: 医院聘请了一名营养师来帮助患者规划健康饮食。
entries.example_en: The hospital hired a dietitian to help patients plan healthy meals.

entries.definition_en: to be not the same as something else
entries.example_cn: 这两张地图在描绘海岸线的方式上有所不同。
entries.example_en: The two maps differ in the way they show the coastline.

entries.definition_en: to have different opinions about something
entries.example_cn: 我们在解决这个问题的最佳方法上意见相左。
entries.example_en: We differ on the best way to solve the problem.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unlike or dissimilar
entries.example_cn: 这两幅画有很大的不同。
entries.example_en: There is a big difference between the two paintings.

entries.definition_en: a variation that deviates from the standard or norm
entries.example_cn: 测量结果显示它与标准存在偏差。
entries.example_en: The measurement showed a difference from the standard.

entries.definition_en: a disagreement or argument about something important
entries.example_cn: 他们在预算问题上产生了分歧。
entries.example_en: They had a difference of opinion about the budget.

entries.definition_en: a significant change
entries.example_cn: 会议后，公司对其政策进行了重大调整。
entries.example_en: The company made a significant difference in its policy after the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the number that remains after subtraction; the number that when added to the subtrahend gives the minuend
entries.example_cn: 十和三的差是七。
entries.example_en: The difference between ten and three is seven.

entries.definition_en: not the same in nature, quality, form, or degree
entries.example_cn: 这两幅画非常不同。
entries.example_en: These two paintings are very different.

entries.definition_en: clearly separate from the first one
entries.example_cn: 第二章与第一章截然不同。
entries.example_en: The second chapter is different from the first.

entries.definition_en: not like any other; unusual
entries.example_cn: 她对这件事有不同的看法。
entries.example_en: She has a different opinion on the matter.

entries.definition_en: distinct or separate
entries.example_cn: 请将这两个账户分开。
entries.example_en: Please keep the two accounts separate.

entries.definition_en: a distinguishing characteristic that separates one species or group from another within a genus
entries.example_cn: 特定类型鳞片的存在是区分这两种密切相关鱼类物种的关键区别特征。
entries.example_en: The presence of a specific type of scale is a key differentia between these two closely related fish species.

entries.definition_en: able to be seen or understood as being different
entries.example_cn: 即使从远处看，这两种颜色也是可区分的。
entries.example_en: The two colors are differentiable even from a distance.

entries.definition_en: having a derivative or differential coefficient
entries.example_cn: 该函数在其定义域内的每一点都是可微的。
entries.example_en: The function is differentiable at every point in its domain.

entries.definition_en: relating to or showing a difference between things
entries.example_cn: 差别工资反映了两种工作之间不同的风险水平。
entries.example_en: The differential pay reflects the different levels of risk between the two jobs.

entries.definition_en: involving or containing one or more derivatives
entries.example_cn: 这个微分方程描述了人口随时间的变化。
entries.example_en: The differential equation describes how the population changes over time.

entries.definition_en: a quality or feature that distinguishes one thing from another similar thing
entries.example_cn: 他们成功的关键区别在于对团队合作的投入。
entries.example_en: The differential factor in their success was their dedication to teamwork.

entries.definition_cn: 变量的无穷小变化量，或在线性近似中表示变化的函数；微分
entries.definition_en: an infinitesimal change in a variable, or a function representing change in a linear approximation
entries.example_cn: 对于 f(x) = x²，其微分为 df = 2x dx。
entries.example_en: For f(x) = x², the differential is df = 2x dx.

entries.definition_en: a bevel gear used on the rear axle of automobiles to allow wheels to rotate at different speeds on curves
entries.example_cn: 差速器使汽车能够平稳转弯而不打滑。
entries.example_en: The differential allows the car to turn smoothly without skidding.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows differences
entries.example_cn: 这两个群体受新政策的影响程度不同。
entries.example_en: The two groups were differentially affected by the new policy.

entries.definition_en: to show or make clear that something is different from something else
entries.example_cn: 区分事实和观点很重要。
entries.example_en: It is important to differentiate between fact and opinion.

entries.definition_en: to distinguish someone or something from others
entries.example_cn: 她的善良使她与同事区分开来。
entries.example_en: Her kindness differentiates her from her colleagues.

entries.definition_en: to calculate the derivative of a mathematical function
entries.example_cn: 学生必须学习如何对多项式求导。
entries.example_en: Students must learn how to differentiate polynomials.

entries.definition_cn: 在发育过程中变得不同
entries.definition_en: to become different during the process of development
entries.example_cn: 随着胚胎的生长，细胞分化为各种组织。
entries.example_en: The cells differentiate into various tissues as the embryo grows.

entries.definition_cn: 在进化中分化并形成不同特征
entries.definition_en: to develop differently in form or function during evolution
entries.example_cn: 数百万年来，该物种进化以适应沙漠生存。
entries.example_en: Over millions of years, the species differentiated to survive in the desert.

entries.definition_cn: 变得独特并具备不同特征
entries.definition_en: to become distinct and acquire a different character
entries.example_cn: 随着社区分离，这两种方言变得不同。
entries.example_en: The two dialects differentiated as the communities moved apart.

entries.definition_en: made different, especially during development
entries.example_cn: 这些有差异的产品面向不同的细分市场。
entries.example_en: The differentiated products target different market segments.

entries.definition_en: adapted during development to a specific function or environment
entries.example_cn: 细胞特化以在体内执行专门任务。
entries.example_en: The cells become differentiated to perform specialized tasks in the body.

entries.definition_en: the act of distinguishing between things based on their characteristics or attributes
entries.example_cn: 该品牌依靠产品差异化在市场中脱颖而出。
entries.example_en: The brand relies on product differentiation to stand out in the market.

entries.definition_en: the mathematical process of obtaining the derivative of a function
entries.example_cn: 微积分是研究求导和积分的数学分支。
entries.example_en: Calculus is the branch of mathematics concerned with differentiation and integration.

entries.definition_cn: （细胞或组织为特定功能而发生的）分化过程
entries.definition_en: the process by which cells or tissues become specialized for particular functions
entries.example_cn: 干细胞的分化使它们能够变成各种类型的组织。
entries.example_en: The differentiation of stem cells allows them to become various types of tissue.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that distinguishes one from others
entries.example_cn: 卓越的客户服务是该公司在竞争激烈的市场中的主要差异化因素。
entries.example_en: Excellent customer service is the company's main differentiator in a competitive market.

entries.definition_en: in another and different manner
entries.example_cn: 人们对同样的情况会有不同的反应。
entries.example_en: People react differently to the same situation.

entries.definition_en: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.example_cn: 这场困难的考试需要极大的脑力才能理解。

entries.definition_cn: 难以应付的；难以控制的

entries.definition_cn: 难以完成或应对的状态；困难；难度
entries.definition_en: the state of being difficult or hard to do or deal with

entries.example_en: The difficulty of the exam made many students feel discouraged.

entries.definition_cn: 妨碍实现目标的障碍；困难

entries.example_en: The lack of funds created a difficulty that delayed the project's completion.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of shy uncertainty or lack of self-confidence
entries.example_cn: 他的羞怯使他不敢在会议上发言。
entries.example_en: His diffidence prevented him from speaking up in the meeting.

entries.definition_en: lacking self-confidence; shy and unsure of oneself
entries.example_cn: 这位缺乏自信的发言人在回答问题前犹豫了。
entries.example_en: The diffident speaker hesitated before answering the question.

entries.definition_en: showing modest reserve and shyness
entries.example_cn: 她对自己的成就很谦逊，不愿成为焦点。
entries.example_en: She was diffident about her achievements and avoided the spotlight.

entries.definition_en: in a shy, modest, or unsure manner

entries.example_en: She diffidently accepted the award, thanking her team.

entries.definition_en: to undergo diffraction; to bend and spread out when passing an obstacle
entries.example_cn: 当光波通过狭缝时会发生衍射。

entries.definition_en: the bending of light waves around sharp edges or through narrow openings, creating patterns of light and dark bands
entries.example_cn: 该实验展示了光通过狭缝时的衍射现象。
entries.example_en: The experiment demonstrated the diffraction of light passing through a narrow slit.

entries.definition_en: spread out over a wide area; not concentrated
entries.example_cn: 人口分散在广阔的乡村地区。

entries.example_cn: 他的解释冗长难懂。

entries.example_cn: 房间被透过云层漫射的日光照亮。
entries.example_en: The room was lit by diffuse daylight coming through the clouds.

entries.example_cn: 气味开始在房间里扩散。

entries.example_en: The findings were diffused through the scientific community.

entries.example_en: The diffused smoke spread through the room.

entries.example_cn: 来自大窗户的柔和漫射光均匀地照亮了房间。

entries.definition_en: in a way that is spread out or not clearly focused

entries.example_en: He spoke diffusely about the project, failing to mention the budget.

entries.definition_cn: 使声波扩散以改善声音分布的装置

entries.example_en: The diffusing light created a soft atmosphere in the room.

entries.definition_en: the process in which a substance moves from an area of high concentration to an area of lower concentration
entries.example_cn: 香水的扩散使整个房间都充满了气味。
entries.example_en: The diffusion of perfume scent fills the entire room.

entries.definition_en: the spread of social institutions, myths, and skills from one society to another
entries.example_cn: 技术的传播改变了人们全球沟通的方式。
entries.example_en: The diffusion of technology has changed how people communicate globally.

entries.definition_en: the act of dispersing or diffusing something
entries.example_cn: 种子的散布有助于植物在新区域繁殖。
entries.example_en: The diffusion of seeds helps plants reproduce in new areas.

entries.definition_en: the property of being diffused or dispersed
entries.example_cn: 人群的分散使得很难找到演讲者。
entries.example_en: The diffusion of the crowd made it difficult to locate the speaker.

entries.definition_en: spreading or moving by diffusion
entries.example_cn: 该气体的扩散性质使其能迅速充满整个房间。
entries.example_en: The diffusive nature of the gas allowed it to fill the entire room quickly.

entries.definition_en: a device used to spread sound waves evenly
entries.example_cn: 这座音乐厅配备了专门的扩散板，以确保清晰的声学效果。
entries.example_en: The concert hall features a specialized diffusor to ensure clear acoustics.

entries.definition_en: an optical device that spreads light evenly
entries.example_cn: 摄影师在灯上安装了扩散器，以柔和阴影。
entries.example_en: The photographer attached a diffusor to the lamp to soften the shadows.

entries.definition_en: undergo digestion

entries.example_en: It took several hours for the heavy meal to digest.

entries.example_en: He spent the weekend digesting the vast amount of data.

entries.example_en: The professor published a digest of his research papers.

entries.example_en: She reads the weekly digest every morning.

entries.example_en: I can't digest his rude behavior any longer.

entries.example_en: The chemist digested the sample in a heated vessel.

entries.example_en: The industrial digester breaks down organic waste into biogas.

entries.example_cn: 这种食物的消化性使其适合儿童食用。

entries.definition_en: the assimilation and understanding of ideas or information

entries.definition_en: the process of breaking down organic matter (like sewage) using bacteria, chemicals, or heat

entries.example_en: The treatment plant uses bacteria to speed up the digestion of sewage.

entries.definition_cn: 助消化的；与消化有关的

entries.definition_en: any substance that promotes digestion

entries.example_en: After the heavy meal, he took a digestive to help his stomach.

entries.example_en: A large digger was used to clear the road.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to dig

entries.example_en: The digging took several hours.

entries.definition_en: of a circuit or device that represents magnitudes in digits

entries.definition_en: any plant of the genus Digitalis, known for its medicinal properties
entries.example_cn: 园丁从花坛里拔掉了洋地黄属植物，因为它对猫有毒。
entries.example_en: The gardener removed the digitalis from the flower bed because it is poisonous to cats.

entries.definition_en: to convert information into digital form for use in computers

entries.example_cn: 医生仔细监测患者，以便有效给予洋地黄治疗而不引起毒性。

entries.example_en: The scanner acts as a digitizer for the old photographs.

entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed digitoxin to manage the patient's congestive heart failure.

entries.definition_en: having or showing dignity, especially with a formal or stately appearance
entries.example_cn: 那位老人庄严地缓缓走过过道。
entries.example_en: The dignified old man walked slowly down the aisle.

entries.definition_en: having or showing self-esteem and pride
entries.example_cn: 她举止端庄，从不让人看轻她。
entries.example_en: She carried herself in a dignified manner, never letting others belittle her.

entries.definition_cn: 把……视为值得认可或考虑
entries.definition_en: to treat someone or something as worthy of recognition or consideration
entries.example_cn: 她拒绝对他的侮辱做出回应，以示不屑。
entries.example_en: She refused to dignify his insults with an answer.

entries.definition_en: to raise the status or importance of something
entries.example_cn: 委员会决定通过正式议程来提升这次会议的地位。
entries.example_en: The committee decided to dignify the meeting with a formal agenda.

entries.definition_en: giving someone a sense of dignity or honor
entries.example_cn: 这场仪式对老兵们来说是一次赋予尊严的经历。
entries.example_en: The ceremony was a dignifying experience for the veterans.

entries.definition_en: an important or influential person, especially one of high rank or position
entries.example_cn: 这位显要人物乘坐私人飞机抵达机场。
entries.example_en: The dignitary arrived at the airport in a private jet.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being worthy of respect and admiration
entries.example_cn: 她对待每个人都充满尊严和尊重。

entries.definition_en: formal and serious behavior and appearance

entries.definition_en: a high social rank or official position

entries.definition_en: a cardiac glycoside medication derived from digitalis, used to treat heart failure and irregular heartbeats

entries.definition_en: two letters written one after the other that represent a single sound

entries.definition_cn: 有向图（数学中由带方向的边连接的顶点组成的图）

entries.example_en: The computer scientist represented the network as a digraph.

entries.definition_en: to turn aside from the main subject of attention or argument
entries.example_cn: 请不要离题；我们必须完成这个话题。
entries.example_en: Please do not digress; we must finish this topic.

entries.definition_en: to wander from a direct or straight course
entries.example_cn: 小路偏离了直线，进入了森林。
entries.example_en: The trail digressed from its direct course and entered the forest.

entries.definition_en: a part of a speech or text that departs from the main subject
entries.example_cn: 教授关于古代历史的离题延误了讲座。
entries.example_en: The professor's digression on ancient history delayed the lecture.

entries.definition_en: a turning aside of one's course or attention from the main point
entries.example_cn: 我为此偏离主题道歉；让我们回到预算上来。
entries.example_en: I apologize for the digression; let us return to the budget.

entries.definition_en: a wandering from the main path during a journey
entries.example_cn: 我们穿过森林偏离主路去看了瀑布。
entries.example_en: We took a digression through the forest to see the waterfall.

entries.definition_en: tending to wander away from the main point or cover too many subjects
entries.example_cn: 教授的离题讲座在一个小时内涵盖了历史、政治和艺术。
entries.example_en: The professor's digressive lecture covered history, politics, and art in one hour.

entries.definition_en: constituting a digression; off-topic
entries.example_cn: 他那些离题的评论分散了听众对严肃议题的注意力。
entries.example_en: His digressive comments distracted the audience from the serious issue.

entries.definition_en: temporary living quarters

entries.example_en: While the new building is under construction, the workers are staying in the digs.

entries.definition_en: in a state of disrepair or ruin as a result of age or neglect
entries.example_cn: 那座破败的建筑已被列入拆除计划。

entries.definition_en: the state of being in a state of disrepair due to age or long use
entries.example_cn: 这座古堡的破败从摇摇欲坠的墙壁上显而易见。

entries.definition_en: the process of becoming dilapidated

entries.example_cn: 水常被用作浓缩清洁液的稀释剂。

entries.example_cn: 在使用清洁剂之前，你应该先将其与水稀释。
entries.example_en: You should dilute the cleaning agent with water before using it on the floor.

entries.example_en: The artist added water to achieve the desired dilution of the paint.

entries.definition_en: to become dim or lusterless

entries.example_en: The colors of the painting began to dim over time.

entries.example_en: The dim-witted plan failed to consider the risks.

entries.definition_en: a construct whereby objects or individuals can be distinguished

entries.example_en: We must consider the social dimension of the problem.

entries.example_cn: x、y 和 z 坐标确定一个点在空间中的位置。

entries.definition_en: magnitude or extent

entries.definition_en: to shape or form to required dimensions
entries.example_cn: 木匠按尺寸将木材加工成桌子。
entries.example_en: The carpenter dimensioned the wood for the table.

entries.definition_en: relating to dimensions

entries.example_en: The dimensional analysis helps us understand the physical properties of the object.

entries.definition_cn: 有维度的；有性格或地位的
entries.definition_en: having dimension; having character or stature

entries.example_en: The novel is a dimensional character study of a struggling artist.

entries.definition_en: the spatial property of having dimensions
entries.example_cn: 数据集的维度性会影响其处理方式。
entries.example_en: The dimensionality of the data set affects how it is processed.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound made of two identical molecules joined together

entries.example_cn: 这位患者嗅觉减退。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered from a diminished sense of smell.

entries.definition_cn: 显得不那么重要、令人印象深刻或有价值的
entries.definition_en: made to seem less important, impressive, or valuable
entries.example_cn: 他因受到批评而觉得自己不再那么重要。
entries.example_en: He felt diminished by the criticism.

entries.definition_en: (of musical intervals) reduction by a semitone of any perfect or minor musical interval
entries.example_cn: 作曲家在该和弦中使用了减五度音程。
entries.example_en: The composer used a diminished fifth in the chord.

entries.definition_en: becoming smaller or less in amount
entries.example_cn: 资源的日益减少使得该项目难以完成。
entries.example_en: The diminishing supply of resources made the project difficult to complete.

entries.definition_en: (music) a gradual decrease in loudness
entries.example_cn: 乐团演奏了一段长长的渐弱，使交响乐柔和地结束。
entries.example_en: The orchestra played a long diminuendo to end the symphony softly.

entries.definition_en: (music) gradually decreasing in volume
entries.example_cn: 指挥示意音乐家们开始渐弱段落。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled the musicians to begin the diminuendo section.

entries.definition_en: a reduction in size, amount, or importance
entries.example_cn: 今年公司的利润明显减少了。
entries.example_en: There has been a noticeable diminution in the company's profits this year.

entries.definition_en: the act of making something smaller or less
entries.example_cn: 政府宣布削减公共服务预算。
entries.example_en: The government announced a diminution of the budget for public services.

entries.definition_cn: 以较短时值演奏的主题变体
entries.definition_en: a musical theme played in shorter notes than the original
entries.example_cn: 作曲家在第二乐章中加入了主旋律的减值变奏。
entries.example_en: The composer included a diminution of the main melody in the second movement.

entries.definition_en: very small in size
entries.example_cn: 酒店房间虽小但很舒适。
entries.example_en: The hotel room was diminutive but cozy.

entries.definition_cn: 表示微小、年幼、不重要或亲昵的词形
entries.definition_en: a word form expressing smallness, youth, unimportance, or endearment
entries.example_cn: “booklet”是“book”的指小形式，意思是“小书”。
entries.example_en: “Booklet” is a diminutive of “book”, meaning “small book”.

entries.definition_cn: 轻薄结实的条纹或方格织物，常用于窗帘或床罩
entries.definition_en: a light, strong fabric woven with stripes or squares, often used for curtains or bedcovers
entries.example_cn: 她为新的窗帘买了一块漂亮的提花棉布。
entries.example_en: She bought a beautiful dimity for the new curtains.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not clear or distinct
entries.example_cn: 他模糊地辨认出阴影中的身影。
entries.example_en: He could dimly make out the figure in the shadows.

entries.definition_en: with a low or weak light
entries.example_cn: 房间被一支蜡烛昏暗地照亮。
entries.example_en: The room was lit dimly by a single candle.

entries.definition_en: in a way that lacks interest or vitality
entries.example_cn: 这场演出表演得乏味，未能吸引观众。
entries.example_en: The performance was delivered dimly, failing to engage the audience.

entries.definition_en: a device used to control the brightness of an electric light by varying the current
entries.example_cn: 她调节调光器，为晚宴营造更柔和的氛围。
entries.example_en: She adjusted the dimmer to create a softer atmosphere for the dinner party.

entries.definition_cn: （北美）用于选择车辆近光灯或远光灯的开关
entries.definition_en: a North American switch used to select between a vehicle's low and high headlamp beams
entries.example_cn: 他拨动远近光切换开关，将远光灯切换成近光灯。
entries.example_en: He flicked the dimmer to switch from high beam to low beam.

entries.definition_en: the state of a place being poorly lit or lacking sufficient light
entries.example_cn: 地下室里的昏暗使得很难找到旧文件。
entries.example_en: The dimness of the basement made it difficult to find the old files.

entries.definition_en: the quality of light or sound that lacks brilliance or intensity
entries.example_cn: 路灯的暗淡加剧了小巷的诡异氛围。
entries.example_en: The dimness of the streetlights contributed to the eerie atmosphere of the alley.

entries.definition_en: the quality of lacking contrast or vividness in appearance
entries.example_cn: 这幅画普遍缺乏对比度，使得颜色混在一起。
entries.example_en: The painting suffered from a general dimness that made the colors blend together.

entries.definition_en: the state of being dim-witted or lacking intelligence
entries.example_cn: 他的愚钝使他很难理解这些简单的说明。
entries.example_en: His dimness made it difficult for him to understand the simple instructions.

entries.definition_en: occurring or existing in two different forms
entries.example_cn: 许多真菌是二态的，在凉爽的天气中以霉菌形式存在，在温暖的天气中以酵母形式存在。
entries.example_en: Many fungi are dimorphic, existing as molds in cool weather and as yeasts in warm weather.

entries.definition_en: the existence of two forms within the same animal species independent of sex
entries.example_cn: 在许多蚂蚁物种中观察到了异形现象。
entries.example_en: Social dimorphism is observed in many ant species.

entries.definition_en: the property of existing in two distinct crystalline forms
entries.example_cn: 该药物具有多晶型特性，这影响了其溶解度。
entries.example_en: The drug exhibits dimorphism, which affects its solubility.

entries.definition_cn: 脸颊或下巴上的小自然凹陷
entries.definition_en: a small natural hollow in the cheek or chin
entries.example_cn: 他左脸颊上有一个迷人的小酒窝。
entries.example_en: He has a charming dimple on his left cheek.

entries.definition_en: any slight depression in a surface
entries.example_cn: 冰球击中后，冰面上出现了一个小凹陷。
entries.example_en: A dimple appeared in the ice after the puck hit it.

entries.definition_cn: 四角仍相连的穿孔纸屑
entries.definition_en: a punched chad with all four corners still attached
entries.example_cn: 由于四角仍然相连，选票扫描仪拒绝识别这个穿孔纸屑。
entries.example_en: The ballot scanner rejected the dimple because all four corners were still attached.

entries.definition_cn: 微笑时使脸颊出现酒窝
entries.definition_en: to produce dimples while smiling
entries.example_cn: 她微笑着迎接老朋友，脸颊上露出了酒窝。
entries.example_en: She dimpled as she greeted her old friends.

entries.definition_en: to mark with, or as if with, dimples
entries.example_cn: 机器在高尔夫球表面制造了凹痕。
entries.example_en: The machine dimpled the surface of the golf balls.

entries.definition_en: a stupid and incompetent person
entries.example_cn: 别听那个傻瓜的；他根本不懂规则。
entries.example_en: Don't listen to that dimwit; he doesn't understand the rules.

entries.definition_en: a loud, harsh, or strident noise
entries.example_cn: 交通的喧嚣声让人无法入睡。
entries.example_en: The din of traffic made it impossible to sleep.

entries.definition_en: a noisy disturbance or commotion
entries.example_cn: 派对制造的喧闹声一直持续到黎明。
entries.example_en: The party created a din that lasted until dawn.

entries.definition_cn: 发出如炮火般的轰鸣声
entries.definition_en: to make a loud, resonant sound, like artillery
entries.example_cn: 大炮开始在山谷中轰鸣。
entries.example_en: The cannons began to din across the valley.

entries.definition_cn: 通过不断重复灌输（某种观念）
entries.definition_en: to instill something into a person by constant repetition
entries.example_cn: 老师反复向学生灌输这些规则。
entries.example_en: The teacher dinned the rules into the students' heads.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Kuwait, equal to 1,000 fils
entries.example_cn: 科威特第纳尔分为1000费尔。
entries.example_en: The Kuwaiti dinar is subdivided into 1,000 fils.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Iraq, equal to 1,000 fils
entries.example_cn: 伊拉克第纳尔上印有该国的国徽。
entries.example_en: Iraqi dinars are printed with the country's national emblem.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Jordan, equal to 1,000 fils
entries.example_cn: 约旦第纳尔在该地区广泛使用。
entries.example_en: The Jordanian dinar is widely used in the region.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Tunisia
entries.example_cn: 游客在突尼斯使用第纳尔购买商品。
entries.example_en: Tourists in Tunisia pay for goods using the dinar.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Bahrain, equal to 1,000 fils
entries.example_cn: 巴林第纳尔的价值比许多其他货币高。
entries.example_en: The Bahraini dinar has a high value compared to many other currencies.

entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Libya
entries.example_cn: 利比亚第纳尔是非洲最强的货币之一。
entries.example_en: The Libyan dinar is one of the strongest currencies in Africa.

entries.definition_cn: 伊朗货币单位，100 第纳尔等于 1 里亚尔
entries.definition_en: the currency unit of Iran, where 100 dinars equal 1 rial
entries.example_cn: 伊朗第纳尔的汇率每日波动。
entries.example_en: The exchange rate for the Iranian dinar fluctuates daily.

entries.definition_en: the former currency unit of Yugoslavia
entries.example_cn: 历史记录中常提到南斯拉夫第纳尔。
entries.example_en: Historical records often mention the Yugoslav dinar.

entries.definition_en: to have supper or eat dinner
entries.example_cn: 我们通常晚上七点吃晚饭。
entries.example_en: We usually dine at seven o'clock in the evening.

usage.label: dine with someone
usage.pattern: The source identifies dine as an intransitive verb meaning eat dinner.

entries.definition_en: to host or provide dinner for someone
entries.example_cn: 市长今晚将设宴招待来访的贵宾。
entries.example_en: The mayor will dine the visiting dignitaries tonight.

entries.definition_cn: 类似餐车的小餐馆（美国）
entries.definition_en: a restaurant that resembles a dining car
entries.example_cn: 我们在主街那家经典的 diner 餐厅吃了早餐。
entries.example_en: We had breakfast at the classic diner on Main Street.

entries.definition_en: a passenger car where food is served in transit
entries.example_cn: 火车行驶时，乘客从餐车买了三明治。
entries.example_en: Passengers bought sandwiches from the diner while the train was moving.

entries.definition_en: a person eating a meal (especially in a restaurant)
entries.example_cn: 这位食客点了一份大牛排和薯条。
entries.example_en: The diner ordered a large steak and fries.

entries.definition_en: an informal word for money
entries.example_cn: 他用自己带的钱付了餐费。
entries.example_en: He paid for the meal with his own dinero.

usage.label: slang; uncountable
usage.pattern: Source w26173r0 explicitly supplies both labels.

entries.definition_cn: 供室内非正式用餐使用的一套桌椅
entries.definition_en: a table and chairs for an informal indoor dining area
entries.example_cn: 我们买了一套餐桌椅，包括一张圆桌和四把椅子。
entries.example_en: We bought a compact dinette with a round table and four chairs.

entries.definition_en: a small dining area located off the main kitchen
entries.example_cn: 厨房角落的小餐室非常适合喝早咖啡。
entries.example_en: The dinette in the corner of the kitchen was perfect for morning coffee.

entries.definition_en: a short, clear ringing sound
entries.example_cn: 铃铛发出了一声响亮的叮当声。
entries.example_en: The bell gave a loud ding.

entries.definition_en: a small dent or mark left on a surface by a blow
entries.example_cn: 汽车侧面有一个凹痕。
entries.example_en: There was a ding in the side of the car.

entries.definition_en: to make a ringing sound like a bell
entries.example_cn: 电话开始发出叮当声。
entries.example_en: The phone started to ding.

entries.definition_en: to hit or strike something
entries.example_cn: 球撞击了金属标牌。
entries.example_en: The ball dinged the metal sign.

entries.definition_en: the noise made by a bell
entries.example_cn: 教堂钟声的叮当声在山谷中回荡。
entries.example_en: The ding-dong of the church bell echoed through the valley.

entries.definition_cn: 势均力敌的；竞争激烈的（非正式）
entries.definition_en: closely fought (informal)
entries.example_cn: 两队进行了一场势均力敌的比赛，一直胶着到最后一分钟。
entries.example_en: The teams played a ding-dong match until the final minute.

entries.definition_en: a silly or foolish person
entries.example_cn: 别像个傻瓜一样，听从指示。
entries.example_en: Stop acting like a dingbat and listen to the instructions.

entries.definition_en: to make a sound like a bell ringing
entries.example_cn: 火车进站时，铃声开始叮当响起。
entries.example_en: The bell began to dingdong as the train approached the station.

entries.definition_en: vigorously or fiercely
entries.example_cn: 两队为争夺冠军展开了激烈的较量。
entries.example_en: The two teams battled dingdong for the championship.

entries.definition_en: to make a dent or impression in something
entries.example_cn: 那个沉重的箱子在木柜侧面留下了凹痕。
entries.example_en: The heavy box dinged the side of the wooden cabinet.

entries.definition_en: to make something dingy
entries.example_cn: 浓雾使窗外的景色变得昏暗。
entries.example_en: The thick fog dinged the view from the window.

entries.definition_en: a discoloration caused by dirt
entries.example_cn: 旧地毯上有一块因猫抓地板而留下的变色痕迹。
entries.example_en: The old carpet has a dinge where the cat scratched the floor.

entries.definition_en: a small boat with seats across the bottom and oarlocks for rowing
entries.example_cn: 他们划着小船到了岛上。
entries.example_en: They rowed the dinghy to the island.

entries.definition_en: a small, secluded hollow in a landscape, often covered with trees
entries.example_cn: 我们在山脚下发现了一个宁静的幽谷。
entries.example_en: We found a peaceful dingle at the foot of the mountain.

entries.definition_en: a wild dog native to Australia that looks like a wolf and is yellowish-brown in color
entries.example_cn: 那只澳洲野犬在山顶上对着月亮嚎叫。
entries.example_en: The dingo howled at the moon from the top of the hill.

entries.definition_en: thickly covered with ingrained dirt or soot
entries.example_cn: 厨房的窗户因多年的油烟而布满污垢。
entries.example_en: The kitchen window was dingy from years of smoke and grease.

entries.definition_en: discolored by impurities; not bright and clear
entries.example_cn: 暗淡的黄色墙壁让房间显得狭小而阴郁。
entries.example_en: The dingy yellow walls made the room feel small and gloomy.

entries.definition_en: dark, dull, or gloomy in appearance or atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 废弃工厂阴郁的氛围让访客们感到沮丧。
entries.example_en: The dingy atmosphere of the abandoned factory discouraged the visitors.

entries.definition_cn: 用餐；进餐（尤指作为社交活动的晚餐）
entries.definition_en: the activity of eating, especially dinner, often as a social occasion
entries.example_cn: 与客户共进晚餐需要周密安排。
entries.example_en: Dining with clients requires careful planning.

entries.definition_cn: 大学或学院里主要用于用餐的大厅
entries.definition_en: a large room in a college or university used mainly for eating meals
entries.example_cn: 学生们在食堂聚集吃晚餐。
entries.example_en: Students gather in the dining-hall for their evening meals.

entries.definition_en: a room used for eating meals
entries.example_cn: 我们通常在餐厅吃晚饭。
entries.example_en: We usually have dinner in the dining-room.

entries.definition_en: a small locomotive
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一台用于搬运铁轨的罕见小型机车。
entries.example_en: The museum displays a rare dinkey used for moving rails.

entries.definition_en: small and unattractive or insignificant (US informal)
entries.example_cn: 他们住在一间小而不起眼的旅馆房间里，但旅途很愉快。
entries.example_en: They stayed in a dinky hotel room, but they had a great trip.

entries.definition_en: small and attractive (British informal)
entries.example_cn: 她去参加聚会时穿了一条小巧漂亮的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She wore a dinky little dress to the party.

entries.definition_en: a small locomotive
entries.example_cn: 那辆小型机车在迷你铁轨上哐当哐当地行驶。
entries.example_en: The dinky chugged along the miniature railway track.

entries.definition_en: the main meal eaten in the evening or at noon
entries.example_cn: 我们通常七点吃晚饭。
entries.example_en: We usually have dinner at seven o'clock.

entries.definition_en: a formal meal or social event at which people eat dinner together
entries.example_cn: 公司举办宴会庆祝周年纪念日。
entries.example_en: The company held a dinner to celebrate its anniversary.

entries.definition_en: the customary or habitual hour for the evening meal
entries.example_cn: 这家人通常在晚餐时间聚在一起分享故事。
entries.example_en: The family usually gathers at dinnertime to share stories.

entries.definition_cn: 用餐时使用的餐具（如盘子、大盘和盛菜碗等）
entries.definition_en: the tableware (plates and platters and serving bowls etc.) used in serving a meal
entries.example_cn: 她仔细清洗了全家晚餐后所有的餐具。
entries.example_en: She carefully washed all the dinnerware after the family dinner.

entries.definition_en: a marine protozoan with two flagella that is a major component of plankton
entries.example_cn: 甲藻的爆发有时会使海水变成红色。
entries.example_en: Blooms of dinoflagellates can sometimes turn the ocean water red.

entries.definition_en: any of numerous extinct terrestrial reptiles that lived during the Mesozoic era
entries.example_cn: 科学家在偏远的山谷中发现了一种新的恐龙物种。
entries.example_en: Scientists discovered a new species of dinosaur in the remote valley.

entries.definition_en: a means or method of achieving something, especially by force or effort
entries.example_cn: 他靠辛勤工作取得了成功。
entries.example_en: He succeeded by dint of hard work.

entries.definition_en: belonging to or governed by a diocese
entries.example_cn: 教区主教为大教堂任命了一位新助理主教。
entries.example_en: The diocesan bishop appointed a new vicar for the cathedral.

entries.definition_en: a bishop who has authority over a diocese
entries.example_cn: 教区主教视察了各个教区的学校。
entries.example_en: The diocesan visited the parishes to inspect the schools.

entries.definition_en: the area of land under the authority of a bishop
entries.example_cn: 大教堂是该教区的所在地。
entries.example_en: The cathedral is the seat of the diocese.

entries.definition_en: a semiconductor that consists of a p-n junction
entries.example_cn: 现代电子学严重依赖硅二极管进行信号处理。
entries.example_en: Modern electronics rely heavily on silicon diodes for signal processing.

entries.definition_en: a thermionic tube having two electrodes; used as a rectifier
entries.example_cn: 这台旧收音机使用真空二极管将交流电转换为直流电。
entries.example_en: The old radio used a vacuum diode to convert alternating current to direct current.

entries.definition_en: having male and female reproductive organs in separate plants or animals
entries.example_cn: 柳树是雌雄异株的，意味着单株树木只开雄花或雌花。
entries.example_en: Willows are dioecious, meaning individual trees bear either male or female flowers.

entries.definition_en: an alcohol containing two hydroxyl groups in each molecule
entries.example_cn: 乙二醇是一种常用于防冻剂的常见二醇。
entries.example_en: Ethylene glycol is a common diol used in antifreeze.

entries.definition_en: A unit used to measure the refractive power of a lens.
entries.example_cn: 验光师配了一副屈光度为 -2.0 的眼镜来矫正她的近视。
entries.example_en: The optometrist prescribed glasses with a diopter of -2.0 to correct her nearsightedness.

entries.definition_cn: 双筒望远镜或相机取景器的屈光度调节装置
entries.definition_en: The adjustment mechanism for focusing the view through binoculars or a camera viewfinder.
entries.example_cn: 她调节双筒望远镜的屈光度调节装置，直到图像变得清晰。
entries.example_en: She turned the diopter adjustment on the binoculars until the image was sharp.

entries.definition_cn: 展示场景的立体模型，通常在绘制的背景前布置模型
entries.definition_en: a three-dimensional display showing a scene, with models arranged before a painted background
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一个令人惊叹的古代战役立体模型。
entries.example_en: The museum features a stunning diorama of the ancient battle.

entries.definition_en: a granular crystalline intrusive rock
entries.example_cn: 这座山峰几乎完全由坚硬的闪长岩构成。
entries.example_en: The mountain peak is composed almost entirely of solid diorite.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound containing two oxygen atoms in each molecule
entries.example_cn: 二氧化碳是我们呼吸时释放的一种气体。
entries.example_en: Carbon dioxide is a gas released when we breathe.

entries.definition_en: a highly toxic and cancer-causing chemical that is often found as an unwanted substance in weed killers
entries.example_cn: 该工厂因当地水源中检测到二噁英而被关闭。
entries.example_en: The factory was shut down after dioxin was detected in the local water supply.

entries.definition_en: to put something into a liquid briefly
entries.example_cn: 她把面包蘸进汤里。
entries.example_en: She dipped the bread into the soup.

entries.definition_en: to put food into a liquid while eating
entries.example_cn: 他把薯条蘸了莎莎酱。
entries.example_en: He dipped the chips in the salsa.

entries.definition_en: to decrease slightly
entries.example_cn: 昨晚气温降到了零度以下。
entries.example_en: The temperature dipped below zero last night.

entries.definition_en: to stain something by putting it in a liquid
entries.example_cn: 她把布料浸入染料中以改变颜色。
entries.example_en: She dipped the fabric in dye to change its color.

entries.definition_en: a low point or depression in a surface
entries.example_cn: 前方道路有一个凹陷处。
entries.example_en: There is a dip in the road ahead.

entries.definition_en: a tasty liquid or mixture used for dipping food
entries.example_cn: 巧克力蘸料非常美味。
entries.example_en: The chocolate dip was delicious.

entries.definition_en: the angle between a magnetic needle and the horizon
entries.example_cn: 指南针显示该地区磁倾角很大。
entries.example_en: The compass shows a significant dip in this region.

entries.definition_en: a person who steals from people's pockets in public
entries.example_cn: 小心不要让包挂得太低，否则可能会引起扒手的注意。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to let your bag hang low, or you might attract a dip.

entries.definition_en: an antihistamine drug (brand name Benadryl) used to treat allergies like hay fever and motion sickness
entries.example_cn: 医生给她开了苯海拉明来治疗严重的花粉症症状。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed diphenhydramine to help with her severe hay fever symptoms.

entries.definition_en: a serious contagious disease caused by bacteria, which forms a false membrane in the throat and makes breathing difficult
entries.example_cn: 医生警告说，如果不及时治疗，白喉可能是致命的。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned that diphtheria can be fatal if not treated quickly.

entries.definition_en: a vowel sound that begins near the position for one vowel and moves toward the position for another
entries.example_cn: 单词 'house' 包含双元音 /aʊ/。
entries.example_en: The word 'house' contains the diphthong /aʊ/.

entries.definition_en: paralysis affecting corresponding parts on both sides of the body
entries.example_cn: 这个孩子出生时患有脑性瘫痪。
entries.example_en: The child was born with cerebral diplegia.

entries.definition_en: a huge, four-legged herbivorous dinosaur with a long neck and tail from the late Jurassic period
entries.example_cn: 梁龙的化石已在北美西部被发现。
entries.example_en: Fossils of the diplodocus have been found in western North America.

entries.definition_en: of a cell or organism having two sets of chromosomes or twice the haploid number
entries.example_cn: 体内的二倍体细胞分裂产生单倍体配子。
entries.example_en: The diploid cells in the body divide to produce haploid gametes.

entries.definition_en: an organism or cell having the normal amount of DNA per cell; i.e., two sets of chromosomes or twice the haploid number
entries.example_cn: 人类是二倍体生物，意味着我们的细胞包含两套染色体。
entries.example_en: Humans are diploid organisms, meaning our cells contain two sets of chromosomes.

entries.definition_en: a document certifying the successful completion of a course of study
entries.example_cn: 她把大学文凭挂在了墙上。
entries.example_en: She hung her university diploma on the wall.

entries.definition_en: the art and practice of conducting negotiations between nations
entries.example_cn: 大使的外交努力帮助解决了两国之间的冲突。
entries.example_en: The ambassador's diplomacy helped to resolve the conflict between the two countries.

entries.definition_en: the ability to handle difficult situations carefully and skillfully
entries.example_cn: 她在处理愤怒的顾客时表现出了极大的圆滑处理能力。
entries.example_en: She showed great diplomacy in dealing with the angry customers.

entries.definition_en: wisdom and skill in managing public affairs
entries.example_cn: 他在政府多年的外交经历使他深刻理解公共政策。
entries.example_en: His years of diplomacy in government gave him a deep understanding of public policy.

entries.definition_en: a person who works for their country in international relations
entries.example_cn: 这位外交官促成了两国之间的和平条约。
entries.example_en: The diplomat negotiated a peace treaty between the two nations.

entries.definition_en: a person who handles difficult situations with tact and skill
entries.example_cn: 作为家里的外交官，他总是能让大家平静下来。
entries.example_en: As a diplomat in the family, he always managed to calm everyone down.

entries.definition_cn: 持专业文凭的医学专家
entries.definition_en: a medical specialist whose competence has been certified by a professional diploma
entries.example_cn: 作为持专业文凭的医学专家，她得到了医学委员会在其领域的认可。
entries.example_en: As a diplomate, she is recognized as an expert in her field by the medical board.

entries.definition_en: skillful in handling sensitive situations tactfully
entries.example_cn: 他给出了一个圆滑的回答以避免冒犯她。
entries.example_en: He gave a diplomatic answer to avoid offending her.

entries.definition_en: relating to diplomacy
entries.example_cn: 这次外交任务取得了成功。
entries.example_en: The diplomatic mission was successful.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows skill in dealing with difficult situations
entries.example_cn: 大使以圆融的方式发言，避免冒犯东道主。
entries.example_en: The ambassador spoke diplomatically to avoid offending the host.

entries.definition_en: an official who is engaged in international negotiations
entries.example_cn: 这位外交官不知疲倦地工作，以解决两国之间的边界争端。
entries.example_en: The diplomatist worked tirelessly to resolve the border dispute between the two nations.

entries.definition_en: a visual condition where a single object appears as two separate images
entries.example_cn: 这位患者在眼部受伤后抱怨出现复视。
entries.example_en: The patient complained of diplopia after the eye injury.

entries.definition_en: having or relating to a dipole
entries.example_cn: 由于正负电荷分离，该分子具有偶极结构。
entries.example_en: The molecule has a dipolar structure due to the separation of positive and negative charges.

entries.definition_en: a system consisting of two equal and opposite electric or magnetic charges separated by a small distance
entries.example_cn: 由于电荷分布不对称，该分子具有永久偶极矩。
entries.example_en: The molecule has a permanent dipole due to its asymmetric charge distribution.

entries.definition_en: an antenna consisting of two rods connected to a transmission line at the center
entries.example_cn: 收音机使用偶极天线来接收广播塔的信号。
entries.example_en: The radio receiver uses a dipole to capture signals from the broadcast tower.

entries.definition_en: having abnormal sagging of the spine, especially in horses
entries.example_cn: 那匹老马长途跋涉后看起来疲惫不堪，脊柱下塌。
entries.example_en: The old horse looked tired and dipped after the long journey.

entries.definition_en: a ladle with a cup and a long handle
entries.example_cn: 她用长柄勺从大锅里盛汤。
entries.example_en: She used a dipper to serve the soup from the large pot.

entries.definition_cn: 将物体浸入液体的人或工具
entries.definition_en: a person or thing that dips something into a liquid
entries.example_cn: 巧克力浸蘸工将奶油夹心浸入温热的巧克力中。
entries.example_en: A chocolate dipper dipped the cream centers into warm chocolate.

entries.definition_en: a small stocky diving bird without webbed feet that lives in fast-flowing streams
entries.example_cn: 河乌在湍急河流的岩石底部跳跃前行。
entries.example_en: The dipper hopped along the rocky bottom of the rushing river.

entries.definition_en: a person who habitually drinks alcohol to excess
entries.example_cn: 这位酗酒者努力克制自己饮酒的冲动。
entries.example_en: The dipsomaniac struggled to control his urge to drink.

entries.definition_en: a rod with markings used to measure the level of liquid in a container
entries.example_cn: 他用量油尺检查了汽车发动机的油位。
entries.example_en: He used the dipstick to check the oil level in the car engine.

entries.definition_en: an insect having usually a single pair of functional wings with the posterior pair reduced to small knobbed structures
entries.example_cn: 那只双翅目昆虫被灯光吸引，落在了窗户上。
entries.example_en: The dipteran was attracted to the light and landed on the window.

entries.definition_en: a large tree belonging to the family Dipterocarpaceae, common in tropical rainforests
entries.example_cn: 这棵古老的龙脑香科植物为当地的建设项目提供了宝贵的木材。
entries.example_en: The ancient dipterocarp provided valuable timber for the local construction projects.

entries.definition_en: a painting or carving on two panels that are usually hinged like a book
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一幅描绘圣人一生的中世纪双联画。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a medieval diptych depicting the life of a saint.

entries.definition_cn: 由两个对比部分组成的文学作品，常从相反的角度呈现同一主题
entries.definition_en: a literary work consisting of two contrasting parts, often presenting the same subject from opposing points of view
entries.example_cn: 这部由两部分组成的文学作品先从一位富裕农民的视角讲述同一个故事，随后又从一位怀疑论者的视角讲述。
entries.example_en: The author’s diptych tells the same story first from a wealthy farmer’s perspective and then from a skeptic’s.

entries.definition_en: fraught with extreme danger; nearly hopeless
entries.example_cn: 他们面临一个毫无出路的危急局面。
entries.example_en: They faced a dire situation with no way out.

entries.definition_en: dreadful; terrible
entries.example_cn: 袭击的消息令人恐惧且可怕。
entries.example_en: The news of the attack was dire and terrifying.

entries.definition_en: direct in spatial dimensions; proceeding without deviation or interruption; straight and short
entries.example_cn: 我们走了去机场的直达路线。
entries.example_en: We took the direct route to the airport.

entries.definition_en: straightforward in means or manner or behavior or language or action
entries.example_cn: 他是一个直率的人，说话不隐瞒任何事。
entries.example_en: He is a direct person who tells the truth without hiding anything.

entries.definition_en: having no intervening persons, agents, conditions
entries.example_cn: 两个部门之间有直接的沟通渠道。
entries.example_en: There was a direct line of communication between the two departments.

entries.definition_en: without deviation
entries.example_cn: 这列火车直达伦敦，中途不停靠。
entries.example_en: The train goes direct to London without stopping.

entries.definition_en: guide or aim something toward a particular person, place, or goal
entries.example_cn: 老师将学生的注意力引向黑板。
entries.example_en: The teacher directed the students' attention to the blackboard.

entries.definition_en: command with authority
entries.example_cn: 将军将命令部队前进。
entries.example_en: The general will direct the troops to advance.

entries.definition_en: guide the actors in (plays and films)
entries.example_cn: 她将于下个月导演这部新剧。
entries.example_en: She will direct the new play next month.

entries.definition_en: govern or manage
entries.example_cn: 委员会将管理该项目直到完成。
entries.example_en: The committee will direct the project until it is finished.

entries.definition_en: having a specified direction
entries.example_cn: 定向的光束穿透了黑暗。
entries.example_en: The directed beam of light cut through the darkness.

entries.definition_en: guided or controlled by a person or organization
entries.example_cn: 该项目由一位高级经理负责管理。
entries.example_en: The project was directed by a senior manager.

entries.definition_en: a line leading to a place or point
entries.example_cn: 沿着那个方向的道路走。
entries.example_en: Follow the road in that direction.

entries.definition_en: the spatial relation between something and the course along which it points or moves
entries.example_cn: 风向突然改变了。
entries.example_en: The wind changed direction suddenly.

entries.definition_en: a message describing how something is to be done
entries.example_cn: 请仔细阅读说明。
entries.example_en: Please read the directions carefully.

entries.definition_en: something that provides direction or advice as to a decision or course of action
entries.example_cn: 她的建议给了我需要的指引。
entries.example_en: Her advice gave me the direction I needed.

entries.definition_en: a general course along which something has a tendency to develop
entries.example_cn: 公司正在朝着新的发展方向前进。
entries.example_en: The company is moving in a new direction.

entries.definition_en: the act of managing or directing something
entries.example_cn: 她负责团队的管理。
entries.example_en: She is responsible for the direction of the team.

entries.definition_en: the act of setting and holding a course
entries.example_cn: 船长设定了船的航向。
entries.example_en: The captain set the ship's direction.

entries.definition_en: a formal statement of a command or injunction to do something
entries.example_cn: 军官向士兵们发出了严格的命令。
entries.example_en: The officer gave a strict direction to the soldiers.

entries.definition_cn: 电影、戏剧等作品的导演工作；执导技巧
entries.definition_en: The work or skill of directing a film, play, or other theatrical production
entries.example_cn: 剧本很好，但导演工作不够出色。
entries.example_en: The screenplay was good, but the direction was weak.

entries.definition_en: relating to or indicating directions in space
entries.example_cn: 地图上的方向箭头帮助我们找到了出口。
entries.example_en: The directional arrows on the map helped us find the exit.

entries.definition_en: relating to direction toward a (nonspatial) goal
entries.example_cn: 公司的方向战略专注于长期增长。
entries.example_en: The company's directional strategy focuses on long-term growth.

entries.definition_en: showing the way by conducting or leading; imposing direction on
entries.example_cn: 老师给新生提供了引导性的建议。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave directional advice to the new students.

entries.definition_en: the quality of having a specific direction or moving in a particular way
entries.example_cn: 对河流定向性的研究有助于工程师预测洪水模式。
entries.example_en: The study of river directionality helps engineers predict flood patterns.

entries.definition_cn: 麦克风或天线在某一方向上比其他方向更敏感的程度
entries.definition_en: a measure of how much a microphone or antenna is more sensitive in one direction than in others
entries.example_cn: 麦克风的指向性使其能收录舞台上的声音，同时忽略观众席的噪音。
entries.example_en: The microphone's directionality allows it to pick up sound from the stage while ignoring the audience.

entries.definition_en: moving or living without a clear purpose or goal
entries.example_cn: 失业后，他感到漫无目的，对未来感到迷茫。
entries.example_en: After losing his job, he felt directionless and unsure of his future.

entries.definition_en: an official order or statement encouraging or banning an activity
entries.example_cn: 新的环境指令要求工厂减少排放。
entries.example_en: The new environmental directive requires factories to reduce emissions.

entries.definition_en: showing the way by conducting or leading; imposing direction on
entries.example_cn: 项目经理在项目开始前发表了指导性的讲话。
entries.example_en: The manager gave a directive speech to the team before the project started.

entries.definition_en: the characteristic of a device like a microphone or antenna that responds more strongly in one direction than others
entries.example_cn: 麦克风的高方向性使其能够拾取舞台上的声音，同时忽略观众的噪音。
entries.example_en: The microphone's high directivity allows it to pick up sound from the stage while ignoring audience noise.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being directive or giving orders
entries.example_cn: 这位领导管理团队的方式体现了他的指令性。
entries.example_en: The leader's directivity was evident in the way he managed the team.

entries.definition_en: in a straight line without deviation
entries.example_cn: 这条路直通机场。
entries.example_en: The road goes directly to the airport.

entries.definition_en: without delay or hesitation
entries.example_cn: 他听到消息后立即行动。
entries.example_en: He acted directly upon hearing the news.

entries.definition_cn: 直接地；不经过中间环节地
entries.definition_en: without anyone or anything intervening
entries.example_cn: 她直接向经理说话。
entries.example_en: She spoke directly to the manager.

entries.definition_en: in a forthright manner; candidly
entries.example_cn: 他直率地告诉我他不高兴。
entries.example_en: He told me directly that he was unhappy.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being honest and straightforward in attitude and speech
entries.example_cn: 我很欣赏他的直率；他总是对我实话实说，不隐瞒任何事。
entries.example_en: I appreciate his directness; he always tells me the truth without hiding anything.

entries.definition_cn: 朝目标直行的性质；直接性
entries.definition_en: the quality of following a straight course toward a goal
entries.example_cn: 她路线的直接性帮助团队按时到达现场。
entries.example_en: The directness of her route helped the team reach the site on time.

entries.definition_en: someone who supervises the actors and directs the action in the production of a show
entries.example_cn: 导演在片场给演员们下达了指令。
entries.example_en: The director gave instructions to the actors on set.

entries.definition_en: the person who directs the making of a film
entries.example_cn: 这位导演因她的最新电影获奖。
entries.example_en: The director won an award for her latest film.

entries.definition_en: member of a board of directors
entries.example_cn: 她当选为董事会董事。
entries.example_en: She was elected as a director of the board.

entries.definition_en: someone who controls resources and expenditures
entries.example_cn: 公司负责人批准了新预算。
entries.example_en: The company director approved the new budget.

entries.definition_en: the person who leads a musical group
entries.example_cn: 音乐总监带领乐团完成了最后一次排练。
entries.example_en: The musical director led the orchestra through the final rehearsal.

entries.definition_cn: 由主管领导的机构，通常是大型政府部门的下属机构。
entries.definition_en: An agency headed by a director, usually a subdivision of a major government department.
entries.example_cn: 该司负责监督本部门的国际发展项目。
entries.example_en: The directorate oversees the department’s international development programs.

entries.definition_en: a group of persons chosen to govern the affairs of a corporation or other large institution
entries.example_cn: 新一届董事会将于下周开会讨论预算。
entries.example_en: The new directorate will meet next week to discuss the budget.

entries.definition_cn: 公司、机构或其他组织的董事、主任或主管职位
entries.definition_en: the position or office of a director of a company, institution, or other organization
entries.example_cn: 她接受了这家新科技公司的董事职位。
entries.example_en: She accepted the directorship of the new technology firm.

entries.definition_en: a list of names and addresses arranged alphabetically
entries.example_cn: 我在电话名录中查找了电话号码。
entries.example_en: I looked up the phone number in the telephone directory.

entries.definition_en: a computer file listing the files stored on a disk
entries.example_cn: 当程序试图访问系统目录时崩溃了。
entries.example_en: The program crashed when it tried to access the system directory.

entries.definition_en: causing fear, dread, or terror
entries.example_cn: 关于风暴的可怕消息让村民们陷入了恐慌。
entries.example_en: The direful news of the storm caused panic among the villagers.

entries.definition_en: a song or hymn of mourning composed or performed as a memorial to a dead person
entries.example_cn: 合唱团为这位阵亡的英雄唱了一首庄重的挽歌。
entries.example_en: The choir sang a solemn dirge for the fallen hero.

entries.definition_cn: 阿联酋的基本货币单位（等于100费尔）
entries.definition_en: the basic unit of money in the United Arab Emirates, equal to 100 fils
entries.example_cn: 菜单上的咖啡价格是用迪拉姆标出的。
entries.example_en: The price of the coffee was listed in dirhams on the menu.

entries.definition_cn: 摩洛哥的基本货币单位（等于100生丁）
entries.definition_en: the basic unit of money in Morocco, equal to 100 centimes
entries.example_cn: 她从口袋里掏出几张迪拉姆买了票。
entries.example_en: She paid for the ticket with a few dirhams from her pocket.

entries.definition_cn: 卡塔尔货币单位（100迪拉姆等于1里亚尔）
entries.definition_en: a unit of currency in Qatar, where 100 dirhams equal 1 riyal
entries.example_cn: 旅行者在到达多哈之前将美元兑换成了迪拉姆。
entries.example_en: The traveler exchanged dollars for dirhams before arriving in Doha.

entries.definition_cn: 突尼斯货币单位（等于第纳尔的千分之一）
entries.definition_en: a unit of currency in Tunisia, equal to one thousandth of a dinar
entries.example_cn: 当地店主更喜欢用迪拉姆收款。
entries.example_en: The local shopkeeper preferred to receive payment in dirhams.

entries.definition_cn: 利比亚货币单位（等于第纳尔的千分之一）
entries.definition_en: a unit of currency in Libya, equal to one thousandth of a dinar
entries.example_cn: 历史记录显示，利比亚的迪拉姆价值曾波动不定。
entries.example_en: Historical records show the value of the dirham fluctuated in Libya.

entries.definition_cn: 科威特货币单位（价值第纳尔的十分之一，等于100费尔）
entries.definition_en: a unit of currency in Kuwait, worth one tenth of a dinar and equal to 100 fils
entries.example_cn: 商人用迪拉姆为顾客计算了总费用。
entries.example_en: The merchant calculated the total cost in dirhams for the customer.

entries.definition_en: a steerable, self-propelled airship
entries.example_cn: 那艘可操纵的自推进飞行器无声地漂浮在城市上空。
entries.example_en: The dirigible floated silently over the city.

entries.definition_en: capable of being steered or directed
entries.example_cn: 这架可操纵的飞机可以被引导至着陆场。
entries.example_en: The dirigible aircraft could be guided toward the landing field.

entries.definition_en: a long dagger with a straight blade
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一把中世纪的古代匕首。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed an ancient dirk from the medieval period.

entries.definition_cn: 上身紧身、裙摆宽大的连衣裙
entries.definition_en: a dress with a tight bodice and full skirt
entries.example_cn: 那位奥地利妇女穿着一件色彩鲜艳的上身紧身、裙摆宽大的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: The Austrian woman was dressed in a colorful dirndl.

entries.definition_en: a full skirt with a gathered waistband
entries.example_cn: 她穿着一条传统的迪恩德尔裙去参加民间节日庆典。
entries.example_en: She wore a traditional dirndl to the folk festival.

entries.definition_en: the top layer of soil containing organic matter and broken-down rock
entries.example_cn: 孩子们整个下午都在泥土里玩耍。
entries.example_en: The children played in the dirt all afternoon.

entries.definition_cn: 被视为使某物不洁之物
entries.definition_en: anything regarded as making something unclean
entries.example_cn: 她进屋前擦掉了鞋上的脏东西。
entries.example_en: She wiped the dirt off her shoes before entering the house.

entries.definition_cn: 关于他人私生活的令人难堪的流言蜚语
entries.definition_en: disgraceful gossip about the private lives of other people
entries.example_cn: 报纸刊登了一些关于市长私生活的恶毒流言。
entries.example_en: The newspaper printed some nasty dirt about the mayor's personal life.

entries.definition_en: excrement; dung (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 在这篇古文中，dirt 指粪便。
entries.example_en: In this archaic text, dirt refers to excrement.

entries.definition_cn: （指道路）未铺路面的，通常缺乏平整或排水设施的
entries.definition_en: (of roads) unpaved and generally lacking proper grading or drainage
entries.example_cn: 山区的土路在雨季无法通行。
entries.example_en: The dirt roads in the mountains are impassable during the rainy season.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unsanitary or unclean
entries.example_cn: 厨房地板上满是油污，显示出其不卫生的状况。
entries.example_en: The dirtiness of the kitchen was evident from the grease on the floor.

entries.definition_en: the state of containing dirty impurities
entries.example_cn: 供水中含有脏污杂质，导致该地区出现了一些健康问题。
entries.example_en: The high dirtiness of the water supply caused several health issues in the region.

entries.definition_en: obscenity in speech or writing
entries.example_cn: 这本书因其极端的淫秽内容和冒犯性语言而被禁。
entries.example_en: The book was banned for its extreme dirtiness and offensive language.

entries.definition_en: soiled or likely to soil with dirt or grime
entries.example_cn: 请不要让孩子们在脏沙子里玩耍。
entries.example_en: Please don't let the children play in the dirty sand.

entries.definition_en: (of behavior or especially language) characterized by obscenity or indecency
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因语言下流而被禁。
entries.example_en: The movie was banned for its dirty language.

entries.definition_en: vile; despicable
entries.example_cn: 欺骗朋友是一种卑鄙的手段。
entries.example_en: It was a dirty trick to cheat your friends.

entries.definition_cn: （颜色）因杂质而变暗、不鲜明的
entries.definition_en: (of color) discolored by impurities; not bright and clear
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨期间，天空变成了暗黄色。
entries.example_en: The sky turned a dirty yellow during the storm.

entries.definition_en: spreading pollution or contamination; especially radioactive contamination
entries.example_cn: 由于核事故，该地区仍然受到污染。
entries.example_en: The area remains dirty due to the nuclear accident.

entries.definition_en: make soiled, filthy, or dirty
entries.example_cn: 泥泞的雨水很快就会把干净的地板弄脏。
entries.example_en: The muddy rain will dirty the clean floor quickly.

entries.definition_en: contaminated with infecting organisms
entries.example_cn: 伤口被感染，开始发臭。
entries.example_en: The wound became dirty and started to smell.

entries.definition_en: (of a manuscript) defaced with changes
entries.example_cn: 编辑用红笔在涂改过的手稿上做了标记。
entries.example_en: The editor marked the dirty manuscript with red ink.

entries.definition_en: having thoughts about sex that are considered improper
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因思想下流而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The movie was criticized for being too dirty-minded.

entries.definition_en: the act of soiling something
entries.example_cn: 那件白衬衫在红酒突然泼洒时弄脏了。
entries.example_en: The dirtying of the white shirt happened during the sudden spill of red wine.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being unable to perform as a consequence of physical or mental unfitness
entries.example_cn: 法律保护残疾人免受歧视。
entries.example_en: The law protects people with disabilities from discrimination.

entries.definition_cn: 使失去能力；使无法工作；禁用；使失效
entries.definition_en: to make a person, ability, device, or feature unable to function; to deactivate
entries.example_cn: 事故使汽车的制动系统无法工作。
entries.example_en: The accident disabled the car's braking system.

entries.definition_cn: 使身体或心理受损；致残
entries.definition_en: to cause a physical or mental impairment, especially one that limits normal functioning
entries.example_cn: 这名士兵在战争中致残。
entries.example_en: The soldier was disabled in the war.

entries.definition_cn: 有身体或精神障碍的；丧失身体部位或功能的
entries.definition_en: having a physical or mental disability, or having lost the use of a body part or function
entries.example_cn: 他在事故中致残，现在使用轮椅。
entries.example_en: He was disabled in an accident and now uses a wheelchair.

entries.definition_en: people who have physical or mental disabilities
entries.example_cn: 该组织为残疾人提供支持服务。
entries.example_en: The organization provides support services for the disabled.

entries.definition_cn: 使失效；丧失能力的状态
entries.definition_en: the act of disabling or the state of being disabled
entries.example_cn: 使所有核武器失效将使世界更安全。
entries.example_en: The disablement of all nuclear weapons would make the world safer.

entries.definition_en: causing someone to be unable to move or function properly
entries.example_cn: 那次使他丧失能力的伤势让他缺席了数月。
entries.example_en: The disabling injury kept him out of the game for months.

entries.definition_en: depriving someone of legal rights or rendering them legally disqualified
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定合同中的剥夺法律权利条款无效。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the disabling clause in the contract was invalid.

entries.definition_en: to free someone from a mistaken belief or idea
entries.example_cn: 我试图让他摆脱那种不努力也能成功的错误想法。
entries.example_en: I tried to disabuse him of the idea that he could succeed without hard work.

entries.definition_en: a carbohydrate composed of two monosaccharide molecules linked together
entries.example_cn: 蔗糖是食糖中常见的一种双糖。
entries.example_en: Sucrose is a common disaccharide found in table sugar.

entries.definition_en: a condition that makes it harder to succeed or compete
entries.example_cn: 缺乏经验是这份工作的一个劣势。
entries.example_en: Lack of experience is a disadvantage in this job.

entries.definition_en: to put someone in a worse position than others
entries.example_cn: 大雨使在室外比赛的队伍处于不利地位。
entries.example_en: The heavy rain disadvantaged the team playing outside.

entries.definition_cn: 处于不利地位的；贫困的
entries.definition_en: lacking the basic necessities of life or healthy surroundings
entries.example_cn: 政府为处于不利地位的儿童提供特别支持。
entries.example_en: The government provides special support for disadvantaged children.

entries.definition_en: creating circumstances that are harmful to success or effectiveness
entries.example_cn: 熬夜工作对他的健康不利。
entries.example_en: Working late into the night was disadvantageous to his health.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes disadvantage; to someone's disadvantage
entries.example_cn: 新规定对小企业产生了不利影响。
entries.example_en: The new regulations disadvantageously affect small businesses.

entries.definition_cn: 对权威不满且抱有敌意的；愤懑不满的
entries.definition_en: feeling discontented and hostile toward authority
entries.example_cn: 那些对学校现状不满的学生组织了一场抗议新校规的活动。
entries.example_en: The disaffected students organized a protest against the new school rules.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of alienation or estrangement from others
entries.example_cn: 缺乏社区活动导致居民们产生了日益增长的疏离感。
entries.example_en: The lack of community events led to a growing sense of disaffection among the residents.

entries.definition_cn: 对政府或既有权威的不忠；离心倾向
entries.definition_en: disloyalty to the government or to established authority
entries.example_cn: 抗议活动是由对执政党的广泛不满情绪引发的。
entries.example_en: The protests were fueled by widespread disaffection with the ruling party.

entries.definition_en: to have different opinions from someone
entries.example_cn: 我不同意你出售公司的计划。
entries.example_en: I disagree with your plan to sell the company.

entries.definition_en: to be different from one another
entries.example_cn: 这两份报告对事件的日期说法不一致。
entries.example_en: The two reports disagree on the exact date of the event.

entries.definition_en: not to your liking
entries.example_cn: 这食物太辣了，让人吃不下去。
entries.example_en: The food was too spicy and disagreeable to eat.

entries.definition_en: unpleasant to interact with
entries.example_cn: 他是个难以相处的人，从不听别人的意见。
entries.example_en: He is a disagreeable person who never listens to others.

entries.definition_cn: 不合适的；不相符或不相合的（古旧用法）
entries.definition_en: not suitable; not conforming or fitting (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 这种行为与正义原则不相容。
entries.example_en: Such conduct was disagreeable to the principles of justice.

entries.definition_en: in a disagreeable manner
entries.example_cn: 天气一夜之间变得令人不快地寒冷。
entries.example_en: The weather turned disagreeably cold overnight.

entries.definition_en: a situation where people have different opinions or act differently
entries.example_cn: 他们在出发时间上存在分歧。
entries.example_en: There was a disagreement about the best time to leave.

entries.definition_en: a difference between conflicting facts, claims, or opinions
entries.example_cn: 报告指出了数据与理论之间的不一致。
entries.example_en: The report highlighted a disagreement between the data and the theory.

entries.definition_en: the expression of a lack of agreement or opposition to an idea
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上表达了自己的异议。
entries.example_en: He voiced his disagreement during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: to officially say that something is not allowed or is not valid
entries.example_cn: 裁判决定判罚这个进球无效，因为球员用手触球了。
entries.example_en: The referee decided to disallow the goal because the player had touched the ball with his hand.

usage.label: disallow something; disallow someone from doing something
usage.pattern: The sources attest refusal of permission and rejection as invalid (w29098r0–r1).

entries.definition_en: to state unambiguously or remove ambiguities from
entries.example_cn: 在进行分析之前，我们需要消除该术语的歧义。
entries.example_en: We need to disambiguate the term before proceeding with the analysis.

entries.definition_en: the act of clarifying something to remove ambiguity
entries.example_cn: 作者包含了一个关于消除歧义的部分，以帮助读者理解技术术语。
entries.example_en: The author included a section on disambiguation to help readers understand the technical terms.

entries.definition_en: to go missing, especially unexpectedly
entries.example_cn: 大人们分心时，孩子突然不见了。
entries.example_en: The child disappeared while the adults were distracted.

entries.definition_en: to become invisible or unnoticeable
entries.example_cn: 星星消失在云层后面。
entries.example_en: The stars disappeared behind the clouds.

entries.definition_en: to cease to exist
entries.example_cn: 许多古老的传统已经不复存在。
entries.example_en: Many ancient traditions have disappeared.

entries.definition_en: to become less intense and fade away gradually
entries.example_cn: 服用药物后，疼痛开始逐渐减弱。
entries.example_en: The pain began to disappear after taking the medicine.

entries.definition_en: the event of passing out of sight
entries.example_cn: 太阳被群山遮蔽而消失，标志着白天的结束。
entries.example_en: The disappearance of the sun behind the mountains marked the end of the day.

entries.definition_cn: 秘密或不明不白地离开
entries.definition_en: the act of leaving secretly or without explanation
entries.example_cn: 他在派对上的不告而别被大家注意到了。
entries.example_en: His disappearance from the party was noticed by everyone.

entries.definition_en: gradually ceasing to be visible
entries.example_cn: 在明亮的城市灯光下星星逐渐消失的景象令人失望。
entries.example_en: The disappearance of the stars in the bright city light was disappointing.

entries.definition_en: ceasing to exist
entries.example_cn: 该物种的灭绝是生态系统的悲剧。
entries.example_en: The disappearance of the species is a tragedy for the ecosystem.

entries.definition_en: the act or process of disappearing
entries.example_cn: 突然而大规模的消失会使我们震惊和困惑。
entries.example_en: Sudden and extensive disappearings would startle and confound us.

entries.definition_en: to fail to meet someone's hopes or expectations
entries.example_cn: 球队糟糕的表现让粉丝们很失望。
entries.example_en: The team's poor performance disappointed the fans.

entries.definition_en: feeling sad because something did not go as well as you hoped
entries.example_cn: 她对电影太短感到失望。
entries.example_en: She was disappointed that the movie was so short.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing disappointment or letdown
entries.example_cn: 她失望地看着破碎的花瓶，想知道它是如何发生的。
entries.example_en: She looked at the broken vase disappointedly, wondering how it could have happened.

entries.definition_en: not up to expectations
entries.example_cn: 令人失望的结果让每个人都很难过。
entries.example_en: The disappointing result made everyone sad.

entries.definition_en: in a disappointing manner
entries.example_cn: 令人失望的是，天气搞砸了我们的野餐计划。
entries.example_en: Disappointingly, the weather ruined our plans for a picnic.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of dissatisfaction when your expectations are not met
entries.example_cn: 他未能露面让朋友们非常失望。
entries.example_en: His failure to show up was a great disappointment to his friends.

entries.definition_en: an act or failure to act that causes someone to feel disappointed
entries.example_cn: 项目的延误让团队非常失望。
entries.example_en: The delay in the project was a major disappointment to the team.

entries.definition_en: the act of expressing strong disapproval or declaring something morally wrong
entries.example_cn: 当提案被提出时，委员会表示了谴责。
entries.example_en: The committee met with disapprobation when the proposal was presented.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of disliking something or what someone is doing
entries.example_cn: 大家普遍不赞成他鲁莽的驾驶行为。
entries.example_en: There was a general disapproval of his reckless driving.

entries.definition_en: the expression of disapproval
entries.example_cn: 她得到了父母表示不赞成的眼神。
entries.example_en: She received a look of disapproval from her parents.

entries.definition_en: the act of disapproving or condemning
entries.example_cn: 演讲遭到了观众的强烈反对。
entries.example_en: The speech was met with loud disapproval from the audience.

entries.definition_en: an inclination to withhold approval from some person or group
entries.example_cn: 委员会对新政策的不信任显而易见。
entries.example_en: The committee's disapproval of the new policy was clear.

entries.definition_en: to think that something is bad or wrong
entries.example_cn: 我的父母不赞成我搬去国外的决定。
entries.example_en: My parents disapprove of my decision to move abroad.

entries.definition_en: to judge something as wrong or inappropriate
entries.example_cn: 委员会认为对政策的提议是不当的。
entries.example_en: The committee disapproved of the proposed changes to the policy.

entries.definition_cn: 表示不赞成的；表示反对的
entries.definition_en: showing that you believe something is wrong or unacceptable
entries.example_cn: 她迟到时，他投去不赞成的目光。
entries.example_en: He gave her a disapproving look when she arrived late.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that shows disapproval
entries.example_cn: 当他建议破坏规则时，她不赞成地摇了摇头。
entries.example_en: She shook her head disapprovingly when he suggested breaking the rules.

entries.definition_en: to remove weapons or the means of attack or defense from a person or group
entries.example_cn: 士兵们被命令解除叛军的武装。
entries.example_en: The soldiers were ordered to disarm the rebels.

entries.definition_cn: 使（人）消除戒心；使（人）不再敌对
entries.definition_en: to make someone less hostile or suspicious, often by winning their trust
