entries.definition_en: (of a marching cadence) very quick
entries.example_cn: 士兵们以极快的步伐行军。
entries.example_en: The soldiers marched at double-quick.

entries.definition_en: to type or write with a blank line between each line of text
entries.example_cn: 请在提交论文前将其设置为双倍行距。
entries.example_en: Please double-space your essay before submitting it.

entries.definition_cn: 在句子之间输入两个空格
entries.definition_en: to type or format text with two spaces between consecutive sentences
entries.example_cn: 格式指南要求在每个句子后输入两个空格。
entries.example_en: The style guide says to double-space after each sentence.

entries.definition_en: (of type or print) having a blank line between lines of type
entries.example_cn: 请提交双行距的论文。
entries.example_en: Please submit your essay double-spaced.

entries.definition_en: cover with two defensive players
entries.example_cn: 教练命令后卫双人包夹那名明星球员。
entries.example_en: The coach ordered the guards to double-team the star player.

entries.definition_cn: 由两人联手应对或对付（某人或某事）
entries.definition_en: To deal with or confront someone or something using a team of two people.
entries.example_cn: 两名记者联手追问部长有关丑闻的问题。
entries.example_en: The two reporters double-teamed the minister with questions about the scandal.

entries.definition_en: to march at double time
entries.example_cn: 士兵们以倍速行军穿过田野。
entries.example_en: The soldiers double-timed across the field.

entries.definition_en: to order troops to march at double time
entries.example_cn: 将军命令部队以倍速行军，以便快速覆盖这段距离。
entries.example_en: The general double-timed the troops to cover the distance quickly.

entries.definition_en: saying one thing to one person and something different to another; deceitful in speech
entries.example_cn: 这位政客被指责两面三刀，向不同群体作出不同承诺。
entries.example_en: The politician was accused of being double-tongued, making different promises to different groups.

entries.definition_en: the name of the 23rd letter of the Roman alphabet, W
entries.example_cn: “double-u”是字母 W 的名称。
entries.example_en: The word “double-u” is the name for the letter W.

entries.definition_cn: 双赛制（尤指棒球中同一天同一两队进行的两场比赛）
entries.definition_en: a sporting event where two games are played between the same teams on the same day
entries.example_cn: 球迷们坚持看完了双赛制的两场比赛。
entries.example_en: The fans stayed until the end of the doubleheader to see both games.

entries.definition_en: an electronic device that doubles the voltage or the frequency of an input signal
entries.example_cn: 无线电工程师安装了倍频器以提高信号频率。
entries.example_en: The radio engineer installed a doubler to increase the signal frequency.

entries.definition_en: a game of tennis played with two players on each side
entries.example_cn: 他们本周末在网球俱乐部打双打。
entries.example_en: They are playing doubles at the tennis club this weekend.

entries.definition_en: a game of badminton played with two players on each side
entries.example_cn: 该队在双打比赛中直落三局获胜。
entries.example_en: The team won the doubles match in straight sets.

entries.definition_en: language that appears to communicate meaning but actually does not, often used to deceive
entries.example_cn: 政府使用双重语言将经济危机描述为“暂时性调整”。
entries.example_en: The government used doublespeak to describe the economic crisis as a 'temporary adjustment'.

entries.definition_cn: 文艺复兴时期男子穿着的紧身短上衣
entries.definition_en: a man's close-fitting jacket worn during the Renaissance
entries.example_cn: 这位演员身穿一件正宗的紧身短上衣，扮演了一位 16 世纪的贵族。
entries.example_en: The actor wore an authentic doublet to portray the nobleman from the 16th century.

entries.definition_en: the practice of accepting two contradictory beliefs simultaneously
entries.example_cn: 宣传鼓吹双重思想，声称战争既必要又不义。
entries.example_en: The propaganda encouraged doublethink by claiming the war was both necessary and unjust.

entries.definition_en: (bridge) a pair of playing cards that are the only cards of that suit in a player's hand
entries.example_cn: 她领出她手中的两张红心，以避免陷入困境。
entries.example_en: She led with her doubleton of hearts to avoid being trapped.

entries.definition_en: a crossbar on a wagon or carriage used to attach two whiffletrees for harnessing two horses side by side
entries.example_cn: 这辆旧马车有一个双辕，以便用两匹马牵引。
entries.example_en: The old wagon had a doubletree to pull it with two horses.

entries.definition_en: the act of increasing something to twice its original size or amount
entries.example_cn: 人口正在经历快速翻倍。
entries.example_en: The population is experiencing rapid doubling.

entries.definition_en: the act of turning around or doubling back
entries.example_cn: 折返使我们的行程多出了几英里。
entries.example_en: The doubling back added several miles to our journey.

entries.definition_en: a former Spanish gold coin
entries.example_cn: 海盗船长在将宝藏分给船员之前数了他的西班牙金币。
entries.example_en: The pirate captain counted his doubloons before dividing the treasure among the crew.

entries.definition_en: to an extent or degree that is twice as great
entries.example_cn: 由于缺乏风，热浪加倍强烈。
entries.example_en: The heat was doubly intense because of the lack of wind.

entries.definition_en: in a twofold manner; in two ways
entries.example_cn: 这项政策双重有益，既省钱又省时。
entries.example_en: The policy is doubly beneficial as it saves money and time.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of uncertainty about whether something is true or will happen
entries.example_cn: 人们怀疑他是否能赢得比赛。
entries.example_en: There is some doubt about whether he will win the competition.

entries.definition_en: the state of not being sure about the truth or existence of something
entries.example_cn: 他对这个计划表示了疑虑。
entries.example_en: He expressed his doubts about the plan.

entries.definition_en: to think that something is unlikely to be true or will not happen
entries.example_cn: 我怀疑今天会下雨。
entries.example_en: I doubt that it will rain today.

entries.definition_en: to feel that someone or something is not trustworthy or reliable
entries.example_cn: 不要怀疑他做这项工作的能力。
entries.example_en: Do not doubt his ability to do the job.

entries.definition_cn: 习惯怀疑公认信念的人
entries.definition_en: someone who habitually doubts accepted beliefs
entries.example_cn: 作为一名科学怀疑论者，他对每一个既定理论都提出质疑。
entries.example_en: As a scientific doubter, he questions every established theory.

entries.definition_cn: 对某事持怀疑或保留态度的人
entries.definition_en: someone who is doubtful or noncommittal about something
entries.example_cn: 这位持怀疑态度的人在获得更多保证之前犹豫不决，不愿签署合同。
entries.example_en: The doubter hesitated to sign the contract without more guarantees.

entries.definition_en: not certain; open to doubt or suspicion
entries.example_cn: 证据仍然可疑，所以我们不能做出最终决定。
entries.example_en: The evidence is still doubtful, so we cannot make a final decision.

entries.definition_en: full of uncertainty or doubt
entries.example_cn: 该项目的未来仍充满不确定性。
entries.example_en: The future of the project remains doubtful.

entries.definition_cn: 内心不安的；犹豫不决的
entries.definition_en: feeling uncertain or unsure about something
entries.example_cn: 她对自己能否按时完成这项任务感到犹豫不决。
entries.example_en: She felt doubtful about whether she could finish the task on time.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows you are not sure or are suspicious
entries.example_cn: 她怀疑地看着那个奇怪的包裹。
entries.example_en: She looked at the strange package doubtfully.

entries.definition_en: characterized by or showing doubt
entries.example_cn: 怀疑的人群在等待结果。
entries.example_en: The doubting crowd waited for the results.

entries.definition_en: without doubt; certainly
entries.example_cn: 无疑，她会在会议开始前到达。
entries.example_en: Doubtless, she will arrive before the meeting starts.

entries.definition_en: without doubt; certainly
entries.example_cn: 毫无疑问，如果我们共同努力，这个项目肯定会成功。
entries.example_en: Doubtlessly, the project will succeed if we work together.

entries.definition_en: to clean a bodily cavity by directing a spray of water into it
entries.example_cn: 她用生理盐水冲洗伤口。
entries.example_en: She douches the wound with saline solution.

entries.definition_en: the act of irrigating a body part with water or solution
entries.example_cn: 该治疗包括每日冲洗以清洁该区域。
entries.example_en: The treatment involves a daily douche to cleanse the area.

entries.definition_en: a small syringe with detachable nozzles used for medical lavage
entries.example_cn: 医生为感染开具了一种特殊的冲洗器。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a special douche for the infection.

entries.definition_en: a mixture of flour and water that is stiff enough to be kneaded or rolled
entries.example_cn: 她把面粉和水混合起来做成柔软的面团。
entries.example_en: She mixed the flour and water to make a soft dough.

entries.definition_en: informal terms for money
entries.example_cn: 他用现金付了餐费，但手头缺钱。
entries.example_en: He paid for the meal with cash, but he was short on dough.

entries.definition_en: an American soldier in World War I
entries.example_cn: 这部历史小说描绘了一战期间美国士兵在西线的日常生活。
entries.example_en: The historical novel depicted the daily life of a doughboy on the Western Front.

entries.definition_cn: 一种油炸后作为面包食用的面团食品
entries.definition_en: a piece of dough that is deep-fried and served as bread
entries.example_cn: 早餐时，他们享用了一个淋着蜂蜜的热乎乎的油炸面团面包。
entries.example_en: For breakfast, they enjoyed a warm doughboy with honey.

entries.definition_en: a small ring-shaped cake made of fried dough
entries.example_cn: 她早餐买了一个巧克力甜甜圈。
entries.example_en: She bought a chocolate doughnut for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: a shape that is round with a hole in the middle
entries.example_cn: 这座桥呈环形。
entries.example_en: The bridge has a doughnut shape.

entries.definition_en: having the soft, sticky consistency of raw dough, often due to being undercooked or lacking proper leavening
entries.example_cn: 面包烤得不够久，太黏软了。
entries.example_en: The bread was too doughy because it was not baked long enough.

entries.definition_en: a trained support person who provides emotional, physical, and practical assistance to a pregnant woman or couple before, during, or after childbirth
entries.example_cn: 导乐师帮助母亲在分娩过程中保持冷静并使用呼吸技巧。
entries.example_en: The doula helped the mother stay calm and use breathing techniques during labor.

entries.definition_cn: 为接受临终照护的绝症患者提供情感、实际及其他支持的受训人员
entries.definition_en: a trained support person who provides emotional, practical, and other assistance to someone with an incurable illness receiving end-of-life care
entries.example_cn: 临终关怀导乐师帮助患者及其家人为他最后的日子做好准备。
entries.example_en: The end-of-life doula helped the patient and his family prepare for his final days.

entries.definition_cn: 态度或外貌严厉而令人望而生畏的
entries.definition_en: harshly uninviting or formidable in manner or appearance
entries.example_cn: 船长脸上严厉的表情让船员们感到紧张。
entries.example_en: The dour expression on the captain's face made the crew nervous.

entries.definition_en: stubbornly unyielding
entries.example_cn: 那位顽固的老头拒绝改变主意。
entries.example_en: The dour old man refused to change his mind.

entries.definition_cn: 表现出阴沉的坏心情的
entries.definition_en: showing a brooding ill humor
entries.example_cn: 听到坏消息后，她看起来心情阴沉。
entries.example_en: She looked dour after hearing the bad news.

entries.definition_cn: 亚洲和北非干旱地区种植的一种高粱
entries.definition_en: a type of sorghum grown in dry regions of Asia and North Africa
entries.example_cn: 干旱地区的农民依靠这种坚韧的高粱进行收获。
entries.example_en: Farmers in the arid regions rely on the hardy doura for their harvest.

entries.definition_en: in a gloomy or sullen way
entries.example_cn: 她阴沉地拒绝向客人微笑。
entries.example_en: She dourly refused to smile at the guests.

entries.definition_en: put out, as of a candle or a light
entries.example_cn: 他离开房间前迅速熄灭了蜡烛。
entries.example_en: He quickly doused the candle before leaving the room.

entries.definition_cn: 用液体覆盖；将液体倒在...上
entries.definition_en: cover with liquid; pour liquid onto
entries.example_cn: 他们用消毒剂洒满地板进行清洁。
entries.example_en: They doused the floor with disinfectant to clean it.

entries.definition_en: wet thoroughly
entries.example_cn: 雨水把他的衣服彻底淋湿了。
entries.example_en: The rain thoroughly doused his clothes.

entries.definition_en: dip into a liquid
entries.example_cn: 她把海绵浸入水桶里。
entries.example_en: She doused the sponge in the bucket of water.

entries.definition_cn: 短暂浸入液体以弄湿、覆盖或浸透
entries.definition_en: immerse briefly into a liquid so as to wet, coat, or saturate
entries.example_cn: 厨师在烤蔬菜前将它们短暂浸入油中。
entries.example_en: The chef doused the vegetables in oil before roasting them.

entries.definition_en: to lower quickly, especially a sail
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴中迅速降下帆。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to douse the sails in the storm.

entries.definition_en: slacken
entries.example_cn: 随着风暴过去，风开始减弱。
entries.example_en: The wind began to douse as the storm passed.

entries.definition_cn: 用液体浇湿或浸透某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of soaking or drenching something with liquid
entries.example_cn: 消防员给着火的大楼浇水灭火。
entries.example_en: The firefighters finished dousing the burning building with water.

entries.definition_en: a small bird that is a type of pigeon
entries.example_cn: 一只白鸽飞过天空。
entries.example_en: A white dove flew across the sky.

entries.definition_en: a person who prefers talking and negotiation to fighting in international relations
entries.example_cn: 这位外交官以寻求和平解决方案的鸽派人士而闻名。
entries.example_en: The diplomat was known as a dove who sought peaceful solutions.

entries.definition_en: a symbol representing peace
entries.example_cn: 旗帜上的鸽子是和平的象征。
entries.example_en: The dove on the flag is an emblem of peace.

entries.definition_en: the meat of a young pigeon, often roasted or braised
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐点了烤乳鸽。
entries.example_en: We ordered roasted dove for dinner.

entries.definition_en: a building or structure designed to house pigeons
entries.example_cn: 那座古老的庄园屋顶上有一个巨大的鸽舍。
entries.example_en: The old manor house featured a large dovecote on its roof.

entries.definition_en: to fit together perfectly or work in harmony
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策与现有法规紧密配合。
entries.example_en: The new policy dovetails with the existing regulations.

entries.definition_en: a joint made by interlocking pieces of wood
entries.example_cn: 这个橱柜使用了燕尾榫以增加强度。
entries.example_en: The cabinet was constructed using a dovetail joint for extra strength.

entries.definition_en: opposed to war or favoring peaceful solutions
entries.example_cn: 总统在外交政策上采取了鸽派立场以避免冲突。
entries.example_en: The president adopted a dovish stance on foreign policy to avoid conflict.

entries.definition_cn: 反对加息的，尤其指政策上倾向于维持较低利率的
entries.definition_en: Opposed to raising interest rates, especially as a policy approach.
entries.example_cn: 投资者认为央行维持利率不变的决定是偏向鸽派的。
entries.example_en: Investors viewed the central bank's decision to keep rates unchanged as dovish.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有亡夫留下的财产或头衔的寡妇
entries.definition_en: a widow who holds property that was given to her by her deceased husband
entries.example_cn: 这位遗孀住着她丈夫留给她的豪宅。
entries.example_en: The dowager lived in the grand house her husband had left her.

entries.definition_en: lacking in smartness or taste
entries.example_cn: 她那身寒酸的装束让她在聚会上感到不自在。
entries.example_en: Her dowdy outfit made her feel uncomfortable at the party.

entries.definition_en: primly out of date
entries.example_cn: 那些老式的家具看起来像是放在博物馆里的。
entries.example_en: The dowdy furniture looked like it belonged in a museum.

entries.definition_en: a deep-dish apple dessert with a rich crust
entries.example_cn: 她端上了一道热腾腾的深盘苹果派作为甜点。
entries.example_en: She served a warm dowdy for dessert.

entries.definition_cn: 插入相邻部件孔中以固定它们的木制或金属销钉
entries.definition_en: a pin or block, usually of wood or metal, fitted into holes in two adjoining pieces to hold them together
entries.example_cn: 木匠用一根木销钉将桌子的两半连接起来。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a wooden dowel to connect the two halves of the table.

entries.definition_cn: 用销钉将两个或多个物体固定在一起
entries.definition_en: to fasten two or more things together with dowels
entries.example_cn: 木匠在加螺钉之前，先用销钉将框架部件固定在一起。
entries.example_en: The cabinetmaker doweled the frame pieces together before adding the screws.

entries.definition_cn: 新郎在婚前或婚礼时给新娘或其家人的婚嫁财产
entries.definition_en: property given by a groom to his bride or her family at or before marriage
entries.example_cn: 结婚时，他给新娘置办了一份聘礼。
entries.example_en: At marriage, he settled a dower on his bride.

entries.definition_cn: 寡妇对亡夫遗产的终身权益
entries.definition_en: a life interest in a deceased husband's property to which his widow is entitled
entries.example_cn: 根据旧法律，寡妇保留了对亡夫财产的终身使用权。
entries.example_en: Under old laws, a widow retained the dower of her late husband's estate.

entries.definition_en: to provide someone with money or property as a dower
entries.example_cn: 富有的阿姨在婚礼前为侄女提供了嫁妆。
entries.example_en: The wealthy aunt dowered her niece before the wedding ceremony.

entries.definition_en: a shorebird belonging to the sandpiper family that resembles a snipe
entries.example_cn: 白腰草鹬在浅水中涉水觅食。
entries.example_en: The dowitcher waded through the shallow water searching for food.

entries.definition_en: from a higher place to a lower place
entries.example_cn: 她从楼梯上摔了下来。
entries.example_en: She fell down the stairs.

entries.definition_en: situated at a lower level or having a lower value
entries.example_cn: 价格显著下降了。
entries.example_en: The price has gone down significantly.

entries.definition_en: going from a higher place to a lower place
entries.example_cn: 我们走下坡路去了海滩。
entries.example_en: We took the road down to the beach.

entries.definition_en: soft feathers found on birds
entries.example_cn: 这件夹克里填充了羽绒。
entries.example_en: The jacket is filled with down.

entries.definition_en: to eat something completely and quickly
entries.example_cn: 那只狗狼吞虎咽地吃光了食物。
entries.example_en: The dog wolfed down the food.

entries.definition_en: to drink something completely
entries.example_cn: 他一口气把整瓶酒喝光了。
entries.example_en: He drank the whole bottle down in one go.

entries.definition_en: away from a central or northern place
entries.example_cn: 他们从北方南下。
entries.example_en: They traveled down from the north.

entries.definition_en: a play in American football to advance the ball
entries.example_cn: 球队在第一次进攻中得分了。
entries.example_en: The team scored on the first down.

entries.definition_cn: 穷困潦倒的；一无所有的
entries.definition_en: lacking resources (or any prospect of resources)
entries.example_cn: 生意破产后，他感到一无所有。
entries.example_en: After losing his business, he felt down-and-out.

entries.definition_en: a person who is destitute
entries.example_cn: 他是一个睡在公园里的穷光蛋。
entries.example_en: He was a down-and-out who slept in the park.

entries.definition_en: a downward stroke from the heel to the tip of the bow
entries.example_cn: 小提琴手在第一个音符上拉了一个柔和的下弓。
entries.example_en: The violinist played a soft down-bow on the first note.

entries.definition_en: sensible and practical
entries.example_cn: 她是一个务实的人，总是倾听他人的烦恼。
entries.example_en: She is a down-to-earth person who always listens to others' problems.

entries.definition_en: sad or pessimistic
entries.example_cn: 有人问起他未来的计划时，他听起来情绪低落。
entries.example_en: He sounded downbeat when asked about his future plans.

entries.definition_en: the first beat of a musical measure, indicated by the conductor's arm moving downward
entries.example_cn: 指挥用一个向下的动作示意了第一拍。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled the downbeat with a sharp downward motion.

entries.definition_en: heading in any direction that is conventionally down
entries.example_cn: 顺流而下的渡轮恰好在潮水转向时抵达码头。
entries.example_en: The downbound ferry arrived at the dock just as the tide turned.

entries.definition_en: filled with melancholy and despondency
entries.example_cn: 他心情忧郁，一言不发地坐着。
entries.example_en: He sat in a downcast mood, unable to speak.

entries.definition_en: directed downward
entries.example_cn: 她低着头穿过人群。
entries.example_en: She walked through the crowd with her head downcast.

entries.definition_en: a ventilation shaft used to let air into a mine
entries.example_cn: 这条通风道将新鲜空气输送到矿井深处。
entries.example_en: The downcast carried fresh air deep into the mine.

entries.definition_en: a strong current of air moving downwards
entries.example_cn: 从窗户吹来的下冲气流把桌上的纸吹落了。
entries.example_en: The downdraft from the open window blew the papers off the table.

entries.definition_en: a drug that reduces excitability and calms a person
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种温和的镇静剂来帮助他入睡。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a mild downer to help him sleep.

entries.definition_en: failure that results in a loss of position or reputation
entries.example_cn: 他的傲慢导致了他作为领导人的垮台。
entries.example_en: His arrogance led to his downfall as a leader.

entries.definition_en: the falling to earth of any form of water (rain or snow or hail or sleet or mist)
entries.example_cn: 突如其来的降雪让徒步者感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: The sudden downfall of snow surprised the hikers.

entries.definition_en: a sudden decline in strength or number or importance
entries.example_cn: 该公司在上一个季度经历了销售额的急剧下降。
entries.example_en: The company experienced a sharp downfall in sales last quarter.

entries.definition_en: located at, or relatively closer to, the defending team's end of the playing field
entries.example_cn: 四分卫将球传到了防守方的区域。
entries.example_en: The quarterback threw the ball downfield to the receiver.

entries.definition_en: in the direction of the defending team's end of the playing field
entries.example_cn: 跑卫突破防线，向防守方跑去。
entries.example_en: The running back broke through the line and ran downfield.

entries.definition_en: to rate something lower or lower its value or esteem
entries.example_cn: 由于预算削减，公司决定将该项目降级。
entries.example_en: The company decided to downgrade the project due to budget cuts.

entries.definition_en: the property of a slope or surface that goes downwards
entries.example_cn: 汽车难以爬上这个陡峭的下坡。
entries.example_en: The car struggled to climb the steep downgrade.

entries.definition_en: feeling sad, depressed, and lacking hope or confidence.
entries.example_cn: 听到坏消息后，她感到非常沮丧，便疏远了朋友。
entries.example_en: After hearing the bad news, she felt very downhearted and withdrew from her friends.

entries.definition_en: going down a slope or hill; sloping downward
entries.example_cn: 过桥后，下坡路变得更陡。
entries.example_en: The downhill road becomes steeper after the bridge.

entries.definition_en: toward a lower or inferior state
entries.example_cn: 事故后他的健康状况每况愈下。
entries.example_en: His health went downhill after the accident.

entries.definition_en: toward the bottom of a hill
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者向下坡走去寻找庇护所。
entries.example_en: The hikers headed downhill to find shelter.

entries.definition_cn: 高山滑雪中速度最快的项目
entries.definition_en: the fastest discipline of alpine skiing
entries.example_cn: 速降是高山滑雪中速度最快的项目。
entries.example_en: Downhill is the fastest discipline in alpine skiing.

entries.definition_cn: 速降滑雪比赛；滑雪下坡的快速下降
entries.definition_en: a downhill ski race or rapid descent
entries.example_cn: 高山速降滑雪赛是比赛中最激动人心的项目。
entries.example_en: The downhill was the most exciting event of the competition.

entries.definition_en: to transfer a file from a central computer to a local computer
entries.example_cn: 请从网站下载该软件。
entries.example_en: Please download the software from the website.

entries.definition_en: designed to appeal to people with low incomes
entries.example_cn: 这家商店出售面向学生的、价格实惠的电子产品。
entries.example_en: The store sells downmarket electronics that are affordable for students.

entries.definition_cn: 朝向较低档或较不高端的市场
entries.definition_en: toward the less prestigious or less expensive part of the market
entries.example_cn: 随着较富裕的居民搬走，这个社区逐渐变得不那么高档了。
entries.example_en: The neighborhood has gradually gone downmarket as wealthier residents moved away.

entries.definition_cn: 使某物变得较低档或较不昂贵；变得较低档或较不昂贵
entries.definition_en: to make something less prestigious or expensive, or to become less prestigious or expensive
entries.example_cn: 这家公司让其产品线变得更低档，以吸引更多注重价格的顾客。
entries.example_en: The company downmarketed its product line to attract more price-conscious customers.

entries.definition_en: represent as less significant or important
entries.example_cn: 政府试图轻描淡写地描述新政策的风险。
entries.example_en: The government tried to downplay the risks of the new policy.

entries.definition_en: understate the importance or quality of
entries.example_cn: 批评家指责这位艺术家贬低了她作品的复杂性。
entries.example_en: Critics accused the artist of downplaying the complexity of her work.

entries.definition_en: a very heavy rain
entries.example_cn: 由于突如其来的暴雨，我们不得不取消野餐。
entries.example_en: We had to cancel the picnic due to the sudden downpour.

entries.definition_cn: 完全的；无限制的；有时用作加强语气的副词
entries.definition_en: complete and without restriction or qualification; sometimes used informally as intensifiers
entries.example_cn: 这简直是一场彻底的灾难。
entries.example_en: It was a downright disaster.

entries.definition_en: direct, plain, and blunt in manner or speech
entries.example_cn: 他直截了当地回答，说出了自己的真实想法。
entries.example_en: He gave a downright answer and said exactly what he thought.

entries.definition_en: thoroughgoing
entries.example_cn: 这房子乱得一塌糊涂。
entries.example_en: The house was in a downright mess.

entries.definition_en: away from the source or with the current of a river
entries.example_cn: 我们顺流而下，到达了河流入海口的城市。
entries.example_en: We sailed downriver to reach the city at the mouth of the river.

entries.definition_en: less expensive, prestigious, or exclusive than something comparable
entries.example_cn: 这家新购物中心是附近豪华购物中心的低档版本。
entries.example_en: The new shopping mall is a downscale version of the luxury center nearby.

entries.definition_cn: 缩小（某物）的规模或尺寸
entries.definition_en: to reduce the size or scale of something
entries.example_cn: 需求下降后，公司计划缩小经营规模。
entries.example_en: The company plans to downscale its operations after a drop in demand.

entries.definition_en: a change to a lower gear in a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 他必须迅速降档才能爬上陡峭的山坡。
entries.example_en: He had to downshift quickly to climb the steep hill.

entries.definition_cn: 从高薪高压职业转向薪资较低但压力较小、更加充实的职业或生活方式
entries.definition_en: a change from a stressful, high-paying career to a less stressful, lower-paying but more fulfilling one
entries.example_cn: 多年精疲力竭后，她决定转向一份压力更小、薪资较低但更有成就感的职业。
entries.example_en: After years of burnout, she decided that a downshift to a less stressful career would be more fulfilling.

entries.definition_en: a disadvantage or negative aspect
entries.example_cn: 住在城市的缺点是住房成本高昂。
entries.example_en: The downside of living in the city is the high cost of housing.

entries.definition_cn: (公司) 缩减规模或减少员工数量
entries.definition_en: (of a company) to reduce in size or number of employees
entries.example_cn: 许多科技公司正在缩减业务，以适应不断变化的市场。
entries.example_en: Many tech firms are downsizing their operations to adapt to the changing market.

entries.definition_en: to dismiss from work
entries.example_cn: 由于财务困难，公司不得不裁员。
entries.example_en: The company had to downsize its workforce due to financial difficulties.

entries.definition_cn: 设计或制造成较小尺寸
entries.definition_en: to design or manufacture in a smaller size
entries.example_cn: 新款智能手机旨在缩小机身尺寸，同时保持高性能。
entries.example_en: The new smartphone is designed with a smaller form factor while keeping performance high.

entries.definition_en: reducing spending to achieve financial stability
entries.example_cn: 公司宣布缩减开支以改善其财务状况。
entries.example_en: The company announced downsizing to improve its financial position.

entries.definition_en: a slope or bend that goes downwards.
entries.example_cn: 这条路在到达谷底之前有一个陡峭的下坡。
entries.example_en: The road has a steep downslope before it reaches the valley floor.

entries.definition_en: going down a slope
entries.example_cn: 下坡的小路直通河边。
entries.example_en: The downslope path leads directly to the river.

entries.definition_en: down a slope
entries.example_cn: 骑自行车的人沿坡向下朝村庄飞驰。
entries.example_en: The cyclists raced downslope toward the village.

entries.definition_en: toward the front part of the stage
entries.example_cn: 导演指示主角在高潮部分向前走到舞台前部。
entries.example_en: The director instructed the lead to step downstage during the climax.

entries.definition_cn: 朝向电影或电视摄像机
entries.definition_en: toward a film or television camera
entries.example_cn: 演员朝摄像机向前走，以便拍摄特写。
entries.example_en: The actor moved downstage toward the camera for the close-up.

entries.definition_en: located at the front part of a stage
entries.example_cn: 舞台前部的灯光比舞台后方更亮。
entries.example_en: The downstage lighting was brighter than the back of the stage.

entries.definition_en: the front part of a stage visible to the audience
entries.example_cn: 演员走到舞台前部，直接面对人群讲话。
entries.example_en: The actor moved to the downstage area to address the crowd directly.

entries.definition_en: located on or belonging to a lower floor of a building
entries.example_cn: 下层的房间比楼上的安静得多。
entries.example_en: The downstair rooms are much quieter than the ones upstairs.

entries.definition_en: on a floor below
entries.example_cn: 做完作业后请下楼。
entries.example_en: Please come downstairs when you have finished your homework.

entries.definition_en: on or of lower floors of a building
entries.example_cn: 楼下的厨房靠近花园。
entries.example_en: The downstairs kitchen is near the garden.

entries.definition_en: located or moving in the direction of a stream's current
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂位于河流源头向下游的地方。
entries.example_en: The factory is located downstream from the river source.

entries.definition_en: away from the source or with the current
entries.example_cn: 污染物向下游流入海洋。
entries.example_en: Pollutants flow downstream into the ocean.

entries.definition_en: a stroke normally made in a downward direction
entries.example_cn: 游泳者专注于向下划的效率以获得更快的速度。
entries.example_en: The swimmer focused on the efficiency of the downstroke to gain more speed.

entries.definition_en: a period when business or economic activity worsens
entries.example_cn: 该公司在房地产市场严重衰退期间艰难求生。
entries.example_en: The company struggled to survive the severe downswing in the housing market.

entries.definition_en: the downward movement of a golf club during a swing
entries.example_cn: 他专注于使挥杆下摆更流畅，以改善击球效果。
entries.example_en: He focused on smoothing out his downswing to improve his contact with the ball.

entries.definition_cn: 原本稳定或上升的事物的小幅下降
entries.definition_en: a small decrease in something that has been steady or rising
entries.example_cn: April对功课的热情有所下降。
entries.example_en: There was a downtick in April's enthusiasm for schoolwork.

entries.definition_cn: 低于前一笔交易价格的股票市场交易
entries.definition_en: a stock market transaction made at a lower price than the previous one
entries.example_cn: 新闻发布后，该股票出现了一笔低于前次交易价格的交易。
entries.example_en: The stock recorded a downtick after the news announcement.

entries.definition_en: a period when a machine or system is not working
entries.example_cn: 由于停电，工厂经历了数小时的停机时间。
entries.example_en: The factory experienced several hours of downtime due to a power failure.

entries.definition_cn: （加拿大和美国）城镇或城市的主要商业区，通常位于市中心或其附近
entries.definition_en: the main business area of a town or city, usually at or near its center, especially in Canada and the US
entries.example_cn: 该市的市中心今天挤满了购物者。
entries.example_en: The city's downtown is crowded with shoppers today.

entries.definition_en: the center of a city
entries.example_cn: 市议会每周一在城市中心开会。
entries.example_en: The city council meets in downtown every Monday.

entries.definition_cn: 位于城镇下部或商业中心的
entries.definition_en: of or located in the lower part of a town, or in the business center
entries.example_cn: 新图书馆位于市中心。
entries.example_en: The new library is located downtown.

entries.definition_cn: 往城镇下部或中心区；在城镇下部或中心区
entries.definition_en: toward or in the lower or central part of town
entries.example_cn: 我们下班后在市中心见面吧。
entries.example_en: Let's meet downtown after work.

entries.definition_en: abused or oppressed by people in power
entries.example_cn: 受压迫的人们向政府寻求正义。
entries.example_en: The downtrodden people sought justice from the government.

entries.definition_en: trodden down or pressed flat
entries.example_cn: 大门周围有一片被踩实的泥土。
entries.example_en: A patch of downtrodden soil surrounded the gate.

entries.definition_cn: 商业或经济活动恶化的时期；衰退
entries.definition_en: a period when business or economic activity becomes worse
entries.example_cn: 上周股市经历了急剧下跌。
entries.example_en: The stock market experienced a sharp downturn last week.

entries.definition_cn: 在空间或隐喻上从高到低
entries.definition_en: spatially or metaphorically from a higher to a lower level or position
entries.example_cn: 第二季度利润有所下降。
entries.example_en: Profits moved downward during the second quarter.

entries.definition_cn: 从高处向低处延伸或移动的
entries.definition_en: extending or moving from a higher to a lower place
entries.example_cn: 山坡的下坡路使得行走变得困难。
entries.example_en: The downward slope of the hill made the walk difficult.

entries.definition_cn: 在或朝向被视为基面的表面
entries.definition_en: on or toward a surface regarded as a base
entries.example_cn: 重量的向下压力作用在地板上。
entries.example_en: The downward pressure of the weight was felt on the floor.

entries.definition_en: from a higher to a lower level or position, either physically or metaphorically
entries.example_cn: 这张图表从左向右向下倾斜。
entries.example_en: The graph slopes downwardly from left to right.

entries.definition_en: from a higher to a lower level or position
entries.example_cn: 气温整夜持续下降。
entries.example_en: The temperature dropped downwards throughout the night.

entries.definition_en: in the direction the wind is blowing
entries.example_cn: 烟雾顺风飘过田野。
entries.example_en: The smoke drifted downwind across the field.

entries.definition_cn: 位于某物的下风处，因此能闻到其气味
entries.definition_en: in a position downwind of something, so that its smell can be detected
entries.example_cn: 我们住在工厂的下风处，因此能闻到它的气味。
entries.example_en: We lived downwind of the factory, so we could smell it.

entries.definition_en: located towards the side away from the wind
entries.example_cn: 营地建在工厂的下风向，以避免闻到气味。
entries.example_en: The camp was set up downwind from the factory to avoid the smell.

entries.definition_en: covered with fine soft hairs or down
entries.example_cn: 这只幼鸟身上覆盖着细软的绒毛，还不会飞。
entries.example_en: The young bird was downy and unable to fly yet.

entries.definition_en: having the soft, fluffy texture of down
entries.example_cn: 婴儿的头上有一层绒毛般的头发。
entries.example_en: The baby had a downy coat of hair on its head.

entries.definition_en: money or property that a woman brings to her husband when they get married
entries.example_cn: 她的家人为她的婚礼提供了丰厚的嫁妆。
entries.example_en: Her family provided a generous dowry for her wedding.

entries.definition_en: to wet something thoroughly
entries.example_cn: 请在清洁地毯前将其彻底弄湿。
entries.example_en: Please dowse the dry carpet with water before cleaning it.

entries.definition_cn: 用液体覆盖；将液体倒在...上
entries.definition_en: to cover with liquid or pour liquid onto something
entries.example_cn: 她将冷水倒在热锅上以停止燃烧。
entries.example_en: She dowsed the hot pan with cold water to stop the burning.

entries.definition_cn: 用探水棒寻找地下水或金属
entries.definition_en: to use a divining rod in search of underground water or metal
entries.example_cn: 他在花园里用探水棒寻找隐藏的泉水。
entries.example_en: He dowsed the garden to locate the hidden spring.

entries.definition_en: to slacken or loosen
entries.example_cn: 园丁不得不放松根部的土壤以帮助它们呼吸。
entries.example_en: The gardener had to dowse the soil around the roots to help them breathe.

entries.definition_en: the act of searching for underground water or minerals using a dowsing rod
entries.example_cn: 农夫决定使用探水术为他的田地寻找新的水源。
entries.example_en: The farmer decided to dowse to find a new water source for his fields.

entries.definition_en: someone who uses a divining rod to find underground water
entries.example_cn: 当地的探水者声称他能在任何地方找到水。
entries.example_en: The local dowser claimed he could find water anywhere.

entries.definition_en: forked stick that is said to dip down to indicate underground water or oil
entries.example_cn: 探水者拿着分叉的探水棒在干地上挥舞。
entries.example_en: The dowser swung the forked stick over the dry ground.

entries.definition_cn: 用探水棒寻找地下水源或矿物的做法
entries.definition_en: the practice of searching for underground water or minerals using a dowsing rod
entries.example_cn: 村民们相信探水法可以帮助找到隐藏的泉水。
entries.example_en: The villagers believe that dowsing can help locate hidden springs.

entries.definition_en: personal information about an individual that is published without consent
entries.example_cn: 记者拒绝发表证人的个人信息。
entries.example_en: The journalist refused to publish the dox of the witness.

entries.definition_en: documents containing personal information about an individual
entries.example_cn: 黑客在互联网上发布了一份包含个人信息的文件列表。
entries.example_en: The hacker released a list of dox on the internet.

entries.definition_cn: 未经同意公开他人个人信息
entries.definition_en: to publish personal information about someone without their consent
entries.example_cn: 该网站被创建用于未经同意公开腐败官员的个人信息。
entries.example_en: The website was created to dox corrupt officials.

entries.definition_en: a medicine used to lower high blood pressure and treat enlarged prostate by relaxing blood vessels
entries.example_cn: 医生开了多沙唑嗪来帮助控制他的血压。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed doxazosin to help manage his hypertension.

usage.label: uncountable
usage.pattern: The source explicitly marks the drug as uncountable.

entries.definition_cn: 多塞平（一种三环类抗抑郁药，副作用包括口干、镇静和胃肠道紊乱）
entries.definition_en: a tricyclic antidepressant with numerous side effects such as dry mouth, sedation, and gastrointestinal disturbances
entries.example_cn: 医生给他开了多塞平治疗抑郁症，但警告他可能会有副作用。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed doxepin for his depression but warned him about the potential side effects.

entries.definition_cn: 基督教礼拜中赞美上帝的颂歌或短诗
entries.definition_en: a hymn or verse in Christian worship that praises God
entries.example_cn: 礼拜以一首传统的赞美诗结束。
entries.example_en: The service ended with a traditional doxology.

entries.definition_cn: 蒽环类抗肿瘤抗生素；多柔比星
entries.definition_en: an anthracycline antibiotic drug with broad antineoplastic activity
entries.example_cn: 医生给患者开具了多柔比星来治疗其侵袭性肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed doxorubicin to treat the patient's aggressive tumor.

entries.definition_cn: 情人、妓女或情妇（多用于旧式语境）
entries.definition_en: a sweetheart, prostitute, or mistress, chiefly in archaic usage
entries.example_cn: 丑闻揭露了那位政客的情妇住在他的高级公寓里。
entries.example_en: The scandal revealed that the politician had a doxy living in his penthouse.

entries.definition_cn: 一种由四环素衍生的抗生素，用于治疗多种感染
entries.definition_en: an antibiotic derived from tetracycline used to treat many infections
entries.example_cn: 医生开了多西环素来治疗细菌感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed doxycycline to treat the bacterial infection.

entries.definition_en: the most senior or respected member of a particular group
entries.example_cn: 法律界的资深人士被邀请在会议上发言。
entries.example_en: The doyen of the legal community was invited to speak at the conference.

entries.definition_en: a woman who is the senior member of a group, often due to age or experience
entries.example_cn: 作为该部门的资深女性，她以智慧和耐心指导年轻的研究人员。
entries.example_en: As the doyenne of the department, she guided the younger researchers with wisdom and patience.

entries.definition_en: a small ornamental mat placed under a dish or bowl
entries.example_cn: 她把杯垫放在茶杯下面，以保护桌子。
entries.example_en: She placed a doyley under the teacup to protect the table.

entries.definition_en: sleep lightly or for a short period of time
entries.example_cn: 婴儿在温暖的阳光下睡着了。
entries.example_en: The baby dozed off in the warm sun.

entries.definition_en: a light fitful sleep
entries.example_cn: 在长途驾驶前，我小睡了一会儿。
entries.example_en: I took a quick doze before the long drive.

entries.definition_en: a group of twelve things
entries.example_cn: 她买了一打鸡蛋做早餐。
entries.example_en: She bought a dozen eggs for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: being one more than eleven
entries.example_cn: 聚会上有十二个人。
entries.example_en: There were dozens of people at the party.

entries.definition_en: a large number or amount
entries.example_cn: 我们收到了几十份工作申请。
entries.example_en: We received dozens of applications for the job.

entries.definition_en: a large powerful tractor with a blade in front for flattening ground
entries.example_cn: 建筑队使用重型推土机清理了场地。
entries.example_en: The construction crew used a heavy dozer to clear the site.

entries.definition_en: feeling half asleep or drowsy
entries.example_cn: 漫长的旅程让他感到昏昏欲睡。
entries.example_en: The long journey left him feeling dozy.

entries.definition_en: lacking in liveliness, charm, or surprise
entries.example_cn: 这部电影沉闷乏味，没能吸引观众的注意力。
entries.example_en: The movie was a drab affair that failed to hold the audience's attention.

entries.definition_en: lacking brightness or color; dull
entries.example_cn: 她穿着一套由灰色和米色组成的暗淡服装。
entries.example_en: She wore a drab outfit consisting of grey and beige tones.

entries.definition_en: of a dull brownish-yellow or dun color
entries.example_cn: 墙壁被漆成暗黄褐色。
entries.example_en: The walls were painted a drab brownish yellow.

entries.definition_en: causing dejection or sadness
entries.example_cn: 沉闷的天气让每个人都感到沮丧。
entries.example_en: The drab weather made everyone feel down in the dumps.

entries.definition_en: a dull greyish to yellowish or light olive brown color
entries.example_cn: 阴沉天空的灰黄褐色与下方荒凉的景色相映成趣。
entries.example_en: The drab of the overcast sky matched the dull landscape below.

entries.definition_en: in a dull and uninteresting way
entries.example_cn: 这部电影以沉闷的方式结束，让观众感到无聊。
entries.example_en: The movie ended drably, leaving the audience bored.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being dull, plain, and lacking style or elegance
entries.example_cn: 酒店房间的单调乏味让这次住宿非常不愉快。
entries.example_en: The drabness of the hotel room made the stay very unpleasant.

entries.definition_en: any plant of the genus Dracaena, generally with woody stems and funnel-shaped flowers
entries.example_cn: 房间角落里的龙血树为客厅增添了一抹绿色。
entries.example_en: The dracaena in the corner of the room adds a touch of green to the living space.

entries.definition_en: a unit of volume in the apothecary system equal to one eighth of a fluid ounce
entries.example_cn: 药剂师用德拉克马来量取药物。
entries.example_en: The apothecary measured the medicine in drachms.

entries.definition_en: an old unit of weight equal to an eighth of an ounce or 60 grains
entries.example_cn: 这枚古币价值一德拉克马银。
entries.example_en: The ancient coin was valued at one drachm of silver.

entries.definition_en: a British imperial measure of capacity equal to 60 minims or 3.5516 cubic centimeters
entries.example_cn: 处方需要精确到德拉克马的计量。
entries.example_en: The prescription required a precise measurement in drachms.

entries.definition_cn: 希腊以前的基本货币单位
entries.definition_en: the former basic unit of money in Greece
entries.example_cn: 古代硬币曾以德拉克马计价。
entries.example_en: Coins from the ancient era were once valued in drachmas.

entries.definition_cn: 药剂师重量单位，等于八分之一盎司或60格令
entries.definition_en: a unit of apothecary weight equal to an eighth of an ounce or 60 grains
entries.example_cn: 药剂师称取了一德拉克马的粉末。
entries.example_en: The apothecary measured out one drachma of the powder.

entries.definition_en: an early version of a written work
entries.example_cn: 作者寄来了小说的第一稿。
entries.example_en: The author sent the first draft of the novel.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指啤酒等桶装饮料的）一份
entries.definition_en: a serving of beer drawn from a keg
entries.example_cn: 他在酒吧点了一份桶装啤酒。
entries.example_en: He ordered a draft at the bar.

entries.definition_en: a flow of cold air entering a room
entries.example_cn: 关上窗户以阻止穿堂风。
entries.example_en: Close the window to stop the draft.

entries.definition_en: a written order to pay money
entries.example_cn: 银行立即处理了这张汇票。
entries.example_en: The bank processed the draft immediately.

entries.definition_en: to create a preliminary plan or outline
entries.example_cn: 委员会将于下周起草一项新政策。
entries.example_en: The committee will draft a new policy next week.

entries.definition_en: to select someone to serve in the military
entries.example_cn: 他在战争期间被征召入伍。
entries.example_en: He was drafted into the army during the war.

entries.definition_en: a rough sketch or preliminary design
entries.example_cn: 艺术家向我们展示了这幅画的草图。
entries.example_en: The artist showed us the draft of the painting.

entries.definition_en: to create a detailed plan or blueprint
entries.example_cn: 工程师为新桥绘制了蓝图。
entries.example_en: Engineers drafted the plans for the new bridge.

entries.definition_cn: 应征入伍者；被征召服兵役的人
entries.definition_en: a person who is required to join the military
entries.example_cn: 作为一名征召兵，他必须立即去报到参军。
entries.example_en: As a draftee, he had to report to the army immediately.

entries.definition_en: a person who writes a draft of a document or plan
entries.example_cn: 法律顾问花了数周时间修订合同，以确保其无懈可击。
entries.example_en: The legal drafter spent weeks revising the contract to ensure it was watertight.

entries.definition_en: the process of writing a preliminary version of a document to be improved later
entries.example_cn: 团队花了一上午起草新的政策提案。
entries.example_en: The team spent the morning on drafting the new policy proposal.

entries.definition_en: the professional skill of creating technical drawings and blueprints
entries.example_cn: 她正在学习制图，希望成为一名认证的建筑设计师。
entries.example_en: She is studying drafting to become a certified architectural designer.

entries.definition_cn: 跟车滑行；利用尾流减小风阻
entries.definition_en: the practice of following closely behind another vehicle or cyclist to reduce wind resistance
entries.example_cn: 骑行者轮流跟在领骑者身后，以减小风阻。
entries.example_en: The cyclists took turns drafting behind the lead rider.

entries.definition_en: a man who draws plans for buildings or machines
entries.example_cn: 他在一家大型工程公司担任制图员。
entries.example_en: He worked as a draftsman for a large engineering firm.

entries.definition_en: a man who is skilled at drawing pictures or designs
entries.example_cn: 绘图员草绘了新建筑的设计图。
entries.example_en: The draftsman sketched the new building design.

entries.definition_en: the skill of creating artistic pictures or diagrams
entries.example_cn: 她出色的绘图技巧在详细的素描中显而易见。
entries.example_en: Her exceptional draftsmanship was evident in the detailed sketches.

entries.definition_en: a skilled worker who draws plans of buildings or machines
entries.example_cn: 建筑师聘请了一位绘图员为新大楼绘制详细的蓝图。
entries.example_en: The architect hired a draftsperson to create detailed blueprints for the new building.

entries.definition_en: allowing cold air to enter freely; not airtight
entries.example_cn: 这所老房子在冬天非常漏风。
entries.example_en: The old house was very drafty in the winter.

entries.definition_en: to pull something against resistance
entries.example_cn: 他们不得不费力地把那个重箱子拖上楼梯。
entries.example_en: They had to drag the heavy box up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: to draw something slowly or heavily
entries.example_cn: 那匹马拖着马车在泥泞的路上缓慢前行。
entries.example_en: The horse dragged the cart along the muddy road.

entries.definition_en: to move slowly and with great effort
entries.example_cn: 那位老人拖着双腿在地板上移动。
entries.example_en: The old man dragged his legs across the floor.

entries.definition_cn: 迫使某人进入某种境地或采取某种行动
entries.definition_en: to force someone into a situation or course of action
entries.example_cn: 警察试图把嫌疑人强行塞进车里。
entries.example_en: The police tried to drag the suspect into the car.

entries.definition_en: something that slows or delays progress
entries.example_cn: 资金不足是这个项目的主要阻碍。
entries.example_en: Lack of funding is a major drag on the project.

entries.definition_en: something tedious and boring
entries.example_cn: 填写税务表格真是一件烦人的事。
entries.example_en: Filling out tax forms is a real drag.

entries.definition_en: clothing conventionally worn by the opposite sex
entries.example_cn: 他为了参加化装舞会，穿了一件女装。
entries.example_en: He wore a dress as a drag for the costume party.

entries.definition_en: the resistance to motion through a fluid
entries.example_cn: 由于水中的阻力很大，船移动得很慢。
entries.example_en: The boat moved slowly because of the high drag in the water.

entries.definition_en: a fishing boat that uses a trawl net to catch fish
entries.example_cn: 那艘拖网渔船驶向深海，开始了它的夜间捕捞。
entries.example_en: The dragger sailed out into the deep ocean to begin its nightly hunt.

entries.definition_en: a person who pulls or drags something to move it
entries.example_cn: 那个拖拽者费力地将沉重的圆木拖过泥地。
entries.example_en: The dragger struggled to pull the heavy log across the mud.

entries.definition_en: marked by a painfully slow and effortful manner
entries.example_cn: 漫长的徒步旅行对疲惫的徒步者来说是一段缓慢而费力的经历。
entries.example_en: The long walk was a dragging experience for the tired hikers.

entries.definition_en: a coordinated system of measures used to catch criminals or other individuals
entries.example_cn: 警方展开大规模搜捕以寻找失踪的儿童。
entries.example_en: Police launched a dragnet to find the missing child.

entries.definition_en: a conical fishnet dragged through deep water
entries.example_cn: 渔民使用沉重的拖网在海底捕鱼。
entries.example_en: The fishermen used a heavy dragnet to catch fish at the bottom of the ocean.

entries.definition_en: an interpreter and guide in the Near East, especially in the Ottoman Empire
entries.example_cn: 这位东方通事将欧洲外交官与土耳其官员之间的条约进行了翻译。
entries.example_en: The dragoman translated the treaty between the European diplomats and the Turkish officials.

entries.definition_en: a mythical creature from Germanic legends, usually depicted as having a reptilian body, sometimes wings, and breathing fire
entries.example_cn: 骑士勇敢地与守护宝藏的恶龙搏斗。
entries.example_en: The knight fought bravely against the dragon guarding the treasure.

entries.definition_cn: （贬义）凶悍而令人讨厌的女人；泼妇
entries.definition_en: a fierce and unpleasant woman; a harridan, usually used derogatorily
entries.example_cn: 这位婆婆像恶龙般严厉，让儿媳妇根本无法放松。
entries.example_en: The dragon of a mother-in-law made it impossible for her daughter-in-law to relax.

entries.definition_en: a small lizard found in tropical Asia that can glide by spreading wing-like membranes
entries.example_cn: 我们在雨林中看见一只飞蜥在树木间无声地滑翔。
entries.example_en: We spotted a dragon gliding silently between the trees in the rainforest.

entries.definition_en: a small, colorful, scaleless fish that lives on the sea floor in warm waters
entries.example_cn: 海龙在海底的沙地上优雅地游动。
entries.example_en: The dragonet swam gracefully along the sandy bottom of the ocean.

entries.definition_en: a slender insect with iridescent wings that are spread out when resting; it does not sting and eats mosquitoes.
entries.example_cn: 蜻蜓在水面上盘旋，用长腿捕捉蚊子。
entries.example_en: The dragonfly hovered over the pond, catching mosquitoes with its long legs.

entries.definition_cn: 青兰属植物，尤其指香青兰
entries.definition_en: a plant of the genus Dracocephalum, especially D. moldavica
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了香青兰鲜艳的蓝色花朵。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the vibrant blue flowers of the dragonhead plant.

entries.definition_en: to force someone to do something by using threats or pressure
entries.example_cn: 经理强迫员工在周末加班。
entries.example_en: The manager dragooned the staff into working overtime on the weekend.

entries.definition_en: to conquer a region by forcing people to serve in the military
entries.example_cn: 帝国强迫当地人口加入其军队。
entries.example_en: The empire dragooned the local population into its army.

entries.definition_en: a soldier who was part of a heavy cavalry unit in European armies
entries.example_cn: 历史记录将龙骑兵描述为一名装备精良的重骑兵。
entries.example_en: Historical records describe the dragoon as a heavily armed cavalryman.

entries.definition_en: to empty of liquid
entries.example_cn: 烹饪前请把锅里的水排干。
entries.example_en: Please drain the water from the pan before cooking.

entries.definition_en: to deplete of resources
entries.example_cn: 漫长的旅程耗尽了他的精力。
entries.example_en: The long journey drained his energy completely.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人因精力耗尽而虚弱
entries.definition_en: to make someone weak by draining their strength
entries.example_cn: 疾病使他虚弱无力。
entries.example_en: The illness drained him of his strength.

entries.definition_en: a pipe through which liquid is carried away
entries.example_cn: 我们需要修理厨房里的旧排水管。
entries.example_en: We need to fix the old drain in the kitchen.

entries.definition_cn: 排出液体使某物变空的过程
entries.definition_en: the act or process of emptying something by allowing liquid to run out
entries.example_cn: 排干地下室排出了积聚在那里的水。
entries.example_en: Draining the basement removed the water that had collected there.

entries.definition_cn: 精力或资源的逐渐消耗
entries.definition_en: a gradual depletion of energy or resources
entries.example_cn: 持续的噪音消耗了工人的精神力。
entries.example_en: The constant noise was a mental drain on the workers.

entries.definition_en: a tube inserted into a body cavity during surgery to remove unwanted material
entries.example_cn: 外科医生插入引流管以排出伤口中的多余液体。
entries.example_en: The surgeon inserted a drain to remove excess fluid from the wound.

entries.definition_en: to flow off gradually
entries.example_cn: 泪水顺着她的脸颊流了下来。
entries.example_en: The tears began to drain down her cheeks.

entries.definition_en: the process of emptying something by allowing liquid to flow out of it
entries.example_cn: 花园的排水系统需要修理。
entries.example_en: The drainage system in the garden needs repair.

entries.definition_en: extremely exhausted
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，她感到精疲力竭。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, she felt completely drained.

entries.definition_en: emptied of liquid
entries.example_cn: 雨停后，桶里的水被排空了。
entries.example_en: The bucket was drained after the rain stopped.

entries.definition_en: having no electric charge left; discharged
entries.example_cn: 电池电量已耗尽，需要充电。
entries.example_en: The battery is drained and needs to be recharged.

entries.definition_cn: 消耗精力或资源的；令人筋疲力尽的
entries.definition_en: causing depletion of energy or resources; exhausting
entries.example_cn: 长途旅行令人筋疲力尽，使他精疲力竭。
entries.example_en: The long journey was draining and left him exhausted.

entries.definition_en: a pipe used to carry away rainwater or wastewater
entries.example_cn: 水管工换掉了旧的排水管以防止漏水。
entries.example_en: The plumber replaced the old drainpipe with a new one to prevent leaks.

entries.definition_en: an adult male duck
entries.example_cn: 我们在池塘里看到一只雄鸭在母鸭中间游泳。
entries.example_en: We saw a drake swimming among the female ducks in the pond.

entries.definition_en: a small amount of a strong alcoholic drink or poison
entries.example_cn: 他在热茶中加了少量白兰地。
entries.example_en: He added a dram of brandy to the hot tea.

entries.definition_cn: 德拉姆（亚美尼亚货币单位）
entries.definition_en: the basic unit of currency in Armenia
entries.example_cn: 游客在埃里温用餐时以德拉姆支付。
entries.example_en: Tourists in Yerevan pay for their meals in drams.

entries.definition_cn: 德拉克马（十六分之一盎司）
entries.definition_en: a unit of weight equal to one-sixteenth of an ounce
entries.example_cn: 在某些历史背景下，德拉克马指代较小的 1.771 克单位。
entries.example_en: In some historical contexts, a dram referred to a smaller measure of 1.771 grams.

entries.definition_en: an old unit of weight equal to an eighth of an ounce
entries.example_cn: 药剂师用小型天平以德拉克马为单位称量药物。
entries.example_en: The apothecary measured the medicine in drams using a small balance scale.

entries.definition_en: a play or other work written for actors to perform on a stage
entries.example_cn: 学校的戏剧在大厅上演。
entries.example_en: The school drama was performed in the main hall.

entries.definition_cn: 动荡或情绪高度激烈的事件或局面
entries.definition_en: a turbulent or highly emotional event or situation
entries.example_cn: 他们的争吵变成了一场真正的风波。
entries.example_en: Their argument turned into a real drama.

entries.definition_cn: 作为文学或戏剧体裁的戏剧作品；戏剧艺术
entries.definition_en: plays considered as a literary or theatrical genre
entries.example_cn: 莎士比亚以其对戏剧文学的贡献而闻名。
entries.example_en: Shakespeare is famous for his contribution to drama.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being exciting or causing strong emotions
entries.example_cn: 这部电影情节跌宕起伏，让观众一直屏息凝神。
entries.example_en: The movie had a lot of drama and kept the audience on the edge of their seats.

entries.definition_cn: 引人注目的；令人印象深刻的
entries.definition_en: striking or impressive in appearance or effect
entries.example_cn: 天气的剧烈变化引起了每个人的注意。
entries.example_en: The dramatic change in the weather caught everyone's attention.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to drama or the theater
entries.example_cn: 这部戏剧是对真实故事的戏剧性重述。
entries.example_en: The play was a dramatic retelling of the true story.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of drama or theatrical performance
entries.example_cn: 这部电影包含了充满冲突与和解的戏剧性场景。
entries.example_en: The movie featured dramatic scenes of conflict and resolution.

entries.definition_en: having a powerful, expressive, and theatrical singing style
entries.example_cn: 这位歌剧歌手的戏剧化嗓音响彻了整个大厅。
entries.example_en: The opera singer had a dramatic voice that filled the entire hall.

entries.definition_en: to a great or striking degree
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术极大地提高了我们的沟通能力。
entries.example_en: The new technology has dramatically improved our ability to communicate.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is like a play or movie
entries.example_cn: 演出期间天气发生了戏剧性的变化。
entries.example_en: The weather changed dramatically during the performance.

entries.definition_en: in terms of dramatic quality or value
entries.example_cn: 小说的结局在戏剧效果上非常成功。
entries.example_en: The ending of the novel is dramatically effective.

entries.definition_en: the art of acting and stagecraft
entries.example_cn: 她加入了学校的戏剧俱乐部以提高演技。
entries.example_en: She joined the school's dramatics club to improve her acting skills.

entries.definition_en: dramatic behavior
entries.example_cn: 他的夸张举止让一场小争执看起来像危机。
entries.example_en: His dramatics made a simple disagreement seem like a crisis.

entries.definition_en: conversion into dramatic form
entries.example_cn: 这部小说是对真实事件成功的戏剧化改编。
entries.example_en: The novel was a successful dramatisation of the true events.

entries.definition_en: a dramatic representation
entries.example_cn: 这部电影生动地表现了这场历史冲突。
entries.example_en: The film offered a vivid dramatisation of the historical conflict.

entries.definition_en: to represent something in a dramatic manner
entries.example_cn: 这部电影以戏剧的方式表现了两国之间的紧张局势。
entries.example_en: The movie dramatises the tension between the two rival nations.

entries.definition_en: to present a story or event in a dramatic form, such as a play or film
entries.example_cn: 作者决定将这些历史事件戏剧化，用于新的电视剧系列。
entries.example_en: The author decided to dramatise the historical events for the new television series.

entries.definition_cn: 使某事显得更戏剧化，常通过夸张
entries.definition_en: make something seem more dramatic, often by exaggerating it
entries.example_cn: 他往往把童年回忆说得比实际更加精彩，以此使其显得更戏剧化。
entries.example_en: He tends to dramatise his childhood memories, making them sound more exciting than they were.

entries.definition_en: a person who writes plays
entries.example_cn: 莎士比亚被认为是历史上最伟大的剧作家之一。
entries.example_en: Shakespeare is considered one of the greatest dramatists in history.

entries.definition_en: a dramatic representation of a story
entries.example_cn: 这部舞台剧提供了小说独特的戏剧化表现。
entries.example_en: The stage production offered a unique dramatization of the novel.

entries.definition_en: a version of a story that has been dramatized
entries.example_cn: 这部电影忠实地改编了真实事件。
entries.example_en: The movie was a faithful dramatization of the true events.

entries.definition_cn: 以戏剧化或夸张煽情的方式表现
entries.definition_en: to present something in a dramatic or melodramatic manner
entries.example_cn: 新闻报道渲染了这两个国家之间的冲突。
entries.example_en: The news report dramatizes the conflict between the two nations.

entries.definition_cn: 把文学作品改编成适合在剧院、广播或电视上演出或播出的形式
entries.definition_en: to adapt a literary work so that it can be performed in the theatre, on radio, or on television
entries.example_cn: 导演将这部小说改编成电视剧。
entries.example_en: The director dramatizes the novel for television.

entries.definition_en: to make a story or account more dramatic, often by exaggerating it
entries.example_cn: 他试图添油加醋地描述他的童年经历，使其更有趣。
entries.example_en: He tried to dramatize his childhood experiences to make them more interesting.

entries.definition_en: relating to the technical aspects and structure of drama
entries.example_cn: 导演专注于戏剧理论元素，以改善剧本的节奏。
entries.example_en: The director focused on the dramaturgical elements to improve the play's pacing.

entries.definition_cn: 舞台剧作的艺术与理论
entries.definition_en: the art and theory of composing plays for the stage
entries.example_cn: 她学习戏剧创作与制作，以了解如何为舞台构建引人入胜的叙事。
entries.example_en: She studied dramaturgy to understand how to structure a compelling narrative for the stage.

entries.definition_cn: 松垂地挂在或搭在某物上
entries.definition_en: to hang or place loosely over something
entries.example_cn: 他把外套随意地搭在椅子背上。
entries.example_en: He draped his coat over the back of the chair.

entries.definition_en: to cover someone or something with a cloth
entries.example_cn: 他们用白布遮盖了桌子，为婚礼做准备。
entries.example_en: They draped the table with a white cloth for the wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 用布料覆盖或装饰；使形成褶皱
entries.definition_en: to cover or adorn something with drapery or folds of cloth
entries.example_cn: 设计师将丝绸布料布置在人体模型上。
entries.example_en: The designer draped the silk fabric over the mannequin.

entries.definition_en: to dress someone loosely with cloth
entries.example_cn: 士兵们用毯子松散地包裹了受伤的男子。
entries.example_en: The soldiers draped the wounded man with a blanket.

entries.definition_en: a piece of cloth hung to cover a window
entries.example_cn: 她拉上厚重的窗帘挡住阳光。
entries.example_en: She pulled the heavy drape across the window to block the sun.

entries.definition_en: the way in which fabric hangs or falls
entries.example_cn: 天鹅绒具有美丽的垂坠感，非常适合做窗帘。
entries.example_en: The velvet has a beautiful drape that makes it ideal for curtains.

entries.definition_cn: 检查或手术时盖在患者身上的无菌布单
entries.definition_en: a sterile cloth covering used during surgery
entries.example_cn: 外科医生在病人的腿上盖上了无菌手术单。
entries.example_en: The surgeon placed a sterile drape over the patient's legs.

entries.definition_en: covered with or as if with clothes or a wrap or cloak
entries.example_cn: 雕像披着白布。
entries.example_en: The statue was draped in a white sheet.

entries.definition_cn: 布料松垂并形成褶皱的
entries.definition_en: hanging in loose folds of fabric
entries.example_cn: 窗帘以优雅的褶皱垂挂在窗前。
entries.example_en: The curtains were draped elegantly across the window.

entries.definition_en: a person who sells fabrics and sewing materials
entries.example_cn: 那位布料商帮我挑选了做窗帘的完美面料。
entries.example_en: The draper helped me choose the perfect fabric for my curtains.

entries.definition_en: hanging cloth used as a blind (especially for a window)
entries.example_cn: 她调整厚重的窗帘，让更多阳光照进来。
entries.example_en: She adjusted the heavy drapery to let in more sunlight.

entries.definition_en: cloth gracefully draped and arranged in loose folds
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家研究织物的垂褶，以了解光线如何落在褶皱上。
entries.example_en: The artist studied the drapery of the fabric to understand how light falls on folds.

entries.definition_en: extremely severe or forceful
entries.example_cn: 政府采取了严厉的措施来控制通货膨胀。
entries.example_en: The government introduced drastic measures to control inflation.

entries.definition_en: in a drastic manner
entries.example_cn: 公司不得不大幅裁员以生存下去。
entries.example_en: The company had to drastically reduce its staff to survive.

entries.definition_en: a serving of beer or other drink poured directly from a keg
entries.example_cn: 他在酒吧点了一杯生啤。
entries.example_en: He ordered a draught of ale at the pub.

entries.definition_en: a current of cool air moving into a room or vehicle
entries.example_cn: 关上窗户以阻止冷风灌入。
entries.example_en: Close the window to stop the cold draught.

entries.definition_en: the vertical distance from the waterline to the bottom of a ship's keel
entries.example_cn: 这艘船的吃水深度太深，无法通过这条浅河。
entries.example_en: The ship's draught was too deep for the shallow river.

entries.definition_en: a large, hurried swallow of liquid
entries.example_cn: 长跑结束后，他大口喝了一口水。
entries.example_en: After the long run, he took a draught of water.

entries.definition_en: a single dose of liquid medicine
entries.example_cn: 每四小时服用一次这种糖浆。
entries.example_en: Take one draught of this syrup every four hours.

entries.definition_en: to create a technical drawing or blueprint of something
entries.example_cn: 建筑师下周将绘制新建筑的蓝图。
entries.example_en: The architect will draught the new building plans next week.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving a heavy load by pulling or drawing it
entries.example_cn: 牛被用来拖曳沉重的原木。
entries.example_en: The oxen were used for the draught of heavy logs.

entries.definition_en: a board game for two players where the goal is to jump over and capture the opponent's pieces
entries.example_cn: 他们下午在花园的桌子上玩跳棋。
entries.example_en: They spent the afternoon playing draughts on the garden table.

entries.definition_en: a man who draws technical plans or designs for buildings or machines
entries.example_cn: 建筑师聘请了一位熟练的制图员来绘制新桥的详细蓝图。
entries.example_en: The architect hired a skilled draughtsman to create the detailed blueprints for the new bridge.

entries.definition_en: A piece used in the game of draughts (checkers).
entries.example_cn: 她将自己的跳棋棋子沿对角线移动，吃掉了对手的棋子。
entries.example_en: She moved her draughtsman diagonally across the board and captured her opponent's piece.

entries.definition_en: allowing cold air to enter freely
entries.example_cn: 这所老房子在冬天非常漏风。
entries.example_en: The old house was very draughty in winter.

entries.definition_en: to make marks or lines on a surface
entries.example_cn: 你能画一只猫吗？
entries.example_en: Can you draw a picture of a cat?

entries.definition_en: to cause to move by pulling
entries.example_cn: 他拉开窗帘。
entries.example_en: He drew the curtain open.

entries.definition_en: to get or derive something
entries.example_cn: 她从旅行中获得灵感。
entries.example_en: She drew inspiration from her travels.

entries.definition_en: to formulate or derive in the mind
entries.example_cn: 他从证据中得出了结论。
entries.example_en: He drew a conclusion from the evidence.

entries.definition_en: a contest where the score is tied and no winner is decided
entries.example_cn: 比赛以平局结束。
entries.example_en: The match ended in a draw.

entries.definition_en: an entertainer who attracts large audiences
entries.example_cn: 这位著名歌手是音乐会的一大吸引力。
entries.example_en: The famous singer was a major draw at the concert.

entries.definition_en: items chosen at random
entries.example_cn: 我们用抽签方式选出赢家。
entries.example_en: We used a draw to select the winner.

entries.definition_en: a shallow gully
entries.example_cn: 河流在地面上形成了一条浅沟。
entries.example_en: The river formed a shallow draw in the earth.

entries.definition_en: a disadvantage or something that makes a situation less favorable
entries.example_cn: 高昂的费用是这款新软件的主要缺点。
entries.example_en: The high cost is the main drawback of this new software.

entries.definition_en: a strong metal bar with a hook used to attach something to be pulled
entries.example_cn: 这辆卡车配备了重型牵引杆来拖拽拖车。
entries.example_en: The truck was equipped with a heavy drawbar to pull the trailer.

entries.definition_cn: 哈蒙德风琴上控制波形音量的滑杆
entries.definition_en: a sliding bar on a Hammond organ that controls the volume of a waveform
entries.example_cn: 她调节哈蒙德风琴上的滑杆来改变声音的音量。
entries.example_en: She adjusted the drawbars on the Hammond organ to change the sound's volume.

entries.definition_en: a bridge that can be raised to block passage or to allow boats or ships to pass beneath it
entries.example_cn: 吊桥被升起以阻止敌人进入城堡。
entries.example_en: The drawbridge was raised to stop the enemy from entering the castle.

entries.definition_en: the person or bank expected to pay a check or draft
entries.example_cn: 付款银行因资金不足而拒绝兑付汇票。
entries.example_en: The drawee bank refused to honor the draft due to insufficient funds.

entries.definition_en: a box-shaped container in furniture that slides in and out
entries.example_cn: 她把钥匙放进了最上面的抽屉里。
entries.example_en: She put her keys in the top drawer.

entries.definition_en: the person who writes a check or draft instructing the drawee to pay someone else
entries.example_cn: 支票的出票人必须签名才能使支票生效。
entries.example_en: The drawer of the check must sign it to make it valid.

entries.definition_en: an artist skilled at drawing
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的画家创作了许多风景素描。
entries.example_en: The famous drawer created many sketches of the landscape.

entries.definition_cn: （过时、非正式的地区用语，仅用复数形式）内裤，尤指长内裤
entries.definition_en: dated, informal, regional, plural-only: underpants, especially long underpants
entries.example_cn: 客人到达时，他还穿着内裤。
entries.example_en: He was still in his drawers when the guests arrived.

entries.definition_cn: （俚语，仅用复数形式）腿部衣物，如短裤、长裤或紧身裤
entries.definition_en: slang, plural-only: clothing covering the legs, such as shorts, trousers, or tights
entries.example_cn: 在俚语中，drawers 可以指短裤或长裤。
entries.example_en: In slang, drawers can refer to shorts or trousers.

entries.definition_en: an illustration created by hand and published in books, magazines, or newspapers
entries.example_cn: 报纸刊登了事故现场的一张详细插图。
entries.example_en: The newspaper featured a detailed drawing of the accident scene.

entries.definition_en: a representation of forms or objects on a surface using lines
entries.example_cn: 她花了一下午在黑板上画了几何线条画。
entries.example_en: She spent the afternoon creating a geometric drawing on the blackboard.

entries.definition_en: the activity of creating artistic pictures or diagrams
entries.example_cn: 他很有绘画天赋，经常素描动物。
entries.example_en: He has a talent for drawing and often sketches animals.

entries.definition_en: a game where players buy chances and prizes are distributed by casting lots
entries.example_cn: 公司举行了一次抽奖活动来选出幸运赢家。
entries.example_en: The company held a drawing to select the lucky winner.

entries.definition_en: the act of getting or draining something such as electricity or a liquid from a source
entries.example_cn: 这台机器旨在高效地从井中抽取水。
entries.example_en: The machine is designed for the efficient drawing of water from the well.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving a load by pulling or dragging
entries.example_cn: 重型卡车被用来在田野上拖曳货物。
entries.example_en: The heavy truck was used for the drawing of the cargo across the field.

entries.definition_en: a slow way of speaking with long vowels
entries.example_cn: 她用一种难以理解的南方拖长语调说话。
entries.example_en: She spoke with a Southern drawl that was hard to understand.

entries.definition_en: to speak slowly with prolonged vowels
entries.example_cn: 他拖长音讲了一个小时的故事。
entries.example_en: He drawled the story out for an hour.

entries.definition_en: looking tired because of too much work or suffering
entries.example_cn: 经过一周的加班，她看起来憔悴不堪。
entries.example_en: She looked drawn after the long week of overtime.

entries.definition_en: having curtains or draperies closed
entries.example_cn: 房间昏暗且拉上了窗帘。
entries.example_en: The room was dark and drawn, with the curtains pulled shut.

entries.definition_en: lasting for a long time, often in a boring way
entries.example_cn: 那场冗长的会议持续了四个小时。
entries.example_en: The drawn-out meeting lasted for four hours.

entries.definition_en: (of speech) spoken slowly with long vowel sounds
entries.example_cn: 他把最后一个元音的发音拖得很长。
entries.example_en: He gave a drawn-out pronunciation of the final vowel.

entries.definition_en: a cord threaded through a seam to close an opening
entries.example_cn: 她系紧袋子的抽绳，以防里面的东西掉出来。
entries.example_en: She tied the drawstring of her bag to keep the contents secure.

entries.definition_cn: （历史上）无侧板、用于运货的低矮重型马车
entries.definition_en: historically, a low, heavy horse-drawn cart without sides, used for hauling goods
entries.example_cn: 他们把沉重的箱子装上运货马车运往仓库。
entries.example_en: They loaded the heavy crates onto the dray to transport them to the warehouse.

entries.definition_en: be afraid or scared of
entries.example_cn: 许多人畏惧飞行。
entries.example_en: Many people dread flying.

entries.definition_en: fearful expectation or anticipation
entries.example_cn: 她深深恐惧即将到来的风暴。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep dread of the coming storm.

entries.definition_en: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.example_cn: 可怕的考试终于结束了。
entries.example_en: The dreaded exam was finally over.

entries.definition_en: causing great fear or terror
entries.example_cn: 令人恐惧的考试终于结束了。
entries.example_en: The dreaded exam was finally over.

entries.definition_en: exceptionally bad or displeasing
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅的服务极差。
entries.example_en: The service at the restaurant was dreadful.

entries.definition_en: extremely disagreeable and unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 那是一个大雨滂沱、寒风刺骨的极其令人不快的日子。
entries.example_en: It was a dreadful day with heavy rain and cold wind.

entries.definition_en: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.example_cn: 那场可怕的暴风雨让村民们陷入了恐慌。
entries.example_en: The dreadful storm caused panic among the villagers.

entries.definition_en: to an exceptionally great degree; very much (dated)
entries.example_cn: 那家餐馆似乎贵得离谱。
entries.example_en: That restaurant seems dreadfully expensive.

entries.definition_en: in a dreadful or terrible manner; terribly
entries.example_cn: 他在正式晚宴上的表现糟糕透顶。
entries.example_en: He behaved dreadfully at the formal dinner.

entries.definition_en: one of many long thin braids of hair radiating from the scalp, popularized by Rastafarians
entries.example_cn: 她留着紧实的脏辫，长度及肩。
entries.example_en: She wore her hair in tight dreadlocks that reached her shoulders.

entries.definition_en: a battleship equipped with big guns of the same caliber
entries.example_cn: 那艘无畏舰凭借其巨大的火力主导了海战。
entries.example_en: The dreadnaught dominated the naval battle with its massive firepower.

entries.definition_en: a large battleship with guns of uniform caliber
entries.example_cn: 舰队包括几艘现代化的无畏舰。
entries.example_en: The fleet included several modern dreadnoughts.

entries.definition_en: a series of mental images and emotions occurring during sleep
entries.example_cn: 我昨晚做了一个奇怪的梦。
entries.example_en: I had a strange dream last night.

entries.definition_en: a cherished desire
entries.example_cn: 她的梦想是环游世界。
entries.example_en: Her dream is to travel around the world.

entries.definition_en: imaginative thoughts indulged in while awake
entries.example_cn: 他整个下午都在幻想在巴黎的生活。
entries.example_en: He spent the whole afternoon dreaming of a life in Paris.

entries.definition_en: someone or something wonderful
entries.example_cn: 他是我的梦中伴侣。
entries.example_en: He is my dream partner.

entries.definition_en: experience while sleeping
entries.example_cn: 我昨晚没做梦。
entries.example_en: I didn't dream last night.

entries.definition_en: have a daydream; indulge in a fantasy
entries.example_cn: 她正做着成为著名歌手的白日梦。
entries.example_en: She was dreaming about becoming a famous singer.

entries.definition_en: a state of mind characterized by abstraction and release from reality
entries.example_cn: 听着音乐，她陷入了出神的状态。
entries.example_en: She was in a dream while listening to the music.

entries.definition_cn: 不切实际的幻想；鸦片梦
entries.definition_en: a fantastic but vain hope (from fantasies induced by the opium pipe)
entries.example_cn: 那位政治家的承诺不过是空中楼阁。
entries.example_en: The politician's promises were nothing but a dream.

entries.definition_en: someone guided more by ideals than by practical considerations
entries.example_cn: 他是一个相信更美好未来的理想主义者。
entries.example_en: He is a dreamer who believes in a better future.

entries.definition_en: a person who escapes into a world of fantasy
entries.example_cn: 别叫他幻想家，他只是喜欢想象事情。
entries.example_en: Don't call him a dreamer; he just likes to imagine things.

entries.definition_en: someone who is dreaming
entries.example_cn: 那个梦者在睡梦中笑了。
entries.example_en: The dreamer smiled in his sleep.

entries.definition_en: in a dreamy manner
entries.example_cn: 她梦幻般地凝视着星星。
entries.example_en: She looked at the stars dreamily.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being dreamy
entries.example_cn: 女孩无法理解母亲目光中那种梦幻般的神情。
entries.example_en: There was a dreaminess in her mother's look that the girl could not understand.

entries.definition_en: a series of mental images and emotions occurring during sleep
entries.example_cn: 梦见自己飞越海洋让她觉得这一切真实而美妙。
entries.example_en: Dreaming that she was flying over the ocean felt wonderfully real to her.

entries.definition_en: imaginative thoughts indulged in while awake
entries.example_cn: 他花了一下午的时间畅想未来的职业。
entries.example_en: He spent his afternoon dreaming of a future career.

entries.definition_cn: 梦境；想象中的理想世界
entries.definition_en: an imaginary world experienced in a dream or imagined as ideal
entries.example_cn: 这个故事描述了一个神奇的梦境乐土，那里的动物会说话。
entries.example_en: The story describes a magical dreamland where animals can talk.

entries.definition_en: having no dreams; without dreaming
entries.example_cn: 婴儿整夜无梦地沉睡。
entries.example_en: The baby slept through the night in a dreamless slumber.

entries.definition_en: resembling a dream
entries.example_cn: 清晨的薄雾中，山谷呈现出如梦似幻的景象。
entries.example_en: The valley had a dreamlike quality in the morning mist.

entries.definition_cn: 梦幻世界；想象中的世界
entries.definition_en: an imaginary world, especially one experienced in dreams or fantasy
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在沙箱里建造了一个宏伟的梦幻世界。
entries.example_en: The children built a magnificent dreamworld in the sandbox.

entries.definition_en: having a soft, romantic, or imaginative quality
entries.example_cn: 这部电影有着梦幻般的氛围，配乐柔和。
entries.example_en: The movie had a dreamy atmosphere with soft music.

entries.definition_en: tending to dream or daydream
entries.example_cn: 她望着火车窗外，脸上带着爱幻想的神情。
entries.example_en: She had a dreamy expression as she gazed out of the train window.

entries.definition_en: causing sadness or depression
entries.example_cn: 阴沉的天气让每个人都感到情绪低落。
entries.example_en: The drear weather made everyone feel gloomy.

usage.label: literary; poetic
usage.pattern: Source w46346r0 labels the adjective literary and poetic.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that is cheerless and dull
entries.example_cn: 雨整夜沉闷地打在窗户上。
entries.example_en: The rain fell drearily against the window all night long.

entries.definition_en: a state of being extremely dull and lacking spirit or interest
entries.example_cn: 漫长冬季的沉闷让每个人都感到疲惫。
entries.example_en: The dreariness of the long winter made everyone feel tired.

entries.definition_en: boring and lacking in interest or excitement
entries.example_cn: 我们度过了一个沉闷的周末，坐在雨中。
entries.example_en: We spent a dreary weekend sitting in the rain.

entries.definition_en: causing sadness or depression
entries.example_cn: 令人沮丧的消息让每个人都感到低落。
entries.example_en: The dreary news made everyone feel down.

entries.definition_en: merchandise that is shoddy or inferior
entries.example_cn: 这家商店里全是没人想买的劣质货。
entries.example_en: The store was full of dreck that nobody wanted to buy.

entries.definition_en: to remove material from the bottom of a river or harbor using a dredge
entries.example_cn: 港口当局疏浚航道以便大型船只通行。
entries.example_en: The port authority dredged the channel to allow larger ships to pass.

entries.definition_en: to search the bottom of a body of water for lost or valuable items
entries.example_cn: 他们雇佣了一个团队在湖底搜寻丢失的戒指。
entries.example_en: They hired a team to dredge the lake for the missing ring.

entries.definition_en: to cover food with a dry ingredient like breadcrumbs or flour before cooking
entries.example_cn: 炸鸡肉前应该先用面粉裹一下。
entries.example_en: You should dredge the chicken in flour before frying it.

usage.label: dredge something with/in flour
usage.pattern: Source w17395r3 supports the transitive food-preparation construction.

entries.definition_en: a large machine with a shovel used to remove sand or mud from a river or harbor
entries.example_cn: 挖泥船清除了河底的淤泥。
entries.example_en: The dredge cleared the silt from the bottom of the river.

entries.definition_en: a barge or vessel used for dredging
entries.example_cn: 挖泥船清除了港口入口处的沙子。
entries.example_en: The dredger cleared the sand from the harbor entrance.

entries.definition_en: a small amount of solid matter left at the bottom of a liquid
entries.example_cn: 他把酒倒进杯子里，把瓶底的渣滓留了下来。
entries.example_en: He poured the wine into a glass, leaving the dregs in the bottle.

entries.definition_cn: 沉淀在液体底部的残渣
entries.definition_en: sediment that has settled at the bottom of a liquid
entries.example_cn: 他喝完了最后一口咖啡，连渣滓也没放过。
entries.example_en: He drank the last of the coffee, including the dregs.

entries.definition_cn: 某事物最糟糕或最低劣的部分
entries.definition_en: the worst or lowest part of something
entries.example_cn: 社会上的败类聚集在这座城市废弃的建筑物里。
entries.example_en: The dregs of society gathered in the city's abandoned buildings.

entries.definition_en: to pour liquid onto something
entries.example_cn: 她在清洁地板前把干海绵浇上了水。
