entries.definition_en: vastness of size or extent
entries.example_cn: 这项任务的巨大规模需要一支专家团队。
entries.example_en: The enormity of the task required a team of experts.

entries.definition_en: the quality of extreme wickedness
entries.example_cn: 他的残忍行径极度邪恶，令所有人震惊。
entries.example_en: The enormity of his cruelty shocked everyone.

entries.definition_en: an act of extreme wickedness
entries.example_cn: 战争罪行的极度邪恶是无可否认的。
entries.example_en: The enormity of the war crimes was undeniable.

entries.definition_en: extraordinarily large in size, extent, amount, power, or degree
entries.example_cn: 巨大的人群挤满了整个体育场。
entries.example_en: The enormous crowd filled the entire stadium.

entries.definition_en: to a very great degree or extent; vastly
entries.example_cn: 这场风暴对那栋房屋造成了极大的破坏。
entries.example_en: The storm damaged the house enormously.

entries.definition_cn: 希腊与塞浦路斯的合并
entries.definition_en: the union of Greece and Cyprus
entries.example_cn: 希腊与塞浦路斯的合并是20世纪中叶希腊塞浦路斯人的主要政治目标。
entries.example_en: The concept of enosis was a major political goal for Greek Cypriots in the mid-20th century.

entries.definition_en: as much as necessary
entries.example_cn: 你今天已经学够了。
entries.example_en: You have studied enough for today.

entries.definition_en: sufficient for the purpose
entries.example_cn: 有足够的食物给每个人吗？
entries.example_en: Is there enough food for everyone?

entries.definition_en: an adequate quantity; a quantity that is large enough to achieve a purpose
entries.example_cn: 我们有足够的东西去旅行。
entries.example_en: We have enough for the trip.

entries.definition_en: to address a question to and expect an answer from
entries.example_cn: 我想询问一下这家酒店是否有空房。
entries.example_en: I would like to enquire about the availability of the hotel.

entries.definition_en: to conduct an inquiry or investigation of
entries.example_cn: 警方将调查事故原因。
entries.example_en: The police will enquire into the cause of the accident.

entries.definition_en: to have a wish or desire to know something
entries.example_cn: 她想知道是否还有座位。
entries.example_en: She enquired if there were any seats left.

entries.definition_en: someone who asks a question
entries.example_cn: 询问者耐心地等待回答。
entries.example_en: The enquirer waited patiently for an answer.

entries.definition_en: an act of asking questions to get information
entries.example_cn: 我询问了火车时刻表。
entries.example_en: I made an enquiry about the train schedule.

entries.definition_en: an effort to find out something or learn more about a subject
entries.example_cn: 这位科学家对疾病的成因进行了探究。
entries.example_en: The scientist conducted an enquiry into the causes of the disease.

entries.definition_en: a formal investigation into a matter of public interest
entries.example_cn: 议会启动了一项调查以审查该丑闻。
entries.example_en: A parliamentary enquiry was launched to examine the scandal.

entries.definition_en: to put someone into a rage; to make them violently angry
entries.example_cn: 这个不公平的决定激怒了整个团队。
entries.example_en: The unfair decision enraged the entire team.

entries.definition_en: extremely angry
entries.example_cn: 狂怒的人群冲进了大楼。
entries.example_en: The enraged crowd stormed the building.

entries.definition_en: to hold someone spellbound or in a state of great delight
entries.example_cn: 美丽的日落令所有观赏者陶醉。
entries.example_en: The beautiful sunset enraptured everyone who watched it.

entries.definition_en: feeling great delight or ecstasy
entries.example_cn: 她陶醉于日落的美景。
entries.example_en: She was enraptured by the beauty of the sunset.

entries.definition_en: to make something better or improve its quality
entries.example_cn: 去不同的国家旅行可以增进你对其他文化的理解。
entries.example_en: Traveling to different countries can enrich your cultural understanding.

entries.definition_en: to make someone wealthy or richer
entries.example_cn: 石油的发现极大地丰富了当地社区。
entries.example_en: The discovery of oil enriched the local community significantly.

entries.definition_cn: 使更充实、更有意义或更有回报的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of making something fuller, more meaningful, or more rewarding
entries.example_cn: 大学为国际学生提供了一项充实课程计划。
entries.example_en: The university offers an enrichment program for international students.

entries.definition_cn: 大幅增加受赠者财富的礼物
entries.definition_en: a gift that significantly increases the recipient's wealth
entries.example_cn: 这笔继承款是他储蓄的一笔意外之财。
entries.example_en: The inheritance was a welcome enrichment to his savings.

entries.definition_en: to register formally as a participant or member
entries.example_cn: 学生必须在截止日期前注册该课程。
entries.example_en: Students must enrol in the course before the deadline.

usage.label: British, Australian, Canadian, Irish, New Zealand spelling
usage.pattern: Source w27863r0 labels enrol as the standard regional spelling of enroll.

entries.definition_en: to register formally as a participant or member
entries.example_cn: 学生必须在截止日期前注册。
entries.example_en: Students must enroll before the deadline.

usage.label: enroll in something
usage.pattern: 常与 in 连用，表示加入课程或机构。

entries.definition_en: a person who has enrolled in a class or course of study.
entries.example_cn: 每位注册学员在学期开始前都收到了一份欢迎手册。
entries.example_en: Every enrollee received a welcome packet before the semester began.

entries.definition_en: the act of signing up to join an organization or course
entries.example_cn: 今年的大学注册人数显著增加。
entries.example_en: The university enrollment increased significantly this year.

entries.definition_cn: 同时注册或入学的一群人
entries.definition_en: the group of people who have registered at the same time
entries.example_cn: 新入学的学生来自五十多个国家。
entries.example_en: The new enrollment includes students from over fifty countries.

entries.definition_en: the act of enrolling
entries.example_cn: 今年该校的注册人数创下了历史新高。
entries.example_en: The university saw a record increase in enrolment this year.

entries.definition_cn: 使安全安置；使舒适安坐
entries.definition_en: to place someone or something securely, or settle comfortably
entries.example_cn: 木匠把那件贵重工具安全地放进了上锁的柜子里。
entries.example_en: The carpenter ensconced the valuable tool in a locked cabinet.

entries.definition_en: a group of musicians who play or sing together
entries.example_cn: 爵士乐团演奏了一首活泼的歌曲。
entries.example_en: The jazz ensemble performed a lively song.

entries.definition_cn: 整体组合；协调的各部分
entries.definition_en: a coordinated group of parts or details forming a whole
entries.example_cn: 这座建筑的设计是不同风格的整体组合。
entries.example_en: The design of the building is an ensemble of different styles.

entries.definition_en: a set of matching clothes worn together
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一套时尚的套装去参加派对。
entries.example_en: She wore a stylish ensemble to the party.

entries.definition_en: the group of actors in a play or movie who are not the main stars
entries.example_cn: 这部新剧的配角群非常有才华。
entries.example_en: The ensemble in the new play is very talented.

entries.definition_en: the group of dancers in a ballet company
entries.example_cn: 全体舞者为开演夜排练。
entries.example_en: The ensemble rehearsed for the opening night.

entries.definition_cn: 将（思想、理想或权利）载入法律或条约予以保护
entries.definition_en: to preserve or protect an idea, ideal, or right in an official law or treaty
entries.example_cn: 宪法奉言论自由为神圣权利。
entries.example_en: The constitution enshrines the right to free speech.

entries.definition_en: to enclose something in a shrine
entries.example_cn: 这座古庙是为了供奉神圣的遗物而建的。
entries.example_en: The ancient temple was built to enshrine the sacred relics.

entries.definition_cn: 用裹尸布覆盖；笼罩；遮蔽
entries.definition_en: to cover something completely, as if with a funeral shroud
entries.example_cn: 薄雾开始笼罩那座古老的城堡。
entries.example_en: Mist began to enshroud the ancient castle.

entries.definition_cn: 悬挂在船上以示国籍的旗帜
entries.definition_en: a flag flown on a ship to show its nationality
entries.example_cn: 当船只驶入港口时，升起了它的国旗。
entries.example_en: The ship raised its national ensign as it entered the harbor.

entries.definition_cn: 船只悬挂以示国籍的旗帜
entries.definition_en: the colors flown by a ship to show its nationality
entries.example_cn: 船长下令在仪式期间降下旗帜。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the ensign to be lowered during the ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 海军或海岸警卫队中低于少尉的军官
entries.definition_en: a commissioned officer in the United States Navy or Coast Guard who is below the rank of lieutenant junior grade
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻军官在完成训练后被晋升为少尉。
entries.example_en: The young officer was promoted to ensign after completing his training.

entries.definition_en: to make someone a slave or to force them to work for someone else
entries.example_cn: 那个古帝国企图奴役邻近的部落。
entries.example_en: The ancient empire sought to enslave the neighboring tribes.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being a slave
entries.example_cn: 该地区的历史以数个世纪的奴役状态为标志。
entries.example_en: The history of the region is marked by centuries of enslavement.

entries.definition_en: the act of making people into slaves
entries.example_cn: 数百万非洲人被奴役是人类历史上悲惨的一章。
entries.example_en: The enslavement of millions of Africans was a tragic chapter in human history.

entries.definition_en: to catch someone or something as if in a trap
entries.example_cn: 猎人试图用网诱捕那只鹿。
entries.example_en: The hunter tried to ensnare the deer with a net.

entries.definition_en: to entangle or involve someone in a difficult or compromising situation
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家陷入了谎言的罗网。
entries.example_en: The politician was ensnared by a web of lies.

entries.definition_en: to happen or occur as a result of something
entries.example_cn: 一场暴风雨爆发，随后下起了大雨。
entries.example_en: A storm broke out, and heavy rain ensued.

usage.label: intransitive; ensue after/from
usage.pattern: ensue after something or as a result

entries.definition_cn: 发生在前述情况之后、并常由其引起的
entries.definition_en: following and often resulting from what went before
entries.example_cn: 随后的辩论非常激烈。
entries.example_en: The ensuing debate was heated.

entries.definition_en: to make certain that something happens or is true
entries.example_cn: 请在离开前确保所有门都已锁好。
entries.example_en: Please ensure that all doors are locked before leaving.

entries.definition_en: to be careful or certain to do something; to make certain of something
entries.example_cn: 你必须确保准时参加会议。
entries.example_en: You must ensure that you arrive on time for the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the structure above the columns of a classical temple, between the capital and the roof
entries.example_cn: 建筑师设计了檐部以支撑神庙沉重的屋顶。
entries.example_en: The architect designed the entablature to support the heavy roof of the temple.

entries.definition_en: to have something as a necessary result or consequence
entries.example_cn: 新的安全规定将给公司带来巨大的成本。
entries.example_en: The new safety regulations will entail significant costs for the company.

entries.definition_en: to require something as a necessary part or result of an action
entries.example_cn: 搬到一个新城市将意味着要学习一门新语言并找一份新工作。
entries.example_en: Moving to a new city will entail learning a new language and finding a new job.

entries.definition_cn: 将财产继承权限制在特定类别的继承人身上
entries.definition_en: to restrict the inheritance of property to a specific class of heirs
entries.example_cn: 旧法允许土地所有者将财产限定继承给他们的直系后代。
entries.example_en: The old law allowed landowners to entail their property to only their direct descendants.

entries.definition_cn: 创设限定继承地产的行为
entries.definition_en: the legal process of creating a fee tail from a fee simple
entries.example_cn: 这种限定继承地产的创设是一种复杂的法律手段，旨在让土地留在家族内部。
entries.example_en: The entail was a complex legal maneuver designed to keep the land in the family.

entries.definition_cn: 限定继承地产；限定继承的不动产
entries.definition_en: an estate held in fee tail and subject to restricted inheritance
entries.example_cn: 该庄园是限定继承地产，现任所有者无权出售。
entries.example_en: The estate was an entail that could not be sold by the current owner.

entries.definition_en: a conclusion that is necessarily implied by a statement
entries.example_cn: 该论证的推论是项目将会失败。
entries.example_en: The entailment of the argument was that the project would fail.

entries.definition_en: to twist or wind together into a confused mass
entries.example_cn: 藤蔓已经缠绕在那棵老橡树上。
entries.example_en: The vines had become entangled around the old oak tree.

entries.definition_en: to trap someone or something so that they cannot escape
entries.example_cn: 猎人设法用网困住了那只鹿。
entries.example_en: The hunter managed to entangle the deer in a net.

entries.definition_en: deeply involved in something complicated
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家发现自己深陷于谎言的罗网中。
entries.example_en: The politician found himself entangled in a web of lies.

entries.definition_en: twisted together in a tangled mass
entries.example_cn: 老树的根纠缠在一起。
entries.example_en: The roots of the old trees were entangled with each other.

entries.definition_en: involved in difficulties
entries.example_cn: 这家公司陷入了法律纠纷。
entries.example_en: The company is entangled in legal troubles.

entries.definition_en: the act or condition of being entangled, especially in a complicated situation
entries.example_cn: 谈判陷入了法律和政治争端交织的复杂困境。
entries.example_en: The negotiations became an entanglement of legal and political disputes.

entries.definition_en: a slight convexity in the shaft of a column; compensates for the illusion of concavity that viewers experience when the sides are perfectly straight
entries.example_cn: 建筑师在柱身应用了柱身微凸技术，使其在人类眼中看起来更直。
entries.example_en: The architect applied entasis to the column shafts to make them appear straighter to the human eye.

entries.definition_cn: （亚里士多德哲学）事物充分实现其潜能的状态；完满实现
entries.definition_en: (in Aristotelian philosophy) the state in which a thing fully realizes its potential
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家认为，人生的目的在于实现自身的潜能。
entries.example_en: The philosopher argued that the purpose of life is to achieve one's entelechy.

entries.definition_en: an informal alliance between countries
entries.example_cn: 两国签署了一项秘密同盟以保护共同的边界。
entries.example_en: The two nations signed a secret entente to protect their shared borders.

entries.definition_en: a friendly understanding between political powers
entries.example_cn: 领导人之间的友好谅解有助于缓解该地区的紧张局势。
entries.example_en: The entente between the leaders helped to ease tensions in the region.

entries.definition_en: to go inside a place or building
entries.example_cn: 请安静地进入房间。
entries.example_en: Please enter the room quietly.

entries.definition_en: to put something into a container or system
entries.example_cn: 输入代码以解锁门。
entries.example_en: Enter the code to unlock the door.

entries.definition_en: to write down information in a record
entries.example_cn: 职员将数据录入计算机系统。
entries.example_en: The clerk entered the data into the computer system.

entries.definition_en: to take part in an activity or competition
entries.example_cn: 许多学生决定参加科学展览。
entries.example_en: Many students decided to enter the science fair.

entries.definition_en: to officially sign up for a course or program
entries.example_cn: 您必须在网站上登记详细信息才能注册。
entries.example_en: You must enter your details on the website to register.

entries.definition_en: to appear on a stage for a performance
entries.example_cn: 这位演员自信满满地登台了。
entries.example_en: The actor entered with great confidence.

entries.definition_en: to play a role in a situation or story
entries.example_cn: 新角色将在第三幕中登场。
entries.example_en: The new character will enter the plot in the third act.

entries.definition_en: to start working in a job or holding an office
entries.example_cn: 她将于下个月就职。
entries.example_en: She will enter office next month.

entries.definition_en: relating to or occurring inside the intestines
entries.example_cn: 肠内营养直接输送到胃或肠道中。
entries.example_en: Enteral nutrition is delivered directly into the stomach or intestine.

entries.definition_en: relating to the enteron, the primitive gut of an embryo
entries.example_cn: 肠胚腔是胚胎中形成的第一个消化结构。
entries.example_en: The enteral cavity is the first digestive structure to form in the embryo.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or inside the intestines
entries.example_cn: 肠道细菌在人类消化过程中起着至关重要的作用。
entries.example_en: Enteric bacteria play a crucial role in human digestion.

entries.definition_en: remaining intact in the stomach and dissolving in the intestine
entries.example_cn: 肠溶片在肠道而不是胃中溶解。
entries.example_en: The enteric-coated tablet dissolves in the intestine rather than the stomach.

entries.definition_en: the act of entering
entries.example_cn: 录入数据花了几个小时。
entries.example_en: The entering of the data took several hours.

entries.definition_en: a movement into or inward
entries.example_cn: 有人进入房间时发出了一声巨响。
entries.example_en: The entering of the room was marked by a loud noise.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the intestine, especially the small intestine, often causing diarrhea
entries.example_cn: 这只狗在吃了变质的食物后被诊断出患有严重的肠炎。
entries.example_en: The dog was diagnosed with severe enteritis after eating spoiled food.

entries.definition_cn: 肠杆菌科中多种革兰氏阴性杆状细菌中的一种，其中许多具有致病性
entries.definition_en: any of many gram-negative rod-shaped bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae, many of which are pathogenic
entries.example_cn: 实验室在水样中鉴定出一种危险的肠杆菌科细菌。
entries.example_en: The laboratory identified a dangerous enterobacterium in the water sample.

entries.definition_en: a disease affecting the intestines
entries.example_cn: 这位患者被诊断出一种罕见的肠病，导致严重的吸收不良。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with a rare enteropathy that caused severe malabsorption.

entries.definition_en: a toxin that specifically damages cells in the intestinal lining
entries.example_cn: 这种细菌释放了一种肠毒素，导致严重腹泻。
entries.example_en: The bacteria released an enterotoxin that caused severe diarrhea.

entries.definition_en: a type of virus that infects the digestive system and can spread to the nervous system
entries.example_cn: 该地区的肠道病毒爆发导致了几例脑膜炎病例。
entries.example_en: The enterovirus outbreak caused several cases of meningitis in the region.

entries.definition_cn: 有目的或勤奋的事业（尤其是需要努力或勇气的事业）
entries.definition_en: a purposeful or industrious undertaking (especially one that requires effort or boldness)
entries.example_cn: 创办一家新企业是一项充满挑战的事业。
entries.example_en: Starting a new business is a challenging enterprise.

entries.definition_cn: 为商业冒险而成立的组织
entries.definition_en: an organization created for business ventures
entries.example_cn: 该企业将业务扩展到了三个国家。
entries.example_en: The enterprise expanded its operations to three countries.

entries.definition_cn: 投身大胆新事业的意愿
entries.definition_en: readiness to embark on bold new ventures
entries.example_cn: 她创办自己的初创公司展现了极大的进取心。
entries.example_en: She showed great enterprise in launching her own startup.

entries.definition_en: a person who starts a business and takes the risk of losing money
entries.example_cn: 这位企业家投入了全部积蓄来创办这家新技术公司。
entries.example_en: The enterpriser invested all his savings to launch the new technology company.

entries.definition_en: showing imagination and initiative in undertaking new projects
entries.example_cn: 她是一位有进取心的年轻企业家。
entries.example_en: She is an enterprising young entrepreneur.

entries.definition_en: to provide amusement or enjoyment for someone
entries.example_cn: 魔术师用魔术逗乐了孩子们。
entries.example_en: The magician entertained the children with tricks.

entries.definition_en: to consider or keep in mind
entries.example_cn: 我们必须考虑到下雨的可能性。
entries.example_en: We must entertain the possibility of rain.

entries.definition_en: to hold or maintain a belief or thought
entries.example_cn: 他仍然抱有回家的希望。
entries.example_en: He still entertains the hope of returning home.

entries.definition_cn: 感到愉快的；觉得有趣的
entries.definition_en: feeling happy and interested because you are doing or watching something enjoyable
entries.example_cn: 孩子们看魔术表演看得很开心。
entries.example_en: The children were entertained by the magic show.

entries.definition_cn: 为他人提供娱乐的人，尤指以此为业者
entries.definition_en: someone who entertains others, especially as a profession
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的艺人为孩子们表演了魔术。
entries.example_en: The famous entertainer performed magic tricks for the children.

entries.definition_en: providing enjoyment and amusement
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员讲了一个有趣的故事，逗得大家哈哈大笑。
entries.example_en: The comedian told an entertaining story that made everyone laugh.

entries.definition_en: in an entertaining manner
entries.example_cn: 魔术师表演得很有趣，令观众惊叹不已。
entries.example_en: The magician performed entertainingly, keeping the audience in awe.

entries.definition_en: an activity that is diverting and that holds the attention
entries.example_cn: 在一个下雨的周日，我们去电影院娱乐一下。
entries.example_en: We went to the cinema for some entertainment on a rainy Sunday.

entries.definition_en: a thermodynamic quantity equal to the internal energy of a system plus the product of its volume and pressure
entries.example_cn: 焓的变化表明化学反应是放热还是吸热。
entries.example_en: The change in enthalpy indicates whether a chemical reaction releases or absorbs heat.

entries.definition_en: to hold someone spellbound or fascinated
entries.example_cn: 魔术师的表演完全迷住了观众。
entries.example_en: The magician's performance completely enthralled the audience.

entries.definition_en: to hold someone completely spellbound or fascinated
entries.example_cn: 魔术师的表演完全迷住了观众中的孩子们。
entries.example_en: The magician's performance completely enthralled the children in the audience.

entries.definition_en: fascinated or captivated
entries.example_cn: 观众们对魔术师令人难以置信的幻术着迷不已。
entries.example_en: The audience was enthralled by the magician's incredible illusions.

entries.definition_cn: 令人着迷的；引人入胜的
entries.definition_en: extremely fascinating and exciting
entries.example_cn: 魔术师表演了一场令人屏息的精彩演出。
entries.example_en: The magician performed an enthralling show that left the audience breathless.

entries.definition_cn: 使人着迷的行为；着迷或入迷的状态
entries.definition_en: the act of captivating or the state of being captivated or fascinated
entries.example_cn: 当魔术师表演他看似不可能的戏法时，人群的着迷之情显而易见。
entries.example_en: The enthrallment of the crowd was evident as the magician performed his impossible tricks.

entries.definition_en: to put a monarch on the throne
entries.example_cn: 举行了为新国王登基的典礼。
entries.example_en: The ceremony was held to enthrone the new king.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人成为领导者或主导人物
entries.definition_en: to establish someone as a leader or dominant figure
entries.example_cn: 这场胜利使将军成为国家的领导者。
entries.example_en: The victory enthroned the general as the leader of the nation.

entries.definition_en: the formal act or ceremony of installing someone on a throne
entries.example_cn: 全国民众聚集在电视机前观看国王的登基仪式。
entries.example_en: The nation gathered to watch the king's enthronement on television.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to feel enthusiastic
entries.example_cn: 演讲者试图让观众对新项目充满热情。
entries.example_en: The speaker tried to enthuse the audience about the new project.

entries.definition_en: to speak enthusiastically about something
entries.example_cn: 她热情洋溢地讲述了自己环游世界的计划。
entries.example_en: She enthused about her plans to travel around the world.

entries.definition_en: a strong feeling of excitement
entries.example_cn: 她对新项目表现出极大的热情。
entries.example_en: She showed great enthusiasm for the new project.

entries.definition_en: a lively interest
entries.example_cn: 他对学习语言有着浓厚的兴趣。
entries.example_en: He has a real enthusiasm for learning languages.

entries.definition_en: showing eager enjoyment or approval
entries.example_cn: 人群兴高采烈地欢迎获胜者。
entries.example_en: The crowd greeted the winner with great enthusiasm.

entries.definition_cn: 充满热情的人，尤指热心支持某人、事业或活动的人
entries.definition_en: a person filled with enthusiasm, especially an ardent supporter of a person, cause, or activity
entries.example_cn: 这项运动最热心的支持者组织了会议并招募了志愿者。
entries.example_en: The campaign's most ardent enthusiast organized meetings and recruited volunteers.

entries.definition_en: a person who has a strong liking for something
entries.example_cn: 他是一位复古车迷。
entries.example_en: He is a keen enthusiast of vintage cars.

entries.definition_en: showing great excitement and interest
entries.example_cn: 她对那个新项目充满热情。
entries.example_en: She was enthusiastic about the new project.

entries.definition_en: with great excitement and interest
entries.example_cn: 当他们的球队得分时，球迷们热情地欢呼起来。
entries.example_en: The fans cheered enthusiastically when their team scored.

entries.definition_en: in a lavish or enthusiastic manner
entries.example_cn: 他们为派对热情且慷慨地装饰了大厅。
entries.example_en: They decorated the hall enthusiastically for the party.

entries.definition_en: to attract or persuade someone to do something, often using false promises
entries.example_cn: 销售员试图用免费礼物引诱顾客。
entries.example_en: The salesman tried to entice the customer with a free gift.

entries.definition_en: something that attracts or seduces someone
entries.example_cn: 明亮的灯光和免费样品是商场吸引顾客的主要因素。
entries.example_en: The bright lights and free samples were the main enticement for shoppers at the mall.

entries.definition_en: qualities that attract people by promising a reward or benefit
entries.example_cn: 高薪的承诺是这份新工作提议的主要吸引力。
entries.example_en: The promise of a high salary was the primary enticement for the new job offer.

entries.definition_cn: 通过激发希望或欲望来影响他人的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of influencing someone by exciting their hope or desire
entries.example_cn: 政治家的演讲是一种旨在争取对新政策支持的引诱行为。
entries.example_en: The politician's speech was an enticement designed to rally support for the new policy.

entries.definition_en: very attractive and likely to make someone want something
entries.example_cn: 新鲜面包的香气令人垂涎。
entries.example_en: The scent of the fresh bread was enticing.

entries.definition_en: complete; consisting of the whole
entries.example_cn: 她一天读完了整本书。
entries.example_en: She read the entire book in one day.

entries.definition_en: whole and undamaged; lacking nothing essential
entries.example_cn: 花瓶摔下来后依然完好无损。
entries.example_en: The vase was entire after the fall.

entries.definition_en: having a smooth edge without teeth or lobes
entries.example_cn: 这片叶子具有全缘边缘。
entries.example_en: The leaf had an entire margin.

entries.definition_en: sexually competent (of domestic animals)
entries.example_cn: 那只未阉割的公狗被保留用于繁殖。
entries.example_en: The entire male dog was kept for breeding.

entries.definition_en: an adult male horse that has not been castrated
entries.example_cn: 那匹公马被关在单独的围栏里。
entries.example_en: The entire was kept in a separate pen.

entries.definition_en: completely or to the full extent
entries.example_cn: 我对项目的结果完全满意。
entries.example_en: I am entirely satisfied with the results of the project.

entries.definition_en: without any other parts or people involved
entries.example_cn: 整个团队独自完成了这项任务。
entries.example_en: The entire team worked on the task entirely by themselves.

entries.definition_en: the state of being total and complete
entries.example_cn: 她不间断地听完了整个演讲。
entries.example_en: She listened to the entirety of the speech without interruption.

entries.definition_en: to give someone the right to receive something or do something
entries.example_cn: 法律赋予员工一周带薪假的权利。
entries.example_en: The law entitles employees to a week of paid leave.

usage.label: entitle someone to something
usage.pattern: 表示赋予某人获得某物的权利

entries.definition_en: to give a title to something
entries.example_cn: 作者给他的新书取名为《沉默之海》。
entries.example_en: The author entitled his new book 'The Silent Sea'.

entries.definition_cn: 授予某人荣誉头衔或等级
entries.definition_en: to give someone an honorary title or rank
entries.example_cn: 国王授予他的儿子约克公爵的头衔。
entries.example_en: The king entitled his son Duke of York.

entries.definition_en: having a legal or moral right to something
entries.example_cn: 每个公民都有权接受免费教育。
entries.example_en: Every citizen is entitled to free education.

entries.definition_cn: 权利；（尤指）领取福利的权利
entries.definition_en: a legal or contractual right, especially to receive benefits
entries.example_cn: 新政策扩大了工人享受带薪假期的权利。
entries.example_en: The new policy expanded the workers' entitlement to paid leave.

entries.definition_en: a person, place, thing, or idea that exists as a separate and distinct unit
entries.example_cn: 该公司是一个拥有自身权利和责任的法人实体。
entries.example_en: The company is a legal entity with its own rights and responsibilities.

entries.definition_en: to place someone or something in a grave or tomb
entries.example_cn: 这位古代国王被埋葬在一个金棺中。
entries.example_en: The ancient king was entombed in a golden sarcophagus.

entries.definition_cn: 把某人或某物困在受限制的环境中
entries.definition_en: to confine someone or something in restrictive surroundings
entries.example_cn: 这名囚犯实际上被困在狭小的牢房里。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was effectively entombed in the tiny cell.

entries.definition_en: the ritual placing of a corpse in a grave
entries.example_cn: 古老的仪式标志着国王的埋葬。
entries.example_en: The ancient ceremony marked the entombment of the king.

entries.definition_en: relating to the scientific study of insects
entries.example_cn: 该昆虫学期刊发表了关于甲虫迁徙的新发现。
entries.example_en: The entomological journal published new findings on beetle migration.

entries.definition_en: a scientist who studies insects
entries.example_cn: 这位昆虫学家花了几个小时在显微镜下检查标本。
entries.example_en: The entomologist spent hours examining the specimen under a microscope.

entries.definition_en: the branch of zoology that studies insects
entries.example_cn: 她决定主修昆虫学，以了解昆虫的行为。
entries.example_en: She decided to major in entomology to understand insect behavior.

entries.definition_en: the group following and attending to some important person
entries.example_cn: 这位名人带着庞大的随从抵达。
entries.example_en: The celebrity arrived with a large entourage.

entries.definition_en: a break or interlude between two acts of a play
entries.example_cn: 在最后一幕之前的幕间休息时，观众热烈欢呼。
entries.example_en: The audience cheered loudly during the entr'acte before the final act.

entries.definition_en: a short performance inserted between sections of a longer show
entries.example_cn: 一段生动的舞蹈插播节目在准备主菜时娱乐了客人们。
entries.example_en: A lively dance entr'acte entertained the guests while the main meal was prepared.

entries.definition_en: to get on a train
entries.example_cn: 他匆忙赶到站台，以便在发车前上车。
entries.example_en: He hurried to the platform to entrain before the departure.

entries.definition_cn: 使大脑活动形成特定模式
entries.definition_en: to condition brain activity to follow a particular pattern
entries.example_cn: 研究人员利用视觉刺激使患者的大脑活动形成规律的模式。
entries.example_en: The researchers used visual stimulation to entrain the patient's brain activity to a regular pattern.

entries.definition_en: something that provides access (to get in or get out)
entries.example_cn: 建筑物的侧门入口被锁上了。
entries.example_en: The side entrance to the building was locked.

entries.definition_en: the act of entering
entries.example_cn: 他进入房间的方式非常戏剧化。
entries.example_en: His entrance into the room was very dramatic.

entries.definition_en: the beginning or commencement of something
entries.example_cn: 她开始从事这一职业，标志着一个新的开端。
entries.example_en: Her entrance into the profession marked a new beginning.

entries.definition_en: attract; cause to be enamored
entries.example_cn: 美丽的景色完全迷住了游客们。
entries.example_en: The beautiful scenery completely entranced the visitors.

entries.definition_en: put into a trance
entries.example_cn: 催眠师用声音使观众进入了催眠状态。
entries.example_en: The hypnotist entranced the audience, putting them into a trance with his voice.

entries.definition_en: filled with wonder and delight
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被魔术师的表演迷住了。
entries.example_en: The children were entranced by the magician's performance.

entries.definition_cn: 被催眠的；处于恍惚状态的
entries.definition_en: held in a hypnotic or trance-like state
entries.example_cn: 那个处于催眠状态的病人凝视前方，回答着催眠师的问题。
entries.example_en: The entranced patient stared ahead and answered the hypnotist's questions.

entries.definition_en: a passage or area that provides access to a building or room
entries.example_cn: 宏伟的入口通道直接通向主厅。
entries.example_en: The grand entranceway leads directly to the main hall.

entries.definition_en: captivating or enchanting as if by magic
entries.example_cn: 那位舞者的表演令人着迷。
entries.example_en: The dancer's performance was entrancing.

entries.definition_en: a person who takes part in a competition
entries.example_cn: 国际象棋锦标赛有超过一百名参赛者。
entries.example_en: There were over a hundred entrants in the chess tournament.

entries.definition_en: someone who enters a place
entries.example_cn: 保安在门口拦下了每一位进入者。
entries.example_en: The security guard stopped every entrant at the gate.

entries.definition_en: a new participant in an activity
entries.example_cn: 俱乐部欢迎了几名新队员加入。
entries.example_en: The club welcomed several new entrants to the team.

usage.label: newcomer
usage.pattern: a new entrant to an activity or field

entries.definition_en: a new product that competes with existing ones
entries.example_cn: 这款新手机是市场上的强劲竞争者。
entries.example_en: The new smartphone is a strong entrant in the market.

entries.definition_cn: 诱骗；诱使（某人陷入危险处境或实施违法行为）
entries.definition_en: to lure someone into a dangerous situation or into committing an illegal act
entries.example_cn: 卧底警察诱使嫌疑人试图购买毒品。
entries.example_en: The undercover officer entrapped the suspect into trying to buy drugs.

entries.definition_en: to catch in a trap
entries.example_cn: 猎人设法用网困住了那只鹿。
entries.example_en: The hunter managed to entrap the deer in the net.

entries.definition_en: a legal defense claiming the defendant committed the crime only because they were tricked by police or officials
entries.example_cn: 律师辩称，供词是侦探诱捕的结果。
entries.example_en: The lawyer argued that the confession was the result of entrapment by the detectives.

entries.definition_cn: 从混合物中分离特定细胞或分子的过程，尤其是通过将其固定在凝胶上进行分离
entries.definition_en: the isolation of specific cells or molecules from a mixture, especially by immobilizing them on a gel
entries.example_cn: 研究人员利用包埋法将目标分子固定在凝胶上并分离出来。
entries.example_en: The researchers used entrapment to isolate the target molecules on a gel.

entries.definition_en: ask for or request earnestly
entries.example_cn: 她恳求他在为时已晚之前重新考虑他的决定。
entries.example_en: She entreated him to reconsider his decision before it was too late.

entries.definition_en: an earnest or urgent request.
entries.example_cn: 他恳求原谅，却只得到沉默。
entries.example_en: His entreaty for forgiveness was met with silence.

entries.definition_en: the main dish served in the middle of a meal
entries.example_cn: 我们要了当天的主菜。
entries.example_en: We ordered the entree of the day.

entries.definition_en: the right to enter a place or group
entries.example_cn: 会员资格赋予参加独家活动的权利。
entries.example_en: Membership grants an entree to exclusive events.

entries.definition_en: something that provides access to a place
entries.example_cn: 这把钥匙是进入大楼的通道。
entries.example_en: The key is the entree to the building.

entries.definition_en: a dramatic entrance onto a stage
entries.example_cn: 这位演员隆重登场。
entries.example_en: The actor made a grand entree to the stage.

entries.definition_en: a dessert served after a meal
entries.example_cn: 这道精美的餐后甜点由四种不同的冰品组合而成。
entries.example_en: The elaborate entremets combined four different ices.

entries.definition_en: a side dish served alongside the main course of a meal
entries.example_cn: 厨师准备了一道精致的副菜来搭配烤鸭。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a delicate entremets to accompany the roasted duck.

entries.definition_en: to make something firmly established or fixed in place
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策旨在巩固该地区的民主价值观。
entries.example_en: The new policy aims to entrench democratic values in the region.

entries.definition_en: to dig in or occupy a trench or fortified position
entries.example_cn: 士兵们在进攻前躲在沙袋后面构筑工事。
entries.example_en: The soldiers entrench themselves behind the sandbags before the attack.

entries.definition_en: to encroach on or infringe upon
entries.example_cn: 不断扩张的城市开始侵占周围的农田。
entries.example_en: The expanding city has begun to entrench on the surrounding farmland.

entries.definition_cn: 由战壕构成的防御工事
entries.definition_en: a fortification constructed of trenches
entries.example_cn: 士兵们建立了一座由战壕构成的防御工事，以保护村庄免受敌军攻击。
entries.example_en: The soldiers established an entrenchment to protect the village from enemy attacks.

entries.definition_en: a port where merchandise can be imported and then exported without paying import duties
entries.example_cn: 新加坡长期以来一直是该地区贸易的主要转口港。
entries.example_en: Singapore has long served as a major entrepot for trade in the region.

entries.definition_en: a depository for goods
entries.example_cn: 该仓库作为当地农产品的货栈。
entries.example_en: The warehouse functioned as an entrepot for the local agricultural products.

entries.definition_en: a person who starts and manages a business, taking on the financial risks involved
entries.example_cn: 这位企业家用少量资金创办了自己的新科技公司。
entries.example_en: The entrepreneur launched her new tech company with a small investment.

entries.definition_cn: 具有企业家精神的；有进取心的
entries.definition_en: having the spirit, attitude, or qualities of an entrepreneur; enterprising
entries.example_cn: 她非常有创业精神，并创办了自己的公司。
entries.example_en: She is very entrepreneurial and started her own business.

entries.definition_en: relating to an entrepreneur
entries.example_cn: 这家公司具有企业家的精神。
entries.example_en: The company has an entrepreneurial spirit.

entries.definition_cn: （热力学中表示无序程度或不可用能量的）熵
entries.definition_en: a thermodynamic measure of disorder or of energy unavailable for doing work
entries.example_cn: 随着发动机运转，一些能量变得无法用于做功，使系统的熵增加。
entries.example_en: As the engine runs, some energy becomes unavailable for doing work, increasing the system's entropy.

entries.definition_cn: （通信理论中的）不确定性度量
entries.definition_en: a measure of uncertainty in communication theory
entries.example_cn: 这条消息的熵值表明了其不可预测的程度。
entries.example_en: The entropy of the message indicates how unpredictable it is.

entries.definition_en: to give something to someone to look after or protect
entries.example_cn: 她把重要文件托付给律师保管。
entries.example_en: She entrusted her valuable documents to a lawyer for safekeeping.

entries.definition_en: to give someone responsibility for something
entries.example_cn: 我离开时会把孩子们托付给你照顾。
entries.example_en: I will entrust my children to your care while I am away.

entries.definition_en: a record written in a book or list
entries.example_cn: 请为每次访问在日志簿中做一条记录。
entries.example_en: Please make an entry in the logbook for every visit.

entries.definition_en: something that allows access to a place
entries.example_cn: 大楼的主要入口在北面。
entries.example_en: The main entry to the building is on the north side.

entries.definition_en: the act of going inside a place
entries.example_cn: 警察的闯入让罪犯们大吃一惊。
entries.example_en: The entry of the police surprised the criminals.

entries.definition_en: the act of starting something new
entries.example_cn: 这本书描述了女性进入职场的开端。
entries.example_en: The book describes the entry of women into the workforce.

entries.definition_en: a written record of a business transaction
entries.example_cn: 会计检查了这笔销售交易的记录。
entries.example_en: The accountant checked the entry for the sale.

entries.definition_en: a work submitted for a competition or judgment
entries.example_cn: 她的画作是艺术比赛中的获奖作品。
entries.example_en: Her painting was the winning entry in the art contest.

entries.definition_en: something that provides access (to get in or get out)
entries.example_cn: 新的入口直接通向厨房。
entries.example_en: The new entryway leads directly to the kitchen.

entries.definition_en: to tie or link things together
entries.example_cn: 藤蔓缠绕在古老的橡树上。
entries.example_en: The vines entwine around the old oak tree.

entries.definition_en: to spin, wind, or twist things together
entries.example_cn: 舞者们优雅地缠绕着手臂，围成一圈。
entries.example_en: The dancers entwine their arms in a graceful circle.

entries.definition_cn: （器官、肿瘤或囊肿的）完整摘除术
entries.definition_en: the surgical removal of an organ, tumor, or cyst intact, especially from its surrounding tissue
entries.example_cn: 外科医生进行了眼球摘除术。
entries.example_en: The surgeon performed an enucleation to remove the eye.

entries.definition_en: capable of being counted or listed one by one
entries.example_cn: 自然数集是可数的，但实数集不是。
entries.example_en: The set of natural numbers is enumerable, but the set of real numbers is not.

entries.definition_en: specify individually
entries.example_cn: 请列举你做决定的理由。
entries.example_en: Please enumerate the reasons for your decision.

entries.definition_en: determine the number or amount of
entries.example_cn: 很难统计雨林中的物种总数。
entries.example_en: It is difficult to enumerate the total number of species in the rainforest.

entries.definition_en: a numbered list
entries.example_cn: 报告包含了一份详细的错误编号列表。
entries.example_en: The report included a detailed enumeration of the errors.

entries.definition_en: the act of counting; reciting numbers in ascending order
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喜欢从一到十报数的游戏。
entries.example_en: The children enjoyed the enumeration of numbers from one to ten.

entries.definition_en: a person who visits homes to collect census data
entries.example_cn: 普查员敲遍了社区里的每一扇门以记录人口数据。
entries.example_en: The enumerator knocked on every door in the neighborhood to record the population.

entries.definition_en: to express or state something clearly
entries.example_cn: 她无法就那个有争议的问题明确表达自己的观点。
entries.example_en: She could not enunciate her opinion on the controversial issue.

entries.definition_en: to speak or pronounce words clearly
entries.example_cn: 老师要求学生更清晰地发音。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the students to enunciate their words more clearly.

entries.definition_en: the clear and precise way in which words are pronounced so that they are easy to understand
entries.example_cn: 这位演员吐字清晰，使剧中的每一句台词都易于理解。
entries.example_en: The actor's excellent enunciation made every line of the play easy to follow.

entries.definition_en: a medical condition where a person involuntarily urinates, especially during sleep
entries.example_cn: 这个孩子因反复尿床被诊断为夜间遗尿症。
entries.example_en: The child was diagnosed with nocturnal enuresis after wetting the bed repeatedly.

entries.definition_en: to cover or surround something completely, as if with a wrapping
entries.example_cn: 雾气开始笼罩这座城市。
entries.example_en: The fog began to envelop the city.

entries.definition_en: a flat container for a letter or thin package
entries.example_cn: 请把信放进信封里。
entries.example_en: Please put the letter in the envelope.

entries.definition_en: a covering or wrapper
entries.example_cn: 这本书装在一个薄薄的塑料封套里。
entries.example_en: The book came in a thin plastic envelope.

entries.definition_en: a natural covering formed by a fluid
entries.example_cn: 湖面上形成了一层冰盖。
entries.example_en: An envelope of ice formed on the lake.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指飞机的）性能包线；安全运行范围
entries.definition_en: the range of conditions in which a system can operate safely and effectively
entries.example_cn: 这架飞机始终处于其运行包线内。
entries.example_en: The aircraft remained within its operating envelope.

entries.definition_en: the bag containing gas in a balloon
entries.example_cn: 这个气球的囊是用橡胶做的。
entries.example_en: The envelope of the balloon was made of rubber.

entries.definition_en: a curve tangent to a family of curves
entries.example_cn: 这位数学家研究了这些曲线的包络线。
entries.example_en: The mathematician studied the envelope of the curves.

entries.definition_en: the action of covering or enclosing something completely
entries.example_cn: 用保护布包裹幼苗使它们保持温暖。
entries.example_en: The envelopment of the seedlings in protective fabric kept them warm.

entries.definition_en: an attack in which an attacking force moves around or over the enemy to strike from behind
entries.example_cn: 指挥官计划实施包围攻击，从后方袭击敌军。
entries.example_en: The commander planned an envelopment to attack the enemy from the rear.

entries.definition_en: to add poison to something
entries.example_cn: 这条蛇用一口咬住了猎物并注入了毒液。
entries.example_en: The snake envenomed its prey with a single bite.

entries.definition_en: to make something bitter or embittered, or cause resentment
entries.example_cn: 他刻薄的话语只会使两位朋友的关系变得怨恨重重。
entries.example_en: His cruel words served only to envenom the relationship between the two friends.

entries.definition_en: causing people to feel jealous because it is good or desirable
entries.example_cn: 她在公司里拥有令人羡慕的地位。
entries.example_en: She has an enviable position in the company.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is worthy of envy
entries.example_cn: 她令人羡慕地提前完成了项目。
entries.example_en: She managed to complete the project enviably ahead of schedule.

entries.definition_en: feeling a strong desire to have what someone else has
entries.example_cn: 她嫉妒朋友的新车。
entries.example_en: She felt envious of her friend's new car.

entries.definition_en: with a feeling of wanting what someone else has
entries.example_cn: 他嫉妒地看着那辆昂贵的汽车。
entries.example_en: He looked at the expensive car enviously.

entries.definition_en: all the surrounding conditions affecting an organism or system
entries.example_cn: 污染正在破坏环境。
entries.example_en: Pollution is damaging the environment.

entries.definition_en: the natural surroundings and conditions in which an organism lives
entries.example_cn: 这种鱼无法在这种环境中生存。
entries.example_en: The fish cannot survive in this environment.

entries.definition_cn: 有关外部条件或周围环境的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to the external conditions or surroundings
entries.example_cn: 沙漠的环境条件十分恶劣。
entries.example_en: The environmental conditions in the desert are harsh.

entries.definition_cn: 涉及改变环境所产生的生态影响的
entries.definition_en: concerned with the ecological effects of altering the environment
entries.example_cn: 他们正在开展一个清理河流的环保项目。
entries.example_en: They are working on an environmental project to clean the river.

entries.definition_cn: 环境保护主义；寻求防止人类活动破坏环境的政治和社会思想
entries.definition_en: a political and social ideology seeking to protect the environment from human-caused degradation
entries.example_cn: 现代环保活动侧重于减少碳排放和保护自然栖息地。
entries.example_en: Modern environmentalism focuses on reducing carbon emissions and preserving natural habitats.

entries.definition_cn: 认为环境而非遗传或文化是个人或群体发展主要因素的学说
entries.definition_en: the doctrine that environment, rather than heredity or culture, is the main factor in the development of an individual or group
entries.example_cn: 这种意义上的环境决定论强调环境而非遗传对个人发展的作用。
entries.example_en: Environmentalism in this sense emphasizes environment over heredity in shaping an individual's development.

entries.definition_en: someone who works to protect the environment from destruction or pollution
entries.example_cn: 这位环保主义者倡导制定更严格的法律以减少污染。
entries.example_en: The environmentalist advocated for stricter laws to reduce pollution.

entries.definition_cn: 环境保护主义的；与环境保护主义原则有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to environmentalism or its principles
entries.example_cn: 这家公司采取了环境保护主义政策，以减少碳排放。
entries.example_en: The company adopted an environmentalist policy to reduce its carbon emissions.

entries.definition_cn: 从环境角度看；在环境方面
entries.definition_en: with regard to, or in a way affecting, the environment
entries.example_cn: 这一过程对环境有害。
entries.example_en: The process is environmentally harmful.

entries.definition_en: to form a mental image of something that is not present or that is not the case
entries.example_cn: 很难设想一个没有互联网的世界。
entries.example_en: It is hard to envisage a world without the internet.

entries.definition_en: to imagine or conceive of something in one's mind
entries.example_cn: 她构想了一个人人都有权获得清洁水的未来。
entries.example_en: She envisioned a future where everyone had access to clean water.

entries.definition_en: to picture something as possible or likely to happen
entries.example_cn: 很难想象一个没有互联网的世界。
entries.example_en: It is hard to envision a world without the internet.

entries.definition_en: something that is envisioned
entries.example_cn: 展览展示了她对可持续城市的构想。
entries.example_en: The exhibition presented her envisioning of a sustainable city.

entries.definition_cn: 诗末短诗（用于致意或评论前文）
entries.definition_en: a brief stanza concluding certain forms of poetry
entries.example_cn: 诗人在十四行诗组诗的末尾加了一节短小的终诗。
entries.example_en: The poet added a final envoi to the sonnet sequence.

entries.definition_en: a diplomat who is sent to a foreign country but has less power than an ambassador
entries.example_cn: 公使抵达首都谈判贸易协定。
entries.example_en: The envoy arrived in the capital to negotiate the trade agreement.

entries.definition_en: a person sent on a special mission to represent someone else
entries.example_cn: 国王派使者送去和平条约。
entries.example_en: The king sent an envoy to deliver the peace treaty.

entries.definition_cn: 巴拉德诗体的结尾诗节；尾声
entries.definition_en: a short concluding stanza in a ballade
entries.example_cn: 这首巴拉德诗体的尾声总结了诗歌的主要论点。
entries.example_en: The envoy of the ballade summarizes the poem's main argument.

entries.definition_cn: 对他人所拥有之物的嫉妒和渴望
entries.definition_en: resentful desire for something possessed by another person
entries.example_cn: 她嫉妒他的成功。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep envy of his success.

entries.definition_en: malice or resentment caused by someone else's success
entries.example_cn: 他的成功因同事的嫉妒而蒙上阴影。
entries.example_en: His success was marred by the envy of his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: to feel admiration and desire for what someone else has
entries.example_cn: 我羡慕你会说三种语言的能力。
entries.example_en: I envy your ability to speak three languages.

entries.definition_cn: 嫉妒地渴望拥有他人拥有的东西
entries.definition_en: to resentfully desire something that another person has
entries.example_cn: 她嫉妒邻居的新车，希望那是自己的。
entries.example_en: She envied her neighbor's new car and wished it were hers.

entries.definition_en: to enclose or enfold completely with or as if with a covering
entries.example_cn: 她小心地用气泡膜将易碎的花瓶包裹起来。
entries.example_en: She carefully enwrapped the fragile vase in bubble wrap.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人完全入迷；使全神贯注
entries.definition_en: to absorb someone completely; engross
entries.example_cn: 这部悬疑小说使她完全入迷。
entries.example_en: The mystery novel completely enwrapped her.

entries.definition_cn: 动物地方病的；动物地方性流行的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to a disease consistently prevalent among animals in a particular area
entries.example_cn: 该病毒的地方性特征意味着它始终存在于牛群中，尽管很少引起严重疾病。
entries.example_en: The enzootic nature of the virus meant it was always present in the cattle herd, though rarely causing severe illness.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or produced by an enzyme
entries.example_cn: 酶促反应加速了蛋白质的分解。
entries.example_en: The enzymatic reaction accelerated the breakdown of the protein.

entries.definition_cn: 能催化特定生化反应的生物分子，通常是蛋白质，有时是催化性RNA
entries.definition_en: a biomolecule, usually a protein but sometimes catalytic RNA, that speeds up a specific biochemical reaction
entries.example_cn: 消化酶帮助胃分解食物。
entries.example_en: Digestive enzymes help break down food in the stomach.

entries.definition_en: the scientific study of enzymes and their chemical reactions
entries.example_cn: 她在酶学方面的研究集中在酶如何分解蛋白质。
entries.example_en: Her research in enzymology focuses on how enzymes break down proteins.

entries.definition_cn: 始新世已灭绝的原始马类哺乳动物，现代马的祖先
entries.definition_en: an extinct primitive horse-like mammal from the Eocene, ancestral to modern horses
entries.example_cn: 始马的化石为现代马的进化提供了证据。
entries.example_en: Fossils of the eohippus provide evidence of the evolution of modern horses.

entries.definition_en: an immeasurably long period of time
entries.example_cn: 我们上次见面已经过了漫长的岁月。
entries.example_en: It has been an eon since we last met.

entries.definition_cn: 地质年代中最长的时间单位，细分为若干代
entries.definition_en: the longest division of geologic time, subdivided into eras
entries.example_cn: 这件化石被确定形成于显生宙，而显生宙又细分为若干代。
entries.example_en: The fossil was dated to the Phanerozoic Eon, which is subdivided into eras.

entries.definition_cn: （诺斯替教）从至高神发出的神圣力量或本性，在宇宙运行中扮演各种角色
entries.definition_en: (Gnosticism) a divine power or nature emanating from the Supreme Being and playing various roles in the operation of the universe
entries.example_cn: 在诺斯替宇宙论中，埃昂是从至高神发出的神圣力量。
entries.example_en: In Gnostic cosmology, the eon is a divine power emanating from the Supreme Being.

entries.definition_cn: （韩语）女性对姐姐或其他年长女性的称呼
entries.definition_en: a Korean term used by a female for an older sister or another older woman
entries.example_cn: 她称姐姐为“eonni”。
entries.example_en: She called her older sister eonni.

entries.definition_en: a red fluorescent dye used in cosmetics and as a biological stain
entries.example_cn: 科学家在载玻片上添加伊红以染色细胞结构。
entries.example_en: The scientist added eosin to the slide to stain the cell structures.

entries.definition_en: a type of white blood cell that is easily stained with the dye eosin
entries.example_cn: 嗜酸性粒细胞在机体对寄生虫的免疫反应中起着关键作用。
entries.example_en: The eosinophil plays a key role in the body's immune response to parasites.

entries.definition_en: a condition characterized by an increased number of eosinophils in the blood, often indicating an allergic reaction
entries.example_cn: 由于对花粉产生了严重的过敏反应，该患者被诊断为嗜酸性粒细胞增多症。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with eosinophilia due to a severe allergic reaction to pollen.

entries.definition_en: of, relating to, or readily stained by eosin; especially relating to an eosinophil
entries.example_cn: 嗜酸性细胞在显微镜下清晰可见。
entries.example_en: The eosinophilic cells were clearly visible under the microscope.

entries.definition_en: a diocese of the Eastern Orthodox Church
entries.example_cn: 主教被任命领导北部的教区。
entries.example_en: The bishop was appointed to lead the eparchy in the northern region.

entries.definition_en: an administrative district or province in the Greek-speaking Eastern Roman Empire or post-Ottoman Greece
entries.example_cn: 这位历史学家研究了拜占庭帝国一个行政区的行政结构。
entries.example_en: The historian studied the administrative structure of an eparchy in the Byzantine Empire.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental cloth pad worn on the shoulder as part of a uniform
entries.example_cn: 将军在仪式前调整了他的肩章。
entries.example_en: The general adjusted his epaulet before the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental cloth pad worn on the shoulder of a uniform
entries.example_cn: 将军在仪式前调整了他的肩章。
entries.example_en: The general adjusted his epaulette before the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: a fencing sword with a heavier blade than a foil
entries.example_cn: 这位击剑运动员使用重剑赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The fencer won the match using the epee.

entries.definition_en: the process of inserting a sound into a word to make it easier to pronounce
entries.example_cn: 有些人读“athlete”时会插入一个元音，这是增音的例子。
entries.example_en: Some speakers pronounce “athlete” with an inserted vowel, an example of epenthesis.

entries.definition_en: relating to the insertion of a sound or letter into a word
entries.example_cn: 插入元音有助于打破某些语言中困难的辅音丛。
entries.example_en: The epenthetic vowel helps to break up difficult consonant clusters in some languages.

entries.definition_cn: 伊法（古希伯来干量单位）
entries.definition_en: an ancient Hebrew unit of dry measure equal to about a bushel
entries.example_cn: 先知吩咐人们将十分之一的伊法谷物捐给圣殿。
entries.example_en: The prophet instructed the people to give a tenth of an ephah of grain to the temple.

entries.definition_en: a shrub of the genus Ephedra, typically with jointed stems and reduced scale-like leaves
entries.example_cn: 麻黄生长在干旱地区，并已被用于传统医学。
entries.example_en: The ephedra grows in arid regions and has been used in traditional medicine.

entries.definition_cn: 从麻黄植物中提取的兴奋剂，用于某些传统药物和减肥产品
entries.definition_en: a stimulant made from the Ephedra plant, used in some traditional medicines and weight-loss products
entries.example_cn: 这名运动员得知麻黄的健康风险后停止服用。
entries.example_en: The athlete stopped taking ephedra after learning about its health risks.

entries.definition_en: a white, odorless powder or crystal made from certain plants or synthetically; used as medicine to treat asthma and bronchitis
entries.example_cn: 医生开了麻黄碱来帮助患者在哮喘发作时呼吸更顺畅。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed ephedrine to help the patient breathe easier during an asthma attack.

entries.definition_cn: 短期使用后即弃、具有收藏价值的物品，如旧票据、宣传册或包装
entries.definition_en: collectible items of little lasting value, such as old tickets, pamphlets, or packaging
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家收集旧票据、宣传册和产品包装等短期使用品。
entries.example_en: The artist collected ephemera such as old tickets, pamphlets, and product packaging.

entries.definition_en: lasting for a very short time
entries.example_cn: 时尚是短暂的，每个季节都在变化。
entries.example_en: Fashions are ephemeral, changing with every season.

entries.definition_cn: 短命之物；尤指有翅成虫期仅持续一天的昆虫
entries.definition_en: a short-lived thing, especially an insect that lives for only one day in its winged form
entries.example_cn: 有些短命昆虫（如蜉蝣）的有翅成虫期只有一天。
entries.example_en: Some ephemerals, such as mayflies, live for only a day in their winged form.

entries.definition_en: the quality of lasting for a very short time
entries.example_cn: 樱花的短暂性使其美丽更加动人。
entries.example_en: The ephemerality of the cherry blossoms makes their beauty all the more poignant.

entries.definition_cn: 记录一年中天体视位置的表；星历表
entries.definition_en: a table giving the apparent positions of celestial bodies throughout a year
entries.example_cn: 天文学家查阅星历表以确定行星的确切位置。
entries.example_en: Astronomers consulted the ephemeris to determine the planet’s exact position.

entries.definition_en: very impressive or imposing in size or scale
entries.example_cn: 建造这座新大坝是一项宏伟的工程。
entries.example_en: The construction of the new dam was an epic project.

entries.definition_en: having the characteristics of a literary epic
entries.example_cn: 穿越沙漠的旅程是一场史诗般的冒险。
entries.example_en: The journey across the desert was an epic adventure.

entries.definition_en: a long narrative poem about a hero's deeds
entries.example_cn: 《伊利亚特》是一部著名的史诗。
entries.example_en: The Iliad is a famous epic poem.

entries.definition_en: relating to epic literature; epic or grandiose
entries.example_cn: 作者写了一首关于国家建立的史诗般的诗歌。
entries.example_en: The author wrote an epical poem about the founding of the nation.

entries.definition_en: relating to the fold of skin covering the inner corner of the eye
entries.example_cn: 内眦褶是东亚人群的一个常见特征。
entries.example_en: The epicanthic fold is a common feature in East Asian populations.

entries.definition_cn: 覆盖心脏外表面的膜，即浆膜心包的脏层
entries.definition_en: the membrane covering the outer surface of the heart; the visceral layer of the serous pericardium
entries.example_cn: 外科医生仔细检查心外膜以寻找炎症迹象。
entries.example_en: The surgeon carefully examined the epicardium for signs of inflammation.

entries.definition_en: having an ambiguous sexual identity
entries.example_cn: 在古代希腊，男女都穿性征模糊的服装。
entries.example_en: In ancient Greece, epicene garments were worn by both men and women.

entries.definition_cn: 阴柔的；（尤指男子）女性化的
entries.definition_en: effeminate, especially of a man
entries.example_cn: 评论家形容这位演员的表演阴柔过度，缺乏男子气概。
entries.example_en: The critic described the actor's performance as epicene, lacking masculine vigor.

usage.label: 贬义
usage.pattern: 描述男性时通常含贬义；源自 w49513r7 和 w49513r9。

entries.definition_cn: 间性人；性征无法明确归为男性或女性的人
entries.definition_en: a person whose sex characteristics cannot be classified unambiguously as male or female
entries.example_cn: 历史上，epicene 曾用于指称被认为性征不明确的人。
entries.example_en: Historically, epicene was used to describe a person whose sex characteristics were considered indeterminate.

entries.definition_en: the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake
entries.example_cn: 地震的震中位于海洋中部。
entries.example_en: The epicenter of the earthquake was located in the middle of the ocean.

entries.definition_en: the point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake
entries.example_cn: 地震的震中位于一个偏远的山脉中。
entries.example_en: The epicentre of the earthquake was located in a remote mountain range.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being grand, heroic, and momentous in scale or character
entries.example_cn: 小说生动地描绘了这场战役的史诗般特质。
entries.example_en: The epicness of the battle was captured vividly in the novel.

entries.definition_cn: 上髁；位于骨的髁上方、供肌肉、韧带或肌腱附着的骨性突起
entries.definition_en: a bony projection above a condyle that serves as an attachment point for muscles, ligaments, or tendons
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了肱骨上髁的骨折。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the fractured epicondyle of the humerus.

entries.definition_cn: 肘部骨突周围肌肉和软组织的疼痛性炎症
entries.definition_en: pain and inflammation affecting the muscles and tissues around the bony bumps on the elbow
entries.example_cn: 打了一整天网球后，他的肘部患上了严重的上髁炎。
entries.example_en: After playing tennis all day, he suffered from severe epicondylitis in his elbow.

entries.definition_en: a person who enjoys refined sensuous pleasures, especially good food and drink
entries.example_cn: 作为一名真正的美食家，他每晚品尝珍稀美酒和佳肴。
entries.example_en: As a true epicure, he spent his evenings tasting rare wines and delicacies.

entries.definition_en: a philosophical doctrine of hedonism defended by ancient Greek philosophers
entries.example_cn: 这位学者写了一篇关于伊壁鸠鲁主义对罗马文学影响的论文。
entries.example_en: The scholar wrote a thesis on the influence of epicureanism on Roman literature.

entries.definition_en: a circle that rolls around another circle, either inside or outside it
entries.example_cn: 古代天文学家使用本轮的概念来解释行星的逆行运动。
entries.example_en: The ancient astronomers used the concept of an epicycle to explain the retrograde motion of planets.

entries.definition_en: relating to an epicycle
entries.example_cn: 该本轮齿轮系统使变速箱能够平稳地换挡。
entries.example_en: The epicyclic gear system allows the transmission to change gears smoothly.

entries.definition_cn: 仪式性或颂扬性的；用于正式演说或典礼修辞的
entries.definition_en: relating to ceremonial, declamatory, or demonstrative rhetoric, often used for praise or formal occasions
entries.example_cn: 这篇演讲是一篇颂扬性的致辞，旨在向退休的总统致敬。
entries.example_en: The speech was an epideictic address delivered to honor the retiring president.

entries.definition_en: a widespread outbreak of an infectious disease affecting many people at the same time
entries.example_cn: 今年冬天，流感在北半球成为一种流行病。
entries.example_en: The flu became an epidemic in the northern hemisphere this winter.

entries.definition_cn: 流行的；像流行病一样的
entries.definition_en: of disease or anything resembling a disease; attacking or affecting many individuals in a community simultaneously
entries.example_cn: 关于该病毒的错误信息传播达到了流行病的规模。
entries.example_en: The spread of misinformation about the virus reached epidemic proportions.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to epidemiology
entries.example_cn: 这项流行病学研究追踪了病毒在全国范围内的传播情况。
entries.example_en: The epidemiologic study tracked the spread of the virus across the country.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to epidemiology
entries.example_cn: 该团队开展了一项流行病学研究以追踪病毒的传播。
entries.example_en: The team conducted an epidemiological study to track the virus spread.

entries.definition_en: a scientist who studies how diseases spread and how to control them
entries.example_cn: 这位流行病学家分析了数据以预测病毒的传播。
entries.example_en: The epidemiologist analyzed the data to predict the spread of the virus.

entries.definition_en: the branch of medical science that studies how diseases spread and how to control them
entries.example_cn: 流行病学帮助科学家了解病毒如何在人群中传播。
entries.example_en: Epidemiology helps scientists understand how a virus spreads through a population.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the epidermis, the outer layer of skin or plant tissue
entries.example_cn: 表皮细胞保护身体免受外部伤害。
entries.example_en: The epidermal cells protect the body from external damage.

entries.definition_en: the outermost layer of skin that covers the body of vertebrates
entries.example_cn: 表皮是抵御感染和伤害的第一道防线。
entries.example_en: The epidermis is the first line of defense against infection and injury.

entries.definition_cn: 无脊椎动物和植物中类似的外层细胞层
entries.definition_en: the similar outer layer of cells in invertebrates and plants
entries.example_cn: 植物的表皮有助于防止其失水。
entries.example_en: The plant's epidermis helps protect it from drying out.

entries.definition_en: a coiled tube in each testicle that transports sperm to the vas deferens
entries.example_cn: 附睾在精子释放前对其进行储存和成熟。
entries.example_en: The epididymis stores and matures sperm before they are released.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the epididymis
entries.example_cn: 患者在经历严重的睾丸疼痛后被诊断为附睾炎。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with epididymitis after experiencing severe testicular pain.

entries.definition_en: located on or outside the dura mater
entries.example_cn: 外科医生进行了硬膜外注射以麻醉下半身。
entries.example_en: The surgeon performed an epidural injection to numb the lower body.

entries.definition_en: anesthesia administered by injecting medicine into the space around the spinal cord
entries.example_cn: 她在分娩期间接受了硬膜外麻醉以缓解疼痛。
entries.example_en: She received an epidural to manage the pain during labor.

entries.definition_cn: 上腹部中央（心窝部）的；与腹上区有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to the epigastrium, the upper central region of the abdomen
entries.example_cn: 外科医生在上腹部做了一个切口以接触胃部。
entries.example_en: The surgeon made an epigastric incision to access the stomach.

entries.definition_en: lying on or over the stomach
entries.example_cn: 吃完辛辣餐后，她感到胃部上方一阵剧痛。
entries.example_en: She felt a sharp epigastric pain after eating the spicy meal.

entries.definition_en: a geological change in the mineral content of rock after the rock has formed
entries.example_cn: 石灰岩的成岩作用在数百万年间改变了其原始的矿物成分。
entries.example_en: The epigenesis of the limestone altered its original mineral composition over millions of years.

entries.definition_en: a flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe while swallowing
entries.example_cn: 会厌在吞咽时防止食物进入气管。
entries.example_en: The epiglottis prevents food from entering the trachea during swallowing.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the epiglottis, causing fever, severe sore throat, and difficulty swallowing
entries.example_cn: 该患者因急性会厌炎被送进医院。
entries.example_en: The patient was admitted to the hospital for acute epiglottitis.

entries.definition_en: a short, witty, and clever saying
entries.example_cn: 这位诗人写了一首关于时间流逝的警句。
entries.example_en: The poet wrote an epigram about the fleeting nature of time.

entries.definition_cn: 警句式的；简练而机智的
entries.definition_en: short, witty, and expressing a general truth or maxim
entries.example_cn: 他关于天气的警句式评论让全场鸦雀无声。
entries.example_en: His epigrammatic remark about the weather silenced the room.

entries.definition_en: a quotation placed at the beginning of a piece of writing
entries.example_cn: 这本书以一位著名诗人的题词开篇。
entries.example_en: The book opens with an epigraph from a famous poet.

entries.definition_en: an engraved inscription
entries.example_cn: 石碑上刻有铭文以纪念阵亡的士兵。
entries.example_en: The stone bears an epigraph commemorating the fallen soldiers.

entries.definition_cn: 铭文研究或释读，尤指古代铭文
entries.definition_en: the study or decipherment of inscriptions, especially ancient ones
entries.example_cn: 博物馆有一个专门的铭文学展区，用于展示古代石刻。
entries.example_en: The museum has a dedicated section for epigraphy to display ancient stone carvings.

entries.definition_en: inscriptions considered collectively
entries.example_cn: 这本书概述了古希腊的铭文，包括神庙和纪念碑上的铭文。
entries.example_en: The book surveys the epigraphy of ancient Greece, including inscriptions on temples and monuments.

entries.definition_cn: 从皮肤上脱毛，尤指去除或破坏毛根
entries.definition_en: the removal of hair from the skin, especially by removing or destroying the root
entries.example_cn: 医生建议通过脱毛来治疗过度毛发增生。
entries.example_en: The doctor recommended epilation to treat the excessive hair growth.

entries.definition_en: the act of removing hair from an animal skin
entries.example_cn: 传统的脱毛方法被用来为鞋子准备皮革。
entries.example_en: The traditional method of epilation was used to prepare the leather for the shoes.

entries.definition_en: a device used to remove unwanted hair
entries.example_cn: 她买了一个新的脱毛器来去除腿毛。
entries.example_en: She bought a new epilator to get rid of her leg hair.

entries.definition_en: a nervous system disorder causing loss of consciousness and convulsions
entries.example_cn: 癫痫是一种影响大脑并导致抽搐的疾病。
entries.example_en: Epilepsy is a condition that affects the brain and causes seizures.

entries.definition_en: a person who has epilepsy
entries.example_cn: 这家医院设有专门收治癫痫患者的病房。
entries.example_en: The hospital has a specialized ward for epileptic patients.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or characteristic of epilepsy
entries.example_cn: 医生为癫痫病情开了药。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed medication for the epileptic condition.

entries.definition_en: a short passage added at the end of a literary work
entries.example_cn: 小说以一段简短的结尾附言作结，反思了角色们的未来。
entries.example_en: The novel concludes with a brief epilog reflecting on the characters' futures.

entries.definition_en: a short speech, often in verse, spoken directly to the audience by an actor at the end of a play
entries.example_cn: 演员在离开舞台前向观众发表了一段感人的终场独白。
entries.example_en: The actor delivered a moving epilog to the audience before leaving the stage.

entries.definition_en: a short passage added at the end of a literary work to provide a conclusion or comment
entries.example_cn: 小说以一个尾声结束，揭示了多年后人物的命运。
entries.example_en: The novel ends with an epilogue that reveals the fate of the characters years later.

entries.definition_cn: （戏剧结尾演员面向观众发表的）结尾致辞
entries.definition_en: a short speech, often in verse, delivered by an actor directly to the audience at the end of a play
entries.example_cn: 这位演员发表了一段感人的结尾独白，感谢观众的支持。
entries.example_en: The actor delivered a moving epilogue to thank the audience for their support.

entries.definition_en: a hormone released by the adrenal glands during stress
entries.example_cn: 医生注射了肾上腺素来治疗过敏反应。
entries.example_en: The doctor injected epinephrine to treat the allergic reaction.

entries.definition_en: a secondary phenomenon that is a by-product of another phenomenon
entries.example_cn: 情绪波动通常被认为是潜在神经变化的副现象。
entries.example_en: Mood swings are often considered an epiphenomenon of the underlying neurological changes.

entries.definition_en: the repetition of the ends of two or more successive sentences or verses
entries.example_cn: 这首诗的结构很大程度上依赖句尾重复来营造节奏感。
entries.example_en: The poem's structure relies heavily on epiphora to create a rhythmic effect.

entries.definition_en: a cactus of the genus Epiphyllum having flattened jointed irregularly branching stems and showy tubular flowers
entries.example_cn: 这种罕见的昙花属仙人掌只在夜间开花。
entries.example_en: The rare epiphyllum blooms only at night.

entries.definition_en: relating to the epiphysis, the end part of a long bone
entries.example_cn: 骨骺板在青春期闭合。
entries.example_en: The epiphyseal plate closes during adolescence.

entries.definition_en: the end part of a long bone, which is initially separated from the main bone by cartilage before fusing together
entries.example_cn: 股骨的骨骺是儿童时期生长的部位。
entries.example_en: The epiphysis of the femur is where growth occurs during childhood.

entries.definition_en: a small endocrine gland located in the brain beneath the corpus callosum that secretes melatonin
entries.example_cn: 松果体通过分泌褪黑素调节身体的睡眠 - 觉醒周期。
entries.example_en: The epiphysis regulates the body's sleep-wake cycle by producing melatonin.

entries.definition_en: a plant that grows on another plant for support but gets its moisture and nutrients from the air and rain
entries.example_cn: 兰花是雨林中常见生长在树枝上的附生植物。
entries.example_en: Orchids are common epiphytes found growing on tree branches in the rainforest.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to epiphytes
entries.example_cn: 这些附生兰花生长在高大树木的树枝上，而不扎根于土壤。
entries.example_en: The epiphytic orchids grow on the branches of tall trees without rooting in the soil.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the episclera, the thin tissue overlying the sclera
entries.example_cn: 医生开了眼药水来治疗患者的表层巩膜炎。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed eye drops to treat the patient's episcleritis.

entries.definition_en: the collective body of bishops
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策在年度会议上得到了主教团的批准。
entries.example_en: The new policy was approved by the episcopacy during the annual meeting.

entries.definition_en: the collective body of bishops
entries.example_cn: 主教团召开会议讨论主教团的未来。
entries.example_en: The council of bishops convened to discuss the future of the episcopate.

entries.definition_en: the term of office of a bishop
entries.example_cn: 新任主教以一系列牧灵访问开始了他的任期。
entries.example_en: The new bishop began his episcopate with a series of pastoral visits.

entries.definition_en: the office and dignity of a bishop
entries.example_cn: 他将主教的职位视为神圣的信托，而非政治权力。
entries.example_en: He viewed the episcopate as a sacred trust rather than a political power.

entries.definition_en: the territorial jurisdiction of a bishop
entries.example_cn: 这位主教的辖区包括三个乡村县。
entries.example_en: The bishop's episcopate included three rural counties.

entries.definition_en: a surgical cut made in the perineum to help a baby be born
entries.example_cn: 医生建议进行会阴侧切术以加快分娩。
entries.example_en: The doctor recommended an episiotomy to speed up the delivery.

entries.definition_cn: 一系列相关事件中的一个独特事件
entries.definition_en: a distinctive event in a series of related events
entries.example_cn: 车祸只是他漫长人生中的一件事。
entries.example_en: The car accident was just one episode in his long life.

entries.definition_en: a part of a broadcast serial
entries.example_cn: 昨晚我们看了新剧的第一集。
entries.example_en: We watched the first episode of the new show last night.

entries.definition_en: a brief section of a literary or dramatic work that forms part of a connected series
entries.example_cn: 这部剧的这一集非常激动人心。
entries.example_en: This episode of the series was very exciting.

entries.definition_cn: （电影中）一段连续镜头组成的影片片段
entries.definition_en: a film consisting of a succession of related shots that develop a given subject in a movie
entries.example_cn: 导演拍摄了一段展示英雄旅程的长镜头片段。
entries.example_en: The director filmed a long episode showing the hero's journey.

entries.definition_en: occurring or appearing at usually irregular intervals
entries.example_cn: 她患有间歇性头痛，发作时间无法预测。
entries.example_en: She suffers from episodic headaches that come and go unpredictably.

entries.definition_cn: 由若干独立剧集组成的
entries.definition_en: divided into or composed of separate episodes
entries.example_cn: 他们观看了关于太空探索的新剧集系列。
entries.example_en: They watched the new episodic series about space exploration.

entries.definition_en: limited in duration to a single episode
entries.example_cn: 该团队的成就只是昙花一现，而非持续数年。
entries.example_en: The team's success was episodic rather than sustained over years.

entries.definition_en: in a way that happens at irregular intervals or in separate episodes
entries.example_cn: 患者在剧烈运动后会间歇性地感到疼痛。
entries.example_en: The patient experiences pain episodically after heavy exercise.

entries.definition_en: the suppression of a gene by the effect of an unrelated gene
entries.example_cn: 上位作用现象使得遗传特征的预测变得复杂。
entries.example_en: The phenomenon of epistasis complicates the prediction of genetic traits.

entries.definition_en: bleeding from the nose
entries.example_cn: 患者在挖鼻孔后出现了严重的鼻出血。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered a severe epistaxis after picking his nose.

entries.definition_cn: 知识型；界定某一时代真理知识边界的思想体系
entries.definition_en: the collective body of ideas that define what is considered certain knowledge at a specific time
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家认为，那个时代的知识体系限制了科学探究。
entries.example_en: The philosopher argued that the episteme of the era limited scientific inquiry.

entries.definition_cn: 认识的；与知识、认知或信念的论证有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to knowledge, cognition, or the justification of belief
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家探讨了人类感知的认识论界限。
entries.example_en: The philosopher debated the epistemic limits of human perception.

entries.definition_en: relating to the theory of knowledge
entries.example_cn: 人工智能的认识论影响仍在争论中。
entries.example_en: The epistemological implications of artificial intelligence are still being debated.

entries.definition_en: a person who studies the nature and scope of knowledge
entries.example_cn: 这位认识论学家认为所有知识都是主观的。
entries.example_en: The epistemologist argued that all knowledge is subjective.

entries.definition_en: the branch of philosophy that studies the nature, origin, and limits of human knowledge
entries.example_cn: 康德关于认识论的工作改变了我们对心灵的理解。
entries.example_en: Kant's work on epistemology changed how we understand the mind.

entries.definition_cn: 某种认识论或知识理论
entries.definition_en: a particular theory or school of thought about knowledge
entries.example_cn: 在他的认识论中，柏拉图认为我们对普遍概念的认识是一种回忆。
entries.example_en: In his epistemology, Plato maintains that our knowledge of universal concepts is a kind of recollection.

entries.definition_cn: 书信体文学作品；（尤指）正式或韵文书信
entries.definition_en: a literary work in the form of a letter, especially a formal or verse letter
entries.example_cn: 这位诗人发表了一篇书信体韵文作品。
entries.example_en: The poet published an epistle in verse.

entries.definition_cn: 新约中由使徒以书信形式写成的书卷
entries.definition_en: a book in the New Testament written as a letter from an Apostle
entries.example_cn: 《罗马书》是使徒保罗写的一封书信。
entries.example_en: Romans is an epistle written by the Apostle Paul.

entries.definition_en: relating to letters or written correspondence
entries.example_cn: 这部小说是一系列书信构成的书信体故事。
entries.example_en: The novel is an epistolary story told through a series of letters.

entries.definition_en: a written message on a tombstone or monument to remember someone who has died
entries.example_cn: 古老的墓地充满了风化的墓志铭。
entries.example_en: The old churchyard was filled with weathered epitaphs.

entries.definition_cn: 纪念死者的诗或其他简短文字
entries.definition_en: a poem or other short text written in memory of a deceased person
entries.example_cn: 报纸刊登了一篇纪念这位著名科学家的墓志铭。
entries.example_en: The newspaper published an epitaph commemorating the famous scientist.

entries.definition_cn: 在晶体基底上生长与基底具有确定晶体取向的晶体层
entries.definition_en: the growth of a crystalline layer on a crystalline substrate, with a defined crystallographic orientation relative to the substrate
entries.example_cn: 该半导体芯片是使用外延生长技术制造的。
entries.example_en: The semiconductor chip was manufactured using epitaxy techniques.

entries.definition_en: a poem or song written to honor a bride and groom on their wedding day
entries.example_cn: 诗人创作了一首婚礼颂歌来庆祝新婚夫妇的结合。
entries.example_en: The poet composed an epithalamium to celebrate the newlyweds' union.

entries.definition_en: relating to the epithelium, the tissue that lines body surfaces and cavities
entries.example_cn: 活检显示胃内壁的上皮细胞受损。
entries.example_en: The biopsy showed damage to the epithelial cells lining the stomach.

entries.definition_en: resembling or belonging to the epithelium
entries.example_cn: 这些肿瘤细胞呈上皮样外观。
entries.example_en: The tumor cells were epithelioid in appearance.

entries.definition_cn: 覆盖身体内外表面并衬覆器官和腔隙的组织层，即上皮
entries.definition_en: a layer of tissue that covers internal or external body surfaces and lines internal organs and cavities
entries.example_cn: 肠道内壁是能够吸收营养物质的上皮。
entries.example_en: The lining of the intestine is an epithelium that absorbs nutrients.

entries.definition_en: a word or phrase used to describe someone or something
entries.example_cn: 作者选择了一个诗意的描述语来形容这座古城。
entries.example_en: The author chose a poetic epithet to describe the ancient city.

entries.definition_cn: 辱骂性或蔑视性的词语或短语
entries.definition_en: an abusive or contemptuous word or phrase
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家因在辩论中使用侮辱性称呼而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was criticized for using an offensive epithet during the debate.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type
entries.example_cn: 这座城市是现代建筑的典型代表。
entries.example_en: This city is the epitome of modern architecture.

entries.definition_en: a short summary or abstract of a longer text
entries.example_cn: 她为通讯写了一篇该文章的摘要。
entries.example_en: She wrote an epitome of the article for the newsletter.

entries.definition_en: to be a perfect example of something or to show its essential characteristics
entries.example_cn: 这个小村庄是这一地区传统生活方式的典型代表。
entries.example_en: The small village epitomises the traditional way of life in this region.

entries.definition_en: to be a perfect example of something or to show all its important features
entries.example_cn: 这个小村庄体现了该地区传统的生活方式。
entries.example_en: This small village epitomizes the traditional way of life in the region.

entries.definition_en: the site on the surface of an antigen molecule to which an antibody attaches itself
entries.example_cn: 研究人员正试图确定引发免疫反应的特定位点。
entries.example_en: Researchers are trying to identify the specific epitope that triggers the immune response.

entries.definition_cn: （指动物疾病）在某一地区同类动物中流行的
