entries.definition_en: people in general (often used in the plural)
entries.example_cn: 这个村子里的人们非常友好。
entries.example_en: The folk of this village are very friendly.

entries.definition_en: people descended from a common ancestor
entries.example_cn: 我们都是同一族群的一部分。
entries.example_en: We are all part of the same folk.

entries.definition_cn: （通常指文盲社会的）民族或部落
entries.definition_en: a social division of (usually preliterate) people
entries.example_cn: 这些民族生活在孤立的小社区中。
entries.example_en: The folk lived in small, isolated communities.

entries.definition_en: the traditional and typically anonymous music that is an expression of the life of people in a community
entries.example_cn: 他们在节日上演奏了传统的民间音乐。
entries.example_en: They played traditional folk music at the festival.

entries.definition_cn: 一个文化或群体口耳相传的传统信仰、故事、歌曲和习俗；民俗
entries.definition_en: traditional beliefs, stories, songs, and customs of a culture or community, passed down orally
entries.example_cn: 这个村庄以其关于森林精灵的独特民间传说而闻名。
entries.example_en: The village is famous for its unique folklore about the forest spirits.

entries.definition_cn: （非正式，通常仅用复数）人们；大家
entries.definition_en: informal, plural-only: people in general; everybody or anybody
entries.example_cn: 商店里的人们非常友好。
entries.example_en: The folks at the store were very friendly.

usage.label: plural-only
usage.pattern: The source marks the general-people sense plural and plural-only.

entries.definition_cn: （非正式，通常仅用复数）家人，尤指父母
entries.definition_en: informal, plural-only: one's immediate family, especially one's parents
entries.example_cn: 我打算这个周末去看望我的父母。
entries.example_en: I am going to visit my folks this weekend.

entries.definition_en: a song traditionally sung by the common people of a region as part of their culture
entries.example_cn: 这首古老的民歌讲述了当地英雄的故事。
entries.example_en: The old folksong tells the story of the local hero.

entries.definition_en: having a style that belongs to ordinary people, especially in speech or attitude
entries.example_cn: 歌手那民间风格的嗓音让我想起了我的祖母。
entries.example_en: The singer's folksy voice reminded me of my grandmother.

entries.definition_en: informal, friendly, and familiar
entries.example_cn: 他用一种非常非正式的方式说话，让听众感到自在。
entries.example_en: He spoke in a folksy way that made the audience feel comfortable.

entries.definition_en: a story passed from person to person among ordinary people
entries.example_cn: 祖母给我们讲了一个关于勇敢英雄的奇妙民间故事。
entries.example_en: The grandmother told us a wonderful folktale about a brave hero.

entries.definition_cn: 小囊或囊状腔体，如毛囊
entries.definition_en: a small cavity or sac, such as a hair follicle
entries.example_cn: 头发从皮肤中的毛囊长出。
entries.example_en: Hair grows from a follicle located in the skin.

entries.definition_cn: 沿一条缝开裂以释放种子的干果，蓇葖果
entries.definition_en: a dry fruit that opens along one seam to release its seeds
entries.example_cn: 一枚马利筋的蓇葖果裂开了，释放出种子。
entries.example_en: A milkweed follicle split open and released its seeds.

entries.definition_en: relating to or forming a follicle
entries.example_cn: 卵泡细胞产生激素。
entries.example_en: The follicular cells produce hormones.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of a hair follicle
entries.example_cn: 医生开了抗生素来治疗毛囊炎。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed antibiotics to treat the folliculitis.

entries.definition_en: a revue with elaborate costuming
entries.example_cn: 这家剧院呈现了一系列壮观的华丽歌舞剧。
entries.example_en: The theater company presented a spectacular series of follies.

entries.definition_en: to go behind or after someone or something
entries.example_cn: 请跟我到教室来。
entries.example_en: Please follow me to the classroom.

entries.definition_en: to come after something in time or order
entries.example_cn: 在季节循环中，春天紧随冬天之后。
entries.example_en: Spring follows winter in the cycle of seasons.

entries.definition_en: to obey rules, orders, or instructions
entries.example_cn: 你必须时刻遵守安全规则。
entries.example_en: You must follow the safety rules at all times.

entries.definition_en: to move along a path or route
entries.example_cn: 我们沿着河流一直走到海边。
entries.example_en: We followed the river all the way to the sea.

entries.definition_cn: 随之而来；作为结果出现
entries.definition_en: to happen after something as a consequence
entries.example_cn: 热浪过后紧接着是一场风暴。
entries.example_en: A storm followed the heatwave.

entries.definition_en: to be a logical result of something
entries.example_cn: 由此可见，如果两个数不相等，其中一个必然大于另一个。
entries.example_en: It follows that if two numbers are unequal, one must be larger than the other.

entries.definition_en: to act in agreement with or according to something
entries.example_cn: 他的行为与他的言语不符。
entries.example_en: His actions did not follow his words.

entries.definition_en: to be next to or after something in a sequence
entries.example_cn: 星期一在星期日的后面。
entries.example_en: Monday follows Sunday in the week.

entries.definition_cn: 后续的结果、发展或进程
entries.definition_en: a consequence, development, or progression that follows from something else
entries.example_cn: 新规定对小企业产生了几项后续影响。
entries.example_en: The new regulations had several follow-on effects on small businesses.

entries.definition_cn: 供稍大一些的婴儿食用的配方奶
entries.definition_en: formula milk for infants who are slightly older
entries.example_cn: 医生说，宝宝六个月时可以改喝较大婴儿配方奶。
entries.example_en: The doctor said the baby could move on to follow-on formula at six months.

entries.definition_cn: （板球）一队在第一局落后达到规定分数后被迫立即进行的第二局
entries.definition_en: an immediate second innings in cricket forced on a team that trails by the required number of runs after the first innings
entries.example_cn: 该队第一局落后250分后，被迫立即进行第二局比赛。
entries.example_en: The team was made to follow on after trailing by 250 runs in the first innings.

entries.definition_en: the quality of carrying a project or intention to full completion
entries.example_cn: 她在商业计划上展现了极大的坚持到底的精神。
entries.example_en: She showed great follow-through on her business plan.

entries.definition_en: the action of completing a stroke naturally
entries.example_cn: 这位高尔夫球手的挥杆完整动作非常完美。
entries.example_en: The golfer's follow-through was perfect.

entries.definition_en: an activity that continues something that has already begun or repeats something done before
entries.example_cn: 医生安排了后续会议来讨论病人的进展。
entries.example_en: The doctor arranged a follow-up meeting to discuss the patient's progress.

entries.definition_en: a piece of work that builds on or continues earlier work
entries.example_cn: 这部电影是那本畅销书的成功续作。
entries.example_en: The movie was a successful follow-up to the popular book.

entries.definition_en: a subsequent examination of a patient to monitor earlier treatment
entries.example_cn: 你下个月需要回来做复查。
entries.example_en: You need to come back for a follow-up check-up next month.

entries.definition_en: a person who supports or follows another person, group, or movement
entries.example_cn: 他在社交媒体上有很多追随者。
entries.example_en: He has many followers on social media.

entries.definition_en: a person who pursues another
entries.example_cn: 逃犯设法在森林里甩掉了追赶者。
entries.example_en: The escaping prisoner managed to lose his followers in the forest.

entries.definition_en: about to be mentioned or specified
entries.example_cn: 下述几点对你的安全很重要。
entries.example_en: The following points are important for your safety.

entries.definition_en: coming immediately after in time or order
entries.example_cn: 随后的章节解释了实验结果。
entries.example_en: The following chapter explains the results of the experiment.

entries.definition_en: going or proceeding in the same direction as something else
entries.example_cn: 我们沿着随后的路径到达了山顶。
entries.example_en: We took the following path to reach the summit.

entries.definition_en: blowing in the direction of travel; downwind
entries.example_cn: 顺风帮助船快速移动。
entries.example_en: The following wind helped the boat move quickly.

entries.definition_en: a group of people who follow or support someone or something
entries.example_cn: 新领导人宣布后，其追随者迅速增加。
entries.example_en: The following of the new leader grew rapidly after the announcement.

entries.definition_en: the act of pursuing someone in an effort to overtake or capture them
entries.example_cn: 警察追捕嫌疑人长达数小时。
entries.example_en: The police were on the following of the suspect for hours.

entries.definition_en: an action that continues or repeats a previous activity
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构组织了一场后续活动以筹集更多资金。
entries.example_en: The charity organized a followup event to raise more funds.

entries.definition_en: a medical check to monitor a patient's recovery
entries.example_cn: 医生安排了复查以检查患者的康复进展。
entries.example_en: The doctor scheduled a followup appointment to check the patient's progress.

entries.definition_en: work that continues or develops from earlier efforts
entries.example_cn: 研究团队发表了关于初步发现的后续研究。
entries.example_en: The research team published a followup study on the initial findings.

entries.definition_cn: 愚蠢或轻率的行为，常因缺乏远见而导致
entries.definition_en: foolish or impractical behavior, often resulting from lack of foresight
entries.example_cn: 他决定把所有钱都投进那个计划，简直是鲁莽。
entries.example_en: His decision to invest all his money in that scheme was pure folly.

entries.definition_en: a stupid mistake or foolish action
entries.example_cn: 在不了解市场的情况下买房是一个巨大的愚蠢失误。
entries.example_en: Buying a house without checking the market was a great folly.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being rash and foolish
entries.example_cn: 由于最初计划的鲁莽轻率，该项目被放弃了。
entries.example_en: The project was abandoned due to the folly of the initial plan.

entries.definition_en: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.example_cn: 年轻人认为规则不适用于自己，这是愚蠢的行为。
entries.example_en: It is the folly of youth to believe that rules do not apply to them.

entries.definition_en: to stir up public opinion or unrest
entries.example_cn: 该组织被指控煽动抗议者之间的暴力行为。
entries.example_en: The group was accused of fomenting violence among the protesters.

entries.definition_en: to treat a wound or sore with warm water or medicated lotions
entries.example_cn: 医生建议他用热毛巾热敷发炎的关节。
entries.example_en: The doctor advised him to foment the inflamed joint with a warm compress.

entries.definition_en: showing warmth or affection
entries.example_cn: 她慈爱地对孩子们微笑。
entries.example_en: She gave her children a fond smile.

entries.definition_en: having a strong preference or liking for
entries.example_cn: 我非常喜爱古典音乐。
entries.example_en: I am very fond of classical music.

entries.definition_en: extravagantly or foolishly loving and indulgent
entries.example_cn: 他对狗太溺爱了，任由它到处乱跑。
entries.example_en: He is too fond of his dog and lets it run wild.

entries.definition_en: absurd or silly because unlikely
entries.example_cn: 希望他很快回来，这不过是美好的幻想罢了。
entries.example_en: It is a fond hope that he will return soon.

entries.definition_en: a creamy sugar preparation used for icing cakes or as a base for candies
entries.example_cn: 面包师用光滑的巧克力翻糖覆盖了蛋糕。
entries.example_en: The baker covered the cake with smooth chocolate fondant.

entries.definition_en: to touch or stroke someone or something gently and affectionately
entries.example_cn: 她温柔地爱抚着那只小猫。
entries.example_en: She gently fondled the kitten.

entries.definition_cn: 爱抚；亲昵地抚摸，有时不涉及性接触
entries.definition_en: the act of caressing or touching affectionately, sometimes without sexual contact
entries.example_cn: 这对情侣的爱抚是亲昵的，没有性接触。
entries.example_en: The couple's fondling was affectionate and nonsexual.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows love or affection
entries.example_cn: 她深情地凝视着那张旧照片。
entries.example_en: She looked at the old photograph fondly.

entries.definition_en: a tendency to like something
entries.example_cn: 他喜爱古典音乐。
entries.example_en: He has a fondness for classical music.

entries.definition_en: a positive feeling of liking
entries.example_cn: 她给新老师送花，表达了她对他的好感。
entries.example_en: She showed her fondness for the new teacher by bringing him flowers.

entries.definition_en: a quality arising from feelings of affection or love
entries.example_cn: 老人慈爱地看着他的孙子。
entries.example_en: The old man looked at his grandson with great fondness.

entries.definition_en: melted cheese or chocolate served for dipping bread or fruit
entries.example_cn: 我们享用了一碗温暖的格鲁耶尔奶酪蘸酱，搭配脆面包。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a warm fondu of Gruyère cheese with crusty bread.

entries.definition_en: cubes of meat or seafood cooked in hot oil and served with sauce
entries.example_cn: 厨师准备了用胡椒酱调味的油浸羊肉块。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a fondu of lamb cubes with a peppercorn sauce.

entries.definition_cn: 奶酪或巧克力火锅（用于蘸面包或水果）
entries.definition_en: hot cheese or chocolate melted into a sauce for dipping bread or fruits
entries.example_cn: 我们享用了一顿奶酪和新鲜水果火锅晚餐。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a fondue dinner with melted cheese and fresh fruit.

entries.definition_cn: 在热油中烹熟的肉块或海鲜，蘸各种酱料食用
entries.definition_en: cubes of meat or seafood cooked in hot oil and then dipped in various sauces
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅专门提供勃艮第火锅：将肉在热油中烹熟后配蘸酱食用。
entries.example_en: The restaurant specializes in fondue bourguignonne, with meat cooked in hot oil and served with dipping sauces.

entries.definition_en: a specific size and style of type within a type family
entries.example_cn: 设计师为报纸的标题选择了一种粗体字体。
entries.example_en: The designer chose a bold font for the headline of the newspaper.

entries.definition_en: a bowl for holding baptismal water
entries.example_cn: 牧师在仪式前将圣水倒入洗礼盆中。
entries.example_en: The priest poured holy water into the font before the ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 婴儿或胎儿头骨之间的膜状间隙
entries.definition_en: a membranous gap between the bones of the cranium in an infant or fetus
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了婴儿的囟门以确保头骨发育正常。
entries.example_en: The doctor checked the infant's fontanel to ensure proper skull development.

entries.definition_en: a soft spot on an infant's skull where the bones have not yet fused
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了婴儿的囟门以确保发育正常。
entries.example_en: The doctor checked the baby's fontanelle to ensure proper development.

entries.definition_en: any substance consumed by an animal or person to sustain life and provide energy or nutrients
entries.example_cn: 蔬菜是健康饮食的重要组成部分，能提供必需的营养。
entries.example_en: Vegetables are an important part of a healthy diet and provide essential nutrients.

entries.definition_en: anything that nourishes or stimulates the mind
entries.example_cn: 书籍能为思考提供有益的素材。
entries.example_en: Books provide food for thought.

entries.definition_cn: 因吃食物而产生的愉悦感
entries.definition_en: a pleasurable sensation caused by eating food
entries.example_cn: 昨天我吃了晒干的番茄后，感到一阵极度愉悦。
entries.example_en: Yesterday I had a foodgasm after eating sun-dried tomatoes.

entries.definition_en: a person who enjoys good food and drink and is interested in culinary matters
entries.example_cn: 作为一名美食家，她周末会去探索城市里的新餐厅。
entries.example_en: As a foodie, she spends her weekends exploring new restaurants in the city.

entries.definition_cn: 缺少食物的；没有食物的
entries.definition_en: lacking food or having no food available
entries.example_cn: 探险家面临着一段没有食物的沙漠旅程。
entries.example_en: The explorers faced a foodless journey across the desert.

entries.definition_en: any substance that can be eaten or prepared for eating
entries.example_cn: 小麦是许多文化中的主要食物原料。
entries.example_en: Wheat is a staple foodstuff in many cultures.

entries.definition_en: items of food sold in a grocery store
entries.example_cn: 这家超市出售来自世界各地的各种食品。
entries.example_en: The supermarket sells a wide variety of foodstuffs from around the world.

entries.definition_en: a person who lacks good judgment
entries.example_cn: 别这么傻，开这么快。
entries.example_en: Don't be such a fool and drive so fast.

entries.definition_en: a person who is easily deceived
entries.example_cn: 他太容易上当了，竟然中了那个骗局。
entries.example_en: He was such a fool that he fell for the scam.

entries.definition_en: to trick or deceive someone
entries.example_cn: 魔术师用他的戏法愚弄了观众。
entries.example_en: The magician fooled the audience with his tricks.

entries.definition_en: to play around or joke roughly
entries.example_cn: 孩子们正在花园里嬉戏打闹。
entries.example_en: The children were fooling around in the garden.

entries.definition_en: to hoax or trick someone
entries.example_cn: 他们骗他以为自己中了彩票。
entries.example_en: They fooled him into thinking he won the lottery.

entries.definition_en: to spend money wastefully
entries.example_cn: 他把遗产挥霍在赌博上了。
entries.example_en: He fooled away his inheritance on gambling.

entries.definition_en: a professional clown in the Middle Ages
entries.example_cn: 小丑用笑话逗乐了国王。
entries.example_en: The fool entertained the king with jokes.

entries.definition_en: behavior that is silly or lacks good sense
entries.example_cn: 别再胡闹了，听我讲指示。
entries.example_en: Stop your foolery and listen to the instructions.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being reckless and taking great risks without thinking about the danger
entries.example_cn: 在没有绳索的情况下攀登悬崖的鲁莽行为显而易见。
entries.example_en: The foolhardiness of climbing the cliff without a rope was evident to everyone.

entries.definition_en: marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences
entries.example_cn: 在没有适当装备的情况下尝试攀登是鲁莽的行为。
entries.example_en: It was foolhardy to attempt the climb without proper equipment.

entries.definition_en: characterized by a feeling of irresponsibility
entries.example_cn: 经理不负责任的行为导致了项目的失败。
entries.example_en: The fooling behavior of the manager led to the project's failure.

entries.definition_en: lacking good sense or judgment
entries.example_cn: 没带伞就出门是不明智的。
entries.example_en: It was foolish to leave the house without an umbrella.

entries.definition_en: showing or caused by stupidity
entries.example_cn: 他在计算中犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
entries.example_en: He made a foolish mistake in the calculation.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows a lack of good sense or judgment
entries.example_cn: 他愚蠢地决定将所有积蓄投入到那个冒险的计划中。
entries.example_en: He foolishly decided to invest all his savings in that risky scheme.

entries.definition_cn: 愚蠢或鲁莽的行为习惯
entries.definition_en: the habit of behaving in a stupid or rash way
entries.example_cn: 他的愚蠢导致他把所有钱都投进了一个危险的计划中。
entries.example_en: His foolishness led him to invest all his money in a risky scheme.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being rash and foolish
entries.example_cn: 当计划失败时，其鲁莽和愚蠢的特质变得显而易见。
entries.example_en: The foolishness of the plan became obvious when it failed.

entries.definition_en: a stupid mistake
entries.example_cn: 那是个愚蠢的错误；你应该先查一下地图。
entries.example_en: That was a foolishness; you should have checked the map first.

entries.definition_en: not liable to failure
entries.example_cn: 说明不易出错，所以任何人都能照着做。
entries.example_en: The instructions were foolproof, so anyone could follow them.

entries.definition_en: proof against human misuse or error
entries.example_cn: 软件团队在发布前努力使系统不易出错。
entries.example_en: The software team worked hard to foolproof the system before launch.

entries.definition_cn: 一种传统纸张尺寸；大张纸或其对折、裁半后的纸张
entries.definition_en: a traditional paper size, especially a large sheet measuring about 13¼ by 16½ inches, or a sheet of that size folded or cut in half
entries.example_cn: 这份报告印在这种传统尺寸的纸张上。
entries.example_en: The report was printed on foolscap paper.

entries.definition_en: the part of the leg of a human being below the ankle joint
entries.example_cn: 她跑步时伤了脚。
entries.example_en: She hurt her foot while running.

entries.definition_en: a linear unit of length equal to 12 inches or a third of a yard
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子长六英尺。
entries.example_en: The table is six feet long.

entries.definition_en: the lower part of anything
entries.example_cn: 山的底部覆盖着积雪。
entries.example_en: The foot of the mountain is covered in snow.

entries.definition_en: the pedal extremity of vertebrates other than human beings
entries.example_cn: 马快速地移动了它的脚。
entries.example_en: The horse moved its foot quickly.

entries.definition_en: lowest support of a structure
entries.example_cn: 桥的底部支撑在河床上。
entries.example_en: The foot of the bridge rests on the riverbed.

entries.definition_en: pay for something
entries.example_cn: 我将支付晚餐的费用。
entries.example_en: I will foot the bill for dinner.

entries.definition_en: walk
entries.example_cn: 我们步行回家以节省公交车费。
entries.example_en: We footed it home to save money on the bus fare.

entries.definition_en: add a column of numbers
entries.example_cn: 请计算这笔开支列的总额。
entries.example_en: Please foot the column of expenses.

entries.definition_cn: 旧制亮度单位，等于每平方英尺 1/π 坎德拉
entries.definition_en: a former unit of luminance equal to 1/π candela per square foot
entries.example_cn: 屏幕的亮度是以英尺坎德拉为单位的。
entries.example_en: The brightness of the screen was measured in foot-lamberts.

entries.definition_cn: 英尺-磅力（功、能量或扭矩单位）
entries.definition_en: a unit of work or energy equal to one pound-force acting through one foot; also a unit of torque
entries.example_cn: 发动机的扭矩以英尺 - 磅为单位测量。
entries.example_en: The torque of the engine is measured in foot-pounds.

entries.definition_en: a unit of energy equal to 2,240 foot-pounds
entries.example_cn: 这台机器做了一英尺吨的功。
entries.example_en: The machine performed one foot-ton of work.

entries.definition_en: film that has been shot
entries.example_cn: 这部纪录片使用了20世纪60年代的档案录像。
entries.example_en: The documentary is made of archival footage from the 1960s.

entries.definition_en: a rate of charging by the linear foot of work done
entries.example_cn: 承包商对管道工程按英尺收取了高额费用。
entries.example_en: The contractor charged a high rate for the plumbing footage.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用球进行的运动，两队试图将球踢、带或推进入对方球门
entries.definition_en: a game played with a ball where two teams try to kick or carry or propel the ball into each other's goal
entries.example_cn: 足球在许多国家非常受欢迎。
entries.example_en: Football is very popular in many countries.

entries.definition_cn: 美式橄榄球比赛中使用的充气长形球
entries.definition_en: the inflated oblong ball used in playing American football
entries.example_cn: 他把球踢进了达阵区。
entries.example_en: He kicked the football into the end zone.

entries.definition_en: an athlete who plays American football
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的美式橄榄球运动员在最后一分钟达阵得分。
entries.example_en: The famous footballer scored a touchdown in the final minute.

entries.definition_en: a small tub used for warming, washing, or disinfecting the feet
entries.example_cn: 她用温水和草药填满了足浴盆，以舒缓她疲惫的双脚。
entries.example_en: She filled the footbath with warm water and herbs to soothe her tired feet.

entries.definition_en: a narrow platform for standing or bracing the feet
entries.example_cn: 他站在马车的脚踏板上去够行李架。
entries.example_en: He stood on the footboard of the carriage to reach the luggage rack.

entries.definition_en: a vertical board forming the foot of a bed
entries.example_cn: 那张古董床尾板雕刻着复杂的花卉图案。
entries.example_en: The antique footboard was carved with intricate floral patterns.

entries.definition_en: a bridge built specifically for people to walk across
entries.example_cn: 河上的那座旧人行桥需要修理。
entries.example_en: The old footbridge over the river needs to be repaired.

entries.definition_en: having feet
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子有四条结实的腿作为脚。
entries.example_en: The table is footed with four sturdy legs.

entries.definition_cn: 足部偏好（如踢球时惯用某只脚）
entries.definition_en: the property of favoring one foot over the other (as in kicking a ball)
entries.example_cn: 教练分析了该球员的足部偏好，以确定他在场上的最佳位置。
entries.example_en: The coach analyzed the player's footedness to determine the best position for him on the field.

entries.definition_en: a printed note placed below the text on a printed page
entries.example_cn: 请查看页脚以获取出版日期。
entries.example_en: Please check the footer for the publication date.

entries.definition_cn: 身高或长度以英尺计的人或物（用于复合词）
entries.definition_en: a person or thing of a specified height or length in feet, used in compounds
entries.example_cn: 这艘新船是一艘六英尺长的小船。
entries.example_en: The new boat is a six-footer.

entries.definition_en: a person who travels by walking
entries.example_cn: 长途跋涉后，这些徒步旅行者成了疲惫的步行者。
entries.example_en: The hikers were tired footers after a long day of walking.

entries.definition_en: the sound of a step of someone walking
entries.example_cn: 沉重的脚步声在空旷的走廊里回荡。
entries.example_en: The heavy footfall echoed down the empty hallway.

entries.definition_cn: 进入或经过某处的人数，尤指商店的客流量；人流量
entries.definition_en: the number of people entering or passing through a place, especially a shop; pedestrian traffic
entries.example_cn: 节日期间，这家商店的客流量增加了。
entries.example_en: The shop's footfall increased during the holiday season.

entries.definition_en: clothing or equipment worn on the feet
entries.example_cn: 徒步者在开始攀登前检查了他们的足部装备。
entries.example_en: The hikers checked their footgear before starting the climb.

entries.definition_en: a relatively low hill on the lower slope of a mountain
entries.example_cn: 我们在俯瞰山谷的山麓扎营。
entries.example_en: We camped on the foothill overlooking the valley.

entries.definition_cn: （站立或攀爬时的）落脚处；立足点
entries.definition_en: a place that supports the foot when standing or climbing
entries.example_cn: 登山者在湿滑的岩壁上寻找可以落脚的地方。
entries.example_en: The climber searched for a foothold on the slippery rock face.

entries.definition_cn: （为进一步发展铺路的）初步成就
entries.definition_en: an initial success that enables further progress
entries.example_cn: 赢得第一份合同为这家初创公司在市场上奠定了至关重要的基础。
entries.example_en: Winning the first contract gave the startup a crucial foothold in the market.

entries.definition_en: an area in enemy territory that has been captured and is being held
entries.example_cn: 军队在发动最后攻击之前，先在山谷中确立了一个立足点。
entries.example_en: The army secured a foothold in the valley before launching the final attack.

entries.definition_cn: 相对于他人或群体的地位或关系
entries.definition_en: a position or relationship with respect to other people or groups
entries.example_cn: 他们彼此处于平等地位。
entries.example_en: They were on an equal footing with each other.

entries.definition_cn: 为某事物提供支持的基础或依据
entries.definition_en: a basis or foundation that supports something
entries.example_cn: 该条约确立了未来合作的坚实基础。
entries.example_en: The treaty established a strong footing for future cooperation.

entries.definition_cn: 站立或攀爬时支撑双脚的表面或地方
entries.definition_en: a surface or place that supports the feet when standing or climbing
entries.example_cn: 他在岩石突出的边缘找到了稳固的落脚处。
entries.example_en: He found firm footing on the rocky ledge.

entries.definition_en: having no feet or similar body parts for walking
entries.example_cn: 蛇是一种无足的动物，通过蜿蜒爬行来移动。
entries.example_en: The snake is a footless creature that moves by wriggling.

entries.definition_en: [colloquial] clumsy or inept
entries.example_cn: 即使是最简单的机器，他修起来也很笨拙。
entries.example_en: He is footless at fixing even the simplest machines.

entries.definition_en: a light placed at the front edge of a stage to illuminate actors from below
entries.example_cn: 演员们的脸庞被脚灯照得通亮。
entries.example_en: The actors' faces were brightly lit by the footlights.

entries.definition_en: small and of little importance
entries.example_cn: 合同中微不足道的细节被忽略了。
entries.example_en: The footling details of the contract were overlooked.

entries.definition_en: a trunk for storing personal possessions, typically kept at the foot of a bed in a barracks
entries.example_cn: 士兵打开他的脚箱，发现制服整齐地叠在里面。
entries.example_en: The soldier opened his footlocker to find his uniform neatly folded inside.

entries.definition_en: free to go or do as one pleases without restriction
entries.example_cn: 毕业后，她感到无拘无束，准备环游世界。
entries.example_en: After graduating, she felt footloose and ready to travel the world.

entries.definition_en: a male servant in a large household who runs errands and does chores
entries.example_cn: 男仆为客人打开了沉重的门。
entries.example_en: The footman opened the heavy door for the guests.

entries.definition_en: a note printed at the bottom of a page to explain or cite a reference
entries.example_cn: 作者在脚注中澄清了历史数据的来源。
entries.example_en: The author included a footnote to clarify the origin of the historical data.

entries.definition_cn: 广义上指相对于某个较大事件而言重要性较低的事件
entries.definition_en: broadly, an event of lesser importance in relation to a larger event
entries.example_cn: 这场失利最终只是这支球队漫长历史中的一个注脚。
entries.example_en: The defeat became only a footnote in the team's long history.

entries.definition_en: to add explanatory notes to a text
entries.example_cn: 编辑决定在小说中为每一处关于古代神话的引用加注脚注。
entries.example_en: The editor decided to footnote every reference to ancient mythology in the novel.

entries.definition_en: (archaic) a highway robber who attacks travellers on foot
entries.example_cn: 这部旧小说描述了由于拦路抢劫者的袭击，在乡间独自旅行的危险。
entries.example_en: The old novel describes the dangers of traveling alone in the countryside due to footpad attacks.

usage.label: archaic
usage.pattern: a thief who robs travellers on the road

entries.definition_en: a path made by people walking
entries.example_cn: 我们沿着穿过树林的小径散步，景色宜人。
entries.example_en: We took a scenic walk along the footpath through the woods.

entries.definition_cn: 机车驾驶室的操作平台
entries.definition_en: the platform in the cab of a train engine where the driver stands to operate the controls
entries.example_cn: 工程师站在操作平台上调节蒸汽阀门。
entries.example_en: The engineer stood on the footplate to adjust the steam valves.

entries.definition_en: a mark left on a surface by a foot or shoe
entries.example_cn: 侦探在犯罪现场发现了一个泥泞的脚印。
entries.example_en: The detective found a muddy footprint at the scene of the crime.

entries.definition_en: the amount of space occupied by an object
entries.example_cn: 新的服务器机房将在地下室占据很大的占地面积。
entries.example_en: The new server room will take up a large footprint in the basement.

entries.definition_en: a trace indicating that something was once present or significant
entries.example_cn: 这座旧建筑是原城市唯一剩下的痕迹。
entries.example_en: The old building is the only remaining footprint of the original city.

entries.definition_en: a race run on foot
entries.example_cn: 马拉松是今年该市最受欢迎的赛跑。
entries.example_en: The marathon was the most popular footrace in the city this year.

entries.definition_en: a low seat or stool used to rest one's feet while seated
entries.example_cn: 她在腿下放了一个带垫子的脚踏板以改善坐姿。
entries.example_en: She placed a cushioned footrest under her legs to improve her posture.

entries.definition_en: having sore or tired feet
entries.example_cn: 徒步一整天后，我感到双脚酸痛无力。
entries.example_en: After hiking all day, I felt completely footsore.

entries.definition_en: the sound made when someone walks
entries.example_cn: 我听到身后楼梯上传来一声轻微的脚步声。
entries.example_en: I heard a faint footstep on the stairs behind me.

entries.definition_en: the act of taking a step while walking
entries.example_cn: 他小心翼翼地迈了一步走进黑暗的房间里。
entries.example_en: He took a cautious footstep into the dark room.

entries.definition_en: the distance covered by one step
entries.example_cn: 两块石头相距只有一步之遥。
entries.example_en: The two stones were only a footstep apart.

entries.definition_en: a low seat or stool used to rest one's feet while sitting
entries.example_cn: 他在脚踏凳上放了一个垫子，让它更舒服。
entries.example_en: He placed a cushion on the footstool to make it more comfortable.

entries.definition_en: the lower wall of an inclined fault
entries.example_cn: 矿工们沿着矿脉向下挖掘，直到到达下盘。
entries.example_en: The miners followed the vein down to the footwall.

entries.definition_en: clothing worn on a person's feet
entries.example_cn: 这家商店提供适合所有季节的各种鞋类。
entries.example_en: The store offers a wide range of footwear for all seasons.

entries.definition_en: covering for a person's feet
entries.example_cn: 实验室要求穿着防护足部覆盖物。
entries.example_en: Protective footwear is required in the laboratory.

entries.definition_en: the way in which someone uses their feet to move
entries.example_cn: 拳击手的步法使他能够躲开每一拳。
entries.example_en: The boxer's footwork allowed him to dodge every punch.

entries.definition_en: skillful handling of a difficult situation
entries.example_cn: 外交官在谈判中的巧妙周旋令人印象深刻。
entries.example_en: The diplomat's footwork in the negotiations was impressive.

entries.definition_cn: 花花公子；过分讲究衣着和外表的男子
entries.definition_en: a man who cares excessively about his clothes and looks
entries.example_cn: 那个花花公子把所有的钱都花在了昂贵的西装上。
entries.example_en: The fop spent all his money on expensive suits.

entries.definition_cn: 过分讲究衣着和举止的
entries.definition_en: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner
entries.example_cn: 他那过分讲究的衣着在正式晚宴上引人注目。
entries.example_en: His foppish attire drew attention at the formal dinner.

entries.definition_en: towards; in the direction of
entries.example_cn: 她朝公交车站走去。
entries.example_en: She headed for the bus stop.

entries.definition_en: directed at; intended to belong to.
entries.example_cn: 这份礼物是给你的。
entries.example_en: This gift is for you.

entries.definition_cn: 为了（帮助、造福或尊敬某人）
entries.definition_en: in order to help, benefit, or honor someone.
entries.example_cn: 他们为了家人努力工作。
entries.example_en: They worked hard for their family.

entries.definition_en: befitting of someone's beliefs, needs, or tastes.
entries.example_cn: 这条裙子适合正式场合。
entries.example_en: This dress is for formal occasions.

entries.definition_en: to be used or treated in a stated way.
entries.example_cn: 我们把那间房间用作会议室。
entries.example_en: We used the room for a meeting.

entries.definition_en: supporting; in favour of.
entries.example_cn: 我支持新计划。
entries.example_en: I am for the new plan.

entries.definition_en: because
entries.example_cn: 他待在家里，因为他病了。
entries.example_en: He stayed home for he was ill.

entries.definition_en: marking the following verb as an infinitive.
entries.example_cn: 我想去。（注：非标准用法）
entries.example_en: I want for to go.

entries.definition_en: to collect or search for food.
entries.example_cn: 士兵们不得不在乡间觅食。
entries.example_en: Soldiers had to forage for food in the countryside.

entries.definition_en: to wander around while feeding.
entries.example_cn: 鹿在白天于森林中游荡觅食。
entries.example_en: Deer forage in the forest during the day.

entries.definition_en: bulky food like grass or hay intended for horses or cattle.
entries.example_cn: 农夫给马带来了新鲜的粗饲料。
entries.example_en: The farmer brought fresh forage for the horses.

entries.definition_en: the act of searching for food and provisions.
entries.example_cn: 探险队在荒野中搜寻补给度过了几周时间。
entries.example_en: The expedition spent weeks foraging in the wilderness.

entries.definition_cn: 觅食者；（尤指人类）采集者
entries.definition_en: an animal or person that searches for food and other resources in the wild
entries.example_cn: 早期人类作为采集者生存，采集坚果并捕猎小动物。
entries.example_en: Early humans survived as foragers, gathering nuts and hunting small animals.

entries.definition_en: the act of searching for food and provisions
entries.example_cn: 鸟儿正在花园里觅食种子。
entries.example_en: The birds were foraging for seeds in the garden.

entries.definition_en: a marine microorganism with a calcareous shell that has openings for pseudopods
entries.example_cn: 古生物学家研究有孔虫以了解古代海洋环境。
entries.example_en: Paleontologists study forams to understand ancient ocean environments.

entries.definition_en: a natural hole or opening through a bone or a membrane
entries.example_cn: 外科医生仔细检查了头骨上的孔。
entries.example_en: The surgeon carefully examined the foramen in the skull.

entries.definition_en: a sudden short attack
entries.example_cn: 军队对敌占区发动了一次短暂的突袭。
entries.example_en: The army launched a brief foray into enemy territory.

entries.definition_en: an initial attempt, especially outside one's usual areas of competence
entries.example_cn: 写小说是她涉足虚构文学的首次尝试。
entries.example_en: Writing a novel was her first foray into fiction.

entries.definition_en: to briefly enter enemy territory
entries.example_cn: 士兵们越境侦察，收集情报。
entries.example_en: The soldiers forayed across the border to gather intelligence.

entries.definition_en: to scour an area for goods as part of a raid (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 袭击者搜掠村庄，抢走食物和其他财物。
entries.example_en: The raiders forayed the village for food and other goods.

entries.definition_en: to refrain from doing something
entries.example_cn: 会议结束前，他克制住了不开口的冲动。
entries.example_en: He forbore to speak until the meeting was over.

entries.definition_en: to resist doing something
entries.example_cn: 她忍住了拆开礼物的冲动，一直等到生日。
entries.example_en: She forbore from opening the gift until her birthday.

entries.definition_en: a person from whom you are descended
entries.example_cn: 我的祖先是一位在此山谷定居的拓荒者。
entries.example_en: My forbear was a pioneer who settled in this valley.

entries.definition_en: patient tolerance of delay or incompetence
entries.example_cn: 由于进展缓慢，该项目需要极大的耐心。
entries.example_en: The project required great forbearance due to the slow progress.

entries.definition_cn: 暂缓行使权利或克制行动
entries.definition_en: the act of delaying the enforcement of rights or refraining from acting
entries.example_cn: 该公司没有立即起诉客户，表现出了克制。
entries.example_en: The company showed forbearance by not suing the customer immediately.

entries.definition_en: showing patient self-control and restraint, especially under difficult circumstances
entries.example_cn: 她宽容忍耐的性格使她能够倾听愤怒的顾客而不发脾气。
entries.example_en: Her forbearing nature allowed her to listen to the angry customer without losing her temper.

entries.definition_en: to command someone not to do something
entries.example_cn: 老师禁止学生在考试期间使用手机。
entries.example_en: The teacher forbade the students from using their phones during the exam.

usage.label: forbid someone from doing something
usage.pattern: forbade the students from using their phones

entries.definition_en: to prevent something from happening or arising
entries.example_cn: 大雨阻止了我们在公园野餐。
entries.example_en: Heavy rain forbade us from having a picnic in the park.

entries.definition_en: not allowed to be used or mentioned
entries.example_cn: 图书馆内禁止使用手机。
entries.example_en: The use of mobile phones is forbidden in the library.

entries.definition_en: harshly uninviting or formidable in manner or appearance
entries.example_cn: 这片令人望而却步的景观劝退了徒步旅行者。
entries.example_en: The forbidding landscape discouraged hikers.

entries.definition_en: threatening or foreshadowing evil or tragic developments
entries.example_cn: 那乌云密布预示着暴风雨即将来临。
entries.example_en: The forbidding clouds promised a storm.

entries.definition_en: an official prohibition or edict against something
entries.example_cn: 保护区内严禁狩猎的新禁令得到了严格执行。
entries.example_en: The new forbidding against hunting in the reserve was strictly enforced.

entries.definition_cn: 令人望而生畏地；威胁性地
entries.definition_en: in an unpleasant or menacing manner
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨来临前，天空变得阴森而令人畏惧。
entries.example_en: The sky turned forbiddingly dark before the storm arrived.

entries.definition_en: to make someone do something by using pressure
entries.example_cn: 他们强迫他打开门。
entries.example_en: They forced him to open the door.

entries.definition_en: to push or urge someone to act
entries.example_cn: 恐惧驱使她逃跑。
entries.example_en: Fear forced her to run away.

entries.definition_en: to impose something urgently
entries.example_cn: 他们强行将新规则加诸工人身上。
entries.example_en: They forced the new rules on the workers.

entries.definition_en: physical strength, power, or intensity
entries.example_cn: 爆炸释放出巨大的力量。
entries.example_en: The explosion released an enormous amount of force.

entries.definition_en: a powerful effect or influence
entries.example_cn: 风的力量把树吹倒了。
entries.example_en: The force of the wind blew the tree down.

entries.definition_en: a push or pull that changes motion
entries.example_cn: 重力是一种将物体拉下的力。
entries.example_en: Gravity is a force that pulls objects down.

entries.definition_en: to move something with strength
entries.example_cn: 他用力把重箱子推过地板。
entries.example_en: He forced the heavy box across the floor.

entries.definition_en: a group of people who obey orders
entries.example_cn: 军队是一支军事力量。
entries.example_en: The army is a military force.

entries.definition_en: to feed someone who will not or cannot eat
entries.example_cn: 囚犯们被看守强行喂食。
entries.example_en: The prisoners were force-fed by the guards.

entries.definition_cn: 强迫某人接受信息或某种意识形态
entries.definition_en: to force someone to accept information or an ideology
entries.example_cn: 这所学校试图把一种狭隘的意识形态强行灌输给学生。
entries.example_en: The school tried to force-feed its students a narrow ideology.

entries.definition_en: an act in baseball where a fielder catches a ball to stop a runner from reaching a base safely.
entries.example_cn: 游击手完成了一次精彩的封杀，结束了这一局。
entries.example_en: The shortstop made a great force-out to end the inning.

entries.definition_en: obtained or produced by force
entries.example_cn: 囚犯被迫从事强制劳动。
entries.example_en: The prisoners were subjected to forced labor.

entries.definition_en: compelled to do something against one's will
entries.example_cn: 由于罢工，工人们被迫停止生产。
entries.example_en: The workers were forced to stop production due to the strike.

entries.definition_en: made necessary by an unexpected situation or emergency
entries.example_cn: 由于道路封闭，我们不得不绕道而行。
entries.example_en: We had to take a forced detour because of the road closure.

entries.definition_en: lacking spontaneity; not natural
entries.example_cn: 她的笑声听起来不自然且勉强。
entries.example_en: Her laughter sounded forced and unnatural.

entries.definition_en: having or showing great strength or power, often in a physical way.
entries.example_cn: 强劲的大风把树吹倒了。
entries.example_en: The forceful wind knocked over the trees.

entries.definition_en: expressing opinions or taking action in a strong and determined way.
entries.example_cn: 她有力地反对了这项新政策。
entries.example_en: She made a forceful argument against the new policy.

entries.definition_en: in a way that uses great strength or power
entries.example_cn: 风强力地吹开了门。
entries.example_en: The wind blew the door open forcefully.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being forceful or intense
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨的猛烈程度对沿海城镇造成了严重破坏。
entries.example_en: The forcefulness of the storm caused significant damage to the coastal town.

entries.definition_en: a mixture of finely ground or minced meat and fat, sometimes mixed with other ingredients, served alone or used as stuffing
entries.example_cn: 厨师用松露和蘑菇调制肉馅，把它用作填料。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared forcemeat with truffles and mushrooms to use as a stuffing.

entries.definition_cn: 手术钳；（尤指助产用的）产钳
entries.definition_en: a surgical instrument with two blades or pincers used to grasp, hold, or manipulate objects, especially during childbirth
entries.example_cn: 外科医生用手术钳夹住并固定组织。
entries.example_en: The surgeon used forceps to grasp and hold the tissue.

entries.definition_en: groups of soldiers or military units
entries.example_cn: 军队向边境派遣了特种部队。
entries.example_en: The army sent special forces to the border.

entries.definition_en: groups of people or things that have power or influence
entries.example_cn: 自然力量是强大的。
entries.example_en: The forces of nature are powerful.

entries.definition_en: the musical instruments and voices used in a performance
entries.example_cn: 这部歌剧拥有庞大的歌手和乐手阵容。
entries.example_en: The opera featured large forces of singers and musicians.

entries.definition_en: to push or move someone or something with strength
entries.example_cn: 他用尽全力把门推开。
entries.example_en: He forces the door open with all his might.

entries.definition_en: done by using physical strength to overcome resistance
entries.example_cn: 警察强行闯入大楼以营救人质。
entries.example_en: The police made a forcible entry into the building to rescue the hostages.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that uses force
entries.example_cn: 保安强行打开了门。
entries.example_en: The door was opened forcibly by the security guard.

entries.definition_en: a shallow part of a river or stream where you can cross it on foot or in a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 那条旧路把我们带到了一个可以安全渡河的浅滩。
entries.example_en: The old road led us to a ford where we could cross the river safely.

entries.definition_en: the action of crossing a river or stream by wading or driving through it
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，渡河很危险。
entries.example_en: The ford was dangerous after the heavy rain.

entries.definition_en: to cross a river or stream by walking or driving through the shallow water
entries.example_cn: 我们决定涉水过河，而不是绕远路。
entries.example_en: We decided to ford the stream rather than take the long detour.

entries.definition_en: shallow enough to be crossed by walking, riding an animal, or driving a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 这条河在此处可以涉水而过，让徒步旅行者安全通过。
entries.example_en: The river was fordable at this point, allowing the hikers to cross safely.

entries.definition_en: the act of crossing a river by wading or driving through shallow water
entries.example_cn: 危险的涉水过河需要强流将船推向前方。
entries.example_en: The dangerous fording required a strong current to push the boat forward.

entries.definition_en: near or toward the front of a ship or cockpit
entries.example_cn: 飞行员将飞机向前飞行以避开风暴。
entries.example_en: The pilot flew the plane fore to avoid the storm.

entries.definition_en: situated at or toward the front of a vessel
entries.example_cn: 前舱可以俯瞰开阔的海洋。
entries.example_en: The fore cabin offers a view of the open ocean.

entries.definition_en: the front part of a ship or aircraft
entries.example_cn: 船长站在船的前部观看日出。
entries.example_en: The captain stood in the fore of the ship to watch the sunrise.

entries.definition_en: running parallel with the keel of a boat or ship
entries.example_cn: 船员将沿船首尾方向的帆固定在桅杆上。
entries.example_en: The crew secured the fore-and-aft sail to the mast.

entries.definition_en: a sailing vessel with a fore-and-aft rig
entries.example_cn: 船长驾驶着那艘纵帆船穿过狭窄的航道。
entries.example_en: The captain steered the fore-and-after through the narrow channel.

entries.definition_en: the part of the arm between the elbow and the wrist
entries.example_cn: 他用前臂举起了那个重箱子。
entries.example_en: He lifted the heavy box using his forearm.

entries.definition_en: to arm or prepare in advance
entries.example_cn: 他们预先做好了应对丧亲之痛的心理准备。
entries.example_en: They forearmed themselves against the anxieties of bereavement.

entries.definition_en: an ancestor from whom you are descended
entries.example_cn: 全家人聚集在一起，纪念创立这家企业的祖先。
entries.example_en: The family gathered to honor their forebear who founded the business.

entries.definition_cn: 预示；预告（尤指坏事将要发生）
entries.definition_en: to predict or indicate that something will happen, especially something bad
entries.example_cn: 乌云预示着暴风雨即将来临。
entries.example_en: Dark clouds forebode a storm.

usage.label: literary
usage.pattern: 常用于文学语境，表示预示未来事件

entries.definition_en: a feeling that something bad is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 城市上空笼罩着一层乌云，让人感到不祥的预感。
entries.example_en: A dark cloud hung over the city, creating a sense of foreboding.

entries.definition_en: a sign or feeling that something bad is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 黑猫穿过道路被视为不祥之兆。
entries.example_en: The black cat crossing the path was seen as an ill omen.

entries.definition_en: suggesting that something bad is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 房间里那令人不安的沉默让每个人都感到紧张。
entries.example_en: The foreboding silence in the room made everyone nervous.

entries.definition_cn: 前脑（包括大脑、丘脑和下丘脑）
entries.definition_en: the anterior part of the brain, including the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus
entries.example_cn: 前脑包括大脑、丘脑和下丘脑。
entries.example_en: The forebrain includes the cerebrum, thalamus, and hypothalamus.

entries.definition_en: a prediction about how something (as the weather) will develop
entries.example_cn: 天气预报预测明天有雨。
entries.example_en: The weather forecast predicts rain tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: predict in advance
entries.example_cn: 专家预测明年经济将强劲增长。
entries.example_en: Experts forecast a strong economy next year.

entries.definition_en: judge to be probable
entries.example_cn: 很难确切料想项目何时完成。
entries.example_en: It is hard to forecast exactly when the project will finish.

entries.definition_en: to show or indicate something, often as a sign
entries.example_cn: 乌云预示着暴风雨。
entries.example_en: Dark clouds forecast a storm.

entries.definition_en: someone who predicts what will happen in the future, usually using special knowledge
entries.example_cn: 气象预报员预测周末将有暴雨。
entries.example_en: The weather forecaster predicted heavy rain for the weekend.

entries.definition_cn: 预测或预报的行为；预测过程
entries.definition_en: the act or process of making forecasts or predictions
entries.example_cn: 近年来经济预测的准确性有所提高。
entries.example_en: The accuracy of economic forecasting has improved in recent years.

entries.definition_cn: 商船船头部的船员居住区
entries.definition_en: living quarters consisting of a superstructure in the bow of a merchant ship where the crew is housed
entries.example_cn: 风暴期间，水手们被限制在船头居住区。
entries.example_en: The sailors were confined to the forecastle during the storm.

entries.definition_cn: 使……无法发生；使……成为不可能
entries.definition_en: to prevent something from happening or from being possible
entries.example_cn: 缺乏资金将使启动该项目的任何希望化为泡影。
entries.example_en: The lack of funding will foreclose any chance of launching the project.

entries.definition_cn: （借款人违约后）依法取消赎回权并收回或出售抵押财产
entries.definition_en: to take legal action to repossess or sell mortgaged property after the borrower defaults
entries.example_cn: 业主连续几次未付款后，银行不得不对那所房子启动止赎程序。
entries.example_en: The bank had to foreclose on the house after the owner missed several payments.

entries.definition_cn: 债权人收回违约贷款而接管财产的法律诉讼程序
entries.definition_en: the legal process by which a creditor takes possession of property to recover a loan that is in default
entries.example_cn: 银行对房主的财产启动了止赎程序。
entries.example_en: The bank initiated foreclosure proceedings on the homeowner's property.

entries.definition_cn: 建筑物或建筑群的外院或前庭
entries.definition_en: the outer or front area of a building or group of buildings
entries.example_cn: 汽车停在酒店的前庭里。
entries.example_en: Cars were parked in the forecourt of the hotel.

entries.definition_cn: 船的前甲板；桅杆前方的甲板
entries.definition_en: the forward part of a ship's deck, ahead of the mast
entries.example_cn: 船员们聚集在船首甲板上检查损坏情况。
entries.example_en: The crew gathered on the foredeck to inspect the damage.

entries.definition_en: the founder of a family
entries.example_cn: 根据传说，该部落的家族始祖曾居住在山区。
entries.example_en: According to legend, the forefather of the tribe lived in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: a person from an earlier time who contributed to the tradition shared by a group
entries.example_cn: 我们敬重那位制定了游戏规则的先辈。
entries.example_en: We honor our forefather who established the rules of the game.

entries.definition_en: the finger next to the thumb
entries.example_cn: 他用食指指着地图。
entries.example_en: He pointed at the map with his forefinger.

entries.definition_en: the front foot of a four-legged animal
entries.example_cn: 马抬起前蹄挠耳朵。
entries.example_en: The horse lifted its forefoot to scratch its ear.

entries.definition_en: the leading position in a movement or field
entries.example_cn: 我们公司旨在成为可再生能源领域的领先者。
entries.example_en: Our company aims to be at the forefront of renewable energy.

entries.definition_en: the front part or leading position
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术处于现代科学的前沿。
entries.example_en: The new technology is at the forefront of modern science.

entries.definition_en: do without or cease to hold or adhere to
entries.example_cn: 他决定今天早上放弃喝他平常的咖啡。
entries.example_en: He decided to forego his usual coffee this morning.

entries.definition_cn: 因错误、冒犯或犯罪而失去（某物）或失去（某物）的权利
entries.definition_en: lose (something) or lose the right to (something) by some error, offense, or crime
entries.example_cn: 如果公司违法，可能会失去其税收优惠。
entries.example_en: The company may forego its tax benefits if it violates the law.

entries.definition_cn: 发生在更早的时间；追溯得更远
entries.definition_en: be earlier in time; go back further
entries.example_cn: 战争的事件发生在随后的和平谈判之前。
entries.example_en: The events of the war forego the peace talks that followed.

entries.definition_en: occurring or mentioned before something else, especially earlier in a text
entries.example_cn: 前述几点对你的决定很重要。
entries.example_en: The foregoing points are important for your decision.

entries.definition_en: already decided or certain to happen; inevitable
entries.example_cn: 既定的结论是那支球队会输。
entries.example_en: The foregone conclusion was that the team would lose.

entries.definition_en: the part of a scene that is near the viewer
entries.example_cn: 画作前景中的树木被描绘得非常细致。
entries.example_en: The trees in the foreground of the painting were painted with great detail.

entries.definition_cn: （计算机科学）活动应用程序的窗口
entries.definition_en: (computer science) a window for an active application
entries.example_cn: 您可以在前景窗口和后台窗口之间切换以管理任务。
entries.example_en: You can switch between the foreground and background windows to manage your tasks.

entries.definition_cn: 将某物置于前景；使某事突出
entries.definition_en: to place something in the foreground, physically or metaphorically
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策使气候变化问题在政府的议程中变得突出。
entries.example_en: The new policy has foregrounded the issue of climate change in the government's agenda.

entries.definition_en: a stroke in which the palm of the hand faces the direction of the stroke
entries.example_cn: 她打了一个有力的正手球赢得了这一分。
entries.example_en: She hit a powerful forehand that won the point.

entries.definition_en: describing a stroke made with the palm facing the direction of the stroke
entries.example_cn: 教练纠正了他的正手握拍方式以提高控制力。
entries.example_en: The coach corrected his forehand grip to improve his control.

entries.definition_en: the part of the face above the eyes
entries.example_cn: 她在前额上戴了一条发带。
entries.example_en: She wore a headband across her forehead.

entries.definition_en: the large cranial bone forming the front part of the cranium
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了患者额骨的骨折情况。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the fracture in the patient's forehead bone.

entries.definition_cn: 与别国事务有关的；外交的
entries.definition_en: of concern to or concerning the affairs of other nations (other than your own)
entries.example_cn: 政府关心外交政策。
entries.example_en: The government is concerned about foreign policy.

entries.definition_cn: 来自或具有其他地方的特征的
entries.definition_en: relating to or originating in or characteristic of another place or part of the world
entries.example_cn: 她喜爱外国食物。
entries.example_en: She loves foreign food.

entries.definition_cn: 不属于其所在之物；由外部引入的
entries.definition_en: not belonging to that in which it is contained; introduced from an outside source
entries.example_cn: 外来病毒可能导致这种疾病。
entries.example_en: A foreign virus can cause the disease.

entries.definition_en: not part of, or not arising from, the essential nature of something; introduced from outside
entries.example_cn: 合金中的外来元素使其变脆。
entries.example_en: The foreign element in the alloy made it brittle.

entries.definition_cn: 在国外出生的；出生于现居住国以外的
entries.definition_en: born in a country other than the one where one currently lives.
entries.example_cn: 该调查包含了关于外籍出生人口的问题。
entries.example_en: The survey included questions about the foreign-born population.

entries.definition_cn: 在居住国或拥有公民身份的国家以外出生的人
entries.definition_en: a person born outside the country where they live or hold citizenship
entries.example_cn: 人口普查将外国出生者与本国出生的公民分开统计。
entries.example_en: The census counts the foreign-born separately from native-born citizens.

entries.definition_en: a person who comes from a different country
entries.example_cn: 那个外国人问去火车站怎么走。
entries.example_en: The foreigner asked for directions to the train station.

entries.definition_en: an outsider; someone who is not a member of a particular group
entries.example_cn: 在这个关系紧密的群体中，他觉得自己像个外人。
entries.example_en: In the close-knit group, he felt like a foreigner.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being alien or not native to a place
entries.example_cn: 这门语言的外来性使得新学生难以交流。
entries.example_en: The foreignness of the language made it difficult for the new student to communicate.

entries.definition_cn: 预知；对某事的事先知晓
entries.definition_en: knowledge of something before it happens
entries.example_cn: 他对那场事故有一种奇怪的预知。
entries.example_en: He had a strange foreknowledge of the accident.

entries.definition_cn: 岬角；伸入海中的岩石高地
entries.definition_en: a natural land elevation, especially a rocky one that juts out into the sea
entries.example_cn: 船只在危险的岬附近抛锚。
entries.example_en: The ship anchored near the dangerous foreland.

entries.definition_cn: （板块构造中的）前陆区，即山脉附近沉积侵蚀物质的地带
entries.definition_en: in plate tectonics, the zone adjacent to a mountain chain where eroded material is deposited
entries.example_cn: 大多数前陆褶皱冲断带形成于未变形克拉通与变形更强的内部带之间。
entries.example_en: Most foreland fold and thrust belts form between an undeformed craton and a more intensely deformed inner zone.

entries.definition_en: the forelimb of a quadruped
entries.example_cn: 马抬起前腿向训练师展示它的蹄子。
entries.example_en: The horse lifted its foreleg to show the trainer its hoof.

entries.definition_cn: 前肢（或其他动物中同源的结构，如鳍或翼）
entries.definition_en: the front limb (or the homologous structure in other animals, such as a flipper or wing)
entries.example_cn: 鲸鱼用前肢作为鳍来转向。
entries.example_en: The whale uses its forelimb as a flipper for steering.

entries.definition_en: a lock of hair that grows over the forehead
entries.example_cn: 他向后拨开长长的额发，露出了眼睛。
entries.example_en: He pushed back his long forelock to reveal his eyes clearly.

entries.definition_en: a lock of a horse's mane that grows forward between the ears
entries.example_cn: 驯马师在比赛前仔细梳理了马的额毛。
entries.example_en: The groom carefully brushed the horse's forelock before the race.

entries.definition_en: a person who is in charge of a group of workers
entries.example_cn: 工头命令工人们停下来吃午饭。
entries.example_en: The foreman ordered the workers to stop for lunch.

entries.definition_en: a person who presides over a jury and speaks on its behalf
entries.example_cn: 陪审团主席宣布陪审团已作出裁决。
entries.example_en: The foreman announced that the jury had reached a verdict.

entries.definition_en: the mast located nearest the front of a ship that has two or more masts
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴来临前修理前桅。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to repair the foremast before the storm arrived.

entries.definition_en: ranking above all others
entries.example_cn: 她是该领域的首席专家。
entries.example_en: She is the foremost expert in her field.

entries.definition_cn: 在空间位置上位于所有其他事物之前
entries.definition_en: preceding all others in spatial position
entries.example_cn: 最前排的座位是为贵宾预留的。
entries.example_en: The foremost row of seats was reserved for the VIPs.

entries.definition_cn: 位于最靠近船头的位置
entries.definition_en: situated closest to the bow
entries.example_cn: 船长的舱室位于船的最前端。
entries.example_en: The captain's cabin is located in the foremost part of the ship.

entries.definition_en: before anything else
entries.example_cn: 安全必须是我们心中首要考虑的事情。
entries.example_en: Safety must be foremost in our minds.

entries.definition_en: prominently forward
entries.example_cn: 演讲者向前迈了一步，站在人群的最前面。
entries.example_en: The speaker stepped forward and stood foremost in the crowd.

entries.definition_en: the first part of a person's name, which comes before the family name
entries.example_cn: 请在注册表上写下您的名和姓。
entries.example_en: Please write your forename and surname on the registration form.

entries.definition_en: the period of time from dawn until noon
entries.example_cn: 我们通常在上午结束工作。
entries.example_en: We usually finish our work by the end of the forenoon.

entries.definition_en: used in the investigation and establishment of facts or evidence in a court of law
entries.example_cn: 法医学证据证明了嫌疑人的清白。
entries.example_en: The forensic evidence proved the suspect's innocence.

entries.definition_en: relating to or used in public debate or argument
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家发表了一场精彩的论辩性演讲来捍卫他的政策。
entries.example_en: The politician made a forensic speech to defend his policies.

entries.definition_en: scientific tests or techniques used in the investigation of crimes
entries.example_cn: 警方利用法医科学从犯罪现场确定了嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police used forensics to identify the suspect from the crime scene.

entries.definition_en: decided or arranged to happen in a specific way before it occurs
entries.example_cn: 古老的预言暗示国王的死是神预先注定的。
entries.example_en: The ancient prophecy suggested that the king's death was foreordained by the gods.

entries.definition_en: the front or forward section of something
entries.example_cn: 船的前部在风暴中受损。
entries.example_en: The forepart of the ship was damaged during the storm.

entries.definition_en: the front paw of an animal, which functions like a human hand
entries.example_cn: 猫用它的前爪轻轻拍打玩具老鼠。
entries.example_en: The cat used its forepaw to gently bat the toy mouse.

entries.definition_en: the presiding member of the jury and the one who speaks on their behalf
entries.example_cn: 陪审团主席要求陪审团对裁决进行审议。
entries.example_en: The foreperson asked the jury to deliberate on the verdict.

entries.definition_en: a leader of a work crew
entries.example_cn: 施工开始前，工头给每名工人分配了任务。
entries.example_en: The foreperson assigned each worker a task before construction began.

entries.definition_en: sexual touching and kissing that happens before intercourse
entries.example_cn: 他们在那晚的卧室里进行了一些前戏。
entries.example_en: They spent the evening in the bedroom, engaging in some foreplay.

entries.definition_en: something that precedes and indicates the approach of something or someone
entries.example_cn: 乌云是暴风雨的前兆。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds were a forerunner of a storm.

entries.definition_en: a person who goes before or announces the coming of another
entries.example_cn: 一队侦察员充当主探险队的先遣人员。
entries.example_en: A band of scouts acted as forerunners for the main expedition.

entries.definition_en: anything that precedes something similar in time
entries.example_cn: 第一台电脑是当今智能手机的先行事物。
entries.example_en: The first computer was a forerunner of today's smartphones.

entries.definition_en: the lowest sail located on the front mast of a ship with square sails
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员升起前桅下帆以捕捉晨风。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to raise the foresail to catch the morning wind.

entries.definition_cn: 帆船前桅后方设置的一面纵帆
entries.definition_en: a fore-and-aft sail set on the foremast behind it, on a schooner or similar vessel
entries.example_cn: 这艘纵帆船驶离港口时，在前桅后方升起了前桅纵帆。
entries.example_en: The schooner set its foresail behind the foremast as it left the harbor.

entries.definition_cn: 设置在前桅前方的三角帆
entries.definition_en: a triangular sail set forward of the foremast
entries.example_cn: 船员在前桅前方升起三角帆，以使船身保持平稳。
entries.example_en: The crew set the foresail forward of the foremast to steady the boat.

entries.definition_en: to know or understand something will happen before it actually occurs
entries.example_cn: 很难预见如此草率决定的后果。
entries.example_en: It is difficult to foresee the consequences of such a drastic decision.

entries.definition_en: to imagine a possible situation or outcome in your mind
entries.example_cn: 试着设想你的朋友们会对这个消息做出什么反应。
entries.example_en: Try to foresee how your friends will react to the news.

entries.definition_cn: （过时用法）预先提供；预作准备
entries.definition_en: (obsolete) to provide for something in advance
entries.example_cn: 定居者必须预先为自己提供生活所需的物资。
entries.example_en: The settlers had to foresee means of life for themselves.

entries.definition_en: able to be seen or known in advance
entries.example_cn: 公司的未来前景看起来光明。
entries.example_en: The foreseeable future looks bright for the company.

entries.definition_en: to indicate something, especially a future event, as with a sign or an omen
entries.example_cn: 乌云预示着即将到来的风暴。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds foreshadowed the storm that was coming.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving vague hints about something that will happen later
entries.example_cn: 乌云是后来那场风暴的预兆。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds were a foreshadowing of the storm that arrived later.

entries.definition_cn: 带有预示意味的；隐约预示未来的
entries.definition_en: indistinctly prophetic; giving vague hints of the future
entries.example_cn: 那幅古老的画作带有隐约预示未来的意味，让观看者感到不安。
entries.example_en: The old painting had a foreshadowing quality that unsettled the viewers.

entries.definition_cn: 主震前发生的地震颤动
entries.definition_en: a tremor that occurs before a main earthquake
entries.example_cn: 一次前震震动城市后，居民们被疏散了。
entries.example_en: Residents were evacuated after a foreshock shook the city.

entries.definition_en: the area of the seashore located between the high-water and low-water marks
entries.example_cn: 鸟类经常在潮间带聚集，以捕食裸露的海藻。
entries.example_en: Birds often gather on the foreshore to feed on the exposed seaweed.

entries.definition_en: the quality of planning prudently for the future
entries.example_cn: 该公司的成功归功于其长远的远见。
entries.example_en: The company's success was due to its long-term foresight.

entries.definition_en: the ability to see ahead or know something in advance
entries.example_cn: 他的预见力使他能在风暴来临前做好准备。
entries.example_en: His foresight allowed him to prepare for the storm before it arrived.

entries.definition_en: planning prudently for the future
entries.example_cn: 她富有远见的规划确保了公司在经济衰退中生存下来。
entries.example_en: Her foresighted planning ensured the company survived the economic downturn.

entries.definition_en: a fold of skin covering the tip of the penis
entries.example_cn: 包皮覆盖着未割礼男性的阴茎头。
entries.example_en: The foreskin covers the head of the penis in uncircumcised males.

entries.definition_en: a fold of skin covering the tip of the clitoris
entries.example_cn: 阴蒂包皮保护着阴蒂敏感的尖端。
entries.example_en: The foreskin protects the sensitive tip of the clitoris.

entries.definition_en: a large area densely covered with trees and other plants
entries.example_cn: 我们穿过茂密的森林。
entries.example_en: We walked through the deep forest.

entries.definition_en: land that is covered with trees and shrubs
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子被一片小林地环绕。
entries.example_en: The old house was surrounded by a small forest.

entries.definition_en: to establish a forest on previously unforested land
entries.example_cn: 他们计划在这些贫瘠的山丘上造林。
entries.example_en: They plan to forest the barren hills.

entries.definition_en: to prevent something from happening or arising
entries.example_cn: 这项新法律旨在阻止进一步的环境破坏。
entries.example_en: The new law was designed to forestall further environmental damage.

entries.definition_en: to act before something happens; to deal with something in advance
entries.example_cn: 他提前公布结果，从而预先应对了可能提出的问题。
entries.example_en: He forestalled any questions by announcing the results early.

entries.definition_cn: 预先阻止；先发制人的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of preventing something by anticipating it and dealing with it effectively beforehand
entries.example_cn: 他敏捷的思维使他先发制人，在危机升级前将其化解。
entries.example_en: His quick thinking involved forestalling the crisis before it escalated.

entries.definition_en: a rope on a sailing ship that runs from the foremast to the deck or bowsprit to control the mast's bending
entries.example_cn: 水手收紧前支索以稳定桅杆。
entries.example_en: The sailor tightened the forestay to stabilize the mast.

entries.definition_en: covered with forest
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者穿过被森林覆盖的山谷。
entries.example_en: The hikers walked through the heavily forested valley.

entries.definition_en: a person trained in the science and practice of forestry
entries.example_cn: 这位林务员检查了树木以评估风暴造成的损害。
entries.example_en: The forester inspected the trees to assess the damage from the storm.

entries.definition_en: the science of planting and caring for forests and managing timber growth
entries.example_cn: 现代林业利用技术监测森林健康状况并规划可持续的木材采伐。
entries.example_en: Modern forestry uses technology to monitor forest health and plan sustainable timber harvesting.

entries.definition_cn: 预尝；对将要发生之事的预先体验或预示
entries.definition_en: a taste or experience of something beforehand
entries.example_cn: 这道开胃菜预示了即将享用的美味大餐。
entries.example_en: The appetizer was a foretaste of the delicious meal to come.

entries.definition_en: to say what will happen in the future
entries.example_cn: 古代文献经常预言帝国的兴衰。
entries.example_en: Ancient texts often foretell the rise and fall of empires.

entries.definition_en: to be a sign or omen of something that will happen
entries.example_cn: 乌云似乎预示着暴风雨即将来临。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds seemed to foretell a storm.

entries.definition_en: to show or suggest something by a sign
entries.example_cn: 那奇怪的噪音预示着前面的麻烦。
entries.example_en: The strange noise foretold trouble ahead.

entries.definition_en: a statement made about what will happen in the future
entries.example_cn: 这部古籍包含了一个关于王国最终覆灭的预言。
entries.example_en: The ancient text contains a foretelling of the kingdom's eventual fall.

entries.definition_en: the ability or practice of predicting the future through supernatural means
entries.example_cn: 村民们相信牧师拥有预知未来的天赋。
entries.example_en: The villagers believed the priest possessed the gift of foretelling.

entries.definition_en: planning or plotting in advance of acting
entries.example_cn: 项目的成功归功于周密的预先谋划和准备。
entries.example_en: The success of the project was due to careful forethought and preparation.

entries.definition_cn: 为避免伤害或危险而作的谨慎预见
entries.definition_en: judicious anticipation intended to avoid harm or danger
entries.example_cn: 他的事先谋划帮助他避开了陷阱。
entries.example_en: His forethought helped him avoid the trap.

entries.definition_en: a platform located at the top of the front mast of a ship
entries.example_cn: 瞭望员爬上船首桅顶，扫描地平线以寻找其他船只。
entries.example_en: The lookout climbed to the foretop to scan the horizon for other vessels.

entries.definition_cn: 马耳朵之间向前生长的一绺鬃毛
entries.definition_en: a lock of a horse's mane that grows forward between the ears
entries.example_cn: 马夫在比赛前仔细修剪了赛马的耳前鬃毛。
entries.example_en: The groom carefully trimmed the foretop of the racehorse before the competition.

entries.definition_en: for an unlimited amount of time
entries.example_cn: 我会永远爱你。
entries.example_en: I will love you forever.

entries.definition_en: for a very long time
entries.example_cn: 我已经等了很久。
entries.example_en: I've been waiting forever.

entries.definition_en: always; every time
entries.example_cn: 他总是丢钥匙。
entries.example_en: He is forever losing his keys.

entries.definition_en: forever; at all times in the future
entries.example_cn: 他们发誓从此以后永远是朋友。
entries.example_en: They promised to be friends forevermore.

entries.definition_en: to give a warning before something happens
entries.example_cn: 路标预先警告司机前方道路结冰。
entries.example_en: The signs forewarned drivers of the icy road ahead.

entries.definition_en: an early alert or notice about a future event
entries.example_cn: 船长向我们发出了风暴即将来临的预先警告。
entries.example_en: The captain gave us a forewarning of the approaching storm.

entries.definition_en: one of the front pair of wings on an insect that has four wings
entries.example_cn: 这只蝴蝶的前翅上有鲜艳的橙色斑点。
entries.example_en: The butterfly's forewing was patterned with bright orange spots.

entries.definition_en: a woman who is in charge of a group of workers
entries.example_cn: 女工头在轮班开始前检查了安全设备。
entries.example_en: The forewoman inspected the safety equipment before the shift began.

entries.definition_en: a woman who serves as the foreperson of a jury
entries.example_cn: 女陪审团主席宣读了陪审团的一致裁决。
entries.example_en: The forewoman delivered the jury's unanimous verdict.

entries.definition_en: an introductory section preceding the main text of a book or other document, especially one written by someone other than the author
entries.example_cn: 那位著名作家为小说的新版撰写了序言。
entries.example_en: The famous writer contributed a foreword to the new edition of the novel.

entries.definition_cn: 因过错、冒犯或犯罪而丧失（某物）或权利
entries.definition_en: to lose something or the right to something because of a mistake, offense, or crime
entries.example_cn: 如果他酒后驾车，他将失去驾驶执照。
entries.example_en: He will forfeit his license if he drives while intoxicated.

entries.definition_cn: 作为惩罚而被放弃或没收的物品
entries.definition_en: something that is lost or given up as a punishment
entries.example_cn: 该队违反规则后，不得不交出奖杯作为罚没物。
entries.example_en: The team had to hand over its trophy as a forfeit after breaking the rules.

entries.definition_cn: 因过错或错误而需丧失或放弃某物的惩罚
entries.definition_en: a penalty that involves losing or giving up something for a fault or mistake
entries.example_cn: 规则规定，对不道德的行为将处以 forfeit（罚没/取消资格）。
entries.example_en: The rules state that a player receives a forfeit for unsportsmanlike conduct.

entries.definition_cn: 因错误或过失而丧失或放弃某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of losing or surrendering something as a penalty for a mistake or fault
entries.example_cn: 合同的 forfeit（失效/被没收）是违反条款的直接后果。
entries.example_en: The forfeit of the contract was a direct result of the breach of terms.

entries.definition_en: given up as a penalty
entries.example_cn: 被没收的货物已被当局销毁。
entries.example_en: The forfeit goods were destroyed by the authorities.

entries.definition_cn: 因受罚而丧失或放弃之物
entries.definition_en: something that is lost or surrendered as a penalty
entries.example_cn: 法院下令没收他的资产。
entries.example_en: The court ordered the forfeiture of his assets.

entries.definition_cn: 因过错或错误而需丧失或放弃某物的处罚
entries.definition_en: a penalty for a fault or mistake that involves losing or giving up something
entries.example_cn: 由于屡犯违规，他面临执照被吊销的处罚。
entries.example_en: He faced the forfeiture of his license due to repeated violations.

entries.definition_cn: 因过错、失误或未履行义务等而丧失或放弃某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of losing or surrendering something as a penalty for a mistake or fault or failure to perform etc.
entries.example_cn: 他违反协议后，押金被没收了。
entries.example_en: The forfeiture of his deposit followed his breach of the agreement.

entries.definition_cn: 制作仿制品以欺骗他人
entries.definition_en: make a copy of with the intent to deceive
entries.example_cn: 有人试图伪造合同上的签名。
entries.example_en: Someone tried to forge the signature on the contract.

entries.definition_cn: 通过共同努力建立或创造某物
entries.definition_en: create or form something through concerted effort
entries.example_cn: 尽管存在分歧，他们还是共同建立了牢固的联盟。
entries.example_en: They forged a strong alliance despite their differences.

entries.definition_en: create by hammering
entries.example_cn: 他们用旧金属锻造了一把新剑。
entries.example_en: They forged a new sword from the old metal.

entries.definition_en: move ahead steadily
entries.example_cn: 尽管遇到困难，团队仍稳步前进。
entries.example_en: The team forged ahead despite the difficulties.

entries.definition_cn: 经过脑力劳动提出（想法、计划、解释、理论或原则）
entries.definition_en: come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
entries.example_cn: 她制定了一个巧妙的计划来解决这个问题。
entries.example_en: She forged a brilliant plan to solve the problem.

entries.definition_cn: 通过加热和锤打加工金属的工作场所
entries.definition_en: a workplace where metal is worked by heating and hammering
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂有一个大型锻造车间用于制造工具。
entries.example_en: The factory has a large forge for making tools.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用于在塑形前加热金属的特殊炉灶
entries.definition_en: a furnace consisting of a special hearth where metal is heated before shaping
entries.example_cn: 铁匠在炉子里加热铁块。
entries.example_en: The blacksmith heated the iron in the forge.

entries.definition_cn: 突然加速或充满活力地行动
entries.definition_en: move or act with a sudden increase in speed or energy
entries.example_cn: 汽车在高速公路上疾驰。
entries.example_en: The car forged down the highway.

entries.definition_en: made to look like something else in order to deceive
entries.example_cn: 警方发现支票上的签名是伪造的。
entries.example_en: The police discovered that the signature on the check was forged.

entries.definition_en: a person who illegally makes copies of documents or artworks
entries.example_cn: 警方逮捕了制造假护照的伪造者。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the forger who had created fake passports.

entries.definition_en: a person who forges metal
entries.example_cn: 这名铁匠整天在车间里敲打铁器。
entries.example_en: The forger spent his days hammering iron in the workshop.

entries.definition_en: a copy made to look like the original
entries.example_cn: 博物馆发现了一幅名画的赝品。
entries.example_en: The museum discovered a forgery of the famous painting.

entries.definition_en: the act of falsifying a document with intent to defraud
entries.example_cn: 他因伪造银行支票被捕。
entries.example_en: He was arrested for the forgery of bank checks.

entries.definition_en: dismiss from the mind; stop remembering
entries.example_cn: 我永远不会忘记你的好意。
entries.example_en: I will never forget your kindness.

entries.definition_en: be unable to remember
entries.example_cn: 我无法忘记那个陌生人的脸。
entries.example_en: I cannot forget the face of the stranger.

entries.definition_en: forget to do something
entries.example_cn: 离开时别忘了锁门。
entries.example_en: Don't forget to lock the door when you leave.

entries.definition_en: leave behind unintentionally
entries.example_cn: 我把雨伞落在家里了。
entries.example_en: I forgot my umbrella at home.

entries.definition_en: small perennial herb having bright blue or white flowers
entries.example_cn: 她从花园里摘了一朵勿忘我。
entries.example_en: She picked a forget-me-not from the garden.

entries.definition_en: having a poor memory; tending to forget things easily
entries.example_cn: 她太健忘了，经常把钥匙忘在家里。
entries.example_en: She is so forgetful that she often leaves her keys at home.

entries.definition_en: not paying enough attention; careless
entries.example_cn: 他疏忽了规则，犯了一个错误。
entries.example_en: He was forgetful of the rules and made a mistake.

entries.definition_en: failing to keep something in mind; not remembering
entries.example_cn: 我忘记了我们的约会，结果迟到了。
entries.example_en: I was forgetful of our appointment and arrived late.

entries.definition_en: tendency to forget
entries.example_cn: 他的健忘常常导致错过约会。
entries.example_en: His forgetfulness often leads to missed appointments.

entries.definition_en: failure to remember something; loss of recollection
entries.example_cn: 她忘记了约会，因此错过了它。
entries.example_en: Her forgetfulness of the appointment caused her to miss it.

entries.definition_en: easy to forget
entries.example_cn: 他是小说中一个容易被遗忘的角色。
entries.example_en: He is a forgettable character in the novel.

entries.definition_en: the process of shaping metal by heating it and hammering it
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂专门通过锻造大规模生产汽车零部件。
entries.example_en: The factory specializes in the mass production of car parts through forging.

entries.definition_en: an action or mistake that can easily be excused or forgiven
entries.example_cn: 考虑到任务的复杂性，这是一个可以原谅的错误。
entries.example_en: It was a forgivable error given the complexity of the task.

entries.definition_en: to stop being angry with someone and not blame them for a mistake
entries.example_cn: 我无法原谅他对我撒谎。
entries.example_en: I cannot forgive him for lying to me.

entries.definition_en: to free someone from the obligation to pay a debt
entries.example_cn: 银行决定免除剩余的余额。
entries.example_en: The bank decided to forgive the remaining balance.

entries.definition_en: compassionate feelings that support a willingness to forgive
entries.example_cn: 她向背叛她的朋友展现了极大的宽恕。
entries.example_en: She showed great forgiveness toward her friend who had betrayed her.

entries.definition_en: the act of excusing a mistake or offense
entries.example_cn: 经理决定原谅这一举动令人意外。
entries.example_en: The manager's decision to grant forgiveness was unexpected.

entries.definition_en: a person who pardons someone for a fault or offense
entries.example_cn: 宽恕者选择放下过去的错误。
entries.example_en: The forgiver chose to let go of the past mistake.

entries.definition_en: inclined or able to forgive and show mercy
entries.example_cn: 那是一个宽恕的环境，错误被忽略了。
entries.example_en: It was a forgiving environment where mistakes were overlooked.

entries.definition_cn: 容错的；不易因错误而造成严重后果的
entries.definition_en: designed to tolerate mistakes or minimize their harmful effects
entries.example_cn: 这款软件的界面容错性很好，用户可以撤销错误操作。
entries.example_en: The software has a forgiving interface that lets users undo mistakes.

entries.definition_en: to choose not to have or do something
entries.example_cn: 他们决定放弃甜点以节省热量。
entries.example_en: They decided to forgo dessert to save calories.

entries.definition_en: to lose something or the right to something due to an error or crime
entries.example_cn: 由于他的行为，他不得不丧失继承权。
entries.example_en: He had to forgo his inheritance because of his actions.

entries.definition_en: to be earlier in time or go back further
entries.example_cn: 该条约的签署旨在取代之前的协议。
entries.example_en: The treaty was signed to forgo previous agreements.

entries.definition_cn: 被遗忘的；不再被记得的
entries.definition_en: no longer remembered
entries.example_cn: 被遗忘的计划细节导致项目失败。
entries.example_en: The forgotten details of the plan caused the project to fail.

entries.definition_en: the basic unit of money in Hungary
entries.example_cn: 这顿饭的价格是三百福林。
entries.example_en: The price of the meal was three hundred forints.

entries.definition_en: a utensil with two or more prongs, used for serving or eating food
