entries.definition_en: to lose one's nerve or become panicked
entries.example_cn: 看到蜘蛛时别惊慌失措。
entries.example_en: Don't freak out when you see the spider.

entries.definition_en: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.example_cn: 她在正式晚宴上穿了一套极不寻常的服装。
entries.example_en: She wore a freakish outfit to the formal dinner.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of a freak; strange or abnormal
entries.example_cn: 这种动物的怪异行为让研究人员感到困惑。
entries.example_en: The freakish behavior of the animal puzzled the researchers.

entries.definition_en: liable to change frequently or unpredictably
entries.example_cn: 最近天气变化无常，几小时内就从炎热转为寒冷。
entries.example_en: The weather has been freakish lately, swinging from heat to cold in hours.

entries.definition_en: in an unpredictable way
entries.example_cn: 天气变化无常，几分钟内就从晴天变成了暴风雨。
entries.example_en: The weather changed freakishly, turning from sunny to stormy in minutes.

entries.definition_en: a quality of being strangely abnormal
entries.example_cn: 这个生物外貌的怪诞性让探险者们大吃一惊。
entries.example_en: The freakishness of the creature's appearance startled the explorers.

entries.definition_cn: 怪异的；令人有点害怕的
entries.definition_en: strange and somewhat frightening
entries.example_cn: 地下室里发出的怪异噪音让我整夜睡不着。
entries.example_en: The freaky noises in the basement kept me awake all night.

usage.label: slang
usage.pattern: informal adjective meaning odd or frightening

entries.definition_en: conspicuously or grossly unconventional or unusual
entries.example_cn: 他的音乐品味极其独特，偏爱极端金属而非流行乐。
entries.example_en: He has a freaky taste in music, preferring extreme metal to pop.

entries.definition_en: a small brownish spot (of the pigment melanin) on the skin
entries.example_cn: 她的鼻子上有几颗雀斑。
entries.example_en: She has a few freckles on her nose.

entries.definition_en: become freckled
entries.example_cn: 他在太阳下待太久后，皮肤开始长出雀斑。
entries.example_en: His skin began to freckle after spending too much time in the sun.

entries.definition_en: mark with freckles
entries.example_cn: 阳光使她的脸颊布满了雀斑。
entries.example_en: The sun freckled her cheeks.

entries.definition_en: having small brown spots on the skin
entries.example_cn: 她因在太阳下待得太久而鼻梁上长满了雀斑。
entries.example_en: She has a freckled nose from spending too much time in the sun.

entries.definition_en: not limited or under restraint
entries.example_cn: 你想走随时可以走。
entries.example_en: You are free to leave whenever you want.

entries.definition_en: costing nothing
entries.example_cn: 博物馆入场是免费的。
entries.example_en: The museum entry is free.

entries.definition_en: grant freedom to someone
entries.example_cn: 军队释放了囚犯。
entries.example_en: The army freed the prisoners.

entries.definition_en: relieve someone from something
entries.example_cn: 这种药使他摆脱了疼痛。
entries.example_en: The medicine freed him from pain.

entries.definition_en: without restraint
entries.example_cn: 她自由自在地歌唱。
entries.example_en: She sang free and easy.

entries.definition_en: people who are not slaves or prisoners
entries.example_cn: 自由人们庆祝他们的独立。
entries.example_en: The free people celebrated their independence.

entries.definition_en: remove or force out from a position
entries.example_cn: 这个工具清除了卡住的螺栓。
entries.example_en: The tool freed the stuck bolt.

entries.definition_en: not chemically bound or fixed
entries.example_cn: 电子可以自由移动。
entries.example_en: The electrons are free to move.

entries.definition_en: natural and unstudied
entries.example_cn: 她的穿衣风格自然不做作。
entries.example_en: She has a free-and-easy style of dress.

entries.definition_en: able to fly through the air (as a bird)
entries.example_cn: 那些能自由飞翔的鸟儿在湖面上盘旋。
entries.example_en: The free-flying birds circled above the lake.

entries.definition_en: a chaotic situation or fight with few or no rules or controls
entries.example_cn: 规则被取消后，比赛变成了一场混战。
entries.example_en: When the rules were abandoned, the contest became a free-for-all.

entries.definition_en: someone who eats and drinks with excessive freedom
entries.example_cn: 假期过后，他觉得自己像个贪吃贪饮者，毫无节制地享受每一顿饭。
entries.example_en: After the holiday, he felt like a free-liver, enjoying every meal without restraint.

entries.definition_en: not parasitic on another organism
entries.example_cn: 许多昆虫是自由生活的，而另一些则寄生在植物上。
entries.example_en: Many insects are free-living, while others live as parasites on plants.

entries.definition_en: kept outside in fields to eat grass instead of being kept indoors
entries.example_cn: 我们买了来自放养鸡的鸡蛋。
entries.example_en: We bought eggs from free-range chickens.

entries.definition_cn: （指育儿方式）允许孩子独自外出探索的
entries.definition_en: relating to a parenting style in which children are allowed to go out and explore independently
entries.example_cn: 他们选择了放手式育儿方式，允许儿子独自探索附近的街区。
entries.example_en: They chose a free-range parenting approach and allowed their son to explore the neighborhood alone.

entries.definition_cn: 可以在户外无人看管地自由活动的
entries.definition_en: allowed to move around outdoors without supervision
entries.example_cn: 这对父母让他们的孩子独自步行上学，自由地在户外活动。
entries.example_en: The parents let their free-range children walk to school by themselves.

entries.definition_en: speaking directly without being subtle or avoiding the truth
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上直言不讳地谈论了自己的错误。
entries.example_en: He was free-spoken about his mistakes during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: (of animals) able to swim freely; not attached to a surface
entries.example_cn: 水母的自由游动的幼虫随水流漂浮。
entries.example_en: The free-swimming larvae of the jellyfish drift with the current.

entries.definition_en: not willing to accept authority or religious dogma
entries.example_cn: 她是一个不盲从传统信念的人。
entries.example_en: She is a free-thinking person who questions traditional beliefs.

entries.definition_en: an item given for free, often as part of a promotion
entries.example_cn: 顾客在购买新款咖啡机时获赠了一份赠品。
entries.example_en: Customers received a freebee with their purchase of the new coffee maker.

entries.definition_en: something that is free, usually provided as part of a promotional scheme
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志每期订阅都附赠一份免费赠品。
entries.example_en: The magazine included a freebie with every subscription.

entries.definition_en: a person who takes goods or money by force, especially during a war
entries.example_cn: 这些海盗是劫掠船只的强盗。
entries.example_en: The pirates were freebooters who raided ships along the coast.

entries.definition_en: born to parents who are free
entries.example_cn: 作为自由出生的公民，他有权参加选举投票。
entries.example_en: As a freeborn citizen, he had the right to vote in the election.

entries.definition_en: a man who has been freed from slavery
entries.example_cn: 这位获释奴隶在战争结束后回到了家人身边。
entries.example_en: The freedman returned to his family after the war.

entries.definition_cn: 自由；不受外部强制约束而行动、说话或思考的能力
entries.definition_en: the condition of being free; the power to act or speak or think without externally imposed restraints
entries.example_cn: 他们为自由和独立而战。
entries.example_en: They fought for their freedom and independence.

entries.definition_en: immunity from an obligation or duty
entries.example_cn: 这项豁免使她免于陪审员义务。
entries.example_en: The exemption gave her freedom from jury duty.

entries.definition_en: created by hand without the use of mechanical tools or guides
entries.example_cn: 她徒手画了一幅美丽的素描。
entries.example_en: She drew a beautiful sketch freehand.

entries.definition_en: done by hand without using machines or tools
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家完全手工绘制了这幅肖像，没有使用任何模板。
entries.example_en: The artist painted the portrait freehanded, without any stencils.

entries.definition_en: generous or openhanded
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构收到了一笔来自社区的慷慨捐赠。
entries.example_en: The charity received a freehanded donation from the community.

entries.definition_en: the tenure system where land is held in fee simple or for life
entries.example_cn: 这栋房子是在永久产权制度下建造的。
entries.example_en: The house was built under the freehold tenure system.

entries.definition_en: an estate owned in fee simple or for life
entries.example_cn: 他们在乡下购买了一处大型永久产权地产。
entries.example_en: They purchased a large freehold property in the countryside.

entries.definition_en: a person who owns the freehold of a property
entries.example_cn: 作为自由产权人，他有权随时出售土地。
entries.example_en: As a freeholder, he has the right to sell the land whenever he wishes.

entries.definition_en: the act of setting someone or something free
entries.example_cn: 囚犯的获释是一重大事件。
entries.example_en: The freeing of the prisoners was a major event.

entries.definition_en: to work independently on temporary contracts rather than for a long-term employer
entries.example_cn: 许多平面设计师选择自由职业以获得更灵活的工作时间。
entries.example_en: Many graphic designers choose to freelance to have more flexible hours.

entries.definition_en: working for yourself without a permanent employer
entries.example_cn: 他是一位周游世界的自由摄影师。
entries.example_en: He is a freelance photographer who travels the world.

entries.definition_en: serving as a mercenary
entries.example_cn: 这些雇佣兵受雇为当地军阀作战。
entries.example_en: The mercenaries were hired to fight as freelance soldiers for the local warlord.

entries.definition_en: a writer or artist who works for different employers without a long-term contract
entries.example_cn: 她在离开报社工作后决定成为一名自由记者。
entries.example_en: She decided to become a freelance journalist after leaving her newspaper job.

entries.definition_en: a writer or artist who sells services to different employers without a long-term contract
entries.example_cn: 作为一名自由职业者，她同时为几位客户服务。
entries.example_en: As a freelancer, she works for several clients at once.

entries.definition_en: to live off someone's generosity without paying
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在旅行中蹭朋友们的款待。
entries.example_en: They decided to freeload on their friends' hospitality during the trip.

entries.definition_en: a person who lives off the kindness or generosity of others without paying for what they use
entries.example_cn: 房东抱怨那个从不支付自己那份房租的白吃白喝者。
entries.example_en: The landlord complained about the freeloader who never paid his share of the rent.

entries.definition_en: in a free manner; without restriction
entries.example_cn: 鸟儿在天空中自由飞翔。
entries.example_en: The birds flew freely across the sky.

entries.definition_en: a man who is not a slave or serf
entries.example_cn: 在中世纪，自由民拥有拥有土地和自由贸易的权利。
entries.example_en: In medieval times, a freeman had the right to own land and trade freely.

entries.definition_en: a plant valued for its clusters of fragrant, tubular flowers that curve to one side
entries.example_cn: 她为婚礼餐桌布置了一束小苍兰。
entries.example_en: She arranged a bouquet of freesias for the wedding table.

entries.definition_en: standing alone; not attached to or supported by anything else
entries.example_cn: 那个独立的书架被放在房间的角落里。
entries.example_en: The freestanding bookshelf was placed in the corner of the room.

entries.definition_cn: （计算机程序）可直接在硬件上运行、无需操作系统管理的
entries.definition_en: of a computer program, running directly on the hardware without being managed by an operating system
entries.example_cn: 这个独立运行的程序无需操作系统即可直接在计算机硬件上运行。
entries.example_en: This freestanding program runs directly on the computer's hardware without an operating system.

entries.definition_en: a fruit whose flesh separates easily from the pit
entries.example_cn: 油桃是一种容易剥皮的离核果。
entries.example_en: Nectarines are a type of freestone that is easy to peel.

entries.definition_en: a swimming race where swimmers can choose any stroke
entries.example_cn: 她在自由泳项目中赢得了金牌。
entries.example_en: She won the gold medal in the freestyle event.

entries.definition_en: a form of rapping where lyrics are improvised while performing
entries.example_cn: 观众非常喜欢开放麦之夜的即兴说唱表演。
entries.example_en: The crowd loved the freestyling at the open mic night.

entries.definition_cn: 自由思想者；通过理性探究形成观点、尤指拒绝宗教教条的人
entries.definition_en: a person who forms opinions through reason and rational inquiry, especially one who rejects religious dogma
entries.example_cn: 作为一名自由思想者，他质疑所有宗教教条。
entries.example_en: As a freethinker, he questioned all religious dogmas.

entries.definition_cn: 自由思想；独立思考，尤指不受宗教或其他权威约束
entries.definition_en: the practice or principles of thinking independently, especially free from religious or other authority
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家捍卫自由思想，反对宗教教条。
entries.example_en: The philosopher defended freethinking against religious dogma.

entries.definition_en: computer software that is provided free of charge to users
entries.example_cn: 许多用户更喜欢免费软件，因为它不需要订阅费。
entries.example_en: Many users prefer freeware because it does not require a subscription fee.

entries.definition_cn: （美国）设有立体交叉、供高速行驶的公路
entries.definition_en: a highway with grade-separated crossings, designed for high-speed traffic
entries.example_cn: 我们走高速公路以避开城市交通。
entries.example_en: We took the freeway to avoid the city traffic.

entries.definition_cn: 自由随意地生活或行动；放任自流
entries.definition_en: to live or act freely, without constraints or a plan
entries.example_cn: 他决定在大学期间没有计划地放任自流。
entries.example_en: He decided to freewheel through his college years without a plan.

entries.definition_en: to move a vehicle by coasting using the freewheel
entries.example_cn: 我们顺着山坡滑行下去。
entries.example_en: We freewheeled down the hill.

entries.definition_cn: 飞轮；（自行车等的）自由轮
entries.definition_en: a device on a bicycle wheel that allows it to turn freely without driving the pedals
entries.example_cn: 这个自转齿轮让自行车能顺着山坡滑行。
entries.example_en: The freewheel lets the bike coast down the hill.

entries.definition_en: acting without rules or restrictions
entries.example_cn: 该公司对创新采取了无拘无束的方法，鼓励员工承担风险。
entries.example_en: The company adopted a freewheeling approach to innovation, encouraging employees to take risks.

entries.definition_en: cheerfully irresponsible
entries.example_cn: 他们轻率而快活的生活方式导致后来出现了财务困难。
entries.example_en: Their freewheeling lifestyle led to financial difficulties later in life.

entries.definition_en: done voluntarily or of one's own accord
entries.example_cn: 她自愿向慈善机构捐款。
entries.example_en: She made a freewill donation to the charity.

entries.definition_en: a female person who is not a serf or a slave
entries.example_cn: 这位自由妇女在王国里自由地旅行。
entries.example_en: The freewoman traveled freely across the kingdom.

entries.definition_en: to change from a liquid to ice
entries.example_cn: 池塘里的水今晚会结冰。
entries.example_en: The water in the pond will freeze tonight.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to become ice
entries.example_cn: 这台机器设计用于快速冷冻食物。
entries.example_en: The machine is designed to freeze food quickly.

entries.definition_en: to stop moving or become unable to move
entries.example_cn: 当她听到身后的巨大声响时，她僵住了。
entries.example_en: She froze when she heard the loud noise behind her.

entries.definition_en: reach or fall below the temperature at which water turns to ice
entries.example_cn: 这里每年冬天有三个月会降到冰点以下。
entries.example_en: It freezes here for three months every winter.

entries.definition_en: the act of fixing prices or wages at a specific level
entries.example_cn: 政府宣布冻结租金上涨。
entries.example_en: The government announced a freeze on rent increases.

entries.definition_en: weather that is cold enough to cause things to turn to ice
entries.example_cn: 由于严寒，我们不得不待在室内。
entries.example_en: We had to stay indoors because of the severe freeze.

entries.definition_en: the process of removing heat to turn a liquid into a solid
entries.example_cn: 突如其来的霜冻损害了山谷里的庄稼。
entries.example_en: The sudden freeze damaged the crops in the valley.

entries.definition_en: a temporary stop in progress or movement
entries.example_cn: 在新提案提出后，谈判陷入了停顿。
entries.example_en: There was a freeze in negotiations after the new proposal was presented.

entries.definition_en: preserved by freezing and drying in a vacuum
entries.example_cn: 我们买了真空冷冻干燥的咖啡放在背包里。
entries.example_en: We bought freeze-dried coffee to keep in our backpack.

entries.definition_en: used of tissue or blood or serum or other biological substances; dried by freezing in a high vacuum
entries.example_cn: 实验室将冷冻干燥的血清储存起来以备将来使用。
entries.example_en: The laboratory stored the freeze-dried serum for future use.

entries.definition_en: to preserve something by freezing it and then drying it in a vacuum
entries.example_cn: 科学家冷冻干燥血液样本以保持其长期稳定。
entries.example_en: Scientists freeze-dry blood samples to keep them stable for long-term storage.

entries.definition_en: a preservation method where frozen material is dried in a vacuum to sublimate ice
entries.example_cn: 冷冻干燥法常用于保存食品和药品，且不会破坏其结构。
entries.example_en: Freeze-drying is commonly used to preserve food and pharmaceuticals without destroying their structure.

entries.definition_cn: 用于在0°C（32°F）以下储存食物或其他易腐物品的电器或房间
entries.definition_en: an appliance or room used to store food or other perishable items at temperatures below 0°C (32°F)
entries.example_cn: 请在肉变质前把它放进冷冻柜。
entries.example_en: Please put the meat in the freezer before it spoils.

entries.definition_en: the withdrawal of heat to change something from a liquid to a solid
entries.example_cn: 水凝固成冰是一种物理变化。
entries.example_en: The freezing of water into ice is a physical change.

entries.definition_en: goods that are transported by a large vehicle
entries.example_cn: 这艘船装满了来自世界各地的货物。
entries.example_en: The ship was loaded with freight from all over the world.

entries.definition_en: the transportation of goods, especially by a commercial carrier
entries.example_cn: 这个包裹通过货运而不是快递发送。
entries.example_en: The package was sent by freight rather than by express delivery.

entries.definition_en: the money charged for transporting something by a common carrier
entries.example_cn: 重型机械的运费非常高。
entries.example_en: The cost of freight for the heavy machinery was very high.

entries.definition_en: to transport goods commercially as cargo
entries.example_cn: 公司决定通过海运运输设备。
entries.example_en: The company decided to freight the equipment by sea.

entries.definition_en: to load with goods for transportation
entries.example_cn: 工人们用苹果箱装满了卡车。
entries.example_en: Workers freighted the trucks with boxes of apples.

entries.definition_en: a large ship used to carry cargo
entries.example_cn: 那艘货船停靠在港口卸货。
entries.example_en: The freighter docked at the port to unload its containers.

entries.definition_cn: 疯狂忙乱的；精力或活动极其旺盛的
entries.definition_en: frenzied and frantic; characterized by extreme energy or activity
entries.example_cn: 这座城市疯狂忙乱的节奏让她感到不堪重负。
entries.example_en: The frenetic pace of the city left her feeling overwhelmed.

entries.definition_en: in a very excited, agitated, or frantic way
entries.example_cn: 当球队攻入制胜一球时，人群疯狂地欢呼起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd cheered frenetically when the team scored the winning goal.

entries.definition_en: excessively agitated; distraught with fear or other violent emotion
entries.example_cn: 听到坏消息后，她看起来极度激动。
entries.example_en: She looked frenzied after hearing the bad news.

entries.definition_en: affected with or marked by frenzy or mania uncontrolled by reason
entries.example_cn: 音乐会开始时，人群变得狂乱起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd became frenzied when the concert started.

entries.definition_en: in a frenzied manner
entries.example_cn: 当球队攻入制胜球时，人群疯狂地欢呼起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd cheered frenziedly when the team scored the winning goal.

entries.definition_en: state of violent mental agitation
entries.example_cn: 当乐队登台时，人群陷入了狂乱。
entries.example_en: The crowd was in a frenzy when the band took the stage.

entries.definition_en: the number of times something happens in a given period
entries.example_cn: 这个地区发生地震的频率非常低。
entries.example_en: The frequency of earthquakes in this region is very low.

entries.definition_cn: 某统计类别中的观测数占观测总数的比例（相对频数）
entries.definition_en: the proportion of observations in a category relative to the total number of observations
entries.example_cn: 调查结果中红色的比率高于预期。
entries.example_en: The frequency of the red color in the survey results was higher than expected.

entries.definition_en: the count of items belonging to a specific statistical category
entries.example_cn: 通过考试的学生频数被记录在表中。
entries.example_en: The frequency of students who passed the exam was recorded in the table.

entries.definition_en: happening often or at short intervals
entries.example_cn: 频繁的雷暴使得出行变得困难。
entries.example_en: The frequent thunderstorms made it difficult to travel.

entries.definition_en: frequently encountered
entries.example_cn: 夏季，游客在这座城市很常见。
entries.example_en: Tourists are a frequent sight in this city during summer.

entries.definition_en: to visit a place regularly
entries.example_cn: 他过去常常下班后每晚去图书馆。
entries.example_en: He used to frequent the library every evening after work.

entries.definition_cn: 常去（某商店或商家）光顾
entries.definition_en: to be a regular customer of a shop or business
entries.example_cn: 她决定常去街角那家新开的咖啡店。
entries.example_en: She decided to frequent the new coffee shop on the corner.

entries.definition_cn: 表示反复动作的一类未完成体动词
entries.definition_en: a verb in a subclass of imperfective verbs that denotes repeated action
entries.example_cn: 在芬兰语中，反复动词是一种表示反复动作的未完成体动词。
entries.example_en: In Finnish, a frequentative is an imperfective verb that denotes repeated action.

entries.definition_en: a regular customer who visits a place often
entries.example_cn: 咖啡师总是微笑着迎接这位常客，并知道他的常点饮品。
entries.example_en: The barista always greets the frequenter with a smile and knows his usual order.

entries.definition_en: often; many times at short intervals.
entries.example_cn: 她经常在周末去看望她的祖母。
entries.example_en: She frequently visits her grandmother on weekends.

entries.definition_en: a mural painting done with watercolors on wet plaster
entries.example_cn: 该博物馆收藏了一幅著名的文艺复兴时期湿壁画。
entries.example_en: The museum houses a famous fresco from the Renaissance.

entries.definition_en: a durable method of painting on a wall using watercolors on wet plaster
entries.example_cn: 湿壁画技法使色彩能够保存数百年。
entries.example_en: The fresco technique allows the colors to last for centuries.

entries.definition_en: to paint onto wet plaster on a wall
entries.example_cn: 艺术家绘制了大厅的整个天花板湿壁画。
entries.example_en: The artist frescoed the entire ceiling of the hall.

entries.definition_en: recently made, produced, or harvested
entries.example_cn: 我更喜欢新鲜面包，而不是不新鲜的面包。
entries.example_en: I prefer fresh bread to stale bread.

entries.definition_en: not canned or otherwise preserved
entries.example_cn: 我们从市场买了新鲜的蔬菜。
entries.example_en: We bought fresh vegetables from the market.

entries.definition_cn: 充满活力的；令人精神振奋的
entries.definition_en: imparting vitality and energy
entries.example_cn: 清新的空气让每个人都感到充满活力。
entries.example_en: The fresh air made everyone feel energetic.

entries.definition_en: not containing or composed of salt water
entries.example_cn: 淡水对于饮用至关重要。
entries.example_en: Fresh water is essential for drinking.

entries.definition_en: original and of a kind not seen before
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家为画作提出了一个新颖的想法。
entries.example_en: The artist presented a fresh idea for the painting.

entries.definition_en: very recently
entries.example_cn: 她刚从机场到达。
entries.example_en: She arrived fresh from the airport.

entries.definition_en: (of a cycle) beginning or occurring again
entries.example_cn: 新一轮的谈判已经开始了。
entries.example_en: The fresh round of negotiations has begun.

entries.definition_en: having recently calved and therefore able to give milk
entries.example_cn: 刚产犊的母牛将为小牛提供牛奶。
entries.example_en: The fresh cow will provide milk for the calves.

entries.definition_en: make something cooler or fresher
entries.example_cn: 一阵凉风使炎热的房间凉爽起来。
entries.example_en: A cool breeze freshened the hot room.

entries.definition_en: become refreshed or invigorated
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，他去游泳恢复体力。
entries.example_en: He went for a swim to freshen up after the long hike.

entries.definition_cn: 使某物恢复新鲜；使焕然一新
entries.definition_en: to make something fresh again
entries.example_cn: 她修剪花茎并换水，让花恢复了鲜艳。
entries.example_en: She freshened the flowers by trimming the stems and changing the water.

entries.definition_en: anything that freshens
entries.example_cn: 她使用织物清新剂去掉了沙发的异味。
entries.example_en: She used a fabric freshener to remove the smell from the sofa.

entries.definition_en: a first-year undergraduate
entries.example_cn: 大学为所有大一新生组织了一场欢迎活动。
entries.example_en: The university organized a welcome event for all freshers.

entries.definition_cn: 由暴雨或春季融雪引起的洪水
entries.definition_en: a flood caused by heavy rain or a spring thaw
entries.example_cn: 突如其来的洪水导致河水漫出了河岸。
entries.example_en: The sudden freshet caused the river to overflow its banks.

entries.definition_en: very recently
entries.example_cn: 她最近当选为新总统。
entries.example_en: She was freshly elected as the new president.

entries.definition_en: in an impudent or impertinent manner
entries.example_cn: 他无礼地提出了那个问题，无视老师的警告。
entries.example_en: He asked the question freshly, ignoring the teacher's warning.

entries.definition_en: a university student in their first year of study
entries.example_cn: 这名大一新生很难适应大学严格的日程安排。
entries.example_en: The freshman struggled to adjust to the rigorous university schedule.

entries.definition_en: a new participant in an activity or organization
entries.example_cn: 团队欢迎这位新成员加入项目。
entries.example_en: The team welcomed the freshman to the project.

entries.definition_en: relating to a person in their first year of an experience, such as high school or college
entries.example_cn: 作为俱乐部的新手，他渴望学习规则。
entries.example_en: As a freshman in the club, he was eager to learn the rules.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being pure and fresh, not stale or deteriorated
entries.example_cn: 牛奶放在外面后失去了新鲜度。
entries.example_en: The milk has lost its freshness after being left out.

entries.definition_en: originality that is refreshingly new
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家因其风格的新颖独创性而受到赞誉。
entries.example_en: The artist's work is praised for its freshness of style.

entries.definition_en: originality by virtue of being new and surprising
entries.example_cn: 小说的新奇独特性立刻吸引了读者的注意。
entries.example_en: The novel's freshness caught the readers' attention immediately.

entries.definition_en: a state of being alert and refreshed
entries.example_cn: 短途散步让他恢复了精神。
entries.example_en: A short walk restored his freshness.

entries.definition_en: the trait of being rude and impertinent
entries.example_cn: 他对老板的无礼态度很不恰当。
entries.example_en: His freshness with the boss was inappropriate.

entries.definition_en: water that is not salty
entries.example_cn: 淡水湖里的鱼与海洋里的鱼不同。
entries.example_en: The fish in the freshwater lake are different from those in the ocean.

entries.definition_en: to worry excessively or unnecessarily
entries.example_cn: 别再为那些你无法控制的事情担忧了。
entries.example_en: Stop fretting about things you cannot control.

entries.definition_en: to become or remain agitated or irritated
entries.example_cn: 噪音让他整个晚上都很烦躁。
entries.example_en: The noise made him fret all evening.

entries.definition_en: to make sore or painful by rubbing
entries.example_cn: 粗糙的布料磨伤了她的皮肤。
entries.example_en: The rough fabric fretted her skin.

entries.definition_en: to fit frets onto a musical instrument
entries.example_cn: 制琴师在吉他完工前给它装上了品丝。
entries.example_en: The luthier fretted the guitar before finishing it.

entries.definition_cn: 因担忧而产生的焦虑或烦躁状态
entries.definition_en: a state of anxiety or agitation caused by worry
entries.example_cn: 不要让不确定性让你过于焦虑。
entries.example_en: Don't let the uncertainty cause you too much fret.

entries.definition_en: a metal bar on a musical instrument's fingerboard that divides the strings into segments
entries.example_cn: 他将弦按在品上以改变音高。
entries.example_en: He pressed the string against the fret to change the pitch.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental pattern of repeated vertical and horizontal lines
entries.example_cn: 这块布料采用了经典的方格纹设计。
entries.example_en: The fabric featured a classic fret design.

entries.definition_en: a spot worn away by friction or erosion
entries.example_cn: 持续的摩擦在金属表面造成了一个磨损处。
entries.example_en: The constant rubbing created a fret on the metal surface.

entries.definition_en: feeling nervous and unable to relax
entries.example_cn: 那个焦虑不安的孩子在嘈杂的房间里无法入睡。
entries.example_en: The fretful child could not sleep in the noisy room.

entries.definition_en: irritable or bad-tempered
entries.example_cn: 她烦躁的抱怨让办公室里的每个人都感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: Her fretful complaints made everyone in the office uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: in a fretful manner
entries.example_cn: 他焦虑地等待着儿子归来的消息。
entries.example_en: He waited fretfully for the news of his son's return.

entries.definition_cn: 有品（乐器上的金属条）的
entries.definition_en: having frets (musical bars on a stringed instrument)
entries.example_cn: 这把有品的吉他发出了清晰而共鸣的声音。
entries.example_en: The fretted guitar produced a clear, resonant sound.

entries.definition_en: having a pattern of fretwork or latticework
entries.example_cn: 这扇窗户由精致的雕花木头制成。
entries.example_en: The window was made of delicate, fretted wood.

entries.definition_cn: 雕花木工或金属工艺；镂雕装饰
entries.definition_en: ornamental woodwork or metalwork carved in low relief or cut through
entries.example_cn: 教堂的门上装饰着复杂的镂雕装饰。
entries.example_en: The church door was decorated with intricate fretwork.

entries.definition_en: easily crumbled into small pieces or powder
entries.example_cn: 这件古陶器非常易碎，一碰就碎了。
entries.example_en: The ancient pottery was so friable that it shattered when touched.

entries.definition_en: describing soil that is loose and coarse-grained
entries.example_cn: 这些葡萄藤生长在松散、颗粒粗大的花岗岩土壤中。
entries.example_en: The vines grew in friable, granitic soil.

entries.definition_cn: 基督教托钵修会的成员；托钵修士
entries.definition_en: a member of a Christian mendicant order
entries.example_cn: 这位修士走遍各个城镇向穷人布道。
entries.example_en: The friar traveled from town to town preaching to the poor.

entries.definition_en: a monastery inhabited by friars
entries.example_cn: 古老的修道院静静地矗立在城镇中心。
entries.example_en: The old friary stands quietly in the center of the town.

entries.definition_en: a dish made of pieces of meat stewed in gravy with vegetables
entries.example_cn: 我们点了一份胡萝卜和洋葱烩鸡肉。
entries.example_en: We ordered a fricassee of chicken with carrots and onions.

entries.definition_en: to cook meat by stewing it in gravy with vegetables
entries.example_cn: 厨师用浓郁的酱汁烩了鸭子。
entries.example_en: The chef fricasseeed the duck with a rich sauce.

entries.definition_en: a type of consonant sound made by air passing through a narrow part of the mouth
entries.example_cn: 英语中的 /s/ 和 /f/ 音是摩擦音。
entries.example_en: The /s/ and /f/ sounds in English are fricatives.

entries.definition_en: relating to speech sounds produced by forcing air through a constricted passage
entries.example_cn: “thin”和“then”的首音都是摩擦音。
entries.example_en: The initial sounds in “thin” and “then” are fricative sounds.

entries.definition_en: a situation where people disagree or have a difficult relationship
entries.example_cn: 这两个部门之间有很多摩擦。
entries.example_en: There was a lot of friction between the two departments.

entries.definition_en: the force that opposes the motion of one surface sliding over another
entries.example_cn: 轮胎与路面之间的摩擦力帮助汽车停下。
entries.example_en: Friction between the tires and the road helps the car stop.

entries.definition_cn: 一个物体或表面与另一个物体或表面之间的摩擦
entries.definition_en: the rubbing of one object or surface against another
entries.example_cn: 粗布与玻璃之间的摩擦产生了热量。
entries.example_en: The friction of the rough cloth against the glass produced heat.

entries.definition_cn: 与摩擦有关或由摩擦产生的
entries.definition_en: relating to or produced by friction
entries.example_cn: 摩擦力使滑动的木块减速。
entries.example_en: The frictional force slowed the sliding block down.

entries.definition_en: lacking all friction
entries.example_cn: 该理论模型假设表面是无摩擦的。
entries.example_en: The theoretical model assumes a frictionless surface.

entries.definition_cn: 贸易或交易中没有关税或其他贸易壁垒的
entries.definition_en: of trade or transactions, without tariffs or other trade barriers
entries.example_cn: 该协议旨在实现两国之间无关税和其他贸易壁垒的贸易。
entries.example_en: The agreement aims to create frictionless trade between the two countries.

entries.definition_en: an informal term for a refrigerator
entries.example_cn: 我需要把牛奶放进冰箱。
entries.example_en: I need to put the milk in the fridge.

entries.definition_en: cooked by frying in fat
entries.example_cn: 我们点了炸鸡作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We ordered fried chicken for dinner.

entries.definition_en: a person you know well and trust
entries.example_cn: 我最好的朋友住在伦敦。
entries.example_en: My best friend lives in London.

entries.definition_en: an associate who provides cooperation or assistance
entries.example_cn: 团队需要一个伙伴来帮助他们完成项目。
entries.example_en: The team needs a friend to help them finish the project.

entries.definition_en: a person with whom you are acquainted
entries.example_cn: 我在聚会上遇到了一位朋友的朋友。
entries.example_en: I met a friend of a friend at the party.

entries.definition_en: a person who supports a cause, organization, or institution
entries.example_cn: 她支持当地的艺术中心。
entries.example_en: She is a friend of the local arts center.

entries.definition_en: without friends; having no friends
entries.example_cn: 搬到新城市后，他感到没有朋友。
entries.example_en: After moving to the new city, he felt friendless.

entries.definition_en: a friendly disposition or nature
entries.example_cn: 她友善的天性使她成为聚会上受欢迎的女主人。
entries.example_en: Her friendliness made her a popular hostess at the party.

entries.definition_en: a friendly attitude toward another person
entries.example_cn: 孩子们对新来的学生表现出了极大的喜爱之情。
entries.example_en: The children showed great friendliness toward the new student.

entries.definition_en: willing to help and not hostile
entries.example_cn: 邻居对新家庭非常友善。
entries.example_en: The neighbors were very friendly to the new family.

entries.definition_en: like a friend
entries.example_cn: 帮助他是一种友好的姿态。
entries.example_en: It was a friendly gesture to help him.

entries.definition_en: easy to use or understand
entries.example_cn: 这个软件的用户界面很友好。
entries.example_en: This software has a friendly interface.

entries.definition_en: belonging to your own country's forces or allies
entries.example_cn: 友军火力造成了事故。
entries.example_en: The friendly fire caused an accident.

entries.definition_en: soldiers from your own army or an ally
entries.example_cn: 这些部队是友军。
entries.example_en: The troops were friendly forces.

entries.definition_en: the state of being friends (or friendly)
entries.example_cn: 他们的友谊已经持续了二十多年。
entries.example_en: Their friendship has lasted for over twenty years.

entries.definition_cn: （对某人）只当朋友（而对方有浪漫情感）
entries.definition_en: to treat someone as a friend despite their romantic interest
entries.example_cn: 当她拒绝他的约会请求时，他觉得自己被只当朋友了。
entries.example_en: He felt friendzoned when she refused his date request.

entries.definition_en: a kitchen appliance used for deep frying food
entries.example_cn: 他买了一个新的电炸锅来制作他最爱的小吃。
entries.example_en: He bought a new electric frier to cook his favorite snacks.

entries.definition_cn: 适合油炸的幼鸡；炸鸡用嫩鸡
entries.definition_en: a young chicken suitable for frying
entries.example_cn: 这道食谱需要一只嫩鸡，才能做出完美的炸鸡。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for a tender frier to make the perfect fried chicken.

entries.definition_en: strips of potato fried in deep fat
entries.example_cn: 我想在汉堡包旁边点一份大份的炸薯条。
entries.example_en: I would like a large order of fries with my burger.

entries.definition_en: a decorative horizontal band in architecture, especially between the architrave and cornice
entries.example_cn: 该博物馆展示了一条描绘古代战争的精美檐壁饰带。
entries.example_en: The museum features a magnificent frieze depicting ancient battles.

entries.definition_en: a coarse woolen fabric with a shaggy or tufted nap
entries.example_cn: 在寒冷的冬天，她裹上一条温暖的长毛绒毯子。
entries.example_en: She wrapped herself in a warm frieze blanket during the cold winter.

entries.definition_cn: 通常小于驱逐舰的现代护卫舰
entries.definition_en: a modern escort warship, typically smaller than a destroyer
entries.example_cn: 这艘护卫舰在海岸巡逻，以防范潜在威胁。
entries.example_en: The frigate patrolled the coast to protect against potential threats.

entries.definition_cn: 有一层连续炮甲板的中型帆船战舰
entries.definition_en: a medium-sized sailing warship with a single continuous gun deck
entries.example_cn: 这部历史小说描述了战舰与敌舰之间激烈的战斗。
entries.example_en: The historical novel described the fierce battle between the frigate and the enemy ship.

entries.definition_en: a sudden feeling of fear or panic, often caused by the expectation of danger or pain
entries.example_cn: 突然的噪音让孩子们感到惊恐。
entries.example_en: The sudden noise caused a fright in the children.

entries.definition_en: to frighten (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 雷声轰鸣，吓坏了马匹。
entries.example_en: The loud thunder frights the horses.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to feel fear
entries.example_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子们。
entries.example_en: The loud noise frightened the children.

entries.definition_en: feeling afraid
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被巨大的雷声吓坏了。
entries.example_en: The children were frightened by the loud thunder.

entries.definition_en: extremely scared or panicked
entries.example_cn: 当她看到那条蛇时，吓得魂飞魄散。
entries.example_en: She was frightened out of her wits when she saw the snake.

entries.definition_en: causing fear or dread or terror
entries.example_cn: 那场令人恐惧的风暴迫使我们待在室内。
entries.example_en: The frightening storm forced us to stay indoors.

entries.definition_en: the act of making someone feel afraid
entries.example_cn: 小丑吓唬孩子们的行为太过分了。
entries.example_en: The frightening of the children by the clown was too much.

entries.definition_cn: 非常；达到令人惊讶或担忧的程度
entries.definition_en: Very; to a surprisingly or alarmingly great degree.
entries.example_cn: 摆在我面前的水罐大得惊人。
entries.example_en: The pitcher that was set before me was frighteningly large.

entries.definition_en: in a terrifying manner
entries.example_cn: 这场风暴猛烈得骇人。
entries.example_en: The storm was frighteningly violent.

entries.definition_en: Extremely severe in degree, extent, amount, or impact.
entries.example_cn: 该项目的极度高昂成本超出了我们的初始预算。
entries.example_en: The frightful cost of the project exceeded our initial budget.

entries.definition_en: Extremely distressing or upsetting.
entries.example_cn: 听到这个悲剧消息后，她感到极度悲伤。
entries.example_en: She felt frightful sadness after hearing the tragic news.

entries.definition_en: Causing extreme fear or horror.
entries.example_cn: 那场可怕的暴风雨损坏了老房子的屋顶。
entries.example_en: The frightful storm damaged the roof of the old house.

entries.definition_en: used as intensifiers
entries.example_cn: 这部电影非常令人兴奋。
entries.example_en: The movie was frightfully exciting.

entries.definition_en: extremely cold
entries.example_cn: 刺骨的寒风刮在他们的脸上。
entries.example_en: The frigid wind bit at their faces.

entries.definition_en: devoid of warmth and cordiality; expressive of unfriendliness or disdain
entries.example_cn: 他冷冷地跟她打了个招呼。
entries.example_en: He gave her a frigid greeting.

entries.definition_cn: （口语，尤指女性）性冷淡的；无性欲的
entries.definition_en: sexually unresponsive, especially of a woman (colloquial)
entries.example_cn: 小说中，她因毫无性兴趣而被描述为性冷淡。
entries.example_en: The novel described her as frigid because she showed no sexual interest.

entries.definition_en: lack of sexual arousal or inability to achieve sexual satisfaction
entries.example_cn: 医生与患者讨论了性冷淡的原因。
entries.example_en: The doctor discussed the causes of frigidity with the patient.

entries.definition_en: a lack of warmth, affection, or enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 他对家人的冷漠让朋友们感到担忧。
entries.example_en: His frigidity towards his family worried his friends.

entries.definition_en: the state of being very cold
entries.example_cn: 冬季的极端严寒使得户外活动变得困难。
entries.example_en: The extreme frigidity of the winter made outdoor activities difficult.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows no warmth or enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 她冷淡地回答了他的问题。
entries.example_en: She replied frigidly to his questions.

entries.definition_cn: 用作装饰或镶边的褶皱布条
entries.definition_en: a strip of pleated material used as a decoration or trim
entries.example_cn: 这条连衣裙的领口处装饰着一条白色的褶边。
entries.example_en: The dress was adorned with a white frill along the neckline.

entries.definition_en: ornamental objects that have little value
entries.example_cn: 酒店房间里充满了不必要的装饰品，比如精致的肥皂盒。
entries.example_en: The hotel room was filled with unnecessary frills like fancy soap dispensers.

entries.definition_cn: 鸟类或动物颈部周围形成的羽毛或毛发外部身体部位
entries.definition_en: feathers or hair forming an external body part around the neck of a bird or animal
entries.example_cn: 猫头鹰颈部周围的羽毛让它看起来更大。
entries.example_en: The owl's frill of feathers around its neck made it look larger.

entries.definition_cn: 许多角龙类恐龙头骨后方向上弯曲的骨板
entries.definition_en: a bony plate curving upward behind the skull of many ceratopsian dinosaurs
entries.example_cn: 三角龙头后的颈盾有助于保护其颈部肌肉。
entries.example_en: The frill on the Triceratops helped protect its neck muscles.

entries.definition_en: having decorative ruffles or frills
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件饰有褶边的衬衫去参加聚会。
entries.example_en: She wore a frilled blouse to the party.

entries.definition_en: having decorative ruffles or frills
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件饰有褶边的连衣裙去参加婚礼。
entries.example_en: She wore a frilly dress to the wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 性质或外表过分繁复或炫耀的
entries.definition_en: over-elaborate or showy in character or appearance
entries.example_cn: 这些装饰对于如此正式的活动来说过于花哨了。
entries.example_en: The decorations were too frilly for such a formal event.

entries.definition_en: the outer edge or boundary of something
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在人群的外围观看游行。
entries.example_en: They sat on the fringe of the crowd to watch the parade.

entries.definition_en: a border of hair cut short across the forehead
entries.example_cn: 她把刘海剪得很短以衬托她的脸庞。
entries.example_en: She cut her fringe very short to frame her face.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental border made of hanging threads or tassels
entries.example_cn: 地毯的边缘有一圈厚厚的流苏饰边。
entries.example_en: The rug has a thick fringe along its edges.

entries.definition_en: a social group with extreme or unconventional views
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志被政治极端分子阅读。
entries.example_en: The magazine was read by the political fringe.

entries.definition_en: a part of a city that is far from the center
entries.example_cn: 那座旧工厂位于城市的边缘地带。
entries.example_en: The old factory is located in the fringe of the city.

entries.definition_en: to decorate something with a fringe
entries.example_cn: 她决定给窗帘镶边以匹配沙发。
entries.example_en: She decided to fringe the curtains to match the sofa.

entries.definition_en: to decorate with or as if with a surrounding fringe
entries.example_cn: 设计师用精致的蕾丝饰以流苏装饰了这条裙子。
entries.example_en: The designer fringed the dress with delicate lace.

entries.definition_en: a light or dark band produced by the interference of light waves
entries.example_cn: 实验在屏幕上产生了一系列彩色的干涉条纹。
entries.example_en: The experiment produced a series of colorful fringes on the screen.

entries.definition_en: having a border or edge like a fringe
entries.example_cn: 湖边长满了芦苇。
entries.example_en: The lake was fringed with reeds.

entries.definition_en: decorated with hanging strips of fabric
entries.example_cn: 窗帘饰有金色的流苏。
entries.example_en: The curtains were fringed with gold tassels.

entries.definition_cn: 边缘呈不规则细裂状的
entries.definition_en: having edges cut into irregular, fine slits
entries.example_cn: 织物被切成不规则的细裂状，形成了精致的图案。
entries.example_en: The fabric was fringed to create a delicate pattern.

entries.definition_cn: 非正式：边缘的；非主流的
entries.definition_en: informal: peripheral or outside the mainstream
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家的非主流风格受到主流之外人群的喜爱。
entries.example_en: The artist's fringy style appealed to people outside the mainstream.

entries.definition_cn: 华而不实的装饰；无用的小物件
entries.definition_en: something of little value or significance, especially showy or useless decoration
entries.example_cn: 房间里堆满了华而不实的装饰，而不是实用的家具。
entries.example_en: The room was filled with frippery rather than useful furnishings.

entries.definition_en: to search as for concealed weapons by running the hands rapidly over the clothing and through the pockets
entries.example_cn: 安保人员在登机前对每位乘客进行了搜身。
entries.example_en: Security personnel frisked every passenger before boarding.

entries.definition_en: to play boisterously
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在花园里嬉戏打闹。
entries.example_en: The children frisked around in the garden.

entries.definition_en: the act of searching someone for concealed weapons or illegal drugs
entries.example_cn: 警察拦下汽车，对司机进行了搜身。
entries.example_en: The police stopped the car and gave the driver a frisk.

entries.definition_en: the act of searching someone's body for concealed weapons or illegal drugs
entries.example_cn: 安检后的搜身发现他口袋里藏着一把小刀。
entries.example_en: After the security check, the frisking revealed a small knife in his pocket.

entries.definition_en: playful and full of energy
entries.example_cn: 当看到球时，那只狗变得活泼好动起来。
entries.example_en: The dog became frisky when it saw the ball.

entries.definition_en: (informal) sexually aroused
entries.example_cn: 喝了几杯酒后，他变得性兴奋起来，不停地和约会对象调情。
entries.example_en: After a few drinks, he became frisky and kept flirting with his date.

entries.definition_cn: 一阵战栗或激动、恐惧带来的兴奋感
entries.definition_en: a sudden shiver or thrill of excitement, fear, or pleasure
entries.example_cn: 紧张的音乐让观众感到一阵战栗。
entries.example_en: The suspenseful music caused a frisson of fear among the audience.

entries.definition_en: a butterfly with brownish wings marked with black and silver
entries.example_cn: 我们在花园里发现了一只蛱蝶停在一片叶子上。
entries.example_en: We spotted a fritillary resting on a leaf in the garden.

entries.definition_en: a plant with nodding flowers of various colors
entries.example_cn: 贝母属植物下垂的紫色花朵吸引了许多蜜蜂。
entries.example_en: The fritillary's nodding purple flowers attracted many bees.

entries.definition_en: an Italian omelet containing diced vegetables and meats, cooked until the bottom is set and then flipped to cook the top
entries.example_cn: 我们早餐点了一份蔬菜煎蛋卷。
entries.example_en: We ordered a vegetable frittata for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: to spend money frivolously and unwisely
entries.example_cn: 他把遗产挥霍在赌博上了。
entries.example_en: He frittered away his inheritance on gambling.

entries.definition_en: a small quantity of fried batter containing fruit or meat or vegetables
entries.example_cn: 我们早餐享用了一盘炸面糊点心。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a plate of fritters for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: the trait of being frivolous; not serious or sensible
entries.example_cn: 派对客人的轻浮让整晚显得毫无意义。
entries.example_en: The frivolity of the party guests made the evening feel unimportant.

entries.definition_en: something of little value or significance
entries.example_cn: 他驳斥了这个论点，认为那只是琐事。
entries.example_en: He dismissed the argument as mere frivolity.

entries.definition_en: a frivolous act or behavior
entries.example_cn: 演员在舞台上的滑稽行为逗乐了观众。
entries.example_en: The actor's frivolity on stage delighted the audience.

entries.definition_en: not serious or sensible in content, attitude, or behavior
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上的轻浮言论冒犯了所有人。
entries.example_en: His frivolous comments offended everyone at the meeting.

entries.definition_en: in a frivolous manner
entries.example_cn: 他轻率地把钱花在玩具上。
entries.example_en: He spent his money frivolously on toys.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being not serious or sensible
entries.example_cn: 他的轻浮使他成为商业上不可靠的伙伴。
entries.example_en: His frivolousness made him an unreliable partner in business.

entries.definition_en: to become or make hair curl tightly and unevenly
entries.example_cn: 化学处理让她的直发变得毛躁。
entries.example_en: The chemical treatment made her straight hair frizz.

entries.definition_en: hair that is formed into small, tight curls
entries.example_cn: 夏季的湿气使她的头发形成了一团蓬乱的卷发。
entries.example_en: Humidity caused a frizz to form in her hair during the summer.

entries.definition_en: to curl tightly
entries.example_cn: 热量让头发卷曲得很紧。
entries.example_en: The heat caused the hair to frizzle.

entries.definition_en: to fry food until it curls and becomes crisp
entries.example_cn: 她决定把洋葱炸得卷曲酥脆，做成沙拉。
entries.example_en: She decided to frizzle the onions for the salad.

entries.definition_en: having hair that is curly and rough to the touch
entries.example_cn: 她在太阳下待了一整天后，头发看起来毛躁。
entries.example_en: Her hair looked frizzy after spending the day in the sun.

entries.definition_en: a long, loose outer garment
entries.example_cn: 这位演员在历史剧中穿了一件黑色长袍。
entries.example_en: The actor wore a black frock for the historical play.

entries.definition_en: a one-piece garment for a woman with a skirt and bodice
entries.example_cn: 在20世纪50年代，连衣裙是女性的标准着装。
entries.example_en: In the 1950s, the frock was the standard dress for women.

entries.definition_en: a habit worn by clerics
entries.example_cn: 神父在进入厨房前脱下了他的长袍。
entries.example_en: The priest removed his frock before entering the kitchen.

entries.definition_en: to put a frock on (someone)
entries.example_cn: 修女们在这些新成员宣誓前给她们穿上了修女服。
entries.example_en: The nuns frocked the new recruits before they took their vows.

entries.definition_en: a tailless amphibian with strong hind legs used for jumping
entries.example_cn: 那只青蛙静静地坐在一片睡莲叶上。
entries.example_en: The frog sat quietly on a lily pad.

entries.definition_en: a French person (offensive slur)
entries.example_cn: “frog”一词可能会冒犯法国人。
entries.example_en: The term “frog” can offend French people.

entries.definition_en: a decorative loop of braid or cord worn on clothing
entries.example_cn: 制服上装饰着一个金色的饰带环。
entries.example_en: The uniform was decorated with a gold frog.

entries.definition_en: to hunt for frogs to eat
entries.example_cn: 过去，人们在沼泽里捕蛙作为食物。
entries.example_en: In the past, people frogged for food in the marshes.

entries.definition_cn: 欧洲浮水植物，有近圆形的心形叶和白色花朵
entries.definition_en: European floating plant with roundish heart-shaped leaves and white flowers
entries.example_cn: 这种欧洲浮水植物轻轻漂浮在池塘表面。
entries.example_en: The frog's-bit floated gently on the surface of the pond.

entries.definition_en: a fish with a frog-like mouth and a lure on its snout
entries.example_cn: 蛙鱼利用它的诱饵吸引小型猎物。
entries.example_en: The frogfish uses its lure to attract small prey.

entries.definition_en: a diver, especially one wearing a diving suit, often a military diver
entries.example_cn: 潜水员检查了沉船是否有损坏的迹象。
entries.example_en: The frogman inspected the sunken ship for signs of damage.

entries.definition_en: a bird from Australia and southeastern Asia that eats insects and has a wide mouth resembling a frog's
entries.example_cn: 蟆口鸱静静地坐在树枝上，等待猎物。
entries.example_en: The frogmouth sat silently on the branch, waiting for its prey.

entries.definition_en: to play boisterously
entries.example_cn: 大雪过后，狗们在雪地里嬉戏打闹。
entries.example_en: The dogs frolic in the snow after a heavy storm.

entries.definition_en: gay or light-hearted recreational activity for diversion or amusement
entries.example_cn: 孩子们下午在公园里嬉戏玩耍。
entries.example_en: The children spent the afternoon frolicking in the park.

entries.definition_en: given to merry frolicking
entries.example_cn: 那些爱嬉戏的孩子们在草地上奔跑。
entries.example_en: The frolicsome children ran through the meadow.

entries.definition_en: indicating where something comes from or its origin
entries.example_cn: 我从图书馆得到了这本书。
entries.example_en: I got this book from the library.

entries.definition_en: indicating a starting point or initial reference
entries.example_cn: 我们从公园走到车站。
entries.example_en: We walked from the park to the station.

entries.definition_en: indicating removal or separation
entries.example_cn: 把标签从盒子上取下来。
entries.example_en: Take the label from the box.

entries.definition_en: made using a specific substance or material
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子是用木头做的。
entries.example_en: This table is made from wood.

entries.definition_cn: 表示被排除在某事物之外，或被禁止进入或参加某事。
entries.definition_en: Indicating exclusion or prevention from entering or participating in something.
entries.example_cn: 她被禁止进入。
entries.example_en: She was barred from entering.

entries.definition_en: indicating differentiation or distinction
entries.example_cn: 这与我的预期不同。
entries.example_en: This is different from what I expected.

entries.definition_en: starting at a specific time or year
entries.example_cn: 这场战争始于1939年。
entries.example_en: The war dates from 1939.

entries.definition_en: because of; as a result of
entries.example_cn: 他因为交通堵塞而迟到了。
entries.example_en: He was late from the traffic.

entries.definition_en: a large leaf of a fern, palm, or cycad
entries.example_cn: 那只鸟藏在棕榈树的绿色羽状叶中。
entries.example_en: The bird hid among the green fronds of the palm tree.

entries.definition_en: the side of something that is forward or most visible
entries.example_cn: 房子的正面朝向街道。
entries.example_en: The front of the house faces the street.

entries.definition_en: the side that is seen first or comes first
entries.example_cn: 书的正面是标题页。
entries.example_en: The front of the book contains the title page.

entries.definition_en: the line where opposing armies face each other in battle
entries.example_cn: 士兵们在前线战斗了几天。
entries.example_en: Soldiers fought along the front for days.

entries.definition_en: a person used as a cover for illegal or questionable activities
entries.example_cn: 那个罪犯让他的朋友充当毒品交易的幌子。
entries.example_en: The criminal used his friend as a front for the drug deal.

entries.definition_en: located at or relating to the front part
entries.example_cn: 请坐在前排。
entries.example_en: Please sit in the front row.

entries.definition_en: to face or be oriented in a particular direction
entries.example_cn: 窗户朝向花园。
entries.example_en: The window fronts the garden.

entries.definition_en: to confront or face someone directly
entries.example_cn: 她正面面对袭击者并呼救。
entries.example_en: She fronted her attacker and called for help.

entries.definition_en: the outward appearance or image of a person
entries.example_cn: 他的外表非常迷人。
entries.example_en: His front is very charming.

entries.definition_en: important enough to be featured on the first page of a newspaper
entries.example_cn: 头版报道揭露了市长的腐败行为。
entries.example_en: The front-page story revealed the mayor's corruption.

entries.definition_en: appearing on the first page of a publication
entries.example_cn: 头版广告非常昂贵。
entries.example_en: The front-page advertisement was very expensive.

entries.definition_en: the first page of a newspaper or magazine
entries.example_cn: 头版头条震惊了整个国家。
entries.example_en: The front-page headline shocked the entire country.

entries.definition_en: a competitor thought likely to win
entries.example_cn: 总统职位的领跑者宣布了她的竞选策略。
entries.example_en: The front-runner for the presidency announced her campaign strategy.

entries.definition_en: the length of land that borders on a street or body of water
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店在海滩上有很长的临海地段。
entries.example_en: The hotel has a long frontage on the beach.

entries.definition_en: the face or front of a building
entries.example_cn: 这栋建筑的正面是红砖砌成的。
entries.example_en: The building's frontage is made of red brick.

entries.definition_en: the direction in which a building faces
entries.example_cn: 这所房子的朝向是朝南的。
entries.example_en: The frontage of the house faces south.

entries.definition_en: belonging to the front part
entries.example_cn: 大脑的前部负责控制随意运动。
entries.example_en: The frontal lobe of the brain controls voluntary movement.

entries.definition_en: of or adjacent to the forehead or frontal bone
entries.example_cn: 受伤部位位于头骨的额部。
entries.example_en: The injury was located on the frontal region of the skull.

entries.definition_cn: 锋面的；与天气锋面有关的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to the front of an advancing mass of air
entries.example_cn: 风暴系统伴随着强烈的锋面边界移动。
entries.example_en: The storm system moved with a strong frontal boundary.

entries.definition_en: meeting front to front
entries.example_cn: 两军在正面交锋中相遇。
entries.example_en: The two armies met in a frontal clash.

entries.definition_en: the face or front of a building
entries.example_cn: 建筑师为博物馆设计了一个引人注目的正面。
entries.example_en: The architect designed a striking frontal for the museum.

entries.definition_en: an adornment worn on the forehead
entries.example_cn: 节日期间她戴了一顶花卉额饰。
entries.example_en: She wore a floral frontal during the festival.

entries.definition_en: a drapery that covers the front of an altar
entries.example_cn: 牧师在仪式前调整了金色的祭坛前帘。
entries.example_en: The priest adjusted the golden frontal before the service.

entries.definition_en: in, at, or toward the front
entries.example_cn: 外科医生从正面接近肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The surgeon approached the tumor frontally.

entries.definition_cn: 英国下议院前座议员，通常为内阁成员或影子内阁成员
entries.definition_en: a member of the House of Commons who sits on the front bench, typically in the cabinet or shadow cabinet
entries.example_cn: 作为资深前座议员，她预计将在辩论中回答问题。
entries.example_en: As a senior frontbencher, she was expected to answer questions during the debate.

entries.definition_en: a wilderness area at the edge of a settled region
entries.example_cn: 拓荒者前往边疆寻找新土地。
entries.example_en: The pioneers moved to the frontier to find new land.

entries.definition_en: an international boundary or the area immediately inside it
entries.example_cn: 士兵们仔细守卫着国境线。
entries.example_en: The soldiers guarded the frontier carefully.

entries.definition_en: an undeveloped field of study or research
entries.example_cn: 人工智能是现代科学的前沿领域。
entries.example_en: Artificial intelligence is a frontier in modern science.

entries.definition_en: a person who lives on a frontier or in a wild, undeveloped area
entries.example_cn: 这位拓荒者在河边建了一座小屋。
entries.example_en: The frontiersman built a cabin near the river.

entries.definition_cn: 书籍、章节或杂志书名页前的插图
entries.definition_en: an illustration on the page before the title page of a book, section, or magazine
entries.example_cn: 书名页前的插图描绘了主角站在城堡前的场景。
entries.example_en: The frontispiece depicted the main character standing before a castle.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental facade or front face of a building
entries.example_cn: 旧图书馆的正面装饰着历史人物的复杂雕刻。
entries.example_en: The frontispiece of the old library featured intricate carvings of historical figures.

entries.definition_en: in a direction toward the front
entries.example_cn: 汽车向前开进了车库。
entries.example_en: The car moved frontwards into the garage.

entries.definition_en: ice crystals forming a white deposit on objects outside
entries.example_cn: 厚厚的霜覆盖了车窗。
entries.example_en: A thick layer of frost covered the car windows.

entries.definition_en: weather cold enough to cause freezing
entries.example_cn: 霜冻使得无法外出。
entries.example_en: The frost made it impossible to go outside.

entries.definition_en: decorate with frosting
entries.example_cn: 她用白色糖霜给蛋糕裱花。
entries.example_en: She frosted the cake with white icing.

entries.definition_en: damage by frost
entries.example_cn: 早霜损害了庄稼。
entries.example_en: The early frost damaged the crops.

entries.definition_en: cover with frost
entries.example_cn: 树枝被寒冷的夜晚覆盖了霜。
entries.example_en: The branches were frosted by the cold night.

entries.definition_en: provide with a rough or speckled surface or appearance
entries.example_cn: 这种处理使玻璃表面呈现出斑驳的图案。
entries.example_en: The treatment frosted the glass with a speckled pattern.

entries.definition_en: the formation of frost or ice on a surface
entries.example_cn: 草上 overnight 结了一层霜。
entries.example_en: Frost formed on the grass overnight.

entries.definition_en: damage to body tissue caused by freezing, often resulting in numbness, blisters, or gangrene.
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者在雪地里过夜后，脚趾受了严重的冻伤。
entries.example_en: The hikers suffered severe frostbite on their toes after spending the night in the snow.

entries.definition_en: injured by freezing or partial freezing
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者在雪地里过夜后，脚趾冻伤了。
entries.example_en: The hikers had frostbitten toes after spending the night in the snow.

entries.definition_cn: （指玻璃）表面有类似霜的粗糙涂层的
entries.definition_en: (of glass) having a roughened coating resembling frost
entries.example_cn: 窗户上覆盖着磨砂玻璃以确保隐私。
entries.example_en: The window was covered with frosted glass to ensure privacy.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that is cold and unenthusiastic
entries.example_cn: 她冷淡地迎接客人，拒绝微笑。
entries.example_en: She greeted the guests frostily, refusing to smile.

entries.definition_en: a sweet mixture of sugar and other ingredients used to cover cakes
entries.example_cn: 她用五颜六色的糖霜装饰了生日蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She decorated the birthday cake with colorful frosting.

entries.definition_en: lacking warmth and friendliness; cold and unfriendly
entries.example_cn: 他到达时，她给了他一个冷淡的招呼。
entries.example_en: She gave him a frosty greeting when he arrived.

entries.definition_en: covered with a layer of ice crystals formed by freezing
entries.example_cn: 清晨窗户上结了一层霜。
entries.example_en: The windows were frosty in the early morning.

entries.definition_en: cold or chilly
entries.example_cn: 我们在公园里享受了一个寒冷的清晨散步。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a frosty morning walk in the park.

entries.definition_en: a mass of small bubbles formed in or on a liquid
entries.example_cn: 啤酒顶部的泡沫又厚又白。
entries.example_en: The froth on top of the beer was thick and white.

entries.definition_en: to become bubbly or frothy
entries.example_cn: 当水碰到热岩石时，开始起泡。
entries.example_en: The water began to froth as it hit the hot rocks.

entries.definition_en: to create froth or foam in a liquid
entries.example_cn: 打蛋器把牛奶打出了泡沫。
entries.example_en: The whisk frothed the milk.

entries.definition_en: to exude or expel foam
entries.example_cn: 爆炸后，机器喷出蒸汽。
entries.example_en: The machine frothed with steam after the explosion.

entries.definition_en: covered with or producing a thick foam of sweat or saliva, usually due to extreme exhaustion or illness
entries.example_cn: 那条精疲力竭的狗口吐白沫。
entries.example_en: The exhausted dog was frothing at the mouth.

entries.definition_en: the act or process of producing foam or froth
entries.example_cn: 狗嘴边起泡沫是它需要立即救治的迹象。
entries.example_en: The frothing at the mouth was a sign that the dog needed immediate care.

entries.definition_en: covered with or full of bubbles, often from carbonation or fermentation
entries.example_cn: 这啤酒泡沫丰富，闻起来很新鲜。
entries.example_en: The beer was frothy and smelled fresh.

entries.definition_en: lighthearted, frivolous, or lacking seriousness
entries.example_cn: 这场派对是对球队胜利的兴高采烈的庆祝。
entries.example_en: The party was a frothy celebration of the team's victory.

entries.definition_cn: 通过摩擦他人（如在人群中）进行自慰
entries.definition_en: masturbation by rubbing against another person (as in a crowd)
entries.example_cn: 警方调查了地铁站内发生的摩擦自慰事件。
entries.example_en: The police investigated the incident of frottage in the subway station.

entries.definition_cn: 生气或阴沉地看人，皱起前额，以示不赞成
entries.definition_en: look angry or sullen, wrinkle one's forehead, as if to signal disapproval
entries.example_cn: 老师对学生粗心的错误皱起了眉头。
entries.example_en: The teacher frowned at the student's careless mistake.

entries.definition_cn: 表示厌恶或不悦的面部表情
entries.definition_en: a facial expression of dislike or displeasure
entries.example_cn: 他迟到时，她向他皱起了眉头。
entries.example_en: She gave him a frown when he arrived late.

entries.definition_en: showing displeasure or anger on one's face
entries.example_cn: 他带着不悦的表情看着她。
entries.example_en: He looked at her with a frowning expression.

entries.definition_en: turned into ice or affected by severe cold
entries.example_cn: 湖面完全结冰了。
entries.example_en: The lake is completely frozen.

entries.definition_en: not thawed
entries.example_cn: 肉还没解冻。
entries.example_en: The meat is still frozen.

entries.definition_en: preserved by rapid freezing to keep flavor and nutrition
entries.example_cn: 我们买了一些速冻蔬菜。
entries.example_en: We bought some frozen vegetables.

entries.definition_cn: 因震惊或恐惧而动弹不得的
entries.definition_en: unable to move, often because of shock or fear
entries.example_cn: 劫匪用枪指着他时，他吓得站在那里一动不动。
entries.example_en: He stood frozen in terror as the robber pointed a gun at him.

entries.definition_en: in a state where access to or transactions involving assets are prohibited
entries.example_cn: 该公司的资产被冻结了。
entries.example_en: The company's assets are frozen.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being changed or undone
entries.example_cn: 价格固定到下个月。
entries.example_en: The prices are frozen until next month.

entries.definition_en: cold and unfriendly in manner
entries.example_cn: 她对他报以冷淡的微笑。
entries.example_en: She gave him a frozen smile.

entries.definition_en: the process of producing fruit
entries.example_cn: 苹果树的结实在夏末开始。
entries.example_en: The fructification of the apple tree began in late summer.

entries.definition_cn: 蕨类和苔藓的生殖器官
entries.definition_en: the reproductive organs of ferns and mosses
entries.example_cn: 植物学家研究苔藓的生殖器官以了解其生命周期。
entries.example_en: Botanists study the fructification of mosses to understand their life cycles.

entries.definition_en: to become productive or fruitful
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策在实施几年后才开始显现成效。
entries.example_en: The new policy began to fructify only after several years of implementation.

entries.definition_en: to make something productive or fruitful
entries.example_cn: 导师的指导帮助学生使他们的研究想法变得富有成效。
entries.example_en: The mentor's guidance helped the student fructify their research ideas.

entries.definition_en: to produce fruit
entries.example_cn: 那棵老苹果树在长期休眠后终于结果了。
entries.example_en: The old apple tree finally fructified after a long period of dormancy.

entries.definition_en: a simple sugar found in honey and many ripe fruits
entries.example_cn: 蜂蜜富含果糖。
entries.example_en: Honey is rich in fructose.

entries.definition_en: avoiding waste, especially of money or food
entries.example_cn: 他们在艰难时期过着节俭的生活。
entries.example_en: They lived a frugal life during the hard times.

entries.definition_en: prudence in avoiding waste
entries.example_cn: 这个家庭的节俭使他们存够了钱去度假。
entries.example_en: The family's frugality allowed them to save enough for a vacation.

entries.definition_en: in a way that avoids waste or unnecessary spending
entries.example_cn: 他们在退休的岁月里节俭地生活。
entries.example_en: They managed to live frugally during their years of retirement.

entries.definition_cn: 种子植物的成熟繁殖体
entries.definition_en: the ripened reproductive body of a seed plant
entries.example_cn: 苹果是一种水果。
entries.example_en: Apples are a type of fruit.

entries.definition_cn: 某种努力或行动的结果
entries.definition_en: the consequence of some effort or action
entries.example_cn: 这个项目没有像预期那样取得成果。
entries.example_en: The project did not bear fruit as expected.

entries.definition_en: an amount of a product
entries.example_cn: 今年我们收获了一大堆小麦。
entries.example_en: We harvested a good fruit of wheat this year.

entries.definition_cn: 结果实；产生果实、种子或孢子
entries.definition_en: to produce fruit, seeds, or spores
entries.example_cn: 这些苹果树今年结出了大量果实。
entries.example_en: The apple trees fruited abundantly this year.

entries.definition_en: cause to bear fruit
entries.example_cn: 园丁给树浇水以帮助它结果。
entries.example_en: The gardener watered the tree to help it fruit.

entries.definition_en: a rich cake containing dried fruit, nuts, and citrus peel
entries.example_cn: 她为节日烤了一个传统的水果蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She baked a traditional fruitcake for the holiday.

entries.definition_en: a whimsically eccentric person
entries.example_cn: 别听他的；他是个十足的怪人。
entries.example_en: Don't listen to him; he is a total fruitcake.

entries.definition_en: a person whose business is selling fruit
entries.example_cn: 街角那位老水果商卖苹果已经五十年了。
entries.example_en: The old fruiterer on the corner has been selling apples for fifty years.

entries.definition_en: productive or conducive to producing in abundance
entries.example_cn: 这次会议很有成效，我们商定了一项新计划。
entries.example_en: The meeting was fruitful, and we agreed on a new plan.

entries.definition_en: in a way that produces good results or is productive
entries.example_cn: 团队在周末富有成效地推进了项目。
entries.example_en: The team worked fruitfully on the project over the weekend.

entries.definition_cn: 丰产、多产或富饶的状态或性质
entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being fruitful, productive, or abundantly productive
entries.example_cn: 肥沃的土壤确保了本季作物的茁壮成长。
entries.example_en: The rich soil ensured the fruitfulness of the crops this season.

entries.definition_en: the intellectual productivity of a creative imagination
entries.example_cn: 她最新的小说证明了其艺术思维的创造力。
entries.example_en: Her latest novel is a testament to the fruitfulness of her artistic mind.

entries.definition_en: capable of bearing fruit
entries.example_cn: 苹果树结果实的枝条上挂满了成熟的苹果。
entries.example_en: The fruiting branches of the apple tree were heavy with ripe apples.

entries.definition_en: the fulfillment of something worked for
entries.example_cn: 他梦想的实现体现在那座新建筑上。
entries.example_en: The fruition of his dreams was visible in the new building.

entries.definition_cn: 使用或拥有某物带来的乐趣
entries.definition_en: the pleasure or satisfaction gained from using or owning something
entries.example_cn: 她从自己丰富的艺术收藏中获得了极大的享受。
entries.example_en: She found great fruition in her extensive art collection.

entries.definition_en: the condition of bearing fruit
entries.example_cn: 苹果树在夏末结出了果实。
entries.example_en: The apple tree reached fruition in late summer.

entries.definition_en: not producing any results or success
entries.example_cn: 他们谈判合同的徒劳尝试最终以失败告终。
entries.example_en: Their fruitless attempts to negotiate the contract ended in failure.

entries.definition_en: without achieving any useful result or success
entries.example_cn: 那支团队彻夜徒劳地搜寻丢失的文件。
entries.example_en: The team searched fruitlessly for the missing documents all night.

entries.definition_en: the quality of yielding nothing of value
entries.example_cn: 谈判徒劳无益，最终陷入僵局。
entries.example_en: The fruitlessness of the negotiations led to a stalemate.

entries.definition_en: a lack of creative imagination
entries.example_cn: 评论家指出作者最新小说缺乏创造力。
entries.example_en: The critic noted the fruitlessness of the author's latest novel.

entries.definition_en: wood from various fruit trees, such as apple or cherry, used especially in cabinetwork
entries.example_cn: 这件古董橱柜是用优质果木制成的。
entries.example_en: The antique cabinet was crafted from high-quality fruitwood.

entries.definition_en: having a strong taste or smell of fruit
entries.example_cn: 这个蛋糕果味很浓。
entries.example_en: The cake has a very fruity flavor.

entries.definition_cn: （非正式）精神不正常的；古怪的
entries.definition_en: informal: mentally unstable or eccentric
entries.example_cn: 他的举止有点古怪。
entries.example_en: He was acting a bit fruity.

usage.label: informal
usage.pattern: fruity meaning mentally unstable or eccentric

entries.definition_cn: 衣着或外表老土的人，尤指女性
entries.definition_en: a person, especially a woman, whose appearance or clothing is dowdy and unfashionable
entries.example_cn: 她穿着那件破旧的衣服，看起来像个衣着老土的人。
entries.example_en: She looked like a frump in that old, shabby dress.

entries.definition_en: dowdy, unkempt, or unfashionable
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件过时且显得老气的连衣裙，看起来像是20世纪50年代的款式。
entries.example_en: She wore a frumpy dress that looked like it was from the 1950s.

entries.definition_en: to prevent someone from achieving their plans or desires
entries.example_cn: 下雨打乱了我们野餐的计划。
entries.example_en: The rain frustrated our plans for a picnic.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人沮丧、失望或烦恼
entries.definition_en: to cause someone to feel annoyed, disappointed, or discouraged
entries.example_cn: 一再延误使乘客感到沮丧。
entries.example_en: The repeated delays frustrated the passengers.

entries.definition_en: disappointingly unsuccessful
entries.example_cn: 这个赛季球队表现令人沮丧，一场胜利都没有。
entries.example_en: The team had a frustrated season with no wins.

entries.definition_en: preventing you from achieving your goal
entries.example_cn: 当电脑在你保存工作前崩溃时，真是令人沮丧。
entries.example_en: It is frustrating when the computer crashes right before you save your work.

entries.definition_en: causing you to feel annoyed because it stops you from doing what you want
entries.example_cn: 连绵不断的雨水让徒步旅行者感到非常沮丧。
entries.example_en: The constant rain was very frustrating for the hikers.

entries.definition_en: the feeling that accompanies an experience of being thwarted in attaining your goals
entries.example_cn: 当他的项目被拒绝时，他深感挫败。
entries.example_en: He felt deep frustration when his project was rejected.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of annoyance at being hindered or criticized
entries.example_cn: 她对不断的延误表达了她的恼怒。
entries.example_en: She expressed her frustration at the constant delays.

entries.definition_cn: 阻挠或挫败某人计划或努力的行为；阻碍
entries.definition_en: the act of frustrating or hindering someone's plans or efforts
entries.example_cn: 意外延误阻挠了组织者按时完成工作的努力。
entries.example_en: The frustration of the organizers' efforts by the unexpected delay made it impossible to finish on time.

entries.definition_cn: 截头锥体或截头棱锥体
entries.definition_en: the part of a cone or pyramid that remains after the top is cut off by a plane parallel to the base
entries.example_cn: 建筑师计算了截头锥体的体积，以确定所需的混凝土量。
entries.example_en: The architect calculated the volume of the frustum to determine the concrete needed.

entries.definition_cn: 球台；由两个平行平面截出的球体或一般立体的部分
entries.definition_en: a portion of a sphere, or in general any solid, bounded by two parallel planes
entries.example_cn: 工程师计算了两个平行平面之间球台的体积。
entries.example_en: The engineer calculated the volume of the spherical frustum between the two parallel planes.

entries.definition_en: cook in hot fat or oil
entries.example_cn: 她决定用黄油煎鱼。
entries.example_en: She decided to fry the fish in butter.
