entries.definition_en: having the spine and corners bound in leather and the rest of the covers in another material
entries.example_cn: 这本罕见的书采用半皮装订，书脊和书角用皮革，封面和封底的其余部分用布料。
entries.example_en: This rare book is half-bound in leather and cloth.

entries.definition_cn: （动物）一方亲本为纯种的；半纯种的
entries.definition_en: (of an animal) having one purebred parent and one non-purebred parent
entries.example_cn: 他们养了一只半纯种的狗，它的母亲是纯种，父亲则不是。
entries.example_en: They raised a half-bred dog whose mother was purebred and whose father was not.

entries.definition_cn: 过时且带有贬义、冒犯性的称呼，指父母或祖先来自不同种族的人，尤指白人与美洲原住民的混血后代
entries.definition_en: a dated, derogatory, offensive term for a person of mixed racial ancestry, especially mixed White and Native American ancestry
entries.example_cn: half-breed 是一个过时且带有贬义的冒犯性词语，不应用来称呼混血人士。
entries.example_en: The dated, derogatory term half-breed is offensive and should not be used for a mixed-race person.

usage.label: dated; derogatory; offensive
usage.pattern: Avoid this slur in contemporary usage.

entries.definition_cn: （动物）混种的；杂交的；有不同品种血统的
entries.definition_en: having mixed ancestry from different breeds, including offspring with only one purebred parent
entries.example_cn: 这只混种狗的父母属于不同品种。
entries.example_en: This half-breed dog has parents of different breeds.

entries.definition_cn: 同父异母或同母异父的兄弟
entries.definition_en: a brother who has only one parent in common with you
entries.example_cn: 我的同父异母兄弟住在隔壁镇。
entries.example_en: My half-brother lives in the next town over.

entries.definition_cn: 对具有不同种族血统的人所用的冒犯性称呼
entries.definition_en: an offensive term for a person of mixed racial descent
entries.example_cn: half-caste 是对混血人士的冒犯性称呼，不应使用。
entries.example_en: The term half-caste is offensive and should not be used for a mixed-race person.

entries.definition_en: a period of fifty years
entries.example_cn: 这家公司已经经营了五十年。
entries.example_en: The company has been in business for a half-century.

entries.definition_cn: 因准备不足而产生的混乱
entries.definition_en: confusion resulting from lack of preparation
entries.example_cn: 团队在会议上的半吊子表现让每个人都感到尴尬。
entries.example_en: The team's half-cock performance at the meeting embarrassed everyone.

entries.definition_en: only partially alive; on the verge of death
entries.example_cn: 霜冻后，那株植物看起来半死不活的。
entries.example_en: The plant looked half-dead after the frost.

entries.definition_en: being one more than five
entries.example_cn: 这个食谱我们需要六个鸡蛋。
entries.example_en: We need a half-dozen eggs for this recipe.

entries.definition_en: describing a plant that is not fully evergreen
entries.example_cn: 花园里的灌木是半常绿的，冬天会掉一些叶子。
entries.example_en: The shrubs in this garden are half-evergreen, losing some leaves in winter.

entries.definition_en: a plant that is incompletely evergreen
entries.example_cn: 这种半常绿植物在冬季仍会保留一些叶子。
entries.example_en: This half-evergreen keeps some of its leaves through the winter.

entries.definition_en: (of plants) requiring protection from frost
entries.example_cn: 这些半耐寒的植物需要在第一次霜冻来临前搬进室内。
entries.example_en: These half-hardy plants need to be brought indoors before the first frost.

entries.definition_en: showing little interest or enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 他敷衍地道了歉，看起来并不真诚。
entries.example_en: He gave a half-hearted apology that didn't seem sincere.

entries.definition_en: without enthusiasm or effort
entries.example_cn: 她没什么热情，只是答应帮忙做这个项目。
entries.example_en: She half-heartedly agreed to help with the project.

entries.definition_en: a day when half the usual work or school day is a holiday
entries.example_cn: 学校宣布在节日当天放半天假。
entries.example_en: The school announced a half-holiday to celebrate the festival.

entries.definition_en: a period of time lasting thirty minutes
entries.example_cn: 会议安排了半小时。
entries.example_en: The meeting is scheduled for a half-hour.

entries.definition_en: every thirty minutes
entries.example_cn: 火车从车站每半小时发一班。
entries.example_en: The train runs half-hourly from the station.

entries.definition_en: occurring every half hour
entries.example_cn: 白天的公交车服务是每半小时一班。
entries.example_en: The bus service is half-hourly during the day.

entries.definition_en: only partly human
entries.example_cn: 这个角色被描述为半人半机器。
entries.example_en: The character is described as half-human and half-machine.

entries.definition_en: a hybrid of a human and some other creature
entries.example_cn: 在故事中，英雄与一个半人半兽的怪物战斗。
entries.example_en: In the story, the hero fights against a half-human monster.

entries.definition_en: a portrait showing the body from the waist up
entries.example_cn: 艺术家画了一幅女王的半身像。
entries.example_en: The artist painted a half-length portrait of the queen.

entries.definition_en: representing only the upper half of the body
entries.example_cn: 博物馆收藏了一系列仅表现上半身的雕像。
entries.example_en: The museum has a collection of half-length statues.

entries.definition_en: abridged to half its original length
entries.example_cn: 他们看了一部缩短至原长度一半的电影。
entries.example_en: They watched a half-length version of the movie.

entries.definition_en: the time required for something to fall to half its initial value, especially for half the atoms in a radioactive substance to disintegrate
entries.example_cn: 科学家测量放射性物质的半衰期。
entries.example_en: Scientists measure the half-life of radioactive materials.

entries.definition_en: a greyish light found at dawn, dusk, or in dimly lit interiors
entries.example_cn: 房间里充满了柔和的昏暗光线。
entries.example_en: The room was filled with a soft half-light.

entries.definition_cn: 旗帜降至旗杆顶部以下一段距离的位置；降半旗状态
entries.definition_en: a position some distance below the top of a mast to which a flag is lowered in mourning or to signal distress
entries.example_cn: 旗帜降半旗，以纪念那名阵亡的士兵。
entries.example_en: Flags were flown at half-mast to honor the fallen soldier.

entries.definition_cn: 处于上弦或下弦时、可见面有一半被照亮的月亮
entries.definition_en: the Moon at its first or last quarter, when half of its visible face is illuminated
entries.example_cn: 一轮半月悬在山丘上方。
entries.example_en: A half-moon hung above the hills.

entries.definition_cn: 指甲根部的月牙形区域
entries.definition_en: the crescent-shaped area at the base of a fingernail
entries.example_cn: 她注意到大拇指上有一个小小的月牙。
entries.example_en: She noticed a small half-moon on her thumb.

entries.definition_en: a small or short person, used disparagingly
entries.example_cn: 教练把那个矮小的球员叫作“小不点”。
entries.example_en: The coach called the short player a half-pint.

entries.definition_en: at half the normal cost
entries.example_cn: 学生可以半价购买这些票。
entries.example_en: Students can buy the tickets half-price.

entries.definition_en: a type of sculpture where the design projects from the background more than in low relief but less than in high relief
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展出了用大理石雕刻的古代半浮雕。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed ancient half-reliefs carved from marble.

entries.definition_cn: 同父异母或同母异父的姐妹
entries.definition_en: a sister who shares only one parent with you
entries.example_cn: 我的同父异母姐妹和我有不同的父亲。
entries.example_en: My half-sister and I have different fathers.

entries.definition_en: a position some distance below the top of a mast to which a flag is lowered in mourning or to signal distress
entries.example_cn: 旗帜降半旗以纪念阵亡的士兵。
entries.example_en: Flags were flown at half-staff to honor the fallen soldier.

entries.definition_en: a short vacation about halfway through a school term
entries.example_cn: 我们计划在期中假期去探望祖父母。
entries.example_en: We plan to visit our grandparents during the half-term break.

entries.definition_en: having exposed wood framing with spaces filled with masonry, as seen in Tudor architecture
entries.example_cn: 这座木筋墙房屋以黑色横梁衬托白色灰泥墙壁为特色。
entries.example_en: The half-timbered house featured black beams against white plaster walls.

entries.definition_en: having a structure with exposed wooden beams and spaces filled with brick or stone
entries.example_cn: 这个村庄以其木筋墙房屋而闻名。
entries.example_en: The village is famous for its half-timbered houses.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involving half the standard or customary time for an activity
entries.example_cn: 她是一名半时制学生，同时从事全职工作。
entries.example_en: She was a half-time student while working full-time.

entries.definition_en: at half the usual number of working hours
entries.example_cn: 我们上周按半工时工作。
entries.example_en: We worked half-time last week.

entries.definition_cn: 前部装有轮子、后部装有履带的车辆
entries.definition_en: a vehicle with wheels at the front and caterpillar tracks at the rear
entries.example_cn: 军队使用半履带车在崎岖地形上运输补给品。
entries.example_en: The army used half-tracks to transport supplies across rough terrain.

entries.definition_cn: 后部为履带、前部为轮子的
entries.definition_en: having caterpillar treads on the rear and wheels in front
entries.example_cn: 这种半履带车辆可以轻松通过深泥地。
entries.example_en: The half-track vehicle could move through deep mud easily.

entries.definition_en: a statement that is only partly true and is used to deceive people
entries.example_cn: 他对我说了关于他工作情况的半真半假的话，以掩盖他失业的事实。
entries.example_en: He told me a half-truth about his job to hide the fact that he was unemployed.

entries.definition_en: at or to the halfway point of a distance or period
entries.example_cn: 我们旅程已过半。
entries.example_en: We are half-way through the journey.

entries.definition_en: a stupid and incompetent person
entries.example_cn: 别听那个傻瓜的，他对这个主题一无所知。
entries.example_en: Don't listen to that half-wit; he knows nothing about the subject.

entries.definition_en: a person who has less than normal intelligence
entries.example_cn: 这个傻瓜犯了一个大家都看得出的错误。
entries.example_en: The half-wit made a mistake that everyone could see.

entries.definition_cn: 非常愚蠢或缺乏智慧的
entries.definition_en: very foolish or unintelligent
entries.example_cn: 称某人为“half-witted”是侮辱性地说对方非常愚蠢。
entries.example_en: Calling someone half-witted is an insulting way to say that they are very unintelligent.

entries.definition_en: happening or due to be paid twice in a year
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志是半年刊。
entries.example_en: The magazine is published half-yearly.

entries.definition_en: once every six months
entries.example_cn: 我们每半年开会一次以回顾进展。
entries.example_en: We meet half-yearly to review our progress.

entries.definition_en: a running back who plays the offensive halfback position in football
entries.example_cn: 半卫突破防线达阵得分。
entries.example_en: The halfback broke through the line for a touchdown.

entries.definition_en: the position of a back on a football team, generally smaller in size than a fullback
entries.example_cn: 教练决定将半卫移到外接手的位置。
entries.example_en: The coach decided to move the halfback to the wide receiver spot.

entries.definition_en: done without much interest, enthusiasm, or effort
entries.example_cn: 他半心半意地尝试修理引擎。
entries.example_en: He gave a halfhearted attempt at fixing the engine.

entries.definition_en: an old English coin worth half a penny
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一枚罕见的18世纪铜制半便士。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a rare copper halfpenny from the 18th century.

entries.definition_en: an intermission between the first and second half of a game
entries.example_cn: 教练利用中场休息的时间向队员们解释了新的战术。
entries.example_en: The coach used the halftime break to explain the new strategy.

entries.definition_cn: 用半调工艺制成的图像或印刷品
entries.definition_en: a picture or print made by the halftone process
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件罕见的19世纪半调印刷品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a rare halftone from the 19th century.

entries.definition_cn: 用于印刷复制插图的半调版
entries.definition_en: a halftone plate used to reproduce an illustration in print
entries.example_cn: 印刷工使用半调版来复制这幅插图。
entries.example_en: The printer used a halftone plate to reproduce the illustration.

entries.definition_en: at half the distance or at the middle point
entries.example_cn: 我们的旅程已经过半。
entries.example_en: We are halfway through the journey.

entries.definition_cn: 处于两极之间同等距离的
entries.definition_en: equally distant from two extremes
entries.example_cn: 温度处于冰点和沸点的正中间。
entries.example_en: The temperature was halfway between freezing and boiling.

entries.definition_cn: 处于两个极端之间的中间点
entries.definition_en: at a point midway between two extremes
entries.example_cn: 他的观点介于两种对立观点之间。
entries.example_en: His opinion was halfway between the two opposing views.

entries.definition_cn: 不完整的；只涉及一部分的
entries.definition_en: partial or incomplete
entries.example_cn: 他们对这个问题只提出了一个不完整的解决方案。
entries.example_en: They offered only a halfway solution to the problem.

entries.definition_en: a large flatfish native to the northern Atlantic or Pacific, one of the largest teleost fishes
entries.example_cn: 阿拉斯加的渔民常在深水区捕捞大比目鱼。
entries.example_en: Fishermen in Alaska often catch halibut in deep waters.

entries.definition_en: the lean meat of very large flatfish found in the Atlantic or Pacific
entries.example_cn: 厨师用新鲜的大比目鱼肉做了一道美味佳肴。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a delicious meal using fresh halibut.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound formed from a halogen and a metal or hydrogen
entries.example_cn: 氯化钠是食盐中常见的一种卤化物。
entries.example_en: Sodium chloride is a common halide found in table salt.

entries.definition_en: naturally occurring crystalline sodium chloride
entries.example_cn: 地质学家在沙漠中发现了岩盐矿藏。
entries.example_en: Geologists found halite deposits in the desert.

entries.definition_en: bad breath that smells unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 医生让他刷牙以治疗他的口臭。
entries.example_en: The doctor asked him to brush his teeth to cure his halitosis.

entries.definition_en: a corridor inside a building where rooms open out
entries.example_cn: 我们进客厅前把外套脱在走廊里。
entries.example_en: We dropped our coats in the hall before going into the living room.

entries.definition_en: a large room at the entrance of a building for greeting guests
entries.example_cn: 客人们被迎进了酒店的大厅。
entries.example_en: The guests were welcomed in the grand hall of the hotel.

entries.definition_en: a large building used for meetings or entertainment
entries.example_cn: 会议在市政厅举行。
entries.example_en: The conference was held in the town hall.

entries.definition_en: a large room used for parties or entertaining guests
entries.example_cn: 婚礼招待会在主厅举行。
entries.example_en: The wedding reception was held in the main hall.

entries.definition_en: a building at a university where students live
entries.example_cn: 许多学生住在大学宿舍里。
entries.example_en: Many students live in the university hall.

entries.definition_en: the large main room in a manor or castle
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在古堡的大厅里。
entries.example_en: They sat in the hall of the old castle.

entries.definition_en: a large building at a college or university for teaching or research
entries.example_cn: 科学教学楼位于图书馆旁边。
entries.example_en: The science hall is located next to the library.

entries.definition_en: a large and impressive house
entries.example_cn: 这家人搬到了乡下的一座宏伟宅邸。
entries.example_en: The family moved into a magnificent hall in the countryside.

entries.definition_cn: 哈利路亚（赞美上帝的欢呼或歌曲）
entries.definition_en: a shout or song of praise to God
entries.example_cn: 唱诗班在礼拜结束时唱起了哈利路亚。
entries.example_en: The choir sang hallelujah at the end of the service.

entries.definition_en: a distinctive characteristic or attribute of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 守时是她职业工作的显著特征。
entries.example_en: Punctuality is a hallmark of her professional work.

entries.definition_en: a mark on an article of trade to indicate its origin and authenticity
entries.example_cn: 这个银杯上刻有伦敦铸币厂的印记。
entries.example_en: The silver cup bears the hallmark of the London mint.

entries.definition_en: a loud shout used to attract attention
entries.example_cn: 他大声呼喊以警告马匹他来了。
entries.example_en: He gave a halloo to warn the horses that he was coming.

entries.definition_en: to shout 'halloo' to greet someone or attract attention
entries.example_cn: 她穿过田野大声呼喊以引起狗的注意。
entries.example_en: She hallooed across the field to get the dog's attention.

entries.definition_en: to urge someone on by shouting
entries.example_cn: 教练大声呼喊催促跑者们加快速度。
entries.example_en: The coach hallooed at the runners to make them go faster.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: halloo someone to encourage or urge them

entries.definition_en: to make something holy through religious ceremonies
entries.example_cn: 牧师将在本周日祝圣新教堂。
entries.example_en: The priest will hallow the new church this Sunday.

entries.definition_en: worthy of religious veneration
entries.example_cn: 这座大教堂的神圣之地已被保存了几个世纪。
entries.example_en: The hallowed ground of the cathedral has been preserved for centuries.

entries.definition_en: to see, hear, or feel things that are not actually present
entries.example_cn: 睡眠不足导致他在走廊里看到了奇怪的身影。
entries.example_en: The lack of sleep caused him to hallucinate strange figures in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: a false perception of something that is not present
entries.example_cn: 这位病人看到了一条巨大的蛇的生动幻觉。
entries.example_en: The patient experienced a vivid hallucination of a giant snake.

entries.definition_cn: 人工智能系统自信地生成的错误回答或信息；幻觉
entries.definition_en: a confident but incorrect response or piece of information produced by an artificial intelligence system
entries.example_cn: 聊天机器人捏造了一篇并不存在的研究论文，产生了人工智能幻觉。
entries.example_en: The chatbot produced a hallucination by inventing a research paper that did not exist.

entries.definition_en: a mistaken or unfounded opinion
entries.example_cn: 他认为地球是平的这种信念是一种危险的谬见。
entries.example_en: His belief that the earth is flat is a dangerous hallucination.

entries.definition_en: an object perceived during a hallucinatory episode
entries.example_cn: 幻象出现在天空中，是一束亮光。
entries.example_en: The hallucination appeared as a bright light in the sky.

entries.definition_en: characterized by or resembling hallucinations
entries.example_cn: 那些幻觉般的光线似乎在他眼前舞动。
entries.example_en: The hallucinatory lights seemed to dance before his eyes.

entries.definition_en: a drug that causes hallucinations or changes in sensory perception
entries.example_cn: 这种致幻剂让用户看到了实际上并不存在的颜色。
entries.example_en: The hallucinogen caused the user to see colors that were not actually present.

entries.definition_en: capable of producing hallucinations
entries.example_cn: 这些致幻蘑菇被发现生长在森林里。
entries.example_en: The hallucinogenic mushrooms were found growing in the forest.

entries.definition_en: a hallucinogenic substance; a hallucinogen
entries.example_cn: 这名研究人员研究了致幻剂如何影响感知。
entries.example_en: The researcher studied how hallucinogenics affect perception.

entries.definition_en: the largest toe on the inner side of the foot
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了患者受伤的大脚趾。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the patient's injured hallux.

entries.definition_en: an interior passage or corridor onto which rooms open
entries.example_cn: 她把钥匙掉在了走廊里。
entries.example_en: She dropped her keys in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: the dry stalks of plants like beans, peas, or grasses used for thatching roofs or making bedding
entries.example_cn: 农民们收集禾秆来搭建谷仓的屋顶。
entries.example_en: Farmers gathered halm to thatch the roof of the barn.

entries.definition_en: a board game where players move their pieces into their opponent's bases
entries.example_cn: 他们花了一下午时间和朋友一起玩哈玛棋。
entries.example_en: They spent the afternoon playing halma with their friends.

entries.definition_en: a circle of light appearing around the sun or moon
entries.example_cn: 雨后月亮周围形成了一个美丽的光晕。
entries.example_en: A beautiful halo formed around the moon after the rain.

entries.definition_en: a circle of light drawn around the head of a saint in art
entries.example_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位头顶金色光环的圣人。
entries.example_en: The painting depicts a saint with a golden halo above his head.

entries.definition_cn: （天体周围的）弥散光环或区域
entries.definition_en: a diffuse cloud or region surrounding an astronomical object
entries.example_cn: 一个微弱的气体光环环绕着这个星系。
entries.example_en: A faint halo of gas surrounds the galaxy.

entries.definition_cn: 属于盐杆菌属、生活在盐分饱和或近饱和水中的嗜盐极端微生物
entries.definition_en: an extremophile of the genus Halobacterium that lives in water saturated or nearly saturated with salt
entries.example_cn: 科学家发现了一种在超高盐湖中繁衍生长的独特盐杆菌。
entries.example_en: Scientists discovered a unique halobacterium thriving in the hypersaline lake.

entries.definition_en: any element of group 17, including fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine, and tennessine
entries.example_cn: 氟是一种高活性的卤素，广泛应用于许多工业过程中。
entries.example_en: Fluorine is a highly reactive halogen used in many industrial processes.

entries.definition_en: a stable chemical compound used in fire extinguishers, which can deplete the ozone layer
entries.example_cn: 飞行员使用哈龙灭火器扑灭了驾驶舱内的火灾。
entries.example_en: The pilot used a halon extinguisher to put out the fire in the cockpit.

entries.definition_en: a powerful tranquilizer used to treat psychotic disorders and Tourette's syndrome
entries.example_cn: 医生开了抗精神病药来治疗患者严重的症状。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed haloperidol to manage the patient's severe symptoms.

entries.definition_en: a volatile, nonflammable liquid anesthetic used to induce general anesthesia during surgery
entries.example_cn: 麻醉师给病人使用了氟烷。
entries.example_en: The anesthesiologist administered halothane to the patient.

entries.definition_en: come to a halt, stop moving
entries.example_cn: 火车在下一站停下了。
entries.example_en: The train halted at the next station.

entries.definition_en: cause to come to an abrupt stop
entries.example_cn: 警察拦下了那辆超速的汽车。
entries.example_en: The police officer halted the speeding car.

entries.definition_en: stop from happening or developing
entries.example_cn: 他们设法阻止了疾病的传播。
entries.example_en: They managed to halt the spread of the disease.

entries.definition_en: an interruption or temporary suspension of progress or movement
entries.example_cn: 由于天气恶劣，施工暂停了。
entries.example_en: There was a halt in construction work because of bad weather.

entries.definition_en: the state of inactivity following an interruption
entries.example_cn: 谈判陷入了长时间的停顿。
entries.example_en: There was a long halt in the negotiations.

entries.definition_en: archaic and obsolete: lame or limping in the feet or legs
entries.example_cn: 那名跛足的骑士一瘸一拐地走向城门。
entries.example_en: The halt knight limped toward the gate.

entries.definition_en: the event of something ending
entries.example_cn: 项目的结束出乎意料。
entries.example_en: The halt of the project was unexpected.

entries.definition_en: stop the flow of a liquid
entries.example_cn: 大坝是为了阻断河流的流动而建的。
entries.example_en: The dam was built to halt the flow of the river.

entries.definition_en: a piece of equipment made of rope or canvas that is placed on a horse's head to control it
entries.example_cn: 骑手在牵马出马厩前调整了皮革马笼头。
entries.example_en: The rider adjusted the leather halter before leading the horse out of the stable.

entries.definition_en: a woman's top that fastens behind the back and neck, leaving the back and arms uncovered
entries.example_cn: 她在聚会上穿了一件黑色露背露臂上衣。
entries.example_en: She wore a black halter at the party.

entries.definition_en: a rope used by an executioner to hang a condemned person
entries.example_cn: 行刑前，被判刑的男子被绑在绞索上。
entries.example_en: The condemned man was tied to the halter before the execution.

entries.definition_en: one of the small, undeveloped hind wings found on some flies, which help them stay balanced while flying.
entries.example_cn: 平衡棒帮助苍蝇在快速飞行时保持稳定。
entries.example_en: The halter helps the fly maintain stability during rapid flight.

entries.definition_en: to put a halter on
entries.example_cn: 农夫给驴套上笼头后把它牵到牧场。
entries.example_en: The farmer haltered the donkey before leading it to the pasture.

entries.definition_en: to stop someone or something from moving freely or continuing forward.
entries.example_cn: 警察不得不拦下那辆车，却无法阻止那名超速的司机。
entries.example_en: The police had to halt the car, but they could not halter the speeding driver.

entries.definition_cn: 因情感压力而支离破碎或断续的
entries.definition_en: fragmentary or halting from emotional strain
entries.example_cn: 她断断续续地解释事故，显露出内心的痛苦。
entries.example_en: Her halting explanation of the accident revealed how distressed she was.

entries.definition_en: disabled in the feet or legs
entries.example_cn: 那只腿脚不便的狗艰难地爬上楼梯。
entries.example_en: The halting dog struggled to walk up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not smooth or continuous
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子用外语断断续续地说话。
entries.example_en: The child spoke haltingly in a foreign language.

entries.definition_en: divide by two; divide into halves
entries.example_cn: 我们决定将儿童票的价格减半。
entries.example_en: We decided to halve the price of the tickets for the children.

entries.definition_cn: 在高尔夫比洞赛中以与对手相同的杆数打平一个洞
entries.definition_en: in golf match play, to tie a hole by taking the same number of strokes as one's opponent
entries.example_cn: 两名选手经过一场漫长而激烈的较量后以相同的杆数打平了最后一洞。
entries.example_en: The two players halved the final hole after a long and closely fought contest.

entries.definition_en: a rope used to raise or lower a sail or flag
entries.example_cn: 水手爬上桅杆去调整升降索。
entries.example_en: The sailor climbed the mast to adjust the halyard.

entries.definition_en: meat from the thigh or buttock of a hog, usually cured or smoked
entries.example_cn: 我买了一些火腿夹在三明治里。
entries.example_en: I bought some ham to put on the sandwiches.

entries.definition_en: a person who holds a license to operate amateur radio
entries.example_cn: 那位业余无线电操作员与另一个国家的电台进行了通信。
entries.example_en: The ham radio operator communicated with a station in another country.

entries.definition_en: an actor who performs in an exaggerated and unskilled manner
entries.example_cn: 评论家因其夸张的表演称主演是个蹩脚演员。
entries.example_en: The critic called the lead actor a ham for his exaggerated performance.

entries.definition_en: to act in an exaggerated and unnatural way
entries.example_cn: 他在试镜时夸张表演以给导演留下深刻印象。
entries.example_en: He hammed it up during the audition to impress the director.

entries.definition_en: lacking physical movement skills, especially with the hands
entries.example_cn: 他笨手笨脚地试图修理那个精密的装置。
entries.example_en: He gave a ham-fisted attempt at fixing the delicate mechanism.

entries.definition_cn: 非正式用语，笼统指缺乏技能或能力的；不称职的
entries.definition_en: informal, broadly lacking skill or competence
entries.example_cn: 他笨拙无能的管理导致几名优秀员工离职。
entries.example_en: His ham-fisted management caused several talented employees to leave.

entries.definition_en: lacking skill in using one's hands
entries.example_cn: 他修电脑时笨手笨脚的。
entries.example_en: He is ham-handed at fixing computers.

entries.definition_en: the state of being clumsy or awkward, especially in handling things
entries.example_cn: 他笨手笨脚的，结果打碎了那个精致的花瓶。
entries.example_en: His ham-handedness caused him to drop and break the delicate vase.

entries.definition_en: the character flaw or error of a tragic hero that leads to their downfall
entries.example_cn: 傲慢是最终导致俄狄浦斯毁灭的悲剧缺陷。
entries.example_en: Hubris was the hamartia that ultimately caused Oedipus's ruin.

entries.definition_en: a benign growth in an organ that looks like a tumor but is caused by abnormal development
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出患者肺部有一个错构瘤。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed a hamartoma in the patient's lung.

entries.definition_en: a wrist bone located in line with the fourth and fifth fingers
entries.example_cn: 骨折后，外科医生检查了患者的小钩骨。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the patient's hamate bone after the fracture.

entries.definition_en: a sandwich consisting of a fried cake of minced beef served on a bun
entries.example_cn: 我想要一个加奶酪的汉堡包。
entries.example_en: I would like a hamburger with cheese.

entries.definition_en: beef that has been ground
entries.example_cn: 这道食谱需要一磅绞碎的牛肉。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for a pound of hamburger.

entries.definition_en: the patty used in a hamburger sandwich
entries.example_cn: 我点了一块不带面包的汉堡肉饼。
entries.example_en: I ordered a hamburger patty without the bun.

entries.definition_cn: 挽具鞍木；挽马颈圈两侧用来固定挽索的弧形支架
entries.definition_en: a curved metal bar attached to a horse's collar to hold the traces
entries.example_cn: 农夫在将犁连接到马身上之前，调整了挽马的挽具。
entries.example_en: The farmer adjusted the hames on the draft horse before attaching the plow.

entries.definition_en: a community of people smaller than a village
entries.example_cn: 那个古老的小村庄位于两座山之间的山谷里。
entries.example_en: The old hamlet is located in the valley between the two mountains.

entries.definition_en: a settlement smaller than a town
entries.example_cn: 游客经常在小定居点购买当地手工艺品。
entries.example_en: Visitors often stop at the hamlet to buy local crafts.

entries.definition_en: a hand tool with a heavy rigid head and a handle; used to deliver an impulsive force by striking
entries.example_cn: 她拿起锤子来修理架子。
entries.example_en: She picked up the hammer to fix the shelf.

entries.definition_cn: 枪锁中撞击底火帽的部件
entries.definition_en: the part of a gunlock that strikes the percussion cap when the trigger is pulled
entries.example_cn: 击锤击中了底火帽，枪发射了。
entries.example_en: The hammer struck the cap, firing the gun.

entries.definition_en: a striker that is covered in felt and that causes the piano strings to vibrate
entries.example_cn: 钢琴琴槌击打琴弦发出音符。
entries.example_en: The piano hammer hit the strings to produce a note.

entries.definition_en: a light drumstick with a rounded head that is used to strike such percussion instruments as chimes, kettledrums, marimbas, glockenspiels, etc.
entries.example_cn: 音乐家用槌演奏木琴。
entries.example_en: The musician used a hammer to play the xylophone.

entries.definition_en: beat with or as if with a hammer
entries.example_cn: 他把钉子敲进了木头里。
entries.example_en: He hammered the nail into the wood.

entries.definition_en: create by hammering
entries.example_cn: 金属被敲打成了薄片。
entries.example_en: The metal was hammered into a thin sheet.

entries.definition_en: a heavy metal sphere attached to a flexible wire; used in the hammer throw
entries.example_cn: 运动员用力投掷链球。
entries.example_en: The athlete threw the hammer with great force.

entries.definition_en: the ossicle attached to the eardrum
entries.example_cn: 锤骨是中耳中的三块小骨头之一。
entries.example_en: The hammer is one of the three small bones in the middle ear.

entries.definition_en: shaped or worked with a hammer, often showing marks left by the hammer
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子是用一块整橡木锤打而成的。
entries.example_en: The table was hammered from a single piece of solid oak.

entries.definition_cn: 一种中等体型、头部呈扁平锤状的鲨鱼，分布于世界各地的温暖水域
entries.definition_en: a medium-sized shark with a flattened, hammer-shaped head found in warm waters worldwide
entries.example_cn: 潜水员发现一只锤头鲨在珊瑚礁附近游动。
entries.example_en: The divers spotted a hammerhead swimming near the coral reef.

entries.definition_en: the part of a hammer that strikes
entries.example_cn: 锤头发出响亮的铿锵声，击中了钉子。
entries.example_en: The hammerhead struck the nail with a loud clang.

entries.definition_en: a stupid person
entries.example_cn: 别再叫他愚蠢的人；他很聪明。
entries.example_en: Stop calling him a hammerhead; he is very smart.

entries.definition_en: the act of pounding something by delivering repeated heavy blows
entries.example_cn: 房子因暴风雨的持续猛击而受损。
entries.example_en: The house was damaged by the constant hammering of the storm.

entries.definition_en: a heavy defeat (slang)
entries.example_cn: 主队在决赛中遭遇惨败。
entries.example_en: The home team suffered a hammering in the final.

entries.definition_en: a wrestling hold in which the opponent's arm is twisted up behind their back
entries.example_cn: 摔跤手通过扭动身体摆脱了背锁。
entries.example_en: The wrestler escaped the hammerlock by twisting his body.

entries.definition_en: poor acting by a ham actor
entries.example_cn: 这位演员的拙劣表演毁掉了那场严肃的戏。
entries.example_en: The actor's hamming ruined the serious scene.

entries.definition_en: a hanging bed of canvas or rope netting (usually suspended between two trees); swings easily
entries.example_cn: 他们在棕榈树下睡在吊床上。
entries.example_en: They slept in a hammock under the palm trees.

entries.definition_en: a tract of land thickly wooded and usually covered with bushes and vines (US)
entries.example_cn: 徒步者穿过了一片灌木和藤蔓丛生的林地。
entries.example_en: The hikers crossed a wooded hammock covered with bushes and vines.

entries.definition_en: affectedly dramatic; overacted
entries.example_cn: 他做作的表演让观众发笑而不是哭泣。
entries.example_en: His hammy performance made the audience laugh instead of cry.

entries.definition_en: to prevent the progress or free movement of something
entries.example_cn: 恶劣天气阻碍了救援队前往被困徒步者的努力。
entries.example_en: Bad weather hampered the rescue team's efforts to reach the stranded hikers.

entries.definition_en: to put someone or something at a disadvantage
entries.example_cn: 资金不足使公司难以创新。
entries.example_en: The lack of funding hampered the company's ability to innovate.

entries.definition_en: a basket, typically with a cover, used for carrying goods
entries.example_cn: 她把野餐用品装进了一个柳条提篮里。
entries.example_en: She packed the picnic supplies into a wicker hamper.

entries.definition_en: a shackle, fetter, or other restraint (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 囚犯挣扎着摆脱那副把他的脚踝锁在一起的铁镣。
entries.example_en: The prisoner struggled against the iron hamper that held his ankles together.

entries.definition_en: a small rodent with a short tail and large cheek pouches used for storing food
entries.example_cn: 这只仓鼠正忙着把种子塞进它的颊囊里。
entries.example_en: The hamster was busy stuffing its cheek pouches with seeds.

entries.definition_en: make ineffective or powerless
entries.example_cn: 新规定削弱了公司快速扩张的能力。
entries.example_en: The new regulations hamstring the company's ability to expand quickly.

entries.definition_cn: 通过割断腿后侧的肌腱使（人或动物）残废
entries.definition_en: cripple by cutting the hamstring
entries.example_cn: 有人故意割断了这匹马后腿的肌腱，使它不得不退役。
entries.example_en: The horse was deliberately hamstrung when someone cut the tendons in its hind legs, and it had to be retired.

entries.definition_cn: 大腿后侧的肌肉或肌腱之一
entries.definition_en: one of the muscles or tendons at the back of the thigh
entries.example_cn: 赛跑后，跑步者感到大腿后侧肌腱一阵剧痛。
entries.example_en: The runner felt a sharp pain in his hamstring after the race.

entries.definition_en: the part of the arm at the end of which the fingers are attached
entries.example_cn: 她挥手打招呼。
entries.example_en: She waved her hand to say hello.

entries.definition_en: a position on the side of something
entries.example_cn: 门在左侧。
entries.example_en: The door is on the left hand side.

entries.definition_en: the cards held by a player in a card game
entries.example_cn: 在这局游戏中我手牌很好。
entries.example_en: I have a good hand in this game.

entries.definition_en: the ability to do something well
entries.example_cn: 她擅长绘画。
entries.example_en: She has a good hand at painting.

entries.definition_en: something written or drawn by hand
entries.example_cn: 这封信是亲笔写的。
entries.example_en: The letter was written by hand.

entries.definition_en: to give something to someone so that they have it or take care of it
entries.example_cn: 请把书递给我。
entries.example_en: Please hand me the book.

entries.definition_en: a person who works for wages on a farm or ranch
entries.example_cn: 农场雇了一名新雇工帮忙收割。
entries.example_en: The farm hired a new hand to help with the harvest.

entries.definition_en: to lead or guide someone somewhere
entries.example_cn: 他会把你带到队伍前面。
entries.example_en: He will hand you to the front of the line.

entries.definition_en: small and light enough to be operated while you hold it in your hands
entries.example_cn: 这台相机是手持设备，可以轻松放进口袋。
entries.example_en: This camera is a hand-held device that fits easily in your pocket.

entries.definition_cn: 手持式电子设备，如个人数字助理或掌上游戏机
entries.definition_en: a small electronic device, such as a personal digital assistant or video game console, designed to be held in the hands
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在旅途中用掌上游戏机玩游戏。
entries.example_en: The children played a game on a handheld during the journey.

entries.definition_en: together and in close cooperation
entries.example_cn: 两国正携手合作，开发清洁能源。
entries.example_en: The two countries are working hand in hand to develop clean energy.

entries.definition_en: clasping each other's hands
entries.example_cn: 孩子们手拉手穿过公园。
entries.example_en: The children walked hand-in-hand through the park.

entries.definition_en: clothes that have been outgrown and given to someone else to wear
entries.example_cn: 她穿着姐姐的旧连衣裙去参加聚会。
entries.example_en: She wore her sister's hand-me-down dress to the party.

entries.definition_en: passed from one person to another
entries.example_cn: 他弹着父亲给他的那把传下来的吉他。
entries.example_en: He played the hand-me-down guitar his father gave him.

entries.definition_en: worked or controlled by hand
entries.example_cn: 这台机器是手动的，你需要转动曲柄才能启动它。
entries.example_en: This machine is hand-operated, so you need to turn the crank to start it.

entries.definition_en: pick personally and very carefully
entries.example_cn: 经理将亲自挑选参加最终面试的候选人。
entries.example_en: The manager will hand-pick the candidates for the final interview.

entries.definition_en: fighting at very close range
entries.example_cn: 士兵们展开了肉搏战。
entries.example_en: The soldiers engaged in hand-to-hand combat.

entries.definition_en: having only enough money to buy the most basic necessities
entries.example_cn: 失业后，他过着勉强糊口的生活。
entries.example_en: After losing his job, he lived a hand-to-mouth existence.

entries.definition_en: to wash clothes or other items by hand instead of using a washing machine
entries.example_cn: 我更喜欢手洗我的丝绸衬衫以保持它们的良好状态。
entries.example_en: I prefer to hand-wash my silk shirts to keep them in good condition.

entries.definition_en: a bag used by women to carry personal items
entries.example_cn: 她把钥匙和钱包放进了手提包里。
entries.example_en: She put her keys and wallet in her handbag.

entries.definition_cn: 手球运动：两队各由七名球员组成，设法将球投进对方球门
entries.definition_en: a team sport in which two teams of seven players try to throw a ball into the opposing team’s goal
entries.example_cn: 手球比赛由两支各有七名球员的球队进行。
entries.example_en: Handball is played with two teams of seven players.

entries.definition_en: a game played in a walled court or against a single wall by two or four players who strike a rubber ball with their hands
entries.example_cn: 他们在体育馆里打手球。
entries.example_en: They played handball in the gymnasium.

entries.definition_en: a small rubber ball used in the game of handball
entries.example_cn: 裁判将手球重新投入比赛。
entries.example_en: The referee threw the handball back into play.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指足球中）用手或手臂非法触球
entries.definition_en: to illegally touch the ball with the hand or arm, especially in football (soccer)
entries.example_cn: 防守队员在禁区内用手触球，因此裁判判罚了点球。
entries.example_en: The defender handballed in the penalty area, so the referee awarded a penalty.

entries.definition_en: a container that is usually woven and has handles
entries.example_cn: 她用一个大手提篮装着杂货。
entries.example_en: She carried her groceries in a large handbasket.

entries.definition_en: a small bell held in the hand and rung by striking it
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在教堂礼拜期间摇响了手铃。
entries.example_en: The children rang the handbells during the church service.

entries.definition_en: a loose printed sheet distributed by hand, often an advertisement
entries.example_cn: 该公司分发数千份传单以推广新产品。
entries.example_en: The company distributed thousands of handbills to promote the new product.

entries.definition_en: a short book that gives specific information about a subject or place
entries.example_cn: 公司为新员工发行了手册。
entries.example_en: The company issued a handbook for new employees.

entries.definition_cn: 手摇铁路车；铁路手摇车
entries.definition_en: a small railway car propelled by a hand-operated pumping mechanism
entries.example_cn: 维修人员使用铁路手摇车检查偏远路段的轨道。
entries.example_en: The maintenance crew used a handcar to inspect the tracks in the remote section.

entries.definition_en: a cart designed to be pushed or pulled by hand
entries.example_cn: 他们将沉重的箱子装上手推车，以便在院子里搬运。
entries.example_en: They loaded the heavy boxes onto the handcart to move them across the yard.

entries.definition_cn: 一声拍手，尤指表示赞许
entries.definition_en: a single clap of the hands, especially to show approval
entries.example_cn: 她拍了一下手以表示赞许。
entries.example_en: She gave a handclap to show her approval.

entries.definition_en: the act of grasping and shaking someone's hand to acknowledge an introduction or agree on a contract
entries.example_cn: 他们在签署条约前有力地握了握手。
entries.example_en: They exchanged a firm handclasp before signing the treaty.

entries.definition_en: an object made by hand
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件精美的陶土手工艺品。
entries.example_en: The museum displays a beautiful handcraft made of clay.

entries.definition_en: to make something using your hands
entries.example_cn: 她决定亲手为朋友制作一份礼物。
entries.example_en: She decided to handcraft a gift for her friend.

entries.definition_en: shackle that consists of a metal loop that can be locked around the wrist; usually used in pairs
entries.example_cn: 警察在嫌疑人的每只手腕上戴了一只手铐。
entries.example_en: The police officer put a handcuff on each of the suspect's wrists.

entries.definition_en: confine or restrain with or as if with manacles or handcuffs
entries.example_cn: 登机前，安保人员不得不将那位不守规矩的乘客用手铐铐住。
entries.example_en: The security guard had to handcuff the unruly passenger before boarding.

entries.definition_cn: 有某种或一定数量手的（尤用于复合词）
entries.definition_en: having a specified kind or number of hands, especially in compounds
entries.example_cn: 这座三针钟清楚地显示着时间。
entries.example_en: The three-handed clock showed the time clearly.

entries.definition_en: the quality of preferring to use one hand over the other
entries.example_cn: 这项研究检查了参与者的用手偏好。
entries.example_en: The study examined the handedness of the participants.

entries.definition_cn: （不对称物体的）手性，即物体与其镜像的区别
entries.definition_en: the property of an asymmetric object that makes it different from its mirror image
entries.example_cn: 左手手套的手性意味着它不能当作右手手套使用。
entries.example_en: The handedness of a left glove means that it cannot be used as a right glove.

entries.definition_en: a small number or amount of something
entries.example_cn: 只有少数人参加了会议。
entries.example_en: Only a handful of people attended the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the quantity that can be held in the hand
entries.example_cn: 她从沙滩上抓起一把沙子。
entries.example_en: She picked up a handful of sand from the beach.

entries.definition_en: a handle or part of an object designed to be held in the hand
entries.example_cn: 这辆新自行车有一个舒适的橡胶手柄。
entries.example_en: The new bicycle has a comfortable rubber handgrip.

entries.definition_en: a gun designed to be held and fired with one hand
entries.example_cn: 警察拔出他的手枪以保护平民。
entries.example_en: The police officer drew his handgun to protect the civilians.

entries.definition_en: small and light enough to be operated while you hold it in your hands
entries.example_cn: 这款新智能手机是一款轻便的手持设备。
entries.example_en: The new smartphone is a lightweight handheld device.

entries.definition_cn: 可供抓握以支撑身体的突出物或抓握处
entries.definition_en: a projection or feature that one can hold onto for support
entries.example_cn: 登山者在陡峭的岩壁上寻找一个牢固的抓握处。
entries.example_en: The climber searched for a secure handhold on the steep rock face.

entries.definition_cn: 舞蹈中舞者彼此握手的方式
entries.definition_en: the way dancers hold each other's hands during a dance
entries.example_cn: 教练示范了起始舞步的正确握手姿势。
entries.example_en: The instructor demonstrated the proper handhold for the opening step.

entries.definition_en: something immaterial that interferes with or delays action or progress
entries.example_cn: 缺乏资金是我们项目的主要障碍。
entries.example_en: Lack of money was a major handicap to our project.

entries.definition_en: an advantage given to a competitor to equalize chances of winning
entries.example_cn: 实力较弱的选手获得了十杆的让步。
entries.example_en: The weaker player received a handicap of ten strokes.

entries.definition_cn: 身体或心理上的障碍；残疾
entries.definition_en: a physical or mental condition that limits a person's ability to perform
entries.example_cn: 这位运动员克服了残疾赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The athlete overcame his handicap to win the race.

entries.definition_en: to put at a disadvantage
entries.example_cn: 新规则使小企业处于不利地位。
entries.example_en: The new rules handicap small businesses.

entries.definition_en: to injure permanently
entries.example_cn: 那次摔伤使他无法再快速奔跑。
entries.example_en: The fall handicapped his ability to run fast.

entries.definition_cn: （赛马等）预测胜负并设定赔率
entries.definition_en: to attempt to forecast the winner and assign odds for a contestant
entries.example_cn: 比赛开始前他们为马匹预测胜负并设定赔率。
entries.example_en: They handicap the horses before the race starts.

entries.definition_en: having the total or partial absence of bodily or mental functions
entries.example_cn: 这座建筑对残疾人完全无障碍。
entries.example_en: The building is fully accessible for the handicapped.

entries.definition_en: people collectively who are physically disabled or crippled
entries.example_cn: 该组织为残疾人提供服务。
entries.example_en: The organization provides services for the handicapped.

entries.definition_cn: 让分或赔率制定者，尤指赛马比赛中的此类人员
entries.definition_en: a person who assigns handicaps or sets betting odds, especially for horse races
entries.example_cn: 赔率制定者在设定比赛赔率前为每匹马评定了等级。
entries.example_en: The handicapper assigned each horse a rating before setting the race's betting odds.

entries.definition_en: an object made by hand labor
entries.example_cn: 她在当地市场买了一件精美的手工艺品。
entries.example_en: She bought a beautiful handicraft at the local market.

entries.definition_en: a craft requiring skillful hands
entries.example_cn: 陶艺是这个地区的一项传统手艺。
entries.example_en: Pottery is a traditional handicraft in this region.

entries.definition_en: with no difficulty
entries.example_cn: 该队在决赛中毫不费力地击败了对手。
entries.example_en: The team handily defeated their opponents in the final match.

entries.definition_en: in a convenient manner
entries.example_cn: 你可以方便地从移动设备访问这些文件。
entries.example_en: You can handily access the files from your mobile device.

entries.definition_en: skillfulness with the hands
entries.example_cn: 她手巧，用工具很熟练，是个很好的帮手。
entries.example_en: Her handiness with tools made her a great helper.

entries.definition_cn: 在需要时随手可得的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being at hand when needed
entries.example_cn: 维修时备有备用零件很方便，节省了时间。
entries.example_en: The handiness of having spare parts saved time during the repair.

entries.definition_en: something made or done by hand
entries.example_cn: 这精美的刺绣是一件出色的手工制品。
entries.example_en: The intricate embroidery was a piece of fine handiwork.

entries.definition_cn: 通常为方形的布，用于擦脸、眼睛、鼻子或手，也可作颈部饰物
entries.definition_en: a usually square piece of cloth for wiping the face, eyes, nose, or hands, or worn as a neck accessory
entries.example_cn: 她伸手拿手帕擦眼泪。
entries.example_en: She reached for a handkerchief to wipe her tears.

entries.definition_en: a part of an object that you hold to use or move it
entries.example_cn: 这个手提箱有一个长把手。
entries.example_en: The suitcase has a long handle.

entries.definition_en: to be responsible for dealing with a situation or problem
entries.example_cn: 她负责处理所有客户投诉。
entries.example_en: She handles all customer complaints.

entries.definition_en: to touch, lift, or hold something with your hands
entries.example_cn: 请小心拿这个玻璃杯。
entries.example_en: Please handle the glass carefully.

entries.definition_en: to deal with someone in a particular way
entries.example_cn: 你应该耐心地对待孩子。
entries.example_en: You should handle children with patience.

entries.definition_en: to deal with a difficult situation successfully
entries.example_cn: 他很有技巧地妥善处理了这场危机。
entries.example_en: He handled the crisis with great skill.

entries.definition_en: to express or deal with something through words or art
entries.example_cn: 这部戏剧很好地表现了战争的主题。
entries.example_en: The play handles the theme of war very well.

entries.definition_cn: （俚语）用作身份标识的名字或绰号，尤指在网上或无线电中使用的名字。
entries.definition_en: (slang) A name or nickname used as an identifier, especially online or over the radio.
entries.example_cn: 你的网名是什么？
entries.example_en: What is your online handle?

entries.definition_cn: 训练、牵引并展示（马或狗）
entries.definition_en: train, lead, and show a horse or dog
entries.example_cn: 训练师将在场地内牵引并展示这匹马。
entries.example_en: The trainer will handle the horse in the ring.

entries.definition_cn: 在某一时期或某一赛事中下注的总金额。
entries.definition_en: The total amount of money wagered during a particular period or on a particular event.
entries.example_cn: 这家赌场每天的赌注总额达到数百万美元。
entries.example_en: The casino's daily handle reached several million dollars.

entries.definition_en: the curved bar used to steer a bicycle or motorcycle
entries.example_cn: 他调整了车把以使骑行更舒适。
entries.example_en: He adjusted the handlebar to make the ride more comfortable.

entries.definition_en: having a handle attached to it
entries.example_cn: 那个带把手的行李箱在火车上很容易携带。
entries.example_en: The handled suitcase was easy to carry on the train.

entries.definition_en: an agent who manages or deals with something or someone
entries.example_cn: 她聘请了一位法律代理人来处理她的案子。
entries.example_en: She hired a legal handler to manage her case.

entries.definition_en: a person who trains or exhibits animals
entries.example_cn: 驯兽员把狮子领上了舞台。
entries.example_en: The handler led the lion onto the stage.

entries.definition_en: a person in charge of training an athlete or a team
entries.example_cn: 这位新教练将带领游泳队备战奥运会。
entries.example_en: The new handler will train the swim team for the Olympics.

entries.definition_en: having no hands or lacking hands
entries.example_cn: 这台机器人采用了无手设计以确保安全。
entries.example_en: The robot had a handless design for safety.

entries.definition_cn: （古）笨手笨脚的；手部动作不灵活的
entries.definition_en: obsolete: awkward or unskilled, especially in using the hands
entries.example_cn: 我们喝一小杯酒图个吉利；我的这个笨手笨脚的伙计一做好肉片，我们就用餐，随后像绅士一样玩几局牌。
entries.example_en: We’ll take a dram for luck, and as soon as this handless man of mine has the collops ready, we’ll dine and take a hand at the cartes as gentlemen should.

entries.definition_en: a fishing line managed principally by hand
entries.example_cn: 他们用手钓线捕鱼，而不是用网。
entries.example_en: They caught the fish with a handline instead of a net.

entries.definition_en: a line used for climbing steep sections with limited protection
entries.example_cn: 攀登者在上升前将绳索固定在攀岩手线上。
entries.example_en: The climber secured the rope to the handline before ascending.

entries.definition_en: manual (or mechanical) carrying or moving or delivering or working with something
entries.example_cn: 搬运易碎物品需要小心。
entries.example_en: The handling of fragile items requires care.

entries.definition_en: the action of touching with the hands (or the skillful use of the hands) or by the use of mechanical means
entries.example_cn: 这台机器需要特殊操作。
entries.example_en: The machine requires special handling.

entries.definition_en: the management of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 对危机的处理受到了赞扬。
entries.example_en: The handling of the crisis was praised.

entries.definition_cn: 销赃罪；涉及买卖赃物的犯罪行为
entries.definition_en: a criminal offence involving dealing in stolen goods
entries.example_cn: 销赃属于犯罪行为。
entries.example_en: Handling stolen goods is a criminal offence.

entries.definition_en: a loom that is powered by hand rather than by machinery
entries.example_cn: 工匠用传统的手织机编织了一块美丽的地毯。
entries.example_en: The artisan wove a beautiful rug on a traditional handloom.

entries.definition_en: made by hand or a hand process
entries.example_cn: 她买了一个完全手工制作的漂亮花瓶。
entries.example_en: She bought a beautiful vase that was entirely handmade.

entries.definition_cn: 手工艺品；手工制作的物品
entries.definition_en: an art or craft object made by hand
entries.example_cn: 这个市场出售手工艺品，包括篮子和陶器。
entries.example_en: The market sells handmades, including baskets and pottery.

entries.definition_en: a personal maid or female attendant
entries.example_cn: 在那座古老的城堡里，贴身女仆服侍着女主人。
entries.example_en: In the old castle, the handmaid served the lady of the house.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that is subordinate to or serves another
entries.example_cn: 这个部门成了那个更大政治组织的附属机构。
entries.example_en: The department became a handmaid to the larger political organization.

entries.definition_en: a personal maid or female attendant
entries.example_cn: 侍女为客人们端上了茶。
entries.example_en: The handmaiden served tea to the guests.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that helps achieve something, often in a subordinate role
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术是该公司成功的助手。
entries.example_en: The new technology was the handmaiden of the company's success.

entries.definition_cn: （美式橄榄球）交接球；一名球员将球交给队友的战术
entries.definition_en: a play in American football in which one player hands the ball to a teammate
entries.example_cn: 四分卫迅速将球交给跑卫。
entries.example_en: The quarterback made a quick handoff to the running back.

entries.definition_cn: 免费发放的印刷材料，如传单、宣传册或练习单
entries.definition_en: a printed sheet, leaflet, pamphlet, or worksheet given out free for information or a specific purpose
entries.example_cn: 讲师给每位学生发了一份概述课程要点的讲义。
entries.example_en: The lecturer gave each student a handout outlining the main points of the lesson.

entries.definition_en: an act of handing something out, especially free of charge
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构为无家可归者组织了衣物施舍活动。
entries.example_en: The charity organized a handout of warm clothes to the homeless.

entries.definition_en: a written statement given to journalists to provide information about an event
entries.example_cn: 媒体收到了关于新政府政策的新闻通稿。
entries.example_en: The press received a handout detailing the new government policies.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving up control, authority, or property to someone else
entries.example_cn: 向新政府移交权力是和平进行的。
entries.example_en: The handover of power to the new government was peaceful.

entries.definition_en: a railing at the side of a staircase or balcony to prevent people from falling
entries.example_cn: 爬陡峭的楼梯时，请小心握住扶手。
entries.example_en: Please hold the handrail carefully when you climb the steep stairs.

entries.definition_en: the number of workers available for a job
entries.example_cn: 工厂需要更多的人力才能按时完成工作。
entries.example_en: The factory needs more hands to finish the work on time.

entries.definition_en: the right to care for and control a child
entries.example_cn: 法院决定由母亲行使对孩子的监护权。
entries.example_en: The court decided that the mother would have the hands over the child.

entries.definition_en: very easy to achieve or win
entries.example_cn: 主队取得了轻而易举的胜利。
entries.example_en: It was a hands-down victory for the home team.

entries.definition_en: not involving participation or intervention
entries.example_cn: 经理对新项目采取了不干预的态度。
entries.example_en: The manager adopted a hands-off approach to the new project.

entries.definition_en: involving active participation
entries.example_cn: 该课程提供实验室里的亲身实践机会。
entries.example_en: The course offers hands-on experience in the laboratory.

entries.definition_en: a saw used with one hand for cutting wood
entries.example_cn: 木匠用手锯切割木材。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a handsaw to cut the timber.

entries.definition_en: a mobile phone
entries.example_cn: 这部手机可以利用附近基站的信号确定自己的位置。
entries.example_en: The handset can determine its position using signals from nearby base stations.

entries.definition_en: a telephone receiver with the mouthpiece and earpiece attached to a single handle
entries.example_cn: 他拿起听筒打电话。
entries.example_en: He picked up the handset to make a call.

entries.definition_en: made by sewing with a needle and thread rather than a machine
entries.example_cn: 这件夹克非常用心地手工缝制而成。
entries.example_en: This jacket is handsewn with great care.

entries.definition_en: the act of grasping and shaking someone's hand to greet them or agree to something
entries.example_cn: 他们在签订合同前有力地握了握手。
entries.example_en: They exchanged a firm handshake before signing the contract.

entries.definition_cn: 通信开始时两个设备之间为确保同步而进行的信号交换
entries.definition_en: an exchange of signals between two devices when communication begins to ensure synchronization
entries.example_cn: 数据传输前，这些设备会完成握手。
entries.example_en: The devices complete a handshake before data is transferred.

entries.definition_en: to perform a handshake with another device
entries.example_cn: 打印机在接收文件前会与电脑进行握手通信。
entries.example_en: The printer handshakes with the computer before receiving the file.

entries.definition_en: grasping and shaking a person's hand
entries.example_cn: 仪式在代表们正式握手后结束。
entries.example_en: The ceremony concluded with a formal handshaking between the delegates.

entries.definition_cn: 计算设备之间为建立通信连接而进行的信息交换
entries.definition_en: The exchange of information between computing devices to establish a communication connection.
entries.example_cn: 调制解调器完成握手后，文件传输才开始。
entries.example_en: The modems completed their handshaking before the file transfer began.

entries.definition_cn: 外貌令人愉悦，尤其是符合形式和比例的审美理想
entries.definition_en: pleasing in appearance especially by reason of conformity to ideals of form and proportion
entries.example_cn: 那座宏伟的建筑矗立在城市中心。
entries.example_en: The handsome building stood tall in the center of the city.

entries.definition_en: generous, often in a substantial amount
entries.example_cn: 他向慈善机构捐赠了一笔巨款。
entries.example_en: He made a handsome donation to the charity.

entries.definition_en: in a generously handsome manner
entries.example_cn: 公司大方地奖励了这位员工，以表彰他的杰出贡献。
entries.example_en: The company handsomely rewarded the employee for his outstanding contribution.

entries.definition_en: in an attractively handsome manner
entries.example_cn: 他盛装出席晚上的舞会，显得英俊潇洒。
entries.example_en: He was handsomely dressed for the evening gala.

entries.definition_en: the quality of having regular, well-defined facial features, especially in a man
entries.example_cn: 他棱角分明的下巴和清澈的眼睛显示出他的英俊。
entries.example_en: His handsomeness was evident in his sharp jawline and clear eyes.

entries.definition_cn: 用手撑地完成的翻腾动作
entries.definition_en: an acrobatic somersault performed with the hands placed on the ground
entries.example_cn: 这位体操运动员在平衡木上完成了一个困难的手翻动作。
entries.example_en: The gymnast performed a difficult handspring across the balance beam.

entries.definition_en: the act of supporting yourself by your hands alone in an upside-down position
entries.example_cn: 体操运动员在平衡木上做了一个完美的倒立。
entries.example_en: The gymnast performed a perfect handstand on the balance beam.

entries.definition_en: a liquid soap used for washing the hands
entries.example_cn: 她在浴室洗手池旁放着一瓶洗手液。
entries.example_en: She keeps a bottle of handwash beside the bathroom sink.

entries.definition_en: to wash clothes or other items by hand rather than using a washing machine
entries.example_cn: 因为面料很娇嫩，你必须轻柔地手洗。
entries.example_en: Because the fabric is delicate, you must handwash it gently.

entries.definition_en: a wheel that is operated by hand
entries.example_cn: 操作员使用控制面板上的手轮调节压力。
entries.example_en: The operator adjusted the pressure using the handwheel on the control panel.

entries.definition_en: a control consisting of a wheel whose rim serves as the handle for operating a part
entries.example_cn: 要拧紧阀门，请顺时针转动操纵轮。
entries.example_en: To tighten the valve, turn the handwheel clockwise.

entries.definition_en: work that is made by hand rather than by machine
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了精美的传统手工艺品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed beautiful examples of traditional handwork.

entries.definition_en: made by weaving on a loom operated by hand
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一组来自安第斯山脉的手工编织纺织品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a collection of handwoven textiles from the Andes.

entries.definition_en: to write something using a pen or pencil instead of a typewriter or computer
entries.example_cn: 请在表格上手写你的名字。
entries.example_en: Please handwrite your name on the form.

entries.definition_en: something written by hand
entries.example_cn: 这封信是用他独特的笔迹写成的。
entries.example_en: The letter was written in his distinctive handwriting.

entries.definition_en: the activity of writing by hand
entries.example_cn: 她更喜欢手写笔记而不是打字。
entries.example_en: She prefers handwriting her notes rather than typing them.

entries.definition_en: written by hand
entries.example_cn: 请用墨水手写填写表格。
entries.example_en: Please fill out the form in handwritten ink.

entries.definition_en: useful and convenient
entries.example_cn: 旅行时带手机非常方便。
entries.example_en: It is very handy to have a mobile phone when you are traveling.

entries.definition_en: easy to reach
entries.example_cn: 把剪刀放在容易拿到的地方，这样你就能很快找到它们。
entries.example_en: Keep the scissors in a handy place so you can find them quickly.

entries.definition_en: skillful with the hands
entries.example_cn: 她非常擅长修理损坏的家具。
entries.example_en: She is very handy at fixing broken furniture.

entries.definition_en: a man who is skilled at doing various odd jobs and small tasks
entries.example_cn: 我们请了一位杂工来修理漏水的龙头并粉刷墙壁。
entries.example_en: We hired a handyman to fix the leaky faucet and paint the walls.

usage.label: informal
usage.pattern: especially for building repairs and similar work

entries.definition_en: be suspended or hanging
entries.example_cn: 这幅画挂在墙上。
entries.example_en: The picture hangs on the wall.

entries.definition_en: cause to be hanging or suspended
entries.example_cn: 请把外套挂在钩子上。
entries.example_en: Please hang the coat on the hook.

entries.definition_en: let drop or droop
entries.example_cn: 她羞愧地垂下头。
entries.example_en: Her head hung low in shame.

entries.definition_en: kill by hanging
entries.example_cn: 这名罪犯因谋杀罪被绞死。
entries.example_en: The criminal was hanged for murder.

entries.definition_cn: 悬挂物；垂挂的一团东西
entries.definition_en: a mass of hanging material
entries.example_cn: 他们从一大片悬垂的岩石下方经过。
entries.example_en: They passed beneath a hang of rock.

entries.definition_en: the way a garment hangs
entries.example_cn: 这条裙子的垂坠方式很好看。
entries.example_en: This dress has a nice hang.

entries.definition_cn: 以某种方式落下或流动
entries.definition_en: fall or flow in a certain way
entries.example_cn: 水流成细线状落下。
entries.example_en: The water hung in a thin stream.

entries.definition_en: a gymnastic exercise performed on the rings or horizontal bar or parallel bars when the gymnast's weight is supported by the arms
entries.example_cn: 他擅长吊环运动。
entries.example_en: He is good at the hang.

entries.definition_en: an emotional preoccupation
entries.example_cn: 他害怕在公众面前讲话。
entries.example_en: He has a hang-up about speaking in public.

entries.definition_en: an unforeseen obstacle
entries.example_cn: 资金短缺是该项目的主要障碍。
entries.example_en: The lack of funding was a major hang-up for the project.

entries.definition_en: a large building at an airport used for storing and maintaining aircraft
entries.example_cn: 飞行员走进机库检查飞机。
entries.example_en: The pilot walked into the hangar to inspect the plane.

entries.definition_en: looking guilty or ashamed
entries.example_cn: 当他意识到自己忘了带钥匙时，他投来羞愧的一瞥。
entries.example_en: He gave a hangdog look when he realized he had forgotten his keys.

entries.definition_en: frightened into submission or compliance
entries.example_cn: 那些被吓服帖的囚犯静静地等待着命令。
entries.example_en: The hangdog prisoners waited silently for their orders.

entries.definition_cn: 衣架；用于悬挂物品的挂钩
entries.definition_en: an object used to support something by suspending it
entries.example_cn: 她把外套挂在门边的木衣架上。
entries.example_en: She hung her coat on the wooden hanger by the door.

entries.definition_en: a worker who hangs objects in place
entries.example_cn: 悬挂工在门厅安装了那盏沉重的吊灯。
entries.example_en: The hanger installed the heavy chandelier in the lobby.

entries.definition_cn: 因饥饿而产生的愤怒或烦躁感
entries.definition_en: a feeling of anger caused by hunger
entries.example_cn: 到了下午晚些时候，我因饥饿而烦躁，无法集中精力工作。
entries.example_en: By late afternoon, I was experiencing hanger and couldn't concentrate on my work.

entries.definition_en: a person who follows someone important in a persistent and annoying way
entries.example_cn: 那位名人身边围着一群跟班。
entries.example_en: The celebrity was surrounded by a group of hangers-on.

entries.definition_en: the action of suspending something from above
entries.example_cn: 挂画的动作做得很小心。
entries.example_en: The hanging of the picture was done carefully.

entries.definition_en: a piece of decorative cloth or tapestry hung on a wall
entries.example_cn: 房间里装饰着色彩鲜艳的挂毯。
entries.example_en: The room was decorated with colorful hangings.

entries.definition_en: execution by suspending a person from a gallows
entries.example_cn: 绞刑是在黎明时分执行的。
entries.example_en: The hanging was carried out at dawn.

entries.definition_cn: 猜单词游戏；玩家逐个猜字母，猜错时逐步画出上吊人的图形
entries.definition_en: a guessing game in which players guess a word one letter at a time, with incorrect guesses adding parts to a picture of a hanging person
entries.example_cn: 火车旅途中，我们玩猜单词游戏来打发时间。
entries.example_en: We played hangman to pass the time during the train journey.

entries.definition_en: a man whose job is to execute criminals by hanging them
entries.example_cn: 行刑前，刽子手准备好了绞索。
entries.example_en: The hangman prepared the noose before the execution.

entries.definition_en: a small piece of loose skin at the base of a fingernail that can tear and cause pain or infection
entries.example_cn: 她小心地用小剪刀剪掉倒刺，以防出血。
entries.example_en: She carefully cut off the hangnail with small scissors to prevent it from bleeding.

entries.definition_en: a place that is visited frequently
entries.example_cn: 当地的咖啡店已成为学生常去的地方。
entries.example_en: The local coffee shop has become a popular hangout for students.

entries.definition_cn: 过量饮酒或吸毒后产生的不适症状
entries.definition_en: unpleasant physical effects after excessive use of alcohol or drugs
entries.example_cn: 她醒来时感到宿醉难忍。
entries.example_en: She woke up with a terrible hangover.

entries.definition_en: something that has survived from the past
entries.example_cn: 这些古老的传统是中世纪的遗留物。
entries.example_en: The old traditions are a hangover from medieval times.

entries.definition_cn: （引申）过去事件或时期留下的令人不快的影响或遗留物
entries.definition_en: (figurative) an unpleasant lingering effect or remnant from a previous event or period
entries.example_cn: 这项过时的政策是上一届政府留下的遗患。
entries.example_en: The outdated policy was a hangover from the previous administration.

entries.definition_en: a coil of rope or wool or yarn
entries.example_cn: 她买了一团羊毛来织毛衣。
entries.example_en: She bought a hank of wool to knit a sweater.

entries.definition_en: to desire something strongly or persistently
entries.example_cn: 她渴望远离城市的宁静生活。
entries.example_en: She hankered for a quiet life away from the city.

entries.definition_en: a strong desire or yearning for something or to do something
entries.example_cn: 人们渴望远离繁忙城市，过上宁静的生活。
entries.example_en: There was a hankering for a quiet life away from the busy city.

entries.definition_en: a square piece of cloth used for wiping the eyes or nose or as a costume accessory
entries.example_cn: 她伸手去拿手帕擦眼泪。
entries.example_en: She reached for her hankey to wipe her tears.

entries.definition_en: a square piece of cloth used for wiping the eyes or nose or as a costume accessory
entries.example_cn: 她伸手去拿手帕擦掉眼泪。
entries.example_en: She reached for her hankie to wipe away the tears.

entries.definition_en: a small square of cloth used for wiping the nose or eyes
entries.example_cn: 她伸手拿手帕擦眼泪。
entries.example_en: She reached for a hanky to wipe her tears.

entries.definition_en: a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with the driver's seat above and behind the passengers
entries.example_cn: 维多利亚时代的伦敦曾充满了双轮马车。
entries.example_en: Victorian London was once filled with hansom cabs.

entries.definition_cn: 长尾叶猴（印度视为神圣）
entries.definition_en: a type of langur monkey found in southern Asia, considered sacred in India
entries.example_cn: 人们看到神圣的长尾叶猴在森林的树间跳跃。
entries.example_en: The sacred hanuman was seen leaping through the trees of the forest.

entries.definition_cn: 越南旧货币单位，等于一东的十分之一
entries.definition_en: a former currency unit of Vietnam, equal to one tenth of a dong
entries.example_cn: 那份零食的价格只有几毫。
entries.example_en: The price of the snack was only a few hao.

entries.definition_cn: 一种无叶的东印度藤本植物，其酸牛奶汁曾用于酿造致醉饮料
entries.definition_en: a leafless East Indian vine whose sour milky juice was historically used to make an intoxicating drink
entries.example_cn: 古代文献描述了哈奥玛在宗教仪式中的仪式性使用。
entries.example_en: Ancient texts describe the ritual use of haoma in religious ceremonies.

entries.definition_en: an accidental happening or chance event
entries.example_cn: 偶遇我的老老师是一件开心的偶然事件。
entries.example_en: Meeting my old teacher was a happy hap.

entries.definition_en: to come to pass or happen
entries.example_cn: 人们不知道事故是如何发生的。
entries.example_en: It is not known how the accident happed.

entries.definition_en: lacking any obvious plan or organization; done by chance
entries.example_cn: 书架上的书摆放得杂乱无章。
entries.example_en: The books on the shelf were arranged in a haphazard manner.

entries.definition_en: marked by great carelessness
entries.example_cn: 调查的草率性质导致了一些线索被遗漏。
entries.example_en: The haphazard nature of the investigation led to missed clues.

entries.definition_en: in a careless or unplanned way
entries.example_cn: 修理工作是草率进行的。
entries.example_en: The repairs were done in a haphazard way.

entries.definition_en: in a random manner
entries.example_cn: 书被随意地堆在桌子上。
entries.example_en: The books were stacked haphazardly on the table.

entries.definition_en: without care; in a slapdash manner
entries.example_cn: 他草率地粉刷了墙壁，忽略了边缘。
entries.example_en: He painted the wall haphazardly, ignoring the edges.

entries.definition_en: unlucky and deserving of pity
entries.example_cn: 那个不幸的旅客弄丢了护照和钱包。
entries.example_en: The hapless traveler lost his passport and his wallet.

entries.definition_en: of a cell or organism having a single set of chromosomes
entries.example_cn: 人类的单倍体染色体数目是 23。
entries.example_en: The haploid number of chromosomes in humans is 23.

entries.definition_en: an organism or cell that has only one complete set of chromosomes
entries.example_cn: 在许多植物中，配子是单倍体。
entries.example_en: In many plants, the gametes are haploid.

entries.definition_en: (genetics) a combination of alleles (for different genes) that are located closely together on the same chromosome and that tend to be inherited together
entries.example_cn: 科学家分析了患者的单倍型以追溯其血统。
entries.example_en: Scientists analyzed the patient's haplotype to trace their ancestry.

entries.definition_en: come to pass
entries.example_cn: 昨天发生了什么？
entries.example_en: What happened yesterday?

entries.definition_en: happen, occur, or be the case in the course of events or by chance
entries.example_cn: 我偶然在街上看见了他。
entries.example_en: I happened to see him on the street.

entries.definition_en: chance to be or do something, without intention or causation
entries.example_cn: 我碰巧带着钥匙。
entries.example_en: I happened to have the key with me.

usage.label: happen to + verb
usage.pattern: I happened to see him; source w01398r3.

entries.definition_en: come into being; become reality
entries.example_cn: 他们的梦想终于实现了。
entries.example_en: Their dream finally happened.

entries.definition_en: come upon, as if by accident; meet with
entries.example_cn: 我偶然遇到了一位老朋友。
entries.example_en: I happened upon an old friend.

entries.definition_en: an event that happens
entries.example_cn: 公园里发生的事出乎意料。
entries.example_en: The happening at the park was unexpected.

entries.definition_cn: 偶然发生的事件或情况；巧合
entries.definition_en: an event or circumstance that happens by chance
entries.example_cn: 他们的相遇纯属巧合，并非事先安排。
entries.example_en: Their meeting was pure happenstance, not a planned appointment.

entries.definition_en: in a joyous manner
entries.example_cn: 他们从此幸福地生活在一起。
entries.example_en: They lived happily ever after.

entries.definition_en: fortunately; by good luck
entries.example_cn: 幸运的是，比赛开始前雨停了。
entries.example_en: Happily, the rain stopped just before the game started.

entries.definition_en: a state of well-being characterized by emotions ranging from contentment to intense joy
entries.example_cn: 她在帮助他人中找到了真正的幸福。
entries.example_en: She found true happiness in helping others.

entries.definition_en: emotions experienced when in a state of well-being
entries.example_cn: 孩子们的笑声显示出他们的幸福感。
entries.example_en: The children's happiness was evident in their laughter.

entries.definition_en: feeling or showing great pleasure and joy
entries.example_cn: 她很高兴见到她的朋友们。
entries.example_en: She was very happy to see her friends.

entries.definition_en: marked by good fortune
entries.example_cn: 这次意外的重逢是一个幸运的巧合。
entries.example_en: The unexpected meeting was a happy coincidence.

entries.definition_en: willing and eager to help others
entries.example_cn: 他总是乐意伸出援手。
entries.example_en: He is always happy to lend a hand.

entries.definition_en: expressed clearly and effectively
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家清晰地解释了他的作品。
entries.example_en: The artist gave a happy explanation of his work.

entries.definition_en: cheerful but careless about responsibilities
entries.example_cn: 她对工作持有一种无忧无虑的态度。
entries.example_en: She has a happy-go-lucky attitude towards her work.

entries.definition_en: relating to the sense of touch or the ability to perceive through touch
entries.example_cn: 这款新智能手机具有模拟按键按压的触觉反馈系统。
entries.example_en: The new smartphone features a haptic feedback system that simulates button presses.

entries.definition_cn: 血浆中一种结合游离血红蛋白并将其从体内清除的蛋白质
entries.definition_en: a protein in the blood plasma that binds to free hemoglobin to remove it from the body
entries.example_cn: 实验室测试了 haptoglobin 的水平以评估溶血情况。
entries.example_en: The laboratory test measured the level of haptoglobin to assess hemolysis.

entries.definition_en: ritual suicide by self-disembowelment on a sword; practiced by samurai in the traditional Japanese society
entries.example_cn: 这部历史小说描绘了那位失势武士进行的剖腹自杀。
entries.example_en: The historical novel depicted the hara-kiri performed by the disgraced samurai.

entries.definition_en: ritual suicide by self-disembowelment on a sword; practiced by samurai in the traditional Japanese society
entries.example_cn: 这部历史剧描绘了战败将军进行的悲剧性切腹。
entries.example_en: The historical drama depicted the tragic harakiri performed by the defeated general.

entries.definition_en: a loud, bombastic speech expressed with strong emotion
entries.example_cn: 那位政治家向人群发表了一场激昂的长篇演说。
entries.example_en: The politician delivered a fiery harangue to the crowd.

entries.definition_cn: 对某人进行严厉的长篇训斥
entries.definition_en: to address someone forcefully with a loud speech
entries.example_cn: 经理严厉地训斥了员工，指责他们缺乏生产力。
entries.example_en: The manager harangued the employees about their lack of productivity.

usage.label: ambitransitive
usage.pattern: Can be used with or without an object.

entries.definition_en: to annoy someone repeatedly or over a long period
entries.example_cn: 建筑工地的持续噪音开始骚扰邻居们。
entries.example_en: The constant noise from the construction site began to harass the neighbors.

entries.definition_cn: 通过反复攻击使筋疲力尽
entries.definition_en: to exhaust someone by attacking them repeatedly
entries.example_cn: 猎人们不断追赶那只鹿，直到它筋疲力尽并倒下。
entries.example_en: The relentless pursuit by the hunters harassed the deer until it collapsed.

entries.definition_cn: 受到骚扰的；持续受到困扰或烦扰的
entries.definition_en: subject to harassment; persistently troubled or annoyed by unwanted treatment or interruptions
entries.example_cn: 团队在会议期间因不断的打断而感到备受困扰。
entries.example_en: The team felt harassed by constant interruptions during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: a person who persistently attacks or bothers someone
entries.example_cn: 那个网络骚扰者不断威胁批评他帖文的人。
entries.example_en: The online harasser repeatedly threatened people who criticized his posts.

entries.definition_en: a person who persistently bothers or torments someone
entries.example_cn: 公司对任何充当性骚扰者的行为实行零容忍政策。
entries.example_en: The company has a zero-tolerance policy for anyone acting as a sexual harasser.

entries.definition_cn: 通过持续的攻击和批评进行折磨的行为

entries.definition_en: deliberate pestering or intimidation

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that indicates that something else is about to happen

entries.definition_en: to be a sign that something else is going to happen

entries.example_en: The rising temperatures harbingered the arrival of summer.

entries.definition_en: a protected area of water where ships can load or unload goods

entries.definition_en: a place that provides safety, comfort, and security

entries.definition_en: to keep a belief, idea, or feeling in your mind
entries.example_cn: 她仍然对这项新计划心存疑虑。
entries.example_en: She still harbors doubts about the new plan.

entries.definition_en: to hide someone secretly, especially a criminal or fugitive

entries.example_en: The police suspect that the man is harboring a fugitive in his basement.

entries.definition_en: to provide shelter for or keep animals in one's care
entries.example_cn: 这家动物保护区收容了几只获救的动物。
entries.example_en: The sanctuary harbors several rescued animals.

entries.definition_en: to suppress or hold back a thought or feeling
entries.example_cn: 他试图抑制怒火，但没能忍住没有大喊。
entries.example_en: He tried to harbor his anger but could not stop himself from shouting.

entries.definition_en: a place where ships can find shelter from storms
entries.example_cn: 在飓风期间，避风港为受损的船只提供了安全的避难所。
entries.example_en: During the hurricane, the harborage provided a safe haven for the damaged vessels.

entries.definition_en: a sheltered port where ships can take on or discharge cargo
entries.example_cn: 船只在港口抛锚以装载货物。

entries.definition_cn: 避风港；慰藉和安全之所
entries.definition_en: a place of refuge and comfort and security

entries.example_en: The old library became a harbour for the lonely children.

entries.definition_cn: 秘密庇护（如逃犯或罪犯）
entries.definition_en: secretly shelter (as of fugitives or criminals)

entries.example_en: The suspect was accused of harbouring fugitives in his basement.

entries.definition_en: hold back a thought or feeling about
entries.example_cn: 她对他动机怀有深深的怀疑。
entries.example_en: She harboured a deep suspicion about his motives.

entries.definition_cn: 保持（某种理论、想法或感情）
entries.definition_en: maintain (a theory, thoughts, or feelings)

entries.example_en: He harboured the belief that he would succeed eventually.

entries.definition_en: keep in one's possession; of animals
entries.example_cn: 他们在花园里饲养大量珍稀鸟类。
entries.example_en: They harbour a large number of exotic birds in their garden.

entries.definition_en: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
entries.example_cn: 这道数学题很难解。
entries.example_en: The math problem was very hard to solve.

entries.definition_en: resisting weight or pressure
entries.example_cn: 钻石是一种非常坚硬的材料。
entries.example_en: The diamond is a very hard material.

entries.definition_cn: 不讲情面的；冷酷无情的
entries.definition_en: not showing sympathy or emotion; harsh and unsentimental

entries.example_en: The judge took a hard, dispassionate view of the defendant's circumstances.

entries.definition_en: with effort or force or vigor
entries.example_cn: 她努力工作以按时完成项目。
entries.example_en: She worked hard to finish the project on time.

entries.definition_en: causing great damage or hardship
entries.example_cn: 昨晚风暴猛烈袭击了海岸。
entries.example_en: The storm hit the coast hard last night.

entries.definition_en: earnestly or intently

entries.example_en: He stared hard at the screen to find the error.

entries.definition_en: in a firm or resolute manner

entries.example_en: She held hard to her principles despite the pressure.

entries.definition_en: very strong or vigorous

entries.definition_en: (of rules) stringently enforced

entries.definition_cn: 因饱经世故而变得坚韧冷酷的

entries.example_en: The hard-bitten detective had seen it all before.

entries.definition_cn: 冷酷无情且不感伤的（尤指侦探等人）
entries.definition_en: tough, callous, and unsentimental, especially of a person such as a detective

entries.example_en: The detective was a hard-boiled man who had seen too much violence.

entries.definition_en: emotionally hardened or unfeeling
entries.example_cn: 经过多年的忽视，她对家人变得麻木不仁。
entries.example_en: After years of neglect, she became hard-boiled toward her family.

entries.definition_en: cooked until the yolk is completely solid

entries.definition_en: intensely loyal

entries.definition_en: firm and unwilling to change one's opinion or position

entries.example_en: The government took a hard-line stance on the new tax laws.

entries.definition_en: guided by practical experience and observation rather than theory

entries.example_en: The hard-nosed manager refused to approve the theoretical proposal without real-world data.

entries.definition_en: having a reduced ability to hear sounds
