entries.example_cn: 在古代，猎头者会将战败敌人的头颅作为战利品展示。
entries.example_en: In ancient times, a headhunter would display the heads of defeated enemies.

entries.definition_en: a short line of text at the top of a page or section to show what it is about
entries.example_cn: 她在报告的每一章前面写了一个清晰的标题。
entries.example_en: She wrote a clear heading for each chapter of her report.

entries.definition_en: the direction or path in which something moves or is located
entries.example_cn: 船长调整航向以避开风暴。
entries.example_en: The captain adjusted the heading to avoid the storm.

entries.definition_en: a horizontal tunnel or passage dug in a mine
entries.example_cn: 矿工们沿着矿道工作，以到达新的矿藏。
entries.example_en: The miners worked their way along the heading to reach the new ore deposit.

entries.definition_en: a flashlight worn on the head, leaving the hands free
entries.example_cn: 她进入黑暗的洞穴前戴上了头灯。
entries.example_en: She put on her headlamp before entering the dark cave.

entries.definition_en: a powerful light attached to the front of a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 司机打开前灯以便在雾中看得更清楚。
entries.example_en: The driver turned on the headlamp to see better in the fog.

entries.definition_cn: 自然隆起，尤指伸入海中的岩石高地
entries.definition_en: a natural elevation, especially a rocky one that juts out into the sea
entries.example_cn: 我们爬上那个岩石高地，以获得更好的海岸线视野。
entries.example_en: We climbed the headland to get a better view of the coastline.

entries.definition_en: having no head or not formed with a head
entries.example_cn: 这座雕像是一个无头的国王形象。
entries.example_en: The statue was a headless figure of a king.

entries.definition_cn: 没有领导的；群龙无首的
entries.definition_en: without a leader or leadership
entries.example_cn: 将军死后，这支群龙无首的军队踉跄前进。
entries.example_en: The headless army blundered along after the death of its general.

entries.definition_en: a strong light with a reflector attached to the front of a vehicle to illuminate the road
entries.example_cn: 当雾气开始弥漫时，司机打开了前照灯。
entries.example_en: The driver turned on the headlights as the fog began to roll in.

entries.definition_en: the heading or caption of a newspaper article
entries.example_cn: 标题写着“市议会批准新计划”。
entries.example_en: The headline read 'City Council Approves New Plan'.

entries.definition_en: to publicize widely or highly, as if with a headline
entries.example_cn: 这起丑闻在所有主要新闻网络上都被大肆宣扬。
entries.example_en: The scandal was headlined across all major news networks.

entries.definition_cn: 为（报纸版面或故事）加标题
entries.definition_en: to provide a newspaper page or a story with a headline
entries.example_cn: 编辑为关于当地节日的故事加了标题。
entries.example_en: The editor headlined the story about the local festival.

entries.definition_en: a performer who is given the most prominent position in a program
entries.example_cn: 这场音乐会的头牌表演者是一支著名的摇滚乐队。
entries.example_en: The headliner of the concert was a famous rock band.

entries.definition_cn: 车辆内顶棚的衬布或其他覆盖材料
entries.definition_en: the fabric or other material covering the inside ceiling of a vehicle
entries.example_cn: 这辆车的顶棚衬布有污渍，而且开始下垂。
entries.example_en: The car's headliner was stained and starting to sag.

entries.definition_en: a wrestling hold where you lock your opponent's head between your elbow and your body
entries.example_cn: 摔跤手通过给对手施加紧的头锁赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The wrestler won the match by applying a tight headlock to his opponent.

entries.definition_en: at breakneck speed
entries.example_cn: 他们极速地跑去赶公交车。
entries.example_en: They ran headlong to catch the bus.

entries.definition_en: in a hasty and foolhardy manner
entries.example_cn: 他们没做计划就鲁莽地一头扎进了这个项目。
entries.example_en: They made a headlong rush into the project without planning.

entries.definition_en: with the head before the body
entries.example_cn: 他头朝前地掉进了水里。
entries.example_en: He fell headlong into the water.

entries.definition_en: with the head foremost
entries.example_cn: 那匹马头先冲向敌人。
entries.example_en: The horse charged headlong at the enemy.

entries.definition_en: moving or happening with excessive speed
entries.example_cn: 那辆车飞快地冲下了山坡。
entries.example_en: The car went headlong down the hill.

entries.definition_cn: 男性村长或部落、宗族首领
entries.definition_en: a male leader of a village, tribe, or clan
entries.example_cn: 部落首领召集村民讨论收成。
entries.example_en: The headman gathered the villagers to discuss the harvest.

entries.definition_en: a man whose job is to cut off the heads of people who have been sentenced to death
entries.example_cn: 刽子手在古老的广场上将被判死刑的囚犯斩首。
entries.example_en: The headman beheaded the condemned prisoner in the ancient square.

entries.definition_cn: 男校长；（尤指）学校负责人
entries.definition_en: a male head teacher, especially the head of a school
entries.example_cn: 校长在集会上对学生们发表了讲话。
entries.example_en: The headmaster addressed the students during the assembly.

entries.definition_en: a woman who is the headmaster of a school
entries.example_cn: 女校长用热情的演讲欢迎了新学生。
entries.example_en: The headmistress welcomed the new students with a warm speech.

entries.definition_en: a device worn over or inserted into the ears to hear sound
entries.example_cn: 请戴上耳机，以便收听指示。
entries.example_en: Please put on your headphones so you can listen to the instructions.

entries.definition_en: a helmet worn to protect the head
entries.example_cn: 建筑工人为了安全戴上了硬质头盔。
entries.example_en: The construction worker wore a hard headpiece for safety.

entries.definition_en: the part of a bridle that goes around a horse's head
entries.example_cn: 骑手调整了马笼头，以确保马匹舒适。
entries.example_en: The rider adjusted the headpiece to ensure the horse was comfortable.

entries.definition_en: to provide with a headquarters
entries.example_cn: 公司决定将其新分部的总部设在伦敦。
entries.example_en: The company decided to headquarter its new branch in London.

entries.definition_en: the main office where a company or organization is managed
entries.example_cn: 公司将总部搬到了市中心的一栋新大楼里。
entries.example_en: The company moved its headquarters to a new building in the city center.

entries.definition_en: a military base where a commander directs operations
entries.example_cn: 将军在战斗中从指挥部发出命令。
entries.example_en: The general issued orders from the headquarters during the battle.

entries.definition_en: a military group consisting of a commander and their staff
entries.example_cn: 军队建立了一个新的指挥部来协调部队。
entries.example_en: The army established a new headquarters to coordinate the troops.

entries.definition_en: a cushion attached to the top of the back of an automobile's seat to prevent whiplash
entries.example_cn: 她调整了头枕，以确保在长途驾驶中颈部得到适当支撑。
entries.example_en: She adjusted the headrest to ensure her neck was properly supported during the long drive.

entries.definition_cn: （椅子或床等上的）头部支撑物
entries.definition_en: a support for the head, especially on a chair or bed
entries.example_cn: 他阅读时，扶手椅的头枕支撑着他的头部。
entries.example_en: The armchair's headrest supported his head as he read.

entries.definition_cn: 头顶上方供人通行的净空高度
entries.definition_en: the vertical space available for someone to pass under something without hitting their head
entries.example_cn: 天花板很低，所以走廊里的垂直空间非常有限。
entries.example_en: The ceiling is low, so there is very little headroom in the hallway.

entries.definition_cn: 音响系统在不失真的情况下再现大音量的能力（动态余量）
entries.definition_en: the capacity of an audio system to reproduce loud sounds without distortion
entries.example_cn: 这套音响系统的动态余量很大，允许乐团大声演奏而不失真。
entries.example_en: This audio system has excellent headroom, allowing the orchestra to play loudly without distortion.

entries.definition_cn: 算法实际性能与其最大可能性能之间的差距
entries.definition_en: the distance between an algorithm’s actual performance and its maximum possible performance
entries.example_cn: 该算法在达到最大可能性能之前仍有相当大的提升空间。
entries.example_en: The algorithm still has considerable headroom before reaching its maximum possible performance.

entries.definition_en: One side of a coin.
entries.example_cn: 她通过抛硬币正面朝上来赢了比赛。
entries.example_en: She won the game by flipping heads.

entries.definition_cn: （通常指）硬币上有头像或其他国家标志的一面
entries.definition_en: the side of a coin bearing a head or other national symbol
entries.example_cn: 他抛起硬币，结果正面朝上，国王的肖像朝向上方。
entries.example_en: He tossed the coin and it landed on heads, with the king's portrait facing up.

entries.definition_en: The plural form of head.
entries.example_cn: 老师数了教室里的学生人数。
entries.example_en: The teacher counted the heads in the classroom.

entries.definition_en: The toilets on an older sailing ship.
entries.example_cn: 船员们在船上用厕所解决生理需求。
entries.example_en: The crew used the heads for their relief.

entries.definition_cn: （动词 head 的第三人称单数现在时）
entries.definition_en: Third-person singular present form of head.
entries.example_cn: 他作为首席执行官领导着这家公司。
entries.example_en: He heads the company as its CEO.

entries.definition_en: A shouted warning that something is falling from above.
entries.example_cn: 小心！注意那根掉下来的树枝。
entries.example_en: Heads! Watch out for the falling branch.

entries.definition_en: A short form of headphones.
entries.example_cn: 电影开始前戴上你的耳机。
entries.example_en: Put on your heads before the movie starts.

entries.definition_en: High-grade marijuana.
entries.example_cn: 警方查获了几袋优质大麻。
entries.example_en: The police seized several bags of heads.

entries.definition_en: a warning message or advance notice
entries.example_cn: 如果你要迟到，请提前告诉我一声。
entries.example_en: Please give me a heads-up if you are going to be late.

entries.definition_en: fully alert and watchful
entries.example_cn: 安保团队整夜保持高度警惕。
entries.example_en: The security team remained heads-up throughout the night.

entries.definition_en: a sail located forward of the foremast on a sailing ship
entries.example_cn: 他们调整了前帆以更好地捕捉风力。
entries.example_en: They adjusted the headsail to catch the wind better.

entries.definition_en: a kerchief worn over the head and tied under the chin
entries.example_cn: 她头上系了一条色彩鲜艳的头巾。
entries.example_en: She tied a colorful headscarf around her head.

entries.definition_cn: 单只或一副耳机，通常带有麦克风
entries.definition_en: a headphone or earphone, or a pair of headphones or earphones, typically with an attached microphone
entries.example_cn: 飞行员戴上头戴式耳机以收听空中交通管制员的指令。
entries.example_en: The pilot put on the headset to hear the air traffic controller.

entries.definition_en: the act of turning your head from side to side to show denial, disbelief, or confusion
entries.example_cn: 当我提到那个不可能的截止日期时，她微微摇了摇头。
entries.example_en: She gave a slight headshake when I mentioned the impossible deadline.

entries.definition_en: the position of being in charge or leading a group
entries.example_cn: 这位新经理渴望证明自己在部门中的领导地位。
entries.example_en: The new manager is eager to prove his headship in the department.

entries.definition_en: the role or position of a headmaster or headmistress
entries.example_cn: 她在退休后担任了该校的校长职位。
entries.example_en: She took on the headship of the school after retiring from teaching.

entries.definition_cn: （通常为头部和肩部的）肖像照
entries.definition_en: a photograph showing only a person's head and shoulders
entries.example_cn: 这位演员需要一张专业的肖像照放在简历上。
entries.example_en: The actor needed a professional headshot for his resume.

entries.definition_en: an attempt to score a goal in soccer by hitting the ball with the head
entries.example_cn: 前锋在最后一分钟打进了一个精彩的头球。
entries.example_en: The striker scored a brilliant headshot in the final minute.

entries.definition_cn: 射向某人头部的枪击；爆头
entries.definition_en: a shot fired at someone's head
entries.example_cn: 狙击手在远处向目标头部开了一枪。
entries.example_en: The sniper took a headshot from a distance.

entries.definition_en: a man whose job is to cut off the head of a person who has been sentenced to death
entries.example_cn: 这幅历史画作描绘了刽子手处决囚犯的那悲惨时刻。
entries.example_en: The historical painting depicted the grim moment when the headsman executed the prisoner.

entries.definition_cn: 一个人的心理承受能力或精神状态（视为有界限的空间）
entries.definition_en: one's mental capacity or state of mind, viewed as a space with limits
entries.example_cn: 忙碌了一周后，我已经没有心理空间再进行一次艰难的谈话了。
entries.example_en: After a demanding week, I had no headspace left for another difficult conversation.

entries.definition_en: the empty space at the top of a container before it is sealed
entries.example_cn: 制造商必须在罐子中留出足够的空隙，以便在装罐过程中允许膨胀。
entries.example_en: The manufacturer must leave enough headspace in the jar to allow for expansion during canning.

entries.definition_en: the part of a bridle that goes around a horse's head
entries.example_cn: 骑手调整了马笼头以确保马匹舒适。
entries.example_en: The rider adjusted the headstall to ensure the horse was comfortable.

entries.definition_en: an acrobatic feat in which a person balances on the head (usually with the help of the hands)
entries.example_cn: 经过几年的练习，她终于学会了坚持倒立三十秒。
entries.example_en: After years of practice, she finally learned how to hold a headstand for thirty seconds.

entries.definition_cn: （机器或工具中）支撑并驱动旋转部件的固定部分
entries.definition_en: the part of a machine or tool that holds and turns a moving part, such as a chuck or spindle
entries.example_cn: 操作员通过转动主轴箱上的旋钮来调节车床的速度。
entries.example_en: The operator adjusted the speed of the lathe by turning the knob on the headstock.

entries.definition_en: a stone placed on a grave to mark it
entries.example_cn: 他们去墓地清洗祖父的墓碑。
entries.example_en: They visited the cemetery to clean the headstone of their grandfather.

entries.definition_cn: 建筑物的基石或主要石块
entries.definition_en: the cornerstone or principal stone of a building
entries.example_cn: 铭文刻在那座老建筑角落的基石上。
entries.example_en: The inscription was carved into the headstone at the corner of the old building.

entries.definition_en: stubborn and unwilling to listen to advice or others
entries.example_cn: 这个固执的青少年拒绝遵守父母的规矩。
entries.example_en: The headstrong teenager refused to follow his parents' rules.

entries.definition_en: a senior dining-room attendant who supervises other waiters and manages customer seating
entries.example_cn: 领班侍者安排客人入座。
entries.example_en: The headwaiter assigned tables to the guests as they arrived.

entries.definition_en: the source or upper reaches of a river
entries.example_cn: 河流上游的鱼类种群比下游的健康得多。
entries.example_en: The fish population in the headwaters is much healthier than downstream.

entries.definition_en: progress or forward movement towards a goal
entries.example_cn: 尽管困难重重，该项目终于取得了一些进展。
entries.example_en: Despite the difficulties, the project is finally making some headway.

entries.definition_en: the vertical space needed for a vehicle to pass under an obstacle
entries.example_cn: 卡车无法从桥下通过，因为净空高度不够。
entries.example_en: The truck could not fit under the bridge because there was not enough headway.

entries.definition_en: wind blowing opposite to the path of a ship or aircraft
entries.example_cn: 飞机在起飞时与强逆风搏斗。
entries.example_en: The plane struggled against the strong headwind during takeoff.

entries.definition_cn: 严重阻碍进展的力量或情况
entries.definition_en: a force or circumstance that seriously hinders progress
entries.example_cn: 成本上涨给这家小企业的发展造成了阻力。
entries.example_en: Rising costs created headwinds for the small business.

entries.definition_en: the word at the start of a dictionary entry
entries.example_cn: 在这本词典中，头词后面跟着它的发音和定义。
entries.example_en: In this dictionary, the headword is followed by its pronunciation and definition.

entries.definition_cn: 短语中决定其语法或语义特征的中心词
entries.definition_en: the main word in a phrase, which determines its grammatical or semantic character
entries.example_cn: 在“一个非常挑剔的购车者”中，“购车者”是该短语的中心词。
entries.example_en: In “a very discerning car shopper,” “shopper” is the headword of the phrase.

entries.definition_en: extremely exciting, as if caused by alcohol or a narcotic
entries.example_cn: 音乐节令人眩晕的氛围让每个人都感到充满活力。
entries.example_en: The heady atmosphere of the music festival made everyone feel alive.

entries.definition_en: marked by defiant disregard for danger or consequences
entries.example_cn: 他鲁莽地冒险驾车穿过被洪水淹没的街道。
entries.example_en: He took a heady risk by driving through the flooded street.

entries.definition_cn: 需要动脑筋的；深奥难懂的
entries.definition_en: intellectually challenging or demanding
entries.example_cn: 对高中生来说，克尔凯郭尔的作品相当深奥难懂。
entries.example_en: Kierkegaard is rather heady reading for a high school student.

entries.definition_en: to become healthy again or to make something healthy again
entries.example_cn: 伤口几周后就会痊愈。
entries.example_en: The wound will heal in a few weeks.

entries.definition_en: to recover from an illness or injury
entries.example_cn: 手术后他花了很长时间才恢复。
entries.example_en: It took him a long time to heal after the surgery.

entries.definition_en: to provide a cure for or make healthy again
entries.example_cn: 这种药有助于快速治愈感染。
entries.example_en: This medicine helps to heal infections quickly.

entries.definition_cn: 调和关系或局面；化解分歧
entries.definition_en: to restore harmony in a relationship or situation; to resolve a disagreement
entries.example_cn: 双方会面以化解长期以来的分歧。
entries.example_en: The two sides met to heal their long-standing differences.

entries.definition_cn: 治疗者；（尤指通过信仰或传统疗法的）治疗师
entries.definition_en: a person who heals, especially through faith or traditional remedies
entries.example_cn: 治疗师用古老的草药治疗伤口。
entries.example_en: The healer used ancient herbs to treat the wound.

entries.definition_cn: 身体自我修复的自然过程
entries.definition_en: the natural process by which the body repairs itself
entries.example_cn: 愈合过程持续了数周。
entries.example_en: The healing process took several weeks.

entries.definition_en: tending to cure or restore to health
entries.example_cn: 这种草药的治愈功效众所周知。
entries.example_en: The healing properties of this herb are well known.

entries.definition_en: a state of being free from disease
entries.example_cn: 健康对每个人都很重要。
entries.example_en: Good health is important for everyone.

entries.definition_en: the condition of body and mind
entries.example_cn: 她担心自己的健康状况。
entries.example_en: She is worried about her health.

entries.definition_en: the preservation of mental and physical health by preventing or treating illness through services offered by the health profession
entries.example_cn: 获得负担得起的医疗保健是一项基本权利。
entries.example_en: Access to affordable healthcare is a fundamental right.

entries.definition_en: conducive to good health of body or mind
entries.example_cn: 富含蔬菜和全谷物的健康饮食对于长寿至关重要。
entries.example_en: A healthful diet rich in vegetables and whole grains is essential for longevity.

entries.definition_cn: 有益于道德或精神福祉的
entries.definition_en: conducive to moral or spiritual well-being
entries.example_cn: 这次经历成为有益于精神成长的震撼，改变了他的观念。
entries.example_en: The experience proved to be a healthful shock that changed his outlook.

entries.definition_en: the quality of promoting good health
entries.example_cn: 这种饮食是否有益健康是运动员十分关注的问题。
entries.example_en: The healthfulness of the diet was a major concern for the athletes.

entries.definition_en: in a healthy manner
entries.example_cn: 你可以健康饮食，感觉会很棒。
entries.example_en: You can eat healthily and feel great.

entries.definition_en: the state of being vigorous and free from disease
entries.example_cn: 这次静修活动旨在帮助社区在大流行病后恢复健康。
entries.example_en: The retreat focused on restoring the community's healthiness after the pandemic.

entries.definition_en: having or indicating good health in body or mind; free from infirmity or disease
entries.example_cn: 她经常锻炼以保持健康。
entries.example_en: She exercises regularly to stay healthy.

entries.definition_en: promoting health; healthful
entries.example_cn: 吃健康的饮食对儿童很重要。
entries.example_en: Eating a healthy diet is important for children.

entries.definition_en: financially secure and functioning well
entries.example_cn: 尽管市场低迷，该公司财务状况依然稳健。
entries.example_en: The company is financially healthy despite the market downturn.

entries.definition_en: exercising or showing good judgment
entries.example_cn: 早点离开聚会是一个明智的决定。
entries.example_en: It was a healthy decision to leave the party early.

entries.definition_en: large in amount or extent or degree
entries.example_cn: 人们对新项目表现出了浓厚的兴趣。
entries.example_en: There was a healthy interest in the new project.

entries.definition_en: a large pile of objects placed on top of each other
entries.example_cn: 他们把树叶堆在院子的一角。
entries.example_en: They cleared the leaves into a heap in the corner of the yard.

entries.definition_en: a very large number or amount of something
entries.example_cn: 关于这项新政策有大量投诉。
entries.example_en: There was a heap of complaints about the new policy.

entries.definition_en: an old and unreliable car
entries.example_cn: 他开着一辆几乎无法行驶的破车。
entries.example_en: He drives an old heap that barely runs.

entries.definition_en: to give something to someone in large quantities
entries.example_cn: 国王向忠诚的臣民大量赠送礼物。
entries.example_en: The king heaped gifts upon his loyal subjects.

entries.definition_en: to arrange things in stacks or piles
entries.example_cn: 请把木柴整齐地堆在门口。
entries.example_en: Please heap the firewood neatly by the door.

entries.definition_en: to fill something until it overflows
entries.example_cn: 雨水导致河水漫过河岸。
entries.example_en: The rain caused the river to heap over its banks.

entries.definition_en: a very large number or amount of something
entries.example_cn: 她收到了朋友们送来的大量礼物。
entries.example_en: She received heaps of gifts from her friends.

entries.definition_en: to a very great degree
entries.example_cn: 我非常喜欢这部电影。
entries.example_en: I enjoyed the movie heaps.

usage.label: colloquial
usage.pattern: heaps meaning very much or a lot

entries.definition_en: to perceive sound using your ears
entries.example_cn: 我能听见花园里鸟儿在歌唱。
entries.example_en: I could hear the birds singing in the garden.

entries.definition_en: to become aware of something, often by accident
entries.example_cn: 我在收音机上偶然得知了这起事故。
entries.example_en: I heard about the accident on the radio.

entries.definition_en: to receive a message or communication from someone
entries.example_cn: 你最近收到你妹妹的消息了吗？
entries.example_en: Did you hear from your sister lately?

entries.definition_en: to listen carefully and pay attention to what is said
entries.example_cn: 在做决定之前，请听我把话说完。
entries.example_en: Please hear me out before you make a decision.

entries.definition_en: to examine evidence or a case in a court of law
entries.example_cn: 法官将于下周一审理此案。
entries.example_en: The judge will hear the case next Monday.

entries.definition_en: perceived by the sense of hearing
entries.example_cn: 声音在整个房间里都听得清清楚楚。
entries.example_en: The sound was heard clearly across the room.

entries.definition_en: a person who hears or listens to something
entries.example_cn: 老师要求那位倾听者重复一遍指示。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the hearer to repeat the instructions.

entries.definition_en: the ability to hear; the sense of hearing
entries.example_cn: 他的听力非常敏锐，所以他能从很远的地方听到鸟叫。
entries.example_en: His hearing is very sharp, so he can hear birds singing from far away.

entries.definition_en: a legal proceeding where evidence is examined to decide a fact
entries.example_cn: 法官将听证会推迟到下周。
entries.example_en: The judge postponed the hearing until next week.

entries.definition_en: a session where witnesses are called to give testimony
entries.example_cn: 委员会举行听证会调查事故。
entries.example_en: The committee held a hearing to investigate the accident.

entries.definition_en: an opportunity to present your case and be listened to
entries.example_cn: 她被给予申辩的机会来解释她的一面之词。
entries.example_en: She was granted a hearing to explain her side of the story.

entries.definition_cn: 听见或听取某事的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of hearing or perceiving something
entries.example_cn: 听众听讲的过程被嘈杂的施工声打断了。
entries.example_en: The audience's hearing of the lecture was interrupted by loud construction noise.

entries.definition_en: able to perceive sound
entries.example_cn: 助听器帮助他更好地听到孙辈的声音。
entries.example_en: The hearing aid helped him hear his grandchildren better.

entries.definition_cn: 声音能够被听见的距离或范围
entries.definition_en: the distance or area within which a sound can be heard
entries.example_cn: 大厅里的每个人都在这位歌手声音的可听范围内。
entries.example_en: Everyone in the hall was within hearing of the singer's voice.

entries.definition_en: having a reduced ability to hear.
entries.example_cn: 这位听力受损的学生使用特殊设备来听老师讲课。
entries.example_en: The hearing-impaired student uses a special device to listen to the teacher.

entries.definition_en: to listen carefully; often used in the imperative
entries.example_cn: 倾听长辈的劝告。
entries.example_en: Hearken to the advice of your elders.

entries.definition_cn: 传闻（证据）；并非来自亲身经历的信息
entries.definition_en: information or evidence reported by others rather than based on firsthand knowledge, especially in legal contexts
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定该传闻证据不可采纳。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the evidence was inadmissible hearsay.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: Source w17399r0 and w17399r1 explicitly mark this noun as usually uncountable.

entries.definition_en: based on information or evidence reported by others rather than direct knowledge
entries.example_cn: 关于这起事故，我们只有传闻证据。
entries.example_en: We only have hearsay evidence about the accident.

entries.definition_en: a vehicle used to carry a coffin to a church or cemetery
entries.example_cn: 黑色的灵车抵达教堂参加葬礼游行。
entries.example_en: The black hearse arrived at the church for the funeral procession.

entries.definition_en: the center of feelings and emotions
entries.example_cn: 她发自内心地说话。
entries.example_en: She spoke from the heart.

entries.definition_en: the organ that pumps blood
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了他的心脏。
entries.example_en: The doctor checked his heart.

entries.definition_en: the most important part of something
entries.example_cn: 爱是故事的核心。
entries.example_en: Love is the heart of the story.

entries.definition_en: a central area
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店位于市中心。
entries.example_en: The hotel is in the heart of the city.

entries.definition_en: courage
entries.example_cn: 他有勇气面对危险。
entries.example_en: He had the heart to face the danger.

entries.definition_cn: 喜欢；喜爱（常用心形符号表示，幽默、非正式）
entries.definition_en: to be fond of or like, often represented by a heart symbol; humorous and informal
entries.example_cn: 我喜欢这首新歌。
entries.example_en: I heart this new song.

entries.definition_en: an inclination or disposition toward a particular activity or concern
entries.example_cn: 他无意做这种工作。
entries.example_en: He has no heart for such work.

entries.definition_en: a shape used on cards
entries.example_cn: 她在卡片上画了一个心形。
entries.example_en: She drew a heart on the card.

entries.definition_cn: （通常指牛或小牛的）可食用心脏；心肉
entries.definition_en: the edible heart of an animal, usually beef or veal, used as meat
entries.example_cn: 他们把牛心肉和炖菜一起端上来。
entries.example_en: They served beef heart with the stew.

entries.definition_cn: 形容脂肪和盐含量低、有助于预防过早发生心脏病的食物
entries.definition_en: describing food that is low in fat and salt and may help prevent premature heart disease
entries.example_cn: 燕麦是一种有益心脏健康的食物，你应该每天食用。
entries.example_en: Oats are a heart-healthy food that you should eat every day.

entries.definition_en: wild ginger having persistent heart-shaped pungent leaves; West Virginia to Alabama
entries.example_cn: 心叶山姜在西弗吉尼亚的森林中野生生长。
entries.example_en: The heart-leaf grows wild in the forests of West Virginia.

entries.definition_en: evergreen low-growing perennial having mottled green and silvery-grey heart-shaped pungent leaves; Virginia to South Carolina
entries.example_cn: 弗吉尼亚的园丁常种植心叶香薷，因其叶片美观。
entries.example_en: Gardeners in Virginia often plant the heart-leaf for its attractive foliage.

entries.definition_en: having the shape of a heart
entries.example_cn: 花园里长满了心形的叶子。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with heart-shaped leaves.

entries.definition_en: an intimate private talk
entries.example_cn: 我们就未来的计划进行了一次推心置腹的谈话。
entries.example_en: We had a heart-to-heart about our future plans.

entries.definition_en: openly straightforward and direct
entries.example_cn: 她就我的职业生涯与我进行了一次坦诚的交谈。
entries.example_en: She had a heart-to-heart conversation with me about my career.

entries.definition_en: showing complete and enthusiastic devotion
entries.example_cn: 她全心全意地服务于她的社区。
entries.example_en: She served her community with heart-whole dedication.

entries.definition_cn: 深切的情感痛苦或悲伤，尤指因失去或思念所爱之人而产生
entries.definition_en: intense emotional pain or sorrow, especially caused by the loss or absence of someone loved
entries.example_cn: 祖母的去世给她带来了巨大的悲痛。
entries.example_en: The death of her grandmother caused her great heartache.

entries.definition_en: the rhythmic contraction and expansion of the arteries with each beat of the heart
entries.example_cn: 医生听了病人的心跳。
entries.example_en: The doctor listened to the patient's heartbeat.

entries.definition_en: a very short time (as the time it takes the eye to blink or the heart to beat)
entries.example_cn: 她等了他极短的时间才回答。
entries.example_en: She waited a heartbeat for him to answer.

entries.definition_en: a driving impulse or vital force; the vital center of something
entries.example_cn: 强烈的社区意识是团队成功的核心动力。
entries.example_en: A strong sense of community was the heartbeat of the team’s success.

entries.definition_cn: 极度的悲痛，尤指因失去亲人或失望而起
entries.definition_en: overwhelming mental anguish or grief, especially that caused by loss or disappointment
entries.example_cn: 她去世的消息让他悲痛欲绝。
entries.example_en: The news of her death caused him great heartbreak.

entries.definition_cn: 在恋爱关系中不负责任的迷人者；负心人
entries.definition_en: a charming person who behaves irresponsibly in romantic relationships
entries.example_cn: 他是个臭名昭著的负心人，和许多女人约会，却从不对任何一个人认真负责。
entries.example_en: He was a notorious heartbreaker who dated many women without ever committing to any of them.

entries.definition_cn: 令人痛心的险败；最后一刻的失利
entries.definition_en: a very narrow defeat or a loss that occurs at the last possible moment
entries.example_cn: 这支球队在冠军赛最后几秒遭遇了一场令人痛心的险败。
entries.example_en: The team suffered a heartbreaker in the final seconds of the championship game.

entries.definition_en: causing great sadness or pain
entries.example_cn: 看着她不辞而别，令人心碎。
entries.example_en: It was heartbreaking to see her leave without saying goodbye.

entries.definition_en: feeling very sad because of a loss or disappointment
entries.example_cn: 她最喜爱的球队在决赛中失利时，她心碎了。
entries.example_en: She was heartbroken when her favorite team lost the final match.

entries.definition_en: a painful burning sensation in the chest caused by stomach acid flowing back into the esophagus
entries.example_cn: 吃完辛辣食物后，他遭受了严重的胃灼热。
entries.example_en: After eating spicy food, he suffered from severe heartburn.

entries.definition_en: to give someone courage or hope when they are feeling discouraged
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛中的胜利鼓舞了那些整个赛季都担心的球迷。
entries.example_en: The team's victory in the final match heartened the fans who had been worried all season.

entries.definition_en: cheerfully encouraging; giving hope or confidence
entries.example_cn: 球队最近的胜利是取得进步的令人振奋的迹象。
entries.example_en: The team's recent victory was a heartening sign of their progress.

entries.definition_en: sincerely earnest
entries.example_cn: 她为自己的错误致以诚挚的道歉。
entries.example_en: She gave a heartfelt apology for her mistake.

entries.definition_en: the open space in a fireplace where a fire is built
entries.example_cn: 他们围坐在壁炉旁观看火焰噼啪作响。
entries.example_en: They gathered around the hearth to watch the fire crackle.

entries.definition_cn: 壁炉前的炉台或铺砌地面
entries.definition_en: a paved area extending from a fireplace into a room
entries.example_cn: 石砌的壁炉前厅为客人们提供了一个温暖的座位。
entries.example_en: The stone hearth provided a warm spot for the guests to sit.

entries.definition_en: a home or family, symbolized by the fireplace
entries.example_cn: 古老的壁炉迎接了我们几代人的家庭。
entries.example_en: The old hearth has welcomed generations of our family.

entries.definition_cn: 用来砌成壁炉炉床的扁平石头
entries.definition_en: a flat stone used to form a hearth
entries.example_cn: 那块古老的壁炉石还残留着火的余温。
entries.example_en: The ancient hearthstone was still warm from the fire.

entries.definition_en: with gusto and without reservation
entries.example_cn: 他们热烈地欢迎新客人。
entries.example_en: They heartily welcomed the new guests.

entries.definition_en: in a hearty manner
entries.example_cn: 他豪爽地享受了这顿丰盛的饭菜。
entries.example_en: He heartily enjoyed the hearty meal.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being sincere and enthusiastic
entries.example_cn: 她欢迎客人时的诚挚热情让每个人都感到宾至如归。
entries.example_en: Her heartiness in welcoming the guests made everyone feel at home.

entries.definition_en: great physical or mental strength and energy
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛中展现了巨大的精力。
entries.example_en: The team showed great heartiness during the final match.

entries.definition_en: the central part of a country or continent, especially an area that is culturally or politically important to it
entries.example_cn: 总统的政治支持在其家乡腹地最为强劲。
entries.example_en: The president's political support is strongest in his home heartland.

entries.definition_en: showing no sympathy, kindness, or pity for others
entries.example_cn: 他让狗在冰冷的雨中待在室外，真是太冷酷无情了。
entries.example_en: It was heartless of him to leave his dog outside in the freezing rain.

entries.definition_en: archaic: lacking enthusiasm or spirit; spiritless
entries.example_cn: 那支球队打得毫无斗志，轻易放弃了比赛。
entries.example_en: The team played a heartless game, giving up without trying.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows no care or sympathy for others
entries.example_cn: 她被朋友们冷酷地抛弃了。
entries.example_en: She was heartlessly abandoned by her friends.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unkind and unconcerned about others' feelings
entries.example_cn: 他在聚会上表现出的冷酷无情震惊了所有人。
entries.example_en: His heartlessness shocked everyone at the party.

entries.definition_en: causing or marked by deep grief or anguish
entries.example_cn: 那个令人心碎的家庭悲剧故事让房间里每个人都流下了眼泪。
entries.example_en: The heartrending story of the lost family moved everyone in the room to tears.

entries.definition_cn: 一种惠斯特牌戏，玩家应避免赢得包含红心或黑桃Q的牌墩
entries.definition_en: a form of whist in which players avoid winning tricks containing hearts or the queen of spades
entries.example_cn: 他们昨晚在俱乐部玩红心牌。
entries.example_en: They played hearts at the club last night.

entries.definition_en: a common European wild flower, Viola tricolor; the wild pansy
entries.example_cn: 园丁在花园里种下了三色堇。
entries.example_en: The gardener planted heartsease in the garden.

entries.definition_cn: 一种常见的旧大陆堇菜，花朵乳白色，常带紫色
entries.definition_en: a common Old World viola with creamy flowers often tinged with violet
entries.example_cn: 她从草地上摘了一朵紫罗兰来制作花束。
entries.example_en: She picked a heartsease from the meadow to make a bouquet.

entries.definition_cn: 北美太平洋沿岸的一种紫罗兰，花瓣白色，带黄色和深紫色斑纹
entries.definition_en: a violet species from the Pacific coast of North America with white petals tinged with yellow and deep violet
entries.example_cn: 这种稀有的北美紫罗兰生长在沿海悬崖上。
entries.example_en: The rare heartsease grows wild along the coastal cliffs.

entries.definition_en: the absence of mental stress or anxiety
entries.example_cn: 度假回来后，他重新感到心安。
entries.example_en: After the vacation, he felt a sense of heartsease return to him.

entries.definition_en: feeling deep sorrow or sadness
entries.example_cn: 听到那个坏消息后，她感到心碎。
entries.example_en: She felt heartsick after hearing the bad news.

entries.definition_en: lacking hope or feeling hopeless
entries.example_cn: 在输掉最后一场比赛后，球队感到绝望。
entries.example_en: The team was heartsick after losing the final match.

entries.definition_en: the deepest feelings of love and compassion one has
entries.example_cn: 这首歌触动了他心弦，使他热泪盈眶。
entries.example_en: The song touched his heartstrings and brought tears to his eyes.

entries.definition_en: a person who is the object of someone's infatuation
entries.example_cn: 她是全校学生的梦中情人。
entries.example_en: She was a heartthrob for the entire student body.

entries.definition_en: causing gladness and pleasure
entries.example_cn: 这个故事是一个关于友谊和牺牲的令人欣慰的故事。
entries.example_en: The story was a heartwarming tale of friendship and sacrifice.

entries.definition_en: the hard, dark inner wood of a tree trunk that no longer transports water
entries.example_cn: 木匠挑选了一块橡木心材来做桌腿。
entries.example_en: The carpenter selected a piece of oak heartwood for the table legs.

entries.definition_en: showing warm and heartfelt friendliness
entries.example_cn: 他们讲起旧事时开怀大笑。
entries.example_en: They shared a hearty laugh over the old stories.

entries.definition_en: providing abundant nourishment
entries.example_cn: 这顿营养丰富的餐食包括汤、肉和蔬菜。
entries.example_en: The hearty meal included soup, meat, and vegetables.

entries.definition_en: endowed with or exhibiting great bodily or mental health
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，他感到身体健壮，精力充沛。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, he felt hearty and full of energy.

entries.definition_en: eating or drinking large amounts with enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 他饭量很大，晚餐经常能吃完两大份食物。
entries.example_en: He is a hearty eater, regularly finishing two large portions at dinner.

entries.definition_en: deeply felt
entries.example_cn: 她为她的错误致以深切的歉意。
entries.example_en: She offered a hearty apology for her mistake.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being hot
entries.example_cn: 厨房里的热度让做饭变得很困难。
entries.example_en: The heat in the kitchen made it hard to cook.

entries.definition_en: energy that moves from a hotter object to a cooler one
entries.example_cn: 太阳为地球提供热能。
entries.example_en: The sun provides heat for the Earth.

entries.definition_en: the feeling of warmth on the skin
entries.example_cn: 她脸上突然感到一阵灼热。
entries.example_en: She felt a sudden heat on her face.

entries.definition_en: to make something hot or hotter
entries.example_cn: 请在喝水前把水加热。
entries.example_en: Please heat the water before you drink it.

entries.definition_en: to supply something with heat
entries.example_cn: 锅炉在冬天为房子供热。
entries.example_en: The boiler heats the house in winter.

entries.definition_en: to become hot
entries.example_cn: 金属在火中很快变热。
entries.example_en: The metal heats quickly in the fire.

entries.definition_en: intense emotion or excitement
entries.example_cn: 每个人都明显感受到了辩论中的激烈情绪。
entries.example_en: The heat of the debate was obvious to everyone.

entries.definition_en: to cause strong feelings or excitement
entries.example_cn: 这次演讲激起了人群采取行动的热情。
entries.example_en: The speech heated the crowd to action.

entries.definition_en: made warm or hot
entries.example_cn: 请在准备好饮用前保持水处于加热状态。
entries.example_en: Please keep the water heated until you are ready to drink it.

entries.definition_en: marked by emotional heat; vehement
entries.example_cn: 辩论变成了两位候选人之间激烈的争吵。
entries.example_en: The debate turned into a heated argument between the two candidates.

entries.definition_en: in a heated manner
entries.example_cn: 这两位政治家就新政策激烈地争论起来。
entries.example_en: The two politicians argued heatedly about the new policy.

entries.definition_en: a device used to heat water or make a room warm
entries.example_cn: 中央加热器在冬天让房子保持温暖。
entries.example_en: The central heater keeps the house warm during winter.

entries.definition_en: a very fast pitch thrown in baseball
entries.example_cn: 投手投出了一个极速球，击球手无法击中。
entries.example_en: The pitcher threw a heater that the batter could not hit.

entries.definition_en: a tract of level wasteland with sandy soil and scrubby vegetation
entries.example_cn: 他们穿过荒原到达了村庄。
entries.example_en: They walked across the heath to reach the village.

entries.definition_en: a low evergreen shrub with small bell-shaped pink or purple flowers
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了石南花。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with blooming heath.

entries.definition_cn: 异教的；非亚伯拉罕诸教的
entries.definition_en: not adhering to an Abrahamic religion; pagan
entries.example_cn: 历史学家称这个部落为异教部落，因为它既不信奉基督教、犹太教，也不信奉伊斯兰教。
entries.example_en: The historian described the tribe as heathen because it followed neither Christianity, Judaism, nor Islam.

entries.definition_en: a person who does not acknowledge your god
entries.example_cn: 这部古籍描述了生活在北部山区的异教部落。
entries.example_en: The ancient text described the heathen tribes living in the northern mountains.

entries.definition_cn: 异教徒般的；异教的；非基督教的
entries.definition_en: resembling a heathen; pagan or non-Christian
entries.example_cn: 这些异教仪式是在古代神庙中举行的。
entries.example_en: The heathenish rituals were performed in the ancient temple.

entries.definition_cn: 异教信仰或习俗；异教世界
entries.definition_en: pagan religious beliefs or practices; heathendom
entries.example_cn: 对异教的研究提供了对古代文化信仰的见解。
entries.example_en: The study of heathenism provides insight into ancient cultural beliefs.

entries.definition_cn: 帚石南等杜鹃花科植物
entries.definition_en: an evergreen plant of the heath family, especially Calluna vulgaris, with small purple, pink, or white flowers
entries.example_cn: 山丘上覆盖着紫色的帚石南花。
entries.example_en: The hills were covered in purple heather.

entries.definition_cn: 将不同颜色的纱线交织以产生斑点的织法或效果
entries.definition_en: the use or effect of interweaving yarns of mixed colors to produce flecks
entries.example_cn: 织物中的混色效果是通过交织不同颜色的纱线形成的。
entries.example_en: The heather effect in the fabric was created by interweaving yarns of different colors.

entries.definition_en: a tract of open scrubland dominated by low-growing woody vegetation, usually on infertile acidic soil
entries.example_cn: 稀有的鸟类经常能在海岸附近的荒原上筑巢。
entries.example_en: Rare birds can often be found nesting in the heathland near the coast.

entries.definition_en: a system for heating a room or building
entries.example_cn: 这所房子的中央供暖系统非常高效。
entries.example_en: The central heating in this house is very efficient.

entries.definition_cn: 使某物变热的行为或过程
entries.definition_en: the act or process of making something hot
entries.example_cn: 空气受热后上升。
entries.example_en: The heating of the air causes it to rise.

entries.definition_en: without heat
entries.example_cn: 这种无热过程在不额外加热的情况下运行。
entries.example_en: The heatless process operates without added heat.

entries.definition_en: a serious medical condition caused by exposure to extreme heat
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者在沙漠中走了几个小时后就中暑昏倒了。
entries.example_en: The hikers collapsed from heatstroke after walking in the desert for hours.

entries.definition_en: to lift or raise something
entries.example_cn: 她设法把箱子举到了桌子上。
entries.example_en: She managed to heave the box onto the table.

entries.definition_en: to throw something with great physical effort
entries.example_cn: 水手不得不费力地将沉重的锚扔过船舷。
entries.example_en: The sailor had to heave the heavy anchor over the side.

entries.definition_cn: 费力地发出（叹息等声音）
entries.definition_en: to utter a sigh or other sound with effort
entries.example_cn: 考试结束后，他长舒了一口气。
entries.example_en: He heaved a sigh of relief when the exam was over.

entries.definition_en: to rise and move in a rolling way, like waves
entries.example_cn: 随着风暴逼近，大海开始翻滚。
entries.example_en: The sea began to heave as the storm approached.

entries.definition_en: an upward movement, especially a rhythmical rising and falling
entries.example_cn: 船随着波浪上下起伏。
entries.example_en: The ship heaved up and down with the waves.

entries.definition_en: the action of lifting something heavy with great effort
entries.example_cn: 那块石头被举起的动作足以震裂墙壁。
entries.example_en: The heave of the stone was enough to crack the wall.

entries.definition_en: an involuntary spasm of vomiting that does not produce anything
entries.example_cn: 垃圾的气味让他干呕了一下。
entries.example_en: The smell of the garbage caused a heave.

entries.definition_en: a horizontal shift in rock layers caused by geological forces
entries.example_cn: 地震导致断层线发生了显著的错动。
entries.example_en: The earthquake caused a significant heave in the fault line.

entries.definition_en: peculiarly fortunate or appropriate; as if by divine intervention
entries.example_cn: 遇见我的老朋友是一个天赐的机会。
entries.example_en: It was a heaven-sent opportunity to meet my old friend.

entries.definition_en: relating to or inhabiting a divine heaven
entries.example_cn: 天使唱了一首天上的歌。
entries.example_en: The angels sang a heavenly song.

entries.definition_en: of or belonging to heaven or god
entries.example_cn: 祈祷后，他感到一种神圣的宁静。
entries.example_en: He felt a heavenly peace after the prayer.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the sky
entries.example_cn: 天体在夜空中移动。
entries.example_en: The heavenly bodies move across the night sky.

entries.definition_en: the apparent surface of the imaginary sphere on which celestial bodies appear to be projected
entries.example_cn: 古代天文学家在天穹中绘制了星图。
entries.example_en: The ancient astronomers mapped the stars in the heavens.

entries.definition_en: toward heaven
entries.example_cn: 他仰望天堂祈祷。
entries.example_en: He looked heavenward in prayer.

entries.definition_cn: 向天堂（或天空）的；朝向天堂（或天空）的
entries.definition_en: directed toward heaven or the sky
entries.example_cn: 那条通往天空的道路穿过云层。
entries.example_en: The heavenward path led through the clouds.

entries.definition_en: in the direction of heaven or the sky
entries.example_cn: 火箭向天发射，消失在云层中。
entries.example_en: The rocket shot heavenwards, disappearing into the clouds.

entries.definition_en: a workman who heaves freight or bulk goods (especially at a dockyard)
entries.example_cn: 那位老搬运工记得每艘船都必须手工装载的日子。
entries.example_en: The old heaver remembered the days when every ship had to be loaded by hand.

entries.definition_en: a bar used as a lever (as in twisting rope)
entries.example_cn: 水手们用一个沉重的杠杆将粗绳缠绕在柱子上。
entries.example_en: The sailors used a heavy heaver to twist the thick rope around the post.

entries.definition_cn: 马的慢性呼吸道疾病，表现为呼气困难和腹侧起伏
entries.definition_en: a chronic lung disease in horses causing difficulty breathing out and rising and falling of the sides
entries.example_cn: 这匹老马冬天患了喘气病。
entries.example_en: The old horse suffered from heaves during the winter.

entries.definition_en: relating to an aircraft that weighs more than the air it displaces
entries.example_cn: 重于空气的飞行发展是航空史上的一个重大里程碑。
entries.example_en: The development of heavier-than-air flight was a major milestone in aviation history.

entries.definition_en: to a considerable degree
entries.example_cn: 该公司在新技术上投入了大量资金。
entries.example_en: The company has heavily invested in new technology.

entries.definition_en: to an excessive degree
entries.example_cn: 他在聚会上酗酒。
entries.example_en: He was drinking heavily at the party.

entries.definition_en: with great force
entries.example_cn: 风猛烈地吹打着窗户。
entries.example_en: The wind blew heavily against the window.

entries.definition_en: slowly as if burdened by much weight
entries.example_cn: 他缓慢地走上楼梯，仿佛背负着重物。
entries.example_en: He walked heavily up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: in a labored manner
entries.example_cn: 她费力地说话，努力寻找合适的词汇。
entries.example_en: She spoke heavily, struggling to find the words.

entries.definition_en: in a heavy-footed manner
entries.example_cn: 士兵在雪地上笨重地走着。
entries.example_en: The soldier walked heavily across the snow.

entries.definition_cn: 以坚固、厚重或加强的结构
entries.definition_en: with a strong, solid, or reinforced construction
entries.example_cn: 他们使用了一辆重型卡车来搬运机器。
entries.example_en: They used a heavily built truck to move the machinery.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being very heavy
entries.example_cn: 手提箱的沉重使得携带变得困难。
entries.example_en: The heaviness of the suitcase made it difficult to carry.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of persistent sadness
entries.example_cn: 听到坏消息后，她心中笼罩着一层沉重的悲伤。
entries.example_en: A heaviness settled over her heart after the bad news.

entries.definition_en: an unwelcome burdensome difficulty
entries.example_cn: 繁重的税收法规拖慢了企业的发展。
entries.example_en: The heaviness of the tax regulations slowed down the business.

entries.definition_cn: 沉闷、呆板、缺乏流畅的特质
entries.definition_en: an oppressive quality that is laborious and solemn and lacks grace or fluency
entries.example_cn: 散文的笨拙与庄严使得阅读体验变得乏味。
entries.example_en: The heaviness of the prose made the reading experience tedious.

entries.definition_cn: 线条或标记的粗重程度
entries.definition_en: the quality of being thick or heavy in a line or mark
entries.example_cn: 艺术家用粗笔使树的轮廓呈现出一定的粗重感。
entries.example_en: The artist used a thick brush to give the tree's outline a certain heaviness.

entries.definition_cn: 喘息；（尤指剧烈运动后的）沉重而急促的呼吸
entries.definition_en: heavy, labored breathing, especially after exertion
entries.example_cn: 马拉松后，他喘着粗气，显得十分疲惫。
entries.example_en: His heaving breaths after the marathon showed how exhausted he was.

entries.definition_en: an upward movement, especially a rhythmical rising and falling
entries.example_cn: 这艘船被汹涌的波涛抛来抛去。
entries.example_en: The ship was tossed by the heaving waves.

entries.definition_en: the act of lifting something with great effort
entries.example_cn: 工人们开始费力地举起那块巨石，人群惊叹不已。
entries.example_en: The crowd watched in awe as the workers began the heaving of the massive stone.

entries.definition_en: the act of throwing something heavy with great effort
entries.example_cn: 将炮弹费力地投掷到田野上，展示了巨大的力量。
entries.example_en: The heaving of the cannonball across the field was a display of immense strength.

entries.definition_en: of comparatively great physical weight or density
entries.example_cn: 那个沉重的箱子很难抬起。
entries.example_en: The heavy box was difficult to lift.

entries.definition_en: unusually great in degree or quantity or number
entries.example_cn: 昨晚下了大雨。
entries.example_en: There was a heavy rain last night.

entries.definition_en: of the military or industry; using (or being) the heaviest and most powerful armaments or weapons or equipment
entries.example_cn: 军队将重型坦克部署到前线。
entries.example_en: The army deployed heavy tanks to the front line.

entries.definition_en: marked by great psychological weight; weighted down especially with sadness or troubles or weariness
entries.example_cn: 葬礼后，他感到悲痛欲绝。
entries.example_en: He felt heavy with grief after the funeral.

entries.definition_en: in a heavy manner; heavily
entries.example_cn: 听到坏消息后，他步履沉重。
entries.example_en: He walked heavily after hearing the bad news.

entries.definition_en: an actor who plays villainous roles
entries.example_cn: 剧中的反派演员非常逼真。
entries.example_en: The heavy in the play was very convincing.

entries.definition_en: usually describes a large person who is fat but has a large frame to carry it
entries.example_cn: 那个壮实的人很容易搬动家具。
entries.example_en: The heavy man could easily lift the furniture.

entries.definition_en: a serious (or tragic) role in a play
entries.example_cn: 他在新的制作中被选为悲剧角色。
entries.example_en: He was cast as the heavy in the new production.

entries.definition_en: designed for heavy work
entries.example_cn: 我们需要一辆重型卡车来搬运这些家具。
entries.example_en: We need a heavy-duty truck to move this furniture.

entries.definition_cn: （非正式）非常严肃、强烈或要求很高的
entries.definition_en: very serious, intense, or demanding (informal)
entries.example_cn: 项目落后于计划时，团队面临着一个要求极高的挑战。
entries.example_en: The team faced a heavy-duty challenge when the project fell behind schedule.

entries.definition_en: slow-moving and lacking ease or lightness
entries.example_cn: 那位老人在房间里迈着笨重的步伐移动。
entries.example_en: The old man moved with heavy-footed steps across the room.

entries.definition_en: unjustly domineering
entries.example_cn: 政府对待抗议者的专横手段遭到了广泛谴责。
entries.example_en: The government's heavy-handed tactics against the protesters were widely condemned.

entries.definition_cn: 笨手笨脚的；手上动作粗拙的
entries.definition_en: clumsy or awkward, especially in using the hands
entries.example_cn: 有些人说：“我不会做糕点，我手太笨了。”
entries.example_en: Some people say, “I can’t make pastry; I’m too heavy-handed.”

entries.definition_cn: 强硬粗暴或缺乏策略与圆通
entries.definition_en: the quality of being forceful, domineering, or lacking tact and finesse
entries.example_cn: 政府处理抗议活动时表现出的强硬粗暴引发了公众的愤怒。
entries.example_en: The government's heavy-handedness in dealing with the protest caused public anger.

entries.definition_en: having a large, solid, and somewhat overweight build
entries.example_cn: 那个矮胖的男人舒适地坐在扶手椅里。
entries.example_en: The heavyset man sat comfortably in the armchair.

entries.definition_en: a person of exceptional importance and reputation
entries.example_cn: 她被认为是环境科学领域的重要人物。
entries.example_en: She is considered a heavyweight in the field of environmental science.

entries.definition_en: a very large or heavy person
entries.example_cn: 那位大块头拳击手比对手高大许多。
entries.example_en: The heavyweight boxer towered over his opponents.

entries.definition_en: the heaviest weight class division in combat sports
entries.example_cn: 重量级是拳击中最负盛名的类别。
entries.example_en: The heavyweight division is the most prestigious category in boxing.

entries.definition_en: a professional boxer weighing more than 190 pounds
entries.example_cn: 粉丝们聚集在一起观看世纪重量级拳击赛。
entries.example_en: Fans gathered to watch the heavyweight fight of the century.

entries.definition_en: an amateur boxer in the heavyweight division
entries.example_cn: 这位重量级业余拳击选手昨晚赢得了地区锦标赛的冠军。
entries.example_en: The heavyweight won the regional amateur championship last night.

entries.definition_en: a heavyweight wrestler
entries.example_cn: 这位摔跤重量级选手凭借巨大的力量主宰了比赛。
entries.example_en: The heavyweight wrestler dominated the match with his sheer power.

entries.definition_en: happening once every seven days
entries.example_cn: 教堂每周日上午举行一次礼拜。
entries.example_en: The church holds a hebdomadal service every Sunday morning.

entries.definition_en: a great sacrifice; an ancient Greek or Roman sacrifice of 100 oxen
entries.example_cn: 古希腊人在危机时期举行百牲祭以敬奉众神。
entries.example_en: The ancient Greeks performed a hecatomb to honor the gods during times of crisis.

entries.definition_cn: 严厉质问或起哄打断（尤指演出中的表演者）
entries.definition_en: to question or interrupt someone harshly, especially during a performance
entries.example_cn: 观众用大声的提问向演讲者挑衅。
entries.example_en: The audience heckled the speaker with loud questions.

entries.definition_en: comb with a heckle
entries.example_cn: 他们用梳麻器梳理生亚麻，为编织做准备。
entries.example_en: They heckled the raw flax to prepare it for weaving.

entries.definition_en: a comb for separating flax fibers
entries.example_cn: 织工在纺线前使用梳麻器将亚麻纤维分开。
entries.example_en: The weaver used a heckle to separate the flax fibers before spinning.

entries.definition_en: someone who tries to embarrass you by making gibes, asking questions, or raising objections.
entries.example_cn: 演讲者被一个从房间后方大声提问的挑衅者打断。
entries.example_en: The speaker was interrupted by a heckler shouting questions from the back of the room.

entries.definition_en: the act of shouting to interrupt a speech with which you disagree
entries.example_cn: 尽管观众起哄，演讲者仍努力继续下去。
entries.example_en: The speaker struggled to continue despite the heckling from the audience.

entries.definition_en: a unit of surface area equal to 10,000 square meters
entries.example_cn: 这座农场占地五公顷肥沃土地。
entries.example_en: The farm covers five hectares of fertile land.

entries.definition_en: very busy with activity and confusion
entries.example_cn: 市中心早上八点十分忙乱。
entries.example_en: The city center is hectic at eight in the morning.

entries.definition_en: in a frenzied or wildly excited manner
entries.example_cn: 她忙乱地工作，以便在截止日期前完成项目。
entries.example_en: She worked hectically to finish the project before the deadline.

entries.definition_cn: 一种历史上的明胶印刷机，通过将原稿上的油墨转印到明胶板上复制文件
entries.definition_en: a historical duplicator that makes copies by transferring ink from an original onto a gelatin plate
entries.example_cn: 在复印机普及之前，学生使用明胶印刷机复制笔记。
entries.example_en: Before photocopiers were common, students used a hectograph to duplicate their notes.

entries.definition_cn: 用明胶印刷机复制文件
entries.definition_en: to duplicate a document using a hectograph
entries.example_cn: 老师用明胶印刷机为全班复制了教案。
entries.example_en: The teacher hectographed the lesson plan for the entire class.

entries.definition_en: a metric unit of volume equal to 100 liters
entries.example_cn: 这家酒厂每年生产五千百升葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: The winery produces five thousand hectoliters of wine annually.

entries.definition_cn: 等于100升的公制体积单位；百升
entries.definition_en: a metric unit of volume equal to 100 liters
entries.example_cn: 这家酿酒厂每年生产五千百升葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: The winery produces five thousand hectolitres of wine every year.

entries.definition_en: to bully or domineer over someone
entries.example_cn: 经理从不犹豫地斥责下属的错误。
entries.example_en: The manager never hesitated to hector his subordinates about their mistakes.

entries.definition_en: a fence made of closely planted shrubs or bushes
entries.example_cn: 他们沿着高大树篱旁边的小路行走。
entries.example_en: They walked along the path next to the tall hedge.

entries.definition_en: a technique used to reduce financial risk
entries.example_cn: 该公司通过对冲来防范股价下跌的风险。
entries.example_en: The company used a hedge to protect itself against falling stock prices.

entries.definition_en: an intentionally ambiguous statement
entries.example_cn: 他的演讲充满了含糊其辞的言论，没有给出明确的方向。
entries.example_en: His speech was full of hedges that gave no clear direction.

entries.definition_en: to avoid giving a direct answer or fulfilling a duty
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家含糊其辞地回答，以避免引发争议。
entries.example_en: The politician hedged his answer to avoid controversy.

entries.definition_en: to minimize loss or risk
entries.example_cn: 投资者对冲其投资组合以减少潜在损失。
entries.example_en: Investors hedge their portfolios to minimize potential losses.

entries.definition_en: to enclose with a hedge
entries.example_cn: 他们决定用树篱围起花园，把狗关在里面。
entries.example_en: They decided to hedge the garden to keep the dogs inside.

entries.definition_en: to hinder or restrict with a hedge
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子被一排茂密的灌木丛围住了。
entries.example_en: The old house was hedged by a thick row of bushes.

entries.definition_en: worded evasively to avoid making a definite statement
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家给出了一个含糊其辞的回答，以避免对某项具体政策做出承诺。
entries.example_en: The politician gave a hedged answer to avoid committing to a specific policy.

entries.definition_cn: 通过另一项金融资产进行对冲以防范财务损失的
entries.definition_en: protected against financial loss by being offset with another financial asset
entries.example_cn: 该基金持有对冲头寸，以限制其对汇率波动的风险敞口。
entries.example_en: The fund held a hedged position to limit its exposure to currency fluctuations.

entries.definition_en: small nocturnal Old World mammal covered with both hair and protective spines
entries.example_cn: 孩子对花园里的刺猬很着迷。
entries.example_en: The child was fascinated by the hedgehog in the garden.

entries.definition_cn: （美国）类似刺猬的多种带刺哺乳动物（如豪猪）
entries.definition_en: (US) any of several spiny mammals, such as a porcupine, resembling a hedgehog
entries.example_cn: 在美国的一些用法中，豪猪可能被称为 hedgehog。
entries.example_en: In some US usage, a porcupine may be called a hedgehog.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes or mends hedges
entries.example_cn: 这位树篱工人在冬天来临前修好了受损的树篱。
entries.example_en: The hedger repaired the damaged hedge before winter.

entries.definition_en: a person who avoids giving a clear or direct answer
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家是个老练的回避者，从不承诺具体的政策。
entries.example_en: The politician was a skilled hedger, never committing to a specific policy.

entries.definition_en: someone who counterbalances one transaction against another to protect against loss
entries.example_cn: 基金经理聘请了一位对冲者，以抵消新股票投资组合的风险。
entries.example_en: The fund manager hired a hedger to offset the risks of the new stock portfolio.

entries.definition_en: a fence made by planting shrubs or bushes in a row
entries.example_cn: 那座旧农场被一道茂密的树篱环绕。
entries.example_en: The old farm was surrounded by a thick hedgerow.

entries.definition_en: a technique used to reduce or eliminate financial risk, such as taking two opposite positions to offset potential price changes.
entries.example_cn: 该公司利用对冲来保护自己免受股市波动的影响。
entries.example_en: The company used hedging to protect itself against fluctuations in the stock market.

entries.definition_cn: 使用故意含糊或不置可否的说法
entries.definition_en: the use of intentionally ambiguous or noncommittal statements
entries.example_cn: 当被问及项目的未来时，经理没有给出明确答复，而是含糊其辞。
entries.example_en: When asked about the project's future, the manager resorted to hedging instead of giving a clear answer.

entries.definition_cn: 享乐的；与快乐或享乐主义有关的
entries.definition_en: devoted to or concerned with pleasure and enjoyment
entries.example_cn: 富人的享乐主义生活方式往往忽视长期后果。
entries.example_en: The hedonic lifestyle of the wealthy often ignores long-term consequences.

entries.definition_en: the pursuit of pleasure as a matter of ethical principle
entries.example_cn: 他的哲学植根于享乐主义，将个人幸福置于一切之上。
entries.example_en: His philosophy was rooted in hedonism, prioritizing personal happiness above all else.

entries.definition_en: an ethical system that evaluates the pursuit of pleasure as the highest good
entries.example_cn: 辩论的中心在于享乐主义是否能作为一个完整的道德框架。
entries.example_en: The debate centered on whether hedonism could serve as a complete moral framework.

entries.definition_en: a person motivated by desires for sensual pleasures
entries.example_cn: 这位享乐主义者认为追求快乐是最高尚的美德。
entries.example_en: The hedonist believed that the pursuit of pleasure was the highest good.

entries.definition_en: devoted to pleasure
entries.example_cn: 他们享乐主义的生活方式包括不断的派对和奢华享受。
entries.example_en: Their hedonistic lifestyle involved constant parties and luxury.

entries.definition_en: the characteristic cry of a donkey
entries.example_cn: 那头驴发出了一声响亮的驴叫。
entries.example_en: The donkey let out a loud hee-haw.

entries.definition_en: to make a braying sound characteristic of donkeys
entries.example_cn: 那头驴在田野里大声发出驴叫。
entries.example_en: The donkey hee-hawed loudly in the field.

entries.definition_cn: 焦虑、恐惧、不安或恶心的感觉
entries.definition_en: a feeling of anxiety, fear, uneasiness, or nausea
entries.example_cn: 那条黑暗的小巷让他心里发毛。
entries.example_en: The dark alley gave him the heebie-jeebies.

entries.definition_en: to pay close attention to or take notice of
entries.example_cn: 下雨开车前，你应该注意警示标志。
entries.example_en: You should heed the warning signs before driving in the rain.

entries.definition_en: careful attention
entries.example_cn: 她注意听从了医生的建议。
entries.example_en: She paid heed to the doctor's advice.

usage.label: pay heed to + noun
usage.pattern: w12094r0 supports the fixed phrase pattern.

entries.definition_en: paying close and thoughtful attention to something
entries.example_cn: 她在签署合同前对每一个细节都仔细留意。
entries.example_en: She was heedful of every detail in the contract before signing it.

entries.definition_en: showing cautious attention
entries.example_cn: 司机对结冰的路况始终保持谨慎留意。
entries.example_en: The driver remained heedful of the icy road conditions.

entries.definition_en: giving attention or care
entries.example_cn: 一位关注孩子的父母会注意到孩子行为的变化。
entries.example_en: A heedful parent will notice changes in their child's behavior.

entries.definition_cn: 没有注意到某事的；不留心的
entries.definition_en: unaware of or inattentive to something
entries.example_cn: 他没有注意到眼前的危险。
entries.example_en: He was heedless of the danger ahead.

entries.definition_en: carelessly unconcerned; thoughtless
entries.example_cn: 她随口说了一句漫不经心的话，伤害了他的感情。
entries.example_en: She made a heedless remark that hurt his feelings.

entries.definition_en: in a manner without care or concern
entries.example_cn: 他漫不经心地穿过拥挤的十字路口。
entries.example_en: He drove heedlessly through the crowded intersection.

entries.definition_en: a lack of attentiveness, especially towards children or helpless people
entries.example_cn: 这起事故是由司机的疏忽造成的。
entries.example_en: The accident was caused by the driver's heedlessness.

entries.definition_en: the trait of acting rashly and without prudence
entries.example_cn: 他的鲁莽导致他做出了危险的投资。
entries.example_en: His heedlessness led him to make a dangerous investment.

entries.definition_en: the trait of forgetting or ignoring your responsibilities
entries.example_cn: 她的失职导致错过了好几个截止日期。
entries.example_en: Her heedlessness resulted in several missed deadlines.

entries.definition_en: the back part of a shoe or boot that touches the ground
entries.example_cn: 她在结冰的人行道上滑倒时，鞋跟断了。
entries.example_en: The heel of her shoe broke on the icy sidewalk.

entries.definition_en: the back part of the human foot
entries.example_cn: 他走了一整天，脚后跟起了水泡。
entries.example_en: He has a blister on his heel from walking all day.

entries.definition_en: one of the hard, crusty ends of a loaf of bread
entries.example_cn: 我们把面包头留下来做面包屑。
entries.example_en: We saved the heel of the bread to make breadcrumbs.

entries.definition_en: a person who is morally bad or wicked
entries.example_cn: 警察警告居民不要信任那个坏人。
entries.example_en: The police warned the neighborhood not to trust the heel.

entries.definition_en: to tilt or lean to one side
entries.example_cn: 船在强风中开始倾斜。
entries.example_en: The boat began to heel in the strong wind.

entries.definition_en: to follow closely behind someone
entries.example_cn: 侦探设法在拥挤的市场中尾随嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The detective managed to heel the suspect through the crowded market.

entries.definition_en: to perform a dance or movement using the heels
entries.example_cn: 舞者在表演中完美地用脚跟踢了一下。
entries.example_en: The dancer executed a perfect heel kick during the routine.

entries.definition_en: to strike with the heel of a club
entries.example_cn: 高尔夫球手不得不将球杆后部击打出来，将球从沙坑中打出。
entries.example_en: The golfer had to heel the ball out of the sand trap.

entries.definition_en: to test the weight of something by lifting it
entries.example_cn: 她掂了掂那个包，看是否太重拿不动。
entries.example_en: She hefted the bag to see if it was too heavy to carry.

entries.definition_en: to lift or elevate something
entries.example_cn: 他把箱子举到了架子上。
entries.example_en: He hefted the box onto the shelf.

entries.definition_en: the feel or amount of weight; heaviness
entries.example_cn: 那扇沉重的门手感极佳。
entries.example_en: The heavy door had a satisfying heft to it.

entries.definition_en: of considerable weight and size
entries.example_cn: 她费力地提着沉重的行李箱走上楼梯。
entries.example_en: She struggled to carry the hefty suitcase up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: large in amount or extent or degree
entries.example_cn: 这个项目需要大量的时间和资金投入。
entries.example_en: The project required a hefty investment of time and money.

entries.definition_en: having great physical strength and weight; rugged and powerful
entries.example_cn: 这位强壮有力的拳击手轻易地击败了对手。
entries.example_en: The hefty boxer easily overpowered his opponent.

entries.definition_en: a leading or paramount power
entries.example_cn: 该国寻求维持其作为地区霸权国的地位。
entries.example_en: The nation sought to maintain its status as the regional hegemon.

entries.definition_en: the dominance or leadership of one social group or nation over others
entries.example_cn: 该国试图在该地区维持其文化霸权。
entries.example_en: The country sought to maintain its cultural hegemony in the region.

entries.definition_en: a mass migration of people fleeing from a dangerous or hostile place
entries.example_cn: 历史上的迁徙标志着伊斯兰历法的开始。
entries.example_en: The historical hegira marked the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

entries.definition_en: a young female cow
entries.example_cn: 农场主买了一头怀孕的小母牛来扩充牛群。
entries.example_en: The farmer bought a pregnant heifer to add to his herd.

entries.definition_cn: 垂直延伸的维度；从某物底部到顶部的距离
entries.definition_en: the vertical dimension of extension; distance from the base of something to the top
entries.example_cn: 这座建筑的高度是五十米。
entries.example_en: The height of the building is fifty meters.

entries.definition_cn: （对于站立的人）从头到脚的距离
entries.definition_en: (of a standing person) the distance from head to foot
entries.example_cn: 他的身高正好是一米八。
entries.example_en: His height is exactly one meter eighty.

entries.definition_cn: 可达到的最高水平或程度；发展的最高阶段
entries.definition_en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development
entries.example_cn: 这座山代表了人类成就的巅峰。
entries.example_en: The mountain represents the height of human achievement.

entries.definition_cn: 海拔高度，特别是相对于海平面或地球表面的高度
entries.definition_en: elevation especially above sea level or above the earth's surface
entries.example_cn: 飞机在极高的海拔飞行。
entries.example_en: The plane flew at a great height.

entries.definition_en: to make something more extreme, raise its quantity, degree, or intensity
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策旨在提高公众对该问题的认识。
entries.example_en: The new policy aims to heighten public awareness of the issue.

entries.definition_en: to become more extreme or intense
entries.example_cn: 随着争论的继续，房间里的紧张气氛加剧了。
entries.example_en: The tension in the room heightened as the argument continued.

entries.definition_en: to make something more intense, stronger, or more marked
entries.example_cn: 风暴加剧了低洼地区发生洪水的危险。
entries.example_en: The storm heightened the danger of flooding in the low-lying areas.

entries.definition_en: to increase the level of something
entries.example_cn: 教练试图在决赛前提升球队的士气。
entries.example_en: The coach tried to heighten the team's morale before the final match.

entries.definition_en: to make one's senses more acute or alert
entries.example_cn: 清新的空气似乎使她的感官更加敏锐。
entries.example_en: The fresh air seemed to heighten her senses.

entries.definition_en: to increase the height of something
entries.example_cn: 他们决定加高围栏以防止入侵者。
entries.example_en: They decided to heighten the fence to prevent intruders.

entries.definition_cn: 逐渐加剧的；变得更强烈的
entries.definition_en: becoming more intense or pronounced
entries.example_cn: 随着争论升级，房间里日益加剧的紧张气氛显而易见。
entries.example_en: The heightening tension in the room was palpable as the argument escalated.

entries.definition_cn: 山坡上的住宅区或开发区
entries.definition_en: a neighborhood or development built on a hill or mountain
entries.example_cn: 他们搬到了高地上一处新的住宅区。
entries.example_en: They moved to a new development in the Heights.

entries.definition_cn: 极其邪恶的；令人发指的
entries.definition_en: extremely wicked, deeply criminal
entries.example_cn: 这起极其邪恶的罪行震惊了整个社区。
entries.example_en: The heinous crime shocked the entire community.

entries.definition_en: in a terribly evil manner
entries.example_cn: 那个恶棍极其邪恶地策划摧毁这座城市。
entries.example_en: The villain plotted heinously to destroy the city.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being shockingly cruel and inhumane
entries.example_cn: 这桩罪行的极度残忍震惊了整个社区。
entries.example_en: The heinousness of the crime shocked the entire community.

entries.definition_en: a person who is entitled by law or by the terms of a will to inherit the estate of another
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻的继承人从祖父那里继承了一大笔财富。
entries.example_en: The young heir inherited a vast fortune from his grandfather.

entries.definition_en: a person who inherits some title or office
entries.example_cn: 王位的继任者将于下个月加冕。
entries.example_en: The heir to the throne will be crowned next month.

entries.definition_cn: （无遗嘱情况下）依法有权继承死者财产的人
entries.definition_en: the person legally entitled to inherit the property of someone who dies intestate
entries.example_cn: 作为唯一的法定继承人，她将继承全部遗产。
entries.example_en: As the only heir-at-law, she will receive the entire estate.

entries.definition_en: a woman who inherits property or title
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻的女继承人回到家族庄园管理生意。
entries.example_en: The young heiress returned to the family estate to manage the business.

entries.definition_en: something that has been in a family for generations
entries.example_cn: 我祖母的结婚戒指是一件珍贵的传家宝。
entries.example_en: My grandmother's wedding ring is a precious heirloom.

entries.definition_en: property that is considered by law or custom as inseparable from an inheritance
entries.example_cn: 家族银器是必须传给长子的一项法定继承财产。
entries.example_en: The family silver is an heirloom that must pass to the eldest son.

entries.definition_cn: 抢劫或盗窃（尤指针对银行、博物馆等机构的）
entries.definition_en: a robbery or burglary, especially one targeting a bank, museum, or other institution
entries.example_cn: 警方正在调查一起银行重大盗窃案。
entries.example_en: The police are investigating a major heist at the bank.

entries.definition_en: robbery at gunpoint
entries.example_cn: 这次持枪抢劫涉及一支武装团伙。
entries.example_en: The heist involved a team of armed robbers.

entries.definition_en: commit a burglary; enter and rob a dwelling
entries.example_cn: 罪犯在清晨抢劫了珠宝店。
entries.example_en: Criminals heisted the jewelry store early in the morning.

entries.definition_cn: 大规模逃离敌对环境的迁徙
entries.definition_en: a journey undertaken by a large group to escape from a hostile environment
entries.example_cn: 难民们开始了从战乱地区的迁徙。
entries.example_en: The refugees began their hejira from the war-torn region.

entries.definition_cn: 与星体的晨见或昏见有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to a star's first visible rising just before sunrise or last visible setting just after sunset
entries.example_cn: 古代天文学家记录天狼星的晨见升起，以此标记洪水季节的开始。
entries.example_en: Ancient astronomers recorded the heliacal rising of Sirius to mark the start of the flood season.

entries.definition_en: any plant of the genus Helianthus characterized by large flower heads with dark disk florets and showy yellow rays
entries.example_cn: 向日葵属植物巨大的黄色花盘随着太阳在天空中移动而转动。
entries.example_en: The helianthus turned its large yellow face to follow the sun across the sky.

entries.definition_en: shaped like a spiral or coil
entries.example_cn: DNA分子具有双螺旋结构。
entries.example_en: The DNA molecule has a double helical structure.

entries.definition_cn: 海利康号（一种绕在演奏者肩上的大号）
entries.definition_en: a large brass instrument resembling a tuba that is coiled over the shoulder
entries.example_cn: 乐团安排了一位演奏罕见海利康号的独奏家。
entries.example_en: The orchestra featured a soloist playing the rare helicon.

entries.definition_cn: 在某些等离子体中观测到的低频电磁波（螺旋波）
entries.definition_en: a low-frequency electromagnetic wave observed in certain plasmas
entries.example_cn: 科学家在实验室等离子体中探测到了一种螺旋波。
entries.example_en: Scientists detected a helicon wave in the laboratory plasma.

entries.definition_en: an aircraft that flies by rotating blades on top
entries.example_cn: 直升机降落在屋顶上。
entries.example_en: The helicopter landed on the roof.

entries.definition_en: having the sun as the center
entries.example_cn: 太阳系的日心模型将太阳置于中心。
entries.example_en: The heliocentric model of the solar system places the sun at the center.

entries.definition_en: a device that uses a mirror and sunlight to send telegraphic messages
entries.example_cn: 士兵们使用日光信号镜向基地发出信号。
entries.example_en: The soldiers used a heliograph to signal their position to the base.

entries.definition_en: to send a signal using a mirror and sunlight
entries.example_cn: 他们用日光信号镜发报了敌营的坐标。
entries.example_en: They heliographed the coordinates of the enemy camp.

entries.definition_en: the boundary marking the edge of the sun's influence; the boundary between the interplanetary medium and the interstellar medium
entries.example_cn: 航天器终于穿越日球层顶，进入了星际空间。
entries.example_en: Spacecraft have finally crossed the heliopause to enter interstellar space.

entries.definition_en: the region of space containing the sun and solar system
entries.example_cn: 科学家们正在研究日球层的边界。
entries.example_en: Scientists are studying the boundary of the heliosphere.

entries.definition_en: a green chalcedony with red spots that resemble blood
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商为戒指挑选了一块稀有的血滴石。
entries.example_en: The jeweler selected a rare heliotrope for the ring.

entries.definition_en: a designated area or facility for the takeoff and landing of helicopters
entries.example_cn: 直升机降落在酒店屋顶的直升机停机坪上。
entries.example_en: The helicopter landed at the heliport on the roof of the hotel.

entries.definition_en: a very light, colorless gas that is one of the six inert gases; it is the most difficult gas to turn into a liquid and is found in extractable amounts in certain natural gases.
entries.example_cn: 氦气比空气轻，因此被用来填充气球。
entries.example_en: Helium is used to fill balloons because it is lighter than air.

entries.definition_en: a structure made of something wound in a continuous loop, like DNA
entries.example_cn: DNA 是一种双螺旋结构，携带遗传信息。
entries.example_en: DNA is a double helix that carries genetic information.

entries.definition_en: a spiral line that winds around a cylinder or cone
entries.example_cn: 弹簧绕着圆柱体形成螺旋线。
entries.example_en: The spring forms a helix around the cylinder.

entries.definition_en: recklessly determined to achieve something
entries.example_cn: 那个不顾一切的司机无视红灯，引发了一起事故。
entries.example_en: The hell-bent driver ignored the red light and caused an accident.

entries.definition_en: at a very high speed
entries.example_cn: 汽车沿着高速公路飞快地疾驰而去。
entries.example_en: The car sped off hell-for-leather down the highway.

entries.definition_en: a large, dark-colored salamander found in rivers and streams in North America
entries.example_cn: 科学家在一条河流冰冷深水中发现了一只罕见的美东大蝾螈。
entries.example_en: Scientists discovered a rare hellbender living in the deep, cold waters of the river.

entries.definition_en: a malicious woman with a fierce temper
entries.example_cn: 邻居们抱怨隔壁那个泼妇。
entries.example_en: The neighbors complained about the hellcat next door.

entries.definition_cn: 铁筷子属的任一种植物
entries.definition_en: any plant of the Eurasian genus Helleborus
entries.example_cn: 冬季铁筷子的花常被误认为是雪花莲。
entries.example_en: Winter hellebore blooms are often mistaken for snowdrops.

entries.definition_cn: 一种具有粗大有毒根茎的百合科多年生草本植物
entries.definition_en: perennial herbs of the lily family having thick toxic rhizomes
entries.example_cn: 园丁从花坛里拔掉了这种植物，因为它有毒。
entries.example_en: The gardener removed the hellebore from the flowerbed because it was poisonous.

entries.definition_en: A rowdy or mischievous person, usually a young man.
entries.example_cn: 那个捣蛋鬼在聚会上到处惹是生非。
entries.example_en: The heller ran around causing trouble at the party.

entries.definition_cn: 捷克克朗的历史货币子单位，相当于克朗的百分之一
entries.definition_en: a historical Czech currency subunit equal to one hundredth of a koruna
entries.example_cn: 捷克克朗过去分为100个赫勒。
entries.example_en: The Czech koruna was formerly divided into 100 hellers.

entries.definition_cn: 斯洛伐克克朗的历史货币子单位，相当于克朗的百分之一
entries.definition_en: a historical Slovak currency subunit equal to one hundredth of a koruna
entries.example_cn: 斯洛伐克克朗过去分为100个赫勒。
entries.example_en: The Slovak koruna was formerly divided into 100 hellers.

entries.definition_en: the fire of Hell, imagined as punishment for the damned
entries.example_cn: 牧师生动地讲述了地狱之火的折磨。
entries.example_en: The preacher spoke vividly of the torments of hellfire.

entries.definition_en: a place characterized by extreme suffering and chaos
entries.example_cn: 难民形容这座饱受战争摧残的城市为地狱般的场所。
entries.example_en: The war-torn city was described as a hellhole by the refugees.

entries.definition_cn: 地狱犬（通常被描绘成体型、力量或速度异常的恶魔之犬）
entries.definition_en: a demonic dog of hell, typically depicted as unnaturally large, strong, or swift
entries.example_cn: 传说中，地狱犬守卫着冥界入口。
entries.example_en: In the legend, the hellhound guarded the entrance to the underworld.

entries.definition_en: an evil or otherwise unpleasant person
entries.example_cn: 侦探怀疑那个制造这起犯罪的恶人仍然逍遥法外。
entries.example_en: The detective suspected that the hellhound behind the crime was still at large.

entries.definition_en: a person, especially a young man, who is noisy, rude, and difficult to control
entries.example_cn: 父母担心他们的儿子——他在聚会上就是个捣蛋鬼。
entries.example_en: The parents were worried about their son, a hellion at parties.

entries.definition_cn: 极其糟糕的；极其难受的（非正式）
entries.definition_en: very unpleasant or difficult (informal)
entries.example_cn: 我们冒雨修理坏电脑时，经历了一段极其难熬的时光。
entries.example_en: We had a hellish time trying to fix the broken computer in the rain.

entries.definition_en: extremely cruel or evil
entries.example_cn: 这个故事描述了对叛徒施加的极其邪恶的惩罚。
entries.example_en: The story describes a hellish punishment inflicted on the traitor.

entries.definition_en: in a diabolical manner
entries.example_cn: 那个恶棍恶魔般地策划要摧毁这座城市。
entries.example_en: The villain plotted hellishly to destroy the city.

entries.definition_en: a word used to greet someone
entries.example_cn: 她向邻居挥手并打了个招呼。
entries.example_en: She waved and said hello to her neighbor.

entries.definition_en: the device used to steer a ship or boat
entries.example_cn: 船长站在舵旁引导船只穿过风暴。
entries.example_en: The captain stood at the helm to guide the ship through the storm.

entries.definition_en: a position of leadership or control
entries.example_cn: 他被邀请担任新研究项目的负责人。
entries.example_en: He was offered the helm of the new research project.

entries.definition_en: to be in charge of or control an organization or situation
entries.example_cn: 她掌管这家公司已超过二十年。
entries.example_en: She has helmed the company for over twenty years.

entries.definition_en: protective headgear made of hard material to resist blows
entries.example_cn: 建筑工人在现场必须佩戴安全头盔。
entries.example_en: Construction workers must wear a safety helmet on site.

entries.definition_cn: 纹章中置于盾牌上方的头盔
