entries.example_en: The inclination of the satellite's orbit is 51.6 degrees.

entries.definition_cn: （几何）直线相对于正 x 轴的倾角
entries.definition_en: in geometry, the angle formed by the positive x-axis and a given line, measured counterclockwise
entries.example_cn: 直线的倾角是从正 x 轴逆时针测量的。
entries.example_en: The inclination of the line is measured counterclockwise from the positive x-axis.

entries.definition_en: in physics, the angle a magnetic needle makes with the horizon
entries.example_cn: 磁倾角因你在地球上的位置不同而变化。
entries.example_en: The magnetic inclination varies depending on your location on Earth.

entries.definition_en: a slope or inclined surface
entries.example_cn: 陡峭的斜坡让攀爬变得筋疲力尽。
entries.example_en: The steep incline made the climb exhausting.

entries.definition_cn: 连接两个不同高度的斜面
entries.definition_en: an inclined surface connecting two levels
entries.example_cn: 他们使用坡道作为斜面来装载卡车。
entries.example_en: They used a ramp as an incline to load the truck.

entries.definition_en: be at an angle
entries.example_cn: 这条路在爬坡时急剧倾斜。
entries.example_en: The road inclines sharply as it goes up the hill.

entries.definition_cn: 有做某事或成为某种状态的倾向
entries.definition_en: have a tendency or disposition to do or be something
entries.example_cn: 我倾向于相信这个项目会成功。
entries.example_en: I incline to believe that the project will succeed.

usage.label: incline to
usage.pattern: incline to do or believe something

entries.definition_en: feel favorably disposed or willing
entries.example_cn: 我倾向于同意你的建议。
entries.example_en: I incline to agree with your suggestion.

entries.definition_cn: 点头或鞠躬时低下或弯曲头部或上身
entries.definition_en: lower or bend the head or upper body, as in a nod or bow
entries.example_cn: 他向长者低头表示尊敬。
entries.example_en: He inclined his head in respect to the elder.

entries.definition_en: bend one's ear towards a speaker to listen well
entries.example_cn: 她把耳朵侧向说话者，以便听清耳语。
entries.example_en: She inclined her ear toward the speaker to hear the whisper clearly.

entries.definition_cn: 使对某种行动或态度变得接受或愿意
entries.definition_en: make receptive or willing towards an action or attitude
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生们重视努力工作。
entries.example_en: The teacher inclined the students to value hard work.

entries.definition_en: having a preference or tendency to do something
entries.example_cn: 我倾向于同意你的提议。
entries.example_en: I am inclined to agree with your proposal.

entries.definition_en: tilted at an angle rather than being flat or vertical
entries.example_cn: 梯子斜靠在墙上，呈倾斜角度。
entries.example_en: The ladder was leaning against the wall at an inclined angle.

entries.definition_en: having made the necessary preparations
entries.example_cn: 我们现在准备动身去机场了。
entries.example_en: We are inclined to leave for the airport now.

entries.definition_cn: 倾向；倾斜或弯曲的动作
entries.definition_en: an inclination or tendency; the act of leaning or bending
entries.example_cn: 塔楼的倾斜是由地震引起的。
entries.example_en: The inclining of the tower was caused by the earthquake.

entries.definition_en: an instrument used by surveyors to measure angles of slope or elevation
entries.example_cn: 测量员使用倾角仪来测绘陡峭的山坡。
entries.example_en: The surveyor used an inclinometer to map the steep hillside.

entries.definition_en: a device used to measure the angle of an aircraft relative to the horizon
entries.example_cn: 飞行员检查倾斜仪以确保飞机处于水平状态。
entries.example_en: The pilot checked the inclinometer to ensure the plane was level.

entries.definition_en: a tool for measuring the angle of magnetic dip, often used in aviation
entries.example_cn: 倾角仪帮助导航员测量地磁倾角。
entries.example_en: The inclinometer helped the navigator measure the Earth's magnetic dip.

entries.definition_en: to surround something completely
entries.example_cn: 篱笆围住了整个花园。
entries.example_en: The fence incloses the entire garden.

entries.definition_en: to put something inside another thing
entries.example_cn: 请把信放入信封中。
entries.example_en: Please inclose the letter in the envelope.

entries.definition_en: a document enclosed with a letter
entries.example_cn: 请查收关于您申请的附函。
entries.example_en: Please find the inclosure regarding your application.

entries.definition_en: the act of putting something inside something else
entries.example_cn: 将包裹装入箱中只花了几秒钟。
entries.example_en: The inclosure of the package took only a few seconds.

entries.definition_en: to have something as a part of a whole
entries.example_cn: 价格包含早餐和晚餐。
entries.example_en: The price includes breakfast and dinner.

entries.definition_en: to add something to a set, group, or category
entries.example_cn: 请在名单上写上你的名字。
entries.example_en: Please include your name on the list.

entries.definition_en: to consider something as part of a group or category
entries.example_cn: 我们必须把安全纳入计划中。
entries.example_en: We must include safety in our planning.

entries.definition_en: to allow someone to participate or exercise rights
entries.example_cn: 俱乐部让所有成员参与决策过程。
entries.example_en: The club includes all members in the decision-making process.

entries.definition_cn: 使用 include 指令将另一个文件中的源代码引入程序
entries.definition_en: to use an include directive to bring source code from another file into a program
entries.example_cn: 程序在编译前使用 include 指令引入头文件的内容。
entries.example_en: The program includes the contents of the header file before compilation.

entries.definition_en: provided or enclosed as part of something
entries.example_cn: 订单里附带了一本小册子。
entries.example_en: A brochure was included with the order.

entries.definition_cn: 例如；指刚提到的群体中的部分
entries.definition_en: such as; introducing one or more parts of the group just mentioned
entries.example_cn: 该队包括来自几个国家的球员，其中包括法国和德国。
entries.example_en: The team included players from several countries, including France and Germany.

entries.definition_cn: 引入限定动词从句（非标准、罕见用法）
entries.definition_en: introducing a finite clause
entries.example_cn: 我一直认为，这是一个值得彻底审查的问题；审查可能得出各种结论，包括“它正在做政府当时希望它做的事情”这一结论。
entries.example_en: I have always argued that it is one that deserves a thorough-going policy review, which might come to all sorts of conclusions, including it is doing what the Government of the day wants it to.

entries.definition_cn: include 的现在分词和动名词形式
entries.definition_en: present participle and gerund of include
entries.example_cn: 该项目正在增加比原计划更多的功能。
entries.example_en: The project is including more features than originally planned.

entries.definition_en: the state of being included
entries.example_cn: 包含此项是标准做法。
entries.example_en: The inclusion of this item is standard practice.

entries.definition_en: the act of including something
entries.example_cn: 新政策的包含行为已于昨日宣布。
entries.example_en: The inclusion of the new policy was announced yesterday.

entries.definition_en: something included in a group, set, or total
entries.example_cn: 这首诗最近被纳入了教材。
entries.example_en: The poem was a recent inclusion in the textbook.

entries.definition_en: a small body found inside a cell, often indicating disease
entries.example_cn: 医生在组织样本中检测到一个异常细胞内小体。
entries.example_en: The doctor detected an abnormal inclusion in the tissue sample.

entries.definition_cn: 包含一切的；特别是包含规定界限的
entries.definition_en: including much or everything; and especially including stated limits
entries.example_cn: 价格包含早餐和税费。
entries.example_en: The price is inclusive of breakfast and taxes.

entries.definition_cn: 隐姓埋名的；匿名的；乔装的
entries.definition_en: having one's identity concealed; in disguise
entries.example_cn: 这位名流在整个活动期间都隐姓埋名。
entries.example_en: The celebrity was incognito throughout the event.

entries.definition_en: without revealing one's identity
entries.example_cn: 他匿名旅行以避免被认出。
entries.example_en: He traveled incognito to avoid being recognized.

entries.definition_en: the lack of logical connection or clarity in speech or writing
entries.example_cn: 演讲者的条理不清让听众难以跟上论点。
entries.example_en: The speaker's incoherence made it difficult for the audience to follow the argument.

entries.definition_en: speech or writing that is so confused it cannot be understood
entries.example_cn: 事故发生后，他处于完全胡言乱语的状态。
entries.example_en: After the accident, he spoke in a state of total incoherence.

entries.definition_en: the state of lacking logical connection or clarity
entries.example_cn: 报告的不连贯性使得理解要点变得困难。
entries.example_en: The incoherency of the report made it difficult to understand the main points.

entries.definition_en: nonsense that is unintelligible and lacks organization
entries.example_cn: 演讲者语无伦次的讲话完全是胡言乱语。
entries.example_en: The speaker's rambling speech was pure incoherency.

entries.definition_en: lacking logical or meaningful connection
entries.example_cn: 他的解释不连贯，难以理解。
entries.example_en: His explanation was incoherent and difficult to follow.

entries.definition_en: unable to express yourself clearly or fluently
entries.example_cn: 事故发生后，他变得口齿不清，无法清晰说话。
entries.example_en: After the accident, he became incoherent and could not speak clearly.

entries.definition_en: of waves having no stable phase relation
entries.example_cn: 该光源产生了非相干波。
entries.example_en: The light source produced incoherent waves.

entries.definition_cn: 语无伦次地；前后不连贯地
entries.definition_en: in an incoherent manner; without logical connection or clarity
entries.example_cn: 事故发生后，他说话语无伦次。
entries.example_en: He spoke incoherently after the accident.

entries.definition_en: not capable of catching fire and burning
entries.example_cn: 实验室出于安全考虑需要使用不燃材料。
entries.example_en: The laboratory requires the use of incombustible materials for safety.

entries.definition_en: money received, especially from work or investments, over a period of time
entries.example_cn: 他们的主要收入来自出售手工艺品。
entries.example_en: Their main income comes from selling handmade crafts.

entries.definition_cn: 正在到达的；即将到来的
entries.definition_en: arriving at a specific place or position
entries.example_cn: 进站的火车因大雨而延误。
entries.example_en: The incoming train was delayed by heavy rain.

entries.definition_en: about to take over a job or position held by someone else
entries.example_cn: 新任经理将于下周一开始工作。
entries.example_en: The incoming manager will start next Monday.

entries.definition_cn: 到达或进入的行为或过程
entries.definition_en: the action or process of arriving or entering
entries.example_cn: 新数据的传入导致系统变慢。
entries.example_en: The incoming of the new data caused the system to slow down.

entries.definition_en: unable to be measured or compared in value or size
entries.example_cn: 他们目标之间无法比较的巨大差距使得合作变得困难。
entries.example_en: The incommensurable gap between their goals made cooperation difficult.

entries.definition_cn: 不可公度的；没有共同度量单位的
entries.definition_en: not having a common measure
entries.example_cn: 正方形的边长与对角线不可公度。
entries.example_en: The side and diagonal of a square are incommensurable.

entries.definition_en: not matching in size, degree, or extent
entries.example_cn: 这种惩罚与罪行不相称。
entries.example_en: The punishment was incommensurate with the crime.

entries.definition_cn: 无法或不愿与外界交流的
entries.definition_en: unable or unwilling to communicate with outsiders
entries.example_cn: 这名囚犯被单独关押了数周，无法与外界联系。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was held incommunicado for several weeks.

entries.definition_cn: 以无法或不愿与外界交流的方式
entries.definition_en: in a way that prevents or avoids communication with outsiders
entries.example_cn: 这位歌手在偏远的录音室里与外界隔绝地工作，以避开媒体。
entries.example_en: The singer worked incommunicado in a remote studio to avoid the press.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being so much better than another that comparison is impossible
entries.example_cn: 她无与伦比的天才使她成名。
entries.example_en: The incomparability of her talent made her famous.

entries.definition_en: the condition of not being able to be compared
entries.example_cn: 这两种理论之间的不可比较性仍然是争论的话题。
entries.example_en: The incomparability of the two theories remains a subject of debate.

entries.definition_cn: 无法比较的；无与伦比的
entries.definition_en: impossible or unsuitable to compare; exceptionally good beyond comparison
entries.example_cn: 山顶的景色无与伦比。
entries.example_en: The view from the mountain top was incomparable.

entries.definition_en: in a way that cannot be compared; to an unmatched degree
entries.example_cn: 从山顶看到的景色美得无可比拟。
entries.example_en: The view from the mountain peak was incomparably beautiful.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unable to exist or work together harmoniously
entries.example_cn: 他们的工作风格存在深刻的冲突。
entries.example_en: There was a deep incompatibility between their working styles.

entries.definition_en: the state of two propositions being unable to be true at the same time
entries.example_cn: 这两个理论的不相容性导致了新假设的产生。
entries.example_en: The incompatibility of the two theories led to a new hypothesis.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which the immune system rejects foreign material
entries.example_cn: 由于供体和受体之间严重的免疫不相容性，移植手术失败了。
entries.example_en: The transplant failed due to severe incompatibility between donor and recipient.

entries.definition_en: not compatible
entries.example_cn: 这两个软件程序彼此不兼容。
entries.example_en: The two software programs are incompatible with each other.

entries.definition_cn: 无法与其他设备或组件连接使用的
entries.definition_en: incapable of being used with or connected to other devices or components without modification
entries.example_cn: 这台旧打印机无法与现代计算机连接使用。
entries.example_en: This old printer is incompatible with modern computers.

entries.definition_cn: （药物或其他物质）不能合用的，因相互作用而产生不良反应的
entries.definition_en: of drugs or other substances: unable to be used together because they react adversely
entries.example_cn: 这两种药物相互抵消，不应同时服用。
entries.example_en: These two medications are incompatible and should not be taken together.

entries.definition_en: not compatible with other facts
entries.example_cn: 他的故事与现场发现的证据不符。
entries.example_en: His story is incompatible with the evidence found at the scene.

entries.definition_en: not in keeping with what is correct or proper
entries.example_cn: 他的行为与其教师身份不相称。
entries.example_en: His behavior was incompatible with his position as a teacher.

entries.definition_cn: 不符合个人口味或需求的
entries.definition_en: not suitable to your tastes or needs
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店房间不符合我对豪华的期望。
entries.example_en: The hotel room was incompatible with my expectations of luxury.

entries.definition_en: not easy to combine harmoniously
entries.example_cn: 画中的颜色难以和谐结合，显得冲突。
entries.example_en: The colors in the painting are incompatible and clash.

entries.definition_en: of words so related that one contrasts with the other
entries.example_cn: “热”和“冷”这两个词在意义上是对立的。
entries.example_en: The words 'hot' and 'cold' are incompatible in meaning.

entries.definition_en: lack of physical or intellectual ability or qualifications
entries.example_cn: 由于经理的无能，项目失败了。
entries.example_en: The project failed due to the incompetence of the manager.

entries.definition_cn: 器官或身体部位功能障碍
entries.definition_en: inability of an organ or body part to function properly
entries.example_cn: 检查显示患者存在二尖瓣关闭不全。
entries.example_en: The tests revealed incompetence of the patient's mitral valve.

entries.definition_cn: 无能；不称职；不具备资格
entries.definition_en: the state of lacking the necessary ability, skill, or qualifications to do something
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定他的无能使他不具备担任该职位的资格。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that his incompetency disqualified him from the position.

entries.definition_en: not qualified or suited for a purpose
entries.example_cn: 这个工具不适合干重活。
entries.example_en: This tool is incompetent for heavy-duty work.

entries.definition_en: showing lack of skill or aptitude
entries.example_cn: 他在剧中的表演毫无技巧。
entries.example_en: He gave an incompetent performance in the play.

entries.definition_en: not doing a good job
entries.example_cn: 那位表现不佳的司机引发了一起事故。
entries.example_en: The incompetent driver caused an accident.

entries.definition_cn: （法律上）不可采纳或不足以支持法律主张的
entries.definition_en: not legally admissible or sufficient for a legal purpose
entries.example_cn: 该证据不足以支持这项指控。
entries.example_en: The evidence was incompetent to support the charge.

entries.definition_en: not meeting requirements
entries.example_cn: 这些材料不符合建筑要求。
entries.example_en: The materials were incompetent for the construction.

entries.definition_en: someone who is not competent to take effective action
entries.example_cn: 由于经理无能，项目失败了。
entries.example_en: The project failed because of the incompetent manager.

entries.definition_en: in a manner lacking the necessary ability or skill
entries.example_cn: 该项目管理无能，导致其失败。
entries.example_en: The project was managed incompetently, leading to its failure.

entries.definition_en: not complete or total; not completed
entries.example_cn: 由于缺少一些数据，这份报告不完整。
entries.example_en: The report was incomplete because some data was missing.

entries.definition_en: not yet finished
entries.example_cn: 该项目尚未完成，将于下周结束。
entries.example_en: The project is still incomplete and will be finished next week.

entries.definition_en: not to a full degree or extent
entries.example_cn: 这份报告写得并不完整。
entries.example_en: The report was written incompletely.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unfinished, lacking parts, or not fully developed
entries.example_cn: 报告的不完善阻止了委员会做出最终决定。
entries.example_en: The incompleteness of the report prevented the committee from making a final decision.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being impossible to understand
entries.example_cn: 这部古文的不可理解性让翻译者们感到沮丧。
entries.example_en: The incomprehensibility of the ancient text frustrated the translators.

entries.definition_en: something that cannot be understood
entries.example_cn: 他叙述中的突然变化对调查人员来说又是一个无法理解的地方。
entries.example_en: The sudden change in his story was another incomprehensibility for the investigators.

entries.definition_en: difficult to understand
entries.example_cn: 教授那堂难以理解的讲座让许多学生感到困惑。
entries.example_en: The professor's incomprehensible lecture left many students confused.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being explained or accounted for
entries.example_cn: 他突然离开的理由仍然无法解释。
entries.example_en: The reasons for his sudden departure remain incomprehensible.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unable to understand something
entries.example_cn: 玩家们对复杂的规则普遍感到不理解。
entries.example_en: There was a general incomprehension of the complex rules among the players.

entries.definition_en: the quality of not being able to be compressed
entries.example_cn: 水的不可压缩性使其成为极好的液压流体。
entries.example_en: The incompressibility of water makes it an excellent hydraulic fluid.

entries.definition_en: unable to be squeezed into a smaller volume
entries.example_cn: 在通常条件下，水通常被视为不可压缩的。
entries.example_en: Water is generally considered incompressible under normal conditions.

entries.definition_en: so unlikely that it cannot be imagined
entries.example_cn: 他违背诺言是难以想象的。
entries.example_en: It is inconceivable that he would break his promise.

entries.definition_en: to an inconceivable degree; in a way that cannot be imagined
entries.example_cn: 结果比我们希望的好得难以想象。
entries.example_en: The results were inconceivably better than we had hoped.

entries.definition_en: not conclusive; not putting an end to doubt or question
entries.example_cn: 关于事故原因的调查结果没有得出结论。
entries.example_en: The investigation yielded inconclusive results regarding the cause of the accident.

entries.definition_en: in a way that does not provide a definite conclusion
entries.example_cn: 调查以不明确的方式结束，留下了许多未解的问题。
entries.example_en: The investigation ended inconclusively, leaving many questions unanswered.

entries.definition_en: not in agreement or harmony; not matching or consistent with something else
entries.example_cn: 他的行为与他宣称的信念不一致。
entries.example_en: His actions were incongruent with his stated beliefs.

entries.definition_en: the state of being incongruous; a lack of harmony or agreement
entries.example_cn: 他富有的外表与简朴的生活方式之间形成了鲜明的不协调。
entries.example_en: There was a striking incongruity between his wealthy appearance and his humble lifestyle.

entries.definition_en: lacking harmony or compatibility; inappropriate in a specific context
entries.example_cn: 那条鲜红色的领带与他深色的正装看起来很不协调。
entries.example_en: The bright red tie looked incongruous with his dark formal suit.

entries.definition_en: in a way that does not fit or is out of place
entries.example_cn: 他穿着燕尾服在泥泞的花园里干活，显得极不协调。
entries.example_en: He wore a tuxedo incongruously while working in the muddy garden.

entries.definition_en: lacking worth or importance
entries.example_cn: 他的错误无关紧要，没有影响最终结果。
entries.example_en: His mistake was inconsequential and did not affect the final result.

entries.definition_en: not following logically as a consequence
entries.example_cn: 该结论并非由这些前提合乎逻辑地推出。
entries.example_en: The conclusion did not follow logically from the premises.

entries.definition_en: in a way that lacks consequence or importance
entries.example_cn: 他无足轻重地谈论了项目的次要细节。
entries.example_en: He spoke inconsequentially about the minor details of the project.

entries.definition_en: too small or unimportant to merit attention
entries.example_cn: 那微不足道的降雨量并未影响收成。
entries.example_en: The inconsiderable amount of rain did not affect the harvest.

entries.definition_cn: 不顾及他人权利或感受的
entries.definition_en: lacking regard for the rights or feelings of others
entries.example_cn: 你在图书馆大声说话真是不顾及他人感受。
entries.example_en: It was inconsiderate of you to speak so loudly in the library.

entries.definition_en: without proper consideration or reflection
entries.example_cn: 他做了一个未经深思熟虑的决定，在没有计划的情况下辞职。
entries.example_en: He made an inconsiderate decision to quit his job without a plan.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows a lack of consideration for others; without thinking about the consequences
entries.example_cn: 演讲者解释复杂理论时，他不经考虑地打断了对方。
entries.example_en: He inconsiderately interrupted the speaker while they were explaining the complex theory.

entries.definition_cn: 缺乏应有的体谅；不考虑后果；轻率
entries.definition_en: lack of due consideration; inattention to consequences; thoughtlessness
entries.example_cn: 他的不体谅给团队带来了很大困扰。
entries.example_en: His inconsideration caused great distress to the team.

entries.definition_en: the quality of lacking uniformity or harmony among parts
entries.example_cn: 该设计在配色方案上存在不协调之处。
entries.example_en: The design suffered from an inconsistency in its color scheme.

entries.definition_en: a situation where two statements cannot both be true at the same time
entries.example_cn: 他的论点中存在逻辑矛盾。
entries.example_en: There is a logical inconsistency in his argument.

entries.definition_en: not compatible or in agreement with something else
entries.example_cn: 他的行为与他的言语不一致。
entries.example_en: His behavior is inconsistent with his words.

entries.definition_cn: 前后不一致的；自相矛盾的
entries.definition_en: lacking internal consistency; self-contradictory
entries.example_cn: 他对当晚的叙述前后不一致，先说自己八点前给她打过电话，后来却说直到九点以后才和她说过话。
entries.example_en: He gave an inconsistent account of the evening, saying he called her before eight, but later that he had not talked to her until after nine.

entries.definition_en: unable to be made consistent or harmonious
entries.example_cn: 这两个理论彼此无法协调。
entries.example_en: The two theories are inconsistent with each other.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not consistent or uniform
entries.example_cn: 本周的天气忽冷忽热，变化无常。
entries.example_en: The weather has been inconsistently warm and cold throughout the week.

entries.definition_en: too sad to be comforted
entries.example_cn: 在失去宠物后，她悲痛欲绝。
entries.example_en: She was inconsolable after the loss of her pet.

entries.definition_en: not prominent or easily noticed
entries.example_cn: 他戴了一顶不显眼的帽子以避免引人注目。
entries.example_en: He wore an inconspicuous hat to avoid drawing attention.

entries.definition_en: in a way that does not attract attention
entries.example_cn: 他坐在房间的角落里，不引人注目。
entries.example_en: He sat inconspicuously in the corner of the room.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being changeable and variable
entries.example_cn: 天气的多变使得计划旅行变得困难。
entries.example_en: The inconstancy of the weather made it hard to plan the trip.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unfaithful because one is unreliable or treacherous
entries.example_cn: 他在爱情中的不忠让伴侣离开了他。
entries.example_en: His inconstancy in love made his partner leave him.

entries.definition_cn: 不稳定的；易变的；不坚定的
entries.definition_en: not constant; changeable, wavering, or unreliable
entries.example_cn: 他易变的性格让朋友难以依赖他。
entries.example_en: His inconstant nature made it difficult for friends to rely on him.

entries.definition_en: not faithful to a romantic partner
entries.example_cn: 他对她仍负有承诺，却又追求其他恋人，对她不忠。
entries.example_en: He was inconstant, pursuing other romantic partners while still committed to her.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being contested or disputed
entries.example_cn: 提供的证据无可争议。
entries.example_en: The evidence provided was incontestable.

entries.definition_en: not open to question; obviously true
entries.example_cn: 她的才华毋庸置疑。
entries.example_en: Her talent is incontestable.

entries.definition_en: involuntary urination or defecation
entries.example_cn: 这位老年患者患有尿失禁。
entries.example_en: The elderly patient suffered from urinary incontinence.

entries.definition_en: indiscipline with regard to sensuous pleasures
entries.example_cn: 他的纵欲使他毫无节制地追求感官享受。
entries.example_en: His incontinence led him to pursue sensual pleasures without restraint.

usage.label: dated
usage.pattern: Often refers to lack of sexual self-restraint.

entries.definition_en: unable to control urination or defecation
entries.example_cn: 这位老年病人失禁，需要特别护理。
entries.example_en: The elderly patient was incontinent and required special care.

entries.definition_en: impossible to deny or disprove
entries.example_cn: 提出的证据无可辩驳，导致迅速定罪。
entries.example_en: The evidence presented was incontrovertible and led to a quick conviction.

entries.definition_en: necessarily or demonstrably true
entries.example_cn: 气候变化对地球构成严重威胁是必然真实的。
entries.example_en: It is incontrovertible that climate change poses a serious threat to the planet.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is clearly provable and cannot be denied
entries.example_cn: 证据无可争辩地证明了他的清白。
entries.example_en: The evidence incontrovertibly proved his innocence.

entries.definition_en: a situation that causes discomfort or trouble
entries.example_cn: 延误给乘客带来了极大的不便。
entries.example_en: The delay caused a great inconvenience to the passengers.

entries.definition_en: a difficulty that causes anxiety or worry
entries.example_cn: 未来的不确定性是一个持续的困扰。
entries.example_en: The uncertainty of the future is a constant inconvenience.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being inconvenient
entries.example_cn: 偏远地点的不便性劝退了游客。
entries.example_en: The inconvenience of the remote location discouraged tourists.

entries.definition_en: to cause inconvenience or discomfort to someone
entries.example_cn: 抱歉我的问题打扰了你。
entries.example_en: I apologize for inconveniencing you with my questions.

entries.definition_en: causing trouble or discomfort because it is not suitable for your needs
entries.example_cn: 会议安排的时间对大多数员工来说很不方便。
entries.example_en: The meeting was scheduled at an inconvenient time for most of the staff.

entries.definition_en: not happening at a suitable or easy time
entries.example_cn: 周一去博物馆很不方便，因为那天闭馆。
entries.example_en: It is inconvenient to visit the museum on Mondays as it is closed.

entries.definition_en: in an inconvenient manner
entries.example_cn: 会议被安排在晚上很晚的时候，很不方便。
entries.example_en: The meeting was scheduled inconveniently late in the evening.

entries.definition_en: unable to be exchanged for another currency of equal value
entries.example_cn: 这种不可兑换的货币无法在国外购买商品。
entries.example_en: The inconvertible currency could not be used to buy goods abroad.

entries.definition_en: unable to be changed into something else
entries.example_cn: 这件古代文物的不可转化性使其独一无二。
entries.example_en: The inconvertible nature of the ancient artifact made it unique.

entries.definition_en: the inability to control body movements smoothly
entries.example_cn: 中风后，这位病人出现了不协调的症状。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered from incoordination after the stroke.

entries.definition_cn: 将……并入；使成为整体的一部分
entries.definition_en: to include something as part of a whole
entries.example_cn: 公司决定将这些新想法纳入其中。
entries.example_en: The company decided to incorporate the new ideas.

usage.label: incorporate A into B
usage.pattern: incorporate a feature into a design

entries.definition_en: to include or contain something
entries.example_cn: 这种饮食包含大量的蔬菜。
entries.example_en: The diet incorporates plenty of vegetables.

entries.definition_en: to unite with something that already exists
entries.example_cn: 这个小村庄被并入该市。
entries.example_en: The small village was incorporated into the city.

entries.definition_en: to form a business corporation
entries.example_cn: 他们计划明年组建公司。
entries.example_en: They plan to incorporate next year.

entries.definition_en: formed into a single whole
entries.example_cn: 这两个部门被合并成了一个。
entries.example_en: The two departments were incorporated into one.

entries.definition_en: organized and maintained as a legal corporation
entries.example_cn: 这家公司去年在特拉华州依法成立。
entries.example_en: The business was incorporated in Delaware last year.

entries.definition_en: introduced into as a part of the whole
entries.example_cn: 新的安全功能已被纳入汽车设计中。
entries.example_en: New safety features were incorporated into the car design.

entries.definition_en: formed or united into a single whole
entries.example_cn: 两家较小的公司合并成了一家公司。
entries.example_en: The two smaller firms were incorporated into one company.

entries.definition_en: the act of combining two or more things into one
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司的合并创造了一个新的市场领导者。
entries.example_en: The incorporation of the two companies created a new market leader.

entries.definition_en: the state of being included by incorporating
entries.example_cn: 将这项技术纳入系统提高了效率。
entries.example_en: The incorporation of the technology into the system improved efficiency.

entries.definition_en: the internalization of values or attitudes
entries.example_cn: 将传统价值观融入现代教育是一个关键目标。
entries.example_en: The incorporation of traditional values into modern education is a key goal.

entries.definition_en: without material form or substance
entries.example_cn: 灵魂常被描述为一种无形的实体。
entries.example_en: The soul is often described as an incorporeal entity.

entries.definition_en: not correct; not in conformity with fact or truth
entries.example_cn: 你输入的数据是不正确的。
entries.example_en: The data you entered is incorrect.

entries.definition_cn: 不符合既定用法或程序的
entries.definition_en: not in accord with established usage or procedure
entries.example_cn: 直呼经理的名字是不符合规范的。
entries.example_en: It is incorrect to address the manager by their first name.

entries.definition_cn: (单词或表达) 不符合语法规则的
entries.definition_en: (of a word or expression) not agreeing with grammatical principles
entries.example_cn: 这个句子包含一个动词形式错误。
entries.example_en: The sentence contains an incorrect verb form.

entries.definition_en: faulty or defective in design or operation
entries.example_cn: 计算机因程序设计有误而崩溃。
entries.example_en: The computer crashed because of incorrect programming.

entries.definition_en: in an incorrect manner
entries.example_cn: 他错误地回答了这个问题。
entries.example_en: He answered the question incorrectly.

entries.definition_en: in a false manner
entries.example_cn: 数据被错误地输入了。
entries.example_en: The data was entered incorrectly.

entries.definition_en: the state of being wrong or not true
entries.example_cn: 数据的错误性导致了一个有缺陷的结论。
entries.example_en: The incorrectness of the data led to a flawed conclusion.

entries.definition_en: the quality of not following social rules or expectations
entries.example_cn: 他行为的不合礼俗让客人们感到震惊。
entries.example_en: The incorrectness of his behavior shocked the guests.

entries.definition_en: impervious to correction by punishment
entries.example_cn: 这位屡教不改的学生尽管受到警告，仍继续扰乱课堂。
entries.example_en: The incorrigible student continued to disrupt the class despite the warnings.

entries.definition_en: difficult or impossible to manage or control
entries.example_cn: 这只屡教不改的小狗一旦逃进公园，就根本无法控制。
entries.example_en: The incorrigible puppy was impossible to control once it escaped into the park.

entries.definition_en: in a way that cannot be corrected
entries.example_cn: 他无可救药地懒惰，拒绝帮助任何人。
entries.example_en: He was incorrigibly lazy and refused to help anyone.

entries.definition_en: free from dishonesty or moral corruption
entries.example_cn: 这位法官以廉洁公正著称，在所有判决中都是如此。
entries.example_en: The judge was known for being incorrupt and fair in all his rulings.

entries.definition_en: not decayed or spoiled
entries.example_cn: 由于干燥的沙漠环境，这具古木乃伊得以保持未腐烂的状态。
entries.example_en: The ancient mummy remained incorrupt due to the dry desert conditions.

entries.definition_cn: 不受腐蚀或不受不正当影响的品质；廉正不阿
entries.definition_en: the quality of not being able to be corrupted or influenced dishonestly
entries.example_cn: 法官拒绝贿赂，证明了他的廉正不阿。
entries.example_en: The judge's incorruptibility was proven when he refused the bribe.

entries.definition_cn: 不可收买的；正直廉洁的
entries.definition_en: incapable of being morally corrupted
entries.example_cn: 这位法官以不可收买、正直廉洁而闻名。
entries.example_en: The judge is known for being incorruptible.

entries.definition_cn: 不会腐败或腐烂的；不易腐坏的
entries.definition_en: not subject to corruption or decay
entries.example_cn: 这部古籍写在一种历经数百年仍不会腐坏的材料上。
entries.example_en: The ancient text was written on an incorruptible material that survived for centuries.

entries.definition_en: become bigger or greater in amount
entries.example_cn: 价格在过去一年里增加了。
entries.example_en: Prices have increased over the last year.

entries.definition_en: make bigger or more
entries.example_cn: 我们需要提高机器的速度。
entries.example_en: We need to increase the speed of the machine.

entries.definition_en: a change resulting in an increase
entries.example_cn: 交通流量突然增加了。
entries.example_en: There was a sudden increase in traffic.

entries.definition_en: a quantity that is added
entries.example_cn: 人口的增长是显著的。
entries.example_en: The increase in population is significant.

entries.definition_cn: 变得更大、更长、更多或更重要的过程
entries.definition_en: the process of becoming larger, longer, more numerous, or more important
entries.example_cn: 这座城市规模的迅速扩大使其需要修建新的道路。
entries.example_en: The rapid increase in the city's size required new roads.

entries.definition_en: the amount by which something increases
entries.example_cn: 增幅约为百分之十。
entries.example_en: The increase was about ten percent.

entries.definition_cn: 提高或增加某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of making something larger or greater
entries.example_cn: 部长提高税率的做法受到广泛批评。
entries.example_en: The minister's increase of the tax rate was widely criticized.

entries.definition_en: becoming greater or larger in amount
entries.example_cn: 使用智能手机的人数正在增加。
entries.example_en: There is an increasing number of people using smartphones.

entries.definition_en: (music) becoming faster and/or louder
entries.example_cn: 音乐的速度和音量都在逐渐增强。
entries.example_en: The music was increasing in tempo and volume.

entries.definition_en: advancing in amount or intensity over time
entries.example_cn: 越来越多的人选择在家工作。
entries.example_en: Increasingly, people are choosing to work from home.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being impossible to believe
entries.example_cn: 这个故事的难以置信程度让人难以相信它是真的。
entries.example_en: The sheer incredibility of the story made it hard to accept as true.

entries.definition_cn: 难以置信的事物；不可相信的事情
entries.definition_en: something that is incredible or impossible to believe
entries.example_cn: 这本书充满了难以置信、很难当作事实接受的事情。
entries.example_en: The book is full of incredibilities that are difficult to accept as fact.

entries.definition_en: so amazing that it is hard to believe
entries.example_cn: 猎豹惊人的速度让每个人都感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: The incredible speed of the cheetah amazed everyone.

entries.definition_en: to a very great extent
entries.example_cn: 从山顶看到的景色极其美丽。
entries.example_en: The view from the top was incredibly beautiful.

entries.definition_en: to such a degree that it is hard to believe
entries.example_cn: 难以置信的是，那座老桥仍在使用。
entries.example_en: Incredibly, the old bridge is still in use.

entries.definition_en: doubt about the truth of something
entries.example_cn: 他带着怀疑听完了这个故事。
entries.example_en: He listened to the story with incredulity.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: Source w29649r0 labels this noun usually uncountable.

entries.definition_en: not disposed or willing to believe; unbelieving
entries.example_cn: 当他讲述那个故事时，她带着怀疑的表情看着他。
entries.example_en: She looked at him with an incredulous expression when he told the story.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing disbelief or skepticism
entries.example_cn: 她怀疑地听着关于中彩票的故事。
entries.example_en: She listened incredulously to the story about winning the lottery.

entries.definition_en: the amount by which something increases
entries.example_cn: 算法中的每一步都会向总和增加一个增量。
entries.example_en: Each step in the algorithm adds an increment to the total sum.

entries.definition_cn: 增长或变得更大、更长、更多或更重要的过程
entries.definition_en: the process of becoming larger, longer, more numerous, or more important
entries.example_cn: 该公司过去五年的利润稳步增长。
entries.example_en: The company's profits showed a steady increment over the last five years.

entries.definition_en: increasing gradually by regular degrees or additions
entries.example_cn: 该公司采用逐步改进的方法来完善其软件。
entries.example_en: The company adopted an incremental approach to improve its software.

entries.definition_en: to make someone appear guilty of a crime
entries.example_cn: 证人的证词似乎使被告显得参与了抢劫。
entries.example_en: The witness's testimony seemed to incriminate the defendant in the robbery.

entries.definition_en: to bring an accusation or charge against someone
entries.example_cn: 证据足以控告该嫌疑人在欺诈案中涉案。
entries.example_en: The evidence was enough to incriminate the suspect in the fraud case.

entries.definition_en: providing evidence that someone is guilty of a crime or wrong
entries.example_cn: 在现场发现的不利证据导致他被捕。
entries.example_en: The incriminating evidence found at the scene led to his arrest.

entries.definition_cn: 指控某人犯有错误或不当行为
entries.definition_en: the act or process of accusing someone of a crime or wrongdoing
entries.example_cn: 证人的证词导致了对嫌疑人的指控。
entries.example_en: The witness's testimony led to the incrimination of the suspect.

entries.definition_en: serving to charge someone with a crime or suggesting guilt or blame
entries.example_cn: 证人提供了指控嫌疑人的证据。
entries.example_en: The witness provided incriminatory evidence against the suspect.

entries.definition_en: a hard crust or coating on or in something
entries.example_cn: 管道内壁覆盖着一层坚硬的矿物沉积物。
entries.example_en: A hard incrustation of mineral deposits covered the inside of the pipe.

entries.definition_en: the formation of a crust on a surface
entries.example_cn: 管道上的石灰结壳减少了水流。
entries.example_en: The incrustation of lime on the pipes reduced the water flow.

entries.definition_en: a decorative coating of contrasting material applied to a surface
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子在木头上镶嵌了复杂的金箔装饰层。
entries.example_en: The table featured an intricate incrustation of gold leaf on the wood.

entries.definition_cn: 在促进发展的条件下生长
entries.definition_en: to grow or develop under conditions that encourage it
entries.example_cn: 病毒可以在宿主体内潜伏数周，之后才出现症状。
entries.example_en: The virus can incubate inside the host for several weeks before symptoms appear.

entries.definition_en: to sit on eggs to keep them warm until they hatch
entries.example_cn: 母鸡安静地坐着孵蛋。
entries.example_en: The hen sat quietly to incubate her clutch of eggs.

entries.definition_cn: 经过一段时间认真思考并逐步完善一个想法
entries.definition_en: to think about and develop an idea carefully over time
entries.example_cn: 她花了几个月酝酿这个想法，才把它提交给团队。
entries.example_en: She incubated the idea for months before presenting it to the team.

entries.definition_en: the phase in the development of an infection between the time a pathogen enters the body and the time the first symptoms appear
entries.example_cn: 这种病毒的潜伏期因人而异。
entries.example_en: The incubation period of the virus can vary from person to person.

entries.definition_en: maintaining something at the most favorable temperature for its development
entries.example_cn: 这些蛋的孵化花了三周时间。
entries.example_en: The incubation of the eggs took three weeks.

entries.definition_en: sitting on eggs so as to hatch them by the warmth of the body
entries.example_cn: 母鸡下完蛋后开始孵卵。
entries.example_en: The mother hen began her incubation after laying the eggs.

entries.definition_cn: 酝酿：在有意识思考之后，通过无意识地重新组合思想而产生新想法的过程
entries.definition_en: the unconscious recombination of thoughts that leads to a new idea after a period of conscious work
entries.example_cn: 经过几天的酝酿，她突然找到了问题的解决办法。
entries.example_en: After several days of incubation, she suddenly found a solution to the problem.

entries.definition_en: a machine that keeps a constant temperature for keeping eggs warm or for caring for premature babies
entries.example_cn: 这家医院使用特殊的孵化器来照顾早产儿。
entries.example_en: The hospital uses a special incubator to care for the premature infant.

entries.definition_cn: 被认为会压迫熟睡者、尤其会与熟睡女性交媾的男恶魔
entries.definition_en: a male demon believed to oppress sleeping people, especially by having sex with sleeping women
entries.example_cn: 梦魔的传说困扰着中世纪的想象力。
entries.example_en: The legend of the incubus haunted the medieval imagination.

entries.definition_cn: 睡眠中的压迫感；睡眠瘫痪、夜惊或噩梦
entries.definition_en: a feeling of oppression during sleep; sleep paralysis, a night terror, or a nightmare
entries.example_cn: 她从噩梦中惊醒，感到被困住且无法动弹。
entries.example_en: She awoke from a nightmare feeling trapped and unable to move.

entries.definition_cn: 令人压抑的人或事物；负担
entries.definition_en: an oppressive person or thing; a burden
entries.example_cn: 他不断的抱怨使他成了同事们的一个令人沮丧的人。
entries.example_en: His constant complaining made him an incubus to his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: to teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions
entries.example_cn: 父母试图从小向孩子灌输良好的礼仪。
entries.example_en: Parents try to inculcate good manners in their children from a young age.

entries.definition_en: the act of teaching something by repeating it often until it is firmly learned
entries.example_cn: 老师对纪律的反复灌输帮助学生集中了注意力。
entries.example_en: The teacher's constant inculcation of discipline helped the students focus.

entries.definition_cn: 证明某人有罪或使其负有罪责的；对被告不利的
entries.definition_en: tending to show that someone is responsible for or guilty of a crime
entries.example_cn: 这些证据对他不利，并导致他被捕。
entries.example_en: The evidence was inculpatory and led to his arrest.

entries.definition_en: the term during which some position is held
entries.example_cn: 在她的任期内，她通过了几项重要法律。
entries.example_en: During her incumbency, she passed several important laws.

entries.definition_en: an obligation or duty
entries.example_cn: 维护公共秩序的职责在于地方当局。
entries.example_en: The incumbency of maintaining public order lies with the local authorities.

entries.definition_en: the office of an incumbent
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策旨在支持地方官员的现任职位。
entries.example_en: The new policy was designed to support the incumbency of local officials.

entries.definition_en: currently holding an office
entries.example_cn: 执政党赢得了大多数席位。
entries.example_en: The incumbent party won the majority of seats.

entries.definition_en: necessary as a duty or responsibility; morally binding
entries.example_cn: 每个公民都有责任参加选举投票。
entries.example_en: It is incumbent on every citizen to vote in the election.

entries.definition_en: lying or leaning on something else
entries.example_cn: 那本厚重的书倚靠在其他书上。
entries.example_en: The heavy book lay incumbent upon the other books.

entries.definition_en: the official who currently holds a public office
entries.example_cn: 现任总统不会寻求第三个任期。
entries.example_en: The incumbent president will not seek a third term.

entries.definition_en: to become subject to something unpleasant or liable to pay for it
entries.example_cn: 由于违反安全规定，该公司招致了巨额罚款。
entries.example_en: The company incurred heavy fines due to the safety violations.

entries.definition_en: to receive a specific treatment or condition
entries.example_cn: 手术后，这位病人遭受了严重的感染。
entries.example_en: The patient incurred a serious infection after the surgery.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being cured
entries.example_cn: 该病毒无法治愈的特性使得疫苗研发变得困难。
entries.example_en: The incurable nature of the virus made it difficult to develop a vaccine.

entries.definition_cn: 性情或习惯无法改变的
entries.definition_en: unalterable in disposition or habits
entries.example_cn: 他无法改变的坏脾气经常引发家庭争吵。
entries.example_en: His incurable bad temper often caused arguments in the family.

entries.definition_cn: 患有无法治愈疾病的人
entries.definition_en: a person suffering from a disease that cannot be cured
entries.example_cn: 医院为需要长期支持的绝症患者提供了特别护理。
entries.example_en: The hospital provided special care for incurables who needed long-term support.

entries.definition_en: to an incurable degree
entries.example_cn: 尽管尽了最大的医疗努力，疾病仍不可治愈地恶化了。
entries.example_en: The disease progressed incurably despite the best medical efforts.

entries.definition_en: in a manner impossible to cure
entries.example_cn: 他从小就无可救药地沉迷于赌博。
entries.example_en: He was incurably addicted to gambling from a young age.

entries.definition_cn: 缺乏好奇心的；不好奇的
entries.definition_en: showing a lack of interest in learning or asking questions
entries.example_cn: 这个缺乏好奇心的学生从不举手提问。
entries.example_en: The incurious student never raised his hand to ask questions.

entries.definition_en: the act of incurring something
entries.example_cn: 公司因疏忽而招致巨额罚款。
entries.example_en: The incurrence of heavy fines was a result of the company's negligence.

entries.definition_en: the act of entering some territory or domain, often in large numbers
entries.example_cn: 军队对敌占区发动了一次短暂的入侵。
entries.example_en: The army launched a brief incursion into enemy territory.

entries.definition_en: an attack that penetrates into enemy territory
entries.example_cn: 这次突袭被防守部队击退了。
entries.example_en: The incursion was repelled by the defending forces.

entries.definition_cn: 【澳大利亚】教育机构举办的活动，尤指用于娱乐、研究、教育或展示作品的活动
entries.definition_en: [Australian] a function hosted within an educational institution, especially for recreation, research, education, or displaying works
entries.example_cn: 学校组织了一场活动，展示学生的艺术作品。
entries.example_en: The school organized an incursion to showcase its students' artwork.

entries.definition_en: bent or shaped so that it curves inward
entries.example_cn: 贝壳向内弯曲的边缘保护着里面的动物。
entries.example_en: The incurved edges of the shell protect the animal inside.

entries.definition_cn: 砧骨（位于锤骨和镫骨之间的小骨头）
entries.definition_en: a small bone in the middle ear located between the malleus and the stapes
entries.example_cn: 砧骨是人类中耳三块小骨头之一。
entries.example_en: The incus is one of the three tiny bones in the human middle ear.

entries.definition_cn: 砧状云；积雨云顶部扩展形成的附属云
entries.definition_en: an accessory cloud shaped like an anvil that forms by spreading at the top of a cumulonimbus cloud
entries.example_cn: 随着积雨云顶部扩展，雷暴上方形成了砧状云。
entries.example_en: An incus formed above the thunderstorm as the cumulonimbus cloud spread at the top.

entries.definition_en: a traditional meeting in southern Africa where indigenous people gather to discuss important matters
entries.example_cn: 村落的长老们召开了一次部落会议，以决定如何解决土地纠纷。
entries.example_en: The village elders called an indaba to decide how to resolve the land dispute.

entries.definition_cn: （南非）主要用于“某人自己的或他人的indaba”：事情、问题或烦恼。
entries.definition_en: South African, chiefly in one's own or someone's indaba: a concern, matter, or problem.
entries.example_cn: 那是你的事，不是我的事。
entries.example_en: That is your indaba, not mine.

entries.definition_en: a diuretic medication used to treat high blood pressure.
entries.example_cn: 医生开了吲达帕胺来帮助控制患者的血压。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed indapamide to help manage the patient's hypertension.

entries.definition_en: feeling grateful for help received
entries.example_cn: 我对我老师的指导深感感激。
entries.example_en: I am deeply indebted to my teacher for her guidance.

usage.label: usually be indebted to someone for something
usage.pattern: w15088r1: “We are indebted to an officer ... for sending us ...”

entries.definition_en: legally obligated to pay money to someone
entries.example_cn: 诉讼之后，他欠银行一大笔钱。
entries.example_en: After the lawsuit, he was indebted to the bank for a large sum.

entries.definition_en: the state of owing money to someone
entries.example_cn: 由于经济衰退，该公司的负债迅速增加。
entries.example_en: The company's indebtedness grew rapidly due to the economic downturn.

entries.definition_cn: 对某人所给予的服务或恩惠的感激或亏欠
entries.definition_en: the state of owing someone gratitude or an obligation for a service or favor
entries.example_cn: 他承认自己因导师的指导而对导师心怀感激和亏欠，正是那份指导开启了他的职业生涯。
entries.example_en: He acknowledged his indebtedness to his mentor for the guidance that launched his career.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being indecent
entries.example_cn: 这种行为的不道德性震惊了观众。
entries.example_en: The indecency of the behavior shocked the audience.

entries.definition_en: an indecent or improper act
entries.example_cn: 警方调查了聚会上发生的一起不雅行为。
entries.example_en: The police investigated an act of indecency at the party.

entries.definition_cn: 不合乎礼仪的；不体面的
entries.definition_en: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.example_cn: 在葬礼上发笑是不体面的。
entries.example_en: It was indecent to laugh during the funeral.

entries.definition_en: offensive to good taste, especially in sexual matters
entries.example_cn: 警方禁止放映那部淫秽的电影。
entries.example_en: The police banned the indecent film.

entries.definition_en: offending against sexual mores in conduct or appearance
entries.example_cn: 他在派对上的有伤风化的行为引起了丑闻。
entries.example_en: His indecent behavior at the party caused a scandal.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is offensive to public standards of morality or decency
entries.example_cn: 该杂志因以露骨的方式不道德地描绘暴力而被禁。
entries.example_en: The magazine was banned for indecently depicting violence in a graphic manner.

entries.definition_en: to an extreme degree; excessively
entries.example_cn: 仅仅一年间，租金就涨到了极高的程度。
entries.example_en: The rent had risen indecently high in just one year.

entries.definition_cn: 难以辨认、解读或破译的
entries.definition_en: not easily deciphered
entries.example_cn: 那份古手稿已经褪色，难以破译。
entries.example_en: The ancient manuscript was faded and indecipherable.

entries.definition_cn: 无法或很难理解、解释的
entries.definition_en: impossible or very difficult to understand or interpret
entries.example_cn: 他的隐晦言论让听众难以理解。
entries.example_en: His cryptic remarks were indecipherable to the audience.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unable to make a decision between two or more options
entries.example_cn: 他的犹豫不决导致会议被推迟了。
entries.example_en: His indecision caused the meeting to be delayed.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unable to make firm decisions; lack of determination
entries.example_cn: 她的优柔寡断让朋友们难以信任她的判断。
entries.example_en: Her indecision made it difficult for her friends to trust her judgment.

entries.definition_en: characterized by lack of decision and firmness
entries.example_cn: 他对于选择哪条职业道路犹豫不决。
entries.example_en: He was indecisive about which career path to choose.

entries.definition_en: not definitely settling something
entries.example_cn: 谈判的结果仍未确定。
entries.example_en: The outcome of the negotiations remains indecisive.

entries.definition_en: not clearly defined
entries.example_cn: 这两个地区之间的边界界限不清。
entries.example_en: The boundary between the two regions is indecisive.

entries.definition_en: in a manner lacking firmness or the ability to make a decision
entries.example_cn: 她犹豫了一下，优柔寡断地回答了那个问题。
entries.example_en: She hesitated and answered the question indecisively.

entries.definition_en: without reaching a final conclusion
entries.example_cn: 谈判以未决的方式结束，许多问题仍未解决。
entries.example_en: The negotiations ended indecisively, leaving many issues unresolved.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unable to decide between two or more possible options or actions
entries.example_cn: 他的优柔寡断使得团队难以制定策略。
entries.example_en: His indecisiveness made it difficult for the team to choose a strategy.

entries.definition_en: the quality of lacking firmness of character or purpose; irresolution
entries.example_cn: 项目的部分失败归因于领导者的优柔寡断。
entries.example_en: The project failed partly due to the leader's indecisiveness.

entries.definition_en: lacking propriety and good taste in manners and conduct
entries.example_cn: 婚礼仪式上迟到是不合礼仪的。
entries.example_en: It was indecorous to arrive late to the wedding ceremony.

entries.definition_en: not in keeping with accepted standards of what is right or proper in polite society
entries.example_cn: 那位客人的不得体行为冒犯了主人。
entries.example_en: The indecorous behavior of the guest offended the host.

entries.definition_en: used to emphasize that something is true
entries.example_cn: 他确实是一位有才华的音乐家。
entries.example_en: He is indeed a talented musician.

entries.definition_en: an expression of surprise or skepticism
entries.example_cn: 你中了彩票？真的吗！
entries.example_en: You won the lottery? Indeed!

entries.definition_en: never tired of working or trying; showing constant energy and enthusiasm
entries.example_cn: 这位不知疲倦的研究者花了数年时间收集研究数据。
entries.example_en: The indefatigable researcher spent years gathering data for the study.

entries.definition_en: with indefatigable energy; tirelessly
entries.example_cn: 她不知疲倦地工作了一整夜以完成项目。
entries.example_en: She indefatigably worked through the night to finish the project.

entries.definition_en: not liable to being annulled or voided
entries.example_cn: 该合同包含一条不可撤销的条款，保证贷款的发放。
entries.example_en: The contract contained an indefeasible clause guaranteeing the loan.

entries.definition_en: unable to be defended or justified, especially in an argument
entries.example_cn: 他对错误的解释完全无法辩护。
entries.example_en: His explanation for the mistake was completely indefensible.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being explained
entries.example_cn: 政策的突然变化令人无法解释，因为没人能说明它为何发生。
entries.example_en: The sudden change in policy was indefensible: no one could explain why it had occurred.

entries.definition_en: not able to be protected against attack
entries.example_cn: 那个没有防御的村庄无法抵御庞大的军队。
entries.example_en: The undefended village was indefensible against the large army.

entries.definition_en: unable to be described precisely or easily put into words
entries.example_cn: 日落那难以描述的美让每个人都无言以对。
entries.example_en: The indefinable beauty of the sunset left everyone speechless.

entries.definition_en: defying expression or description
entries.example_cn: 随着暴风雨逼近，她感到一种无法言表的恐惧。
entries.example_en: She felt an indefinable sense of dread as the storm approached.

entries.definition_en: not clearly defined or stated; vague
entries.example_cn: 委员会对这个问题给出了一个模糊的回答。
entries.example_en: The committee gave an indefinite answer to the question.

entries.definition_cn: 不确定的；未确定的；无固定期限的
entries.definition_en: not fixed or settled; uncertain in duration, outcome, or extent
entries.example_cn: 在做出最终决定之前，我们要等待一段不确定的时间。
entries.example_en: We are waiting for an indefinite period before making a final decision.

entries.definition_en: to an indefinite extent; for an indefinite time
entries.example_cn: 会议将无限期继续下去。
entries.example_en: The meeting will continue indefinitely.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being vague and poorly defined
entries.example_cn: 合同条款的模糊不清引发了法律纠纷。
entries.example_en: The indefiniteness of the contract terms caused legal disputes.

entries.definition_en: not opening up on its own when ripe to let seeds out
entries.example_cn: 这种不开裂的果实从树上落下时并没有裂开。
entries.example_en: The indehiscent fruit fell from the tree without splitting open.

entries.definition_en: cannot be removed or erased
entries.example_cn: 护照上无法擦除的墨水印记无法被移除或擦除。
entries.example_en: The indelible ink on the passport cannot be removed or erased.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that cannot be removed or forgotten
entries.example_cn: 那一天的记忆深刻地印在她的脑海中。
entries.example_en: The memory of that day is indelibly etched in her mind.

entries.definition_en: an act or expression that is impolite
entries.example_cn: 在典礼上打断发言者是一种极大的失礼。
entries.example_en: It was a great indelicacy to interrupt the speaker during the ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 不得体；冒犯他人的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being indelicate and offensive
entries.example_cn: 他谈论事故时的粗鲁引起了令人尴尬的沉默。
entries.example_en: His indelicacy in discussing the accident caused an awkward silence.

entries.definition_en: lacking proper manners and good taste in behavior
entries.example_cn: 你在他面前讨论他的薪水是很失礼的。
entries.example_en: It was indelicate of you to discuss his salary in front of him.

entries.definition_en: lacking good taste and bordering on indecency
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员讲了一个关于已故政治家的粗俗笑话。
entries.example_en: The comedian made an indelicate joke about the deceased politician.

entries.definition_en: verging on indecent behavior
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志包含了几幅近乎下流的插图。
entries.example_en: The magazine contained several indelicate illustrations.

entries.definition_en: a sum of money paid as compensation for a loss or injury
entries.example_cn: 该保险政策为受损财产提供了全额赔偿款。
entries.example_en: The insurance policy provided full indemnification for the damaged property.

entries.definition_en: the act of compensating someone for actual loss, damage, or trouble
entries.example_cn: 公司向受服务中断影响的客户提供了补偿。
entries.example_en: The company offered indemnification to the clients affected by the service outage.

entries.definition_en: to pay compensation to someone for a loss or injury
entries.example_cn: 公司必须就员工承受的压力向他们赔偿。
entries.example_en: The company must indemnify the employees for the stress they suffered.

entries.definition_en: to protect someone from financial loss or damage
entries.example_cn: 保险公司同意赔偿司机因事故遭受的任何损失。
entries.example_en: The insurance company agreed to indemnify the driver for any damages caused by the accident.

entries.definition_cn: 防止损失或损害的保障
entries.definition_en: protection against future loss
entries.example_cn: 保险单为火灾损失提供赔偿保障。
entries.example_en: The insurance policy provides indemnity against fire damage.

entries.definition_cn: （合同中的）赔偿或损失保障责任
entries.definition_en: a contractual obligation or right to compensate for or protect against loss or damage
entries.example_cn: 合同包含要求供应商承担赔偿责任的条款。
entries.example_en: The contract includes a clause of indemnity for the supplier.

entries.definition_cn: 因损失或伤害获得的赔偿金
entries.definition_en: a sum of money paid in compensation for loss or injury
entries.example_cn: 该公司就受损设备收到了赔偿金。
entries.example_en: The company received an indemnity for the destroyed equipment.

entries.definition_en: to set text in from the margin
entries.example_cn: 请将每个段落的开头一行缩进。
entries.example_en: Please indent the first line of each paragraph.

entries.definition_en: to make a depression into something
entries.example_cn: 大雨使那条松软的粘土小径凹陷下去。
entries.example_en: The heavy rain indented the soft clay path.

entries.definition_en: to notch the edge of or make jagged
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨使屋顶的边缘变得参差不齐。
entries.example_en: The storm indented the edge of the roof.

entries.definition_cn: 沿不规则的线切开或撕开，以便日后核对各部分
entries.definition_en: to cut or tear along an irregular line so that the parts can later be matched for authentication
entries.example_cn: 合同沿中线锯齿状切开，以便双方各持一半。
entries.example_en: The contract was indented down the middle so each party could hold half.

entries.definition_en: the space left between the margin and the start of an indented line
entries.example_cn: 这段文字的缩进量对于狭窄的栏宽来说太宽了。
entries.example_en: The indent of the text was too wide for the narrow column.

entries.definition_en: an official order for goods to be exported or imported
entries.example_cn: 该公司收到了一份来自外国供应商的五十吨钢材的进出口订单。
entries.example_en: The company received an indent for fifty tons of steel from the foreign supplier.

entries.definition_cn: 以契约形式束缚（如学徒或仆人）
entries.definition_en: to bind by or as if by indentures, as of an apprentice or servant
entries.example_cn: 这个男孩被签订契约，跟随一名工匠学艺七年。
entries.example_en: The young boy was indented to a master craftsman for seven years.

entries.definition_en: the space between the left margin and the beginning of a line of text
entries.example_cn: 该段落以标准的五个空格缩进开头。
entries.example_en: The paragraph begins with a standard indentation of five spaces.

entries.definition_en: a curved cut or hollow space in the edge of a surface
entries.example_cn: 海岸线在河流入海口处有一个深深的凹口。
entries.example_en: The coastline features a deep indentation where the river meets the sea.

entries.definition_en: small holes formed on a surface due to corrosion
entries.example_cn: 锈蚀在金属梁上造成了许多凹坑。
entries.example_en: The rust caused numerous indentations on the metal beam.

entries.definition_en: the act of cutting notches or angular cuts into an edge
entries.example_cn: 木匠沿着木头的边缘切出了一个精确的槽。
entries.example_en: The carpenter made a precise indentation along the wood's edge.

entries.definition_en: the space left between the margin and the start of an indented line
entries.example_cn: 段落首行的缩进间距有助于将其与其余文本区分开来。
entries.example_en: The indention of the first line in the paragraph helps distinguish it from the rest of the text.

entries.definition_en: a contract binding one party to serve another for a specified period
entries.example_cn: 他签署了一份服役契约，承诺担任水手五年。
entries.example_en: He signed an indenture to serve as a sailor for five years.

entries.definition_en: a formal agreement between a bond issuer and bondholders regarding debt terms
entries.example_cn: 该债券契约规定了债券的利率和还款时间表。
entries.example_en: The indenture specified the interest rate and repayment schedule for the bonds.

entries.definition_en: the space left between the margin and the beginning of an indented line of text
entries.example_cn: 编辑调整了缩进空格，以确保段落开头正确。
entries.example_en: The editor adjusted the indenture to ensure the paragraph started correctly.

entries.definition_en: a concave cut or notch made into a surface or edge
entries.example_cn: 侵蚀在海岸线上形成了一个深深的凹痕。
entries.example_en: The erosion created a deep indenture along the coastline.

entries.definition_en: to bind someone by a legal contract, typically as an apprentice or servant
entries.example_cn: 在18世纪，许多年轻人被以契约束缚在种植园工作。
entries.example_en: In the 18th century, many young men were indentured to work on plantations.

entries.definition_en: bound by contract
entries.example_cn: 许多工人受契约约束，需为主人服务数年。
entries.example_en: Many workers were indentured to serve a master for several years.

entries.definition_en: the state of being free from control or influence by another person or group
entries.example_cn: 该国为争取独立而发动了一场战争。
entries.example_en: The country fought a war to gain its independence.

entries.definition_en: the successful conclusion of the American Revolution
entries.example_cn: 约克镇战役的胜利标志着美国的独立。
entries.example_en: The victory at Yorktown marked the independence of the United States.

entries.definition_en: the state of being free from control or influence by others
entries.example_cn: 该国进行了一场长期的战争，以摆脱殖民统治，获得独立。
entries.example_en: The country fought a long war to secure its independency from colonial rule.

entries.definition_en: free from external control and constraint
entries.example_cn: 她是一个独立思考的人，自己做决定。
entries.example_en: She is an independent thinker who makes her own decisions.

entries.definition_cn: （指政治机构）不受外部势力控制
entries.definition_en: (of political bodies) not controlled by outside forces
entries.example_cn: 该委员会保持独立，不受政府影响。
entries.example_en: The committee remained independent of government influence.

entries.definition_cn: 不受政党或利益集团控制
entries.definition_en: not controlled by a party or interest group
entries.example_cn: 媒体应保持独立，不受政党控制。
entries.example_en: The media should remain independent of political parties.

entries.definition_cn: （指从句）能单独作为完整句子存在的
entries.definition_en: (of a clause) capable of standing syntactically alone as a complete sentence
entries.example_cn: 独立子句可以单独构成一个句子。
entries.example_en: The independent clause can stand alone in a sentence.

entries.definition_cn: 不依附任何政党的中立人士
entries.definition_en: a person who does not support any political party
entries.example_cn: 这次选举由一位独立候选人获胜。
entries.example_en: The election was won by an independent candidate.

entries.definition_cn: 没有长期合同而为不同雇主工作的作家或艺术家
entries.definition_en: a writer or artist who works for different employers without a long-term contract
entries.example_cn: 她是一名为多家出版物工作的独立记者。
entries.example_en: She works as an independent journalist for several publications.

entries.definition_en: on your own; without outside help
entries.example_cn: 搬出去住后，他独立学会了做饭。
entries.example_en: He learned to cook independently after moving out.

entries.definition_en: individually or separately
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司分别开发了该软件。
entries.example_en: The two companies developed the software independently.

entries.definition_en: defying expression or description
entries.example_cn: 日落的美丽难以形容。
entries.example_en: The beauty of the sunset was indescribable.

entries.definition_en: in a way that cannot be described in words
entries.example_cn: 从山上看到的景色美得难以形容。
entries.example_en: The view from the mountain was indescribably beautiful.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unable to be destroyed or damaged
entries.example_cn: 尽管神学观点不断变化，灵魂不灭的教义仍然流传下来。
entries.example_en: The doctrine of the soul's indestructibility persisted despite changing theological views.

entries.definition_en: not easily destroyed
entries.example_cn: 这种不易被摧毁的材料被用来建造桥梁。
entries.example_en: The indestructible material was used to build the bridge.

entries.definition_en: very long lasting
entries.example_cn: 尽管多年分离，他们的友谊依然非常持久。
entries.example_en: Their friendship remained indestructible despite the years apart.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being measured
entries.example_cn: 地下蓄水层中的水量无法测量。
entries.example_en: The quantity of water in the underground reservoir is indeterminable.

entries.definition_en: incapable of being definitely ascertained or calculated
entries.example_cn: 由于混乱，伤亡的确切数字无法确证或计算。
entries.example_en: The exact number of casualties is indeterminable due to the chaos.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unclear, vague, or not precisely defined
entries.example_cn: 未来的不确定性使得长期规划变得困难。
entries.example_en: The indeterminacy of the future makes long-term planning difficult.

entries.definition_en: not precisely determined or established; not fixed or known in advance
entries.example_cn: 会议时间仍不确定。
entries.example_en: The meeting time is still indeterminate.

entries.definition_en: of uncertain or ambiguous nature
entries.example_cn: 证据性质模糊，无法在法庭上使用。
entries.example_en: The evidence was indeterminate and could not be used in court.

entries.definition_cn: （指数量或方程）无确定值或唯一解的
entries.definition_en: (of a quantity or equation) having no definite value or unique solution
entries.example_cn: 该方程的解是不确定的。
entries.example_en: The equation has an indeterminate solution.

entries.definition_en: not leading to a definite ending or result
entries.example_cn: 故事以一个没有明确结局的音符结束。
entries.example_en: The story ended on an indeterminate note.

entries.definition_en: having a capacity for continuing to grow at the apex
entries.example_cn: 这种植物具有顶端可继续生长的特性，意味着它会一直长高。
entries.example_en: The plant has indeterminate growth, meaning it will keep growing taller.

usage.label: botany
usage.pattern: Of a plant, lacking a terminal bud and continuing to grow at the apex.

entries.definition_en: a list of words or topics with page numbers where they appear.
entries.example_cn: 我在书后面的索引中查到了这个词。
entries.example_en: I looked up the word in the index at the back of the book.

entries.definition_en: a number used to show how something has changed compared to a reference point.
entries.example_cn: 股市指数今天大幅上涨。
entries.example_en: The stock market index rose sharply today.

entries.definition_en: a value calculated from data to show trends over time.
entries.example_cn: 通胀指数表明价格正在上涨。
entries.example_en: The inflation index indicates that prices are increasing.

entries.definition_en: the finger next to the thumb.
entries.example_cn: 他用食指指着那个标志。
entries.example_en: He pointed at the sign with his index finger.

entries.definition_en: a symbol showing how many times a number is multiplied by itself.
entries.example_cn: 在 2 的 3 次方中，3 是指数。
entries.example_en: In the number 2 to the power of 3, the 3 is the index.

entries.definition_en: to list items in an alphabetical order for easy reference.
entries.example_cn: 图书管理员下周将为新书编索引。
entries.example_en: The librarian will index the new books next week.

entries.definition_en: to provide with an index.
entries.example_cn: 我们需要为这份文件编索引，以便人们能快速找到信息。
entries.example_en: We need to index this document so people can find information quickly.

entries.definition_en: to adjust prices or values based on an index.
entries.example_cn: 工资经常根据通货膨胀进行调整。
entries.example_en: Salaries are frequently indexed to inflation.

entries.definition_cn: 按照指数（尤其是通胀指数）调整工资等经济变量
entries.definition_en: the adjustment of an economic variable, such as wages, according to an index, especially one tracking inflation
entries.example_cn: 政府实施指数化制度以保护工人工资免受物价上涨的影响。
entries.example_en: The government implemented indexation to protect workers' salaries from rising prices.

entries.definition_cn: 索引编制者；创建索引的程序
entries.definition_en: a person or program that creates indexes
entries.example_cn: 图书馆聘请了一名专业的索引编制者来整理新档案。
entries.example_en: The library hired a professional indexer to organize the new archive.

entries.definition_cn: 索引的；指示性的，所指或意义随语境而变化的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to an index; having a reference or meaning that varies according to context
entries.example_cn: “我”这个词的指示意义取决于说话者。
entries.example_en: The indexical value of the word 'I' changes depending on who is speaking.

entries.definition_en: the process of organizing data to make it easier to search and retrieve
entries.example_cn: 图书馆为新书编制索引，提高了检索效率。
entries.example_en: The library's indexing of new books improved retrieval.

entries.definition_en: to point out or show the location or direction of something
entries.example_cn: 请在地图上指出最近的出口。
entries.example_en: Please indicate the nearest exit on the map.

entries.definition_en: to show that something is true or likely to happen
entries.example_cn: 这些症状表明病情严重。
entries.example_en: The symptoms indicate a serious illness.

entries.definition_en: to say or express something briefly
entries.example_cn: 报告指出销售额已增加。
entries.example_en: The report indicates that sales have increased.

entries.definition_en: to show evidence of something
entries.example_cn: 数据显示气温呈上升趋势。
entries.example_en: The data indicates a trend towards higher temperatures.

entries.definition_en: to suggest that medical treatment is needed
entries.example_cn: 测试结果表明需要立即手术。
entries.example_en: The test results indicate the need for immediate surgery.

entries.definition_en: a sign or piece of evidence that shows something is true or likely to happen
entries.example_cn: 有迹象表明经济正在复苏。
entries.example_en: There are early indications that the economy is recovering.

entries.definition_cn: （被证明）必要或明智的行动方案
entries.definition_en: a course of action that is shown to be necessary or advisable
entries.example_cn: 在此阶段，进一步调查是唯一合乎逻辑的方案。
entries.example_en: Further investigation is the only logical indication at this stage.

entries.definition_en: a medical reason for prescribing a drug or performing a procedure
entries.example_cn: 医生根据扫描结果指出有强烈的手术指征。
entries.example_en: The doctor noted a strong indication for surgery based on the scan results.

entries.definition_cn: 明确指出或指名某人或某事物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of pointing out or naming someone or something specifically
entries.example_cn: 警方记录了证人指出涉案嫌疑人的行为。
entries.example_en: The witness's indication of which suspect was involved was recorded by the police.

entries.definition_cn: 仪表显示的物理状态数据
entries.definition_en: data shown by a meter or instrument about a physical state
entries.example_cn: 仪表盘清晰地显示了燃油水平。
entries.example_en: The dashboard provided a clear indication of the fuel level.

entries.definition_en: showing or suggesting something clearly
entries.example_cn: 高失业率是经济困难的明显迹象。
entries.example_en: The high unemployment rate is an indicative sign of economic trouble.

entries.definition_en: relating to the grammatical mood used for simple statements of fact
entries.example_cn: 动词的陈述语气形式在日常对话中最常见。
entries.example_en: The indicative form of the verb is the most common in everyday speech.

entries.definition_en: a grammatical mood that presents an action or state as a fact
entries.example_cn: 在这个句子中，陈述语气被用来陈述一个明确的事实。
entries.example_en: In this sentence, the indicative mood is used to state a clear fact.

entries.definition_en: a value or ratio used to show changes or trends over time
entries.example_cn: 失业率是一个关键的经济指标。
entries.example_en: The unemployment rate is a key economic indicator.

entries.definition_en: a device that shows the operating condition of a system
entries.example_cn: 启动发动机前检查机油压力指示器。
entries.example_en: Check the oil pressure indicator before starting the engine.

entries.definition_en: a signal used to attract attention
entries.example_cn: 闪烁的灯光作为给司机的信号。
entries.example_en: The flashing light served as an indicator for the driver.

entries.definition_en: a substance that changes color to show the presence of another substance
entries.example_cn: 石蕊试纸是化学实验中使用的指示剂。
entries.example_en: Litmus paper is an indicator used in chemistry experiments.

entries.definition_en: to formally accuse someone of committing a serious crime.
entries.example_cn: 大陪审团决定起诉该商人逃税。
entries.example_en: The grand jury decided to indict the businessman for tax evasion.

entries.definition_cn: 可被起诉的；（行为）可依法提起公诉的
entries.definition_en: able or deserving of being indicted; of an act, subject to indictment
entries.example_cn: 该罪行可根据联邦法律提起公诉。
entries.example_en: The offense was indictable under federal law.

entries.definition_en: a 15-year period used for dating in ancient Rome and some medieval kingdoms
entries.example_cn: 历史学家利用15年周期来标注中世纪早期的事件。
entries.example_en: Historians use the indiction to date events in the early Middle Ages.

entries.definition_en: a formal document charging a person with a crime
entries.example_cn: 陪审团在做出决定之前听取了起诉书。
entries.example_en: The jury heard the indictment before making a decision.

entries.definition_en: a strong criticism or accusation of wrongdoing
entries.example_cn: 该报告严厉谴责了政府的政策。
entries.example_en: The report contained a severe indictment of the government's policies.

entries.definition_cn: 失败或表现不佳的证据
entries.definition_en: evidence of failure or poor performance
entries.example_cn: 球队屡屡失利，说明其管理不善。
entries.example_en: The team's repeated losses were an indictment of its management.

entries.definition_en: (of pop groups) not affiliated with a major recording company
entries.example_cn: 他们去年发布了第一张独立专辑。
entries.example_en: They released their first indie album last year.

entries.definition_en: an independent publisher
entries.example_cn: 这家独立出版商专门出版翻译小说。
entries.example_en: The indie publisher specializes in translated fiction.

entries.definition_en: a work released by an independent publisher
entries.example_cn: 这部小说由独立出版商发行后，成为一部成功的独立出版物。
entries.example_en: The novel became a successful indie after an independent publisher released it.

entries.definition_en: a state of being unbiased and impartial, without concern
entries.example_cn: 法官不因双方的财富或地位而偏袒，公正地作出了裁决。
entries.example_en: The judge ruled with complete indifference to the wealth or status of either side.

entries.definition_en: a lack of emotional reaction or feeling
entries.example_cn: 他对这场悲剧的冷漠震惊了所有人。
entries.example_en: His indifference to the tragedy shocked everyone.

entries.definition_en: a lack of enthusiasm or interest in things generally
entries.example_cn: 她对最新的时尚趋势表现出完全的漠不关心。
entries.example_en: She showed total indifference to the latest fashion trends.

entries.definition_en: a casual lack of concern or a calm appearance of not caring
entries.example_cn: 他漫不经心地接受了这个坏消息。
entries.example_en: He accepted the bad news with an air of indifference.

entries.definition_cn: 不感兴趣或不关心的；漠不关心的
entries.definition_en: not interested or concerned; apathetic
entries.example_cn: 他对晋升的消息漠不关心。
entries.example_en: He was indifferent to the news about his promotion.

entries.definition_cn: 表现出漠不关心的；冷漠的
entries.definition_en: showing a lack of care or concern
entries.example_cn: 警察对呼救声置若罔闻。
entries.example_en: The police were indifferent to the cries for help.

entries.definition_en: marked by no especial liking or dislike or preference for one thing over another
entries.example_cn: 他对茶和咖啡没有特别的偏好。
entries.example_en: He is indifferent between tea and coffee.

entries.definition_en: (usually followed by 'to') unwilling or refusing to pay heed
entries.example_cn: 她对他的道歉尝试不予理睬。
entries.example_en: She remained indifferent to his attempts to apologize.

entries.definition_en: (often followed by 'to') lacking importance; not mattering one way or the other
entries.example_cn: 到达的确切时间对会议来说无关紧要。
entries.example_en: The exact time of arrival is indifferent to the meeting.

entries.definition_en: fairly poor to not very good
entries.example_cn: 服务质量充其量只是一般。
entries.example_en: The quality of the service was indifferent at best.

entries.definition_en: characterized by a lack of partiality
entries.example_cn: 法官必须对私人关系保持公正。
entries.example_en: The judge must remain indifferent to personal relationships.

entries.definition_en: having only a limited ability to react chemically; chemically inactive
entries.example_cn: 就化学反应性而言，金是一种化学惰性的金属。
entries.example_en: Gold is an indifferent metal in terms of chemical reactivity.

entries.definition_cn: 漠不关心地；漫不经心地
entries.definition_en: without concern, interest, or care
entries.example_cn: 他冷漠地无视了关于风暴的警告。
entries.example_en: He indifferently ignored the warnings about the storm.

entries.definition_en: a state of extreme poverty or destitution
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构旨在帮助家庭摆脱赤贫。
entries.example_en: The charity aims to lift families out of indigence.

entries.definition_en: a person who was born in a particular place and is native to it
entries.example_cn: 这位土著居民向游客讲述了关于这片土地的故事。
entries.example_en: The indigene shared stories about the land with the visitors.

entries.definition_cn: 本土的；原生的；（指人或文化）原住民的
entries.definition_en: originating or occurring naturally in a particular place
entries.example_cn: 土著人民在这个地区生活了数千年。
entries.example_en: The indigenous people have lived in this region for thousands of years.

entries.definition_cn: 以本土方式；以本地特有的方式
entries.definition_en: in a way that is native to a particular place or people
entries.example_cn: 这个部落已经在这里本土地生活了数千年。
entries.example_en: The tribe has lived here indigenously for thousands of years.

entries.definition_en: poor enough to require assistance from others
entries.example_cn: 政府为贫困者提供免费餐食。
entries.example_en: The government provides free meals for the indigent.

entries.definition_en: a person who is in need or living in poverty
entries.example_cn: 这家慈善机构为贫困者提供餐食和保暖衣物。
entries.example_en: The charity provides meals and warm clothing for indigents.

entries.definition_en: difficult to digest
entries.example_cn: 那顿饭很油腻且难以消化，让他感到恶心。
entries.example_en: The meal was heavy and indigestible, leaving him feeling sick.

entries.definition_cn: 难以接受或忍受的；令人不快的
entries.definition_en: Difficult to accept or tolerate; unpleasant.
entries.example_cn: 这份报告中有一些令人难以接受的关于公司失败的事实。
entries.example_en: The report contained some indigestible truths about the company's failures.

entries.definition_en: a condition causing discomfort, heartburn, or nausea after eating
entries.example_cn: 他吃太多辛辣食物后患上了消化不良。
entries.example_en: He suffered from indigestion after eating too much spicy food.

entries.definition_en: feeling or showing anger because something is unfair or wrong
entries.example_cn: 群众对法官的判决感到愤慨。
entries.example_en: The crowd was indignant at the judge's decision.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows you are very angry about something unfair
entries.example_cn: 她愤慨地拒绝签署那份不公平的合同。
entries.example_en: She indignantly refused to sign the unfair contract.
