entries.example_cn: 女王在仪式上戴着一顶镶嵌珠宝的皇冠。
entries.example_en: The queen wore a jewelled crown to the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: someone who sells jewelry
entries.example_cn: 我们去当地的珠宝商那里买了一枚订婚戒指。
entries.example_en: We visited a local jeweller to buy an engagement ring.

entries.definition_en: someone who makes jewelry
entries.example_cn: 这位珠宝匠用黄金和钻石制作了一枚美丽的戒指。
entries.example_en: The jeweller crafted a beautiful ring from gold and diamonds.

entries.definition_cn: 戒指、项链、胸针和手镯等由贵金属制成的个人饰品，有时镶嵌宝石或仿制宝石
entries.definition_en: personal ornaments such as rings, necklaces, brooches, and bracelets, made of precious metals and sometimes set with gemstones or imitation gems
entries.example_cn: 那家商店的珠宝非常昂贵。
entries.example_en: The jewellery was very expensive in that shop.

entries.definition_en: adornments made of precious metals and set with gems
entries.example_cn: 她买了一件漂亮的珠宝。
entries.example_en: She bought a beautiful piece of jewelry.

entries.definition_cn: 水凤仙；凤仙花属植物（尤指水凤仙和黄花凤仙）
entries.definition_en: a North American annual plant with yellow or orange flowers that grows in wet, acidic soil
entries.example_cn: 池塘边生长的水凤仙开着鲜艳的橙色花朵。
entries.example_en: The jewelweed growing by the pond has bright orange flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 一种大型石斑鱼，尤其指大西洋巨石斑鱼（Epinephelus itajara）
entries.definition_en: a large grouper, especially the Atlantic goliath grouper (Epinephelus itajara)
entries.example_cn: 大西洋巨石斑鱼能够长到非常大的体型。
entries.example_en: The Atlantic jewfish, or goliath grouper, can grow to an enormous size.

entries.definition_cn: 一种澳大利亚大型食用鱼，尤其指澳洲拟石首鱼（mulloway）
entries.definition_en: a large Australian food fish, especially the mulloway (Argyrosomus japonicus)
entries.example_cn: 拟石首鱼又称 jewfish，是澳大利亚渔民珍视的捕获物。
entries.example_en: The mulloway, also called jewfish, is a prized catch for Australian fishermen.

entries.definition_cn: 不知羞耻、厚颜无耻且工于心计的女人（贬义）
entries.definition_en: a shameless, impudent, scheming woman
entries.example_cn: 小报称这位工于心计、厚颜无耻的女演员是个不知羞耻的女人。
entries.example_en: The tabloids branded the calculating, shameless actress a jezebel.

entries.definition_en: a unit of currency in China equal to one-tenth of a yuan
entries.example_cn: 在中国，一元分为十角。
entries.example_en: In China, one yuan is divided into ten jiao.

entries.definition_en: any triangular fore-and-aft sail (set forward of the foremast)
entries.example_cn: 水手调整三角前帆以捕捉风力。
entries.example_en: The sailor adjusted the jib to catch the wind.

entries.definition_en: stop and refuse to go forward, usually of a horse
entries.example_cn: 那匹马不肯前进，拒绝过桥。
entries.example_en: The horse jibbed and refused to cross the bridge.

entries.definition_en: shift or swing a sail, boom, or yard around, as in tacking
entries.example_cn: 船员在抢风换舷时转动了帆。
entries.example_en: The crew jibbed the sail while tacking.

entries.definition_en: to be compatible, similar or consistent; coincide in their characteristics
entries.example_cn: 这两项测试的结果不一致。
entries.example_en: The results of the two tests do not jibe with each other.

entries.definition_cn: （帆船）通过让帆杆横过船尾来换舷转向
entries.definition_en: to change a sailing vessel's course by shifting the boom across the stern
entries.example_cn: 风向改变时，帆船换舷转向了。
entries.example_en: The sailboat jibed when the wind shifted.

entries.definition_en: an aggressive remark directed at a person intended to have a telling effect
entries.example_cn: 他因新小说受到评论家尖锐的讽刺。
entries.example_en: He received a sharp jibe from the critic about his new novel.

entries.definition_en: a very short time
entries.example_cn: 我马上就到。
entries.example_en: I'll be there in a jiffy.

entries.definition_en: music written in a fast rhythm for dancing
entries.example_cn: 乐队演奏了一首欢快的吉格舞曲，让人群开始跳舞。
entries.example_en: The band played a lively jig to get the crowd dancing.

entries.definition_en: a fishing lure that is jerked up and down in the water
entries.example_cn: 渔夫将他的颤饵抛入深水中，希望能钓到鳟鱼。
entries.example_en: The fisherman cast his jig into the deep water hoping to catch a trout.

entries.definition_en: a machine tool that holds and guides workpieces
entries.example_cn: 机械师调整了夹具，以确保金属零件被正确钻孔。
entries.example_en: The machinist adjusted the jig to ensure the metal part was drilled correctly.

entries.definition_cn: 一种伴随踢踏和跳跃的传统吉格舞
entries.definition_en: an old rustic dance involving kicking and leaping
entries.example_cn: 村民们在丰收节上表演了传统的吉格舞。
entries.example_en: The villagers performed a traditional jig during the harvest festival.

entries.definition_en: to dance a jig
entries.example_cn: 在聚会上，他精力充沛地在房间里跳起了吉格舞。
entries.example_en: At the party, he jigged around the room with great energy.

entries.definition_cn: （过时、冒犯性俚语）对黑人的极度侮辱性称呼
entries.definition_en: a dated, highly offensive slang term for a Black person
entries.example_cn: “jigaboo”是一个极具冒犯性的种族蔑称。
entries.example_en: The word 'jigaboo' is a highly offensive ethnic slur.

entries.definition_cn: 量酒器；通常容量为1.5液盎司（约44毫升）的小量杯
entries.definition_en: a small measuring vessel, typically holding 1½ fluid ounces (about 44 ml)
entries.example_cn: 调酒师用量酒器量取波本威士忌，然后将其倒入玻璃杯中。
entries.example_en: The bartender used a jigger to measure bourbon before pouring it into the glass.

entries.definition_en: larval mite that sucks the blood of vertebrates including human beings causing intense irritation
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者在高草丛中露营时被恙螨幼虫叮咬了。
entries.example_en: The hikers were bitten by jiggers while camping in the tall grass.

entries.definition_en: any small mast on a sailing vessel; especially the mizzenmast of a yawl
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴来临前固定好小桅杆。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to secure the jigger before the storm hit.

entries.definition_cn: 调整或改动某物，尤指以非原先设想的方式
entries.definition_en: to alter or adjust something, especially in a way not originally intended
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不调整设置，才能让这款旧软件运行起来。
entries.example_en: We had to jigger the settings to get the old software to work.

entries.definition_cn: 该死的；倒霉的（英国委婉语）
entries.definition_en: damned; doomed or in trouble (British euphemistic)
entries.example_cn: 真见鬼，我怎么也弄不懂这件事。
entries.example_en: I'm jiggered if I can make sense of this.

entries.definition_en: deceptive talk or actions intended to trick someone
entries.example_cn: 推销员的欺骗手段让那位老人买下了那块昂贵的表。
entries.example_en: The salesman's jiggery-pokery convinced the old man to buy the expensive watch.

entries.definition_en: to move back and forth in a shaking way
entries.example_cn: 她抖动钥匙看看是否卡住了。
entries.example_en: She jiggle the keys to see if they were stuck.

entries.definition_en: a slight shaking movement
entries.example_cn: 果冻被触碰时会有轻微的抖动。
entries.example_en: The jelly had a slight jiggle when touched.

entries.definition_en: a portable power saw with a reciprocating blade used for various cuts
entries.example_cn: 木匠用曲线锯切割木材上的复杂图案。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a jigsaw to cut the intricate pattern in the wood.

entries.definition_en: a fine-toothed power saw with a narrow blade used to cut curved outlines
entries.example_cn: 她买了一把新的细齿曲线锯，以便在金属板上进行精确的曲线切割。
entries.example_en: She bought a new jigsaw to make precise curved cuts in the metal sheet.

entries.definition_cn: 吉哈德；穆斯林为道德、精神或政治目标而进行的奋斗（有时指圣战）
entries.definition_en: a holy struggle or striving by a Muslim for a moral, spiritual, or political goal
entries.example_cn: 许多穆斯林认为，为正义而奋斗是吉哈德的一种形式。
entries.example_en: Many Muslims view the struggle for justice as a form of jihad.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of a jihad
entries.example_cn: 该圣战组织声称对此次袭击负责。
entries.example_en: The jihadi group claimed responsibility for the attack.

entries.definition_cn: 无数；极多（通常用于夸张）
entries.definition_en: a very large indefinite number, usually used for exaggeration
entries.example_cn: 我已经无数次让你打扫房间了。
entries.example_en: I've told you a jillion times to clean your room.

usage.label: slang
usage.pattern: Informal exaggerated reference to a very large number.

entries.definition_en: cast aside capriciously or unfeelingly
entries.example_cn: 他决定在婚礼当天无情地抛弃未婚妻。
entries.example_en: He decided to jilt his fiancée on their wedding day.

entries.definition_en: a woman who jilts a lover
entries.example_cn: 那个抛弃情人的女子以残酷对待前男友而闻名。
entries.example_en: The jilt was known for her cruel treatment of her ex-boyfriend.

entries.definition_en: rebuffed (by a lover) without warning
entries.example_cn: 她在婚礼上被抛弃后感到心碎。
entries.example_en: She felt heartbroken after being jilted at the altar.

entries.definition_en: to force something open or to tamper with something (informal)
entries.example_cn: 他试图撬开窗户透透气。
entries.example_en: He tried to jim the window open to get some fresh air.

entries.definition_en: a one-pound banknote (Australian colloquial)
entries.example_cn: 他用一张一英镑的纸币付了咖啡钱。
entries.example_en: He paid for the coffee with a jim.

entries.definition_cn: 阿拉伯字母jim的另一种拼写
entries.definition_en: an alternative spelling for the Arabic letter jeem
entries.example_cn: 在某些文本中，阿拉伯字母被写作jim。
entries.example_en: In some texts, the Arabic letter is written as jim.

entries.definition_en: a humorous alternative spelling for gym
entries.example_cn: 下班后我要去健身房举举铁。
entries.example_en: I'm going to the jim after work to hit the weights.

entries.definition_cn: 糖针；糖屑（常作冰淇淋配料）
entries.definition_en: small pieces of candy used as a topping, especially on ice cream
entries.example_cn: 她在香草冰淇淋上撒了一些巧克力碎。
entries.example_en: She sprinkled jimmies over the vanilla ice cream.

entries.definition_en: to move or force something, especially in an effort to get it open
entries.example_cn: 他们试图用一块木头撬开门。
entries.example_en: They tried to jimmy the door open with a piece of wood.

entries.definition_en: a short metal bar used for prying things open
entries.example_cn: 小偷用撬棍强行打开了窗户。
entries.example_en: The thief used a jimmy to force the window open.

entries.definition_en: a tall, poisonous annual weed with rank-smelling leaves, trumpet-shaped flowers, and prickly fruits.
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被警告不要触摸路边生长的曼陀罗。
entries.example_en: The children were warned not to touch the jimsonweed growing by the roadside.

entries.definition_en: a short, clear metallic sound
entries.example_cn: 钥匙的叮当声在走廊里回荡。
entries.example_en: The jingle of the keys echoed in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: a comic verse of irregular measure
entries.example_cn: 孩子们背诵了一首关于天气的打油诗。
entries.example_en: The children recited a jingle about the weather.

entries.definition_en: to make a sound typical of metallic objects
entries.example_cn: 硬币在口袋里发出叮当声。
entries.example_en: The coins jingled in the pocket.

entries.definition_en: to make a jingling or jangling sound
entries.example_cn: 他走路时，口袋里的钥匙叮叮当当地响着。
entries.example_en: The keys jingle-jangled in the pocket as he walked.

entries.definition_en: making a series of high-pitched ringing sounds like many small bells
entries.example_cn: 她钱包里叮当作响的硬币引起了店主的注意。
entries.example_en: The jingling coins in her purse caught the shopkeeper's attention.

entries.definition_en: making a series of high-pitched ringing sounds like many small bells
entries.example_cn: 钥匙发出的叮当声引起了我的注意。
entries.example_en: The jingly sound of the keys caught my attention.

entries.definition_en: an extreme bellicose nationalist
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家在竞选期间因其好战的言论而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was criticized for his jingo rhetoric during the election.

entries.definition_cn: 沙文主义；狂热爱国主义

entries.example_en: The jingoist demanded immediate military action against the neighbor.

entries.definition_cn: 沙文主义的；狂热爱国的

entries.definition_cn: 被认为会给周围人带来厄运的人或事物

entries.definition_en: a small public-transport vehicle, such as a minibus or shared taxi

entries.example_en: They took the jitney to the city center.

entries.definition_en: a state of nervousness
entries.example_cn: 那部恐怖电影让我紧张不安。
entries.example_en: That creepy movie gave me the jitters.

entries.definition_cn: 轻微而常为不自主的不规则运动；抽动

entries.example_en: The camera captured a slight jitter in the actor's hand.

entries.definition_cn: 信号一个或多个特征的突发性非预期变化
entries.definition_en: an abrupt, unwanted variation in one or more signal characteristics
entries.example_cn: 由于连接不佳，视频画面出现了抖动。
entries.example_en: The video feed suffered from jitter due to a poor connection.

entries.definition_en: a jerky American dance popular in the 1940s
entries.example_cn: 那对舞伴在舞厅表演了一段充满活力的吉特巴舞。

entries.example_en: Everyone on the floor started to jitterbug to the upbeat music.

entries.definition_en: a state of nervous anxiety or trembling, often called having the jitters
entries.example_cn: 她在公开演讲前的紧张不安使她难以集中注意力。
entries.example_en: Her jitteriness before the public speech made it hard for her to focus.

entries.definition_en: shaking or vibrating rapidly and irregularly
entries.example_cn: 不断抖动的信号使数据难以读取。

entries.definition_cn: 紧张不安的；坐立不安的

entries.example_en: The jittery video playback made the presentation difficult to follow.

entries.definition_en: a martial art of self-defense that uses holds and blows combined with the attacker's weight and strength

entries.definition_en: the smallest detectable difference between two stimuli
entries.example_cn: 该实验测量了重量感知的最小可觉差。

entries.definition_en: a paid position of regular employment
entries.example_cn: 她在银行找到了一份新工作。

entries.definition_en: a specific task that needs to be done

entries.example_en: The carpenter showed us his latest job—a beautifully carved table.

entries.definition_en: a person or business that buys and sells goods as an intermediary

entries.definition_en: a government office where job information is shown and unemployment benefits are managed

entries.example_cn: 许多失业的工人正在努力在当前市场上找到新工作。

entries.example_en: The joinery produced finely crafted doors and cabinets for the restoration project.

entries.definition_en: the act or result of joining things together; a connection or juncture

entries.example_cn: 别再跟你哥哥开玩笑逗他了，去帮他吧。
entries.example_en: Stop joking with your brother and help him.

entries.definition_en: a person who likes to tell jokes or make people laugh
entries.example_cn: 他是班里的开心果，总是逗得我们发笑。
entries.example_en: He is the class joker and always makes us laugh.

entries.definition_en: a playing card depicting a jester
entries.example_cn: 她从牌堆里抽出了小丑牌。
entries.example_en: She drew the joker from the deck.

entries.definition_en: a silly, annoying, or disreputable person
entries.example_cn: 别这么爱捣乱了，帮帮我吧。
entries.example_en: Stop being such a joker and help me with this.

entries.definition_en: a hidden or tricky clause in a legal document
entries.example_cn: 律师警告我们要留意合同中的隐蔽条款。
entries.example_en: The lawyer warned us about the joker in the contract.

entries.definition_en: a person who enjoys telling or playing jokes
entries.example_cn: 这位爱开玩笑的人在会议上的机智评论让每个人都笑了。
entries.example_en: The jokester made everyone laugh with his witty remarks during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: characterized by jokes and good humor
entries.example_cn: 他爱开玩笑，从不把自己看得太严肃。
entries.example_en: He has a joking manner and never takes himself too seriously.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not serious; as a joke
entries.example_cn: 他开玩笑地问我想不想请他喝一杯。
entries.example_en: He jokingly asked if I wanted to buy him a drink.

entries.definition_en: without serious intent; not meant to be taken seriously
entries.example_cn: 她非正式地批评了他的新发型。
entries.example_en: She jokingly criticized his new haircut.

entries.definition_en: a boisterous celebration; a merry festivity
entries.example_cn: 新年的狂欢一直持续到黎明。
entries.example_en: The New Year's jollification lasted until dawn.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of being cheerful, jovial, and full of good humor
entries.example_cn: 派对充满了欢乐和笑声。
entries.example_en: The party was full of jollity and laughter.

entries.definition_en: a merry or festive gathering
entries.example_cn: 村民举行了一场欢乐的聚会，庆祝收获季结束。
entries.example_en: The village held a jollity to celebrate the end of the harvest.

entries.definition_en: full of or showing high-spirited merriment
entries.example_cn: 他们在节日里玩得很开心。
entries.example_en: They had a jolly time at the festival.

entries.definition_en: to a certain extent or degree
entries.example_cn: 今天天气相当冷。
entries.example_en: The weather was jolly cold today.

entries.definition_cn: （英国，常带幽默色彩）短途旅行；游玩
entries.definition_en: a pleasure trip or excursion, especially an expenses-paid or unnecessary one (UK, often humorous)
entries.example_cn: 他们沿着海岸去游玩。
entries.example_en: They went on a jolly along the coast.

entries.definition_en: a small boat used by sailors for general work
entries.example_cn: 船员们用一艘划艇将物资运送到主船上。
entries.example_en: The crew used a jolly to transport supplies to the main ship.

entries.definition_en: to amuse or entertain someone
entries.example_cn: 表演者用歌曲和笑话逗孩子们开心。
entries.example_en: The entertainer jollied the children with songs and jokes.

entries.definition_en: to move or cause to move with a sudden, jerky motion
entries.example_cn: 崎岖的道路颠簸得乘客们醒了过来。
entries.example_en: The rough road jolted the passengers awake.

entries.definition_en: to disturb someone's calm or composure suddenly
entries.example_cn: 那个坏消息把她从白日梦中惊醒。
entries.example_en: The bad news jolted her out of her daydream.

entries.definition_en: a sudden shock or impact that makes you move physically
entries.example_cn: 汽车撞进了一个坑，给了我一个猛烈的震动。
entries.example_en: The car hit a pothole and gave me a sudden jolt.

entries.definition_en: a sudden, involuntary physical movement
entries.example_cn: 一阵突如其来的剧痛让他掉下了杯子。
entries.example_en: A sudden jolt of pain made him drop the cup.

entries.definition_cn: 引起或具有颠簸和不规则运动的
entries.definition_en: causing or characterized by sudden, irregular movements or shocks.
entries.example_cn: 由于路上的坑洼，乘车过程颠簸不已。
entries.example_en: The car ride was jolting because of the potholes on the road.

entries.definition_en: a person believed to bring bad luck to those around them
entries.example_cn: 大家都避免坐在乔纳旁边，因为他被认为是个倒霉鬼。
entries.example_en: Everyone avoided sitting next to Jonah because he was considered a jinx.

entries.definition_en: to have a strong desire or craving for something
entries.example_cn: 我现在非常想喝一杯咖啡。
entries.example_en: I'm jonesing for a cup of coffee right now.

entries.definition_en: to consume cocaine and/or alcohol heavily
entries.example_cn: 警察发现他在巷子里狂饮酒并吸食可卡因。
entries.example_en: The police found him bingeing on cocaine and alcohol in the alleyway.

entries.definition_en: he/she/it has a strong desire or craving
entries.example_cn: 她渴望最新的时尚潮流。
entries.example_en: She joneses for the latest fashion trends.

entries.definition_en: an addiction or a very strong desire for something
entries.example_cn: 他非常想吃巧克力冰淇淋。
entries.example_en: He has a real jones for chocolate ice cream.

entries.definition_en: a medieval entertainer who sang folk songs and performed tricks
entries.example_cn: 吟游诗人用骑士精神和魔法的故事娱乐了宫廷。
entries.example_en: The jongleur entertained the court with tales of chivalry and magic.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental plant with fragrant yellow or white clustered flowers, native to southern Europe
entries.example_cn: 早春时节，花园里弥漫着盛开的黄水仙的香气。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the scent of blooming jonquils in early spring.

entries.definition_en: a yellow daffodil
entries.example_cn: 她从路边摘了一朵黄水仙送给母亲。
entries.example_en: She picked a jonquil from the roadside to give to her mother.

entries.definition_cn: （美国东南部）提供食物、饮料和点唱机音乐的小路边餐馆
entries.definition_en: a small roadside establishment in the southeastern United States where you can eat and drink and dance to music provided by a jukebox
entries.example_cn: 我们在一家路边餐馆停下吃午饭并听音乐。
entries.example_en: We stopped at a jook to grab some lunch and listen to the music.

entries.definition_en: a Chinese rice gruel eaten for breakfast
entries.example_cn: 早餐时，他吃了一碗粥。
entries.example_en: For breakfast, he ate a bowl of jook.

entries.definition_en: A woman's riding coat from the 18th century, featuring a long cape and buttons down the front.
entries.example_cn: 这幅历史画作描绘了一位身穿华丽骑装的女贵族。
entries.example_en: The historical painting depicts a noblewoman wearing a richly embroidered joseph.

entries.definition_en: to act in a silly way or to tease someone playfully
entries.example_cn: 男孩们在走廊里互相开玩笑。
entries.example_en: The boys were joshing each other in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: a Chinese god worshipped in the form of an idol
entries.example_cn: 他们在财神像前放了红包以祈求财富。
entries.example_en: They placed a red envelope on the joss to pray for wealth.

entries.definition_en: to make your way by pushing or shoving other people
entries.example_cn: 游客们推挤着导游，挤进了入口。
entries.example_en: The tourists jostled past the guide to reach the entrance.

entries.definition_en: to come into rough contact with while moving
entries.example_cn: 两辆车在试图汇入高速公路时发生了碰撞。
entries.example_en: The two cars jostled as they tried to merge onto the highway.

entries.definition_en: the act of pushing people roughly to get through a crowd
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不推挤才能挤上拥挤的公交车。
entries.example_en: We had to jostle to get a seat on the crowded bus.

entries.definition_en: the act of jostling (forcing your way by pushing)
entries.example_cn: 拥挤的地铁车厢里有很多推挤。
entries.example_en: There was a lot of jostling in the crowded subway car.

entries.definition_en: to write something down quickly and briefly
entries.example_cn: 请在离开前匆匆记下电话号码。
entries.example_en: Please jot down the phone number before you leave.

entries.definition_en: a short note written quickly
entries.example_cn: 她在桌上留了一张便条让他稍后阅读。
entries.example_en: She left a jot on the table for him to read later.

entries.definition_en: a very small amount of something
entries.example_cn: 没有任何一点证据支持他的说法。
entries.example_en: There was not a jot of evidence to support his claim.

entries.definition_en: a small notebook used for taking rough notes
entries.example_cn: 他口袋里总带着一本记事本，以便随时记下脑海中闪现的想法。
entries.example_en: He kept a jotter in his pocket to jot down ideas as they occurred to him.

entries.definition_cn: 简短的随手记录或草图
entries.definition_en: a brief note or sketch, often written hurriedly by hand
entries.example_cn: 离开前他随手记下了电话号码。
entries.example_en: He made a quick jotting of the phone number before leaving.

entries.definition_en: a unit of energy equal to the work done when a current of one ampere passes through a resistance of one ohm for one second
entries.example_cn: 灯泡消耗的能量以焦耳为单位进行测量。
entries.example_en: The energy consumed by the light bulb was measured in joules.

entries.definition_en: to move up and down repeatedly
entries.example_cn: 船在汹涌的波浪中剧烈颠簸。
entries.example_en: The boat jounced over the rough waves.

entries.definition_en: a sudden jarring impact
entries.example_cn: 马撞到石头时剧烈颠簸了一下。
entries.example_en: The horse gave a violent jounce as it hit the stone.

entries.definition_en: a daily written record of (usually personal) experiences and observations
entries.example_cn: 她每晚写日记。
entries.example_en: She writes in her journal every night.

entries.definition_en: a periodical dedicated to a particular subject
entries.example_cn: 他订阅了一份医学期刊。
entries.example_en: He subscribes to a medical journal.

entries.definition_en: a ledger in which transactions have been recorded as they occurred
entries.example_cn: 会计详细记录了所有销售的日记账。
entries.example_en: The accountant kept a detailed journal of all sales.

entries.definition_en: a record book as a physical object
entries.example_cn: 请把记录本还给图书馆。
entries.example_en: Please return the journal to the library.

entries.definition_en: the part of a shaft or axle that rests on a bearing
entries.example_cn: 机械师更换了车轴上磨损的轴颈。
entries.example_en: The mechanic replaced the worn journal on the axle.

entries.definition_cn: 新闻腔；报刊中带有套话、夸张、特定行业词汇和简略句法的写作风格
entries.definition_en: a newspaper or magazine writing style marked by clichés, hyperbole, genre-specific vocabulary, and clipped syntax
entries.example_cn: 这篇文章采用典型的新闻腔，充斥着套话和夸张的说法，而不是清晰简洁的文风。
entries.example_en: The article was written in typical journalese, full of clichés and hyperbole rather than clear, concise prose.

entries.definition_en: the profession of reporting news stories
entries.example_cn: 她决定从事新闻业。
entries.example_en: She decided to pursue a career in journalism.

entries.definition_en: newspapers and magazines collectively
entries.example_cn: 20世纪初的报刊包括许多有影响力的报纸和杂志。
entries.example_en: The journalism of the early twentieth century included many influential newspapers and magazines.

entries.definition_en: a person who writes for newspapers or magazines
entries.example_cn: 记者就新政策采访了市长。
entries.example_en: The journalist interviewed the mayor about the new policy.

entries.definition_en: someone who keeps a diary or journal
entries.example_cn: 她年轻时写日记记录旅行。
entries.example_en: She kept a journal as a young journalist to record her travels.

entries.definition_en: relating to journalism or having the qualities of a journalist
entries.example_cn: 这家报纸发表了一篇关于该丑闻的新闻调查报道。
entries.example_en: The newspaper published a journalistic investigation into the scandal.

entries.definition_cn: 以新闻报道的方式；从新闻业的角度
entries.definition_en: in a manner characteristic of journalists or journalism
entries.example_cn: 这篇报道以新闻报道的方式处理，既关注经核实的事实，也关注人情味角度。
entries.example_en: The story was handled journalistically, with attention to verified facts and the human-interest angle.

entries.definition_en: the act of traveling from one place to another
entries.example_cn: 去山区的旅程花了三天时间。
entries.example_en: The journey to the mountains took three days.

entries.definition_en: to travel from one place to another
entries.example_cn: 他们穿越沙漠寻找水源。
entries.example_en: They journeyed across the desert to find water.

entries.definition_en: to travel upon or across a surface
entries.example_cn: 火车沿着海岸行驶。
entries.example_en: The train journeyed along the coast.

entries.definition_en: the act of traveling from one place to another
entries.example_cn: 穿越沙漠的漫长旅程花费了数周时间。
entries.example_en: The long journeying across the desert took several weeks.

entries.definition_en: a skilled tradesperson who has completed an apprenticeship and works independently or for a master tradesperson
entries.example_cn: 作为一名熟练木匠，他以极高的精度制作了定制家具。
entries.example_en: As a journeyman carpenter, he built the custom furniture with great precision.

entries.definition_en: a medieval contest where knights on horseback fight each other with lances
entries.example_cn: 锦标赛中两位著名骑士进行了一场精彩的比武。
entries.example_en: The tournament featured a spectacular joust between two famous knights.

entries.definition_en: to fight against someone in a tournament on horseback with lances
entries.example_cn: 冠军在最后一轮中与对手进行了骑士决斗。
entries.example_en: The champion jousted against the challenger in the final round.

entries.definition_cn: 就重要问题与某人进行言语交锋
entries.definition_en: to engage in verbal sparring with someone over an important issue
entries.example_cn: 两位政治家就拟议中的法律展开了言语交锋。
entries.example_en: The two politicians jousted verbally over the proposed law.

entries.definition_en: full of or showing high-spirited merriment
entries.example_cn: 这群朋友聚在一起，度过了一个充满欢笑和游戏的快乐夜晚。
entries.example_en: The group of friends gathered for a jovial evening of laughter and games.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being cheerful and full of good humor
entries.example_cn: 派对上充满了欢声笑语，每个人都笑逐颜开。
entries.example_en: The party was full of joviality, with everyone laughing and joking.

entries.definition_en: a cheerful and friendly nature
entries.example_cn: 他乐天派的性格使他成为社区中受欢迎的人物。
entries.example_en: His joviality made him a popular figure in the community.

entries.definition_en: in a jovial manner
entries.example_cn: 主人欢快地迎接客人，让每个人都感到受欢迎。
entries.example_en: The host greeted the guests jovially, making everyone feel welcome.

entries.definition_cn: 下颌和下颚处肉质的丰满与松弛（衰老的特征）
entries.definition_en: a fullness and looseness of the flesh of the lower cheek and jaw (characteristic of aging)
entries.example_cn: 他的脸上显露出衰老的迹象，下巴下方挂着松弛的下颌肉。
entries.example_en: His face showed signs of aging, with loose jowls hanging below his chin.

entries.definition_cn: 下颌或下颌骨，尤指下颌骨的侧部
entries.definition_en: the jaw or jawbone, especially one of the lateral parts of the mandible
entries.example_cn: 这只狗的下颌很有力。
entries.example_en: The dog had a powerful lower jaw.

entries.definition_en: having sagging folds of flesh beneath the chin or lower jaw
entries.example_cn: 这只老狗的下巴有赘肉，让每个人都想起了它的年龄。
entries.example_en: The old dog had a jowly face that reminded everyone of his age.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of great happiness
entries.example_cn: 这消息给她带来了巨大的喜悦。
entries.example_en: The news brought her great joy.

entries.definition_en: something or someone that provides a source of happiness
entries.example_cn: 她的孩子们是她最大的快乐源泉。
entries.example_en: Her children are her greatest joy.

entries.definition_en: to feel happiness or joy
entries.example_cn: 他们看到老朋友时感到很高兴。
entries.example_en: They joyed at the sight of their old friends.

entries.definition_en: to make glad or happy
entries.example_cn: 惊喜派对让全家人都高兴起来。
entries.example_en: The surprise party joyed the whole family.

entries.definition_en: full of or producing joy
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节早晨打开礼物时充满了喜悦。
entries.example_en: The children were joyful as they opened their presents on Christmas morning.

entries.definition_en: full of high-spirited delight
entries.example_cn: 当球队攻入制胜球时，兴高采烈的人群大声欢呼。
entries.example_en: The joyful crowd cheered loudly when the team scored the winning goal.

entries.definition_en: in a happy and cheerful manner
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在公园里奔跑时欢快地歌唱。
entries.example_en: The children sang joyfully as they ran through the park.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of feeling great happiness
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在雪中玩耍时的欢乐显而易见。
entries.example_en: The joyfulness of the children was evident as they played in the snow.

entries.definition_en: not experiencing or inspiring joy
entries.example_cn: 那场仪式冷冷清清，毫无欢愉可言。
entries.example_en: The ceremony was a joyless affair attended by few people.

entries.definition_en: in a manner without joy
entries.example_cn: 他闷闷不乐地接受了这个消息，茫然地盯着墙壁。
entries.example_en: He accepted the news joylessly, staring blankly at the wall.

entries.definition_en: full of or characterized by joy
entries.example_cn: 节日期间，人群唱着欢乐的歌曲。
entries.example_en: The crowd sang joyous songs during the festival.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows great happiness and excitement
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在公园里兴高采烈地跳舞。
entries.example_en: The children danced joyously through the park.

entries.definition_en: the state of being extremely happy
entries.example_cn: 庆祝活动中每个人的笑容都显示出那种高兴的状态。
entries.example_en: The joyousness of the celebration was evident in everyone's smiles.

entries.definition_en: a car ride taken solely for pleasure without a specific destination
entries.example_cn: 那群青少年决定在夜间去乡下兜风。
entries.example_en: The teenagers decided to go on a joyride through the countryside at night.

entries.definition_en: to take a car for a ride without a specific goal, just for fun
entries.example_cn: 一些青少年晚上在城里兜风。
entries.example_en: Some teenagers joyride around the city at night.

entries.definition_en: a handle that moves in two directions to control a computer or game
entries.example_cn: 他使用游戏手柄控制角色穿过迷宫。
entries.example_en: He used the joystick to navigate the character through the maze.

entries.definition_en: a lever used by a pilot to control an airplane's flight surfaces
entries.example_cn: 飞行员调整操纵杆使飞机急转弯。
entries.example_en: The pilot adjusted the joystick to turn the plane sharply.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of great joy; jubilation
entries.example_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，他们的狂喜显而易见。
entries.example_en: The team's jubilance was evident when they won the championship.

entries.definition_cn: 因胜利或成功而欣喜和自豪的；欢欣鼓舞的
entries.definition_en: feeling or showing great joy and pride, especially after a victory
entries.example_cn: 他们的球队赢得冠军后，球迷们欣喜若狂。
entries.example_en: The fans were jubilant after their team won the championship.

entries.definition_en: full of high-spirited delight and excitement
entries.example_cn: 随着烟花在夜空中绽放，人群兴高采烈。
entries.example_en: The crowd was jubilant as the fireworks exploded in the sky.

entries.definition_en: in a joyous manner
entries.example_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，人群欢欣鼓舞地欢呼起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd cheered jubilantly when the team won the championship.

entries.definition_en: to show great happiness and excitement
entries.example_cn: 当他们的球队进球时，球迷们欣喜若狂。
entries.example_en: The fans jubilate when their team scores a goal.

entries.definition_en: to celebrate a special anniversary or festival
entries.example_cn: 该镇将庆祝其建城一百周年。
entries.example_en: The town will jubilate the centenary of its founding.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of extreme joy
entries.example_cn: 当球队赢得冠军时，球迷们掀起了一阵狂喜的浪潮。
entries.example_en: There was a wave of jubilation among the fans when the team won the championship.

entries.definition_en: a joyful occasion for special festivities to mark a happy event
entries.example_cn: 这座城市举行了盛大的庆祝盛会，以纪念战争的结束。
entries.example_en: The city held a grand jubilation to celebrate the end of the war.

entries.definition_en: triumphant shouting
entries.example_cn: 进球时，人群爆发出胜利的欢呼声。
entries.example_en: The crowd erupted in triumphant shouts when the goal was scored.

entries.definition_en: a special anniversary or the celebration of it
entries.example_cn: 女王举行了盛大的仪式庆祝她的金禧庆典。
entries.example_en: The Queen celebrated her Golden Jubilee with a grand ceremony.

entries.definition_en: to shake or vibrate rapidly and violently
entries.example_cn: 这辆旧车在爬陡坡时开始剧烈震动。
entries.example_en: The old car began to judder as it climbed the steep hill.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: shake or move violently; no object

entries.definition_en: a public official who decides legal cases in a court
entries.example_cn: 法官走进法庭并坐下。
entries.example_en: The judge entered the courtroom and took her seat.

entries.definition_en: to form a critical opinion about something
entries.example_cn: 我通过他的行为来评判他的品格。
entries.example_en: I judge his character by his actions.

usage.label: judge somebody/something by something
usage.pattern: judge a person's character by their actions

entries.definition_en: to estimate the amount or duration of something
entries.example_cn: 在雾中很难估计距离。
entries.example_en: It is hard to judge the distance in the fog.

entries.definition_en: to decide the winner of a competition
entries.example_cn: 裁判将裁决体操比赛。
entries.example_en: The referee will judge the gymnastics competition.

entries.definition_en: to hear and decide a legal case
entries.example_cn: 法官明天将审理此案。
entries.example_en: The judge will judge the case tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: to make a formal legal decision about someone's guilt or innocence
entries.example_cn: 法官将宣判被告有罪或无罪。
entries.example_en: The judge will pronounce the defendant guilty or not guilty.

entries.definition_en: an expert who can evaluate the quality or value of something
entries.example_cn: 她是葡萄酒鉴赏家。
entries.example_en: She is a judge of fine wine.

entries.definition_en: an opinion or conclusion reached after considering evidence
entries.example_cn: 我的判断是，如果我们努力工作，这个项目会成功的。
entries.example_en: My judgement is that the project will succeed if we work hard.

entries.definition_en: the skill of assessing situations wisely and making sound decisions
entries.example_cn: 船长的明智判断使船只免于风暴。
entries.example_en: The captain's judgement saved the ship from the storm.

entries.definition_en: the ability to understand and distinguish between different things
entries.example_cn: 她在辨别是非方面具有出色的辨别力。
entries.example_en: She has excellent judgement in distinguishing between right and wrong.

entries.definition_en: the act of forming an opinion or evaluating something
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生们对这篇作文做出评判。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the students to make a judgement on the essay.

entries.definition_cn: 作出决定或得出结论的思维过程
entries.definition_en: the mental process of thinking carefully to reach a decision or draw a conclusion
entries.example_cn: 委员会的判断过程包括在作出决定前仔细权衡所有证据。
entries.example_en: The committee's judgement involved carefully weighing all the evidence before reaching a decision.

entries.definition_en: a legal decision made by a court on a case brought before it
entries.example_cn: 法院经过一周的审议后作出了裁决。
entries.example_en: The court's judgement was delivered after a week of deliberation.

entries.definition_en: a formal written statement by a judge explaining the reasons for a court decision
entries.example_cn: 法官下达了判决书，命令被告支付赔偿金。
entries.example_en: The judge issued a judgement ordering the defendant to pay damages.

entries.definition_en: the position or office of a judge
entries.example_cn: 她在多年的法律实践后被任命为法官。
entries.example_en: She was appointed to the judgeship after years of legal practice.

entries.definition_en: the cognitive process of reaching a decision or drawing conclusions
entries.example_cn: 判断需要仔细考虑证据。
entries.example_en: Judging requires careful consideration of the evidence.

entries.definition_en: an opinion or conclusion formed after thinking about something
entries.example_cn: 我对形势的判断是错误的。
entries.example_en: My judgment of the situation was wrong.

entries.definition_en: the ability to make wise and correct decisions
entries.example_cn: 她在选择朋友方面具有极佳的判断力。
entries.example_en: She has excellent judgment in choosing her friends.

entries.definition_en: the act of forming an opinion or making a decision
entries.example_cn: 老师对学生作业的评价很公正。
entries.example_en: The teacher's judgment of the student's work was fair.

entries.definition_en: a formal decision made by a court of law
entries.example_cn: 法官在审判结束时宣布判决。
entries.example_en: The judge announced the judgment at the end of the trial.

entries.definition_en: the mental process of deciding or concluding something
entries.example_cn: 良好的决断力对于做出重要决定至关重要。
entries.example_en: Good judgment is essential for making important decisions.

entries.definition_en: the ability to understand differences and relationships between things
entries.example_cn: 孩子们随着年龄增长而发展出辨别力。
entries.example_en: Children develop judgment as they grow older.

entries.definition_en: a written document explaining the reasons for a court's decision
entries.example_cn: 律师向陪审团宣读了判决书。
entries.example_en: The lawyer read the judgment aloud to the jury.

entries.definition_en: based on or involving judgment
entries.example_cn: 这个决定是由委员会凭判断做出的。
entries.example_en: The decision was a judgmental one made by the committee.

entries.definition_en: the system of courts that administer justice and form the judicial branch of government
entries.example_cn: 对司法体系的改革提高了公民获得司法公正的机会。
entries.example_en: Reforms to the judicature have improved access to justice for citizens.

entries.definition_en: a group of judges that handles legal cases
entries.example_cn: 该案被提交给完整的司法机构进行最终裁决。
entries.example_en: The case was referred to the full judicature for a final ruling.

entries.definition_cn: 法官的职位、职权或管辖权
entries.definition_en: the office, authority, or jurisdiction of a judge
entries.example_cn: 他在首都担任一个显要的法官职位。
entries.example_en: He held a prestigious judicature in the capital.

entries.definition_en: the act of administering justice according to the law
entries.example_cn: 古代的司法严格遵循成文法典。
entries.example_en: The ancient judicature was based on strict adherence to written codes.

entries.definition_en: concerning the administration of justice
entries.example_cn: 司法制度确保审判的公平性。
entries.example_en: The judicial system ensures fairness in trials.

entries.definition_en: made or decided by a court of law
entries.example_cn: 这项司法裁决是最终的且具有约束力的。
entries.example_en: The judicial decision was final and binding.

entries.definition_en: related to the duties of a judge
entries.example_cn: 她在法律领域拥有法官职务背景。
entries.example_en: She has a judicial background in the legal field.

entries.definition_en: showing careful and wise judgment
entries.example_cn: 她以审慎的态度处理这个棘手的伦理问题。
entries.example_en: She brought a judicial mind to the difficult ethical question.

entries.definition_en: in a manner ordered or authorized by a court
entries.example_cn: 法院依法令没收了该财产。
entries.example_en: The property was seized judicially by the court.

entries.definition_en: in a manner characteristic of a judge or court
entries.example_cn: 该争端是通过司法途径而非谈判解决的。
entries.example_en: The dispute was resolved judicially rather than through negotiation.

entries.definition_en: the system of law courts that administer justice and constitute the judicial branch of government
entries.example_cn: 司法体系的改革提高了人们获得司法公正的机会。
entries.example_en: Reforms in the judiciary have improved access to justice.

entries.definition_en: persons who administer justice
entries.example_cn: 司法人员必须保持独立，不受政治压力影响。
entries.example_en: The judiciary must remain independent of political pressure.

entries.definition_en: showing good judgment and common sense in practical matters
entries.example_cn: 决定等风暴过去后再开会是一个明智之举。
entries.example_en: It was a judicious decision to postpone the meeting until the storm passed.

entries.definition_en: in a wise and sensible way
entries.example_cn: 委员会经过仔细考虑后明智地选定了候选人。
entries.example_en: The committee selected the candidate judiciously after careful consideration.

entries.definition_en: a Japanese martial art and sport based on grappling and throwing techniques
entries.example_cn: 她从小就开始练习柔道。
entries.example_en: She has been practicing judo since she was a child.

entries.definition_cn: 带柄、有壶嘴或壶口、用于盛装和倾倒液体的容器
entries.definition_en: a container with a handle and a mouth or spout, used for holding and pouring liquids
entries.example_cn: 她把牛奶从壶里倒进杯子里。
entries.example_en: She poured the milk from the jug into the glass.

entries.definition_en: the quantity of liquid contained in a jug
entries.example_cn: 桌上有一壶水。
entries.example_en: There is a jug of water on the table.

entries.definition_en: to lock up or confine someone in a jail
entries.example_cn: 这名罪犯被监禁了十年。
entries.example_en: The criminal was jugged for ten years.

entries.definition_en: to cook food by stewing it in an earthenware jug
entries.example_cn: 他们用陶罐炖了一整天的鸡肉和蔬菜。
entries.example_en: They jugged the chicken with vegetables all day.

entries.definition_en: to throw, catch, and keep several things in the air at once
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喜欢看小丑抛接三个球。
entries.example_en: The children loved watching the clown juggle three balls.

entries.definition_en: to deal with several tasks or problems at the same time
entries.example_cn: 作为一名经理，他必须同时处理多个项目和截止日期。
entries.example_en: As a manager, he has to juggle multiple projects and deadlines.

entries.definition_cn: 通过移动各个部分来操控或重新安排某物
entries.definition_en: to manipulate or rearrange something by moving its components around
entries.example_cn: 编辑重新调整了段落，以改善文章的行文。
entries.example_en: The editor juggled the paragraphs to improve the article's flow.

entries.definition_en: to deceive or manipulate by trickery
entries.example_cn: 他试图暗中操纵反对派支持他的提议。
entries.example_en: He tried to juggle the opposition into supporting his proposal.

entries.definition_en: the skill of throwing and catching several objects simultaneously
entries.example_cn: 街头艺人用他令人印象深刻的杂耍表演逗乐了观众。
entries.example_en: The street performer entertained the crowd with his impressive juggle.

entries.definition_en: the act of rearranging things to give a misleading impression
entries.example_cn: 该公司的财务报告纯属弄虚作假，旨在掩盖亏损。
entries.example_en: The company's financial report was nothing but a juggle of numbers to hide the losses.

entries.definition_en: to hold something with difficulty and balance insecurely
entries.example_cn: 他一边下楼梯一边勉强支撑着那个重箱子。
entries.example_en: He struggled to juggle the heavy box while walking down the stairs.

entries.definition_en: a person who performs tricks by throwing and catching objects in the air
entries.example_cn: 这位杂耍演员在空中抛接三个球。
entries.example_en: The juggler tossed and caught three balls in the air.

entries.definition_en: artful trickery designed to achieve an end
entries.example_cn: 这位政客在预算上的狡诈诡计让选民感到困惑。
entries.example_en: The politician's jugglery with the budget confused the voters.

entries.definition_en: the performance of a juggler
entries.example_cn: 孩子们饶有兴致地观看杂耍表演。
entries.example_en: The children watched the jugglery with great fascination.

entries.definition_en: the skill of throwing and catching several objects simultaneously
entries.example_cn: 街头艺人用他的杂耍技艺逗乐了观众。
entries.example_en: The street performer entertained the crowd with his juggling.

entries.definition_en: the act of rearranging things to give a misleading impression
entries.example_cn: 该公司的财务报告充满了弄虚作假的行为。
entries.example_en: The company's financial reports were full of juggling.

entries.definition_en: the veins in the neck that carry blood back from the head
entries.example_cn: 伤口险些伤及颈静脉。
entries.example_en: The wound narrowly missed the jugular.

entries.definition_en: a vital part that is vulnerable to attack
entries.example_cn: 公司缺乏安全措施是其致命弱点，让黑客得以窃取数据。
entries.example_en: The company's lack of security was its jugular, allowing hackers to steal data.

entries.definition_en: relating to or located in the neck or throat area
entries.example_cn: 外科医生在颈部区域做了一个精确的切口。
entries.example_en: The surgeon made a precise incision in the jugular region.

entries.definition_cn: 从植物或动物组织中通过挤压或烹饪提取的液体
entries.definition_en: liquid extracted from plants or animals by squeezing or cooking
entries.example_cn: 她把橙汁挤进杯子里。
entries.example_en: She squeezed orange juice into the glass.

entries.definition_en: energetic vitality or liveliness
entries.example_cn: 派对充满了活力和兴奋。
entries.example_en: The party was full of juice and excitement.

entries.definition_en: electric current or power
entries.example_cn: 这辆车由电池供电。
entries.example_en: The car runs on juice from the battery.

entries.definition_en: any of several liquids found in the body
entries.example_cn: 医生检测了病人的消化液。
entries.example_en: The doctor tested the patient's digestive juices.

entries.definition_cn: 榨汁机；用于榨取水果或蔬菜汁液的设备
entries.definition_en: a device used to extract juice from fruits or vegetables
entries.example_cn: 她买了一个新的榨汁器，每天早上榨新鲜橙汁。
entries.example_en: She bought a new juicer to make fresh orange juice every morning.

entries.definition_en: a person who drinks alcoholic beverages, especially in large amounts
entries.example_cn: 这位酗酒者以在当地酒吧大量饮酒而闻名。
entries.example_en: The juicer was known for his heavy drinking at the local bar.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being juicy
entries.example_cn: 西瓜汁水丰富，非常适合炎热的夏天。
entries.example_en: The juiciness of the watermelon made it perfect for a hot summer day.

entries.definition_en: containing a lot of juice
entries.example_cn: 这个西瓜非常多汁且甜美。
entries.example_en: The watermelon was very juicy and sweet.

entries.definition_en: exciting or interesting, often because it is sensational
entries.example_cn: 记者揭露了一桩令人震惊的丑闻。
entries.example_en: The reporter uncovered a juicy scandal.

entries.definition_cn: （俚语）性感丰满的；极具性吸引力的
entries.definition_en: slang: sexually attractive, especially voluptuous or curvy
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志把那位女演员形容为性感丰满。
entries.example_en: The magazine described the actress as juicy.

entries.definition_en: suggestive of sexual impropriety
entries.example_cn: 这条标题对家庭报纸来说有点过于露骨了。
entries.example_en: The headline was a bit too juicy for the family newspaper.

entries.definition_en: a martial art developed in China and Japan that uses an attacker's own weight and strength against them
entries.example_cn: 这名学生练习柔术以提高自卫技能。
entries.example_en: The student practiced jujitsu to improve his self-defense skills.

entries.definition_en: supernatural power or magic
entries.example_cn: 那位老人相信魔力的存在。
entries.example_en: The old man believed in the power of juju.

entries.definition_cn: （非正式）某种行为通常会带来的负面因果报应
entries.definition_en: (informal) the usually negative karmic consequences of an action or behavior
entries.example_cn: 他对朋友撒了谎，现在正自食恶果。
entries.example_en: He lied to his friends, and now he is dealing with some bad juju.

entries.definition_en: a West African fetish or charm believed to have magical or supernatural powers
entries.example_cn: 她戴着护身符项链以求保护。
entries.example_en: She wore a juju necklace for protection.

entries.definition_en: a dark red plumlike fruit of Old World buckthorn trees
entries.example_cn: 鼠李树的深红色浆果状果实被称为鼠李果。
entries.example_en: The dark red plumlike fruit of the buckthorn tree is known as a jujube.

entries.definition_en: a spiny tree that produces dark red edible fruits
entries.example_cn: 他们在花园里从多刺的枣树上摘下了新鲜的枣。
entries.example_en: They picked fresh jujubes from the spiny tree in the garden.

entries.definition_cn: 一种有嚼劲的水果味果冻糖；有时会加入药物以缓解喉咙痛
entries.definition_en: a chewy fruit-flavored jellied candy, sometimes medicated to soothe a sore throat
entries.example_cn: 她吃了一颗水果味的果冻糖来缓解喉咙痛。
entries.example_en: She ate a fruit-flavored jujube candy to soothe her sore throat.

entries.definition_en: a Japanese martial art of self-defense that uses an attacker's weight and strength against them
entries.example_cn: 他学习柔术，以掌握不使用武器的自卫方法。
entries.example_en: He studied jujutsu to learn how to defend himself without using weapons.

entries.definition_en: a deceptive move made by a football player to evade an opponent
entries.example_cn: 四分卫使用假动作骗过防守者并投出了达阵传球。
entries.example_en: The quarterback used a juke to slip past the defender and throw a touchdown pass.

entries.definition_cn: 美国南部路边的小酒吧或咖啡馆，常有舞会和自动点唱机
entries.definition_en: a small roadside cafe or bar in the southern United States, often with dancing and a jukebox
entries.example_cn: 他们在一家酒吧舞厅度过了晚上，随着自动点唱机的音乐跳舞并吃东西。
entries.example_en: They spent the evening at a juke, dancing to music from a jukebox and eating.

entries.definition_cn: 一种源自芝加哥、以快速抽象节奏著称的电子舞曲音乐类型
entries.definition_en: a genre of electronic dance music from Chicago, known for its fast, abstract rhythms
entries.example_cn: DJ深夜一直播放芝加哥的juke音乐。
entries.example_en: The DJ played Chicago juke music late into the night.

entries.definition_en: a cabinet containing an automatic record player
entries.example_cn: 角落里那台老式点唱机播放着经典摇滚歌曲。
entries.example_en: The old jukebox in the corner played classic rock songs.

entries.definition_cn: 用于播放数字音乐收藏中曲目的软件应用程序
entries.definition_en: a software application that plays tracks from a digital music collection
entries.example_cn: 我用一个点唱机应用来播放我的数字音乐收藏。
entries.example_en: I use a jukebox app to play my digital music collection.

entries.definition_en: bourbon and sugar and mint over crushed ice
entries.example_cn: 我们在炎热的一天点了薄荷朱利普来降温。
entries.example_en: We ordered a julep to cool down on the hot day.

entries.definition_en: to cut food into long thin strips
entries.example_cn: 她把黄瓜切成丝后再加入炒菜中。
entries.example_en: She julienned the cucumber before adding it to the stir-fry.

entries.definition_en: vegetables cut into thin strips
entries.example_cn: 这道沙拉里有新鲜的切丝胡萝卜和芹菜。
entries.example_en: The salad featured fresh julienne carrots and celery.

entries.definition_en: a clear soup garnished with julienne vegetables
entries.example_cn: 厨师端上了一碗精致的清汤配丝菜，旁边配着面包。
entries.example_en: The chef served a delicate julienne soup with a side of bread.

entries.definition_en: to arrange things in a random or disorderly way
entries.example_cn: 他在洗牌前把牌胡乱地排列了一下。
entries.example_en: He jumbled the cards before shuffling them.

entries.definition_en: to be mixed up in a confused way
entries.example_cn: 页面上的说明全部混杂在一起。
entries.example_en: The instructions were all jumbled together on the page.

entries.definition_en: to put things in a random order
entries.example_cn: 风把地上的树叶吹得乱七八糟。
entries.example_en: The wind jumbled the leaves on the ground.

entries.definition_en: a confused mixture of things
entries.example_cn: 房间里杂乱无章地堆满了衣服和书。
entries.example_en: The room was a jumble of clothes and books.

entries.definition_en: a small, thin, usually ring-shaped sugared cake
entries.example_cn: 她吃了一块巧克力小圆环饼干当零食。
entries.example_en: She ate a chocolate jumble for a snack.

usage.label: archaic
usage.pattern: Historical term for a small, thin, usually ring-shaped cake.

entries.definition_cn: 由不相关或不一致的观点拼凑而成的论点
entries.definition_en: an argument based on unrelated or inconsistent ideas
entries.example_cn: 他的解释只是事实和观点的拼凑。
entries.example_en: His explanation was just a jumble of facts and opinions.

entries.definition_en: in utter disorder
entries.example_cn: 房间里乱成一团，堆满了衣服和书。
entries.example_en: The room was a jumbled mess of clothes and books.

entries.definition_en: very large in size or mass
entries.example_cn: 尽管有暴风雨，巨型喷气式飞机还是安全着陆了。
entries.example_en: The jumbo jet landed safely despite the storm.

entries.definition_en: to move suddenly because of surprise or fear
entries.example_cn: 听到巨大的噪音，她惊跳了一下。
entries.example_en: She jumped when she heard the loud noise.

entries.definition_en: to increase suddenly and greatly
entries.example_cn: 公告发布后价格暴涨。
entries.example_en: Prices jumped after the announcement.

entries.definition_en: to move forward quickly and successfully
entries.example_cn: 该公司在市场上突飞猛进。
entries.example_en: The company jumped to the top of the market.

entries.definition_en: a sudden and large increase
entries.example_cn: 气温一夜之间激增。
entries.example_en: There was a jump in the temperature overnight.

entries.definition_en: a sudden change from one state to another
entries.example_cn: 故事从白天跳到晚上。
entries.example_en: There was a jump in the story from day to night.

entries.definition_en: an involuntary physical movement
entries.example_cn: 他的腿突然跳动了一下。
entries.example_en: His leg gave a sudden jump.

entries.definition_en: to attack suddenly
entries.example_cn: 那只狗突袭了陌生人。
entries.example_en: The dog jumped the stranger.

entries.definition_en: an abrupt transition from one film scene to another; a jump cut
entries.example_cn: 导演使用跳切来改变时间。
entries.example_en: The director used a jump cut to change the time.

entries.definition_en: to start a car engine whose battery is dead by connecting it to another car's battery
entries.example_cn: 我用搭电线给车搭电启动了。
entries.example_en: I used jumper cables to jump-start the vehicle.

entries.definition_cn: 使（某事物）充满活力地重新开始
entries.definition_en: to start or re-start something vigorously
entries.example_cn: 在新经理接手后，这个项目停滞不前，他使其重新充满活力地推进。
entries.example_en: The new manager jump-started the project after it had stalled.

entries.definition_en: starting a car engine with a weak battery by connecting it to another car's battery
entries.example_cn: 因为电池没电了，我们不得不给车搭电启动。
entries.example_en: We had to jump-start our car because the battery was dead.

entries.definition_cn: 自命不凡的；妄自尊大的（英国非正式）
entries.definition_en: (British informal) upstart
entries.example_cn: 那个自命不凡的新人试图掌控会议。
entries.example_en: The jumped-up newcomer tried to take charge of the meeting.

entries.definition_en: a crocheted or knitted garment covering the upper part of the body
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件羊毛针织上衣保暖。
entries.example_en: She wore a wool jumper to keep warm.

entries.definition_en: someone or something that jumps
entries.example_cn: 这位跳跃者轻松越过了横杆。
entries.example_en: The jumper cleared the high bar with ease.

entries.definition_en: a jump shot in basketball
entries.example_cn: 这位明星球员在半场投进了一个漂亮的跳投。
entries.example_en: The star player made a perfect jumper from half-court.

entries.definition_en: an athlete who competes at jumping
entries.example_cn: 这位跳远运动员赢得了金牌。
entries.example_en: The long jumper won the gold medal.

entries.definition_en: a coverall worn by children
entries.example_cn: 婴儿穿着一件蓝色的连体衣。
entries.example_en: The baby was dressed in a blue jumper.

entries.definition_en: a small connector used to make temporary electrical connections
entries.example_cn: 技术员使用一个临时电气连接器绕过了故障的电线。
entries.example_en: The technician used a jumper to bypass the faulty wire.

entries.definition_cn: 类似围裙的无袖连衣裙
entries.definition_en: a sleeveless dress resembling an apron; worn over other clothing
entries.example_cn: 她在连衣裙外穿了一件白色的无袖罩衫。
entries.example_en: She wore a white jumper over her dress.

entries.definition_cn: 工人穿的宽松夹克或罩衫
entries.definition_en: a loose jacket or blouse worn by workmen
entries.example_cn: 建筑工人穿上了他的皮夹克。
entries.example_en: The construction worker put on his leather jumper.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of nervous anxiety or restlessness
entries.example_cn: 她的紧张不安使她很难专注于演讲。
entries.example_en: Her jumpiness made it hard for her to focus on the presentation.

entries.definition_en: the act of propelling yourself off the ground
entries.example_cn: 孩子们正在练习跳跃。
entries.example_en: The children were practicing jumping.

entries.definition_en: the act of participating in an athletic competition in which you must jump
entries.example_cn: 这位运动员赢得了跳高比赛。
entries.example_en: The athlete won the jumping competition.

entries.definition_en: to start a car engine whose battery is dead by connecting it to another car's battery
entries.example_cn: 你能帮我给车搭电启动吗？我的电池好像完全没电了。
entries.example_en: Could you help me jumpstart my car? My battery seems to be completely dead.

entries.definition_cn: 使（某事物）重新启动或恢复活力
entries.definition_en: to start or re-start something vigorously
entries.example_cn: 新经理希望在本季度使公司的销售额重新启动并恢复增长。
entries.example_en: The new manager hopes to jumpstart the company's sales figures this quarter.

entries.definition_en: the act of starting an automobile engine with a weak battery by connecting it to another car's battery
entries.example_cn: 我们的车在高速公路上抛锚后，不得不叫拖车来搭电启动。
entries.example_en: We had to call a tow truck to jumpstart our car after it stalled on the highway.

entries.definition_en: a one-piece garment resembling a parachutist's uniform
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件时尚的连体衣去参加晚上的派对。
entries.example_en: She wore a stylish jumpsuit to the evening party.

entries.definition_en: feeling nervous or anxious and easily startled
entries.example_cn: 在巨大的噪音之后，那只狗变得非常紧张。
entries.example_en: After the loud noise, the dog became very jumpy.

entries.definition_en: characterized by sudden, irregular movements or shocks
entries.example_cn: 这辆旧车在过坑洼时颠簸得很厉害。
entries.example_en: The old car had a jumpy ride over the potholes.

entries.definition_cn: 灯草鹀属鸟；（尤指）北美雀类
entries.definition_en: a bird of the genus Junco, especially a North American sparrow
entries.example_cn: 一群灯草鹀聚集在喂食器附近的地面上。
entries.example_en: A flock of juncos gathered on the ground near the feeder.

entries.definition_en: a place where two or more things meet or connect
entries.example_cn: 交通灯位于两条主干道的交汇处。
entries.example_en: The traffic lights are at the junction of the two main roads.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being joined together
entries.example_cn: 两条河流的结合处形成了一个宽阔的河口。
entries.example_en: The junction of the two rivers created a wide estuary.

entries.definition_en: an object that joins or connects two things
entries.example_cn: 这个金属接头牢固地连接了两根管道。
entries.example_en: The metal junction connects the two pipes securely.

entries.definition_en: the shape or manner in which things are connected
entries.example_cn: 这个铁路枢纽的布局复杂，有许多轨道。
entries.example_en: The railway junction has a complex layout with many tracks.

entries.definition_en: the act of joining or adjoining things
entries.example_cn: 这两家公司的合并已于昨日宣布。
entries.example_en: The junction of the two companies was announced yesterday.

entries.definition_en: an important point or stage in a situation or process
entries.example_cn: 选举结果在竞选的关键时刻公布。
entries.example_en: The election results were announced at a critical juncture in the campaign.

entries.definition_cn: 必须作出关键决定的关头
entries.definition_en: a point at which a critical decision must be made
entries.example_cn: 我们正处于一个必须决定是否继续该项目的危急关头。
entries.example_en: We are at a juncture where we must decide whether to continue the project.

entries.definition_en: a place or point where things join
entries.example_cn: 这两块木头在一个精确的连接处接合在一起。
entries.example_en: The two pieces of wood were joined at a precise juncture.

entries.definition_cn: 赤道附近茂密且难以进入的森林
entries.definition_en: a dense, difficult-to-enter forest near the equator
entries.example_cn: 他们花了数周时间探索那片茂密的丛林。
entries.example_en: They spent weeks exploring the deep jungle.

entries.definition_en: a situation where people or groups compete fiercely for survival
entries.example_cn: 就业市场是一个弱肉强食的环境，只有最强者才能生存。
entries.example_en: The job market is a jungle where only the strongest survive.

entries.definition_en: a place where homeless people sleep and live
entries.example_cn: 市中心在冬天变成了流浪汉的聚居地。
entries.example_en: The city center has become a jungle for homeless people during the winter.

entries.definition_en: overgrown with tropical vegetation
entries.example_cn: 我们穿过热带植被茂密的森林，看到了许多奇花异草。
entries.example_en: We walked through the jungly forest and saw many exotic plants.

entries.definition_cn: 较年轻的；级别较低的；任职时间较短的
entries.definition_en: younger; lower in rank; shorter in length of tenure or service
entries.example_cn: 她是这家公司的初级合伙人。
entries.example_en: She is the junior partner in the firm.

entries.definition_cn: 指美国高中或大学的第三年或倒数第二年
entries.definition_en: used of the third or next to final year in United States high school or college
entries.example_cn: 高中三年级通常是压力最大的一年。
entries.example_en: Junior year is often the most stressful time in high school.

entries.definition_cn: 包括或专为年轻人设计的
entries.definition_en: including or intended for youthful persons
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志是供青少年阅读的。
entries.example_en: This magazine is for junior readers.

entries.definition_en: the younger of two persons
entries.example_cn: 两兄弟中较年轻的那个继承了生意。
entries.example_en: The junior of the two brothers inherited the business.

entries.definition_cn: （美国或菲律宾）高中或大学三年级学生
entries.definition_en: a third-year student at a high school or university, especially in the United States or the Philippines
entries.example_cn: 在美国，他是高中三年级学生。
entries.example_en: In the United States, he is a high-school junior.

entries.definition_cn: 对年轻男子（尤指无礼或令人讨厌者）的轻蔑称呼
entries.definition_en: a patronizing term of address for a young man, especially one being disrespectful or annoying
entries.example_cn: 教练带着轻蔑口吻对那个无礼的新手说：“注意你的语气，小子。”
entries.example_en: The coach told the disrespectful rookie, “Watch your tone, junior.”

entries.definition_cn: 一种带有浆果状球果的常绿灌木或小树
entries.definition_en: a coniferous shrub or small tree with berrylike cones
entries.example_cn: 鸟儿喜欢吃这种灌木的浆果。
entries.example_en: Birds love to eat the berries of the juniper.

entries.definition_cn: 一种带有浆果状球果的常绿灌木或小树的木材
entries.definition_en: the wood of a coniferous shrub or small tree with berrylike cones
entries.example_cn: 这种木材常被用来制作小盒子和器具。
entries.example_en: Juniper wood is often used for making small boxes and utensils.

entries.definition_cn: 叙利亚和阿拉伯半岛的一种开小白花的沙漠灌木；有时被认为是《旧约》中提到的杜松
entries.definition_en: a desert shrub native to Syria and Arabia with small white flowers; sometimes identified as the juniper mentioned in the Old Testament
entries.example_cn: 有些译本将《旧约》中提到的那种灌木认作杜松。
entries.example_en: Some translations identify the shrub mentioned in the Old Testament as juniper.

entries.definition_cn: 处理掉（无用或陈旧之物）
entries.definition_en: dispose of (something useless or old)
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把这些破椅子处理掉。
entries.example_en: We need to junk these broken chairs.

entries.definition_cn: 废旧物品；无价值的杂物
entries.definition_en: discarded or unwanted items; miscellaneous material of little value
entries.example_cn: 车库里堆满了废旧物品。
entries.example_en: The garage was full of junk.

entries.definition_cn: 一种带有高艉楼和横帆的中国帆船
entries.definition_en: any of various Chinese boats with a high poop and lugsails
entries.example_cn: 那艘中国帆船在平静的海面上平稳航行。
entries.example_en: The junk sailed smoothly across the calm sea.

entries.definition_cn: 以公务为名、通常用公款进行的享乐旅行
entries.definition_en: a pleasure trip ostensibly made for business, often involving entertainment at public expense
entries.example_cn: 该报告批评了该部门过高的公款出差费用。
entries.example_en: The report criticized the excessive junket expenses of the department.

entries.definition_en: a journey taken for pleasure
entries.example_cn: 他们的享乐之旅包括参观几个历史遗迹。
entries.example_en: Their junket included visits to several historic sites.

entries.definition_cn: 赌场中容量和限额每天变化、通常出租给带旅游团入场的私人经营者的博彩厅
entries.definition_en: a casino gaming room whose capacity and limits change daily and that is often rented to private vendors who bring in tour groups
entries.example_cn: 旅游团被带到了一间由私人经营者运营的博彩厅。
entries.example_en: The tour group was taken to a junket where a private vendor operated the gaming room.

entries.definition_cn: 用凝乳酶凝固的甜牛奶制成的甜点
entries.definition_en: a dessert made of sweetened milk coagulated with rennet
entries.example_cn: 她端上了一份配新鲜浆果的热甜点。
entries.example_en: She served a warm junket with fresh berries.

entries.definition_en: to go on a pleasure trip
entries.example_cn: 委员会决定去海边度周末享乐。
entries.example_en: The committee decided to junket to the coast for the weekend.

entries.definition_en: to provide a feast or banquet for
entries.example_cn: 市长在市厅为来访的贵宾举办了盛宴。
entries.example_en: The mayor junketed the visiting dignitaries at the city hall.

entries.definition_en: to partake in a feast or banquet
entries.example_cn: 他们享用了主人准备的丰盛宴席。
entries.example_en: They junketed on the lavish spread prepared by the host.

entries.definition_cn: （贬义、俚语）吸毒成瘾者，尤指吸食海洛因的人
entries.definition_en: A derogatory slang term for a person addicted to narcotics, especially heroin.
entries.example_cn: 这家诊所为吸食海洛因的瘾君子提供治疗。
entries.example_en: The clinic offers treatment for heroin junkies.

entries.definition_en: Someone who is so ardently devoted to something that it resembles an addiction.
entries.example_cn: 他是个彻头彻尾的游戏迷，整天都在玩游戏。
entries.example_en: He is a total junkie for video games, playing them all day long.

entries.definition_en: someone who is extremely devoted to something, as if it were an addiction
entries.example_cn: 他是个真正的老车迷，把所有钱都花在收藏老爷车上。
entries.example_en: He is a real junky for vintage cars and spends all his money on them.

entries.definition_en: a person who is addicted to illegal drugs
entries.example_cn: 警察在小巷里逮捕了那个吸毒者。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the junky in the alleyway.

entries.definition_cn: 收集或出售废弃物、尤其是废金属的场所；废品场
entries.definition_en: a place where discarded or unwanted items, especially scrap metal, are collected or sold
entries.example_cn: 他们从废品收购站买了那辆旧车。
entries.example_en: They bought the old car from a junkyard.

entries.definition_en: a group of military officers who take control of a country by force
entries.example_cn: 该国由军事政变集团统治了十年。
entries.example_en: The country was ruled by a military junta for ten years.

entries.definition_en: relating to law or legal rights and obligations
entries.example_cn: 律师们详细讨论了该合同的法律含义。
entries.example_en: The jural implications of the contract were discussed in detail by the lawyers.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the law or jurisprudence
entries.example_cn: 新条约的法律影响仍在争论中。
entries.example_en: The juridical implications of the new treaty are still being debated.

entries.definition_cn: 关于司法管理或法官职能的
entries.definition_en: relating to the administration of justice or the function of a judge
entries.example_cn: 法院就该案作出了司法裁决。
entries.example_en: The court issued a juridical ruling on the case.

entries.definition_cn: 解释和适用法律的法律权力或权限
entries.definition_en: the legal power or authority to interpret and apply the law
entries.example_cn: 该法院对此案拥有司法权。
entries.example_en: The court has jurisdiction over this case.

entries.definition_en: the area where a law or authority applies
entries.example_cn: 此事不在我们的管辖范围内。
entries.example_en: This matter falls outside our jurisdiction.

entries.definition_en: relating to or within a jurisdiction
entries.example_cn: 这场争端通过两个州之间的管辖权协议得到了解决。
entries.example_en: The dispute was resolved through jurisdictional agreements between the two states.

entries.definition_en: the branch of philosophy concerned with the law and the principles that lead courts to make the decisions they do
entries.example_cn: 教授讲授了一门现代法理学课程。
entries.example_en: The professor taught a course on modern jurisprudence.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: theoretical study of law; source w17785r0

entries.definition_cn: 有关某一主题的判例法
entries.definition_en: the body of case law concerning a particular subject
entries.example_cn: 法院依据既有判例法作出了裁决。
entries.example_en: The court relied on established jurisprudence in reaching its decision.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study or theory of law
entries.example_cn: 这场法理辩论聚焦于法律权利的本质。
entries.example_en: The jurisprudential debate focused on the nature of legal rights.

entries.definition_en: a legal expert or scholar, especially one who studies jurisprudence
entries.example_cn: 这位法学家撰写了一篇详细的宪法分析。
entries.example_en: The jurist wrote a detailed analysis of constitutional law.

entries.definition_cn: 法官（尤指加拿大或美国的用法）
entries.definition_en: a judge, especially in Canadian or US usage
entries.example_cn: 这位法官作出了最终裁决。
entries.example_en: The jurist delivered the final verdict.

entries.definition_en: relating to law or to legal rights and obligations
entries.example_cn: 律师们讨论了该合同的法律含义。
entries.example_en: The juristic implications of the contract were debated by the lawyers.

entries.definition_en: a person who is selected to serve on a jury in a court of law
entries.example_cn: 每位陪审员都必须公正并遵循法官的指示。
entries.example_en: Every juror must be impartial and follow the judge's instructions.

entries.definition_en: a group of people chosen to decide the outcome of a legal case based on evidence
entries.example_cn: 陪审团花了两个小时才做出裁决。
entries.example_en: The jury took two hours to reach a verdict.

entries.definition_en: a group of people appointed to judge the quality of entries in a competition
entries.example_cn: 评审团从一百多份作品中选出了获胜者。
entries.example_en: The jury selected the winner from over a hundred entries.

entries.definition_en: made or done using whatever materials are available, often in a temporary way
entries.example_cn: 我们用一座临时拼凑的桥梁渡过了河流。
entries.example_en: We used a jury-rigged bridge to cross the river.

entries.definition_en: a male who serves (or waits to be called to serve) on a jury
entries.example_cn: 审判开始前，这位陪审员宣誓就职。
entries.example_en: The juryman was sworn in before the trial began.

entries.definition_en: and nothing more
entries.example_cn: 我只有一个问题。
entries.example_en: I have just one question.

entries.definition_en: only a moment ago
entries.example_cn: 我刚才看见他了。
entries.example_en: I saw him just now.

entries.definition_en: indicating exactness or preciseness
entries.example_cn: 这个钟的时间很准确。
entries.example_en: The clock is just right.

entries.definition_en: Used for emphasis; really or very.
entries.example_cn: 我真的很喜欢这首歌。
entries.example_en: I just love this song.

entries.definition_en: fair to all parties as dictated by reason and conscience
entries.example_cn: 法官做出了公平的判决。
entries.example_en: The judge made a just decision.

entries.definition_en: legally or ethically right or proper
entries.example_cn: 给每个人公平的机会是公正的。
entries.example_en: It is just to give everyone a fair chance.

entries.definition_en: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
entries.example_cn: 这项比赛公正无私，向所有人开放。
entries.example_en: The competition was just and open to all.

entries.definition_en: of moral excellence
entries.example_cn: 她是一个正直的人。
entries.example_en: She is a just person.

entries.definition_en: a high judicial officer in former times
entries.example_cn: 国王任命了一名司法官来监督该省的法律体系。
entries.example_en: The king appointed a justiciar to oversee the legal system in the province.

usage.label: historical
usage.pattern: Refers to a medieval judicial office.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指英格兰或苏格兰中世纪的）高级司法官员
entries.definition_en: a high-ranking judicial officer, especially in medieval England or Scotland
entries.example_cn: 这位司法长官在该地区的法律体系中拥有最高权力。
entries.example_en: The justiciary held supreme authority over the legal system in the region.

entries.definition_en: the jurisdiction or authority of a justiciar
entries.example_cn: 此案属于该司法长官的专属管辖范围。
entries.example_en: The case fell under the justiciary's exclusive jurisdiction.

entries.definition_en: capable of being justified; able to be shown as right or reasonable
entries.example_cn: 考虑到当时的情况，警察的行为是合理的。
entries.example_en: The police officer's actions were justifiable given the circumstances.

entries.definition_en: with good reason
entries.example_cn: 她有充分理由对他的无礼行为感到愤怒。
entries.example_en: She was justifiably angry at his rude behavior.

entries.definition_en: a fact or situation that makes an action seem reasonable or necessary
entries.example_cn: 医生提供了手术的医学理由。
entries.example_en: The doctor provided a medical justification for the surgery.

entries.definition_en: a statement explaining an action or belief
entries.example_cn: 他为自己的迟到提供了辩解。
entries.example_en: He offered a justification for his late arrival.

entries.definition_en: the act of defending or explaining something by reasoning
entries.example_cn: 律师为客户行为所做的辩护很有说服力。
entries.example_en: The lawyer's justification of the client's actions was convincing.

entries.definition_en: serving to justify or defend something in speech or writing
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家发表了一篇辩解性的演讲来为丑闻开脱。
entries.example_en: The politician made a justificatory speech to explain away the scandal.

entries.definition_cn: 为某事提供正当理由的；说明理由的
entries.definition_en: providing a reason or justification for something
entries.example_cn: 该报告提供了对公司近期亏损的合理解释。
entries.example_en: The report offered a justificatory analysis of the company's recent losses.

entries.definition_cn: 被证明是合理、正确或可以接受的
entries.definition_en: shown to be reasonable, right, or acceptable
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定使用武力是正当的。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the use of force was justified.

entries.definition_en: having words spaced so that lines have straight edges
entries.example_cn: 这段文字采用两端对齐，两侧边缘都很整齐。
entries.example_en: The paragraph is fully justified, with straight margins on both sides.

entries.definition_en: a person who argues to defend or justify some policy or institution
entries.example_cn: 这项新税收政策的辩护者声称它将有利于经济。
entries.example_en: The justifier of the new tax policy claimed it would benefit the economy.

entries.definition_cn: 通过调整间距使文本两端对齐的机器、程序或算法。
entries.definition_en: A machine, program, or algorithm that justifies text by adjusting spacing so both margins are aligned.
entries.example_cn: 文本对齐程序使每一行的两端都整齐对齐。
entries.example_en: The text justifier aligned every line evenly along both margins.

entries.definition_en: to show that something is right or reasonable by giving reasons or proof.
entries.example_cn: 证据将证明他离开公司的决定是正当的。
entries.example_en: The evidence will justify his decision to leave the company.

entries.definition_cn: 调整一行文字中单词之间的间距
entries.definition_en: to adjust the spaces between words in a line of text so that the edges are straight.
entries.example_cn: 排版工人必须调整文字间距，使栏目看起来整齐。
entries.example_en: The typesetter had to justify the text to make the columns look neat.

entries.definition_cn: （用于上帝）宣告……无罪，免除……的罪罚
entries.definition_en: (used of God) to declare someone innocent and free from the punishment for sin.
entries.example_cn: 在基督教神学中，上帝通过信仰使罪人得称为义。
entries.example_en: In Christian theology, God justifies the sinner through faith.

entries.definition_en: in a fair or morally right way; rightfully
entries.example_cn: 法官公正地裁决了这个复杂的案件。
entries.example_en: The judge ruled justly on the complex case.

entries.definition_en: with good reason; properly
entries.example_cn: 这项政策因损害居民利益而受到有充分理由的批评。
entries.example_en: The policy was justly criticized for harming residents.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being just or fair
entries.example_cn: 许多人质疑该判决的公正性。
entries.example_en: The justness of the verdict was questioned by many.

entries.definition_en: conformity with an aesthetic standard of correctness
entries.example_cn: 建筑设计的恰当性一目了然。
entries.example_en: The justness of the architectural design was immediately apparent.

entries.definition_en: extend out or project in space
entries.example_cn: 灯塔伸入海中。
entries.example_en: The lighthouse juts out into the sea.

entries.definition_en: something that bulges out or is protuberant or projects from its surroundings
entries.example_cn: 一大块突出的岩石从悬崖面伸出。
entries.example_en: A large jut of rock projected from the cliff face.

entries.definition_en: the act of projecting out from something
entries.example_cn: 建筑物的突出部分在下面的街道上投下了阴影。
entries.example_en: The jut of the building created a shadow on the street below.

entries.definition_en: extending out above or beyond a surface or boundary
entries.example_cn: 突出的岩石在沙滩上投下长长的阴影。
entries.example_en: The jutting rocks cast long shadows on the beach.

entries.definition_en: the action of sticking out from something
entries.example_cn: 悬崖的突出部分使小路变得危险。
entries.example_en: The jutting of the cliff made the path dangerous.

entries.definition_en: relating to or suitable for children or young people.
entries.example_cn: 图书馆有一个专门收藏青少年文学作品的区域。
entries.example_en: The library has a special section for juvenile literature.

entries.definition_en: showing a lack of maturity.
entries.example_cn: 他那种不成熟的态度让人难以与他合作。
entries.example_en: His juvenile attitude made it difficult to work with him.

entries.definition_en: a young person, especially one below the legal age of adulthood
entries.example_cn: 警方正在寻找一名未成年嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police are searching for a juvenile suspect.

entries.definition_en: to place two or more things side by side for comparison or effect
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家选择将明亮的色彩与深色的阴影并列放置。
entries.example_en: The artist chose to juxtapose the bright colors with the dark shadows.

entries.definition_en: placed side by side, often for comparison
entries.example_cn: 并列的明亮色彩和深色阴影形成了鲜明对比。
entries.example_en: The juxtaposed bright colors and dark shadows created a dramatic contrast.

entries.definition_en: the act of positioning things close together or side by side
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家巧妙地运用了明暗色彩的并置。
entries.example_en: The artist used a striking juxtaposition of light and dark colors.

entries.definition_en: a side-by-side position
entries.example_cn: 这本书探讨了传统价值观与现代价值观的并列。
entries.example_en: The book explores the juxtaposition of traditional and modern values.

entries.definition_cn: 英语字母表的第11个字母
entries.definition_en: the eleventh letter of the English alphabet
entries.example_cn: 这个单词以字母K开头。
entries.example_en: The word starts with the letter K.

entries.definition_en: a soft silver-white metal that reacts violently with water
entries.example_cn: 钾（符号为K）是一种高反应性的金属。
entries.example_en: Potassium, known as K, is a highly reactive metal.

entries.definition_en: the basic unit of thermodynamic temperature in the International System of Units
entries.example_cn: 温度是以开尔文测量的。
entries.example_en: The temperature was measured in K.

entries.definition_en: the number one thousand, especially in informal notation
entries.example_cn: 这座体育场可容纳1000名观众。
entries.example_en: The stadium can hold 1K spectators.

entries.definition_en: a unit of information equal to 1000 bytes
entries.example_cn: 文件大小为5千字节。
entries.example_en: The file size is 5 K.

entries.definition_cn: （互联网聊天或短信中）好的；行
entries.definition_en: (in informal Internet or messaging use) okay; all right
entries.example_cn: “好的，爸爸，我去自己的房间。”
entries.example_en: “K, Dad, I’ll go to my room.”

entries.definition_en: a unit of information equal to 1024 bytes
entries.example_cn: 内存容量为8千字节。
entries.example_en: The memory capacity is 8 K.

entries.definition_cn: 表示已收到并理解上一条消息的单字符信息
entries.definition_en: a single-character message meaning that a previous message was received and understood
entries.example_cn: 我发去详细信息后，收到一个“K”作为回复。
entries.example_en: I sent the details and received a “K” in reply.

entries.definition_en: street names for the drug ketamine
entries.example_cn: 警方严厉打击使用氯胺酮的行为。
entries.example_en: Police cracked down on the use of K.

entries.definition_en: a unit of digital information equal to 1024 bytes
entries.example_cn: 在计算机科学中，1 KB 通常被定义为 1024 字节。
entries.example_en: In computer science, one KB is often defined as 1024 bytes.

entries.definition_en: a unit of digital information equal to 1000 bytes
entries.example_cn: 文件大小约为 5 KB。
entries.example_en: The file size is approximately 5 KB.

entries.definition_en: an object orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt beyond Neptune
