entries.example_cn: 布满斑点的天空充满了乌云。
entries.example_en: The maculated sky was filled with dark clouds.

entries.definition_en: to make dirty or spotty, especially by exposure to air; also used metaphorically
entries.example_cn: 阳光使白色的船帆染上了黄色的污渍。
entries.example_en: The sun maculated the white sails with a yellow stain.

entries.definition_en: to spot, stain, or pollute
entries.example_cn: 雨水弄脏了原本洁白的墙壁。
entries.example_en: The rain maculated the pristine white walls.

entries.definition_en: a Brazilian religious cult of African origin combining voodoo elements with singing, chanting, and dancing
entries.example_cn: 参观者在庙宇中目睹了一场传统的马昆巴仪式。
entries.example_en: Visitors to the temple witnessed a traditional macumba ceremony.

entries.definition_en: popular dance music from Brazil derived from the macumba religious cult
entries.example_cn: 乐队演奏了充满活力的马昆巴节奏，填满了舞池。
entries.example_en: The band played lively macumba rhythms that filled the dance floor.

entries.definition_en: a follower of a Brazilian religious cult of African origin
entries.example_cn: 马昆巴信徒们聚集在一起，通过歌唱和舞蹈庆祝节日。
entries.example_en: The macumba gathered to celebrate the festival with singing and dancing.

entries.definition_en: very angry
entries.example_cn: 别对他生气，他不是故意伤害你的。
entries.example_en: Don't get mad at him; he didn't mean to hurt you.

entries.definition_en: suffering from mental illness
entries.example_cn: 医生说他没有疯，只是压力很大。
entries.example_en: The doctor said he was not mad, just very stressed.

entries.definition_en: extremely excited or emotional
entries.example_cn: 乐队一演奏，人群就狂热起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd went mad when the band started playing.

entries.definition_en: very foolish
entries.example_cn: 下雨天开这么快太愚蠢了。
entries.example_en: It was mad to drive so fast in the rain.

entries.definition_en: a polite form of address for a woman
entries.example_cn: 接待员称那位顾客为女士。
entries.example_en: The receptionist addressed the customer as madam.

entries.definition_en: a woman who manages a brothel
entries.example_cn: 这位妓院老板严密监视着屋内的活动。
entries.example_en: The madam kept a strict eye on the activities in the house.

entries.definition_en: a French title or form of address for a woman
entries.example_cn: 服务员称那位顾客为“女士”。
entries.example_en: The waiter addressed the customer as madame.

entries.definition_en: characterized by undue haste and lack of thought or deliberation
entries.example_cn: 那个鲁莽的在一日内建好房屋的计划注定会失败。
entries.example_en: The madcap plan to build a house in a day was doomed to fail.

entries.definition_en: a reckless impetuous irresponsible person
entries.example_cn: 那个鲁莽的人决定不带降落伞就从悬崖跳下。
entries.example_en: The madcap decided to jump off the cliff without a parachute.

entries.definition_en: cause to go crazy; cause to lose one's mind
entries.example_cn: 持续的噪音开始让他发疯。
entries.example_en: The constant noise began to madden him.

entries.definition_en: drive up the wall; go on someone's nerves
entries.example_cn: 他的坏习惯真的激怒了他的妻子。
entries.example_en: His bad habits really madden his wife.

entries.definition_en: make mad
entries.example_cn: 令人困惑的指示让新员工发狂。
entries.example_en: The confusing instructions madden the new employee.

entries.definition_en: filled with extreme anger
entries.example_cn: 群众因受到不公平待遇而暴怒。
entries.example_en: The crowd was maddened by the unfair treatment.

entries.definition_en: extremely annoying or displeasing
entries.example_cn: 持续的噪音令人恼怒。
entries.example_en: The constant noise was maddening.

entries.definition_en: a Eurasian plant with yellow flowers and red roots used historically for dyeing
entries.example_cn: 历史上，茜草曾是纺织品红色染料的重要来源。
entries.example_en: Historically, madder was a crucial source of red dye for textiles.

entries.definition_en: to dye with madder
entries.example_cn: 古老的染色工艺用茜草把羊毛染成深红色。
entries.example_en: The ancient dyeing process used madder to color the wool a deep crimson.

entries.definition_en: produced by a manufacturing process
entries.example_cn: 这是工厂制造的产品。
entries.example_en: This is a factory-made product.

entries.definition_en: successful or certain to succeed
entries.example_cn: 他现在已经功成名就了。
entries.example_en: He is a made man now.

entries.definition_en: (of a bed) having the sheets and blankets set in order
entries.example_cn: 酒店房间为客人准备了铺好的床。
entries.example_en: The hotel room had a made bed ready for guests.

entries.definition_en: of clothing that is custom-made
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙是量身定做的，完美贴合她的身材。
entries.example_en: The dress was made-to-order to fit her perfectly.

entries.definition_en: made specifically for a particular individual
entries.example_cn: 我们为婚礼定制了一套西装。
entries.example_en: We ordered a made-to-order suit for the wedding.

entries.definition_en: built up to a higher level, especially with deposited material
entries.example_cn: 这条路建在填高的地基上。
entries.example_en: The road was built on made-up ground.

entries.definition_en: a small silvery drumfish often mistaken for white perch
entries.example_cn: 银鼓鱼沿着海岸游动。
entries.example_en: The mademoiselle swims along the coast.

entries.definition_en: a chaotic, noisy, and uproarious place
entries.example_cn: 所有客人同时到达后，这所房子变得一片混乱喧闹。
entries.example_en: The house became a madhouse when all the guests arrived at once.

entries.definition_en: a pejorative term for an insane asylum
entries.example_cn: 在19世纪，当地的疯人院以其恶劣的条件而闻名。
entries.example_en: In the 19th century, the local madhouse was known for its harsh conditions.

entries.definition_en: used to emphasize that something is done to an extreme degree
entries.example_cn: 她极其喜爱那部新电影。
entries.example_en: She madly loved the new movie.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not controlled or reasonable
entries.example_cn: 当球队得分时，人群疯狂地欢呼。
entries.example_en: The crowd cheered madly when the team scored.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows insanity or extreme foolishness
entries.example_cn: 他发疯似的挥舞手臂，并朝空荡荡的街道大喊。
entries.example_en: He madly waved his arms and shouted at the empty street.

entries.definition_en: a man who is insane
entries.example_cn: 人群在街上追赶那个疯子。
entries.example_en: The crowd chased the madman through the streets.

entries.definition_en: a state of mental illness or insanity; extreme irrationality
entries.example_cn: 这部小说描写了他逐渐陷入疯狂的过程。
entries.example_en: The novel portrays his descent into madness.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being rash and foolish
entries.example_cn: 没有降落伞就从悬崖跳下简直是鲁莽至极。
entries.example_en: It was pure madness to jump off the cliff without a parachute.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of intense anger
entries.example_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他暴怒不已。
entries.example_en: He was overcome by madness when he heard the news.

entries.definition_en: a fatal viral disease of warm-blooded animals transmitted by bite
entries.example_cn: 这只狗被一只疑似患狂犬病的野生动物咬伤后，被送往兽医处。
entries.example_en: The dog was taken to the vet after being bitten by a wild animal suspected of madness.

entries.definition_en: legal insanity (obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定被告因精神错乱而无罪。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the defendant was not guilty by reason of madness.

entries.definition_en: a light cotton cloth with a colorful pattern
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一条色彩鲜艳的花布连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She wore a dress made of bright madras.

entries.definition_cn: （孟加拉国和巴基斯坦的）伊斯兰学校
entries.definition_en: a Muslim school in Bangladesh and Pakistan
entries.example_cn: 学生们去伊斯兰学校学习宗教经典。
entries.example_en: Students attend the madrasa to learn religious texts.

entries.definition_en: a school for teaching Islamic theology or other subjects, especially in Muslim countries
entries.example_cn: 许多学生去伊斯兰学校学习宗教文本。
entries.example_en: Many students attend a madrasah to learn religious texts.

entries.definition_en: an unaccompanied partsong for two or three voices that follows a strict poetic form
entries.example_cn: 合唱团表演了一首需要精确声乐和声的文艺复兴时期牧歌。
entries.example_en: The choir performed a Renaissance madrigal that required precise vocal harmony.

entries.definition_en: to sing madrigals
entries.example_cn: 在音乐会期间，该合奏团演唱了帕莱斯特里纳的著名牧歌作品。
entries.example_en: During the concert, the ensemble madrigaled the famous works of Palestrina.

entries.definition_cn: 北美太平洋沿岸的一种常绿树，叶片有光泽且革质，结橙红色可食浆果；木材用于制作家具，树皮用于制革
entries.definition_en: an evergreen tree of the Pacific coast of North America with glossy leathery leaves and orange-red edible berries; its wood is used for furniture and bark for tanning
entries.example_cn: 太平洋杨梅树为徒步者提供了阴凉和可食用的浆果。
entries.example_en: The madrona tree provided shade and edible berries for the hikers.

entries.definition_en: a woman who is mentally ill or insane
entries.example_cn: 这部小说讲述了一位被关在精神病院里的疯女人的悲剧故事。
entries.example_en: The novel tells the tragic story of a madwoman confined in an asylum.

entries.definition_en: a chaotic or turbulent situation
entries.example_cn: 这个国家陷入了政治动荡之中。
entries.example_en: The country was caught in a political maelstrom.

entries.definition_en: a powerful circular current of water, usually caused by conflicting tides
entries.example_cn: 那艘船在近海处被卷入一个猛烈的漩涡中。
entries.example_en: The boat was caught in a violent maelstrom near the coast.

entries.definition_en: an unnaturally frenzied or distraught woman
entries.example_cn: 古代文献描述狂女为被狂野、无法控制之愤怒所占据的女人。
entries.example_en: The ancient texts describe the maenad as a woman possessed by wild, uncontrollable rage.

entries.definition_cn: （希腊神话）参加狄俄尼索斯狂欢仪式的女人
entries.definition_en: (Greek mythology) a woman participant in the orgiastic rites of Dionysus
entries.example_cn: 在希腊神话中，狂女跟随狄俄尼索斯进行狂喜的舞蹈。
entries.example_en: In Greek mythology, the maenad followed Dionysus in ecstatic dances.

entries.definition_en: an artist who has perfect skill and control
entries.example_cn: 这支管弦乐队由一位著名的意大利大师指挥。
entries.example_en: The orchestra was led by a famous Italian maestro.

entries.definition_en: a member of the Mafia crime syndicate in the United States
entries.example_cn: 这本书详述了一名纽约权势黑手党成员的兴衰史。
entries.example_en: The book details the rise and fall of a powerful mafioso in New York.

entries.definition_en: a member of the Sicilian Mafia
entries.example_cn: 这部电影描绘了20世纪20年代西西里一名臭名昭著的黑手党成员的生活。
entries.example_en: The film portrays the life of a notorious mafioso in 1920s Sicily.

entries.definition_en: a magazine
entries.example_cn: 我在报摊上买了一本新杂志。
entries.example_en: I bought a new mag at the newsstand.

entries.definition_en: a periodic publication with pictures and stories
entries.example_cn: 我每周读一本时尚杂志。
entries.example_en: I read a fashion magazine every week.

entries.definition_en: the physical object of a paperback publication
entries.example_cn: 报亭出售这本杂志的最新一期。
entries.example_en: The newsstand sells the latest issue of the magazine.

entries.definition_en: a frame holding cartridges for a gun
entries.example_cn: 他把一个新的弹匣装进了步枪里。
entries.example_en: He inserted a new magazine into the rifle.

entries.definition_en: a chamber holding film for exposure
entries.example_cn: 摄影师检查了胶卷盒，以确保里面装好了胶卷。
entries.example_en: The photographer checked the magazine to ensure it was loaded.

entries.definition_en: a storehouse for weapons on a warship
entries.example_cn: 船员们在战斗前锁好了弹药库。
entries.example_en: The crew secured the magazine before the battle.

entries.definition_en: a firm that publishes magazines
entries.example_cn: 这家杂志社扩大了其发行网络。
entries.example_en: The magazine company expanded its distribution network.

entries.definition_en: a woman who has reformed after being a prostitute
entries.example_cn: 这部小说探讨了一位试图重新融入社会的悔改妓女的艰难生活。
entries.example_en: The novel explores the difficult life of a magdalen trying to reintegrate into society.

entries.definition_en: of a deep purplish red color
entries.example_cn: 洋红色的日落将天空染成了鲜艳的色调。
entries.example_en: The magenta sunset painted the sky in vibrant hues.

entries.definition_cn: 深紫红色；减色法三原色之一
entries.definition_en: a dark purplish-red color; a primary subtractive color
entries.example_cn: 设计师选择洋红色作为标志的主色调。
entries.example_en: The designer chose magenta as the primary color for the logo.

entries.definition_cn: 家蝇或丽蝇的幼虫，常发现于腐烂的有机物中
entries.definition_en: the larva of the housefly and blowfly commonly found in decaying organic matter
entries.example_cn: 蛆虫从腐烂的水果里爬了出来。
entries.example_en: The maggot crawled out of the rotting fruit.

entries.definition_en: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.example_cn: 那块旧奶酪已经生蛆了，不得不扔掉。
entries.example_en: The old cheese had become maggoty and had to be thrown away.

entries.definition_en: the art of using supernatural powers
entries.example_cn: 巫师施展魔法让花朵绽放。
entries.example_en: The wizard performed magic to make the flowers bloom.

entries.definition_en: an illusion that seems real to those who do not understand it
entries.example_cn: 魔术师表演了一个让兔子消失的魔术。
entries.example_en: The magician performed a magic trick that made the rabbit disappear.

entries.definition_en: having supernatural powers
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一枚能让她隐身的魔戒。
entries.example_en: She wore a magic ring that made her invisible.

entries.definition_en: having powers that are not natural or scientific
entries.example_cn: 这个故事充满了有魔力的生物。
entries.example_en: The story was full of magical creatures.

entries.definition_en: in a magical manner
entries.example_cn: 魔术师神奇地让兔子消失了。
entries.example_en: The magician made the rabbit disappear magically.

entries.definition_en: someone who performs magic tricks to amuse an audience
entries.example_cn: 魔术师让兔子从帽子里消失了。
entries.example_en: The magician made the rabbit disappear from the hat.

entries.definition_en: one who practices magic or sorcery
entries.example_cn: 在故事中，那位老巫师能控制天气。
entries.example_en: In the story, the old magician could control the weather.

entries.definition_cn: 配得上显赫人物的；庄严而威严的
entries.definition_en: befitting an eminent person; dignified and imposing
entries.example_cn: 她为皇家典礼穿了一件庄严的长袍。
entries.example_en: She wore a magisterial gown for the royal ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 令人反感地自负的；专横的
entries.definition_en: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power
entries.example_cn: 经理对新员工那种傲慢的态度很不专业。
entries.example_en: The manager's magisterial attitude towards the new employees was unprofessional.

entries.definition_cn: 与治安法官或其职位有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to a magistrate or the office of a magistrate
entries.example_cn: 治安法院就这起争议作出了裁决。
entries.example_en: The magisterial court issued a ruling on the dispute.

entries.definition_en: in an authoritative and impressive manner
entries.example_cn: 教授权威地解释了这一理论。
entries.example_en: The professor explained the theory magisterially.

entries.definition_en: in a domineering and authoritarian way
entries.example_cn: 他专横地对那群人说话，无视他们的问题。
entries.example_en: He spoke magisterially to the group, ignoring their questions.

entries.definition_en: the office or position of a magistrate
entries.example_cn: 他怀着极大的荣誉感接受了法官职位。
entries.example_en: He accepted the magistracy with great honor.

entries.definition_cn: 某一地区的治安法官集体
entries.definition_en: the collective body of magistrates in a particular area
entries.example_cn: 当地治安法官集体就拟议中的改革发表了声明。
entries.example_en: The local magistracy issued a statement about the proposed reforms.

entries.definition_en: a lay judge or civil authority who administers the law, especially one who conducts a court dealing with minor offenses
entries.example_cn: 治安法官审理了此案，并对这起轻微交通违规开出了罚单。
entries.example_en: The magistrate heard the case and issued a fine for the minor traffic violation.

entries.definition_en: the official position or office of a magistrate
entries.example_cn: 他辞去了法官职位，转而追求学术生涯。
entries.example_en: He resigned from the magistrature to pursue a career in academia.

entries.definition_en: a high-speed train that floats on a magnetic cushion above the track to avoid friction
entries.example_cn: 磁悬浮列车的时速超过了300公里。
entries.example_en: The maglev train reached speeds of over 300 kilometers per hour.

entries.definition_en: molten rock beneath or within the earth’s surface, before it reaches the surface as lava
entries.example_cn: 科学家研究岩浆以了解火山爆发。
entries.example_en: Scientists study magma to understand volcanic eruptions.

entries.definition_en: generosity and nobility of spirit, especially in forgiving or dealing generously with others
entries.example_cn: 她原谅了对手的侮辱，展现了她的慷慨大度。
entries.example_en: Her magnanimity was shown when she forgave her rival's insult.

entries.definition_en: noble and generous in spirit
entries.example_cn: 这位宽宏大量的领导人在选举后原谅了他的政治对手。
entries.example_en: The magnanimous leader forgave his political opponents after the election.

entries.definition_cn: 慷慨、善解人意且宽容的
entries.definition_en: generous and understanding and tolerant
entries.example_cn: 她慷慨得足以把笔记分享给那个 struggling 的学生。
entries.example_en: She was magnanimous enough to share her notes with the struggling student.

entries.definition_en: in a generous and forgiving way
entries.example_cn: 她宽宏大量地原谅了对手的失误。
entries.example_en: She magnanimously forgave her rival's mistake.

entries.definition_en: a very wealthy or powerful businessperson
entries.example_cn: 这位石油大亨向慈善机构捐赠了数百万美元。
entries.example_en: The oil magnate donated millions to the charity.

entries.definition_cn: 氧化镁（一种白色固体矿物，天然存在时称方镁石）
entries.definition_en: magnesium oxide, a white solid mineral occurring naturally as periclase
entries.example_cn: 氧化镁常用于耐火砖的生产中。
entries.example_en: Magnesia is often used in the production of refractory bricks.

entries.definition_en: a white mineral made of magnesium carbonate, used as a source of magnesium
entries.example_cn: 地质学家从山上采集了一块菱镁矿样本。
entries.example_en: The geologist collected a sample of magnesite from the mountain.

entries.definition_en: a light silver-white metallic element
entries.example_cn: 镁被用于许多合金和信号弹中。
entries.example_en: Magnesium is used in many alloys and flares.

entries.definition_cn: 能产生磁场并吸引铁或其他某些金属的物体或材料；磁铁
entries.definition_en: an object or material that produces a magnetic field and attracts iron or certain other metals
entries.example_cn: 老师用磁铁把桌上的铁屑吸了起来。
entries.example_en: The teacher used a magnet to pick up the iron filings from the table.

entries.definition_en: a characteristic that provides pleasure and attracts
entries.example_cn: 这座城市友好的居民对游客有着极大的吸引力。
entries.example_en: The city's friendly people are a real magnet for tourists.

entries.definition_en: relating to or caused by magnetism
entries.example_cn: 磁场影响了指南针的指针。
entries.example_en: The magnetic field affects the compass needle.

entries.definition_en: having the properties of a magnet; attracting iron or steel
entries.example_cn: 这种磁性材料会粘在冰箱门上。
entries.example_en: The magnetic material sticks to the refrigerator door.

entries.definition_en: capable of being magnetized
entries.example_cn: 软铁是一种容易被磁化的磁性物质。
entries.example_en: Soft iron is a magnetic substance that can be easily magnetized.

entries.definition_en: possessing an extraordinary ability to attract
entries.example_cn: 她极具吸引力的人格魅力让人们被她吸引。
entries.example_en: She has a magnetic personality that draws people to her.

entries.definition_en: determined by earth's magnetic fields
entries.example_cn: 鸟类在迁徙过程中利用地球磁场。
entries.example_en: Birds use Earth's magnetic field during migration.

entries.definition_en: using magnetism to operate or function
entries.example_cn: 当你靠近时，门通过磁力自动打开。
entries.example_en: The door opens magnetically when you approach it.

entries.definition_en: in a way that suggests magnetism or attraction
entries.example_cn: 她被那座古老的图书馆深深地吸引住了。
entries.example_en: She was magnetically drawn to the old library.

entries.definition_en: the branch of science that studies magnetism
entries.example_cn: 这位教授专攻磁学，并发表了多篇关于磁场的论文。
entries.example_en: The professor specializes in magnetics and has published several papers on magnetic fields.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which a material is magnetized
entries.example_cn: 随着电流的增加，铁芯的磁化程度也随之增加。
entries.example_en: The magnetisation of the core increased as the current rose.

entries.definition_en: the process of making a substance magnetic
entries.example_cn: 通过用磁铁摩擦，使针发生了磁化。
entries.example_en: The magnetisation of the needle was achieved by stroking it with a magnet.

entries.definition_en: the physical property of being magnetic
entries.example_cn: 该材料的磁性使其能够吸引铁。
entries.example_en: The magnetisation of the material allows it to attract iron.

entries.definition_en: having the properties of a magnet; able to attract iron or steel
entries.example_cn: 针头在与磁铁摩擦后变得磁化了。
entries.example_en: The needle became magnetised after being rubbed against the magnet.

entries.definition_en: the physical force that attracts iron and other materials, or the force produced by electric currents.
entries.example_cn: 地球的磁性保护我们免受有害的太阳辐射。
entries.example_en: The magnetism of the earth protects us from harmful solar radiation.

entries.definition_en: the scientific study of magnetic forces and materials.
entries.example_cn: 她正在大学学习磁学。
entries.example_en: She is studying magnetism at the university.

entries.definition_en: a naturally occurring iron oxide that is strongly attracted to magnets
entries.example_cn: 矿工们在山区发现了大量的磁铁矿矿藏。
entries.example_en: Miners discovered large deposits of magnetite in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which a material is magnetized
entries.example_cn: 随着电流流过线圈，铁芯的磁化程度增加了。
entries.example_en: The magnetization of the core increased as the current flowed through the coil.

entries.definition_en: the process of making a substance magnetic
entries.example_cn: 该机器施加强磁场以实现钢的快速磁化。
entries.example_en: The machine applies a strong field to achieve rapid magnetization of the steel.

entries.definition_en: the state of being magnetized
entries.example_cn: 移除外部磁场后，该样品仍保持磁化状态。
entries.example_en: The sample retained its magnetization after the external field was removed.

entries.definition_en: to make something magnetic
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把针磁化，这样它才能指向北方。
entries.example_en: We need to magnetize the needle so it can point north.

entries.definition_en: to attract someone strongly, as if with a magnet
entries.example_cn: 美丽的景色强烈吸引着游客，把他们引到了山顶。
entries.example_en: The beautiful view magnetized the tourists, drawing them to the hilltop.

entries.definition_en: to become magnetic
entries.example_cn: 这根铁棒放入磁场后被磁化了。
entries.example_en: The iron bar magnetized after being placed in the magnetic field.

entries.definition_en: having the properties of a magnet; able to attract iron or steel
entries.example_cn: 指南针上的磁化针指向北方。
entries.example_en: The magnetized needle on the compass pointed north.

entries.definition_en: a small generator that creates high voltage to produce a spark for a gasoline engine
entries.example_cn: 这辆旧车使用磁电机来点燃燃料。
entries.example_en: The old car uses a magneto to ignite the fuel.

entries.definition_en: the study of the interaction between magnetic fields and electrically conducting fluids
entries.example_cn: 磁流体力学被用于研究恒星中等离子体的行为。
entries.example_en: Magnetohydrodynamics is used to study the behavior of plasma in stars.

entries.definition_en: an instrument used to measure the strength of magnetic fields
entries.example_cn: 科学家使用磁力计探测海底的磁场异常。
entries.example_en: Scientists used a magnetometer to detect magnetic anomalies on the ocean floor.

entries.definition_en: a unit used to measure the magnetic moment of a particle
entries.example_cn: 物理学家使用磁子来描述电子的磁性属性。
entries.example_en: Physicists use the magneton to describe the magnetic properties of electrons.

entries.definition_cn: 磁层；行星周围受其磁场控制、使带电粒子被俘获或偏转的区域
entries.definition_en: the region around a planet in which charged particles are trapped or deflected by its magnetic field
entries.example_cn: 地球的磁层保护我们免受有害的太阳辐射。
entries.example_en: Earth's magnetosphere protects us from harmful solar radiation.

entries.definition_en: a vacuum tube that uses magnetic and electric fields to control electron flow, used mainly in microwave oscillators
entries.example_cn: 微波炉内部的磁控管产生加热食物的微波。
entries.example_en: The magnetron inside the microwave oven generates the waves that heat the food.

entries.definition_en: the process of making something appear larger
entries.example_cn: 望远镜提供了五十倍的放大效果，使我们能看到遥远的恒星。
entries.example_en: The telescope provided a magnification of fifty times, allowing us to see distant stars.

entries.definition_en: the ratio between the size of an image and the size of the object
entries.example_cn: 显微镜的放大倍数是通过将图像尺寸除以物体尺寸来计算的。
entries.example_en: The microscope's magnification is calculated by dividing the image size by the object size.

entries.definition_en: the act of exaggerating the importance of something
entries.example_cn: 政治家的演讲中充满了对自己成就的夸大。
entries.example_en: The politician's speech was full of magnification of his own achievements.

entries.definition_en: a photographic print that has been enlarged
entries.example_cn: 侦探仔细研究了犯罪现场照片的放大版以寻找线索。
entries.example_en: The detective studied the magnification of the crime scene photo for clues.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being magnificent or splendid
entries.example_cn: 日落的壮丽景象被拍摄在了照片中。
entries.example_en: The magnificence of the sunset was captured in the photograph.

entries.definition_en: being very large, impressive, or beautiful
entries.example_cn: 大教堂的宏伟景象让所有游客惊叹不已。
entries.example_en: The magnificence of the cathedral amazed all the visitors.

entries.definition_en: very impressive and beautiful
entries.example_cn: 这座壮丽的宫殿是用黄金和大理石建造的。
entries.example_en: The magnificent palace was built with gold and marble.

entries.definition_en: wonderfully
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛中表现精彩。
entries.example_en: The team performed magnificently in the final match.

entries.definition_en: in an impressively beautiful manner
entries.example_cn: 这座城堡壮丽地建在山坡上。
entries.example_en: The castle was built magnificently on the hillside.

entries.definition_en: made to appear larger, especially through a lens or magnification
entries.example_cn: 放大的图像揭示了肉眼无法看到的细节。
entries.example_en: The magnified image revealed details invisible to the naked eye.

entries.definition_en: a scientific instrument that magnifies an image
entries.example_cn: 科学家使用放大镜来检查幻灯片上的微小细节。
entries.example_en: The scientist used a magnifier to examine the tiny details on the slide.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指用镜头或光学仪器）使图像或物体看起来更大
entries.definition_en: to make an image or object appear larger, especially by using a lens or optical instrument
entries.example_cn: 显微镜可以将微小的细菌放大，使我们能清楚地看到它们。
entries.example_en: The microscope can magnify tiny bacteria so we can see them clearly.

entries.definition_en: to make something seem more important or serious than it really is
entries.example_cn: 媒体经常将小冲突夸大成重大的国际危机。
entries.example_en: The media often magnifies minor conflicts into major international crises.

entries.definition_en: to make something physically larger
entries.example_cn: 设计师在印刷前放大了标志。
entries.example_en: The designer magnified the logo before printing it.

entries.definition_en: the property of relative size or extent
entries.example_cn: 这次地震的震级为6.5级。
entries.example_en: The earthquake had a magnitude of 6.5.

entries.definition_en: relative importance
entries.example_cn: 这个问题的重要性不容忽视。
entries.example_en: The magnitude of the problem cannot be ignored.

entries.definition_en: a number assigned to the ratio of two quantities
entries.example_cn: 这两个数量相差一个数量级。
entries.example_en: The two quantities differ by one order of magnitude.

entries.definition_cn: 木兰属的灌木或乔木（以芳香花朵著称）
entries.definition_en: a shrub or tree of the genus Magnolia known for fragrant blooms
entries.example_cn: 公园里的木兰树开满了芳香美丽的花朵。
entries.example_en: The magnolia tree in the park is covered in exquisite fragrant blooms.

entries.definition_cn: 木兰树皮（用于民间医学）
entries.definition_en: dried bark of magnolia trees used in folk medicine
entries.example_cn: 草药师推荐干木兰树皮，认为它具有药用价值。
entries.example_en: The herbalist recommended dried magnolia bark for its medicinal properties.

entries.definition_cn: 容量为1.5升的大号葡萄酒瓶
entries.definition_en: a large wine bottle holding 1.5 litres, twice the volume of a standard wine bottle
entries.example_cn: 他们为庆祝活动订购了一瓶香槟。
entries.example_en: They ordered a magnum of champagne for the celebration.

entries.definition_en: a long-tailed black-and-white bird that makes a loud chattering sound
entries.example_cn: 一只喜鹊落在篱笆柱上，大声鸣叫。
entries.example_en: A magpie landed on the fence post and chattered loudly.

entries.definition_cn: 喜欢囤积或偷拿东西的人
entries.definition_en: a person who hoards or steals things
entries.example_cn: 大家都知道他喜欢囤积东西，有时还会拿走不属于他的物品，因此称他为“喜鹊”。
entries.example_en: Everyone knew him as a magpie because he hoarded trinkets and sometimes took things that were not his.

entries.definition_en: a foolish and talkative person
entries.example_cn: 别这么饶舌又愚蠢，听我说！
entries.example_en: Stop being such a magpie and listen to what I am saying!

entries.definition_en: a Mexican plant used to make pulque and mescal
entries.example_cn: 这种传统饮料是用龙舌兰制成的。
entries.example_en: The traditional drink is made from the maguey plant.

entries.definition_en: a Philippine plant yielding hard fibre for twine
entries.example_cn: 粗麻绳是用马尼拉麻的纤维制成的。
entries.example_en: Coarse twine is made from the fibre of the maguey.

entries.definition_en: a magician or sorcerer from ancient times
entries.example_cn: 这部古籍描述了巫师进行的仪式。
entries.example_en: The ancient text describes the rituals performed by the magus.

entries.definition_cn: 古代波斯琐罗亚斯德教祭司
entries.definition_en: a member of the ancient Persian Zoroastrian priesthood
entries.example_cn: 这位祭司担任国王在宗教事务上的顾问。
entries.example_en: The magus served as an advisor to the king on religious matters.

entries.definition_en: a great raja; a Hindu prince or king in India ranking above a raja
entries.example_cn: 这位大君统治着一片拥有巨大财富和权力的广阔领土。
entries.example_en: The maharaja ruled over a vast territory with great wealth and power.

entries.definition_en: a Hindu prince or king in India who ranks higher than a raja
entries.example_cn: 这位王侯为来访的贵宾举办了一场盛大的宴会。
entries.example_en: The maharajah hosted a grand banquet for the visiting dignitaries.

entries.definition_cn: 大君夫人；（约相当于）王后
entries.definition_en: the wife of a maharaja; approximately, a queen consort
entries.example_cn: 玛哈拉尼身着传统服饰出席了皇家仪式。
entries.example_en: The maharani attended the royal ceremony in traditional attire.

entries.definition_cn: 被认为具有渊博知识并热爱人类的印度或西藏人士
entries.definition_en: a person in India or Tibet believed to have great knowledge and love of humanity
entries.example_cn: 村民们因他的智慧而尊敬这位圣人。
entries.example_en: The mahatma was revered by the villagers for his wisdom.

entries.definition_cn: 马哈马希鱼（一种在夏威夷周围温暖海域广泛分布的大型细长食用和游钓鱼）
entries.definition_en: a large, slender fish that is both a food source and a game fish, widely found in warm seas around Hawaii
entries.example_cn: 游客在访问夏威夷群岛时经常钓到马哈马希鱼。
entries.example_en: Tourists often catch mahimahi while visiting the Hawaiian islands.

entries.definition_cn: 马哈马希鱼（一种热带咸水鱼）的瘦肉
entries.definition_en: the lean meat of a saltwater fish found in warm waters, especially in Hawaii
entries.example_cn: 厨师为晚餐准备了一道美味的马哈马希鱼排。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a delicious mahimahi steak for the dinner.

entries.definition_en: a Chinese game played by four people using 144 tiles
entries.example_cn: 他们下午在社区中心打麻将。
entries.example_en: They spent the afternoon playing mahjong at the community center.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用麻将牌进行的单人游戏，通过移除相同且未被遮挡的牌对来进行
entries.definition_en: a solitaire game played with mahjong tiles by removing matching exposed pairs
entries.example_cn: 她在火车上用平板电脑玩麻将接龙。
entries.example_en: She played mahjong solitaire on her tablet during the train ride.

entries.definition_en: hard wood from mahogany trees, often used for making furniture
entries.example_cn: 那张古董书桌由富丽的桃花心木制成，上面有精美的雕刻。
entries.example_en: The antique desk was made of rich mahogany and had intricate carvings.

entries.definition_en: a tropical tree known for its hard, reddish-brown wood
entries.example_cn: 桃花心木树在加勒比潮湿的森林中缓慢生长。
entries.example_en: Mahogany trees grow slowly in the humid forests of the Caribbean.

entries.definition_en: a brown color with a reddish tint
entries.example_cn: 她的头发在阳光下呈现出自然的红褐色，非常漂亮。
entries.example_en: Her hair has a natural mahogany shade that looks beautiful in the sunlight.

entries.definition_en: a person who drives and takes care of an elephant
entries.example_cn: 象夫引导大象穿过狭窄的林间小道。
entries.example_en: The mahout guided the elephant through the narrow forest path.

entries.definition_en: a female domestic worker
entries.example_cn: 女佣每天早上打扫房间。
entries.example_en: The maid cleaned the rooms every morning.

entries.definition_cn: 未婚少女；年轻女子（旧时或诗歌用语）
entries.definition_en: an unmarried girl or young woman, especially in older or poetic use
entries.example_cn: 在那个古老的故事里，这位年轻姑娘在等待她的王子。
entries.example_en: In the old story, the young maid was waiting for her prince.

entries.definition_cn: 少女；未婚年轻女子（尤用于文学或旧式语境）
entries.definition_en: a girl or young unmarried woman, especially in literary or old-fashioned use
entries.example_cn: 少女静静地坐在窗边。
entries.example_en: The maiden sat quietly by the window.

entries.definition_en: in cricket, an over in which the batting team scores no runs
entries.example_cn: 投球手在无得分的一轮中击出了一球。
entries.example_en: The bowler took a wicket on the maiden over.

entries.definition_en: serving to start or set something in motion for the first time
entries.example_cn: 新船的首航非常成功。
entries.example_en: The maiden voyage of the new ship was a great success.

entries.definition_en: a type of fern with delicate, palmately branched leaves
entries.example_cn: 那株娇嫩的铁线蕨生长在花园潮湿的角落里。
entries.example_en: The delicate maidenhair ferns grew in the damp corner of the garden.

entries.definition_en: the hymen, a membrane that may partially cover the vaginal opening
entries.example_cn: 医疗专业人员建议，处女膜的存在与否并不能决定一个人是否为处女。
entries.example_en: Medical professionals advise that the presence or absence of a maidenhead does not determine virginity.

entries.definition_cn: 少女时期；未婚女子身份
entries.definition_en: the state or period of being a maiden or young unmarried woman
entries.example_cn: 她在少女时期游历了欧洲。
entries.example_en: She spent her maidenhood traveling across Europe.

entries.definition_en: befitting or characteristic of a maiden
entries.example_cn: 她为仪式穿了一件朴素、少女般的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She wore a simple, maidenly dress for the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: a female domestic worker employed in a household
entries.example_cn: 女佣在客人到来前仔细地摆放了银器。
entries.example_en: The maidservant carefully arranged the silverware before the guests arrived.

entries.definition_cn: 一种欧洲大型海鱼；石首鱼
entries.definition_en: a large European marine fish, the meagre
entries.example_cn: 厨师用从北海捕获的新鲜石首鱼做了一道美味的汤。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a delicious soup using fresh maigre caught from the North Sea.

entries.definition_en: letters and packages that are sent by the postal service
entries.example_cn: 我今天收到了邮件。
entries.example_en: I received a package in the mail today.

entries.definition_en: the system for sending messages through the post office
entries.example_cn: 这个国家的邮政系统非常高效。
entries.example_en: The mail system is very efficient in this country.

entries.definition_en: a specific collection of letters or packages delivered at one time
entries.example_cn: 邮件被送到了前门。
entries.example_en: The mail was delivered to the front door.

entries.definition_en: a vehicle that transports letters and packages for the postal service
entries.example_cn: 邮车今天早上很早就到了。
entries.example_en: The mail van arrived early this morning.

entries.definition_en: to send something via the postal service
entries.example_cn: 请把这封信寄到我的地址。
entries.example_en: Please mail this letter to my address.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to be directed or transmitted to another place
entries.example_cn: 服务器会将报告发送给所有团队成员。
entries.example_en: The server will mail the report to all team members.

entries.definition_en: flexible armor made of interlinked metal rings (historical)
entries.example_cn: 骑士们穿着锁子甲在战斗中保护自己。
entries.example_en: Knights wore mail to protect themselves in battle.

entries.definition_cn: （某些鱼类）每侧脸颊有骨板的
entries.definition_en: having a bony plate across each cheek, as in certain fishes
entries.example_cn: 这种脸颊有骨板的鱼每侧脸颊都有一块骨板。
entries.example_en: The mail-cheeked fish had a bony plate across each cheek.

entries.definition_en: to buy or sell goods with the intention of having them delivered by mail
entries.example_cn: 他们决定邮购家具，而不是去当地的商店购买。
entries.example_en: They decided to mail-order the furniture instead of visiting a local store.

entries.definition_en: a pouch used for carrying mail during shipment
entries.example_cn: 邮递员从卡车上提起沉重的邮袋。
entries.example_en: The postal worker lifted the heavy mailbag from the truck.

entries.definition_cn: 出版物（如杂志或网站）收到的来信或留言（广义，喻）
entries.definition_en: the letters or messages received by a publication, such as a magazine or website (broadly, figuratively)
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志收到的来信中有几封批评这项新政策。
entries.example_en: The magazine's mailbag included several letters criticizing the new policy.

entries.definition_en: a shoulder bag carried by a letter carrier
entries.example_cn: 他开始早间路线前调整了一下邮差肩袋。
entries.example_en: He adjusted his mailbag before starting his morning route.

entries.definition_en: a boat designed for transporting mail
entries.example_cn: 这艘历史悠久的邮船在夏季仍在河上运营。
entries.example_en: The historic mailboat still operates on the river during the summer season.

entries.definition_en: a private box for receiving mail
entries.example_cn: 请把信放进信箱里。
entries.example_en: Please put the letter in the mailbox.

entries.definition_en: a public box for depositing mail
entries.example_cn: 我把包裹投进了街角的邮筒。
entries.example_en: I dropped the package in the mailbox on the corner.

entries.definition_en: wearing or protected by mail, armor made of interlinked metal rings
entries.example_cn: 骑士在战斗开始前已全身披甲。
entries.example_en: The knight was fully mailed before the battle began.

entries.definition_en: an advertisement that is sent by mail
entries.example_cn: 我在信箱里收到了一封关于新车的邮寄广告。
entries.example_en: I received a mailer for a new car in my mailbox.

entries.definition_en: a container for something to be mailed
entries.example_cn: 请使用提供的邮寄容器发送文件。
entries.example_en: Please use the provided mailer to send the documents.

entries.definition_en: a person who mails something
entries.example_cn: 寄信人把包裹放在了邮局。
entries.example_en: The mailer dropped the package at the post office.

entries.definition_en: a batch of letters or packages sent by mail at the same time
entries.example_cn: 公司向所有客户发送了一封邮件。
entries.example_en: The company sent a mailing to all its customers.

entries.definition_en: the act of sending a letter
entries.example_cn: 邀请函的寄送因暴风雨而延误。
entries.example_en: The mailing of the invitation was delayed due to the storm.

entries.definition_en: a one-piece bathing suit worn by women
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件鲜红色的连体泳衣去海滩。
entries.example_en: She wore a bright red maillot to the beach.

entries.definition_cn: 舞者或体操运动员穿的弹力针织紧身衣或紧身裤
entries.definition_en: a leotard or tights made of stretchable jersey fabric, worn especially by dancers or gymnasts
entries.example_cn: 体操运动员在表演前调整了她的白色紧身裤。
entries.example_en: The gymnast adjusted her white maillot before the routine.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to deliver mail
entries.example_cn: 邮递员今天早上很早就到了。
entries.example_en: The mailman arrived early this morning.

entries.definition_en: to injure someone seriously so that they are permanently disabled or disfigured
entries.example_cn: 爆炸导致人群中数人受伤致残。
entries.example_en: The explosion maimed several people in the crowd.

entries.definition_en: having a part of the body crippled or disabled due to injury
entries.example_cn: 他在爆炸中致残，再也无法行走了。
entries.example_en: He was maimed in the explosion and could no longer walk.

entries.definition_en: people who have been maimed
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构为伤残者提供支持。
entries.example_en: The charity provides support for the maimed.

entries.definition_en: most important
entries.example_cn: 延误的主要原因是交通堵塞。
entries.example_en: The main reason for the delay was traffic.

entries.definition_en: of the greatest possible intensity
entries.example_cn: 风暴达到了最强级别。
entries.example_en: The storm reached main force.

entries.definition_en: able to stand alone as a complete sentence
entries.example_cn: 主句包含主语和谓语。
entries.example_en: The main clause contains the subject and verb.

entries.definition_en: a very large body of (salt) water
entries.example_cn: 船驶入大海。
entries.example_en: The ship sailed into the main.

entries.definition_en: a large pipe that carries water, gas, or electricity
entries.example_cn: 总水管破裂了。
entries.example_en: The water main was broken.

entries.definition_en: the topmast next above the mainmast
entries.example_cn: 水手爬上主桅杆上方的顶桅去修理索具。
entries.example_en: The sailor climbed the main-topmast to repair the rigging.

entries.definition_en: a large digital computer that serves many users and occupies a special room
entries.example_cn: 公司依赖一台大型计算机来处理所有的财务数据。
entries.example_en: The company relies on a mainframe to process all its financial data.

entries.definition_cn: 容纳并连接各功能模块的计算机机箱
entries.definition_en: a computer chassis that houses and interconnects modules performing various tasks
entries.example_cn: 计算机机箱容纳并连接各个处理模块。
entries.example_en: The computer chassis houses and interconnects the processing modules.

entries.definition_cn: 国家或大陆的主要陆地部分（区别于岛屿或半岛）
entries.definition_en: the main land mass of a country or continent, as distinguished from an island or peninsula
entries.example_cn: 他们从大陆飞往了那个岛屿。
entries.example_en: They flew from the mainland to the island.

entries.definition_en: the principal island of a group of islands
entries.example_cn: 大多数游客会先在主岛上停留，然后再探索较小的岛屿。
entries.example_en: Most visitors stay on the mainland before exploring the smaller islands.

entries.definition_en: inject into the vein
entries.example_cn: 急救员给病人静脉注射了生理盐水。
entries.example_en: The paramedic mainlined the patient with saline.

usage.label: slang
usage.pattern: inject a drug directly into a vein

entries.definition_cn: 如饥似渴地大量消费某物
entries.definition_en: to consume something eagerly and in large amounts
entries.example_cn: 她整个周末都如饥似渴地追看那部新犯罪剧。
entries.example_en: She spent the weekend mainlining the new crime series.

entries.definition_cn: 将代码合并到软件项目的主代码库，而不是保留在单独的分支中
entries.definition_en: to integrate code into a software project's main repository rather than keeping it in a separate fork
entries.example_cn: 改动经过测试后，开发人员将代码合并到了主代码库。
entries.example_en: Once the changes were tested, the developers mainlined the code.

entries.definition_en: for the most part
entries.example_cn: 这个班级主要由初学者组成。
entries.example_en: The class is mainly composed of beginners.

entries.definition_cn: 多桅帆船最高的桅杆；非帆船的第二桅
entries.definition_en: the tallest mast of a sailing ship, or the second-foremost mast of a nonsailing vessel, when there is more than one mast
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴来临前修理主桅。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to repair the mainmast before the storm.

entries.definition_en: the largest sail on the mainmast of a ship
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴来临前降下主帆。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to lower the mainsail before the storm.

entries.definition_en: a rope or chain used on a boat to control the angle of a sail
entries.example_cn: 水手调整主帆索以更有效地捕捉风力。
entries.example_en: The sailor adjusted the mainsheet to catch the wind more effectively.

entries.definition_en: the main spring in a clock or watch that stores energy to drive the mechanism
entries.example_cn: 钟表匠更换了损坏的发条以修复这台古董钟。
entries.example_en: The watchmaker replaced the broken mainspring to fix the antique clock.

entries.definition_cn: 某事最重要的原因或关键因素
entries.definition_en: the most important reason for, or element of, something
entries.example_cn: 她的善良是她成功的关键因素。
entries.example_en: Her kindness was the mainspring of her success.

entries.definition_en: something that provides essential support or stability
entries.example_cn: 储蓄是他们退休计划的支柱。
entries.example_en: Savings are the mainstay of their retirement plan.

entries.definition_cn: 提供持续可靠支持的人
entries.definition_en: a person who provides dependable, regular support
entries.example_cn: 二十年来，她一直是该慈善机构可靠的支持者。
entries.example_en: She has been the mainstay of the charity for twenty years.

entries.definition_en: a stay running from high on the mainmast to the base of the foremast
entries.example_cn: 水手调整主桅横桁以固定桅杆。
entries.example_en: The sailor adjusted the mainstay to secure the mast.

entries.definition_cn: 被大多数人或群体广泛使用或接受的；主流的
entries.definition_en: broadly used or accepted by most people or groups
entries.example_cn: 这部纪录片在一家主流电视频道播出。
entries.example_en: The documentary was shown on a mainstream television channel.

entries.definition_en: the prevailing or broadly accepted current of thought, culture, practice, or social opinion
entries.example_cn: 他的观点被认为偏离了主流政治思想。
entries.example_en: His ideas were considered outside the mainstream of political thought.

entries.definition_cn: 使某事物被广泛接受或流行；使主流化
entries.definition_en: to make something widely accepted or popular
entries.example_cn: 这项活动帮助电动汽车在普通驾驶者中普及开来。
entries.example_en: The campaign helped mainstream electric vehicles among ordinary drivers.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to continue in a certain state, position, or activity
entries.example_cn: 在高速公路上行驶时，你必须保持稳定的速度。
entries.example_en: You must maintain a steady speed while driving on the highway.

entries.definition_cn: 使处于良好状态以供使用和服务
entries.definition_en: to keep something in good condition for use and service
entries.example_cn: 定期清洁有助于保持地毯的质量。
entries.example_en: Regular cleaning helps maintain the quality of the carpet.

entries.definition_en: to keep something safe and protect it from harm, decay, loss, or destruction
entries.example_cn: 我们需要维护这座老建筑以防止其倒塌。
entries.example_en: We need to maintain the old building to prevent it from collapsing.

entries.definition_en: to state or assert something firmly
entries.example_cn: 律师坚称他的客户是无辜的。
entries.example_en: The lawyer maintains that his client is innocent.

entries.definition_en: to state something categorically or assert it as true
entries.example_cn: 他断言该项目将在下个月完成。
entries.example_en: He maintains that the project will be completed by next month.

entries.definition_en: to keep records by writing them regularly
entries.example_cn: 会计师为公司维护详细的财务记录。
entries.example_en: The accountant maintains detailed financial records for the company.

entries.definition_en: to supply someone with necessities and support
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构致力于维持受害者家属的生活。
entries.example_en: The charity works to maintain the families of the victims.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有并行使权利、特权或地位
entries.definition_en: to have and exercise a right, privilege, or status
entries.example_cn: 尽管她住在国外，她仍保留其公民身份。
entries.example_en: She maintains her citizenship even though she lives abroad.

entries.definition_en: able to be kept in good condition or continued over time
entries.example_cn: 在目前的预算下，这座旧桥无法维持。
entries.example_en: The old bridge is not maintainable with the current budget.

entries.definition_en: kept in good condition
entries.example_cn: 这所房子保养得很好，看起来很漂亮。
entries.example_en: The house was well maintained and looked beautiful.

entries.definition_en: continued in your keeping or use or memory
entries.example_cn: 她多年来一直保留着旅行日记。
entries.example_en: She maintained a diary of her travels for many years.

entries.definition_en: a person who keeps something in good condition or continues to support it
entries.example_cn: 该软件需要专门的维护者定期修复错误。
entries.example_en: The software requires a dedicated maintainer to fix bugs regularly.

entries.definition_en: the work needed to keep something in good condition
entries.example_cn: 定期维护汽车对安全至关重要。
entries.example_en: Regular maintenance of the car is essential for safety.

entries.definition_en: financial support for a family or group
entries.example_cn: 公司为员工的子女提供抚养费。
entries.example_en: The company provides maintenance for the employees' children.

entries.definition_en: money paid by one spouse to another after separation
entries.example_cn: 法院命令他向他的前妻支付赡养费。
entries.example_en: The court ordered him to pay maintenance to his ex-wife.

entries.definition_en: means of supporting oneself or making a living
entries.example_cn: 务农是他们在这个村庄唯一的谋生手段。
entries.example_en: Farming was their only means of making a living in the village.

entries.definition_en: unauthorized interference in a legal case
entries.example_cn: 律师指控对方非法干预诉讼以拖延审判。
entries.example_en: The lawyer accused the opponent of maintenance to delay the trial.

entries.definition_en: highly decorated earthenware covered with a glaze containing tin oxide
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件精美的十六世纪锡釉陶盘。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a beautiful maiolica plate from the 16th century.

entries.definition_cn: 带独立外门的复式公寓
entries.definition_en: a self-contained apartment, usually on two floors, within a larger building with its own external entrance
entries.example_cn: 他们决定租下市中心的一套复式公寓。
entries.example_en: They decided to rent a maisonette in the city center.

entries.definition_en: a small house
entries.example_cn: 这家人搬进了乡下的一所迷人小房子。
entries.example_en: The family moved into a charming maisonette in the countryside.

entries.definition_en: a tall cereal grass with large ears of kernels, widely cultivated in the Americas
entries.example_cn: 玉米是墨西哥和中美洲的主要谷物。
entries.example_en: Maize is the principal cereal in Mexico and Central America.

entries.definition_en: a strong yellow color resembling the color of maize
entries.example_cn: 墙壁被漆成了鲜艳的玉米黄色。
entries.example_en: The walls were painted a bright maize color.

entries.definition_en: showing great dignity and nobility
entries.example_cn: 国王以庄严的姿态走进大厅。
entries.example_en: The king entered the hall in a majestic manner.

entries.definition_en: impressive in appearance or behavior; grand or noble
entries.example_cn: 宏伟的山脉主宰了这片风景。
entries.example_en: The majestic mountains dominated the landscape.

entries.definition_cn: 属于或适合君主或最高统治者的；帝王般的
entries.definition_en: belonging to or befitting a monarch or supreme ruler
entries.example_cn: 这座宫殿以适合皇帝身份的宏伟风格建造。
entries.example_en: The palace was built in a majestic style befitting the emperor.

entries.definition_en: in a majestic manner
entries.example_cn: 雄鹰在群山上空壮丽地翱翔。
entries.example_en: The eagle soared majestically above the mountains.

entries.definition_en: impressiveness in scale or proportion
entries.example_cn: 大教堂的宏伟体现在其高耸的尖塔上。
entries.example_en: The majesty of the cathedral was evident in its towering spires.

entries.definition_cn: 施不透明白色锡釉并饰有彩色金属氧化物釉彩的陶器
entries.definition_en: earthenware coated with an opaque white tin glaze and decorated with coloured metal-oxide enamels
entries.example_cn: 收藏家展示了一套色彩斑斓的马约利卡陶盘。
entries.example_en: The collector displayed a set of colorful majolica plates.

entries.definition_en: of greater importance, rank, or stature
entries.example_cn: 该国面临的主要问题是经济稳定。
entries.example_en: The major issue facing the country is economic stability.

entries.definition_en: having a greater scope or effect
entries.example_cn: 政策的主要变化将影响每个人。
entries.example_en: The major changes in the policy will affect everyone.

entries.definition_en: the main subject of study chosen by a university student
entries.example_cn: 计算机科学是她的主修科目。
entries.example_en: Computer science is her major.

entries.definition_en: a commissioned officer in the US Army, Air Force, or Marines who ranks above a captain and below a lieutenant colonel
entries.example_cn: 他在服役十年后被晋升为少校。
entries.example_en: He was promoted to major after ten years of service.

entries.definition_en: a university student who studies a specific subject as their main focus
entries.example_cn: 她是英语专业的学生。
entries.example_en: She is an English major.

entries.definition_en: to choose a particular subject as your main area of study at university
entries.example_cn: 我本科主修历史。
entries.example_en: I majored in history during my undergraduate studies.

entries.definition_en: greater in number, size, or amount
entries.example_cn: 预算的大部分花在了教育上。
entries.example_en: The major part of the budget was spent on education.

entries.definition_cn: 成年的；已达到法定年龄的
entries.definition_en: of full legal age; adult
entries.example_cn: 该法律将年满十八岁的人视为成年人。
entries.example_en: The statute treats anyone eighteen or older as major.

entries.definition_en: the chief steward or butler of a great household
entries.example_cn: 总管管理着庄园的员工和日常事务。
entries.example_en: The major-domo managed the staff and the daily operations of the estate.

entries.definition_en: a general officer ranking above a brigadier general and below a lieutenant general
entries.example_cn: 少将在战斗前检阅了部队。
entries.example_en: The major-general inspected the troops before the battle.

entries.definition_cn: 女棍操表演者；伴随行进乐队表演的女仪仗队员
entries.definition_en: a female baton twirler who accompanies a marching band
entries.example_cn: 这名女棍操表演者随着音乐旋转表演棒操。
entries.example_en: The majorette twirled her baton in time with the music.

entries.definition_en: a female drum major
entries.example_cn: 女鼓号指挥带领乐队走上场地。
entries.example_en: The majorette led the band onto the field.

entries.definition_en: the greater part of two things
entries.example_cn: 大部分观众都欣赏了这场演出。
entries.example_en: The majority of the audience enjoyed the performance.

entries.definition_en: more than half of the votes in an election
entries.example_cn: 这位候选人以微弱的多数票赢得了选举。
entries.example_en: The candidate won the election by a slim majority.

entries.definition_en: the age at which persons are considered competent to manage their own affairs
entries.example_cn: 她已成年，现在可以参加地方选举投票了。
entries.example_en: She reached the majority and could now vote in local elections.

entries.definition_en: one of the large alphabetic characters used as the first letter in writing or printing proper names and sometimes for emphasis
entries.example_cn: 这份文件以一个大写字母 M 开头。
entries.example_en: The document began with a majuscule M.

entries.definition_en: uppercase
entries.example_cn: 请用大写字母写下你的名字。
entries.example_en: Please write your name in majuscule letters.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to a style of writing characterized by somewhat rounded capital letters; 4th to 8th centuries
entries.example_cn: 这份手稿是用大写字母体书写的。
entries.example_en: The manuscript is written in majuscule script.

entries.definition_en: to create or manufacture a product
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂制造家具。
entries.example_en: They make furniture in this factory.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to exist or become something
entries.example_cn: 她让他很开心。
entries.example_en: She made him happy.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to do something
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生努力学习。
entries.example_en: The teacher made the students study hard.

entries.definition_en: perform or engage in an activity
entries.example_cn: 我们一起演奏音乐。
entries.example_en: We make music together.

entries.definition_en: to cause an event to happen, often unintentionally
entries.example_cn: 这消息让每个人都哭了。
entries.example_en: The news made everyone cry.

entries.definition_en: a brand or manufacturer of a product
entries.example_cn: 这是一个新的汽车品牌。
entries.example_en: This is a new make of car.

entries.definition_en: to give specific qualities to something
entries.example_cn: 雨水让地面变湿了。
entries.example_en: The rain made the ground wet.

entries.definition_en: the action of shuffling cards randomly
entries.example_cn: 发牌前他把牌洗了。
entries.example_en: He made the deck before dealing.

entries.definition_en: imagined as in a play
entries.example_cn: 他们玩了一个虚构的海盗游戏。
entries.example_en: They played a make-believe game of pirates.

entries.definition_en: the activity of pretending or imagining
entries.example_cn: 孩子们整个下午都在玩假装游戏。
entries.example_en: The children spent the afternoon in make-believe.

entries.definition_en: a state or instance of pretending
entries.example_cn: 这一切都只是假装。
entries.example_en: The whole thing was just make-believe.

entries.definition_en: something made quickly or poorly because you have no better choice
entries.example_cn: 我们只能吃面包和奶酪凑合的一顿饭。
entries.example_en: We had to eat a make-do meal of bread and cheese.

entries.definition_en: to understand or decipher something indistinct
entries.example_cn: 她无法看清小屏幕上的字。
entries.example_en: She could not make out the words on the small screen.

entries.definition_en: to see or hear something clearly enough to understand it
entries.example_cn: 我从这里能辨认出那个标志。
entries.example_en: I can make-out the sign from here.

entries.definition_en: to fill in all the necessary details on a form
entries.example_cn: 请仔细填写申请表。
entries.example_en: Please make out the application form carefully.

entries.definition_cn: 与某人亲吻或进行性抚摸
entries.definition_en: to kiss or fondle someone sexually
entries.example_cn: 那对情侣开始在后排亲热。
entries.example_en: The couple began to make out in the back row.

entries.definition_en: to manage to continue or succeed in a situation
entries.example_cn: 尽管下着大雨，我们还是应付过来了。
entries.example_en: We managed to make out despite the heavy rain.

entries.definition_cn: 填写或开具（文件，如收据）
entries.definition_en: to write or complete a document, such as a receipt
entries.example_cn: 职员将为您开具收据。
entries.example_en: The clerk will make out a receipt for you.

entries.definition_en: to succeed in doing something with limited resources
entries.example_cn: 他们只能靠仅有的食物勉强维持。
entries.example_en: They had to make-out with what little food they had.

entries.definition_en: to have sexual intercourse with someone
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在卧室里发生性关系。
entries.example_en: They decided to make-out in the bedroom.

entries.definition_en: someone who tries to bring peace
entries.example_cn: 这位调停者努力结束了冲突。
entries.example_en: The make-peace worked hard to end the conflict.

entries.definition_en: cosmetics applied to the face
entries.example_cn: 她化了些妆。
entries.example_en: She put on some make-up.

entries.definition_en: the way in which someone or something is composed
entries.example_cn: 团队的构成发生了变化。
entries.example_en: The make-up of the team changed.

entries.definition_en: an event that replaces a cancelled one
entries.example_cn: 这场比赛是补赛。
entries.example_en: The match was a make-up game.

entries.definition_en: active work of little value
entries.example_cn: 委员会花了几个小时做没人关心的无意义工作。
entries.example_en: The committee spent hours on make-work that nobody cared about.

entries.definition_en: a beauty treatment that changes or improves a person's appearance, including hair, makeup, and clothes
entries.example_cn: 她决定为婚礼进行一次彻底的美容改造。
entries.example_en: She decided to get a complete makeover for her wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 对某物外观或整体呈现的重大改造或翻新
entries.definition_en: a substantial transformation or renovation of something, especially its appearance or presentation
entries.example_cn: 这座旧工厂经过彻底改造，变成了一座现代化的办公大楼。
entries.example_en: The old factory underwent a massive makeover to become a modern office complex.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes things
entries.example_cn: 这座雕塑的制作人使用了回收材料。
entries.example_en: The maker of the sculpture used recycled materials.

entries.definition_en: a business engaged in manufacturing some product
entries.example_cn: 这家汽车制造商以质量著称。
entries.example_en: This car maker has a reputation for quality.

entries.definition_en: done or made using whatever is available
entries.example_cn: 他们只用储藏室里现有的食材做了一顿临时的饭菜。
entries.example_en: They cooked a makeshift meal using only the ingredients they had in the pantry.

entries.definition_cn: 为满足紧急需要而临时使用的替代物
entries.definition_en: a temporary substitute used to meet an urgent need
entries.example_cn: 这个临时替代物只是权宜之计。
entries.example_en: The makeshift was only a temporary solution.

entries.definition_en: cosmetics applied to the face to improve or change your appearance
entries.example_cn: 她为生日买了一盒新的化妆品。
entries.example_en: She bought a new box of makeup for her birthday.

entries.definition_en: the way in which someone or something is composed
entries.example_cn: 委员会的构成包括来自五个不同国家的专家。
entries.example_en: The makeup of the committee includes experts from five different countries.

entries.definition_en: an event that is substituted for a previously cancelled event
entries.example_cn: 足球赛因雨推迟，所以我们下周将观看补赛。
entries.example_en: The football match was postponed due to rain, so we will watch the makeup game next week.

entries.definition_en: a weight added to a scale to reach a specific total weight
entries.example_cn: 屠夫用一个砝码使秤盘完全平衡。
entries.example_en: The butcher used a makeweight to balance the scale exactly.

entries.definition_en: something added to complete a set or fill a gap
entries.example_cn: 最后一章只是为了凑足字数而写的凑数之作。
entries.example_en: The final chapter was just a makeweight to reach the required word count.

entries.definition_en: the act that results in something coming to be
entries.example_cn: 这项条约的达成经过了几个月的谈判。
entries.example_en: The making of the treaty took several months of negotiation.

entries.definition_en: (usually plural) the components needed for making or doing something
entries.example_cn: 我们有了做一顿美味晚餐的所有必需品。
entries.example_en: We have all the makings for a delicious dinner.

entries.definition_en: qualities or potential that make someone suitable for a particular role
entries.example_cn: 她具备成为成功领导者的所有潜质。
entries.example_en: She has all the makings of a successful leader.

entries.definition_en: a powerful mackerel shark
entries.example_cn: 真鲨以其速度著称。
entries.example_en: The mako shark is known for its speed.

entries.definition_en: illness or affliction
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出一种罕见的疾病，需要立即治疗。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed a rare mal that required immediate treatment.

entries.definition_en: a longboard, a type of surfboard
entries.example_cn: 他租了一块长板去海滩尝试大波浪。
entries.example_en: He rented a mal to try out the big waves at the beach.

entries.definition_cn: 踝部骨性突起（非正式用语）
entries.definition_en: a malleolus, the bony projection on either side of the ankle (informal)
entries.example_cn: 他扭伤了脚踝，感觉踝部突起处很痛。
entries.example_en: He twisted his ankle and felt pain in the mal.

entries.definition_en: the condition where the body cannot properly absorb nutrients from the digestive tract
entries.example_cn: 该患者在患有慢性腹泻后被诊断为吸收不良。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with malabsorption after suffering from chronic diarrhea.

usage.label: 可数或不可数
usage.pattern: malabsorption has both countable and uncountable uses

entries.definition_en: a cane made from the stem of a rattan palm
entries.example_cn: 他拄着那根旧藤条手杖在花园里散步。
entries.example_en: He leaned on his old malacca as he walked through the garden.

entries.definition_en: the stem of a rattan palm used to make canes and umbrella handles
entries.example_cn: 工匠挑选了一段藤条茎来制作一根结实的拐杖。
entries.example_en: The craftsman selected a piece of malacca to craft a sturdy walking cane.

entries.definition_en: a green or blue mineral used as a copper ore and for decoration
entries.example_cn: 艺术家用一块孔雀石雕刻了一个精美的碗。
entries.example_en: The artist carved a beautiful bowl from a piece of malachite.

entries.definition_en: the branch of zoology that studies the structure and behavior of mollusks
entries.example_cn: 这位教授专攻软体动物学，并研究过各种蜗牛物种。
entries.example_en: The professor specializes in malacology and has studied various species of snails.

entries.definition_en: not helping an organism to adjust to its environment
entries.example_cn: 这种适应不良的行为阻止了动物找到食物。
entries.example_en: The maladaptive behavior prevented the animal from finding food.

entries.definition_cn: 调整不当的；适应不良的
entries.definition_en: adjusted badly or wrongly; poorly adapted to a person, thing, or situation
entries.example_cn: 搬到新国家后，这名青少年感到难以适应。
entries.example_en: The teenager felt maladjusted after moving to a new country.

entries.definition_cn: 情绪不稳定且难以处理人际关系的
entries.definition_en: emotionally unstable and having difficulty coping with personal relationships
entries.example_cn: 他情绪不稳定且难以处理人际关系的行为给婚姻带来了问题。
entries.example_en: His maladjusted behavior caused problems in his marriage.

entries.definition_en: not well adjusted to one's environment
entries.example_cn: 这孩子似乎无法适应严格的校规。
entries.example_en: The child seemed maladjusted to the strict school rules.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being unable to adapt properly to your environment with resulting emotional instability
entries.example_cn: 他对城市生活的适应不良给他带来了巨大的压力。
entries.example_en: His maladjustment to city life caused him great stress.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指机械装置的）调节不当或调节失误
entries.definition_en: a poor or faulty adjustment, especially of a mechanism
entries.example_cn: 刹车调节不当导致机器发生振动。
entries.example_en: A slight maladjustment of the brake caused the machine to vibrate.

entries.definition_en: awkward, clumsy, or inept
entries.example_cn: 他操作精密仪器时笨手笨脚。
entries.example_en: He was maladroit at handling the delicate instrument.

entries.definition_en: a disease or disorder affecting an organism
entries.example_cn: 这种病毒在牲畜中引发了广泛的病症。
entries.example_en: The virus caused a widespread malady among the livestock.

entries.definition_cn: 道德或精神上的缺陷或障碍
entries.definition_en: a moral or mental defect or disorder
entries.example_cn: 爱情是一种无药可治的心病。
entries.example_en: Love's a malady without a cure.

entries.definition_en: physical discomfort (as mild sickness or depression)
entries.example_cn: 他醒来时感到浑身不适，决定留在床上。
entries.example_en: He woke up with a general feeling of malaise and decided to stay in bed.

entries.definition_en: a breed of strong sled dog developed in Alaska
entries.example_cn: 队伍用阿拉斯加雪橇犬拉着沉重的雪橇穿过雪地。
entries.example_en: The team used malamutes to pull their heavy sleds across the snow.

entries.definition_cn: 象耳芋；象耳芋的可食块茎
entries.definition_en: a tropical American plant of the genus Xanthosoma, or its edible tuber
entries.example_cn: 他们用新鲜的象耳芋块茎作为主要食材炖了一道菜。
entries.example_en: They prepared a stew using fresh malanga tubers as the main ingredient.

entries.definition_cn: 因与发音相似的词混淆而造成的无意词语误用
entries.definition_en: the unintentional misuse of a word by confusion with one that sounds similar
entries.example_cn: 她把“flamenco”误说成“flamingo”，这是一个因发音相似而造成的无意词语误用。
entries.example_en: Her use of “flamingo” for “flamenco” was a malaprop.

entries.definition_cn: 把发音相近但不合适的词误用来替代目标词；词语误用
entries.definition_en: the accidental use of a word that sounds like the one you intended to say
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上的口误让大家都笑了起来。
entries.example_en: His malapropism made everyone laugh during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: the bony arch beneath the eye that forms the cheekbone
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了患者骨折的颧骨。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the patient's fractured malar bone.

entries.definition_en: a serious infectious disease spread by mosquito bites, causing high fevers and chills.
entries.example_cn: 前往热带地区的旅行者应预防疟疾。
entries.example_en: Travelers to tropical regions should take precautions against malaria.

entries.definition_en: relating to or caused by malaria
entries.example_cn: 该患者接受了疟疾性发热的治疗。
entries.example_en: The patient was treated for malarial fever.

entries.definition_en: nonsense or foolish talk
entries.example_cn: 别再胡扯了，告诉我真相。
entries.example_en: Stop talking malarkey and tell me the truth.

entries.definition_en: nonsense or foolish talk
entries.example_cn: 那位政治家的演讲全是胡话。
entries.example_en: The politician's speech was nothing but malarky.

entries.definition_en: a yellow insecticide used as a dust or spray to control garden pests and house flies and mites
entries.example_cn: 园丁在玫瑰上喷洒马拉硫磷以杀死蚜虫。
entries.example_en: The gardener applied malathion to the roses to kill the aphids.

entries.definition_en: a person who is discontented or disgusted
entries.example_cn: 这场革命是由一群不满者领导的。
entries.example_en: The revolution was led by a group of malcontents.

entries.definition_en: discontented as toward authority
entries.example_cn: 这些不满的士兵拒绝服从命令。
entries.example_en: The malcontent soldiers refused to follow the orders.

entries.definition_en: being the sex that produces sperm
entries.example_cn: 雄花产生花粉。
entries.example_en: The male flowers produce pollen.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of a man
entries.example_cn: 他的声音很有男性特点。
entries.example_en: He has a very male voice.

entries.definition_en: for or pertaining to men or boys
entries.example_cn: 这家商店销售男装和配饰。
entries.example_en: The store sells male clothing and accessories.

entries.definition_en: a person of the sex or gender that typically produces sperm
entries.example_cn: 在许多文化中，男性被期望在外工作。
entries.example_en: In many cultures, the male is expected to work outside the home.

entries.definition_en: an animal that produces sperm to fertilize female eggs
entries.example_cn: 雄狮咆哮以保护它的领地。
entries.example_en: The male lion roared to protect his territory.

entries.definition_en: a salt or ester of maleic acid
entries.example_cn: 这种化合物是马来酸盐，即马来酸形成的盐。
entries.example_en: The compound is a maleate, a salt of maleic acid.

entries.definition_en: the act of calling down a curse that invokes evil (and usually serves as an insult)
entries.example_cn: 这部古文献警告人们不要低估诅咒的力量。
entries.example_en: The ancient text warned against the power of a malediction.

entries.definition_en: a person who commits a crime or does evil
entries.example_cn: 这名罪犯被判处十年监禁。
entries.example_en: The malefactor was sentenced to ten years in prison.

entries.definition_en: having or exerting a malignant or harmful influence
entries.example_cn: 毒素的有害影响在暴露几小时后便显而易见。
entries.example_en: The malefic effects of the toxin were evident within hours of exposure.

entries.definition_en: the act of doing or causing evil
entries.example_cn: 这个恶棍对无辜者的残酷对待显示了他的作恶本性。
entries.example_en: The villain's maleficence was evident in his cruel treatment of the innocent.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being harmful or evil
entries.example_cn: 这种治疗对患者造成的有害影响显示了其有害性。
entries.example_en: The treatment's maleficence was evident in its harmful effects on patients.

entries.definition_en: causing harm or evil, especially in intent or effect
entries.example_cn: 那个恶毒的统治者压迫村民。
entries.example_en: The maleficent ruler oppressed the villagers.

entries.definition_cn: 男性特质；男性身份或状态
entries.definition_en: the characteristic, state, or condition of being male
entries.example_cn: 男性特征通常与力量和攻击性联系在一起。
entries.example_en: The concept of maleness is often associated with strength and aggression.

entries.definition_en: the desire or wish to cause harm or evil to others
entries.example_cn: 他的行为是由纯粹的恶意驱动的。
entries.example_en: His actions were driven by pure malevolence.

entries.definition_cn: 表现出敌意或恶意的行为
entries.definition_en: behavior that displays hostility or ill will
entries.example_cn: 这次蓄意破坏是针对该慈善机构的恶意行为。
entries.example_en: The deliberate sabotage was an act of malevolence against the charity.

entries.definition_en: wishing or appearing to wish evil to others; arising from intense ill will or hatred
entries.example_cn: 那些恶意的话语旨在伤害她的感情。
entries.example_en: The malevolent remarks were intended to hurt her feelings.

entries.definition_en: having or exerting a malignant influence
entries.example_cn: 这部小说描绘了一个威胁村庄的邪恶力量。
entries.example_en: The novel depicts a malevolent force threatening the village.

entries.definition_en: in a malevolent manner
entries.example_cn: 看到对手失败时，他恶意地笑了。
entries.example_en: He malevolently smiled as his rival failed.

entries.definition_en: wrongful or illegal conduct, especially by a public official
entries.example_cn: 法官因渎职被弹劾。
entries.example_en: The judge was impeached for malfeasance.

entries.definition_en: a condition where a part of the body is not shaped correctly
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出婴儿心脏存在先天性畸形。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed a congenital malformation in the infant's heart.

entries.definition_en: an abnormal developmental feature in an offspring
entries.example_cn: 婴儿出生前就被检测出存在发育畸形。
entries.example_en: The malformation was detected in the infant before birth.

entries.definition_en: so badly formed or out of shape as to be ugly
entries.example_cn: 这根畸形扭曲的树枝已经断裂了。
entries.example_en: The malformed branch was twisted and broken.

entries.definition_en: a failure to function normally
entries.example_cn: 电脑突然发生故障。
entries.example_en: The computer experienced a sudden malfunction.

entries.definition_en: to fail to function or function improperly
entries.example_cn: 引擎在比赛期间发生故障。
entries.example_en: The engine malfunctioned during the race.

entries.definition_en: not performing or able to perform its regular function
entries.example_cn: 发动机故障导致汽车突然停下。
entries.example_en: The malfunctioning engine caused the car to stop suddenly.

entries.definition_en: the desire to cause harm or suffering to others
entries.example_cn: 这次袭击是怀着极大的恶意实施的。
entries.example_en: The attack was carried out with great malice.

entries.definition_en: an intention to cause injury, especially one relevant to criminal liability
entries.example_cn: 检方认为这一行为是在怀有恶意的情况下实施的。
entries.example_en: The prosecution argued that the act was committed with malice.

entries.definition_en: intended to cause harm or suffering
entries.example_cn: 攻击者使用恶意软件窃取数据。
entries.example_en: The attacker used malicious software to steal data.

entries.definition_en: with malice; in a malicious manner
entries.example_cn: 他恶意地散布关于同事的谣言，以毁坏她的声誉。
entries.example_en: He maliciously spread rumors about his colleague to ruin her reputation.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being malicious; malice or malevolence
entries.example_cn: 这个恶作剧的恶意让孩子们感到难过。
entries.example_en: The maliciousness of the prank upset the children.

entries.definition_en: to speak about someone or something in a way that is unfair and damaging to their reputation
entries.example_cn: 竞争对手试图诋毁我们产品的安全记录。
entries.example_en: The rival company tried to malign our product's safety record.

entries.definition_en: evil or harmful in nature or influence
entries.example_cn: 那位腐败政治家的邪恶影响使全城笼罩在恐惧之中。
entries.example_en: The malign influence of the corrupt politician spread fear throughout the city.

entries.definition_en: malignant, especially of a tumor
entries.example_cn: 医生警告说，这个恶性肿瘤需要立即手术。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned that the malign tumor required immediate surgery.

entries.definition_cn: 恶性的状态或状况；恶性肿瘤
entries.definition_en: the state or condition of being malignant; a malignant cancer
entries.example_cn: 医生警告说这种恶性肿瘤对常规治疗具有耐药性。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned that the malignancy was resistant to standard treatments.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being disposed to evil or showing intense ill will
entries.example_cn: 他对前同事的恶意在他的尖刻评论中显而易见。
entries.example_en: His malignancy towards his former colleagues was evident in his harsh comments.

entries.definition_en: dangerous to health, especially when referring to a tumor that grows uncontrollably
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出患者患有恶性肿瘤。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the patient with a malignant tumor.

entries.definition_en: harmful, hostile, or showing a desire to cause harm
entries.example_cn: 他那些恶意的言论是故意要伤害她的。
entries.example_en: His malignant remarks were intended to hurt her.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows great hatred or malice
entries.example_cn: 那个恶棍恶毒地对着他的受害者微笑。
entries.example_en: The villain smiled malignantly at his victims.

entries.definition_cn: 邪恶的倾向；强烈的敌意
entries.definition_en: quality of being disposed to evil; intense ill will
entries.example_cn: 这个故事揭示了角色彬彬有礼的外表下隐藏的邪恶倾向。
entries.example_en: The story reveals the malignity hidden beneath the character's polite exterior.

entries.definition_en: wishing evil to others
entries.example_cn: 他的行为纯粹是出于对对手的恶意。
entries.example_en: His actions were driven by pure malignity towards his rivals.

entries.definition_en: a cancerous growth or condition; malignancy
entries.example_cn: 活检显示原发肿瘤中没有恶性病变的证据。
entries.example_en: The biopsy showed no evidence of malignity in the primary tumor.

entries.definition_cn: （阿富汗、巴基斯坦某些地区或现代亚述人社会的）部落酋长
entries.definition_en: a tribal chieftain in certain areas of Afghanistan and Pakistan or in modern Assyrian society
entries.example_cn: 这位部落酋长组织村民抵御入侵者。
entries.example_en: The malik organized the village's defense against the invaders.

entries.definition_en: to pretend to be ill in order to avoid work or duty
entries.example_cn: 这名士兵被指控装病以逃避部署。
entries.example_en: The soldier was accused of malingering to avoid deployment.

entries.definition_en: a person who pretends to be ill to avoid work or duty
entries.example_cn: 上校怀疑这名士兵是在装病。
entries.example_en: The captain suspected the soldier was a malingerer.

entries.definition_en: the act of pretending to be ill or unable to work in order to avoid duty
entries.example_cn: 这名士兵被指控装病以逃避危险任务。
entries.example_en: The soldier was accused of malingering to avoid a dangerous mission.

entries.definition_en: a fawn-colored short-haired sheepdog
entries.example_cn: 这只警犬是一只训练有素的马利诺犬，以敏捷著称。
entries.example_en: The police dog was a trained malinois known for its agility.

entries.definition_en: a shopping center or complex of shops
entries.example_cn: 一家人在购物中心度过了整个下午。
entries.example_en: The family spent the whole afternoon at the mall.

entries.definition_cn: 步行街；林荫步道；散步道
entries.definition_en: a public walk or promenade, especially a pedestrianized street
entries.example_cn: 我们沿着步行街走到公园。
entries.example_en: We walked along the mall to get to the park.

entries.definition_en: a wild duck that is the ancestor of domestic ducks
entries.example_cn: 野鸭是公园和池塘里最常见的鸭子。
entries.example_en: The mallard is the most common duck found in parks and ponds.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being able to be hammered or pressed into shape without breaking
entries.example_cn: 黄金因其高延展性而备受珍视，可被打造成薄片。
entries.example_en: Gold is prized for its high malleability, allowing it to be shaped into thin sheets.

entries.definition_cn: 密码算法的一种性质，允许攻击者修改密文，使其解密后得到相关的明文
entries.definition_en: a property of a cryptographic algorithm that allows an attacker to alter a ciphertext so that it decrypts to a related plaintext
entries.example_cn: 该协议经过重新设计，以防止攻击者篡改密文并使其解密为相关明文。
entries.example_en: The protocol was redesigned to prevent attackers from altering ciphertexts so that they decrypt to related plaintexts.

entries.definition_en: easily influenced
entries.example_cn: 他太容易受影响了，不适合当领导。
entries.example_en: He was too malleable to be a good leader.

entries.definition_en: capable of being shaped or bent
entries.example_cn: 黄金是一种可塑的金属。
entries.example_en: Gold is a malleable metal.

entries.definition_en: any of several low-growing Australian eucalypts
entries.example_cn: 这种桉树生长在澳大利亚南部的干旱灌丛中。
entries.example_en: The mallee grows in the dry scrublands of southern Australia.

entries.definition_en: a sports implement with a long handle and a head like a hammer, used to hit a ball in sports like polo or croquet
entries.example_cn: 球员在槌球比赛中挥动球槌击打球。
entries.example_en: The player swung the mallet to strike the ball in the croquet match.

entries.definition_en: a light drumstick with a rounded head used to strike percussion instruments
entries.example_cn: 打击乐手用软音槌演奏马林巴琴。
entries.example_en: The percussionist used a soft mallet to play the marimba.

entries.definition_en: a tool resembling a hammer with a large head, used to drive wedges or flatten surfaces
entries.example_cn: 木匠用木锤将楔子打入木头中。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a wooden mallet to drive the wedge into the wood.

entries.definition_en: one of the small bones in the middle ear that vibrates when sound waves hit the eardrum
entries.example_cn: 锤骨是人类耳部听小骨链中的第一块骨头。
entries.example_en: The malleus is the first bone in the chain of ossicles in the human ear.

entries.definition_cn: 锦葵科植物；尤其指锦葵属植物
entries.definition_en: any plant of the mallow family (Malvaceae), especially one of the genus Malva
entries.example_cn: 孩子们从花园里摘下了锦葵。
entries.example_en: The children picked mallow flowers from the garden.

entries.definition_en: a sweet wine from Madeira
entries.example_cn: 甜点配了一杯马德拉甜酒。
entries.example_en: The dessert was accompanied by a glass of malmsey.

entries.definition_en: not receiving enough food to stay healthy
entries.example_cn: 由于缺乏食物，这些孩子营养不良。
entries.example_en: The children were malnourished due to the lack of food.
