entries.definition_en: a solid shape with eight flat faces
entries.example_cn: 这块晶体形成了一个完美的八面体。
entries.example_en: The crystal formed a perfect octahedron.

entries.definition_en: relating to a number system that uses eight as its base
entries.example_cn: 该计算机程序将十进制数转换为八进制格式进行存储。
entries.example_en: The computer program converts decimal numbers into octal format for storage.

entries.definition_cn: 辛烷值，表示燃料抗发动机爆震能力的数值
entries.definition_en: the octane number of a fuel, indicating how resistant it is to engine knocking
entries.example_cn: 这种燃料辛烷值高，适用于高性能发动机。
entries.example_en: This fuel has a high octane number and is suitable for high-performance engines.

entries.definition_cn: 石油中的一种饱和烃（C₈H₁₈），有18种异构体，用作燃料或溶剂
entries.definition_en: any of eighteen isomeric saturated hydrocarbons (C₈H₁₈) found in petroleum and used as fuel or solvent
entries.example_cn: 辛烷可用作某些燃料的成分和溶剂。
entries.example_en: Octane is used as a component of some fuels and as a solvent.

entries.definition_cn: 用于测量天体高度角、带有45度刻度弧的航海仪器
entries.definition_en: a navigational instrument for measuring the altitude of a celestial body, using a graduated 45-degree arc
entries.example_cn: 水手利用八分仪通过测量太阳的角度来确定船只的纬度。
entries.example_en: The sailor used the octant to determine the ship's latitude by measuring the sun's angle.

entries.definition_cn: 圆的八分之一，即45度的圆弧
entries.definition_en: an eighth of a circle, equal to an arc of 45 degrees
entries.example_cn: 45度的圆弧就是八分之一圆。
entries.example_en: A 45-degree arc is an octant.

entries.definition_cn: 跨越八个音级、包含十二个半音的音乐音程
entries.definition_en: a musical interval of twelve semitones spanning eight scale degrees
entries.example_cn: 钢琴的音域有七个八度。
entries.example_en: The piano has a range of seven octaves.

entries.definition_en: a group of eight lines in a poem
entries.example_cn: 十四行诗由两个四行诗节和两个八行诗节组成。
entries.example_en: The sonnet is made up of two quatrains and two octaves.

entries.definition_en: the eight days following a feast day
entries.example_cn: 教堂庆祝圣诞八日节期。
entries.example_en: The church celebrates the octave of Christmas.

entries.definition_en: a book size made by folding a sheet of paper three times to create eight leaves
entries.example_cn: 图书馆收购了一批18世纪的八开本珍本。
entries.example_en: The library acquired a rare collection of octavo volumes from the 18th century.

entries.definition_en: a set of eight similar things considered as a unit
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家创作了一系列画作，以八幅为一组展出。
entries.example_en: The artist created a series of paintings displayed as an octet.

entries.definition_en: a group of eight performers or singers who perform together
entries.example_cn: 合唱团以八人组合的形式演奏了一首复杂的乐曲。
entries.example_en: The choir performed a complex piece as an octet.

entries.definition_en: a musical composition written for eight performers
entries.example_cn: 管弦乐团首演了一首由著名现代主义作曲家创作的八人乐。
entries.example_en: The orchestra premiered a new octet composed by a famous modernist.

entries.definition_en: a group of eight people considered as a unit
entries.example_cn: 安保团队被组织成一个八人组来负责此次活动。
entries.example_en: The security team was organized into an octet for the event.

entries.definition_en: a byte consisting of eight bits
entries.example_cn: 网络数据包中的每个八位字节都包含八个位。
entries.example_en: Each octet in the network packet contains eight bits.

entries.definition_en: a person who is between 80 and 89 years old
entries.example_cn: 这位八十岁的老人沿着花园小径缓慢而稳健地走着。
entries.example_en: The octogenarian walked slowly but steadily down the garden path.

entries.definition_en: being from 80 to 89 years old
entries.example_cn: 这对八十多岁的夫妇与孩子们一起庆祝了他们的金婚纪念日。
entries.example_en: The octogenarian couple celebrated their golden anniversary with their children.

entries.definition_en: a cephalopod with eight arms but lacking an internal shell
entries.example_cn: 这只章鱼通过挤过一条小裂缝从水箱里逃走了。
entries.example_en: The octopod managed to escape from the tank by squeezing through a tiny crack.

entries.definition_cn: 底栖头足类动物，身体柔软呈椭圆形，有八条长触手
entries.definition_en: bottom-living cephalopod having a soft oval body with eight long tentacles
entries.example_cn: 潜水员发现一只章鱼正躲在海底的岩石间。
entries.example_en: The diver spotted an octopus hiding among the rocks on the sea floor.

entries.definition_en: the flesh of an octopus prepared or eaten as food
entries.example_cn: 厨师把烤章鱼作为主菜端了上来。
entries.example_en: The chef served grilled octopus as the main course.

entries.definition_en: a person who is one-eighth Black, historically referring to the offspring of a quadroon and a white parent
entries.example_cn: 术语“八分之一黑人”在 19 世纪被用来描述一种特定的种族分类。
entries.example_en: The term octoroon was used in the 19th century to describe a specific racial classification.

entries.definition_en: having eight syllables
entries.example_cn: 诗人写了一首八音节的诗，以匹配歌曲的节奏。
entries.example_en: The poet wrote an octosyllabic verse to match the rhythm of the song.

entries.definition_en: a tax levied on goods brought into a town
entries.example_cn: 进口葡萄酒的价格包含了当地的进城税。
entries.example_en: The price of the imported wine included the local octroi.

entries.definition_en: eightfold; eight times as great in amount or number
entries.example_cn: 产量八倍的增长超出了工厂的产能.
entries.example_en: The octuple increase in production exceeded the factory's capacity.

entries.definition_en: an amount or number that is eight times another
entries.example_cn: 新体育场可容纳的观众人数是旧体育场的八倍。
entries.example_en: The new stadium can hold an octuple of the number of spectators in the old one.

entries.definition_cn: 与眼睛有关或像眼睛的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to or resembling the eye
entries.example_cn: 眼肌控制眼球的运动。
entries.example_en: The ocular muscles control the movement of the eyeball.

entries.definition_cn: 与视觉有关或使用视觉的
entries.definition_en: relating to or using sight
entries.example_cn: 眼科检查可以发现眼部疾病的迹象。
entries.example_en: Ocular examination can reveal signs of eye disease.

entries.definition_en: seen by, or involving, the eyes; visual
entries.example_cn: 目击证据无可否认。
entries.example_en: The ocular evidence was undeniable.

entries.definition_cn: 光学仪器目镜端的透镜组合
entries.definition_en: a combination of lenses at the viewing end of optical instruments
entries.example_cn: 这台望远镜的目镜允许高倍放大。
entries.example_en: The oculars on this telescope allow for high magnification.

entries.definition_en: a doctor who specializes in treating diseases of the eye
entries.example_cn: 事故发生后，眼科医生检查了病人的眼睛。
entries.example_en: After the accident, the oculist examined the patient's eyes.

entries.definition_en: a specialist who tests eyesight and prescribes corrective glasses
entries.example_cn: 验光师调整了我的眼镜以改善我的视力。
entries.example_en: The oculist adjusted my glasses to improve my vision.

entries.definition_en: the nerve that supplies the muscles controlling eye movement
entries.example_cn: 动眼神经受损可能导致复视。
entries.example_en: Damage to the oculomotor nerve can cause double vision.

entries.definition_en: an opening at the apex of a dome
entries.example_cn: 透过罗马万神殿穹顶的圆孔，人们可以看到天空。
entries.example_en: One can glimpse the sky through the oculus of the Pantheon in Rome.

entries.definition_en: a woman slave in a harem
entries.example_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位美丽的后宫女奴斜倚在长沙发上。
entries.example_en: The painting depicts a beautiful odalisque reclining on a divan.

usage.label: 历史用语
usage.pattern: historical female slave in a harem

entries.definition_en: not divisible by two
entries.example_cn: 三是一个奇数。
entries.example_en: Three is an odd number.

entries.definition_en: unusual or unexpected
entries.example_cn: 这个季节的天气异常。
entries.example_en: The weather is odd for this time of year.

entries.definition_en: strange or difficult to explain
entries.example_cn: 他不接电话很奇怪。
entries.example_en: It was odd that he didn't answer the phone.

entries.definition_en: an extra or unspecified amount
entries.example_cn: 我口袋里还剩下一美元零头。
entries.example_en: I have an odd dollar left in my pocket.

entries.definition_en: the one remaining from a pair
entries.example_cn: 抽屉里有一只落单的袜子。
entries.example_en: There was an odd sock in the drawer.

entries.definition_en: remaining after the rest has been used or accounted for
entries.example_cn: 我们还剩下一点零星的油漆。
entries.example_en: We have an odd bit of paint left.

entries.definition_en: not regular or skilled; done as a casual task
entries.example_cn: 他是一名杂工，负责修理篱笆和粉刷房屋。
entries.example_en: He works as an odd-job man, fixing fences and painting houses.

entries.definition_en: having a pinnate leaf shape with a single leaflet at the tip
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子是奇数羽状复叶，顶端有一个小叶。
entries.example_en: The leaves of this plant are odd-pinnate, featuring a terminal leaflet.

entries.definition_en: a person with an unusual or odd personality
entries.example_cn: 新邻居真是个怪人，总是穿着鲜艳的服装。
entries.example_en: The new neighbor is quite an oddball, always wearing bright costumes.

entries.definition_en: somewhat strange
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子有一种有点奇怪的氛围，让我感到不安。
entries.example_en: The old house had an oddish atmosphere that made me uneasy.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being strange or unusual
entries.example_cn: 这个无法解释的结果很奇怪，令研究人员困惑不已。
entries.example_en: The oddity of the unexplained result puzzled the researchers.

entries.definition_en: something unusual that might be worth collecting
entries.example_cn: 博物馆从探险家的收藏中收购了一件稀有的奇珍。
entries.example_en: The museum acquired a rare oddity from the explorer's collection.

entries.definition_en: a strange person; an oddball
entries.example_cn: 大家都认为那位古怪的收藏家是个怪人。
entries.example_en: Everyone considered the eccentric collector an oddity.

entries.definition_en: in a manner differing from the usual or expected
entries.example_cn: 奇怪的是，我以前从未见过他。
entries.example_en: Oddly, I have never seen him before.

entries.definition_en: in a strange manner
entries.example_cn: 他古怪地跟那个陌生人说话。
entries.example_en: He spoke oddly to the stranger.

entries.definition_en: a mixed collection of various small items
entries.example_cn: 店主以折扣价出售这些零碎物品。
entries.example_en: The shopkeeper sold the oddments at a discount.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being odd, unusual, or eccentric
entries.example_cn: 艺术家的怪癖吸引了评论家，他们认为这是一种独特的表达方式。
entries.example_en: The artist's oddness fascinated the critics, who saw it as a unique form of expression.

entries.definition_en: an instance or manifestation of oddness
entries.example_cn: 他的种种怪事，例如对着空椅子说话，让同事们感到不安。
entries.example_en: His oddnesses, such as speaking to empty chairs, unsettled his colleagues.

entries.definition_cn: 某事件发生的概率与其不发生的概率之比
entries.definition_en: the ratio of the probability of an event happening to that of it not happening
entries.example_cn: 明天下雨的概率与不下雨的概率之比为 2 比 1。
entries.example_en: The odds of rain tomorrow are 2 to 1.

entries.definition_en: the ratio of winnings to stake in betting
entries.example_cn: 庄家提供的赔率是 5 比 1。
entries.example_en: The bookmaker offered odds of 5 to 1.

entries.definition_cn: 胜算大于一半的；很可能获胜的
entries.definition_en: more likely than not to win or succeed
entries.example_cn: 胜算最大的选手轻松赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The odds-on favorite won the race easily.

entries.definition_en: very likely
entries.example_cn: 由于暴风雨，火车很可能会晚点。
entries.example_en: It's odds-on that the train will arrive late because of the storm.

entries.definition_cn: 赌注获利少于下注金额的
entries.definition_en: in which the amount won on a bet is less than the amount staked
entries.example_cn: 这是一个低赔率投注，因此可能获得的利润很少。
entries.example_en: It was an odds-on bet, so the potential profit was small.

entries.definition_en: a lyric poem, often expressing sustained noble feeling in a dignified style
entries.example_cn: 诗人写了一首优美的颂歌来庆祝这座城市的周年纪念日。
entries.example_en: The poet wrote a beautiful ode to celebrate the anniversary of the city.

entries.definition_en: extremely unpleasant or hateful
entries.example_cn: 独裁者令人憎恶的行为遭到了全世界的谴责。
entries.example_en: The odious behavior of the dictator was condemned by the entire world.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is extremely offensive and hateful
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家因令人憎恶地攻击反对派而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was criticized for odiously attacking the opposition.

entries.definition_en: intense hate mixed with disgust
entries.example_cn: 公众对这位腐败官员的憎恶之情溢于言表。
entries.example_en: The public's odium toward the corrupt official was overwhelming.

entries.definition_en: a state of disgrace caused by detestable behavior
entries.example_cn: 丑闻使这位政治家蒙受耻辱。
entries.example_en: The scandal brought the politician into odium.

entries.definition_en: a device that shows the total distance a vehicle has traveled
entries.example_cn: 她查看里程表，看看本周开了多少英里。
entries.example_en: She checked the odometer to see how many miles she had driven that week.

entries.definition_cn: 牙唇兰属的一种兰花，通常具有总状排列的艳丽花朵
entries.definition_en: an orchid of the genus Odontoglossum, with showy flowers often arranged in racemes
entries.example_cn: 这株稀有的牙唇兰开出了鲜艳的紫色花朵。
entries.example_en: The rare odontoglossum bloomed with vibrant purple flowers.

entries.definition_en: the branch of medicine concerned with the structure, development, and diseases of teeth
entries.example_cn: 这位教授专攻牙科学，用于鉴定人类遗骸。
entries.example_en: The professor specializes in the study of odontology to identify human remains.

entries.definition_en: a smell that is detected by the nose
entries.example_cn: 厨房里充满了新鲜面包的香气。
entries.example_en: The odor of fresh bread filled the kitchen.

entries.definition_cn: 强烈而普遍存在的气息；氛围
entries.definition_en: a strong, pervasive quality or atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 腐败的气息弥漫在整个机构中。
entries.example_en: An odor of corruption pervaded the institution.

entries.definition_en: emitting an odor
entries.example_cn: 那个有气味的垃圾桶整晚都敞开着。
entries.example_en: The odoriferous garbage can was left open all night.

entries.definition_en: having a natural fragrance
entries.example_cn: 花园里充满了芳香茉莉花的香气。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the scent of odoriferous jasmine.

entries.definition_en: having no smell
entries.example_cn: 这种无味的香水非常适合嗅觉敏感的人。
entries.example_en: The odorless perfume was perfect for sensitive noses.

entries.definition_en: having a characteristic or distinctive odor
entries.example_cn: 实验室里小心地密封了那些有气味的化学品。
entries.example_en: The odorous chemicals were carefully sealed in the laboratory.

entries.definition_en: emitting an odor
entries.example_cn: 散发气味的废物是按照严格的环境法规处理的。
entries.example_en: The odorous waste was disposed of according to strict environmental regulations.

entries.definition_en: having a natural fragrance
entries.example_cn: 花园里充满了盛开的茉莉花散发出的天然香气。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the odorous scent of blooming jasmine.

entries.definition_en: a smell caused by chemicals in the air stimulating the nose
entries.example_cn: 厨房里充满了浓郁的食物香味。
entries.example_en: The strong odour of cooking food filled the kitchen.

entries.definition_en: any quality that can be detected by the sense of smell
entries.example_cn: 科学家研究了这种未知物质的嗅觉特征。
entries.example_en: The scientist studied the odour of the unknown substance.

entries.definition_en: having no smell
entries.example_cn: 这种无味气体没有专门设备就无法察觉。
entries.example_en: The odourless gas was impossible to detect without specialized equipment.

entries.definition_cn: 漫长而充满波折的旅程或探索
entries.definition_en: a long, eventful journey or quest
entries.example_cn: 公司进军新市场是一场耗时五年的漫长冒险。
entries.example_en: The company's expansion into new markets was an odyssey that took five years.

entries.definition_cn: 促进教会或宗教统一的
entries.definition_en: concerned with promoting unity among churches or religions
entries.example_cn: 这次普世会议汇集了不同教派的领导人。
entries.example_en: The oecumenical council brought together leaders from different denominations.

entries.definition_en: of worldwide scope or applicability
entries.example_cn: 这个问题的全球性质影响着每一个国家。
entries.example_en: The oecumenical nature of the problem affects every nation.

entries.definition_en: swelling caused by an excessive accumulation of watery fluid in cells, tissues, or body cavities
entries.example_cn: 医生开了利尿剂来治疗患者腿部严重的水肿。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed diuretics to treat the severe oedema in the patient's legs.

entries.definition_en: an expert who specializes in the science and production of wine
entries.example_cn: 这位酿酒专家分析了土壤样本，以确定该年份最适合酿造的葡萄品种。
entries.example_en: The oenologist analyzed the soil samples to determine the best grapes for the vintage.

entries.definition_cn: 葡萄酒学；葡萄酒酿造学
entries.definition_en: the scientific study of wine and winemaking
entries.example_cn: 她在大学学习葡萄酒学，随后创办了自己的酒庄。
entries.example_en: She studied oenology at university before starting her own winery.

entries.definition_en: a person who has a great appreciation for wine
entries.example_cn: 作为一名葡萄酒爱好者，他仅凭品尝就能识别出葡萄酒的年份和产地。
entries.example_en: As an oenophile, he could identify the vintage and region of the wine just by tasting it.

entries.definition_cn: 磁化场强度的厘米-克-秒制单位，等于每米1000/(4π)安培
entries.definition_en: the CGS unit of magnetizing field strength, equal to 1000/(4π) amperes per metre
entries.example_cn: 磁场强度以奥斯特为单位进行测量。
entries.example_en: The magnetic field strength was measured in oersteds.

entries.definition_en: the tube connecting the throat to the stomach
entries.example_cn: 食物从口腔通过食道进入胃。
entries.example_en: Food passes from the mouth through the oesophagus to the stomach.

entries.definition_en: the most potent naturally occurring estrogen, synthesized to treat estrogen deficiency and some cancers
entries.example_cn: 雌二醇通常被合成用于治疗绝经后女性的雌激素缺乏症。
entries.example_en: Oestradiol is often synthesized and used to treat estrogen deficiency in postmenopausal women.

entries.definition_en: female hormones produced by the ovaries that control sexual characteristics
entries.example_cn: 雌激素水平在整个月经周期中波动。
entries.example_en: Oestrogen levels fluctuate throughout the menstrual cycle.

entries.definition_en: in nonhuman mammals, a state or period of heightened sexual arousal and activity
entries.example_cn: 兽医解释说，不同种类的非人类哺乳动物的发情期差异很大。
entries.example_en: The veterinarian explained that the oestrus cycle varies significantly among different species of nonhuman mammals.

entries.definition_en: the complete body of work produced by a writer or artist
entries.example_cn: 评论家们花了数十年时间分析这位著名画家的毕生作品。
entries.example_en: Critics have spent decades analyzing the oeuvre of the famous painter.

entries.definition_en: used to show what something is made of
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子是木头做的。
entries.example_en: The table is made of wood.

entries.definition_en: used to show a part of a whole
entries.example_cn: 一杯茶是一种受欢迎的饮料。
entries.example_en: A cup of tea is a popular drink.

entries.definition_en: used to introduce the topic of discussion
entries.example_cn: 我们长时间讨论了政治。
entries.example_en: We had a long discussion of politics.

entries.definition_en: used to show where something comes from
entries.example_cn: 这酒产自法国。
entries.example_en: This wine is of French origin.

entries.definition_en: used to show separation
entries.example_cn: 这两件事之间相隔十年。
entries.example_en: There is a gap of ten years between the two events.

entries.definition_en: a colloquial spelling of have
entries.example_cn: 我现在该回家了。
entries.example_en: I of to go home now.

entries.definition_en: used to show distance or movement
entries.example_cn: 这所房子距车站不到两英里。
entries.example_en: The house is within two miles of the station.

entries.definition_cn: 表示动作的施动者，尤其用于被动结构（现代英语通常用 by）
entries.definition_en: Indicating the agent of an action, especially in passive constructions; now usually expressed with by.
entries.example_cn: 所有认识他的人都爱戴他。
entries.example_en: He was beloved of all who knew him.

entries.definition_en: not working or in use
entries.example_cn: 灯是关着的。
entries.example_en: The lights are off.

entries.definition_en: no longer planned or scheduled
entries.example_cn: 会议取消了。
entries.example_en: The meeting is off.

entries.definition_en: away from a place or position
entries.example_cn: 她下了公共汽车。
entries.example_en: She stepped off the bus.

entries.definition_en: at a distance in space or time
entries.example_cn: 那所房子离主干道很远。
entries.example_en: The house is off the main road.

entries.definition_en: no longer in contact or attached
entries.example_cn: 按钮脱落了。
entries.example_en: The button came off.

entries.definition_en: to kill someone intentionally
entries.example_cn: 他被指控杀害了他的对手。
entries.example_en: He was accused of offing his rival.

entries.definition_en: below a satisfactory level
entries.example_cn: 他的表现很差。
entries.example_en: His performance was off.

entries.definition_en: in an unpalatable state
entries.example_cn: 食物变质了。
entries.example_en: The food went off.

entries.definition_en: happening or continuing at irregular intervals
entries.example_cn: 雨断断续续下了一整天。
entries.example_en: It has been raining off-and-on all day.

entries.definition_en: located outside a military base
entries.example_cn: 士兵们在周末驻扎在基地外。
entries.example_en: The soldiers were stationed off-base during the weekend.

entries.definition_en: not in the middle; situated away from the center or axis
entries.example_cn: 这张桌子在地毯上放偏了。
entries.example_en: The table is off-center on the rug.

entries.definition_cn: 不得体的，甚至近乎下流的
entries.definition_en: in violation of good taste, even verging on the indecent
entries.example_cn: 喜剧演员的不雅笑话冒犯了观众。
entries.example_en: The comedian's off-color jokes offended the audience.

entries.definition_en: humorously vulgar
entries.example_cn: 他讲了一个粗俗的笑话，逗得大家哈哈大笑。
entries.example_en: He told an off-color story that made everyone laugh.

entries.definition_en: in violation of good taste, even verging on the indecent
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员的玩笑被保守的观众认为是不雅的。
entries.example_en: The comedian's jokes were considered off-colour by the conservative audience.

entries.definition_en: not engaged in an assigned task, duty, or occupation
entries.example_cn: 这位警察帮助被困司机时，正好不在值班。
entries.example_en: The police officer was off-duty when he helped the stranded driver.

entries.definition_en: Not connected to the main electrical or communication network.
entries.example_cn: 他们住在山里的一座离网小屋中。
entries.example_en: They live in an off-grid cabin in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: not prepared or vigilant
entries.example_cn: 当这家人的防备松懈时，小偷闯了进来。
entries.example_en: The thief broke in while the family was off-guard.

entries.definition_en: without previous consideration
entries.example_cn: 他未经思考就回答了那个难题。
entries.example_en: He answered the difficult question off-hand.

entries.definition_en: singing with a voice that is not at the correct musical pitch
entries.example_cn: 歌手在副歌部分稍微跑调了。
entries.example_en: The singer was slightly off-key during the chorus.

entries.definition_en: a shop that sells alcohol to be drunk elsewhere
entries.example_cn: 我们在街角的酒类专卖店买了一些葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: We bought some wine at the off-licence on the corner.

entries.definition_en: barred to a designated group
entries.example_cn: 施工区域禁止公众进入。
entries.example_en: The construction area is off-limits to the public.

entries.definition_en: not connected to a computer network
entries.example_cn: 我更喜欢脱网工作以避免分心。
entries.example_en: I prefer to work off-line to avoid distractions.

entries.definition_en: not on a regular route of a transportation system
entries.example_cn: 这辆公交车走一条穿过乡村的非定线路线。
entries.example_en: The bus takes an off-line route through the countryside.

entries.definition_en: causing annoyance or disgust
entries.example_cn: 他令人反感的态度让所有人都离开了房间。
entries.example_en: His off-putting attitude made everyone leave the room.

entries.definition_en: tending to repel or discourage
entries.example_cn: 高昂的价格让许多潜在买家却步。
entries.example_en: The high price was off-putting to many potential buyers.

entries.definition_en: designed for use on unpaved surfaces like beaches or rugged terrain
entries.example_cn: 他们开着越野车穿过泥地。
entries.example_en: They drove their off-road vehicle through the mud.

entries.definition_cn: 远离公共道路的；非道路上的
entries.definition_en: used or taking place away from public roads
entries.example_cn: 非道路停车区在大楼后面。
entries.example_en: The off-road parking area is behind the building.

entries.definition_en: to travel on unpaved terrain instead of roads
entries.example_cn: 我们决定越野去观赏野生动物。
entries.example_en: We decided to off-road to see the wildlife.

entries.definition_en: a bicycle with a strong frame and wide tires, originally made for riding in mountains
entries.example_cn: 他买了一辆新的山地车来探索崎岖的小径。
entries.example_en: He bought a new off-roader to explore the rugged trails.

entries.definition_en: existing or happening outside the frame of a cinema or television screen
entries.example_cn: 演员们在摄像机开机前在屏幕外进行了排练。
entries.example_en: The actors rehearsed off-screen before the cameras started rolling.

entries.definition_en: the season when travel is least active and rates are lowest
entries.example_cn: 他们在淡季预订了酒店。
entries.example_en: They booked their hotel during the off-season.

entries.definition_en: located or taking place away from a particular site
entries.example_cn: 公司下周将举行一次外出会议。
entries.example_en: The company is holding an off-site meeting next week.

entries.definition_en: not on the streets
entries.example_cn: 停车场是非街道的。
entries.example_en: The parking area is off-street.

entries.definition_en: with little or no preparation or forethought
entries.example_cn: 他即兴发表了一场演讲，其机智让所有人都感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: He gave an off-the-cuff speech that surprised everyone with its wit.

entries.definition_en: made in standard sizes and available from stock
entries.example_cn: 他为婚礼买了一套成衣西装。
entries.example_en: He bought an off-the-peg suit for the wedding.

entries.definition_en: made in standard sizes and ready to buy from stock, especially of clothing
entries.example_cn: 她决定买一套成衣去参加面试。
entries.example_en: She decided to buy an off-the-rack suit for the interview.

entries.definition_en: available ready-made from stock, without customization
entries.example_cn: 因为我们需要今天的面试，所以我们买了一套现货西装。
entries.example_en: We bought an off-the-shelf suit because we needed it for the interview today.

entries.definition_en: describing a blouse or dress that does not cover the shoulders
entries.example_cn: 她穿着一件优雅的露肩连衣裙去参加聚会。
entries.example_en: She wore an elegant off-the-shoulder dress to the party.

entries.definition_cn: 离奇古怪的；非常规的；（行为）不合适的
entries.definition_en: wildly unconventional, bizarre, or, of behavior, inappropriate
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家离奇古怪的想法令观众惊叹。
entries.example_en: The artist's off-the-wall ideas amazed the audience.

entries.definition_en: of something having a color tending toward white
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一条米白色的连衣裙去参加婚礼。
entries.example_en: She wore an off-white dress to the wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 近乎白色的浅色；米白色
entries.definition_en: a very pale colour that is almost white
entries.example_cn: 墙壁被刷成了米白色。
entries.example_en: The walls were painted off-white.

entries.definition_en: located or existing outside of Earth
entries.example_cn: 那座地外殖民地建在月球上。
entries.example_en: The off-world colony was built on the moon.

entries.definition_cn: 动物的内脏，常作为食物食用
entries.definition_en: the internal organs of a butchered animal, often eaten as food
entries.example_cn: 厨师在准备炖菜前小心地剔除了内脏。
entries.example_en: The chef carefully removed the offal before preparing the stew.

entries.definition_en: (informal) strikingly unconventional
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家标新立异的风格吸引了许多年轻粉丝。
entries.example_en: The artist's offbeat style attracted many young fans.

entries.definition_cn: 弱拍（尤其是小节中的最后一拍）
entries.definition_en: an unaccented beat (especially the last beat of a measure)
entries.example_cn: 鼓手在弱拍上演奏了切分节奏。
entries.example_en: The drummer played a syncopated rhythm on the offbeat.

entries.definition_en: a lack of politeness; a failure to show regard for others
entries.example_cn: 他不断打断别人，被视为有失礼仪。
entries.example_en: His constant interruptions were considered an offence against good manners.

entries.definition_en: a transgression that constitutes a violation of what is judged to be right
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定他的行为是一项严重的罪行。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that his actions were a serious offence.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of anger caused by being offended
entries.example_cn: 她对他的粗鲁言论感到深深的愤慨。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep offence at his rude comments.

entries.definition_en: the team that has the ball and is trying to score
entries.example_cn: 进攻方迅速将球带向前场。
entries.example_en: The offence moved the ball down the field quickly.

entries.definition_en: the act of attacking an enemy
entries.example_cn: 将军率领军队突然进攻那座堡垒。
entries.example_en: The general led his army on a sudden offence against the fortress.

entries.definition_en: to make someone feel angry or upset by saying or doing something rude
entries.example_cn: 他粗鲁的评论冒犯了许多同事。
entries.example_en: His rude comments offended many of his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: to hurt someone's feelings or dignity
entries.example_cn: 请不要提起那个话题，以免伤害她的感情。
entries.example_en: Please do not offend her by bringing up that topic.

entries.definition_en: to break or violate a law, rule, or agreement
entries.example_cn: 该公司因违反环保法规而被罚款。
entries.example_en: The company was fined for offending against environmental regulations.

usage.label: offend against
usage.pattern: offend against a law or rule

entries.definition_en: to cause discomfort, disgust, or revulsion
entries.example_cn: 腐烂食物的景象使他感到反感。
entries.example_en: The sight of the rotting food offended his senses.

entries.definition_en: feeling hurt or annoyed because someone said or did something rude
entries.example_cn: 她对他粗鲁的评论感到被冒犯。
entries.example_en: She was offended by his rude comment.

entries.definition_en: a person who transgresses moral or civil law
entries.example_cn: 警察逮捕了这名偷车的违法者。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the offender for stealing the car.

entries.definition_cn: 违法的；有过错的；造成问题的
entries.definition_en: responsible for an offense, wrongdoing, or other problem
entries.example_cn: 造成漏水的管道被查明后更换了。
entries.example_en: The offending pipe was identified and replaced after it caused the leak.

entries.definition_en: a lack of politeness that hurts someone's feelings
entries.example_cn: 他粗鲁的评论冒犯了她。
entries.example_en: His rude comment was an offense to her.

entries.definition_en: the feeling of anger caused by being offended
entries.example_cn: 她因他的行为感到深深的愤慨。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep offense at his behavior.

entries.definition_en: an act that violates moral or legal rules
entries.example_cn: 警方调查了这起严重的罪行。
entries.example_en: The police investigated the serious offense.

entries.definition_en: the team attacking to score in a game
entries.example_cn: 进攻方将球带向对方球门。
entries.example_en: The offense moved the ball down the field.

entries.definition_en: the action of attacking an enemy
entries.example_cn: 将军仔细策划了下一次进攻。
entries.example_en: The general planned the next offense carefully.

entries.definition_en: causing people to feel offended or upset
entries.example_cn: 他冒犯的言论引发了一场争吵。
entries.example_en: His offensive comments caused an argument.

entries.definition_en: designed to attack rather than defend
entries.example_cn: 军队采取了进攻战略。
entries.example_en: The army adopted an offensive strategy.

entries.definition_en: violating moral standards
entries.example_cn: 这部电影被许多家长认为在道德上令人反感。
entries.example_en: The movie was considered offensive by many parents.

entries.definition_en: causing anger or annoyance
entries.example_cn: 那种气味让她敏感的鼻子感到不快。
entries.example_en: The smell was offensive to her sensitive nose.

entries.definition_en: unpleasant or disgusting to the senses
entries.example_cn: 小巷里的垃圾令人厌恶。
entries.example_en: The garbage in the alley was offensive.

entries.definition_en: an attack or series of attacks
entries.example_cn: 将军对敌人发起了突然进攻。
entries.example_en: The general launched a surprise offensive against the enemy.

entries.definition_en: causing nausea
entries.example_cn: 化学品的味道令人作呕。
entries.example_en: The smell of the chemicals was offensive.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes anger or annoyance
entries.example_cn: 他冒犯地批评了她。
entries.example_en: He criticized her offensively.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is extremely unpleasant or annoying
entries.example_cn: 那股气味令人讨厌地浓烈。
entries.example_en: The smell was offensively strong.

entries.definition_en: in an aggressive or attacking manner
entries.example_cn: 这支球队打得攻势凌厉。
entries.example_en: The team played offensively.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being offensive
entries.example_cn: 这句话的冒犯性立即引发了一场争吵。
entries.example_en: The offensiveness of the remark caused an immediate argument.

entries.definition_en: to give something useful or necessary to someone
entries.example_cn: 你能给我一杯水吗？
entries.example_en: Can you offer me a glass of water?

entries.definition_en: to present something for someone to accept or refuse
entries.example_cn: 老师向学生提供了选题选择。
entries.example_en: The teacher offered the students a choice of topics.

entries.definition_en: to agree willingly
entries.example_cn: 她主动提出帮忙打扫。
entries.example_en: She offered to help with the cleaning.

entries.definition_en: to put forward an idea for discussion
entries.example_cn: 经理提出了一个项目新计划。
entries.example_en: The manager offered a new plan for the project.

entries.definition_en: to say something aloud to someone
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上提出了一个建议。
entries.example_en: He offered a suggestion during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: something offered for acceptance
entries.example_cn: 该公司对这块土地提出了低价收购提议。
entries.example_en: The company made a low offer for the land.

entries.definition_en: the act of offering something
entries.example_cn: 他向陌生人提供了帮助。
entries.example_en: He made an offer of help to the stranger.

entries.definition_en: a usually brief attempt to do something
entries.example_cn: 他尝试修理汽车但失败了。
entries.example_en: He made an offer to fix the car but failed.

entries.definition_en: a person who presents something to another for acceptance or rejection
entries.example_cn: 提议者伸出手与新伙伴握手。
entries.example_en: The offerer extended a hand to shake with the new partner.

entries.definition_en: something offered as a proposal or bid
entries.example_cn: 该公司的报价是这份合同的最高投标价。
entries.example_en: The company's offering was the highest bid for the contract.

entries.definition_en: money or items contributed to a religious organization
entries.example_cn: 会众将奉献物带到了祭坛前。
entries.example_en: The congregation brought their offerings to the altar.

entries.definition_en: the act of contributing to the funds of a church or charity
entries.example_cn: 她对教会的捐款意义重大。
entries.example_en: Her offering to the church was very significant.

entries.definition_en: the verbal act of offering
entries.example_cn: 他主动提出为团队提供服务。
entries.example_en: He made an offering of his services to the team.

entries.definition_en: a person or entity that makes an offer to another party
entries.example_cn: 要约人必须等待受要约人接受条款，合同才能成立。
entries.example_en: The offeror must wait for the offeree to accept the terms before the contract is formed.

usage.label: 法律术语；与 offeree 相对

entries.definition_en: done without preparation or careful thought
entries.example_cn: 他没有看笔记，就随口回答了这个问题。
entries.example_en: He gave an offhand answer to the question without looking at his notes.

entries.definition_cn: 不经意而欠考虑的；随意伤人的
entries.definition_en: casually thoughtless or inconsiderate
entries.example_cn: 他粗鲁的评论伤害了她的感情，因为那缺乏敏感性。
entries.example_en: His offhand comment hurt her feelings because it lacked sensitivity.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is done without prior thought or preparation
entries.example_cn: 她在会议期间随口评论了一下天气。
entries.example_en: She made an offhand remark about the weather during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: in a casually inconsiderate manner
entries.example_cn: 他冷淡地挥了挥手，打发掉她的担忧。
entries.example_en: He dismissed her concerns with an offhand gesture.

entries.definition_en: done with little or no preparation or forethought
entries.example_cn: 她对那个难题给出了一个草率的回答。
entries.example_en: She gave an offhanded answer to the difficult question.

entries.definition_en: casually thoughtless or inconsiderate
entries.example_cn: 他粗鲁的评论伤害了她的感情。
entries.example_en: His offhanded comment hurt her feelings.

entries.definition_en: without previous thought or preparation
entries.example_cn: 他草率地评论了她的外表。
entries.example_en: He made an offhanded remark about her appearance.

entries.definition_en: in a casually inconsiderate manner
entries.example_cn: 她粗鲁地无视了他的担忧。
entries.example_en: She dismissed his concerns in an offhanded way.

entries.definition_en: without thinking carefully or preparing beforehand
entries.example_cn: 他随口提到他可能会下周来访。
entries.example_en: He offhandedly mentioned that he might visit next week.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows a lack of care or consideration
entries.example_cn: 她漫不经心地无视了他对安全的担忧。
entries.example_en: She offhandedly dismissed his concerns about safety.

entries.definition_en: place of business where professional or clerical duties are performed
entries.example_cn: 请在午饭后来我的办公室。
entries.example_en: Please come to my office after lunch.

entries.definition_en: a position of responsibility or employment in an organization
entries.example_cn: 她申请了财务主管这一职位。
entries.example_en: She applied for the office of treasurer.

entries.definition_en: an administrative unit of government
entries.example_cn: 首相府发表了一份声明。
entries.example_en: The Prime Minister's office issued a statement.

entries.definition_en: professional or clerical workers in an office
entries.example_cn: 办公室职员非常高效。
entries.example_en: The office staff is very efficient.

entries.definition_en: (of a government or government official) holding an office means being in power
entries.example_cn: 他已经执政十年了。
entries.example_en: He has been in office for ten years.

entries.definition_en: the actions and activities assigned to or required or expected of a person or group
entries.example_cn: 教师的职责是教育学生。
entries.example_en: It is the office of the teacher to educate students.

entries.definition_en: a religious rite or service prescribed by ecclesiastical authorities
entries.example_cn: 每日的宗教仪式在七点举行。
entries.example_en: The daily office is said at seven o'clock.

entries.definition_en: a person appointed or elected to a public position who holds a place of trust
entries.example_cn: 新任官员昨日宣誓就职。
entries.example_en: The new officeholder took the oath of office yesterday.

entries.definition_en: the official who holds an office
entries.example_cn: 预计该官员下个月将辞职。
entries.example_en: The officeholder was expected to resign next month.

entries.definition_en: any person in the armed services who holds a position of authority or command
entries.example_cn: 军官向士兵下达了命令。
entries.example_en: The officer gave orders to the soldiers.

entries.definition_en: a member of a police force
entries.example_cn: 警官因超速拦下了那辆车。
entries.example_en: The officer stopped the car for speeding.

entries.definition_en: someone who is appointed or elected to an office and who holds a position of trust
entries.example_cn: 她当选为学校官员。
entries.example_en: She was elected as a school officer.

entries.definition_en: a person authorized to serve in a position of authority on a vessel
entries.example_cn: 船上的船员检查了安全设备。
entries.example_en: The ship's officer checked the safety equipment.

entries.definition_en: direct or command as an officer
entries.example_cn: 将军将在阅兵时指挥部队。
entries.example_en: The general will officer the troops during the parade.

entries.definition_en: having official authority or sanction

entries.definition_en: verified officially

entries.example_en: The official results were verified.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to an office

entries.example_en: She has to work long hours on official business.

entries.definition_en: conforming to set usage, procedure, or discipline
entries.example_cn: 请按照正式的申请程序办理。
entries.example_en: Please follow the official procedure for applying.

entries.definition_en: a person who holds a public job or position
entries.example_cn: 警察要求我们出示身份证明。
entries.example_en: The police official asked us to show our identification.

entries.definition_en: someone who administers the rules of a game or sport
entries.example_cn: 足球裁判吹响了结束比赛的哨子。
entries.example_en: The football official blew the whistle to end the match.

entries.definition_en: (of a church) given official status as a national or state institution
entries.example_cn: 该国的国教是英国国教。
entries.example_en: The official church of the country is the Church of England.

entries.definition_en: government officials or civil servants collectively
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策受到了官僚阶层中反对派的批评。
entries.example_en: The new policy was criticized by the opposition within the officialdom.

entries.definition_en: with official authorization
entries.example_cn: 该文件由总统正式签署。
entries.example_en: The document was signed officially by the president.

entries.definition_en: in an official role or capacity
entries.example_cn: 他正式担任该项目的经理。
entries.example_en: He is officially the manager of the project.

entries.definition_cn: 主持宗教或民事仪式的人
entries.definition_en: a person who officiates at a religious or civil ceremony
entries.example_cn: 这位神职人员优雅地主持了婚礼仪式。
entries.example_en: The officiant led the wedding ceremony with grace.

entries.definition_en: to act as an official in a ceremony or ritual, such as a wedding
entries.example_cn: 牧师将于下周日主持婚礼仪式。
entries.example_en: The priest will officiate at the wedding ceremony next Sunday.

entries.definition_en: to serve as an umpire or referee in a sports match
entries.example_cn: 他将担任周日杯赛决赛的裁判。
entries.example_en: He will officiate at the cup final on Sunday.

entries.definition_en: to perform the duties of a particular office or function, especially as an official
entries.example_cn: 她在婚礼上担任登记员。
entries.example_en: She officiated as registrar at the wedding.

entries.definition_en: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.example_cn: 这位爱管闲事的邻居不停地提供关于如何修理栅栏的不请自来的建议。
entries.example_en: The officious neighbor kept offering unsolicited advice on how to fix the fence.

entries.definition_en: in an officious manner

entries.example_en: He officiously offered to help me with my homework even though I had finished it.

entries.definition_en: the near or foreseeable future
entries.example_cn: 一项重大突破即将到来。
entries.example_en: A major breakthrough is in the offing.

usage.label: in the offing
usage.pattern: usually used in the phrase ‘in the offing’

entries.definition_en: the part of the sea visible from the shore, beyond the anchoring area
entries.example_cn: 船驶向离岸海域，那里的水域更平静。
entries.example_en: The ship sailed out into the offing where the waters were calmer.

entries.definition_en: lacking cordiality; unfriendly
entries.example_cn: 经理冷淡的态度让新员工感到不受欢迎。
entries.example_en: The manager's offish attitude made the new employee feel unwelcome.

entries.definition_en: to remove the load from a container or vehicle
entries.example_cn: 工人们花了一上午的时间从船上卸货。
entries.example_en: The workers spent the morning offloading the cargo from the ship.

usage.label: 及物动词：offload something
usage.pattern: w22770r0 explicitly labels the unloading verb transitive.

entries.definition_cn: 将（计算机数据）传输到外围设备
entries.definition_en: to transfer computer data to a peripheral device
entries.example_cn: 技术人员需要将备份文件转储到外部硬盘上。
entries.example_en: The technician needs to offload the backup files to the external hard drive.

entries.definition_en: a separately printed article that originally appeared in a larger publication
entries.example_cn: 学者们经常收集学术期刊中的单行本以建立个人图书馆。
entries.example_en: Scholars often collect offprints from academic journals to build their personal libraries.

entries.definition_en: to compensate for something bad or unbalanced
entries.example_cn: 该公司计划通过植树来抵消其碳排放。
entries.example_en: The company plans to offset its carbon emissions by planting trees.

entries.definition_en: to make up for a mistake or problem
entries.example_cn: 你可以通过下次更努力工作来弥补你的错误。
entries.example_en: You can offset your mistake by working harder next time.

entries.definition_cn: 使墙、杆、管道等形成偏移或折角
entries.definition_en: form an offset in a wall, rod, pipe, or similar structure
entries.example_cn: 这根管道发生偏移，以避开承重梁。
entries.example_en: The pipe is offset to avoid the supporting beam.

entries.definition_en: to cause ink or paint to transfer to another surface
entries.example_cn: 处理湿页时，小心不要把墨水蹭到别处。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to offset the ink when handling the wet pages.

entries.definition_en: something that compensates for a loss or disadvantage
entries.example_cn: 奖金是对低薪的一种补偿。
entries.example_en: The bonus served as an offset for the low salary.

entries.definition_en: a shoot or branch growing from the base of a plant that can produce a new plant
entries.example_cn: 这株老植物长出了分株，后来发育成了新植株。
entries.example_en: The old plant produced offsets that grew into new plants.

entries.definition_en: the time when something is scheduled to start
entries.example_cn: 会议的开始时间是上午9点。
entries.example_en: The offset for the meeting is 9:00 AM.

entries.definition_en: a natural result that follows from development
entries.example_cn: 城市发展的自然结果是交通拥堵加剧。
entries.example_en: The offset of the city's growth was increased traffic.

entries.definition_en: a result that develops from a previous situation or event
entries.example_cn: 新部门是原研究团队的衍生机构。
entries.example_en: The new department was an offshoot of the original research team.

entries.definition_cn: 位于或涉及另一个国家的，尤指位于税收或劳动力成本较低国家的；海外的，境外的。
entries.definition_en: Located in or relating to another country, especially one with lower taxes or labor costs.
entries.example_cn: 美国公司使用海外服务，是因为那里的劳动力成本低。
entries.example_en: American companies use offshore services because of the cheap labor.

entries.definition_en: at some distance from the shore
entries.example_cn: 他们在离岸的岛上建了一座房子。
entries.example_en: They built a house on the offshore island.

entries.definition_cn: （风）离岸的，从陆地吹向海上的
entries.definition_en: of winds, blowing from the land toward the sea
entries.example_cn: 离岸风从陆地吹向海上。
entries.example_en: Offshore winds blew from the land toward the sea.

entries.definition_en: away from shore; away from land
entries.example_cn: 小船离岸驶向开阔的大海。
entries.example_en: The boat sailed offshore into the open sea.

entries.definition_cn: 将生产或业务活动（包括服务）转移到另一个地区或国家，以降低经营成本。

entries.example_cn: 这家公司把部分服务岗位转移到了海外，以降低劳动力成本。
entries.example_en: The company offshored some of its service jobs to reduce labor costs.

entries.definition_en: illegally beyond a prescribed line or area or ahead of the ball or puck
entries.example_cn: 这名球员在接球时处于越位位置。
entries.example_en: The player was offside when he received the pass.

entries.definition_en: (sport) the mistake of occupying an illegal position on the playing field
entries.example_cn: 裁判判罚前锋越位。
entries.example_en: The referee called an offside against the striker.

entries.definition_en: illegally in advance of the ball or puck
entries.example_cn: 他越位地移动去拦截球。
entries.example_en: He moved offside to intercept the ball.

entries.definition_en: the children or descendants of a person or animal
entries.example_cn: 狮子和它的幼崽在树荫下休息。
entries.example_en: The lion and its offspring were resting in the shade.

entries.example_en: The meeting produced no offspring in terms of new ideas.

entries.definition_en: a young animal that has not yet grown up

entries.example_en: The mother bird fed her offspring with worms.

entries.example_en: The director gave instructions offstage while the actors rehearsed.

entries.definition_en: concealed from public view or attention
entries.example_cn: 谈判在远离媒体的幕后秘密进行。
entries.example_en: The negotiations took place offstage, away from the media.

entries.definition_en: behind the scenes; not on stage
entries.example_cn: 特效是在幕后制作的，然后投射到屏幕上。
entries.example_en: The special effects were created offstage and projected onto the screen.

entries.definition_en: not in public
entries.example_cn: 他们私下讨论了那个敏感问题，以避免引起争议。
entries.example_en: They discussed the sensitive issue offstage to avoid controversy.

entries.definition_en: the area of a stage that is not visible to the audience
entries.example_cn: 幕布升起前，演员们在舞台侧面准备好了戏服。
entries.example_en: The actors prepared their costumes offstage before the curtain rose.

entries.definition_en: many times at short intervals
entries.example_cn: 他经常去村里的祖母家。
entries.example_en: Oft he would visit his grandmother in the village.

entries.definition_en: many times at short intervals

entries.example_en: It often rains in this city during the summer.

entries.definition_en: frequently or in great quantities
entries.example_cn: 她周末经常去看望祖母。
entries.example_en: She often visits her grandmother on weekends.

entries.definition_en: in many cases or instances
entries.example_cn: 在许多情况下，最好的解决方案往往是最简单的。
entries.example_en: Often, the best solution is the simplest one.

entries.definition_en: more often or more frequently
entries.example_cn: 夏天比冬天更常下雨。
entries.example_en: It rains oftener in the summer than in the winter.

entries.definition_en: frequently; often
entries.example_cn: 冬天公交车经常晚点。
entries.example_en: Oftentimes, the bus arrives late during the winter.

entries.definition_en: often; frequently
entries.example_cn: 风暴来临前，那座旧钟频繁地发出响亮的钟声。
entries.example_en: Ofttimes, the old clock chimed loudly before the storm broke.

entries.definition_en: a group or set of eight; an eight-part unit
entries.example_cn: 这幅图展示了由八个相互连接的符号组成的八元组。
entries.example_en: The diagram shows an ogdoad of interconnected symbols.

entries.definition_en: a decorative molding with an S-shaped curve, convex on top and concave on the bottom
entries.example_cn: 建筑师为屋顶线选择了S形线脚以增加优雅感。
entries.example_en: The architect chose an ogee for the roofline to add elegance.

entries.definition_cn: 由两个S形曲线构成的尖拱
entries.definition_en: a pointed arch formed by two ogee curves
entries.example_cn: 教堂门道上方饰有一个由两个S形曲线构成的尖拱。
entries.example_en: The church doorway is crowned by an ogee arch.

entries.definition_cn: 子弹、导弹或火箭的尖弧形头部
entries.definition_en: the pointed, curved nose of a bullet, missile, or rocket
entries.example_cn: 火箭的尖弧形头部经过设计，可承受极端高温。
entries.example_en: The ogive of the rocket was designed to withstand extreme temperatures.

entries.definition_cn: 累积分布函数所表示的曲线
entries.definition_en: the curve shown by a cumulative distribution function
entries.example_cn: 这条累积分布曲线显示了低于各个数值的观测值比例。
entries.example_en: The ogive shows the proportion of observations below each value.

entries.definition_cn: 哥特式尖拱，或哥特式拱顶的一条肋拱
entries.definition_en: a pointed Gothic arch, or a rib forming part of a Gothic vault
entries.example_cn: 大教堂的尖拱使拱顶呈现出特有的尖形。
entries.example_en: The cathedral's ogives give the vaulted ceiling its characteristic pointed shape.

entries.definition_cn: 用爱慕或色迷迷的目光盯着
entries.definition_en: to stare at someone with amorous or covetous intent
entries.example_cn: 当他在街上被陌生人用色迷迷的目光盯着时，他感到很不舒服。
entries.example_en: He felt uncomfortable when he was ogled by strangers on the street.

entries.definition_en: (folklore) a giant who likes to eat human beings
entries.example_cn: 孩子们害怕故事里的食人魔。
entries.example_en: The children were terrified of the ogre in the story.

entries.definition_en: a cruel wicked and inhuman person
entries.example_cn: 那个霸凌者被其他孩子当作恶棍对待。
entries.example_en: The bully was treated like an ogre by the other children.

entries.definition_en: a female ogre in folklore
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被女妖的故事吓坏了。
entries.example_en: The children were terrified by the story of the ogress.

entries.definition_en: used to show surprise
entries.example_cn: 哦，我没看见你在那儿。
entries.example_en: Oh, I didn't see you there.

entries.definition_en: used to show understanding, agreement, or realization
entries.example_cn: 哦，我现在明白了。
entries.example_en: Oh, I understand now.

entries.definition_en: used to show wonder, amazement, or awe
entries.example_cn: 哦，从上面看风景太令人惊叹了！
entries.example_en: Oh, the view from the top is amazing!

entries.definition_cn: 用于引出随口或恼怒的评论
entries.definition_en: used before an offhand or annoyed remark
entries.example_cn: 哦，你又迟到了。
entries.example_en: Oh, you're late again.

entries.definition_cn: 发出“哦”的声音；表示惊讶或认可的口头表达
entries.definition_en: an utterance of oh; a spoken expression of surprise or acknowledgement
entries.example_cn: 当她看到礼物时，发出了一声惊讶的“哦”。
entries.example_en: She let out an oh of surprise when she saw the gift.

entries.definition_cn: 发出“哦”的声音；表示惊讶
entries.definition_en: to utter the interjection oh; to express surprise
entries.example_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，大声地“哦”了一声。
entries.example_en: He ohed loudly when he heard the news.

entries.definition_cn: 拉丁字母 O/o 的名称
entries.definition_en: the name of the Latin-script letter O/o
entries.example_cn: 单词“oh”以字母 O 开头。
entries.example_en: The word 'oh' starts with the letter oh.

entries.definition_cn: 数字 0（特别是在语音表示中）
entries.definition_en: the digit 0 (especially in representations of speech)
entries.example_cn: 在电话号码中，第一位数字是零。
entries.example_en: In the phone number, the first digit is oh.

entries.definition_en: an exclamation showing worry or that something is wrong
entries.example_cn: 哎呀，我忘了锁门！
entries.example_en: Oh-oh, I forgot to lock the door!

entries.definition_en: a unit of electrical resistance equal to the resistance between two points on a conductor when a potential difference of one volt between them produces a current of one ampere
entries.example_cn: 导线的电阻以欧姆为单位测量。
entries.example_en: The resistance of the wire was measured in ohms.

entries.definition_en: relating to or measured in ohms
entries.example_cn: 这根导线的电阻是欧姆性的。
entries.example_en: The resistance of the wire is ohmic.

entries.definition_en: an instrument used to measure electrical resistance in ohms
entries.example_cn: 技术员使用欧姆表检查电路的电阻。
entries.example_en: The technician used an ohmmeter to check the resistance of the circuit.

entries.definition_en: a slippery liquid that does not mix with water
entries.example_cn: 她把油洒在了地板上。
entries.example_en: She spilled oil on the floor.

entries.definition_en: edible fats obtained from plants
entries.example_cn: 我们使用植物油烹饪。
entries.example_en: We use oil for cooking.

entries.definition_en: a dark liquid consisting mainly of hydrocarbons
entries.example_cn: 原油埋藏在地底深处。
entries.example_en: Oil is found deep underground.

entries.definition_en: paint made with oil and pigment used by artists
entries.example_cn: 艺术家仔细地混合油画颜料。
entries.example_en: The artist mixed the oil paints carefully.

entries.definition_en: to apply oil to something, especially to lubricate it
entries.example_cn: 他给铰链涂了油以便它们能顺畅运转。
entries.example_en: He oiled the hinges to make them work smoothly.

entries.definition_en: to apply oil or ointment to someone, especially in a religious ceremony
entries.example_cn: 神父为病人傅油。
entries.example_en: The priest oiled the sick man.

entries.definition_en: powered by burning oil
entries.example_cn: 那座旧工厂使用燃油锅炉来给大楼供暖。
entries.example_en: The old factory used an oil-fired boiler to heat the building.

entries.definition_en: cloth treated on one side with a drying oil or synthetic resin
entries.example_cn: 桌子上铺着一块防水的油布。
entries.example_en: The table was covered with a waterproof oilcloth.

entries.definition_en: covered or treated with oil
entries.example_cn: 机器零件被涂油以防生锈。
entries.example_en: The machine parts were oiled to prevent rust.

entries.definition_en: an oil tanker; a cargo ship designed to carry oil in bulk
entries.example_cn: 那艘油轮停靠在炼油厂卸货。
entries.example_en: The oiler docked at the refinery to unload its cargo.

entries.definition_en: an oil well
entries.example_cn: 人们在北海偏远地区发现了一口新的油井。
entries.example_en: A new oiler was discovered in the remote region of the North Sea.

entries.definition_en: a worker, especially in a ship's engine room, who oils machinery
entries.example_cn: 该船的船员包括一名熟练的加油工，负责维护主发动机。
entries.example_en: The ship's crew included a skilled oiler who maintained the main engines.

entries.definition_en: a region rich in petroleum deposits, especially one with producing oil wells
entries.example_cn: 该公司在该油田钻探了数口新井。
entries.example_en: The company drilled several new wells in the oilfield.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being oily
entries.example_cn: 鱼皮的油性使其难以处理。
entries.example_en: The oiliness of the fish skin made it difficult to handle.

entries.definition_cn: 自鸣得意、讨好且自私自利的举止；油滑奉承
entries.definition_en: smug, self-serving, or obsequiously ingratiating behavior
entries.example_cn: 他在会议上的自私自利的殷勤惹恼了其他同事。
entries.example_en: His oiliness during the meeting annoyed the other colleagues.

entries.definition_en: a male person who owns or operates oil wells
entries.example_cn: 这位富有的石油业者向大学捐赠了数百万美元。
entries.example_en: The wealthy oilman donated millions to the university.

entries.definition_en: a male worker who produces or sells petroleum
entries.example_cn: 这位石油工人在偏远的沙漠地区工作了数十年。
entries.example_en: The oilman worked in the remote desert region for decades.

entries.definition_en: a seed that is used to produce oil
entries.example_cn: 大豆是一种常用于烹饪和工业的油料种子。
entries.example_en: Soybeans are a common oilseed used in cooking and industry.

entries.definition_cn: 用于生产植物油的油料作物
entries.definition_en: a plant grown for seeds that are used commercially to produce vegetable oil
entries.example_cn: 油菜是一种因其食用油而被广泛种植的油料作物。
entries.example_en: Canola is an oilseed grown widely for its edible oil.

entries.definition_en: a waterproof coat made from cotton fabric treated with oil and pigment
entries.example_cn: 水手穿上油布雨衣以抵御大雨。
entries.example_en: The sailor put on his oilskin to protect against the heavy rain.

entries.definition_cn: 经过油和颜料处理以防水的棉布
entries.definition_en: cotton cloth treated with oil and pigment to make it waterproof
entries.example_cn: 这顶帐篷用油布制成，可以让露营者保持干燥。
entries.example_en: The tent was made of oilskin to keep the campers dry.

entries.definition_cn: 水手穿的防风雨服装，采用天然或合成防水材料制成
entries.definition_en: foul-weather clothing worn by sailors, made of natural or synthetic waterproof material
entries.example_cn: 船员们出舱到甲板上之前穿上了防风雨服。
entries.example_en: The crew put on their oilskins before going out on deck.

entries.definition_en: containing an unusual amount of grease or oil
entries.example_cn: 油腻的皮肤使得化妆变得困难。
entries.example_en: The oily skin made it difficult to apply makeup.

entries.definition_en: coated or covered with oil
entries.example_cn: 机械师将沾满油污的抹布扔进了垃圾桶。
entries.example_en: The mechanic wiped the oily rags into the bin.

entries.definition_en: smeared or soiled with grease or oil
entries.example_cn: 泄漏后，地板变得油腻且湿滑。
entries.example_en: The floor was oily and slippery after the spill.

entries.definition_cn: 令人不悦地过分圆滑或谄媚的
entries.definition_en: unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech
entries.example_cn: 他圆滑的举止让会议上的每个人都感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: His oily manner made everyone feel uncomfortable during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: to make a high-pitched cry characteristic of pigs
entries.example_cn: 当它看到食物时，猪大声地叫了起来。
entries.example_en: The pig oinked loudly when it saw the food.

entries.definition_en: the sound made by a pig
entries.example_cn: 猪叫声从房子后面的谷仓里传来。
entries.example_en: The sound of oinking came from the barn behind the house.

entries.definition_cn: 用于模仿猪叫声的拟声词
entries.definition_en: used to imitate the sound made by a pig
entries.example_cn: 孩子们笑着喊道：“哼哼！”
entries.example_en: The children laughed and shouted, “Oink, oink!”

entries.definition_en: a semisolid preparation containing medicine applied externally as a remedy or to soothe irritation
entries.example_cn: 每天两次将药膏涂抹在患处。
entries.example_en: Apply the ointment to the affected area twice a day.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: Used with both countable and uncountable grammar.

entries.definition_cn: 用于涂抹或膏油礼的物质，尤指宗教仪式中的膏油
entries.definition_en: a substance used to anoint someone or something, especially in a religious ritual
entries.example_cn: 牧师在涂油仪式中使用了这种膏油。
entries.example_en: The priest used the ointment during the anointing ritual.

entries.definition_cn: 旧时土耳其、埃及、匈牙利和罗马尼亚的重量单位，通常略超过1千克
entries.definition_en: a former Turkish, Egyptian, Hungarian, and Romanian unit of weight, usually a little more than 1 kilogram
entries.example_cn: 商人用奥卡（土耳其重量单位）称量香料。
entries.example_en: The merchant weighed the spices in okas.

entries.definition_cn: 埃及的容量单位，旧时土耳其也使用，约合1.2升
entries.definition_en: a unit of volume in Egypt, and formerly Turkey, of about 1.2 litres
entries.example_cn: 她用奥卡（土耳其液体容量单位）量了茶。
entries.example_en: She measured the tea in an oka.

entries.definition_cn: 一种南美洲的木酢浆草，因其可食用的块茎而被种植
entries.definition_en: South American wood sorrel cultivated for its edible tubers
entries.example_cn: 园丁们在潮湿的土壤里种植了木酢浆草（oka）。
entries.example_en: The gardeners planted okas in the damp soil.

entries.definition_en: a small, forest-dwelling animal resembling a giraffe but with a short neck and striped legs
entries.example_cn: 珍稀的霍加狓仅生活在刚果茂密的森林中。
entries.example_en: The rare okapi is found only in the dense forests of the Congo.

entries.definition_en: being satisfactory or in good condition
entries.example_cn: 食物还可以吗？
entries.example_en: Is the food okay?

entries.definition_en: in a satisfactory or adequate manner
entries.example_cn: 工作做得还可以。
entries.example_en: The job was done okay.

entries.definition_en: to give sanction or approval to
entries.example_cn: 董事会批准了新政策。
entries.example_en: The board okayed the new policy.

entries.definition_en: an endorsement or approval
entries.example_cn: 经理批准了该项目。
entries.example_en: The manager gave the okay for the project.

entries.definition_en: an endorsement or approval
entries.example_cn: 委员会认可了这项新提议。
entries.example_en: The committee gave its okeh to the new proposal.

entries.definition_cn: 土耳其的一种牌（或骨牌）游戏，玩家设法收集特定的牌组
entries.definition_en: a Turkish tile game in which players try to collect certain groups of tiles
entries.example_cn: 他们晚饭后玩土耳其牌戏。
entries.example_en: They played okey after dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 秋葵（植物）的长绿色可食用蒴果
entries.definition_en: long green edible beaked pods of the okra plant
entries.example_cn: 她在汤里加了一些新鲜的秋葵。
entries.example_en: She added some fresh okra to the soup.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: often used as an uncountable food noun

entries.definition_cn: 秋葵的长而黏滑的绿色嫩荚，常用于汤和炖菜
entries.definition_en: long mucilaginous green pods; may be simmered or sauteed but used especially in soups and stews
entries.example_cn: 我们用大蒜和洋葱炒了秋葵。
entries.example_en: We sauteed the okras with garlic and onions.

entries.definition_en: tall coarse annual of Old World tropics widely cultivated in southern United States and West Indies for its long mucilaginous green pods used as basis for soups and stews
entries.example_cn: 秋葵是美国南部的一种流行蔬菜。
entries.example_en: Okra is a popular vegetable in the southern United States.

entries.definition_en: leaf or strip from a leaf of the talipot palm used in India for writing paper
entries.example_cn: 古代的手稿通常写在叶纸上。
entries.example_en: Ancient manuscripts were often written on ola leaves.

entries.definition_en: having lived for a long time or reached a specific age
entries.example_cn: 我的祖母很老了。
entries.example_en: My grandmother is very old.

entries.definition_en: existing for a long time; not new
entries.example_cn: 这是一本旧书。
entries.example_en: This is an old book.

entries.definition_en: belonging to a time before now
entries.example_cn: 我们正在看过去的照片。
entries.example_en: We are looking at old photos.

entries.definition_en: former; previous
entries.example_cn: 比起新工作，我更喜欢以前的工作。
entries.example_en: I prefer my old job to my new one.

entries.definition_en: skilled due to long experience
entries.example_cn: 他是这项工作的老手。
entries.example_en: He is an old hand at this job.

entries.definition_en: old people considered as a group
entries.example_cn: 老年人需要获得良好的医疗保健。
entries.example_en: The old need access to good healthcare.

entries.definition_en: very familiar through repeated experience
entries.example_cn: 我对这座城市很熟悉。
entries.example_en: I am old to this city.

entries.definition_en: having been stored or matured for a long time, especially of wine or other food
entries.example_cn: 这是一款产自该地区的陈年葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: This is an old wine from the region.

entries.definition_en: no longer in fashion or style
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件领口很高的过时连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She wore an old-fashioned dress with a high collar.

entries.definition_en: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
entries.example_cn: 那个笑话太老套了，我们已经听过一百遍了。
entries.example_en: That joke is old-hat; we've heard it a hundred times.

entries.definition_en: out of fashion
entries.example_cn: 在现代时尚中，戴高顶帽被视为过时之举。
entries.example_en: Wearing a top hat is considered old-hat in modern fashion.

entries.definition_en: long-established
entries.example_cn: 这家历史悠久的报纸已出版了一个多世纪。
entries.example_en: The old-line newspaper has been published for over a century.

entries.definition_en: adhering to conservative or reactionary principles
entries.example_cn: 该保守政党拒绝改变其政策。
entries.example_en: The old-line party refused to change its policies.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of a method, style, or way of thinking from a former era, often remembered for being inferior to or superior to the current method
entries.example_cn: 公司决定坚持使用老派的方法，而不是采用新技术。
entries.example_en: The company decided to stick with old-school methods rather than adopting new technology.

entries.definition_cn: 老派的（指嘻哈或说唱音乐）
entries.definition_en: of or relating to hip-hop or rap music of the late 1970s and 1980s
entries.example_cn: 比起现代的说唱风格，他更喜欢老派的嘻哈音乐。
entries.example_en: He prefers old-school hip-hop to the modern rap style.

entries.definition_cn: 保守的；传统的（指基督教或政治观点）
entries.definition_en: having conservative or traditional views on Christianity or politics
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家以他在政府问题上的保守观点而闻名。
entries.example_en: The politician is known for his old-school views on government.

entries.definition_cn: 旧式的；具有过去时代特色的
entries.definition_en: from or reminiscent of an earlier time or era; old-fashioned
entries.example_cn: 他喜欢听具有过去时代特色的音乐。
entries.example_en: He likes to listen to old-time music.

entries.definition_en: an experienced person who has given long service
entries.example_cn: 这位老资格的人知道这份工作的所有秘密。
entries.example_en: The old-timer knew all the secrets of the job.

entries.definition_en: an elderly man
entries.example_cn: 那位老家伙坐在门廊上看孩子们玩耍。
entries.example_en: The old-timer sat on the porch watching the children play.

entries.definition_cn: 具有刻板印象中老妇人缺点的；拘谨而爱挑剔的
entries.definition_en: having the stereotypical negative traits of an elderly woman, such as peevishness, primness, or fussiness
entries.example_cn: 她过分拘谨的举止使她对新生显得不友好。
entries.example_en: Her old-womanish manner made her seem unfriendly to the new students.

entries.definition_en: having the style or character of earlier times, especially in Europe
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店有着石墙和木梁的古老魅力。
entries.example_en: The hotel has an old-world charm with its stone walls and wooden beams.

entries.definition_en: relating to or belonging to a time long past
entries.example_cn: 他们怀着极大的怀旧之情谈论昔日的时光。
entries.example_en: They spoke of the olden days with great nostalgia.

entries.definition_en: having lived for a long time; aged
entries.example_cn: 老一辈人有不同的价值观。
entries.example_en: The older generation has different values.

entries.definition_cn: （用于区分同名父子中的）年长的
entries.definition_en: used to distinguish a father from his son of the same name
entries.example_cn: 年长的约翰是年幼约翰的父亲。
entries.example_en: John the older is the father of John the younger.

entries.definition_en: skilled through long experience
entries.example_cn: 她在这项工作上经验丰富。
entries.example_en: She is an older hand at this job.

entries.definition_en: a song that was popular in the past
entries.example_cn: 他们随着一首20世纪80年代的老歌跳舞。
entries.example_en: They danced to an oldie from the 1980s.

entries.definition_en: somewhat old
entries.example_cn: 这辆车有些老了，尽管车龄已久，运行依然平稳。
entries.example_en: The oldish car still runs smoothly despite its age.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being old; the opposite of newness
entries.example_cn: 数据的陈旧性使其无法用于现代分析。
entries.example_en: The oldness of the data made it unreliable for modern analysis.

entries.definition_en: the state of being old; the opposite of being young
entries.example_cn: 这栋建筑年久失修的状态在其摇摇欲坠的墙壁上显而易见。
entries.example_en: The oldness of the building was evident in its crumbling walls.

entries.definition_en: an elderly person
entries.example_cn: 社区中心专门为老人组织了活动。
entries.example_en: The community center organized activities specifically for the oldster.

entries.definition_en: an experienced person who has served for a long time
entries.example_cn: 作为公司的老资格员工，他了解所有的秘密。
entries.example_en: As an oldtimer of the company, he knows all the secrets.

entries.definition_en: an elderly man
entries.example_cn: 这位老男人给孩子们讲了他年轻时的故事。
entries.example_en: The oldtimer told stories about his youth to the children.

entries.definition_en: containing an unusual amount of grease or oil
entries.example_cn: 这种酱汁含油量极高，用叉子很难食用。
entries.example_en: The oleaginous texture of the sauce made it difficult to eat with a fork.

entries.definition_cn: 令人不悦地过分圆滑或谄媚的
entries.definition_en: unpleasantly and excessively suave or ingratiating in manner or speech
entries.example_cn: 他试图赢得委员会成员欢心的圆滑举动显而易见，却令人反感。
entries.example_en: His oleaginous attempts to win favor with the committee members were obvious.

entries.definition_en: an ornamental but poisonous flowering shrub with narrow evergreen leaves and clusters of fragrant white, pink, or red flowers

entries.definition_en: at a previous time

entries.example_en: Once upon a time, there was a king.

entries.definition_en: a quick look at something to see what it is like
entries.example_cn: 她离开前快速扫视了一下房间。
entries.example_en: She gave the room a quick once-over before leaving.

entries.definition_en: a quick cleaning or polishing of something
entries.example_cn: 我用布把桌子快速擦了一遍。
entries.example_en: I gave the table a quick once-over with a cloth.

entries.definition_en: a disease caused by threadlike roundworms deposited under the skin by black flies, which can cause blindness if the eyes are involved; common in Africa and tropical America
entries.example_cn: 公共卫生官员正在努力消除热带美洲受影响地区的河盲症。
entries.example_en: Public health officials are working to eradicate onchocerciasis in the affected regions of tropical America.

entries.definition_en: a type of orchid with slender branches of small yellow and brown flowers; often grown indoors
entries.example_cn: 她细心地给她的文心兰浇水，以保持花朵的健康。
entries.example_en: She carefully watered her oncidium to keep the delicate flowers healthy.

entries.definition_cn: 在发生突变或高表达时可促使正常细胞转变为癌细胞的基因
entries.definition_en: a gene that can contribute to the conversion of a normal cell into a cancerous cell when mutated or highly expressed
entries.example_cn: 研究人员确定了一个导致肿瘤快速生长的特定癌基因。
entries.example_en: Researchers identified a specific oncogene responsible for the tumor's rapid growth.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study or treatment of cancer
entries.example_cn: 肿瘤科专门治疗各种类型的癌症。
entries.example_en: The oncologic department specializes in treating various types of cancer.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study or treatment of cancer
entries.example_cn: 肿瘤科专门治疗各种类型的癌症。
entries.example_en: The oncological department specializes in treating various types of cancer.

entries.definition_en: a doctor who specializes in treating cancer
entries.example_cn: 肿瘤学家建议对该患者进行化疗。
entries.example_en: The oncologist recommended chemotherapy for the patient.

entries.definition_cn: 研究和治疗肿瘤的医学分支
entries.definition_en: the branch of medicine concerned with the study and treatment of tumors
entries.example_cn: 她在医院专门从事肿瘤学工作。
entries.example_en: She specializes in oncology at the hospital.

entries.definition_en: moving toward one
entries.example_cn: 迎面而来的交通迫使我们停车。
entries.example_en: The oncoming traffic forced us to stop.

entries.definition_en: the approach or onset of something
entries.example_cn: 冬天来临时，鸟儿会迁徙。
entries.example_en: At the oncoming of winter, the birds migrate.

entries.definition_en: The first positive integer, or the numeral representing it.
entries.example_cn: 一是第一个数字。
entries.example_en: One is the first number.

entries.definition_en: a single person or thing
entries.example_cn: 他是最好的球员之一。
entries.example_en: He is one of the best players.

entries.definition_en: referring to a single unit or thing
entries.example_cn: 我需要再一个苹果。
entries.example_en: I need one more apple.

entries.definition_en: having the character of a unit
entries.example_cn: 这是一个完整的系统。
entries.example_en: It is one complete system.

entries.definition_en: Indefinite or unspecified in time, identity, or choice.
entries.example_cn: 总有一天，我会去日本。
entries.example_en: One day, I will visit Japan.

entries.definition_en: of the same kind or quality
entries.example_cn: 他们都是一家人。
entries.example_en: They are all one family.

entries.definition_cn: 由多个部分组成的整体
entries.definition_en: made by combining separate components into a single entity
entries.example_cn: 这辆车是一台机器。
entries.example_en: The car is one machine.

entries.definition_en: very; used as an intensifier
entries.example_cn: 那是非常炎热的一天。
entries.example_en: It was one hot day.

entries.definition_en: a short play that consists of only one act
entries.example_cn: 剧团昨晚上演了一部经典的独幕剧。
entries.example_en: The theater group performed a classic one-acter last night.

entries.definition_cn: 篮球中第一球罚进后才能获得第二次罚球机会的罚球回合
entries.definition_en: in basketball, a free-throw opportunity in which the first shot must be made to earn a second
entries.example_cn: 她罚进了这个一加一罚球，将比分扳平。
entries.example_en: She made the one-and-one to tie the game.

entries.definition_en: having only one arm
entries.example_cn: 那个独臂男子用假肢打开了门。
entries.example_en: The one-armed man used his prosthetic to open the door.

entries.definition_en: having a single cell (and thus not divided into cells)
entries.example_cn: 变形虫是简单的单细胞生物。
entries.example_en: Amoebas are simple one-celled organisms.

entries.definition_en: lasting one day
entries.example_cn: 我们去城市进行了一日游。
entries.example_en: We went on a one-day trip to the city.

entries.definition_cn: 缺乏深度、复杂性或可信度的；单薄的
entries.definition_en: lacking depth, complexity, or believability; flat
entries.example_cn: 电影中的这个角色缺乏深度和复杂性，显得很单薄。
entries.example_en: The character in the movie was one-dimensional, lacking depth and complexity.

entries.definition_cn: 一维的；只有一个维度的
entries.definition_en: of or in or along or relating to a line; involving or having a single dimension
entries.example_cn: 这个问题可以用一维模型来解决。
entries.example_en: The problem can be solved using a one-dimensional model.

entries.definition_en: one part of a whole divided into eight equal parts
entries.example_cn: 她吃了蛋糕的八分之一。
entries.example_en: She ate one-eighth of the cake.

entries.definition_en: having only one eye
entries.example_cn: 那个独眼海盗眯着眼睛望着地平线。
entries.example_en: The one-eyed pirate squinted at the horizon.

entries.definition_en: one part in five equal parts
entries.example_cn: 她吃了蛋糕的五分之一。
entries.example_en: She ate one-fifth of the cake.

entries.definition_en: one of four equal parts
entries.example_cn: 她吃了四分之一的蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She ate one-fourth of the cake.

entries.definition_en: one of two equal parts of a whole
entries.example_cn: 她吃了一半的披萨。
entries.example_en: She ate one-half of the pizza.

entries.definition_en: using or performed with only one hand
entries.example_cn: 她在舞台上做了一个单手侧手翻。
entries.example_en: She performed a one-handed cartwheel across the stage.

entries.definition_cn: 一场比赛中投手仅让对手击出一支安打
entries.definition_en: a game in which a pitcher allows the opposing team only one hit
entries.example_cn: 这位新秀投手在对阵对手时投出了一场仅让对方击出一支安打的比赛。
entries.example_en: The rookie pitcher threw a one-hitter against the rivals.

entries.definition_en: small and insignificant
entries.example_cn: 他们住在一个只有几家商店的偏僻小镇。
entries.example_en: They live in a one-horse town with only a few shops.

entries.definition_en: being number 100,000,000 in a series
entries.example_cn: 第1亿位顾客获得了一份特别奖品。
entries.example_en: The one-hundred-millionth customer received a special prize.

entries.definition_en: one part in a hundred million equal parts
entries.example_cn: 中彩票的概率不到一亿分之一。
entries.example_en: The probability of winning the lottery is less than one-hundred-millionth.

entries.definition_en: a single part among one hundred thousand equal parts
entries.example_cn: 中彩票的概率不到十万分之一。
entries.example_en: The probability of winning the lottery is less than one-hundred-thousandth.

entries.definition_en: one part in a hundred equal parts
entries.example_cn: 误差范围不超过百分之一度。
entries.example_en: The error margin was no more than one-hundredth of a degree.

entries.definition_en: being number 100 in a series
entries.example_cn: 第一百名跑步者在中午刚过时冲过了终点线。
entries.example_en: The one-hundredth runner crossed the finish line just after noon.

entries.definition_en: a short joke told in a single sentence
entries.example_cn: 他讲了一个有趣的笑话，逗得大家哈哈大笑。
entries.example_en: He told a funny one-liner that made everyone laugh.

entries.definition_cn: 旨在被媒体引用的简短、令人印象深刻的话
entries.definition_en: a short, memorable remark intended to be quoted in the media
entries.example_cn: 部长说了一句犀利的短评，很快就成了媒体争相引用的话。
entries.example_en: The minister delivered a sharp one-liner that quickly became a sound bite.

entries.definition_cn: 由一行输入组成的命令或小型计算机程序
entries.definition_en: a command or small computer program written as a single line of input
entries.example_cn: 这个脚本可以在终端中用一行命令运行。
entries.example_en: The script can be run with a one-liner in the terminal.

entries.definition_en: designed for or restricted to a single person
entries.example_cn: 这是一项需要极大体力的单人工作。
entries.example_en: This is a one-man job that requires great strength.

entries.definition_en: one part of a whole that has been divided into nine equal parts
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕的九分之一留作甜点。
entries.example_en: One-ninth of the cake was left for dessert.

entries.definition_en: unique, singular, or sui generis
entries.example_cn: 这幅独一无二的画作是由一位当地艺术家创作的。
entries.example_en: This one-of-a-kind painting was created by a local artist.

entries.definition_en: a unique example
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件来自古埃及的独特文物。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a one-of-a-kind artifact from ancient Egypt.

entries.definition_en: a happening that occurs only once and is not repeated
entries.example_cn: 那场音乐会是一次性活动。
entries.example_en: The concert was a one-off event.

usage.label: Commonwealth; idiomatic
usage.pattern: one-off noun for something done only once

entries.definition_en: directly between two individuals
entries.example_cn: 他们就计划进行了一次一对一的交谈。
entries.example_en: They had a one-on-one conversation about their plans.

entries.definition_en: being a system of play in which an individual defensive player guards an individual offensive player
entries.example_cn: 教练决定采用人盯人的防守策略。
entries.example_en: The coach decided to use a one-on-one defense strategy.

entries.definition_en: (of two persons) in direct encounter
entries.example_cn: 两位对手在最后一轮面对面相遇。
entries.example_en: The two rivals met one-on-one in the final round.

entries.definition_en: controlled by only one political party
entries.example_cn: 这个国家实行一党制，只允许一个政党执政。
entries.example_en: The country has a one-party system where only one political party is allowed to govern.

entries.definition_en: designed for or restricted to a single person
entries.example_cn: 这是一个单人帐篷。
entries.example_en: This is a one-person tent.

entries.definition_en: made as a single piece of clothing
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件连体泳衣去海滩。
entries.example_en: She wore a one-piece swimsuit to the beach.

entries.definition_en: one of four equal parts
entries.example_cn: 她吃了四分之一的蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She ate one-quarter of the cake.

entries.definition_en: one part out of seven equal parts
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕的七分之一留作甜点。
entries.example_en: One-seventh of the cake was left for dessert.

entries.definition_cn: 偏袒某个人或某一方而忽视另一方的
entries.definition_en: favoring one person or side over another
entries.example_cn: 法官被指控对该案件持有偏袒一方的观点。
entries.example_en: The judge was accused of having a one-sided view of the case.

entries.definition_en: involving only one part or side
entries.example_cn: 这场单方面的辩论忽略了相反的观点。
entries.example_en: The one-sided argument ignored the opposing viewpoint.
