entries.definition_en: having only one side
entries.example_cn: 莫比乌斯带的单面结构使其难以区分内侧和外侧。
entries.example_en: The one-sided form of a Möbius strip makes it difficult to distinguish inside from outside.

entries.definition_en: in a one-sided or biased manner
entries.example_cn: 这场辩论是片面进行的，另一方没有机会回应。
entries.example_en: The argument was conducted one-sidedly, with no opportunity for the other party to respond.

entries.definition_cn: 以在物理上偏向某物一侧或只使用某物一侧的方式
entries.definition_en: in a manner which physically favors or uses only one side of something
entries.example_cn: 那个人嘴角歪向一边笑了。
entries.example_en: The man smiled one-sidedly.

entries.definition_en: one part of a whole that has been divided into six equal parts
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕的六分之一还留在盘子里。
entries.example_en: One-sixth of the cake was left on the plate.

entries.definition_en: an early ballroom dance; precursor to the fox-trot
entries.example_cn: 他们在婚礼招待会上表演了一段活泼的一步舞。
entries.example_en: They performed a lively one-step at the wedding reception.

entries.definition_en: dance the one-step
entries.example_cn: 这对夫妇随着爵士乐队的节奏跳了一步舞。
entries.example_en: The couple danced the one-step to the rhythm of the jazz band.

entries.definition_en: Providing everything a customer needs in one place so they do not have to visit another location.
entries.example_cn: 这家购物中心是满足您全家需求的一站式目的地。
entries.example_en: This shopping mall is a one-stop destination for all your family needs.

entries.definition_en: A wholesaler that supplies the music industry.
entries.example_cn: 唱片公司与一家主要的音乐业批发商签订了合同。
entries.example_en: The record label signed a contract with a major one-stop.

entries.definition_en: one part out of ten equal parts
entries.example_cn: 蛋糕的十分之一被吃掉了。
entries.example_en: One-tenth of the cake was eaten.

entries.definition_en: one of three equal parts of a divisible whole
entries.example_cn: 她吃了蛋糕的三分之一。
entries.example_en: She ate one-third of the cake.

entries.definition_cn: 曾经的；过去某一时期的
entries.definition_en: belonging to a specific period in the past and not continuing to the present
entries.example_cn: 他曾是该俱乐部的主席。
entries.example_en: He was the one-time president of the club.

entries.definition_en: used of relations such that each member of one set is associated with one member of a second set
entries.example_cn: 老师为 struggling 的学生提供一对一辅导。
entries.example_en: The teacher offers one-to-one tutoring to struggling students.

entries.definition_en: limited to one idea or thought
entries.example_cn: 他思想狭隘，无法看到其他解决方案。
entries.example_en: His one-track thinking made it impossible for him to see other solutions.

entries.definition_en: having a single set of lines so that trains can run only in one direction at a time
entries.example_cn: 这条铁路是单轨的，火车必须互相等待才能通过。
entries.example_en: The railway line is one-track, so trains must wait for each other to pass.

entries.definition_cn: （球类运动中）两人之间的快速一传一接
entries.definition_en: A quick pass between two players in a ball game.
entries.example_cn: 前锋通过一个巧妙的配合打进了球。
entries.example_en: The striker scored with a clever one-two.

entries.definition_en: Two punches delivered in rapid succession.
entries.example_cn: 拳击手打出了一记毁灭性的连击。
entries.example_en: The boxer landed a devastating one-two.

entries.definition_en: Two things that happen in short succession.
entries.example_cn: 这家公司接连遭受了两项坏消息的打击。
entries.example_en: The company suffered a one-two punch of bad news.

entries.definition_cn: 同一车队两辆车包揽冠亚军
entries.definition_en: A race victory where two cars from the same team finish first and second.
entries.example_cn: 法拉利在大奖赛中包揽了冠亚军。
entries.example_en: Ferrari achieved a one-two in the Grand Prix.

entries.definition_en: very quickly; immediately
entries.example_cn: 转眼间，孩子们就离开了房间。
entries.example_en: One-two-three, the children were out of the room.

entries.definition_en: the practice of trying to appear superior to someone else, especially in conversation or competition
entries.example_cn: 他们的争论充满了争强好胜。
entries.example_en: Their argument was full of one-upmanship.

entries.definition_en: allowing movement in only one direction
entries.example_cn: 这是一条单向街道，车辆只能朝一个方向行驶。
entries.example_en: This is a one-way street where traffic moves in only one direction.

entries.definition_cn: 由一名女性完成或专为一名女性设计的
entries.definition_en: designed for or involving one woman
entries.example_cn: 她主演了一部关于她一生的独幕剧。
entries.example_en: She starred in a one-woman play about her life.

entries.definition_en: one year of age
entries.example_cn: 那个一岁大的孩子正在学走路。
entries.example_en: The one-year-old child is learning to walk.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or suggestive of dreams
entries.example_cn: 这部小说如梦似幻的特质让读者捉摸不透。
entries.example_en: The oneiric quality of the novel kept readers guessing.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being united into one
entries.example_cn: 这个团队的统一性体现在他们完美的配合上。
entries.example_en: The oneness of the team was evident in their perfect coordination.

entries.definition_en: not easily borne; wearing
entries.example_cn: 打扫整个房子这项繁重的任务花了一整天。
entries.example_en: The onerous task of cleaning the entire house took all day.

entries.definition_en: plural of one
entries.example_cn: 比起青苹果，我更喜欢红苹果。
entries.example_en: I prefer the red apples to the green ones.

entries.definition_cn: one 的复数形式（名词用法）
entries.definition_en: plural of one
entries.example_cn: 数字11中有两个1。
entries.example_en: The number 11 contains two ones.

entries.definition_en: a senior or first team
entries.example_cn: 主力队去年赢得了冠军。
entries.example_en: The ones won the championship last year.

entries.definition_en: cells located on the ground floor
entries.example_cn: 一楼的铺位更便宜。
entries.example_en: The ones on the ground floor are cheaper.

entries.definition_en: third-person singular simple present indicative of one
entries.example_cn: 他每天数数。
entries.example_en: He ones the number every day.

entries.definition_en: formerly the stated thing; having been so in the past
entries.example_cn: 他曾是总统的朋友。
entries.example_en: He was a onetime friend of the president.

entries.definition_en: currently happening or continuing
entries.example_cn: 这项进行中的调查尚未产生任何结果。
entries.example_en: The ongoing investigation has not yet produced any results.

entries.definition_en: bulbous plant having hollow leaves cultivated worldwide for its rounded edible bulb
entries.example_cn: 洋葱是许多菜系中的常见食材。
entries.example_en: Onions are a common ingredient in many cuisines.

entries.definition_en: the bulb of an onion plant
entries.example_cn: 她切了洋葱做汤。
entries.example_en: She chopped the onion for the soup.

entries.definition_en: an aromatic flavorful vegetable
entries.example_cn: 这汤闻起来像洋葱。
entries.example_en: The soup smells like onion.

entries.definition_en: a very thin, strong, and translucent paper used for making carbon copies
entries.example_cn: 他在复写纸上打印合同，以便一次性制作多份副本。
entries.example_en: He typed the contract on onionskin so he could make several copies at once.

entries.definition_en: via a computer network
entries.example_cn: 你可以在线购买车票。
entries.example_en: You can buy tickets online.

entries.definition_en: connected to a computer network
entries.example_cn: 该网站目前处于联网状态。
entries.example_en: The website is currently online.

entries.definition_en: active and operating, especially of a system or service
entries.example_cn: 电力系统又恢复在线运行了。
entries.example_en: The power system is online again.

entries.definition_cn: 可在计算机系统上使用的
entries.definition_en: available on a computer system, even without a network connection
entries.example_cn: 按 F1 键访问在线帮助。
entries.example_en: Press F1 to access the online help.

entries.definition_en: a person who watches an event without participating in it
entries.example_cn: 围观的人群震惊地看着那场事故。
entries.example_en: The crowd of onlookers watched the accident with shock.

entries.definition_en: and nothing more
entries.example_cn: 我只有五美元。
entries.example_en: I only have five dollars.

entries.definition_cn: 不包括其他人或事物；单独地；仅仅
entries.definition_en: without anyone or anything else being included; alone or exclusively
entries.example_cn: 只有他一个人去了聚会。
entries.example_en: Only he went to the party.

entries.definition_en: merely; no more than
entries.example_cn: 这个计划只失败过一次。
entries.example_en: The plan only failed once.

entries.definition_cn: 用于 only to 结构，引出出乎意料或相反的结果
entries.definition_en: used before a to-infinitive to indicate an unexpected or contrary result
entries.example_cn: 他努力学习，结果却没能通过考试。
entries.example_en: He studied hard, only to fail the exam.

entries.definition_en: being the only one; single and isolated from others
entries.example_cn: 她是班上唯一的学生。
entries.example_en: She is the only student in the class.

entries.definition_en: exclusive of anyone or anything else
entries.example_cn: 这个房间仅供教师使用。
entries.example_en: This room is only for teachers.

entries.definition_en: as recently as
entries.example_cn: 他就在昨天还在这里。
entries.example_en: He was here only yesterday.

entries.definition_en: except that
entries.example_cn: 大家都来了，除了他。
entries.example_en: Everyone came only.

entries.definition_cn: 专名学的；与名称及其来源有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to the study of names and their origins
entries.example_cn: 专名分析揭示了该家族姓氏背后的文化影响。
entries.example_en: The onomastic analysis revealed the cultural influences on the family's surname.

entries.definition_cn: 人名等名称的书、列表或词汇表
entries.definition_en: a book, list, or vocabulary of names, especially names of people
entries.example_cn: 这位学者编纂了一份列出所有古希腊城邦名称的词表。
entries.example_en: The scholar compiled an onomasticon of all the ancient Greek city-states.

entries.definition_en: the study of the forms and origins of proper names
entries.example_cn: 这位教授专攻姓名学及姓氏历史。
entries.example_en: The professor specializes in onomastics and the history of family names.

entries.definition_cn: 拟声；形成或使用模仿所指声音的词语
entries.definition_en: the formation or use of words whose sounds imitate what they denote
entries.example_cn: “buzz”是一个拟声词的例子。
entries.example_en: The word 'buzz' is an example of onomatopoeia.

entries.definition_en: formed in imitation of a natural sound.
entries.example_cn: 单词“嗡嗡”是拟声词，因为它模仿了蜜蜂的声音。
entries.example_en: The word 'buzz' is onomatopoeic because it imitates the sound of a bee.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characterized by onomatopoeia.
entries.example_cn: 儿童书中的拟声词帮助他们学习了各种声音。
entries.example_en: The onomatopoeic words in the children's book helped them learn about sounds.

entries.definition_en: formed by imitating a natural sound
entries.example_cn: 拟声词“嗡嗡”描述了蜜蜂的声音。
entries.example_en: The onomatopoetic word 'buzz' describes the sound of a bee.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characterized by onomatopoeia
entries.example_cn: 这首诗中的拟声词模仿了雷声。
entries.example_en: The onomatopoetic words in the poem mimic the sound of thunder.

entries.definition_en: a sudden, powerful forward movement or flow
entries.example_cn: 一股突如其来的洪水淹没了山谷。
entries.example_en: A sudden onrush of water flooded the valley.

entries.definition_en: a military attack launched against an enemy
entries.example_cn: 将军下令立即渡河进攻。
entries.example_en: The general ordered an immediate onrush across the river.

entries.definition_en: the beginning or early stages of something
entries.example_cn: 春天的到来带来了温暖的温度和盛开的花朵。
entries.example_en: The onset of spring brought warmer temperatures and blooming flowers.

entries.definition_en: (archaic) an attack or assault, especially by an army
entries.example_cn: 黎明时分，军队的进攻让敌人措手不及。
entries.example_en: The army's onset at dawn caught the enemy by surprise.

entries.definition_en: toward or onto the land
entries.example_cn: 巨浪猛烈地拍向陆地。
entries.example_en: The waves crashed onshore with great force.

entries.definition_cn: 向岸的；从海上吹向陆地的
entries.definition_en: (of winds) blowing from the sea toward the land
entries.example_cn: 海风让炎热的下午变得凉爽。
entries.example_en: The onshore breeze cooled the hot afternoon.

entries.definition_en: located on the edge of the land
entries.example_cn: 他们在海滩附近的陆地上建了一所房子。
entries.example_en: They built a house onshore near the beach.

entries.definition_en: not offside; being within the prescribed area of play
entries.example_cn: 那名球员接到传球时并未越位。
entries.example_en: The player was onside when he received the pass.

entries.definition_cn: 赞成并支持的；愿意配合的
entries.definition_en: in agreement or support; willing to cooperate
entries.example_cn: 经理解释了变动的原因，从而争取到了员工的支持。
entries.example_en: The manager kept the staff onside by explaining the reasons for the changes.

entries.definition_cn: 人或事物突然而猛烈的大量涌来
entries.definition_en: a sudden and overwhelming influx of people or things
entries.example_cn: 产品发布后，大量投诉突然涌向该公司。
entries.example_en: The company faced an onslaught of complaints after the product launch.

entries.definition_en: (military) an offensive against an enemy (using weapons)
entries.example_cn: 军队对堡垒发起了猛烈的进攻。
entries.example_en: The army launched a fierce onslaught on the fortress.

entries.definition_en: the rapid and continuous delivery of linguistic communication (spoken or written)
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家在辩论中滔滔不绝地发表演说。
entries.example_en: The politician delivered an onslaught of rhetoric during the debate.

entries.definition_en: on the stage
entries.example_cn: 导演从幕后发出指令，而演员们在舞台上排练。
entries.example_en: The director shouted instructions from backstage, while the actors rehearsed onstage.

entries.definition_en: situated or taking place on the area of a stage visible to the audience
entries.example_cn: 演员们在舞台上表演了最后一幕。
entries.example_en: The actors performed their final scene onstage.

entries.definition_en: arriving upon or on top of (speaking of a physical or metaphorical movement)
entries.example_cn: 她爬上了屋顶。
entries.example_en: She climbed onto the roof.

entries.definition_en: aware of
entries.example_cn: 他意识到了她在撒谎的事实。
entries.example_en: He was onto the fact that she was lying.

entries.definition_cn: 到（作为满射函数的陪域）
entries.definition_en: being an onto function with a codomain of
entries.example_cn: 该映射是到实数集的满射。
entries.example_en: The mapping is onto the set of real numbers.

entries.definition_en: attaining each of the values in its codomain; having its image equal to its codomain
entries.example_cn: 这个函数是满射的。
entries.example_en: This function is onto.

entries.definition_en: the biological process by which an individual organism develops and grows from a simple to a more complex form
entries.example_cn: 个体发生的研究揭示了单个细胞如何转变为复杂的人类。
entries.example_en: The study of ontogenesis reveals how a single cell transforms into a complex human being.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the origin and development of individual organisms
entries.example_cn: 这项研究侧重于神经系统的个体发育变化。
entries.example_en: The study focuses on ontogenetic changes in the nervous system.

entries.definition_cn: 个体发生；个体发育过程
entries.definition_en: the process of an individual organism growing organically; a purely biological unfolding of events involved in an organism changing gradually from a simple to a more complex level
entries.example_cn: 对个体发生学的研究揭示了复杂结构如何从简单细胞发育而来。
entries.example_en: The study of ontogeny reveals how complex structures develop from simple cells.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study of the nature of being
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家写了一篇关于存在的本体论著作。
entries.example_en: The philosopher wrote an ontological treatise on existence.

entries.definition_cn: （形而上学）对存在及其本质的研究
entries.definition_en: the metaphysical study of the nature of being and existence
entries.example_cn: 教授讲解了古希腊本体论的历史。
entries.example_en: The professor lectured on the history of ontology in ancient Greece.

entries.definition_cn: （计算机科学）对某个知识领域的严格且详尽的组织，通常是层次化的，并包含所有相关实体及其关系
entries.definition_en: in computer science, a rigorous and exhaustive organization of some knowledge domain that is usually hierarchical and contains all the relevant entities and their relations
entries.example_cn: 软件工程师设计了一个新的本体论来组织数据库架构。
entries.example_en: The software engineer designed a new ontology to organize the database schema.

entries.definition_cn: 法律义务或负担，尤指举证责任
entries.definition_en: a legal obligation or burden, especially the burden of proof
entries.example_cn: 证明他无罪的举证责任落在了被告身上。
entries.example_en: The onus of proving his innocence fell on the defendant.

entries.definition_en: forward in time or order or degree
entries.example_cn: 该公司正进军新市场。
entries.example_en: The company is moving onward to new markets.

entries.definition_en: in a forward direction
entries.example_cn: 他们穿过森林继续前进。
entries.example_en: They marched onward through the forest.

entries.definition_en: from this time or place and continuing into the future
entries.example_cn: 新政策将从一月起生效。
entries.example_en: The new policy will take effect from January onwards.

entries.definition_en: a type of chalcedony featuring alternating black and white bands, often used to create cameos
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商用一块缟玛瑙雕刻了一件精美的浮雕。
entries.example_en: The jeweler carved a beautiful cameo from a piece of onyx.

entries.definition_en: a female gametocyte that develops into an ovum after two meiotic divisions
entries.example_cn: 科学家在实验室中研究了卵母细胞的成熟过程。
entries.example_en: Scientists studied the maturation process of the oocyte in the laboratory.

entries.definition_en: a very large number or amount
entries.example_cn: 我们仍然有大把时间。
entries.example_en: We still have oodles of time.

usage.label: informal; usually plural
usage.pattern: oodles of + plural or uncountable noun

entries.definition_en: the biological process of developing egg cells
entries.example_cn: 卵子发生始于出生前，并持续贯穿女性的生殖期。
entries.example_en: Oogenesis begins before birth and continues throughout a woman's reproductive life.

entries.definition_en: express admiration and pleasure by uttering 'ooh' or 'aah'
entries.example_cn: 当魔术师从帽子里变出兔子时，观众发出了惊叹声。
entries.example_en: The audience oohed when the magician pulled the rabbit out of the hat.

entries.definition_en: Chinese tea leaves that have been partially fermented before being dried
entries.example_cn: 她为客人们泡了一壶乌龙茶。
entries.example_en: She brewed a pot of oolong tea for the guests.

entries.definition_en: strength, energy, passion, or effectiveness
entries.example_cn: 这场聚会缺乏活力，感觉非常沉闷。
entries.example_en: The party lacked oomph and felt very dull.

usage.label: informal, uncountable
usage.pattern: have enough oomph to do something

entries.definition_en: sex appeal
entries.example_cn: 这位演员自信的笑容使他魅力十足。
entries.example_en: The actor's confident smile gave him considerable oomph.

entries.definition_en: surgical removal of one or both ovaries
entries.example_cn: 患者接受了卵巢切除术以治疗该病症。
entries.example_en: The patient underwent an oophorectomy to treat the condition.

entries.definition_en: to flow slowly through small openings
entries.example_cn: 水从墙上的裂缝中渗了出来。
entries.example_en: Water oozed through the cracks in the wall.

entries.definition_en: to release liquid in drops
entries.example_cn: 海绵被挤压时渗出了水。
entries.example_en: The sponge oozed water when squeezed.

entries.definition_en: thick, sticky liquid
entries.example_cn: 油开始从损坏的管道中渗出。
entries.example_en: Oil began to ooze from the damaged pipe.

entries.definition_en: the action of seeping slowly
entries.example_cn: 伤口处有血液缓慢渗出。
entries.example_en: There was a slow ooze of blood from the wound.

entries.definition_en: the process of liquid seeping out slowly
entries.example_cn: 伤口有血渗出。
entries.example_en: There was an oozing of blood from the wound.

entries.definition_cn: （3D打印中的）拉丝缺陷，指熔融材料持续从喷嘴渗出并留下细丝
entries.definition_en: a defect in 3D printing in which melted material continues to ooze from the nozzle, leaving thin strands
entries.example_cn: 降低喷嘴温度有助于防止打印部件之间出现拉丝。
entries.example_en: Lowering the nozzle temperature helped prevent oozing between the printed parts.

entries.definition_en: leaking out slowly
entries.example_cn: 天花板正在渗水。
entries.example_en: The ceiling was oozing water.

entries.definition_en: resembling or consisting of ooze; slimy
entries.example_cn: 黏滑的泥浆粘在了他的靴底。
entries.example_en: The oozy mud stuck to the bottom of his boots.

entries.definition_en: the process of becoming cloudy or not transparent
entries.example_cn: 晶状体的浑浊是由长期暴露在紫外线中引起的。
entries.example_en: The opacification of the lens was caused by prolonged exposure to UV light.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which something blocks the passage of light
entries.example_cn: 这款防晒霜的遮光程度足以抵御紫外线。
entries.example_en: The opacity of the sunscreen is rated to protect against UV rays.

entries.definition_en: the quality of not allowing light or other electromagnetic radiation to pass through
entries.example_cn: 雾的不透明性使得无法看清前方的道路。
entries.example_en: The opacity of the fog made it impossible to see the road ahead.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being difficult to understand due to obscurity
entries.example_cn: 法律文本的晦涩难懂让新员工感到困惑。
entries.example_en: The opacity of the legal text confused the new employees.

entries.definition_cn: 月鱼科的一种大型、色彩鲜艳、体高的远洋鱼类；月鱼
entries.definition_en: a large, brightly colored, deep-bodied pelagic fish of the family Lamprididae
entries.example_cn: 月鱼是一种独特的深海鱼，以其鲜艳的色彩和调节体温的能力而闻名。
entries.example_en: The opah is a unique deep-sea fish known for its vibrant colors and ability to regulate its body temperature.

entries.definition_cn: 一种由水合二氧化硅组成、具有各种颜色的半透明矿物；某些品种用作宝石
entries.definition_en: a translucent mineral consisting of hydrated silica and occurring in various colors; some varieties are used as gemstones
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一条项链，上面有一颗美丽的欧泊，在灯光下闪闪发光。
entries.example_en: She wore a necklace with a beautiful opal that shimmered in the light.

entries.definition_en: a milky brightness with a play of colors on the surface
entries.example_cn: 珍珠的乳光令人着迷。
entries.example_en: The opalescence of the pearl was mesmerizing to watch.

entries.definition_en: having a play of lustrous rainbow colors
entries.example_cn: 那枚乳光色的贝壳闪烁着彩虹般的色彩。
entries.example_en: The opalescent shell shimmered with iridescent hues.

entries.definition_cn: 类似蛋白石的，尤指具有乳白色虹彩的
entries.definition_en: resembling opal, especially in having a milky-white iridescence
entries.example_cn: 艺术家选择了一种具有彩虹光泽的玻璃，以捕捉窗户中变幻的光线。
entries.example_en: The artist chose an opaline glass to capture the shifting light in the window.

entries.definition_en: not allowing light to pass through; impenetrable to sight
entries.example_cn: 不透明的玻璃挡住了所有阳光。
entries.example_en: The opaque glass blocked all the sunlight.

entries.definition_en: difficult or impossible to understand
entries.example_cn: 说明如此难以理解，以至于没人能看懂。
entries.example_en: The instructions were so opaque that no one could follow them.

entries.definition_en: in an opaque manner
entries.example_cn: 数据以不透明的方式呈现，使公众难以理解。
entries.example_en: The data was presented opaquely, making it difficult for the public to understand.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which something blocks the passage of light
entries.example_cn: 窗帘的不透明度阻止了任何光线进入房间。
entries.example_en: The opaqueness of the curtain prevented any light from entering the room.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being difficult to understand due to obscurity
entries.example_cn: 法律文本的晦涩难懂使得普通人无法理解。
entries.example_en: The opaqueness of the legal text made it impossible for the average person to comprehend.

entries.definition_en: affording unobstructed entrance and exit; not shut or closed
entries.example_cn: 门是开着的，请关上它。
entries.example_en: The door is open, so please close it.

entries.definition_en: affording free passage or access
entries.example_cn: 学校周末对公众开放。
entries.example_en: The school is open to the public on weekends.

entries.definition_en: cause to open or to become open
entries.example_cn: 请打开窗户让一些新鲜空气进来。
entries.example_en: Please open the window to let some fresh air in.

entries.definition_en: become open
entries.example_cn: 花朵会在早晨开放。
entries.example_en: The flowers will open in the morning.

entries.definition_en: start to operate or function or cause to start operating or functioning
entries.example_cn: 工厂将于下个月开始运作。
entries.example_en: The factory will open next month.

entries.definition_en: where the air is unconfined
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在开阔处欣赏日落。
entries.example_en: They sat in the open to enjoy the sunset.

entries.definition_en: a clear or unobstructed space or expanse of land or water
entries.example_cn: 我们骑马穿过了开阔地。
entries.example_en: We crossed the open on horseback.

entries.definition_en: a tournament in which both professionals and amateurs may play
entries.example_cn: 他赢得了公开赛网球锦标赛。
entries.example_en: He won the open tennis championship.

entries.definition_en: in the open air
entries.example_cn: 他们在公园里欣赏了一场户外音乐会。
entries.example_en: They enjoyed an open-air concert in the park.

entries.definition_cn: 显而易见，容易解决或决定的
entries.definition_en: so obvious as to be easily solved or decided
entries.example_cn: 这起案件是一起显而易见的盗窃案。
entries.example_en: The case was an open-and-shut case of theft.

entries.definition_en: having a structure that forms an open chain rather than a ring
entries.example_cn: 这种分子是开链化合物。
entries.example_en: This molecule is an open-chain compound.

entries.definition_en: having no fixed limits or restrictions
entries.example_cn: 这个项目的预算没有固定上限。
entries.example_en: The project has an open-ended budget.

entries.definition_cn: 可根据未来情况调整或修改的
entries.definition_en: allowing for future changes or revisions
entries.example_cn: 我们需要一份可以日后调整的开放式合同。
entries.example_en: We need an open-ended contract that can be adjusted later.

entries.definition_en: allowing for a spontaneous response
entries.example_cn: 老师问了一个开放性问题以鼓励讨论。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked an open-ended question to encourage discussion.

entries.definition_en: carefully observant or attentive; on the lookout for possible danger
entries.example_cn: 她警惕地注视着局势，以便发现任何麻烦的迹象。
entries.example_en: She kept an open-eyed watch on the situation to spot any signs of trouble.

entries.definition_cn: 平炉的；平炉炼钢法生产的
entries.definition_en: relating to or produced in an open-hearth furnace or by the open-hearth process
entries.example_cn: 平炉生产的钢以其质量而闻名。
entries.example_en: The steel produced in the open-hearth furnace is known for its quality.

entries.definition_en: willing to consider new ideas and different opinions
entries.example_cn: 一位思想开放的教师鼓励学生提问。
entries.example_en: An open-minded teacher encourages students to ask questions.

entries.definition_cn: （指房间或建筑）空间开阔，隔断很少
entries.definition_en: having large rooms with few dividing partitions
entries.example_cn: 他们搬进了一套现代化的开放式公寓。
entries.example_en: They moved into a modern open-plan apartment.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to computer software whose source code is freely available
entries.example_cn: 我们决定为新的项目使用开源操作系统。
entries.example_en: We decided to use an open-source operating system for our new project.

entries.definition_en: relating to mining where minerals are extracted from the surface rather than underground
entries.example_cn: 公司决定从地下开采转为露天开采方法以降低成本。
entries.example_en: The company decided to switch from underground mining to opencast methods to reduce costs.

entries.definition_en: opened wide, especially of the mouth or eyes
entries.example_cn: 她惊讶得张大了嘴站在那里。
entries.example_en: She stood there with her mouth opened wide in surprise.

entries.definition_en: not sealed or having been unsealed
entries.example_cn: 包裹送到时已经打开了。
entries.example_en: The package was already opened when it arrived.

entries.definition_en: made open or clear
entries.example_cn: 拉开的窗帘让阳光照进来。
entries.example_en: The opened curtains let in the sunlight.

entries.definition_cn: 用于打开密封容器（如瓶子或罐头）的手动工具
entries.definition_en: a hand tool used for opening sealed containers (bottles or cans)
entries.example_cn: 他用开瓶器打开了啤酒瓶。
entries.example_en: He used an opener to crack the beer bottle.

entries.definition_en: the first event in a series
entries.example_cn: 这场音乐会是为音乐节举办的开场演出。
entries.example_en: The concert was the opener for the music festival.

entries.definition_cn: 打开、解开或拆开东西的人
entries.definition_en: a person who unfastens or unwraps or opens
entries.example_cn: 那个人小心翼翼地拆开了礼物的包装。
entries.example_en: The opener carefully removed the wrapping from the gift.

entries.definition_en: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.example_cn: 她宽厚仁慈，足以原谅朋友的错误。
entries.example_en: She was openhearted enough to forgive her friend's mistake.

entries.definition_en: freely communicative; candidly straightforward
entries.example_cn: 这位坦诚的领导者向全体员工透露了公司的所有秘密。
entries.example_en: The openhearted leader shared all the company's secrets with the staff.

entries.definition_en: an open or empty space in or between things
entries.example_cn: 墙上有个小洞。
entries.example_en: There is a small opening in the wall.

entries.definition_en: the act of opening something
entries.example_cn: 打开门让冷空气了进来。
entries.example_en: The opening of the door let in the cold air.

entries.definition_en: becoming open or being made open
entries.example_cn: 打开包裹后，里面的礼物显露出来。
entries.example_en: The opening of the package revealed the gift inside.

entries.definition_en: a ceremony accompanying the start of some enterprise
entries.example_cn: 新体育场的开幕典礼由市长出席。
entries.example_en: The opening of the new stadium was attended by the mayor.

entries.definition_en: opportunity especially for employment or promotion
entries.example_cn: 这份工作机会对她职业生涯来说是个真正的契机。
entries.example_en: The job offer was a real opening for her career.

entries.definition_en: first or beginning
entries.example_cn: 第一章设定了场景。
entries.example_en: The opening chapter sets the scene.

entries.definition_en: the initial part of the introduction
entries.example_cn: 演讲的开头部分非常鼓舞人心。
entries.example_en: The opening of the speech was very inspiring.

entries.definition_en: the first performance (as of a theatrical production)
entries.example_cn: 昨晚该剧首演非常成功。
entries.example_en: The play had a successful opening last night.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is not secret or hidden
entries.example_cn: 他们公开谈论了他们的分歧。
entries.example_en: They spoke openly about their differences.

entries.definition_cn: 接受新思想、信息、经历或他人的意愿；开放态度
entries.definition_en: willingness to receive or accept new ideas, information, experiences, or people
entries.example_cn: 她对新思想的开放态度给研究团队留下了深刻印象。
entries.example_en: Her openness to new ideas impressed the research team.

entries.definition_en: the degree to which a person or organization is receptive to new ideas or experiences
entries.example_cn: 公司对新技术的开放性使其具备了竞争优势。
entries.example_en: The company's openness to new technologies gave it a competitive edge.

entries.definition_en: lack of secrecy; candor and transparency
entries.example_cn: 公司坦诚公开这一错误，帮助重建了公众的信任。
entries.example_en: The company's openness about the error helped rebuild public trust.

entries.definition_en: decorative work made with a pattern of holes, such as embroidery or latticework
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙的袖子上有精致的镂空工艺。
entries.example_en: The dress featured intricate openwork on the sleeves.

entries.definition_en: a dramatic performance set to music with singing and orchestral accompaniment
entries.example_cn: 昨晚我们去看了著名的歌剧。
entries.example_en: We went to see a famous opera last night.

entries.definition_en: a building where musical dramas are performed
entries.example_cn: 新的歌剧院昨天向公众开放了大门。
entries.example_en: The new opera house opened its doors to the public yesterday.

entries.definition_cn: 可使用的；可投入使用的
entries.definition_en: ready to be used or put into service
entries.example_cn: 该软件更新在旧设备上尚不可操作。
entries.example_en: The new software update is not yet operable on older devices.

entries.definition_en: suitable for a particular purpose
entries.example_cn: 在装修期间，这间房可作为临时办公室使用。
entries.example_en: This room is operable as a temporary office during the renovation.

entries.definition_en: able to be treated by surgery
entries.example_cn: 发现肿瘤可以手术，因此患者安排了手术。
entries.example_en: The tumor was found to be operable, so the patient was scheduled for surgery.

entries.definition_en: a number or value on which a mathematical operation is performed
entries.example_cn: 在表达式 5 + 3 中，5 和 3 都是运算对象。
entries.example_en: In the expression 5 + 3, both 5 and 3 are operands.

entries.definition_en: having influence or producing an effect
entries.example_cn: 风的有效力量将船推过了湖面。
entries.example_en: The operant force of the wind pushed the boat across the lake.

entries.definition_en: to handle and cause something to function
entries.example_cn: 请按照说明书操作这台机器。
entries.example_en: Please operate the machine according to the manual.

entries.definition_en: to direct or control a project or business
entries.example_cn: 他们在市中心经营一家小面包店。
entries.example_en: They operate a small bakery in the city center.

entries.definition_en: to function as expected when applied
entries.example_cn: 新软件在旧电脑上无法正常运行。
entries.example_en: The new software does not operate correctly on older computers.

entries.definition_en: to perform surgery on a patient
entries.example_cn: 外科医生将于明天早上为病人动手术。
entries.example_en: The surgeon will operate on the patient tomorrow morning.

entries.definition_en: to keep someone or something engaged
entries.example_cn: 老师用有趣的活动让学生们保持忙碌。
entries.example_en: The teacher operates the students with interesting activities.

entries.definition_en: to perform a military or naval movement to gain an advantage
entries.example_cn: 将军决定在黎明时分实施一次突袭。
entries.example_en: The general decided to operate against the enemy at dawn.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of opera
entries.example_cn: 这场歌剧表演充满了戏剧性的场景和优美的歌声。
entries.example_en: The operatic performance was filled with dramatic scenes and beautiful singing.

entries.definition_en: being in effect or operation
entries.example_cn: 生效的规则上周被修改了。
entries.example_en: The operating rules were changed last week.

entries.definition_en: involved in a kind of operation
entries.example_cn: 手术团队正在为手术做准备。
entries.example_en: The operating team is preparing for the surgery.

entries.definition_en: the state of being in effect or functioning
entries.example_cn: 新政策现已生效。
entries.example_en: The new policy is now in operation.

entries.definition_en: a business run on a large scale
entries.example_cn: 该公司将业务扩展到了三个国家。
entries.example_en: The company expanded its operation to three countries.

entries.definition_en: a medical procedure involving an incision
entries.example_cn: 病人接受了一次成功的手术。
entries.example_en: The patient underwent a successful operation.

entries.definition_en: a planned activity involving many people
entries.example_cn: 军队发起了一次重大行动。
entries.example_en: The military launched a major operation.

entries.definition_en: activity by a military or naval force
entries.example_cn: 这次军事行动发生在沙漠中。
entries.example_en: The operation took place in the desert.

entries.definition_en: a process or series of acts involved in work
entries.example_cn: 操作这台机器需要技巧。
entries.example_en: The operation of the machine requires skill.

entries.definition_en: the manner of functioning or operating
entries.example_cn: 该系统的运作方式是自动的。
entries.example_en: The operation of the system is automatic.

entries.definition_en: data processing specified by a rule
entries.example_cn: 计算机执行了一次复杂的数学运算。
entries.example_en: The computer performed a complex mathematical operation.

entries.definition_cn: 与实际操作或运行有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to the practical work or operations involved in achieving a result
entries.example_cn: 该行动计划得到了经理的批准。
entries.example_en: The operational plan was approved by the manager.

entries.definition_en: ready to be used or started
entries.example_cn: 新系统现已可投入使用。
entries.example_en: The new system is now operational.

entries.definition_en: related to military operations
entries.example_cn: 士兵们正在执行作战任务。
entries.example_en: The soldiers were on operational duty.

entries.definition_en: currently in effect or working
entries.example_cn: 新规定将于下周一生效。
entries.example_en: The new rule becomes operational next Monday.

entries.definition_en: in relation to the operation or functioning of something
entries.example_cn: 该系统在操作上效率很高，但外观平淡。
entries.example_en: The system is operationally efficient but aesthetically plain.

entries.definition_cn: 经纪交易；买卖执行与客户记录管理
entries.definition_en: financial transactions at a brokerage; activities involving the execution of trades and keeping customer records
entries.example_cn: 经纪人高效地管理所有客户交易。
entries.example_en: The broker manages all client operations efficiently.

entries.definition_cn: 生效的；在特定情境中起决定作用或有重要影响的
entries.definition_en: being in force, or having a decisive effect or influence in a particular situation
entries.example_cn: 起决定作用的因素是资金不足。
entries.example_en: The operative factor was the lack of funding.

entries.definition_en: relating to or requiring or amenable to treatment by surgery especially as opposed to medicine
entries.example_cn: 该患者需要手术治疗。
entries.example_en: The patient required operative treatment.

entries.definition_en: effective; producing a desired effect
entries.example_cn: 这种药未能治愈疾病。
entries.example_en: The medicine was not operative in curing the disease.

entries.definition_en: (of e.g. a machine) performing or capable of performing
entries.example_cn: 由于停电，机器无法运转。
entries.example_en: The machine is not operative due to a power outage.

entries.definition_en: a person secretly employed in espionage for a government
entries.example_cn: 这名间谍被派去收集情报。
entries.example_en: The operative was sent to gather intelligence.

entries.definition_en: someone who can be employed as a detective to collect information and assist in criminal investigations
entries.example_cn: 这名侦探协助解决了案件。
entries.example_en: The operative helped solve the case.

entries.definition_en: in a way that produces a result or effect
entries.example_cn: 新政策将在下个季度有效地降低成本。
entries.example_en: The new policy will operatively reduce costs by next quarter.

entries.definition_en: an agent that operates some apparatus or machine
entries.example_cn: 操作员按下按钮启动了机器。
entries.example_en: The operator pressed the button to start the machine.

entries.definition_cn: （数学）表示数学运算的符号或函数
entries.definition_en: (mathematics) a symbol or function representing a mathematical operation
entries.example_cn: 加号是一个运算符。
entries.example_en: The plus sign is an operator.

entries.definition_en: someone who owns or operates a business
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店的经营者非常友好。
entries.example_en: The operator of the hotel is very friendly.

entries.definition_cn: 精明能干且常用可疑手段办事的人
entries.definition_en: a person adept at making deals or getting results, especially by questionable methods
entries.example_cn: 那个投机者找到了避税的方法。
entries.example_en: The operator found a way to avoid the tax.

entries.definition_cn: 在股票或商品市场上积极交易的投机者
entries.definition_en: a speculator who trades aggressively on stock or commodity markets
entries.example_cn: 那位投机者在市场上赚了一大笔钱。
entries.example_en: The operator made a huge profit in the market.

entries.definition_en: having an operculum
entries.example_cn: 这只蜗牛具盖，意味着它的壳口有一个保护性的盖子。
entries.example_en: The snail is operculate, meaning it has a protective lid over its shell opening.

entries.definition_en: a hard flap that covers the gill slits in fishes or the shell opening in certain gastropods
entries.example_cn: 当蜗牛缩回壳内时，厣会封住开口。
entries.example_en: When the snail retracts into its shell, the operculum seals the opening.

entries.definition_en: a short, light, and amusing opera
entries.example_cn: 我们观看了一场情节滑稽、旋律朗朗上口的轻歌剧。
entries.example_en: We attended a charming operetta featuring a comic plot and catchy tunes.

entries.definition_en: a segment of DNA containing adjacent genes including structural genes and an operator gene and a regulatory gene
entries.example_cn: 科学家研究操纵子以了解细菌如何控制蛋白质生产。
entries.example_en: Scientists studied the operon to understand how bacteria control protein production.

entries.definition_en: a snake or serpent
entries.example_cn: 那条蛇悄无声息地穿过高高的草丛。
entries.example_en: The ophidian slithered silently through the tall grass.

entries.definition_cn: 眼炎，尤指严重的结膜炎
entries.definition_en: severe inflammation of the eye, especially conjunctivitis
entries.example_cn: 患者因眼部感染恶化而被诊断为眼炎。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with ophthalmia after the eye infection worsened.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study of the eye and its diseases
entries.example_cn: 她在医院担任眼科外科医生。
entries.example_en: She works as an ophthalmic surgeon at the hospital.

entries.definition_en: resembling or pertaining to the eye
entries.example_cn: 这种眼状透镜将光线聚焦到视网膜上。
entries.example_en: The ophthalmic lens focuses light onto the retina.

entries.definition_en: a medical doctor specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the eye
entries.example_cn: 眼科医生检查了患者的眼睛以寻找感染的迹象。
entries.example_en: The ophthalmologist examined the patient's eyes for signs of infection.

entries.definition_en: the branch of medicine concerned with the eye and its diseases
entries.example_cn: 她实习后决定专攻眼科学。
entries.example_en: She decided to specialize in ophthalmology after her internship.

entries.definition_en: paralysis of the muscles that move the eye
entries.example_cn: 患者在失去眼球运动后被诊断为眼肌麻痹。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with ophthalmoplegia after losing eye movement.

entries.definition_en: medical instrument for examining the retina of the eye
entries.example_cn: 医生使用检眼镜检查了患者的视网膜。
entries.example_en: The doctor used an ophthalmoscope to check the patient's retina.

entries.definition_en: examination of the interior of an eye using an ophthalmoscope
entries.example_cn: 医生进行了眼底镜检查以检查患者的视网膜。
entries.example_en: The doctor performed an ophthalmoscopy to check the patient's retina.

entries.definition_en: a narcotic drug that contains opium or an opium derivative
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种温和的鸦片类药物帮助患者入睡。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a mild opiate to help the patient sleep.

entries.definition_cn: 麻痹感官、制造虚假安慰或满足感的事物
entries.definition_en: something that dulls the senses and creates a false sense of comfort or contentment
entries.example_cn: 他认为赌博是一种麻醉剂，使人逃避面对自己的问题。
entries.example_en: He regarded gambling as an opiate that kept people from facing their problems.

entries.definition_en: to express one's opinion openly and freely
entries.example_cn: 参议员拒绝在新闻发布会上就这项有争议的法案发表意见。
entries.example_en: The senator refused to opine on the controversial bill during the press conference.

entries.definition_en: to believe or suppose something
entries.example_cn: 我认为这个项目将在明年夏天完成。
entries.example_en: I opine that the project will be completed by next summer.

entries.definition_en: a personal belief or judgment not based on proof
entries.example_cn: 依我看，这是今年最好的电影。
entries.example_en: In my opinion, this is the best movie of the year.

entries.definition_en: a statement expressing a belief held with confidence
entries.example_cn: 他就新政策发表了看法。
entries.example_en: He wrote an opinion on the new policy.

entries.definition_en: a belief shared by most people
entries.example_cn: 公众舆论反对战争。
entries.example_en: Public opinion is against the war.

entries.definition_en: a legal document explaining the reasons for a court decision
entries.example_cn: 法官在法庭上宣读了判决书。
entries.example_en: The judge read the opinion aloud in court.

entries.definition_en: the reasons given by a court for its judgment
entries.example_cn: 法院的判决书详细说明了作出该裁决的理由。
entries.example_en: The court's opinion gave detailed reasons for its decision.

entries.definition_en: a vague idea in which some confidence is placed
entries.example_cn: 我的暂时看法是明天会下雨。
entries.example_en: My tentative opinion is that it will rain tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: having a strong belief in one's own opinions and being unwilling to change them.
entries.example_cn: 这位固执己见的评论家拒绝接受对该艺术作品的任何其他解释。
entries.example_en: The opinionated critic refused to accept any alternative interpretations of the art.

entries.definition_en: an addictive narcotic extracted from seed capsules of the opium poppy
entries.example_cn: 鸦片是一种极易上瘾的物质。
entries.example_en: Opium is a highly addictive substance.

entries.definition_cn: 一种夜行性的树栖有袋类动物，产于北美南部至南美北部，长着无毛的可抓握的尾巴
entries.definition_en: a nocturnal arboreal marsupial having a naked prehensile tail found from southern North America to northern South America
entries.example_cn: 有人在花园的树枝上看到一只倒挂着的负鼠。
entries.example_en: An opossum was seen hanging upside down from a branch in the garden.

entries.definition_cn: 一种小型、毛茸茸的澳大利亚树栖有袋类动物，长着一条通常可抓握的长尾巴
entries.definition_en: a small, furry Australian arboreal marsupial with a long, usually prehensile tail
entries.example_cn: 这只澳大利亚树栖有袋动物爬下树，在地面上寻找食物。
entries.example_en: The opossum climbed down the tree to find food on the ground.

entries.definition_cn: 韩国女性对哥哥或熟悉的年长男性的亲昵称呼
entries.definition_en: an affectionate Korean term used by a female for her older brother or a somewhat older man with whom she is familiar
entries.example_cn: 她称呼男朋友为“哥哥”，因为他比她年长。
entries.example_en: She called her boyfriend oppa because he was older than her.

entries.definition_cn: 年轻女性粉丝崇拜的男性偶像
entries.definition_en: a male idol revered by a younger female fan
entries.example_cn: 那位年轻女粉丝把她最喜欢的男偶像的照片贴满了手机。
entries.example_en: The young fan covered her phone with photos of her favorite oppa.

entries.definition_en: a person or team that you are competing against
entries.example_cn: 对手在决赛中表现出色。
entries.example_en: The opponent played very well in the final match.

entries.definition_en: someone who opposes a plan, idea, or person
entries.example_cn: 新政策遭到了反对集团的强烈反对。
entries.example_en: The new policy faced strong opposition from the opponent group.

entries.definition_cn: 敌对的；对立的（过时用法）
entries.definition_en: opposing or hostile (obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 在这篇古文中，敌人被描述为反对和平与正义。
entries.example_en: In the old text, the enemies are described as opponent to peace and justice.

entries.definition_cn: 合适的；有利的；时机恰当的
entries.definition_en: suitable or advantageous for a particular purpose or occasion
entries.example_cn: 宣布消息的时机恰到好处。
entries.example_en: It was an opportune moment to make the announcement.

entries.definition_en: in a suitable or advantageous manner or at a suitable time
entries.example_cn: 雨及时停了，使我们得以完成野餐。
entries.example_en: The rain stopped opportunely, allowing us to finish the picnic.

entries.definition_en: the practice of taking advantage of opportunities without regard for consequences
entries.example_cn: 他的政治生涯因被指控机会主义而毁于一旦。
entries.example_en: His political career was ruined by accusations of opportunism.

entries.definition_en: a person who places expediency above principle
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家因是一个为了选票而改变观点的机会主义者而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was criticized for being an opportunist who changed his views for votes.

entries.definition_en: taking immediate advantage, often unethically, of any circumstance of possible benefit
entries.example_cn: 这位投机取巧的政治家利用危机谋取个人利益。
entries.example_en: The opportunist politician exploited the crisis for personal gain.

entries.definition_en: taking immediate advantage of any situation, often in an unethical way
entries.example_cn: 这位见风使舵的政治家只在经济繁荣时承诺降低税收。
entries.example_en: The opportunistic politician promised to lower taxes only when the economy was booming.

entries.definition_cn: 利用出现的机会或形势的
entries.definition_en: taking advantage of opportunities or situations as they arise
entries.example_cn: 免疫系统虚弱时，这种疾病可能引发机会性感染。
entries.example_en: The disease can cause opportunistic infections when the immune system is weak.

entries.definition_en: a chance to do something because the situation is favorable
entries.example_cn: 这是一个学习新语言的好机会。
entries.example_en: This is a great opportunity to learn a new language.

entries.definition_en: able to be placed opposite to something
entries.example_cn: 对生拇指使人类能够轻松抓取物体。
entries.example_en: The opposable thumb allows humans to grasp objects easily.

entries.definition_en: to be against something or someone
entries.example_cn: 许多人反对这项新法律。
entries.example_en: Many people oppose the new law.

entries.definition_en: to act against something
entries.example_cn: 他通过投票反对该计划来与之作对。
entries.example_en: He opposed the plan by voting against it.

entries.definition_en: to fight against or resist strongly
entries.example_cn: 军队抵抗敌人的进攻。
entries.example_en: The army opposed the enemy's attack.

entries.definition_en: to set into opposition or rivalry
entries.example_cn: 这两支球队将在决赛中相互对抗。
entries.example_en: The two teams were set to oppose each other in the final.

entries.definition_en: to contrast with something of equal weight
entries.example_cn: 在这幅画中，光与暗形成对比。
entries.example_en: Light opposes dark in this painting.

entries.definition_en: to be resistant to something
entries.example_cn: 这种材料防水，不会吸收水分。
entries.example_en: The material opposes water and does not absorb it.

entries.definition_en: being in opposition or having an opponent
entries.example_cn: 这两个政党彼此强烈对立。
entries.example_en: The two political parties are strongly opposed to each other.

entries.definition_en: a person or group that opposes something or someone
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策遭到了主要政治反对派的强烈反对。
entries.example_en: The new policy faced strong opposition from the main political opposer.

entries.definition_en: on the opposite side; in opposition
entries.example_cn: 对阵双方在比赛前列队。
entries.example_en: The opposing teams lined up before the match.

entries.definition_en: located directly across from something
entries.example_cn: 银行在街道的对面。
entries.example_en: The bank is on the opposite side of the street.

entries.definition_en: moving or facing away from each other
entries.example_cn: 两辆车朝相反的方向驶去。
entries.example_en: The two cars drove in opposite directions.

entries.definition_en: in a position facing something or someone across from it
entries.example_cn: 他们面对面地坐在桌子旁。
entries.example_en: They sat opposite each other at the table.

entries.definition_en: a word that means the reverse of another word
entries.example_cn: "Hot"和"cold"是反义词。
entries.example_en: "Hot" and "cold" are opposites.

entries.definition_en: something that is the reverse in sequence or character
entries.example_cn: 这部电影完全出乎我的意料。
entries.example_en: The movie was the opposite of what I expected.

entries.definition_en: a person or team matched against you in a competition
entries.example_cn: 对手队表现得非常出色。
entries.example_en: The opposite team played very well.

entries.definition_en: growing in pairs on either side of a stem
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子是对生的。
entries.example_en: The leaves of the plant are opposite.

entries.definition_en: a relationship of direct opposition between two things
entries.example_cn: 白天和夜晚之间存在紧密的对立关系。
entries.example_en: There is a close opposite between day and night.

entries.definition_en: in opposite directions or positions
entries.example_cn: 两块磁铁的朝向相反，北极彼此相对。
entries.example_en: The two magnets were oriented oppositely, with their north poles facing each other.

entries.definition_en: to treat someone unfairly by using power to keep them down
entries.example_cn: 独裁者利用军队压迫人民。
entries.example_en: The dictator used his army to oppress the people.

entries.definition_cn: 使感到压抑、悲苦或沉重
entries.definition_en: to make someone feel sad, gloomy, or heavily burdened
entries.example_cn: 连绵阴沉的天空使我们感到压抑。
entries.example_en: We were oppressed by the constant grey skies.

entries.definition_en: subject to oppression
entries.example_cn: 工人们感到受到该政权的压迫。
entries.example_en: The workers felt oppressed by the regime.

entries.definition_en: the state of being kept down by unjust use of force or authority
entries.example_cn: 人民起来反抗政府的压迫。
entries.example_en: The people rose up against the oppression of the government.

entries.definition_cn: 残酷或不公正地压迫某人的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of oppressing someone cruelly or unjustly
entries.example_cn: 这个国家在多年的残酷统治下受苦。
entries.example_en: The country suffered under years of oppression.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of being oppressed
entries.example_cn: 她感到拥挤的房间里有深深的受压迫感。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep sense of oppression in the crowded room.

entries.definition_cn: 沉重难忍的；令人压抑的
entries.definition_en: weighing heavily on the senses or spirit
entries.example_cn: 令人窒息的炎热使得在户外工作变得困难。
entries.example_en: The oppressive heat made it difficult to work outside.

entries.definition_en: marked by unjust severity or arbitrary behavior
entries.example_cn: 那个专横的政权控制着公民生活的方方面面。
entries.example_en: The oppressive regime controlled every aspect of citizens' lives.

entries.definition_en: in a way that feels heavy, burdensome, or stifling
entries.example_cn: 天气热得令人窒息，让人难以呼吸。
entries.example_en: The heat was oppressively hot, making it difficult to breathe.

entries.definition_en: the feeling of being oppressed or burdened
entries.example_cn: 拥挤房间的压迫感让人难以呼吸。
entries.example_en: The oppressiveness of the crowded room made it difficult to breathe.

entries.definition_cn: 压迫性；令人感到沉重难耐的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being oppressive
entries.example_cn: 工作量所具有的压迫性让员工疲惫不堪。
entries.example_en: The oppressiveness of the workload left the staff exhausted.

entries.definition_en: a person in authority who subjects others to unfair pressure
entries.example_cn: 人民起来反抗压迫者，要求他们的权利。
entries.example_en: The people rose up against the oppressor to demand their rights.

entries.definition_en: expressing angry or insulting criticism
entries.example_cn: 人群向那位腐败的官员喊出辱骂的话语。
entries.example_en: The crowd shouted opprobrious words at the corrupt official.

entries.definition_en: deserving or bringing disgrace or shame
entries.example_cn: 他可耻的行为导致他被公司立即解雇。
entries.example_en: His opprobrious behavior led to his immediate dismissal from the company.

entries.definition_en: public disgrace or shame resulting from abuse
entries.example_cn: 丑闻给整个组织带来了耻辱。
entries.example_en: The scandal brought opprobrium upon the entire organization.

entries.definition_cn: 因可耻行为而蒙受的不名誉；耻辱
entries.definition_en: disgrace or bad reputation resulting from shameful behavior
entries.example_cn: 这起丑闻使整个组织蒙受了耻辱。
entries.example_en: The scandal brought opprobrium upon the entire organization.

entries.definition_cn: 视网膜感光细胞中的感光蛋白，包括视紫红质的蛋白质成分
entries.definition_en: a light-sensitive protein in retinal photoreceptors, including the protein component of rhodopsin
entries.example_cn: 眼中的视蛋白使我们能够感知颜色。
entries.example_en: The opsin in the eye allows us to perceive color.

entries.definition_en: to choose one thing instead of another
entries.example_cn: 你可以选择素食菜单或海鲜菜单。
entries.example_en: You can opt for the vegetarian menu or the seafood menu.

usage.label: intransitive: opt to do; opt for something
usage.pattern: opt to do / opt for sth

entries.definition_en: a grammatical mood used in languages like Greek or Sanskrit to express a wish or hope
entries.example_cn: 愿语气用于表达愿望或希望。
entries.example_en: The optative mood is used to express a wish or hope.

entries.definition_en: indicating an option or wish
entries.example_cn: 该从句表达了一种愿望。
entries.example_en: The optative clause expresses a desire.

entries.definition_cn: 与某些语言中的动词语气有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to a mood of verbs in some languages
entries.example_cn: 该动词形式表示愿望。
entries.example_en: The optative verb form indicates a wish.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or resembling the eye
entries.example_cn: 视神经是视觉系统的关键部分。
entries.example_en: The optic nerve is a crucial part of the visual system.

entries.definition_en: relating to or using sight
entries.example_cn: 视觉错觉会让大脑看到实际上不存在的东西。
entries.example_en: Optic illusions can trick the brain into seeing things that are not there.

entries.definition_en: an eye (archaic or humorous)
entries.example_cn: 在这首古诗中，说话者把自己的眼睛称为 optic。
entries.example_en: In the old poem, the speaker called his eye an optic.

entries.definition_en: relating to the science of light or optics
entries.example_cn: 该透镜的光学特性使其非常有效。
entries.example_en: The optical properties of the lens make it very effective.

entries.definition_en: relating to or using sight
entries.example_cn: 视觉错觉会让大脑看到实际上不存在的东西。
entries.example_en: Optical illusions can trick the brain into seeing things that are not there.

entries.definition_en: resembling the eye
entries.example_cn: 这台相机的光学变焦功能模仿了人眼的对焦能力。
entries.example_en: The camera has an optical zoom that mimics the human eye's ability to focus.

entries.definition_cn: 通过光学方式；在光学方面
entries.definition_en: by means of optics; in relation to optics
entries.example_cn: 图像通过透镜系统以光学方式放大。
entries.example_en: The image was enlarged optically through a system of lenses.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes, dispenses, or sells lenses and spectacles; in the UK, also a person who examines eyes and prescribes corrective lenses
entries.example_cn: 验光师调整了我的新眼镜以确保清晰度完美。
entries.example_en: The optician adjusted my new glasses to ensure perfect clarity.

entries.definition_en: the branch of physics dealing with light
entries.example_cn: 这门课程涵盖了光学的基本原理。
entries.example_en: The course covers the fundamental principles of optics.

entries.definition_en: the way light behaves
entries.example_cn: 这种新镜头改善了相机的光学特性。
entries.example_en: The new lens improves the optics of the camera.

entries.definition_en: best possible under the given conditions
entries.example_cn: 种植这种植物的最佳温度是 25 摄氏度。
entries.example_en: The optimal temperature for growing this plant is 25 degrees Celsius.

entries.definition_en: in an optimal and most desirable way
entries.example_cn: 软件应以最佳方式进行配置，以实现最高性能。
entries.example_en: The software should be configured optimally for maximum performance.

entries.definition_en: the process of making something as effective or perfect as possible
entries.example_cn: 这位软件工程师专注于数据库查询的优化。
entries.example_en: The software engineer focused on the optimisation of the database queries.

entries.definition_en: to make something as good or efficient as possible
entries.example_cn: 我们需要优化工作流程以节省时间。
entries.example_en: We need to optimise our workflow to save time.

entries.definition_en: to modify something to achieve maximum efficiency in storage, time, or cost
entries.example_cn: 该软件旨在优化内存使用。
entries.example_en: The software was designed to optimise memory usage.

entries.definition_en: to act as an optimist and take a sunny view of the world
entries.example_cn: 即使在困难时期，他也喜欢对未来保持乐观。
entries.example_en: Even in difficult times, he likes to optimise about the future.

entries.definition_en: a feeling that everything will turn out well
entries.example_cn: 尽管困难重重，他的乐观情绪让他坚持下去。
entries.example_en: Despite the difficulties, his optimism kept him going.

entries.definition_en: a general tendency to expect the best outcome
entries.example_cn: 她对未来的乐观倾向众所周知。
entries.example_en: Her optimism about the future is well known.

entries.definition_cn: 相信善最终会战胜恶的信念
entries.definition_en: the belief that good will eventually triumph over evil
entries.example_cn: 她相信善会战胜恶，这种乐观信念帮助她度过了危机。
entries.example_en: Her optimism that good would triumph over evil helped her endure the crisis.

entries.definition_cn: 认为这个世界是一切可能世界中最好的哲学学说
entries.definition_en: the philosophical doctrine that this world is the best of all possible worlds
entries.example_cn: 莱布尼茨在他的哲学著作中为乐观主义学说辩护。
entries.example_en: Leibniz defended the doctrine of optimism in his philosophical writings.

entries.definition_en: a person who tends to see the good side of things and expects positive outcomes
entries.example_cn: 作为一个乐观主义者，她相信尽管有困难，这个项目也会成功。
entries.example_en: As an optimist, she believed that the project would succeed despite the difficulties.

entries.definition_en: expecting the best
entries.example_cn: 赢得第一场比赛后，队伍变得乐观起来。
entries.example_en: The team was optimistic after winning the first match.

entries.definition_en: expecting the best outcome in a situation
entries.example_cn: 尽管有困难，她对未来依然保持乐观。
entries.example_en: Despite the difficulties, she remained optimistic about the future.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing hope and confidence about the future
entries.example_cn: 团队乐观地工作，相信他们会找回丢失的数据。
entries.example_en: The team worked optimistically, believing they would recover the lost data.

entries.definition_en: the process of making something as effective or perfect as possible
entries.example_cn: 软件更新侧重于性能优化。
entries.example_en: The software update focused on performance optimization.

entries.definition_en: to make something as good or efficient as possible
entries.example_cn: 我们需要优化工作流程以按时完工。
entries.example_en: We need to optimize our workflow to finish the project on time.

entries.definition_en: to modify something to achieve maximum efficiency in storage, time, or cost
entries.example_cn: 该软件旨在优化存储容量。
entries.example_en: The software was designed to optimize storage capacity.

entries.definition_en: to act as an optimist and take a sunny view of the world
entries.example_cn: 尽管消息不好，他还是选择乐观地看待光明的一面。
entries.example_en: Despite the bad news, he chose to optimize and see the bright side.

entries.definition_en: most desirable possible under given restrictions
entries.example_cn: 我们需要为预算危机找到一个最佳的解决方案。
entries.example_en: We need to find an optimum solution for the budget crisis.

entries.definition_en: the best possible conditions or amount
entries.example_cn: 研究人员确定了这种植物生长的最佳状态。
entries.example_en: The researchers determined the optimum for the plant’s growth.

entries.definition_en: one of a number of things from which only one can be chosen
entries.example_cn: 你可以选择坐火车或公交车。
entries.example_en: You have the option of taking the train or the bus.

entries.definition_en: the right to buy or sell property at an agreed price
entries.example_cn: 他购买了一份购买该房屋的期权。
entries.example_en: He bought an option to purchase the house.

entries.definition_en: the freedom or right to choose
entries.example_cn: 员工可以选择远程办公。
entries.example_en: Employees have the option to work remotely.

entries.definition_en: possible to choose but not required
entries.example_cn: 甜点是可选择的，所以你可以选择不吃。
entries.example_en: The dessert is optional, so you can choose not to have it.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of allowing choice or discretion
entries.example_cn: 额外功能的可选性允许客户定制他们的购买内容。
entries.example_en: The optionality of the extra features allows customers to customize their purchase.

entries.definition_cn: 初次投资后可获得额外投资机会的价值
entries.definition_en: The value of having additional investment opportunities available after an initial investment.
entries.example_cn: 这项初次投资的短期回报较为有限，但为后续项目提供资金的选择价值很高。
entries.example_en: The initial investment had modest short-term returns but considerable optionality for funding later projects.

entries.definition_en: in an optional manner; not necessarily required
entries.example_cn: 您可以可选地在表格中包含电话号码。
entries.example_en: You can optionally include your phone number in the form.

entries.definition_en: a specialist who tests eyesight and prescribes corrective glasses
entries.example_cn: 验光师调整了我的眼镜以改善我的视力。
entries.example_en: The optometrist adjusted my glasses to improve my vision.

entries.definition_en: the practice of an optometrist
entries.example_cn: 她决定学习验光学以帮助人们看得更清楚。
entries.example_en: She decided to study optometry to help people see better.

entries.definition_en: wealth shown by luxurious living
entries.example_cn: 这座宫殿是皇家奢华的象征。
entries.example_en: The palace was a symbol of royal opulence.

entries.definition_en: ostentatiously rich and superior in quality
entries.example_cn: 宫殿用奢华的黄金和丝绸装饰。
entries.example_en: The palace was decorated with opulent gold and silk.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows great wealth, luxury, and richness
entries.example_cn: 宫殿用黄金和珠宝装饰得极其豪华。
entries.example_en: The palace was decorated opulently with gold and jewels.

entries.definition_en: a work, especially a musical or artistic work
entries.example_cn: 他最后的作品是一部献给和平的交响曲。
entries.example_en: His final opus was a symphony dedicated to peace.

entries.definition_en: used to connect two or more alternatives
entries.example_cn: 你可以喝茶或者咖啡。
entries.example_en: You can have tea or coffee.

entries.definition_en: used to mean otherwise or in the alternative case
entries.example_cn: 快点，否则你会迟到的。
entries.example_en: Hurry up, or you will be late.

entries.definition_en: used to connect two equivalent names or terms
entries.example_cn: 法国首都巴黎，即光明之城。
entries.example_en: The capital of France, Paris, or the City of Light.

entries.definition_en: used to count elements as two distinct possibilities
entries.example_cn: 我们需要二选一。
entries.example_en: We need to choose one or the other.

entries.definition_en: an alternative form of the symbol OR used in logic and engineering
entries.example_cn: 该电路使用符号 OR 表示析取。
entries.example_en: The circuit uses the symbol OR to represent disjunction.

entries.definition_en: having the color of gold or yellow tincture in heraldry
entries.example_cn: 狮子被描绘成金色。
entries.example_en: The lion is depicted in or.

entries.definition_en: a logical operator indicating that at least one of the propositions is true
entries.example_cn: 如果A为真或B为真，则条件满足。
entries.example_en: The condition is met if A is true or B is true.

entries.definition_en: the gold or yellow tincture used in heraldry
entries.example_cn: 盾徽上饰有金色。
entries.example_en: The shield is charged with or.

entries.definition_en: any of various herbaceous plants of the genus Atriplex that thrive in deserts and salt marshes
entries.example_cn: 滨藜在海岸附近的咸水沼泽中野生生长。
entries.example_en: The orach grows wild in the salty marshes near the coast.

entries.definition_en: an authoritative person who predicts the future
entries.example_cn: 古人向神谕者请教以知晓他们的命运。
entries.example_en: The ancient people consulted the oracle to learn their fate.

entries.definition_en: a prophecy revealed by a priest or priestess, believed to be infallible
entries.example_cn: 神谕用晦涩的术语警告了一场即将到来的灾难。
entries.example_en: The oracle warned of a coming disaster in obscure terms.

entries.definition_en: a shrine where an oracular god is consulted
entries.example_cn: 游客前往神谕所寻求神明的指引。
entries.example_en: Visitors traveled to the oracle to seek guidance from the gods.

entries.definition_en: relating to an oracle or the practice of seeking divine knowledge
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的寺庙以其神谕预言而闻名。
entries.example_en: The ancient temple was famous for its oracular prophecies.

entries.definition_cn: 晦涩难解且带有预言性的
entries.definition_en: obscurely prophetic or mysterious
entries.example_cn: 他晦涩难懂的预言性言论让每个人都猜不透他的真实意图。
entries.example_en: His oracular remarks left everyone guessing about his true intentions.

entries.definition_cn: 像神谕一样思想晦涩难解的
entries.definition_en: resembling an oracle in the obscurity of thought
entries.example_cn: 诗人晦涩难解的风格使得他的诗句难以解读。
entries.example_en: The poet's oracular style made his verses difficult to interpret.

entries.definition_en: using speech rather than writing
entries.example_cn: 老师向全班发出了口头指令。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave an oral instruction to the class.

entries.definition_en: of or involving the mouth or mouth region or the surface on which the mouth is located
entries.example_cn: 口腔由嘴唇和牙齿保护。
entries.example_en: The oral cavity is protected by the lips and teeth.

entries.definition_en: taken by mouth, especially as medication
entries.example_cn: 她服用口服药物治疗牙痛。
entries.example_en: She uses an oral medicine to treat her toothache.

entries.definition_cn: 口头传播信息或文学作品的
entries.definition_en: relating to the transmission of information or literature by word of mouth
entries.example_cn: 这个故事通过口头传统流传了好几代。
entries.example_en: The story survived through oral tradition for generations.

entries.definition_en: relating to a stage in psychosexual development when the child's interest is concentrated in the mouth
entries.example_cn: 这位心理学家研究了儿童发展的口欲期。
entries.example_en: The psychologist studied the oral stage of development in children.

entries.definition_en: an examination conducted by spoken communication
entries.example_cn: 学生们对他们的口试感到紧张。
entries.example_en: The students were nervous about their oral exam.

entries.definition_en: by spoken rather than written means
entries.example_cn: 这项协议是口头达成的，而非书面。
entries.example_en: The agreement was made orally, not in writing.

entries.definition_en: (of drugs) through the mouth rather than through injection; by mouth
entries.example_cn: 这种药物必须口服。
entries.example_en: The medication must be taken orally.

entries.definition_en: an orangutan
entries.example_cn: 这只红毛猩猩大部分时间都在雨林的树枝间荡来荡去。
entries.example_en: The orang spent most of its day swinging through the branches of the rainforest.

entries.definition_en: having the color between red and yellow
entries.example_cn: 日落将天空染成了橙色。
entries.example_en: The sunset painted the sky orange.

entries.definition_en: a round fruit that is yellow to orange in color
entries.example_cn: 我早餐吃了一个新鲜的橙子。
entries.example_en: I ate a fresh orange for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: the color between red and yellow
entries.example_cn: 她选了一条橙色的围巾来搭配她的裙子。
entries.example_en: She chose an orange scarf to match her dress.

entries.definition_en: a tree that produces oranges
entries.example_cn: 花园里的柑橘树正在开花。
entries.example_en: The orange tree in the garden is blooming.

entries.definition_en: a pigment that produces the orange color
entries.example_cn: 艺术家使用橙色颜料来突出日落。
entries.example_en: The artist used orange paint to highlight the sunset.

entries.definition_en: sweetened beverage of diluted orange juice
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在炎热的夏日里享受着清爽的橙汁汽水。
entries.example_en: The children enjoyed refreshing orangeade on the hot summer day.

entries.definition_en: a greenhouse, garden, or plantation where orange trees are grown
entries.example_cn: 这座历史庄园拥有一座美丽的橘园，里面种满了异国情调的柑橘树。
entries.example_en: The historic estate features a beautiful orangery filled with exotic citrus trees.

entries.definition_en: high-quality wood from an orange tree, used for fine woodworking
entries.example_cn: 这把古董椅子是用稀有的柑橘木制成的。
entries.example_en: The antique chair was crafted from rare orangewood.

entries.definition_en: having a color that is a mixture of red and yellow, resembling the color of a ripe orange
entries.example_cn: 日落将天空染成了粉色和橙色的色调。
entries.example_en: The sunset painted the sky in shades of pink and orangish hues.

entries.definition_en: a large ape with long arms found in Borneo and Sumatra that lives in trees
entries.example_cn: 保护工作者努力保护濒临灭绝的红毛猩猩。
entries.example_en: Conservationists work hard to protect the endangered orangutan.

entries.definition_cn: 以夸夸其谈或矫饰的方式说话
entries.definition_en: to speak in a pompous or pretentious manner
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家选择夸夸其谈地讲了一小时，而不是回答选民的问题。
entries.example_en: The politician chose to orate for an hour instead of answering the voters' questions.

entries.definition_en: a formal speech delivered on a public occasion
entries.example_cn: 总统向人群发表了一篇激昂的演说。
entries.example_en: The president delivered a stirring oration to the crowd.

entries.definition_en: a person who is skilled at giving formal speeches
entries.example_cn: 那位著名的演说家充满激情地发表了演讲。
entries.example_en: The famous orator addressed the crowd with great passion.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of an orator or oratory
entries.example_cn: 他在辩论中的演说技巧吸引了整个观众。
entries.example_en: His oratorical skills captivated the entire audience during the debate.

entries.definition_en: a large musical work for voices and orchestra based on a religious story or text
entries.example_cn: 亨德尔的《弥赛亚》是古典音乐中最著名的清唱剧之一。
entries.example_en: Handel's Messiah is one of the most famous oratorios in classical music.

entries.definition_en: the art or skill of making formal speeches
entries.example_cn: 他在大学学习雄辩术，以便成为一名更好的公众演讲者。
entries.example_en: He studied oratory at university to become a better public speaker.

entries.definition_en: to encircle or surround (poetic)
entries.example_cn: 战车的车轮被金色环饰环绕。
entries.example_en: The chariot's wheels were orbed with gold.

entries.definition_en: an object with a spherical shape
entries.example_cn: 艺术家用石头雕刻出一个完美的球体。
entries.example_en: The artist carved a perfect orb from the stone.

entries.definition_cn: 眼睛（尤指被视为发光球体时）
entries.definition_en: the eye, viewed as a luminous spherical object
entries.example_cn: 诗人描写了她明亮的双眼。
entries.example_en: The poet described her bright orbs.

entries.definition_en: shaped like a circle or almost like a circle
entries.example_cn: 舞者手臂的圆形运动吸引了观众的注意。
entries.example_en: The orbicular motion of the dancer's arms drew the audience's attention.

entries.definition_en: having the shape of a sphere or ball
entries.example_cn: 这座雕塑的球形外观使它看起来像一个球体。
entries.example_en: The orbicular shape of the sculpture made it resemble a sphere.

entries.definition_en: the path described by one celestial body in its revolution about another
entries.example_cn: 月球绕地球运行。
entries.example_en: The moon travels in an orbit around the Earth.

entries.definition_cn: 势力范围；（某行业的）领域
entries.definition_en: an area in which something acts or operates or has power or control
entries.example_cn: 这家公司在科技界占据主导地位。
entries.example_en: The company dominates the tech orbit.

entries.definition_en: a particular environment or walk of life
entries.example_cn: 她一生都在医疗圈子里工作。
entries.example_en: She has spent her whole life in the medical orbit.

entries.definition_en: the path of an electron around the nucleus of an atom
entries.example_cn: 电子在原子核周围沿特定轨道运动。
entries.example_en: Electrons move in specific orbits around the nucleus.

entries.definition_en: the bony cavity in the skull containing the eyeball
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查眼眶是否有骨折。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the orbit for fractures.

entries.definition_en: move in an orbit
entries.example_cn: 这颗卫星每九十分钟绕行星运行一圈。
entries.example_en: The satellite orbits the planet every ninety minutes.

entries.definition_en: relating to an orbit
entries.example_cn: 这颗卫星处于低轨道路径上。
entries.example_en: The satellite is in a low orbital path.

entries.definition_cn: （英国，指道路或铁路）环绕城市外围的
entries.definition_en: UK: (of a road or railway) passing around the outside of an urban area
entries.example_cn: M25 是一条环绕伦敦的环城高速公路。
entries.example_en: The M25 is an orbital motorway around London.

entries.definition_en: relating to the eye socket
entries.example_cn: 外科医生修复了眼眶骨。
entries.example_en: The surgeon repaired the orbital bone.

entries.definition_cn: 绕另一物体运行的物体，尤指不着陆而绕行星运行的航天器
entries.definition_en: an object that orbits another body, especially a spacecraft that orbits a planet without landing
entries.example_cn: 航天局发射了一艘新的绕月轨道器，以研究月球表面。
entries.example_en: The space agency launched a new orbiter to study the moon's surface.

entries.definition_en: A large, predatory black-and-white toothed whale with a prominent dorsal fin, found in cold seas.
entries.example_cn: 虎鲸以其高智商和复杂的社会结构而闻名。
entries.example_en: The orca is known for its intelligence and complex social structures.

entries.definition_en: a garden containing a small area of cultivated trees without undergrowth
entries.example_cn: 这家人夏天周末去果园摘苹果。
entries.example_en: The family spends their summer weekends picking apples in the orchard.

entries.definition_en: a large group of musicians playing various instruments together
entries.example_cn: 管弦乐队昨晚演奏了一首优美的交响乐。
entries.example_en: The orchestra performed a beautiful symphony last night.

entries.definition_cn: （主要用于北美）剧院正厅的座位
entries.definition_en: chiefly North American: the seats on the main floor of a theater
entries.example_cn: 我们买了正厅座位区的票，以便看得更清楚。
entries.example_en: We bought tickets in the orchestra section for a better view.

entries.definition_en: relating to or composed for an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 这场音乐会包含了一套宏伟的管弦乐组曲。
entries.example_en: The concert featured a magnificent orchestral suite.

entries.definition_en: to plan and organize a complex event or action carefully
entries.example_cn: 营销团队精心策划了一场新产品惊喜发布会。
entries.example_en: The marketing team orchestrated a surprise launch event for the new product.

entries.definition_en: to write music for an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 这位作曲家花了数年时间为其交响曲为完整的管弦乐队配器。
entries.example_en: The composer spent years orchestrating his symphony for a full orchestra.

entries.definition_en: the arrangement of a musical piece for an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 作曲家为这部交响曲所作的管弦乐配器非常出色。
entries.example_en: The composer's orchestration of the symphony was brilliant.

entries.definition_en: a musical composition arranged for performance by an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 这位学生研究了一首古典协奏曲的管弦乐改编曲。
entries.example_en: The student studied an orchestration of the classical concerto.

entries.definition_en: the arrangement of events to achieve a maximum effect
entries.example_cn: 营销团队专注于产品发布的精心策划。
entries.example_en: The marketing team focused on the orchestration of the product launch.

entries.definition_cn: 自动协调和管理配置、部署或其他流程的系统
entries.definition_en: a system that automatically coordinates and manages configuration, deployment, or other processes
entries.example_cn: 该编排系统会自动部署应用程序并配置所需的服务。
entries.example_en: The orchestrator automatically deploys the application and configures the required services.

entries.definition_en: a person who arranges music to be performed by an orchestra
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的作曲家聘请了一位技艺高超的管弦乐配器者，将他的钢琴作品改编为完整的交响乐团演奏曲。
entries.example_en: The famous composer hired a skilled orchestrator to adapt his piano pieces for a full symphony orchestra.

usage.label: figurative
usage.pattern: a person who coordinates or orchestrates an activity

entries.definition_en: a plant with flowers of unusual shapes and beautiful colors
entries.example_cn: 这种珍稀的兰花每年只开一次花。
entries.example_en: The rare orchid bloomed only once a year.

entries.definition_en: surgery to remove one or both testicles
entries.example_cn: 该患者接受了睾丸切除术以治疗该病症。
entries.example_en: The patient underwent an orchiectomy to treat the condition.

entries.definition_en: one of the two male reproductive glands that produce spermatozoa and secrete androgens
entries.example_cn: 睾丸中的激素水平调节男性的第二性征。
entries.example_en: The hormone levels in the orchis regulate male secondary sexual characteristics.

entries.definition_cn: 兰属的落叶陆生兰花，具有肉质块茎和顶生直立总状花序
entries.definition_en: any of various deciduous terrestrial orchids having fleshy tubers and flowers in erect terminal racemes
entries.example_cn: 植物学家将这种稀有的兰属植物归类为一个独特的物种。
entries.example_en: Botanists classify this rare orchis as a distinct species.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of one or both testes, causing pain and swelling
entries.example_cn: 患者在经历严重的睾丸疼痛后被诊断为睾丸炎。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with orchitis after experiencing severe testicular pain.

entries.definition_en: to give an official order or command by virtue of superior authority
entries.example_cn: 国王颁布法令，要求所有公民缴纳税款。
entries.example_en: The king ordained that all citizens must pay taxes.

entries.definition_en: to appoint someone to a clerical post or religious office
entries.example_cn: 主教去年任命他为神父。
entries.example_en: The bishop ordained him as a priest last year.

entries.definition_en: to invest someone with ministerial or priestly authority
entries.example_cn: 他被授予在教堂服务的资格。
entries.example_en: He was ordained to serve in the church.

entries.definition_en: to issue an official order or decree
entries.example_cn: 委员会为工厂颁布了新的安全规定。
entries.example_en: The council ordained new safety regulations for the factory.

entries.definition_en: fixed or established especially by order or command
entries.example_cn: 这些规则是由委员会确立的。
entries.example_en: The rules are ordained by the council.

entries.definition_cn: 被赋予神职或祭司职能的
entries.definition_en: invested with ministerial or priestly functions
entries.example_cn: 他去年被祝圣为神父。
entries.example_en: He was ordained as a priest last year.

entries.definition_en: a very difficult or unpleasant experience
entries.example_cn: 等待测试结果是一段可怕的煎熬。
entries.example_en: Waiting for the test results was a terrible ordeal.

entries.definition_en: a dangerous test used in the past to prove someone's guilt or innocence
entries.example_cn: 在中世纪，神判是一种通过将被告置于痛苦中来判定其是否有罪的方法。
entries.example_en: In medieval times, an ordeal was a method to determine guilt by subjecting the accused to pain.

entries.definition_en: a command given by someone in authority that must be obeyed
entries.example_cn: 将军下达了进攻的命令。
entries.example_en: The general gave the order to attack.

entries.definition_en: a logical or comprehensible arrangement of separate elements
entries.example_cn: 她按大小顺序排列了这些书。
entries.example_en: She arranged the books in order of size.

entries.definition_en: the established way things are done in society
