entries.example_en: The popularity of the new smartphone has surprised many experts.

entries.definition_en: the act of making something popular with the general public
entries.example_cn: 互联网的普及改变了人们的沟通方式。
entries.example_en: The popularization of the internet changed how people communicate.

entries.definition_cn: 面向大众的通俗化表达
entries.definition_en: an accessible presentation of specialized or complex material for the general public
entries.example_cn: 这本书提供了复杂量子物理学的通俗化解释。
entries.example_en: The book offers a popularization of complex quantum physics.

entries.definition_en: to make something popular and present it to the general public
entries.example_cn: 作者写了一本书来普及复杂的科学理论。
entries.example_en: The author wrote a book to popularize complex scientific theories.

entries.definition_en: to make something understandable to the general public
entries.example_cn: 老师试图让学生们理解这些困难的数学概念。
entries.example_en: The teacher tried to popularize the difficult math concepts for the students.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes a subject or activity attractive and accessible to the general public
entries.example_cn: 这位教授是向高中生普及复杂量子物理学的优秀普及者。
entries.example_en: The professor is an excellent popularizer of complex quantum physics for high school students.

entries.definition_en: in the way that most people believe or do
entries.example_cn: 人们普遍认为这个故事发生在18世纪。
entries.example_en: The story is popularly believed to have happened in the 18th century.

entries.definition_en: to fill a place with inhabitants
entries.example_cn: 这个新的住房项目旨在让家庭搬入那个偏远的山谷。
entries.example_en: The new housing project aims to populate the remote valley with families.

entries.definition_en: to become filled with items
entries.example_cn: 约翰点击了“搜索”按钮，等待列表自动填充内容。
entries.example_en: John clicked the Search button and waited for the list to populate.

entries.definition_en: to be an inhabitant of or reside in a place
entries.example_cn: 这座古城曾经居住着一个庞大的商人部落。
entries.example_en: The ancient city was once populated by a large tribe of traders.

entries.definition_en: furnished with inhabitants
entries.example_cn: 地图显示了哪些地区有人居住，哪些没有。
entries.example_en: The map shows which areas are populated and which are not.

entries.definition_en: the people who live in a specific territory or state
entries.example_cn: 这座城市的居民欢迎新图书馆。
entries.example_en: The city's population welcomed the new library.

entries.definition_en: the total number of inhabitants in a given place, or the number of a particular group
entries.example_cn: 这个国家的人口超过一亿。
entries.example_en: The population of the country is over one hundred million.

entries.definition_en: a group of organisms of the same species living in a given area
entries.example_cn: 这片森林里狼的种群数量非常少。
entries.example_en: The population of wolves in this forest is very small.

entries.definition_en: in statistics, the entire group of items from which samples can be drawn
entries.example_cn: 这项调查是基于全国人口样本进行的。
entries.example_en: The survey was based on a sample of the national population.

entries.definition_en: the act of populating; causing people or organisms to live in a place
entries.example_cn: 该岛的殖民是一个缓慢的定居过程。
entries.example_en: The colonization of the island was a slow process of population.

entries.definition_en: a political belief that supports the rights and powers of ordinary people against the privileged elite
entries.example_cn: 该党凭借民粹主义纲领赢得了选举。

entries.definition_en: a person who supports the rights of ordinary people against the elite
entries.example_cn: 这位民粹主义领导人承诺降低工人阶级的税收。
entries.example_en: The populist leader promised to lower taxes for the working class.

entries.definition_en: Of or relating to populism.
entries.example_cn: 该党采取了民粹主义的经济政策。
entries.example_en: The party adopted a populist approach to economic policy.

entries.definition_en: having a large number of people living in it
entries.example_cn: 这座岛屿以其庞大且人口稠密的城市而闻名。

entries.definition_en: a structure attached to the outside of a building that provides a covered entrance

entries.definition_en: relating to or suggesting swine
entries.example_cn: 该疫苗是使用猪细胞开发的。
entries.example_en: The vaccine was developed using porcine cells.

entries.definition_cn: 像猪一样的；粗俗地贪吃或贪婪的
entries.definition_en: resembling swine; coarsely gluttonous or greedy

entries.example_en: His porcine appetite for money never seemed to be satisfied.

entries.example_en: The porousness of the sponge allowed it to soak up the spilled water quickly.

entries.definition_cn: 卟啉（一类含吡咯环的杂环化合物）
entries.definition_en: any of a class of heterocyclic compounds containing pyrrole rings arranged in a roughly square or similar structure

entries.example_en: Scientists are studying how porphyrin absorbs light in plant cells.

entries.definition_en: to bring a ship to a port
entries.example_cn: 这艘船将于明天早上靠港。
entries.example_en: The vessel will port tomorrow morning.

entries.definition_en: to turn a ship to the left

entries.definition_en: an opening in a wall or vehicle for firing
entries.example_cn: 士兵们通过坦克上的炮口开火。
entries.example_en: The soldiers fired through the port in the tank.

entries.definition_en: the hilum of an organ, where its blood vessels, nerves, or ducts enter and leave

entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the liver's porta to locate the main blood vessels.

entries.definition_cn: 便于携带或移动的特性；便携性

entries.example_en: The portability of this laptop makes it perfect for business travelers.

entries.definition_en: easily or conveniently transported
entries.example_cn: 这个便携式设备很容易放进你的包里。
entries.example_en: This portable device is easy to carry in your bag.

entries.example_cn: 这艘船有一个舷外马达。
entries.example_en: The boat has a portable engine.

entries.example_cn: 商人利用这条陆路路线把船从河里运到湖里。
entries.example_en: Traders used the portage to move boats from the river to the lake.

entries.definition_en: the cost of carrying or transporting goods
entries.example_cn: 重货的运输费非常高。
entries.example_en: The portage for the heavy cargo was very high.

entries.definition_en: a grand and imposing entrance
entries.example_cn: 这座城堡有一个宏伟的石门。
entries.example_en: The castle has a magnificent stone portal.

entries.definition_en: a website that serves as an entrance to other websites
entries.example_cn: 这个新闻门户网站汇集了世界各地的故事。
entries.example_en: This news portal aggregates stories from around the world.

entries.definition_en: a small vein that carries blood into the liver
entries.example_cn: 门静脉将富含营养的血液从肠道输送到肝脏。
entries.example_en: The portal vein transports nutrient-rich blood from the intestines to the liver.

entries.definition_en: a heavy iron or wooden gate that hangs in a castle entrance and can be lowered to block passage
entries.example_cn: 守卫放下吊闸以保护城堡免受攻击。
entries.example_en: The guards lowered the portcullis to protect the castle from attackers.

entries.definition_en: a canopy extending from a building entrance to shelter people entering or leaving vehicles
entries.example_cn: 遮雨篷保护乘客免受雨水侵袭，方便他们搬运行李。
entries.example_en: The porte-cochere protected passengers from the rain as they loaded their luggage.

entries.definition_en: a covered entrance through a building leading to a courtyard for carriages
entries.example_cn: 马车廊穿过建筑，通向一个封闭的庭院。
entries.example_en: The porte-cochere led through the building into an enclosed courtyard.

entries.definition_en: to serve as a warning or omen of; to signify or denote
entries.example_cn: 乌云预示着暴风雨即将来临。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds portend a storm.

entries.definition_en: a sign or omen that an event is about to happen, especially an unfortunate or evil one
entries.example_cn: 乌云是即将到来的风暴的预兆。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds were a portent of the storm to come.

entries.definition_en: of great importance or significance, often in a serious or threatening way
entries.example_cn: 宣布前的房间里一片寂静，气氛显得十分不祥。
entries.example_en: The silence in the room felt portentous before the announcement.

entries.definition_en: ominously prophetic
entries.example_cn: 那位老人的话似乎是在预言灾难。
entries.example_en: The old man's portentous words seemed to warn of disaster.

entries.definition_cn: 自命不凡的；装腔作势的
entries.definition_en: puffed up with vanity
entries.example_cn: 他发表了一篇关于新发明的自命不凡的演讲。
entries.example_en: He gave a portentous speech about his new invention.

entries.definition_en: in an ominous or pompous manner
entries.example_cn: 乌云不祥地聚集在城市上空。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds gathered portentously over the city.

entries.definition_en: a person employed to carry luggage and supplies
entries.example_cn: 搬运工帮我们把沉重的行李箱搬上了火车。
entries.example_en: The porter helped us carry our heavy suitcases to the train.

entries.definition_en: someone who guards an entrance
entries.example_cn: 看门人为访客打开了大门。
entries.example_en: The porter opened the gate for the visitors.

entries.definition_en: a very dark sweet ale brewed from roasted unmalted barley
entries.example_cn: 他们点了一杯波特啤酒搭配晚餐。
entries.example_en: They ordered a glass of porter to go with their dinner.

entries.definition_en: a railroad employee who assists passengers, especially on sleeping cars
entries.example_cn: 列车员给我们的卧铺车厢送来了热毛巾和毯子。
entries.example_en: The porter brought us hot towels and blankets in our cabin.

entries.definition_en: to carry luggage or supplies
entries.example_cn: 搬运工把箱子搬上了楼梯。
entries.example_en: The porter portered the boxes up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: the charge for carrying burdens by porters
entries.example_cn: 探险队必须支付搬运费才能翻越高山。
entries.example_en: The expedition had to pay porterage to cross the high mountains.

entries.definition_en: the transportation of burdens by porters
entries.example_cn: 在过去，人力搬运是丛林中运输货物的唯一方式。
entries.example_en: In the old days, porterage was the only way to move goods through the jungle.

entries.definition_en: a large steak cut from the thick end of the short loin, featuring a T-shaped bone and a substantial piece of tenderloin
entries.example_cn: 厨师推荐T骨牛排给两个人吃，因为它分量充足且风味浓郁。
entries.example_en: The chef recommended the porterhouse for two people because of its generous size and rich flavor.

entries.definition_en: a list of financial assets held by an individual or institution
entries.example_cn: 银行经理审查了客户的投资组合，建议新的投资。
entries.example_en: The bank manager reviewed the client's portfolio to suggest new investments.

entries.definition_en: a collection of creative work shown to potential employers
entries.example_cn: 那位艺术家向画廊提交了她的作品集以供审阅。
entries.example_en: The artist submitted her portfolio to the gallery for review.

entries.definition_en: a flat case used for carrying papers, drawings, or maps
entries.example_cn: 她提着一个皮质文件夹，里面装着自己的素描。
entries.example_en: She carried her sketches in a leather portfolio.

entries.definition_en: the position of a minister in charge of a government department
entries.example_cn: 他上个月被任命为教育部长。
entries.example_en: He was appointed to the portfolio of education last month.

entries.definition_en: a window in a ship or airplane
entries.example_cn: 她透过舷窗向下看，看到了大海。
entries.example_en: She looked out of the porthole to see the ocean below.

entries.definition_cn: 用于射击的开口（如在墙壁、船只或装甲车上）
entries.definition_en: an opening in a wall, ship, or armored vehicle for firing through
entries.example_cn: 士兵们通过坦克侧面的射击孔向敌人开火。
entries.example_en: The soldiers fired their weapons through the porthole in the tank's side.

entries.definition_en: a covered entrance to a building, often supported by columns
entries.example_cn: 游客们穿过宏伟的门廊进入博物馆。
entries.example_en: Visitors entered the museum through the grand portico.

entries.definition_en: a heavy curtain hung across a doorway
entries.example_cn: 她拉上门帘以阻挡寒风。
entries.example_en: She pulled the portiere closed to block the wind.

entries.definition_en: a single serving of food or drink
entries.example_cn: 我要一份鸡肉和一份米饭。
entries.example_en: I will have a portion of chicken and a portion of rice.

entries.definition_en: a part of something that is included in a larger whole
entries.example_cn: 她吃了很多蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She ate a large portion of the cake.

entries.definition_en: an amount of something that is given or assigned to someone
entries.example_cn: 每位工人每天都能分到一份食物。
entries.example_en: Each worker received a daily portion of food.

entries.definition_en: money or property that belongs to or is owed to a person or group
entries.example_cn: 这家公司所占的利润份额很高。
entries.example_en: The company's portion of the profits was very high.

entries.definition_en: a part of something that is less than the whole
entries.example_cn: 我们需要存一部分钱以备将来之用。
entries.example_en: We need to save a portion of our money for the future.

entries.definition_en: to divide something into parts and give them out
entries.example_cn: 老师把书分给了学生们。
entries.example_en: The teacher portioned the books among the students.

entries.definition_en: the general situation or condition of someone's life
entries.example_cn: 他的人生境遇非常艰难。
entries.example_en: His portion in life has been very difficult.

entries.definition_en: money or property brought by a woman to her husband when they get married
entries.example_cn: 她结婚时给丈夫带来了丰厚的嫁妆。
entries.example_en: She brought a large portion to her husband at marriage.

entries.definition_en: somewhat fat or overweight, especially with a dignified appearance
entries.example_cn: 那位身材臃肿的绅士舒适地坐在扶手椅里。
entries.example_en: The portly gentleman sat comfortably in the armchair.

entries.definition_en: a new word created by combining parts of two other words to merge their meanings
entries.example_cn: “Brunch”是“breakfast”和“lunch”组合而成的混成词。
entries.example_en: “Brunch” is a portmanteau of “breakfast” and “lunch.”

entries.definition_en: a large, stiff leather bag with two hinged sections used for traveling
entries.example_cn: 在长途旅行前，他把衣服装进了一个大双折皮箱里。
entries.example_en: He packed his clothes into a large portmanteau before the long journey.

entries.definition_en: any likeness of a person, in any medium
entries.example_cn: 她买了一幅祖父的画像。
entries.example_en: She bought a portrait of her grandfather.

entries.definition_cn: 描绘某人外貌和性格的文字画像
entries.definition_en: a word picture of a person's appearance and character
entries.example_cn: 这部小说生动地描绘了主人公的形象。
entries.example_en: The novel provides a vivid portrait of the protagonist.

entries.definition_en: an artist who paints or draws portraits
entries.example_cn: 这位肖像画家花了几个小时来捕捉模特的表情。
entries.example_en: The portraitist spent hours capturing the subject's expression.

entries.definition_en: the activity or art of creating portraits
entries.example_cn: 她的肖像画创作生涯始于在著名艺术家门下学习。
entries.example_en: Her career in portraiture began when she studied under a famous artist.

entries.definition_en: a written or spoken description that vividly depicts a person's appearance and character
entries.example_cn: 作者对那位老人的肖像描写捕捉到了他疲惫的眼神和慈祥的微笑。
entries.example_en: The author's portraiture of the elderly man captured his weary eyes and kind smile.

entries.definition_en: to describe or represent someone or something in words
entries.example_cn: 这部小说描写了19世纪一位年轻艺术家的生活。
entries.example_en: The novel portrays the life of a young artist in the 19th century.

entries.definition_en: to create a picture or image of someone
entries.example_cn: 画家被要求为那位著名将军画像。
entries.example_en: The painter was asked to portray the famous general.

entries.definition_en: to act the part of a character in a play or film
entries.example_cn: 她在最新电影中扮演一名侦探。
entries.example_en: She portrays a detective in the new movie.

entries.definition_en: to represent an idea or concept in art
entries.example_cn: 这座雕塑描绘了自由的概念。
entries.example_en: The sculpture portrays the concept of freedom.

entries.definition_en: a description of a person's appearance and character
entries.example_cn: 这部小说生动地描绘了主人公的童年。
entries.example_en: The novel offers a vivid portrayal of the protagonist's childhood.

entries.definition_en: acting a role on stage
entries.example_cn: 她扮演那位悲剧女王令人动容。
entries.example_en: Her portrayal of the tragic queen was moving.

entries.definition_en: a picture or portrait of someone
entries.example_cn: 博物馆收藏了一幅这位历史人物的精美画像。
entries.example_en: The museum houses an exquisite portrayal of the historical figure.

entries.definition_en: any likeness of a person
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家创作了一幅当地领导人的引人注目的肖像。
entries.example_en: The artist created a striking portrayal of the local leader.

entries.definition_en: a drawing or painting of someone
entries.example_cn: 画廊展出了一幅关于这位著名诗人的新画作。
entries.example_en: The gallery features a new portrayal of the famous poet.

entries.definition_cn: 描绘者；（尤指）肖像画家或扮演者
entries.definition_en: a person who portrays someone or something, especially in a portrait or performance
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的肖像画家以惊人的准确性描绘出了人物的形象。
entries.example_en: The famous portrayer captured the subject's likeness with remarkable accuracy.

entries.definition_en: a plant with small, colorful flowers that often close during the day
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了鲜艳的马齿苋属植物。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with bright portulaca flowers.

entries.definition_en: a body position assumed by models for photos or art
entries.example_cn: 模特为相机摆出了一个高难度的姿势。
entries.example_en: The model struck a difficult pose for the camera.

entries.definition_en: an affected manner intended to impress others
entries.example_cn: 他那种礼貌的态度只是为了给客人留下印象而做的做作表现。
entries.example_en: His polite manner was just a pose to impress the guests.

entries.definition_en: to assume a body position for artistic purposes
entries.example_cn: 演员们在剧终时摆出姿势。
entries.example_en: The actors posed for the final scene of the play.

entries.definition_en: to offer something for others to consider
entries.example_cn: 委员会将把这个问题提出来供公众讨论。
entries.example_en: The committee will pose the question to the public for discussion.

entries.definition_en: to pretend to be someone else, sometimes fraudulently
entries.example_cn: 他冒充医生以进入大楼。
entries.example_en: He posed as a doctor to gain access to the building.

entries.definition_en: to behave in an affected way to impress others
entries.example_cn: 她故意装腔作势以给评委留下印象。
entries.example_en: She posed to impress the judges.

entries.definition_en: a deliberate pretense or exaggerated display
entries.example_cn: 这个慈善活动纯粹是为了吸引捐赠者而搞的伪装。
entries.example_en: The charity event was nothing but a pose to attract donors.

entries.definition_en: to put something in a certain place or location
entries.example_cn: 艺术家把雕像放在花园入口处。
entries.example_en: The artist posed the statue at the garden entrance.

entries.definition_en: holding a particular pose, especially for a photograph or painting
entries.example_cn: 模特为了相机摆出了完美的姿势。
entries.example_en: The model stood perfectly posed for the camera.

entries.definition_en: a person who pretends to be something they are not
entries.example_cn: 他是个十足的伪装者，假装是艺术专家。
entries.example_en: He is a real poser, pretending to be an expert on art.

entries.definition_en: a person who poses for a photographer or artist
entries.example_cn: 这位著名画家为他的最新肖像画聘请了一位当地模特。
entries.example_en: The famous painter hired a local poser for his latest portrait.

entries.definition_en: a difficult or confusing question or problem
entries.example_cn: 这道数学题对学生们来说真是个难题。
entries.example_en: The math problem was a real poser for the students.

entries.definition_en: a person who habitually pretends to be something they are not
entries.example_cn: 他只是一个假装是艺术家的矫揉造作的人。
entries.example_en: He was just a poseur pretending to be an artist.

entries.definition_en: elegant and fashionable
entries.example_cn: 他们住在海边的一家豪华酒店里。
entries.example_en: They stayed in a posh hotel by the sea.

entries.definition_en: the act of assuming a certain position, especially for a photograph or portrait
entries.example_cn: 摄影师指导后，模特摆姿势时显得更加自然。
entries.example_en: The model's posing became more natural after the photographer gave her some direction.

entries.definition_en: to propose something for consideration or study
entries.example_cn: 研究人员提出了一种解释这一现象的新说法。
entries.example_en: The researcher posited a new explanation for the pattern.

entries.definition_en: to assume something as a given fact or principle
entries.example_cn: 科学家们通常假定重力是自然界的一种基本力。
entries.example_en: Scientists often posit that gravity is a fundamental force of nature.

entries.definition_en: to place something firmly in a specific position
entries.example_cn: 他小心翼翼地将那个重箱子稳稳地放在狭窄的架子上。
entries.example_en: He posited the heavy box carefully on the narrow shelf.

entries.definition_en: a statement accepted as true to serve as a starting point for reasoning
entries.example_cn: 该理论基于这样一个假设：所有物质都由原子组成。
entries.example_en: The theory is based on the posit that all matter is composed of atoms.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用于表示实数、旨在替代 IEEE 754 浮点格式的数字格式
entries.definition_en: a number format for real numbers designed as an alternative to IEEE 754 floating-point formats
entries.example_cn: 研究人员在人工智能系统中比较了使用 32 位 posit 和 32 位浮点数进行的计算。
entries.example_en: The researchers compared computations using 32-bit posits and 32-bit floating-point numbers in their AI system.

entries.definition_en: the specific part of space that something occupies
entries.example_cn: 花瓶被放在架子上显眼的位置。
entries.example_en: The vase was placed in a prominent position on the shelf.

entries.definition_en: a job or role within an organization
entries.example_cn: 她申请了团队领导的职位。
entries.example_en: She applied for the position of team leader.

entries.definition_en: a way of thinking about or viewing a situation
entries.example_cn: 从我的角度来看，这个项目继续下去似乎风险太大。
entries.example_en: From my position, the project seems too risky to continue.

entries.definition_en: the arrangement of the body and its limbs
entries.example_cn: 体操运动员在动作中保持了一个高难度的姿势。
entries.example_en: The gymnast held a difficult position during the routine.

entries.definition_en: to put something in a specific place or abstract location
entries.example_cn: 请把椅子放好，这样你就能清楚地看到屏幕。
entries.example_en: Please position the chair so you can see the screen clearly.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to be in a suitable place or state
entries.example_cn: 经理把新员工安排在接待台。
entries.example_en: The manager positioned the new employee at the front desk.

entries.definition_en: one's rank or status in society
entries.example_cn: 他努力工作以提高自己在公司的地位。
entries.example_en: He worked hard to improve his position in the company.

entries.definition_en: a place where troops are located for military strategy
entries.example_cn: 士兵们坚守阵地抵御敌人的进攻。
entries.example_en: The soldiers held their position against the enemy attack.

entries.definition_cn: （体育运动中的）位置；场上职责
entries.definition_en: A position on a sports field, together with the duties assigned to the player in that position.
entries.example_cn: 别满场乱跑，守好你的位置。
entries.example_en: Stop running all over the field and play your position.

entries.definition_cn: （个人或机构持有的）证券、商品或其他金融工具的数量；持仓
entries.definition_en: An amount of securities, commodities, or other financial instruments held by a person or organization.
entries.example_cn: 该基金减少了对科技股的持仓。
entries.example_en: The fund reduced its position in technology stocks.

entries.definition_en: able to be placed or arranged in a specific position
entries.example_cn: 相机支架可调节位置，以便从任何角度拍摄。
entries.example_en: The camera mount is positionable to capture angles from any direction.

entries.definition_en: relating to or determined by position
entries.example_cn: 位置优势帮助球队赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The positional advantage helped the team win the game.

entries.definition_cn: 控制阀定位器；用电信号或气动信号控制执行器开闭的部件
entries.definition_en: the part of a control valve that controls an actuator's opening or closing using electric or pneumatic signals
entries.example_cn: 控制阀的定位器根据气动信号调节执行器。
entries.example_en: The control valve's positioner adjusts the actuator in response to pneumatic signals.

entries.definition_en: a device that moves a read/write head to the correct track on a disk
entries.example_cn: 硬盘的定位器确保数据从正确的扇区读取。
entries.example_en: The hard drive's positioner ensures data is read from the right sector.

entries.definition_en: the act of placing something in a specific location
entries.example_cn: 卫星的定位对于任务的成功至关重要。
entries.example_en: The positioning of the satellite was critical for the success of the mission.

entries.definition_en: causing something to fall into line or into position
entries.example_cn: 新的定位系统确保所有部件完美对齐。
entries.example_en: The new positioning system ensures that all components align perfectly.

entries.definition_cn: 表示肯定、赞同或确定的
entries.definition_en: showing agreement, approval, or certainty
entries.example_cn: 她对这项提议给予了肯定的答复。
entries.example_en: She gave a positive response to the proposal.

entries.definition_en: involving benefits or good outcomes
entries.example_cn: 运动对健康的积极影响众所周知。
entries.example_en: The positive effects of exercise on health are well known.

entries.definition_cn: 呈阳性的；显示存在某种疾病或病原体的
entries.definition_en: showing that a disease or condition exists
entries.example_cn: 病毒检测呈阳性。
entries.example_en: The test came back positive for the virus.

entries.definition_cn: 深信不疑的；非常有把握的
entries.definition_en: fully convinced or very sure about something
entries.example_cn: 我深信他会准时到达。
entries.example_en: I am positive that he will arrive on time.

entries.definition_cn: 不可否认的；无法反驳的
entries.definition_en: undeniable or impossible to disprove
entries.example_cn: 证据确凿地证明了他的罪行。
entries.example_en: The evidence was positive proof of his guilt.

entries.definition_en: the basic form of an adjective or adverb, without any comparison
entries.example_cn: 在短语“更积极”中，“积极”是形容词的原级形式。
entries.example_en: In the phrase 'more positive', 'positive' is the positive form of the adjective.

entries.definition_cn: 与原物色调一致的正片或照片
entries.definition_en: a photograph where the tones match the original subject
entries.example_cn: 摄影师从底片上冲洗出了正片。
entries.example_en: The photographer developed the positive from the negative.

entries.definition_cn: 正式规定的；强制要求的
entries.definition_en: officially established or required
entries.example_cn: 成文法规定所有驾驶员必须系安全带。
entries.example_en: The positive law requires all drivers to wear seatbelts.

entries.definition_en: in a very strong or extreme way
entries.example_cn: 今天的天气简直冷得要命。
entries.example_en: The weather is positively freezing today.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows you are sure or agree
entries.example_cn: 我肯定他会成功。
entries.example_en: I positively believe that he will succeed.

entries.definition_cn: 令人鼓舞或预示成功结果的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being encouraging or promising a successful outcome
entries.example_cn: 早期结果的积极性质给了团队希望。
entries.example_en: The positiveness of the early results gave the team hope.

entries.definition_cn: 确信、肯定及独断的坚决态度
entries.definition_en: a quality characterized by certainty, acceptance, affirmation, and dogmatic assertiveness
entries.example_cn: 他对项目成功的坚定信心具有感染力。
entries.example_en: His positiveness about the project's success was contagious.

entries.definition_cn: 无可否认且不值得争论的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being undeniable and not worth arguing about
entries.example_cn: 他证据的确定性不容置疑。
entries.example_en: The positiveness of his evidence left no room for doubt.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being greater than zero
entries.example_cn: 该值的正值表明净收益。
entries.example_en: The positiveness of the value indicates a net gain.

entries.definition_en: the characteristic of being the positive electric pole
entries.example_cn: 用电压表测量了该端子的正极特性。
entries.example_en: The positiveness of the terminal was measured with a voltmeter.

entries.definition_en: the form of empiricism that bases all knowledge on perceptual experience (not on intuition or revelation)
entries.example_cn: 这位科学家摒弃了形而上学，转而信奉实证主义，仅依赖可观察的数据。
entries.example_en: The scientist rejected metaphysics in favor of positivism, relying only on observable data.

entries.definition_en: the doctrine that law is based on rules enacted or posited by human authorities, rather than on moral values
entries.example_cn: 法律实证主义认为，法律的有效性与其道德价值相分离。
entries.example_en: Legal positivism treats the validity of a law as separate from its moral worth.

entries.definition_en: a person who believes that only observable facts are valid knowledge
entries.example_cn: 作为一名实证主义者，这位科学家拒绝那些无法验证的理论。
entries.example_en: As a positivist, the scientist rejected theories that could not be tested.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of positivism
entries.example_cn: 实证主义方法严格关注经验证据。
entries.example_en: The positivist approach focuses strictly on empirical evidence.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to positivism
entries.example_cn: 这种实证主义的科学方法强调观察和证据。
entries.example_en: The positivistic approach to science emphasizes observation and evidence.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being positive; optimism
entries.example_cn: 团队的乐观情绪提升了他们的士气。
entries.example_en: The positivity of the team boosted their morale.

entries.definition_cn: 以确定、肯定和武断断言为特征的性质或状态
entries.definition_en: a quality or state characterized by certainty, affirmation, and dogmatic assertiveness
entries.example_cn: 她以如此肯定而武断的语气陈述结论，以至于没人觉得可以质疑。
entries.example_en: She stated her conclusion with such positivity that no one felt able to challenge it.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being undeniable
entries.example_cn: 他的成就的无可争辩性对每个人来说都很清楚。
entries.example_en: The positivity of his achievements is clear to everyone.

entries.definition_en: an amount greater than zero
entries.example_cn: 结果的正值表明带有正电荷。
entries.example_en: The positivity of the result indicates a positive charge.

entries.definition_en: the characteristic of having a positive electric charge
entries.example_cn: 该实验测量了离子的正电性。
entries.example_en: The experiment measured the positivity of the ion.

entries.definition_en: an elementary particle with positive charge; interaction of a positron and an electron results in annihilation
entries.example_cn: 物理学家研究正电子以了解物质的基本结构。
entries.example_en: Physicists study positrons to understand the fundamental structure of matter.

entries.definition_en: a temporary police force
entries.example_cn: 治安官召集了一支警队去追捕那个逃犯。
entries.example_en: The sheriff assembled a posse to track down the outlaw.

entries.definition_en: to have ownership or possession of something
entries.example_cn: 他们拥有一大批罕见的书籍。
entries.example_en: They possess a large collection of rare books.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有（某种特质、知识或技能）
entries.definition_en: to have a specific attribute, knowledge, or skill
entries.example_cn: 她拥有极大的耐心和同理心。
entries.example_en: She possesses great patience and understanding.

entries.definition_en: to be controlled by an emotion or idea
entries.example_cn: 他突然被愤怒控制了。
entries.example_en: He was possessed by a sudden rage.

entries.definition_en: influenced or controlled by a powerful force such as a strong emotion
entries.example_cn: 她突然被愤怒支配，把一切都扔了出去。
entries.example_en: She was possessed by a sudden rage and threw everything.

entries.definition_en: of, pertaining to, or like a demon or possession by a demon
entries.example_cn: 那个古老的故事描述了一个被恶魔附身、说着异语的女人。
entries.example_en: The old story describes a possessed woman who speaks in tongues.

entries.definition_en: the state of having or controlling something
entries.example_cn: 警方正在调查非法持有枪支的行为。
entries.example_en: The police are investigating the illegal possession of firearms.

entries.definition_en: anything owned or possessed
entries.example_cn: 他在搬去新城市前列出了自己所有的财产。
entries.example_en: He listed all his possessions before moving to a new city.

entries.definition_en: (sport) the act of controlling the ball (or puck)
entries.example_cn: 中场球员连续几分钟控制着球。
entries.example_en: The midfielder maintained possession of the ball for several minutes.

entries.definition_cn: 被激情或超自然力量控制的状态
entries.definition_en: being controlled by passion or the supernatural
entries.example_cn: 这个故事描述了一位被鬼魂附身的女子。
entries.example_en: The story describes a woman in a state of possession by a spirit.

entries.definition_cn: 坚决控制自己行为的特质
entries.definition_en: the trait of resolutely controlling your own behavior
entries.example_cn: 在危机中，领导者必须具备沉着冷静的特质。
entries.example_en: Self-possession is essential for a leader in a crisis.

entries.definition_en: a territory that is controlled by a ruling state
entries.example_cn: 该条约划定了该领土的边界。
entries.example_en: The treaty defined the boundaries of the possession.

entries.definition_cn: 对某事或某个想法的痴迷
entries.definition_en: a mania restricted to one thing or idea
entries.example_cn: 他对集邮的痴迷在收藏爱好者中众所周知。
entries.example_en: His possession for collecting stamps is well known among hobbyists.

entries.definition_cn: 表示所有关系的；所有格的
entries.definition_en: used to express or indicate possession
entries.example_cn: 名词 child 的所有格形式是 child's。
entries.example_en: The possessive form of the noun 'child' is 'child's'.

entries.definition_en: showing a desire to control or dominate others
entries.example_cn: 她控制欲强的行为让朋友们感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: Her possessive behavior made her friends uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: wanting to own something
entries.example_cn: 他对他的新车有一种非常渴望拥有的态度。
entries.example_en: He has a very possessive attitude towards his new car.

entries.definition_en: a grammatical case used to show ownership
entries.example_cn: 在英语中，所有格通常通过添加撇号和 s 来表示。
entries.example_en: In English, the possessive is often shown by adding an apostrophe and s.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows you want to own or control someone or something completely
entries.example_cn: 他带着占有欲看着她。
entries.example_en: He looked at her possessively.

entries.definition_cn: 过度的占有欲或支配欲
entries.definition_en: excessive desire to possess or dominate
entries.example_cn: 他的占有欲让他的伴侣感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: His possessiveness made his partner feel uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: a person who owns or has something
entries.example_cn: 那位拥有罕见手稿的人拒绝出售它。
entries.example_en: The possessor of the rare manuscript refused to sell it.

entries.definition_cn: 用奶油、糖和柠檬等调味料制成的布丁状甜点
entries.definition_en: a pudding-like dessert made from cream, sugar, and flavoring such as lemon
entries.example_cn: 我们以柠檬奶油布丁结束了这顿饭。
entries.example_en: We ended the meal with a lemon posset.

entries.definition_cn: 用葡萄酒等酒精饮料使牛奶凝结而成的热饮
entries.definition_en: a hot drink of milk curdled with a strong infusion such as wine
entries.example_cn: 在18世纪，奶酒是正式晚宴上常见的一种热饮。
entries.example_en: In the 18th century, a posset was a popular hot drink served at formal dinners.

entries.definition_cn: 未来成功或发展的前景；潜力
entries.definition_en: a prospect of future success or development
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术具有很大的未来发展潜力。
entries.example_en: The new technology offers great possibilities for future development.

entries.definition_cn: 存在、发生或为真的能力
entries.definition_en: capability of existing or happening or being true
entries.example_cn: 明天可能会下雨。
entries.example_en: It is a possibility that it will rain tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: a possible alternative
entries.example_cn: 在做选择之前，我们考虑了每一个备选方案。
entries.example_en: We considered every possibility before making a choice.

entries.definition_cn: 对自然界的初步见解；一种尚未证实但若能成立则能解释某些事实或现象的概念
entries.definition_en: a tentative insight into the natural world; a concept that is not yet verified but that if true would explain certain facts or phenomena
entries.example_cn: 这位科学家提出了一个新的假说来解释数据。
entries.example_en: The scientist proposed a new possibility to explain the data.

entries.definition_en: capable of happening or existing
entries.example_cn: 今天能完成工作吗？
entries.example_en: Is it possible to finish the work today?

entries.definition_en: possible or plausible as an explanation or reason
entries.example_cn: 他缺席可能有原因。
entries.example_en: There is a possible reason for his absence.

entries.definition_en: something that can be done
entries.example_cn: 我们需要考虑所有可能的解决方案。
entries.example_en: We need to consider all possible solutions.

entries.definition_en: an applicant who might be suitable
entries.example_cn: 她是这份工作的可能候选人。
entries.example_en: She is a possible candidate for the job.

entries.definition_en: to the extent that it is possible
entries.example_cn: 你有可能在明天之前完成工作。
entries.example_en: You can possibly finish the work by tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: perhaps; indicating that something may be true
entries.example_cn: 我们或许会在车站遇到他。
entries.example_en: We might possibly meet him at the station.

entries.definition_en: a nocturnal arboreal marsupial with a naked prehensile tail, found from southern North America to northern South America
entries.example_cn: 这只负鼠爬下树在地面上寻找食物。
entries.example_en: The possum climbed down the tree to find food on the ground.

entries.definition_en: a small furry Australian arboreal marsupial having a long, usually prehensile tail
entries.example_cn: 这只澳洲袋貂安静地坐在桉树上。
entries.example_en: The possum sat quietly in the eucalyptus tree.

entries.definition_en: a job in an organization
entries.example_cn: 他被提供了一份财务部门的职位。
entries.example_en: He was offered a post in the finance department.

entries.definition_en: an upright piece of timber or metal fixed in the ground
entries.example_cn: 篱笆由木柱支撑。
entries.example_en: The fence is supported by wooden posts.

entries.definition_en: the position where a guard or sentry stands
entries.example_cn: 士兵整夜站在他的哨位上站岗。
entries.example_en: The soldier stood guard at his post all night.

entries.definition_en: a military installation where troops are stationed
entries.example_cn: 士兵们在演习结束后回到了军营。
entries.example_en: The soldiers returned to their post after the exercise.

entries.definition_en: to attach something in a public place for notice
entries.example_cn: 他们在社区公告栏上张贴了一张通知。
entries.example_en: They posted a notice on the community board.

entries.definition_en: to assign to a station
entries.example_cn: 警察在入口处派驻了警官。
entries.example_en: The police posted officers at the entrance.

entries.definition_en: to publicize using a poster
entries.example_cn: 艺术家在墙上张贴了她的作品。
entries.example_en: The artist posted her work on the wall.

entries.definition_en: to assign someone to a job or position
entries.example_cn: 经理将他调派到新的分支机构。
entries.example_en: The manager posted him to a new branch office.

entries.definition_cn: （语音学）舌头在齿龈隆起后部附近或与其接触发出的音
entries.definition_en: a sound made by placing the tongue near or touching the back of the alveolar ridge
entries.example_cn: 单词“ship”中的 /ʃ/ 音是一个后齿龈擦音。
entries.example_en: The /ʃ/ sound in 'ship' is a post-alveolar fricative.

entries.definition_en: existing after the period of communism
entries.example_cn: 后共产主义时代给经济带来了重大变化。
entries.example_en: The post-communist era brought significant changes to the economy.

entries.definition_en: having the postage paid by the sender
entries.example_cn: 请将包裹免费邮寄（由寄件人付邮资）到以下地址。
entries.example_en: Please send the package post-free to the address below.

entries.definition_cn: （英）邮寄给顾客且无需另付邮资的；免邮资的
entries.definition_en: British: supplied by post to a customer without an additional charge for postage
entries.example_cn: 订购三本或以上的书可免邮资寄送。
entries.example_en: The books are post-free when you order three or more.

entries.definition_en: very quickly; with all possible speed
entries.example_cn: 她急忙寄出那封信，以确保它在截止日期前到达。
entries.example_en: She sent the letter post-haste to ensure it arrived before the deadline.

entries.definition_en: a horse kept at an inn for mail carriers or travelers to use
entries.example_cn: 旅行者租了一匹驿马以加快行程。
entries.example_en: The traveler rented a post-horse to continue his journey quickly.

entries.definition_en: a discussion of an event after it has occurred
entries.example_cn: 经理召开了一次事后分析会议，以回顾失败的发布活动。
entries.example_en: The manager held a post-mortem meeting to review the failed launch.

entries.definition_en: an examination of a dead body to determine cause of death
entries.example_cn: 警方进行了尸检以确定死因。
entries.example_en: The police performed a post-mortem to find the cause of death.

entries.definition_en: when the postage is paid by the sender
entries.example_cn: 我昨天寄出了这封邮资已付的信。
entries.example_en: I sent the post-paid letter yesterday.

entries.definition_en: pertaining to a period of time immediately following the end of a war
entries.example_cn: 战后经济面临重大挑战。
entries.example_en: The post-war economy faced significant challenges.

entries.definition_en: the money you pay to send a letter or package through the post
entries.example_cn: 我需要买更多的邮资来寄这个包裹。
entries.example_en: I need to buy more postage to send this package.

entries.definition_en: a small adhesive token stuck on a letter or package to indicate that postal fees have been paid
entries.example_cn: 她忘了在信封上贴邮票，所以邮资缺失了。
entries.example_en: She forgot to put a stamp on the envelope, so the postage was missing.

entries.definition_en: relating to the system for sending and delivering letters and packages
entries.example_cn: 寄包裹前请填写邮政表格。
entries.example_en: Please fill out the postal form before sending the package.

entries.definition_cn: 邮袋；邮差装邮件用的袋子
entries.definition_en: a bag used by a postal worker for carrying mail
entries.example_cn: 邮递员在邮局柜台前将邮差肩包里的信件倒了出来。
entries.example_en: The postman emptied his postbag onto the counter at the post office.

entries.definition_en: a public box where people put letters to be sent by mail
entries.example_cn: 我把信投进了街角的邮筒。
entries.example_en: I dropped the letter in the postbox on the corner.

entries.definition_en: a small card used to send a message by post without an envelope
entries.example_cn: 我从海滩给她寄了一张明信片。
entries.example_en: I sent her a postcard from the beach.

entries.definition_en: a code of letters and digits added to a postal address to aid in the sorting of mail
entries.example_cn: 请在信封上清楚地写上邮政编码。
entries.example_en: Please write your postcode clearly on the envelope.

entries.definition_cn: 发生或存在于某事件或时间之后
entries.definition_en: to occur or exist later than an event or time
entries.example_cn: 后面的章节写于作者搬到伦敦之后。
entries.example_en: The later chapters postdate the author’s move to London.

entries.definition_cn: 确立某事相对于另一事较晚的时间关系
entries.definition_en: to establish something as being later relative to something else
entries.example_cn: 合同被填上了较晚的日期，以反映签署的延迟。
entries.example_en: The contract was postdated to reflect the delay in signing.

entries.definition_en: a postdoctoral research position
entries.example_cn: 这名博士后研究人员在大学的高级计算实验室工作。
entries.example_en: The postdoctoral researcher works in the university's advanced computing laboratory.

entries.definition_en: a person in a postdoctoral research position
entries.example_cn: 作为一名博士后研究人员，她在大学的高级计算实验室工作。
entries.example_en: As a postdoc, she works in the university's advanced computing laboratory.

entries.definition_en: relating to study or research done after obtaining a doctoral degree
entries.example_cn: 他正在大学从事一个博士后项目。
entries.example_en: He is working on a postdoctoral project at the university.

entries.definition_cn: 博士后；博士后研究人员
entries.definition_en: a person who has completed a doctorate and is doing postdoctoral research; a postdoc
entries.example_cn: 她获得博士学位后以博士后研究人员身份加入了该实验室。
entries.example_en: She joined the laboratory as a postdoctoral researcher after earning her doctorate.

entries.definition_en: a large printed picture or notice displayed in a public place to advertise something
entries.example_cn: 电影海报挂在电影院墙上。
entries.example_en: The movie poster was hanging on the wall of the cinema.

entries.definition_en: a person who puts up advertisements or notices on walls
entries.example_cn: 这名张贴广告的人因在街墙上张贴非法告示而被抓获。
entries.example_en: The bill poster was caught putting up illegal notices on a street wall.

entries.definition_en: a horse kept at an inn for travelers to use
entries.example_cn: 疲惫的旅行者在驿站租了一匹驿马继续他的旅程。
entries.example_en: The weary traveler rented a poster at the post house to continue his journey.

entries.definition_en: a thick cardboard used for making posters
entries.example_cn: 我们将海报板切成条状，为活动制作了一个展示板。
entries.example_en: We cut the posterboard into strips to create a display board for the event.

entries.definition_en: located at or near or behind a part or near the end of a structure
entries.example_cn: 眼睛的后房含有液体。
entries.example_en: The posterior chamber of the eye contains fluid.

entries.definition_en: coming at a subsequent time or stage
entries.example_cn: 战争后期的事件记录较少。
entries.example_en: The posterior events of the war were less well documented.

entries.definition_en: the fleshy part of the human body that you sit on
entries.example_cn: 他坐在床沿，感到臀部疼痛。
entries.example_en: He sat on the edge of the bed, feeling his sore posterior.

entries.definition_cn: 位于口腔后部的牙齿；后牙
entries.definition_en: a tooth situated at the back of the mouth
entries.example_cn: 牙医拔掉了他的一颗后牙。
entries.example_en: The dentist extracted one of his posterior teeth.

entries.definition_en: all future generations
entries.example_cn: 我们必须为了未来世代的利益保护环境。
entries.example_en: We must protect the environment for the sake of posterity.

entries.definition_en: all of the offspring of a given progenitor
entries.example_cn: 这个古老的部落确保他们的后代会记住他们的历史。
entries.example_en: The ancient tribe ensured their posterity would remember their history.

entries.definition_en: a small gate located in the rear of a fort or castle
entries.example_cn: 士兵们从后门溜出去，以免被敌人发现。
entries.example_en: The soldiers slipped out through the postern to avoid detection by the enemy.

entries.definition_en: an affix that is added at the end of the word
entries.example_cn: 在单词'happiness'中，'ness'是一个后缀。
entries.example_en: In the word 'happiness', 'ness' is a postfix.

entries.definition_cn: 神经节后的；位于神经节远端或后方的
entries.definition_en: located distal to or posterior to a ganglion
entries.example_cn: 节后纤维将信号传递至平滑肌。
entries.example_en: The postganglionic fibers transmit signals to the smooth muscles.

entries.definition_en: relating to the time after a glacial period
entries.example_cn: 冰川期后的地貌是由退却的冰盖塑造而成的。
entries.example_en: The postglacial landscape was shaped by retreating ice sheets.

entries.definition_cn: 大学毕业后继续学习的人；研究生
entries.definition_en: a person who continues studying after completing a degree
entries.example_cn: 她决定成为一名研究生，专攻计算机科学。
entries.example_en: She decided to become a postgraduate to specialize in computer science.

entries.definition_cn: 研究生阶段的；大学毕业后学习的
entries.definition_en: relating to studies undertaken after completing a degree
entries.example_cn: 这所大学提供许多工商管理方面的研究生课程。
entries.example_en: The university offers many postgraduate courses in business management.

entries.definition_en: a hole dug in the ground to hold a fence post
entries.example_cn: 他们必须为新的门挖一个深深的柱坑。
entries.example_en: They had to dig a deep posthole for the new gate.

entries.definition_en: happening or created after someone has died
entries.example_cn: 这位作者在去世后出版了一部小说，该书成为了畅销书。
entries.example_en: The author published a posthumous novel that became a bestseller.

entries.definition_en: after someone has died
entries.example_cn: 这本书是在作者死后出版的。
entries.example_en: The book was published posthumously.

entries.definition_en: relating to the period after a seizure or convulsion
entries.example_cn: 患者在发作后的状态中持续困惑了好几个小时。
entries.example_en: The patient remained confused in the postictal state for several hours.

entries.definition_cn: 骑在一对或一队挽马中近侧马匹上、为马车引导马匹的人
entries.definition_en: a rider mounted on the near horse of a pair or team, who guides the horses pulling a carriage
entries.example_cn: 驭手引导马匹绕过急转弯。
entries.example_en: The postilion guided the horses around the sharp turn.

entries.definition_en: relating to a society or economy where manufacturing is less important and services, information, and research are more dominant
entries.example_cn: 这座后工业城市已将工厂改造为技术中心。
entries.example_en: The postindustrial city has transformed its factories into technology hubs.

entries.definition_cn: 后工业音乐的；与源自工业音乐并受电子音乐和摇滚音乐影响的音乐流派有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to a genre of music derived from industrial music and influenced by electronic and rock music
entries.example_cn: 这支乐队的后工业音乐风格将刺耳的电子音色与厚重的摇滚吉他声融合在一起。
entries.example_en: The band’s postindustrial sound combines harsh electronic textures with heavy rock guitars.

entries.definition_en: a sign posted in a public place as an advertisement
entries.example_cn: 市政府移除了电线杆上的非法张贴物。
entries.example_en: The city removed the illegal posting from the telephone pole.

entries.definition_en: (bookkeeping) a listing on the company's records
entries.example_cn: 会计更正了上个月费用账目条目中的错误。
entries.example_en: The accountant corrected the error in the posting for last month's expenses.

entries.definition_en: the act of mailing a letter
entries.example_cn: 由于风暴，信件的寄出被延误了。
entries.example_en: The posting of the letter was delayed due to the storm.

entries.definition_cn: 作品的结尾部分，尤指宗教仪式结束时演奏的音乐
entries.definition_en: the final part of a piece, especially music played at the end of a church service
entries.example_cn: 教堂礼拜结束时，管风琴师演奏了一首轻柔的结束曲。
entries.example_en: The organist played a gentle postlude at the end of the church service.

entries.definition_en: a person who delivers or collects mail
entries.example_cn: 邮递员早早到来投递早报。
entries.example_en: The postman arrived early to deliver the morning newspapers.

entries.definition_en: a cancellation mark stamped on mail by postal officials to show the post office and date
entries.example_cn: 这封信昨天盖了邮戳，所以很快寄出了。
entries.example_en: The letter was sent quickly because it had a postmark from yesterday.

entries.definition_en: to stamp mail with a postmark to indicate the date and time of mailing
entries.example_cn: 职员会在你离开前给你的信封盖邮戳。
entries.example_en: The clerk will postmark your envelope before you leave.

entries.definition_en: the person in charge of a post office
entries.example_cn: 邮政局长宣布了新的投递时间表。
entries.example_en: The postmaster announced the new delivery schedule.

entries.definition_en: the person who administers an electronic mail system
entries.example_cn: 电子邮件系统管理员帮助我恢复了邮箱账户的访问权限。
entries.example_en: The postmaster helped me recover access to my email account.

entries.definition_en: occurring or existing after menopause
entries.example_cn: 医生建议所有绝经后的女性定期进行骨密度扫描。
entries.example_en: Doctors recommend regular bone density scans for all postmenopausal women.

entries.definition_en: relating to the time period after the year 2000
entries.example_cn: 后千禧年文化随着数字技术的普及而发展。
entries.example_en: Postmillennial culture developed alongside widespread digital technology.

entries.definition_cn: 与相信基督复临将在千禧年之后发生有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to the belief that the Second Coming of Christ will occur after the millennium
entries.example_cn: 后千禧年神学认为，基督将在一段长期的和平与繁荣时期之后复临。
entries.example_en: Postmillennial theology teaches that Christ will return after a long period of peace and prosperity.

entries.definition_cn: 后千禧一代成员；Z世代成员
entries.definition_en: a member of the generation that follows the millennials; a member of Generation Z
entries.example_cn: 作为一名后千禧一代成员，她从小就使用智能手机和社交媒体。
entries.example_en: As a postmillennial, she grew up using smartphones and social media.

entries.definition_en: a woman postmaster
entries.example_cn: 女邮政局长微笑着迎接每一位顾客。
entries.example_en: The postmistress greeted every customer with a friendly smile.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to postmodernism
entries.example_cn: 这家博物馆展示了一座后现代雕塑。
entries.example_en: The museum features a postmodern sculpture.

entries.definition_en: an artistic and literary style that rejects the principles of modernism
entries.example_cn: 博物馆的展览探讨了后现代主义的复杂性。
entries.example_en: The museum exhibition explored the complexities of postmodernism.

entries.definition_cn: 对现代主义思想持怀疑或反讽态度的立场
entries.definition_en: an attitude that questions or rejects modernist ideas, often through skepticism or irony
entries.example_cn: 后现代主义常常质疑存在唯一客观真理这一观点。
entries.example_en: Postmodernism often questions the idea that there is one objective truth.

entries.definition_cn: 后现代主义的倡导者或追随者
entries.definition_en: a person who advocates or follows postmodernism
entries.example_cn: 作为一名后现代主义者，她质疑艺术必须遵循传统规则这一观念。
entries.example_en: As a postmodernist, she questions the idea that art must follow traditional rules.

entries.definition_en: relating to postmodernism
entries.example_cn: 这部后现代小说挑战了传统的叙事结构。
entries.example_en: The postmodernist novel challenges traditional narrative structures.

entries.definition_en: a discussion or analysis of an event after it has occurred
entries.example_cn: 团队举行了一次事后分析会议，以回顾项目的失败之处。
entries.example_en: The team held a postmortem to review the project's failures.

entries.definition_en: an examination and dissection of a dead body to determine cause of death
entries.example_cn: 验尸官下令进行尸检以排除他杀的可能性。
entries.example_en: The coroner ordered a postmortem to rule out foul play.

entries.definition_en: occurring or done after death
entries.example_cn: 尸检揭示了事故的原因。
entries.example_en: The postmortem examination revealed the cause of the accident.

entries.definition_en: after death or after an event
entries.example_cn: 事后报告在两天后发布。
entries.example_en: The postmortem report was released two days later.

entries.definition_en: happening or occurring right after a baby is born
entries.example_cn: 医院为新生母亲提供专门的产后护理。
entries.example_en: The hospital offers special postnatal care for new mothers.

entries.definition_en: relating to events after a marriage
entries.example_cn: 他们签署了一份婚后协议以保护他们的资产。
entries.example_en: They signed a postnuptial agreement to protect their assets.

entries.definition_en: happening or done after a surgical operation
entries.example_cn: 病人在恢复室接受了术后护理。
entries.example_en: The patient received postoperative care in the recovery room.

entries.definition_en: after a surgical operation
entries.example_cn: 术后医护人员密切监测患者是否出现感染迹象。
entries.example_en: The patient was monitored postoperatively for any signs of infection.

entries.definition_en: paid after the service is used, especially regarding mail
entries.example_cn: 这个手机计划是后付的，所以你在月底支付通话费用。
entries.example_en: The mobile phone plan is postpaid, so you pay for calls at the end of the month.

entries.definition_en: occurring or relating to the period after childbirth
entries.example_cn: 她在产后期间经历了情绪波动。
entries.example_en: She experienced mood swings during the postpartum period.

entries.definition_en: to decide to do something at a later time instead of now
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不把会议推迟到下周。
entries.example_en: We had to postpone the meeting until next week.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: postpone something until/to a later time

entries.definition_en: the act of delaying something to a later time
entries.example_cn: 由于预算削减，项目推迟一事被宣布。
entries.example_en: The postponement of the project was announced due to budget cuts.

entries.definition_cn: 事件或行动被推迟的一段时间
entries.definition_en: a period during which an event or action is delayed
entries.example_cn: 该项目被推迟了三个月。
entries.example_en: The project was subject to a three-month postponement.

entries.definition_en: a word placed after the word it modifies in a sentence
entries.example_cn: 在日语中，后置词“ni”表示地点。
entries.example_en: In Japanese, the postposition 'ni' indicates location.

entries.definition_en: placed after the word it modifies
entries.example_cn: 在短语“attorney general”中，形容词“general”后置修饰名词“attorney”。
entries.example_en: In the phrase 'attorney general', the adjective 'general' is postpositive and modifies 'attorney'.

usage.label: not comparable
usage.pattern: The source marks this adjective as not comparable.

entries.definition_en: occurring or happening after a meal
entries.example_cn: 医生建议他餐后服药。
entries.example_en: The doctor advised him to take the medicine postprandial.

entries.definition_en: a note added to a letter after the signature
entries.example_cn: 她加了一段附言，提醒他明天的会议。
entries.example_en: She added a postscript to remind him about the meeting tomorrow.

entries.definition_cn: 书籍或其他作品正文完成后添加的文字
entries.definition_en: text added to a book or other work after its main text is complete
entries.example_cn: 作者在书中加了一段后记，感谢读者的支持。
entries.example_en: The author included a postscript thanking the readers for their support.

entries.definition_cn: 申请加入宗教团体的人
entries.definition_en: a person who applies for admission to a religious order
entries.example_cn: 这位申请者在被接纳之前花了几个月时间学习规则。
entries.example_en: The postulant spent months studying the rules before being accepted.

entries.definition_cn: 提交请愿书或请求的人；请愿者
entries.definition_en: a person who submits a petition or request; a petitioner
entries.example_cn: 每位请愿者都向委员会提交了书面请求。
entries.example_en: Each postulant submitted a written request to the committee.

entries.definition_en: to put forward or state something as a proposition or basis for reasoning
entries.example_cn: 作者断言经济将很快复苏。
entries.example_en: The author postulates that the economy will recover soon.

entries.definition_en: to assume something to be true without proof
entries.example_cn: 我们必须假定证人在说真话。
entries.example_en: We must postulate that the witness is telling the truth.

entries.definition_en: to require something as necessary or proper
entries.example_cn: 这份工作要求具备高水平的技术技能。
entries.example_en: The job postulates a high level of technical skill.

entries.definition_en: a statement accepted as true to serve as a starting point for logical reasoning
entries.example_cn: 该理论基于能量既不能被创造也不能被消灭的公理。
entries.example_en: The theory is based on the postulate that energy cannot be created or destroyed.

entries.definition_cn: 作为推理基础提出的命题或原则
entries.definition_en: a proposition or principle put forward as a basis for reasoning
entries.example_cn: 物质守恒这一命题指导了研究人员的推理。
entries.example_en: The postulation that matter is conserved guided the researchers' reasoning.

entries.definition_cn: （废）为自己提出主张；索取；请求
entries.definition_en: (obsolete) a claim or request for something
entries.example_cn: 他提出赔偿请求，但遭到了拒绝。
entries.example_en: His postulation for compensation was rejected.

entries.definition_en: relating to the way a person holds their body while standing or sitting
entries.example_cn: 不良的姿势习惯会导致长期的背痛。
entries.example_en: Poor postural habits can lead to back pain over time.

entries.definition_en: the way in which someone holds their body
entries.example_cn: 她调整了姿势，以便在椅子上坐得更舒服。
entries.example_en: She adjusted her posture to sit more comfortably on the chair.

entries.definition_en: a person's characteristic way of holding their body
entries.example_cn: 他笔挺的体态显示出自信和自律。
entries.example_en: His upright posture suggested confidence and discipline.

entries.definition_cn: 对某问题的态度或立场
entries.definition_en: an attitude or position toward an issue
entries.example_cn: 政府在这一问题上的冷静立场让投资者感到安心。
entries.example_en: The government's calm posture on the issue reassured investors.

entries.definition_en: the military strength and resources available for fighting
entries.example_cn: 自从批准了新国防预算以来，该国的军事实力有了显著改善。
entries.example_en: The country's posture has improved significantly since the new defense budget was approved.

entries.definition_en: to behave in an unnatural way to impress others
entries.example_cn: 他试图矫揉造作地表现自己是一位严肃的艺术家，但他的作品却显得业余。
entries.example_en: He tried to posture as a serious artist, but his work was amateurish.

entries.definition_en: to assume a specific body position, often for art or photography
entries.example_cn: 模特必须对着镜头摆姿势几分钟。
entries.example_en: The model had to posture for the camera for several minutes.

entries.definition_en: the assumption of an exaggerated pose or attitude
entries.example_cn: 他不断的做作让其他客人感到不自在。
entries.example_en: His constant posturing made the other guests feel uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: relating to the time after a war has ended
entries.example_cn: 战后许多国家的经济迅速增长。
entries.example_en: The postwar economy saw rapid growth in many countries.

entries.definition_en: a female mail carrier who delivers letters and packages
entries.example_cn: 女邮递员在门口放下包裹前按响了门铃。
entries.example_en: The postwoman rang the bell before leaving the package at the door.

entries.definition_cn: 花束（通常作为礼物赠送）
entries.definition_en: a small bunch of flowers given as a gift
entries.example_cn: 她在邻居的门口留下了一束野花。
entries.example_en: She left a posy of wildflowers on the doorstep for her neighbor.

entries.definition_en: a deep round container made of metal or clay used for cooking
entries.example_cn: 她在锅里搅拌着汤。
entries.example_en: She stirred the soup in the pot.

entries.definition_en: a container used for growing plants
entries.example_cn: 这些花需要一个新的花盆。
entries.example_en: The flowers need a new pot.

entries.definition_en: the total amount of money bet in a game
entries.example_cn: 随着更多玩家加入，赌注总额越来越大。
entries.example_en: The pot grew larger as more players joined.

entries.definition_en: the quantity of food or drink contained in a pot
entries.example_cn: 晚饭后，我们把整锅汤都喝光了。
entries.example_en: We ate the whole pot of soup after dinner.

entries.definition_en: a large number or amount
entries.example_cn: 银行里有一大笔钱。
entries.example_en: There is a pot of money in the bank.

entries.definition_en: to put a plant into a container for growing
entries.example_cn: 我们下周会把幼苗种进盆里。
entries.example_en: We will pot the seedlings next week.

entries.definition_cn: 大肚子或腹部隆起（非正式）
entries.definition_en: a large belly or paunch (informal)
entries.example_cn: 多年暴饮暴食后，他明显有了个大肚子。
entries.example_en: He developed a noticeable pot after years of overeating.

entries.definition_en: an archaic chamber pot; (figuratively, slang) a toilet
entries.example_cn: 护士把便盆拿到了床边。
entries.example_en: The nurse brought a chamber pot to the bedside.

entries.definition_en: a traditional French stew made with beef and vegetables
entries.example_cn: 我们在法国餐厅点了法式牛肉蔬菜炖菜作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We ordered pot-au-feu for dinner at the French restaurant.

entries.definition_en: a woman who works in a pub or inn serving customers and doing various chores
entries.example_cn: 女侍在乐队演奏时为我们端来了新鲜的饮料。
entries.example_en: The pot-girl brought us fresh drinks while the band played.

entries.definition_en: suitable for drinking; safe to consume as a beverage
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，河里的水不再可以饮用。
entries.example_en: After the storm, the water in the river was no longer potable.

entries.definition_en: a drinkable liquid; a beverage
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者带了几种饮料，以备长途旅行之需。
entries.example_en: The hikers packed several potables for the long journey.

entries.definition_en: a thick soup, often made with vegetables and sometimes cream
entries.example_cn: 厨师端上了一道带有香草的浓郁浓汤。
entries.example_en: The chef served a rich potage with herbs.

entries.definition_en: a potassium salt, especially potassium carbonate, used in making soap and glass and as a fertilizer
entries.example_cn: 农民使用钾碱来改善土壤质量。
entries.example_en: Farmers use potash to improve the soil quality.

entries.definition_en: a soft, silver-white metallic element that oxidizes quickly in air and reacts violently with water
entries.example_cn: 钾是一种存在于许多水果和蔬菜中的必需矿物质。
entries.example_en: Potassium is an essential mineral found in many fruits and vegetables.

entries.definition_en: an edible tuber native to South America; a staple food of Ireland
entries.example_cn: 我们煮了一些土豆当晚餐。
entries.example_en: We boiled some potatoes for dinner.

entries.definition_en: an annual plant native to South America having underground stolons bearing edible starchy tubers; widely cultivated as a garden vegetable; vines are poisonous
entries.example_cn: 马铃薯植株在地下产生淀粉块茎。
entries.example_en: The potato plant produces starchy tubers underground.

entries.definition_en: having a large, round belly
entries.example_cn: 那个大腹便便的老人坐在椅子上看电视。
entries.example_en: The potbellied old man sat in his chair watching television.

entries.definition_en: a bulbous stove in which wood or coal is burned
entries.example_cn: 他们在冬天围坐在圆肚炉旁取暖。
entries.example_en: They gathered around the potbelly to keep warm during the winter.

entries.definition_en: slang for a paunch
entries.example_cn: 这位老水手因多年食用油腻食物而大腹便便。
entries.example_en: The old sailor had a potbelly from years of eating rich food.

entries.definition_en: a literary work of poor quality written quickly to earn money
entries.example_cn: 这位作者在找到严肃的文学事业之前写了几部谋生之作。
entries.example_en: The author wrote several potboilers before finding a serious literary career.

entries.definition_en: unlawfully distilled Irish whiskey
entries.example_cn: 游客被警告不要喝私酿威士忌，因为那是违法的。
entries.example_en: The tourists were warned not to drink poteen as it is illegal.

entries.definition_cn: 力量；（尤指男性的）性能力
entries.definition_en: the state of being potent, especially a man's capacity to have sexual intercourse
entries.example_cn: 这篇医学文献用 potence 指男性发生性关系的能力。
entries.example_en: The medical text used potence for a man's capacity to have sexual intercourse.

entries.definition_cn: 钟表中支撑转轴的柱销
entries.definition_en: a stud that supports a pivot in a watch or clock
entries.example_cn: 钟表匠更换了支撑摆轮转轴的磨损柱销。
entries.example_en: The watchmaker replaced the worn potence that supported the balance-wheel pivot.

entries.definition_en: the capacity to produce strong physiological or chemical effects.
entries.example_cn: 这种药物的效力在实验室进行了测试。
entries.example_en: The potency of the medicine was tested in the lab.

entries.definition_en: the power or right to give orders or make decisions.
entries.example_cn: 国王的权力是绝对的。
entries.example_en: The potency of the king was absolute.

entries.definition_en: the state of being potent; a male's capacity to have sexual intercourse.
entries.example_cn: 年龄有时会影响男性的性能力。
entries.example_en: Age can sometimes affect a man's potency.

entries.definition_en: the inherent capacity for coming into being or existing.
entries.example_cn: 种子的潜能在于其生长的能力。
entries.example_en: The potency of the seed lies in its ability to grow.

entries.definition_en: powerful or effective
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策对经济有巨大的影响。
entries.example_en: The new policy has a potent effect on the economy.

entries.definition_en: having a strong physiological or chemical effect
entries.example_cn: 这种药对严重感染疗效显著。
entries.example_en: The medicine is potent against severe infections.

entries.definition_en: having or wielding force or authority
entries.example_cn: 这位拥有实权的领导人发表了果断的演讲。
entries.example_en: The potent leader made a decisive speech.

entries.definition_en: (of a male) capable of copulation
entries.example_cn: 公牛在繁殖季节有交配能力。
entries.example_en: The bull is potent during the breeding season.

entries.definition_en: a powerful ruler, especially a monarch
entries.example_cn: 这位专制君主用铁腕统治着王国。
entries.example_en: The potentate ruled the kingdom with an iron fist.

entries.definition_en: existing in possibility; able to happen
entries.example_cn: 今天下午晚些时候可能会下雨。
entries.example_en: There is potential for rain later this afternoon.

entries.definition_en: expected to become or be; in prospect
entries.example_cn: 她可能是这份工作的候选人。
entries.example_en: She is a potential candidate for the job.

entries.definition_en: the ability to develop into something in the future
entries.example_cn: 这支队伍有很大的潜力赢得冠军。
entries.example_en: The team has great potential to win the championship.

entries.definition_en: the difference in electrical charge between two points in a circuit, measured in volts
entries.example_cn: 两个端子之间的电势差是 12 伏特。
entries.example_en: The potential between the two terminals is 12 volts.

entries.definition_en: an aptitude that may be developed
entries.example_cn: 她年轻时便发现自己有数学天赋。
entries.example_en: She recognized her potentiality for mathematics at a young age.

entries.definition_en: the inherent capacity for coming into being
entries.example_cn: 种子的潜能在于它能长成大树。
entries.example_en: The potentiality of the seed lies in its ability to grow into a tree.

entries.definition_en: in a way that makes it possible for something to happen in the future
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术可能会彻底改变该行业。
entries.example_en: The new technology could potentially revolutionize the industry.

entries.definition_cn: 增强（药物或生理过程）的作用
entries.definition_en: to increase the effect of a drug or physiological process
entries.example_cn: 这种药物会增强酒精的作用。
entries.example_en: This medication can potentiate the effects of alcohol.

entries.definition_en: the effect where two drugs taken together produce a stronger result than each would alone
entries.example_cn: 医生警告说，同时服用这两种药物可能会使副作用增强。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned about the potentiation of side effects when combining these two medications.

entries.definition_en: a device used to measure direct current electromotive forces
entries.example_cn: 科学家使用电动势计测量电路中的电压。
entries.example_en: The scientist used a potentiometer to measure the voltage in the circuit.

entries.definition_en: a resistor with three terminals, including an adjustable center terminal, used to adjust voltages in radios and TV sets
entries.example_cn: 要改变音量，你需要转动电位器上的旋钮。
entries.example_en: To change the volume, you need to turn the knob on the potentiometer.

entries.definition_en: in a way that has a strong or powerful effect
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策有力地影响了整个行业的发展方向。
entries.example_en: The new policy has potently influenced the direction of the entire industry.

entries.definition_en: the amount of something that fills a pot
entries.example_cn: 她提着一锅水去花园。
entries.example_en: She carried a potful of water to the garden.

entries.definition_en: someone who smokes marijuana habitually
entries.example_cn: 警察怀疑这名大麻吸食者在社区里贩卖毒品。
entries.example_en: The police suspected the pothead of selling drugs in the neighborhood.

entries.definition_en: make a fuss; be agitated
entries.example_cn: 别为小事大惊小怪，让我们开始工作吧。
entries.example_en: Stop pothering about nothing and let us get to work.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: make a bustle or stir; be fussy

entries.definition_en: puzzle or perplex; make troubled
entries.example_cn: 复杂的说明使新员工感到困惑。
entries.example_en: The complicated instructions pothered the new employee.

entries.definition_en: an excited state of agitation
entries.example_cn: 当事故发生的消息传出时，房间里一片激动不安。
entries.example_en: There was a lot of pother in the room when the news of the accident broke.

entries.definition_en: an insulated pad used for holding hot pots
entries.example_cn: 从炉子上取下锅时，请使用隔热垫。
entries.example_en: Please use the potholder when removing the pot from the stove.

entries.definition_en: a deep hole or depression in a road surface caused by wear or weathering
entries.example_cn: 汽车撞上了一个大坑洼，轮子受损了。
entries.example_en: The car hit a large pothole and the wheel was damaged.

entries.definition_en: having holes or pits on a paved surface
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，这条路变得坑坑洼洼。
entries.example_en: The road was potholed after the heavy rain.

entries.definition_en: evergreen liana widely cultivated for its variegated foliage
entries.example_cn: 她在阳台上挂了一盆绿萝，为公寓增添了一抹绿色。
entries.example_en: She hung a potted pothos on the balcony to add a touch of green to her apartment.

entries.definition_en: any of various tropical lianas belonging to the genus Scindapsus
entries.example_cn: 园丁修剪了这种崖角藤属植物，以促使它在棚架上长出新的枝叶。
entries.example_en: The gardener pruned the pothos to encourage new growth on the trellis.

entries.definition_en: a medicinal or magical or poisonous beverage
entries.example_cn: 巫师调制了一种发光的药水来治愈龙的伤口。
entries.example_en: The wizard mixed a glowing potion to cure the dragon's wound.

entries.definition_cn: 北美西北部沿海一些原住民举行的展示财富的赠礼仪式宴会，有时还会毁坏财物
entries.definition_en: a ceremonial feast held by some Indigenous peoples of the northwestern coast of North America to display wealth through gift-giving, sometimes involving destruction of property
entries.example_cn: 社区聚集在一起举行宴会，以庆祝酋长新的地位。
entries.example_en: The community gathered for a potlatch to celebrate the chief's new status.

entries.definition_cn: 聚餐时各人带一道菜共享；百家饭
entries.definition_en: a shared meal to which each guest brings a dish, or the food brought to it
entries.example_cn: 我们决定举办百家饭晚餐来庆祝节日。
entries.example_en: We decided to have a potluck dinner to celebrate the holiday.

entries.definition_cn: 咸味馅饼，尤指肉馅或蔬菜馅；（地区用法）肉类炖菜配面团饺子
entries.definition_en: a savory pie, especially one filled with meat or vegetables; also, regionally, a meat stew with dumplings
entries.example_cn: 我们在寒冷的夜晚享用了一顿热腾腾的肉馅派作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a warm potpie for dinner on a cold night.

entries.definition_en: a collection containing a variety of different things
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志是关于政治、科学和文化的大杂烩。
entries.example_en: The magazine is a potpourri of articles on politics, science, and culture.

entries.definition_en: a musical composition made up of various songs or pieces
entries.example_cn: 这场音乐会演奏了十九世纪古典名曲的组曲。
entries.example_en: The concert featured a potpourri of classical hits from the 19th century.

entries.definition_cn: 用来散发香味的干燥芳香植物材料（通常放在装饰碗中）
entries.definition_en: a mixture of dried flower petals and spices used for scent
entries.example_cn: 她把一碗干花香料混合物放在桌上，让房间充满宜人的香气。
entries.example_en: She placed a potpourri on the table to fill the room with a pleasant aroma.

entries.definition_en: a shard of pottery
entries.example_cn: 考古学家在古定居点附近发现了一块破碎的陶片。
entries.example_en: Archaeologists found a broken potsherd near the ancient settlement.

entries.definition_en: criticism aimed at an easy target and made without careful consideration
entries.example_cn: 他对那位政治家政策的轻率批评缺乏深入研究。
entries.example_en: His potshot at the politician's policy was poorly researched.

entries.definition_en: a shot taken at an easy or casual target
entries.example_cn: 猎人在那只鸟飞走前随意开了一枪。
entries.example_en: The hunter fired a potshot at the bird before it flew away.

entries.definition_cn: 蔬菜（有时加肉或鱼）炖菜
entries.definition_en: a stew of vegetables, sometimes with meat or fish
entries.example_cn: 穷人们靠简单的豆子芜菁炖菜度日。
entries.example_en: The poor families survived on a simple pottage of beans and turnips.

entries.definition_en: thick, often creamy soup
entries.example_cn: 他们晚餐吃了一顿丰盛的浓汤。
entries.example_en: They ate a hearty pottage for dinner.

entries.definition_en: of plants; planted or grown in a pot
entries.example_cn: 她买了几盆盆栽来装饰新办公室。
entries.example_en: She bought several potted plants to decorate the new office.

entries.definition_en: preserved in a pot, can, or jar
entries.example_cn: 我们午餐吃了罐装肉。
entries.example_en: We ate the potted meat for lunch.

entries.definition_en: (British informal) summarized or abridged
entries.example_cn: 杂志发表了该历史事件的简略版。
entries.example_en: The magazine published a potted version of the historical event.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes pots and other clay objects by shaping them on a wheel and baking them in a kiln
entries.example_cn: 这位陶工花了数小时在陶轮上塑造黏土。
entries.example_en: The potter spent hours shaping the clay on his wheel.

entries.definition_en: to do random, unplanned work or activities or spend time idly
entries.example_cn: 我整个下午都在花园里闲逛，除草和浇水。
entries.example_en: I spent the afternoon pottering around the garden, weeding and watering the plants.

entries.definition_en: to work lightly or casually
entries.example_cn: 她轻快地整理着书籍，没有花太多力气。
entries.example_en: She was pottering over the books, organizing them without much effort.

entries.definition_en: to move around aimlessly
entries.example_cn: 孩子们漫无目的地在房间里走动，寻找玩具。
entries.example_en: The children were pottering about the room, looking for toys.

entries.definition_en: ceramic ware made from clay and baked in a kiln
entries.example_cn: 她在市场上买了一件精美的陶器。
entries.example_en: She bought a beautiful piece of pottery at the market.

entries.definition_en: the craft of making earthenware
entries.example_cn: 他在当地学院学习陶艺。
entries.example_en: He studied pottery at the local college.

entries.definition_en: a workshop where clayware is made
entries.example_cn: 这家陶器作坊以其传统技艺而闻名。
entries.example_en: The pottery is famous for its traditional techniques.

entries.definition_cn: 旧时的容量单位，等于两夸脱；也指容量约为两夸脱的罐或容器
entries.definition_en: a former unit of volume equal to two quarts; a pot or vessel of about this size
entries.example_cn: 这个罐子装有两夸脱蜂蜜。
entries.example_en: The pottle held two quarts of honey.

usage.label: archaic
usage.pattern: 旧容量单位或相应大小的容器。

entries.definition_cn: 一种灰褐色的狐猴（Perodicticus potto）
entries.definition_en: a kind of gray-brown lemur (Perodicticus potto)
entries.example_cn: 研究人员观察到倭狐猴在夜间以树叶为食。
entries.example_en: Researchers observed the potto feeding on leaves at night.

entries.definition_cn: 一种具有长卷尾的美洲热带树栖食果哺乳动物
entries.definition_en: an arboreal fruit-eating mammal of tropical America with a long prehensile tail
entries.example_cn: 倭狐猴大部分时间都在树冠中睡觉。
entries.example_en: The potto spends most of its life sleeping in the canopy.

entries.definition_cn: 厕所；卫生间（儿童用语或非正式）
entries.definition_en: a toilet or lavatory, especially in childish or informal use
entries.example_cn: 孩子问厕所在哪里。
entries.example_en: The child asked where the potty was.

entries.definition_en: a portable toilet used in a bedroom
entries.example_cn: 婴儿坐在便盆上练习上厕所。
entries.example_en: The baby sat on the potty to practice using the toilet.

entries.definition_en: insane or crazy (informal)
entries.example_cn: 邻居家孩子制造的噪音快把弗雷德逼疯了。
entries.example_en: The noise from the neighboring children was driving Fred potty.

entries.definition_en: trivial or unimportant (British informal)
entries.example_cn: 别担心这些琐碎的细节。
entries.example_en: Don't worry about such potty details.

entries.definition_en: easy to pot the ball on (of a playing surface)
entries.example_cn: 这张球台非常适合初学者击球入袋。
entries.example_en: The table is a very potty one for beginners.

entries.definition_cn: （指儿童）已学会独立使用厕所的
entries.definition_en: (of a child) having been taught to use the toilet independently
entries.example_cn: 这个幼儿终于学会独立如厕，不再需要尿布了。
entries.example_en: The toddler is finally potty-trained and no longer needs diapers.

entries.definition_en: a small bag used for carrying things
entries.example_cn: 他把工具装在一个皮包里。
entries.example_en: He carried his tools in a leather pouch.

entries.definition_en: a saclike body part in certain animals like marsupials
entries.example_cn: 袋鼠把幼崽放在腹部的皮囊里。
entries.example_en: A kangaroo carries its young in a pouch on its belly.

entries.definition_en: a pocket-like enclosed space in an animal or object
entries.example_cn: 颊囊是用来储存食物的囊状空间。
entries.example_en: The cheek pouch is an enclosed space used to store food.

entries.definition_en: to put something into a small bag
entries.example_cn: 请在寄出前把文件装进小包。
entries.example_en: Please pouch the documents before sending them.

entries.definition_en: to swell or bulge outwards
entries.example_cn: 他开始鼓起脸颊。
entries.example_en: His cheeks puffed out as he began to pouch.

entries.definition_en: to send mail through special diplomatic channels
entries.example_cn: 大使通过外交邮袋将机密信件寄往首都。
entries.example_en: The ambassador pouches sensitive letters to the capital.

entries.definition_en: having a pouch or pocket-like structure
entries.example_cn: 袋鼠是一种有袋动物，它将幼崽放在育儿袋中。
entries.example_en: The kangaroo is a pouched animal that carries its young in a pouch.

entries.definition_cn: 厚实的坐垫；无靠背的软垫凳
entries.definition_en: a thick cushion used as a seat
entries.example_cn: 她坐在壁炉旁柔软的坐垫上。
entries.example_en: She sat on a soft pouf by the fireplace.

entries.definition_en: an offensive term for a homosexual man
entries.example_cn: 有人叫他“pouf”，这是对同性恋男子的冒犯性侮辱。
entries.example_en: He was called a pouf, an offensive insult for a homosexual man.

entries.definition_en: a thick cushion used as a seat
entries.example_cn: 她坐在壁炉旁的软脚凳上读书。
entries.example_en: She sat on the soft pouffe by the fireplace to read her book.

entries.definition_en: a soft, heated mass of meal or clay spread on cloth and applied to the skin to treat inflammation or improve circulation
entries.example_cn: 医生在肿胀的脚踝上敷了一剂温热的药泥。
entries.example_en: The doctor applied a warm poultice to the swollen ankle.

entries.definition_en: to treat by covering with a therapeutic substance
entries.example_cn: 护士给病人发炎的关节敷了药。
entries.example_en: The nurse poulticed the patient's inflamed joint.

entries.definition_en: the flesh of domesticated birds such as chickens, turkeys, ducks, or geese, used as food
entries.example_cn: 我们今晚点了烤禽肉作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We ordered roasted poultry for dinner tonight.

entries.definition_en: a domesticated bird such as a chicken, turkey, or duck, raised for food or eggs
entries.example_cn: 这位农民饲养了几种家禽，包括鸡和火鸡。
entries.example_en: The farmer raised several types of poultry, including chickens and turkeys.

entries.definition_en: to leap suddenly onto or at something as an attack
entries.example_cn: 老鹰从上方猛扑向它的猎物。
