entries.definition_en: having superior power and influence
entries.example_cn: 新领导人的占优势影响力改变了组织的方向。
entries.example_en: The predominant influence of the new leader changed the organization's direction.

entries.definition_cn: 主要地；在数量或影响力上占优势地
entries.definition_en: mostly; in greater number or influence than others
entries.example_cn: 该市的人口主要由年轻专业人士组成。
entries.example_en: The population of the city is predominantly composed of young professionals.

entries.definition_en: to be the largest in number, quantity, power, status, or importance
entries.example_cn: 红色在这幅画中占主导地位。
entries.example_en: The red color predominates in the painting.

entries.definition_cn: 显得巨大或占据显要位置
entries.definition_en: to appear very large or occupy a commanding position
entries.example_cn: 山峰在周围的景观中显得格外突出。
entries.example_en: The mountain peak predominates over the surrounding landscape.

entries.definition_cn: 占主导地位的（不规范用法）
entries.definition_en: predominant; having the greatest power or influence
entries.example_cn: 北部地区是该国政治决策中的主导力量。
entries.example_en: The northern region was the predominate force in the country's political decisions.

usage.label: proscribed/nonstandard adjective
usage.pattern: predominate is used adjectivally for predominant.

entries.definition_en: a serious condition during pregnancy involving high blood pressure and protein in the urine.
entries.example_cn: 医院密切监测这位母亲是否出现子痫前期的迹象。
entries.example_en: The hospital monitored the mother closely for signs of preeclampsia.

entries.definition_en: a baby born before the full 37 weeks of pregnancy
entries.example_cn: 这家医院有一个专门收治早产儿的科室。
entries.example_en: The hospital has a special unit for preemies.

entries.definition_en: a position of superior importance or status compared to others
entries.example_cn: 这所大学在医学研究领域的卓越地位举世公认。
entries.example_en: The university's preeminence in medical research is recognized worldwide.

entries.definition_en: greatest in importance, degree, or achievement
entries.example_cn: 她被认为是她那一代最杰出的科学家。
entries.example_en: She is considered the preeminent scientist of her generation.

entries.definition_en: to a very high degree; with superiority above others
entries.example_cn: 她完全有资格担任领导职务。
entries.example_en: She is preeminently qualified for the leadership role.

entries.definition_en: to acquire something before others can do so
entries.example_cn: 公司在竞争对手能够取得这块可用土地之前抢先取得了它。
entries.example_en: The company preempted the available land before competitors could acquire it.

entries.definition_en: to take the place of or have precedence over something else
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术将取代旧的数据存储方法。
entries.example_en: The new technology will preempt the old methods of data storage.

entries.definition_en: to gain possession of by prior right, especially to secure the right to buy land
entries.example_cn: 该公司在政府将土地出售给他人之前，凭优先权取得了这块土地。
entries.example_en: The company preempted the land before the government could sell it to others.

entries.definition_en: to make a preemptive bid in the game of bridge
entries.example_cn: 她用手牌较弱时抢叫，以破坏对手的沟通。
entries.example_en: She preempted with a weak hand to disrupt the opponents' communication.

entries.definition_en: a high bid in bridge intended to stop the opponents from bidding
entries.example_cn: 他在桥牌比赛中抢叫，以迷惑对手。
entries.example_en: He made a preempt to confuse the opposing team during the bridge game.

entries.definition_en: the right to buy something before anyone else.
entries.example_cn: 作为股东，他对新发行的股票享有优先购买权。
entries.example_en: As a shareholder, he has preemption rights on new stock issues.

entries.definition_en: the right of a government to take possession of property.
entries.example_cn: 土地的征用权使城市得以建造一个新的公园。
entries.example_en: The preemption of the land allowed the city to build a new park.

entries.definition_en: the legal principle that federal laws take precedence over state laws on the same topic.
entries.example_cn: 该案件的核心在于关于环境法规的联邦优先权问题。
entries.example_en: The case turned on the issue of preemption regarding environmental regulations.

entries.definition_en: the act of taking something before others can.
entries.example_cn: 该公司抢先占领市场，让竞争对手难以生存。
entries.example_en: The company's preemption of the market left competitors struggling to survive.

entries.definition_en: taken to prevent something from happening before it occurs
entries.example_cn: 政府发动了先发制人的打击以阻止袭击。
entries.example_en: The government launched a preemptive strike to stop the attack.

entries.definition_en: to dress or groom with elaborate care
entries.example_cn: 她在面试前花时间精心打扮自己的外表。
entries.example_en: She took time to preen her appearance before the interview.

entries.definition_en: to feel proud or congratulate oneself for an achievement
entries.example_cn: 获奖后，他开始自夸自己的成功。
entries.example_en: After winning the award, he began to preen about his success.

entries.definition_en: to clean one's feathers with the beak
entries.example_cn: 孔雀花了几个小时梳理它五颜六色的羽毛。
entries.example_en: The peacock spent hours preening its colorful feathers.

entries.definition_en: the state of existing before something else or in a previous state
entries.example_cn: 先存理论认为灵魂在出生前就已存在。
entries.example_en: The theory of preexistence suggests that souls exist before birth.

entries.definition_en: existing before something else happens
entries.example_cn: 翻新前，检查了建筑物原有的状况。
entries.example_en: The preexisting conditions of the building were inspected before renovation.

entries.definition_en: a building or structure that is manufactured in sections and assembled on site
entries.example_cn: 公司决定用一座新的预制建筑取代旧办公室。
entries.example_en: The company decided to replace the old office with a new prefab structure.

entries.definition_en: made in standard sizes to be shipped and assembled elsewhere
entries.example_cn: 他们选择了一栋预制房屋，因为它只需几周时间就能送达并完工。
entries.example_en: They chose a prefab house because it could be delivered and ready in just a few weeks.

entries.definition_en: the process of making parts of a building in a factory so they can be quickly put together on the construction site
entries.example_cn: 预制技术的运用使得该住宅区的快速完工成为可能。
entries.example_en: The rapid completion of the housing estate was made possible by the use of prefabrication techniques.

entries.definition_en: an introductory section or essay preceding the main text of a book, often written by the author
entries.example_cn: 序言解释了这部小说的历史背景。
entries.example_en: The preface explains the historical context of the novel.

entries.definition_cn: 为（书）作序；在陈述前作开场说明
entries.definition_en: to provide a preface to a book or introduce a statement with preliminary remarks
entries.example_cn: 他在批评之前先简短地道了歉。
entries.example_en: He prefaced his criticism with a brief apology.

entries.definition_en: serving as an introduction or preface
entries.example_cn: 这本书以一段说明作者目的的序言开始。
entries.example_en: The book begins with a prefatory note explaining the author's purpose.

entries.definition_cn: 长官；地方或部门行政长官
entries.definition_en: a chief official or magistrate in charge of an area or department
entries.example_cn: 这位地方长官负责监督该省的行政管理。
entries.example_en: The prefect supervised the administration of the province.

entries.definition_cn: （英国学校中）负责管理其他学生的学生；级长
entries.definition_en: a British school pupil given authority over other pupils
entries.example_cn: 级长带新生找到了他们的教室。
entries.example_en: The prefect showed the new students where to find their classrooms.

entries.definition_cn: （日本等的）都道府县的；行政区的
entries.definition_en: relating to a prefecture or a comparable administrative division
entries.example_cn: 该行政区政府宣布了该地区的新规定。
entries.example_en: The prefectural government announced new regulations for the region.

entries.definition_en: a district administered by a prefect
entries.example_cn: 该专区覆盖了该国的大片区域。
entries.example_en: The prefecture covers a large area of the country.

usage.label: administrative
usage.pattern: a jurisdiction or region administered by a prefect

entries.definition_cn: 行政长官一职；行政长官职位
entries.definition_en: the office or position of a prefect
entries.example_cn: 晋升后，他被任命担任行政长官一职。
entries.example_en: He was appointed to the office of prefect after his promotion.

entries.definition_en: to like one thing better than another
entries.example_cn: 比起咖啡，我更喜欢茶。
entries.example_en: I prefer tea to coffee.

entries.definition_en: to choose one option over another
entries.example_cn: 比起红色的，她更喜欢蓝色的裙子。
entries.example_en: She prefers the blue dress over the red one.

entries.definition_en: dated: to advance or promote someone to a position
entries.example_cn: 赞助人提拔那位年轻学者担任一个重要职位。
entries.example_en: The patron preferred the young scholar to an important post.

entries.definition_en: to give priority to one creditor over another
entries.example_cn: 法律优先偿还有担保的债权人。
entries.example_en: The law prefers secured creditors over unsecured ones.

entries.definition_en: more desirable than another
entries.example_cn: 在这种天气下，坐火车比开车更可取。
entries.example_en: Taking the train is preferable to driving in this weather.

entries.definition_en: in preference; by choice; if possible, in a preferable way
entries.example_cn: 最好我们周二见面，而不是周三。
entries.example_en: Preferably, we would meet on Tuesday rather than Wednesday.

entries.definition_en: a strong liking for something
entries.example_cn: 比起咖啡，我更喜欢茶。
entries.example_en: I have a preference for tea over coffee.

entries.definition_en: a tendency to favor one thing over another
entries.example_cn: 人们越来越倾向于在线购物。
entries.example_en: There is a growing preference for online shopping.

entries.definition_en: the right or opportunity, especially priority, to choose
entries.example_cn: 会员在选择座位时享有优先权。
entries.example_en: Members are given preference when choosing their seats.

entries.definition_en: a special advantage given to one country in trade
entries.example_cn: 该贸易协定给予成员国关税优惠待遇。
entries.example_en: The trade agreement grants tariff preferences to member nations.

entries.definition_en: showing or involving preference, especially by giving someone favorable treatment
entries.example_cn: 经理优待朋友的做法引起了其他员工的不满。
entries.example_en: The manager's preferential treatment of his friend caused resentment among the other staff.

entries.definition_en: in a way that gives priority to one thing over others
entries.example_cn: 该公司优先从当地大学招聘员工。
entries.example_en: The company hires preferentially from local universities.

entries.definition_en: advancement to a higher position or office; promotion
entries.example_cn: 他在公司里迅速得到擢升，这让同事们感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: His rapid preferment in the company surprised his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: the act of making accusations against someone
entries.example_cn: 这起丑闻导致几名高级官员遭到检举。
entries.example_en: The scandal led to the preferment of several high-ranking officials.

entries.definition_en: considered more desirable than another
entries.example_cn: 更受青睐的选择是价格较低的那个。
entries.example_en: The preferred option is the one with the lower price.

entries.definition_en: treated with special favor or partiality
entries.example_cn: 尽管有人反对，受偏袒的候选人还是得到了这份工作。
entries.example_en: The preferred candidate was given the job despite others' objections.

entries.definition_en: preferred stock
entries.example_cn: 该基金投资优先股，以获得定期股息。
entries.example_en: The fund invested in preferreds for their regular dividends.

entries.definition_en: an example that prefigures or foreshadows what is to come
entries.example_cn: 风暴早期的迹象是随后灾难的预兆。
entries.example_en: The early signs of the storm were a prefiguration of the disaster that followed.

entries.definition_en: the act of providing vague advance indications; representing beforehand
entries.example_cn: 艺术家的草图是对最终雕塑的预先预示。
entries.example_en: The artist's sketch served as a prefiguration of the final sculpture.

entries.definition_en: serving as a sign or representation of something that comes later
entries.example_cn: 早期草图预示性的特质暗示了未来的杰作。
entries.example_en: The prefigurative nature of the early sketches suggested a future masterpiece.

entries.definition_en: imagine or consider beforehand
entries.example_cn: 在绘制方案前，建筑师预想了建筑将如何发挥作用。
entries.example_en: Before drafting the plans, the architect prefigured how the building would function.

entries.definition_cn: 预示，如通过征兆或预兆
entries.definition_en: indicate, as with a sign or an omen
entries.example_cn: 这场风暴预示着政治格局即将到来的变化。
entries.example_en: The storm prefigures the coming changes in the political landscape.

entries.definition_en: a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning
entries.example_cn: 单词 'unhappy' 包含前缀 'un-'。
entries.example_en: The word 'unhappy' contains the prefix 'un-'.

entries.definition_en: to add a prefix to a word
entries.example_cn: 你可以在 'happy' 前面加上 'un-' 来使其表示相反的意思。
entries.example_en: You can prefix 'happy' with 'un-' to make it mean the opposite.

entries.definition_en: to shape something so that it resembles its final intended form
entries.example_cn: 模具被设计用来将塑料预成型为复杂的形状。
entries.example_en: The mold was designed to preform the plastic into a complex shape.

entries.definition_en: to determine or shape something beforehand
entries.example_cn: 工程师在组装前预先定型结构部件以确保稳定性。
entries.example_en: Engineers preform the structural components before assembly to ensure stability.

entries.definition_en: situated in front of the frontal structure of the brain
entries.example_cn: 前额叶皮层受损可能会影响决策能力。
entries.example_en: Damage to the prefrontal cortex can affect decision-making abilities.

entries.definition_en: the condition of carrying a developing baby in the womb
entries.example_cn: 她向家人宣布自己怀孕了。
entries.example_en: She announced her pregnancy to her family.

entries.definition_en: carrying a developing baby inside the body
entries.example_cn: 她怀上了第一个孩子。
entries.example_en: She is pregnant with her first child.

entries.definition_en: full of deep meaning or implication
entries.example_cn: 他的话充满了警告意味。
entries.example_en: His words were pregnant with warning.

entries.definition_en: filled with or accompanied by something
entries.example_cn: 房间里充满了紧张气氛。
entries.example_en: The room was pregnant with tension.

entries.definition_en: to heat something before the main cooking process begins
entries.example_cn: 请在烘烤蛋糕前将烤箱预热至200摄氏度。
entries.example_en: Please preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius before baking the cake.

entries.definition_en: to take something into your hands deliberately
entries.example_cn: 他无法抓住那个滑溜溜的物体。
entries.example_en: He could not prehend the slippery object.

entries.definition_en: adapted for grasping objects by wrapping around them
entries.example_cn: 猴子用其适于抓握的尾巴在树枝间摆动。
entries.example_en: The monkey used its prehensile tail to swing from branch to branch.

entries.definition_en: having a keen intellect
entries.example_cn: 这名学生头脑敏锐，很快掌握了复杂的理论。
entries.example_en: The student's prehensile mind grasped the complex theory quickly.

entries.definition_en: immoderately desirous of acquiring wealth
entries.example_cn: 他贪婪的本性驱使他不惜一切代价追求利润。
entries.example_en: His prehensile nature drove him to seek profit at any cost.

entries.definition_en: the act of gripping something firmly with the hands
entries.example_cn: 猴子的抓握能力让它能轻松地爬上树。
entries.example_en: The monkey's prehension allowed it to climb the tree easily.

entries.definition_cn: 存在于有记录的历史之前的
entries.definition_en: existing in times before recorded history
entries.example_cn: 考古学家在洞穴中发现了史前工具。
entries.example_en: Archaeologists discovered prehistoric tools in the cave.

entries.definition_cn: 与文字历史之前的时代有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to times before written history
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展出了石器时代的史前文物。
entries.example_en: The museum exhibits prehistoric artifacts from the Stone Age.

entries.definition_en: very old-fashioned; outdated
entries.example_cn: 该公司正试图摆脱过时的生产方法。
entries.example_en: The company is trying to move away from prehistoric methods of production.

entries.definition_en: existing or occurring before the beginning of recorded history
entries.example_cn: 考古学家研究史前文物以了解早期人类社会。
entries.example_en: Archaeologists study prehistorical artifacts to understand early human societies.

entries.definition_en: the period of human history before written records began
entries.example_cn: 考古学家研究史前时期，以了解早期人类是如何生活的。
entries.example_en: Archaeologists study prehistory to understand how early humans lived.

entries.definition_cn: 预先判断，尤指在没有足够证据的情况下
entries.definition_en: to judge beforehand, especially without sufficient evidence
entries.example_cn: 在听取所有事实之前，我们不应预先判断审判的结果。
entries.example_en: We must not prejudge the outcome of the trial before hearing all the facts.

entries.definition_en: a decision or opinion formed before all relevant evidence has been considered
entries.example_cn: 法官警告陪审团不要根据被告的外表形成预断。
entries.example_en: The judge warned the jury against forming a prejudgment based on the defendant's appearance.

entries.definition_en: an unfair opinion formed before knowing all the facts, which makes it hard to be objective
entries.example_cn: 许多人对外国人持有偏见。
entries.example_en: Many people hold a prejudice against people from other countries.

entries.definition_en: to harm or disadvantage someone or something
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策损害了小企业的利益。
entries.example_en: The new policy prejudices the interests of small businesses.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to form an opinion before they have enough information
entries.example_cn: 这则广告预先影响了观众，使他们倾向于该产品。
entries.example_en: The advertisement prejudices the audience in favor of the product.

entries.definition_en: having an opinion formed before having all the facts
entries.example_cn: 她对来自其他国家的人有成见。
entries.example_en: She was prejudiced against people from other countries.

entries.definition_en: showing bias based on personal feelings rather than facts
entries.example_cn: 这位有偏见的法官拒绝听取被告的解释。
entries.example_en: The prejudiced judge refused to listen to the defendant's explanation.

entries.definition_en: causing harm or injury
entries.example_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
entries.example_en: Smoking is prejudicial to your health.

entries.definition_en: tending to favor preconceived ideas
entries.example_cn: 法官回避了此案，以免产生偏见。
entries.example_en: The judge recused himself to avoid being prejudicial in the case.

entries.definition_en: the office or station of a prelate
entries.example_cn: 他辞去了主教的职位，去追求沉思的生活。
entries.example_en: He resigned from the prelacy to pursue a life of contemplation.

entries.definition_en: the body of prelates collectively
entries.example_cn: 这项新政策在颁布前由主教团进行了辩论。
entries.example_en: The new policy was debated by the prelacy before being enacted.

entries.definition_cn: 堕落前的；伊甸园时期的
entries.definition_en: relating to the time before the Fall of Adam and Eve in Christian theology
entries.example_cn: 堕落前的纯真状态常与人类的苦难形成对比。
entries.example_en: The prelapsarian state of innocence is often contrasted with human suffering.

entries.definition_en: a high-ranking member of the clergy
entries.example_cn: 这位高级神职人员向会众布道。
entries.example_en: The prelate delivered a sermon to the congregation.

entries.definition_en: the official position or rank of a high church official
entries.example_cn: 他在多年服务后被任命为主教职位。
entries.example_en: He was appointed to the prelature after years of service.

entries.definition_en: the group of high-ranking church officials collectively
entries.example_cn: 新政策在会议上得到了主教团的批准。
entries.example_en: The new policy was approved by the prelature during the meeting.

entries.definition_en: a minor match or competition held before the main event
entries.example_cn: 冠军在主赛前参加了一场预赛。
entries.example_en: The champion competed in a prelim before the main event.

entries.definition_en: an examination taken by graduate students to determine their fitness to continue their studies
entries.example_cn: 她出色地通过了资格考试。
entries.example_en: She passed her prelim with flying colors.

entries.definition_en: denoting an action or event preceding or in preparation for something more important
entries.example_cn: 在开始项目之前，我们需要做一些初步研究。
entries.example_en: We need to do some preliminary research before starting the project.

entries.definition_en: something that serves as a preceding event or introduces what follows
entries.example_cn: 音乐会以乐队的预演作为序幕。
entries.example_en: The concert began with a preliminary performance by the orchestra.

entries.definition_en: a minor match preceding the main event
entries.example_cn: 网球锦标赛的预赛非常精彩。
entries.example_en: The preliminary round of the tennis tournament was exciting.

entries.definition_en: preliminary examinations taken as a group
entries.example_cn: 你考完预考了吗？
entries.example_en: Are you done with prelims yet?

entries.definition_cn: 书籍正文前的文字；书前部分
entries.definition_en: written matter that appears before the main text of a book
entries.example_cn: 前言包括目录和插图列表。
entries.example_en: The prelims include a table of contents and a list of illustrations.

entries.definition_cn: 尚未学会读写的；不识字的
entries.definition_en: not yet able to read and write
entries.example_cn: 那个尚未学会读写的孩子认识字母，但还不会读写句子。
entries.example_en: The preliterate child recognized letters but could not yet read or write sentences.

entries.definition_en: used of a society that has not developed writing
entries.example_cn: 考古学家研究前文字社会，以了解文字发明之前的人类历史。
entries.example_en: Archaeologists study preliterate cultures to understand human history before the invention of writing.

entries.definition_en: an event or action that happens before something else and introduces it
entries.example_cn: 谈判是最终协议的前奏。
entries.example_en: The negotiations were a prelude to the final agreement.

entries.definition_en: a piece of music played before a fugue or to introduce an act in an opera
entries.example_cn: 音乐会以一首古典前奏曲开始。
entries.example_en: The concert began with a classical prelude.

entries.definition_en: to serve as an introduction or beginning to something
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨是飓风季节的前奏。
entries.example_en: The storm served as a prelude to the hurricane season.

entries.definition_cn: 演奏前奏曲；以……作为开场
entries.definition_en: to play a piece of music as a prelude
entries.example_cn: 音乐家们用乐器演奏前奏曲。
entries.example_en: The musicians preluded on their instruments.

entries.definition_en: relating to events before a marriage
entries.example_cn: 这对夫妇参加了一次婚前咨询。
entries.example_en: The couple attended a premarital counseling session.

entries.definition_en: happening too soon or too quickly
entries.example_cn: 根据这么小的样本得出结论为时过早。
entries.example_en: It was premature to draw conclusions from such a small sample.

entries.definition_en: occurring earlier than expected
entries.example_cn: 春天来得比预期早，导致花儿提前开放。
entries.example_en: The premature arrival of spring caused the flowers to bloom early.

entries.definition_en: born before the normal time for birth
entries.example_cn: 这个早产儿提前三个月出生了。
entries.example_en: The premature baby was born three months early.

entries.definition_en: too soon
entries.example_cn: 他过早地决定辞去工作。
entries.example_en: He decided to quit his job prematurely.

entries.definition_en: before the end of the normal period of gestation
entries.example_cn: 这个婴儿早产了。
entries.example_en: The baby was born prematurely.

entries.definition_en: the state of being premature
entries.example_cn: 婴儿的早产导致了并发症。
entries.example_en: The premature birth caused complications due to the prematurity of the infant.

entries.definition_en: relating to the preparation for the study of medicine
entries.example_cn: 他在申请医学院之前修读了医学预科的生物和化学课程。
entries.example_en: He took premedical courses in biology and chemistry before applying to medical school.

entries.definition_en: preceding and preparing for the study of medicine
entries.example_cn: 该校提供医学预科项目，旨在帮助学生过渡到医学学习。
entries.example_en: The university offers a premedical program designed to help students transition into medical studies.

entries.definition_cn: 预先考虑、盘算或计划（某项行动）
entries.definition_en: to consider, ponder, or plan an action beforehand
entries.example_cn: 他们预谋抢劫已经几周了。
entries.example_en: They premeditated the robbery for weeks.

entries.definition_en: to think or reflect beforehand or in advance
entries.example_cn: 她在会议前预先思考了她的回应。
entries.example_en: She premeditated her response before the meeting.

entries.definition_en: done with deliberate purpose and planning beforehand
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定该谋杀案是预谋的。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the murder was premeditated.

entries.definition_en: the act of planning something before doing it
entries.example_cn: 警方怀疑抢劫是事先策划的。
entries.example_en: The police suspected premeditation in the robbery.

entries.definition_en: the deliberate planning of a crime before it is committed
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定该谋杀案是蓄意策划的。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the murder was committed with premeditation.

entries.definition_en: occurring or existing before menopause
entries.example_cn: 许多女性在绝经前几年经历荷尔蒙变化。
entries.example_en: Many women experience hormonal changes during the premenopausal years.

entries.definition_en: relating to the period just before a woman's monthly period
entries.example_cn: 她上周经历了严重的经前症状。
entries.example_en: She experienced severe premenstrual symptoms last week.

entries.definition_en: a baby born before 37 weeks of pregnancy
entries.example_cn: 医生们正在密切监测早产儿的健康状况。
entries.example_en: The doctors are monitoring the health of the premie closely.

entries.definition_en: first in rank or degree
entries.example_cn: 顶级联赛是英格兰足球的最高级别。
entries.example_en: The premier league is the highest level of football in England.

entries.definition_en: preceding all others in time
entries.example_cn: 该杂志的最初一期于1990年发行。
entries.example_en: The premier edition of the magazine was released in 1990.

entries.definition_en: the head of the government in the United Kingdom
entries.example_cn: 首相今天宣布了新的经济政策。
entries.example_en: The premier announced new economic policies today.

entries.definition_en: the person who is head of government in several countries
entries.example_cn: 总理访问首都与外国领导人会面。
entries.example_en: The premier visited the capital to meet with foreign leaders.

entries.definition_en: be performed for the first time
entries.example_cn: 该剧昨晚在座无虚席的情况下首演。
entries.example_en: The play premiered last night to a full house.

entries.definition_en: perform a work for the first time
entries.example_cn: 导演在纽约首映了这部电影。
entries.example_en: The director premiered the movie in New York City.

entries.definition_cn: 戏剧、电影、电视节目或其他作品的首次公开演出或放映
entries.definition_en: the first public performance or showing of a play, film, television programme, or other work
entries.example_cn: 新音乐剧的首演吸引了许多名流参加。
entries.example_en: The premiere of the new musical was attended by many celebrities.

entries.definition_en: be performed for the first time
entries.example_cn: 该剧昨晚首演，座无虚席。
entries.example_en: The play premiered last night to a sold-out audience.

entries.definition_en: perform a work for the first time
entries.example_cn: 乐团将于下个月首次演奏贝多芬的第九交响曲。
entries.example_en: The orchestra will premiere Beethoven's Ninth Symphony next month.

entries.definition_en: preceding all others in time
entries.example_cn: 该杂志的首期包含了独家采访。
entries.example_en: The premiere edition of the magazine included exclusive interviews.

entries.definition_en: the office or position of a premier
entries.example_cn: 她在大选后被任命为总理。
entries.example_en: She was appointed to the premiership after the general election.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指澳式足球中）赛季结束时冠军队所保持的冠军头衔
entries.definition_en: the title of champion held by the winning team at the end of a particular season, especially in Australian rules football
entries.example_cn: 这家俱乐部赢得总决赛后庆祝夺冠。
entries.example_en: The club celebrated its premiership after winning the grand final.

entries.definition_en: a statement assumed to be true from which a conclusion is drawn
entries.example_cn: 这个论证基于所有人都是平等的前提。
entries.example_en: The argument was based on the premise that all humans are equal.

entries.definition_en: to state something beforehand as an explanation or basis
entries.example_cn: 作者基于最近的科学发现提出了他的理论。
entries.example_en: The author premised his theory on recent scientific discoveries.

entries.definition_en: to take something as preexisting and given
entries.example_cn: 该计划以资金能够到位这一假设为前提。
entries.example_en: The plan was premised on the assumption that funding would be available.

entries.definition_en: to furnish with a preface or introduction
entries.example_cn: 出版商为这本书加了一个历史概述作为序言。
entries.example_en: The publisher premised the book with a historical overview.

entries.definition_cn: 房屋及其周围土地；经营场所
entries.definition_en: a piece of land and the buildings on it
entries.example_cn: 公司把全体员工搬到了新的办公场所。
entries.example_en: The company moved its entire staff to new premises.

entries.definition_en: a statement that is assumed to be true and from which a conclusion can be drawn
entries.example_cn: 这个论证有缺陷，因为它基于一个虚假的前提。
entries.example_en: The argument was flawed because it relied on a false premiss.

entries.definition_en: to take something as preexisting and given
entries.example_cn: 该理论以所有人类都是理性生物为前提。
entries.example_en: The theory premisses that all humans are rational beings.

entries.definition_en: of superior quality or value; costing more
entries.example_cn: 他们选择了优质品牌，因为它的可靠性。
entries.example_en: They chose the premium brand for its reliability.

entries.definition_en: a payment made for insurance coverage
entries.example_cn: 每月的健康保险费相当高。
entries.example_en: The monthly premium for health insurance is quite high.

entries.definition_en: the extra amount something is valued at due to scarcity
entries.example_cn: 这枚稀有硬币以远高于面值的价格售出。
entries.example_en: The rare coin sold for a high premium over its face value.

entries.definition_en: a prize or bonus given to encourage purchase or participation
entries.example_cn: 商店提供奖品，鼓励顾客购买五件商品。
entries.example_en: The store offered a premium for buying five items.

entries.definition_en: a fee charged for exchanging currencies
entries.example_cn: 银行通常会收取货币兑换费。
entries.example_en: Banks usually charge a premium for currency exchange.

entries.definition_en: a payment or reward for specific acts like catching criminals
entries.example_cn: 政府悬赏提供关于逃犯的信息。
entries.example_en: The government offered a premium for information on the fugitive.

entries.definition_cn: 预先混合供使用或进一步加工的配料
entries.definition_en: a mixture of components prepared in advance for use or further processing
entries.example_cn: 面包师买了一种预先混合的干料混合物，以便更快地制作面包。
entries.example_en: The baker bought a premix to make the bread faster.

entries.definition_cn: 预先混合配料或组成部分
entries.definition_en: to blend ingredients or components in advance
entries.example_cn: 厨师先把干料混合好，再将其加入面糊中。
entries.example_en: The chef premixed the dry ingredients before adding them to the batter.

entries.definition_en: a tooth with two cusps located between the incisors and the molars
entries.example_cn: 牙医指着患者需要补牙的前臼齿。
entries.example_en: The dentist pointed to the patient's premolar that needed filling.

entries.definition_cn: 预示未来事件的通灵体验（如梦）
entries.definition_en: a clairvoyant or clairaudient experience, such as a dream, that seems to anticipate a future event
entries.example_cn: 她做了一个似乎预示那场事故的梦。
entries.example_en: She had a dream that seemed to be a premonition of the accident.

entries.definition_en: a feeling that something bad is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 她有一种不祥之兆，觉得这次旅行会以灾难告终。
entries.example_en: She had a premonition that the trip would end in disaster.

entries.definition_en: giving warning of something bad that is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 她有一种预感，这次旅行不会顺利。
entries.example_en: She had a premonitory feeling that the trip would not go well.

entries.definition_en: occurring or existing before birth
entries.example_cn: 医生建议孕妇服用产前维生素。
entries.example_en: Doctors recommend prenatal vitamins for expectant mothers.

entries.definition_en: placed before the nouns they modify
entries.example_cn: 前置形容词“红色的”出现在“汽车”之前。
entries.example_en: The prenominal adjective 'red' appears before 'car'.

entries.definition_en: an apprentice; an obsolete term
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻的学徒整天都在模仿师傅的作品。
entries.example_en: The young prentice spent his days copying the master's work.

entries.definition_en: relating to events or agreements that occur before a marriage
entries.example_cn: 他们签署了一份婚前协议以保护各自的资产。
entries.example_en: They signed a prenuptial agreement to protect their individual assets.

entries.definition_en: US: a prenuptial agreement
entries.example_cn: 他们结婚前签署了一份婚前协议。
entries.example_en: They signed a prenuptial before getting married.

entries.definition_en: an idea that keeps your mind busy and holds your attention
entries.example_cn: 她因忙于工作而忘记给母亲打电话。
entries.example_en: Her preoccupation with work made her forget to call her mother.

entries.definition_en: the state of being so focused on something that you ignore everything else
entries.example_cn: 他因专注于比赛而错过了公交车。
entries.example_en: His preoccupation with the game caused him to miss the bus.

entries.definition_cn: 在他人之前占据某物的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of occupying something before someone else does
entries.example_cn: 该队先占了场地，使对手无法使用。
entries.example_en: The team's preoccupation of the field prevented the rival from using it.

entries.definition_en: deeply absorbed in thought
entries.example_cn: 她全神贯注于自己的思绪，以至于没听到电话响。
entries.example_en: She was so preoccupied with her thoughts that she did not hear the phone ring.

entries.definition_cn: 对某事表现出过度或强迫性的关注
entries.definition_en: having or showing excessive or compulsive concern with something
entries.example_cn: 他开始对赢得彩票的想法表现出过度的关注。
entries.example_en: He became preoccupied with the idea of winning the lottery.

entries.definition_en: to occupy someone's mind so much that they cannot think about other things
entries.example_cn: 即将到来的考试会让他在接下来的几周里全神贯注。
entries.example_en: The upcoming exam will preoccupy him for the next few weeks.

entries.definition_en: to take possession of something before others do
entries.example_cn: 他们在音乐会开始前抢占了最好的座位。
entries.example_en: They managed to preoccupy the best seats before the concert started.

entries.definition_en: happening or done before and in preparation for a surgical operation
entries.example_cn: 手术前的测试在手术开始前已完成。
entries.example_en: The preoperative tests were completed before the surgery began.

entries.definition_cn: 家庭作业；课外准备工作
entries.definition_en: homework or preparatory work done outside class, especially at home
entries.example_cn: 我必须在晚饭前完成家庭作业。
entries.example_en: I have to finish my prep before dinner.

entries.definition_en: prepared and wrapped beforehand and ready for sale
entries.example_cn: 超市里大部分食物都是预包装的，以节省时间。
entries.example_en: Most of the food in the supermarket is prepackaged to save time.

entries.definition_en: prepared and wrapped in advance, ready for immediate sale or use.
entries.example_cn: 超市里大部分食品都是预包装的，并标有营养信息。
entries.example_en: Most of the food in the supermarket is prepacked and labeled with nutritional information.

entries.definition_en: paid in advance, especially of mail
entries.example_cn: 我为旅行买了一张预付电话卡。
entries.example_en: I bought a prepaid phone card for my trip.

entries.definition_cn: 为某事或某个目的而提前整理或安排
entries.definition_en: the activity of putting or setting in order in advance of some act or purpose
entries.example_cn: 备考花了数周时间。
entries.example_en: The preparation for the exam took several weeks.

entries.definition_cn: 准备就绪的状态；（尤指）战备状态
entries.definition_en: the state of being ready for use or action, especially military action
entries.example_cn: 检查人员评估了军队为即将到来的演习所处的战备状态。
entries.example_en: Inspectors assessed the army's state of preparation for the upcoming exercise.

entries.definition_cn: 思考在某种情况发生时该做什么的认知过程
entries.definition_en: the cognitive process of thinking about what you will do in the event of something happening
entries.example_cn: 他对最坏情况的预想帮助他保持了冷静。
entries.example_en: His preparation for the worst scenario helped him stay calm.

entries.definition_cn: 导致熟练行为的训练活动
entries.definition_en: activity leading to skilled behavior
entries.example_cn: 掌握这件乐器需要多年的训练。
entries.example_en: Years of preparation were needed to master the instrument.

entries.definition_en: a substance prepared according to a formula
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种治疗皮肤状况的特殊制剂。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a special preparation for the skin condition.

entries.definition_en: the act of cooking food by applying heat
entries.example_cn: 做饭是家里的传统。
entries.example_en: The preparation of the meal was a family tradition.

entries.definition_en: homework or study done before school hours to prepare for class
entries.example_cn: 她花晚上时间预习第二天的数学课。
entries.example_en: She spent her evening doing preparation for the next day's math lesson.

entries.definition_cn: （音乐）一个产生不协和和弦的音符首先在一个协和和弦中被听到
entries.definition_en: the prior sounding of a note in a consonant chord before it continues into a dissonance
entries.example_cn: 作曲家巧妙地使用了一个预备音，在旋律中制造了紧张感。
entries.example_en: The composer used a clever preparation to create tension in the melody.

entries.definition_en: serving to prepare for or precede something
entries.example_cn: 预备练习帮助学生在考试前集中注意力。
entries.example_en: The preparative exercises helped the students focus before the exam.

entries.definition_en: serving to prepare for something that follows
entries.example_cn: 预备练习帮助学生理解了主要课程。
entries.example_en: The preparatory exercises helped the students understand the main lesson.

entries.definition_en: to make something ready for a specific purpose or event.
entries.example_cn: 请为会议准备好房间。
entries.example_en: Please prepare the room for the meeting.

entries.definition_en: to organize something through careful planning and teamwork.
entries.example_cn: 他们为该项目制定了一个详细的计划。
entries.example_en: They prepared a detailed plan for the project.

entries.definition_en: to cook food by applying heat.
entries.example_cn: 她今晚会为我们做晚饭。
entries.example_en: She will prepare dinner for us tonight.

entries.definition_cn: 通过组合各种成分制作；合成
entries.definition_en: to produce or make by combining elements; to synthesize or compound
entries.example_cn: 她用橱柜里剩下的东西做了一顿饭。
entries.example_en: She prepared a meal from what was left in the cupboards.

entries.definition_en: to train someone for a future job or role.
entries.example_cn: 这所学校为学生进入大学做准备。
entries.example_en: The school prepares students for university.

entries.definition_en: to write or speak something in advance for delivery.
entries.example_cn: 这位演员为戏剧排练了他的台词。
entries.example_en: The actor prepared his lines for the play.

entries.definition_en: to receive training for a specific profession.
entries.example_cn: 他通过参加课程为新工作做准备。
entries.example_en: He prepared for his new job by taking courses.

entries.definition_cn: 预备不协和音：在前一个和弦中先把该音作为协和音奏出
entries.definition_en: to prepare a dissonance by sounding its note as a consonance in the preceding chord
entries.example_cn: 作曲家先在前一个和弦中把该音作为协和音奏出，以预备不协和音。
entries.example_en: The composer prepared the dissonance by sounding the note as a consonance in the preceding chord.

entries.definition_en: made ready or fit or suitable beforehand
entries.example_cn: 学生们为这场艰难的考试做好了准备。
entries.example_en: The students were prepared for the difficult exam.

entries.definition_en: having made preparations
entries.example_cn: 雨一停，我们就已准备好出发了。
entries.example_en: We are prepared to leave as soon as the rain stops.

entries.definition_en: equipped or prepared with necessary intellectual resources
entries.example_cn: 她已准备好与同事讨论这个复杂的话题。
entries.example_en: She was prepared to discuss the complex topic with her colleagues.

entries.definition_en: the state of being prepared, especially for a possible event or emergency
entries.example_cn: 该国应对自然灾害的准备水平已显著提高。
entries.example_en: The country's preparedness for natural disasters has improved significantly.

usage.label: preparedness for
usage.pattern: Source w15440r0 explicitly supplies “preparedness for battle.”

entries.definition_en: to pay for something before receiving it
entries.example_cn: 你可以在线预付机票费用。
entries.example_en: You can prepay for your flight tickets online.

entries.definition_en: payment made before goods or services are provided
entries.example_cn: 租赁合同要求预付第一个月的租金。
entries.example_en: The rental agreement requires a prepayment of the first month's rent.

entries.definition_cn: 为当期发生、但利益将在未来期间获得的费用确认的资产
entries.definition_en: an asset recognized for an expense incurred now whose benefit will be received in a future period
entries.example_cn: 公司将未来保险保障的保费记作预付款。
entries.example_en: The company recorded the insurance premium for future coverage as a prepayment.

entries.definition_en: a superiority in numbers or amount
entries.example_cn: 花园里蓝色的花占多数。
entries.example_en: There was a preponderance of blue flowers in the garden.

entries.definition_en: superiority in power or influence
entries.example_cn: 大量证据表明他是无辜的。
entries.example_en: The preponderance of evidence suggests he is innocent.

entries.definition_en: greater physical weight (obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 前部较大的重量使飞机向前倾斜。
entries.example_en: The preponderance of weight at the front made the aircraft tilt forward.

entries.definition_en: having more power or influence than anything else
entries.example_cn: 该地区占主导地位的力量是军队。
entries.example_en: The preponderant force in the region is the military.

entries.definition_en: to a much greater extent in number or influence
entries.example_cn: 投票结果主要支持新政策。
entries.example_en: The vote was preponderantly in favor of the new policy.

entries.definition_en: to outweigh or predominate
entries.example_cn: 证据明显有利于被告无罪。
entries.example_en: The evidence preponderates in favor of the defendant's innocence.

usage.label: 可不及物，常与 over 或 in favor of 连用
usage.pattern: source w50511r3 supports intransitive use and these complement patterns.

entries.definition_en: a word that connects a noun or pronoun to another word in a sentence to show relationships like location, time, or direction
entries.example_cn: 介词“in”表示书在盒子里面。
entries.example_en: The preposition 'in' indicates that the book is inside the box.

entries.definition_cn: （语言学）前置；将一个语言单位置于另一个语言单位之前，尤指将修饰语置于所修饰词之前或将词缀置于词根之前。
entries.definition_en: (linguistics) The placement of one linguistic element before another, especially a modifier before the word it modifies or an affix before its base.
entries.example_cn: 在语言学中，preposition 可以指将词缀置于词根之前。
entries.example_en: In linguistics, preposition can refer to the placement of an affix before its base.

entries.definition_en: relating to or formed with a preposition
entries.example_cn: 介词短语“在盒子里”修饰名词。
entries.example_en: The prepositional phrase 'in the box' modifies the noun.

entries.definition_en: appearing attractive or impressive in a way that creates a favorable first impression
entries.example_cn: 她有一种令人一见就有好感的气质，立刻引起了人们的注意。
entries.example_en: She had a prepossessing presence that commanded attention immediately.

entries.definition_en: so unreasonable that it invites mockery
entries.example_cn: 没有火箭就飞到月球的想法是荒谬的。
entries.example_en: The idea of flying to the moon without a rocket is preposterous.

entries.definition_en: in an absurd or unreasonable way
entries.example_cn: 今天外面热得离谱。
entries.example_en: It was preposterously hot outside today.

entries.definition_en: someone who prepares for a disaster
entries.example_cn: 这位备灾者储备了罐头食品和饮用水以防紧急情况。
entries.example_en: The prepper stocked canned food and water in case of an emergency.

entries.definition_en: relating to or occurring before puberty
entries.example_cn: 医生注意到这名青春期前的儿童正在经历突然的生长突增。
entries.example_en: The doctor noted that the prepubertal child was experiencing a sudden growth spurt.

entries.definition_en: at the age immediately before puberty, often marked by accelerated growth
entries.example_cn: 这个青春期前的男孩经历了一次突然的生长爆发。
entries.example_en: The prepubescent boy experienced a sudden growth spurt.

entries.definition_en: the fold of skin that covers the head of the penis
entries.example_cn: 割礼涉及切除包皮。
entries.example_en: Circumcision involves the removal of the prepuce.

entries.definition_en: the fold of skin that covers the tip of the clitoris
entries.example_cn: 医学文献详细描述了阴蒂包皮的解剖结构。
entries.example_en: Medical texts describe the anatomy of the prepuce in detail.

entries.definition_en: to record something before it is shown or broadcast
entries.example_cn: 这档节目是预先录制的，以确保高质量的制作。
entries.example_en: The show was prerecorded to ensure high production quality.

entries.definition_en: recorded in advance for later transmission or playback
entries.example_cn: 这场音乐会预先录制并广播给世界各地的观众。
entries.example_en: The concert was prerecorded and broadcast to audiences around the world.

entries.definition_en: something that must be done or known before something else can happen
entries.example_cn: 数学是这门物理课的先决条件。
entries.example_en: Math is a prerequisite for this physics course.

entries.definition_en: required as a prior condition of something else; necessary or indispensable
entries.example_cn: 学生必须修完先修课程，才能选修物理学。
entries.example_en: Students must complete the prerequisite course before enrolling in physics.

entries.definition_en: a right reserved exclusively by a particular person or group
entries.example_cn: 宣战是总统的特权。
entries.example_en: It is the prerogative of the president to declare war.

entries.definition_en: to indicate, as with a sign or an omen
entries.example_cn: 突如其来的寂静预示着前方有麻烦。
entries.example_en: The sudden silence presaged trouble ahead.

entries.definition_en: a foreboding about what is about to happen
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨来临前，他预感到灾难将至。
entries.example_en: He felt a presage of disaster before the storm arrived.

entries.definition_en: a sign of something about to happen
entries.example_cn: 气温升高是夏天的征兆。
entries.example_en: The rising temperature was a presage of summer.

entries.definition_en: a condition where the ability to focus on near objects decreases due to loss of lens elasticity after age 45
entries.example_cn: 四十五岁后，她开始出现老花眼，近距离工作时需要戴老花镜。
entries.example_en: After turning forty-five, she began to experience presbyopia and needed reading glasses for close work.

entries.definition_en: an elder in the Presbyterian Church
entries.example_cn: 长老在礼拜中主持了祈祷。
entries.example_en: The presbyter led the prayer at the service.

entries.definition_cn: 罗马天主教教区神父的住宅
entries.definition_en: the home of a Roman Catholic parish priest
entries.example_cn: 新牧师住宅建在教堂旁边，供神职人员居住。
entries.example_en: The new presbytery was built next to the church to house the priests.

entries.definition_cn: 教堂内祭坛周围供神职人员使用的区域
entries.definition_en: the part of a church around the altar reserved for the clergy
entries.example_cn: 礼拜期间，唱诗班站在圣坛区。
entries.example_en: The choir stood in the presbytery during the service.

entries.definition_en: the presbyters of a congregation considered collectively
entries.example_cn: 长老团开会讨论教会的未来。
entries.example_en: The presbytery met to discuss the congregation's future.

entries.definition_en: an educational institution for children too young for elementary school
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在开始上小学之前去幼儿园。
entries.example_en: The children attend preschool before starting elementary school.

entries.definition_en: a young child who goes to preschool or kindergarten
entries.example_cn: 那个学龄前儿童在沙坑里和其他孩子们快乐地玩耍。
entries.example_en: The preschooler played happily with the other children in the sandbox.

entries.definition_en: the ability to know or foresee future events
entries.example_cn: 她对股市崩盘的先见之明令人惊叹。
entries.example_en: Her prescience about the market crash was remarkable.

entries.definition_en: able to perceive the significance of events before they happen
entries.example_cn: 她对风暴的先知警告挽救了许多生命。
entries.example_en: Her prescient warning about the storm saved many lives.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows knowledge of events before they happen
entries.example_cn: 她在全球转向绿色技术之前，就有先见之明地投资了可再生能源股票。
entries.example_en: She presciently invested in renewable energy stocks before the global shift toward green technology.

entries.definition_en: to order the use of a treatment or medicine by written prescription
entries.example_cn: 医生为感染开了抗生素。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for the infection.

entries.definition_en: to recommend as beneficial
entries.example_cn: 医生经常推荐运动以维护心脏健康。
entries.example_en: Doctors often prescribe exercise for heart health.

entries.definition_en: to lay down or specify authoritatively as a rule or requirement
entries.example_cn: 法规规定要定期进行安全检查。
entries.example_en: The regulations prescribe regular safety checks.

entries.definition_en: set down as a rule or guide
entries.example_cn: 手册中包含了规定的安全程序。
entries.example_en: The manual contains prescribed safety procedures.

entries.definition_en: fixed or established especially by order or command
entries.example_cn: 法院对违规行为发出了强制规定的处罚。
entries.example_en: The court issued a prescribed penalty for the violation.

entries.definition_en: conforming to set usage, procedure, or discipline
entries.example_cn: 仪式遵循了规定的宗教仪式。
entries.example_en: The ceremony followed prescribed religious rituals.

entries.definition_en: formally laid down or imposed
entries.example_cn: 大学对学生贷款有正式制定的限额。
entries.example_en: The university has prescribed limits on student loans.

entries.definition_cn: 行为或行动的既定准则
entries.definition_en: a prescribed guide for conduct or action
entries.example_cn: 法律准则禁止招聘中的任何形式的歧视。
entries.example_en: The legal prescript forbids any form of discrimination in hiring.

entries.definition_cn: 医生为特定药物和剂量开具的书面医嘱
entries.definition_en: a doctor's written order for a specific medicine and dosage
entries.example_cn: 医生给病人开了抗生素处方。
entries.example_en: The doctor wrote the patient a prescription for antibiotics.

entries.definition_en: a medicine that can only be bought with a doctor's order
entries.example_cn: 没有处方你买不到抗生素。
entries.example_en: You cannot buy antibiotics without a prescription.

entries.definition_en: written instructions for making eyeglass lenses
entries.example_cn: 她把配镜处方拿给了验光师。
entries.example_en: She took her prescription to the optician.

entries.definition_en: official instructions or rules given by an authority
entries.example_cn: 该法规对违规报告作出了详细规定。
entries.example_en: The statute contained detailed prescriptions for reporting violations.

entries.definition_en: requiring a doctor's written order to be obtained
entries.example_cn: 这种药是处方药。
entries.example_en: This medicine is a prescription drug.

entries.definition_cn: 规定性的；旨在规定规则、标准或行为要求的
entries.definition_en: intended to prescribe rules, standards, or required conduct
entries.example_cn: 这项新法律具有规范性，明确规定了公司如何处理废物。
entries.example_en: The new law is prescriptive, telling companies exactly how to dispose of waste.

entries.definition_en: a doctrine supporting or promoting prescriptive linguistics
entries.example_cn: 现代语言学经常批评语言教学中规定论的僵化性。
entries.example_en: Modern linguistics often critiques the rigidity of prescriptivism in language teaching.

entries.definition_en: a doctrine holding that moral statements prescribe appropriate attitudes and behavior
entries.example_cn: 这位哲学家认为，规定论对于维持社会秩序至关重要。
entries.example_en: The philosopher argued that prescriptivism is essential for maintaining social order.

entries.definition_cn: 赛季前期；赛季前用于训练和准备的时期
entries.definition_en: the period before the regular season used for training and preparation
entries.example_cn: 季前期，球队为锦标赛进行训练。
entries.example_en: During preseason, the team trained for the championship.

entries.definition_en: the state of being present; current existence
entries.example_cn: 氧气的存在对生命至关重要。
entries.example_en: The presence of oxygen is essential for life.

entries.definition_en: the immediate proximity of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 老师的在场让喧闹的班级安静了下来。
entries.example_en: The teacher's presence calmed the noisy class.

entries.definition_en: the impression that something is present
entries.example_cn: 房间里有一种奇怪的气息。
entries.example_en: There was a strange presence in the room.

entries.definition_en: a quality of poise and effectiveness that makes someone impressive or influential
entries.example_cn: 将军以非凡的气场走进来。
entries.example_en: The general entered with great presence.

entries.definition_en: an invisible spiritual being felt to be nearby
entries.example_cn: 他们觉得祖先的灵体就在那所老房子里。
entries.example_en: They felt the presence of their ancestors in the old house.

entries.definition_en: attendance at an event or gathering
entries.example_cn: 她出席会议的事被记录在案。
entries.example_en: Her presence at the meeting was noted.

entries.definition_en: happening now
entries.example_cn: 目前的情况很困难。
entries.example_en: The present situation is difficult.

entries.definition_en: existing in a specific place
entries.example_cn: 经理在会议上吗？
entries.example_en: Is the manager present at the meeting?

entries.definition_en: something given as a gift
entries.example_cn: 她给母亲买了一份礼物。
entries.example_en: She bought a present for her mother.

entries.definition_en: a verb tense used for actions happening now
entries.example_cn: 现在时描述正在发生的动作。
entries.example_en: The present tense describes actions happening now.

entries.definition_en: to show something to an audience
entries.example_cn: 乐队今晚将展示一场新演出。
entries.example_en: The band will present a new show tonight.

entries.definition_en: to bring an idea to someone's mind
entries.example_cn: 他向团队提出了一个新想法。
entries.example_en: He presented a new idea to the team.

entries.definition_en: the time that is happening now
entries.example_cn: 我们正生活在一个令人兴奋的现在。
entries.example_en: We are living in an exciting present.

entries.definition_en: to perform a play on a stage
entries.example_cn: 演员们明天将演出这部戏剧。
entries.example_en: The actors will present the play tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: belonging to the current time
entries.example_cn: 现在的城市与过去的城市大不相同。
entries.example_en: The present-day city is very different from the one in the past.

entries.definition_en: fit to be seen
entries.example_cn: 他花了好几个小时理发，以便在面试时看起来体面。
entries.example_en: He spent hours getting his hair cut to look presentable for the interview.

entries.definition_en: acceptable and worth considering
entries.example_cn: 委员会认为她的提案可以接受，并邀请她加以修改。
entries.example_en: The committee found her proposal presentable and invited her to revise it.

entries.definition_cn: 向观众或听众作的演讲或报告
entries.definition_en: a lecture or speech given to an audience
entries.example_cn: 她在座无虚席的礼堂里作了一场关于气候变化的演讲。
entries.example_en: She gave a presentation on climate change to a packed auditorium.

entries.definition_en: a visual display of information, such as a slide show
entries.example_cn: 销售团队使用色彩鲜艳的演示来解释新产品功能。
entries.example_en: The sales team used a colorful presentation to explain the new product features.

entries.definition_en: the act of presenting a proposal to a group
entries.example_cn: 她在董事会上详细汇报了这项提案。
entries.example_en: She gave a detailed presentation of the proposal at the board meeting.

entries.definition_en: a show or display of something to an audience
entries.example_cn: 美术馆本周末举办了一场新画展。
entries.example_en: The art gallery hosted a presentation of new paintings this weekend.

entries.definition_cn: 正式颁发（奖品或奖励等）
entries.definition_en: the act of formally giving something (such as a prize or reward) to someone
entries.example_cn: 经理向这位员工颁发了特别奖励，以表彰她的辛勤工作。
entries.example_en: The manager gave a special presentation to the employee for her hard work.

entries.definition_en: the act of introducing someone to others publicly
entries.example_cn: 主持人向观众正式介绍了特邀演讲嘉宾。
entries.example_en: The host made a formal presentation of the guest speaker to the audience.

entries.definition_en: the act of broadcasting or publishing news and information
entries.example_cn: 数百万人观看了选举结果的现场播报。
entries.example_en: The live presentation of the election results was watched by millions.

entries.definition_cn: 胎儿在子宫内相对于产道的位置，尤指分娩时的胎位
entries.definition_en: the position of the fetus in the uterus relative to the birth canal, especially during labor
entries.example_cn: 医生在产前检查时检查了胎儿的胎位。
entries.example_en: The doctor checked the presentation of the fetus during the prenatal visit.

entries.definition_cn: 与呈现（尤指心理学或哲学中的呈现）有关的
entries.definition_en: relating to the way something is shown or displayed, especially in psychology or philosophy
entries.example_cn: 这次讲座的呈现方式对学生们非常有吸引力。
entries.example_en: The presentational style of the lecture was very engaging for the students.

entries.definition_cn: present 的过去式和过去分词
entries.definition_en: simple past and past participle of present
entries.example_cn: 她昨天向委员会展示了她的研究结果。
entries.example_en: She presented her findings to the committee yesterday.

entries.definition_en: Having a specified presentation, or a presentation with specified properties.
entries.example_cn: 该定理以清晰且合乎逻辑的方式被呈示出来。
entries.example_en: The theorem was presented in a clear and logical manner.

entries.definition_cn: 呈递或传达信息、文件等的人
entries.definition_en: someone who presents or delivers a message, document, or other communication
entries.example_cn: 呈递人将请愿书交给了委员会成员。
entries.example_en: The presenter handed the petition to the committee members.

entries.definition_en: an advocate who presents a person for an award or introduction
entries.example_cn: 主持人向观众介绍了这位获奖科学家。
entries.example_en: The presenter introduced the award-winning scientist to the audience.

entries.definition_en: person who makes a gift of property
entries.example_cn: 这位慷慨的赠予者向慈善机构捐赠了一大笔钱。
entries.example_en: The generous presenter donated a large sum of money to the charity.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of evil to come
entries.example_cn: 她有一种不祥的预感，觉得坏事即将发生。
entries.example_en: She had a presentiment that something bad was about to happen.

entries.definition_cn: 认为《圣经》关于世界末日的预言正在当今应验的学说
entries.definition_en: the doctrine that biblical prophecies of the Apocalypse are currently being fulfilled
entries.example_cn: 一些神学家认为，现时主义主张《圣经》关于世界末日的预言正在当今应验。
entries.example_en: Some theologians regard presentism as the doctrine that biblical prophecies of the Apocalypse are being fulfilled in the present.

entries.definition_en: in the near future
entries.example_cn: 我马上就到。
entries.example_en: I will be there presently.

entries.definition_en: at this time or period; now
entries.example_cn: 目前，情况大不相同。
entries.example_en: Presently, the situation is quite different.

usage.label: now/currently versus soon
usage.pattern: The word can contrast with the near-future sense.

entries.definition_cn: 大陪审团提出的正式指控
entries.definition_en: a formal accusation of a crime made by a grand jury
entries.example_cn: 大陪审团对那位腐败官员提出了起诉。
entries.example_en: The grand jury issued a presentment against the corrupt official.

entries.definition_en: the act of presenting a bill or other document for acceptance or payment
entries.example_cn: 会计师在将账单提示给客户付款前进行了审核。
entries.example_en: The accountant reviewed the bill before its presentment to the client for payment.

entries.definition_en: the act of showing something to someone
entries.example_cn: 博物馆对古代文物的展示令人着迷。
entries.example_en: The museum's presentment of ancient artifacts was fascinating.

entries.definition_en: the activity of protecting something from loss or danger
entries.example_cn: 保护这片森林对野生动物至关重要。
entries.example_en: The preservation of the forest is vital for wildlife.

entries.definition_en: a process that saves organic substances from decay
entries.example_cn: 罐装是一种食品防腐方法。
entries.example_en: Canning is a method of food preservation.

entries.definition_en: the condition of being (well or ill) preserved
entries.example_cn: 这幅画的保存状态极佳。
entries.example_en: The painting is in excellent preservation.

entries.definition_en: an occurrence of improvement by virtue of preventing loss or injury or other change
entries.example_cn: 这份文件的保全使得历史学家能够对其进行研究。
entries.example_en: The preservation of the document allowed historians to study it.

entries.definition_en: a person who supports protecting historical sites, endangered species, or natural areas
entries.example_cn: 这位保护主义者反对在森林中修建新公路。
entries.example_en: The preservationist argued against building a new road through the forest.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound added to protect against decay or decomposition
entries.example_cn: 加工食品中常含有防腐剂。
entries.example_en: Artificial preservatives are often found in processed foods.

entries.definition_en: tending or having the power to preserve
entries.example_cn: 蜂蜜的防腐特性使其能保存数年。
entries.example_en: The preservative qualities of honey make it last for years.

entries.definition_en: keep in safety and protect from harm, decay, loss, or destruction
entries.example_cn: 博物馆保护古代文物。
entries.example_en: The museum preserves ancient artifacts.

entries.definition_en: keep or maintain in unaltered condition; cause to remain or last
entries.example_cn: 我们必须保持和平。
entries.example_en: We must preserve the peace.

entries.definition_en: to maintain or retain for personal or special use
entries.example_cn: 他决定保留自己的权利。
entries.example_en: He decided to preserve his rights.

entries.definition_en: prevent (food) from rotting
entries.example_cn: 盐用于腌制肉类以防腐烂。
entries.example_en: Salt is used to preserve meat.

entries.definition_en: maintain in safety from injury, harm, or danger
entries.example_cn: 医生努力保全病人的生命。
entries.example_en: The doctor worked hard to preserve the patient's life.

entries.definition_en: a reservation where animals are protected
entries.example_cn: 他们参观了一个自然保护区。
entries.example_en: They visited a nature preserve.

entries.definition_en: fruit preserved by cooking with sugar
entries.example_cn: 她做了草莓果酱。
entries.example_en: She made strawberry preserves.

entries.definition_en: a domain that seems to be specially reserved for someone
entries.example_cn: 对许多作家来说，这个档案馆是他们自己的专属领域。
entries.example_en: For many writers, the archive is their own preserve.

entries.definition_en: someone who keeps safe from harm or danger
entries.example_cn: 公园管理员充当了这些濒危动物的保护者。
entries.example_en: The park ranger acted as a preserver for the endangered animals.

entries.definition_en: rescue equipment consisting of a buoyant belt or jacket to keep a person from drowning
entries.example_cn: 每位游泳者下水前都必须穿上救生衣。
entries.example_en: Every swimmer must wear a preserver before entering the water.

entries.definition_cn: 制作果酱或腌制肉类的人
entries.definition_en: a person who prepares preserves of fruit or preserved meats
entries.example_cn: 这位果酱制作师制作了几罐果酱，留待冬天食用。
entries.example_en: The preserver made jars of fruit preserves for the winter.

entries.definition_en: a person who refinishes furniture
entries.example_cn: 古董商聘请家具翻新师重新修整柜子。
entries.example_en: The antique dealer hired a preserver to refinish the cabinet.

entries.definition_en: fruit that has been cooked with sugar to prevent it from spoiling
entries.example_cn: 她早餐吃了涂有草莓果酱的热吐司。
entries.example_en: She served warm toast with strawberry preserves for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: set in advance
entries.example_cn: 收音机调到了一个预设频道。
entries.example_en: The radio was tuned to a preset station.

usage.label: not-comparable
usage.pattern: Adjective meaning set in advance or as a default; source w23919r0.

entries.definition_en: to act as the leader or chairperson of a meeting or organization
entries.example_cn: 首席执行官将于下周二主持年度股东大会。
entries.example_en: The CEO will preside over the annual shareholders' meeting next Tuesday.

entries.definition_en: the job and duties of being president
entries.example_cn: 她为公众服务多年后当选总统。
entries.example_en: She was elected to the presidency after years of public service.

entries.definition_en: the period during which someone is president
entries.example_cn: 他的总统任期持续了四年。
entries.example_en: His presidency lasted for four years.

entries.definition_cn: 由总统直接领导的政府机构及施政举措
entries.definition_en: the administration and government initiatives directly controlled by a president
entries.example_cn: 由于总统已进入跛脚鸭任期，总统领导的政府机构及施政举措常常受到国会行动的阻碍。
entries.example_en: Because of the president's lame-duck status, the presidency was often hampered by congressional actions.

entries.definition_en: the head of state of a republic
entries.example_cn: 总统向全国发表了演讲。
entries.example_en: The president gave a speech to the nation.

entries.definition_en: the person in charge of a company or business
entries.example_cn: 新总裁将于下个月上任。
entries.example_en: The new president will start next month.

entries.definition_en: the person who leads meetings for a group or organization
entries.example_cn: 她当选为学生俱乐部的主席。
entries.example_en: She was elected president of the student club.

entries.definition_en: the head administrator of a college or university
entries.example_cn: 大学校长参观了校园。
entries.example_en: The president of the university visited the campus.

entries.definition_en: the leader of the government of the United States
entries.example_cn: 总统签署了新法律。
entries.example_en: The president signed the new law.

entries.definition_en: relating to a president or presidency
entries.example_cn: 总统选举每四年举行一次。
entries.example_en: The presidential election is held every four years.

entries.definition_en: befitting a president
entries.example_cn: 她举止庄重，具有总统般的气度。
entries.example_en: She carried herself with presidential dignity.

entries.definition_en: in a manner characteristic of a president
entries.example_cn: 这位领导人以总统的方式应对危机，表现出冷静和权威。
entries.example_en: The leader addressed the crisis presidentially, showing calm and authority.

entries.definition_en: a fortress built by the Spanish in the southwestern United States to protect missions
entries.example_cn: 这座历史悠久的要塞仍然是殖民时代的见证。
entries.example_en: The historic presidio still stands as a reminder of the colonial era.

entries.definition_en: a permanent executive committee in socialist countries that holds the power of a larger legislative body and acts for it when it is not in session
entries.example_cn: 新政策在提交全体大会之前已由主席团批准。
entries.example_en: The new policy was approved by the presidium before being presented to the full assembly.

entries.definition_cn: 前苏格拉底哲学的；早于或独立于苏格拉底的早期希腊哲学传统的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to the early Greek philosophical tradition preceding or independent of Socrates
entries.example_cn: 前苏格拉底哲学包含早期希腊人解释宇宙本质的尝试。
entries.example_en: Presocratic philosophy includes early Greek attempts to explain the nature of the universe.

entries.definition_en: to apply force or pressure to something
entries.example_cn: 请按按钮启动机器。
entries.example_en: Please press the button to start the machine.

entries.definition_en: to compress or squeeze something between surfaces
entries.example_cn: 她把花压在两张纸之间。
entries.example_en: She pressed the flowers between sheets of paper.

entries.definition_en: to push or force something in a direction
entries.example_cn: 风把船推向岸边。
entries.example_en: The wind pressed the boat against the shore.

entries.definition_en: newspapers and magazines as a whole
entries.example_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这一消息。
entries.example_en: The press reported the news quickly.

entries.definition_cn: 紧迫性；迫切的要求或压力
entries.definition_en: an urgent demand or pressure requiring attention
entries.example_cn: 繁重而紧迫的工作使她没有时间休息。
entries.example_en: The press of work left her no time to rest.

entries.definition_cn: 出版社，尤指出版书籍的出版社
entries.definition_en: a publisher, especially one that produces books
entries.example_cn: 这家出版社出版了她的第一部小说。
entries.example_en: The press published her first novel.

entries.definition_cn: 用于对某物施加压力的装置
entries.definition_en: a device used to apply pressure to something
entries.example_cn: 她把花放进压花器里晾干。
entries.example_en: She placed the flowers in a press to dry them.

entries.definition_en: a machine used for printing
entries.example_cn: 这台旧印刷机曾用于印刷书籍。
entries.example_en: The old press was used to print books.

entries.definition_en: to be burdensome or oppressive
entries.example_cn: 债务负担沉重地压在他身上。
entries.example_en: The burden of debt pressed heavily on him.

entries.definition_en: a large crowd of people
entries.example_cn: 一大群人包围了舞台。
entries.example_en: A press of people surrounded the stage.

entries.definition_en: an exercise where you lie on your stomach and push your body up and down using your arms
entries.example_cn: 他每天早上做十个俯卧撑以保持健康。
entries.example_en: He does ten press-ups every morning to stay fit.

usage.label: 英式及英联邦用法；美式通常说 push-up

entries.definition_en: smoothed and made neat by ironing
entries.example_cn: 这件衬衫熨烫得很平整，看起来很整洁。
entries.example_en: The shirt looked pressed and neat.

entries.definition_en: compelling immediate action
entries.example_cn: 我们迫切需要更多的资金。
entries.example_en: We have a pressing need for more funding.

entries.definition_en: the act of pressing; the exertion of pressure
entries.example_cn: 按下按钮启动了机器。
entries.example_en: The pressing of the button started the machine.

entries.definition_en: a metal or plastic part that is made by a mechanical press
entries.example_cn: 这扇车门是由钢冲压件制成的。
entries.example_en: The car door is made of a steel pressing.

entries.definition_en: in a pressing manner
entries.example_cn: 她迫切地要求立即回答她的问题。
entries.example_en: She asked pressingly for an immediate answer to her question.

entries.definition_en: a journalist who writes news stories for newspapers or broadcast media
entries.example_cn: 这位男记者就新城市计划采访了市长。
entries.example_en: The pressman interviewed the mayor about the new city plan.

entries.definition_en: a man whose job is printing
entries.example_cn: 这位老印刷工在工厂工作了四十年。
entries.example_en: The old pressman worked in the factory for forty years.

entries.definition_cn: 引起血管开口收缩、从而维持或增加血压的物质
entries.definition_en: an agent that causes narrowing of a blood vessel opening, thereby maintaining or increasing blood pressure
entries.example_cn: 肾上腺素在紧急情况下起升压作用。
entries.example_en: Epinephrine acts as a pressor in emergency situations.

entries.definition_cn: 升高或倾向于升高血压的
entries.definition_en: increasing or tending to increase blood pressure
entries.example_cn: 这种药物对心脏有强烈的升压作用。
entries.example_en: The medication has a strong pressor effect on the heart.

entries.definition_en: the force applied to a unit area of surface
entries.example_cn: 水压随深度增加而增大。
entries.example_en: Water pressure increases with depth.

entries.definition_en: a force that compels
entries.example_cn: 截止日期的压力太大了。
entries.example_en: The pressure of the deadline was too much.

entries.definition_cn: 由要求造成的压力或紧迫感
entries.definition_en: a state of stress or urgency caused by demands
entries.example_cn: 她感到必须按时完成项目的压力。
entries.example_en: She felt pressure to finish the project on time.

entries.definition_en: the act of pressing; the exertion of pressure
entries.example_cn: 他对伤口进行了按压。
entries.example_en: He applied pressure to the wound.

entries.definition_en: to cause to do through pressure or necessity
entries.example_cn: 他们强迫他辞职。
entries.example_en: They pressured him to resign.

entries.definition_en: exert pressure on someone through threats
entries.example_cn: 警察威胁要施加压力。
entries.example_en: The police threatened to apply pressure.

entries.definition_en: the somatic sensation that results from applying force to an area of skin
entries.example_cn: 她感到织物压在皮肤上的压力。
entries.example_en: She felt pressure against her skin from the fabric.

entries.definition_en: an oppressive condition of distress
entries.example_cn: 她正处于极大的困境中。
entries.example_en: She is under great pressure.

entries.definition_cn: 用高压水流清洁表面，常用于去除污垢、霉菌或剥落的旧漆
entries.definition_en: to clean a surface with a high-pressure stream of water, often to remove dirt, mildew, or loose paint
entries.example_cn: 在重新粉刷房子之前，我们需要对外墙进行高压清洗。
entries.example_en: We need to pressure-wash the siding before repainting the house.

entries.definition_en: to increase the pressure on a gas or liquid
entries.example_cn: 飞机爬升到高空时，飞行员必须迅速增压机舱。
entries.example_en: The pilot had to pressurise the cabin quickly as the plane climbed to high altitude.

entries.definition_cn: 使内部或某物压力增加
entries.definition_en: to increase the pressure in or of something
entries.example_cn: 我们需要在打开阀门之前给储罐加压。
entries.example_en: We need to pressurise the tank before we can open the valve.

entries.definition_en: to maintain a specified pressure in something
entries.example_cn: 该系统旨在持续给管道加压，以维持恒定压力。
entries.example_en: The system is designed to pressurise the pipes continuously to maintain a constant pressure.

entries.definition_en: to increase the pressure on a gas or liquid
entries.example_cn: 工程师在测试前需要给储罐增压。
entries.example_en: The engineers need to pressurize the tank before testing.

entries.definition_en: to increase the pressure within or of something
entries.example_cn: 他们必须增加管道内的压力以加快水流速度。
entries.example_en: They had to pressurize the pipes to move the water faster.

entries.definition_en: to keep a certain pressure inside something
entries.example_cn: 该系统设计用于在高空维持机舱内的压力。
entries.example_en: The system is designed to pressurize the cabin at high altitudes.

entries.definition_en: manual dexterity in the execution of tricks
entries.example_cn: 魔术师用硬币消失戏法让观众惊叹不已。
entries.example_en: The magician's prestidigitation amazed the audience with his disappearing coin.

entries.definition_cn: 聪明才智或欺骗性技巧的展示
entries.definition_en: a display of cleverness or deceptive skill
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家的巧言掩饰让这个有缺陷的计划显得颇具说服力。
entries.example_en: The politician's prestidigitation made the flawed plan seem convincing.

entries.definition_en: high respect and admiration gained through success or influence
entries.example_cn: 这所大学因其研究而获得了国际声望。
entries.example_en: The university has gained international prestige for its research.

entries.definition_en: having a high reputation and being respected
entries.example_cn: 从那所享有盛誉的大学毕业是一项巨大的荣誉。
entries.example_en: Graduating from that prestigious university is a great honor.

entries.definition_en: influential due to high status
entries.example_cn: 该有威望的组织就此事发表了声明。
entries.example_en: The prestigious organization issued a statement on the issue.

entries.definition_en: (of tempo) as fast as possible
entries.example_cn: 指挥示意乐团以极快的速度演奏最后的乐章，即 presto presto presto 或 prestissimo。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled the orchestra to play the final movement presto presto presto, or prestissimo.

entries.definition_en: extremely fast; as fast as possible
entries.example_cn: 小提琴手以极快的速度演奏了独奏段落。
entries.example_en: The violinist played the solo passage prestissimo.

entries.definition_en: suddenly, as if by magic
entries.example_cn: 魔术师挥动魔杖，兔子突然像施了魔法一样消失了。
entries.example_en: With a wave of his wand, the magician made the rabbit disappear presto.

entries.definition_en: at a very fast tempo in music
entries.example_cn: 交响乐的最后一乐章标记为极快的速度。
entries.example_en: The final movement of the symphony is marked presto.

entries.definition_en: (of music tempo) very fast
entries.example_cn: 指挥示意极快，乐团随即以极快的速度演奏起来。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled presto, and the orchestra played at a rapid pace.

entries.definition_en: capable of being inferred on slight grounds
entries.example_cn: 会议可能会延期，这是可以推测的。
entries.example_en: It is presumable that the meeting will be postponed.

entries.definition_en: according to what is likely or reasonable to assume
entries.example_cn: 据推测，会议将推迟到下周。
entries.example_en: Presumably, the meeting will be postponed until next week.

entries.definition_en: to believe something is true without having proof
entries.example_cn: 我推测你中午前会到达。
entries.example_en: I presume you will arrive by noon.

entries.definition_en: to act without permission or in a way that is too confident
entries.example_cn: 未经敲门，不要擅自进入房间。
entries.example_en: Do not presume to enter the room without knocking.

entries.definition_en: to act with too much confidence or take liberties
entries.example_cn: 他放肆地对经理发号施令。
entries.example_en: He presumed to give orders to the manager.

entries.definition_en: to provide enough evidence to suggest something is true
entries.example_cn: 他的行为在陪审团眼中构成了有罪的证据。
entries.example_en: His behavior presumes guilt in the eyes of the jury.

entries.definition_cn: 未经证明便被接受为真的假定
entries.definition_en: an assumption that is accepted as true without proof
entries.example_cn: 大家都会同意的假定从未得到检验。
entries.example_en: The presumption that everyone would agree was never tested.

entries.definition_en: in law, a conclusion that a fact is true based on other proven facts
entries.example_cn: 法院根据无罪推定原则做出了裁决，直到被证明有罪。
entries.example_en: The court ruled based on the presumption of innocence until proven guilty.

entries.definition_en: bold or arrogant behavior that you are not entitled to
entries.example_cn: 他未经许可擅自进入私人房间，这种放肆的行为很粗鲁。
entries.example_en: His presumption in entering the private room without an invitation was rude.

entries.definition_en: an act of assuming something without permission or right
entries.example_cn: 我为冒昧向你借钱而道歉。
entries.example_en: I apologize for my presumption in asking you to lend me money.

entries.definition_en: based on presumption or conjecture; presumed or likely
entries.example_cn: 在统计完所有选票之前，就宣布了可推定的获胜者。
entries.example_en: The presumptive winner was announced before the final votes were counted.

entries.definition_en: affording reasonable grounds for belief or acceptance
entries.example_cn: 基于新证据，有理由相信他是无辜的。
entries.example_en: There is a presumptive case for his innocence based on the new evidence.

entries.definition_en: based on a reasonable assumption rather than proof
entries.example_cn: 包裹被推定送到了错误的地址。
entries.example_en: The package was presumptively delivered to the wrong address.

entries.definition_en: showing too much confidence or boldness; behaving as if one has more right than one actually has.
entries.example_cn: 你未经邀请就进入房间，这太冒失了。
entries.example_en: It was presumptuous of you to enter the room without being invited.

entries.definition_en: in a way that assumes too much or without proper authority
entries.example_cn: 他放肆地认为自己比经理更懂行。
entries.example_en: He presumptuously assumed that he knew better than the manager.

entries.definition_en: the quality of behaving in an audacious or arrogant way without having the right to do so
entries.example_cn: 他未经邀请就闯入私人会议，这种放肆行为立刻引起了注意。
entries.example_en: His presumptuousness in entering the private meeting without an invitation was immediately noticed.

entries.definition_en: to assume something is true before considering it
entries.example_cn: 该理论假定宇宙是无限的。
entries.example_en: The theory presupposes that the universe is infinite.

entries.definition_en: to require something to exist beforehand as a necessary condition
entries.example_cn: 成功以辛勤工作和奉献为前提。
entries.example_en: Success presupposes hard work and dedication.

entries.definition_en: an assumption made before having knowledge, often for the purpose of argument
entries.example_cn: 这场辩论依赖于一个危险的预设，即所有陌生人都怀有敌意。
entries.example_en: The argument relied on a dangerous presupposition that all strangers are hostile.

entries.definition_en: relating to the early stage of a disease before symptoms appear
entries.example_cn: 这项新检测可以识别病毒的前症状阶段，从而实现早期治疗。
entries.example_en: The new test can detect the presymptomatic phase of the virus, allowing for early treatment.

entries.definition_en: a child approximately 10 to 12 years old, at the onset of adolescence
entries.example_cn: 这部电影是专门为青春期前儿童设计的。
entries.example_en: The movie was designed specifically for preteens.

entries.definition_cn: 青春期前儿童的（约10至12岁）
entries.definition_en: of, relating to, designed for, or characteristic of children approximately 10 to 12 years old
entries.example_cn: 她给妹妹买了一本适合青春期前儿童的杂志。
entries.example_en: She bought a preteen magazine for her younger sister.

entries.definition_en: a false appearance or claim
entries.example_cn: 他丝毫没有表现出对这个项目感兴趣的样子。
entries.example_en: He showed no pretence of interest in the project.

entries.definition_en: an artful or simulated semblance
entries.example_cn: 她假装在读书，其实是在听收音机。
entries.example_en: She made a pretence of reading while listening to the radio.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving a false appearance
entries.example_cn: 在那间混乱的房间里，人们假装一切井然有序。
entries.example_en: There was a pretence of order in the chaotic room.

entries.definition_en: pretending with intention to deceive
entries.example_cn: 他声称生病只是为了逃避工作，纯属欺骗。
entries.example_en: His claim of being ill was just a pretence to avoid work.

entries.definition_en: make-believe; imaginative pretending
entries.example_cn: 孩子们玩起了假装海盗的游戏。
entries.example_en: The children engaged in a pretence of being pirates.

entries.definition_en: make believe with the intent to deceive
