entries.example_cn: 委员会就这项新政策发表了抗议。
entries.example_en: The committee issued a remonstrance against the new policy.

entries.definition_en: to argue against something in a formal or angry way to show you disagree
entries.example_cn: 学生们就新规则向校长提出抗议。
entries.example_en: The students remonstrated with the principal about the new rules.

entries.definition_en: to state reasons against something and urge others to oppose it
entries.example_cn: 他对该计划提出异议，指出其成本高且效率低。
entries.example_en: He remonstrated against the plan, citing its high cost and low efficiency.

entries.definition_en: to criticize or scold someone severely or angrily
entries.example_cn: 老师因学生再次迟到而严厉斥责了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher remonstrated with the student for being late again.

entries.definition_en: a marine fish with a flattened body and a sucking disk on its head used to attach to larger fish or objects
entries.example_cn: 这条吸盘鱼附着在鲨鱼的背上。
entries.example_en: The remora attached itself to the shark's back.

entries.definition_en: a deep feeling of regret for something you have done wrong
entries.example_cn: 他因对朋友撒谎而感到深深的懊悔。
entries.example_en: He felt deep remorse for lying to his friends.

entries.definition_en: feeling or expressing pain or sorrow for sins or offenses
entries.example_cn: 当他向老板承认错误时，他显得十分悔恨。
entries.example_en: He looked remorseful as he admitted his mistake to his boss.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows deep regret and sadness
entries.example_cn: 他悔恨地为他的错误道歉。
entries.example_en: He remorsefully apologized for his mistake.

entries.definition_en: showing no mercy or pity
entries.example_cn: 那场无情的风暴摧毁了整个村庄。
entries.example_en: The storm was a remorseless force that destroyed the entire village.

entries.definition_en: without pity; in a merciless manner
entries.example_cn: 风暴无情地连续几天袭击海岸线。
entries.example_en: The storm remorselessly battered the coastline for days.

entries.definition_en: a device used to control a machine or apparatus from a distance
entries.example_cn: 我用遥控器关掉了电视。
entries.example_en: I used the remote to turn off the television.

entries.definition_en: located far away spatially
entries.example_cn: 他们住在山区的一个偏远村庄里。
entries.example_en: They live in a remote village in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: inaccessible and sparsely populated
entries.example_cn: 那个偏僻地区道路很少。
entries.example_en: The remote area has very few roads.

entries.definition_en: unlikely to occur
entries.example_cn: 我们赢得比赛的可能性很小。
entries.example_en: The possibility that we will win the match is remote.

entries.definition_en: separate or apart in time
entries.example_cn: 这两件事在时间上相隔甚远。
entries.example_en: The two events were remote from each other in time.

entries.definition_en: far apart in relevance or relationship or kinship
entries.example_cn: 这两个家族是远房亲戚。
entries.example_en: The two families are remote relatives.

entries.definition_en: operated by remote control
entries.example_cn: 这艘遥控潜水艇探索了海底。
entries.example_en: The remote-controlled submarine explored the ocean floor.

entries.definition_en: to a very small degree; hardly, usually in negative statements
entries.example_cn: 他对政治毫无兴趣。
entries.example_en: He is not remotely interested in politics.

entries.definition_en: in a remote manner
entries.example_cn: 这颗卫星由地面远程控制。
entries.example_en: The satellite was controlled remotely from the ground.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being far away or distant
entries.example_cn: 该岛屿的偏远使得乘船到达变得困难。
entries.example_en: The remoteness of the island makes it difficult to reach by boat.

entries.definition_en: a tendency to be distant and unsympathetic in manner
entries.example_cn: 他在会议期间的冷漠使得其他人难以与他建立联系。
entries.example_en: His remoteness during the meeting made it hard for others to connect with him.

entries.definition_en: to mould or shape again
entries.example_cn: 工厂决定重新铸造有缺陷的零件以符合安全标准。
entries.example_en: The factory decided to remould the defective parts to meet safety standards.

entries.definition_en: to give new treads to a tire
entries.example_cn: 在长途旅行之前，我们需要翻新这些旧轮胎。
entries.example_en: We need to remould these old tires before the long journey.

entries.definition_cn: 再次骑上（马等动物）或登上交通工具
entries.definition_en: to get back on a horse or other animal or vehicle
entries.example_cn: 敌人逼近时，他不得不迅速再次骑上马。
entries.example_en: He had to remount quickly as the enemy approached.

entries.definition_cn: 将某物重新安装或装回原位，尤指拆下后重新安装
entries.definition_en: to fix or mount something back into position, especially after removal
entries.example_cn: 零件清洗后，技术员将重新组装引擎。
entries.example_en: The technician will remount the engine once the parts are cleaned.

entries.definition_en: to provide with fresh horses
entries.example_cn: 长途行军后，军队为骑兵部队提供了备用战马。
entries.example_en: The army remounted the cavalry after the long march.

entries.definition_cn: 备用战马（尤指为替换阵亡或受伤的战马而提供的）
entries.definition_en: a fresh horse, especially one provided to replace one killed or injured in battle
entries.example_cn: 士兵的马受伤后，他得到了一匹备用战马。
entries.example_en: The soldier received a remount after his horse was wounded.

entries.definition_en: the state of being able to be dismissed from office
entries.example_cn: 总统的可免职性是宪法辩论中的一个关键点。
entries.example_en: The president's removability was a key point of debate in the constitution.

entries.definition_en: able to be taken away or removed
entries.example_cn: 笔记本电脑的盖子是可拆卸的。
entries.example_en: The cover of the laptop is removable.

entries.definition_en: able to be completely erased or destroyed
entries.example_cn: 这种污渍用普通肥皂无法完全消除。
entries.example_en: The stain is not removable by ordinary soap.

entries.definition_en: the action of taking something away
entries.example_cn: 搬走旧家具很困难。
entries.example_en: The removal of the old furniture was difficult.

entries.definition_en: the act of dismissing someone from their job or office
entries.example_cn: 他被委员会免职一事颇具争议。
entries.example_en: His removal from the committee was controversial.

entries.definition_en: the relocation of a business
entries.example_cn: 这家公司搬到一栋更大的大楼花了六个月。
entries.example_en: The removal of the company to a larger building took six months.

entries.definition_en: to take something away by lifting, pushing, or taking off
entries.example_cn: 进入前请脱鞋。
entries.example_en: Please remove your shoes before entering.

entries.definition_en: to take someone away from a position or office
entries.example_cn: 委员会决定罢免经理。
entries.example_en: The committee decided to remove the manager.

entries.definition_en: to dispose of something
entries.example_cn: 他们处理掉了旧家具。
entries.example_en: They removed the old furniture.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to leave
entries.example_cn: 噪音让孩子们离开了房间。
entries.example_en: The noise removed the children from the room.

entries.definition_en: to shift the position or location of something
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把会议转移到另一个房间。
entries.example_en: We need to remove the meeting to another room.

entries.definition_en: the degree of figurative distance or separation
entries.example_cn: 他们的观点相距甚远。
entries.example_en: There is a great remove between their opinions.

entries.definition_en: to stay away or leave
entries.example_cn: 他立即离开了现场。
entries.example_en: He removed himself from the scene immediately.

entries.definition_en: to kill intentionally and with premeditation
entries.example_cn: 嫌疑人被指控谋杀了一名对手。
entries.example_en: The suspect was accused of removing a rival.

entries.definition_en: separate or apart in time
entries.example_cn: 这两件事在时间和空间上是分离的。
entries.example_en: The two events were removed in time and space.

entries.definition_en: separated from someone by a certain number of generations in a family
entries.example_cn: 我的表亲与我隔了三代。
entries.example_en: My cousin is three degrees removed from me.

entries.definition_en: a liquid or substance used to dissolve and take away something from a surface
entries.example_cn: 用指甲油去除剂擦掉桌子上的污渍。
entries.example_en: Use a nail polish remover to clean the stain off the table.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to move furniture for a company
entries.example_cn: 搬运工小心翼翼地搬下沉重的沙发。
entries.example_en: The remover carefully lifted the heavy sofa down the stairs.

entries.definition_en: a group of horses kept together for the purpose of selecting fresh mounts for riders each day
entries.example_cn: 牛仔骑马到换马群去挑选一匹适合长途跋涉的鲜马。
entries.example_en: The cowboy rode out to the remuda to pick a fresh horse for the long journey.

entries.definition_en: to pay someone for their work or services
entries.example_cn: 公司决定给员工发放奖金作为报酬。
entries.example_en: The company decided to remunerate its employees with a bonus.

entries.definition_en: the act of paying for goods or services or to recompense for losses
entries.example_cn: 合同规定了提供咨询服务时的付款方法。
entries.example_en: The contract details the method of remuneration for the consulting services provided.

entries.definition_en: payment given to someone for work done
entries.example_cn: 该公司提供有竞争力的薪酬待遇以吸引顶尖人才。
entries.example_en: The company offers a competitive remuneration package to attract top talent.

entries.definition_en: producing a sizeable profit
entries.example_cn: 他们在科技领域投资了一个利润丰厚的项目。
entries.example_en: They invested in a highly remunerative venture in the technology sector.

entries.definition_en: providing financial compensation or reward
entries.example_cn: 这份实习的报酬足以支付她的生活费。
entries.example_en: The internship was remunerative enough to cover her living expenses.

entries.definition_en: relating to the kidneys
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一项肾功能检查以查看肾脏的健康状况。
entries.example_en: The doctor ordered a renal function test to check the health of the kidneys.

entries.definition_en: to give a new name to something or someone
entries.example_cn: 在保存文件之前，我们需要给它改个名。
entries.example_en: We need to rename the file before saving it.

entries.definition_en: to name again or anew
entries.example_cn: 委员会决定用当地英雄的名字重新命名这座大楼。
entries.example_en: The committee decided to rename the building after the local hero.

entries.definition_en: coming back to life with new energy and strength
entries.example_cn: 这座城市正在经历复兴，许多重获生机的企业正在老城区开业。
entries.example_en: The city is experiencing a renaissance, with many renascent businesses opening in the old district.

entries.definition_en: tear or be torn violently
entries.example_cn: 风暴的大风将旧屋顶从房子上撕了下来。
entries.example_en: The storm winds rended the old roof from the house.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone or something to become in a particular state
entries.example_cn: 大雨使道路在数小时内无法通行。
entries.example_en: The heavy rain rendered the road impassable for several hours.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指用计算机图形技术）生成或显示图像
entries.definition_en: produce or display an image, especially using computer graphics
entries.example_cn: 该软件能快速渲染出高质量的图像。
entries.example_en: The software renders high-quality images quickly.

entries.definition_en: to give something useful or necessary to someone
entries.example_cn: 该慈善机构旨在向受自然灾害影响的人提供援助。
entries.example_en: The charity aims to render aid to those affected by the natural disaster.

entries.definition_en: to give an interpretation or performance of something
entries.example_cn: 管弦乐队将演绎这首著名交响曲的美妙版本。
entries.example_en: The orchestra will render a beautiful version of the famous symphony.

entries.definition_en: deliver or announce, especially a judgment or verdict
entries.example_cn: 法官听取证据后作出了裁决。
entries.example_en: The judge rendered a verdict after hearing the evidence.

entries.definition_en: a substance similar to stucco used exclusively on masonry walls
entries.example_cn: 这座老建筑使用传统抹灰材料进行修复，以恢复其原有外观。
entries.example_en: The old building was repaired using traditional render to restore its original appearance.

entries.definition_en: to make over something as a return or payment
entries.example_cn: 交易完成后，他将地契转让给了新主人。
entries.example_en: After the transaction, he rendered the deed to the new owner.

entries.definition_en: to give back something that was taken or owed
entries.example_cn: 被告将偷来的财物归还给了物主。
entries.example_en: The defendant rendered the stolen property to its owner.

entries.definition_en: a performance of a musical composition or dramatic role
entries.example_cn: 乐团精彩地演出了贝多芬的第九交响曲。
entries.example_en: The orchestra gave a stunning rendering of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

entries.definition_en: the act of interpreting something artistically
entries.example_cn: 她对这首诗的诠释充满了深情。
entries.example_en: Her rendering of the poem was deeply emotional.

entries.definition_en: a perspective drawing of an architectural design
entries.example_cn: 建筑师向市议会展示了建筑设计的透视图。
entries.example_en: The architect presented the rendering to the city council.

entries.definition_en: a translation of written text into another language
entries.example_cn: 合同被认证翻译员翻译成了法语。
entries.example_en: The rendering of the contract into French was done by a certified translator.

entries.definition_en: a coat of stucco applied to a wall
entries.example_cn: 修复工作包括对外墙重新涂抹灰泥。
entries.example_en: The restoration included a new rendering on the exterior walls.

entries.definition_en: an explanation of something not immediately obvious
entries.example_cn: 老师清晰地解释了那个复杂的理论。
entries.example_en: The teacher provided a clear rendering of the complex theory.

entries.definition_en: the act of giving or paying something in fulfillment of an obligation
entries.example_cn: 承包商提供服务，履行了合同义务。
entries.example_en: The contractor's rendering of services fulfilled its contractual obligation.

entries.definition_en: a meeting planned for a specific time and place
entries.example_cn: 两名间谍约好在咖啡馆见面。
entries.example_en: The two spies made a rendezvous at the café.

entries.definition_en: a place where people meet
entries.example_cn: 这座山口成了旅行者的会合处。
entries.example_en: The mountain pass served as a rendezvous for the travelers.

entries.definition_en: a date
entries.example_cn: 这对情侣约会庆祝他们的纪念日。
entries.example_en: The couple had a rendezvous to celebrate their anniversary.

entries.definition_en: to meet at a planned time and place
entries.example_cn: 两名间谍在午夜于公园会合。
entries.example_en: The two spies rendezvoused in the park at midnight.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: The verb means to meet at an agreed time and place.

entries.definition_en: resembling the violent sound of something being torn apart or lightning splitting a tree
entries.example_cn: 爆炸的撕裂般巨响震动了窗户。
entries.example_en: The rending noise of the explosion shook the windows.

entries.definition_en: a performance of a song, piece of music, or dramatic role
entries.example_cn: 她对这首古典歌曲的演绎感人至深且充满力量。
entries.example_en: Her rendition of the classical song was moving and powerful.

entries.definition_en: the act of interpreting something in an artistic performance
entries.example_cn: 演员对反派角色的独特诠释令观众惊讶。
entries.example_en: The actor's unique rendition of the villain surprised the audience.

entries.definition_cn: 某物的视觉呈现或再现
entries.definition_en: a visual representation or reproduction of something
entries.example_cn: 这幅数字再现作品捕捉到了原画的每一个细节。
entries.example_en: The digital rendition captured every detail of the original painting.

entries.definition_en: the act of handing over a prisoner to the country where a crime occurred
entries.example_cn: 该嫌疑人被引渡到法国受审。
entries.example_en: The suspect was extradited to France for his rendition.

entries.definition_en: a person who rebels against a group and becomes an outlaw
entries.example_cn: 这个叛变者被他的前同事追捕。
entries.example_en: The renegade was hunted down by his former colleagues.

entries.definition_en: a disloyal person who betrays or deserts their cause, religion, or political party
entries.example_cn: 这个叛徒向敌人出卖了他的政党。
entries.example_en: The renegade betrayed his party to the enemy.

entries.definition_cn: 背弃事业或改变立场；变节（过时用语）
entries.definition_en: to desert one's cause or change one's loyalties; to betray (dated)
entries.example_cn: 那名士兵变节后加入了敌方。
entries.example_en: The soldier renegaded and joined the enemy.

entries.definition_en: having deserted a cause or principle
entries.example_cn: 叛变的士兵在战斗中倒戈了。
entries.example_en: The renegade soldiers switched sides during the battle.

entries.definition_en: to fail to fulfill a promise or obligation
entries.example_cn: 他答应帮忙，但到了关键时刻却食言了。
entries.example_en: He promised to help but reneged when the time came.

usage.label: intransitive; renege on
usage.pattern: renege on a promise or commitment

entries.definition_en: the mistake of failing to follow suit when able to do so
entries.example_cn: 他明明有同花色的牌却没有跟牌，因此受到了处罚。
entries.example_en: He was penalized for reneging when he failed to follow suit despite holding a card of that suit.

entries.definition_en: to discuss and agree on new terms for a contract or agreement
entries.example_cn: 两国决定重新谈判贸易协定。
entries.example_en: The two countries decided to renegotiate the trade deal.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: takes a contract or agreement as its object

entries.definition_cn: 修订条款以限制或收回承包商获得的超额利润
entries.definition_en: to change the terms of a contract to limit or recover excessive profits made by a contractor
entries.example_cn: 政府计划修订建筑合同，以减少承包商获得的意外暴利。
entries.example_en: The government plans to renegotiate the construction contract to reduce the contractor's windfall profits.

entries.definition_cn: 使更新或恢复原状；延长（有效期等）
entries.definition_en: to make something new or fresh again, restore it, or extend its period of validity
entries.example_cn: 他们决定续签合同一年。
entries.example_en: They decided to renew their contract for another year.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to appear in a new form or version.
entries.example_cn: 公司计划更新其标志的设计。
entries.example_en: The company plans to renew the design of their logo.

entries.definition_en: able to be naturally replenished or sustainably replaced
entries.example_cn: 太阳能是一种可再生能源。
entries.example_en: Solar energy is a renewable resource.

entries.definition_en: capable of being renewed or extended
entries.example_cn: 图书馆为图书提供可续借的借阅期。
entries.example_en: The library offers a renewable loan period for books.

entries.definition_cn: 可再生资源或可再生能源
entries.definition_en: a renewable resource or source of energy
entries.example_cn: 风能是一种可再生能源，有助于减少对化石燃料的依赖。
entries.example_en: Wind is a renewable that can help reduce dependence on fossil fuels.

entries.definition_en: the act of renewing something
entries.example_cn: 合同的续签已于昨日签署。
entries.example_en: The renewal of the contract was signed yesterday.

entries.definition_en: filling again by supplying what has been used up
entries.example_cn: 由于干旱，供水补充工作被推迟了。
entries.example_en: The renewal of the water supply was delayed due to the drought.

entries.definition_en: the conversion of wasteland into land suitable for habitation or cultivation
entries.example_cn: 荒地的改良给村庄带来了新的生机。
entries.example_en: The renewal of the wasteland brought new life to the village.

entries.definition_cn: 恢复到新状态的；焕然一新的
entries.definition_en: restored to a new condition
entries.example_cn: 游乐场重建后，这座公园焕然一新。
entries.example_en: After its playground was rebuilt, the park looked renewed.

entries.definition_en: tending to impart new life and vigor to
entries.example_cn: 那赋予新生命和活力的春风吹醒了花朵。
entries.example_en: The renewing spring breeze woke the flowers.

entries.definition_en: shaped like a kidney
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子是肾形的，像豆子或肾脏一样。
entries.example_en: The leaves of the plant are reniform, resembling a bean or kidney.

entries.definition_en: an enzyme produced by the kidneys that helps control blood pressure
entries.example_cn: 高水平的肾素会导致血压升高。
entries.example_en: High levels of renin can lead to increased blood pressure.

entries.definition_en: a substance used to curdle milk in cheese making
entries.example_cn: 传统奶酪制作通常依赖凝乳酶使牛奶凝固。
entries.example_en: Traditional cheese making often relies on rennet to solidify the milk.

entries.definition_en: to give up power, duties, or obligations formally
entries.example_cn: 国王放弃了对王位的宣称。
entries.example_en: The king renounced his claim to the throne.

usage.pattern: renounce + title, claim, right, or obligation

entries.definition_en: to turn away from something or give it up
entries.example_cn: 他摒弃了旧习，开始了新生活。
entries.example_en: He renounced his old habits and started a new life.

entries.definition_en: to leave a job or position voluntarily
entries.example_cn: 她决定主动辞去经理职务。
entries.example_en: She decided to renounce her post as manager.

entries.definition_en: to cast off or discard
entries.example_cn: 他们宣布放弃暴力并投降。
entries.example_en: They renounced violence and surrendered.

entries.definition_en: a formal declaration that something is given up or disowned
entries.example_cn: 他公开声明放弃以前的政治信仰。
entries.example_en: He made a public renouncement of his previous political beliefs.

entries.definition_en: to restore something to a previous or better condition
entries.example_cn: 我们计划明年夏天翻新那座老房子。
entries.example_en: We plan to renovate the old house next summer.

entries.definition_en: to give new life or energy to something
entries.example_cn: 新经理希望赋予公司新的形象活力。
entries.example_en: The new manager hopes to renovate the company's image.

entries.definition_en: to make something brighter and prettier
entries.example_cn: 团队努力翻新了社区中心，使其更明亮美观。
entries.example_en: The team worked hard to renovate the community center.

entries.definition_en: the act of improving something by renewing and restoring it
entries.example_cn: 旧图书馆的翻新工程耗时两年才完工。
entries.example_en: The renovation of the old library took two years to complete.

entries.definition_en: the state of being restored to its former good condition
entries.example_cn: 翻新之后，这所房子焕然一新。
entries.example_en: After the renovation, the house was in a state of perfect renovation.

entries.definition_cn: 翻修或修复人员，尤指建筑物或古董家具修复师
entries.definition_en: a person who renovates, especially buildings or antique furniture
entries.example_cn: 这位修复师仔细修复了那张古老的木桌。
entries.example_en: The renovator carefully restored the old wooden table.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being widely honored and acclaimed
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家因其独特的风格而享誉国际。
entries.example_en: The artist achieved international renown for his unique style.

entries.definition_en: widely known and esteemed
entries.example_cn: 他是遗传学领域一位著名的科学家。
entries.example_en: He is a renowned scientist in the field of genetics.

entries.definition_en: money paid for using a property or service
entries.example_cn: 这套公寓的月租金是五百美元。
entries.example_en: The monthly rent for the apartment is five hundred dollars.

entries.definition_en: profit from farming land
entries.example_cn: 农场的地租覆盖了所有开支。
entries.example_en: The rent from the farm covered all the expenses.

entries.definition_en: obtain temporary use of something in exchange for payment
entries.example_cn: 他们为建设项目租用了设备。
entries.example_en: They rented equipment for the construction project.

entries.definition_en: to allow someone to use something for money
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在夏天把房子租出去。
entries.example_en: They decided to rent out their house during the summer.

entries.definition_en: to give someone the right to use something for a period
entries.example_cn: 该公司向许多小企业出租办公空间。
entries.example_en: The company rents office space to many small businesses.

entries.definition_en: to keep something under a lease agreement
entries.example_cn: 我们从当地机构租用汽车。
entries.example_en: We rent our car from a local agency.

entries.definition_en: a tear or split in something
entries.example_cn: 布料上有个裂口，让光线透了进来。
entries.example_en: There was a rent in the fabric that let the light through.

entries.definition_en: a division or split, especially in a relationship
entries.example_cn: 这场争端在他们的友谊中造成了深深的裂痕。
entries.example_en: The dispute created a deep rent in their friendship.

entries.definition_en: a car that you pay to use for a specific period
entries.example_cn: 我们决定租一辆车去乡下旅行。
entries.example_en: We decided to take a rent-a-car for our trip to the countryside.

entries.definition_en: provided without the need to pay rent
entries.example_cn: 该公司为这家初创公司提供了一年的免租办公室。
entries.example_en: The company offered the startup a rent-free office for the first year.

entries.definition_en: in a way that does not require paying rent
entries.example_cn: 他们在市中心免租地居住，以便攒钱。
entries.example_en: They managed to live rent-free in the city center while they saved money.

entries.definition_en: the practice of trying to gain wealth by manipulating the economic system rather than creating value
entries.example_cn: 政府正试图减少能源部门的寻租行为。
entries.example_en: The government is trying to reduce rent-seeking in the energy sector.

entries.definition_en: suitable or able to be rented out
entries.example_cn: 这套公寓完全可出租，并包含所有公用事业费用。
entries.example_en: The apartment is fully rentable and includes all utilities.

entries.definition_en: property that is leased or rented out
entries.example_cn: 该出租物业包括市中心的一套带家具的公寓。
entries.example_en: The rental includes a furnished apartment in the city center.

entries.definition_en: the payment made to rent something
entries.example_cn: 这辆车的月租金相当高。
entries.example_en: The monthly rental for the car is quite high.

entries.definition_en: available to rent or lease
entries.example_cn: 我们正在寻找一辆供我们旅行时使用的租赁汽车。
entries.example_en: We are looking for a rental car for our trip.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to rent
entries.example_cn: 入住前必须签署租金协议。
entries.example_en: The rental agreement must be signed before moving in.

entries.definition_en: someone who pays rent to use property owned by another
entries.example_cn: 作为一名承租人，他在搬入前必须支付押金。
entries.example_en: As a renter, he had to pay a security deposit before moving in.

entries.definition_en: an owner of property who receives payment for its use
entries.example_cn: 出租人每月向租户收取费用。
entries.example_en: The renter collected the monthly fees from the tenants.

entries.definition_en: a person who earns income from investments such as property rents or bonds
entries.example_cn: 该国的经济严重依赖食利者阶层。
entries.example_en: The country's economy relies heavily on the rentier class.

entries.definition_en: the act of paying money to use something like a house or car
entries.example_cn: 市中心公寓的租金非常高。
entries.example_en: The cost of renting an apartment in the city center is very high.

entries.definition_cn: 正式拒绝或放弃某事；宣告无效
entries.definition_en: the act of rejecting or disowning something as invalid
entries.example_cn: 法院裁定该合同解除在法律上是有效的。
entries.example_en: The court ruled that the renunciation of the contract was legally binding.

entries.definition_en: the act of sacrificing or giving up a possession, right, or privilege
entries.example_cn: 国王放弃王位，让人民选出了新领导人。
entries.example_en: The king's renunciation of his throne allowed the people to choose a new leader.

entries.definition_en: a formal declaration that something is surrendered or disowned
entries.example_cn: 她签署了一份放弃继承权的声明。
entries.example_en: She signed a renunciation of her claim to the inheritance.

entries.definition_cn: 正式背弃或放弃宗教信仰的行为
entries.definition_en: the formal rejection or abandonment of one's religious faith
entries.example_cn: 他因强烈的政治信念而背弃了自己的宗教信仰。
entries.example_en: His renunciation of his faith was driven by intense political convictions.

entries.definition_en: to open something again after it has been closed
entries.example_cn: 博物馆计划下个月重新开门。
entries.example_en: The museum plans to reopen its doors next month.

entries.definition_en: to place in a new order; to rearrange
entries.example_cn: 这些书原按书名排序，但我打算按作者姓氏重新排列。
entries.example_en: The books were sorted by title, but I'm going to reorder them by author's surname.

entries.definition_en: to order a product or supply again
entries.example_cn: 我们需要在软件许可证到期前再次订购。
entries.example_en: We need to reorder the software license before it expires.

entries.definition_en: a repeated order for the same merchandise
entries.example_cn: 公司为办公用品下了重复订单。
entries.example_en: The company placed a reorder for the office supplies.

entries.definition_en: a rearrangement in a different order
entries.example_cn: 文件的重新排序使得查找文档变得更加容易。
entries.example_en: The reordering of the files made it easier to find the documents.

entries.definition_en: the imposition of a new organization; organizing differently (often involving extensive and drastic changes)
entries.example_cn: 公司宣布对其部门进行重大重组。
entries.example_en: The company announced a major reorganisation of its departments.

entries.definition_en: to arrange something in a new order or system
entries.example_cn: 他们需要重新整理文件以便更容易查找。
entries.example_en: They need to reorganise the files to make them easier to find.

entries.definition_en: to organize something again, especially after a problem or failure
entries.example_cn: 合并后，公司不得不重组其整个结构。
entries.example_en: After the merger, the company had to reorganise its entire structure.

entries.definition_en: the act of arranging something in a new way, often with major changes
entries.example_cn: 公司宣布对其管理结构进行重组。
entries.example_en: The company announced a reorganization of its management structure.

entries.definition_en: a large-scale change in the structure of a business or government
entries.example_cn: 政府计划对税务部门进行大规模改组。
entries.example_en: The government is planning a reorganization of the tax department.

entries.definition_en: organize anew
entries.example_cn: 公司决定重新组织其部门。
entries.example_en: The company decided to reorganize its departments.

entries.definition_en: undergo a reorganization
entries.example_cn: 合并后，公司进行了重组。
entries.example_en: After the merger, the company reorganized.

entries.definition_en: having been organized again
entries.example_cn: 该公司已重组其管理结构。
entries.example_en: The company has reorganized its management structure.

entries.definition_cn: 在迷失方向后重新确定方向
entries.definition_en: orient once again, after a disorientation
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，徒步旅行者必须重新定位自己以找到小径。
entries.example_en: After the storm, the hikers had to reorient themselves to find the trail.

entries.definition_cn: 将某物重新调整到新的或不同的位置
entries.definition_en: set or arrange in a new or different determinate position
entries.example_cn: 博物馆重新布置了展览以突出现代艺术。
entries.example_en: The museum reoriented the exhibit to highlight modern art.

entries.definition_en: cause something to face a new direction
entries.example_cn: 工程师调整了卫星的方向使其面向太阳。
entries.example_en: The engineer reoriented the satellite to face the sun.

entries.definition_cn: 重新确定方向；使朝向不同方向；重新调整
entries.definition_en: to orientate anew or cause to face a different direction
entries.example_cn: 我们需要调整策略以应对新的挑战。
entries.example_en: We need to reorientate our strategy to meet the new challenges.

entries.definition_en: a change in one's attitudes, beliefs, or direction in life
entries.example_cn: 这门课程帮助学生进行了职业方向的重新定位。
entries.example_en: The course helped students with their career reorientation.

entries.definition_en: the act of changing the direction in which something is facing or pointing
entries.example_cn: 望远镜的转向使天文学家能够看到月球的另一面。
entries.example_en: The reorientation of the telescope allowed the astronomers to see the other side of the moon.

entries.definition_cn: 呼肠孤病毒科中感染动物和某些植物的RNA病毒
entries.definition_en: an RNA virus of the family Reoviridae that infects animals and some plants
entries.example_cn: 婴儿出现严重腹泻后，医生检测其是否感染呼肠孤病毒。
entries.example_en: Doctors tested the infant for reovirus after the child developed severe diarrhea.

entries.definition_en: an informal short form of 'representative'
entries.example_cn: 公司派了一名代表参加这次会议。
entries.example_en: The company sent a rep to the conference.

entries.definition_cn: 一种具有明显横向圆状罗纹的织物
entries.definition_en: a type of fabric with prominent rounded ribs running across the width
entries.example_cn: 这件毛衣是用柔软的罗纹织物制成的。
entries.example_en: The sweater was made of a soft rep fabric.

entries.definition_en: to apply a new layer of paint over an existing one
entries.example_cn: 我们需要在冬天来临之前给栅栏再涂一层漆。
entries.example_en: We need to repaint the fence before winter arrives.

entries.definition_en: to paint a subject again
entries.example_cn: 风暴过后，他们决定重绘壁画。
entries.example_en: They decided to repaint the mural after the storm.

entries.definition_en: to restore something by replacing parts or putting broken pieces together
entries.example_cn: 我们需要在暴风雨来临前修补屋顶。
entries.example_en: We need to repair the roof before the storm arrives.

entries.definition_en: to set something straight or right
entries.example_cn: 编辑纠正了手稿中错误的论证。
entries.example_en: The editor repaired the faulty argument in the manuscript.

entries.definition_en: to make amends for or pay compensation for something
entries.example_cn: 他承诺赔偿他造成的损失。
entries.example_en: He promised to repair the damage he caused.

entries.definition_en: to give new life or energy to something
entries.example_cn: 新经理使团队的士气重振起来。
entries.example_en: The new manager repaired the morale of the team.

entries.definition_en: the action of fixing something so it works again
entries.example_cn: 修理的费用比预期的要高得多。
entries.example_en: The cost of the repair was much higher than expected.

entries.definition_en: a formal way of referring to the condition of something
entries.example_cn: 这辆车状况良好。
entries.example_en: The car is in good repair.

entries.definition_en: a place that is visited frequently
entries.example_cn: 海滩是我们周末最喜欢的常去之地。
entries.example_en: The beach is our favorite repair on weekends.

entries.definition_en: to move, travel, or proceed toward a specific place
entries.example_cn: 他们前往花园享受新鲜空气。
entries.example_en: They repaired to the garden to enjoy the fresh air.

entries.definition_en: a skilled worker who mends or repairs things
entries.example_cn: 我们请了一位专业的维修工来修理引擎。
entries.example_en: We hired a professional repairer to fix the engine.

entries.definition_en: a man whose job is to fix broken things
entries.example_cn: 维修工在十分钟内修好了坏掉的烤面包机。
entries.example_en: The repairman fixed the broken toaster in ten minutes.

entries.definition_en: able to be fixed or corrected
entries.example_cn: 发动机的损坏只需几个备用零件即可修复。
entries.example_en: The damage to the engine was reparable with a few spare parts.

entries.definition_en: compensation given or received for an insult or injury
entries.example_cn: 该公司就故障产品造成的损害提供了全额赔偿。
entries.example_en: The company offered a full reparation for the damage caused by the faulty product.

entries.definition_en: compensation exacted from a defeated nation by the victors
entries.example_cn: 条约要求战败国向战胜国支付巨额赔款。
entries.example_en: The treaty required the defeated nation to pay massive reparations to the victors.

entries.definition_en: something done or paid to expiate a wrong
entries.example_cn: 他通过把被盗的钱归还给合法所有者来赎罪。
entries.example_en: He made a reparation by returning the stolen money to its rightful owner.

entries.definition_en: the act of putting something in working order again
entries.example_cn: 工程师们夜以继日地工作，以确保在风暴前修复桥梁。
entries.example_en: The engineers worked tirelessly to ensure the reparation of the bridge before the storm.

entries.definition_en: quick and witty replies in conversation
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员机智的应答逗乐了观众。
entries.example_en: The comedian's sharp repartee delighted the audience.

entries.definition_en: send or bring a person back to their own country
entries.example_cn: 政府拒绝将寻求庇护者遣返至他们面临迫害的国家。
entries.example_en: The government refused to repatriate the asylum seekers to a country where they faced persecution.

entries.definition_en: admit back into the country
entries.example_cn: 大使馆努力将被驱逐的外交官重新接纳回国。
entries.example_en: The embassy worked to repatriate the diplomat who had been expelled.

entries.definition_en: a person who has returned to the country of origin or whose citizenship has been restored
entries.example_cn: 该组织为刚归国的难民提供支持服务。
entries.example_en: The organization provides support services for newly repatriated refugees.

entries.definition_en: the act of returning to one's country of origin
entries.example_cn: 政府为难民归国组织了一个特别项目。
entries.example_en: The government organized a special program for the repatriation of refugees.

entries.definition_cn: 将艺术品或博物馆展品归还原属国的过程
entries.definition_en: the process of returning artworks or museum exhibits to their country of origin
entries.example_cn: 这些雕塑归还希腊的过程历时数年。
entries.example_en: The repatriation of the sculptures to Greece took several years.

entries.definition_cn: 将外币兑换成本国货币的过程
entries.definition_en: the process of converting a foreign currency into the currency of one's own country
entries.example_cn: 这家银行会收取外币兑换成本国货币的手续费。
entries.example_en: The bank charges a fee for the repatriation of foreign currency.

entries.definition_en: to pay back money that you have borrowed
entries.example_cn: 我一拿到工资就会偿还这笔贷款。
entries.example_en: I will repay the loan as soon as I get my salary.

entries.definition_en: to return something that was given to you or to give something in return
entries.example_cn: 她决定通过帮他搬家来回报这份人情。
entries.example_en: She decided to repay the favor by helping him move house.

entries.definition_en: to give something as a reward or punishment for someone's behavior
entries.example_cn: 公司将用晋升来酬谢他的忠诚。
entries.example_en: The company will repay his loyalty with a promotion.

entries.definition_en: to return an insult or injury in kind; retaliate
entries.example_cn: 他用尖刻的反驳回敬了那次侮辱。
entries.example_en: He repaid the insult with a sharp retort.

entries.definition_en: required to be paid back
entries.example_cn: 这笔贷款需在五年内偿还。
entries.example_en: The loan is repayable within five years.

entries.definition_en: the act of returning money that was borrowed
entries.example_cn: 这笔贷款的还款已全额付清。
entries.example_en: The repayment of the loan was made in full.

entries.definition_en: payment made to satisfy a debt or obligation
entries.example_cn: 这家公司正为偿还债务而苦苦挣扎。
entries.example_en: The company is struggling with the repayment of its debts.

entries.definition_en: to officially cancel a law or agreement
entries.example_cn: 议会投票决定废除过时的法规。
entries.example_en: Parliament voted to repeal the outdated regulations.

entries.definition_en: the act of officially cancelling a law or agreement
entries.example_cn: 政府宣布废除有争议的税法。
entries.example_en: The government announced the repeal of the controversial tax law.

entries.definition_en: to say, state, or perform something again
entries.example_cn: 请重复一下问题，让我听得更清楚。
entries.example_en: Please repeat the question so I can hear it better.

entries.definition_en: to do or perform something again
entries.example_cn: 我们需要重复实验以确认结果。
entries.example_en: We need to repeat the experiment to confirm the results.

entries.definition_en: to happen or occur again
entries.example_cn: 风暴很可能下周再次发生。
entries.example_en: The storm is likely to repeat next week.

entries.definition_en: to say something again or imitate it
entries.example_cn: 孩子试图重复她听到的那些词。
entries.example_en: The child tried to repeat the words she heard.

entries.definition_en: to do something over again
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生重做练习。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the student to repeat the exercise.

entries.definition_en: an event that happens again
entries.example_cn: 第二场暴风雨是第一场的重演。
entries.example_en: The second storm was a repeat of the first.

entries.definition_cn: 再次演奏乐曲中的早期主题
entries.definition_en: to play an earlier theme of a musical composition again
entries.example_cn: 交响乐在结尾处重复了主要主题。
entries.example_en: The symphony repeats the main theme at the end.

entries.definition_en: able to be repeated
entries.example_cn: 该实验产生的结果无法重复。
entries.example_en: The experiment produced results that were not repeatable.

entries.definition_en: recurring again and again
entries.example_cn: 重复的噪音让我无法入睡。
entries.example_en: The repeated noise kept me awake.

entries.definition_en: many times over a period of time
entries.example_cn: 闹钟整晚反复响起。
entries.example_en: The alarm clock rang repeatedly throughout the night.

entries.definition_en: an electronic device that amplifies a signal before transmitting it again
entries.example_cn: 中继器将无线网络信号扩展到了地下室。
entries.example_en: The repeater extended the range of the wireless network to the basement.

entries.definition_en: a firearm that can fire several rounds without reloading
entries.example_cn: 这把连发枪让猎人能迅速连续击落多只鸟。
entries.example_en: The repeater allowed the hunter to take down multiple birds in quick succession.

entries.definition_en: a person who repeats something
entries.example_cn: 这位复读者跟不上快节奏的讲座。
entries.example_en: The repeater struggled to keep up with the fast-paced lecture.

entries.definition_en: someone who is repeatedly arrested for criminal behavior
entries.example_cn: 警方正试图查明最近入室盗窃案的累犯。
entries.example_en: The police are trying to identify the repeater responsible for the recent burglaries.

entries.definition_en: the action of doing or performing something again
entries.example_cn: 重复实验证实了结果。
entries.example_en: The repeating of the experiment confirmed the results.

entries.definition_en: a race where runners-up from earlier heats compete for a spot in the final
entries.example_cn: 这位赛艇运动员在预赛中获得第二名后进入了复活赛。
entries.example_en: The rower qualified for the repechage after finishing second in his heat.

entries.definition_en: cause to move back by force or influence
entries.example_cn: 磁场使金属物体后退。
entries.example_en: The magnetic field repels the metal object.

entries.definition_en: be repellent to; cause aversion in
entries.example_cn: 垃圾的气味让狗感到厌恶。
entries.example_en: The smell of the garbage repels the dogs.

entries.definition_en: force or drive back
entries.example_cn: 军队成功击退了敌人的进攻。
entries.example_en: The army managed to repel the enemy attack.

entries.definition_en: reject outright and bluntly
entries.example_cn: 他毫不犹豫地断然拒绝了那个提议。
entries.example_en: He repelled the offer without hesitation.

entries.definition_en: to save or stop a shot
entries.example_cn: 守门员扑出了前锋的射门。
entries.example_en: The goalkeeper repelled the striker's shot.

entries.definition_en: serving or tending to repel
entries.example_cn: 大蒜的排斥性气味驱赶了昆虫。
entries.example_en: The repellant smell of the garlic kept the insects away.

entries.definition_en: highly offensive; arousing aversion or disgust
entries.example_cn: 看到腐烂的食物真是令人厌恶。
entries.example_en: The sight of the rotting food was truly repellant.

entries.definition_en: a chemical substance that repels animals
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者通常携带驱避剂来保护自己免受蚊子叮咬。
entries.example_en: Hikers often carry a repellant to protect themselves from mosquitoes.

entries.definition_en: a chemical treatment applied to fabrics to make them repel water
entries.example_cn: 户外家具经过特殊防水剂处理以保持干燥。
entries.example_en: The outdoor furniture was treated with a special repellant to keep it dry.

entries.definition_en: the power to repel
entries.example_cn: 两块磁铁之间的排斥力使它们无法接触。
entries.example_en: The repulsive force between the two magnets kept them from touching.

entries.definition_en: serving or tending to repel
entries.example_cn: 这种面料的表面非常排斥水。
entries.example_en: The surface of the fabric is highly repellent to water.

entries.definition_en: highly offensive; arousing aversion or disgust
entries.example_cn: 垃圾的气味真是令人厌恶。
entries.example_en: The smell of the garbage was truly repellent.

entries.definition_en: incapable of absorbing or mixing with
entries.example_cn: 这种油完全不吸收水，而是浮在水面上。
entries.example_en: The oil is completely repellent to water and floats on top.

entries.definition_en: a chemical substance that repels animals
entries.example_cn: 进入森林前你应该涂抹驱虫剂。
entries.example_en: You should apply insect repellent before going into the forest.

entries.definition_en: a compound used to treat fabrics so they repel water
entries.example_cn: 这件户外夹克经过特殊防水剂处理。
entries.example_en: The outdoor jacket is treated with a special water-repellent.

entries.definition_en: the power to repel
entries.example_cn: 磁力排斥力使金属物体保持距离。
entries.example_en: The magnetic repellent kept the metal objects at a distance.

entries.definition_en: causing a strong feeling of dislike or disgust
entries.example_cn: 腐烂鱼的气味让房间里每个人都感到厌恶。
entries.example_en: The smell of the rotting fish was repelling to everyone in the room.

entries.definition_en: to feel remorse or be sorry for something
entries.example_cn: 她对自己对朋友说过的刻薄话感到后悔。
entries.example_en: She repented of her harsh words to her friend.

entries.definition_en: to turn away from sin or do penitence
entries.example_cn: 他为自己的罪行悔改并请求宽恕。
entries.example_en: He repented of his sins and asked for forgiveness.

entries.definition_en: deep regret and sorrow for one's past wrong actions
entries.example_cn: 他的悔悟体现在他愿意弥补过错。
entries.example_en: His repentance was shown by his willingness to make amends.

entries.definition_cn: 对恶行感到或表示悔恨的
entries.definition_en: feeling or expressing remorse for misdeeds
entries.example_cn: 那个悔过自新的窃贼归还了偷来的钱。
entries.example_en: The repentant thief returned the stolen money.

entries.definition_en: an indirect or distant result of an action
entries.example_cn: 这场战争对全球经济产生了严重的间接影响。
entries.example_en: The war had serious repercussions for the global economy.

entries.definition_cn: 冲击或声音造成的反弹或回响
entries.definition_en: a rebound or reverberation caused by an impact or sound
entries.example_cn: 炮声的回响震动了窗户。
entries.example_en: The repercussion of the cannon shot shook the windows.

entries.definition_en: a collection of works that an artist or company can perform
entries.example_cn: 歌剧院更新了新演出季的剧目。
entries.example_en: The opera company updated its repertoire for the new season.

entries.definition_en: the entire range of skills or aptitudes or devices used in a particular field or occupation
entries.example_cn: 这位魔术师的技能范围包括许多经典戏法。
entries.example_en: The magician's repertoire includes many classic tricks.

entries.definition_en: the collection of plays, songs, or dances that a theater group performs regularly
entries.example_cn: 这家剧院新增了一套经典剧目。
entries.example_en: The theater company has a new repertory of classic plays.

entries.definition_en: the complete range of skills, abilities, or methods used in a specific job or field
entries.example_cn: 这位演员的全部技能包括唱歌、跳舞和表演。
entries.example_en: The actor's repertory includes singing, dancing, and acting.

entries.definition_en: a place where a large collection of items is stored
entries.example_cn: 这座图书馆是珍稀历史文献的贮藏库。
entries.example_en: The library serves as a repertory for rare historical documents.

entries.definition_en: a theater company that performs plays from a fixed repertoire
entries.example_cn: 他们加入了一个轮演固定剧目的剧团以积累经验。
entries.example_en: They joined a repertory theater to gain experience.

entries.definition_en: the act of doing or performing something again
entries.example_cn: 练习和重复是学习新语言的关键。
entries.example_en: Practice and repetition are key to learning a new language.

entries.definition_en: an event that happens again and again
entries.example_cn: 重复犯同样的错误令人沮丧。
entries.example_en: The repetition of the same mistake was frustrating.

entries.definition_en: the use of the same word or phrase again for emphasis
entries.example_cn: 演讲中充满了反复，以使观点清晰。
entries.example_en: The speech was filled with repetition to make the point clear.

entries.definition_en: characterized by repetition
entries.example_cn: 这篇演讲因内容重复且缺乏新意而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The speech was criticized for being repetitious and lacking new ideas.

entries.definition_en: characterized by repetition
entries.example_cn: 这份工作涉及一些可能令人厌倦的重复性任务。
entries.example_en: The job involves repetitive tasks that can be boring.

entries.definition_en: repetitive and persistent
entries.example_cn: 机器发出的重复噪音令人烦恼。
entries.example_en: The repetitive noise from the machine was annoying.

entries.definition_en: in a repetitive manner
entries.example_cn: 该机器重复运行以生产相同的零件。
entries.example_en: The machine operates repetitively to produce identical parts.

entries.definition_cn: 重复的状态或性质；重复性
entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being repetitive
entries.example_cn: 由于演讲者无法总结要点，这场演讲显得啰嗦且重复。
entries.example_en: The speech suffered from repetitiveness due to the speaker's inability to summarize key points.

entries.definition_en: express the same message in different words
entries.example_cn: 你能改述一下那个问题，让它更容易理解吗？
entries.example_en: Could you rephrase that question so it is easier to understand?

entries.definition_en: the act of saying or writing something again using different words
entries.example_cn: 老师让学生练习用自己的话重新表述指示。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the students to practice rephrasing the instructions in their own words.

entries.definition_en: to complain or be discontented
entries.example_cn: 他们对恶劣的条件感到不满。
entries.example_en: They repined at the harsh conditions.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: Typically followed by at, about, or under.

entries.definition_en: to take the place of something that is broken, lost, or no longer working.
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把旧轮胎换成新的。
entries.example_en: We need to replace the old tires with new ones.

entries.definition_en: to move into a position that was previously occupied by someone or something else.
entries.example_cn: 新任经理将于下个月接替离任者。
entries.example_en: The new manager will replace the outgoing one next month.

entries.definition_en: to put something back in the place where it belongs.
entries.example_cn: 读完书后请把书放回书架上。
entries.example_en: Please replace the book on the shelf after you finish reading it.

entries.definition_en: to switch two items that seem equivalent.
entries.example_cn: 他们决定把车里的座位换一下。
entries.example_en: They decided to replace the seats in the car.

entries.definition_en: capable of being replaced
entries.example_cn: 电池是可替换的，你可以轻松买到新的。
entries.example_en: The battery is replaceable, so you can buy a new one easily.

entries.definition_en: the act of providing a new person or thing to take the place of an old one
entries.example_cn: 昨天宣布更换了旧经理。
entries.example_en: The replacement of the old manager was announced yesterday.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that takes or can take the place of another
entries.example_cn: 这个型号是上一版本的直接替代品。
entries.example_en: This model is a direct replacement for the previous version.

entries.definition_en: someone who takes the place of another person
entries.example_cn: 她是即将退休的首席执行官的接替者。
entries.example_en: She is the replacement for the retiring CEO.

entries.definition_en: an event in which one thing is substituted for another
entries.example_cn: 更换引擎花了三天时间。
entries.example_en: The replacement of the engine took three days.

entries.definition_en: the act of replacing something that has been used up, lost, or removed
entries.example_cn: 补充水箱中的水对系统运行至关重要。
entries.example_en: The replacement of the water in the tank is essential for the system to work.

entries.definition_en: a person who follows next in order
entries.example_cn: 继承顺序中的继任者是堂表亲。
entries.example_en: The replacement in the line of succession is the second cousin.

entries.definition_en: to plant something again or anew
entries.example_cn: 风暴摧毁了庄稼后，农民决定立即重新种植。
entries.example_en: After the storm destroyed the crops, the farmers decided to replant immediately.

entries.definition_en: to play a recording again
entries.example_cn: 请重放这首歌，让我能清楚地听到副歌部分。
entries.example_en: Please replay the song so I can hear the chorus clearly.

entries.definition_en: to play something again
entries.example_cn: 让我们重演一下电影中的那个场景。
entries.example_en: Let's replay that scene from the movie.

entries.definition_en: to play a game again against the same opponent
entries.example_cn: 裁判下令重赛，因为第一场比赛太接近了。
entries.example_en: The referee ordered a replay because the first game was too close.

entries.definition_en: to play a melody again
entries.example_cn: 钢琴家决定以更丰富的情感重奏这首曲子。
entries.example_en: The pianist decided to replay the piece with more emotion.

entries.definition_cn: 重播的录像或动作，尤指体育转播中的重放
entries.definition_en: a recorded action or event shown again, especially in sports broadcasting
entries.example_cn: 那次有争议的比赛动作在重播中再次播放。
entries.example_en: The controversial play was shown again in the replay.

entries.definition_en: a game that is played again
entries.example_cn: 球队输掉了第一场比赛，因此必须进行重赛。
entries.example_en: The team lost the first match, so they had to play a replay.

entries.definition_en: to fill something that had previously been emptied
entries.example_cn: 我们需要在徒步旅行前补充水瓶里的水。
entries.example_en: We need to replenish the water bottles before the hike.

entries.definition_en: the act of filling something again by supplying what has been used up
entries.example_cn: 图书馆馆藏的补充花了数周时间。
entries.example_en: The replenishment of the library's stock took several weeks.

entries.definition_en: filled to satisfaction with food or drink
entries.example_cn: 长途跋涉后，我们饱足得准备睡觉了。
entries.example_en: After the long journey, we were replete and ready to sleep.

entries.definition_en: deeply filled or permeated with something
entries.example_cn: 空气中弥漫着鲜花的香气。
entries.example_en: The air was replete with the scent of fresh flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 使充足；补充耗尽的东西
entries.definition_en: to fill something completely or to the point of satisfaction
entries.example_cn: 这家慈善机构补充了食品银行耗尽的库存。
entries.example_en: The charity repleted the food bank's depleted shelves.

entries.definition_en: the state of being excessively full, especially after eating
entries.example_cn: 在那场丰盛的宴会后，他感到过饱。
entries.example_en: He suffered from repletion after the lavish banquet.

entries.definition_en: the state of being satisfactorily full and unable to take on more
entries.example_cn: 饱足的感觉让他立刻停止了进食。
entries.example_en: The feeling of repletion made him stop eating immediately.

entries.definition_en: an exact copy of something
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一座古代雕像的复制品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a replica of the ancient statue.

entries.definition_en: to produce an exact copy of something
entries.example_cn: 科学家需要复制实验以验证结果。
entries.example_en: Scientists need to replicate the experiment to verify the results.

entries.definition_en: to do or perform something again
entries.example_cn: 团队决定明年重施这一成功的策略。
entries.example_en: The team decided to replicate the successful strategy next year.

entries.definition_en: to bend or turn backward
entries.example_cn: 当风暴来临时，树叶在风中向后弯曲。
entries.example_en: The leaves replicate in the wind when the storm approaches.

entries.definition_en: the act of making copies
entries.example_cn: 复制这份古手稿花了几个月的时间。
entries.example_en: The replication of the ancient manuscript took several months.

entries.definition_cn: （遗传学）DNA在细胞分裂前自我复制的过程
entries.definition_en: (genetics) the process whereby DNA makes a copy of itself before cell division
entries.example_cn: DNA复制发生在细胞周期的S期。
entries.example_en: DNA replication occurs during the S phase of the cell cycle.

entries.definition_cn: 重复实验以验证其结论的有效性
entries.definition_en: the repetition of an experiment in order to test the validity of its conclusion
entries.example_cn: 该研究需要重复初步实验以确认结果。
entries.example_en: The study required a replication of the initial experiment to confirm the results.

entries.definition_cn: 定期将数据从一个数据库或服务器复制到另一个数据库或服务器的过程，通常用于提高容错能力
entries.definition_en: the process of regularly copying data from one database or server to another so that they contain the same information, often to improve fault tolerance
entries.example_cn: 这家公司使用数据库复制，使备份服务器与主服务器保持同步。
entries.example_en: The company uses database replication to keep a backup server synchronized with the primary server.

entries.definition_cn: 非原件的副本；被复制的东西
entries.definition_en: copy that is not the original; something that has been copied
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一幅著名画作的复制品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed a replication of the famous painting.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指机智或批评性的）快速回应
entries.definition_en: a quick reply to a question or remark (especially a witty or critical one)
entries.example_cn: 他对批评者的指控做出了尖锐的回应。
entries.example_en: He gave a sharp replication to the critic's accusation.

entries.definition_cn: （法律）原告针对被告答辩或答复提交的答辩状
entries.definition_en: a pleading made by a plaintiff in reply to the defendant's plea or answer
entries.example_cn: 原告针对被告的答辩提交了答辩状。
entries.example_en: The plaintiff filed a replication in response to the defendant's plea.

entries.definition_cn: 声波反射引起的声音重复（回声）
entries.definition_en: the repetition of a sound resulting from reflection of the sound waves
entries.example_cn: 这个洞穴以其对喊声的长久回声而闻名。
entries.example_en: The cave was famous for its long replication of the shout.

entries.definition_en: to give a spoken or written response to something
entries.example_cn: 他回答说无法参加会议。
entries.example_en: He replied that he would not be able to attend the meeting.

entries.definition_cn: 对问题、请求、批评或指责的答复
entries.definition_en: a statement made in response to a question, request, criticism, or accusation
entries.example_cn: 她礼貌地回复了客户的投诉。
entries.example_en: She sent a polite reply to the customer's complaint.

entries.definition_en: the act of continuing a conversation by speaking or writing
entries.example_cn: 老师在继续讲课之前等待学生的回应。
entries.example_en: The teacher waited for a reply from the students before moving on.

entries.definition_en: a written document describing the findings of some individual or group
entries.example_cn: 委员会昨天提交了最终报告。
entries.example_en: The committee submitted its final report yesterday.

entries.definition_en: a short account of the news
entries.example_cn: 我在收音机上听了早间新闻。
entries.example_en: I read the morning report on the radio.

entries.definition_en: to give an account or representation of in words
entries.example_cn: 这家报纸详细报道了这起事故。
entries.example_en: The newspaper reported the accident in detail.

entries.definition_en: to announce as the result of an investigation or experience or finding
entries.example_cn: 科学家公布了一种新鸟类的发现。
entries.example_en: Scientists reported a new species of bird.

entries.definition_en: to make known to the authorities
entries.example_cn: 目击者向警方举报了这起犯罪。
entries.example_en: Witnesses reported the crime to the police.

entries.definition_en: to announce one's presence
entries.example_cn: 他早上九点向经理报到。
entries.example_en: He reported to the manager at 9 AM.

entries.definition_en: an act or instance of informing someone orally
entries.example_cn: 他口头报告了火灾情况。
entries.example_en: He gave a verbal report of the fire.

entries.definition_en: a sharp explosive sound, especially of a gun firing
entries.example_cn: 我们听到远处传来一声巨响。
entries.example_en: We heard a loud report from the distance.

entries.definition_en: (of income) required by law to be reported to authorities
entries.example_cn: 所有境外收入都需在您的纳税申报表中申报。
entries.example_en: All foreign income is reportable on your tax return.

entries.definition_en: worthy of being reported or mentioned
entries.example_cn: 发现新物种是科学界值得报道的事件。
entries.example_en: The discovery of the new species is a reportable event for the scientific community.

entries.definition_en: news presented by reporters for newspapers, radio, or television.
entries.example_cn: 该杂志以其来自冲突地区的生动新闻报道而闻名。
entries.example_en: The magazine is known for its vivid reportage from conflict zones.

entries.definition_en: according to reports or other information
entries.example_cn: 据报嫌疑人在现场附近出现过。
entries.example_en: The suspect was reportedly seen near the scene.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to investigate news stories and write or broadcast reports about them
entries.example_cn: 记者在事故现场采访了目击者。
entries.example_en: The reporter interviewed the witness at the scene of the accident.

entries.definition_cn: 记录并发布司法或立法程序正式报告的人
entries.definition_en: a person who records and issues official reports of court or legislative proceedings
entries.example_cn: 法庭记录员记录了审判期间说出的每一句话。
entries.example_en: The court reporter recorded every word spoken during the trial.

entries.definition_cn: 用于显示另一基因是否已被细胞或生物体摄取或表达的基因
entries.definition_en: a gene used to show whether another gene has been taken up by or expressed in a cell or organism
entries.example_cn: 研究人员插入了一个报告基因，以检测目标基因是否处于活跃状态。
entries.example_en: The researchers inserted a reporter gene to test whether the target gene was active.

entries.definition_cn: 报告或报道的行为或过程，尤其是新闻报道
entries.definition_en: the act or process of producing reports, especially news reports
entries.example_cn: 关于选举的报道质量非常出色。
entries.example_en: The quality of reporting on the election was excellent.

entries.definition_en: a state of freedom from activity, work, or strain
entries.example_cn: 她在宁静的群山之中找到了安宁与休憩。
entries.example_en: She found peace and repose in the quiet mountains.

entries.definition_en: the absence of mental stress or anxiety
entries.example_cn: 风暴过后，社区里弥漫着一种深深的平静感。
entries.example_en: After the storm, there was a deep sense of repose in the community.

entries.definition_en: a disposition free from stress or emotion
entries.example_cn: 她在危机中表现出的沉着镇定令所有人印象深刻。
entries.example_en: Her calm repose during the crisis impressed everyone.

entries.definition_en: to rest, especially in a reclining position
entries.example_cn: 旅途结束后，他躺在床上休息。
entries.example_en: After the journey, he reposed on the bed.

entries.definition_en: to put or confide something in a person or thing
entries.example_cn: 他选择将信任托付给多年的挚友。
entries.example_en: He chose to repose his trust in his longtime friend.

entries.definition_cn: 把职责、权力或责任托付给某人
entries.definition_en: to entrust a duty, power, or responsibility to someone
entries.example_cn: 国王把该省的治理权托付给了他的顾问。
entries.example_en: The king reposed the administration of the province in his adviser.

entries.definition_en: to lie when dead
entries.example_cn: 遗体被安放于家族墓穴中安息。
entries.example_en: The body was laid to repose in the family vault.

entries.definition_en: to put in a horizontal position
entries.example_cn: 外科医生小心地将骨头复位至其自然位置。
entries.example_en: The surgeon carefully reposed the bone in its natural place.

entries.definition_en: to change place or direction
entries.example_cn: 船只必须迅速改变位置以避开风暴。
entries.example_en: The ship had to reposition quickly to avoid the storm.

entries.definition_en: to place something into another position
entries.example_cn: 护士每两小时为患者调整一次体位。
entries.example_en: Nurses repositioned the patient every two hours.

entries.definition_cn: 将某物置于新位置的行为；重新定位
entries.definition_en: the act of putting something into a new position
entries.example_cn: 设备重新定位后，控制装置更易于操作。
entries.example_en: The reposition of the equipment improved access to the controls.

entries.definition_cn: 将某物或某人置于新位置的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of placing something or someone in a new position
entries.example_cn: 重型机械的重新定位花了几个小时。
entries.example_en: The repositioning of the heavy machinery took several hours.

entries.definition_en: a place where things are stored or kept safe
entries.example_cn: 这座图书馆是珍稀历史文献的仓库。
entries.example_en: The library serves as a repository for rare historical documents.

entries.definition_en: a person who is given a secret to keep
entries.example_cn: 她是他的最深秘密的守密者。
entries.example_en: She was the repository of his deepest secrets.

entries.definition_en: a vault used for burying a famous person
entries.example_cn: 这位伟大的诗人被安葬在家族陵墓中。
entries.example_en: The great poet was laid to rest in a family repository.

entries.definition_cn: （因欠款等）收回财产；重新取得财产所有权
entries.definition_en: to reclaim possession of property, especially because payment remains due
entries.example_cn: 如果你不偿还贷款，银行将收回这辆车。
entries.example_en: The bank will repossess the car if you do not repay the loan.

entries.definition_cn: 重新取得某物，尤指财产的占有
entries.definition_en: to regain possession of something, especially property
entries.example_cn: 寻找多年后，她终于重新找回了那件家传宝物。
entries.example_en: After years of searching, she finally repossessed the family heirloom.

entries.definition_en: the action of regaining possession, especially the seizure of collateral securing a loan that is in default
entries.example_cn: 由于借款人未能付款，银行开始收回那辆汽车。
entries.example_en: The bank initiated repossession of the car because the borrower failed to make payments.

entries.definition_en: a post on social media that has already been posted
entries.example_cn: 她决定转载那篇文章，以便与她的粉丝分享。
entries.example_en: She decided to repost the article to share it with her followers.

entries.definition_en: to transfer a plant into a new, usually larger, container
entries.example_cn: 兰花根系已填满当前花盆，是时候给它换盆了。
entries.example_en: It is time to repot the orchid as its roots have filled the current pot.

entries.definition_en: a fabric characterized by prominent rounded ribs running across the width
entries.example_cn: 这条连衣裙是用一种能反射光线的闪亮罗纹布制成的。
entries.example_en: The dress was made of a shiny repp fabric that caught the light.

entries.definition_en: to rebuke or reprimand someone
entries.example_cn: 老师不得不斥责这名学生对他人的粗鲁行为。
entries.example_en: The teacher had to reprehend the student for his rude behavior.

entries.definition_en: deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.example_cn: 他应受谴责的行为导致他被立即解雇。
entries.example_en: His reprehensible behavior led to his immediate dismissal.

entries.definition_en: in a way that deserves blame or criticism
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家因应受谴责地无视关于经济危机的警告而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was criticized for reprehensibly ignoring the warnings about the economic crisis.

entries.definition_cn: 作为代表或发言人；代表某人的利益
entries.definition_en: to act as a delegate or spokesperson for someone; to represent their interests
entries.example_cn: 律师将在法庭上代表当事人。
entries.example_en: The lawyer will represent the client in court.

entries.definition_en: to take the place of or be equivalent to something
entries.example_cn: 一美元约合七元人民币。
entries.example_en: One dollar represents about seven Chinese yuan.

entries.definition_cn: 象征；用图像或模型表达
entries.definition_en: to express indirectly by an image, form, or model; to be a symbol
entries.example_cn: 鸽子象征和平。
entries.example_en: The dove represents peace.

entries.definition_en: to form or compose a whole
entries.example_cn: 这五个国家构成了人口的大多数。
entries.example_en: These five countries represent the majority of the population.

entries.definition_en: to be representative or typical for a group or category
entries.example_cn: 这幅画是19世纪风格的代表。
entries.example_en: This painting represents the style of the 19th century.

entries.definition_en: to be typical of a particular group or situation
entries.example_cn: 他的行为代表了人性中最糟糕的一面。
entries.example_en: His behavior represents the worst of human nature.

entries.definition_cn: 作为表达某种事物的手段
entries.definition_en: to serve as a means of expressing something
entries.example_cn: 艺术可以表达复杂的情感。
entries.example_en: Art can represent complex emotions.

entries.definition_cn: 在审判中担任辩护律师
entries.definition_en: to act as the defense counsel for someone in a trial
entries.example_cn: 她决定在审判中为被告辩护。
entries.example_en: She decided to represent the accused in the trial.

entries.definition_en: able to be expressed or shown using symbols
entries.example_cn: 许多复杂的数学概念可以用这种符号表示。
entries.example_en: Many complex mathematical concepts are representable in this notation.

entries.definition_cn: 描绘某人或某物外貌的图画、雕像或其他实物
entries.definition_en: a picture, statue, or other object that shows what someone or something looks like
entries.example_cn: 博物馆有一座这位著名画家的新雕像。
entries.example_en: The museum has a new representation of the famous painter.

entries.definition_cn: 在脑海中以观念或图像形式呈现的事物
entries.definition_en: the way something is shown in your mind as an idea or picture
entries.example_cn: 他对那件事的记忆非常清晰。
entries.example_en: The representation of the event in his memory was very clear.

entries.definition_cn: 代表某人或某团体行事并为其发言的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of acting on behalf of someone or a group and speaking for them
entries.example_cn: 她代表工人参加谈判，效果很好。
entries.example_en: Her representation of the workers was effective in the negotiation.

entries.definition_cn: 选区在立法机构中获得代表或席位的情况
entries.definition_en: the ability or arrangement by which a constituency is represented in a legislature
entries.example_cn: 该选区在议会中的席位增加了。
entries.example_en: The representation of the district in the parliament was increased.

entries.definition_en: a performance of a play or other dramatic work
entries.example_cn: 这部经典戏剧的演出已经售罄。
entries.example_en: The representation of the classic play was sold out.

entries.definition_cn: 一方为促使另一方签订合同而作出的事实陈述
entries.definition_en: a statement of facts made by one party to persuade another to sign a contract
entries.example_cn: 律师在合同签署前审查了这份事实陈述。
entries.example_en: The lawyer reviewed the representation before the contract was signed.

entries.definition_cn: 作为某人的正式代表或代理人的身份
entries.definition_en: the official status of being a delegate or agent for someone
entries.example_cn: 他拥有该公司在外国市场的代理身份。
entries.example_en: He holds the representation of the company in the foreign market.

entries.definition_en: a formal statement of facts and reasons used to appeal or protest
entries.example_cn: 他们提交了一份针对该决定的申诉书。
entries.example_en: They filed a representation against the decision.

entries.definition_en: used especially of art to describe works that depict objects, figures, or scenes as they appear to the eye
entries.example_cn: 这家画廊以其收藏的再现派绘画而闻名。
entries.example_en: The gallery is famous for its collection of representational paintings.

entries.definition_en: a person who acts on behalf of or for another person or group
entries.example_cn: 代表为整个委员会发言。
entries.example_en: The representative spoke for the entire committee.

entries.definition_en: a person who supports or promotes a particular cause or policy
entries.example_cn: 她是环保运动的倡导者。
entries.example_en: She is a representative of the environmental movement.

entries.definition_en: a member of the US House of Representatives
entries.example_cn: 众议员对新法律进行了投票。
entries.example_en: The representative voted on the new law.

entries.definition_en: serving to show what something is like or typical of
entries.example_cn: 这幅画是这位艺术家早期作品的典型代表。
entries.example_en: This painting is a representative example of the artist's early work.

entries.definition_en: relating to a system where people choose leaders to make decisions for them
entries.example_cn: 该国实行代议制政府。
entries.example_en: The country operates under a representative government.

entries.definition_en: standing for or symbolizing something else
entries.example_cn: 鸽子是和平的象征。
entries.example_en: The dove is a representative symbol of peace.

entries.definition_en: an item that shows the general characteristics of a group
entries.example_cn: 这朵花是春天的典型代表。
entries.example_en: This flower is a representative of the spring season.

entries.definition_en: represented accurately or precisely
entries.example_cn: 这张地图准确地描绘了该地区的地形。
entries.example_en: The map accurately represented the terrain of the region.

entries.definition_en: to defeat or control a group of people by using force
entries.example_cn: 军队被命令镇压北部的叛乱。
entries.example_en: The army was ordered to repress the rebellion in the northern region.

entries.definition_en: to prevent someone from developing their talents or expressing themselves freely
entries.example_cn: 严格的规则可能会压抑孩子的创造力和天然的好奇心。
entries.example_en: Strict rules can repress a child's creativity and natural curiosity.

entries.definition_en: to hide or keep something secret so that it is not known by others
entries.example_cn: 他试图隐瞒自己过去犯下的错误。
entries.example_en: He tried to repress the truth about his past mistakes.

entries.definition_en: to push unwanted thoughts or feelings out of one's conscious mind
entries.example_cn: 她一直压抑着愤怒，直到最终爆发。
entries.example_en: She repressed her anger until it eventually caused her to explode.

entries.definition_en: to stop something from happening or working
entries.example_cn: 这项新法律旨在阻止非法毒品的蔓延。
entries.example_en: The new law aims to repress the spread of illegal drugs.

entries.definition_en: characterized by the suppression of impulses or emotions
entries.example_cn: 被压抑的愤怒最终导致了爆发。
entries.example_en: The repressed anger eventually led to an outburst.

entries.definition_en: a second or subsequent pressing
entries.example_cn: 唱片公司将这张专辑重新压制成黑胶唱片发行。
entries.example_en: The label issued a repressing of the album on vinyl.

entries.definition_en: the act of repressing; control by holding down
entries.example_cn: 政府利用镇压手段来平息抗议。
entries.example_en: The government used repression to silence the protests.

entries.definition_en: a state of forcible subjugation
entries.example_cn: 该国在多年的政治压迫下受苦。
entries.example_en: The country suffered under years of political repression.

entries.definition_cn: （精神病学）一种防御机制，通过阻止冲动或想法进入意识来防止焦虑
entries.definition_en: the classical defense mechanism that protects you from impulses or ideas that would cause anxiety by preventing them from becoming conscious
entries.example_cn: 他对童年记忆的压抑让他感到痛苦。
entries.example_en: His repression of childhood memories caused him distress.

entries.definition_en: restrictive of action
entries.example_cn: 该政权使用压制性措施来控制人口。
entries.example_en: The regime used repressive measures to control the population.

entries.definition_en: an agent that suppresses or inhibits a process
entries.example_cn: 这种抑制蛋白结合到 DNA 上以阻止基因表达。
entries.example_en: The repressor protein binds to the DNA to stop gene expression.

entries.definition_en: a (temporary) relief from harm or discomfort
entries.example_cn: 雨水带来了短暂的凉爽，缓解了灼热的暑气。
entries.example_en: The rain offered a brief reprieve from the scorching heat.

entries.definition_cn: 许多人反对的拟议事件被取消或推迟
entries.definition_en: a cancellation or postponement of a proposed event that many people oppose
entries.example_cn: 在公众反对后，拟议中的车站关闭计划被暂缓。
entries.example_en: The proposed station closures received a reprieve after public opposition.

entries.definition_cn: 准予推迟（通常是推迟执行死刑）的令状
entries.definition_en: a warrant granting postponement (usually to postpone the execution of the death sentence)
entries.example_cn: 囚犯收到了州长给予的暂缓执行令。
entries.example_en: The prisoner received a reprieve from the governor.

entries.definition_cn: 暂缓或免除惩罚的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of reprieving; postponing or remitting punishment
entries.example_cn: 暂缓执行判决一事成为公众辩论的话题。
entries.example_en: The reprieve of the sentence was a matter of public debate.

entries.definition_cn: 推迟对已定罪罪犯的惩罚，如执行死刑
entries.definition_en: postpone the punishment of a convicted criminal, such as an execution
entries.example_cn: 州长决定暂缓执行死刑。
entries.example_en: The governor decided to reprieve the death sentence.

entries.definition_en: relieve temporarily
entries.example_cn: 凉爽的树荫让徒步者暂时缓解了午后的炎热。
entries.example_en: The cool shade briefly reprieved the hikers from the afternoon heat.

entries.definition_en: an act or expression of criticism and censure
entries.example_cn: 这名员工因上班迟到而受到了正式训斥。
entries.example_en: The employee received a formal reprimand for arriving late to work.

entries.definition_en: to rebuke formally
entries.example_cn: 经理决定正式训斥那名违反规定的员工。
entries.example_en: The manager decided to reprimand the staff member for breaking the rules.

entries.definition_en: to censure severely or angrily
entries.example_cn: 老师大声严厉斥责了在课堂上大喊大叫的学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher reprimanded the student loudly for shouting in class.

entries.definition_en: to print something again
entries.example_cn: 出版商决定重印这本畅销书。
entries.example_en: The publisher decided to reprint the best-selling book.

entries.definition_en: a publication that is printed again without changes and sold again
entries.example_cn: 这个版本是1920年经典小说的再版。
entries.example_en: This edition is a reprint of the classic novel from 1920.

entries.definition_en: an article printed separately that originally appeared in a larger publication
entries.example_cn: 杂志收录了那篇著名演讲的单行本文章。
entries.example_en: The magazine included a reprint of the famous speech.

entries.definition_en: a publication that is reprinted without changes and offered for sale again
entries.example_cn: 这部经典小说的罕见重印本深受收藏家追捧。
entries.example_en: This rare reprinting of the classic novel is highly sought after by collectors.

entries.definition_en: an act of retaliation, especially in response to an attack
entries.example_cn: 政府谴责了针对平民的暴力报复行动。
entries.example_en: The government condemned the violent reprisal against the civilians.

entries.definition_cn: （音乐中乐句的）重复；主题再现
entries.definition_en: a repetition of a musical phrase or a return to an earlier theme
entries.example_cn: 开头主题的再现为这首协奏曲画上了令人难忘的句号。
entries.example_en: The reprise of the opening theme brought the concerto to a memorable close.

entries.definition_en: to repeat an earlier theme in a musical composition
entries.example_cn: 作曲家决定在交响乐的结尾再现开头的旋律。
entries.example_en: The composer decided to reprise the opening melody at the end of the symphony.

entries.definition_cn: 轻微的责备；含蓄的批评
entries.definition_en: a mild or implicit rebuke or criticism
entries.example_cn: 这封信含蓄地责备了他一再迟到。
entries.example_en: The letter contained a mild reproach for his repeated lateness.

entries.definition_en: disgrace or shame
entries.example_cn: 他的背叛给家人带来了耻辱。
entries.example_en: His betrayal was a reproach to his family.

entries.definition_en: to express criticism towards someone
entries.example_cn: 老师因学生迟到而批评了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher reproached the student for being late.

entries.definition_en: expressing reproof or reproach, especially as a corrective
entries.example_cn: 当他迟到时，她给了他一个责备的眼神。
entries.example_en: She gave him a reproachful look when he arrived late.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that expresses disapproval or blame
entries.example_cn: 当他忘了他们的纪念日时，她责备地看了他一眼。
entries.example_en: She looked at him reproachfully when he forgot their anniversary.

entries.definition_en: a person without moral scruples
entries.example_cn: 他是个以欺骗他人闻名的无赖。
entries.example_en: He was known as a reprobate who cheated everyone.

entries.definition_en: deviating from what is considered moral or right or proper or good
entries.example_cn: 他们不道德的行为震惊了社区。
entries.example_en: Their reprobate behavior shocked the community.

entries.definition_en: to reject documents as invalid
entries.example_cn: 法院驳回了辩护方提交的证据。
entries.example_en: The court reprobated the evidence submitted by the defense.

entries.definition_en: to express strong disapproval of
entries.example_cn: 委员会强烈谴责了腐败行为。
entries.example_en: The committee reprobated the corrupt practices.

entries.definition_en: to abandon to eternal damnation
entries.example_cn: 故事描述了恶棍如何被上帝弃绝。
entries.example_en: The story describes how the villain was reprobated by God.

entries.definition_en: severe disapproval or condemnation
entries.example_cn: 委员会对该政策的严厉谴责是一致的。
entries.example_en: The committee's reprobation of the policy was unanimous.

entries.definition_cn: 被神弃绝；被判入地狱、永受苦难的状态
entries.definition_en: rejection by God; the state of being condemned to eternal misery in Hell
entries.example_cn: 在这部小说中，主人公害怕遭神弃绝、永受地狱之苦。
entries.example_en: In the novel, the protagonist faces the fear of reprobation.

entries.definition_en: use again after processing
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂将废料处理后再次制成新产品。
entries.example_en: The factory reprocesses the waste materials into new products.

entries.definition_en: to make a copy or an equivalent of something
entries.example_cn: 你可以用扫描仪复制这份文件。
entries.example_en: You can reproduce this document using the scanner.

entries.definition_en: to have offspring or produce more individuals of a species
entries.example_cn: 许多动物一生中只繁殖一次。
entries.example_en: Many animals reproduce only once in their lifetime.

entries.definition_en: to recreate a sound, image, or atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 特效团队努力工作以重现电影中的场景。
entries.example_en: The special effects team worked hard to reproduce the scene from the movie.

entries.definition_en: to repeat something after memorizing it
entries.example_cn: 老师要求学生背诵并复述这首诗。
entries.example_en: The students were asked to reproduce the poem from memory.

entries.definition_cn: 唱机拾音器；唱机声音再生装置
entries.definition_en: a device in a phonograph that uses a stylus and diaphragm to reproduce recorded sound
entries.example_cn: 这台唱机拾音器曾用于播放20世纪20年代的唱片。
entries.example_en: The phonograph reproducer was used to play records from the 1920s.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being able to be reproduced
entries.example_cn: 独立研究人员验证了实验结果的可重复性。
entries.example_en: The reproducibility of the experiment results was verified by independent researchers.

entries.definition_en: capable of being reproduced
entries.example_cn: 这项研究的结果可以被其他研究人员复现。
entries.example_en: The study results were reproducible by other researchers.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that is reproducible
entries.example_cn: 必须可重复地进行实验以验证结果。
