entries.example_en: At the coronation, the new king was invested with royal power.

entries.definition_cn: 顶桅帆；设在上桅帆之上的帆
entries.definition_en: a sail set above the topgallant sail on a royal mast
entries.example_cn: 船长命令降下顶桅横帆。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the royal to be lowered.

entries.definition_en: a stag with many branches on its antlers
entries.example_cn: 猎人在森林里发现了一只王鹿。
entries.example_en: The hunter spotted a royal in the forest.

entries.definition_en: support for or loyalty to a monarchy or the principle of having a king or queen
entries.example_cn: 该政党的政治纲领基于强烈的保皇主义。
entries.example_en: The political party's platform was based on strong royalism.

entries.definition_en: excessively or thoroughly
entries.example_cn: 如果你改动他的作品，他会非常恼火。
entries.example_en: He will be royally annoyed if you change his work.

entries.definition_en: in a royal manner
entries.example_cn: 国王在访问宫殿期间受到了皇家般的礼遇。
entries.example_en: The king was treated royally during his visit to the palace.

entries.definition_cn: 为使用知识产权或自然资源而支付的版税或使用费
entries.definition_en: payment for the right to use intellectual property or natural resources
entries.example_cn: 作者每月收到版税。
entries.example_en: The author receives royalty payments every month.

entries.definition_en: members of a royal family collectively
entries.example_cn: 皇室成员出席了国家典礼。
entries.example_en: The royalty attended the state ceremony.

entries.definition_cn: 洛神花；玫瑰茄，一种用于制作馅饼和果冻并可取韧皮纤维的印度草本植物
entries.definition_en: an East Indian herb or subshrub cultivated for its fleshy calyces and bast fiber
entries.example_cn: 厨师用洛神花的肉质萼片制作了一道馅饼。
entries.example_en: The chef used the fleshy calyxes of the rozelle to make a tart.

entries.definition_en: the speed at which a motor rotates, measured in revolutions per minute
entries.example_cn: 随着汽车加速，发动机的转速提高了。
entries.example_en: The engine's rpm increased as the car accelerated.

entries.definition_en: to move something over a surface with pressure
entries.example_cn: 请把乳液揉进皮肤里。
entries.example_en: Please rub the cream into your skin.

entries.definition_en: to move against something with pressure and friction
entries.example_cn: 粗糙的布料摩擦着他的手臂。
entries.example_en: The rough fabric rubbed against his arm.

entries.definition_en: to scrape or rub an itchy area to relieve the sensation
entries.example_cn: 她抓挠腿部以止痒。
entries.example_en: She rubbed her leg to stop the itching.

entries.definition_en: an unexpected difficulty or obstacle
entries.example_cn: 资金不足是该项目的主要障碍。
entries.example_en: The lack of funding was a major rub for the project.

entries.definition_en: the action of rubbing or wiping something
entries.example_cn: 他快速擦拭了一下桌子以清洁它。
entries.example_en: He gave the table a quick rub to clean it.

entries.definition_en: the sound produced by beating a drum
entries.example_cn: 有节奏的鼓声充满了空气。
entries.example_en: The rhythmic rub-a-dub of the drum filled the air.

entries.definition_en: an expressive musical technique in which the tempo is flexibly varied
entries.example_cn: 钢琴家以优美的自由速度演奏了慢板部分。
entries.example_en: The pianist played the adagio section with beautiful rubato.

entries.definition_en: an elastic material obtained from the latex sap of trees
entries.example_cn: 轮胎是由天然橡胶制成的。
entries.example_en: The tires are made of natural rubber.

entries.definition_en: an eraser made of rubber
entries.example_cn: 我昨天弄丢了铅笔橡皮擦。
entries.example_en: I lost my pencil rubber yesterday.

entries.definition_en: any of various synthetic elastic materials resembling natural rubber
entries.example_cn: 这种合成橡胶比天然橡胶更耐用。
entries.example_en: This synthetic rubber is more durable than natural rubber.

entries.definition_cn: （美国、加拿大俚语）男用安全套
entries.definition_en: (US/Canadian slang) a condom, especially an external condom
entries.example_cn: 他在抽屉里放了一盒男用安全套。
entries.example_en: He kept a box of rubbers in his drawer.

entries.definition_en: coat or impregnate with rubber
entries.example_cn: 他们给靴子涂了橡胶使其防水。
entries.example_en: They rubbered the boots to make them waterproof.

entries.definition_cn: 因资金不足而被退回的
entries.definition_en: returned for lack of funds
entries.example_cn: 该拨款因部门没有预算而被退回。
entries.example_en: The grant was rubbered because the department had no budget.

entries.definition_en: a contest consisting of a series of successive matches
entries.example_cn: 他们进行了一场由三场比赛组成的系列赛。
entries.example_en: They played a rubber consisting of three matches.

entries.definition_en: a waterproof overshoe that protects shoes from water or snow
entries.example_cn: 下雪前穿上你的雨鞋套。
entries.example_en: Put on your rubber before you go out in the snow.

entries.definition_en: to strain to watch or stare curiously
entries.example_cn: 人群好奇地凝视着事故现场。
entries.example_en: The crowd rubbernecked at the accident scene.

entries.definition_en: a person who stares inquisitively
entries.example_cn: 一个窥探者探出窗外，想看发生了什么事。
entries.example_en: A rubberneck leaned out of the window to see what was happening.

entries.definition_en: a tourist (US, obsolete)
entries.example_cn: 这位观光客停车拍照，拍摄那座历史悠久的城堡。
entries.example_en: The rubberneck stopped the car to take photos of the historic castle.

entries.definition_en: to stamp a document with a rubber stamp, usually to show official approval
entries.example_cn: 文员在将申请表发送给经理之前用橡皮图章盖了章。
entries.example_en: The clerk rubberstamped the application before sending it to the manager.

entries.definition_en: to approve something automatically without careful consideration
entries.example_cn: 委员会没有阅读细节就草率批准了该提案。
entries.example_en: The committee rubberstamped the proposal without reading the details.

entries.definition_en: having a texture that is elastic and flexible like rubber
entries.example_cn: 垫子橡胶般有弹性的表面使它很容易清洁。
entries.example_en: The rubbery surface of the mat made it easy to clean.

entries.definition_en: difficult to chew because it is tough or elastic
entries.example_cn: 这块牛排太难以咀嚼了，我们不得不要求退款。
entries.example_en: The steak was so rubbery that we had to ask for a refund.

entries.definition_en: a copy made by laying paper over an image and rubbing it with charcoal
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一幅石刻拓片。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed an ancient rubbing of a stone inscription.

entries.definition_en: the resistance felt when one object moves against another
entries.example_cn: 粗糙布料摩擦他的皮肤让他感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: The rubbing of the rough fabric against his skin was uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: the act of rubbing one object against another with pressure
entries.example_cn: 他用力擦拭雕像，清除了污垢。
entries.example_en: His vigorous rubbing of the statue removed the dirt.

entries.definition_en: worthless material that is to be disposed of
entries.example_cn: 请把垃圾倒掉。
entries.example_en: Please take out the rubbish.

entries.definition_en: nonsensical talk or writing
entries.example_cn: 他的演讲全是胡言乱语。
entries.example_en: His speech was nothing but rubbish.

entries.definition_en: attack strongly
entries.example_cn: 这位记者猛烈抨击了那位政治家的说法。
entries.example_en: The journalist rubbished the politician's claims.

entries.definition_en: of poor quality and low value; cheap and inferior
entries.example_cn: 这种廉价产品所用的材料非常低劣。
entries.example_en: The materials used in this cheap product are very rubbishy.

entries.definition_cn: 碎石；碎砖瓦等建筑残骸
entries.definition_en: broken fragments, especially of rock or masonry, left after something has been destroyed or broken up
entries.example_cn: 地震后，城市被瓦砾覆盖。
entries.example_en: The city was covered in rubble after the earthquake.

entries.definition_en: the act of rubbing down, usually for relaxation or medicinal purposes
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步之后，她享受了一次舒缓的按摩。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, she enjoyed a soothing rubdown.

entries.definition_en: a person who is not very intelligent or interested in culture
entries.example_cn: 那个城里人嘲笑乡巴佬试图乘坐地铁系统。
entries.example_en: The city slicker laughed at the rube's attempt to navigate the subway system.

usage.label: derogatory
usage.pattern: an uninformed, unsophisticated, or unintelligent person

entries.definition_en: a mild contagious viral disease similar to measles that can harm a fetus
entries.example_cn: 风疹对怀孕早期的孕妇是一个严重的风险。
entries.example_en: Rubella is a serious risk for pregnant women in the first trimester.

entries.definition_en: a contagious viral disease that causes a red rash, mainly affecting children
entries.example_cn: 医生警告父母说麻疹传染性很强。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned the parents that rubeola is highly contagious.

entries.definition_en: having a healthy reddish color, often from being outdoors
entries.example_cn: 经过一个夏天的徒步旅行，他的脸依然红润。
entries.example_en: After a summer of hiking, his face remained rubicund.

entries.definition_en: a soft, silvery metal that burns in air and reacts violently with water
entries.example_cn: 铷是一种存在于某些矿物中的高活性碱金属。
entries.example_en: Rubidium is a highly reactive alkali metal found in certain minerals.

entries.definition_cn: 俄罗斯、白俄罗斯和德涅斯特河沿岸地区的货币单位
entries.definition_en: the basic unit of currency in Russia, Belarus, and Transnistria
entries.example_cn: 游客到达莫斯科时通常会将美元兑换成卢布。
entries.example_en: Tourists often exchange their dollars for rubles upon arriving in Moscow.

entries.definition_cn: 塔吉克斯坦卢布（已停用）
entries.definition_en: the former currency of Tajikistan, used before the somoni
entries.example_cn: 在索莫尼启用前，塔吉克斯坦的价格以卢布标示。
entries.example_en: Before the somoni was introduced, prices in Tajikistan were quoted in rubles.

entries.definition_en: an official rule or guideline that must be followed
entries.example_cn: 学校对学生行为有严格的规章。
entries.example_en: The school has a strict rubric regarding student behavior.

entries.definition_en: instructions for conducting religious services, often printed in red
entries.example_cn: 牧师在弥撒中仔细遵循了礼仪指南。
entries.example_en: The priest followed the rubric carefully during the mass.

entries.definition_en: a name used to classify a group of things
entries.example_cn: 该数据库使用类别名称来组织不同类型的数据。
entries.example_en: The database uses a rubric to organize different types of data.

entries.definition_en: a title or heading printed in a special color or font
entries.example_cn: 她用粗体的红字标题突出了主要部分。
entries.example_en: She highlighted the main sections with a bold rubric.

entries.definition_en: a heading in a law or bill that summarizes its content
entries.example_cn: 新的税法包含一个概述公司税率变更的条款标题。
entries.example_en: The new tax bill includes a rubric outlining the changes to corporate rates.

entries.definition_en: to decorate something with the color red
entries.example_cn: 艺术家决定将整个绘画背景染成红色。
entries.example_en: The artist decided to rubric the entire background of the painting.

entries.definition_en: a note explaining a difficult word found in a text
entries.example_cn: 脚注为诗中使用的古语提供了注释。
entries.example_en: The footnote provided a rubric for the archaic term used in the poem.

entries.definition_en: a cut and polished transparent piece of ruby valued as a precious gem
entries.example_cn: 她在晚会上戴了一条红宝石项链。
entries.example_en: She wore a ruby necklace to the gala.

entries.definition_en: a deep and vivid red color
entries.example_cn: 玫瑰的深红色在绿叶的衬托下格外醒目。
entries.example_en: The ruby of the rose was striking against the green leaves.

entries.definition_en: a deep red variety of corundum used as a gemstone and in lasers
entries.example_cn: 红宝石是订婚戒指中流行的一种宝石。
entries.example_en: Ruby is a popular gemstone for engagement rings.

entries.definition_en: of a deep red color resembling blood or cherries
entries.example_cn: 夕阳将天空染成了深红色。
entries.example_en: The sunset painted the sky in ruby hues.

entries.definition_en: having a deep red color like that of a ruby, blood, or cherries
entries.example_cn: 夕阳将天空染成了红宝石般的红色。
entries.example_en: The sunset painted the sky in ruby-red hues.

entries.definition_en: become wrinkled or drawn together
entries.example_cn: 当风吹过时，布料开始起皱。
entries.example_en: The fabric began to ruck when the wind blew against it.

entries.definition_en: an irregular fold in an otherwise even surface
entries.example_cn: 客人们到来之前，她抚平了桌布上的褶皱。
entries.example_en: She smoothed out the ruck in the tablecloth before the guests arrived.

entries.definition_en: a crowd especially of ordinary or undistinguished persons or things
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家被一群提问的记者包围着。
entries.example_en: The politician was surrounded by a ruck of reporters asking questions.

entries.definition_en: (Scotland) to make a rattling noise in the throat
entries.example_cn: 那名窒息的患者开始发出喉咙的嘎嘎声。
entries.example_en: The choking patient began to ruckle in his throat.

entries.definition_cn: 使表面起皱或产生折痕
entries.definition_en: to make wrinkles or creases on a smooth surface
entries.example_cn: 她使布料起皱以创造出有纹理的图案。
entries.example_en: She ruckled the fabric to create a textured pattern.

entries.definition_en: a bag carried on the back or shoulder using a strap
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行前，他把衣服装进了背包里。
entries.example_en: He packed his clothes into the rucksack before the hike.

entries.definition_en: a noisy disturbance or commotion
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在图书馆里大吵大闹。
entries.example_en: The children caused a ruckus in the library.

entries.definition_en: a European freshwater fish that looks like a roach
entries.example_cn: 钓鱼者从湖里钓到了一条小赤眼鳟。
entries.example_en: The angler caught a small rudd from the lake.

entries.definition_cn: 船尾用于操舵的铰接式垂直舵板
entries.definition_en: a hinged vertical plate at the stern of a vessel, used to steer it
entries.example_cn: 船长转动船舵以绕过暗礁。
entries.example_en: The captain turned the rudder to navigate around the reef.

entries.definition_cn: 飞机尾部的垂直舵面，用于改变水平航向
entries.definition_en: a hinged vertical control surface on an aircraft's tail, used to change its horizontal course
entries.example_cn: 飞行员调整舵面以纠正飞机的漂移。
entries.example_en: The pilot adjusted the rudder to correct the aircraft's drift.

entries.definition_cn: 没有舵的；缺乏指导或方向的
entries.definition_en: lacking a rudder, guidance, or direction
entries.example_cn: 争吵之后，他感到无方向且不确定下一步该怎么做。
entries.example_en: After the argument, he felt rudderless and unsure of his next steps.

entries.definition_cn: 红赭石；用于标记的红色赭石
entries.definition_en: a red iron ore used for dyeing and marking
entries.example_cn: 古代陶工用红赭石给陶器上色。
entries.example_en: The ancient potters used ruddle to color their clay vessels.

entries.definition_en: to redden as if with a red ocher color
entries.example_cn: 夕阳将云朵染上了温暖的火红色。
entries.example_en: The sunset ruddled the clouds with a warm, fiery glow.

entries.definition_en: to twist or braid together; to interlace
entries.example_cn: 她将发丝编结成了复杂的图案。
entries.example_en: She ruddled the strands of hair into an intricate pattern.

entries.definition_en: having a healthy reddish color, often from being outdoors
entries.example_cn: 在公园里跑了一会儿后，他的脸看起来红润健康。
entries.example_en: After running in the park, his face looked ruddy and healthy.

entries.definition_en: of a deep red color, similar to blood or cherries
entries.example_cn: 绯红的日落将天空染成了橙色和红色。
entries.example_en: The ruddy sunset painted the sky in shades of orange and red.

entries.definition_en: behaving in a way that is not polite or socially acceptable
entries.example_cn: 说话者正在讲话时打断他们是很粗鲁的。
entries.example_en: It was rude to interrupt the speaker while they were talking.

entries.definition_en: showing a lack of politeness or good manners
entries.example_cn: 她对服务员很无礼，没有说谢谢。
entries.example_en: She was rude to the waiter and didn't say thank you.

entries.definition_cn: 有些淫秽、色情或冒犯性的
entries.definition_en: somewhat obscene, pornographic, or offensive
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因含有粗俗的场面而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The film was criticized for its rude scenes.

entries.definition_en: belonging to an early stage of development; simple and crude
entries.example_cn: 早期的计算机是简陋的机器，内存非常有限。
entries.example_en: The first computers were rude machines with very limited memory.

entries.definition_en: lacking refinement, elegance, or good manners
entries.example_cn: 他在晚宴上的粗俗行为让每个人都感到冒犯。
entries.example_en: His rude behavior at the dinner party offended everyone.

entries.definition_cn: 未经加工的；粗制的（尤指羊毛）
entries.definition_en: not processed or manufactured using complex methods
entries.example_cn: 他们只出售粗加工的羊毛，还没有纺成纱线。
entries.example_en: They sell only rude wool, which has not been spun into yarn.

entries.definition_en: in an impolite manner
entries.example_cn: 他在演讲期间粗鲁地打断了发言者。
entries.example_en: He rudely interrupted the speaker during the presentation.

entries.definition_en: a manner that is rude and insulting
entries.example_cn: 他对服务员的无礼行为是不可接受的。
entries.example_en: His rudeness towards the waiter was unacceptable.

entries.definition_en: a rude remark or behavior
entries.example_cn: 他一再无礼的言行冒犯了所有人。
entries.example_en: His repeated rudenesses offended everyone.

entries.definition_en: the remains of a body part that was functional at an earlier stage of life
entries.example_cn: 人类的阑尾被认为是一个更大消化器官的退化残留。
entries.example_en: The human appendix is considered a rudiment of a larger digestive organ.

entries.definition_en: involving only basic facts or principles
entries.example_cn: 这门课程提供了计算机编程的基础入门。
entries.example_en: The course provides a rudimentary introduction to computer programming.

entries.definition_en: in the earliest stages of development
entries.example_cn: 这个初步计划在实施前需要更详细的工作。
entries.example_en: The rudimentary plan needs more detailed work before it can be implemented.

entries.definition_en: not fully developed in mature animals
entries.example_cn: 胚胎中的一些未完全发育的结构后来会消失。
entries.example_en: Some rudimentary structures in the embryo will disappear later.

entries.definition_en: to feel regret or sorrow for something you have done
entries.example_cn: 她会后悔决定辞职的那一天。
entries.example_en: She will rue the day she decided to quit her job.

entries.definition_en: sadness or regret caused by a mistake or disappointment
entries.example_cn: 他对自己轻率的举动感到深深的懊悔。
entries.example_en: He felt a deep sense of rue for his careless actions.

entries.definition_en: a European herb with grey-green leaves that smell strong and taste bitter
entries.example_cn: 花园里充满了芸香的气味。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the scent of rue.

entries.definition_en: leaves of the rue plant used for flavoring but which can cause skin irritation
entries.example_cn: 他在酒里加了一枝芸香，尽管知道它可能刺激皮肤。
entries.example_en: He added a sprig of rue to the wine, though he knew it could irritate his skin.

entries.definition_en: a street or road in France
entries.example_cn: 他们在巴黎的和平大道上散步。
entries.example_en: They walked down Rue de la Paix in Paris.

entries.definition_cn: 懊悔的；遗憾的；带有苦笑意味的
entries.definition_en: causing, feeling, or expressing regret or sorrow, especially in a wry or humorous way
entries.example_cn: 当他意识到自己忘了他们的纪念日时，他给她一个悔恨的微笑。
entries.example_en: He gave her a rueful smile when he realized he had forgotten their anniversary.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing regret or sorrow
entries.example_cn: 他悔恨地承认自己犯了一个可怕的错误。
entries.example_en: He ruefully admitted that he had made a terrible mistake.

entries.definition_en: feathers or hair around the neck of a bird or animal
entries.example_cn: 孔雀展开它色彩斑斓的饰羽以吸引配偶。
entries.example_en: The peacock spread its colorful ruff to attract a mate.

entries.definition_en: a high, tight collar worn in the past
entries.example_cn: 这幅肖像画显示一位贵族戴着巨大的高领饰圈。
entries.example_en: The portrait shows a nobleman wearing a large ruff.

entries.definition_cn: 流苏鹬（一种雄鸟繁殖期颈部会竖起饰羽的鹬）
entries.definition_en: a type of sandpiper, the male of which develops an erectile neck ruff during breeding season
entries.example_cn: 雄性流苏鹬在繁殖季节展示引人注目的颈部饰羽。
entries.example_en: The male ruff displays its striking neck feathers during breeding season.

entries.definition_cn: （纸牌游戏中）因无法跟牌而用王牌赢墩
entries.definition_en: the act of winning a trick with a trump when unable to follow suit
entries.example_cn: 因为他没有该花色的牌，所以他用王牌赢了这一墩。
entries.example_en: He ruffed the trick because he had no cards of the suit led.

entries.definition_cn: （纸牌游戏中）无法跟牌时出王牌
entries.definition_en: to play a trump card in a card game when unable to follow suit
entries.example_cn: 因为她没有所引花色的牌，所以她无法跟牌，只能用王牌赢下这一墩。
entries.example_en: She ruffed the trick because she had no card in the suit led.

entries.definition_en: a cruel and brutal fellow
entries.example_cn: 警察穿过拥挤的市场追捕那个恶棍。
entries.example_en: The police chased the ruffian through the crowded market.

entries.definition_cn: 使（羽毛、头发等）蓬松或凌乱
entries.definition_en: to make feathers, hair, or similar material stand out or become disordered
entries.example_cn: 那只鸟起飞前抖松了羽毛。
entries.example_en: The bird ruffled its feathers before taking flight.

entries.definition_en: to trouble or vex someone
entries.example_cn: 别让他粗鲁的评论惹你心烦。
entries.example_en: Don't let his rude comments ruffle your feathers.

entries.definition_en: to discompose or unsettle someone
entries.example_cn: 突如其来的噪音使她心神不宁。
entries.example_en: The sudden noise ruffled her composure.

entries.definition_en: to stir up water so that it forms ripples
entries.example_cn: 那艘船使平静的湖面泛起涟漪。
entries.example_en: The boat ruffled the calm lake.

entries.definition_en: a strip of pleated fabric used as a decorative trim on clothing
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙的领口有一圈精致的褶边。
entries.example_en: The dress had a delicate ruffle along the neckline.

entries.definition_en: a noisy fight or quarrel
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在操场上开始了一场吵闹的打斗。
entries.example_en: The children started a ruffle in the playground.

entries.definition_en: a high, tight collar worn in the past
entries.example_cn: 这幅维多利亚时代的肖像画展示了一位女士戴着僵硬的硬领。
entries.example_en: The Victorian portrait shows a woman wearing a stiff ruffle.

entries.definition_cn: 昂首阔步（以示傲慢或炫耀）
entries.definition_en: to walk with a lofty and proud gait to impress others
entries.example_cn: 他昂首阔步地走进房间，试图显得很重要。
entries.example_en: He ruffled into the room, trying to look important.

entries.definition_en: covered in small waves or undulations caused by wind
entries.example_cn: 湖面泛起涟漪，倒映着月光。
entries.example_en: The ruffled surface of the lake reflected the moonlight.

entries.definition_en: decorated with ruffles or frills
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件饰有褶边的衬衫去参加正式晚宴。
entries.example_en: She wore a ruffled blouse to the formal dinner.

entries.definition_en: a thick piece of fabric used to cover the floor
entries.example_cn: 我们买了一块色彩鲜艳的地毯来覆盖冰冷的地板。
entries.example_en: We bought a colorful rug to cover the cold floor.

entries.definition_en: a fold, wrinkle, or crease, especially in biological tissue
entries.example_cn: 胃壁的皱襞有助于器官扩张以容纳食物。
entries.example_en: The rugae in the stomach lining help expand the organ to hold food.

usage.label: plural normally rugae
usage.pattern: The plural form is normally rugae.

entries.definition_en: a form of football played with an oval ball
entries.example_cn: 他们上周末进行了一场橄榄球比赛。
entries.example_en: They played a match of rugby last weekend.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: play rugby; a game of rugby

entries.definition_en: rubber cement or contact cement (Philippines)
entries.example_cn: 他们用橡胶胶水把从鞋上脱落的鞋底粘了回去。
entries.example_en: They used rugby to reattach the sole that had come off the shoe.

entries.definition_en: a pastry made with cream cheese dough and various fillings such as raisins, walnuts, or chocolate
entries.example_cn: 我们买了一盒填有杏酱和肉桂的鲁格拉赫。
entries.example_en: We bought a box of rugelach filled with apricot preserves and cinnamon.

entries.definition_en: strong and sturdy in structure or constitution
entries.example_cn: 这双坚固的靴子非常适合在山区徒步旅行。
entries.example_en: The rugged boots were perfect for hiking in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: having very uneven terrain
entries.example_cn: 队伍必须攀登崎岖的山丘才能到达顶峰。
entries.example_en: The team had to climb the rugged hills to reach the summit.

entries.definition_en: extremely difficult and demanding
entries.example_cn: 这段艰难的旅程考验着旅行者的耐力。
entries.example_en: The rugged journey tested the travelers' endurance.

entries.definition_cn: 表面有细长、狭窄的浅凹痕（如沟纹或皱褶）的
entries.definition_en: having long, narrow, shallow depressions, such as grooves or wrinkles, on the surface
entries.example_cn: 那件旧皮夹克粗糙的表面布满了细长的浅皱褶。
entries.example_en: The rugged surface of the old leather jacket was covered with long, shallow wrinkles.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is rough, uneven, or full of difficulties
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者艰难地爬上了陡峭的山路。
entries.example_en: The hikers climbed ruggedly up the steep mountain path.

entries.definition_en: the quality of having an uneven or rough surface
entries.example_cn: 地形的崎岖不平使得徒步旅行充满挑战。
entries.example_en: The ruggedness of the terrain made the hike challenging.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being tough, hardy, or robust
entries.example_cn: 登山者坚韧强健的体魄给大家留下了深刻印象。
entries.example_en: The ruggedness of the mountain climber impressed everyone.

entries.definition_cn: 环境等的艰苦、恶劣或难以忍受
entries.definition_en: the quality of being harsh, rough, or difficult to endure
entries.example_cn: 荒野环境的艰苦恶劣使这次探险难以忍受。
entries.example_en: The ruggedness of the wilderness made the expedition difficult to endure.

entries.definition_en: rugby, a form of football played with an oval ball
entries.example_cn: 球队为即将到来的橄榄球比赛进行了艰苦的训练。
entries.example_en: The team practiced hard for the upcoming rugger match.

entries.definition_en: having a surface that is ridged or wrinkled, especially referring to leaves
entries.example_cn: 这片古老叶子起皱的质地使得难以辨认其物种。
entries.example_en: The rugose texture of the ancient leaf made it difficult to identify the species.

entries.definition_en: destroy completely; damage irreparably
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨毁坏了那座旧桥。
entries.example_en: The storm ruined the old bridge.

entries.definition_en: reduce to bankruptcy
entries.example_cn: 公司因经济危机而破产。
entries.example_en: The company was ruined by the economic crisis.

entries.definition_en: reduce to ruins
entries.example_cn: 时间和忽视使这座历史古迹化为废墟。
entries.example_en: Time and neglect ruined the historic monument.

entries.definition_en: an irrecoverable state of devastation and destruction
entries.example_cn: 战争使这座城市彻底毁灭。
entries.example_en: The war left the city in total ruin.

entries.definition_en: a ruined building
entries.example_cn: 他们探索了那座古庙的废墟。
entries.example_en: They explored the ancient ruins of the temple.

entries.definition_cn: 导致严重麻烦、毁灭或失败的事物；祸根
entries.definition_en: something that causes serious trouble, destruction, or failure
entries.example_cn: 那起丑闻毁掉了他的事业。
entries.example_en: The scandal was the ruin of his career.

entries.definition_en: the process of becoming dilapidated
entries.example_cn: 这座城堡已经破败了几个世纪。
entries.example_en: The castle has been in a state of ruin for centuries.

entries.definition_en: destroy or cause to fail
entries.example_cn: 他糟糕的脾气毁了他的晋升机会。
entries.example_en: His bad temper ruined his chances of promotion.

entries.definition_en: a state of complete destruction that cannot be recovered
entries.example_cn: 战争给这座古城带来了彻底的毁灭。
entries.example_en: The war brought about the total ruination of the ancient city.

entries.definition_en: an event that causes destruction
entries.example_cn: 那场大火是博物馆收藏品的毁灭事件。
entries.example_en: The fire was the ruination of the museum's collection.

entries.definition_en: a loss of reputation or standing
entries.example_cn: 这桩丑闻导致他的政治声誉毁于一旦。
entries.example_en: The scandal led to the ruination of his political reputation.

entries.definition_cn: 通过毁坏或破坏某物而使其毁灭的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of destroying something by wrecking or ruining it
entries.example_cn: 蓄意毁坏这座建筑花了数月时间。
entries.example_en: The deliberate ruination of the building took months.

entries.definition_en: in a state of ruin; dilapidated
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子破败不堪，空置了多年。
entries.example_en: The old house stood ruined and empty for years.

entries.definition_en: bankrupt
entries.example_cn: 糟糕的投资使他破产了。
entries.example_en: His bad investments left him ruined.

entries.definition_cn: 因吸毒或饮酒而失去行动能力的（俚语）
entries.definition_en: incapacitated by drugs or alcohol (slang)
entries.example_cn: 那种危险的混合毒品让他失去行动能力，动弹不得。
entries.example_en: The dangerous mixture of drugs left him ruined and unable to move.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that destroys or ruins something.
entries.example_cn: 干旱是农民收成的毁灭者。
entries.example_en: The drought was the ruiner of the farmers' harvest.

entries.definition_en: the act of destroying or causing something to be wrecked
entries.example_cn: 这座历史建筑的毁坏令整个社区感到悲伤。
entries.example_en: The ruining of the historic building saddened the entire community.

entries.definition_cn: 代价高昂到会导致经济破产的
entries.definition_en: so costly as to cause financial ruin
entries.example_cn: 战争毁灭性的成本使这个国家的经济遭受重创。
entries.example_en: The ruinous cost of the war devastated the country's economy.

entries.definition_en: causing destruction or calamity
entries.example_cn: 那场致灾的风暴在几分钟内摧毁了整个村庄。
entries.example_en: The ruinous storm destroyed the entire village in minutes.

entries.definition_cn: 以毁灭性的方式或程度
entries.definition_en: in a ruinous manner or to a ruinous degree
entries.example_cn: 洪水水位暴涨，给沿海城镇造成了毁灭性破坏。
entries.example_en: The floodwaters rose ruinously high and damaged the coastal town.

entries.definition_en: a principle that governs behavior
entries.example_cn: 规定是要准时到达。
entries.example_en: The rule is to arrive on time.

entries.definition_en: a guide for action or conduct
entries.example_cn: 安全是实验室的首要准则。
entries.example_en: Safety is the first rule in the lab.

entries.definition_en: a principle in linguistics describing language use
entries.example_cn: 构成复数的语法规则很复杂。
entries.example_en: The rule for forming plurals is complex.

entries.definition_en: to have authority over a country or group
entries.example_cn: 他们统治了这个国家很多年。
entries.example_en: They ruled the country for many years.

entries.definition_en: to decide a case or issue formally, especially judicially
entries.example_cn: 法官裁定支持原告。
entries.example_en: The judge ruled in favor of the plaintiff.

entries.definition_en: to make a formal declaration or decision
entries.example_cn: 委员会对争端做出了裁定。
entries.example_en: The committee ruled on the dispute.

entries.definition_en: to be greater in number or importance
entries.example_cn: 红队控制了比赛。
entries.example_en: The red team ruled the game.

entries.definition_en: an example of how something should be done
entries.example_cn: 他的诚实是他人效仿的典范。
entries.example_en: His honesty is a rule for others to follow.

entries.definition_en: controlled or governed by a ruling authority
entries.example_cn: 这个国家几十年来一直由独裁者统治。
entries.example_en: The country has been ruled by a dictator for decades.

entries.definition_en: a straight edge used for drawing lines and measuring lengths
entries.example_cn: 请用尺子在纸上画一条直线。
entries.example_en: Please use a ruler to draw a straight line on the paper.

entries.definition_en: a person who rules or commands a country or group
entries.example_cn: 统治者就和平问题向全国发表了演讲。
entries.example_en: The ruler made a speech to the nation about peace.

entries.definition_en: the position or authority of a ruler
entries.example_cn: 这本书探讨了古代帝国统治权的复杂性。
entries.example_en: The book explores the complexities of rulership in ancient empires.

entries.definition_en: exercising power or authority
entries.example_cn: 执政党宣布了新经济政策。
entries.example_en: The ruling party announced new economic policies.

entries.definition_cn: （法院或其他权威机构的）裁决；裁定
entries.definition_en: an authoritative decision or order by a court or other authority
entries.example_cn: 法官向陪审团解释了该案的裁决。
entries.example_en: The judge explained the ruling in the case to the jury.

entries.definition_en: neat and tidy
entries.example_cn: 她把书桌收拾得整洁有序。
entries.example_en: She kept her desk ruly and organized.

usage.label: rare
usage.pattern: Rare adjective meaning neat and orderly.

entries.definition_cn: 用发酵的甘蔗汁或糖蜜蒸馏制成的烈酒
entries.definition_en: liquor distilled from fermented sugarcane juice or molasses
entries.example_cn: 他们晚餐时享用了一杯朗姆酒。
entries.example_en: They enjoyed a glass of rum with their dinner.

entries.definition_en: a card game based on collecting sets and sequences
entries.example_cn: 玩家们花了一下午玩“鲁姆”牌戏。
entries.example_en: The players spent the afternoon playing rum.

entries.definition_en: beyond or deviating from the usual or expected
entries.example_cn: 那是一个关于在老房子里看到鬼魂的离奇故事。
entries.example_en: It was a rum story about a ghost seen in the old house.

entries.definition_en: a ballroom dance based on the Cuban folk dance
entries.example_cn: 他们在舞厅表演了一段优美的伦巴舞。
entries.example_en: They performed a beautiful rumba in the ballroom.

entries.definition_en: syncopated music in duple time for dancing the rumba
entries.example_cn: 乐队演奏了一首欢快的伦巴舞曲。
entries.example_en: The band played a lively rumba.

entries.definition_en: a folk dance in duple time that originated in Cuba with Spanish and African elements; features complex footwork and violent movement
entries.example_cn: 古巴民间伦巴舞以其复杂的舞步为特征。
entries.example_en: The rumba features complex footwork.

entries.definition_en: dance the rumba
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在派对上跳伦巴舞。
entries.example_en: They decided to rumba at the party.

entries.definition_en: a loud, low, and dull continuous noise
entries.example_cn: 远处开始隆隆作响，打雷了。
entries.example_en: The thunder began to rumble in the distance.

entries.definition_en: a street fight or brawl
entries.example_cn: 两个当地帮派之间的斗殴震动了整个社区。
entries.example_en: The neighborhood was shaken by a rumble between two local gangs.

usage.label: slang
usage.pattern: a rumble meaning a street fight

entries.definition_cn: 马车后部的仆人或行李区
entries.definition_en: a servant's seat or luggage compartment in the rear of a carriage
entries.example_cn: 男仆坐在马车后部的座位上。
entries.example_en: The footman sat in the rumble of the carriage.

entries.definition_en: to make a low noise
entries.example_cn: 汽车引擎开始发出隆隆声。
entries.example_en: The car engine started to rumble.

entries.definition_en: to utter or emit low dull rumbling sounds
entries.example_cn: 火山开始发出令人不安的隆隆声。
entries.example_en: The volcano began to rumble ominously.

entries.definition_en: a loud, low, and dull continuous noise
entries.example_cn: 隆隆的雷声充满了天空。
entries.example_en: The rumbling of thunder filled the sky.

entries.definition_en: characterized by a continuous, full, and low-pitched throbbing sound
entries.example_cn: 隆隆行驶的列车震动了地板。
entries.example_en: The rumbling train shook the floorboards.

entries.definition_en: noisy and lacking in restraint or discipline
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喧闹无礼，在走廊里又跑又叫。
entries.example_en: The children were rumbustious, running and shouting through the hall.

entries.definition_en: the first compartment of the stomach in ruminant animals, where food is stored and regurgitated for chewing.
entries.example_cn: 牛的瘤胃储存尚未完全消化的食物，之后食物会被反刍为食团。
entries.example_en: The cow's rumen stores partially digested food before it is regurgitated as cud.

entries.definition_en: a hoofed mammal that chews cud and has a stomach divided into four compartments
entries.example_cn: 牛和羊是反刍动物，它们通过再次咀嚼食物来消化草料。
entries.example_en: Cows and sheep are ruminants that digest grass by chewing their food again.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of animals that chew cud
entries.example_cn: 反刍动物的消化系统专门用于分解坚韧的植物纤维。
entries.example_en: The ruminant digestive system is specialized for breaking down tough plant fibers.

entries.definition_en: think deeply and repeatedly about something
entries.example_cn: 她坐在窗边，沉思过去一年的事件。
entries.example_en: She sat by the window to ruminate on the events of the past year.

entries.definition_en: chew the partially digested food that has been brought back from the stomach
entries.example_cn: 牛在吃草后每天会反刍几个小时。
entries.example_en: Cows ruminate for several hours a day after eating grass.

entries.definition_en: a calm, lengthy, and intent consideration of something
entries.example_cn: 她整个晚上都在沉思自己的未来职业。
entries.example_en: She spent the evening in deep rumination about her future career.

entries.definition_cn: 持续、反复的消极思考或担忧；反刍思维
entries.definition_en: persistent, repetitive negative thinking or worrying
entries.example_cn: 对过去错误的反复消极思考让她夜不能寐。
entries.example_en: Rumination about her past mistakes kept her awake at night.

entries.definition_en: the act of chewing the cud by ruminant animals
entries.example_cn: 那头牛停止吃草开始反刍。
entries.example_en: The cow stopped grazing to engage in rumination.

entries.definition_cn: 反刍综合征（一种进食障碍）
entries.definition_en: an eating disorder involving repeated regurgitation of small amounts of food
entries.example_cn: 这名患者因反复反流食物而被诊断为反刍综合征。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with rumination disorder after repeatedly regurgitating food.

entries.definition_en: deeply or seriously thoughtful
entries.example_cn: 他沉思着，思考着那个复杂的问题。
entries.example_en: He sat in a ruminative mood, pondering the complex problem.

entries.definition_en: to search through things in a careless or haphazard way
entries.example_cn: 她在抽屉里胡乱翻找钥匙。
entries.example_en: She rummaged through the drawers looking for her keys.

usage.label: rummage through/in + place
usage.pattern: Sources w24411r4 and w24411r6 support this construction.

entries.definition_en: a thorough search that often causes disorder
entries.example_cn: 警察对嫌疑人的公寓进行了彻底搜查。
entries.example_en: The police conducted a rummage of the suspect's apartment.

entries.definition_en: a disorganized collection of miscellaneous objects
entries.example_cn: 阁楼里堆满了旧衣服和其他杂物。
entries.example_en: The attic was full of old clothes and other rummage.

entries.definition_cn: 通常带短柄或粗柄、用于盛酒精饮料的大酒杯
entries.definition_en: a large drinking glass, typically with a short or heavy stem, used for alcoholic drinks
entries.example_cn: 他们举起祝酒杯提议为新年干杯。
entries.example_en: They raised their rummers to propose a toast to the new year.

entries.definition_cn: 一种收集牌组或顺子的纸牌游戏
entries.definition_en: a card game based on collecting sets and sequences; the winner is the first to meld all their cards
entries.example_cn: 他们玩纸牌游戏直到深夜。
entries.example_en: They played rummy until late in the evening.

entries.definition_en: a chronic drinker
entries.example_cn: 他是一个酗酒者，大部分钱都花在酒上。
entries.example_en: He is a rummy who spends most of his money on alcohol.

entries.definition_cn: 古怪的；奇怪的（英国，非正式，过时）
entries.definition_en: peculiar or odd, especially in British colloquial dated usage
entries.example_cn: 这周天气异常，突然下起了暴风雨。
entries.example_en: The weather has been rummy this week, with sudden storms.

entries.definition_en: unverified news spread by word of mouth
entries.example_cn: 有谣言说首席执行官要离开公司。
entries.example_en: There is a rumor that the CEO is leaving the company.

entries.definition_en: to spread unverified news
entries.example_cn: 有传言说这家商店很快就要关门了。
entries.example_en: The store was rumored to be closing soon.

entries.definition_en: a story or idea that is reported to be true but has not been officially confirmed
entries.example_cn: 有谣言说公司明年将开设新分店。
entries.example_en: There is a rumour that the company will open a new branch next year.

usage.label: British spelling
usage.pattern: rumour is the Commonwealth spelling of rumor.

entries.definition_en: to spread unconfirmed stories or gossip
entries.example_cn: 人们开始散布谣言，说首席执行官要离开公司。
entries.example_en: People started to rumour that the CEO was leaving the firm.

entries.definition_en: the fleshy part of the human body that you sit on
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，他一屁股坐了下来。
entries.example_en: He sat on his rump after the long hike.

entries.definition_en: the part of an animal that corresponds to the human buttocks
entries.example_cn: 屠夫从牛的臀部切下肉来。
entries.example_en: The butcher cut the meat from the rump of the cow.

entries.definition_en: fleshy hindquarters; behind the loin and above the round
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐点了份臀肉牛排。
entries.example_en: We ordered a rump steak for dinner.

entries.definition_en: to disturb the smoothness or neatness of something
entries.example_cn: 请在我铺床之前不要把床单弄皱。
entries.example_en: Please do not rumple the sheets before I make the bed.

entries.definition_en: to gather something into small wrinkles or folds
entries.example_cn: 她小心地将织物弄皱以创造出有纹理的图案。
entries.example_en: She carefully rumpled the fabric to create a textured pattern.

entries.definition_en: to become wrinkled, crumpled, or creased
entries.example_cn: 风从窗户吹进来时，纸张开始变皱。
entries.example_en: The paper began to rumple as the wind blew through the window.

entries.definition_cn: 起皱的；皱巴巴的；外表不整洁的
entries.definition_en: wrinkled or crumpled; untidy in appearance
entries.example_cn: 长途旅行后，他皱巴巴的衬衫穿在身上显得很不整洁。
entries.example_en: His rumpled shirt hung untidily after the long journey.

entries.definition_en: a loud and disorderly disturbance
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在客厅里大吵大闹。
entries.example_en: The children caused a rumpus in the living room.

entries.definition_en: to create a loud and disorderly disturbance
entries.example_cn: 当音乐停止时，参加聚会的人们开始大吵大闹。
entries.example_en: The partygoers began to rumpus when the music stopped.

entries.definition_en: move fast by using one's feet, with one foot off the ground at any given time
entries.example_cn: 她决定跑去赶公交车。
entries.example_en: She decided to run to catch the bus.

entries.definition_en: direct or control; projects, businesses, etc.
entries.example_cn: 他在市中心经营一家成功的餐厅。
entries.example_en: He runs a successful restaurant in the city center.

entries.definition_en: stretch out over a distance, space, time, or scope; run or extend between two points or beyond a certain point
entries.example_cn: 这条路沿着海岸延伸了数英里。
entries.example_en: The road runs along the coast for miles.

entries.definition_en: flee; take to one's heels; cut and run
entries.example_cn: 当敌人逼近时，士兵们不得不逃跑。
entries.example_en: The soldiers had to run when the enemy approached.

entries.definition_en: an act or period of running
entries.example_cn: 他们一起参加了晨跑。
entries.example_en: They entered the morning run together.

entries.definition_en: an unbroken series of events
entries.example_cn: 我们这周运气一直不好。
entries.example_en: We had a run of bad luck this week.

entries.definition_en: an execution of a program or process
entries.example_cn: 软件的一次运行发现了一个严重错误。
entries.example_en: The software run revealed a critical bug.

entries.definition_en: a score in baseball made by a runner touching all four bases safely
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一局得了一分。
entries.example_en: The team scored a run in the final inning.

entries.definition_cn: 疲惫不堪的；筋疲力尽的
entries.definition_en: Tired and exhausted.
entries.example_cn: 工作了一整夜后，她已经筋疲力尽了。
entries.example_en: After working all night, she was completely run-down.

entries.definition_en: worn and broken down by hard use
entries.example_cn: 那辆旧车看起来非常破旧。
entries.example_en: The old car looked very run-down.

entries.definition_en: having the spring unwound
entries.example_cn: 手表停了，因为发条松开了。
entries.example_en: The watch stopped because it was run-down.

entries.definition_en: an encounter or dispute, especially one involving trouble
entries.example_cn: 他们上周与警察发生了冲突。
entries.example_en: They had a run-in with the police last week.

entries.definition_cn: （比赛等的）最后阶段；冲刺阶段
entries.definition_en: The final stage of a competition or other event.
entries.example_cn: 这支球队进入最后阶段时，仍很有希望赢得联赛冠军。
entries.example_en: The team entered the run-in with a strong chance of winning the league.

entries.definition_en: ordinary and lacking any special quality
entries.example_cn: 这部电影只是一部平庸的动作片，没有任何惊喜。
entries.example_en: The movie was just a run-of-the-mill action film with no surprises.

entries.definition_en: continuing beyond the end of a poetic line without a rhetorical pause
entries.example_cn: 这首诗用跨行来营造连续不断的节奏。
entries.example_en: The poem uses run-on lines to create a continuous flow.

entries.definition_en: an uninterrupted rehearsal
entries.example_cn: 演员们在演出前对剧本进行了连贯排练。
entries.example_en: The actors did a run-through of the play before the opening.

entries.definition_cn: 对某事要点的简要概述；提纲
entries.definition_en: A brief outline or summary of the main points of something.
entries.example_cn: 经理向我们简要介绍了新的安全操作流程。
entries.example_en: The manager gave us a run-through of the new safety procedures.

entries.definition_en: the time when a computer program is being executed
entries.example_cn: 该应用程序的运行时间非常短。
entries.example_en: The run-time of the application is very short.

entries.definition_en: the length of time needed to run a software program
entries.example_cn: 我们需要优化代码以减少程序运行时长。
entries.example_en: We need to optimize the code to reduce the run-time.

entries.definition_en: a large increase in something over a short time
entries.example_cn: 新税实施前价格出现了激增。
entries.example_en: There was a run-up in prices before the new tax was introduced.

entries.definition_en: the distance an athlete runs to build up speed before jumping or throwing
entries.example_cn: 跳高运动员在越过横杆前助跑了很长一段距离。
entries.example_en: The high jumper took a long run-up before clearing the bar.

entries.definition_cn: 小型车辆；（尤指）短途使用的小汽车
entries.definition_en: a small vehicle, especially a small motor car for short journeys
entries.example_cn: 他们开着那辆复古的敞篷小轿车沿着海岸公路行驶。
entries.example_en: They drove their vintage runabout down the coastal highway.

entries.definition_en: out of control; unchecked or accelerating uncontrollably
entries.example_cn: 失控的通货膨胀使物价大幅上涨。
entries.example_en: Runaway inflation pushed prices sharply higher.

entries.definition_en: a person who leaves home or a situation to escape it
entries.example_cn: 那个离家出走的人在附近的一个小镇被找到了。
entries.example_en: The runaway was found safe in a nearby town.

entries.definition_en: a victory that is much larger than the opponent's score
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛中取得了大胜。
entries.example_en: The team secured a runaway victory in the final match.

entries.definition_en: one of the crossbars that form the steps of a ladder
entries.example_cn: 那架旧木梯靠近顶部的一根横档断了。
entries.example_en: The old wooden ladder had a broken rundle near the top.

usage.label: obsolete
usage.pattern: historical term for a ladder rung

entries.definition_cn: 主题、情况、案件或论点的要点概述
entries.definition_en: a summary or outline of the main points of a topic, situation, case, or argument
entries.example_cn: 律师在陪审团面前详细概述了证据。
entries.example_en: The lawyer gave a detailed rundown of the evidence before the jury.

entries.definition_cn: 古日耳曼文字系统中的一个字母或字符，尤指斯堪的纳维亚和盎格鲁-撒克逊文字中的
entries.definition_en: a letter or character in an ancient Germanic writing system, especially that of the Scandinavians and Anglo-Saxons
entries.example_cn: 维京人在石头上刻了一个卢恩字母来标记他的领地。
entries.example_en: The Viking carved a rune into the stone to mark his territory.

entries.definition_cn: 用作魔法或神秘象征的符号或字符
entries.definition_en: a mark or character used as a magical or mystical symbol
entries.example_cn: 算命师在卡片上画了一个作为神秘象征的符文。
entries.example_en: The fortune-teller used a rune as a mystical symbol on the card.

entries.definition_cn: Go 语言中作为 int32 类型别名、用于表示 Unicode 码点的类型
entries.definition_en: in Go, an alias for the int32 type used to represent a Unicode code point
entries.example_cn: 在 Go 语言中，rune 类型是 int32 的别名，可以表示一个 Unicode 码点。
entries.example_en: In Go, the rune type is an alias for int32 and can represent a Unicode code point.

entries.definition_en: one of the steps on a ladder
entries.example_cn: 她爬上梯子的第一级梯级，以便够到顶层架子。
entries.example_en: She climbed the first rung of the ladder to reach the top shelf.

entries.definition_en: a position or level in a hierarchy
entries.example_cn: 她从公司等级体系的最低层级开始。
entries.example_en: She started at the lowest rung of the corporate hierarchy.

entries.definition_en: a horizontal bar connecting the legs of a chair
entries.example_cn: 这把椅子在座位附近有一个低矮的木制椅档，可以用来搁脚。
entries.example_en: The chair had a low wooden rung near the seat for resting feet.

entries.definition_en: relating to or written in runes
entries.example_cn: 那块古老的石头上刻着神秘的符文铭文。
entries.example_en: The ancient stone was covered in mysterious runic inscriptions.

entries.definition_en: a small stream of water
entries.example_cn: 一条细细的小溪顺着岩壁流淌下来。
entries.example_en: A thin runnel of water trickled down the rock face.

entries.definition_cn: 供水流过的小人工水渠
entries.definition_en: a small artificial channel for water to flow in
entries.example_cn: 园丁挖了一条小水渠，把雨水引离小路。
entries.example_en: The gardeners dug a runnel to carry rainwater away from the path.

entries.definition_en: a person who travels by running
entries.example_cn: 这名跑步者在不到三小时内完成了马拉松。
entries.example_en: The runner finished the marathon in under three hours.

entries.definition_en: a trained athlete who competes in foot races
entries.example_cn: 这名赛跑运动员赢得了100米短跑金牌。
entries.example_en: The runner won the gold medal in the 100-meter dash.

entries.definition_en: a baseball player who is on base or trying to reach a base
entries.example_cn: 跑垒员安全滑垒到了二垒。
entries.example_en: The runner slid safely into second base.

entries.definition_en: in football, the player carrying the ball during an offensive play
entries.example_cn: 持球进攻球员突破了防线并达阵得分。
entries.example_en: The runner broke through the defense and scored a touchdown.

entries.definition_en: a person employed to deliver messages or documents
entries.example_cn: 信使把紧急信件送到了经理办公室。
entries.example_en: The runner brought the urgent letter to the manager's office.

entries.definition_en: a horizontal plant branch that grows from the base and produces new plants
entries.example_cn: 草莓因为长长的匍匐茎而迅速蔓延。
entries.example_en: Strawberries spread quickly because of their long runners.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow carpet
entries.example_cn: 她为走廊买了一条新的长条地毯，以保护地板。
entries.example_en: She bought a new runner for the hallway to protect the floor.

entries.definition_en: a person who imports or exports goods without paying the required taxes
entries.example_cn: 海关官员逮捕了这名走私电子产品的走私者。
entries.example_en: The customs officer arrested the runner for smuggling electronics.

entries.definition_en: the competitor who finishes second
entries.example_cn: 我们的队在国家象棋锦标赛中获得亚军。
entries.example_en: Our team was the runner-up in the national chess championship.

entries.definition_en: the act of running; traveling on foot at a fast pace
entries.example_cn: 我喜欢早晨跑步。
entries.example_en: I enjoy the running in the morning.

entries.definition_en: the state of being in operation
entries.example_cn: 经营这家企业需要周密的计划。
entries.example_en: The running of the business requires careful planning.

entries.definition_cn: 管理或负责某事的行为
entries.definition_en: the act of administering or being in charge of something
entries.example_cn: 项目的管理落在了经理身上。
entries.example_en: The running of the project fell to the manager.

entries.definition_cn: （美式足球）持球突破或跑过对方防守的战术
entries.definition_en: (American football) a play in which a player attempts to carry the ball through or past the opposing team
entries.example_cn: 四分卫完成了一次长距离持球推进。
entries.example_en: The quarterback made a long running play.

entries.definition_en: continuing or ongoing over a period of time
entries.example_cn: 主持人在整场比赛中持续进行评论。
entries.example_en: The host provided a running commentary throughout the match.

entries.definition_en: (of fluids) moving or issuing in a stream
entries.example_cn: 水龙头流出的水是凉的。
entries.example_en: The running water from the tap was cold.

entries.definition_en: of advancing the ball by running
entries.example_cn: 球的推进对于得分至关重要。
entries.example_en: The running of the ball was crucial for the score.

entries.definition_cn: 通过跑动执行或发起的
entries.definition_en: executed or initiated by running
entries.example_cn: 赛跑的发起是以发令枪开始的。
entries.example_en: The running of the race started with a gun.

entries.definition_en: having a consistency that allows a substance to flow easily and change shape
entries.example_cn: 这汤太稀了，没法用勺子吃。
entries.example_en: The soup was too runny to eat with a spoon.

entries.definition_en: water that flows over the ground because there is too much of it
entries.example_cn: 大雨导致危险的径流涌入河流。
entries.example_en: Heavy rain caused a dangerous runoff into the river.

entries.definition_en: a second election held to choose a winner when no candidate wins enough votes in the first
entries.example_cn: 决选将于下个月举行。
entries.example_en: The runoff election will be held next month.

entries.definition_en: diarrhea (informal, often plural)
entries.example_cn: 食物中毒让我腹泻了。
entries.example_en: The food poisoning gave me the runs.

usage.label: informal slang, usually plural and with the

entries.definition_en: plural of run
entries.example_cn: 这支球队在比赛中进行了几次冲刺。
entries.example_en: The team made several runs during the game.

entries.definition_cn: run 的第三人称单数一般现在时形式
entries.definition_en: third-person singular simple present of run
entries.example_cn: 她每天早上上班前都跑步。
entries.example_en: She runs every morning before work.

entries.definition_cn: 矮小或发育不良的人（常含贬义）
entries.definition_en: an undersized or stunted person, often used disparagingly
entries.example_cn: 教练称那个异常矮小的新秀为小个子。
entries.example_en: The coach called the unusually short rookie a runt.

entries.definition_en: much smaller than average in height or size
entries.example_cn: 那只矮小的幼犬躲在妈妈的腿后面。
entries.example_en: The runty puppy hid behind its mother's legs.

entries.definition_en: of inferior size or stature, especially when referring to people
entries.example_cn: 与队友相比，他对自己矮小的身材感到不自在。
entries.example_en: He felt self-conscious about his runty appearance compared to his teammates.

entries.definition_en: a substantial increase over a relatively short period of time
entries.example_cn: 在市场崩盘之前，该公司经历了利润的大幅增长。
entries.example_en: The company experienced a significant runup in profits before the market crash.

entries.definition_en: a strip of level paved surface where planes can take off and land
entries.example_cn: 飞机在雨刚开始时下落在跑道上。
entries.example_en: The plane touched down on the runway just as the rain started.

entries.definition_en: a narrow platform extending from the stage into the audience in a theater or nightclub
entries.example_cn: 演员走上伸台向欢呼的人群致辞。
entries.example_en: The actor stepped onto the runway to address the cheering crowd.

entries.definition_en: a bar or pair of parallel bars of rolled steel that form a railway for railroad cars or other vehicles to roll on
entries.example_cn: 这家旧工厂使用钢轨来运输重型机械。
entries.example_en: The old factory used a runway to transport heavy machinery.

entries.definition_en: a chute down which logs can slide
entries.example_cn: 工人们把原木顺着滑木槽推到了河边。
entries.example_en: The workers pushed the logs down the runway to the river.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of India, equal to 100 paise
entries.example_cn: 出租车司机要求用卢比付款。
entries.example_en: The taxi driver asked for payment in rupees.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Pakistan, equal to 100 paisa
entries.example_cn: 市场上蔬菜卖几卢比。
entries.example_en: The market sells vegetables for a few rupees.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Nepal, equal to 100 paisa
entries.example_cn: 他用卢比支付了餐费。
entries.example_en: He paid for the meal with rupees.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Sri Lanka, equal to 100 cents
entries.example_cn: 她前往斯里兰卡前将美元兑换成了卢比。
entries.example_en: She exchanged her dollars for rupees before traveling to Sri Lanka.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Mauritius, equal to 100 cents
entries.example_cn: 他们用卢比计算了总费用。
entries.example_en: They calculated the total cost in rupees.

entries.definition_en: the basic monetary unit of Seychelles, equal to 100 cents
entries.example_cn: 这个纪念品的价格是五卢比。
entries.example_en: The price of the souvenir was five rupees.

entries.definition_en: the basic unit of money in Indonesia; equal to 100 sen
entries.example_cn: 这个纪念品的价格是五百印尼盾。
entries.example_en: The price of the souvenir was five hundred rupiah.

entries.definition_en: a hole or tear in something that has broken open
entries.example_cn: 管道爆裂导致墙壁出现裂口。
entries.example_en: The pipe burst and caused a rupture in the wall.

entries.definition_en: a break in a relationship or alliance between people or groups
entries.example_cn: 这两个国家正处于外交关系破裂的边缘。
entries.example_en: The two countries are on the verge of a diplomatic rupture.

entries.definition_cn: 突然破裂或爆裂的过程或事件
entries.definition_en: the act or process of breaking or bursting suddenly
entries.example_cn: 大坝突然破裂，释放出数百万加仑的水。
entries.example_en: The sudden rupture of the dam released millions of gallons of water.

entries.definition_en: to separate or cause to separate abruptly
entries.example_cn: 地震导致大坝破裂。
entries.example_en: The earthquake caused a rupture in the dam.

entries.definition_en: relating to the countryside rather than the city
entries.example_cn: 他们搬到了乡村地区享受新鲜空气。
entries.example_en: They moved to a rural area to enjoy the fresh air.

entries.definition_en: an advocate of rural living
entries.example_cn: 这位乡村生活倡导者认为搬到乡下会改善心理健康。
entries.example_en: The ruralist argued that moving to the countryside would improve mental health.

entries.definition_cn: 乡下人；具有乡村习性的人
entries.definition_en: a person who lives in the country and has country ways
entries.example_cn: 这位乡下人拒绝使用智能手机，更喜欢他老式的方法。
entries.example_en: The ruralist refused to use the smartphone, preferring his old-fashioned methods.

entries.definition_en: a rural characteristic or trait
entries.example_cn: 这项研究考察了乡村特性对当地经济发展的影响。
entries.example_en: The study examined the impact of rurality on local economic development.

entries.definition_en: in a rural manner
entries.example_cn: 该地区许多家庭过着乡村生活，自己种植大部分食物。
entries.example_en: Many families in the region live rurally, growing much of their own food.

entries.definition_en: a deceptive maneuver, especially to avoid capture
entries.example_cn: 这名士兵用诡计骗敌人放松了警惕。
entries.example_en: The soldier used a ruse to trick the enemy into lowering their guard.

entries.definition_en: move hurriedly
entries.example_cn: 我们必须匆忙赶去坐最后一班公交车。
entries.example_en: We had to rush to catch the last bus.

entries.definition_en: urge someone to proceed with undue haste
entries.example_cn: 教练催促球员们尽快完成训练。
entries.example_en: The coach rushed the players to finish the drill.

entries.definition_en: attack suddenly
entries.example_cn: 那只狗突然向入侵者扑去。
entries.example_en: The dog rushed at the intruder.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving hurriedly and in a careless manner
entries.example_cn: 火车离开前，人们争先恐后地赶往车站。
entries.example_en: There was a rush to get to the station before the train left.

entries.definition_en: a sudden forceful flow
entries.example_cn: 一股水流突然涌入地下室。
entries.example_en: A rush of water flooded the basement.

entries.definition_cn: 匆忙完成的；在压力下完成的
entries.definition_en: done under pressure
entries.example_cn: 这份报告是匆忙赶出来的，包含许多错误。
entries.example_en: The report was a rush job and contained many errors.

entries.definition_cn: 生长在水湿地方的草状植物，具有圆柱形且常为中空的茎
entries.definition_en: grasslike plants growing in wet places and having cylindrical often hollow stems
entries.example_cn: 沼泽地里长满了高高的灯心草。
entries.example_en: The marsh was filled with tall rushes.

entries.definition_en: not accepting reservations
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅不接受预订，所以你必须早点到达。
entries.example_en: The restaurant is a rush, so you must arrive early.

entries.definition_en: done quickly because of pressure or lack of time
entries.example_cn: 这份报告是仓促完成的，包含了几处错误。
entries.example_en: The report was rushed and contained several errors.

entries.definition_en: a person who acts too quickly or without thinking.
entries.example_cn: 别这么鲁莽；花时间仔细计划一下。
entries.example_en: Don't be such a rusher; take your time to plan carefully.

entries.definition_cn: （美式足球）冲传手；负责冲向并擒杀对方四分卫的防守球员
entries.definition_en: a defensive football player whose objective is to rush toward and sack the opposing quarterback
entries.example_cn: 冲传手突破锋线，擒杀了四分卫。
entries.example_en: The rusher broke through the line and sacked the quarterback.

entries.definition_en: a person who moves quickly to a new place to seek opportunity.
entries.example_cn: 许多淘金者涌向西部的新金矿。
entries.example_en: Many rushers flocked to the new gold fields in the west.

entries.definition_en: a rapid surging or rushing movement
entries.example_cn: 河水的奔涌使渡河变得十分危险。
entries.example_en: The rushing of the river made it dangerous to cross.

entries.definition_cn: 美式足球中试图通过冲撞防线推进球的行为
entries.definition_en: an attempt to advance the ball by running into the line in American football
entries.example_cn: 四分卫进行了一次冒险的冲球尝试，结果达阵得分。
entries.example_en: The quarterback made a risky rushing play that resulted in a touchdown.

entries.definition_en: a candle made by soaking dried rush pith in fat or grease
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一盏古代用于照明的灯芯草烛。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed an ancient rushlight used for illumination.

entries.definition_en: abounding in rushes
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，沼泽地变得长满了灯心草。
entries.example_en: The marshland became very rushy after the heavy rains.

entries.definition_cn: 硬而干的饼干或烤脆面包片
entries.definition_en: a hard, dry biscuit or twice-baked slice of bread
entries.example_cn: 他早上喝茶时吃了一片烤脆面包片。
entries.example_en: He ate a rusk with his morning tea.

entries.definition_en: of brown with a reddish tinge
entries.example_cn: 枫树褐红色的叶子标志着秋天的到来。
entries.example_en: The russet leaves of the maple tree signaled the arrival of fall.

entries.definition_en: a reddish brown homespun fabric
entries.example_cn: 裁缝用红褐色粗布制作了这件斗篷。
entries.example_en: The tailor used russet, a coarse reddish-brown homespun fabric, for the cloak.

entries.definition_en: a reddish-brown powder that forms on iron when it is exposed to air and water.
entries.example_cn: 那辆旧车布满了铁锈。
entries.example_en: The old car was covered in rust.

entries.definition_cn: 铁或钢因接触氧气和湿气而生成的红褐色氧化层
entries.definition_en: a red or brown coating that forms on iron or steel when exposed to oxygen and moisture
entries.example_cn: 那辆旧自行车的车架上有一层厚厚的锈迹。
entries.example_en: The old bicycle had a thick layer of rust on its frame.

entries.definition_en: to become covered with a reddish-brown flaky substance caused by oxidation
entries.example_cn: 这把旧铁门被雨淋后开始生锈了。
entries.example_en: The old iron gate began to rust after being left outside in the rain.

entries.definition_en: to become covered with a reddish-brown flaky substance caused by reaction with oxygen and moisture.
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，那扇旧铁门开始生锈了。
entries.example_en: The old iron gate began to rust after the heavy rain.

entries.definition_cn: 使因水、空气或酸的作用而恶化
entries.definition_en: to cause something to deteriorate because of water, air, or acid.
entries.example_cn: 酸会使金属表面生锈。
entries.example_en: The acid will rust the metal surface.

entries.definition_en: having the brownish-red color of iron oxide
entries.example_cn: 那扇锈色的金属门看起来很旧。
entries.example_en: The rust-colored metal gate looked very old.

entries.definition_en: a plant disease causing reddish-brown spots on leaves and stems
entries.example_cn: 农民发现小麦叶子上出现了锈病。
entries.example_en: The farmer noticed that rust appeared on the wheat leaves.

entries.definition_en: a type of fungus that causes a disease in plants
entries.example_cn: 小麦叶片上的锈病真菌在潮湿季节迅速蔓延。
entries.example_en: The rust on the wheat leaves spread quickly during the humid season.

entries.definition_en: covered with rust
entries.example_cn: 那辆旧车看起来糟透了，因为它完全生锈了。
entries.example_en: The old car looked terrible because it was completely rusted.

entries.definition_en: having a style or quality typical of rural life
entries.example_cn: 他们用乡村风格的家具和木梁装饰了房子。
entries.example_en: They decorated the house with rustic furniture and wooden beams.

entries.definition_en: simple and provincial in a way that is awkward or clumsy
entries.example_cn: 这部戏剧是一次粗俗的喜剧尝试，未能逗乐观众。
entries.example_en: The play was a rustic attempt at comedy that failed to amuse the audience.

entries.definition_en: roughly finished or simple in a rural style
entries.example_cn: 小屋的内部装饰粗朴简陋。
entries.example_en: The cabin had a rustic, roughly finished interior.

entries.definition_en: a person from the countryside who is considered unsophisticated
entries.example_cn: 城里人觉得这个乡下人天真得可笑。
entries.example_en: The city dwellers found the rustic amusingly naive.

entries.definition_cn: 在农村居住并过田园生活
entries.definition_en: to live in the country and lead a rustic life
entries.example_cn: 许多艺术家选择去农村居住以寻找灵感。
entries.example_en: Many artists choose to rusticate in the countryside to find inspiration.

entries.definition_en: to send someone to the country
entries.example_cn: 严厉的学校长决定将违反规定的学生送往农村。
entries.example_en: The strict headmaster decided to rusticate the student for breaking the rules.

entries.definition_cn: （英国用法）暂时停学或开除某人
entries.definition_en: to suspend or expel someone temporarily from a college or university (British usage)
entries.example_cn: 由于学术不端行为，他被停学一年。
entries.example_en: Due to academic misconduct, he was rusticated from the university for one year.

entries.definition_cn: 使石材表面粗糙或呈强烈纹理
entries.definition_en: to give stone a jagged or heavily textured surface
entries.example_cn: 石匠将石块加工得表面粗糙、纹理强烈。
entries.example_en: The mason rusticated the blocks to give them a jagged, heavily textured surface.

entries.definition_en: to lend a rustic character to something
entries.example_cn: 园丁将栅栏加工成乡村风格，使其与自然环境融为一体。
entries.example_en: The gardeners rusticated the fence to blend with the natural surroundings.

entries.definition_en: temporary dismissal of a student from a university
entries.example_cn: 由于多次违反行为准则，该学生面临停学处分。
entries.example_en: The student faced rustication due to repeated violations of the code of conduct.

entries.definition_cn: 粗面石工；粗面建筑处理
entries.definition_en: the treatment of masonry with recessed joints to give it a rustic appearance
entries.example_cn: 花园围墙采用了带凹缝的粗面建筑处理。
entries.example_en: The garden wall featured rustication with recessed joints.

entries.definition_en: the action of retiring to and living in the country
entries.example_cn: 退休后，他选择了隐居乡间，搬到了一个小村庄。
entries.example_en: After his retirement, he embraced the rustication of moving to a small village.

entries.definition_en: the natural condition of living in the country
entries.example_cn: 他在乡村生活中找到了内心的宁静。
entries.example_en: He found a sense of peace in the rustication of his rural life.

entries.definition_en: banishment into the country
entries.example_cn: 国王下令将叛徒流放到偏远的乡村地区。
entries.example_en: The king ordered the traitor's rustication to a remote rural district.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being rustic or gauche
entries.example_cn: 家具的粗犷风格很适合那座老房子。
entries.example_en: The rusticity of the furniture suited the old house.

entries.definition_en: a lack of skill or confidence due to not practicing for a long time
entries.example_cn: 他多年未弹钢琴，琴技生疏的迹象显而易见。
entries.example_en: His rustiness at the piano was evident after years of not playing.

entries.definition_en: the state of being covered or blocked by rust
entries.example_cn: 旧铁门的生锈状态使其难以打开。
entries.example_en: The rustiness of the old iron gate made it difficult to open.

entries.definition_en: the process of iron forming reddish-brown oxides when exposed to water and air
entries.example_cn: 这座桥因咸湿的海风而加速生锈。
entries.example_en: The rusting of the bridge has been accelerated by the salty sea air.

entries.definition_en: to make a dry crackling sound
entries.example_cn: 风吹过森林时，干树枝发出沙沙声。
entries.example_en: The dry branches rustled as the wind blew through the forest.

entries.definition_cn: 兴冲冲地弄到或准备（尤指食物）
entries.definition_en: to obtain or prepare something, especially food, in a lively or energetic way
entries.example_cn: 他们弄了顿饭，然后骑马出发了。
entries.example_en: They rustled up a meal before setting off on horseback.

entries.definition_en: to steal something illegally
entries.example_cn: 小偷从外套口袋里偷走了钱包。
entries.example_en: The thief rustled the wallet from the coat pocket.

entries.definition_en: a light, dry sound made by moving fabric or leaves
entries.example_cn: 风使灌木丛中的干树叶发出沙沙声。
entries.example_en: The wind made the dry leaves rustle in the bushes.

entries.definition_cn: 偷窃牲畜的人，尤指偷牛贼
entries.definition_en: a person who steals livestock, particularly cattle
entries.example_cn: 那位牛仔追踪了偷走牧场牛群的偷牛贼。
entries.example_en: The cowboy tracked the rustler who had stolen the herd from the ranch.

entries.definition_en: a series of soft rustling sounds
entries.example_cn: 老师批改试卷时，我们听到了纸张的沙沙声。
entries.example_en: We heard the rustling of paper as the teacher graded the exams.

entries.definition_en: the rounding up and theft of cattle or other animals
entries.example_cn: 偷牛在该地区成为一个严重的问题。
entries.example_en: The rustling of cattle became a serious problem in the region.

entries.definition_en: characterized by soft sounds
entries.example_cn: 沙沙作响的树叶表明有一阵微风。
entries.example_en: The rustling leaves indicated a gentle breeze.

entries.definition_en: protected or treated so that it will not rust
entries.example_cn: 这辆车涂有特殊的防锈涂层，以延长使用寿命。
entries.example_en: The car was treated with a special rustproof coating to last longer.

entries.definition_en: covered with a reddish-brown substance formed by oxidation
entries.example_cn: 那扇旧大门锈迹斑斑。
entries.example_en: The old gate was covered in rust.

entries.definition_en: having lost skill due to lack of practice
entries.example_cn: 多年没说法语，我的法语有点生疏了。
entries.example_en: My French is a bit rusty after years of not speaking it.

entries.definition_en: having the color of rust
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一条锈红色的围巾。
entries.example_en: She wore a rusty red scarf.

entries.definition_cn: （历史用语，尤指深色衣物）破旧的；破败的
entries.definition_en: historical: of clothing, especially dark clothing, worn or shabby
entries.example_cn: 他穿着一件破旧而不成形的黑夹克。
entries.example_en: He wore a black jacket, rusty and shapeless.

entries.definition_cn: 单调的惯例；循规蹈矩的生活
entries.definition_en: a dull and unchanging routine that is difficult to escape
entries.example_cn: 她觉得自己被困在日复一日的单调生活中。
entries.example_en: She felt trapped in the rut of her daily life.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow hole or groove made in soft ground by wheels
entries.example_cn: 卡车在泥地里留下了深深的辙印。
entries.example_en: The truck left deep ruts in the mud.

entries.definition_en: a period of heightened sexual arousal in nonhuman mammals
entries.example_cn: 发情期是许多物种交配的关键时期。
entries.example_en: The rut is a critical time for mating in many species.

entries.definition_en: to be in a state of sexual excitement (of male mammals)
entries.example_cn: 鹿在秋季发情。
entries.example_en: The deer rutted during the autumn season.

entries.definition_en: to make a groove or furrow in the ground
entries.example_cn: 大雨使土壤形成沟槽。
entries.example_en: Heavy rain ruts the soil.

entries.definition_cn: 用作食物的芜菁甘蓝的黄色块根
entries.definition_en: the large yellow root of a rutabaga plant used as food
entries.example_cn: 我们烤了芜菁甘蓝，配上黄油和香草作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We roasted rutabaga with butter and herbs for dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 一种具有厚实球状可食用黄色块根的十字花科植物
entries.definition_en: a cruciferous plant with a thick bulbous edible yellow root
entries.example_cn: 农民在秋天种植芜菁甘蓝，以便在冬天收获。
entries.example_en: The farmer planted rutabaga in the fall to harvest in winter.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of sympathy and sorrow for the misfortunes of others
entries.example_cn: 她对灾难的受害者深感怜悯。
entries.example_en: She felt deep ruth for the victims of the disaster.

entries.definition_cn: 一种稀有的铂族金属元素，常与铂伴生
entries.definition_en: a rare metallic element of the platinum group found associated with platinum
entries.example_cn: 钌通常与铂一起出现在矿藏中。
entries.example_en: Ruthenium is often found in deposits alongside platinum.

entries.definition_cn: 已废弃的放射性活度单位（卢瑟福），等于每秒一百万次衰变
entries.definition_en: an obsolete unit of radioactivity equal to one million disintegrations per second
entries.example_cn: 该样品的放射性活度以卢瑟福为单位测量。
entries.example_en: The sample's activity was measured in rutherfords.

entries.definition_en: showing no mercy or pity
entries.example_cn: 那个无情的老板毫无预警地解雇了所有员工。
entries.example_en: The ruthless boss fired all the staff without warning.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that shows no pity or mercy
entries.example_cn: 为了熬过经济衰退，该公司无情地削减了成本。
entries.example_en: The company ruthlessly cut costs to survive the economic downturn.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being merciless and showing no pity
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨的残忍使村庄化为废墟。
entries.example_en: The ruthlessness of the storm left the village in ruins.

entries.definition_en: feelings of extreme heartlessness
entries.example_cn: 他在商业决策中的冷酷无情震惊了同事们。
entries.example_en: His ruthlessness in business decisions shocked his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: a mineral made of titanium dioxide found in crystalline form within certain rocks
entries.example_cn: 地质学家研究金红石以提取工业用钛。
entries.example_en: Geologists study rutile to extract titanium for industrial use.

entries.definition_en: full of ruts
entries.example_cn: 那条旧路布满车辙，很难驾驶。
entries.example_en: The old road was rutted and difficult to drive on.

entries.definition_en: having many ruts or depressions in the ground
entries.example_cn: 坑洼不平的道路让汽车难以行驶。
entries.example_en: The rutty road made it difficult for the car to drive.

entries.definition_cn: 斯堪的纳维亚式打结绒面羊毛地毯，可用作床罩或挂毯
entries.definition_en: a Scandinavian knotted-pile woollen rug, used as a bedcover or tapestry
entries.example_cn: 他们买了一块传统的瑞典粗毛地毯铺在木地板上。
entries.example_en: They bought a traditional rya to cover the wooden floor.

entries.definition_cn: 里德伯单位：等于里德伯常数的波数单位，用于原子物理学
entries.definition_en: a unit of wavenumber equal to the Rydberg constant, used in atomic physics
entries.example_cn: 氢原子的光谱线通常用里德伯单位来测量。
entries.example_en: The spectral lines of hydrogen are often measured in rydberg units.

entries.definition_en: the seed of a cereal grass
entries.example_cn: 农民在第一次霜冻前收割了黑麦。
entries.example_en: The farmer harvested the rye before the first frost.

entries.definition_en: a hardy cereal grass grown for grain, forage, or soil improvement
entries.example_cn: 黑麦在欧洲北部被广泛种植用于制作黑面包。
entries.example_en: Rye is widely cultivated in northern Europe for making black bread.

entries.definition_en: whiskey distilled from rye or a mixture of rye and malt
entries.example_cn: 他更喜欢黑麦威士忌而不是其他类型的威士忌。
entries.example_en: He prefers a strong rye over other types of whiskey.

entries.definition_en: a type of Eurasian grass often used for pasture
entries.example_cn: 农民种植黑麦草来喂养牛群。
entries.example_en: The farmer planted ryegrass to feed the cattle.

entries.definition_en: the nineteenth letter of the Roman alphabet
entries.example_cn: S是罗马字母表的第19个字母。
entries.example_en: S is the 19th letter of the Roman alphabet.

entries.definition_en: the direction on a compass that is exactly opposite to north
entries.example_cn: 南是罗盘上180度的基本方位点。
entries.example_en: S is the cardinal compass point at 180 degrees.

entries.definition_en: a chemical element that is a yellow crystal and is found in many minerals
entries.example_cn: 硫是一种在火山地区发现的非金属元素。
entries.example_en: S is a nonmetallic element found in volcanic regions.

entries.definition_en: a thermodynamic quantity representing energy unavailable for mechanical work
entries.example_cn: S是一个代表不可用能量的热力学量。
entries.example_en: S is a thermodynamic quantity representing unavailable energy.

entries.definition_en: a unit of electrical conductance equal to one divided by an ohm
entries.example_cn: 单位S代表电导单位。
entries.example_en: The unit S represents a unit of conductance.

entries.definition_en: a Nazi paramilitary organization founded by Hitler in 1921
entries.example_cn: 冲锋队在希特勒于20世纪30年代初掌权的过程中发挥了关键作用。
entries.example_en: The SA played a key role in Hitler's rise to power in the early 1930s.

entries.definition_cn: 北约欧洲盟军最高司令官
entries.definition_en: the Supreme Allied Commander Europe, NATO's senior military commander in Europe
entries.example_cn: 盟军最高司令官负责监督北约在欧洲战区的军事行动。
entries.example_en: The SACEUR oversees all NATO military operations in the European theater.

entries.definition_en: a guided missile fired from land or shipboard against an airborne target
entries.example_cn: 飞行员必须躲避从地面发射的导弹。
entries.example_en: The pilot had to evade the SAMs firing from the ground.

entries.definition_en: severe acute respiratory syndrome, an infectious respiratory disease caused by the SARS coronavirus (SARS-CoV)
entries.example_cn: 卫生官员正在监测该地区严重急性呼吸综合征的传播情况。
entries.example_en: Health officials are monitoring the spread of SARS in the region.

entries.definition_en: a special British army unit trained for secret military operations, especially against terrorists
entries.example_cn: 特种空勤团被部署去营救人质。
entries.example_en: The SAS was deployed to rescue the hostages.

entries.definition_en: a bachelor's degree in science
entries.example_cn: 他获得了物理学科学学士学位。
entries.example_en: He received his SB in physics.

entries.definition_en: an independent US government agency that protects small businesses and ensures they get a fair share of government contracts
entries.example_cn: 小企业管理局提供贷款以帮助中小企业从经济衰退中恢复。
entries.example_en: The SBA provides loans to help small businesses recover from economic downturns.

entries.definition_en: a permanent council of the United Nations responsible for preserving world peace
entries.example_cn: 联合国安理会就冲突问题进行了投票。
entries.example_en: The SC voted on the resolution regarding the conflict.

entries.definition_cn: 分配给航天器上某一事件的时间，即航天器事件时间
entries.definition_en: the time assigned to an event at a spacecraft
entries.example_cn: 任务时间表已与航天器事件时间（SCET）同步。
entries.example_en: The mission timeline was synchronized to SCET.

entries.definition_en: a congenital disease affecting T cells that can result from a mutation in any one of several different genes; children with it are susceptible to infectious disease; if untreated it is lethal within the first year or two of life
entries.example_cn: 这名婴儿被诊断出患有重症联合免疫缺陷病，需要立即治疗。
entries.example_en: The infant was diagnosed with SCID and required immediate treatment.

entries.definition_cn: 海军或海岸警卫队的高级军士长
entries.definition_en: a senior noncommissioned officer in the Navy or Coast Guard with a rank comparable to master sergeant in the Army
entries.example_cn: 这位高级军士长监督着年轻水手的训练。
entries.example_en: The SCPO supervised the training of the junior sailors.

entries.definition_en: a standard interface port used to connect a computer with its peripheral devices
entries.example_cn: 这台老式计算机使用小型计算机系统接口来连接硬盘和扫描仪。
entries.example_en: The vintage computer used a SCSI interface to connect its hard drive and scanner.

entries.definition_en: the compass point midway between south and east
entries.example_cn: 风正从东南方向吹来。
entries.example_en: The wind is blowing from the SE.

entries.definition_en: a member of a special military unit trained for unconventional warfare
entries.example_cn: 海豹突击队执行了一次敌后的秘密行动。
entries.example_en: The SEALs conducted a covert operation behind enemy lines.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用于生物战的葡萄球菌肠毒素
entries.definition_en: a type of staphylococcal enterotoxin used as an incapacitating agent in biological warfare
entries.example_cn: SEB 因其作为生物武器的潜在用途而受到调查。
entries.example_en: SEB was investigated for its potential use as a biological weapon.

entries.definition_en: an independent federal agency that oversees the exchange of securities to protect investors
entries.example_cn: 证券交易委员会宣布了新法规以保护小投资者。
entries.example_en: The SEC announced new regulations to protect small investors.

entries.definition_en: the compass point located one point east of southeast
entries.example_cn: 船只向东南偏东方向航行以避开风暴。
entries.example_en: The ship sailed towards the SEbE to avoid the storm.

entries.definition_en: the compass point that is one point south of southeast
entries.example_cn: 船只向东南偏南方向航行以避开风暴。
entries.example_en: The ship sailed towards SEbS to avoid the storm.

entries.definition_en: a standardized computer language used to describe and mark up documents
entries.example_cn: 该文档使用 SGML 编写，以确保在不同系统中格式一致。
entries.example_en: The document was written in SGML to ensure consistent formatting across different systems.

entries.definition_en: the frequency range from 3 to 30 gigahertz
entries.example_cn: 工作在超高频波段的雷达系统需要精确校准。
entries.example_en: Radar systems operating in the SHF band require precise calibration.

entries.definition_en: a complete system of units for scientists based on seven fundamental quantities
entries.example_cn: 科学家使用国际单位制以确保他们的测量结果在全球范围内一致。
entries.example_en: Scientists use the SI system to ensure their measurements are consistent worldwide.

entries.definition_en: the sudden and unexpected death of a healthy baby while sleeping
entries.example_cn: 医生仍在研究婴儿猝死综合征的原因。
entries.example_en: Doctors are still researching the causes of SIDS.
