entries.definition_en: to ridicule someone or something using satire
entries.example_cn: 这位漫画家决定讽刺这位政治家的新政策。
entries.example_en: The cartoonist decided to satirize the politician's new policy.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of happiness because your wishes or needs have been met
entries.example_cn: 她对新的结果表示满意。
entries.example_en: She expressed her satisfaction with the new results.

entries.definition_en: the state of being pleased or content
entries.example_cn: 看到自己的工作完成，他感到非常满意。
entries.example_en: The satisfaction of seeing his work completed was great.

entries.definition_en: something given to make up for a mistake or wrong
entries.example_cn: 公司就损坏的商品提供了全额赔偿。
entries.example_en: The company offered a full satisfaction for the damaged goods.

entries.definition_en: the act of paying a debt or fulfilling a legal obligation
entries.example_cn: 债务的清偿记录在法院文件中。
entries.example_en: The satisfaction of the debt was recorded in the court documents.

entries.definition_en: the act of fulfilling a desire, need, or appetite
entries.example_cn: 消除饥饿是人类的基本需求。
entries.example_en: The satisfaction of hunger is a basic human need.

entries.definition_en: in a satisfactory manner
entries.example_cn: 该项目在截止日期前令人满意地完成了。
entries.example_en: The project was completed satisfactorily within the deadline.

entries.definition_en: meeting the necessary requirements or standards
entries.example_cn: 安全检查符合要求。
entries.example_en: The safety inspection was satisfactory.

entries.definition_en: giving satisfaction or pleasure
entries.example_cn: 结果令人满意，尽管并不完美。
entries.example_en: The results were satisfactory, though not perfect.

entries.definition_en: able to be satisfied
entries.example_cn: 旅行者的饥饿感无法仅靠一顿饭来满足。
entries.example_en: The hunger of the travelers was not satisfiable by a single meal.

entries.definition_en: feeling contentment because your needs or wishes have been met
entries.example_cn: 她对实验结果感到满意。
entries.example_en: She was satisfied with the results of the experiment.

entries.definition_en: convinced that something is true
entries.example_cn: 警方确信嫌疑人已经逃离了该地区。
entries.example_en: The police were satisfied that the suspect had fled the area.

entries.definition_en: meet the requirements or expectations of
entries.example_cn: 测试结果满足了安全标准。
entries.example_en: The test results satisfied the safety standards.

entries.definition_en: make happy or satisfied
entries.example_cn: 惊喜派对满足了她庆祝的愿望。
entries.example_en: The surprise party satisfied her wish for celebration.

entries.definition_cn: 填满、满足或符合某种需求、条件或限制
entries.definition_en: fill, satisfy or meet a want or need or condition or restriction
entries.example_cn: 这顿大餐完全满足了他的饥饿感。
entries.example_en: The large meal satisfied his hunger completely.

entries.definition_cn: 令人满意的；令人满足的
entries.definition_en: pleasing or fulfilling because it meets a need or removes a feeling of lack
entries.example_cn: 这个解释令人满意，因为它回答了我们所有的问题。
entries.example_en: The explanation was satisfying because it answered all of our questions.

entries.definition_cn: 令人愉悦的（尤指听觉或触觉上）
entries.definition_en: pleasing to the senses, especially hearing or touch
entries.example_cn: 这种柔和而有节奏的声音听起来非常令人愉悦。
entries.example_en: The soft, rhythmic sound was deeply satisfying to listen to.

entries.definition_en: in a way that gives a feeling of pleasure or contentment
entries.example_cn: 经过数小时的工作，谜题终于令人满意地解开了。
entries.example_en: The puzzle was solved satisfyingly after hours of work.

entries.definition_en: a sudden realization or enlightenment in Zen Buddhism
entries.example_cn: 经过多年的冥想，他终于开悟了。
entries.example_en: After years of meditation, he finally experienced satori.

entries.definition_en: a governor of a province in ancient Persia
entries.example_cn: 总督代表波斯国王从遥远的省份征收赋税。
entries.example_en: The satrap collected taxes from the distant provinces on behalf of the Persian king.

entries.definition_cn: （贬义，喻）听命于更有权势者的下属统治者
entries.definition_en: (derogatory, figurative) a subordinate ruler, especially one who obeys a more powerful leader
entries.example_cn: 独裁者身边聚集着一群执行其命令的下属统治者。
entries.example_en: The dictator surrounded himself with satraps who carried out his orders.

entries.definition_cn: 萨摩蜜柑的果实，通常少籽，果皮薄而光滑且易剥
entries.definition_en: the fruit of a largely seedless mandarin cultivar with thin, smooth, easy-peeling skin
entries.example_cn: 篮子里装满了多汁的橘子。
entries.example_en: The basket was filled with juicy satsumas.

entries.definition_cn: 一种日本原产的柑橘品种，即萨摩蜜柑
entries.definition_en: a variety of mandarin orange of Japanese origin, also called a satsuma mandarin
entries.example_cn: 她剥开一个甜美的萨摩蜜柑当早餐吃。
entries.example_en: She peeled a sweet satsuma and ate it for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: to infuse or fill completely
entries.example_cn: 房间里充满了新鲜咖啡的香气。
entries.example_en: The room was saturated with the smell of fresh coffee.

entries.definition_en: to cause a substance to unite with the greatest possible amount of another substance
entries.example_cn: 海绵吸饱了水。
entries.example_en: The sponge was saturated with water.

entries.definition_en: containing the maximum amount of dissolved substance possible at a given temperature
entries.example_cn: 溶液已饱和，不能再溶解更多的盐。
entries.example_en: The solution was saturated with salt, so no more could dissolve.

entries.definition_en: a flavorful liquid or paste served with food to add taste

entries.example_en: You can sauce the chicken with your favorite barbecue sauce.

entries.definition_en: to make something more interesting or exciting

entries.example_en: The director decided to sauce the film with some unexpected twists.

entries.definition_en: to behave in a rude or disrespectful way towards someone

entries.example_en: Don't sauce the waiter; he is just doing his job.

entries.example_en: She picked up the saucer and set it on the table.

entries.definition_cn: 碟形物；圆而浅的曲面物体

entries.example_en: The mysterious saucer-shaped object hovered silently above the field.

entries.example_en: The children rode their plastic saucers down the snowy hill.

entries.definition_en: having large, round, wide-open eyes

entries.example_en: The saucer-eyed child stared at the magician with wonder.

entries.definition_cn: 无礼或放肆的举止；淘气劲

entries.example_en: The child's sauciness amused the adults at the dinner party.

entries.definition_en: impertinently forward or disrespectful

entries.example_en: The saucy remark made the teacher angry.

entries.definition_en: cheerfully bold and lively in a playful way

entries.definition_en: morally wholesome or acceptable
entries.example_cn: 该组织提倡一种道德上健康或可接受的社区服务方式。
entries.example_en: The organization promotes a savory approach to community service.

entries.definition_en: to enjoy the taste of something
entries.example_cn: 她细细品味着最后一口巧克力蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She savoured the last bite of the chocolate cake.

entries.definition_en: to have a particular taste
entries.example_cn: 炖菜带有大蒜和香草的味道。
entries.example_en: The stew savoured of garlic and herbs.

entries.definition_en: to take pleasure in something
entries.example_cn: 他享受着夜晚的宁静时光。
entries.example_en: He savoured the quiet moments of the evening.

entries.definition_en: to give a particular taste to something
entries.example_cn: 香草使肉带上浓郁的泥土香味。
entries.example_en: The herbs savoured the meat with a rich, earthy flavour.

entries.definition_en: the taste of food or drink
entries.example_cn: 这汤的味道浓郁而令人舒适。
entries.example_en: The savour of the soup was rich and comforting.

entries.definition_en: the act of taking a small amount of food into the mouth to taste it
entries.example_cn: 他停下来细细品尝那块浓郁的巧克力，然后才吞下去。
entries.example_en: He paused for a savouring of the rich chocolate before swallowing it.

entries.definition_cn: 味道浓郁而宜人的；带有宜人辛香味的
entries.definition_en: having an agreeably pungent taste
entries.example_cn: 这种奶酪具有令人愉悦的辛辣味。
entries.example_en: The cheese has a savoury flavor.

entries.definition_cn: 味道宜人的，通常指咸味或辛辣而非甜味的
entries.definition_en: having a pleasant, usually salty or spicy rather than sweet, taste
entries.example_cn: 这道咸味菜肴非常美味。
entries.example_en: The savoury dish was delicious.

entries.definition_cn: 道德上健康的或可接受的
entries.definition_en: morally wholesome or acceptable
entries.example_cn: 这个故事包含一个道德上健康的教训。
entries.example_en: The story had a savoury moral lesson.

entries.definition_en: an aromatic or spicy dish served at the end of dinner or as an hors d'oeuvre
entries.example_cn: 我们点了一道咸味小吃作为开胃菜。
entries.example_en: We ordered a savoury to start the meal.

entries.definition_cn: 冬香薄荷或夏香薄荷（两种芳香草本植物之一）
entries.definition_en: either of two aromatic herbs of the mint family
entries.example_cn: 她在汤里加了一枝香薄荷。
entries.example_en: She added a sprig of savoury to the soup.

entries.definition_en: a head of soft, crinkly green leaves
entries.example_cn: 厨师用新鲜的皱叶甘蓝做了一道沙拉。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a salad with fresh savoy leaves.

entries.definition_en: practical knowledge and shrewdness
entries.example_cn: 她很有商业头脑。
entries.example_en: She has real business savvy.

entries.definition_en: to understand the meaning or significance of something
entries.example_cn: 直到他解释后，我才明白那个笑话。
entries.example_en: I didn't savvy the joke until he explained it.

entries.definition_en: to cut something using a saw
entries.example_cn: 他把木头锯成了小块。
entries.example_en: He saw the wood into small pieces.

entries.definition_cn: 带有锯齿刀片的手持切割工具
entries.definition_en: a hand tool with a toothed blade for cutting
entries.example_cn: 她用一把手锯切断了树枝。
entries.example_en: She used a hand saw to cut the branch.

entries.definition_cn: 表达重要真理的简短格言
entries.definition_en: a short, memorable saying expressing an important truth
entries.example_cn: 那位老人告诉我们一句关于耐心的智慧格言。
entries.example_en: The old man told us a wise saw about patience.

entries.definition_cn: 由电力或其他电机驱动的锯
entries.definition_en: a saw powered by electricity or another motor
entries.example_cn: 木匠启动了电动锯。
entries.example_en: The carpenter started the electric saw.

entries.definition_en: having a jagged edge with sharp points like the teeth of a saw
entries.example_cn: 锯齿状的屋顶轮廓在街上清晰可见。
entries.example_en: The saw-toothed roofline was visible from the street.

entries.definition_en: a surgeon (slang)
entries.example_cn: 这位外科医生以高超的技巧完成了这次困难的手术。
entries.example_en: The sawbones performed the difficult operation with great skill.

entries.definition_en: a frame used to hold wood steady while it is being sawed
entries.example_cn: 木匠在切割原木前将其夹紧在锯架上。
entries.example_en: The carpenter clamped the log into the sawbuck before cutting it.

entries.definition_en: fine particles of wood made by sawing wood
entries.example_cn: 木匠扫掉了地板上的锯末。
entries.example_en: The carpenter swept up the sawdust from the floor.

entries.definition_en: shortened by sawing
entries.example_cn: 这把锯短枪管的霰弹枪是违法的，因为较短的枪管使它太容易隐藏。
entries.example_en: The sawed-off shotgun was illegal because its shorter barrel made it too easy to conceal.

entries.definition_en: short, as though truncated
entries.example_cn: 他个子矮小，是个小不点，但这个小个子气势十足，没人敢对他怎么样。
entries.example_en: He was a sawed-off runt, just a little guy, but he packed so much attitude into that little package that no one was going to make anything about it.

entries.definition_en: a primitive ray with sharp teeth along the edges of its long, flattened snout
entries.example_cn: 锯鳐用它长长的吻部搅动沙子来寻找猎物。
entries.example_en: The sawfish uses its long snout to stir up sand and find prey.

entries.definition_en: an insect whose female has a saw-like organ for laying eggs inside plant leaves or stems
entries.example_cn: 叶蜂的幼虫正在吃橡树叶。
entries.example_en: The sawfly larvae are feeding on the oak leaves.

entries.definition_en: a framework used to hold wood while it is being sawed
entries.example_cn: 木匠把木板放在锯木架上以便切割。
entries.example_en: The carpenter placed the board on the sawhorse to cut it.

entries.definition_cn: 伊斯兰教的斋戒，尤指斋月期间的禁食；伊斯兰教五功之一
entries.definition_en: the Islamic practice of fasting, especially during Ramadan; the fourth of the Five Pillars of Islam
entries.example_cn: 在斋月期间，穆斯林通过禁食和禁饮来履行斋戒。
entries.example_en: During the month of Ramadan, Muslims observe the sawm by abstaining from food and drink.

entries.definition_en: a factory where logs are cut and processed into lumber
entries.example_cn: 他们将原木运送到木材加工厂进行加工。
entries.example_en: They transported the logs to the sawmill for processing.

entries.definition_cn: 用于把木材锯成木板的机器
entries.definition_en: a machine used for cutting wood into boards or planks
entries.example_cn: 这台便携式锯木机把原木锯成了木板。
entries.example_en: The portable sawmill cut the logs into planks.

entries.definition_en: to process lumber in a sawmill
entries.example_cn: 工人们在锯木厂把原木加工成木板。
entries.example_en: The workers sawmill the logs into boards.

entries.definition_en: cut short or shortened
entries.example_cn: 这根被截短的树枝太小，没什么用处。
entries.example_en: The sawn-off branch was too small to be useful.

entries.definition_en: of a firearm, having had its stock or barrel shortened by sawing
entries.example_cn: 他把一把锯短的霰弹枪藏在外套下。
entries.example_en: He carried a sawn-off shotgun under his coat.

entries.definition_en: a serration on a saw blade
entries.example_cn: 锋利的锯齿轻易地切穿了木头。
entries.example_en: The sharp sawtooth cut through the wood easily.

entries.definition_en: a wave with a repeating sawtooth-shaped pattern
entries.example_cn: 合成器产生了明亮的锯齿波。
entries.example_en: The synthesizer generated a bright sawtooth wave.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job is to cut wood into pieces using a saw
entries.example_cn: 那位老锯木工人整天在森林里工作。
entries.example_en: The old sawyer worked in the forest all day.

entries.definition_cn: 一种幼虫会在枯死树木中钻孔的甲虫
entries.definition_en: a type of beetle whose larvae make holes in dead or dying trees
entries.example_cn: 锯天牛侵扰了院子里的枯松树。
entries.example_en: Sawyer beetles infested the dead pine trees in the yard.

entries.definition_en: a single-reed woodwind instrument with a conical bore
entries.example_cn: 爵士乐队里有一位才华横溢的萨克斯管手。
entries.example_en: The jazz band featured a talented sax player.

entries.definition_en: any plant belonging to the genus Saxifraga
entries.example_cn: 生长在岩石裂缝中的虎耳草属植物有着精致的白色花朵。
entries.example_en: The saxifrage growing in the rock crevice has delicate white flowers.

entries.definition_en: a very strong poison made by certain sea algae that can build up in shellfish and cause food poisoning in humans
entries.example_cn: 健康警告建议不要吃被石房蛤毒素污染的贝类。
entries.example_en: The health warning advised against eating shellfish contaminated with saxitoxin.

entries.definition_en: a musical instrument with a conical metal tube and a single reed mouthpiece
entries.example_cn: 爵士乐队有一位才华横溢的萨克斯管演奏家。
entries.example_en: The jazz band featured a talented saxophone player.

entries.definition_en: a musician who plays the saxophone
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的萨克斯管演奏家在爵士音乐会上进行了独奏。
entries.example_en: The famous saxophonist performed a solo at the jazz festival.

entries.definition_en: to express thoughts in words
entries.example_cn: 请向你妈妈问好。
entries.example_en: Please say hello to your mother.

entries.definition_en: to report or maintain a belief
entries.example_cn: 他说他很累。
entries.example_en: He says he is tired.

entries.definition_en: to have a specific wording
entries.example_cn: 合同上写着“概不退款”。
entries.example_en: The contract says 'no refunds'.

entries.definition_en: to give orders
entries.example_cn: 老板命令道：“更加努力工作。”
entries.example_en: The boss said, “Work harder.”

entries.definition_en: to communicate without words
entries.example_cn: 她的眼神表明她很生气。
entries.example_en: Her eyes said she was angry.

entries.definition_en: the opportunity to speak
entries.example_cn: 现在轮到你发表意见了。
entries.example_en: It is your turn to have your say.

entries.definition_en: to express a guess or opinion
entries.example_cn: 我猜会下雨。
entries.example_en: I say it will rain.

entries.definition_en: to pronounce words
entries.example_cn: 你能说“苹果”吗？
entries.example_en: Can you say 'apple'?

entries.definition_en: one chap's arbitrary assertion
entries.example_cn: 别信他武断的说法。
entries.example_en: Don't believe his say-so.

entries.definition_en: an authoritative statement or command
entries.example_cn: 经理的批准就足以核准这次购买。
entries.example_en: The manager's say-so was enough to approve the purchase.

entries.definition_cn: 发号施令或作决定的权力；许可
entries.definition_en: the authority or permission to give orders or make decisions
entries.example_cn: 在这件事上他有发号施令的权力。
entries.example_en: He has the say-so in this matter.

entries.definition_en: a proverb, maxim, or commonly repeated phrase
entries.example_cn: 有一句中国谚语：“千里之行，始于足下。”
entries.example_en: There is a Chinese saying: “A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.”

entries.definition_en: Used to say goodbye or farewell.
entries.example_cn: 火车开走时，她喊道：“再见！”
entries.example_en: “Sayonara!” she called as the train pulled away.

entries.definition_en: a remark used to say goodbye
entries.example_cn: 他挥手告别，离开车站时大喊再见。
entries.example_en: He waved goodbye and shouted sayonara as he left the station.

entries.definition_en: a hard crust that forms on a wound as it heals
entries.example_cn: 她小心翼翼地抠掉了膝盖上的痂。
entries.example_en: She carefully picked at the scab on her knee.

entries.definition_cn: 罢工破坏者；在罢工期间继续工作或替代罢工者的人
entries.definition_en: a person who works during a strike, often replacing striking workers
entries.example_cn: 工会谴责了那个在其他人抗议时继续工作的罢工破坏者。
entries.example_en: The union condemned the scab who continued to work while others protested.

entries.definition_en: to form a scab on a wound
entries.example_cn: 他手指上的伤口几天后开始结痂。
entries.example_en: The cut on his finger began to scab over after a few days.

entries.definition_cn: 充当罢工破坏者；顶替罢工者工作
entries.definition_en: to take the place of work of someone on strike
entries.example_cn: 公司雇佣了一名顶班者来填补罢工员工留下的空缺。
entries.example_en: The company hired a scab to fill the gap left by the striking employees.

entries.definition_en: a sheath for a sword or dagger or bayonet
entries.example_cn: 士兵在行军前仔细擦拭了他的剑鞘。
entries.example_en: The soldier carefully cleaned his scabbard before marching.

entries.definition_en: covered with scabs
entries.example_cn: 那只狗在腿上有一处因打斗而结痂的伤口。
entries.example_en: The dog had a scabby wound on its leg from the fight.

entries.definition_cn: 由疥螨寄生引起、导致剧烈瘙痒和皮肤刺激的疥疮
entries.definition_en: an infestation of itch mites causing intense itching and skin irritation
entries.example_cn: 该患者在被诊断为这种传染性皮肤病后接受了疥疮治疗。
entries.example_en: The patient was treated for scabies after being diagnosed with the contagious skin infection.

entries.definition_en: a plant of the genus Scabiosa, often known as pincushion flower
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了精致的蓝色山萝卜花。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with the delicate blue scabiosa.

entries.definition_en: any plant belonging to the genus Scabiosa
entries.example_cn: 花园里开满了五颜六色的山萝卜属植物。
entries.example_en: The garden was filled with colorful scabious flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 由冰川或冰川洪水冲蚀形成、土层薄且沟槽深的高平火成岩荒地
entries.definition_en: high, flat igneous-rock land with thin soil and deep channels cut by glaciers or glacial floods
entries.example_cn: 这片古老的洪水冲蚀岩地很久以前由巨大的洪水雕刻而成。
entries.example_en: The ancient scabland was carved by massive floods long ago.

entries.definition_en: dealing with salacious or indecent material
entries.example_cn: 该杂志因其淫秽内容而被禁止发行。
entries.example_en: The magazine was banned for its scabrous content.

entries.definition_en: having a rough surface; covered with scales or scurf
entries.example_cn: 老树粗糙的树皮使得攀爬变得困难。
entries.example_en: The scabrous skin of the old tree made it difficult to climb.

entries.definition_cn: 【北美，非正式】大量；许多，通常用复数
entries.definition_en: North American informal: a large amount or number, usually used in the plural.
entries.example_cn: 她在衣服上花很多钱。
entries.example_en: She spends scads of money on clothes.

entries.definition_en: a fish belonging to the family Carangidae
entries.example_cn: 渔民经常在海岸附近捕获成群的鲹科鱼类。
entries.example_en: Fishermen often catch scad in large schools near the coast.

entries.definition_en: a temporary structure made of scaffolding for workers to stand on while working on a building
entries.example_cn: 工人们爬上脚手架粉刷屋顶。
entries.example_en: Workers climbed the scaffold to paint the roof.

entries.definition_en: a platform from which criminals are executed (hanged or beheaded)
entries.example_cn: 刑台矗立在广场中央。
entries.example_en: The scaffold stood in the center of the square.

entries.definition_en: provide with a scaffold for support
entries.example_cn: 他们用脚手架支撑旧桥以便进行维修。
entries.example_en: They scaffolded the old bridge to allow repairs.

entries.definition_en: a temporary structure of poles and platforms used for supporting workers during construction
entries.example_cn: 工人们爬上脚手架给大楼外墙刷漆。
entries.example_en: The workers climbed the scaffolding to paint the building's exterior.

entries.definition_en: street slang for heroin
entries.example_cn: 警方正试图追踪该街区海洛因的来源。
entries.example_en: The police were trying to track down the source of the scag in the neighborhood.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being scalable
entries.example_cn: 该软件的可扩展性使其能够处理数百万用户。
entries.example_en: The scalability of the software allows it to handle millions of users.

entries.definition_en: capable of being scaled; possible to scale
entries.example_cn: 这种软件架构具有高度的可扩展性。
entries.example_en: The software architecture is highly scalable.

usage.label: often used of systems or software

entries.definition_en: a quantity that has magnitude but no direction
entries.example_cn: 在物理学中，质量是一个标量，而力则是矢量。
entries.example_en: In physics, mass is a scalar quantity, unlike force which is a vector.

entries.definition_en: having magnitude but no direction
entries.example_cn: 速度是一个无方向的数值，因为它描述了物体运动的快慢，而不指示方向。
entries.example_en: Speed is a scalar value because it describes how fast an object moves without indicating direction.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to a musical scale
entries.example_cn: 作曲家创作了一首音阶式的旋律，该旋律在大调音阶中逐级进行。
entries.example_en: The composer wrote a scalar melody that moved stepwise through the major scale.

entries.definition_cn: 支持美国南北战争后重建政策的南方白人（通常出于私利）
entries.definition_en: a white Southerner who supported Reconstruction policies after the American Civil War, usually for self-interest
entries.example_cn: 这位历史学家称该政治家为背叛社区以谋取私利的南方叛徒。
entries.example_en: The historian described the politician as a scalawag who betrayed his community for personal gain.

usage.label: 美国；历史；贬义
usage.pattern: 历史上指支持重建政策的南方白人

entries.definition_en: a deceitful and unreliable scoundrel
entries.example_cn: 别相信他；他是个诡诈又不可靠的无赖，会偷走你的钱。
entries.example_en: Don't trust him; he is a scalawag who will steal your money.

entries.definition_en: one who is playfully mischievous
entries.example_cn: 孩子们像顽童一样到处乱跑，制造麻烦。
entries.example_en: The children were acting like scalawags, running around and causing trouble.

entries.definition_en: a burn caused by hot liquid or steam
entries.example_cn: 他不小心泼了开水，手臂上受了严重的烫伤。
entries.example_en: He suffered a severe scald on his arm after spilling boiling water.

entries.definition_en: the act of burning something with steam or hot water
entries.example_cn: 牛奶的烫损了汤的质地。
entries.example_en: The scald of the milk ruined the texture of the soup.

entries.definition_en: burn or injure with hot liquid or steam
entries.example_cn: 婴儿的皮肤被热水烫伤了。
entries.example_en: The baby's skin was scalded by the hot bathwater.

entries.definition_en: heat a liquid almost to boiling
entries.example_cn: 将牛奶加热至刚要沸腾，直到出现小气泡。
entries.example_en: Scald the milk until little bubbles form.

entries.definition_en: treat with boiling water, usually to clean or prepare food
entries.example_cn: 农民在加工前用沸水处理羊毛以去除油脂。
entries.example_en: Farmers scald the wool to remove the grease before processing.

entries.definition_en: subject to harsh criticism or ridicule
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家在辩论中遭到了反对派的严厉批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was scalded by the opposition during the debate.

entries.definition_en: a system of numbers or marks used to measure or compare something
entries.example_cn: 地震的震级被评定为 1 到 10 级。
entries.example_en: The earthquake was measured on a scale of 1 to 10.

entries.definition_en: the size or amount of something compared to a standard
entries.example_cn: 这个项目已经达到了很大的规模。
entries.example_en: The project has reached a large scale.

entries.definition_en: the ratio between the size of an object and its drawing or model
entries.example_cn: 这张地图的比例尺是 1:50,000。
entries.example_en: The map is drawn to a scale of 1:50,000.

entries.definition_en: to adjust or arrange something according to a specific rate or standard
entries.example_cn: 该公司按比例扩大了生产以满足增加的需求。
entries.example_en: The company scaled its production to meet the increased demand.

entries.definition_en: to climb a wall or other steep surface using ladders or ropes
entries.example_cn: 士兵们在夜间攀上了悬崖。
entries.example_en: The soldiers scaled the cliff during the night.

entries.definition_en: to climb to the top of something
entries.example_cn: 登山者在中午前登上了珠穆朗玛峰。
entries.example_en: The climbers scaled Everest before noon.

entries.definition_en: to measure something using a scale
entries.example_cn: 我们需要准确地称量配料来做这道菜。
entries.example_en: We need to scale the ingredients accurately for the recipe.

entries.definition_en: a small leaf or bract that protects a flower bud
entries.example_cn: 随着花朵开放，苞片脱落了。
entries.example_en: The scale fell off the bud as the flower opened.

entries.definition_en: covered with thin horny plates like fish or reptiles
entries.example_cn: 鱼身上覆鳞的皮肤在阳光下闪闪发亮。
entries.example_en: The fish's scaled skin shimmered in the sunlight.

entries.definition_en: covered with overlapping metal plates attached to leather
entries.example_cn: 骑士身穿覆甲以在战斗中保护自己。
entries.example_en: The knight wore a scaled armor to protect himself in battle.

entries.definition_en: lacking scales
entries.example_cn: 鳗鱼是无鳞鱼，可以挤过细小的裂缝。
entries.example_en: Eels are scaleless fish that can squeeze through small cracks.

entries.definition_en: describing a triangle where all three sides have different lengths
entries.example_cn: 建筑师画了一个不等边三角形，以确保屋顶没有对称的支撑。
entries.example_en: The architect drew a scalene triangle to ensure the roof had no symmetrical supports.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to any of the scalene muscles
entries.example_cn: 物理治疗侧重于加强斜角肌，以缓解颈部疼痛。
entries.example_en: Physical therapy focused on strengthening the scalene muscles to relieve neck pain.

entries.definition_cn: 电子脉冲计数器（用于计数发生过快而无法单独记录的脉冲）
entries.definition_en: an electronic pulse counter used to count pulses that occur too rapidly to be recorded individually
entries.example_cn: 工程师将电子脉冲计数器连接到高频信号发生器上，以测量脉冲频率。
entries.example_en: The engineer connected the scaler to the high-frequency signal generator to measure the pulse rate.

entries.definition_en: having the body covered with thin horny plates, like some fish or reptiles
entries.example_cn: 那种古老的爬行动物覆着鳞片，鳞片保护着它的皮肤。
entries.example_en: The ancient reptile was scaley, with plates protecting its skin.

entries.definition_cn: 按比例测量、排列或调整
entries.definition_en: the act of measuring or arranging or adjusting according to a scale
entries.example_cn: 将模型按比例调整以适应房间很困难。
entries.example_en: The scaling of the model to fit the room was difficult.

entries.definition_cn: 数据缩放；按比例调整数据
entries.definition_en: the process of scaling or adjusting data, especially to fit a desired distribution
entries.example_cn: 考试分数的缩放处理十分谨慎。
entries.example_en: The scaling of the exam scores was done carefully.

entries.definition_en: ascent by or as if by a ladder
entries.example_cn: 攀登那座山花了一整天。
entries.example_en: The scaling of the mountain took them all day.

entries.definition_cn: 葱，尤指Allium fistulosum；有细长白色基部和中空圆筒形绿叶，可用于烹饪
entries.definition_en: a spring onion, especially Allium fistulosum, with a slender white base and hollow, cylindrical green leaves, used in cooking
entries.example_cn: 她把青葱切碎加到汤里以增加风味。
entries.example_en: She chopped the scallion finely to add flavor to the soup.

entries.definition_cn: 嫩葱（在鳞茎膨大前食用的洋葱）
entries.definition_en: a young onion eaten before the bulb has fully grown
entries.example_cn: 这道沙拉以脆嫩的葱茎和新鲜香草为特色。
entries.example_en: The salad featured crisp scallion stalks and fresh herbs.

entries.definition_cn: 一种可食用的海洋双壳类动物，具有刻纹的扇形壳，通过从壳中连续喷射水来游泳
entries.definition_en: edible marine bivalve having a fluted fan-shaped shell that swim by expelling water from the shell in a series of snapping motions
entries.example_cn: 扇贝是沿海水域的一种美食。
entries.example_en: Scallops are a delicacy found in coastal waters.

entries.definition_cn: 具有扇形壳的软体动物的可食用肌肉；通常烤、水煮或用于沙拉或奶油酱中
entries.definition_en: edible muscle of mollusks having fan-shaped shells; served broiled or poached or in salads or cream sauces
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐点了扇贝。
entries.example_en: We ordered scallops for dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 沿边缘形成的一系列圆弧或凹口之一，形似扇贝壳边缘
entries.definition_en: one of a series of rounded curves or indentations forming an edge, like those of a scallop shell
entries.example_cn: 扇贝壳具有独特的波浪形边缘。
entries.example_en: The scallop shell has a distinctive wavy edge.

entries.definition_cn: 用酱汁、牛奶等烘烤，通常上面撒面包屑
entries.definition_en: bake in a sauce, milk, etc., often with breadcrumbs on top
entries.example_cn: 厨师用奶油蘑菇酱烘烤了鸡肉。
entries.example_en: The chef scalloped the chicken with a creamy mushroom sauce.

entries.definition_en: decorate an edge with scallops
entries.example_cn: 裁缝用扇形装饰了窗帘的下摆。
entries.example_en: The dressmaker scalloped the hem of the curtain.

entries.definition_en: form scallops in
entries.example_cn: 海浪在海岸边的沙子上形成了扇形凹陷。
entries.example_en: The waves scalloped the sand along the shore.

entries.definition_en: fish for scallops
entries.example_cn: 渔民们一大早就在湾里捕捞扇贝。
entries.example_en: The fishermen scalloped in the bay early in the morning.

entries.definition_cn: 薄肉片（尤其是小牛肉），通常煎或烤
entries.definition_en: thin slice of meat (especially veal) usually fried or broiled
entries.example_cn: 屠夫为晚餐准备了几片小牛肉薄片。
entries.example_en: The butcher prepared scallops of veal for dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 用酱汁烹制的，通常为焗烤的，常加奶酪
entries.definition_en: cooked in a sauce, usually by baking, often with cheese
entries.example_cn: 晚餐我们吃了焗烤土豆。
entries.example_en: We had scalloped potatoes with dinner.

entries.definition_en: having a margin with rounded scallops
entries.example_cn: 她用一个边缘呈扇贝形的碗盛汤。
entries.example_en: She served the soup in a scalloped bowl.

entries.definition_cn: 煎制的薄肉排，通常是小牛肉或禽肉，拍薄后裹上面粉
entries.definition_en: sauteed cutlets, usually veal or poultry, pounded thin and coated with flour
entries.example_cn: 厨师用柠檬和酸豆酱制作了鸡肉小排。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared chicken scallopini with a lemon and caper sauce.

entries.definition_en: one who is playfully mischievous
entries.example_cn: 孩子们把藏起玩具的那个淘气鬼叫作“坏小子”。
entries.example_en: The children called the scallywag who hid their toys a rascal.

entries.definition_en: a deceitful and unreliable scoundrel
entries.example_cn: 警察在巷子里追捕那个欺诈不可靠的恶棍。
entries.example_en: The police chased the scallywag through the alley.

entries.definition_cn: 支持战后重建政策的南方白人
entries.definition_en: a white Southerner who supported Reconstruction policies after the American Civil War (usually for self-interest)
entries.example_cn: 这位历史学家分析了南方白人在战后南方的作用。
entries.example_en: The historian analyzed the role of the scallywag in the post-war South.

entries.definition_en: the skin covering the top of the head
entries.example_cn: 外科医生仔细检查了患者的头皮以寻找感染的迹象。
entries.example_en: The surgeon carefully examined the patient's scalp for signs of infection.

entries.definition_en: to sell something illegally, often on the black market
entries.example_cn: 走私者倒卖这些稀有邮票并以高价出售。
entries.example_en: Smugglers scalped the rare stamps and sold them at high prices.

entries.definition_en: to remove the scalp from someone's head
entries.example_cn: 战士们在古代战争中剥下了敌人的头皮。
entries.example_en: The warriors scalped their enemies in ancient battles.

entries.definition_en: a small, very sharp knife used in surgery, dissection, or craftwork
entries.example_cn: 外科医生小心翼翼地用手术刀切开。
entries.example_en: The surgeon carefully used a scalpel to make the incision.

entries.definition_en: someone who buys something and resells it at a price far above the initial cost
entries.example_cn: 当粉丝们发现黄牛以十倍的票价转卖他们的门票时，他们非常愤怒。
entries.example_en: Fans were furious when they found out a scalper had sold their tickets for ten times the face value.

entries.definition_en: rough to the touch; covered with scales or scurf
entries.example_cn: 那面旧墙的表面粗糙，覆有鳞屑。
entries.example_en: The old wall had a scaly texture.

entries.definition_en: having the body covered or partially covered with thin horny plates, as some fish and reptiles
entries.example_cn: 那条有鳞的鱼迅速游走了。
entries.example_en: The scaly fish swam away quickly.

entries.definition_en: a fraudulent business scheme
entries.example_cn: 他们因陷入一个精妙的投资诈骗而损失了积蓄。
entries.example_en: They lost their savings to a sophisticated investment scam.

entries.definition_cn: 通过欺骗骗取某人的某物
entries.definition_en: to cheat someone out of something by deceit
entries.example_cn: 警方逮捕了试图骗取游客钱财的男子。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the man who tried to scam tourists out of their money.

entries.definition_en: a person who deceives others to steal money or property
entries.example_cn: 警方在一名骗子诈骗数十名老人后将其逮捕。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the scammer after he defrauded dozens of elderly people.

entries.definition_en: a person who is playfully mischievous
entries.example_cn: 那个顽皮鬼又把猫的食物藏起来了。
entries.example_en: The scamp hid the cat's food again.

entries.definition_cn: 敷衍草率地做；马马虎虎地完成
entries.definition_en: to do something in a skimpy or slipshod fashion
entries.example_cn: 他草率地完成了家庭作业。
entries.example_en: He scamped the homework assignment.

entries.definition_en: to move about or proceed hurriedly
entries.example_cn: 兔子看到狗时匆忙逃跑了。
entries.example_en: The rabbit scampered away when it saw the dog.

entries.definition_cn: 轻快的奔跑，尤指嬉戏或不得体的乱跑
entries.definition_en: a quick, light run, especially one that is playful or undignified
entries.example_cn: 小狗飞快地跑过院子。
entries.example_en: The puppy made a quick scamper across the yard.

entries.definition_en: large shrimp sautéed in oil or butter with garlic
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅的招牌菜是蒜香大虾。
entries.example_en: The restaurant's famous dish is garlic scampi.

entries.definition_en: the act of examining a region systematically
entries.example_cn: 医生命令对患者胸部进行扫描。
entries.example_en: The doctor ordered a scan of the patient's chest.

entries.definition_en: an image produced by scanning
entries.example_cn: 扫描图显示骨头有骨折。
entries.example_en: The scan showed a fracture in the bone.

entries.definition_en: to move a light beam over a surface to reproduce an image
entries.example_cn: 机器扫描文件以创建数字副本。
entries.example_en: The machine scanned the document to create a digital copy.

entries.definition_en: to examine minutely or intensely
entries.example_cn: 他仔细检查文件中的错误。
entries.example_en: He scanned the document for errors.

entries.definition_en: to examine hastily
entries.example_cn: 她离开前快速粗略地扫视了房间。
entries.example_en: She scanned the room quickly before leaving.

entries.definition_en: to make a wide, sweeping search of an area
entries.example_cn: 警察在人群中广泛搜索嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police scanned the crowd for the suspect.

entries.definition_en: to conform to a metrical pattern in poetry
entries.example_cn: 诗人扫描了这一行诗以确保其符合韵律。
entries.example_en: The poet scanned the line to ensure it fit the rhythm.

entries.definition_en: to read aloud with attention to metrical patterns
entries.example_cn: 老师按韵律朗读诗歌，帮助学生感受节奏。
entries.example_en: The teacher read the poem metrically to help students hear the rhythm.

entries.definition_cn: 丑闻；有损相关个人或组织名誉的事件
entries.definition_en: an incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the people or organization involved
entries.example_cn: 报纸报道了那位政客私生活中的一桩丑闻。
entries.example_en: The newspaper reported a scandal about the politician's private life.

entries.definition_cn: 因冒犯体面或道德而引起的广泛公愤或愤慨
entries.definition_en: widespread moral outrage or indignation caused by an offense against decency
entries.example_cn: 那名官员有伤风化的行为在全镇引起了广泛公愤。
entries.example_en: The official's indecent behavior caused widespread scandal throughout the town.

entries.definition_cn: 使震惊并引起反感或愤慨
entries.definition_en: to shock or offend by violating moral or social standards
entries.example_cn: 这一有争议的决定使社区许多成员感到震惊。
entries.example_en: The controversial decision scandalised many members of the community.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人感到震惊、愤慨或厌恶
entries.definition_en: to cause someone great offense, shock, or disgust
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家的争议性言论使整个社区感到厌恶。
entries.example_en: The politician's controversial remarks scandalized the entire community.

entries.definition_en: giving offense to moral sensibilities and injurious to reputation
entries.example_cn: 这位名人的伤风败俗的行为震惊了公众。
entries.example_en: The scandalous behavior of the celebrity shocked the public.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that is scandalous
entries.example_cn: 有人看到她衣着暴露地拼命奔跑。
entries.example_en: The actor was scandalously rude to the audience.

entries.definition_en: a rare white metal that forms a +3 ion
entries.example_cn: 钪是一种以微量存在于某些矿物中的化学元素。
entries.example_en: Scandium is a chemical element found in trace amounts in some minerals.

entries.definition_en: an electronic device that creates a digital image for computer input
entries.example_cn: 在我旧照片褪色之前，我用扫描仪将它们数字化了。
entries.example_en: I used the scanner to digitize my old photographs before they faded.

entries.definition_cn: 用于扫描条形码或二维码以查询价格、处理付款或追踪货物的设备
entries.definition_en: a device that scans barcodes or QR codes to check prices, process purchases, or track goods
entries.example_cn: 收银员用扫描仪读取每件商品上的条形码。
entries.example_en: The cashier used the scanner to read the barcode on each item.

entries.definition_cn: 利用超声波或X射线等辐射成像，以诊断身体组织或表面的设备
entries.definition_en: a device that uses radiation, such as ultrasound or X-rays, to create images of body tissues or surfaces for diagnosis
entries.example_cn: 医生使用扫描仪检查病人的腹部。
entries.example_en: The doctor used a scanner to examine the patient's abdomen.

entries.definition_en: a radio receiver that automatically moves across frequencies to find a signal
entries.example_cn: 当调谐各个频段时，扫描接收机捕捉到了一则遥远的紧急广播。
entries.example_en: The scanner picked up a distant emergency broadcast while tuning through the bands.

entries.definition_en: a rotating radar dish used to scan a wide area
entries.example_cn: 船的雷达扫描天线缓慢旋转，以探测任何接近的船只。
entries.example_en: The ship's scanner rotated slowly to detect any approaching vessels.

entries.definition_en: a person who scans poetry to count syllables and determine their rhythm
entries.example_cn: 这位文学学者担任韵文扫描者，以分析这首古史诗的格律。
entries.example_en: The literary scholar worked as a scanner to analyze the meter of the ancient epic.

entries.definition_en: the process of converting photographs into a digital format for computer recognition
entries.example_cn: 博物馆正在通过扫描将其藏品数字化。
entries.example_en: The museum is digitizing its collection through scanning.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving a focused beam of light or electrons over a surface to produce an image
entries.example_cn: 安保系统使用扫描来检测金属物体。
entries.example_en: The security system uses scanning to detect metal objects.

entries.definition_en: the analysis of verse into metrical patterns
entries.example_cn: 教授就莎士比亚十四行诗的韵律分析做了一次讲座。
entries.example_en: The professor gave a lecture on the scansion of Shakespeare's sonnets.

entries.definition_en: less than the correct, legal, or full amount, often deliberately
entries.example_cn: 这笔付款不足，几乎无法覆盖材料成本。
entries.example_en: The payment was scant, barely covering the cost of materials.

entries.definition_en: to stint or deprive someone of something
entries.example_cn: 这家慈善机构给难民提供的食物很少。
entries.example_en: The charity scanted the refugees in food.

entries.definition_en: to limit in quality or quantity
entries.example_cn: 预算限制了新项目所需的资源。
entries.example_en: The budget scanted the resources needed for the new project.

entries.definition_cn: 吝惜供给；使某人得到不足的东西
entries.definition_en: to give someone too little of something
entries.example_cn: 干旱使村民得到的水很少。
entries.example_en: The drought scanted the villagers in water.

entries.definition_en: in a way that provides very little
entries.example_cn: 这个家庭靠微薄的养老金过着清贫的生活。
entries.example_en: The family lived scantily on a small pension.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being meager or insufficient
entries.example_cn: 庄稼的歉收让农民们很担心。
entries.example_en: The scantiness of the harvest worried the farmers.

entries.definition_cn: （衣服）过小、轻薄或暴露的程度
entries.definition_en: the property of a garment being very small, light, or revealing
entries.example_cn: 她批评那件晚礼服太暴露了。
entries.example_en: She criticized the scantiness of the dress for the formal event.

entries.definition_en: a small upright beam of timber used in construction
entries.example_cn: 建筑工测量了框架立柱，以确保墙壁笔直。
entries.example_en: The builder measured the scantling to ensure the wall was straight.

entries.definition_en: lacking in magnitude or quantity
entries.example_cn: 提供的证据不足且无法定论。
entries.example_en: The evidence presented was scanty and inconclusive.

entries.definition_en: (of clothing) revealing the body
entries.example_cn: 模特在时装秀上穿了一条暴露身体的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: The model wore a scanty dress for the fashion show.

entries.definition_en: short underpants for women or children
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一条极短的短裤去海滩。
entries.example_en: She wore a pair of scanty shorts to the beach.

entries.definition_en: a leafless flower stalk arising directly from a bulb, root, or other underground structure
entries.example_cn: 一根无叶的花葶直接从郁金香球茎中长出。
entries.example_en: A leafless scape rose directly from the tulip bulb.

entries.definition_cn: 昆虫触角最靠近身体的基节；柄节
entries.definition_en: the basal segment of an insect's antenna, closest to the body
entries.example_cn: 这只昆虫摆动触角，每根触角的柄节都直接连接在头部。
entries.example_en: The insect moved its antennae, each scape attached directly to its head.

entries.definition_en: the vertical part of a column in architecture
entries.example_cn: 建筑师设计了一座建筑，其巨大的石质柱身支撑着屋顶。
entries.example_en: The architect designed a building with a massive stone scape supporting the roof.

entries.definition_en: a person who is blamed for the mistakes or problems of others
entries.example_cn: 经理让新员工成为公司失败的替罪羊。
entries.example_en: The manager made the new employee a scapegoat for the company's failure.

entries.definition_cn: 放荡不羁、毫无原则的人
entries.definition_en: a person who is reckless and lacks moral principles
entries.example_cn: 警察在拥挤的市场里追捕那个放荡不羁的人。
entries.example_en: The police chased the scapegrace through the crowded market.

entries.definition_en: the carpal navicular bone in the wrist
entries.example_cn: 舟骨是手腕中的一块小腕骨。
entries.example_en: The scaphoid is one of the small carpal bones in the wrist.

entries.definition_en: having the shape of a boat
entries.example_cn: 手腕中的舟骨因其船形而得名。
entries.example_en: The scaphoid bone in the wrist is named for its boat-like shape.

entries.definition_en: one of the two flat, triangular bones located on each side of the shoulder in humans
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了患者肩胛骨的骨折情况。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the fracture in the patient's scapula.

entries.definition_en: relating to or near the shoulder blade
entries.example_cn: 外科医生检查了肩胛区域是否有受伤的迹象。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the scapular region for signs of injury.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用于宗教敬奉的物品，由布带连接的两块小布片组成，分别佩戴在胸前和背后
entries.definition_en: a devotional object made of two small cloth panels joined by bands, worn over the chest and back
entries.example_cn: 她佩戴着一副绣有圣徒图像的肩衣。
entries.example_en: She wore a scapular bearing an embroidered image of a saint.

entries.definition_en: garment consisting of a long wide piece of woolen cloth worn over the shoulders with an opening for the head; part of a monastic habit
entries.example_cn: 修士在进入教堂前脱下了他的修士肩衣。
entries.example_en: The monk removed his scapular before entering the church.

entries.definition_en: a feather covering the shoulder of a bird
entries.example_cn: 这只鸟的肩羽呈现出引人注目的蓝色。
entries.example_en: The bird's scapular feathers were a striking shade of blue.

entries.definition_en: a mark left (usually on the skin) by the healing of injured tissue
entries.example_cn: 他的手臂上仍留有那次事故的伤疤。
entries.example_en: He still has a scar on his arm from the accident.

entries.definition_en: an indication of damage
entries.example_cn: 风暴在船体上留下了一道永久的痕迹。
entries.example_en: The storm left a scar on the hull.

entries.definition_en: mark with a scar
entries.example_cn: 大火使这座老建筑永久受损，留下了明显痕迹。
entries.example_en: The fire scarred the old building permanently.

entries.definition_en: a type of beetle worshipped as a divine symbol by ancient Egyptians
entries.example_cn: 古埃及人崇拜圣甲虫，将其视为重生的象征。
entries.example_en: The ancient Egyptians revered the scarab as a symbol of rebirth.

entries.definition_en: deficient in quantity or number compared with the demand
entries.example_cn: 夏季该地区水资源短缺。
entries.example_en: Water is scarce in this region during the summer.

entries.definition_en: only a very short time before
entries.example_cn: 当我们到达车站时，火车几乎就要开了。
entries.example_en: The train was scarce when we arrived at the station.

entries.definition_en: almost not
entries.example_cn: 他几乎没能按时完成这项任务。
entries.example_en: He was scarce able to finish the task on time.

entries.definition_en: almost not; to a very small degree
entries.example_cn: 派对结束后，冰箱里几乎没剩什么食物了。
entries.example_en: There was scarcely any food left in the refrigerator after the party.

entries.definition_en: only a very short time before
entries.example_cn: 他刚到，会议就开始了。
entries.example_en: He had scarcely arrived when the meeting started.

entries.definition_en: the state of being scarce; an inadequate amount or shortage
entries.example_cn: 水的短缺迫使农民改变了作物。
entries.example_en: The scarcity of water forced the farmers to change their crops.

entries.definition_en: to make someone feel afraid
entries.example_cn: 巨大的噪音吓到了孩子们。
entries.example_en: The loud noise scared the children.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to lose courage or be frightened away
entries.example_cn: 恶劣的天气把游客吓跑了。
entries.example_en: The bad weather scared the tourists away from the beach.

entries.definition_cn: 引起公众恐慌或警觉的事件；恐慌
entries.definition_en: a cause or episode of public fear or alarm, often about an anticipated danger
entries.example_cn: 这则消息引起了投资者的普遍恐慌。
entries.example_en: The news caused a general scare among the investors.

entries.definition_en: a sudden attack of fear
entries.example_cn: 当她看到那只蜘蛛时，突然受到惊吓。
entries.example_en: She had a sudden scare when she saw the spider.

entries.definition_en: a dummy figure dressed in old clothes and placed in a field to scare birds away from crops
entries.example_cn: 农民建了一个高高的稻草人来保护他的玉米免受乌鸦侵害。
entries.example_en: The farmer built a tall scarecrow to protect his corn from the crows.

entries.definition_cn: 像稻草人的高瘦笨拙之人，或衣衫褴褛的人（贬义）
entries.definition_en: a tall, thin, awkward person, or a person wearing ragged and tattered clothes, regarded as resembling a scarecrow (derogatory)
entries.example_cn: 那个像稻草人的男人穿着破外套站在那里瑟瑟发抖。
entries.example_en: The scarecrow of a man stood shivering in his torn coat.

entries.definition_en: Feeling fear or being afraid.
entries.example_cn: 巨大的噪音让那只狗感到害怕。
entries.example_en: The loud noise made the dog scared.

entries.definition_cn: 散布谣言、煽动恐慌的人
entries.definition_en: a person who spreads frightening rumors and causes trouble
entries.example_cn: 当地报纸被指控在选举期间散布恐慌。
entries.example_en: The local newspaper was accused of being a scaremonger during the election.

entries.definition_cn: 用于驱赶鸟类的装置，如稻草人
entries.definition_en: a device, such as a scarecrow, used to frighten birds away
entries.example_cn: 农民在田里放了一个稻草人来保护庄稼。
entries.example_en: The farmer placed a scarer in the field to protect the crops.

entries.definition_en: a piece of cloth worn around the neck or head to keep warm or for decoration
entries.example_cn: 她围上一条红色围巾以抵御寒风。
entries.example_en: She wrapped a red scarf around her neck to stay warm in the cold wind.

entries.definition_en: a joint made by cutting notches into the ends of two pieces of timber or metal so they fit together tightly
entries.example_cn: 木匠用斜接将两根长梁首尾相连。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a scarf to join the two long beams end-to-end.

entries.definition_en: to cover or decorate something with a scarf
entries.example_cn: 她用一条节日图案的围巾包裹了礼物盒。
entries.example_en: She scarfed the gift box with a festive patterned scarf.

entries.definition_en: to join two pieces of material together using a scarf joint
entries.example_cn: 他们用斜接将两根金属杆连接起来，以构建更坚固的结构。
entries.example_en: They scarfed the two metal rods together to create a stronger structure.

entries.definition_cn: （美国，俚语）狼吞虎咽；快速吃掉
entries.definition_en: (US, slang) to eat very quickly
entries.example_cn: 你真是狼吞虎咽地吃完了那块披萨。
entries.example_en: You sure scarfed that pizza.

entries.definition_cn: 刺穿皮肤（如用于仪式或标识）
entries.definition_en: to puncture the skin, often as part of a ritual or for identification
entries.example_cn: 部落会刺穿战士的皮肤以标记他们的勇敢。
entries.example_en: The tribe would scarify their warriors to mark their bravery.

entries.definition_en: to scratch or roughen the surface of something
entries.example_cn: 他们刮松土壤以帮助种子更好地生长。
entries.example_en: They scarified the soil to help the seeds grow better.

entries.definition_en: to break up or pulverize something
entries.example_cn: 这台机器用于将大石头粉碎成碎石。
entries.example_en: The machine was used to scarify the large rocks into gravel.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes fear or terror.
entries.example_cn: 浓雾可怕地迅速卷来。
entries.example_en: The fog rolled in scarily fast.

entries.definition_en: a contagious disease causing high fever and a red rash, common in children
entries.example_cn: 医生在看到这个皮疹后诊断出孩子患上了猩红热。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the child with scarlatina after seeing the rash.

entries.definition_cn: 鲜红色的；猩红色的，有时略带橙色
entries.definition_en: bright red, sometimes with an orange tinge
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一条猩红色的裙子去参加聚会。
entries.example_en: She wore a scarlet dress to the party.

entries.definition_cn: 一种鲜艳的红色，有时带有橙色色调
entries.definition_en: a variable color that is vivid red but sometimes with an orange tinge
entries.example_cn: 日落的鲜红色令人叹为观止。
entries.example_en: The scarlet of the sunset was breathtaking.

entries.definition_en: a long, steep slope or cliff at the edge of a plateau or ridge, usually formed by erosion
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者攀登了崎岖的陡崖，到达了高原顶部。
entries.example_en: Hikers climbed the rugged scarp to reach the top of the plateau.

entries.definition_en: a steep artificial slope built in front of a fortification
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的堡垒由一条深沟和高耸的护城坡保护着。
entries.example_en: The ancient fortress was protected by a deep moat and a high scarp.

entries.definition_en: flee; take to one's heels; cut and run
entries.example_cn: 当警察赶到时，嫌疑犯们逃进了人群。
entries.example_en: When the police arrived, the suspects scarpered into the crowd.

usage.label: UK slang
usage.pattern: Usually intransitive: scarper or scarper from a place.

entries.definition_en: deeply affected or marked by mental or physical pain or injury
entries.example_cn: 这位老兵因战争经历而深受创伤。
entries.example_en: The veteran was scarred by his experience in the war.

entries.definition_en: having marks or damage caused by injury or rough use
entries.example_cn: 这张旧桌子因多年重用了而布满伤痕。
entries.example_en: The old table was scarred by years of heavy use.

entries.definition_en: provoking fear or terror
entries.example_cn: 这部电影太可怕了，我昨晚睡不着觉。
entries.example_en: The movie was so scary that I couldn't sleep last night.

entries.definition_cn: 用即兴无意义音节代替歌词的爵士演唱方式
entries.definition_en: a style of jazz singing in which improvised nonsense syllables replace the lyrics
entries.example_cn: 这位爵士歌手表演了一段经典的无词爵士独奏，令观众欣喜不已。
entries.example_en: The jazz singer performed a classic scat solo that delighted the audience.

entries.definition_en: to run away quickly to escape danger
entries.example_cn: 当警察赶到时，小偷试图在他们抓住他之前逃跑。
entries.example_en: When the police arrived, the thief tried to scat before they could catch him.

entries.definition_en: marked by harshly abusive criticism
entries.example_cn: 评论家对这部新电影写了一篇尖刻的评论。
entries.example_en: The critic wrote a scathing review of the new movie.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is very critical and harsh
entries.example_cn: 这位评论家尖刻地批评了作者缺乏原创性。
entries.example_en: The critic scathingly attacked the author's lack of originality.

entries.definition_cn: 涉及排泄物的（尤指以猥亵方式的）
entries.definition_en: dealing pruriently with excrement and excretory functions
entries.example_cn: 喜剧演员涉及排泄物的笑话冒犯了观众。
entries.example_en: The comedian's scatological jokes offended the audience.

entries.definition_en: a preoccupation with obscenity, particularly content dealing with excrement or excretory functions
entries.example_cn: 这部小说因其过度的对污秽的迷恋而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The novel was criticized for its excessive scatology.

entries.definition_cn: 粪便的科学研究或化学分析
entries.definition_en: the scientific study or chemical analysis of excrement, especially for medical or paleontological purposes
entries.example_cn: 医疗团队对患者的粪便进行了化学分析，以确定感染源。
entries.example_en: The medical team conducted a chemical analysis of the patient's excrement to identify the source of the infection.

entries.definition_en: move away from each other
entries.example_cn: 当捕食者出现时，鸟儿四散飞走。
entries.example_en: The birds scattered when the predator appeared.

entries.definition_en: to cause to separate and go in different directions
entries.example_cn: 风吹散了人群。
entries.example_en: The wind scattered the crowd.

entries.definition_en: strew or distribute over an area
entries.example_cn: 他在结冰的小路上撒了盐。
entries.example_en: He scattered salt on the icy path.

entries.definition_en: distribute loosely
entries.example_cn: 她在桌上松散地摆放了鲜花。
entries.example_en: She scattered flowers on the table.

entries.definition_en: cause to separate
entries.example_cn: 这次争吵使团队分崩离析。
entries.example_en: The argument scattered the team.

entries.definition_en: a haphazard distribution in all directions
entries.example_cn: 树叶散落在草坪上。
entries.example_en: The leaves were scattered across the lawn.

entries.definition_en: sow by scattering
entries.example_cn: 农民在田里撒种。
entries.example_en: Farmers scatter seeds over the field.

entries.definition_en: the act of scattering
entries.example_cn: 种子的撒播确保了丰收。
entries.example_en: The scattering of seeds ensures a good harvest.

entries.definition_en: a person who is easily distracted and lacks organization
entries.example_cn: 别把钥匙交给那个丢三落四的人，他还会再忘的。
entries.example_en: Don't leave the keys to the scatterbrain; he will forget them again.

entries.definition_cn: 心不在焉的；健忘的；容易分心的
entries.definition_en: absent-minded, forgetful, or easily distracted
entries.example_cn: 他心不在焉，竟忘了把钥匙放在哪里。
entries.example_en: He was so scatterbrained that he forgot where he had left his keys.

entries.definition_en: guided by whim and fancy; impulsive
entries.example_cn: 她凭一时兴起买了一本从未读过的稀有书籍。
entries.example_en: She made a scatterbrained purchase of a rare book she had never read.

entries.definition_en: occurring or distributed over widely spaced and irregular intervals in time or space
entries.example_cn: 学生们分散在大片田野上。
entries.example_en: The students were scattered across the large field.

entries.definition_en: lacking orderly continuity
entries.example_cn: 这个故事充满了令人困惑的细节，显得不连贯。
entries.example_en: The story was scattered with confusing details.

entries.definition_en: someone who spends money prodigally
entries.example_cn: 他是一个挥霍者，从不存钱。
entries.example_en: He is a scattergood who never saves any money.

entries.definition_en: a double-barreled shotgun used for firing shot at short ranges
entries.example_cn: 他在棚子里放了一把霰弹枪以防身。
entries.example_en: He kept a scattergun in the shed for protection.

entries.definition_cn: 零星的一些；少量散布的东西
entries.definition_en: a small quantity of things dispersed haphazardly
entries.example_cn: 蓝天上只有零星的几朵云。
entries.example_en: There was only a scattering of clouds in the blue sky.

entries.definition_en: a light shower that falls in some locations but not others nearby
entries.example_cn: 我们走到公交车站时，被一场局部降雨淋湿了。
entries.example_en: We got caught in a scattering of rain while walking to the bus stop.

entries.definition_en: the physical process where particles are deflected by collisions
entries.example_cn: 该实验测量了气体对光的散射。
entries.example_en: The experiment measured the scattering of light by the gas.

entries.definition_en: the act of scattering things
entries.example_cn: 农民正忙着在田里撒播种子。
entries.example_en: The farmer was busy with the scattering of seeds across the field.

entries.definition_en: the act of spreading widely or driving off
entries.example_cn: 警察使用催泪瓦斯驱散了人群。
entries.example_en: The police used tear gas to effect a scattering of the crowd.

entries.definition_cn: 漫无目的的；杂乱无章的
entries.definition_en: covering a wide range of topics or areas in a haphazard and unorganized way
entries.example_cn: 委员会解决该问题漫无目的的方法未能解决任何具体问题。
entries.example_en: The committee's scattershot approach to solving the problem failed to address any specific issue.

entries.definition_en: scatterbrained or flighty; lacking organization or good judgment
entries.example_cn: 她散漫的旅行计划方式使几个重要细节都没有得到处理。
entries.example_en: Her scatty way of planning the trip left several important details unresolved.

entries.definition_en: lost in thought; showing preoccupation
entries.example_cn: 她心不在焉，以至于忘了带钥匙。
entries.example_en: She was so scatty that she forgot her keys.

entries.definition_en: diving ducks of North America having a bluish-grey bill
entries.example_cn: 这只北美潜鸭潜入水中捕鱼。
entries.example_en: The scaup dove into the water to catch fish.

entries.definition_en: to collect discarded material
entries.example_cn: 浣熊经常在垃圾桶里翻找食物。
entries.example_en: Raccoons often scavenge through trash cans for food.

entries.definition_en: to feed on carrion or refuse
entries.example_cn: 一些昆虫以大型食肉动物的尸体为食。
entries.example_en: Some insects scavenge on the carcass of a large predator.

entries.definition_en: to clean up refuse or waste
entries.example_cn: 工人们清除了污染河流中的垃圾。
entries.example_en: Workers scavenged refuse from the polluted river.

entries.definition_en: to remove unwanted substances from something
entries.example_cn: 该软件可以从您的硬盘中清除旧文件。
entries.example_en: The software can scavenge old files from your hard drive.

entries.definition_cn: 以腐肉或其他腐败有机物为食的动物
entries.definition_en: an animal that feeds on carrion or other decaying organic matter
entries.example_cn: 秃鹫是食腐动物，以死动物的残骸为食。
entries.example_en: Vultures are scavengers that feed on the remains of dead animals.

entries.definition_en: someone who collects discarded things
entries.example_cn: 当地的拾荒者在垃圾中分拣可回收材料。
entries.example_en: The local scavenger sorted through the trash for recyclable materials.

entries.definition_en: a chemical agent added to a mixture to counteract impurities
entries.example_cn: 化学家向溶液中添加了除杂剂以去除多余的氧气。
entries.example_en: The chemist added a scavenger to the solution to remove excess oxygen.

entries.definition_cn: 可能发生的一系列事件
entries.definition_en: a possible sequence of events that might happen
entries.example_cn: 我们必须为每一种可能发生的情况做好准备。
entries.example_en: We must prepare for every possible scenario.

entries.definition_cn: 剧本大纲；（引申为）文学作品梗概
entries.definition_en: an outline or synopsis of a play (or, by extension, of a literary work)
entries.example_cn: 导演在开拍前阅读了剧本大纲。
entries.example_en: The director read the scenario before filming began.

entries.definition_cn: 艺术作品或文学作品的背景设定
entries.definition_en: a setting for a work of art or literature
entries.example_cn: 这部小说以维多利亚时代的伦敦为背景设定。
entries.example_en: The novel is set in a Victorian scenario of London.

entries.definition_en: a person who writes scripts for films or television
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的编剧因她关于战争的剧本而获奖。
entries.example_en: The famous scenarist won an award for her screenplay about the war.

entries.definition_en: the place where an event or action happens
entries.example_cn: 警察赶到了事故现场。
entries.example_en: The police arrived at the scene of the accident.

entries.definition_cn: （电影中的）一场；一个镜头组接
entries.definition_en: a continuous series of pictures in a film that shows one part of the story
entries.example_cn: 电影中的那场戏非常激动人心。
entries.example_en: That scene in the movie was very exciting.

entries.definition_en: a situation that can be seen or observed
entries.example_cn: 当他们告别时，场面十分悲伤。
entries.example_en: It was a sad scene when they said goodbye.

entries.definition_en: an incident that actually happened or is imagined
entries.example_cn: 电影中的这一幕是基于真实故事改编的。
entries.example_en: The movie scene was based on a true story.

entries.definition_en: a part of a play or performance
entries.example_cn: 演员们完美地表演了最后一场戏。
entries.example_en: The actors performed the final scene perfectly.

entries.definition_en: what you see in a particular place
entries.example_cn: 从山上看到的景色非常美丽。
entries.example_en: The view from the mountain was a beautiful scene.

entries.definition_en: a display of bad temper
entries.example_cn: 他因为新规则跟老板大吵了一架。
entries.example_en: He had a scene with his boss about the new rules.

entries.definition_en: a picture or drawing that represents what you see
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家画了一幅乡村风景画。
entries.example_en: The artist painted a scene of the countryside.

entries.definition_en: an actor who attracts more attention than the other actors in a scene
entries.example_cn: 配角在最后一幕中真是个抢戏者。
entries.example_en: The supporting actor was a true scene-stealer in the final act.

entries.definition_en: the natural appearance of a place
entries.example_cn: 游客们欣赏了美丽的山景。
entries.example_en: The tourists enjoyed the beautiful scenery of the mountains.

entries.definition_en: painted structures on a stage to represent a place
entries.example_cn: 演员穿过舞台布景到达了舞台后方。
entries.example_en: The actors moved through the scenery to reach the back of the stage.

entries.definition_en: having beautiful natural scenery
entries.example_cn: 沿海的这条风景优美的路线提供了令人惊叹的景色。
entries.example_en: The scenic route along the coast offers breathtaking views.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the stage or stage scenery
entries.example_cn: 舞台设计师为这部戏剧创造了一个宏伟的背景。
entries.example_en: The scenic designer created a magnificent backdrop for the play.

entries.definition_en: in relation to stage scenery or visual settings
entries.example_cn: 该剧在舞台布景方面令人印象深刻，布景和灯光都很华丽。
entries.example_en: The play was scenically impressive, with elaborate sets and lighting.

entries.definition_en: a distinctive smell, whether pleasant or unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 花园里充满了茉莉花的甜香。
entries.example_en: The room was filled with the scent of jasmine.

entries.definition_en: an odor left behind that allows someone to be tracked
entries.example_cn: 猎犬顺着兔子的踪迹气味穿过树林。
entries.example_en: The hound followed the scent of the rabbit through the woods.

entries.definition_cn: 气味；嗅觉感知到的味道
entries.definition_en: a smell or odor perceived by the sense of smell
entries.example_cn: 烟味充满了房间。
entries.example_en: The scent of smoke filled the room.

entries.definition_en: to make something smell or become smelly
entries.example_cn: 花朵开始使整个房间散发香气。
entries.example_en: The flowers began to scent the entire room.

entries.definition_en: to discover or become aware of something
entries.example_cn: 侦探开始察觉到官员们之间的阴谋。
entries.example_en: The detective began to scent a conspiracy among the officials.

entries.definition_en: to apply perfume to something or someone
entries.example_cn: 她睡前用薰衣草油给头发喷了香水。
entries.example_en: She scented her hair with lavender oil before going to bed.

entries.definition_en: filled or impregnated with perfume
entries.example_cn: 这款香皂在她的皮肤上留下了淡淡的花香。
entries.example_en: The scented soap left a light floral fragrance on her skin.

entries.definition_en: having a pleasant aroma
entries.example_cn: 花园里带有天然香气的花朵在夏天吸引了许多蜜蜂。
entries.example_en: The scented flowers in the garden attracted many bees during the summer.

entries.definition_en: having the odor of
entries.example_cn: 那本旧书有香草味，因为修复它的胶水带有香草气味。
entries.example_en: The old book smelled of vanilla because the glue used to repair it was vanilla-scented.

entries.definition_en: having the sense of smell
entries.example_cn: 那只狗的嗅觉灵敏，很快闻到了沙发下藏着的零食。
entries.example_en: The dog's scented nose quickly detected the hidden treat under the sofa.

entries.definition_en: emitting or holding no odor
entries.example_cn: 这种无味的肥皂非常适合鼻子敏感的人。
entries.example_en: The scentless soap was perfect for people with sensitive noses.

entries.definition_en: lacking the sense of smell
entries.example_cn: 那只无嗅觉的狗无法追踪失踪的猫。
entries.example_en: The scentless dog could not track the missing cat.

entries.definition_en: a ceremonial or emblematic staff
entries.example_cn: 女王在加冕典礼上手持一根金色的仪仗权杖。
entries.example_en: The queen carried a golden scepter during the coronation ceremony.

usage.label: 美国英语；古旧
usage.pattern: American and archaic form of sceptre

entries.definition_en: the imperial authority symbolized by a scepter
entries.example_cn: 国王手持权杖，象征着他的皇权。
entries.example_en: The king held the scepter as a symbol of his imperial authority.

entries.definition_en: someone who habitually doubts accepted beliefs
entries.example_cn: 作为一个怀疑论者，他拒绝相信任何未经证实的说法。
entries.example_en: As a sceptic, he refused to believe any unproven claims.

entries.definition_en: having doubts about something; not believing it is true
entries.example_cn: 我怀疑他能否按时完成这个项目。
entries.example_en: I am sceptical about his ability to finish the project on time.

entries.definition_cn: 对宗教信仰持怀疑态度的
entries.definition_en: denying or questioning the beliefs of a religion
entries.example_cn: 他在读了那本书之后对组织化的宗教产生了怀疑。
entries.example_en: He became sceptical of organized religion after reading the book.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows doubt or disbelief
entries.example_cn: 她怀疑地看着那个奇怪的声明。
entries.example_en: She looked at the strange claim sceptically.

entries.definition_en: doubt regarding the truth of something
entries.example_cn: 她对报告准确性的怀疑促使她核实了数据。
entries.example_en: Her scepticism about the report's accuracy led her to verify the data.

entries.definition_cn: 对终极知识主张的怀疑态度
entries.definition_en: the attitude of doubting claims of ultimate knowledge
entries.example_cn: 现代科学通常以对绝对真理的合理怀疑为特征。
entries.example_en: Modern science is often characterized by a healthy scepticism about absolute truths.

entries.definition_en: a ceremonial or emblematic staff
entries.example_cn: 主教在仪式中携带了一根金色的权杖。
entries.example_en: The bishop carried a golden sceptre during the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: the imperial authority symbolized by a scepter
entries.example_cn: 权杖象征着君主的帝国权威。
entries.example_en: The sceptre represented the monarch's imperial authority.

entries.definition_en: having the power or authority of a ruler, often symbolized by holding a scepter
entries.example_cn: 拥有王权的君主以盛大的仪式签署了条约。
entries.example_en: The sceptred monarch signed the treaty with great ceremony.

entries.definition_en: a plan that lists when things will happen
entries.example_cn: 出发前我们需要查看火车时刻表。
entries.example_en: We need to check the train schedule before leaving.

entries.definition_en: a list showing the times when events are planned to happen
entries.example_cn: 航班时刻表显示了所有目的地的起飞时间。
entries.example_en: The flight schedule shows the departure times for all destinations.

entries.definition_en: to make a plan for an activity or event
entries.example_cn: 老师下周将安排一次考试。
entries.example_en: The teacher will schedule a test next week.

entries.definition_en: to plan the time and place for events
entries.example_cn: 他们计划周二下午开会。
entries.example_en: They scheduled a meeting for Tuesday afternoon.

entries.definition_en: planned or scheduled for some certain time or times
entries.example_cn: 会议已安排在下周二上午10点。
entries.example_en: The meeting is scheduled for next Tuesday at 10 AM.

entries.definition_cn: 安排计算机任务执行顺序的硬件
entries.definition_en: computer hardware that arranges jobs to be done by the computer in an appropriate order
entries.example_cn: 新的调度器提高了系统的效率。
entries.example_en: The new scheduler improved the system's efficiency.

entries.definition_en: the action of arranging the order and time for planned events
entries.example_cn: 由于天气原因，会议的日程安排已被推迟。
entries.example_en: The scheduling of the conference has been delayed due to the weather.

entries.definition_en: a mineral composed of calcium tungstate (CaWO₄), one of the principal ores of tungsten
entries.example_cn: 地质学家从山上采集了一块白钨矿样本。
entries.example_en: The geologist collected a sample of scheelite from the mountain.

entries.definition_en: an internal organization of concepts and actions that can be updated with new information
entries.example_cn: 孩子在看到不同品种的狗后，对“狗”的概念图式发生了变化。
entries.example_en: The child's schema for 'dog' changed after seeing a different breed.

entries.definition_en: an outline or general plan
entries.example_cn: 建筑师展示了新建筑的大纲。
entries.example_en: The architect presented a schema for the new building.

entries.definition_cn: 数据库模式；对数据库表、列和数据类型等结构的正式描述
entries.definition_en: a formal description of the structure of a database, including its tables, columns, and data types
entries.example_cn: 数据库模式规定了各个表的组织方式。
entries.example_en: The database schema defines how the tables are organized.

entries.definition_cn: 以过于简单或公式化的方式表现的，显示出对复杂事物理解不完整的
entries.definition_en: represented in an overly simple or formulaic way, showing an incomplete understanding of a complex subject
entries.example_cn: 这份报告对危机原因的解释只是过于简单化的概述。
entries.example_en: The report offered only a schematic account of the causes of the crisis.

entries.definition_en: a diagram showing how the parts of a machine or system work
entries.example_cn: 工程师画出了电路的原理图。
entries.example_en: The engineer drew a schematic of the electrical circuit.

entries.definition_en: in a simplified way that shows structure, often using a diagram
entries.example_cn: 为了帮助学生理解，这个复杂的系统被以图解方式进行了说明。
entries.example_en: The complex system was explained schematically to help the students understand.

entries.definition_en: the action of creating a chart or outline to show how a system works
entries.example_cn: 新软件架构的图表化帮助团队理解了数据流向。
entries.example_en: The schematization of the new software architecture helped the team understand the data flow.

entries.definition_en: the process of simplifying something complex into a basic plan or formula
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家对人体解剖的公式化只关注了基本的比例。
entries.example_en: The artist's schematization of human anatomy focused only on the essential proportions.

entries.definition_en: an elaborate and systematic plan of action
entries.example_cn: 他们制定了一个详细的计划来改善城市。
entries.example_en: They created a detailed scheme to improve the city.

entries.definition_cn: 秘密或阴险的计划；阴谋
entries.definition_en: a secret or devious plan
entries.example_cn: 那位政治家策划了一个逃避回答问题的阴谋。
entries.example_en: The politician devised a scheme to avoid answering the question.

entries.definition_cn: 相关部分组成的体系；结构
entries.definition_en: a system or structure of related parts
entries.example_cn: 这台机器的结构由几个相互啮合的部件组成。
entries.example_en: The scheme of the machine consists of several interlocking parts.

entries.definition_en: a chart or diagram showing the structure of a system or object
entries.example_cn: 工程师画了一张机器线路的示意图。
entries.example_en: The engineer drew a scheme of the machine’s wiring.

entries.definition_en: to form intrigues in an underhand manner
entries.example_cn: 他被指控策划反对他的对手。
entries.example_en: He was accused of scheming against his rival.

entries.definition_en: to devise a system or form a scheme for
entries.example_cn: 这位建筑师目前正在为大楼设计新的布局。
entries.example_en: The architect is currently scheming a new layout for the building.

entries.definition_en: an internal representation of the world; an organization of concepts and actions that can be revised by new information
entries.example_cn: 随着孩子们学习新事物，他们形成了对世界的图式。
entries.example_en: Children develop a scheme of the world as they learn new things.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes secret plans to achieve their own goals, often in a dishonest way
entries.example_cn: 这个阴谋家等待完美的时机来揭示他的计划。
entries.example_en: The schemer waited for the perfect moment to reveal his plan.

entries.definition_en: secretly planning to harm others for your own benefit
entries.example_cn: 他被指控对竞争对手进行阴谋陷害。
entries.example_en: He was accused of scheming against his rival.

entries.definition_en: planning carefully to achieve a specific goal
entries.example_cn: 这位有计划的政客有一个明确的胜利计划。
entries.example_en: The scheming politician had a clear plan for victory.

entries.definition_en: a lively and fast musical movement, usually in triple time
entries.example_cn: 交响乐的第三乐章是一首充满活力的谐谑曲，令观众欣喜。
entries.example_en: The symphony's third movement is a spirited scherzo that delights the audience.

entries.definition_en: the former currency of Austria
entries.example_cn: 历史记录显示先令的价值波动很大。
entries.example_en: Historical records show the value of the schilling fluctuated greatly.

entries.definition_en: a division of a group into opposing factions
entries.example_cn: 党内的分裂导致支持率下降。
entries.example_en: The schism within the party led to a loss of support.

entries.definition_en: the formal separation of a church into two churches or the withdrawal of one group over doctrinal differences
entries.example_cn: 大分裂将基督教教会分成了东、西两个分支。
entries.example_en: The Great Schism divided the Christian church into Eastern and Western branches.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involved in a split within a religious or political group
entries.example_cn: 这个分裂主义派别拒绝承认主流教会的权威。
entries.example_en: The schismatic faction refused to recognize the authority of the main church.

entries.definition_en: a coarse-grained crystalline metamorphic rock with a foliated structure that splits into slabs or layers
entries.example_cn: 地质学家从山脊上采集了片岩样本。
entries.example_en: The geologist collected samples of schist from the mountain ridge.

entries.definition_en: a type of flatworm that lives as a parasite in the blood vessels of mammals
entries.example_cn: 医生们正在努力研发一种预防血吸虫感染的疫苗。
entries.example_en: Doctors are working to develop a vaccine to prevent infection by the schistosome.

entries.definition_en: a parasitic infection common in the tropics caused by the Schistosoma parasite
entries.example_cn: 前往热带地区的旅行者应意识到感染血吸虫病的风险。
entries.example_en: Travelers to tropical regions should be aware of the risk of schistosomiasis.

entries.definition_en: marked by social withdrawal and an inability to form close relationships.
entries.example_cn: 他性格孤僻，避免参加社交聚会。
entries.example_en: He has a schizoid personality and avoids social gatherings.

entries.definition_cn: 精神分裂症的或类似精神分裂症的（旧）
entries.definition_en: of or resembling schizophrenia (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 该疾病的分裂性特征使治疗变得复杂。
entries.example_en: The schizoid nature of the disorder complicates treatment.

entries.definition_en: a person with schizoid personality disorder
entries.example_cn: 精神科医生称他为分裂样人格障碍患者。
entries.example_en: The psychiatrist described him as a schizoid.

entries.definition_en: a serious mental disorder where a person loses touch with reality, has confused thoughts, and withdraws from social life.
entries.example_cn: 精神分裂症是一种影响个人思维和行为的复杂疾病。
entries.example_en: Schizophrenia is a complex condition that affects how a person thinks and behaves.

entries.definition_en: suffering from some form of schizophrenia
entries.example_cn: 这位患精神分裂症的患者在接受治疗后显示出好转迹象。
entries.example_en: The schizophrenic patient showed signs of improvement after treatment.

entries.definition_en: relating to or characteristic of schizophrenia
entries.example_cn: 精神分裂症的症状在压力期间突然出现。
entries.example_en: The schizophrenic symptoms appeared suddenly during the stress period.

entries.definition_en: a person who suffers from schizophrenia
entries.example_cn: 医生解释说，这位精神分裂症患者需要专门的护理。
entries.example_en: The doctor explained that the schizophrenic needed specialized care.

entries.definition_en: a clumsy or incompetent person who habitally makes mistakes
entries.example_cn: 别叫那个笨手笨脚的人修电脑，他只会让情况变得更糟。
entries.example_en: Don't ask the schlemiel to fix the computer; he will only make it worse.

entries.definition_en: pull along heavily, like a heavy load against a resistance
entries.example_cn: 我不得不费力地把沉重的箱子搬上楼梯。
entries.example_en: I had to schlep the heavy boxes up the stairs.

usage.label: 非正式；犹太英语；纽约市用语；俚语

entries.definition_en: a tedious or difficult journey
entries.example_cn: 在雨中去机场的旅程漫长而枯燥。
entries.example_en: The trip to the airport was a long schlep in the rain.

entries.definition_cn: 无聊、不中用或邋遢的人
entries.definition_en: a boring, inept, or slovenly person
entries.example_cn: 他真是个笨蛋，连自己的生日都忘了。
entries.example_en: He is such a schlep that he forgot his own birthday.

entries.definition_en: merchandise that is shoddy or inferior
entries.example_cn: 这家商店里堆满了从海外进口的廉价劣质商品。
entries.example_en: The store was full of cheap schlock imported from overseas.

entries.definition_en: excessive sentimentality in art or music
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因其矫揉造作的情感和可预测的情节而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The movie was criticized for its schmaltz and predictable plot.

entries.definition_cn: 熬制的鸡油或鹅油，用于烹饪
entries.definition_en: rendered chicken or goose fat used in cooking
entries.example_cn: 她用鸡油给土豆增添浓郁的风味。
entries.example_en: She used schmaltz to give the potatoes a rich flavor.

entries.definition_en: overly sentimental or maudlin
entries.example_cn: 这部电影太过煽情，让我想离开。
entries.example_en: The movie was too schmaltzy and made me want to leave.

entries.definition_cn: （艺术或音乐中的）过度感伤；矫情
entries.definition_en: excessive sentimentality in art or music
entries.example_cn: 评论家们认为这部交响乐过于煽情。
entries.example_en: The critics dismissed the symphony as too much schmalz.

entries.definition_en: a collection of things that are related or go together
entries.example_cn: 这份报告是一堆过时的统计数据和无关意见的集合。
entries.example_en: The report was a schmear of outdated statistics and irrelevant opinions.

entries.definition_en: a foolish or unimportant person
entries.example_cn: 别听那个傻瓜的话；他根本不知道自己在说什么。
entries.example_en: Don't listen to that schmo; he doesn't know what he is talking about.

entries.definition_cn: 名词：普通人；无名小卒。[美国，贬义，幽默，非正式]
entries.definition_en: noun: An ordinary, unremarkable person; an average Joe.
entries.example_cn: 我只是个普通人。
entries.example_en: I'm just an average schmo.

entries.definition_cn: 闲聊，尤指为建立社交联系或谋取好处
entries.definition_en: to talk casually, especially to make a social connection or gain an advantage
entries.example_cn: 他喜欢和邻居一边喝咖啡一边闲聊。
entries.example_en: He likes to schmooze with his neighbors over coffee.

entries.definition_cn: 闲聊，尤指为建立社交联系或谋取好处的交谈
entries.definition_en: a casual conversation, especially one held to make a social connection or gain an advantage
entries.example_cn: 他们在聚会上的闲聊帮助他们结识了有用的人脉。
entries.example_en: Their schmooze at the party helped them make useful contacts.

entries.definition_en: a foolish or contemptible person
entries.example_cn: 别这么蠢，忘了锁门。
entries.example_en: Don't be such a schmuck and forget to lock the door.

usage.label: US Jewish slang; derogatory
usage.pattern: Source w22573r0 supplies these register and regional labels.

entries.definition_cn: 烈酒，尤指荷兰产的土豆蒸馏酒
entries.definition_en: any of various strong liquors especially a Dutch spirit distilled from potatoes
entries.example_cn: 他们用餐后喝了一小杯烈酒。
entries.example_en: They finished the meal with a shot of schnapps.

entries.definition_cn: 烈性酒（尤指荷兰用土豆蒸馏的酒）
entries.definition_en: a strong alcoholic drink, especially a Dutch spirit made from potatoes
entries.example_cn: 他们饭后喝了一杯烈性酒。
entries.example_en: They finished the meal with a glass of schnaps.

entries.definition_en: a sturdy German breed of black or greyish wire-haired terrier with a blunt muzzle, used as ratters, guard dogs, or police dogs
entries.example_cn: 警官叫来一只雪纳瑞犬协助追踪嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The police officer called a schnauzer to help track the suspect.

entries.definition_cn: 一种裹面包屑煎炸的肉排菜肴
entries.definition_en: a dish consisting of a breaded and fried meat cutlet
entries.example_cn: 我们点了炸肉排作为晚餐，配土豆沙拉。
