entries.example_en: We ordered schnitzel for dinner, served with potato salad.

entries.definition_en: a gullible simpleton who is more to be pitied than despised
entries.example_cn: 销售员意识到他正在和一个轻信每一个承诺的易受骗傻瓜交谈。
entries.example_en: The salesman realized he had been talking to a schnook who believed every promise.

entries.definition_cn: 通过乞求或软磨硬泡取得；讨得
entries.definition_en: to obtain something by begging or wheedling
entries.example_cn: 他试图向富有的邻居乞讨几美元。
entries.example_en: He tried to schnorr a few dollars from his wealthy neighbors.

entries.definition_en: informal term for the nose
entries.example_cn: 他有一个非常突出的大鼻子。
entries.example_en: He has a very large schnoz that sticks out from his face.

entries.definition_en: a person who has studied a subject for a long time and knows it very well
entries.example_cn: 大学邀请了一位著名学者做讲座。
entries.example_en: The university invited a famous scholar to give a lecture.

entries.definition_en: a student who receives financial support to study
entries.example_cn: 她凭奖学金在那所著名学院就读。
entries.example_en: She is a scholar at the prestigious college, supported by a scholarship.

entries.definition_en: a person who is learning from a teacher
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻的学生努力学习以通过考试。
entries.example_en: The young scholar studied hard to pass the exam.

entries.definition_en: characteristic of academic research or learned people
entries.example_cn: 该期刊仅发表关于古代历史的学术文章。
entries.example_en: The journal publishes only scholarly articles on ancient history.

entries.definition_en: financial aid provided to a student on the basis of academic merit
entries.example_cn: 她赢得了全额奖学金去那所大学学习。
entries.example_en: She won a full scholarship to study at the university.

entries.definition_en: profound scholarly knowledge
entries.example_cn: 他在古代历史方面的学识无人能及。
entries.example_en: His scholarship in ancient history is unmatched.

entries.definition_en: in relation to scholastic activities or learning
entries.example_cn: 这名学生在学业上表现优异，但缺乏社交技能。
entries.example_en: The student performed scholastically well but lacked social skills.

entries.definition_en: a scholar who writes explanatory notes on an author, especially an ancient commentator on a classical author
entries.example_cn: 这位中世纪的注释者在古文本的页边添加了有价值的注释。
entries.example_en: The medieval scholiast added valuable notes to the margins of the ancient text.

entries.definition_cn: 注释（古代或古典文学的评注）
entries.definition_en: a note added to a text by a commentator on ancient or classical literature
entries.example_cn: 这部古手稿包含几处注释，解释了难懂的段落。
entries.example_en: The ancient manuscript contains several scholia explaining the difficult passages.

entries.definition_en: an educational institution
entries.example_cn: 她每天去上学。
entries.example_en: She goes to school every day.

entries.definition_en: a building where young people receive education
entries.example_cn: 学校位于公园附近。
entries.example_en: The school is located near the park.

entries.definition_en: the process of being formally educated at a school
entries.example_cn: 他花了十年时间接受学校教育。
entries.example_en: He spent ten years in school.

entries.definition_en: a body of creative artists or writers or thinkers linked by a similar style or by similar teachers
entries.example_cn: 这幅画属于印象派。
entries.example_en: This painting belongs to the impressionist school.

entries.definition_en: the period of instruction in a school; the time period when school is in session
entries.example_cn: 学年在九月开始。
entries.example_en: The school year starts in September.

entries.definition_en: educate in or as if in a school
entries.example_cn: 父母应该教育子女养成良好的礼貌。
entries.example_en: Parents should school their children in good manners.

entries.definition_en: teach or refine to be discriminative in taste or judgment
entries.example_cn: 他的父亲在艺术方面培养了他。
entries.example_en: He was schooled in the arts by his father.

entries.definition_en: swim in or form a large group of fish
entries.example_cn: 鱼群在深水中结群游动。
entries.example_en: The fish school together in the deep water.

entries.definition_en: a bag used to carry school books and supplies
entries.example_cn: 她离开去上课前，把笔记本和铅笔装进了书包。
entries.example_en: She packed her schoolbag with notebooks and pencils before leaving for class.

entries.definition_en: a book prepared for use in schools or colleges
entries.example_cn: 老师把新的科学教科书发给了全班同学。
entries.example_en: The teacher handed out the new science schoolbook to the class.

entries.definition_en: a boy who is attending school
entries.example_cn: 那个男学生忘了带作业，不得不留在教室。
entries.example_en: The schoolboy forgot his homework and had to stay after class.

entries.definition_en: a young person who attends school or is of school age
entries.example_cn: 放学铃声响起后，那个学龄儿童走回家。
entries.example_en: The schoolchild walked home after the final bell rang.

entries.definition_en: the period of time when you are attending school
entries.example_cn: 回首我的上学时光，我记得那个旧操场。
entries.example_en: Looking back at my schooldays, I remember the old playground.

entries.definition_en: a person who is your friend and goes to the same school
entries.example_cn: 她是我们上小学时的同窗好友。
entries.example_en: She has been my schoolfriend since we were in primary school.

entries.definition_en: a female student attending school
entries.example_cn: 那个女学生穿着校服去上课。
entries.example_en: The schoolgirl wore a uniform to class.

entries.definition_cn: 校舍，尤指小型或单间校舍
entries.definition_en: a building housing a school, especially a small or single-room school
entries.example_cn: 那座旧校舍已被改造成社区中心。
entries.example_en: The old schoolhouse has been converted into a community center.

entries.definition_en: the process of being formally educated at a school
entries.example_cn: 他的受教育过程包括公立和私立机构。
entries.example_en: His schooling included both public and private institutions.

entries.definition_en: the act of teaching at school
entries.example_cn: 老师上午花时间为新课程进行教学。
entries.example_en: The teacher spent the morning on schooling for the new curriculum.

entries.definition_en: the training of an animal, especially a horse for dressage
entries.example_cn: 驯马师正在训练这匹小马。
entries.example_en: The trainer is working on the schooling of the young horse.

entries.definition_en: a female teacher, often perceived as strict or old-fashioned
entries.example_cn: 校长认为那位女教师的建议过于死板而将其驳回。
entries.example_en: The principal dismissed the schoolmarm's suggestion as too rigid.

entries.definition_en: the person in charge of a school
entries.example_cn: 校长宣布了新学期的日期。
entries.example_en: The schoolmaster announced the new term dates.

entries.definition_en: any person who acts as an educator
entries.example_cn: 在过去，村里的教育者教所有的孩子。
entries.example_en: In the old days, the village schoolmaster taught all the children.

entries.definition_cn: 一种生活在温暖加勒比海和大西洋水域的食用鱼
entries.definition_en: a food fish found in warm Caribbean and Atlantic waters
entries.example_cn: 这种鱼是当地渔民喜爱的捕获物。
entries.example_en: The schoolmaster is a popular catch for local fishermen.

entries.definition_en: a person you attend school with
entries.example_cn: 她是我的小学同学。
entries.example_en: She is my schoolmate from primary school.

entries.definition_en: a female schoolteacher, often perceived as strict
entries.example_cn: 这位老女教师以高标准著称。
entries.example_en: The old schoolmistress was known for her high standards.

entries.definition_en: a room in a school where lessons take place
entries.example_cn: 那间旧教室仍然保留着20世纪20年代的木制课桌。
entries.example_en: The old schoolroom still has the same wooden desks from the 1920s.

entries.definition_en: a teacher who works in a school below the college level
entries.example_cn: 这位老师给全班同学讲解了课程。
entries.example_en: The schoolteacher explained the lesson to the class.

entries.definition_en: happening or extending across the whole school
entries.example_cn: 全校大会吸引了每一位学生的参加。
entries.example_en: The schoolwide assembly was attended by every student.

entries.definition_en: Throughout the whole school.
entries.example_cn: 这项政策在全校范围内实施。
entries.example_en: The policy was implemented schoolwide.

entries.definition_cn: 学校作业，包括课堂作业和家庭作业
entries.definition_en: work done for school, including work in class and homework
entries.example_cn: 她花了一整晚完成家庭作业。
entries.example_en: She spent the evening finishing her schoolwork.

entries.definition_en: the open area outside a school building used for play
entries.example_cn: 下课后，孩子们在操场上踢足球。
entries.example_en: The children played football in the schoolyard after class.

entries.definition_en: a large glass used for serving beer
entries.example_cn: 他在酒吧点了一杯冰镇拉格啤酒。
entries.example_en: He ordered a cold schooner of lager at the pub.

entries.definition_en: a sailing vessel with two or more masts, all carrying fore-and-aft sails
entries.example_cn: 这艘历史悠久的双桅纵帆船在19世纪横渡了海洋。
entries.example_en: The historic schooner sailed across the ocean in the 19th century.

entries.definition_cn: 一种类似慢波尔卡的双人乡村舞
entries.definition_en: a partnered country dance resembling a slow polka
entries.example_cn: 这对舞伴在舞会上表演了一段优雅的施特西舞。
entries.example_en: The couple performed a graceful schottische at the ball.

entries.definition_en: music played to accompany the dance known as the schottische
entries.example_cn: 乐队演奏了一首欢快的施特西舞曲，引得人群起舞。
entries.example_en: The band played a lively schottische to get the crowd dancing.

entries.definition_en: to dance a schottische
entries.example_cn: 他们随着欢快的音乐在房间里跳施特西舞。
entries.example_en: They schottisched around the room to the lively music.

entries.definition_cn: （表演者为了博取关注而刻意使用的）噱头
entries.definition_en: a contrived and often used bit of business that a performer uses to steal attention
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员的噱头是假装自己是个害羞的图书管理员。
entries.example_en: The comedian's schtick involved pretending to be a shy librarian.

entries.definition_en: a prank or piece of clowning
entries.example_cn: 孩子们把袜子藏起来，给父母玩了一个恶作剧。
entries.example_en: The kids played a schtick on their parents by hiding all the socks.

entries.definition_en: a devious trick; a bit of cheating
entries.example_cn: 那名球员被发现使用狡诈的诡计不公平地赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The player was caught using a schtick to win the game unfairly.

entries.definition_en: a small amount or a single piece
entries.example_cn: 他拿了一块蛋糕吃了。
entries.example_en: He took a schtick of the cake and ate it.

entries.definition_en: to ski down a slope quickly and without stopping
entries.example_cn: 他们创纪录地快速滑下了整座山。
entries.example_en: They schussed down the mountain in record time.

entries.definition_en: a neutral vowel sound used in unstressed syllables
entries.example_cn: 在单词“about”中，第一个元音读作央元音。
entries.example_en: In the word 'about', the first vowel is pronounced as a schwa.

entries.definition_cn: 一种危害蘑菇和幼苗的小型黑色真菌蚋
entries.definition_en: a small black fungus gnat that is destructive to mushrooms and seedlings
entries.example_cn: 蘑菇产量的突然下降是由真菌蚋的侵扰造成的。
entries.example_en: The sudden decline in mushroom yield was caused by an infestation of sciara.

entries.definition_cn: 坐骨神经痛的；由坐骨神经痛引起的
entries.definition_en: relating to or caused by sciatica
entries.example_cn: 坐骨神经痛使她行走困难。
entries.example_en: Sciatic pain made it difficult for her to walk.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to the ischium or the part of the hipbone containing it
entries.example_cn: 髋骨切迹是骨盆的一个显著特征。
entries.example_en: The sciatic notch is a prominent feature of the pelvis.

entries.definition_en: neuralgia along the sciatic nerve
entries.example_cn: 事故后，这位病人遭受了严重的坐骨神经痛。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered from severe sciatica after the accident.

entries.definition_en: a particular branch of scientific knowledge
entries.example_cn: 物理学是一门迷人的学科。
entries.example_en: Physics is a fascinating branch of science.

entries.definition_cn: 在特定问题领域提出解决方案的能力或技巧
entries.definition_en: the ability or skill to produce solutions in a particular problem domain
entries.example_cn: 解决棘手的工程问题是一门学问。
entries.example_en: There is a science to solving difficult engineering problems.

entries.definition_en: (law) deliberately or knowingly
entries.example_cn: 被告明知且故意地隐瞒了缺陷。
entries.example_en: The defendant acted scienter in concealing the defect.

usage.label: 法律用语；通常作状语修饰行为动词

entries.definition_en: relating to the study of science
entries.example_cn: 科学研究中使用科学方法。
entries.example_en: The scientific method is used in research.

entries.definition_en: based on scientific principles
entries.example_cn: 他们的结论是科学的且有充分依据。
entries.example_en: Their conclusion was scientific and well-supported.

entries.definition_en: in a way that uses scientific methods
entries.example_cn: 这些结果经过科学分析以确保准确性。
entries.example_en: The results were analyzed scientifically to ensure accuracy.

entries.definition_en: a person who studies science and uses scientific methods
entries.example_cn: 科学家进行了实验来验证假设。
entries.example_en: The scientist conducted experiments to test the hypothesis.

entries.definition_cn: 蓝铃花（一种旧大陆植物，具狭窄基生叶及粉、蓝或白色穗状花）
entries.definition_en: an Old World plant of the genus Scilla having narrow basal leaves and pink or blue or white racemose flowers
entries.example_cn: 园丁欣赏着春天花园里盛开的精致蓝色蓝铃花。
entries.example_en: The gardener admired the delicate blue scilla blooming in the spring garden.

entries.definition_en: a long, curved sword traditionally used in the Middle East, with the sharp edge on the outer curve
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一把来自奥斯曼帝国的古老弯刀。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed an ancient scimitar from the Ottoman Empire.

entries.definition_en: a tiny or scarcely detectable amount
entries.example_cn: 没有任何证据支持他的说法。
entries.example_en: There was not a scintilla of evidence to support his claim.

entries.definition_en: a sparkling glittering particle
entries.example_cn: 钻石闪烁着一点光芒，吸引了观察者的目光。
entries.example_en: The diamond sparkled with a scintilla of light that caught the observer's eye.

entries.definition_cn: 充满活力、才华横溢或表现出高超技艺
entries.definition_en: to be lively, brilliant, or show great skill
entries.example_cn: 这位喜剧演员在表演中机智风趣，才华横溢。
entries.example_en: The comedian scintillated with wit during the performance.

entries.definition_cn: 以闪烁的方式发射或反射光线
entries.definition_en: to emit or reflect light in a flickering manner
entries.example_cn: 萤火虫在黑暗的花园里闪烁。
entries.example_en: The fireflies scintillated in the dark garden.

entries.definition_en: to reflect light brightly
entries.example_cn: 钻石在聚光灯下明亮地反射着光线。
entries.example_en: The diamond scintillated under the spotlight.

entries.definition_en: to give off sparks
entries.example_cn: 烟花在城市上空迸发出闪光。
entries.example_en: The fireworks scintillated above the city.

entries.definition_cn: 被带电粒子或高能光子击中时瞬间发光
entries.definition_en: to fluoresce momentarily when struck by a charged particle or high-energy photon
entries.example_cn: 气体暴露在辐射下时瞬间发光。
entries.example_en: The gas scintillated when exposed to radiation.

entries.definition_en: extremely clever and witty
entries.example_cn: 她在辩论中表现得机智过人。
entries.example_en: She gave a scintillating performance in the debate.

usage.label: figurative
usage.pattern: brilliantly or impressively clever, exciting, or witty

entries.definition_en: full of high spirits or excitement
entries.example_cn: 派对气氛热烈，笑声和音乐充满了整个房间。
entries.example_en: The party was scintillating, with laughter and music filling the room.

entries.definition_en: producing brief flashes of brilliant light
entries.example_cn: 闪烁的星星消失在云层后面。
entries.example_en: The scintillating stars disappeared behind the clouds.

entries.definition_en: a rapid change in brightness; a brief spark or flash
entries.example_cn: 一道突如其来的闪电照亮了漆黑的天空。
entries.example_en: A sudden scintillation of lightning illuminated the dark sky.

entries.definition_en: the quality of shining with a bright reflected light
entries.example_cn: 钻石的闪耀美丽地捕捉了光线。
entries.example_en: The scintillation of the diamond caught the light beautifully.

entries.definition_cn: 简短而机智风趣的表达；俏皮话
entries.definition_en: a brief expression that is amusing or clever; a witticism
entries.example_cn: 她的回答机智风趣，让全场鸦雀无声。
entries.example_en: Her reply was a scintillation of wit that silenced the room.

entries.definition_en: the twinkling of the stars caused by uneven refraction of starlight in the earth's atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 星光的闪烁让它们看起来像是在跳舞。
entries.example_en: The scintillation of the stars made them look like they were dancing.

entries.definition_en: a flash of light produced in a phosphor when it absorbs a photon or ionizing particle
entries.example_cn: 探测器记录到了来自入射粒子的闪烁。
entries.example_en: The detector registered a scintillation from the incoming particle.

entries.definition_en: a descendant or heir
entries.example_cn: 这个富裕家族的后裔继承了庄园。
entries.example_en: The scion of a wealthy family inherited the estate.

entries.definition_cn: 用于嫁接到砧木上的带芽枝条或嫩枝
entries.definition_en: a shoot or twig with buds, used for grafting onto a rootstock
entries.example_cn: 他把一棵优良李树的接穗嫁接到老砧木上。
entries.example_en: He grafted a scion from a better plum tree onto the old rootstock.

entries.definition_en: the action of dividing something by cutting or splitting it apart
entries.example_cn: 工会的分裂导致了一段极不稳定的时期。
entries.example_en: The scission of the union led to a period of great instability.

entries.definition_en: to cut something using scissors
entries.example_cn: 裁缝会将布料剪成正确的尺寸。
entries.example_en: The tailor will scissor the fabric to the correct size.

entries.definition_en: an edge tool having two crossed pivoting blades
entries.example_cn: 请用剪刀剪开这张纸。
entries.example_en: Please use the scissors to cut the paper.

entries.definition_en: a wrestling hold in which one wraps the legs around an opponent’s body or head, joins the feet, and squeezes
entries.example_cn: 摔跤手在被压制前挣脱了剪刀腿。
entries.example_en: The wrestler escaped the scissors before being pinned.

entries.definition_en: a gymnastic exercise performed on the pommel horse when the gymnast moves their legs as the blades of scissors move
entries.example_cn: 体操运动员在鞍马上完成了一个高难度的剪式动作。
entries.example_en: The gymnast executed a difficult scissors on the pommel horse.

entries.definition_en: the white, tough outer coat of the eye that covers the eyeball except for the cornea
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了患者的巩膜以查看黄疸的迹象。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the patient's sclera to check for signs of jaundice.

entries.definition_cn: 构成某些节肢动物外骨骼的硬化板片
entries.definition_en: a hard plate forming part of an arthropod's exoskeleton
entries.example_cn: 甲虫的外壳由许多小块硬板组成。
entries.example_en: The beetle's shell is made up of many small sclerites.

entries.definition_cn: 一种慢性全身性自身免疫病，可因胶原蛋白过度沉积而使皮肤及有时内脏变硬
entries.definition_en: a chronic systemic autoimmune disease that hardens the skin and sometimes internal organs through excessive collagen deposition
entries.example_cn: 患者在发现皮肤增厚后被诊断为硬皮病。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with scleroderma after noticing skin thickening.

entries.definition_cn: 身体组织的病理性硬化或增厚
entries.definition_en: a medical condition where tissue becomes hard and thick
entries.example_cn: 动脉硬化会使动脉壁变硬。
entries.example_en: Arterial sclerosis causes the artery walls to harden.

entries.definition_en: relating to or having a condition where body tissues become hard and thick
entries.example_cn: 硬化的动脉导致了严重的循环问题。
entries.example_en: The sclerotic arteries were causing severe circulation problems.

entries.definition_en: relating to the white outer layer of the eyeball
entries.example_cn: 外科医生在显微镜下检查了巩膜组织。
entries.example_en: The surgeon examined the sclerotic tissue under a microscope.

entries.definition_en: a hard, dark mass of fungal threads that stores food and can grow into a new fungus
entries.example_cn: 菌核在土壤中休眠，直到春天才萌发。
entries.example_en: The sclerotium remained dormant in the soil until spring.

entries.definition_en: to laugh at with contempt and derision
entries.example_cn: 他们嘲笑登月的想法。
entries.example_en: They scoffed at the idea of flying to the moon.

entries.definition_en: to treat with contemptuous disregard
entries.example_cn: 他轻蔑地无视规则，并立即违反了它们。
entries.example_en: He scoffed at the rules and broke them immediately.

entries.definition_en: an act of showing contempt by derision
entries.example_cn: 他的演讲遭到了观众的一声嘲弄。
entries.example_en: His speech was met with a scoff from the audience.

entries.definition_en: someone who mocks or treats something with contempt
entries.example_cn: 他是一个臭名昭著的嘲笑者，从不认真对待任何人的意见。
entries.example_en: He was a notorious scoffer who never took anyone's opinions seriously.

entries.definition_en: someone who eats food rapidly and greedily
entries.example_cn: 那个狼吞虎咽的人在不到五分钟的时间里就吃完了整顿饭。
entries.example_en: The scoffer finished his entire meal in less than five minutes.

usage.label: UK slang
usage.pattern: noun for someone who eats a large amount

entries.definition_en: an expression of contempt or derision
entries.example_cn: 她嘲笑他的提议，这让他感到受冒犯。
entries.example_en: Her scoffing at his proposal offended him.

entries.definition_en: a person who habitually breaks the law and ignores court orders
entries.example_cn: 法官因该屡犯法者的多次违规行为判处他社区服务。
entries.example_en: The judge sentenced the scofflaw to community service for his repeated violations.

usage.label: US
usage.pattern: 尤指违反轻微法律或无视停车罚单等法院传票的人

entries.definition_en: to speak to someone angrily because they have done something wrong
entries.example_cn: 老师因学生上课迟到而斥责了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher scolded the student for being late to class.

entries.definition_en: of a bird, to make harsh vocalizations in aggression
entries.example_cn: 有人靠近时，那些筑巢的鸟就大声发出攻击性的叫声。
entries.example_en: The nesting birds scolded loudly whenever anyone approached.

entries.definition_en: a person who constantly finds fault with others and annoys them
entries.example_cn: 在家庭琐事上，我妈妈有点爱挑刺。
entries.example_en: My mother is a bit of a scold when it comes to household chores.

entries.definition_en: the act of rebuking someone harshly
entries.example_cn: 老师因学生迟到而严厉地责骂了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave the student a scolding for being late.

entries.definition_en: an abnormal lateral curve to the vertebral column
entries.example_cn: 医生诊断出这名青少年患有严重的脊柱侧弯。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the teenager with severe scoliosis.

entries.definition_cn: 鲭科鱼类，包括鲭鱼和金枪鱼
entries.definition_en: a fish of the family Scombridae, including mackerels and tunas
entries.example_cn: 鲭科鱼类，包括鲭鱼和金枪鱼，是重要的食用鱼和游钓鱼类。
entries.example_en: Scombroid fish, including mackerel and tuna, are important food and game fish.

entries.definition_cn: 因食用变质鱼类引起的一种食物中毒
entries.definition_en: a form of food poisoning caused by eating spoiled fish
entries.example_cn: 食客食用变质金枪鱼后出现了鲭鱼中毒。
entries.example_en: The diners developed scombroid poisoning after eating spoiled tuna.

entries.definition_en: pertaining to mackerel or the mackerel family
entries.example_cn: 这种鲭科鱼具有鲭鱼典型的流线型身体。
entries.example_en: The scombroid fish has the streamlined body typical of mackerel.

entries.definition_en: a decorative bracket mounted on a wall to hold candles or lights
entries.example_cn: 走廊墙上的古董壁灯支架给客人们投下温暖的光芒。
entries.example_en: The antique sconce on the hallway wall cast a warm glow over the guests.

entries.definition_en: a candle or torch fixed in a holder
entries.example_cn: 在18世纪，烛台灯是许多家庭的主要光源。
entries.example_en: In the 18th century, a sconce was the primary source of light in many homes.

entries.definition_cn: （过时）棚屋或摊位，尤指设在路旁的
entries.definition_en: an obsolete hut or stall, especially one set up by a roadside
entries.example_cn: 小贩在路旁搭起一间棚屋来卖枝条。
entries.example_en: The peddler raised a sconce by the highway to sell switches.

entries.definition_en: a small fort built to defend a strategic point like a river crossing or castle gate
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的堡垒守卫着通往首都城市的狭窄通道。
entries.example_en: The ancient sconce guarded the narrow pass leading to the capital city.

entries.definition_en: a small, rich biscuit made with cream and eggs, baked in an oven or on a griddle.
entries.example_cn: 她早餐端上了配着凝脂奶油和果酱的温热司康饼。
entries.example_en: She served warm scones with clotted cream and jam for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: to take out or up using a scoop
entries.example_cn: 她把汤舀进碗里。
entries.example_en: She scooped the soup into bowls.

entries.definition_en: the amount of food or liquid that a scoop can hold
entries.example_cn: 请盛一大勺冰淇淋。
entries.example_en: Please serve the ice cream in a generous scoop.

entries.definition_en: an exclusive news story or fact reported before anyone else
entries.example_cn: 这家报纸获得了有关选举结果的独家新闻。
entries.example_en: The newspaper got an exclusive scoop on the election results.

entries.definition_en: a large ladle
entries.example_cn: 他用一个大汤勺盛炖菜。
entries.example_en: He used a giant scoop to serve the stew.

entries.definition_en: a hollow shape made by removing material
entries.example_cn: 风在沙地上吹出了一个凹坑。
entries.example_en: The wind created a scoop in the sand.

entries.definition_cn: 挖泥机、反铲挖掘机或前端装载机的铲斗
entries.definition_en: the digging attachment or bucket of a dredge, backhoe, or front-end loader
entries.example_cn: 操作员调整铲斗以便挖得更深。
entries.example_en: The operator adjusted the scoop to dig deeper.

entries.definition_en: street names for gamma hydroxybutyrate
entries.example_cn: 警方警告人们不要使用被称为“scoop”的毒品。
entries.example_en: Police warned against the dangers of the drug known as scoop.

entries.definition_en: to report a story before someone else
entries.example_cn: 这家报纸抢在竞争对手之前报道了选举结果。
entries.example_en: The newspaper scooped its rival on the election results.

entries.definition_cn: 迅速或匆忙地跑；快速移动
entries.definition_en: to run or move quickly or hastily
entries.example_cn: 铃响前，孩子们急跑过操场。
entries.example_en: The children scooted across the playground before the bell rang.

entries.definition_en: a small vehicle with small wheels and a low-powered engine attached to the rear wheel
entries.example_cn: 他买了一辆新摩托车以便在城市里出行。
entries.example_en: He bought a new scooter to get around the city.

entries.definition_en: a small two-wheeled vehicle for children that is pushed with the feet
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子推着滑板车沿着人行道走。
entries.example_en: The child pushed the scooter along the sidewalk.

entries.definition_en: a small motorboat that looks like a motor scooter
entries.example_cn: 他们租了一艘摩托艇快速穿过湖泊。
entries.example_en: They rented a scooter to cross the lake quickly.

entries.definition_en: a sailing boat with runners and a cross-shaped frame used on ice
entries.example_cn: 探险家们使用一种特殊的冰上帆船穿越冰封的海洋。
entries.example_en: The explorers used a special scooter to travel across the frozen sea.

entries.definition_en: a large black diving duck found in northern regions
entries.example_cn: 我们在北部的湖里发现了一只罕见的潜鸭。
entries.example_en: We spotted a rare scooter swimming in the northern lake.

entries.definition_en: the range or extent of something
entries.example_cn: 该项目的范围包括网站的设计和建造。
entries.example_en: The scope of the project includes designing and building the website.

entries.definition_en: the potential range of action, freedom, or opportunity available
entries.example_cn: 这份工作给了她充分进行独立研究的余地。
entries.example_en: The job gives her plenty of scope for independent research.

entries.definition_en: a sighting device used for aiming a projectile at a target
entries.example_cn: 他调节步枪瞄准镜，以更清楚地看准目标。
entries.example_en: He adjusted the rifle scope to get a clearer view of the target.

entries.definition_en: electronic equipment that displays electrical signals as images
entries.example_cn: 工程师将示波器连接到电路以监测电压。
entries.example_en: The engineer connected the scope to the circuit to monitor the voltage.

entries.definition_en: an alkaloid that acts as a sedative, treats nausea, and dilates pupils during eye examinations
entries.example_cn: 医生给病人使用东莨菪碱，以帮助其在操作前放松。
entries.example_en: The doctor administered scopolamine to help the patient relax before the procedure.

entries.definition_cn: 使因高温而干枯、焦灼或表面烧焦
entries.definition_en: dry out, parch, or burn something superficially by intense heat
entries.example_cn: 热浪使大地变得炎热干燥。
entries.example_en: The heatwave scorched the landscape.

entries.definition_en: become superficially burned
entries.example_cn: 在强烈的阳光下，草地开始表面灼伤。
entries.example_en: The grass began to scorch under the intense sunlight.

entries.definition_cn: 彻底毁灭（如同被火烧毁）
entries.definition_en: destroy completely by or as if by fire
entries.example_cn: 野火烧毁了整个森林。
entries.example_en: The wildfire scorched the entire forest.

entries.definition_en: subject to harsh criticism
entries.example_cn: 该政治家在辩论中遭到了反对派的严厉批评。
entries.example_en: The politician was scorched by the opposition during the debate.

entries.definition_en: a surface burn
entries.example_cn: 太阳在她的胳膊上留下了灼伤。
entries.example_en: The sun left a scorch on her arm.

entries.definition_en: a discoloration caused by heat
entries.example_cn: 那块布料在熨斗停留过久处出现了变色。
entries.example_en: The fabric showed a scorch where the iron had been left too long.

entries.definition_cn: 轻微且表面地灼烧以影响颜色
entries.definition_en: burn slightly and superficially so as to affect color
entries.example_cn: 烤奶酪时小心不要将其表面烧焦变色。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to scorch the cheese while grilling.

entries.definition_cn: 植物叶片因高温、缺水或真菌而产生的褐变或焦枯
entries.definition_en: brown discoloration of plant leaves caused by heat, drought, or fungi
entries.example_cn: 叶片上的焦枯可能由高温、缺水或真菌感染造成。
entries.example_en: The scorch on the leaves can result from heat, drought, or fungal infection.

entries.definition_en: dried out, damaged, or burned by exposure to intense heat or sunlight
entries.example_cn: 草地被炎热的夏日阳光晒得焦黄。
entries.example_en: The grass was scorched by the intense summer sun.

entries.definition_cn: 被火或高温烧毁或严重损坏的
entries.definition_en: burnt or severely damaged by fire or intense heat
entries.example_cn: 这个被烧毁的村庄没有一座建筑物还屹立着。
entries.example_en: The scorched village had no buildings left standing.

entries.definition_en: an extremely hot day
entries.example_cn: 我们待在室内以躲避酷热的一天。
entries.example_en: We stayed inside to escape the scorcher.

entries.definition_cn: 精彩的进球，尤指大力射门取得的进球
entries.definition_en: a very good goal, especially one made with a very hard shot
entries.example_cn: 他在禁区外大力射门，打进了一记精彩进球。
entries.example_en: He scored a scorcher from outside the penalty area.

entries.definition_en: extremely hot and dry, capable of burning or drying out a surface
entries.example_cn: 烈日炙烤得地面仿佛着了火。
entries.example_en: The scorching sun made the ground feel like fire.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes burns or extreme heat
entries.example_cn: 热风灼热地吹过沙漠。
entries.example_en: The wind blew scorching hot across the desert.

entries.definition_cn: 表示质量或成绩的数字、字母或其他符号，尤指学生成绩；分数
entries.definition_en: a number, letter, or other symbol indicating quality, especially a student's performance
entries.example_cn: 我在数学考试中得了高分。
entries.example_en: I got a high score on my math test.

entries.definition_en: the number of points a team or person has in a game
entries.example_cn: 最终比分是 3 比 1。
entries.example_en: The final score was 3 to 1.

entries.definition_cn: 显示乐曲各部分的书面乐谱，常将不同声部写在分开的五线谱上；乐谱；总谱
entries.definition_en: a written form of a musical composition showing its parts, often on separate staves
entries.example_cn: 指挥在演出前研究了乐谱。
entries.example_en: The conductor studied the score before the performance.

entries.definition_en: to get points in a game or competition
entries.example_cn: 球队在上半场进了三个球。
entries.example_en: The team scored three goals in the first half.

entries.definition_cn: 获得想要的东西（常用于非正式语境）
entries.definition_en: to obtain something desired, often in an informal context
entries.example_cn: 他弄到了两张免费的音乐会门票。
entries.example_en: He scored two free tickets to the concert.

entries.definition_en: to cut or incise a groove or notch into a surface
entries.example_cn: 他用刀沿折线在硬纸板上刻出一道槽。
entries.example_en: He scored the cardboard along the fold line with a knife.

entries.definition_cn: 为指定乐器或声部作曲或配器
entries.definition_en: to compose or arrange music for specified instruments or voices
entries.example_cn: 贝多芬为这部交响曲配器，使其适合大型管弦乐队演奏。
entries.example_en: Beethoven scored the symphony for a large orchestra.

entries.definition_en: to underline text with a line
entries.example_cn: 请在文中给重要的单词划线。
entries.example_en: Please score the important words in the text.

entries.definition_en: a group of twenty people or things
entries.example_cn: 陪审团由二十名成员组成。
entries.example_en: The jury consists of a score of members.

entries.definition_en: a large board for displaying the score of a contest (and some other information)
entries.example_cn: 粉丝们聚集在记分牌周围查看最新比分。
entries.example_en: Fans gathered around the scoreboard to check the latest results.

entries.definition_en: a record of scores kept during a game of golf
entries.example_cn: 这位高尔夫球手检查了他的记分卡，以确保正确记录了每一杆。
entries.example_en: The golfer checked his scorecard to ensure he had recorded every shot correctly.

entries.definition_en: an official who records the score during the progress of a game
entries.example_cn: 记分员在最后几分钟犯了一个错误。
entries.example_en: The scorekeeper made a mistake in the final minutes.

entries.definition_en: having no points scored
entries.example_cn: 球队在上半场一直未得分。
entries.example_en: The team remained scoreless throughout the first half.

entries.definition_en: a player who makes a score in a game or contest
entries.example_cn: 当他们的头号得分手打入制胜一球时，全队欢呼庆祝。
entries.example_en: The team celebrated when their top scorer hit the winning goal.

entries.definition_en: an official who records the score during the progress of a game
entries.example_cn: 记分员将最终分数写在记分牌上。
entries.example_en: The scorer wrote down the final points on the scoreboard.

entries.definition_en: a logger who marks trees to be felled
entries.example_cn: 林务员雇佣了一名伐木标记员来标记待砍伐的树木。
entries.example_en: The forester hired a scorer to mark the trees for the logging crew.

entries.definition_en: a large number or amount
entries.example_cn: 昨晚有数百人参加了音乐会。
entries.example_en: Scores of people attended the concert last night.

entries.definition_cn: 从矿石中冶炼金属后留下的炉渣或浮渣
entries.definition_en: the slag or dross that remains after the smelting of metal from an ore
entries.example_cn: 冶炼过程留下了炉渣。
entries.example_en: The smelting process left scoria as slag.

entries.definition_en: the act of evaluating performance by assigning grades or scores
entries.example_cn: 由于技术问题，考试的评分被推迟了。
entries.example_en: The scoring of the exam was delayed due to technical issues.

entries.definition_en: to regard someone or something as unworthy of respect
entries.example_cn: 评论家们轻视这部新电影，认为它是浪费时间。
entries.example_en: The critics scorned the new movie as a waste of time.

entries.definition_en: to reject something with contempt
entries.example_cn: 他们轻蔑地拒绝了帮助，继续自行其是。
entries.example_en: They scorned the offer of help and continued on their own.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of contempt and intense dislike for someone or something
entries.example_cn: 她对那个粗鲁的评论报以彻底的蔑视。
entries.example_en: She looked at the rude comment with utter scorn.

entries.definition_en: the act of showing open disrespect for a person or thing
entries.example_cn: 他对规则的不敬在他的行为中显而易见。
entries.example_en: His scorn for the rules was evident in his behavior.

entries.definition_en: treated with dislike or contempt
entries.example_cn: 他因思想不循规蹈矩而被同伴蔑视。
entries.example_en: He was scorned by his peers for his unconventional ideas.

entries.definition_en: a person who expresses contempt by remarks or facial expression
entries.example_cn: 人群中的嘲笑者嘲笑演讲者的错误。
entries.example_en: The scorners in the crowd laughed at the speaker's mistakes.

entries.definition_en: expressing extreme contempt or disdain
entries.example_cn: 他对有人建议他懒惰的说法投以轻蔑的一瞥。
entries.example_en: He gave a scornful glance at the suggestion that he was lazy.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows you do not respect or like someone or something
entries.example_cn: 她轻蔑地看了一眼过时的提案，并立即予以拒绝。
entries.example_en: She looked at the outdated proposal scornfully and rejected it immediately.

entries.definition_cn: 一种海洋鱼类，身体呈锥形，头部有甲壳，带有毒刺
entries.definition_en: a type of marine fish with a tapering body, armored head, and venomous spines
entries.example_cn: 潜水员小心地避开了躲在珊瑚丛中的毒鲉。
entries.example_en: The diver carefully avoided the scorpionfish hiding among the coral.

entries.definition_cn: 免受伤害或惩罚地；安然无恙地
entries.definition_en: without suffering any harm or paying any penalty
entries.example_cn: 他设法在事故中毫发无损地逃了出来。
entries.example_en: He managed to escape the accident scot-free.

entries.definition_en: a large black diving duck found in the northern parts of the Northern Hemisphere
entries.example_cn: 我们在海湾里发现了一群正在潜水捕鱼的潜鸭。
entries.example_en: We spotted a flock of scoters diving for fish in the bay.

entries.definition_en: an isolated area of diminished vision within the visual field
entries.example_cn: 病人报告说她的视野中心有一个小暗点。
entries.example_en: The patient reported a small scotoma in the center of her vision.

entries.definition_en: a wicked or evil person; someone who does evil deliberately
entries.example_cn: 侦探终于抓住了那个一直从银行偷窃的恶棍。
entries.example_en: The detective finally caught the scoundrel who had been stealing from the bank.

entries.definition_en: to clean something by rubbing it hard
entries.example_cn: 你需要用力擦洗平底锅以去除烧焦的食物。
entries.example_en: You need to scour the pan to remove the burnt food.

entries.definition_en: to rub or scrub something hard
entries.example_cn: 她用力摩擦地板直到它发亮。
entries.example_en: She scoured the floor until it shone.

entries.definition_en: to clean or empty something using a liquid
entries.example_cn: 这台机器用热水冲洗衣物。
entries.example_en: The machine scours the clothes with hot water.

entries.definition_en: to examine something very carefully and thoroughly
entries.example_cn: 警察仔细搜查大楼寻找线索。
entries.example_en: Police scoured the building for clues.

entries.definition_cn: 被流水冲刷出的地方或凹坑，尤指溪流河床中的冲刷坑
entries.definition_en: a place or depression scoured out by running water, especially in a streambed
entries.example_cn: 瀑布下方形成了一个深深的冲刷坑。
entries.example_en: A deep scour formed below the waterfall.

entries.definition_en: worn away or smoothed by the action of water, ice, or wind
entries.example_cn: 被侵蚀的岩石显示出古代洪水的痕迹。
entries.example_en: The scoured rocks showed signs of ancient flooding.

entries.definition_en: a person or thing that cleanses by scrubbing vigorously
entries.example_cn: 这所老房子需要专业的擦洗者来去除厚厚的污垢。
entries.example_en: The old house needed a professional scourer to remove the thick layers of grime.

entries.definition_en: a person who travels widely and energetically
entries.example_cn: 作为一名文学漫游者，他走访了欧洲的每一座主要图书馆以收集手稿。
entries.example_en: As a literary scourer, he visited every major library in Europe to collect manuscripts.

entries.definition_en: a whip used to inflict punishment
entries.example_cn: 囚犯被迫背着鞭子作为他犯罪的标志。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was forced to carry the scourge as a sign of his crime.

entries.definition_en: something that causes great suffering or destruction
entries.example_cn: 干旱已成为该地区农民的灾难。
entries.example_en: Drought has become a scourge for farmers in the region.

entries.definition_cn: 被视为上天惩罚工具的人
entries.definition_en: a person regarded as an agent of divine punishment
entries.example_cn: 那个暴君被视为众神派来的惩罚者。
entries.example_en: The tyrant was regarded as a scourge sent by the gods.

entries.definition_en: to punish severely or criticize harshly
entries.example_cn: 政府因处理危机不当而遭到媒体的严厉抨击。
entries.example_en: The government was scourged by the media for its handling of the crisis.

entries.definition_en: to whip or beat
entries.example_cn: 骑手鞭打马匹以让它跑得更快。
entries.example_en: The horse was scourged by the rider to make it run faster.

entries.definition_en: to cause great suffering or widespread harm to
entries.example_cn: 战争使整座城市遭受重创，只剩下一片废墟。
entries.example_en: The war scourged the entire city, leaving nothing but rubble.

entries.definition_en: the act of cleaning a surface by scrubbing it with soap and water
entries.example_cn: 厨房需要彻底擦洗以去除烧焦的油脂。
entries.example_en: The kitchen required a thorough scouring to remove the burnt-on grease.

entries.definition_en: erosion caused by moving water, especially in a watercourse
entries.example_cn: 水流冲刷侵蚀了运河河床。
entries.example_en: Scouring had eroded the bed of the canal.

entries.definition_en: severe diarrhea affecting livestock
entries.example_cn: 农民立即治疗了患腹泻的牛。
entries.example_en: The farmer treated the sick cattle for scours immediately.

entries.definition_cn: 利物浦地区的一种炖菜，通常含有肉、洋葱、胡萝卜和土豆
entries.definition_en: a stew associated with Liverpool, usually containing meat, onions, carrots, and potatoes
entries.example_cn: Scouse 是一种传统上与利物浦有关的丰盛炖菜。
entries.example_en: Scouse is a hearty stew traditionally associated with Liverpool.

entries.definition_en: an adult member of the Boy Scouts movement
entries.example_cn: 这位童子军成年成员帮助年轻的小队员们打结。
entries.example_en: The scouter helped the young scouts tie their knots.

entries.definition_en: the act of exploring an area to gather information about it
entries.example_cn: 这次军事行动涉及对地形的广泛侦察。
entries.example_en: The military operation involved extensive scouting of the terrain.

entries.definition_en: the leader of a troop of Scouts
entries.example_cn: 童子军领队向新加入的童子军队员发表了讲话。
entries.example_en: The scoutmaster gave a speech to the new recruits.

entries.definition_en: a flat-bottomed boat with sloping ends
entries.example_cn: 他们将货物装上平底驳船。
entries.example_en: They loaded the cargo onto the scow.

entries.definition_en: a barge for carrying bulk materials
entries.example_cn: 这艘运货驳船顺流而下运送煤炭。
entries.example_en: The scow carried coal down the river.

entries.definition_en: frown with displeasure
entries.example_cn: 老师怒视着那些吵闹的学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher scowled at the noisy students.

entries.definition_en: a facial expression of dislike or displeasure
entries.example_cn: 当他打断她时，她对他投以怒视。
entries.example_en: She gave him a scowl when he interrupted her.

entries.definition_en: looking sullen or unfriendly
entries.example_cn: 老师用怒视的表情看着吵闹的学生们。
entries.example_en: The teacher looked at the noisy students with a scowling expression.

entries.definition_en: an archaic term for a thin or scrawny person or animal
entries.example_cn: 在几个月生病后，他看起来瘦骨嶙峋。
entries.example_en: After months of illness, he looked like a scrag.

entries.definition_en: the lean, thin part of an animal's neck
entries.example_cn: 屠夫将羊颈部的瘦削部分单独出售。
entries.example_en: The butcher sold the scrag of the sheep separately.

entries.definition_cn: 小牛肉颈部的瘦削末端
entries.definition_en: the lean end of a neck of veal
entries.example_cn: 这道炖菜需要一块小牛肉颈部的瘦削末端。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for a piece of scrag to make the stew.

entries.definition_en: to strangle someone using an iron collar
entries.example_cn: 这名罪犯在地牢中被用铁项圈勒死。
entries.example_en: The criminal was scragged in the dungeon.

entries.definition_en: to twist or wring the neck of an animal
entries.example_cn: 农夫扭断了小牛的脖子以防止它乱跑。
entries.example_en: The farmer scragged the calf to stop it from wandering.

entries.definition_cn: 潦草的；瘦削的；不整洁的
entries.definition_en: looking ragged, thin, or untidy
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子有一个长满杂草的凌乱花园。
entries.example_en: The old house had a scraggly garden full of weeds.

entries.definition_en: being very thin
entries.example_cn: 在那场漫长的疾病之后，他看起来瘦骨嶙峋且虚弱。
entries.example_en: After the long illness, he looked scraggly and weak.

entries.definition_en: very thin and bony
entries.example_cn: 那位瘦骨嶙峋的老人坐在门廊上。
entries.example_en: The scraggy old man sat on the porch.

entries.definition_cn: 表面或轮廓凹凸不平的
entries.definition_en: having a sharply uneven surface or outline
entries.example_cn: 那些凹凸不平的山丘覆盖着干草。
entries.example_en: The scraggy hills were covered in dry grass.

entries.definition_en: leave immediately; used usually in the imperative form
entries.example_cn: 警察到了，所以我们得赶紧离开。
entries.example_en: The police arrived, so we had to scram.

entries.definition_cn: 出于安全原因（通常因紧急情况）关闭核反应堆或其他系统
entries.definition_en: to shut down a nuclear reactor or other system for safety reasons, usually because of an emergency
entries.example_cn: 检测到温度危险上升后，操作员让反应堆停堆了。
entries.example_en: The operator scrammed the reactor when a dangerous rise in temperature was detected.

entries.definition_en: to move quickly and hurriedly
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不匆忙赶去赶最后一班火车。
entries.example_en: We had to scramble to catch the last train.

entries.definition_en: to climb awkwardly using hands and feet
entries.example_cn: 孩子们手脚并用地爬上了岩石山。
entries.example_en: The children scrambled up the rocky hill.

entries.definition_cn: 把食物（尤指鸡蛋）搅拌并炒成松散的一团
entries.definition_en: to mix and cook food, especially eggs, into a loose mass
entries.example_cn: 她用叉子用力搅拌鸡蛋。
entries.example_en: She scrambled the eggs with a fork.

entries.definition_en: to arrange things in a random order
entries.example_cn: 在我发牌之前，别把牌弄乱。
entries.example_en: Don't scramble the cards before I deal them.

entries.definition_en: a disorganized and rude struggle
entries.example_cn: 选举变成了对选票的争夺。
entries.example_en: The election turned into a scramble for votes.

entries.definition_en: hasty and undignified rushing about
entries.example_cn: 截止日期前，办公室一直处于持续的慌乱状态。
entries.example_en: The office was in a state of constant scramble before the deadline.

entries.definition_en: to make something unintelligible
entries.example_cn: 噪音使无线电信号难以接收。
entries.example_en: The noise scrambled the radio signal.

entries.definition_cn: 混杂的；（信号等）被扰乱而难以理解的
entries.definition_en: mixed together in a disorderly or confusing way; (of a signal) encoded so that it is difficult to understand
entries.example_cn: 那段被扰乱的电视信号需要解码后才能看懂。
entries.example_en: The scrambled TV signal required decoding before we could understand it.

entries.definition_cn: 配备坚固轮胎和悬挂系统的轻型越野摩托车
entries.definition_en: a lightweight motorcycle equipped with rugged tires and suspension for off-road riding
entries.example_cn: 他们租了一辆越野摩托车来探索国家公园的崎岖地形。
entries.example_en: They rented a scrambler to explore the rugged terrain of the national park.

entries.definition_en: a person who moves rapidly or climbs quickly
entries.example_cn: 那个行动敏捷的人比团队其他人都先到达了山顶。
entries.example_en: The scrambler reached the summit before the rest of the team.

entries.definition_en: electronic equipment that makes speech unintelligible during transmission and restores it at reception
entries.example_cn: 无线电广播使用加密器，防止未经授权的听众理解信息。
entries.example_en: The radio broadcast used a scrambler to prevent unauthorized listeners from understanding the message.

entries.definition_en: a small piece broken off from something larger
entries.example_cn: 他从地板上捡起一张碎纸片。
entries.example_en: He picked up a scrap of paper from the floor.

entries.definition_en: material that is useless and needs to be thrown away
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂收集废金属进行回收。
entries.example_en: The factory collects scrap metal to recycle.

entries.definition_en: a small amount of food or other material left after the main part has been used
entries.example_cn: 袋子里只剩下几片面包屑。
entries.example_en: There were only a few scraps of bread left in the bag.

entries.definition_en: a fight or struggle between people or groups
entries.example_cn: 那场拳击赛是一场激烈的争斗。
entries.example_en: The boxing match was a violent scrap.

entries.definition_en: to get rid of something that is old or useless
entries.example_cn: 他们决定把那辆旧车扔掉，买一辆新的。
entries.example_en: They decided to scrap the old car and buy a new one.

entries.definition_en: to have a disagreement or fight with someone
entries.example_cn: 那两个邻居因边界线问题开始争吵。
entries.example_en: The two neighbors began to scrap over the boundary line.

entries.definition_en: to turn something into waste material
entries.example_cn: 该公司计划把这些机器拆解成废料。
entries.example_en: The company plans to scrap the machines for their metal.

entries.definition_en: an album for pasting clippings, notes, or pictures
entries.example_cn: 她花了一下午时间在她的剪贴簿中整理童年的回忆。
entries.example_en: She spent the afternoon organizing her childhood memories in her scrapbook.

entries.definition_en: to cut the surface of or wear away the surface of
entries.example_cn: 砂纸把墙上的油漆刮掉了。
entries.example_en: The sandpaper scraped the paint off the wall.

entries.definition_en: drag something across a surface, often repeatedly, producing friction
entries.example_cn: 猫开始用爪子在沙发上反复抓挠。
entries.example_en: The cat began to scrape its claws against the sofa.

entries.definition_en: collect or gather, often from limited materials
entries.example_cn: 他们凑集了足够的干木柴来生火。
entries.example_en: They scraped together enough dry wood to make a fire.

usage.label: scrape together + noun
usage.pattern: w12587r8 supports collecting or gathering something, especially without regard to quality.

entries.definition_en: a person who behaves in a very strange and unpredictable way
entries.example_cn: 这位怪人导演决定在一个完全不同的国家拍摄这部电影。
entries.example_en: The screwball director decided to film the movie in a completely different country.

entries.definition_cn: 螺旋球；一种带有旋转、轨迹异常弯曲的棒球投球
entries.definition_en: a baseball pitch thrown with a twisting wrist motion that curves unusually
entries.example_cn: 投手投出一个螺旋球，击球手无法击中。
entries.example_en: The pitcher threw a screwball that the batter could not hit.

entries.definition_en: a hand tool with a handle and a tip that fits into the head of a screw
entries.example_cn: 我需要一把螺丝刀来修这个架子。
entries.example_en: I need a screwdriver to fix this shelf.

entries.definition_en: a cocktail made with vodka and orange juice
entries.example_cn: 让我们点一杯螺丝起子鸡尾酒配午餐。
entries.example_en: Let's order a screwdriver to go with our lunch.

entries.definition_en: sexual intercourse (informal and vulgar slang)
entries.example_cn: 他们性交时被当场发现。
entries.example_en: They were caught in the act of screwing.

entries.definition_en: a substantial mistake, usually causing problems for more people than those who made it
entries.example_cn: 由于规划不当，整个项目彻底搞砸了。
entries.example_en: The entire project was a total screwup due to poor planning.

entries.definition_cn: 经常犯严重错误的人；办事马虎的人（口语）
entries.definition_en: a person who often makes substantial mistakes; a bungler
entries.example_cn: 他们不得不替换那个总是把数字输错的马虎鬼。
entries.example_en: They had to replace the screwup who kept entering the wrong figures.

entries.definition_en: behaving in a strange or irrational way
entries.example_cn: 他古怪的行为让每个人都不舒服。
entries.example_en: His screwy behavior made everyone uncomfortable.

entries.definition_cn: 草率地写下（不注重细节）
entries.definition_en: to write down quickly without paying much attention to detail
entries.example_cn: 他赶紧潦草地记下了电话号码，以免忘记。
entries.example_en: He scribbled down the phone number before he forgot it.

entries.definition_en: to write carelessly
entries.example_cn: 她没读那份文件就潦草地签了名。
entries.example_en: She scribbled her signature on the document without reading it.

entries.definition_en: poor or messy handwriting
entries.example_cn: 那张纸条字迹潦草，很难辨认。
entries.example_en: The note was so hard to read because of the scribble.

entries.definition_en: an aimless or messy drawing
entries.example_cn: 孩子用五颜六色的线条胡乱涂鸦，盖满了整页纸。
entries.example_en: The child covered the page with a scribble of colorful lines.

entries.definition_cn: 潦草或拙劣的作家或艺术家
entries.definition_en: a hasty or untalented writer or artist
entries.example_cn: 评论家认为他不过是个拙劣的写作者。
entries.example_en: The critic dismissed him as a mere scribbler.

entries.definition_en: an informal term for a journalist
entries.example_cn: 该报的首席记者以耸人听闻的标题而闻名。
entries.example_en: The newspaper's chief scribbler was known for his sensational headlines.

entries.definition_en: an informal term for a journalist
entries.example_cn: 这位记者报道了当地的选举。
entries.example_en: The scribe filed a story about the local election.

entries.definition_en: someone employed to make written copies of documents and manuscripts
entries.example_cn: 在修道院里，抄写员用手抄写古代文本。
entries.example_en: In the monastery, the scribe copied the ancient texts by hand.

entries.definition_en: a sharp-pointed awl used for marking wood or metal to be cut
entries.example_cn: 他在锯木头之前用划线器做了标记。
entries.example_en: He used a scribe to mark the wood before sawing.

entries.definition_cn: （在金属加工中）用尖头工具划线
entries.definition_en: to score a line on a surface using a pointed instrument, typically in metalworking
entries.example_cn: 工人在切割金属板之前先在上面划了一条线。
entries.example_en: The worker scribed a line on the metal sheet before cutting.

entries.definition_cn: 书写，尤指以抄写员的身份书写
entries.definition_en: to write, especially in the role of a scribe
entries.example_cn: 修士把国王的诏令抄写在羊皮纸上。
entries.example_en: The monk scribed the king’s decree onto parchment.

entries.definition_en: a sharp tool used for marking lines on wood or metal before cutting
entries.example_cn: 木匠在锯切木材之前使用划线器在木头上标记精确的线条。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a scriber to mark precise lines on the timber before sawing.

entries.definition_cn: 有组织的队伍之间进行的练习赛，尤指锦标赛或其他竞技赛事前的比赛
entries.definition_en: a practice match between organized teams, especially before a tournament or other competitive event
entries.example_cn: 这支队伍在锦标赛前安排了几场练习赛。
entries.example_en: The team scheduled several scrims before the tournament.

entries.definition_en: a firm open-weave fabric used for a curtain in the theater
entries.example_cn: 舞台工作人员拉开薄纱幕布，露出了演员们。
entries.example_en: The stagehand pulled the scrim aside to reveal the actors.

entries.definition_en: to practice playing a sport
entries.example_cn: 教练到达前，球员们进行了一小时的练习赛。
entries.example_en: The players scrimmaged for an hour before the coach arrived.

entries.definition_en: a practice play between a football team's squads
entries.example_cn: 在大比赛之前，球队进行了一场练习赛以测试他们的新战术。
entries.example_en: The team held a scrimmage before the big game to test their new strategies.

entries.definition_en: a noisy and disorderly fight
entries.example_cn: 一场突如其来的争吵演变成了走廊里的全面混战。
entries.example_en: A sudden argument turned into a full-blown scrimmage in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: to live on a very small amount of money or food
entries.example_cn: 他们不得不节衣缩食以维持生计。
entries.example_en: They had to scrimp to make ends meet.

entries.definition_cn: 鲸骨、鲸牙或海象牙上的雕刻品（通常由美国捕鲸者制作）
entries.definition_en: a carving (or engraving) on whalebone, whale ivory, walrus tusk, etc., usually by American whalers
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一件描绘鲸鱼的古老雕刻品。
entries.example_en: The museum displayed an ancient scrimshaw depicting a whale.

entries.definition_en: a certificate that can be exchanged for money or goods but is not official currency
entries.example_cn: 战争期间，士兵们以代金券形式领取薪酬，这些代金券只能在军需商店使用。
entries.example_en: During the war, soldiers were paid in scrip which could be used only at military stores.

entries.definition_en: a written text for a play or movie
entries.example_cn: 演员们在拍摄前阅读了剧本。
entries.example_en: The actors read the script before filming.

entries.definition_cn: 手写文字，尤其是独特的书写风格
entries.definition_en: handwriting, especially a distinctive style of writing
entries.example_cn: 侦探研究了便条上的笔迹。
entries.example_en: The detective studied the script on the note.

entries.definition_en: a specific system of writing
entries.example_cn: 古埃及使用复杂的文字系统。
entries.example_en: Ancient Egypt used a complex script.

entries.definition_en: to write a script for a performance
entries.example_cn: 他们聘请了一位专业人士来编写节目剧本。
entries.example_en: They hired a professional to script the show.

entries.definition_en: written down beforehand for a film, play, or broadcast
entries.example_cn: 演员们很紧张，因为那场戏没有剧本。
entries.example_en: The actors were nervous because the scene was not scripted.

entries.definition_cn: 修道院中用于抄写手稿的抄经室
entries.definition_en: a room in a monastery that is set aside for writing or copying manuscripts
entries.example_cn: 修士们整日在抄经室中借着烛光抄写宗教文本。
entries.example_en: Monks spent their days in the scriptorium copying religious texts by candlelight.

entries.definition_en: of or pertaining to or contained in or in accordance with the Bible
entries.example_cn: 布道集中在关于宽恕的圣经教导上。
entries.example_en: The sermon focused on scriptural teachings about forgiveness.

entries.definition_en: written or relating to writing
entries.example_cn: 该古代文明的书写证据是在泥板上发现的。
entries.example_en: The scriptural evidence of the ancient civilization was found in clay tablets.

entries.definition_en: writing regarded as sacred by a religious group
entries.example_cn: 会众在布道前聚集起来诵读经文。
entries.example_en: The congregation gathered to read from the scripture before the sermon.

entries.definition_en: someone who writes scripts for plays, movies, or broadcast dramas
entries.example_cn: 那位著名的编剧因她在新电视剧集中的作品而获奖。
entries.example_en: The famous scriptwriter won an award for her work on the new television series.

entries.definition_en: someone employed to make written copies of documents and manuscripts
entries.example_cn: 过去，抄写员会受雇手工抄写法律文件并收取费用。
entries.example_en: In the past, a scrivener would copy legal documents by hand for a fee.

entries.definition_cn: 已剖开并去骨、用于烹饪的幼鳕鱼或幼黑线鳕
entries.definition_en: a young Atlantic cod or haddock that has been split and boned for cooking
entries.example_cn: 厨师将鱼剖开去骨后烤制了这道鳕鱼。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared the scrod by splitting and boning the fish before broiling it.

entries.definition_cn: 重量不超过2磅的幼鳕鱼肉；也指幼黑线鳕或幼狭鳕，常烤制
entries.definition_en: the flesh of a young Atlantic cod weighing up to 2 pounds; also young haddock or pollock, often cooked by broiling
entries.example_cn: 我们点了烤鳕鱼当晚餐，因为很新鲜美味。
entries.example_en: We ordered scrod for dinner because it was fresh and delicious.

entries.definition_en: a form of tuberculosis causing swellings in the lymphatic glands
entries.example_cn: 患者在颈部肿块被检查后被诊断为颈淋巴结核。
entries.example_en: The patient was diagnosed with scrofula after the swelling in the neck was examined.

entries.definition_en: suffering from scrofula, a disease affecting the lymph nodes
entries.example_cn: 过去，患颈淋巴结核的儿童常被用阳光照射治疗。
entries.example_en: In the past, scrofulous children were often treated with sunlight.

entries.definition_cn: 邋遢、不健康或有病态外表的
entries.definition_en: having an unkempt, unhealthy, or diseased appearance
entries.example_cn: 那座无人照管的建筑外观邋遢而病态。
entries.example_en: The neglected building had a scrofulous, unhealthy appearance.

entries.definition_en: morally contaminated or corrupt
entries.example_cn: 批评者称这位腐败的官员道德败坏。
entries.example_en: The corrupt official was described as scrofulous by his critics.

entries.definition_en: to move through text or graphics on a screen to see parts not currently visible
entries.example_cn: 你可以向下滚动以阅读文章的其余部分。
entries.example_en: You can scroll down to read the rest of the article.

entries.definition_en: a document that can be rolled up for storage
entries.example_cn: 那个古老的卷轴记载了失落城市的地图。
entries.example_en: The ancient scroll contained maps of the lost city.

entries.definition_en: a round shape formed by concentric circles, like leaves or petals
entries.example_cn: 这个设计在门顶采用了卷叶形图案。
entries.example_en: The design features a scroll pattern at the top of the door.

entries.definition_en: a selfish person who is unwilling to give or spend
entries.example_cn: 他真是个吝啬鬼，连给自己孩子的生日礼物都不肯买。
entries.example_en: He is such a scrooge that he refuses to buy a birthday present for his own child.

entries.definition_en: relating to or situated in the scrotum
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了阴囊区域以寻找感染的迹象。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the scrotal area for signs of infection.

entries.definition_en: the external pouch that contains the testes
entries.example_cn: 阴囊悬挂在阴茎下方。
entries.example_en: The scrotum hangs below the penis.

entries.definition_en: to obtain or seek to obtain something by cadging or wheedling
entries.example_cn: 他设法从朋友那里弄到一些额外的钱来付账单。
entries.example_en: He managed to scrounge some extra money from his friends to pay the bill.

entries.definition_en: to collect or look around for food
entries.example_cn: 野餐结束后，鸟儿在地上四处觅食面包屑。
entries.example_en: The birds scrounge for crumbs on the ground after the picnic.

entries.definition_en: a person who tries to get things for free by asking others
entries.example_cn: 这名无家可归的人被指控是个占便宜的人。
entries.example_en: The homeless man was accused of being a scrounger.

entries.definition_en: clean with hard rubbing
entries.example_cn: 你需要用硬刷子用力擦洗地板以去除污渍。
entries.example_en: You need to scrub the floor with a stiff brush to remove the stains.

entries.definition_en: postpone indefinitely or annul something that was scheduled
entries.example_cn: 由于暴风雨，航班被取消，乘客滞留原地。
entries.example_en: Due to the storm, the flight was scrubbed and passengers were stranded.

entries.definition_en: wash thoroughly
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行结束后，我们必须彻底清洗靴子和袜子以去除泥土。
entries.example_en: After the hike, we had to scrub our boots and socks to get rid of the mud.

entries.definition_en: dense vegetation consisting of stunted trees or bushes
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者必须穿过茂密的灌木丛才能到达山顶。
entries.example_en: The hikers had to push through thick scrub to reach the summit.

entries.definition_en: the act of cleaning a surface by rubbing it with a brush and soap and water
entries.example_cn: 每天擦洗厨房台面使它们一尘不染。
entries.example_en: The daily scrub of the kitchen counters kept them spotless.

entries.definition_en: (of domestic animals) not selectively bred
entries.example_cn: 农民饲养未选育的牛，它们体格健壮，能适应崎岖的地形。
entries.example_en: The farmer raised scrub cattle that were hardy and adapted to the rough terrain.

entries.definition_en: made clean by scrubbing
entries.example_cn: 地板被擦洗得闪闪发光。
entries.example_en: The floor was scrubbed until it shone.

entries.definition_en: a brush with short, stiff bristles used for heavy cleaning
entries.example_cn: 她买了一把新硬毛刷，用来清除厨房地板上的顽固污渍。
entries.example_en: She bought a new scrubber to scrub the stubborn stains off the kitchen floor.

entries.definition_en: a person who cleans a surface, such as a floor or deck, using a scrub brush
entries.example_cn: 船上的船员雇佣了一名清洁工来清理甲板上的油污。
entries.example_en: The ship's crew hired a scrubber to clean the oil from the deck.

entries.definition_en: a device that removes impurities from a gas
entries.example_cn: 工厂安装了一个气体净化器，以过滤废气中的有害化学物质。
entries.example_en: The factory installed a scrubber to filter harmful chemicals from the exhaust gas.

entries.definition_cn: 用于设置音频或视频播放位置的水平条
entries.definition_en: a horizontal bar used to set the playback position of audio or video
entries.example_cn: 拖动播放进度条可以跳到视频中间。
entries.example_en: Drag the scrubber to skip to the middle of the video.

entries.definition_en: the act of cleaning a surface by rubbing it with a brush and soap and water
entries.example_cn: 擦洗地板花了一整个上午。
entries.example_en: The scrubbing of the floor took all morning.

entries.definition_cn: 去除气体中杂质的过程
entries.definition_en: the removal of impurities from gas
entries.example_cn: 气体洗涤会去除废气中的硫化合物。
entries.example_en: Gas scrubbing removes sulfur compounds from the exhaust.

entries.definition_en: covered with small, stunted trees and bushes
entries.example_cn: 那片灌木丛生的山坡很难攀登。
entries.example_en: The scrubby hillside was difficult to climb.

entries.definition_en: of poor quality or small size
entries.example_cn: 这座农场只能种出矮小、长势不佳的作物。
entries.example_en: The farm produced only scrubby crops.

entries.definition_en: an area of land that is not farmed and is covered with low, bushy plants
entries.example_cn: 牛群在干旱的灌木荒地上四处寻找水源。
entries.example_en: The cattle wandered through the dry scrubland in search of water.

entries.definition_en: protective garment worn by surgeons during operations
entries.example_cn: 外科医生在手术前换上了手术服。
entries.example_en: The surgeon changed into scrubs before the operation.

entries.definition_en: the back side of the neck
entries.example_cn: 狗抓住了猫的颈后部。
entries.example_en: The dog grabbed the cat by the scruff of its neck.

entries.definition_en: looking shabby and untidy
entries.example_cn: 他在公园过夜后看起来邋遢不堪。
entries.example_en: He looked scruffy after spending the night in the park.

entries.definition_en: a method in rugby where players from both teams crouch side by side with locked arms to start play
entries.example_cn: 裁判吹哨开始争球。
entries.example_en: The referee blew the whistle to start the scrum.

entries.definition_en: a method in rugby where players from both teams crouch side by side with locked arms to start play
entries.example_cn: 裁判吹哨开始争球。
entries.example_en: The referee blew the whistle to start the scrummage.

entries.definition_en: extremely delicious and pleasing to the taste
entries.example_cn: 我们享用了一顿由厨师准备的美味晚餐。
entries.example_en: We enjoyed a scrumptious dinner prepared by the chef.

entries.definition_en: strong cider, especially as made in western England
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，我们在壁炉旁享用了一瓶烈性苹果酒。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, we enjoyed a bottle of scrumpy by the fire.

entries.definition_cn: 把某物揉皱或挤压成更紧凑的形状
entries.definition_en: to crumple or squeeze something into a more compact form
entries.example_cn: 她不得不把纸揉皱才能塞进信封里。
entries.example_en: She had to scrunch the paper to fit it in the envelope.

entries.definition_en: to contract the muscles of one's face
entries.example_cn: 面对妻子令人困惑的请求，他皱起了脸。
entries.example_en: He scrunched his face at his wife's confusing request.

entries.definition_en: to sit on one's heels
entries.example_cn: 婴儿坐在地板上，双脚蜷缩在屁股底下。
entries.example_en: The baby sat scrunching on the floor.

entries.definition_en: a crunching noise
entries.example_cn: 风穿过干枯的树叶时发出巨大的嘎吱声。
entries.example_en: The wind made a loud scrunch as it passed through the dry leaves.

entries.definition_en: to hesitate on moral grounds
entries.example_cn: 她因礼物是在可疑情况下提供的而犹豫是否接受。
entries.example_en: She scrupled to accept the gift because it was offered under suspicious circumstances.

entries.definition_en: to question or doubt something
entries.example_cn: 她怀疑证人陈述的真实性。
entries.example_en: She scrupled the truth of the witness's account.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人因道德原因犹豫
entries.definition_en: to cause someone to hesitate on moral grounds
entries.example_cn: 这项提议涉及欺骗顾客，使他因道德原因犹豫不决。
entries.example_en: The proposal scrupled him because it involved deceiving customers.

entries.definition_cn: 对行为恰当性的不安，尤其是出于道德或伦理原因
entries.definition_en: uneasiness about the fitness of an action, especially for ethical or moral reasons
entries.example_cn: 他因向朋友撒谎以保护他们的感情而感到深深的不安。
entries.example_en: He felt a deep scruple about lying to his friends to protect their feelings.

entries.definition_cn: 抑制行动的道德或伦理原则
entries.definition_en: an ethical or moral principle that inhibits action
entries.example_cn: 她对暴力的道德原则阻止她参加抗议活动。
entries.example_en: Her scruple against violence prevented her from joining the protest.

entries.definition_cn: 药衡斯克鲁普尔；等于20格令的重量单位
entries.definition_en: a unit of apothecary weight equal to 20 grains
entries.example_cn: 药剂师称取了一斯克鲁普尔的药物。
entries.example_en: The apothecary measured one scruple of the medicine.

entries.definition_cn: 极其小心的；非常用心的
entries.definition_en: showing extreme care and great effort in doing something
entries.example_cn: 会计师在提交报告前极其小心地核对了每一个数字。
entries.example_en: The accountant was scrupulous in checking every figure before submitting the report.

entries.definition_cn: 一丝不苟的；严守道德的
entries.definition_en: having strong moral principles and being very careful about doing what is right
entries.example_cn: 即使在困难的情况下，他也一丝不苟地坚持说真话。
entries.example_en: He was scrupulous about telling the truth, even when it was difficult.

entries.definition_cn: 极其认真地；一丝不苟地
entries.definition_en: with extreme conscientiousness
entries.example_cn: 她一丝不苟地遵守所有安全规定。
entries.example_en: She scrupulously followed all the safety regulations.

entries.definition_en: the quality of conforming to high standards of ethics or excellence
entries.example_cn: 她在处理财务记录时的严谨态度赢得了公司的信任。
entries.example_en: Her scrupulousness in handling financial records earned the company's trust.

entries.definition_en: strict attention to minute details
entries.example_cn: 编辑的一丝不苟确保了每一个逗号都放置正确。
entries.example_en: The editor's scrupulousness ensured that every comma was placed correctly.

entries.definition_cn: 选举监督员；计票监督员
entries.definition_en: a person who scrutinizes or observes an election process, especially to verify that votes are counted fairly
entries.example_cn: 作为选举监督员，她在最终计票前仔细核对了每张选票。
entries.example_en: As the election scrutineer, she carefully verified every ballot before the final count.

usage.label: 加拿大英语：选举观察员

entries.definition_cn: 仔细或批判性地审视，或详细检查
entries.definition_en: to look at critically or searchingly, or in minute detail
entries.example_cn: 委员会在投票前将仔细审查提案的每一个细节。
entries.example_en: The committee will scrutinise every detail of the proposal before voting.

entries.definition_cn: 仔细审查财务记录以核实其准确性
entries.definition_en: to examine financial records carefully to verify their accuracy
entries.example_cn: 审计师必须仔细检查财务记录，以确保符合法规。
entries.example_en: Auditors must scrutinise the financial records to ensure compliance with regulations.

entries.definition_en: to look at something carefully and critically to find details or problems
entries.example_cn: 委员会在做出决定之前将仔细审查提案的每一个细节。
entries.example_en: The committee will scrutinize every detail of the proposal before making a decision.

entries.definition_en: to examine something carefully to verify its accuracy
entries.example_cn: 审计师必须核实财务记录以确保其准确性。
entries.example_en: Auditors must scrutinize the financial records to ensure they are accurate.

entries.definition_en: the act of examining something very carefully to find mistakes or errors
entries.example_cn: 这份财务报告受到了审计员的仔细审查。
entries.example_en: The financial report was subjected to close scrutiny by the auditors.

entries.definition_en: a long and intense look at something
entries.example_cn: 她在决定信任他之前，长时间地审视着他。
entries.example_en: She gave him a long scrutiny before deciding to trust him.

entries.definition_en: to use magical means to see or predict something, often using a crystal ball or other object
entries.example_cn: 巫师试图通过水晶球占卜来寻找失落文物的位置。
entries.example_en: The wizard attempted to scry the location of the lost artifact using a crystal ball.

entries.definition_en: equipment for breathing underwater
entries.example_cn: 他们租用了水肺装备进行水下探险。
entries.example_en: They rented scuba gear for their underwater exploration.

entries.definition_en: to run or move very quickly or hastily
entries.example_cn: 他沿着走廊疾跑以赶上公交车。
entries.example_en: He scudded down the hallway to catch the bus.

entries.definition_en: of a ship: to run before a gale
entries.example_cn: 小船在大风中顺风疾驰，驶向港口。
entries.example_en: The small ship scudded before the gale toward the harbor.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving along swiftly, especially before a gale
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨来临前，云层在天空中疾驰而过。
entries.example_en: The clouds scudded across the sky ahead of the storm.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving swiftly, especially before a strong wind
entries.example_cn: 云朵迅速掠过天空，预示着暴风雨将至。
entries.example_en: The scudding of the clouds across the sky signaled an approaching storm.

entries.definition_cn: 因刮擦或拖擦而弄坏（表面）
entries.definition_en: mar or damage a surface by scraping or dragging against it
entries.example_cn: 小心别把新地毯刮坏。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to scuff the new carpet.

entries.definition_en: walk without lifting the feet
entries.example_cn: 那个疲惫的孩子拖着脚在房间里走动。
entries.example_en: The tired child scuffed across the room.

entries.definition_cn: 被刮擦得留下痕迹或磨损
entries.definition_en: become marked or damaged by scraping or rubbing
entries.example_cn: 那双皮靴在长途徒步后磨损了。
entries.example_en: The leather shoes scuffed after the long hike.

entries.definition_en: poke at with the foot or toe
entries.example_cn: 他用脚趾把球踢了一下。
entries.example_en: He scuffed the ball with his toe.

entries.definition_en: a slipper that has no fitting around the heel
entries.example_cn: 他在湿地板上行走时，脚上的无后跟拖鞋打滑了。
entries.example_en: He slipped on the scuff while walking on the wet floor.

entries.definition_en: the act of scuffing (scraping or dragging the feet)
entries.example_cn: 拖拽鞋子的声音在走廊里回荡。
entries.example_en: The sound of scuffing shoes echoed in the hallway.

entries.definition_en: to fight or struggle in a confused way at close quarters
entries.example_cn: 两名对手在狭窄的小巷里扭打在一起。
entries.example_en: The two rivals scuffled in the narrow alleyway.

entries.definition_en: to walk by dragging one's feet
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子穿着袜子在房间里拖着脚走。
entries.example_en: The child scuffled across the room in his socks.

entries.definition_en: disorderly fighting
entries.example_cn: 警察不得不制止那两名男子之间的扭打。
entries.example_en: The police had to break up the scuffle between the two men.

entries.definition_en: an unceremonious and disorganized struggle
entries.example_cn: 为了最后一块蛋糕发生了一场短暂的混乱争斗。
entries.example_en: There was a brief scuffle over the last piece of cake.

entries.definition_cn: 一种可推可拉、刀刃与作业地面平行的锄
entries.definition_en: a hoe with a sharp blade parallel to the ground, used by pushing and pulling
entries.example_cn: 这个地区的农民用推拉锄给土壤除草。
entries.example_en: Farmers in this region use a scuffle hoe to remove weeds from the soil.

entries.definition_en: a long oar mounted at the stern of a boat to propel it forward
entries.example_cn: 划船者在开始之前调整了长桨的位置。
entries.example_en: The rower adjusted the position of the scull before starting.

entries.definition_en: each of a pair of short oars used by a single oarsman
entries.example_cn: 划船者在开始前更换了一支短桨。
entries.example_en: The rower replaced one of the sculls before starting.

entries.definition_en: a racing shell propelled by sculls
entries.example_cn: 队伍为即将到来的锦标赛准备了他们的赛艇。
entries.example_en: The team prepared their scull for the upcoming championship.

entries.definition_en: to propel a boat using sculls
entries.example_cn: 他们决定在黎明时分划船横渡湖泊。
entries.example_en: They decided to scull across the lake at dawn.

entries.definition_cn: 划艇者；用一支或两支桨划船的人
entries.definition_en: a person who propels a boat by sculling, using one or two oars
entries.example_cn: 划艇者有节奏地移动船桨以推动船只前进。
entries.example_en: The sculler moved the oars rhythmically to push the boat forward.

entries.definition_en: a kitchen servant who does menial tasks, especially washing
entries.example_cn: 那个厨房杂役把锅碗瓢盆擦得闪闪发光。
entries.example_en: The scullion scrubbed the pots and pans until they shone.

entries.definition_cn: 杜父鱼科的一种小鱼，通常无鳞
entries.definition_en: a small fish of the family Cottidae, usually lacking scales
entries.example_cn: 这条杜父鱼躲在河底的岩石之间。
entries.example_en: The sculpin hid among the rocks on the river bottom.

entries.definition_cn: 通过塑造石头、木材或黏土等材料创作雕塑
entries.definition_en: to create a sculpture by shaping a material such as stone, wood, or clay
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家用大理石雕刻了一座精美的人物像。
entries.example_en: The artist sculpted a beautiful figure from marble.

entries.definition_cn: 雕刻；通过切削或去除材料塑形
entries.definition_en: to shape a material by cutting or removing parts of it
entries.example_cn: 他从一块大理石中雕刻出一个人物像。
entries.example_en: He sculpted a figure from a block of marble.

entries.definition_en: well-shaped, with clear, attractive contours
entries.example_cn: 这名游泳运动员的肩膀和手臂线条分明。
entries.example_en: The swimmer had sculpted shoulders and arms.

entries.definition_en: an artist who creates sculptures
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的雕塑家在公园里揭幕了一座新雕像。
entries.example_en: The famous sculptor unveiled a new statue in the park.

entries.definition_en: a female sculptor (dated)
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的女雕塑家创作了一座令人惊叹的城市青铜雕像。
entries.example_en: The famous sculptress created a stunning bronze statue of the city.

entries.definition_en: relating to or consisting of sculpture
entries.example_cn: 博物馆新建了一座专门展示现代艺术的雕塑馆。
entries.example_en: The museum has a new sculptural wing dedicated to modern art.

entries.definition_en: resembling sculpture in form or style
entries.example_cn: 建筑师设计了一座具有扭曲钢制雕塑立面的建筑。
entries.example_en: The architect designed the building with a sculptural facade made of twisted steel.

entries.definition_en: an art object made by shaping materials like stone, wood, or metal into a three-dimensional form
entries.example_cn: 博物馆花园里有一座著名的马雕塑。
entries.example_en: The museum has a famous sculpture of a horse in the garden.

entries.definition_en: the art or process of creating figures or designs in three dimensions
entries.example_cn: 她在大学学习了四年的雕塑艺术。
entries.example_en: She studied sculpture at the university for four years.

entries.definition_en: to create an art object by shaping hard materials like stone or wood
entries.example_cn: 艺术家用一块大理石雕塑了一座雕像。
entries.example_en: The artist sculptured a statue from a block of marble.

entries.definition_en: to shape a material by removing parts of it, such as whittling away wood or stone
entries.example_cn: 艺术家把木块雕琢成了一只鸟。
entries.example_en: The artist sculptured the block of wood into a bird.

entries.definition_en: made or shaped like a sculpture
entries.example_cn: 那块被雕刻成形的石头展示了复杂的图案。
entries.example_en: The sculptured stone displayed intricate patterns.

entries.definition_en: attractively formed
entries.example_cn: 她那形态优美、宛如雕塑的面容吸引了赞赏的目光。
entries.example_en: Her sculptured features drew appreciative looks.

entries.definition_en: a film of impurities or vegetation that forms on the surface of a liquid
entries.example_cn: 静止的池塘表面形成了一层绿色的浮渣。
entries.example_en: A layer of green scum had formed on the stagnant pond.

entries.definition_en: people who are considered worthless or contemptible
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家被指控与政治上的卑鄙小人勾结。
entries.example_en: The politician was accused of associating with political scum.

entries.definition_en: to remove scum from a liquid
entries.example_cn: 厨师在端上汤之前仔细撇去了浮渣。
entries.example_en: The chef carefully scummed the broth before serving it.

entries.definition_en: a person who is deemed to be despicable or contemptible
entries.example_cn: 他称那个小偷为卑鄙之徒。
entries.example_en: He called the thief a scumbag.

usage.label: informal; mildly vulgar
usage.pattern: Used as an insult for a sleazy or despicable person.

entries.definition_en: extremely contemptible or despicable
entries.example_cn: 媒体揭露了这位政客卑鄙的手段。
entries.example_en: The politician's scummy tactics were exposed by the media.

entries.definition_en: covered with a layer of scum
entries.example_cn: 那个死水池塘表面覆盖着一层藻类浮渣。
entries.example_en: The stagnant pond was scummy with algae.

entries.definition_en: a strong feeling of dislike or disgust
entries.example_cn: 看到腐败现象，他深感厌恶。
entries.example_en: He felt a deep scunner at the sight of the corruption.

entries.definition_cn: 北美大西洋沿岸的一种鲷鱼，可煎食
entries.definition_en: a fish found in Atlantic coastal waters of North America from South Carolina to Maine, esteemed as a panfish
entries.example_cn: 这种鲷鱼在当地被视为适合煎食的鱼类。
entries.example_en: The scup is esteemed as a panfish in the region.

entries.definition_cn: 北美南方大西洋沿岸的鲷鱼
entries.definition_en: a porgy found in the southern Atlantic coastal waters of North America
entries.example_cn: 我们在海岸边钓鱼时钓到了一条鲷鱼。
entries.example_en: We caught a scup while fishing off the coast.

entries.definition_cn: 北方大西洋沿岸冷水鱼类的鱼肉
entries.definition_en: the flesh of fish found in colder waters of the northern Atlantic coast of the United States
entries.example_cn: 厨师用新鲜的北方大西洋沿岸冷水鱼类鱼肉做了一道美味佳肴。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared a delicious meal using fresh scup.

entries.definition_cn: 南方大西洋沿岸暖水鱼类的瘦肉
entries.definition_en: the lean flesh of fish found in warm waters of the southern Atlantic coast of the United States
entries.example_cn: 这种鱼以其在暖水中发现的瘦肉而闻名。
entries.example_en: Scup is known for its lean flesh found in warm waters.

entries.definition_cn: 挫败或破坏某事，尤指某人的计划或机会
entries.definition_en: to thwart or ruin something, especially someone's plans or chances
entries.example_cn: 政策的突然变化挫败了他的扩张计划。
entries.example_en: The sudden change in policy scuppered his plans for expansion.

entries.definition_en: to wait in hiding in order to attack someone
entries.example_cn: 叛军在该车队抵达城市前就埋伏袭击了它。
entries.example_en: The rebels scuppered the convoy before it could reach the city.

entries.definition_en: a drain on a ship's deck that lets water flow over the side
entries.example_cn: 船员不得不将积聚在排水孔里的水舀出去。
entries.example_en: The crew had to bail out the water that had collected in the scupper.

entries.definition_en: a variety of amber-green muscadine grape native to the southeastern United States
entries.example_cn: 我们在佐治亚州的葡萄园里采摘了甜美的斯考帕南格葡萄。
entries.example_en: We harvested the sweet scuppernong grapes from the vineyard in Georgia.

entries.definition_cn: 用斯考帕南格葡萄酿制的甜味金黄色或琥珀色美国葡萄酒
entries.definition_en: a sweet, golden or amber-colored American wine made from scuppernong grapes
entries.example_cn: 他们端上了冰镇的斯考帕南格葡萄酒，搭配甜点。
