entries.example_en: He contributed slenderly to the project's success.

entries.definition_en: the property of an attractively thin person
entries.example_cn: 她欣赏舞者肢体的苗条。
entries.example_en: She admired the slenderness of the dancer's limbs.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being slender or thin in one dimension of an object
entries.example_cn: 这根金属丝很纤细，难以弯曲而不折断。
entries.example_en: The slenderness of the wire made it difficult to bend without breaking.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being slight or inadequate
entries.example_cn: 批评家们立刻看出他论点的薄弱之处。
entries.example_en: The slenderness of his argument was immediately apparent to the critics.

entries.definition_en: a person who investigates crimes or mysteries
entries.example_cn: 侦探跟踪嫌疑人的车穿过城市。
entries.example_en: The sleuth followed the suspect's car through the city.

entries.definition_en: to act as a detective or investigate a mystery
entries.example_cn: 记者调查以揭露这起丑闻的细节。
entries.example_en: The journalist sleuthed to uncover details about the scandal.

entries.definition_en: detective work or investigation
entries.example_cn: 侦探工作揭示了关于这起犯罪的新线索。
entries.example_en: The sleuthing revealed new clues about the crime.

entries.definition_en: a very large number or amount of something
entries.example_cn: 公司招聘了大量新员工。
entries.example_en: The company hired a slew of new employees.

entries.definition_en: to veer or turn sharply
entries.example_cn: 汽车急向左转以避开障碍物。
entries.example_en: The car slew to the left to avoid the obstacle.

entries.definition_en: to skid sideways, usually uncontrollably
entries.example_cn: 卡车在结冰的路面上侧滑，撞上了护栏。
entries.example_en: The truck slewed sideways on the icy road and hit a barrier.

entries.definition_en: a piece cut from a larger whole
entries.example_cn: 我吃了一片披萨。
entries.example_en: I ate a slice of pizza.

entries.definition_en: a share or portion of something
entries.example_cn: 每个人都能分到一块蛋糕。
entries.example_en: Everyone gets a slice of the cake.

entries.definition_en: a golf shot that curves right
entries.example_cn: 他的右曲球导致他输掉了这一洞。
entries.example_en: His slice caused him to lose the hole.

entries.definition_en: to cut something into slices
entries.example_cn: 她把西瓜切成了薄片。
entries.example_en: She sliced the watermelon into thin slices.

entries.definition_en: to cut through something with a sharp edge
entries.example_cn: 请在上菜前把面包切了。
entries.example_en: Please slice the bread before serving.

entries.definition_cn: 击出从左向右弯曲的球（右手球员）
entries.definition_en: to hit a shot that curves from left to right for a right-handed player
entries.example_cn: 那名高尔夫球手把开球打成右曲球，落入了长草区。
entries.example_en: The golfer sliced his tee shot into the rough.

entries.definition_en: a wound caused by cutting
entries.example_cn: 医生清理了他手臂上的切口。
entries.example_en: The doctor cleaned the slice on his arm.

entries.definition_en: to hit a ball with spin so it curves
entries.example_cn: 他把球切击到了左角。
entries.example_en: He sliced the ball to the left corner.

entries.definition_en: prepared by cutting into thin pieces
entries.example_cn: 请配上酸奶端上切片的苹果。
entries.example_en: Please serve the sliced apples with yogurt.

entries.definition_en: (used of meat) cut into pieces for serving
entries.example_cn: 菜单上提供配有特制酱汁的切块牛肉。
entries.example_en: The menu features sliced beef served with a special sauce.

entries.definition_en: a machine for cutting; usually with a revolving blade
entries.example_cn: 厨房里的切片机迅速处理好了蔬菜。
entries.example_en: The kitchen slicer made quick work of the vegetables.

entries.definition_en: knife especially designed for slicing particular foods, as cheese
entries.example_cn: 他用专门的切片刀切那块硬奶酪。
entries.example_en: He used a special slicer to cut the hard cheese.

entries.definition_en: a golfer whose shots typically curve right (for right-handed golfers)
entries.example_cn: 这位右曲球手很难让球落在球道中央。
entries.example_en: The slicer struggled to keep the ball on the fairway.

entries.definition_cn: 将三维模型转换为打印薄层的切片软件
entries.definition_en: software that converts a 3D model into thin layers for printing
entries.example_cn: 切片软件将模型转换成了供三维打印机使用的薄层。
entries.example_en: The slicer converted the model into layers for the 3D printer.

entries.definition_en: the act of cutting something into slices
entries.example_cn: 她花了一下午切蔬菜做沙拉。
entries.example_en: She spent the afternoon slicing vegetables for the salad.

entries.definition_cn: 右撇子高尔夫球手将球向右弯曲击出的球路
entries.definition_en: a golf shot that curves to the right for a right-handed golfer
entries.example_cn: 他那一记向右弯曲的击球让球落在了球道之外。
entries.example_en: His slicing shot caused the ball to land far off the fairway.

entries.definition_en: made slick by e.g. ice or grease
entries.example_cn: 小心，地板上有冰很滑。
entries.example_en: Be careful, the floor is slick with ice.

entries.definition_cn: 表面令人印象深刻，但缺乏深度，未关注主题的真正复杂性
entries.definition_en: superficially impressive, but lacking depth and attention to the true complexities of a subject
entries.example_cn: 这部电影是对小说的流畅但肤浅的改编。
entries.example_en: The movie was a slick but shallow adaptation of the novel.

entries.definition_en: make slick or smooth
entries.example_cn: 他用发胶把头发向后梳理得光滑。
entries.example_en: He slicked his hair back with gel.

entries.definition_en: give a smooth and glossy appearance
entries.example_cn: 她把头发梳理得光滑有光泽，看起来很专业。
entries.example_en: She slicked her hair to look professional.

entries.definition_en: a covering of slippery liquid, especially oil
entries.example_cn: 路上的油膜使汽车打滑。
entries.example_en: An oil slick on the road made the car skid.

entries.definition_en: a magazine printed on good quality paper
entries.example_cn: 他们正在读一本关于时尚的精美杂志。
entries.example_en: They were reading a glossy slick about fashion.

entries.definition_cn: 仅具有表面上的合理性
entries.definition_en: having only superficial plausibility
entries.example_cn: 他那个表面合理的借口很容易被识破。
entries.example_en: His slick excuse was easily seen through.

entries.definition_cn: 漂浮在水面上的油膜或垃圾
entries.definition_en: a film of oil or garbage floating on top of water
entries.example_cn: 一层油膜在湖面上扩散开来。
entries.example_en: A slick of oil spread across the lake.

entries.definition_en: a waterproof raincoat or coat
entries.example_cn: 他穿上雨衣，冒着大雨走了出去。
entries.example_en: He put on his slicker before stepping out into the heavy rain.

usage.label: US
usage.pattern: Used for a waterproof coat or jacket.

entries.definition_cn: 诱骗他人相信虚假事实的人
entries.definition_en: someone who deceives you by making you believe something false
entries.example_cn: 那个骗子骗投资者相信公司盈利，而实际上并非如此。
entries.example_en: The slicker convinced the investors that the company was profitable when it was not.

entries.definition_cn: 精明世故、衣着讲究的人，有时含贬义
entries.definition_en: a clever, urbane person, sometimes regarded as disreputable; short for city slicker
entries.example_cn: 那个精明世故的城里人举止得体，赢得了所有人的好感，但有些人并不信任他。
entries.example_en: The city slicker charmed everyone with his polished manner, though some distrusted him.

entries.definition_cn: 圆滑地；油滑地；貌似有理却流于表面地
entries.definition_en: in a smooth, polished, and sometimes deceptively persuasive manner
entries.example_cn: 他圆滑地驳回了少数群体的担忧。
entries.example_en: He slickly dismissed the concerns of the minority group.

entries.definition_en: a slippery smoothness
entries.example_cn: 冰面的光滑使行走变得危险。
entries.example_en: The slickness of the ice made it dangerous to walk.

entries.definition_cn: 流畅却肤浅的风格或表现
entries.definition_en: a kind of fluent easy superficiality
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因流于表面且缺乏深度而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The movie was criticized for its slickness and lack of depth.

entries.definition_cn: 旨在占你便宜的言语欺骗
entries.definition_en: verbal misrepresentation intended to take advantage of you
entries.example_cn: 政客对丑闻的圆滑掩饰显而易见。
entries.example_en: The politician's slickness about the scandal was obvious to everyone.

entries.definition_en: move smoothly along a surface
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喜欢从游乐场的滑梯上滑下来。
entries.example_en: The children loved to slide down the playground slide.

entries.definition_cn: 通常失控地斜向或侧向移动；打滑
entries.definition_en: move obliquely or sideways, usually in an uncontrolled manner
entries.example_cn: 汽车在结冰的道路上滑了出去。
entries.example_en: The car slid off the icy road.

entries.definition_en: to pass or move unobtrusively or smoothly
entries.example_cn: 她设法悄悄加入了谈话，没人注意到。
entries.example_en: She managed to slide into the conversation without being noticed.

entries.definition_en: a plaything consisting of a sloping chute down which children can slide
entries.example_cn: 孩子们整个下午都在玩滑梯。
entries.example_en: The kids spent all afternoon playing on the slide.

entries.definition_en: a small flat rectangular piece of glass used for mounting specimens under a microscope
entries.example_cn: 科学家制备了载玻片来观察细菌。
entries.example_en: The scientist prepared a slide to examine the bacteria.

entries.definition_cn: （地质）大量泥土、岩石、积雪等沿斜坡下滑；滑坡或雪崩
entries.definition_en: the descent of a large mass of earth, rocks, or snow down a slope
entries.example_cn: 大雨导致山上发生了危险的滑坡。
entries.example_en: Heavy rains caused a dangerous slide on the mountain.

entries.definition_en: the act of moving smoothly along a surface while remaining in contact with it
entries.example_cn: 花样滑冰运动员在冰场上优雅地滑行。
entries.example_en: The ice skater performed a graceful slide across the rink.

entries.definition_en: rapid sliding up or down the musical scale
entries.example_cn: 吉他手在吉他上演奏了一个戏剧性的滑音。
entries.example_en: The guitarist played a dramatic slide on the guitar.

entries.definition_cn: 一种接近击球手时横向偏转的棒球滑球
entries.definition_en: a baseball pitch that breaks laterally as it reaches the batter
entries.example_cn: 投手投出一个滑球，击球手没能打中。
entries.example_en: The pitcher threw a slider that the batter could not hit.

entries.definition_en: a person who slips or slides because of loss of traction
entries.example_cn: 湿滑的地面让行人变成了滑倒者。
entries.example_en: The wet floor turned the pedestrian into a slider.

entries.definition_en: someone who races the luge
entries.example_cn: 这位雪橇运动员在雪橇比赛中赢得了金牌。
entries.example_en: The slider won the gold medal in the luge competition.

entries.definition_en: a freshwater turtle of United States and South America; frequently raised commercially; some young sold as pets
entries.example_cn: 农民养殖滑龟用于商业销售。
entries.example_en: Farmers raise sliders for commercial sale.

entries.definition_en: designed or able to slide
entries.example_cn: 滑动门沿着轨道平滑地移动。
entries.example_en: The sliding door moved smoothly along the track.

entries.definition_en: small in quantity or degree; not much or almost none
entries.example_cn: 他的健康状况有轻微改善。
entries.example_en: There was a slight improvement in his health.

entries.definition_en: being of delicate or slender build
entries.example_cn: 她身材纤细。
entries.example_en: She has a slight figure.

entries.definition_en: lacking substance or significance
entries.example_cn: 这场争论是基于一个微不足道的误解。
entries.example_en: The argument was based on a slight misunderstanding.

entries.definition_en: to pay no attention to or show disrespect for
entries.example_cn: 不要轻视这项任务的重要性。
entries.example_en: Do not slight the importance of this task.

entries.definition_en: a deliberate discourteous act, usually as an expression of anger or disapproval
entries.example_cn: 当他的建议被忽视时，他感到受到了怠慢。
entries.example_en: He felt slighted when his suggestion was ignored.

entries.definition_en: belittling or showing that someone or something is unimportant
entries.example_cn: 他轻蔑的语气让听众感到被忽视。
entries.example_en: His slighting tone made the audience feel ignored.

entries.definition_en: to a small degree or extent
entries.example_cn: 门微微开着。
entries.example_en: The door was slightly open.

entries.definition_en: in a slender or delicate manner
entries.example_cn: 他身材瘦削，但个子很高。
entries.example_en: He was slightly built, but tall.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being unimportant and petty or frivolous
entries.example_cn: 他用一句关于这个问题微不足道的话打发了这份投诉。
entries.example_en: He dismissed the complaint with a remark about the slightness of the issue.

entries.definition_en: slenderness
entries.example_cn: 树枝的纤细使得它在风中很容易折断。
entries.example_en: The slightness of the branch made it easy to break in the wind.

entries.definition_en: slenderness of a person's body or figure
entries.example_cn: 她欣赏舞者苗条的身形。
entries.example_en: She admired the slightness of the dancer's figure.

entries.definition_en: having a thin and delicate body shape
entries.example_cn: 这位模特非常苗条，在人群中很显眼。
entries.example_en: The model is very slim and stands out in the crowd.

entries.definition_cn: 微小的；微薄的；可能性很小的
entries.definition_en: small in amount, degree, or likelihood
entries.example_cn: 我们赢得这场比赛的机会微乎其微。
entries.example_en: We only have a slim chance of winning the game.

entries.definition_en: to lose weight
entries.example_cn: 自从夏天以来，她减肥效果显著。
entries.example_en: She has slimmed down significantly since the summer.

entries.definition_en: any thick, viscous matter
entries.example_cn: 青蛙坐在一片绿色的黏液上。
entries.example_en: The frog sat on a patch of green slime.

entries.definition_cn: 覆盖或弄脏（某物）以黏液
entries.definition_en: cover or stain with slime
entries.example_cn: 藻类开始用黏液覆盖潮池里的岩石。
entries.example_en: The algae began to slime the rocks in the tide pool.

entries.definition_en: the quality or state of being slim
entries.example_cn: 设计师的最新系列突显了模特的苗条身材。
entries.example_en: The model's slimness was highlighted by the designer's latest collection.

entries.definition_en: a very small margin or difference
entries.example_cn: 这场胜利仅以两票的微弱优势获得。
entries.example_en: The victory was achieved by a slimness of just two votes.

entries.definition_en: covered with or resembling slime
entries.example_cn: 池塘黏糊糊的表面让我犹豫是否要踏进去。
entries.example_en: The slimy surface of the pond made me hesitate to step in.

entries.definition_en: devious and unpleasantly insincere
entries.example_cn: 他赢得选举的卑鄙手段遭到了广泛谴责。
entries.example_en: His slimy tactics to win the election were widely condemned.

usage.label: slang
usage.pattern: figurative adjective for a person or behavior

entries.definition_en: hurl as if with a sling
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子学会了准确地投掷石子。
entries.example_en: The child learned to sling stones accurately.

entries.definition_en: hold or carry in a sling
entries.example_cn: 护士不得不把沉重的包用吊带挎在肩上。
entries.example_en: The nurse had to sling the heavy bag over her shoulder.

entries.definition_en: a plaything consisting of a Y-shaped stick with elastic between the arms; used to propel small stones
entries.example_cn: 那个男孩在花园里玩他的旧弹弓。
entries.example_en: The boy played with his old sling in the garden.

entries.definition_en: a shoe with a strap that passes around the heel
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一双露跟鞋参加聚会。
entries.example_en: She wore slingback shoes to the party.

entries.definition_en: a simple weapon consisting of a looped strap in which a projectile is whirled and then released
entries.example_cn: 那位古代勇士用投石索击败了巨人。
entries.example_en: The ancient warrior used a sling to defeat the giant.

entries.definition_en: a highball with liquor and water with sugar and lemon or lime juice
entries.example_cn: 他在酒吧点了一杯清爽的含酒精饮料。
entries.example_en: He ordered a refreshing sling at the bar.

entries.definition_en: hang loosely or freely; let swing
entries.example_cn: 窗帘被风吹得随意摆动。
entries.example_en: The curtains were left to sling in the breeze.

entries.definition_en: move with a sling
entries.example_cn: 树枝开始在风中摆动。
entries.example_en: The branches began to sling in the wind.

entries.definition_en: a shoe with a strap behind the heel or ankle
entries.example_cn: 她穿着优雅的露跟鞋参加夏季婚礼。
entries.example_en: She wore elegant slingback shoes to the summer wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 使用投石索投掷东西的人
entries.definition_en: a person who uses a sling to throw something
entries.example_cn: 这位古代战士是一名熟练的投石手。
entries.example_en: The ancient warrior was a skilled slinger.

entries.definition_en: a Y-shaped stick with elastic used to propel small stones
entries.example_cn: 他用弹弓把小石子射过田野。
entries.example_en: He used a slingshot to propel pebbles across the field.

entries.definition_en: to walk stealthily
entries.example_cn: 小偷从后门潜行离开了房子。
entries.example_en: The thief slunk out of the house through the back door.

entries.definition_en: to move sideways or diagonally, often without control
entries.example_cn: 汽车在结冰的路面上侧滑，撞到了路缘。
entries.example_en: The car slipped on the icy road and hit the curb.

entries.definition_en: to put something in a place quickly or quietly
entries.example_cn: 他把纸条悄悄塞进她的口袋。
entries.example_en: He slipped the note into her pocket.

entries.definition_en: to move quietly and secretly
entries.example_cn: 间谍从窗户悄悄溜进了房间。
entries.example_en: The spy slipped into the room through the window.

entries.definition_en: to become worse or of lower quality
entries.example_cn: 事故发生后，他的健康状况开始下降。
entries.example_en: His health began to slip after the accident.

entries.definition_en: a small mistake, especially in speech or writing
entries.example_cn: 她口误说错了名字。
entries.example_en: She made a slip of the tongue and said the wrong name.

entries.definition_en: an awkward or tactless thing that someone says or does
entries.example_cn: 叫他名字有点失礼。
entries.example_en: It was a bit of a slip to call him by his first name.

entries.definition_en: a part of a plant used for growing a new one
entries.example_cn: 园丁从玫瑰丛上剪下一段插条，种在花园里。
entries.example_en: The gardener took a slip from the rose bush to plant in the garden.

entries.definition_en: clay used for coating or decorating pottery
entries.example_cn: 艺术家在把泥浆涂到花瓶上之前先加水调和。
entries.example_en: The artist mixed the slip with water before applying it to the vase.

entries.definition_en: a piece of clothing or footwear that is easy to put on and take off
entries.example_cn: 我买了一双适合散步的套穿式便鞋。
entries.example_en: I bought a pair of comfortable slip-ons for walking.

entries.definition_en: a minor inadvertent mistake, especially in speech or writing
entries.example_cn: 那只是个口误；他本想说“朋友”而不是“敌人”。
entries.example_en: It was just a slip-up; he meant to say 'friend' not 'foe'.

entries.definition_en: a removable fabric cover designed to fit over a piece of upholstered furniture
entries.example_cn: 她买了一个米色的沙发套来保护她的皮沙发。
entries.example_en: She bought a beige slipcover to protect her leather sofa.

entries.definition_en: a knot tied at the end of a rope or cord that can slide along it
entries.example_cn: 他在绳子末端系了一个活结，以便轻松调节。
entries.example_en: He tied a slipknot at the end of the rope so it could be easily adjusted.

entries.definition_en: a decline from a standard level of performance or achievement
entries.example_cn: 公司季度销售额出现了明显下滑。
entries.example_en: There was a noticeable slippage in the company's quarterly sales figures.

entries.definition_en: the act of failing to hold or slipping out of place
entries.example_cn: 松动的纽扣导致布料脱落。
entries.example_en: The loose button caused a slippage of the fabric.

entries.definition_en: a loss of power in a machine caused by parts slipping
entries.example_cn: 皮带导致严重打滑，降低了发动机效率。
entries.example_en: The belt caused significant slippage, reducing the engine's efficiency.

entries.definition_en: a low shoe that is easy to put on and take off, usually worn inside the house
entries.example_cn: 他脱掉鞋子，换上了一只柔软的拖鞋。
entries.example_en: He kicked off his shoes and put on a soft slipper.

entries.definition_en: a person who slips or slides because they lose their grip on the ground
entries.example_cn: 那位老人在结冰的人行道上滑倒了。
entries.example_en: The old man was a slipper on the icy pavement.

entries.definition_en: wearing slippers on one's feet
entries.example_cn: 客人们穿着拖鞋，准备参加晚上的聚会。
entries.example_en: The guests arrived slippered and ready for the evening party.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being smooth and easy to slide on
entries.example_cn: 冰面的滑溜使得行走变得危险。
entries.example_en: The slipperiness of the ice made walking dangerous.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being deceitful or untrustworthy
entries.example_cn: 政治家的狡猾让选民质疑他的诚实。
entries.example_en: The politician's slipperiness made voters question his honesty.

entries.definition_en: having a smooth surface that makes it easy for things to slide
entries.example_cn: 下雨后地板很滑。
entries.example_en: The floor was slippery after it rained.

entries.definition_cn: 难以捉摸的；闪烁其词的
entries.definition_en: evasive and difficult to pin down or understand
entries.example_cn: 他这个人闪烁其词，总是不肯直截了当地回答。
entries.example_en: He is a slippery character who avoids giving a straight answer.

entries.definition_en: moving as if on a slippery surface
entries.example_cn: 汽车在结冰的路面上打滑。
entries.example_en: The car was slipping on the icy road.

entries.definition_en: causing or tending to cause things to slip or slide
entries.example_cn: 下雨后，小心在易滑的地板上行走。
entries.example_en: Be careful on the slippy floor after it rains.

entries.definition_cn: 极不谨慎的；粗枝大叶的
entries.definition_en: marked by great carelessness or lack of attention to detail
entries.example_cn: 这座桥梁粗制滥造的结构导致了它的倒塌。
entries.example_en: The slipshod construction of the bridge led to its collapse.

entries.definition_cn: 快速移动物体正后方由湍流形成的低压区
entries.definition_en: the low-pressure, turbulent region immediately behind a rapidly moving object
entries.example_cn: 骑自行车的人跟在卡车的尾流中，以减少空气阻力。
entries.example_en: The cyclist stayed in the truck's slipstream to reduce air resistance.

entries.definition_en: the stream of air pushed backward by an aircraft's propeller
entries.example_cn: 第二架飞机利用第一架飞机的尾流飞行以节省燃料。
entries.example_en: The second plane flew in the slipstream of the first to save fuel.

entries.definition_cn: 使前进或取得进展更容易的优势
entries.definition_en: an advantage that makes it easier to move forward or make progress
entries.example_cn: 这家小公司借助市场领导者成功带来的优势迅速发展。
entries.example_en: The smaller company grew rapidly in the slipstream of the market leader's success.

entries.definition_en: a sloping structure leading from a shipyard to the water
entries.example_cn: 新船顺着船坞斜坡滑入大海。
entries.example_en: The new ship was launched down the slipway into the sea.

entries.definition_en: a long narrow opening
entries.example_cn: 她在布料上剪了一个狭缝以便装入拉链。
entries.example_en: She cut a slit in the fabric to insert the zipper.

entries.definition_en: a narrow crack or fissure
entries.example_cn: 地震后，墙上出现了一道深深的裂缝。
entries.example_en: A deep slit appeared in the wall after the earthquake.

entries.definition_en: a depression scratched or carved into a surface
entries.example_cn: 考古学家在古老的石碑上发现了一个刻痕。
entries.example_en: The archaeologist found a slit in the ancient stone tablet.

entries.definition_cn: 女性生殖器的粗俗称呼
entries.definition_en: an obscene term for female genitals
entries.example_cn: 内容警告指出，slit 是女性生殖器的粗俗称呼。
entries.example_en: The content warning identifies slit as a vulgar term for female genitals.

entries.definition_en: to cut a long narrow opening in something
entries.example_cn: 外科医生割开了病人的皮肤以进行手术。
entries.example_en: The surgeon slit the patient's skin to perform the operation.

entries.definition_en: to cut a slit into something
entries.example_cn: 他割裂了袋子以取出里面的东西。
entries.example_en: He slit the bag open to take out the contents.

entries.definition_en: to pass or move unobtrusively or smoothly
entries.example_cn: 蛇蜿蜒爬过花园小径。
entries.example_en: The snake slithered across the garden path.

usage.label: intransitive
usage.pattern: The supplied source marks this verb intransitive.

entries.definition_cn: 蜿蜒滑行的；扭动着前行的
entries.definition_en: Moving with a twisting, sliding motion.
entries.example_cn: 那条蜿蜒滑行的蛇消失在草丛中。
entries.example_en: The slithering snake disappeared into the grass.

entries.definition_en: having a slippery surface or quality
entries.example_cn: 那滑溜溜的苔藓使得攀爬古老的石墙变得困难。
entries.example_en: The slithery moss made it difficult to climb the ancient stone wall.

entries.definition_en: a small, thin, sharp piece of wood, glass, or metal
entries.example_cn: 一片玻璃碎片扎进了他的手指。
entries.example_en: A sliver of glass was stuck in his finger.

entries.definition_en: a thin fragment or slice shaved from something
entries.example_cn: 他从奶酪轮上削下一片。
entries.example_en: He took a sliver of cheese from the wheel.

entries.definition_en: a small amount or part of something
entries.example_cn: 他只承担了总费用的一小部分。
entries.example_en: He contributed only a sliver of the total cost.

entries.definition_en: to divide something into slivers or splinters
entries.example_cn: 这台机器把木头切成了细小的碎片。
entries.example_en: The machine slivered the wood into tiny pieces.

entries.definition_en: to break up into splinters or slivers
entries.example_cn: 那张旧木椅子在压力下开始碎裂成碎片。
entries.example_en: The old wooden chair began to sliver under the pressure.

entries.definition_en: to form into slivers
entries.example_cn: 风吹过结冰的湖面时，冰裂成了碎片。
entries.example_en: The ice slivered as the wind blew across the frozen lake.

entries.definition_en: a clear plum brandy popular in the Balkans
entries.example_cn: 漫长的晚餐后，他们享用了一杯李子白兰地。
entries.example_en: They enjoyed a glass of slivovitz after the long dinner.

entries.definition_en: a lazy, slovenly, or obese person
entries.example_cn: 别让他待在你的房间里，他真是个邋遢鬼。
entries.example_en: Don't let him stay in your room; he is such a slob.

usage.label: derogatory; informal
usage.pattern: Source w20111r0 explicitly supplies both labels.

entries.definition_en: to let saliva drivel from the mouth
entries.example_cn: 狗看到骨头时开始流口水。
entries.example_en: The dog began to slobber when it saw the bone.

entries.definition_en: saliva that spills from the mouth
entries.example_cn: 宝宝吃完苹果后，下巴上沾着口水。
entries.example_en: There was slobber on the baby's chin after it ate the apple.

entries.definition_cn: 欧亚黑刺李（Prunus spinosa）灌木或小乔木
entries.definition_en: the thorny Eurasian blackthorn shrub or small tree, Prunus spinosa
entries.example_cn: 深秋时节，花园里长满了黑刺李。
entries.example_en: The garden was full of sloes in late autumn.

entries.definition_en: the small, astringent, dark-purple fruit of the blackthorn
entries.example_cn: 孩子们摘下了酸涩的黑刺李果实来吃。
entries.example_en: The children picked the sour sloes to eat.

entries.definition_cn: 北美东北部的一种野生李树或灌木，尤指阿勒格尼李（Prunus alleghaniensis），结深紫色果实
entries.definition_en: a wild plum shrub or small tree of northeastern North America, especially Prunus alleghaniensis, bearing dark purple fruit
entries.example_cn: 阿勒格尼李是一种原产于北美东北部的野生李树。
entries.example_en: The Allegheny plum is a wild plum native to northeastern North America.

entries.definition_en: to work doggedly or persistently
entries.example_cn: 他们不得不通宵苦干处理数据。
entries.example_en: They had to slog through the data all night.

entries.definition_en: to walk heavily and firmly, especially when weary or through mud
entries.example_cn: 我们跋涉过厚厚的泥沼才到达村庄。
entries.example_en: We slogged through the deep mud to reach the village.

entries.definition_en: to strike heavily, especially with the fist or a bat
entries.example_cn: 击球手用球棒猛击球，但没有击中。
entries.example_en: The batter slogged at the ball but missed.

entries.definition_en: a short phrase or sentence that expresses a particular idea or feeling, often used by a group or organization
entries.example_cn: 该公司推出了一条新口号来宣传其环保理念。
entries.example_en: The company launched a new slogan to promote its environmental values.

entries.definition_en: persuasion by means of empty slogans
entries.example_cn: 这场运动因空洞的口号宣传而非具体计划而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The campaign was criticized for its sloganeering rather than concrete plans.

entries.definition_en: someone who works hard and steadily, often for long hours
entries.example_cn: 工厂里充满了整天生产同一件产品的单调工人。
entries.example_en: The factory floor was filled with sloggers producing the same item all day.

entries.definition_cn: 步履沉重、行走费力的人
entries.definition_en: someone who walks in a laborious, heavy-footed manner
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，这个步履沉重的人艰难地穿过泥地。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, the slogger trudged heavily through the mud.

entries.definition_cn: 以能打出重拳著称的拳击手
entries.definition_en: a boxer noted for an ability to deliver hard punches
entries.example_cn: 这位拳击手在第三回合击倒对手赢得了冠军。
entries.example_en: The slogger won the title by knocking out his opponent in the third round.

entries.definition_en: a sailing vessel with a single mast set about one third of the boat's length aft of the bow
entries.example_cn: 他们乘坐一艘小型单桅纵帆船横渡大洋。
entries.example_en: They sailed across the ocean in a small sloop.

entries.definition_en: wet feed for pigs made from kitchen waste mixed with water or milk
entries.example_cn: 农民用厨房的泔水喂猪。
entries.example_en: The farmer fed the pigs slop from the kitchen.

entries.definition_cn: 难吃的流质食物或饮料
entries.definition_en: weak or watery unappetizing food or drink
entries.example_cn: 囚犯们被迫吃了几周的难吃的流质食物。
entries.example_en: The prisoners were forced to eat slop for weeks.

entries.definition_en: deep soft mud in water or slush
entries.example_cn: 狗陷在河边的烂泥里了。
entries.example_en: The dog got stuck in the slop near the riverbank.

entries.definition_en: to spill or splash a liquid onto something
entries.example_cn: 他不小心把牛奶泼到了地板上。
entries.example_en: He slopped the milk onto the floor by accident.

entries.definition_cn: 笨拙地泼洒（食物或液体）
entries.definition_en: to spill or splash food or liquid clumsily
entries.example_cn: 服务员笨拙地把汤洒了一桌子。
entries.example_en: The waiter slopped the soup all over the table.

entries.definition_en: to feed pigs slop
entries.example_cn: 这份工作包括每天早上喂猪。
entries.example_en: The job involved slopping the pigs every morning.

entries.definition_en: to walk through mud or mire
entries.example_cn: 我们必须穿过沼泽才能到达对岸。
entries.example_en: We had to slop through the marsh to reach the other side.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指便桶中的）尿液或粪便；污物
entries.definition_en: human urine or excrement, especially waste from a chamber pot
entries.example_cn: 便桶必须每天早晨清空。
entries.example_en: The chamber pot had to be emptied every morning.

entries.definition_en: to be at an angle; to go down or up at an angle
entries.example_cn: 这条路平缓地向下延伸到河边。
entries.example_en: The road slopes gently down to the river.

entries.definition_en: the degree of inclination of a line or surface
entries.example_cn: 屋顶的倾斜度很陡。
entries.example_en: The roof has a steep slope.

entries.definition_en: an inclined side of a hill or mountain
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者爬上了陡峭的山坡。
entries.example_en: The hikers climbed the steep slope.

entries.definition_en: having an oblique or slanted direction
entries.example_cn: 屋顶是倾斜的，以便让雨水流走。
entries.example_en: The roof is sloped to allow rainwater to drain away.

entries.definition_en: having an oblique or slanted direction
entries.example_cn: 屋顶有一个陡峭的倾斜表面。
entries.example_en: The roof has a steep sloping surface.

entries.definition_en: having a slanting form or direction
entries.example_cn: 艺术家画了背景中倾斜的山丘。
entries.example_en: The artist painted the sloping hills in the background.

entries.definition_en: in a careless or untidy way
entries.example_cn: 这份报告写得粗率，错误百出。
entries.example_en: The report was sloppily written and full of errors.

entries.definition_en: a lack of order and tidiness
entries.example_cn: 房间的凌乱反映了他粗心的态度。
entries.example_en: The sloppiness of the room reflected his careless attitude.

entries.definition_en: the quality of not being careful or taking pains
entries.example_cn: 报告的草率导致数据中出现了几处错误。
entries.example_en: The sloppiness of the report led to several errors in the data.

entries.definition_en: the state of being covered or soaked with water
entries.example_cn: 地面的泥泞使得行走时很容易滑倒。
entries.example_en: The sloppiness of the ground made it difficult to walk without slipping.

entries.definition_en: an overly sentimental or emotional quality
entries.example_cn: 她感情泛滥的言辞在正式场合显得格格不入。
entries.example_en: The sloppiness of her sentimental speech seemed out of place at the formal event.

entries.definition_en: lacking neatness or order
entries.example_cn: 他的房间又乱又不整洁。
entries.example_en: His room was messy and sloppy.

entries.definition_en: marked by great carelessness
entries.example_cn: 粗心的工作导致了诸多错误。
entries.example_en: The sloppy work led to many mistakes.

entries.definition_en: wet or smeared with a spilled liquid or moist material
entries.example_cn: 地板上洒满了牛奶，湿漉漉的。
entries.example_en: The floor was sloppy with spilled milk.

entries.definition_en: not fitting closely; hanging loosely
entries.example_cn: 这件衬衫太大了，穿在他身上显得很宽松。
entries.example_en: The shirt was too big and looked sloppy on him.

entries.definition_cn: 感情泛滥的；过分多愁善感的
entries.definition_en: excessively or abnormally emotional
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因感情泛滥而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The film was criticized for its sloppy sentimentality.

entries.definition_en: (of soil) soft and watery
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，地面变得泥泞不堪。
entries.example_en: The ground became sloppy after the heavy rain.

entries.definition_cn: 水手过去配发的宽松衣物，尤指裤子
entries.definition_en: loose clothing, especially trousers, formerly issued to sailors
entries.example_cn: 那名水手在甲板上工作时穿着宽松的水手裤。
entries.example_en: The sailor wore his loose slops while working on deck.

entries.definition_en: wet food for animals, especially pigs, made from kitchen waste mixed with water or milk
entries.example_cn: 农民用剩菜和脱脂牛奶混合成的泔水饲料喂猪。
entries.example_en: The farmer fed the pigs slops consisting of leftover vegetables and skimmed milk.

entries.definition_en: to make a splashing sound
entries.example_cn: 海浪拍打着岩石，发出哗啦声。
entries.example_en: The waves sloshed against the rocks.

entries.definition_en: to spill or splash liquid copiously or clumsily
entries.example_cn: 倒牛奶时要小心，别泼洒出来。
entries.example_en: Be careful not to slosh the milk when pouring it.

entries.definition_cn: 在水或其他液体中哗啦啦地行进
entries.definition_en: move noisily through water or another liquid
entries.example_cn: 街道被水淹了，但他们还是设法哗啦啦地涉水去上学。
entries.example_en: We had to slosh through the deep mud to reach the other side.

entries.definition_en: very drunk
entries.example_cn: 他醉得太厉害，无法安全开车回家。
entries.example_en: He was too sloshed to drive home safely.

entries.definition_en: a narrow opening for putting something in
entries.example_cn: 把硬币插入机器的狭缝中。
entries.example_en: Insert the coin into the slot on the machine.

entries.definition_en: a period of time set aside on a schedule
entries.example_cn: 我下午三点有一个午餐的时间段。
entries.example_en: I have a slot at 3 PM for lunch.

entries.definition_en: a position within a hierarchy or organization
entries.example_cn: 她获得了董事会的一个职位。
entries.example_en: She was offered a slot on the board of directors.

entries.definition_en: a socket in a computer for inserting a circuit board
entries.example_cn: 技术人员将新卡插入扩展插槽。
entries.example_en: The technician plugged the new card into the expansion slot.

entries.definition_en: a position in a sentence or phrase where different words can be used
entries.example_cn: 单词“quickly”在这个句子中充当副词位置。
entries.example_en: The word 'quickly' fills the adverb slot in this sentence.

entries.definition_en: to assign a specific time period for an activity
entries.example_cn: 我们需要把会议安排在下午的日程里。
entries.example_en: We need to slot the meeting into the afternoon schedule.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: slot someone/something into a schedule or sequence

entries.definition_en: a gambling machine with a lever or button
entries.example_cn: 他玩老虎机输光了所有的钱。
entries.example_en: He lost all his money playing the slot.

entries.definition_en: the trail left by an animal
entries.example_cn: 猎人顺着鹿在森林里留下的兽径追踪。
entries.example_en: The hunter followed the deer's slot through the forest.

entries.definition_en: a disinclination to work or exert yourself
entries.example_cn: 他被懒惰所困扰，不想开始做作业。
entries.example_en: He was overcome by sloth and did not want to start his homework.

entries.definition_en: any of several slow-moving arboreal mammals of South America and Central America; they hang from branches back downward and feed on leaves and fruits
entries.example_cn: 这只树懒倒挂在雨林的一根树枝上。
entries.example_en: The sloth hung upside down from a branch in the rainforest.

entries.definition_en: apathy and inactivity in the practice of virtue (personified as one of the deadly sins)
entries.example_cn: 这位僧侣警告说，怠惰这种罪过会阻碍灵性的成长。
entries.example_en: The monk warned against the sin of sloth which hinders spiritual growth.

entries.definition_en: disinclined to work or exertion
entries.example_cn: 那个懒惰的员工经常迟到，而且完不成任务。
entries.example_en: The slothful worker was often late and did not finish his tasks.

entries.definition_en: a lack of willingness to work or make an effort
entries.example_cn: 他的懒惰使他无法按时完成项目。
entries.example_en: His slothfulness prevented him from completing the project on time.

entries.definition_cn: 驼背；懒洋洋地坐着或站着
entries.definition_en: to sit or stand with a drooping posture
entries.example_cn: 她坐在椅子上，低着头，姿态懒散。
entries.example_en: She sat in a chair, slouching with her head down.

entries.definition_en: to walk in a lazy or untidy manner
entries.example_cn: 他懒洋洋地走进房间，连外套都没脱。
entries.example_en: He slouched into the room without even taking off his coat.

entries.definition_en: a stooping carriage in standing and walking
entries.example_cn: 他的驼背姿态让他看起来疲惫且无趣。
entries.example_en: His slouch made him look tired and uninterested.

entries.definition_cn: 行动迟缓或无能的人，通常用于否定结构
entries.definition_en: a person who is slow to act or incompetent, usually in negative constructions
entries.example_cn: 说到理财，他一点也不差。
entries.example_en: He is no slouch when it comes to managing his finances.

entries.definition_en: lacking stiffness in form or posture
entries.example_cn: 他穿着一件松垮的毛衣，松松地挂在肩膀上。
entries.example_en: He wore a slouchy sweater that hung loosely on his shoulders.

entries.definition_en: to cast off hair, skin, horn, or feathers
entries.example_cn: 蛇蜕去旧皮以腾出空间让新皮生长。
entries.example_en: The snake sloughed its old skin to make room for new growth.

entries.definition_cn: 脱落或脱去某物的过程，如蜕皮或落叶
entries.definition_en: the process of shedding or losing something, such as skin or leaves
entries.example_cn: 蛇蜕去旧皮的过程为新的生长腾出了空间。
entries.example_en: The snake's sloughing of its old skin makes room for new growth.

entries.definition_en: a habitually dirty or untidy man or boy
entries.example_cn: 那个邋遢的男人把衣服和盘子弄得满屋都是。
entries.example_en: The sloven left his clothes and dishes scattered throughout the room.

entries.definition_en: a state of being untidy and disordered
entries.example_cn: 房间的凌乱使得无法工作。
entries.example_en: The slovenliness of the room made it impossible to work.

entries.definition_en: the habit of being unclean
entries.example_cn: 他个人卫生方面的不洁习惯令人震惊。
entries.example_en: His slovenliness regarding his personal hygiene was shocking.

entries.definition_en: negligent of neatness, especially in dress and person; habitually dirty and unkempt
entries.example_cn: 房间邋遢的样子让客人感到不舒服。
entries.example_en: The slovenly appearance of the room made guests uncomfortable.

entries.definition_en: not moving quickly; taking a comparatively long time
entries.example_cn: 今天早上交通非常缓慢。
entries.example_en: The traffic was very slow this morning.

entries.definition_en: at a slow tempo or pace
entries.example_cn: 这首歌以慢节奏演奏。
entries.example_en: The song is played in a slow rhythm.

entries.definition_en: to lose speed and move more slowly
entries.example_cn: 汽车在接近十字路口时减速了。
entries.example_en: The car slowed down as it approached the intersection.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to proceed more slowly
entries.example_cn: 大雨减缓了施工进度。
entries.example_en: The heavy rain slowed the construction work.

entries.definition_en: to become slower
entries.example_cn: 河流进入湖泊时流速变慢了。
entries.example_en: The river slowed as it entered the lake.

entries.definition_en: without speed (informal for slowly)
entries.example_cn: 请把音乐放慢一点。
entries.example_en: He walked slow because of the ice.

entries.definition_en: showing a time that is earlier than the actual time
entries.example_cn: 我的表慢了五分钟。
entries.example_en: My watch is five minutes slow.

entries.definition_en: slow to learn or understand; lacking intelligence
entries.example_cn: 这孩子学新单词有点慢。
entries.example_en: The child is a bit slow to pick up new words.

entries.definition_en: moving at a slow speed
entries.example_cn: 缓慢移动的交通造成了延误。
entries.example_en: The slow-moving traffic caused a delay.

entries.definition_cn: 进展缓慢的；事件经过较长时间逐步发生的
entries.definition_en: developing or changing slowly, with events occurring over a long period
entries.example_cn: 进展缓慢的谈判已经持续了几个月。
entries.example_en: The slow-moving negotiations have continued for several months.

entries.definition_en: selling slowly
entries.example_cn: 商店给滞销商品打折，以便清仓。
entries.example_en: The store discounted its slow-moving products to clear them out.

entries.definition_cn: 思维迟钝的；不聪明或反应不快的
entries.definition_en: lacking a keen or swift intellect; not very bright or quick
entries.example_cn: 老师耐心地对待那位需要更多时间才能理解问题的智力迟钝的学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher was patient with the slow-witted student who needed extra time to understand.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being mentally slow and limited
entries.example_cn: 他的愚钝使他难以理解复杂的指令。
entries.example_en: His slow-wittedness made it difficult for him to understand complex instructions.

entries.definition_en: the act of slowing down or falling behind in speed or progress
entries.example_cn: 由于供应链问题，该公司的生产出现了显著放缓。
entries.example_en: The company experienced a significant slowdown in production due to supply chain issues.

entries.definition_en: more slowly
entries.example_cn: 这辆车的行驶速度比卡车慢。
entries.example_en: The car moved slower than the truck.

entries.definition_en: a slowing down; deceleration
entries.example_cn: 交通减速导致了延误。
entries.example_en: The slowing of traffic caused a delay.

entries.definition_en: at a low speed; not quickly
entries.example_cn: 汽车在狭窄的道路上缓慢行驶。
entries.example_en: The car moved slowly down the narrow road.

entries.definition_en: at a slow tempo in music
entries.example_cn: 指挥示意乐团慢板演奏。
entries.example_en: The conductor signaled the orchestra to play slowly.

entries.definition_en: a rate that is not hurried
entries.example_cn: 河流流速缓慢，使船很容易漂流。
entries.example_en: The slowness of the river's current allowed the boat to drift easily.

entries.definition_en: lack of mental quickness or intellectual ability
entries.example_cn: 他理解这个概念很慢，让老师感到担忧。
entries.example_en: His slowness to grasp the concept worried his teacher.

entries.definition_en: lack of skill due to insufficient training
entries.example_cn: 他操作新设备笨拙，是因为缺乏培训。
entries.example_en: His slowness in handling the new equipment was due to a lack of training.

entries.definition_en: a person who is habitually slow in their movements or actions
entries.example_cn: 别等那个慢吞吞的人，我们现在就得走。
entries.example_en: Don't wait for the slowpoke to finish; we need to leave now.

usage.label: informal, mildly derogatory
usage.pattern: The source labels this term informal and mildly derogatory.

entries.definition_en: a soft lump or unevenness in a yarn, either an imperfection or a design feature
entries.example_cn: 这种织物具有独特的粗节纹理，为编织增添了特色。
entries.example_en: The fabric has a distinctive slub texture that adds character to the weave.

entries.definition_cn: 牵伸并加捻纤维，为纺纱做准备
entries.definition_en: to draw and twist fibers to prepare them for spinning
entries.example_cn: 纺纱厂在将纤维纺成纱线前先对其进行牵伸和加捻。
entries.example_en: The mill slubs the fibers before they are spun into yarn.

entries.definition_en: any thick, viscous matter
entries.example_cn: 泄漏后，地板上覆盖了一层黑色的粘稠物。
entries.example_en: The floor was covered in a layer of black sludge after the spill.
