entries.example_en: He finally succumbed to her demands.

entries.definition_cn: 屈服于强大的力量、影响或欲望
entries.definition_en: to yield to an overpowering force, influence, or desire
entries.example_cn: 这座城市被敌军彻底攻陷。
entries.example_en: The city succumbed to the enemy forces.

entries.definition_cn: （委婉）去世，尤指因疾病或受伤而死
entries.definition_en: to die, especially from an illness or injury
entries.example_cn: 她八十岁时因肺炎去世。
entries.example_en: She succumbed to pneumonia at the age of eighty.

entries.definition_en: of so extreme a degree or extent
entries.example_cn: 那是如此美好的一天。
entries.example_en: It was such a beautiful day.

entries.definition_en: to so extreme a degree
entries.example_cn: 噪音如此之大，我睡不着。
entries.example_en: The noise was such that I couldn't sleep.

entries.definition_en: of the same kind or type
entries.example_cn: 他收集罕见的书籍和类似物品。
entries.example_en: He collects rare books and suchlike items.

entries.definition_en: to draw something into the mouth by creating a vacuum
entries.example_cn: 他从吸管里吸果汁。
entries.example_en: He sucked the juice from the straw.

entries.definition_en: to pull something in using a vacuum-like force
entries.example_cn: 吸尘器吸走了地毯上的所有灰尘。
entries.example_en: The vacuum cleaner sucked up all the dirt from the carpet.

entries.definition_en: to be very bad or disappointing
entries.example_cn: 这家新餐厅糟透了；食物很糟糕。
entries.example_en: The new restaurant sucks; the food is terrible.

entries.example_cn: 这部电影将观众吸引进了它黑暗的故事中。
entries.example_en: The movie sucked the audience into its dark story.

entries.definition_en: to take in information or experience
entries.example_cn: 她从讲座中吸收了知识。

entries.definition_en: the action of drawing liquid or air into the mouth

entries.example_en: The baby is a good sucker and finishes the bottle quickly.

entries.definition_en: a shoot arising from a plant's roots
entries.example_cn: 园丁拔除了根蘖以促进更好的生长。
entries.example_en: The gardener removed the suckers to encourage better growth.

entries.definition_en: an organ specialized for sucking
entries.example_cn: 章鱼用它的吸盘抓住岩石。

entries.example_cn: 渔夫在河里钓到了一条大吸口鱼。
entries.example_en: The angler caught a large sucker in the river.

entries.definition_en: the action of drawing liquid or air into the mouth by creating a vacuum

entries.example_en: The suddenness of the storm caught everyone off guard.

entries.example_en: They ordered a few suds at the bar.

entries.definition_en: leather with a napped surface

entries.example_en: The jacket is made of a synthetic suede fabric.

entries.example_en: The suer filed a lawsuit to recover the lost property.

entries.definition_en: a man who is trying to win the affection of a woman
entries.example_cn: 这位追求者在晚宴上送了她最爱的花。
entries.example_en: The suer brought her favorite flowers to the dinner party.

entries.definition_en: hard white fat found around the kidneys and loins of beef or sheep

entries.example_en: Traditional Christmas pudding is often made with suet.

entries.definition_en: to experience something bad or unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 许多人遭受污染的影响。

entries.definition_en: to experience or undergo something difficult
entries.example_cn: 他们经历了一个漫长而艰难的冬天。
entries.example_en: They suffered through a long and difficult winter.

entries.definition_en: to become worse in quality
entries.example_cn: 随着风暴逼近，道路状况开始变糟。
entries.example_en: The quality of the roads began to suffer as the storm approached.

entries.definition_en: to tolerate something unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 我不能忍受任何人的粗鲁行为。
entries.example_en: I cannot suffer such rude behavior from anyone.

entries.definition_en: to be put at a disadvantage

entries.example_en: The new rules will suffer the small businesses.

entries.example_cn: 他对不公平安排的默许被误认为是同意。
entries.example_en: His sufferance of the unfair arrangement was mistaken for agreement.

entries.definition_en: patient endurance of pain or distress

entries.example_en: He showed great sufferance during the long illness.

entries.example_cn: 这家医院为慢性病患者提供特别护理。
entries.example_en: The hospital provides special care for chronic sufferers.

entries.example_cn: 这位烈士被视为为自由事业而受难的人。
entries.example_en: The martyr was remembered as a sufferer for the cause of freedom.

entries.example_en: He was in constant suffering from the injury.

entries.definition_en: misery resulting from affliction

entries.example_en: The book describes the suffering of the refugees.

entries.definition_en: feelings of mental or physical pain
entries.example_cn: 她通过艺术表达了自己的痛苦。
entries.example_en: She expressed her suffering through her art.

entries.definition_en: psychological suffering
entries.example_cn: 创伤造成了深重的心理痛苦。
entries.example_en: The trauma caused deep psychological suffering.

entries.definition_en: experiencing pain, distress, or loss
entries.example_cn: 这个痛苦的家庭艰难地维持生计。
entries.example_en: The suffering family struggled to make ends meet.

entries.definition_en: very unhappy; full of misery
entries.example_cn: 他们在战区过着悲惨的生活。
entries.example_en: They lived a suffering life in the war zone.

entries.definition_en: be sufficient; be adequate, either in quality or quantity

entries.definition_en: an amount that is large enough to achieve a specific purpose

entries.example_en: The sufficiency of the evidence was enough to convince the jury.

entries.definition_en: having enough resources to live comfortably and meet responsibilities

entries.example_en: After years of hard work, they finally achieved financial sufficiency.

entries.example_en: The sufficiency of the plan was questioned by the experts.

entries.definition_en: enough to meet a need or requirement, but not more than necessary

entries.definition_en: to a degree that is enough

entries.definition_en: the process of forming a new word by adding a suffix to the end of a base word

entries.definition_en: to be asphyxiated; to die from lack of oxygen
entries.example_cn: 鱼在死水中窒息而死。
entries.example_en: The fish suffocated in the stagnant water.

entries.definition_en: to impair the respiration of or obstruct the air passage of
entries.example_cn: 灰尘呛得工人们呼吸困难。
entries.example_en: The dust choked and suffocated the workers.

entries.definition_en: to suppress the development, creativity, or imagination of
entries.example_cn: 僵化的体制扼杀了他的创造力。
entries.example_en: The rigid system suffocated his creativity.

entries.definition_en: to become stultified, suppressed, or stifled
entries.example_cn: 她感到严格的规章制度令人窒息。
entries.example_en: She felt suffocated by the strict rules.

entries.definition_cn: 因缺乏新鲜空气而感到不适
entries.definition_en: to feel uncomfortable for lack of fresh air
entries.example_cn: 我在拥挤的房间里开始感到呼吸困难。
entries.example_en: I began to suffocate in the crowded room.

entries.definition_en: to suffer severely reduced oxygen intake; struggle to breathe
entries.example_cn: 他在烟雾弥漫的房间里开始窒息。
entries.example_en: He began to suffocate in the smoke-filled room.

entries.definition_en: causing difficulty in breathing due to lack of fresh air or extreme heat
entries.example_cn: 厨房里令人窒息的炎热使得做晚饭变得很困难。
entries.example_en: The suffocating heat in the kitchen made it hard to cook dinner.

entries.definition_en: the state of being unable to breathe due to lack of oxygen
entries.example_cn: 几名受害者吸入烟雾后因窒息接受了治疗。
entries.example_en: Several victims were treated for suffocation after inhaling smoke.

entries.definition_en: the act of killing someone by stopping their breathing
entries.example_cn: 调查发现，受害者是被故意窒息致死的。
entries.example_en: The investigation found that the victim’s suffocation was deliberate.

entries.definition_en: an assistant or subordinate bishop of a diocese
entries.example_cn: 辅理主教协助教区主教履行职责。
entries.example_en: The suffragan bishop assisted the diocesan bishop in his duties.

entries.definition_cn: 选举权；参与政治决策的权利
entries.definition_en: the right to vote in elections or participate in making political decisions
entries.example_cn: 妇女们奋斗了数十年才赢得选举权。
entries.example_en: Women fought for decades to win the right to vote.

entries.definition_en: a woman advocate of women's right to vote, especially a militant advocate in the United Kingdom at the beginning of the 20th century
entries.example_cn: 这位妇女参政论者在街上游行，要求获得投票权。
entries.example_en: The suffragette marched in the street demanding the vote.

entries.definition_cn: 支持或争取选举权的人
entries.definition_en: a person who promotes or campaigns for voting rights
entries.example_cn: 苏珊·B·安东尼是一位著名的美国妇女选举权运动者。
entries.example_en: Susan B. Anthony was a famous American suffragist.

entries.definition_en: to cause to spread or flush or flood through, over, or across
entries.example_cn: 随着太阳升起，房间里弥漫起温暖的光辉。
entries.example_en: A warm glow suffused the room as the sun rose.

entries.definition_cn: 被液体、颜色或光芒覆盖
entries.definition_en: to become overspread as with a fluid, a colour, a gleam of light
entries.example_cn: 当她意识到自己的错误时，她的脸涨得通红。
entries.example_en: Her face suffused with red as she realized her mistake.

entries.definition_en: the process of permeating or infusing something with a substance
entries.example_cn: 听到这个消息，他的脸上泛起一片红晕。
entries.example_en: A suffusion of red covered his face when he heard the news.

entries.definition_cn: 用作甜味剂和防腐剂的白色结晶碳水化合物
entries.definition_en: a white crystalline carbohydrate used as a sweetener and preservative
entries.example_cn: 她在咖啡里加了一勺糖。
entries.example_en: She added a spoonful of sugar to her coffee.

entries.definition_cn: 碳水化合物，包括简单糖和较大的分子，是细胞的组成成分并为动物提供能量
entries.definition_en: a carbohydrate, including simple sugars and larger molecules, that provides energy and forms part of living cells
entries.example_cn: 葡萄糖是一种为我们的身体提供能量的糖。
entries.example_en: Glucose is a type of sugar that provides energy to our bodies.

entries.definition_en: informal terms for money
entries.example_cn: 他用现金而不是“糖”（钱）付了账单。
entries.example_en: He paid the bill with cash, not sugar.

entries.definition_en: sweeten with sugar
entries.example_cn: 食谱要求在烘焙前给苹果加糖。
entries.example_en: The recipe calls for you to sugar the apples before baking.

entries.definition_en: covered with a layer of sugar or syrup
entries.example_cn: 厨师端上了边缘裹着糖的甜点。
entries.example_en: The chef served the dessert with a sugar-coated rim.

entries.definition_en: a deciduous tree native to the southern United States that produces small black berries and soft yellowish wood
entries.example_cn: 糖莓树为当地的野生动物提供了阴凉和果实。
entries.example_en: The sugarberry tree provided shade and fruit for the local wildlife.

entries.definition_en: a small, edible dark purple to black berry with large pits found in the southern United States
entries.example_cn: 我们从灌木丛中摘下了新鲜的糖莓来吃。
entries.example_en: We picked fresh sugarberries from the bush to eat.

entries.definition_en: a tall tropical grass with jointed stalks used for sugar production
entries.example_cn: 甘蔗在温暖潮湿的气候中生长得最好。
entries.example_en: Sugarcane grows best in warm, humid climates.

entries.definition_en: the juicy stalks of the plant used to make sugar and molasses
entries.example_cn: 农民收割甘蔗以生产甜味糖浆。
entries.example_en: Farmers harvest the sugarcane to produce sweet syrup.

entries.definition_en: to make something unpleasant seem more pleasant
entries.example_cn: 他试图美化这个坏消息，但每个人都知道真相。
entries.example_en: He tried to sugarcoat the bad news, but everyone knew the truth.

entries.definition_en: to cover something with a sweet coating
entries.example_cn: 面包师在端上甜甜圈之前仔细地为它们裹上了糖衣。
entries.example_en: The baker carefully sugarcoated the donuts before serving them.

entries.definition_en: containing sugar
entries.example_cn: 她停止食用加糖早餐麦片。
entries.example_en: She stopped eating sugared breakfast cereals.

entries.definition_en: containing no refined sugar as an ingredient
entries.example_cn: 她选择了一种无糖饮料以符合她的饮食要求。
entries.example_en: She chose a sugarless drink to stay within her diet.

entries.definition_en: a large cone-shaped block of refined sugar
entries.example_cn: 旧食谱要求将一整块糖块磨碎。
entries.example_en: The old recipe called for a whole sugarloaf to be grated.

entries.definition_en: a small, round sweet or candy
entries.example_cn: 孩子们吃了一颗糖果当甜点。
entries.example_en: The children ate a sugarplum for dessert.

entries.definition_en: containing or tasting of sugar
entries.example_cn: 那块糖果含糖量很高，让我的牙齿疼了起来。
entries.example_en: The candy was very sugary and made my teeth ache.

entries.definition_en: to make a proposal or declare a plan for something
entries.example_cn: 我建议我们早点出发以避免交通拥堵。
entries.example_en: I suggest we leave early to avoid the traffic.

entries.definition_en: to imply something as a possibility
entries.example_cn: 乌云预示着不久后将会下雨。
entries.example_en: The dark clouds suggest that it will rain soon.

entries.definition_en: to drop a hint or intimate something indirectly
entries.example_cn: 他暗示他对目前的安排不满意。
entries.example_en: He suggested that he was unhappy with the arrangement.

entries.definition_en: to call to mind; to remind someone of something
entries.example_cn: 那首歌唤起了我们对童年的回忆。
entries.example_en: That song suggests memories of our childhood.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being easily influenced by suggestions
entries.example_cn: 儿童的易受暗示性使他们容易受到广告的影响。
entries.example_en: Children's suggestibility makes them vulnerable to advertising.

entries.definition_en: easily influenced by the ideas or opinions of others
entries.example_cn: 在广告方面，儿童往往比成年人更容易受暗示。
entries.example_en: Children are often more suggestible than adults when it comes to advertising.

entries.definition_en: an idea that is offered to someone
entries.example_cn: 他提出了一个关于如何改进项目的建议。
entries.example_en: He made a suggestion about how to improve the project.

usage.label: suggestion for something
usage.pattern: make a suggestion for + noun; source w03008r0

entries.definition_en: a proposal offered for acceptance or rejection
entries.example_cn: 委员会拒绝了推迟会议的提议。
entries.example_en: The committee rejected the suggestion to delay the meeting.

entries.definition_en: something implied, which the mind is liable to take as fact
entries.example_cn: 她的话暗示他应该早点离开。
entries.example_en: Her remark suggested that he should leave early.

entries.definition_en: a just detectable amount
entries.example_cn: 汤里有一点点盐味。
entries.example_en: There was a suggestion of salt in the soup.

entries.definition_en: the sequential mental process in which one thought leads to another by association
entries.example_cn: 度假的念头引发了一系列回忆。
entries.example_en: The suggestion of a holiday triggered a chain of memories.

entries.definition_en: an idea communicated to a hypnotized person to influence their thoughts or behavior
entries.example_cn: 催眠师用催眠暗示让受试者放松下来。
entries.example_en: The hypnotist used a suggestion to make the subject relax.

entries.definition_en: tending to suggest or imply something
entries.example_cn: 侦探在犯罪现场发现了一个暗示性的线索。
entries.example_en: The detective found a suggestive clue at the crime scene.

entries.definition_en: tending to suggest something improper or indecent
entries.example_cn: 该杂志包含了一些不适合儿童观看的挑逗性图片。
entries.example_en: The magazine contained some suggestive images that were not suitable for children.

entries.definition_en: pointing out or revealing clearly
entries.example_cn: 证据表明他与此事有关。
entries.example_en: The evidence was suggestive of his guilt in the matter.

entries.definition_en: in a suggestive manner
entries.example_cn: 她暗示地看了他一眼，希望他能明白她的邀请。
entries.example_en: She looked at him suggestively, hoping he would understand her invitation.

entries.definition_en: the quality of making people think about something or inspiring ideas
entries.example_cn: 这幅画的启发性让观众想象出一个隐藏的故事。
entries.example_en: The suggestiveness of the painting led viewers to imagine a hidden story.

entries.definition_en: a tall evergreen tree native to Japan and China that yields valuable soft wood
entries.example_cn: 花园里那棵古老的杉树已有三百多年历史。
entries.example_en: The ancient sugi tree in the garden is over three hundred years old.

entries.definition_en: dangerous to yourself or your interests
entries.example_cn: 忽视安全规定是自毁行为。
entries.example_en: It is suicidal to ignore the safety regulations.

entries.definition_en: the act of killing yourself
entries.example_cn: 警方调查了这起自杀事件。
entries.example_en: The police investigated the suicide.

entries.definition_en: a person who kills themself intentionally
entries.example_cn: 那名自杀者被发现躺在河里。
entries.example_en: The suicide was found in the river.

entries.definition_en: a set of matching clothes for outerwear
entries.example_cn: 他买了一套新衣服去面试。
entries.example_en: He bought a new suit for the interview.

entries.definition_en: a legal case or proceeding in court
entries.example_cn: 律师对公司提起了诉讼。
entries.example_en: The lawyer filed a suit against the company.

entries.definition_en: to be acceptable or agreeable to someone
entries.example_cn: 这个颜色非常适合你。
entries.example_en: This color suits you very well.

entries.definition_cn: 适合某人；使某人或某物显得好看
entries.definition_en: to be becoming to someone; to make someone or something look good
entries.example_cn: 那个发型很适合她。
entries.example_en: That hairstyle really suits her.

entries.definition_en: to be in agreement with or appropriate for
entries.example_cn: 这双鞋不配这条裙子。
entries.example_en: The shoes do not suit the dress.

entries.definition_en: to correspond with or be consistent with
entries.example_cn: 事实与故事不符。
entries.example_en: The facts do not suit the story.

entries.definition_cn: 穿西装的商界人士，尤指老板或主管（贬义俚语）
entries.definition_en: a person in a business suit, especially a boss or supervisor (derogatory slang)
entries.example_cn: 总部那些穿西装的老板否决了提案。
entries.example_en: The suits at headquarters rejected the proposal.

entries.definition_cn: 男子对女子的求爱；追求
entries.definition_en: a man's courtship of a woman; wooing
entries.example_cn: 她最终接受了他的求爱。
entries.example_en: She finally accepted his suit.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being appropriate or right for a specific purpose
entries.example_cn: 新软件对我们的适用性立即可见。
entries.example_en: The suitability of the new software for our needs was immediately apparent.

entries.definition_en: meant or adapted for an occasion or use
entries.example_cn: 这条裙子适合参加正式派对。
entries.example_en: This dress is suitable for a formal party.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指作为配偶）合适的；相配的
entries.definition_en: worthy of being chosen especially as a spouse
entries.example_cn: 他给女儿找了个合适的伴侣。
entries.example_en: He found a suitable partner for his daughter.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is appropriate or suitable for the circumstances
entries.example_cn: 这个房间被装饰得非常适合正式的晚宴。
entries.example_en: The room was decorated suitably for a formal dinner.

entries.definition_en: a portable container for carrying clothes while traveling
entries.example_cn: 她把衣服装进一个大手提箱里。
entries.example_en: She packed her clothes into a large suitcase.

entries.definition_en: a set of connected rooms in a hotel
entries.example_cn: 我们预订了一间可以俯瞰大海的豪华套房。
entries.example_en: We booked a luxury suite with a view of the sea.

entries.definition_en: a piece of music with several movements
entries.example_cn: 管弦乐队演奏了德彪西的一首著名组曲。
entries.example_en: The orchestra performed a famous suite by Debussy.

entries.definition_en: a set of matching furniture
entries.example_cn: 他们为客厅买了一套新家具。
entries.example_en: They bought a new suite for their living room.

entries.definition_en: a group of people attending an important person
entries.example_cn: 总统带着大批随从抵达。
entries.example_en: The president arrived with a large suite of advisors.

entries.definition_en: appropriate or suitable for a particular purpose or situation
entries.example_cn: 这条裙子非常适合正式场合。
entries.example_en: This dress is perfectly suited for a formal occasion.

entries.definition_en: provided with the necessary equipment or clothing
entries.example_cn: 这支队伍装备齐全，准备出发探险。
entries.example_en: The team was fully suited for the expedition.

entries.definition_en: a fabric used for making suits
entries.example_cn: 裁缝正在为新的制服裁剪西装面料。
entries.example_en: The tailor is cutting the suiting for the new uniform.

entries.definition_en: a person who courts someone, especially for marriage
entries.example_cn: 有许多求婚者争相追求她，但她选择了最懂她的那一位。
entries.example_en: There were many suitors vying for her hand, but she chose the one who understood her best.

entries.definition_en: a Japanese dish of thinly sliced beef and tofu cooked at the table in a sweet soy-based sauce
entries.example_cn: 我们在日本餐厅点了寿喜烧作为晚餐。
entries.example_en: We ordered sukiyaki for dinner at the Japanese restaurant.

entries.definition_en: having deep narrow furrows or grooves
entries.example_cn: 大脑表面有深深的沟槽。
entries.example_en: The surface of the brain is deeply sulcate.

entries.definition_en: a narrow groove in an organ or tissue, especially on the surface of the brain
entries.example_cn: 大脑上的沟和回增加了其表面积。
entries.example_en: The sulci and gyri on the brain increase its surface area.

entries.definition_en: a type of antibacterial drug that stops bacteria from growing
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种磺胺类抗生素来治疗感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a sulfa drug to treat the infection.

entries.definition_en: a sulfa drug used to treat meningitis, pneumonia, and other infections
entries.example_cn: 医生给患有严重肺炎的病人开了磺胺嘧啶。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed sulfadiazine to treat the patient's severe pneumonia.

entries.definition_en: a sulfonamide drug used to treat infections, especially those of the urinary tract
entries.example_cn: 医生开了磺胺甲恶唑来治疗患者的尿路感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed sulfamethoxazole to treat the patient's urinary tract infection.

entries.definition_en: a white, odorless crystalline sulfa drug that is the parent compound of most sulfa drugs
entries.example_cn: 磺胺是一种白色、无臭的结晶磺胺类药物。
entries.example_en: Sulfanilamide is a white, odorless crystalline sulfonamide drug.

entries.definition_en: a salt or ester formed from sulphuric acid
entries.example_cn: 石膏是一种常用于建筑的常见硫酸盐矿物。
entries.example_en: Gypsum is a common sulfate mineral used in construction.

entries.definition_en: to convert something into a sulfate
entries.example_cn: 该化学过程在处置前将废物硫酸化。
entries.example_en: The chemical process sulfates the waste products before disposal.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound containing sulfur and another element
entries.example_cn: 硫化氢是一种有毒气体，有臭鸡蛋味。
entries.example_en: Hydrogen sulfide is a toxic gas with a rotten egg smell.

entries.definition_en: an antibacterial drug that inhibits the growth of bacteria requiring PABA
entries.example_cn: 磺胺类抗生素是治疗细菌感染的首批有效药物之一。
entries.example_en: Sulfonamides were among the first effective treatments for bacterial infections.

entries.definition_en: a salt or ester of a sulfonic acid
entries.example_cn: 磺酸盐化合物常用于制造洗涤剂。
entries.example_en: Sulfonate compounds are often used in the manufacture of detergents.

entries.definition_en: an antidiabetic drug that reduces blood glucose levels to treat diabetes mellitus
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种磺酰脲类降糖药来帮助控制病人的糖尿病。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a sulfonylurea to help control the patient's diabetes.

entries.definition_en: a common nonmetallic element that is tasteless and odorless, often found as yellow crystals
entries.example_cn: 火山地区富含硫矿藏。
entries.example_en: Volcanic regions are rich in sulfur deposits.

entries.definition_en: to treat something with sulfur to preserve it
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂用硫处理肉类以防止腐烂。
entries.example_en: The factory sulfurs the meat to prevent spoilage.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: Source w13133r2 marks this verb transitive.

entries.definition_cn: 含硫的；与硫有关的，尤指含高价态硫的
entries.definition_en: of, relating to, or containing sulfur, especially sulfur in a high oxidation state
entries.example_cn: 火山气体与水反应后形成了硫酸。
entries.example_en: Sulfuric acid formed when the volcanic gases reacted with water.

entries.definition_en: relating to, containing, or produced by sulfur
entries.example_cn: 附近的火山使空气带有一股硫磺味。
entries.example_en: The air had a sulfurous smell from the nearby volcano.

entries.definition_en: harsh or corrosive in tone
entries.example_cn: 她发表了一场刺耳的演讲，激怒了听众。
entries.example_en: She gave a sulfurous speech that offended the audience.

entries.definition_en: characterized by oppressive heat and humidity
entries.example_cn: 夏天的日子漫长而闷热潮湿。
entries.example_en: The summer days were long and sulfurous.

entries.definition_en: a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug sold under the trade name Clinoril
entries.example_cn: 医生开了舒林酸来减轻患者的关节炎症。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed sulindac to reduce the patient's joint inflammation.

entries.definition_en: to be in a huff and display one's displeasure
entries.example_cn: 她拒绝和他说话，只是在自己的房间里赌气。
entries.example_en: She refused to talk to him and just sulked in her room.

entries.definition_cn: 闷闷不乐或赌气的情绪
entries.definition_en: a mood of sullen aloofness or withdrawal
entries.example_cn: 输掉比赛后，他整个下午都在赌气。
entries.example_en: He spent the afternoon in a sulk after losing the game.

usage.label: usually plural for a fit or mood

entries.definition_cn: 爱闹情绪的人；闷闷不乐的人
entries.definition_en: a person who sulks
entries.example_cn: 别老这么闹情绪，利奥！
entries.example_en: Don't be such a sulk, Leo!

entries.definition_cn: 以闹别扭的方式；以坏脾气且沉默的方式
entries.definition_en: in a manner characterized by sulking; in a bad-tempered and silent way
entries.example_cn: 争吵后，他闹别扭地拒绝和哥哥说话。
entries.example_en: He sulkily refused to speak to his brother after the argument.

entries.definition_en: sullen or moody
entries.example_cn: 孩子被拒绝后变得闷闷不乐。
entries.example_en: The child was sulky after being told no.

entries.definition_en: slow or slothful
entries.example_cn: 项目进展迟缓让经理很担心。
entries.example_en: The sulky progress of the project worried the manager.

entries.definition_en: depressingly dark
entries.example_cn: 阴沉的天空预示着要下雨。
entries.example_en: The sulky sky promised rain.

entries.definition_en: a light two-wheeled vehicle for one person; drawn by one horse
entries.example_cn: 他们乘坐轻便马车离开了。
entries.example_en: They rode away in a sulky.

entries.definition_cn: 一种南欧多年生植物，用作饲料，其粉色花朵是重要的蜜源
entries.definition_en: a perennial plant from southern Europe grown for animal feed and for its pink flowers, which are valuable for making honey
entries.example_cn: 养蜂人在草地上种植苏拉草以生产优质蜂蜜。
entries.example_en: Beekeepers cultivate the sulla in the meadows to produce high-quality honey.

entries.definition_en: showing a brooding ill humor
entries.example_cn: 争吵后，他心情阴沉地坐着。
entries.example_en: He sat in a sullen mood after the argument.

entries.definition_en: darkened by clouds
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨前，天空被厚重的阴云笼罩。
entries.example_en: The sky was sullen with heavy clouds before the storm.

entries.definition_en: in a gloomy and bad-tempered way
entries.example_cn: 他阴沉地拒绝与朋友交谈。
entries.example_en: He sullenly refused to speak to his friends.

entries.definition_en: a gloomy and ill-tempered feeling
entries.example_cn: 他的阴郁使别人难以接近他。
entries.example_en: His sullenness made it hard for others to approach him.

entries.definition_cn: 阴郁、闷闷不乐且怨愤的性情
entries.definition_en: a sullen, moody, and resentful disposition
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子拒绝说话，显露出阴郁、闷闷不乐且怨愤的性情。
entries.example_en: The child's sullenness was evident in his refusal to speak.

entries.definition_en: to make something dirty or spotty, often by exposure to air; also used metaphorically to damage purity or reputation.
entries.example_cn: 雨水弄脏了房子的白墙。
entries.example_en: The rain sullied the white walls of the house.

entries.definition_en: to attack someone's good name and reputation, often falsely or with malicious intent.
entries.example_cn: 她拒绝通过撒谎来损害自己的名声。
entries.example_en: She refused to sully her name by lying.

entries.definition_en: to place someone under suspicion or cast doubt on them.
entries.example_cn: 这些无法解释的付款使公众对他产生了怀疑。
entries.example_en: The unexplained payments sullied him in the eyes of the public.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound formed when sulphuric acid reacts with a metal or another substance
entries.example_cn: 石膏是一种主要由硫酸钙组成的软矿物。
entries.example_en: Gypsum is a soft mineral composed mainly of calcium sulphate.

entries.definition_en: a chemical compound consisting of sulphur and another element that is more electropositive
entries.example_cn: 硫化氢是一种有毒气体，有臭鸡蛋味。
entries.example_en: Hydrogen sulphide is a toxic gas with a rotten egg smell.

entries.definition_en: a yellow, tasteless, odorless chemical element that is a nonmetal.
entries.example_cn: 火山地区通常含有天然硫。
entries.example_en: Volcanic regions often contain native sulphur.

entries.definition_en: to treat something with sulphur in order to preserve it.
entries.example_cn: 这种肉经过硫处理以防止腐烂。
entries.example_en: The meat was sulphured to prevent spoilage.

entries.definition_en: relating to or containing sulfur; especially relating to sulfuric acid
entries.example_cn: 硫酸是一种强酸，广泛应用于许多工业过程中。
entries.example_en: Sulphuric acid is a strong acid used in many industrial processes.

entries.definition_cn: 硫的；含硫的；有硫磺气味的；亚硫酸的；亚硫酸盐的
entries.definition_en: of, relating to, containing, or derived from sulfur; having a sulfurous smell; of or relating to sulphurous acid or its salts
entries.example_cn: 山谷里的空气有一股明显的硫磺味。
entries.example_en: The air in the valley had a distinct sulphurous smell.

entries.definition_en: harsh or corrosive in tone
entries.example_cn: 他发表了一场刻薄的演讲，冒犯了许多同事。
entries.example_en: He gave a sulphurous speech that offended many of his colleagues.

entries.definition_en: characterized by oppressive heat and humidity
entries.example_cn: 夏天的日子漫长而闷热潮湿。
entries.example_en: The summer days were long and sulphurous.

entries.definition_en: the ruler of a Muslim country, especially of the former Ottoman Empire
entries.example_cn: 苏丹以极大的智慧统治着帝国。
entries.example_en: The sultan ruled the empire with great wisdom.

entries.definition_en: a pale yellow seedless raisin
entries.example_cn: 她在酸奶上撒了一些葡萄干。
entries.example_en: She sprinkled sultanas over her yogurt.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用于制作葡萄干和葡萄酒的淡黄色无籽葡萄品种
entries.definition_en: a pale-yellow seedless grape variety used to make raisins and wine
entries.example_cn: 苏丹娜葡萄可用于制作葡萄干和葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: Sultana grapes are used to make raisins and wine.

entries.definition_en: a country or territory ruled by a sultan
entries.example_cn: 这个苏丹国以其丰富的贸易历史而闻名。
entries.example_en: The sultanate was known for its rich trade history.

entries.definition_en: weather that is very hot and humid in an uncomfortable way
entries.example_cn: 午后的闷热让人难以在户外工作。
entries.example_en: The sultriness of the afternoon made it hard to work outside.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: the state or quality of being sultry

entries.definition_en: the quality of expressing or arousing sexual desire
entries.example_cn: 她声音中的情欲引起了他的注意。
entries.example_en: There was a sultriness in her voice that drew his attention.

entries.definition_en: characterized by oppressive heat and humidity
entries.example_cn: 七月是一个闷热潮湿的下午。
entries.example_en: It was a sultry afternoon in July.

entries.definition_en: sexually exciting or gratifying
entries.example_cn: 她在影片中饰演一位性感的歌手。
entries.example_en: She played a sultry singer in the film.

entries.definition_en: the result of adding numbers together
entries.example_cn: 5 加 7 的总和是 12。
entries.example_en: The sum of 5 and 7 is 12.

entries.definition_en: an amount of money
entries.example_cn: 该项目所需的资金数额相当大。
entries.example_en: The sum of money required for the project is quite large.

entries.definition_en: the final total amount
entries.example_cn: 页面底部的总额代表了总成本。
entries.example_en: The sum at the bottom of the page represents the total cost.

entries.definition_en: the entire amount
entries.example_cn: 我们的全部积蓄不足以支付这次旅行。
entries.example_en: The sum total of our savings is not enough for the trip.

entries.definition_en: to summarize
entries.example_cn: 本章总结了前文讨论的要点。
entries.example_en: This chapter sums up the main points of the previous discussion.

entries.definition_en: to calculate the total of
entries.example_cn: 请计算 A 列数字的总和。
entries.example_en: Please sum the figures in column A.

entries.definition_en: the most important part of an idea or experience
entries.example_cn: 他经验的核心是诚实为上策。
entries.example_en: The sum of his experience was that honesty is the best policy.

entries.definition_en: a set containing all members of two or more sets
entries.example_cn: 在数学中，两个集合的并集包含来自这两个集合的所有元素。
entries.example_en: In mathematics, the sum of two sets includes every element from both.

entries.definition_en: a brief statement that presents the main points in a concise form
entries.example_cn: 经理简要总结了项目的进展。
entries.example_en: The manager gave a quick sum-up of the project's progress.

entries.definition_cn: 漆属的一种无毒灌木或乔木
entries.definition_en: a non-poisonous shrub or tree of the genus Rhus
entries.example_cn: 红色的漆树沿着河岸野生生长。
entries.example_en: The red sumac grows wild along the riverbank.

entries.definition_en: the wood of a sumac tree
entries.example_cn: 这件家具是用漆树的硬木制成的。
entries.example_en: The furniture was made from the hard wood of a sumac.

entries.definition_cn: 漆树属灌木或乔木（通常指无毒种类）
entries.definition_en: a shrub or tree of the genus Rhus, typically referring to non-poisonous species
entries.example_cn: 花园里长满了漆树鲜艳的红叶。
entries.example_en: The garden is filled with the vibrant red leaves of the sumach.

entries.definition_cn: 概括地；简要地；未经正式程序地
entries.definition_en: in a summary manner; briefly or without formalities
entries.example_cn: 这项决定未经正式程序就作出了。
entries.example_en: The decision was made summarily.

entries.definition_en: to give a short version of something
entries.example_cn: 请在报告中概述主要论点。
entries.example_en: Please summarise the main arguments in your report.

entries.definition_en: to constitute a summary of something
entries.example_cn: 本章概括了之前研究的要点。
entries.example_en: This chapter summarises the key points of the previous research.

entries.definition_en: the act or process of summarizing; a summary produced by summarizing
entries.example_cn: 对长篇报告的摘要只用了十分钟。
entries.example_en: The summarization of the long report took only ten minutes.

entries.definition_en: to give a short statement of the main points of something
entries.example_cn: 请总结报告中的主要论点。
entries.example_en: Please summarize the key arguments in the report.

entries.definition_en: to serve as a short statement of the main points of something
entries.example_cn: 这一章是整个冲突历史的摘要。
entries.example_en: This chapter summarizes the entire history of the conflict.

entries.definition_en: a short statement that includes the main points of something
entries.example_cn: 请在会议前阅读报告的摘要。
entries.example_en: Please read the summary of the report before the meeting.

entries.definition_en: briefly stating the main idea
entries.example_cn: 他对规则做了一个概括性的解释。
entries.example_en: He gave a summary explanation of the rules.

entries.definition_en: done quickly and without formal procedures
entries.example_cn: 法官对该案件做出了草率的判决。
entries.example_en: The judge made a summary decision on the case.

entries.definition_en: the act of adding numbers to find their total
entries.example_cn: 前十个自然数的求和是五十五。
entries.example_en: The summation of the first ten natural numbers is fifty-five.

entries.definition_en: a final summary of arguments presented in a legal case
entries.example_cn: 律师向陪审团发表了有力的结案陈词。
entries.example_en: The lawyer delivered a powerful summation to the jury.

entries.definition_en: the total amount resulting from adding numbers together
entries.example_cn: 所有费用的总计超出了我们的预算。
entries.example_en: The summation of all expenses exceeded our budget.

entries.definition_en: the physiological process where multiple stimuli combine to produce a response that a single stimulus cannot
entries.example_cn: 微弱的神经冲动总和触发了肌肉收缩。
entries.example_en: The summation of weak nerve impulses triggered the muscle contraction.

entries.definition_cn: 总结性的；汇总的；（尤指教育中）评估总体学习成就的
entries.definition_en: relating to or produced by summation; especially denoting assessment of overall educational achievement
entries.example_cn: 老师使用汇总性评估来评价学生的整体进步。
entries.example_en: The teacher used a summative assessment to evaluate the students' overall progress.

entries.definition_cn: （课程结束时）评估学生所学内容的测试或评估
entries.definition_en: a test or assessment that measures what students have learned during a course
entries.example_cn: 期末总结性评估考查了学生在整个课程中学到的内容。
entries.example_en: The final summative measured what the students had learned throughout the course.

entries.definition_en: the warmest season of the year
entries.example_cn: 我们计划今年夏天去海滩。
entries.example_en: We plan to visit the beach this summer.

entries.definition_en: the period of finest development, happiness, or beauty
entries.example_cn: 她人生中最美好的时光是在欧洲度过的。
entries.example_en: The summer of her life was spent traveling through Europe.

entries.definition_en: spend the summer
entries.example_cn: 他们在湖边的小屋里度过了夏天。
entries.example_en: They summered in a small cottage by the lake.

entries.definition_en: a small building with a roof, used for shade and rest in summer
entries.example_cn: 我们坐在凉亭里以躲避炎热的太阳。
entries.example_en: We sat in the summerhouse to escape the hot sun.

entries.definition_cn: 避暑别墅；在暖和的月份用作度假住所而非主要住宅的房屋
entries.definition_en: a house used as a vacation home during the warm months rather than as a main residence
entries.example_cn: 他们在湖边的避暑别墅里度过夏天。
entries.example_en: They spend the summer in their summerhouse by the lake.

entries.definition_en: the warmest season of the year
entries.example_cn: 我们计划夏季去海滩。
entries.example_en: We plan to visit the beach during summertime.

entries.definition_cn: 属于夏季或具有夏季特征的
entries.definition_en: belonging to or characteristic of summer
entries.example_cn: 这件连衣裙采用轻盈的夏季面料，非常适合去海滩。
entries.example_en: The dress has a light, summery fabric perfect for the beach.

entries.definition_cn: （通常指山或丘陵的）顶部或极端点
entries.definition_en: the top or extreme point of something (usually a mountain or hill)
entries.example_cn: 山丘的顶部提供了美丽的景色。
entries.example_en: The summit of the hill offers a beautiful view.

entries.definition_en: a meeting of heads of governments
entries.example_cn: 世界领导人齐聚参加气候峰会。
entries.example_en: World leaders gathered for the climate summit.

entries.definition_en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development
entries.example_cn: 该公司已达到其行业的最高水平。
entries.example_en: The company has reached the summit of its industry.

entries.definition_en: reach the summit (of a mountain)
entries.example_cn: 他们在黎明时分登上了那座山的顶峰。
entries.example_en: They summited the mountain at dawn.

entries.definition_en: to call someone officially to appear in court or for a duty
entries.example_cn: 法官传唤证人出庭作证。
entries.example_en: The judge summoned the witness to testify.

entries.definition_en: to ask someone to come to a place
entries.example_cn: 她把助理叫到了办公室。
entries.example_en: She summoned her assistant to the office.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to become available for use
entries.example_cn: 他调动全身力气搬起那个重箱子。
entries.example_en: He summoned all his strength to lift the heavy box.

entries.definition_en: to gather or bring people together
entries.example_cn: 主席召集委员会开会讨论预算。
entries.example_en: The chair summoned the committee to a meeting to discuss the budget.

entries.definition_en: to make oneself or something ready for action
entries.example_cn: 她急中生智，迅速解开了谜题。
entries.example_en: She summoned her wits to solve the puzzle quickly.

entries.definition_en: the act of summoning someone or something
entries.example_cn: 反复召集使会议推迟了。
entries.example_en: The repeated summonings delayed the meeting.

entries.definition_en: a call or request to come, especially an official one
entries.example_cn: 铃声是召集大家吃饭的信号。
entries.example_en: The ringing bell was a summons to dinner.

entries.definition_en: an official notice ordering someone to appear at a specified place and time
entries.example_cn: 她收到传票，需出庭见治安法官。
entries.example_en: She received a summons to appear before the magistrate.

entries.definition_en: a legal document issued by authority that compels a defendant to attend a civil suit
entries.example_cn: 原告向被告送达民事传票以启动诉讼。
entries.example_en: The plaintiff served the defendant with a summons to start the lawsuit.

entries.definition_cn: 向某人送达传票；传唤某人
entries.definition_en: to serve someone with a summons
entries.example_cn: 法院向证人送达传票，要求其出庭。
entries.example_en: The court summonsed the witness to appear.

entries.definition_en: a traditional Japanese wrestling sport where wrestlers try to force each other out of a ring
entries.example_cn: 相扑选手在比赛开始前深深鞠躬。
entries.example_en: The sumo wrestler bowed deeply before the match began.

entries.definition_cn: 供液体排入的坑或凹穴
entries.definition_en: a hollow or pit into which liquid drains
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，花园里形成了一个巨大的积水坑。
entries.example_en: After the storm, a large sump formed in the garden.

entries.definition_en: a reservoir for oil in an internal combustion engine
entries.example_cn: 机械师从油底壳中排出了旧机油。
entries.example_en: The mechanic drained the old oil from the sump.

entries.definition_en: a covered cistern for waste water and sewage
entries.example_cn: 污水流入污水池后再进行处理。
entries.example_en: The sewage flows into the sump before being treated.

entries.definition_en: an animal used to carry loads
entries.example_cn: 商队使用驮马运输货物。
entries.example_en: The caravan used sumpter horses to transport goods.

entries.definition_en: relating to laws that control spending or personal behavior
entries.example_cn: 限制法禁止下层阶级穿着丝绸。
entries.example_en: The sumptuary laws prohibited the wearing of silk by the lower classes.

usage.label: historical
usage.pattern: 多用于历史性的禁奢法语境

entries.definition_en: luxurious, splendid, or lavish
entries.example_cn: 他们享用了厨师准备的奢华盛宴。
entries.example_en: They enjoyed a sumptuous feast prepared by the chef.

entries.definition_en: in a rich, luxurious, and opulent way
entries.example_cn: 宫殿用黄金和丝绸装饰得极其豪华。
entries.example_en: The palace was decorated sumptuously with gold and silk.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being excessively expensive and luxurious.
entries.example_cn: 酒店套房的极度奢华使其对大多数游客来说无法负担。
entries.example_en: The sumptuousness of the hotel suite made it unaffordable for most tourists.

entries.definition_en: wealth shown through luxurious living.
entries.example_cn: 宴会的奢华在镀金餐具和珍稀葡萄酒中显而易见。
entries.example_en: The sumptuousness of the banquet was evident in the gold-plated dishes and rare wines.

entries.definition_en: the rays of sunlight
entries.example_cn: 阳光照在我的脸上感觉很温暖。
entries.example_en: The sun felt warm on my face.

entries.definition_en: a person who is a source of warmth, energy, or glory
entries.example_cn: 她是家里的太阳。
entries.example_en: She is the sun of our family.

entries.definition_en: a star around which planets revolve
entries.example_cn: 我们的太阳是一颗中等大小的恒星。
entries.example_en: Our sun is a medium-sized star.

entries.definition_en: to expose one's body to the sun
entries.example_cn: 我们去海滩晒太阳。
entries.example_en: We went to the beach to sun ourselves.

entries.definition_en: to expose something to the rays of the sun
entries.example_cn: 请把衣服晾在阳光下。
entries.example_en: Please sun the clothes on the line.

entries.definition_en: covered with sunlight
entries.example_cn: 沐浴在阳光下的露台是放松的完美场所。
entries.example_en: The sun-drenched terrace was the perfect place to relax.

entries.definition_en: dried naturally by the sun
entries.example_cn: 我们买了日晒番茄来给意大利面增添风味。
entries.example_en: We bought sun-dried tomatoes to add flavor to the pasta.

entries.definition_en: a senior or more experienced person, especially in a Korean school or professional context
entries.example_cn: 她在会议前向她的前辈鞠躬致意。
entries.example_en: She greeted her sunbae with a bow before the meeting.

usage.label: Korean
usage.pattern: senior or upperclassman in a Korean context

entries.definition_en: baked or dried by the heat of the sun
entries.example_cn: 在炎热的夏日阳光下，被晒干的土地裂开了。
entries.example_en: The sunbaked earth cracked under the hot summer sun.

entries.definition_en: hardened by exposure to sunlight
entries.example_cn: 经日晒变硬的黏土已经不适合塑形了。
entries.example_en: The sunbaked clay had hardened in the sun and was no longer suitable for molding.

entries.definition_en: to expose one's body to the sun, usually to get a tan
entries.example_cn: 他们下午去海滩日光浴。
entries.example_en: They went to the beach to sunbathe in the afternoon.

entries.definition_en: a person who lies in the sun to get a tan
entries.example_cn: 海滩上挤满了寻求温暖的日光浴者。
entries.example_en: The beach was crowded with sunbathers seeking warmth.

entries.definition_en: a ray of sunlight
entries.example_cn: 一束温暖的阳光洒在地板上。
entries.example_en: A warm sunbeam fell across the floor.

entries.definition_en: a sunscreen with a high sun protection factor (SPF)
entries.example_cn: 她去海滩前涂了防晒霜。
entries.example_en: She applied sunblock before going to the beach.

entries.definition_en: a large bonnet designed to shade the face, typically worn by girls and women
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一顶白色的遮阳帽，以保护她的脸免受正午烈日的照射。
entries.example_en: She wore a white sunbonnet to protect her face from the bright midday sun.

entries.definition_en: red and painful skin caused by too much sun exposure
entries.example_cn: 她涂了防晒霜以避免晒伤。
entries.example_en: She applied sunscreen to avoid getting a sunburn.

entries.definition_en: to become red and painful from too much exposure to the sun
entries.example_cn: 如果你在外面待太久，你会被晒伤。
entries.example_en: If you stay outside too long, you will get sunburned.

entries.definition_en: having skin that is red and painful because of too much exposure to direct sunlight
entries.example_cn: 在海滩待了几个小时后，她全身都晒伤了。
entries.example_en: After spending hours at the beach, she was completely sunburned.

entries.definition_en: suffering from overexposure to direct sunlight
entries.example_cn: 在花园里待了几个小时后，她的胳膊变红且晒伤了。
entries.example_en: After hours in the garden, her arms were red and sunburnt.

entries.definition_en: dried out by the sun’s rays
entries.example_cn: 数周没有下雨后，被阳光晒干的田地又干又裂。
entries.example_en: The sunburnt fields were dry and cracked after weeks without rain.

entries.definition_en: having a color resembling sunburn
entries.example_cn: 这辆货车被漆成了晒伤皮肤般的棕色。
entries.example_en: The van was painted a sunburnt brown.

entries.definition_en: a strong outburst of sunlight
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，一阵强烈的阳光照亮了山谷。
entries.example_en: A sudden sunburst lit up the valley after the storm.

entries.definition_en: a decorative design with a central circle and radiating lines
entries.example_cn: 壁纸上有一个醒目的金色放射状图案。
entries.example_en: The wallpaper features a bold sunburst pattern in gold.

entries.definition_cn: 一种乐器表面处理效果：中央颜色较浅，向深色外缘逐渐变暗
entries.definition_en: a finish for a musical instrument in which a light central area darkens gradually toward the outer rim
entries.example_cn: 这把吉他有漂亮的渐变色表面处理效果，显露出木材的纹理。
entries.example_en: The guitar has a beautiful sunburst finish that shows the grain of the wood.

entries.definition_en: a brooch shaped like the sun with jewels
entries.example_cn: 她在外套上别了一枚复古的太阳胸针。
entries.example_en: She wore a vintage sunburst brooch on her coat.

entries.definition_en: a tuber from a sunflower plant that is eaten raw, boiled, or fried
entries.example_cn: 我们把菊芋和蒜、香草一起烤了。
entries.example_en: We roasted the sunchoke with garlic and herbs.

entries.definition_en: a dessert consisting of ice cream served with a topping
entries.example_cn: 我们要了一份配奶油和坚果的巧克力圣代冰淇淋。
entries.example_en: We ordered a chocolate sundae with whipped cream and nuts.

entries.definition_en: to break apart or in two using violence
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨威胁要将这两个村庄撕裂。
entries.example_en: The storm threatened to sunder the two villages.

entries.definition_en: a bog plant with leaves covered in sticky hairs that trap and digest insects
entries.example_cn: 茅膏菜用它的粘性陷阱捕捉到了一只苍蝇。
entries.example_en: The sundew caught a fly in its sticky trap.

entries.definition_en: a timepiece that tells the time by the shadow cast by a gnomon on a calibrated dial.

entries.example_en: The rash was superficial and would heal quickly.

entries.definition_en: lack of depth of knowledge or thought or feeling
entries.example_cn: 这场辩论的肤浅性阻碍了找到真正的解决方案。
entries.example_en: The superficiality of the debate prevented any real solutions from being found.

entries.definition_en: shallowness in terms of affecting only surface layers of something
entries.example_cn: 这种清洁剂未能解决污渍的表面性，导致污渍依然可见。
entries.example_en: The cleaning product failed to address the superficiality of the stain, leaving it visible.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is only on the surface and not deep or thorough.
entries.example_cn: 该报告表面上解决了问题，但忽略了根本原因。
entries.example_en: The report superficially addresses the problem but ignores the root causes.

entries.definition_en: the outer surface or boundary of an object or area
entries.example_cn: 岩石表面的粗糙度影响了青苔的生长。
entries.example_en: The roughness of the rock's superficies affected the growth of moss.

entries.definition_en: the purely external or superficial appearance of something
entries.example_cn: 光鲜的外表掩盖了严重的结构缺陷。
entries.example_en: The polished superficies hid serious structural flaws.

entries.definition_en: very fine in quality
entries.example_cn: 他们为冬装购买了质量极佳的羊毛。
entries.example_en: They purchased superfine wool for their winter coats.

entries.definition_en: having an extremely fine size or texture
entries.example_cn: 这种极细的丝绸贴在皮肤上感觉柔软得不可思议。
entries.example_en: This superfine silk feels incredibly soft against the skin.

entries.definition_en: excessively delicate or refined
entries.example_cn: 厨师对这道菜过分精致的摆盘分散了人们对味道的注意力。
entries.example_en: The chef's superfine presentation of the dish distracted from its flavor.

entries.definition_en: extreme excess
entries.example_cn: 食物的极度过剩导致了浪费。
entries.example_en: The superfluity of food led to waste.

entries.definition_cn: 超过所需、所愿或所要求的
entries.definition_en: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.example_cn: 他的解释是多余的，因为答案已经很清楚了。
entries.example_en: His explanation was superfluous since the answer was already clear.

entries.definition_en: serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being
entries.example_cn: 额外的行李是多余的，增加了重量。
entries.example_en: The extra luggage was superfluous and added to the weight.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is unnecessary or more than needed
entries.example_cn: 他多余地向困惑的听众解释了显而易见的要点。
entries.example_en: He superfluously explained the obvious points to the confused audience.

entries.definition_cn: 被认为具有非凡健康益处的食物
entries.definition_en: a food that is believed to have exceptional health benefits
entries.example_cn: 牛油果和蓝莓常被宣传为超级食物。
entries.example_en: Avocados and blueberries are often marketed as superfoods.

entries.definition_en: an extremely bright star of very large diameter and low density
entries.example_cn: 参宿七是一颗从地球可见的红超巨星。
entries.example_en: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant visible from Earth.

entries.definition_en: a criminal who gives information to the police about other criminals
entries.example_cn: 警察在告密者供出同伙的名字后将其逮捕。
entries.example_en: The police arrested the supergrass after he revealed the names of his accomplices.

entries.definition_cn: 虚构的英雄，尤指与犯罪作斗争、通常拥有超自然力量或特殊装备的英雄
entries.definition_en: a fictional hero, especially one who fights crime, often with supernatural powers or special equipment
entries.example_cn: 这位超级英雄从恶棍手中拯救了这座城市。
entries.example_en: The superhero saved the city from the villain.

entries.definition_cn: 专为高速交通设计的宽阔公路
entries.definition_en: a very wide road built for fast traffic
entries.example_cn: 这条新超级高速公路连接了两座主要城市。
entries.example_en: The new superhighway connects the two major cities.

entries.definition_cn: 用于快速传输数字数据的庞大电子网络
entries.definition_en: a large electronic network for sending digital data quickly
entries.example_cn: 信息在超级高速公路上以毫秒级的速度传输。
entries.example_en: Information travels across the superhighway in milliseconds.

entries.definition_cn: 超出人类能力或正常水平的；超人的
entries.definition_en: beyond what is possible or normal for a human being
entries.example_cn: 尽管受了伤，这位运动员还是赢得了比赛，完成了一项超人的壮举。
entries.example_en: The athlete performed a superhuman feat by winning the race despite his injury.

entries.definition_cn: 将一个物体或图像叠加在另一个之上，通常使两者都可见
entries.definition_en: to place one object or image over another, usually so that both remain visible
entries.example_cn: 艺术家在风景画上叠加了一层阴影。
entries.example_en: The artist superimposed a shadow over the landscape painting.

entries.definition_en: placed on or over something else
entries.example_cn: 屏幕上出现了一个城市天际线的叠加图像。
entries.example_en: A superimposed image of a city skyline appeared on the screen.

entries.definition_en: having one layer placed on top of another
entries.example_cn: 艺术家使用层叠的颜料层来创造深度。
entries.example_en: The artist used superimposed layers of paint to create depth.

entries.definition_en: lying on top of something and pressing down on it
entries.example_cn: 积雪的压覆重量导致屋顶坍塌。
entries.example_en: The superincumbent weight of the snow caused the roof to collapse.

entries.definition_en: a new infection that occurs during or after another infection or disease process
entries.example_cn: 患者在长期接受抗生素治疗期间发生了继发感染。
entries.example_en: The patient developed a superinfection during prolonged antibiotic treatment.

entries.definition_cn: 超越人类天才水平的智能
entries.definition_en: intelligence surpassing the level of a human genius
entries.example_cn: 科学家们正在争论人工超级智能是否可能。
entries.example_en: Scientists are debating whether artificial superintelligence is possible.

entries.definition_en: to watch and direct the work of others
entries.example_cn: 她受雇监督新图书馆的建造工作。
entries.example_en: She was hired to superintend the construction of the new library.

entries.definition_en: the act of managing by watching over how someone or a group performs their duties
entries.example_cn: 该建筑项目的监督需要工程师的持续监管。
entries.example_en: The superintendence of the construction project required constant oversight by the engineer.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: Source marks both countable and uncountable use.

entries.definition_en: a person who directs and manages an organization
entries.example_cn: 学校主管宣布了新的安全规定。
entries.example_en: The superintendent of the school announced new safety rules.

entries.definition_en: a caretaker for an apartment house who collects rent and acts as a janitor
entries.example_cn: 公寓管理员在周一向所有租户收取租金。
entries.example_en: The superintendent collected the rent from all the tenants on Monday.

entries.definition_en: of very high quality
entries.example_cn: 这个品牌生产优质皮革制品。
entries.example_en: This brand produces superior quality leather goods.

entries.definition_en: of or characteristic of high rank or importance
entries.example_cn: 高级军官们参加了仪式。
entries.example_en: The superior officers attended the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: not subject to or influenced by something
entries.example_cn: 尽管一片混乱，这位上级军官依然保持冷静。
entries.example_en: The superior officer remained calm despite the chaos.

entries.definition_en: a person of higher rank or station
entries.example_cn: 我需要先向上级请示才能提前离开。
entries.example_en: I need to ask my superior for permission before leaving early.

entries.definition_en: the head of a religious community
entries.example_cn: 首领在晨会上对僧侣们讲话。
entries.example_en: The superior addressed the monks during the morning assembly.

entries.definition_en: a combatant who can defeat rivals
entries.example_cn: 这位优胜者轻松赢得了冠军。
entries.example_en: The superior fighter won the championship easily.

entries.definition_en: a character or symbol set above another
entries.example_cn: 在 x 平方表达式中，数字 2 是上标。
entries.example_en: The number 2 is a superior in the expression x squared.

entries.definition_en: written or printed above another character
entries.example_cn: 上方的字母表示数学中的指数。
entries.example_en: The superior letter indicates the exponent in mathematics.

entries.definition_en: the state of being better than others
entries.example_cn: 这支球队的胜利清楚地表明了他们的优越性。
entries.example_en: The team's victory was a clear sign of their superiority.

entries.definition_en: having a competitive advantage over others
entries.example_cn: 我们公司的新技术使我们在市场上具有显著优势。
entries.example_en: Our company's new technology gives us a significant superiority in the market.

entries.definition_en: a feeling of being better than others
entries.example_cn: 他在与新员工交谈时表现出优越感。
entries.example_en: He displayed a sense of superiority when speaking to the new employees.

entries.definition_en: the condition of excelling or going beyond normal limits
entries.example_cn: 这位运动员的表现展示了罕见的卓越水平。
entries.example_en: The athlete's performance demonstrated a level of superiority rarely seen.

entries.definition_en: exceptionally good; of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 这是现代建筑质量最高的典范。
entries.example_en: This is the superlative example of modern architecture.

entries.definition_en: an exaggerated expression, usually of praise
entries.example_cn: 这篇影评充满了赞美这部电影的溢美之词。
entries.example_en: The review was full of superlatives about the film.

entries.definition_cn: 形容词或副词的最高级形式
entries.definition_en: the superlative form of an adjective or adverb
entries.example_cn: 在句子“最快的车”中，单词“fastest”是最高级形式。
entries.example_en: In the sentence 'the fastest car', the word 'fastest' is the superlative.

entries.definition_cn: 所能达到的最高水平或程度；发展的最高阶段
entries.definition_en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development
entries.example_cn: 这位运动员在其职业生涯中达到了表现的最高水平。
entries.example_en: The athlete reached the superlative level of performance in her career.

entries.definition_en: to a superlative degree
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家画风景画的技艺极其高超。
entries.example_en: The artist was superlatively skilled in painting landscapes.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有非凡或超人般力量的男子
entries.definition_en: a man with extraordinary or seemingly superhuman powers
entries.example_cn: 这部电影讲述了一位拯救城市的超人的故事。
entries.example_en: The movie tells the story of a superman who saves the city.

entries.definition_cn: LSD（一种致幻剂）的街头名称
entries.definition_en: a street name for the drug lysergic acid diethylamide
entries.example_cn: 警方警告人们不要滥用这种名为“超人”的毒品。
entries.example_en: The police warned against the dangers of the superman.

entries.definition_en: a large store where customers serve themselves and buy food and household items
entries.example_cn: 我们通常去超市买杂货。
entries.example_en: We usually buy our groceries at the supermarket.

entries.definition_en: a fashion model who is famous and highly successful
entries.example_cn: 这位超级名模身穿设计师礼服在巴黎走秀。
entries.example_en: The supermodel walked the runway in Paris wearing a designer gown.

entries.definition_en: a mother who manages to care for her children while working full-time
entries.example_cn: 许多人钦佩那位在从事高压工作的同时抚养三个孩子的全能妈妈。
entries.example_en: Many people admire the supermom who balances a demanding career with raising three kids.

usage.label: 美国；非正式
usage.pattern: A mother working full-time while caring for home and children.

entries.definition_en: coming from or existing on high; heavenly
entries.example_cn: 天上的光芒照亮了古老的寺庙。
entries.example_en: The supernal light illuminated the ancient temple.

entries.definition_en: related to heaven or the spirit
entries.example_cn: 她在冥想中感到一种神圣的宁静。
entries.example_en: She felt a supernal peace during the meditation.

entries.definition_en: the clear liquid that remains on top after a solid has settled
entries.example_cn: 科学家小心地倒掉上清液以分离沉淀物。
entries.example_en: The scientist carefully poured off the supernatant to isolate the sediment.

entries.definition_en: floating on the surface of a liquid above a sediment or precipitate
entries.example_cn: 在实验的下一步之前，移除了漂浮在沉淀物上方的那层液体。
entries.example_en: The supernatant layer was removed before the next step of the experiment.

entries.definition_en: not existing in nature or subject to explanation according to natural laws; not physical or material
entries.example_cn: 这个故事讲述了一次与鬼魂的超自然遭遇。
entries.example_en: The story features a supernatural encounter with a ghost.

entries.definition_cn: 超自然事物（超自然现象和存在）
entries.definition_en: supernatural beings and events collectively
entries.example_cn: 这本书探讨了超自然现象的神秘之处。
entries.example_en: The book explores the mysteries of the supernatural.

entries.definition_en: the belief that forces exist beyond ordinary human understanding
entries.example_cn: 这部小说探讨了科学与超自然论之间的冲突。
entries.example_en: The novel explores the conflict between science and supernaturalism.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being attributed to power that seems to violate or go beyond natural forces
entries.example_cn: 这个故事中超自然属性体现在魔法违背物理定律的描绘上。
entries.example_en: The story's supernaturalism lies in its depiction of magic defying physical laws.

entries.definition_cn: 相信超自然现象的人；超自然主义者
entries.definition_en: a person who believes in the supernatural
entries.example_cn: 这位超自然主义者相信，那些奇怪的光有超自然的原因。
entries.example_en: The supernaturalist believed that the strange lights had a paranormal cause.

entries.definition_en: relating to or supporting the belief in supernatural powers
entries.example_cn: 这种超自然论的方法忽略了科学证据。
entries.example_en: The supernaturalist approach to the mystery ignored scientific evidence.

entries.definition_en: in a way that involves supernatural forces or powers
entries.example_cn: 古老的传说称，这片森林超自然地免受火灾侵袭。
entries.example_en: The old legend claims the forest was supernaturally protected from fire.

entries.definition_en: exceeding the normal or average level
entries.example_cn: 她展现出超常的力量，举起了那辆重车。
entries.example_en: She displayed supernormal strength to lift the heavy car.

entries.definition_en: beyond the range of what is normal or can be explained by science
entries.example_cn: 这个故事描述了一个超自然事件，一个人穿墙而过。
entries.example_en: The story describes a supernormal event where a man walked through a wall.

entries.definition_cn: 与同类相比拥有非凡能力的生物
entries.definition_en: a being with extraordinary powers compared with others of its species
entries.example_cn: 这部小说讲述了一位能够与动物交流的超常者的故事。
entries.example_en: The novel follows a supernormal who can communicate with animals.

entries.definition_en: supernormal phenomena considered collectively
entries.example_cn: 这本书研究神秘体验中所报告的超常现象。
entries.example_en: The book examines the supernormal as reported in mystical experiences.

entries.definition_en: a star that explodes and becomes extremely bright
entries.example_cn: 天文学家在遥远的星系中观测到一颗超新星。
entries.example_en: Astronomers observed a supernova in a distant galaxy.

entries.definition_en: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.example_cn: 该项目在预算充足的情况下完成，多余的预算允许增加额外的安全功能。
entries.example_en: The project was completed with a supernumerary budget that allowed for extra safety features.

entries.definition_en: a person additional to the regular staff
entries.example_cn: 医院聘请了一名编外护士来顶替额外的班次。
entries.example_en: The hospital hired a supernumerary nurse to cover the extra shifts.

entries.definition_en: a minor actor in crowd scenes
entries.example_cn: 作为一名群众演员，他在整部电影中都站在背景中。
entries.example_en: As a supernumerary, he stood in the background for the entire film.

entries.definition_en: a biological classification rank higher than an order but lower than a class
entries.example_cn: 鲸目超目包括鲸鱼、海豚和鼠海豚。
entries.example_en: The cetacean superorder includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises.

entries.definition_en: of higher rank, status, or value
entries.example_cn: 共同的上位目标将这两支敌对队伍团结在了一起。
entries.example_en: The superordinate goal united the two rival teams.

entries.definition_en: someone who holds a higher rank or station
entries.example_cn: 上级军官下达了最终命令。
entries.example_en: The superordinate officer gave the final orders.

entries.definition_en: a word that is more general than a specific word
entries.example_cn: 在这个分类法中，“动物”是“狗”的上位词。
entries.example_en: In this taxonomy, 'animal' is the superordinate of 'dog'.

entries.definition_en: to place someone or something in a superior order or rank
entries.example_cn: 新政策使初级职员处于高级经理之下。
entries.example_en: The new policy superordinates junior staff to senior managers.

entries.definition_en: the univalent anion O2-.
entries.example_cn: 超氧离子的存在可能会损伤生物组织。
entries.example_en: The presence of superoxide can cause damage to biological tissues.

entries.definition_en: a metallic oxide that contains the univalent anion O2-.
entries.example_cn: 超氧化物是一种用于某些工业过程的化学化合物。
entries.example_en: Superoxide is a type of chemical compound used in certain industrial processes.

entries.definition_en: to place something on top of something else
entries.example_cn: 她在饼干上放了一层奶油奶酪。
entries.example_en: She superposed a layer of cream cheese on the crackers.

entries.definition_en: to place one geometric figure on another so their edges match
entries.example_cn: 为了解开谜题，你必须将这两个形状完美地叠合在一起。
entries.example_en: To solve the puzzle, you must superpose the two shapes perfectly.

entries.definition_cn: 量子力学中两个或多个量子态叠加形成另一个有效量子态的状态
entries.definition_en: the state in quantum mechanics in which two or more quantum states are combined to form another valid quantum state
entries.example_cn: 电子在被测量之前可以处于两个能级的叠加态。
entries.example_en: An electron can exist in a superposition of two energy states until it is measured.

entries.definition_en: the rule stating that in a sequence of sedimentary rocks, the oldest layer is at the bottom
entries.example_cn: 根据叠置律，下层岩系中的化石比上层的更古老。
entries.example_en: According to the law of superposition, the fossils in the lower stratum are older than those above.

entries.definition_en: the act of laying one layer of rock on top of another in geological history
entries.example_cn: 地层叠置原理帮助地质学家确定岩层的相对年代。
entries.example_en: The principle of superposition helps geologists determine the relative ages of rock layers.

entries.definition_en: the act of placing one geometric figure exactly over another to check if they match
entries.example_cn: 建筑师使用叠合方法来验证这两份蓝图是否完全相同。
entries.example_en: The architect used superposition to verify that the two blueprints were identical.

entries.definition_en: the state of having one object placed directly on top of another
entries.example_cn: 新瓦片覆盖在旧瓦片上，导致了一些结构问题。
entries.example_en: The superposition of the new roof tiles over the old ones caused some structural issues.

entries.definition_cn: 非凡的身体或精神能力，尤指超级英雄或超级反派拥有的能力
entries.definition_en: an extraordinary physical or mental ability, especially one possessed by a superhero or supervillain
entries.example_cn: 她的超能力让她能够控制电力。
entries.example_en: Her superpower allows her to control electricity.

entries.definition_en: a state that is powerful enough to influence events globally
entries.example_cn: 这个超级大国就国际贸易做出了重大决定。
entries.example_en: The superpower made a significant decision regarding international trade.

entries.definition_en: containing more dissolved substance than is normally possible at a given temperature
entries.example_cn: 当溶液冷却时，它变成了过饱和状态。
entries.example_en: The solution became supersaturated when it cooled down.

entries.definition_cn: 蒸气压高于通常可能值的
entries.definition_en: having a vapor pressure higher than is normally possible
entries.example_cn: 过饱和蒸气很快在冷表面上凝结了。
entries.example_en: The supersaturated vapor quickly condensed on the cool surface.

entries.definition_en: a letter or symbol written or printed above the line of normal text
entries.example_cn: 在公式中，数字 2 是一个上标，表示平方。
entries.example_en: In the formula, the number 2 is a superscript indicating the square.

entries.definition_en: written or printed above the line of normal text
entries.example_cn: 请用上标输入变量名，以与方程式保持一致。
entries.example_en: Please type the variable name in superscript to match the equation.

entries.definition_cn: 写在某物表面、外部或上方的文字或铭文；特指信件或信封上的地址
entries.definition_en: something written or engraved on the surface, outside, or above something else; especially an address on a letter or envelope
entries.example_cn: 信封外面所写的文字是寄件人的地址。
entries.example_en: The superscription on the envelope was the sender's address.

entries.definition_en: the activity of writing an inscription above something else
entries.example_cn: 艺术家对壁画的题写增加了一层历史背景。
entries.example_en: The artist's superscription of the mural added a layer of historical context.

entries.definition_en: to take the place of something or someone; to replace it or them
entries.example_cn: 新软件将于下个月取代旧版本。
entries.example_en: The new software will supersede the old version next month.

entries.definition_en: having an allergy or peculiar or excessive susceptibility, especially to a specific factor
entries.example_cn: 她对清洁剂中的一些化学物质过敏。
entries.example_en: She is supersensitive to certain chemicals found in cleaning products.

entries.definition_en: the act of superseding, or the fact of having been superseded
entries.example_cn: 这项新技术标志着旧制造方法的被取代。
entries.example_en: The new technology marked the supersession of the old manufacturing methods.

entries.definition_en: (of speed) greater than the speed of sound in a given medium (especially air)
entries.example_cn: 那架超音速飞机飞越了海洋。
entries.example_en: The supersonic jet flew across the ocean.

entries.definition_cn: （口语）超声的；频率高于人耳可听范围的
entries.definition_en: (colloquial) having frequencies above those of audible sound
entries.example_cn: 在口语用法中，人们说蝙蝠利用“超音波”导航。
entries.example_en: In colloquial usage, bats are said to use supersonic waves to navigate.

entries.definition_cn: 超级明星；在某领域极其成功或著名的人
entries.definition_en: a very famous and successful person, especially in entertainment, business, or another field
entries.example_cn: 这部电影由一位好莱坞超级明星主演。
entries.example_en: The movie starred a Hollywood superstar.

entries.definition_en: a belief that is not based on reason or knowledge
entries.example_cn: 穿幸运袜只是一种迷信。
entries.example_en: Wearing lucky socks is just a superstition.

entries.definition_en: believing in magic or luck rather than natural laws
entries.example_cn: 她迷信，拒绝从梯子下走过。
entries.example_en: She is superstitious and refuses to walk under a ladder.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is based on superstition
entries.example_cn: 她迷信地避免从梯子下走过。
entries.example_en: She superstitiously avoided walking under a ladder.

entries.definition_en: any stratum or layer superimposed on another
entries.example_cn: 地质学家研究了火山灰的覆盖层。
entries.example_en: The geologist studied the superstrate of volcanic ash.

entries.definition_en: the language of a later invading people that is imposed on an indigenous population and contributes features to their language
entries.example_cn: 英语在印度常被视为上层语言。
entries.example_en: English is often considered a superstrate language in India.

entries.definition_cn: 光伏组件朝向太阳一面的保护性覆盖层
entries.definition_en: the protective covering on the sun-facing side of a photovoltaic module
entries.example_cn: 这种覆盖层在允许阳光透过的同时保护光伏组件免受撞击。
entries.example_en: The superstrate protects the photovoltaic module from impact while allowing sunlight to pass through.

entries.definition_cn: 弦理论中假设的在多个维度振动的一维弦
entries.definition_en: a hypothetical one-dimensional string that vibrates in multiple dimensions, proposed in string theory
entries.example_cn: 超弦理论认为基本粒子是微小的振动弦。
entries.example_en: Superstring theory proposes that fundamental particles are tiny vibrating strings.

entries.definition_cn: 包含指定子字符串的文本字符串
entries.definition_en: a string of text that contains a specified substring
entries.example_cn: 字符串“cathode”是一个超字符串，包含“cat”“hod”和“ode”。
entries.example_en: The string “cathode” is a superstring containing “cat,” “hod,” and “ode.”

entries.definition_cn: 船舶主甲板以上的上层建筑
entries.definition_en: the part of a ship above the main deck
entries.example_cn: 风暴过后，船长检查了上层建筑是否受损。
entries.example_en: The captain inspected the superstructure for damage after the storm.

entries.definition_cn: 超对称性：一种使费米子和玻色子相联系的理论对称性，某些统一基本力的理论会采用它
entries.definition_en: a theoretical symmetry relating fermions and bosons, proposed in some attempts to unify fundamental forces
entries.example_cn: 超对称性是一个理论框架，提出了费米子和玻色子之间的关系。
entries.example_en: Supersymmetry is a theoretical framework that proposes a relationship between fermions and bosons.

entries.definition_en: a very large oil tanker
entries.example_cn: 巨型油轮触礁后向海洋泄漏了石油。
entries.example_en: The supertanker leaked oil into the ocean after hitting a reef.

entries.definition_en: an additional tax on income that has already been taxed
entries.example_cn: 政府提议对高收入者征收附加税。
entries.example_en: The government proposed a supertax on high earners.

entries.definition_en: the second note of a diatonic scale in music
entries.example_cn: 作曲家使用上主音创造了一个令人惊讶的和声转换。
entries.example_en: The composer used the supertonic to create a surprising harmonic shift.

entries.definition_cn: 作为额外或意外的情况发生
entries.definition_en: to take place as an additional or unexpected development
entries.example_cn: 和平谈判期间爆发了新的冲突。
entries.example_en: A new conflict supervened during the peace negotiations.

entries.definition_en: a villain with superpowers
entries.example_cn: 超级英雄团队聚集起来，对抗威胁这座城市的新的超级反派。
entries.example_en: The superhero team gathered to confront the new supervillain threatening the city.

entries.definition_en: to watch and direct someone or something
entries.example_cn: 经理将在新员工的第一周监督他们。
entries.example_en: The manager will supervise the new employees during their first week.

entries.definition_en: to keep under surveillance or watch closely
entries.example_cn: 安保人员必须时刻监视大楼的周边区域。
entries.example_en: Security personnel must supervise the perimeter of the building at all times.

entries.definition_en: being watched or directed by someone in charge
entries.example_cn: 学生们在受监督的环境中完成了项目。
entries.example_en: The students worked on the project in a supervised environment.

entries.definition_en: the act of managing or overseeing the work of people or groups
entries.example_cn: 该项目将在严格监督下进行。
entries.example_en: The project will be carried out under strict supervision.

entries.definition_en: a person who supervises or has charge and direction of others
entries.example_cn: 主管检查了学生们的作业。
entries.example_en: The supervisor checked the students' work.

entries.definition_en: a program that controls the execution of other programs
entries.example_cn: 该监督程序管理后台任务的执行。
entries.example_en: The supervisor manages the execution of the background tasks.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involving the act of supervising
entries.example_cn: 监督委员会每月开会一次以审查公司的进展。
entries.example_en: The supervisory board meets once a month to review the company's progress.

entries.definition_en: rotation of the hands and forearms so that the palms face upward
entries.example_cn: 物理治疗师指导患者练习旋后动作以增强前臂肌肉。
entries.example_en: The physical therapist instructed the patient to practice supination to strengthen the forearm muscles.

usage.label: countable or uncountable
usage.pattern: Both countable and uncountable uses are sourced.

entries.definition_cn: 足部同时内收和内翻的动作
entries.definition_en: the act of combining adduction and inversion of the foot
entries.example_cn: 足病医生观察到患者走路时足部出现旋后。
entries.example_en: The podiatrist observed supination of the patient's foot as he walked.

entries.definition_en: a muscle in the forearm that turns the palm upward
entries.example_cn: 旋后肌帮助旋转前臂，使手掌朝上。
entries.example_en: The supinator muscle helps rotate the forearm so the palm faces up.

entries.definition_en: lying flat on one's back with the face upward
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，她仰卧在草地上休息。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, she lay supine on the grass to rest.

entries.definition_en: showing a lack of energy or will to act; passive
entries.example_cn: 他太消极，不敢挑战公司的不公平规定。
entries.example_en: He was too supine to challenge the unfair rules of the company.

entries.definition_en: a light meal eaten in the early evening or late at night
entries.example_cn: 我们通常吃简单的晚餐，由汤和面包组成。
entries.example_en: We usually have a simple supper consisting of soup and bread.

entries.definition_en: a social gathering where a light evening meal is served
entries.example_cn: 俱乐部昨晚为它的会员举办了一场晚宴聚会。
entries.example_en: The club hosted a supper for its new members last night.

entries.definition_en: the usual time in the evening when people eat their main meal
entries.example_cn: 我们通常在晚餐时间吃最喜欢的甜点。
entries.example_en: We usually have our favorite dessert at suppertime.

entries.definition_en: the act of drinking liquid food or eating with a spoon
entries.example_cn: 这个婴儿还处于喝汤阶段，不能吃固体食物。
entries.example_en: The baby is still at the supping stage and cannot chew solid food.

entries.definition_en: take the place or move into the position of
entries.example_cn: 新技术已经取代了许多传统方法。
entries.example_en: New technology has supplanted many traditional methods.

entries.definition_cn: 取代（尤指用不正当手段）
entries.definition_en: the act of replacing someone or something, especially by using unfair or secret methods
entries.example_cn: 新技术正导致传统制造方法的被取代。
entries.example_en: The new technology is leading to the supplanting of traditional manufacturing methods.

entries.definition_en: capable of moving or bending freely (used of persons' bodies)
entries.example_cn: 多年的瑜伽训练使她的身体保持柔韧和强壮。
entries.example_en: Years of yoga training kept her body supple and strong.

entries.definition_en: readily adaptable (used of personality traits)
entries.example_cn: 他适应性强的个性使他能够融入任何社交群体。
entries.example_en: His supple personality allowed him to fit into any social group.

entries.definition_en: gracefully thin and bending and moving with ease
entries.example_cn: 她身材纤细优雅，动作流畅自如。
entries.example_en: She had a supple figure that moved with fluid grace.

entries.definition_en: to make something pliant and flexible
entries.example_cn: 体操运动员通过热身运动使关节变得柔韧。
entries.example_en: The gymnast suppled her joints with warm-up exercises.

entries.definition_en: to add something to make up for a deficiency or insufficiency.
entries.example_cn: 政府计划用额外资金来补充预算。
entries.example_en: The government plans to supplement the budget with extra funds.

entries.definition_en: to serve as an addition or extra to something.
entries.example_cn: 这部纪录片作为教科书的补充。
entries.example_en: The documentary serves as a supplement to the textbook.

entries.definition_en: to add something to the very end of a list or text.
entries.example_cn: 编辑决定在文章末尾追加一个总结段落。
entries.example_en: The editor decided to supplement the article with a concluding paragraph.

entries.definition_en: a quantity added to compensate for a lack or deficiency.
entries.example_cn: 维生素D常被作为补充物服用，以确保摄入量充足。
entries.example_en: Vitamin D is often taken as a supplement to ensure adequate intake.

entries.definition_en: additional textual material added to a publication, typically placed at the end.
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志附带了一份关于旅行技巧的增刊。
entries.example_en: The magazine included a supplement on travel tips.

entries.definition_en: a component added to improve the capability or function of a system.
entries.example_cn: 他们安装了一个软件附加组件来增强安全性。
entries.example_en: They installed a software supplement to enhance security.

entries.definition_en: added to complete or make up a deficiency
entries.example_cn: 政府宣布提供补充资金以弥补预算赤字。
entries.example_en: The government announced supplemental funding to cover the budget shortfall.

entries.definition_en: functioning in a supporting capacity to assist something else
entries.example_cn: 辅助材料为学生提供了额外的练习。
entries.example_en: The supplemental materials provided extra practice exercises for students.

entries.definition_en: added to complete something or make up for a lack
entries.example_cn: 她买了一张补充票以进入博物馆。
entries.example_en: She bought a supplementary ticket to enter the museum.

entries.definition_en: providing extra help or support
entries.example_cn: 补充说明将帮助你更好地理解正文。
entries.example_en: The supplementary notes will help you understand the main text better.

entries.definition_en: something added to complete or improve something else, such as a nutrient added to food
entries.example_cn: 这种补充剂为患者的饮食补充了钙。
entries.example_en: The supplement added calcium to the patient's diet.

entries.definition_en: the action of adding something to make up for a deficiency or to improve something
entries.example_cn: 在课程中补充实践练习非常有帮助。
entries.example_en: The supplementation of the curriculum with practical exercises was very helpful.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being pliant and able to bend without breaking
entries.example_cn: 这条皮带因其柔顺和耐用而备受推崇。
entries.example_en: The leather belt was valued for its suppleness and durability.

usage.label: usually uncountable
usage.pattern: Source marks the noun as usually uncountable.

entries.definition_en: the graceful quality of a person or animal that is flexible and moves easily
entries.example_cn: 舞者赞赏那位年轻体操运动员动作的柔韧性。
