entries.example_cn: 风把树吹倒了。
entries.example_en: The wind tipped the tree over.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to tilt or lean
entries.example_cn: 他把桌子弄翻了。
entries.example_en: He tipped the table over.

entries.definition_en: to provide with or cover the tip of something
entries.example_cn: 树枝顶端覆盖着积雪。
entries.example_en: The branches were tipped with snow.

entries.definition_en: a shape that looks like the letter V
entries.example_cn: 屋顶呈尖顶状。
entries.example_en: The roof has a sharp tip.

entries.definition_en: secret information that something is going to happen
entries.example_cn: 警方收到了一起抢劫案的内情。
entries.example_en: The police received a tip-off about the robbery.

entries.definition_en: the starting of a basketball game with a jump ball
entries.example_cn: 裁判抛球开始了比赛。
entries.example_en: The referee tossed the ball for the tip-off.

entries.definition_en: to the highest extent
entries.example_cn: 这支球队为锦标赛做好了最佳准备。
entries.example_en: The team is in tip-top shape for the championship.

entries.definition_cn: 设计成可向上翻起或移开的
entries.definition_en: constructed so as to tip up or out of the way
entries.example_cn: 这辆卡车的驾驶室设计成可向上翻起，以便进入发动机舱。
entries.example_en: The truck had a tip-up cab to allow access to the engine.

entries.definition_cn: 冰钓时鱼咬饵便升起旗子的装置
entries.definition_en: a device used in ice fishing that raises a flag when a fish takes the bait
entries.example_cn: 垂钓者注视着冰钓报警装置，留意是否有鱼咬饵。
entries.example_en: The angler watched the tip-up for any sign that a fish had taken the bait.

entries.definition_cn: 圆锥形的北美印第安人帐篷
entries.definition_en: a Native American tent, usually conical in shape
entries.example_cn: 游客参观博物馆，看到了传统的圆锥形帐篷。
entries.example_en: The tourists visited the museum to see a traditional tipi.

entries.definition_en: a person who leaves a tip
entries.example_cn: 给小费的人在桌上留下了一笔慷慨的小费。
entries.example_en: The tipper left a generous amount on the table.

entries.definition_en: a truck whose contents can be emptied without handling; the front end of the platform can be pneumatically raised so that the load is discharged by gravity
entries.example_cn: 建筑队使用自卸卡车卸载碎石。
entries.example_en: The construction crew used a tipper to unload the gravel.

entries.definition_en: a woman's fur shoulder cape with hanging ends, often made from a whole fox or marten
entries.example_cn: 她披着一条狐狸毛制成的奢华披肩。
entries.example_en: She wore a luxurious tippet made of fox fur.

entries.definition_en: to drink alcohol moderately but regularly
entries.example_cn: 他们过去每个周五晚饭后都会小酌。
entries.example_en: They used to tipple after dinner every Friday.

entries.definition_en: any alcoholic drink
entries.example_cn: 他点了一杯酒来庆祝升职。
entries.example_en: He ordered a tipple to celebrate his promotion.

entries.definition_cn: 经常少量饮酒的人；嗜酒者
entries.definition_en: a person who drinks alcohol frequently in small amounts
entries.example_cn: 那位老酒鬼每晚都在当地酒吧啜饮自己喜欢的艾尔啤酒。
entries.example_en: The old tippler spent his evenings at the local pub, sipping his favorite ale.

entries.definition_en: inclined to heel over easily under sail
entries.example_cn: 那艘易倾覆的船在强风中危险地摇晃。
entries.example_en: The tippy boat rocked dangerously in the strong wind.

entries.definition_en: plural of tip
entries.example_cn: 服务员给了我一些关于如何改进烹饪的建议。
entries.example_en: The waiter gave me some tips on how to improve my cooking.

entries.definition_cn: 一种流行的儿童追逐游戏（澳大利亚）
entries.definition_en: a popular children's chasing game (Australia)
entries.example_cn: 孩子们放学后在公园里玩起了追逐游戏。
entries.example_en: The children played tips in the park after school.

entries.definition_cn: tip 的第三人称单数简单现在时
entries.definition_en: third-person singular simple present indicative of tip
entries.example_cn: 他把瓶子倾斜倒水。
entries.example_en: He tips the bottle to pour the water.

entries.definition_cn: 提供建议或消息的人，尤指提供赛马或股市方面建议的人
entries.definition_en: a person who provides tips or advice, especially about racehorses or the stock market
entries.example_cn: 这位赛马消息提供者在比赛前准确预测了获胜的马匹。
entries.example_en: The tipster predicted the winning horse correctly before the race.

entries.definition_en: slightly intoxicated
entries.example_cn: 她喝了两杯酒后有点微醺。
entries.example_en: She was a little tipsy after two glasses of wine.

entries.definition_en: unstable and likely to tip over
entries.example_cn: 那张高桌子很不稳，他靠上去时晃动了。
entries.example_en: The tall table was tipsy and wobbled when he leaned on it.

entries.definition_en: to walk by keeping your toes on the ground and your heels raised
entries.example_cn: 宝宝学会了踮着脚尖穿过房间去拿玩具。
entries.example_en: The baby learned to tiptoe across the room to reach the toy.

entries.definition_en: in a way that involves walking on the tips of the toes
entries.example_cn: 她踮着脚尖走过走廊，以免吵醒熟睡中的妹妹。
entries.example_en: She tiptoed down the hallway so as not to wake her sleeping sister.

entries.definition_en: the very end of a toe
entries.example_cn: 长跑后，她的脚趾尖感到一阵剧痛。
entries.example_en: She felt a sharp pain at the tip of her toe after the long run.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 整个住宿期间服务都一流。
entries.example_en: The service was tiptop throughout the entire stay.

entries.definition_en: the highest level or degree attainable
entries.example_cn: 该公司已达到行业巅峰。
entries.example_en: The company has reached the tiptop of its industry.

entries.definition_en: the extreme top or summit
entries.example_cn: 他们爬到了山顶。
entries.example_en: They climbed to the tiptop of the mountain.

entries.definition_en: excellently; in a first-rate manner
entries.example_cn: 这辆车又运转得非常好了。
entries.example_en: The car is running tiptop again.

entries.definition_en: a South American tree with feathery leaves and bright yellow flowers, often grown for decoration
entries.example_cn: 花园里有一棵美丽的蒂普树，春天时开满了金色的花朵。
entries.example_en: The garden features a beautiful tipu tree blooming with golden flowers in the spring.

entries.definition_en: a speech of violent denunciation
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家对新税法发起了激烈的抨击。
entries.example_en: The politician launched a tirade against the new tax laws.

entries.definition_en: an Italian dessert with layers of coffee-soaked sponge cake and mascarpone cheese
entries.example_cn: 我们点了一份提拉米苏来结束晚餐。
entries.example_en: We ordered a slice of tiramisu to finish our dinner.

entries.definition_en: a rubber ring covering a wheel
entries.example_cn: 这辆车需要新轮胎。
entries.example_en: The car needs new tires.

entries.definition_en: to lose interest in something
entries.example_cn: 我开始厌倦这种例行公事。
entries.example_en: I am starting to tire of this routine.

entries.definition_en: to make someone exhausted through effort or strain
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步旅行让他完全筋疲力尽。
entries.example_en: The long hike tired him out completely.

entries.definition_en: to cause boredom
entries.example_cn: 重复的工作让工人们感到厌倦，失去了兴趣。
entries.example_en: The repetitive task bored the workers and made them lose interest.

entries.definition_en: to deplete resources
entries.example_cn: 战争耗尽了这个国家的经济。
entries.example_en: The war tired the country's economy.

entries.definition_en: having no more energy or strength
entries.example_cn: 我太累了，走不动了。
entries.example_en: I am too tired to walk any further.

entries.definition_cn: 对某事感到厌烦的；恼火的
entries.definition_en: fed up, annoyed, or irritated by something
entries.example_cn: 她对一直等待晚点的火车感到厌烦。
entries.example_en: She was tired of waiting for the delayed train.

entries.definition_en: old and worn
entries.example_cn: 他们住在车站附近一间看起来陈旧破旧的旅馆房间里。
entries.example_en: They stayed in a tired-looking hotel room near the station.

entries.definition_en: used too often; becoming overfamiliar
entries.example_cn: 这个笑话讲得太多了，有点陈腐了。
entries.example_en: The joke was a bit tired after being told so many times.

entries.definition_en: in a manner showing that one is weary
entries.example_cn: 马拉松结束后，她疲倦地走下长长的走廊。
entries.example_en: She walked tiredly down the long corridor after the marathon.

entries.definition_en: a temporary loss of strength and energy caused by hard physical or mental work
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步使他的双腿非常疲劳。
entries.example_en: The long hike left his legs very tired.

entries.definition_en: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality
entries.example_cn: 不知疲倦的志愿者们日以继夜地帮助受害者。
entries.example_en: The tireless volunteers worked day and night to help the victims.

entries.definition_en: characterized by hard work and perseverance
entries.example_cn: 他勤奋不懈的努力终于使项目取得了成功。
entries.example_en: His tireless efforts finally led to the success of the project.

entries.definition_en: with indefatigable energy; without tiring
entries.example_cn: 她不知疲倦地为这项事业奔走呼号。
entries.example_en: She tirelessly campaigned for the cause.

entries.definition_en: so lacking in interest as to cause mental weariness
entries.example_cn: 漫长的会议令人厌倦且毫无成效。
entries.example_en: The long meeting was tiresome and unproductive.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes boredom or annoyance
entries.example_cn: 他乏味地第三次重复了同一个故事。
entries.example_en: He tiresomely repeated the same story for the third time.

entries.definition_en: causing exhaustion or fatigue
entries.example_cn: 那座山的长途徒步旅行非常令人疲惫。
entries.example_en: The long hike up the mountain was very tiring.

entries.definition_en: someone who is new to a particular field or activity
entries.example_cn: 作为行业新手，她渴望向导师们学习。
entries.example_en: As a tiro in the industry, she was eager to learn from her mentors.

entries.definition_en: an infusion of dried or fresh flowers or leaves, often used for medicinal purposes
entries.example_cn: 她准备了一杯洋甘菊和薰衣草花草茶来帮助睡眠。
entries.example_en: She prepared a soothing tisane of chamomile and lavender to help her sleep.

entries.definition_en: a group of cells with similar structure and function in an organism
entries.example_cn: 肌肉组织帮助身体运动。
entries.example_en: Muscle tissue helps the body move.

entries.definition_en: a soft, thin, usually translucent paper
entries.example_cn: 请用纸巾擦掉洒出来的东西。
entries.example_en: Please use a tissue to wipe the spill.

entries.definition_en: to create cloth by interlacing strands of fabric
entries.example_cn: 古老的织机被用来将羊毛织成毯子。
entries.example_en: The ancient loom was used to tissue wool into blankets.

entries.definition_en: one of the two soft fleshy organs on a woman's chest that produce milk
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件遮住乳房的上衣。
entries.example_en: She wore a top that covered her tits.

entries.definition_en: small insectivorous birds
entries.example_cn: 我们在花园里看到了一群山雀。
entries.example_en: We saw a flock of tits in the garden.

entries.definition_en: the small projection of a mammary gland
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了婴儿的乳头区域。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the infant's titted area.

entries.definition_en: a game played on a 3x3 grid where two players take turns marking spaces with crosses or circles to get three in a row
entries.example_cn: 孩子们花了一下午在人行道上玩井字游戏。
entries.example_en: The children spent the afternoon playing tit-tat-toe on the sidewalk.

entries.definition_en: of great force or power
entries.example_cn: 这艘船在风暴中经历了巨大的搏斗。
entries.example_en: The ship faced a titanic struggle against the storm.

entries.definition_en: a light, strong, grey metal that does not rust easily and is used to make strong but lightweight alloys, such as those for airplane parts
entries.example_cn: 飞机机翼由钛制成，以确保其既坚固又轻便。
entries.example_en: The airplane wings are made of titanium to ensure they are strong yet lightweight.

entries.definition_en: a large, four-legged herbivorous dinosaur with a long neck and a whip-like tail, living during the Cretaceous period mostly in the Southern Hemisphere
entries.example_cn: 在阿根廷发现了一只泰坦龙的化石遗骸。
entries.example_en: The fossilized remains of a titanosaur were discovered in Argentina.

entries.definition_en: a small and tasty piece of food
entries.example_cn: 主菜上桌前，她给我尝了一块蛋糕的美味小块。
entries.example_en: She offered me a titbit of the cake before the main course arrived.

entries.definition_en: the concentration of a substance in a solution, measured by titration
entries.example_cn: 实验室技术员测量了该酸溶液的滴定度。
entries.example_en: The laboratory technician measured the titer of the acid solution.

entries.definition_en: a levy of one tenth of something
entries.example_cn: 那个古代王国被要求向中央政权缴纳什一税。
entries.example_en: The ancient kingdom was required to pay a tithe to the central authority.

entries.definition_en: an offering of a tenth part of some personal income
entries.example_cn: 作为一名虔诚的成员，她将每月工资的十分之一奉献给寺庙。
entries.example_en: As a devout member, she gave a tithe of her monthly salary to the temple.

entries.definition_cn: 缴纳收入的十分之一；缴纳十分之一，尤其是给教会
entries.definition_en: pay a tenth of one's income; pay one tenth of, especially to the church
entries.example_cn: 他决定将收入的十分之一捐给当地慈善机构。
entries.example_en: He decided to tithe his earnings to support the local charity.

entries.definition_en: exact a tithe from
entries.example_cn: 教会官员会从当地农民那里征收什一税。
entries.example_en: The church officials would tithe the harvest from the local farmers.

entries.definition_cn: 对（农产品或作物）征收什一税
entries.definition_en: levy a tithe on (produce or a crop)
entries.example_cn: 领主对其庄园生产的谷物征收什一税。
entries.example_en: The lord tithed the grain produced on his estates.

entries.definition_en: a small South American monkey with long fur and a nonprehensile tail
entries.example_cn: 这种猴子有着美丽的长毛和一条长长的尾巴。
entries.example_en: The titi monkey has beautiful long fur and a long tail.

entries.definition_cn: 美国东南部沿海的一种树
entries.definition_en: a tree of the southeastern United States (Cliftonia monophylla) with glossy leaves and fragrant white flowers
entries.example_cn: 这种树在春天开满芳香的白色花朵。
entries.example_en: The titi tree blooms with fragrant white flowers in spring.

entries.definition_cn: 北美东部的一种落叶灌木状树
entries.definition_en: a deciduous shrubby tree in eastern North America with fissured bark and sour-tasting leaves
entries.example_cn: 这种树树皮深裂，开着小白花。
entries.example_en: The titi has deeply fissured bark and small white flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 使愉悦地或性感地兴奋；挑逗
entries.definition_en: to excite or arouse, especially pleasurably or sexually
entries.example_cn: 这个故事旨在挑逗观众。
entries.example_en: The story was designed to titillate the audience.

entries.definition_cn: 轻触身体部位以刺激表面神经，引起不安、大笑或痉挛
entries.definition_en: to touch a body part lightly so as to excite the surface nerves and cause uneasiness, laughter, or spasmodic movements
entries.example_cn: 冷风开始刺激她的皮肤。
entries.example_en: The cold wind began to titillate her skin.

entries.definition_cn: 令人愉悦但流于肤浅的
entries.definition_en: pleasantly and superficially exciting
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志刊登了关于名人生活方式的浅薄而刺激的故事。
entries.example_en: The magazine featured titillating stories about celebrity lifestyles.

entries.definition_cn: 挑逗性的；使人产生性快感的
entries.definition_en: giving sexual pleasure; sexually arousing
entries.example_cn: 这本小说以其对浪漫的性唤起描写而闻名。
entries.example_en: The novel was known for its titillating descriptions of romance.

entries.definition_cn: 通过轻触引起发笑或抽搐动作而令人兴奋
entries.definition_en: exciting by touching lightly so as to cause laughter or twitching movements
entries.example_cn: 喜剧演员用一个令人发笑的轻触手势逗得观众大笑。
entries.example_en: The comedian used a titillating gesture to make the audience laugh.

entries.definition_en: a pleasurable or sexually exciting sensation
entries.example_cn: 这场挑逗性的表演让观众感到一阵愉悦和兴奋。
entries.example_en: The provocative performance caused a wave of titillation among the audience.

entries.definition_en: an agreeable arousal or stimulation
entries.example_cn: 惊喜派对给她的夜晚带来了愉悦的兴奋感。
entries.example_en: The surprise party brought a sense of titillation to her evening.

entries.definition_cn: 挑逗或刺激以引起兴趣或愉悦的行为
entries.definition_en: the act or process of titillating, especially by arousing interest or pleasure
entries.example_cn: 这则广告靠挑逗性刺激来吸引观众的注意力。
entries.example_en: The advertisement relied on titillation to attract viewers’ attention.

entries.definition_cn: 书名、歌名或艺术品名称
entries.definition_en: the name of a book, song, or artwork
entries.example_cn: 你最喜欢的书叫什么名字？
entries.example_en: What is the title of your favorite book?

entries.definition_en: a word showing someone's rank or job
entries.example_cn: 他的头衔是“博士”。
entries.example_en: His title is 'Doctor'.

entries.definition_en: the status of being a winner
entries.example_cn: 他赢得了世界冠军的头衔。
entries.example_en: He won the title of world champion.

entries.definition_cn: 对财产的合法所有权，或证明该权利的契据等凭证
entries.definition_en: the legal right to own property, or a deed or other certificate proving it
entries.example_cn: 这份契据是该房产的产权凭证。
entries.example_en: The deed serves as the title to the property.

entries.definition_en: a heading for a section of a text
entries.example_cn: 这一章的标题是“开始”。
entries.example_en: The chapter title is 'The Beginning'.

entries.definition_en: give a work a title
entries.example_cn: 他们将这部电影命名为《最后的舞蹈》。
entries.example_en: They titled the movie 'The Last Dance'.

entries.definition_en: a heading that names a law or bill
entries.example_cn: 新法案的标题是《公共安全法》。
entries.example_en: The title of the new bill is 'Public Safety Act'.

entries.definition_cn: 给某人授予特定的头衔或称号，尤指表示等级或身份的头衔
entries.definition_en: give someone a particular title, especially one indicating rank or status
entries.example_cn: 国王授予他约克公爵的头衔。
entries.example_en: The king titled him Duke of York.

entries.definition_cn: 拥有爵位的；贵族出身的
entries.definition_en: belonging to the peerage
entries.example_cn: 这个拥有爵位的家族世世代代居住在这座城堡里。
entries.example_en: The titled family has lived in this castle for centuries.

entries.definition_cn: 小型食虫鸣禽，尤其是 Baeolophus 属的鸟类
entries.definition_en: a small insectivorous songbird, especially one of the genus Baeolophus
entries.example_cn: 一只山雀停在树枝上，大声鸣叫。
entries.example_en: A titmouse perched on the branch and chirped loudly.

entries.definition_cn: 通过滴定法测量（溶液体积或浓度）
entries.definition_en: measure by (the volume or concentration of solutions) by titration
entries.example_cn: 科学家通过滴定法测定酸的浓度。
entries.example_en: Scientists titrate the acid to determine its concentration.

entries.definition_en: a laboratory process where a solution of unknown concentration is gradually added to a known solution until the chemical reaction is complete, allowing the unknown concentration to be calculated
entries.example_cn: 科学家进行滴定以确定酸的浓度。
entries.example_en: The scientist performed a titration to determine the concentration of the acid.

entries.definition_cn: 通过滴定测定的溶液浓度
entries.definition_en: the concentration of a solution as determined by titration
entries.example_cn: 实验室测定了该酸溶液的浓度。
entries.example_en: The titre of the acid solution was measured in the lab.

entries.definition_cn: 通过滴定测定溶液的浓度
entries.definition_en: to determine the strength or concentration of a solution by titration
entries.example_cn: 技术员通过滴定测定了该溶液的酸浓度。
entries.example_en: The technician titred the solution to determine its acid concentration.

entries.definition_en: to laugh nervously
entries.example_cn: 当她意识到自己忘了台词时，开始拘谨地笑起来。
entries.example_en: She began to titter when she realized she had forgotten her lines.

entries.definition_en: a nervous, restrained laugh
entries.example_cn: 喜剧演员讲了个尴尬的笑话后，观众中传出一阵紧张的窃笑。
entries.example_en: A nervous titter went through the audience after the comedian’s awkward joke.

entries.definition_cn: 发出紧张或压抑窃笑的；窃笑般的
entries.definition_en: characterized by or producing nervous or suppressed laughter
entries.example_cn: 她紧张的窃笑使本已紧张的会议更加令人不适。
entries.example_en: Her tittering laughter made the tense meeting even more uncomfortable.

entries.definition_cn: 小点、小笔画或变音符号，尤指字母的一部分，如字母 i 和 j 上的小点
entries.definition_en: A small dot, stroke, or diacritical mark, especially one forming part of a letter, such as the dots over the letters i and j.
entries.example_cn: 字母 i 上的小点不见了。
entries.example_en: The tittle over the i is missing.

entries.definition_en: a very small amount of something
entries.example_cn: 他连一点钱都没剩下。
entries.example_en: He didn't even have a tittle of money left.

entries.definition_cn: 琐碎的闲话；无聊的流言
entries.definition_en: petty, idle gossip or trivial talk
entries.example_cn: 整个下午都在说邻居的闲话。
entries.example_en: The afternoon was spent in tittle-tattle about the neighbors.

entries.definition_en: to engage in or spread gossip
entries.example_cn: 她停止了对邻居的喋喋不休，开始工作了。
entries.example_en: She stopped tittle-tattling about her neighbors and started working.

entries.definition_en: a breast or nipple (vulgar slang)
entries.example_cn: 这个粗俗的笑话提到了女人的乳房。
entries.example_en: The crude joke referred to a woman's titties.

entries.definition_cn: 带有表示地位或职能的头衔的
entries.definition_en: bearing a title that signifies status or function
entries.example_cn: 他在公司担任一个名义上的职位。
entries.example_en: He holds a titular position in the company.

usage.label: not comparable
usage.pattern: Source w24632r0 marks the adjective not-comparable.

entries.definition_cn: 徒有虚名；仅有名义而无实质
entries.definition_en: existing in name only; having a title but no real power or substance
entries.example_cn: 该部门的名义负责人没有实权。
entries.example_en: The titular head of the department has no real authority.

entries.definition_en: relating to a legal title to something
entries.example_cn: 土地的名义所有者有权出售它。
entries.example_en: The titular owner of the land has the right to sell it.

entries.definition_en: pertaining to the title of a work of art
entries.example_cn: 这幅画以其标题而闻名。
entries.example_en: The painting is known by its titular name.

entries.definition_cn: 与表示贵族身份的头衔相关或拥有的
entries.definition_en: associated with or bearing a title signifying nobility
entries.example_cn: 名义上的公爵出席了仪式。
entries.example_en: The titular Duke attended the ceremony.

entries.definition_en: a state of excited agitation or panic
entries.example_cn: 突然的噪音让乘客们一阵慌乱。
entries.example_en: The sudden noise caused a tizzy among the passengers.

entries.definition_cn: 用于动词前，表示不定式
entries.definition_en: Used before a verb to show it is an infinitive.
entries.example_cn: 我想回家。
entries.example_en: I want to go home.

entries.definition_en: Used to mean 'in order to'.
entries.example_cn: 她努力学习是为了通过考试。
entries.example_en: She studied hard to pass the exam.

entries.definition_cn: 用于表示对主语的义务或指令
entries.definition_en: Used to show obligation or a directive given to the subject.
entries.example_cn: 你今天必须完成这项工作。
entries.example_en: You are to finish the work today.

entries.definition_cn: 表示目的地或最终位置
entries.definition_en: Indicating destination or final position.
entries.example_cn: 火车开往伦敦。
entries.example_en: The train goes to London.

entries.definition_cn: 朝……方向；向（不一定到达目的地）
entries.definition_en: In the direction of; towards, without necessarily reaching a destination.
entries.example_cn: 她望向天空。
entries.example_en: She looked to the heavens.

entries.definition_cn: 朝向关闭、接触或接合的位置
entries.definition_en: Toward a closed, touching or engaging position.
entries.example_cn: 将旋钮拧紧。
entries.example_en: Turn the knob to.

entries.definition_cn: 用于隐含的动词前，表示不定式
entries.definition_en: Used before an implied verb to show it is an infinitive.
entries.example_cn: 他似乎忘记了一切。
entries.example_en: He seemed to forget everything.

entries.definition_cn: 城市印度人中常用的填充词
entries.definition_en: A filler word common amongst urban Indians.
entries.example_cn: 哎呀，哎呀，我不知道该怎么办。
entries.example_en: To, to, I don't know what to do.

entries.definition_cn: 待办事项，尤其是清单上列出的任务
entries.definition_en: a task that has been noted as needing to be completed, especially one on a list
entries.example_cn: 我的待办事项清单每天都在变长。
entries.example_en: My to-do list has been growing longer every day.

entries.definition_en: a disorderly outburst or tumult
entries.example_cn: 聚会上闹得很不安静。
entries.example_en: There was a lot of to-do at the party.

entries.definition_en: dated spelling of tonight
entries.example_cn: 我们今晚将在老橡树下见面。
entries.example_en: We shall meet to-night under the old oak tree.

entries.definition_en: dated spelling of tonight
entries.example_cn: 聚会是在今晚举行的。
entries.example_en: The party was held to-night.

entries.definition_en: a tailless amphibian with a stout body and long hind legs for jumping
entries.example_cn: 蟾蜍静静地坐在池塘边的岩石上，等待昆虫。
entries.example_en: The toad sat quietly on a rock near the pond, waiting for insects.

entries.definition_en: a dish consisting of sausages baked inside a batter
entries.example_cn: 我们晚餐点了香肠焗面。
entries.example_en: We ordered toad-in-the-hole for dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 蟾鱼科的一种底栖伏击鱼，皮肤无鳞且黏滑，头宽而厚、口大
entries.definition_en: a bottom-dwelling ambush fish of the family Batrachoididae, with scaleless, slimy skin and a broad, thick head and wide mouth
entries.example_cn: 蟾鱼躲在沙子里，等待猎物游过。
entries.example_en: The toadfish hid in the sand, waiting for prey to swim by.

entries.definition_cn: 一种常见的欧洲多年生植物，开鲜艳的黄色和橙色花；北美的一种归化杂草
entries.definition_en: a common European perennial plant with showy yellow and orange flowers; a naturalized weed in North America
entries.example_cn: 冬雪融化后，花园里长满了柳穿鱼。
entries.example_en: The garden was overrun by toadflax after the winter snow melted.

entries.definition_cn: 不可食用或有毒的蘑菇
entries.definition_en: an inedible or poisonous mushroom
entries.example_cn: 孩子们知道了不能在森林里采摘任何不可食用或有毒的蘑菇。
entries.example_en: The children learned not to pick any toadstool in the forest.

entries.definition_en: a person who flatters others to gain favor or advantage
entries.example_cn: 他因对经理阿谀奉承而被解雇。
entries.example_en: He was dismissed for acting as a toady to the manager.

entries.definition_en: to try to gain favor by flattering or cringing
entries.example_cn: 她拒绝向上司谄媚。
entries.example_en: She refused to toady to her superiors.

entries.definition_en: slices of bread that have been browned by heating
entries.example_cn: 我想要一片烤面包，配咖啡一起吃。
entries.example_en: I would like a slice of toast with my coffee.

entries.definition_cn: 为某人或某事祝酒；祝酒辞
entries.definition_en: a drink offered to honor a person or event
entries.example_cn: 船长为船员的安全致了祝酒辞。
entries.example_en: The captain gave a toast to the crew's safety.

entries.definition_en: a person held in high esteem or receiving much acclaim
entries.example_cn: 获奖后，她成了全镇备受推崇的人。
entries.example_en: After her award, she became the toast of the town.

entries.definition_cn: （美国俚语）完蛋的东西；注定要毁掉的人或物
entries.definition_en: (US slang) something or someone that is doomed or irreparably damaged
entries.example_cn: 如果错过这个截止日期，我们就完蛋了。
entries.example_en: If we miss this deadline, we're toast.

entries.definition_en: to make brown and crisp by heating
entries.example_cn: 请把面包烤到金黄色。
entries.example_en: Please toast the bread until it is golden brown.

entries.definition_en: to propose a drink in honor of someone or something
entries.example_cn: 他们用香槟为新婚夫妇祝酒。
entries.example_en: They toasted the newlyweds with champagne.

entries.definition_en: cooked by toasting
entries.example_cn: 她端上了涂了黄油的烤面包。
entries.example_en: She served the toasted bread with butter.

entries.definition_cn: 喝醉的或处于毒品影响下的【俚语】
entries.definition_en: drunk or under the influence of drugs [slang]
entries.example_cn: 到午夜时，他们已经彻底醉了。
entries.example_en: By midnight, they were completely toasted.

entries.definition_en: a kitchen appliance (usually electric) for toasting bread
entries.example_cn: 她把面包放进烤面包机里。
entries.example_en: She put the bread in the toaster.

entries.definition_en: someone who offers a toast to someone's health or to the success of a venture
entries.example_cn: 宴会上，祝酒者举杯祝新经理成功。
entries.example_en: At the banquet, the toaster raised his glass to the new manager's success.

entries.definition_en: cooking to a brown crispiness over a fire or on a grill
entries.example_cn: 露营者们喜欢在篝火上烤面包片。
entries.example_en: The campers enjoyed toasting slices of bread over the fire.

entries.definition_cn: 在正式宴会上介绍发言人、主持祝酒的人；司仪
entries.definition_en: a person who introduces speakers and proposes toasts at a formal dinner; a master of ceremonies
entries.example_cn: 这位祝酒人热情地介绍了下一位演讲者。
entries.example_en: The toastmaster introduced the next speaker with great enthusiasm.

entries.definition_en: leaves of the tobacco plant dried and prepared for smoking or ingestion
entries.example_cn: 烟草是香烟的主要成分。
entries.example_en: Tobacco is the main ingredient in cigarettes.

entries.definition_en: aromatic annual or perennial herbs and shrubs
entries.example_cn: 烟草属植物在温暖的气候下生长良好。
entries.example_en: The tobacco plant grows well in warm climates.

entries.definition_cn: （过时）烟草商；烟草制品销售者
entries.definition_en: a dated term for a person who sells tobacco and tobacco products
entries.example_cn: 我在街角的烟草商那里买了一些烟斗烟草。
entries.example_en: I bought some pipe tobacco from the tobacconist on the corner.

usage.label: dated
usage.pattern: dated term for a tobacco seller; source w29467r0.

entries.definition_en: a dated term for a shop that sells tobacco products, pipes, and cigars
entries.example_cn: 这家烟草店陈列着各种各样的异国雪茄。
entries.example_en: The tobacconist displayed a wide variety of exotic cigars.

entries.definition_cn: 一种长而窄的雪橇，通常没有滑板，前端向上弯曲
entries.definition_en: a long, narrow sled, usually without runners, with the front end curved upward
entries.example_cn: 他们租了一个雪橇，在雪地里从陡峭的山坡上滑下来。
entries.example_en: They rented a toboggan to slide down the steep hill in the snow.

entries.definition_en: to slide downhill on a toboggan or similar object
entries.example_cn: 孩子们兴奋地乘坐雪橇在结冰的湖面上滑行。
entries.example_en: The children tobogganed down the frozen lake with great excitement.

entries.definition_en: the activity of riding on a long light sled with low handrails
entries.example_cn: 孩子们花了一下午的时间从雪坡上滑下。
entries.example_en: The children spent the afternoon tobogganing down the snowy hill.

usage.label: uncountable; usually
usage.pattern: Normally an uncountable noun for the activity.

entries.definition_en: an antibiotic effective against Gram-negative bacteria
entries.example_cn: 医生开了妥布霉素来治疗严重的细菌感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed tobramycin to treat the severe bacterial infection.

entries.definition_en: a drinking mug in the shape of a stout man wearing a three-cornered hat
entries.example_cn: 他把茶倒进了一个托比杯里。
entries.example_en: He poured his tea into a Toby mug.

entries.definition_en: a Baroque musical piece, usually for keyboard, featuring rapid runs and free rhythm
entries.example_cn: 音乐会以一首震撼人心的管风琴托卡塔曲开场。
entries.example_en: The concert opened with a dramatic toccata for the organ.

entries.definition_cn: 生育酚，维生素E的组成成分之一
entries.definition_en: any of several compounds that make up vitamin E, each containing a chromanol ring and an isoprene side chain
entries.example_cn: 生育酚是维生素E的主要组成成分之一。
entries.example_en: Tocopherol is one of the principal components of vitamin E.

entries.definition_en: the sound of an alarm, typically a bell
entries.example_cn: 警报的响声警告村民们危险正在逼近。
entries.example_en: The ringing of the tocsin warned the villagers of the approaching danger.

entries.definition_en: a bell used to sound an alarm
entries.example_cn: 警报钟被敲响以发出消防演习开始的信号。
entries.example_en: The tocsin was rung to signal the start of the fire drill.

entries.definition_en: alone and on your own
entries.example_cn: 搬到新城市后，她感到有点孤单。
entries.example_en: She felt a bit tod after moving to the new city.

entries.definition_en: a unit of weight for wool equal to about 28 pounds
entries.example_cn: 农夫用托德称量羊毛。
entries.example_en: The farmer weighed the wool in tods.

entries.definition_cn: 在今天（区别于昨天或明天）
entries.definition_en: on this specific day
entries.example_cn: 我今天会给你打电话。
entries.example_en: I will call you today.

entries.definition_en: in these times
entries.example_cn: 人们如今的生活方式有所不同。
entries.example_en: People live differently today.

entries.definition_en: the day of the present moment
entries.example_cn: 今天是晴天。
entries.example_en: Today is a sunny day.

entries.definition_en: the present time or age
entries.example_cn: 如今与过去大不相同。
entries.example_en: Today is very different from the past.

entries.definition_en: walk unsteadily, with short steps
entries.example_cn: 婴儿开始在房间里蹒跚学步。
entries.example_en: The baby began to toddle across the room.

entries.definition_en: a young child who is just beginning to walk
entries.example_cn: 这个学步儿在客厅里迈出了第一步。
entries.example_en: The toddler took his first steps across the living room.

entries.definition_cn: 热 toddy（一种含酒精的热混合饮料）
entries.definition_en: a hot mixed drink made with liquor, water, sugar, and spices
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，他们喝了一杯热气腾腾的香料 toddy 取暖。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, they warmed up with a steaming cup of spiced toddy.

entries.definition_cn: 一种小型食虫西印度鸟，羽毛红绿相间，喙长而直
entries.definition_en: a small bird from the West Indies that eats insects and has red and green feathers with a long straight beak
entries.example_cn: 人们常在热带森林中看到巨嘴鸟停在托迪鸟附近。
entries.example_en: The toucan was often seen perched near the tody in the tropical forest.

entries.definition_en: one of the five digits on the front of a human foot
entries.example_cn: 他在冰上滑倒，弄断了大脚趾。
entries.example_en: He slipped on the ice and broke his big toe.

entries.definition_en: the part of a shoe that covers the toes
entries.example_cn: 这双靴子有加固的鞋头以提供保护。
entries.example_en: This boot has a reinforced toe for protection.

entries.definition_en: the front part of an animal's hoof
entries.example_cn: 马的蹄尖因在硬地上奔跑而磨损了。
entries.example_en: The horse's toe was worn down from running on hard ground.

entries.definition_en: the part of a golf clubhead farthest from the shaft
entries.example_cn: 用杆头前端击球有时会导致右曲球。
entries.example_en: A toe shot can sometimes result in a slice.

entries.definition_en: to hit a golf ball with the front part of the club
entries.example_cn: 他设法用杆头前端将球击上了果岭。
entries.example_en: He managed to toe the ball onto the green.

entries.definition_en: to drive a golf ball using the toe of the club
entries.example_cn: 她不小心用杆头前端将球击进了长草区。
entries.example_en: She accidentally toe'd the ball into the rough.

entries.definition_en: to walk with your toes pointing in a specific direction
entries.example_cn: 宝宝正在学习沿着沙发边缘用脚尖走路。
entries.example_en: The baby is learning to toe along the edge of the sofa.

entries.definition_en: to fasten a piece by driving a fastener obliquely through its side
entries.example_cn: 木匠把不规则的部件斜钉固定在窗台上。
entries.example_en: The carpenters toed the irregular pieces into the sill.

entries.definition_en: in close physical contact during a fight or competition
entries.example_cn: 两位拳击手近身搏斗争夺冠军。
entries.example_en: The two boxers fought toe-to-toe for the championship.

entries.definition_en: having a toe or toes of a specified kind
entries.example_cn: 这只鸟有一只长趾的脚，适合在沙地上行走。
entries.example_en: The bird had a long-toed foot for walking on sand.

usage.label: in compounds
usage.pattern: Usually used in compounds such as narrow-toed.

entries.definition_en: a small starting position that allows for future progress
entries.example_cn: 这家新公司设法在竞争激烈的市场中站稳了脚跟。
entries.example_en: The new company managed to get a toehold in the competitive market.

entries.definition_en: a small part of a rock used for holding one's foot while climbing
entries.example_cn: 攀岩者在湿滑的墙壁上寻找一个可以落脚的支点。
entries.example_en: The climber searched for a toehold on the slippery wall.

entries.definition_cn: 摔跤中扳住对手脚部并向后折其脚的擒拿动作
entries.definition_en: a wrestling hold in which the aggressor bends back the opponent's foot
entries.example_cn: 摔跤手使用扭腿摔法将对手压制在地。
entries.example_en: The wrestler applied a toehold to pin his opponent.

entries.definition_en: the nail at the end of a toe
entries.example_cn: 她洗澡后仔细地修剪了脚趾甲。
entries.example_en: She carefully trimmed her toenails after the bath.

entries.definition_cn: 用斜钉把木板固定在一起
entries.definition_en: to fasten boards by driving nails into them at an angle
entries.example_cn: 木匠以一定角度斜向打入木板以固定框架。
entries.example_en: The carpenter toenailed the boards to the frame at an angle.

entries.definition_en: an upper-class or wealthy person
entries.example_cn: 他真是个有钱有势的人，总是穿着昂贵的西装。
entries.example_en: He is such a toff, always wearing expensive suits.

usage.label: Ireland, UK; derogatory
usage.pattern: upper-class person or someone pretending to be upper-class

entries.definition_cn: 用糖或糖浆与黄油或牛奶熬制而成的硬糖
entries.definition_en: a hard confection made by boiling sugar or treacle with butter or milk
entries.example_cn: 她买了一盒太妃糖带回家给家人。
entries.example_en: She bought a box of toffee to take home for her family.

usage.label: countability
usage.pattern: Usually uncountable for the confection; countable for an individual piece.

entries.definition_en: snobbish and pretentiously superior in attitude
entries.example_cn: 这位势利的评论家贬低这位流行艺术家的作品。
entries.example_en: The toffee-nosed critic dismissed the popular artist's work as inferior.

entries.definition_en: a soft food made from curdled soybean milk
entries.example_cn: 豆腐是许多亚洲菜肴中的流行食材。
entries.example_en: Tofu is a popular ingredient in many Asian dishes.

entries.definition_cn: 字符无法显示时出现的方框或矩形，有时其中带有问号或十六进制代码（也称“豆腐块”）
entries.definition_en: a box or rectangle displayed when a character cannot be rendered, sometimes containing a question mark or hexadecimal code
entries.example_cn: 这个不受支持的字符显示成了一个豆腐块。
entries.example_en: The unsupported character appeared as a tofu box.

entries.definition_en: provide with clothes or put clothes on
entries.example_cn: 请在带婴儿到外面去之前给他穿上衣服。
entries.example_en: Please tog the baby before taking him outside in the cold.

usage.label: transitive
usage.pattern: tog someone; tog someone up or out

entries.definition_en: a one-piece cloak worn by men in ancient Rome
entries.example_cn: 这座雕像描绘了一位身穿白色长袍的罗马参议员。
entries.example_en: The statue depicts a Roman senator wearing a white toga.

entries.definition_en: in each other's company
entries.example_cn: 他们共度了周末。
entries.example_en: They spent the weekend together.

entries.definition_en: with cooperation and interchange
entries.example_cn: 我们合作完成了任务。
entries.example_en: We worked together to finish the task.

entries.definition_en: assembled in one place
entries.example_cn: 大家都聚集在大厅里。
entries.example_en: Everyone gathered together in the hall.

entries.definition_en: with a common plan
entries.example_cn: 他们朝着目标一致努力。
entries.example_en: They moved together towards the goal.

entries.definition_en: at the same time
entries.example_cn: 演讲结束时，观众同时鼓掌。
entries.example_en: The audience clapped together when the speaker finished.

entries.definition_en: mentally and emotionally stable
entries.example_cn: 她精神足够健全，能应对压力。
entries.example_en: She is together enough to handle the stress.

entries.definition_en: in contact with each other
entries.example_cn: 这两座城市相距很近。
entries.example_en: The two cities are close together.

entries.definition_cn: 在一起；团结一致的状态
entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being together
entries.example_cn: 家庭聚会象征着他们的亲密无间。
entries.example_en: The family reunion was a symbol of their togetherness.

entries.definition_en: a switch with two positions
entries.example_cn: 他拨动开关打开了灯。
entries.example_en: He flipped the toggle to turn on the light.

entries.definition_en: a command that switches a setting on and off
entries.example_cn: 使用切换指令来调节屏幕亮度。
entries.example_en: Use the toggle to switch the screen brightness.

entries.definition_en: a pin or crosspiece used to fasten ropes or chains
entries.example_cn: 水手用一个系索扣将绳子系在桅杆上。
entries.example_en: The sailor used a toggle to tie the rope to the mast.

entries.definition_cn: 用开关或操纵杆在两种状态间切换
entries.definition_en: to switch between two states using a switch or lever
entries.example_cn: 机器用开关释放了闩锁以打开门。
entries.example_en: The machine toggled the latch to open the door.

entries.definition_en: to fasten something using a toggle
entries.example_cn: 她用搭扣系紧了背带以固定包。
entries.example_en: She toggled the strap to secure the bag.

entries.definition_en: to provide something with a toggle or toggles
entries.example_cn: 裁缝在外套领口装上一个木制搭扣。
entries.example_en: The tailor toggled the coat at the neck with a wooden peg.

entries.definition_en: informal term for clothing or attire
entries.example_cn: 孩子们穿着旧衣服在玩耍。
entries.example_en: The children were playing in their old togs.

entries.definition_en: work hard
entries.example_cn: 他们辛苦工作了一整天以完成建设项目。
entries.example_en: They toiled all day to finish the construction project.

entries.definition_cn: 艰苦或令人疲惫的劳动，尤指需要体力的劳动
entries.definition_en: hard or exhausting work, especially work requiring physical effort
entries.example_cn: 矿工们在黑暗的隧道里忍受了长时间的艰苦劳动。
entries.example_en: The miners endured long hours of toil in the dark tunnels.

entries.definition_en: a person who works very hard and for a long time
entries.example_cn: 工厂的工人们要求改善工作条件和提高工资。
entries.example_en: The factory toilers demanded better working conditions and higher wages.

entries.definition_en: a plumbing fixture for defecation and urination
entries.example_cn: 公共厕所里的马桶坏了。
entries.example_en: The toilet in the public restroom was broken.

entries.definition_en: a room or building equipped with one or more toilets
entries.example_cn: 进入厕所前请敲门。
entries.example_en: Please knock before entering the toilet.

entries.definition_en: the act of dressing and preparing yourself
entries.example_cn: 聚会前她花了一个小时梳妆打扮。
entries.example_en: She spent an hour at her toilet before the party.

entries.definition_en: a complete failure or disaster
entries.example_cn: 由于计划不周，这个项目彻底失败了。
entries.example_en: The project was a total toilet due to poor planning.

entries.definition_en: to teach a young child to use the toilet independently
entries.example_cn: 花了好几个月才给我们的幼儿进行了如厕训练。
entries.example_en: It took several months to toilet-train our toddler.

entries.definition_en: (of children) trained to use the toilet
entries.example_cn: 父母很高兴他们的小宝宝终于学会如厕了。
entries.example_en: The parents were proud that their toddler was finally toilet-trained.

entries.definition_en: items used for personal hygiene and washing
entries.example_cn: 她把洗发水和牙膏装进了洗漱用品包里。
entries.example_en: She packed her toiletry bag with shampoo and toothpaste.

entries.definition_en: working hard or engaged in hard, tiring work
entries.example_cn: 这些辛勤劳作的工人终于完成了这项繁重的建筑工程。
entries.example_en: The toiling workers finally finished the heavy construction project.

entries.definition_en: requiring great effort and causing exhaustion, especially through physical labor
entries.example_cn: 攀登这座山的费力过程整整花了一天。
entries.example_en: The toilsome climb up the mountain took all day.

entries.definition_en: a large, doughnut-shaped device used in scientific research to contain hot plasma for nuclear fusion
entries.example_cn: 科学家们正在努力提高托卡马克装置的效率，以实现可持续的核聚变能源。
entries.example_en: Scientists are working to improve the efficiency of the tokamak to achieve sustainable fusion energy.

entries.definition_en: a puff of a marijuana or hashish cigarette
entries.example_cn: 他从那根大麻烟卷上吸了一口，然后向后靠去。
entries.example_en: He took a toke from the joint and leaned back.

entries.definition_cn: 某种符号的一个具体实例
entries.definition_en: an individual instance of a type of symbol
entries.example_cn: 句子中的每个词元代表一个特定的单词。
entries.example_en: Each token in the sentence represents a specific word.

entries.definition_cn: 作为其他事物标志的东西
entries.definition_en: something serving as a sign of something else
entries.example_cn: 这枚勋章是他勇敢的象征。
entries.example_en: The medal was a token of his bravery.

entries.definition_cn: 可代替货币或用于操作机器的金属或塑料圆片
entries.definition_en: a metal or plastic disk used as a substitute for money or to operate a machine
entries.example_cn: 他把一枚代币插入老虎机开始游戏。
entries.example_en: He inserted a token into the slot machine to start playing.

entries.definition_en: something of sentimental value
entries.example_cn: 她保留那张旧照片作为他们友谊的纪念。
entries.example_en: She kept the old photo as a token of their friendship.

entries.definition_cn: 象征性的；敷衍的；仅为形式而作的
entries.definition_en: insignificantly small; a matter of form only
entries.example_cn: 公司的举动只是象征性地帮助社区。
entries.example_en: The company's gesture was merely a token effort to help the community.

entries.definition_en: to say something to someone
entries.example_cn: 她告诉我一个秘密。
entries.example_en: She told me a secret.

entries.definition_en: to make it known that something is true
entries.example_cn: 她把这个消息告诉了大家。
entries.example_en: She told everyone the news.

entries.definition_en: to give a detailed story or account
entries.example_cn: 他讲述了自己童年的故事。
entries.example_en: He told the story of his childhood.

entries.definition_en: to give orders to someone
entries.example_cn: 将军命令士兵前进。
entries.example_en: The general told his soldiers to advance.

entries.definition_en: to realize or understand something, especially through observation
entries.example_cn: 我看得出他错了。
entries.example_en: I could tell that he was wrong.

entries.definition_en: to inform someone with certainty
entries.example_cn: 我确告过你会下雨。
entries.example_en: I told you that it would rain.

entries.definition_en: to provide evidence or testimony
entries.example_cn: 证人向法庭陈述了他所看到的情况。
entries.example_en: The witness told the court what he saw.

entries.definition_en: to distinguish or mark as different
entries.example_cn: 老师区分了好的答案和坏的答案。
entries.example_en: The teacher told the good answers from the bad ones.

entries.definition_cn: 表面有漆或珐琅并经彩绘或鎏金的装饰性金属器皿
entries.definition_en: enameled or lacquered metalware (usually gilded and elaborately painted); popular in the 18th century
entries.example_cn: 她在架子上展示了一组古董彩绘金属器皿。
entries.example_en: She displayed a collection of antique tole ware on the shelf.

entries.definition_en: capable of being borne or endured
entries.example_cn: 噪音虽然不悦耳，但尚可忍受。
entries.example_en: The noise was tolerable, though not pleasant.

entries.definition_en: about average; acceptable
entries.example_cn: 夏天的天气过得去，适合度假。
entries.example_en: The weather was tolerable for a summer holiday.

entries.definition_en: in a way that is acceptable but not excellent
entries.example_cn: 食物尚可，虽然并不美味。
entries.example_en: The food was tolerably good, though not delicious.

entries.definition_en: a willingness to allow freedom of choice and behavior
entries.example_cn: 她对不同的观点非常宽容。
entries.example_en: She has a high tolerance for different opinions.

entries.definition_en: willingness to respect the beliefs or practices of others
entries.example_cn: 在多元社会中，宗教容忍很重要。
entries.example_en: Religious tolerance is important in a diverse society.

entries.definition_en: the act of putting up with something unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 我无法忍受粗鲁的行为。
entries.example_en: I have no tolerance for rude behavior.

entries.definition_en: the ability of an organism to endure a substance, disease, or other unfavorable condition
entries.example_cn: 这株植物表现出很强的耐旱性。
entries.example_en: The plant shows great tolerance to drought.

entries.definition_en: a permissible difference or margin of error
entries.example_cn: 机器零件必须在 0.1 毫米的公差范围内。
entries.example_en: The machine parts must be within a tolerance of 0.1 millimeters.

entries.definition_en: showing respect for the rights, opinions, or practices of others
entries.example_cn: 一个宽容的社会接受来自不同文化的人。
entries.example_en: A tolerant society accepts people from different cultures.

entries.definition_en: able to remain calm and forgiving even when provoked
entries.example_cn: 尽管她很生气，但她对他粗鲁的行为表现得宽宏大量。
entries.example_en: She was tolerant of his rude behavior despite being angry.

entries.definition_en: showing or characterized by broad-mindedness
entries.example_cn: 这所大学对不同的政治观点持开明的态度。
entries.example_en: The university has a tolerant attitude toward diverse political views.

entries.definition_en: able to withstand environmental conditions or physiological stress
entries.example_cn: 这种植物耐旱且耐贫瘠土壤。
entries.example_en: This plant is tolerant of drought and poor soil.

entries.definition_en: showing the capacity for endurance
entries.example_cn: 这位跑者展现了惊人的耐力，尽管疼痛难忍，他还是完成了马拉松。
entries.example_en: The runner showed a tolerant spirit by finishing the marathon despite the pain.

entries.definition_en: in a way that shows tolerance
entries.example_cn: 委员会宽容地讨论了这个问题。
entries.example_en: The committee discussed the issue tolerantly.

entries.definition_cn: 忍受；容忍令人不快的事物
entries.definition_en: to endure or put up with something unpleasant
entries.example_cn: 我无法忍受办公室里的持续噪音。
entries.example_en: I cannot tolerate the constant noise in the office.

entries.definition_cn: 容忍（他人的权利和信仰）
entries.definition_en: to accept and respect the rights and beliefs of others
entries.example_cn: 我们必须学会容忍不同的文化和宗教。
entries.example_en: We must learn to tolerate different cultures and religions.

entries.definition_cn: 允许（某事存在或发生）而不反对
entries.definition_en: to allow something to be present or happen without opposing it
entries.example_cn: 学校允许在课间使用手机。
entries.example_en: The school tolerates the use of mobile phones during breaks.

entries.definition_cn: 对（毒药、药物或疾病）有耐受性
entries.definition_en: to be able to withstand a poison, drug, or disease without being harmed
entries.example_cn: 这位患者对青霉素的耐受性不好。
entries.example_en: The patient does not tolerate penicillin well.

entries.definition_en: the willingness to accept people or situations that are different from your own
entries.example_cn: 公司的容忍政策允许员工随意着装。
entries.example_en: The company's policy of toleration allows employees to dress as they wish.

entries.definition_en: official permission for people to hold beliefs different from the majority
entries.example_cn: 新法律保障所有公民的宗教宽容权。
entries.example_en: The new law guarantees religious toleration for all citizens.

entries.definition_en: a fee paid for the use of a road, bridge, or tunnel
entries.example_cn: 司机必须付过桥费才能通过大桥。
entries.example_en: The driver had to pay a toll to cross the bridge.

entries.definition_en: loss or damage incurred through a disaster or other serious event
entries.example_cn: 这场胜利付出了惨重的人员代价。
entries.example_en: The victory came at a high toll in lives.

entries.definition_en: the sound produced by a bell being struck
entries.example_cn: 我们从山谷里听到了教堂的钟声。
entries.example_en: We heard the toll of the church bell from the valley.

entries.definition_en: to ring slowly and heavily
entries.example_cn: 钟声在午夜缓慢而沉重地敲响。
entries.example_en: The bell tolled at midnight.

entries.definition_en: to charge a fee for the use of something
entries.example_cn: 该市开始对主要道路收费。
entries.example_en: The city began to toll its main roads.

entries.definition_cn: 免费的；（电话）免收通话费的
entries.definition_en: free of toll charges, especially for a telephone call or service
entries.example_cn: 我们拨打了公司的免费电话寻求帮助。
entries.example_en: We called the company on a toll-free number to ask for help.

entries.definition_en: a booth at a tollgate where the toll collector collects tolls
entries.example_cn: 司机在收费站停下缴费。
entries.example_en: The driver stopped at the tollbooth to pay the fee.

entries.definition_en: someone employed to collect tolls
entries.example_cn: 收税人向每辆过桥的车辆收取费用。
entries.example_en: The toller collected fees from every vehicle crossing the bridge.

entries.definition_en: a person who rings church bells
entries.example_cn: 那位老敲钟人敲响钟声召集会众。
entries.example_en: The old toller rang the bells to summon the congregation.

entries.definition_en: a gate or bar across a toll bridge or toll road that is lifted when the toll is paid
entries.example_cn: 司机在通过桥梁前停在收费站闸门处缴纳费用。
entries.example_en: The driver stopped at the tollgate to pay the fee before crossing the bridge.

entries.definition_en: a building at a toll road where tolls are collected
entries.example_cn: 那座旧收费站房立在路边，现已改造成一家小咖啡馆。
entries.example_en: The old tollhouse stood by the roadside, now converted into a small cafe.

entries.definition_cn: 收费员；收费站工作人员
entries.definition_en: a person employed to collect tolls.
entries.example_cn: 收费员收取费用后，挥手让卡车通过大门。
entries.example_en: The tollman waved the truck through the gate after collecting the fee.

entries.definition_en: a yellowish brown aromatic balsam used in cough syrups
entries.example_cn: 药剂师在混合物中加入了一滴托卢香脂。
entries.example_en: The pharmacist added a drop of tolu to the mixture.

entries.definition_en: a colorless flammable liquid used as a solvent or in fuels
entries.example_cn: 甲苯常用作工业溶剂。
entries.example_en: Toluene is commonly used as a solvent in industrial applications.

entries.definition_en: any of various drums with small heads
entries.example_cn: 鼓手在节奏部分演奏了小鼓。
entries.example_en: The drummer played the tom-tom during the rhythm section.

entries.definition_en: a fighting ax used by North American Indians
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一把古老的战斧。
entries.example_en: The museum displays an old tomahawk.

entries.definition_en: to cut with a tomahawk
entries.example_cn: 战士用战斧砍碎了敌人的盾牌。
entries.example_en: The warrior tomahawked the enemy's shield.

entries.definition_en: to kill with a tomahawk
entries.example_cn: 在故事中，英雄用战斧杀死了反派。
entries.example_en: In the story, the hero tomahawked the villain.

entries.definition_cn: 一种被薄薄纸质外皮包裹的绿色至绿紫色小果实，类似番茄
entries.definition_en: a small green to green-purple fruit enclosed in a thin papery husk, resembling a tomato
entries.example_cn: 她在食用前剥去了墨西哥酸浆的外皮。
entries.example_en: She peeled the husk off the tomatillo before eating it.

entries.definition_en: a small edible fruit native to Mexico, resembling a small tomato and often used in cooking
entries.example_cn: 厨师在绿莎莎酱中加入了新鲜的墨西哥浆果。
entries.example_en: The chef added fresh tomatillo to the salsa verde.

entries.definition_cn: 产自墨西哥和美国南部、结出类似小番茄的绿色至紫色可食果实的植物
entries.definition_en: a plant from Mexico and the southern United States that produces edible green to purplish fruit resembling small tomatoes
entries.example_cn: 美国南部的园丁种植墨西哥酸浆，以获取其可食用的果实。
entries.example_en: Gardeners in the South grow tomatillos for their edible fruit.

entries.definition_en: a red or yellow fruit eaten as a vegetable
entries.example_cn: 我们在汤里加了新鲜的番茄。
entries.example_en: We added fresh tomatoes to the soup.

entries.definition_cn: 原产于南美洲、广泛栽培且有许多品种的番茄植株
entries.definition_en: the tomato plant, native to South America and widely cultivated in many varieties
entries.example_cn: 番茄植株原产于南美洲。
entries.example_en: The tomato plant is native to South America.

entries.definition_cn: 安放尸体的建筑物或墓室，通常部分或全部位于地下
entries.definition_en: a structure or chamber for a dead body, often partly or wholly underground
entries.example_cn: 这座古老的坟墓被发现埋在沙漠沙土之下。
entries.example_en: The ancient tomb was discovered buried beneath the desert sand.

entries.definition_en: a lottery where tickets are drawn from a rotating drum to win prizes
entries.example_cn: 学校通过在年底举办抽奖游戏筹集了资金。
entries.example_en: The school raised money by holding a tombola at the end of the year.

entries.definition_cn: 抽取彩票的旋转抽奖桶
entries.definition_en: the revolving drum from which lottery tickets are drawn
entries.example_cn: 组织者转动抽奖桶后抽出了中奖彩票。
entries.example_en: The organizer turned the tombola before drawing the winning ticket.

entries.definition_en: a girl who behaves in a boyish manner
entries.example_cn: 她是个假小子，更喜欢爬树而不是玩洋娃娃。
entries.example_en: She was a tomboy who preferred climbing trees to playing with dolls.

entries.definition_cn: 假小子般的；有男孩子气的
entries.definition_en: characterized by behavior conventionally associated with a tomboy
entries.example_cn: 她有假小子般的性格，喜欢爬树。
entries.example_en: She has a tomboyish personality and loves climbing trees.

entries.definition_en: a stone placed on a grave to mark it and usually bear the name of the deceased
entries.example_cn: 那座古老的墓碑长满了青苔，很难辨认。
entries.example_en: The old tombstone was covered in moss and hard to read.

entries.definition_en: an adult male cat
entries.example_cn: 那只公猫在夜间在花园里游荡。
entries.example_en: The tomcat prowled around the garden at night.

entries.definition_en: a large book, especially one that is scholarly or academic
entries.example_cn: 图书馆里有许多关于古代历史的珍稀大部头书。
entries.example_en: The library contains many rare tomes on ancient history.

entries.definition_en: densely covered with short matted woolly hairs
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的毡状多毛茎部有助于保持水分。
entries.example_en: The tomentose stem of the plant helps it retain moisture.

entries.definition_cn: 被密集纠缠的丝状物覆盖的
entries.definition_en: covered with densely matted filaments
entries.example_cn: 叶子被密集纠缠的丝状物覆盖的背面摸起来很柔软。
entries.example_en: The tomentose underside of the leaf felt soft to the touch.

entries.definition_en: a covering of fine, hair-like fibers on a plant
entries.example_cn: 橡树的嫩叶上覆盖着一层柔软的柔毛。
entries.example_en: The young leaves of the oak tree were covered in a soft tomentum.

entries.definition_cn: 软脑膜与大脑皮层之间微小的血管网
entries.definition_en: a network of tiny blood vessels located between the pia mater and the cerebral cortex
entries.example_cn: 大脑中的血管网在营养交换中起着至关重要的作用。
entries.example_en: The tomentum in the brain plays a crucial role in nutrient exchange.

entries.definition_en: foolish or senseless behavior
entries.example_cn: 孩子们沉迷于胡闹而不是学习。
entries.example_en: The children were caught up in tomfoolery instead of studying.

entries.definition_cn: 通过断层成像产生、表示三维物体某一切面的二维图像
entries.definition_en: a two-dimensional image produced by tomography, representing a slice through a three-dimensional object
entries.example_cn: 医生要求做断层扫描图以检查膝盖的内部结构。
entries.example_en: The doctor ordered a tomogram to examine the internal structure of the knee.

entries.definition_en: a machine that uses X-rays to create detailed images of a specific plane within an object
entries.example_cn: 技术人员使用断层扫描仪为患者的大脑成像。
entries.example_en: The technician used a tomograph to image a single plane of the patient's brain.

entries.definition_en: a medical technique that produces images of the inside of the body
entries.example_cn: 医生要求进行断层扫描以检查大脑。
entries.example_en: The doctor ordered a tomography scan to examine the brain.

entries.definition_en: the day after today
entries.example_cn: 明天将是晴天。
entries.example_en: Tomorrow will be sunny.

entries.definition_en: the near future
entries.example_cn: 我们期待不久的将来。
entries.example_en: We are looking forward to tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: the next day, the day after, following the present day
entries.example_cn: 我明天见你。
entries.example_en: I will see you tomorrow.

entries.definition_en: a plug for the muzzle of a gun to keep out dust and moisture
entries.example_cn: 猎人将防尘塞插入步枪枪口后将其存放起来。
entries.example_en: The hunter inserted a tompion into the muzzle of his rifle before storing it.

entries.definition_en: a United States unit of weight equivalent to 2000 pounds
entries.example_cn: 这辆卡车可以运载一吨货物。
entries.example_en: The truck can carry a ton of cargo.

entries.definition_en: a British unit of weight equivalent to 2240 pounds
entries.example_cn: 那艘旧船重好几吨。
entries.example_en: The old ship weighed several tons.

entries.definition_en: organized around a main note or key tone, involving tones and chords
entries.example_cn: 作曲家创作了一部以单一主音为中心的调性交响曲。
entries.example_en: The composer wrote a tonal symphony that centered on a single keynote.

entries.definition_en: using changes in pitch to tell apart words that sound similar
entries.example_cn: 这种语言的辨义性质使得非母语者难以区分单词。
entries.example_en: The tonal nature of the language makes it difficult for non-native speakers to distinguish words.

entries.definition_cn: 调性；音乐作品中音高的体系及其关系，尤其是大小调
entries.definition_en: the system and relationships of pitches in a piece of music, especially its major or minor key
entries.example_cn: 作曲家为交响曲选择了特定的调性。
entries.example_en: The composer chose a specific tonality for the symphony.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that relates to or concerns the tone of voice or sound
entries.example_cn: 尽管措辞礼貌，但发言者的评论在语调上具有攻击性。
entries.example_en: The speaker's comments were tonally aggressive, even though the words were polite.

entries.definition_en: the quality of a person's voice
entries.example_cn: 她用温柔的嗓音说话。
entries.example_en: She spoke in a gentle tone.

entries.definition_en: the general atmosphere of a place or situation and the effect that it has on people
entries.example_cn: 会议的基调非常严肃。
entries.example_en: The tone of the meeting was very serious.

entries.definition_en: (music) the distinctive property of a complex sound (a voice or noise or musical sound)
entries.example_cn: 小提琴的音色温暖。
entries.example_en: The violin has a warm tone.

entries.definition_en: (linguistics) a pitch or change in pitch of the voice that serves to distinguish words in tonal languages
entries.example_cn: 在中文中，词的声调可以改变其含义。
entries.example_en: In Chinese, the tone of a word can change its meaning.

entries.definition_cn: 使说话带有某种语调或口吻
entries.definition_en: to give one’s speech a particular tone or manner
entries.example_cn: 她调整语调，使声音听起来更令人安心。
entries.example_en: She toned her voice to sound more reassuring.

entries.definition_en: change the color or tone of
entries.example_cn: 艺术家调整了画作的色调，使颜色变暗。
entries.example_en: The artist toned the painting to make the colors darker.

entries.definition_en: to utter something in an affected tone
entries.example_cn: 他用矫揉造作、嘲弄的声音说出了这些话。
entries.example_en: He toned the words in an affected, mocking voice.

entries.definition_en: change to a color image
entries.example_cn: 扫描仪可以将黑白照片转成彩色。
entries.example_en: The scanner can tone black and white photos to color.

entries.definition_cn: 听不出音高的；（非正式）缺乏音乐鉴赏力的
entries.definition_en: unable to distinguish musical pitch or, informally, to appreciate music
entries.example_cn: 他不懂音乐，无法分辨歌曲是否走调。
entries.example_en: He is tone-deaf and cannot tell if a song is in tune.

entries.definition_en: having a specific tone or quality of tone
entries.example_cn: 说话者的声音平静而沉稳。
entries.example_en: The speaker's voice was calm and toned.

entries.definition_cn: 身材健美的；肌肉紧实的
entries.definition_en: physically fit, with defined and firm muscles
entries.example_cn: 她通过定期锻炼保持了健美、紧实的体格。
entries.example_en: She maintained a toned physique through regular exercise.

entries.definition_en: lacking in tone or expression; dull and uninteresting
entries.example_cn: 她无表情的声音让人难以判断她是生气还是无聊。
entries.example_en: Her toneless voice made it difficult to tell if she was angry or bored.

entries.definition_en: a black or colored powder used in printers to create images
entries.example_cn: 当打印机用完墨粉时，你需要更换墨粉盒。
entries.example_en: You need to replace the toner cartridge when the printer runs out of powder.

entries.definition_en: a lotion used to cleanse the skin and tighten pores
entries.example_cn: 她洗脸后使用收敛水来收缩毛孔。
entries.example_en: She applies toner after washing her face to close her pores.

entries.definition_cn: 用于减少漂白或染色头发中不想要的黄色或橙色调的护发产品
entries.definition_en: a hair product used to reduce unwanted yellow or orange tones in bleached or dyed hair
entries.example_cn: 她使用护发调色剂去除漂白头发中的黄色调。
entries.example_en: She used a toner to remove the yellow tones from her bleached hair.

entries.definition_cn: 用于改变照片色调的化学溶液
entries.definition_en: a liquid solution with chemicals used to change the color of a photograph
entries.example_cn: 摄影师混合调色液，使照片呈现棕褐色调。
entries.example_en: The photographer mixed the toner to give the print a sepia tone.

entries.definition_en: a tool with two hinged arms used to grasp and lift objects
entries.example_cn: 厨师用钳子将热蔬菜夹到盘子里。
entries.example_en: The chef used tongs to place the hot vegetables on the plate.

entries.definition_en: the muscular organ inside the mouth used for tasting and helping to speak
entries.example_cn: 他伸出舌头表示他在开玩笑。
entries.example_en: He stuck out his tongue to show he was joking.

entries.definition_en: a system of communication used by a community, such as English or Mandarin
entries.example_cn: 英语是世界上使用最广泛的语言。
entries.example_en: English is the most widely spoken tongue in the world.

entries.definition_en: a particular way of speaking or expressing oneself
entries.example_cn: 他说话尖刻，经常给自己惹麻烦。
entries.example_en: His sharp tongue often got him into trouble.

entries.definition_en: the tongue of an animal that is eaten as food
entries.example_cn: 牛舌在许多文化中是一道受欢迎的佳肴。
entries.example_en: Beef tongue is a popular delicacy in many cultures.

entries.definition_en: a long, thin projection that appears temporarily
entries.example_cn: 一团火舌从着火的建筑物中窜出。
entries.example_en: A tongue of fire shot up from the burning building.

entries.definition_en: to articulate sounds by shaping the tongue, as when playing a wind instrument
entries.example_cn: 音乐家用舌头吹奏音符，使声音清脆。
entries.example_en: The musician tongued the notes to make them sound crisp.

entries.definition_en: a narrow strip of land that extends into the sea
entries.example_cn: 灯塔矗立在一块伸入海中的岩石陆地上。
entries.example_en: The lighthouse stood on a rocky tongue of land.

entries.definition_en: to lick or explore something with the tongue
entries.example_cn: 狗开始用舌头舔水碗。
entries.example_en: The dog began to tongue the water bowl.

entries.definition_en: amusing or ironic, and not meant seriously
entries.example_cn: 他对天气发表了一句调侃的评论。
entries.example_en: He made a tongue-in-cheek comment about the weather.

entries.definition_en: in a joking or bantering manner
entries.example_cn: 她调侃地回答了这个问题。
entries.example_en: She answered the question tongue-in-cheek.

entries.definition_cn: 不严肃地；带讽刺意味地
entries.definition_en: without being serious
entries.example_cn: 这篇文章是以非正式的方式写成的，旨在讽刺当时的情况。
entries.example_en: The article was written tongue-in-cheek to mock the situation.

usage.label: ironic
usage.pattern: used to describe an ironic portrayal or statement

entries.definition_en: a very harsh and angry criticism or scolding
entries.example_cn: 老师因作弊严厉地斥责了那名学生。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave the student a severe tongue-lashing for cheating.

entries.definition_cn: 使某人紧张得说不清话来
entries.definition_en: to disconcert or fluster someone so that they cannot speak coherently
entries.example_cn: 这个突如其来的问题使发言者紧张得说不清话来。
entries.example_en: The unexpected question tongue-tied the speaker.

entries.definition_cn: （因紧张等）张口结舌的；一时语塞的
entries.definition_en: unable to speak clearly or fluently
entries.example_cn: 当我遇见那位著名作家时，我紧张得说不出话来。
entries.example_en: I was tongue-tied when I met the famous author.

entries.definition_en: having a tongue or resembling a tongue
entries.example_cn: 这只青蛙舌头很长。
entries.example_en: The frog is long-tongued.

entries.definition_cn: 具有某种说话方式的；（常用于复合词）
entries.definition_en: having a specified manner of speaking, as in sharp-tongued or silver-tongued
entries.example_cn: 他是个说话尖刻的男孩。
entries.example_en: He's a sharp-tongued boy.

entries.definition_en: lacking a tongue
entries.example_cn: 这种无舌的鱼通过皮肤进行独特的呼吸。
entries.example_en: The tongueless fish has a unique way of breathing through its skin.

entries.definition_en: expressed without speech
entries.example_cn: 她无言地道歉，只是点了点头。
entries.example_en: She offered a tongueless apology, only nodding her head.

entries.definition_cn: 含奎宁的柠檬或青柠味碳酸水
entries.definition_en: carbonated water flavored with lime or lemon and containing quinine
entries.example_cn: 他点了一杯加冰的奎宁水。
entries.example_en: He ordered a glass of tonic with ice.

entries.definition_en: a medicine that strengthens and invigorates the body
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种滋补品来增强他的精力。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a tonic to boost his energy.

entries.definition_en: the first note of a diatonic scale in music
entries.example_cn: 主音是音阶的中心音。
entries.example_en: The tonic is the central note of the scale.

entries.definition_cn: 含碳酸水和调味料的甜饮料
entries.definition_en: a sweet drink made with carbonated water and flavoring
entries.example_cn: 她喝了一杯汽水提神。
entries.example_en: She drank a tonic to refresh herself.

entries.definition_en: relating to or producing normal tone or tension in muscles or tissue
entries.example_cn: 患者腿部出现强直性痉挛。
entries.example_en: The patient suffered from tonic spasms in the leg.

entries.definition_en: relating to or being the keynote of a major or minor scale
entries.example_cn: 主和弦决定了乐曲的调性。
entries.example_en: The tonic chord defines the key of the piece.

entries.definition_en: (used of syllables) bearing the principal stress, usually accompanied by a change in pitch
entries.example_cn: 在这个句子中，重读音节是'com'。
entries.example_en: In this sentence, the tonic syllable is 'com'.

entries.definition_en: using variations in pitch to distinguish meanings of similar words
entries.example_cn: 声调语言依靠音高变化来传达意义。
entries.example_en: Tonic languages rely on pitch changes to convey meaning.

entries.definition_cn: 溶液中非渗透性溶质对膜产生渗透压的能力；渗透张力
entries.definition_en: the ability of nonpenetrating solutes in a solution to exert osmotic pressure across a membrane
entries.example_cn: 溶液的渗透张力决定水分是进入细胞还是离开细胞。
entries.example_en: The tonicity of the solution determines whether water enters or leaves the cell.

entries.definition_cn: 肌肉或器官中正常存在的张力；肌张力
entries.definition_en: the normal state of tone or tension in a muscle or organ
entries.example_cn: 医生测试了患者的肌张力以评估神经损伤。
entries.example_en: The doctor tested the patient's muscle tonicity to assess nerve damage.

entries.definition_en: during the night of today
entries.example_cn: 我今晚给你打电话。
entries.example_en: I will call you tonight.

entries.definition_en: the night of the present day
entries.example_cn: 今晚就是我们一直等待的那个夜晚。
entries.example_en: Tonight is the night we've been waiting for.

entries.definition_en: a tax on ships based on their size
entries.example_cn: 船长必须缴纳高额吨税才能进入港口。
entries.example_en: The captain had to pay a heavy tonnage to enter the port.

entries.definition_en: a unit of weight equal to 1000 kilograms
entries.example_cn: 这辆卡车能载重十吨。
entries.example_en: The truck can carry a load of ten tonnes.

entries.definition_en: a device for measuring tension or pressure, especially intraocular pressure to test for glaucoma
entries.example_cn: 医生使用眼压计检查患者的眼内压。
entries.example_en: The doctor used a tonometer to check the patient's eye pressure.

entries.definition_en: the medical measurement of the pressure inside the eye
entries.example_cn: 医生进行了眼压测量以检查青光眼。
entries.example_en: The doctor performed tonometry to check for glaucoma.

entries.definition_en: a very large number or amount
entries.example_cn: 她精力充沛，足以帮助完成这个项目。
entries.example_en: She has tons of energy to help with the project.

entries.definition_en: either of two masses of lymphatic tissue one on each side of the oral pharynx
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了他感染后肿大的扁桃体。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined his swollen tonsil after the infection.

entries.definition_en: surgery to remove the tonsils
entries.example_cn: 医生建议做扁桃体切除术以防止反复感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor recommended a tonsillectomy to prevent recurrent infections.

entries.definition_en: inflammation of the tonsils, often causing sore throat and difficulty swallowing
entries.example_cn: 医生给孩子开了抗生素治疗扁桃体炎。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed antibiotics to treat the child's tonsillitis.

entries.definition_en: relating to barbers or the act of cutting hair
entries.example_cn: 这家店提供各种理发服务，从简单修剪到复杂造型。
entries.example_en: The shop offers a wide range of tonsorial services, from simple trims to complex styling.

entries.definition_cn: 僧侣或神职人员剃光的头顶
entries.definition_en: the shaved crown of a monk's or priest's head
entries.example_cn: 剃发是他宗教承诺的象征。
entries.example_en: The tonsure was a symbol of his religious commitment.

entries.definition_cn: 由神职人员或修道会成员剃去头顶的行为
entries.definition_en: shaving the crown of the head by priests or members of a monastic order
entries.example_cn: 古老的剃发仪式已实行数个世纪。
entries.example_en: The ancient ritual of tonsure has been practiced for centuries.

entries.definition_cn: 为某人剃去头顶的头发，作为谦卑和宗教使命的象征
entries.definition_en: to shave the crown of a person's head as a sign of humility and religious vocation
entries.example_cn: 院长明天早上将为这位新僧侣剃度。
entries.example_en: The abbot will tonsure the novice tomorrow morning.

entries.definition_en: a type of life insurance where the share of a participant who dies or defaults is given to the remaining members
entries.example_cn: 该年金互助会建立于17世纪，旨在为成员提供经济保障。
entries.example_en: The tontine was established in the 17th century to provide financial security for its members.

entries.definition_en: an annuity scheme where participants share benefits, and upon the death of any participant, their benefits are redistributed among the survivors
entries.example_cn: 投资者加入该年金再分配计划，希望随着其他成员的去世而获得更大的收益。
entries.example_en: Investors joined the tontine hoping to receive larger payouts as other members passed away.

entries.definition_en: the natural tension in muscles or arteries that helps the body respond to stimuli
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了病人的肌张力以评估肌肉健康状况。
entries.example_en: The doctor checked the patient's tonus to assess muscle health.

entries.definition_en: stylish, high-class, or upscale
entries.example_cn: 他们住在一个非常高档的街区。
entries.example_en: They live in a very tony neighborhood.

entries.definition_en: to an excessive degree
entries.example_cn: 噪音太吵了，无法入睡。
entries.example_en: The noise was too loud to sleep.

entries.definition_en: in addition
entries.example_cn: 我喜欢苹果，我弟弟也喜欢。
entries.example_en: I like apples, and my brother likes them too.

entries.definition_cn: 职业或贸易中使用的工具
entries.definition_en: an implement used in a job or trade
entries.example_cn: 锤子是木匠常用的工具。
entries.example_en: A hammer is a common tool for carpenters.

entries.definition_cn: 完成某事的途径或手段
entries.definition_en: the means by which an act is accomplished
entries.example_cn: 教育是改变的强大工具。
entries.example_en: Education is a powerful tool for change.

entries.definition_cn: 被他人控制去做不愉快任务的人
entries.definition_en: a person controlled by others to do unpleasant tasks
entries.example_cn: 他被老板当作工具使用。
entries.example_en: He was used as a tool by his boss.

entries.definition_en: to shape or work on something with a tool
entries.example_cn: 她用锤子和凿子加工皮革。
entries.example_en: She tooled the leather with a hammer and chisel.

entries.definition_en: to furnish with tools
entries.example_cn: 这个车间为新机器配备了工具。
entries.example_en: The workshop was tooled for the new machines.

entries.definition_cn: 漫无目的地开车兜风，只为取乐
entries.definition_en: to ride in a car without a specific goal, just for pleasure
entries.example_cn: 他们决定周日去乡下兜风。
entries.example_en: They decided to tool around the countryside on Sunday.

entries.definition_en: a vulgar term for the penis
entries.example_cn: tool 是指阴茎的粗俗俚语。
entries.example_en: “Tool” is a vulgar slang term for a penis.

entries.definition_cn: 驾驶客车或其他车辆（英国英语，过时，俚语）
entries.definition_en: to drive a coach or other vehicle (UK, dated, slang)
entries.example_cn: 司机把那辆旧客车开到了车站。
entries.example_en: The driver tooled the old coach to the station.

entries.definition_en: a box or chest for holding hand tools
entries.example_cn: 他把所有园艺工具都放在工具箱里。
entries.example_en: He kept all his gardening tools in the toolbox.

entries.definition_cn: 用于开发软件的一组可重复使用的程序
entries.definition_en: a set of reusable routines for developing software
entries.example_cn: 这个库为构建网络应用提供了一套实用的程序工具。
entries.example_en: The library provides a useful toolbox for building web applications.

entries.definition_cn: 在特定情况下有用的一套技能或能力
entries.definition_en: a set of skills or abilities useful in a particular situation
entries.example_cn: 良好的沟通能力是任何管理者技能储备中不可或缺的一项。
entries.example_en: Good communication is an essential tool in any manager's toolbox.

entries.definition_en: a person who is skilled at making or repairing tools
entries.example_cn: 这位古代的工具制造者用燧石打造了一把锋利的刀片。
entries.example_en: The ancient toolmaker crafted a sharp blade from flint.

entries.definition_en: a small building for storing tools
entries.example_cn: 他把所有的园艺设备都存放在工具棚里。
entries.example_en: He kept all his gardening equipment in the toolshed.

entries.definition_en: (informal) an animated cartoon, especially an animated television show
entries.example_cn: 孩子们喜欢看那部关于太空探险者的新动画片。
entries.example_en: The children loved watching the new toon about space explorers.

entries.definition_en: a short, loud sound made by a horn or whistle
entries.example_cn: 司机按响喇叭发出巨大的喇叭声以警告行人。
entries.example_en: The driver gave a loud toot on the horn to warn the pedestrians.

entries.definition_en: an informal spree of drinking; a drinking party
entries.example_cn: 学生们在当地酒吧以一场狂饮作乐的酒宴庆祝毕业。
entries.example_en: The students celebrated their graduation with a toot at the local bar.

entries.definition_en: to make the sound of a horn or whistle
entries.example_cn: 他经过学校时按响了汽车喇叭。
entries.example_en: He tooted the car horn as he passed the school.

entries.definition_en: a hard, bony structure in the jaws of vertebrates used for biting and chewing
entries.example_cn: 这只狗在啃骨头时掉了一颗牙齿。
entries.example_en: The dog lost a tooth while chewing on a bone.

entries.definition_en: something that resembles the tooth of an animal
entries.example_cn: 这把锯子有锋利的齿状物，专为切割木材设计。
entries.example_en: The saw has sharp teeth designed to cut wood.

entries.definition_en: one of the projections on a gear
entries.example_cn: 机器停转了，因为齿轮上的一个齿断了。
entries.example_en: The machine stopped because a tooth on the gear was broken.

entries.definition_cn: 无脊椎动物的齿状结构
entries.definition_en: a toothlike structure found in invertebrates
entries.example_cn: 一些软体动物有一个带有许多小齿状结构的硬壳。
entries.example_en: Some mollusks have a hard shell with many small teeth.

entries.definition_cn: 执行规则或施加惩罚的力量或手段
entries.definition_en: the power or means to enforce a rule or punishment
entries.example_cn: 新规赋予该机构足够的强制力来惩罚严重违规行为。
entries.example_en: The new regulations give the agency enough teeth to punish serious violations.

entries.definition_en: pain in a tooth or the area around it
entries.example_cn: 我牙疼得厉害，需要去看牙医。
entries.example_en: I have a terrible toothache and need to see a dentist.

entries.definition_en: a small brush with a long handle used for cleaning teeth
entries.example_cn: 他忘记把牙刷带到旅行了。
entries.example_en: He forgot to bring his toothbrush on the trip.

entries.definition_en: slang term for a mustache
entries.example_cn: 那位老人留着浓密的胡子。
entries.example_en: The old man had a thick toothbrush.

entries.definition_en: having teeth, especially of a certain number or type; often used in combination
entries.example_cn: 这条鱼有带齿的下颚。
entries.example_en: The fish has a toothed jaw.

entries.definition_cn: 有类似牙齿突起的，尤指边缘呈锯齿状的
entries.definition_en: having projections resembling teeth, especially in a sawlike edge
entries.example_cn: 这个齿轮有与小齿轮啮合的锯齿状边缘。
entries.example_en: The gear has a toothed edge that meshes with the smaller wheel.

entries.definition_cn: 边缘不规则地呈锯齿状，仿佛被啃咬过
entries.definition_en: having an irregularly notched or toothed margin as though gnawed
entries.example_cn: 狼在骨头上留下了带齿的痕迹。
entries.example_en: The wolf left a toothed mark on the bone.

entries.definition_en: having no teeth
entries.example_cn: 那只老狗嘴里没有牙齿。
entries.example_en: The old dog had a toothless mouth.

entries.definition_en: lacking necessary force for effectiveness
entries.example_cn: 这个无力的政府无法阻止抗议活动。
entries.example_en: The toothless government could not stop the protests.

entries.definition_en: a paste used for cleaning and polishing teeth
entries.example_cn: 睡前别忘了用牙膏刷牙。
entries.example_en: Don't forget to brush your teeth with toothpaste before bed.

entries.definition_en: a small strip of wood or plastic used to remove food from between teeth
entries.example_cn: 他用牙签剔除了卡在牙齿间的食物残渣。
entries.example_en: He used a toothpick to clean the food stuck between his teeth.

entries.definition_en: acceptable or pleasant to the taste or mind
entries.example_cn: 这汤可口的味道让每个人都感到开心。
entries.example_en: The toothsome flavor of the soup made everyone happy.

entries.definition_en: pleasantly firm or chewy when bitten
entries.example_cn: 她享用了聚会上供应的、咬起来很有嚼劲的甜点。
entries.example_en: She enjoyed the toothsome, pleasantly chewy dessert served at the party.

entries.definition_en: having strong sexual appeal
entries.example_cn: 这位演员因在电影中的性感外表而闻名。
entries.example_en: The actor was known for his toothsome appearance in the film.

entries.definition_en: having or showing prominent teeth
entries.example_cn: 当看到零食时，那只狗露出了露齿的笑容。
entries.example_en: The dog gave a toothy grin when it saw the treat.

entries.definition_en: to play a musical instrument in a casual or playful manner
entries.example_cn: 她喜欢在公园里散步时随意吹奏口琴。
entries.example_en: She likes to tootle on the harmonica while walking in the park.

usage.label: 及物/不及物；非正式
usage.pattern: To play an instrument or make a soft toot.

entries.definition_cn: 随意演奏乐器发出的声音
entries.definition_en: the sound made by playing a musical instrument in a casual or playful way
entries.example_cn: 音乐会开始前，他对着长笛吹了几个随意的音符。
entries.example_en: He gave a quick tootle on the flute before the concert began.

entries.definition_en: the upper part of something.
entries.example_cn: 把盖子放在罐子的上部。
entries.example_en: Put the lid on the top of the jar.

entries.definition_en: the upper surface of something
