entries.example_cn: 桌子的顶面上放着一个花瓶。
entries.example_en: A vase stood on the top of the table.

entries.definition_en: the highest point of a mountain.
entries.example_cn: 我们爬到了山顶。
entries.example_en: We climbed to the top of the hill.

entries.definition_en: being at the highest position.
entries.example_cn: 她住在大楼的顶层。
entries.example_en: She lives in the top floor of the building.

entries.definition_en: to reach the highest rank or position
entries.example_cn: 这首歌上周登上了排行榜榜首。
entries.example_en: This song topped the charts last week.

entries.definition_en: to be better than something else.
entries.example_cn: 我们队今年在联赛中领先。
entries.example_en: Our team topped the league this year.

entries.definition_en: to exceed in height; rise above
entries.example_cn: 这座塔比周围所有建筑都高。
entries.example_en: The tower tops all the surrounding buildings.

entries.definition_en: the first half of a baseball inning.
entries.example_cn: 球队在上半局得了三分。
entries.example_en: The team scored three runs in the top.

entries.definition_en: starting with the highest level of a system and working down to details
entries.example_cn: 该公司采用自上而下的方法重组了其部门。
entries.example_en: The company used a top-down approach to reorganize its departments.

entries.definition_cn: 顶级的；（体育运动中）顶级联赛的
entries.definition_en: of the highest rank or quality; in sports, belonging to the highest division
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店为所有客人提供一流的服务。
entries.example_en: The hotel offers top-flight service to all its guests.

entries.definition_en: surpassing in quality
entries.example_cn: 餐厅提供了一块质量卓越的牛排。
entries.example_en: They served a top-grade steak at the restaurant.

entries.definition_cn: 管理人员过多的；管理层过于庞大的
entries.definition_en: having too many administrators or managers
entries.example_cn: 这家公司管理层过于庞大，经理太多，而真正做事的员工却不够。
entries.example_en: The company is top-heavy, with too many managers and not enough staff doing the actual work.

entries.definition_en: unstable because there is too much weight at the top
entries.example_cn: 那座高塔看起来头重脚轻，可能会倒塌。
entries.example_en: The tall tower looked top-heavy and might fall over.

entries.definition_en: excellent; best possible
entries.example_cn: 球队那场极好的表现使他们赢得了冠军。
entries.example_en: The team's top-hole performance earned them the championship.

entries.definition_en: Highest.
entries.example_cn: 最高层管理人员决定改变政策。
entries.example_en: The top-level executives decided to change the policy.

entries.definition_en: Best.
entries.example_cn: 这是我们提供的最高品质的产品。
entries.example_en: This is a top-level product from our company.

entries.definition_en: Applied to domains at the highest level, such as .uk covering all sites for the United Kingdom.
entries.example_cn: .com 顶级域名在全球范围内用于商业网站。
entries.example_en: The .com top-level domain is used for commercial websites worldwide.

entries.definition_cn: 读 - 求值 - 打印循环
entries.definition_en: read-eval-print loop
entries.example_cn: 程序员使用读 - 求值 - 打印循环来测试该函数。
entries.example_en: The programmer used a top-level loop to test the function interactively.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅提供一流的服务和美味的食物。
entries.example_en: This restaurant offers top-notch service and delicious food.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality or best
entries.example_cn: 这款车是该系列中的顶级型号。
entries.example_en: This car is the top-of-the-line model in the series.

entries.definition_en: surpassing in quality
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店为所有客人提供顶级的服务。
entries.example_en: This hotel offers top-quality service to all its guests.

entries.definition_en: classified at the highest official level of secrecy
entries.example_cn: 绝密文件被保存在一个安全的保险库中。
entries.example_en: The top-secret documents were kept in a secure vault.

entries.definition_en: an amount of money or goods added to restore a level
entries.example_cn: 我需要在手机话费用完之前进行充值。
entries.example_en: I need to make a top-up to my phone credit before I run out.

usage.label: mobile-phone credit
usage.pattern: a top-up on a phone or data plan

entries.definition_cn: 一种铝氟硅酸盐矿物，通常因杂质而呈各种颜色，也用作宝石
entries.definition_en: a mineral (fluosilicate of aluminum) that occurs in crystals of various colors and is used as a gemstone
entries.example_cn: 她戴着一条镶嵌着璀璨蓝色托帕石的项链。
entries.example_en: She wore a necklace featuring a brilliant blue topaz.

entries.definition_en: a light brown the color of topaz
entries.example_cn: 她为夏季婚礼选择了一条托帕石色的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She chose a topaz-colored dress for the summer wedding.

entries.definition_en: a usually yellowish-brown gemstone made from topaz
entries.example_cn: 地质学家认出那块黄色的石头是一块黄石英。
entries.example_en: The geologist identified the yellow stone as a piece of topaz.

entries.definition_en: a heavy coat worn over other clothes in winter
entries.example_cn: 他穿上大衣，然后走出寒冷的风。
entries.example_en: He put on his topcoat before stepping out into the cold wind.

entries.definition_en: to drink alcohol excessively
entries.example_cn: 他可能每个周末都酗酒不停。
entries.example_en: He may tope every weekend without stopping.

entries.definition_en: a dome-shaped shrine built by Buddhists
entries.example_cn: 古老的佛塔矗立在寺庙的中心。
entries.example_en: The ancient tope stands tall in the center of the temple.

entries.definition_en: a person who drinks alcoholic beverages, especially to excess
entries.example_cn: 那个酗酒者被发现倒在街角。
entries.example_en: The toper was found passed out on the street corner.

usage.label: 文学用语
usage.pattern: A literary word for a heavy drinker

entries.definition_en: the section of a mast above the topmast and below the royal mast
entries.example_cn: 那艘旧船的顶桅杆在暴风雨中受损。
entries.example_en: The old ship's topgallant mast was damaged in the storm.

entries.definition_en: a sail set on a yard of a topgallant mast
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在强劲的风中升起顶桅帆。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to raise the topgallant in the fresh wind.

entries.definition_en: a lightweight hat worn in tropical countries to protect against the sun
entries.example_cn: 旅行者戴着一顶遮阳帽，以抵御强烈的热带阳光。
entries.example_en: The traveler wore a topi to shield his head from the intense tropical sun.

entries.definition_en: a large African antelope, Damaliscus korrigum
entries.example_cn: 狷羚是一种生活在非洲的大型羚羊。
entries.example_en: The topi is a large antelope found in Africa.

entries.definition_cn: 植物造型艺术；修剪造型技艺
entries.definition_en: the art of trimming shrubs or trees into decorative shapes
entries.example_cn: 公园里的绿篱修剪术每年春天都需要精心维护。
entries.example_en: The topiary in the park required careful maintenance every spring.

entries.definition_en: a garden where shrubs are trimmed into decorative shapes
entries.example_cn: 我们参观了一座美丽的植物造型花园，那里有修剪成狮子形状的树篱。
entries.example_en: We visited a beautiful topiary featuring hedges shaped like lions.

entries.definition_en: the subject matter of a conversation or discussion
entries.example_cn: 我们会议的主题是气候变化。
entries.example_en: The topic of our meeting was climate change.

entries.definition_en: some situation or event that is thought about
entries.example_cn: 辩论的议题是新税收政策。
entries.example_en: The topic of the debate was the new tax policy.

entries.definition_en: of interest at the present time
entries.example_cn: 辩论集中在影响当地社区的当前问题上。
entries.example_en: The debate focused on topical issues affecting the local community.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or arranged by topics
entries.example_cn: 图书馆将书籍按主题排列在一个区域，以便查阅。
entries.example_en: The library organized the books into a topical section for easy access.

entries.definition_en: pertaining to the surface of a body part
entries.example_cn: 医生开了一种外用药膏来治疗皮肤感染。
entries.example_en: The doctor prescribed a topical cream to treat the skin infection.

entries.definition_en: the attribute of being of interest at the present time
entries.example_cn: 该议题的时效性确保了它仍然是公众辩论的主题。
entries.example_en: The topicality of the issue ensures that it remains a subject of public debate.

entries.definition_cn: 一种将句子的主题或焦点置于句首以强调其重要性的语言技巧
entries.definition_en: a linguistic technique where the topic or focus of a sentence is emphasized by placing it at the beginning
entries.example_cn: 将“猫”置于句首进行主题化，突出了它在故事中的重要性。
entries.example_en: The topicalization of 'the cat' at the start of the sentence highlights its importance in the story.

entries.definition_en: applied to a specific, restricted area of the body
entries.example_cn: 医生建议将药膏局部涂抹在受影响的皮肤上。
entries.example_en: The doctor advised applying the cream topically to the affected skin.

entries.definition_cn: 头顶的装饰性发髻或羽冠
entries.definition_en: a decorative knot of hair, or a crest of feathers, on the head
entries.example_cn: 公鸡在黎明时啼叫，展示着它华丽的红色头顶羽冠。
entries.example_en: The rooster displayed a magnificent red topknot as it crowed at dawn.

entries.definition_cn: 戴在头发上的装饰性缎带或蝴蝶结
entries.definition_en: a decorative ribbon or bow worn in the hair
entries.example_cn: 她把一条装饰性缎带戴在头发上，作为头饰。
entries.example_en: She wore a decorative ribbon in her hair as a topknot.

entries.definition_en: having the breasts uncovered or featuring such nudity
entries.example_cn: 海滩上挤满了穿着袒胸泳衣的日光浴者。
entries.example_en: The beach was crowded with sunbathers in topless swimsuits.

entries.definition_en: having no top
entries.example_cn: 无顶的船游提供了独特的港口视野。
entries.example_en: The topless boat ride offers a unique view of the harbor.

entries.definition_en: the mast next above a lower mast and topmost in a fore-and-aft rig
entries.example_cn: 船长命令船员在风暴来临前修复受损的顶桅。
entries.example_en: The captain ordered the crew to repair the damaged topmast before the storm hit.

entries.definition_en: at or nearest to the top
entries.example_cn: 最顶层的架子太高了，够不着。
entries.example_en: The topmost shelf is too high to reach.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅提供一流的服务和美食。
entries.example_en: The restaurant offers topnotch service and cuisine.

entries.definition_en: relating to the arrangement of natural and artificial features of a place
entries.example_cn: 这张地图显示了该山脉的地形细节。
entries.example_en: The map shows the topographic details of the mountain range.

entries.definition_en: relating to the arrangement of natural and artificial features of a place
entries.example_cn: 这张地图提供了山脉的详细地形视图。
entries.example_en: The map provides a detailed topographical view of the mountain range.

entries.definition_en: in a way that relates to the arrangement of physical features of a place
entries.example_cn: 这张地图旨在从地形上展示该地区。
entries.example_en: The map was designed to show the region topographically.

entries.definition_en: the arrangement of natural and artificial features on a surface
entries.example_cn: 这张地图清楚地显示了山脉的地形。
entries.example_en: The map shows the topography of the mountain range clearly.

entries.definition_en: the detailed study of a region's surface features
entries.example_cn: 学生们为地理项目研究了当地的地形学。
entries.example_en: Students studied the topography of the local area for their geography project.

entries.definition_en: relating to the branch of mathematics that studies properties of space that are preserved under continuous deformations
entries.example_cn: 该流形的拓扑结构保持不变。
entries.example_en: The topological structure of the manifold remains unchanged.

entries.definition_en: in a way that relates to the properties of space that are preserved under continuous deformations
entries.example_cn: 这两个形状在拓扑学上是等价的。
entries.example_en: The two shapes are topologically equivalent.

entries.definition_en: a branch of mathematics dealing with properties of figures that remain unchanged under continuous transformations
entries.example_cn: 高等数学班的学生正在学习拓扑学如何根据连通性而非距离来分析形状。
entries.example_en: Students in the advanced math class are learning how topology analyzes shapes based on connectivity rather than distance.

entries.definition_en: the arrangement or structure of a communication network
entries.example_cn: IT 团队重新设计了网络拓扑结构，以提高数据流的效率和可靠性。
entries.example_en: The IT team redesigned the network topology to improve data flow and reliability.

entries.definition_cn: 身体某一部位的解剖结构
entries.definition_en: the anatomical structure of a part of the body
entries.example_cn: 这位外科医生研究了手部神经和动脉的解剖结构。
entries.example_en: The surgeon studied the topology of the nerves and arteries in the hand.

entries.definition_en: the study of a place's physical features and its history as shown by those features
entries.example_cn: 该博物馆的展览聚焦于当地的地形及其历史演变。
entries.example_en: The museum exhibition focused on the local topology and its historical evolution.

entries.definition_en: the name used to identify a specific place on a map or in geography
entries.example_cn: 珠穆朗玛峰是一个举世闻名的地名。
entries.example_en: Mount Everest is a famous toponym recognized worldwide.

entries.definition_cn: 研究某一地区或语言地名的词汇学分支
entries.definition_en: the branch of lexicology that studies the place names of a region or a language
entries.example_cn: 地名学通过地名揭示了该地区的历史和文化。
entries.example_en: Toponymy reveals much about the history and culture of a region through its place names.

entries.definition_en: the nomenclature of regional anatomy
entries.example_cn: 区域解剖学的命名法研究有助于识别不同文化中的特定结构。
entries.example_en: The study of toponymy in regional anatomy helps identify specific structures across different cultures.

entries.definition_en: a traditional theme, motif, or literary convention
entries.example_cn: 作者利用流浪英雄这一母题来探讨流亡的主题。
entries.example_en: The author uses the topos of the wandering hero to explore themes of exile.

entries.definition_cn: 一种范畴，其性质类似于拓扑空间或（更一般地）位点上的集合层范畴
entries.definition_en: a category that behaves like the category of sheaves of sets on a topological space or, more generally, on a site
entries.example_cn: 在高等几何中，拓扑斯可以作为研究广义空间的框架。
entries.example_en: In advanced geometry, a topos can serve as a setting for studying generalized spaces.

entries.definition_cn: 顶部具有特定形状或覆盖着特定顶层的
entries.definition_en: having or covered with a specified top or top layer
entries.example_cn: 那座山顶平坦的山丘耸立在山谷上方。
entries.example_en: The flat-topped hill stood above the valley.

entries.definition_cn: （印度英语）考试中取得最高分的学生
entries.definition_en: (Indian English) the student who achieves the highest score in an examination
entries.example_cn: 她是班里的佼佼者，每次考试都取得最高分。
entries.example_en: She was the topper of the class, scoring the highest marks in every exam.

usage.label: Indian English
usage.pattern: topper can mean the highest-scoring student; source w16860r5.

entries.definition_cn: （美国英语）女子或儿童穿的短外套
entries.definition_en: (US) a short outer jacket worn by women or children
entries.example_cn: 她穿了一件时髦的短外套搭配连衣裙，以抵御寒风。
entries.example_en: She wore a stylish topper over her dress to stay warm in the wind.

entries.definition_en: an exceedingly good witticism that surpasses all that have gone before
entries.example_cn: 他最后的玩笑真是妙语，引得全场大笑。
entries.example_en: His final joke was a real topper that made the entire audience laugh.

entries.definition_en: a man's hat with a tall crown; usually covered with silk or with beaver fur
entries.example_cn: 这位绅士在登上马车前整理了一下他的高顶礼帽。
entries.example_en: The gentleman adjusted his topper before stepping into the carriage.

entries.definition_cn: 放在某物顶部的东西，尤指顶部装饰或覆盖层
entries.definition_en: something placed on top of something else, especially a topping or upper layer
entries.example_cn: 她加了一层床垫加垫，以提高舒适度。
entries.example_en: She added a mattress topper for extra comfort.

entries.definition_cn: 去顶者；切除顶部的工具
entries.definition_en: a person or tool that cuts off the top of something
entries.example_cn: 这名去顶工砍去了树木的顶部。
entries.example_en: The topper cut the tops off the trees.

entries.definition_en: a flavorful addition on top of a dish
entries.example_cn: 她在披萨上撒了些奶酪作为配料。
entries.example_en: She sprinkled cheese as a topping on her pizza.

entries.definition_en: excellent; best possible
entries.example_cn: 那位年轻歌手的表现棒极了。
entries.example_en: That was a topping performance by the young singer.

entries.definition_en: to fall down, as if collapsing
entries.example_cn: 那座古老的塔楼在地震中开始倒塌。
entries.example_en: The old tower began to topple during the earthquake.

entries.definition_en: to cause something to fall or overturn
entries.example_cn: 强风把树吹倒在了栅栏上。
entries.example_en: The strong wind toppled the tree over the fence.

entries.definition_en: of the highest quality
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅的海鲜是一流的。
entries.example_en: The seafood at this restaurant is tops.

entries.definition_en: a sail located immediately above the lowest sail on a mast, supported by a topmast
entries.example_cn: 随着风力增强，船员们齐心协力升起顶帆。
entries.example_en: The crew worked together to hoist the topsail as the wind strengthened.

entries.definition_cn: 船体高于水线的外侧表面
entries.definition_en: the outer surface of a ship's hull above the waterline
entries.example_cn: 船体高于水线的外侧表面在碰撞中受损。
entries.example_en: The topside of the hull was damaged in the collision.

entries.definition_en: the upper layer of soil found on the surface of the ground
entries.example_cn: 农民必须通过种植覆盖作物来保护表土免受侵蚀。
entries.example_en: Farmers must protect the topsoil from erosion by planting cover crops.

entries.definition_en: forward spin (usually of a moving ball) that is imparted by an upward stroke
entries.example_cn: 他用力打出上旋球，使球迅速下坠。
entries.example_en: He hit the ball with heavy topspin to make it dip quickly.

entries.definition_en: in a state of complete disorder or confusion
entries.example_cn: 派对结束后，房间被弄得乱七八糟。
entries.example_en: The room was left topsy-turvy after the party.

entries.definition_en: in a disordered manner
entries.example_cn: 书被杂乱地堆在架子上。
entries.example_en: The books were stacked topsy-turvy on the shelf.

entries.definition_en: in disorderly haste
entries.example_cn: 她慌乱地收拾好行李，赶去了机场。
entries.example_en: She packed her bags topsy-turvy and left for the airport.

entries.definition_en: a tall white hat with a pouched crown worn by chefs
entries.example_cn: 主厨在宣布新菜单前调整了一下他的厨师帽。
entries.example_en: The head chef adjusted his toque before announcing the new menu.

entries.definition_cn: 针织帽（加拿大英语，通常为圆锥形，也可能有多种形状）
entries.definition_en: a knitted hat, usually conical or variably shaped, often woollen and sometimes topped with a pom-pom
entries.example_cn: 在加拿大，她在雪地散步时戴着一顶保暖的针织帽。
entries.example_en: In Canada, she wore a warm knitted toque on the snowy walk.

entries.definition_en: a prominent rock or pile of rocks situated on a hill
entries.example_cn: 徒步旅行者沿着陡峭的小径爬到山顶巨石处。
entries.example_en: The hikers climbed the steep path to reach the tor.

entries.definition_en: a high rocky hill
entries.example_cn: 我们花了一下午时间探索那座古老的岩石山丘。
entries.example_en: We spent the afternoon exploring the ancient tor.

entries.definition_en: a light source made of flammable material, usually carried in the hand
entries.example_cn: 他们提着火把穿过黑暗的森林寻找出路。
entries.example_en: They carried torches through the dark forest to find their way.

entries.definition_en: a small portable electric lamp powered by batteries
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨中停电时，他伸手去拿手电筒。
entries.example_en: He reached for his torch when the power went out during the storm.

entries.definition_en: a device that mixes air and gas to produce a very hot flame
entries.example_cn: 焊工调节喷灯以获得焊接金属所需的正确温度。
entries.example_en: The welder adjusted the torch to get the right temperature for the metal.

entries.definition_en: a type of tall, woolly plant with yellow flowers used historically for making torches
entries.example_cn: 古希腊人利用火把草为葬礼仪式制作燃料。
entries.example_en: Ancient Greeks used the torch plant to create fuel for funeral ceremonies.

entries.definition_en: to burn something maliciously, often by setting it on fire
entries.example_cn: 破坏分子在离开城镇前将那座旧建筑纵火焚烧。
entries.example_en: The vandals torched the old building before leaving the town.

entries.definition_en: a leader in a campaign or movement
entries.example_cn: 她被誉为环保运动的领袖。
entries.example_en: She was hailed as the torchbearer of the environmental movement.

entries.definition_cn: 火炬或手电筒发出的光
entries.definition_en: light produced by a torch or flashlight
entries.example_cn: 孩子们借着火炬光穿过森林。
entries.example_en: The children walked through the forest by torchlight.

entries.definition_cn: 柱基上通常位于最底部的装饰条
entries.definition_en: commonly the lowest molding at the base of a column
entries.example_cn: 建筑师赞叹寺庙柱基上托雷（装饰条）的精美设计。
entries.example_en: The architect admired the intricate design of the tore on the temple.

entries.definition_en: a person who fights bulls in a bullfight
entries.example_cn: 这位著名的斗牛士在人群的欢呼声中走进了竞技场。
entries.example_en: The famous toreador entered the arena to the cheers of the crowd.

entries.definition_en: a matador or a member of the team that assists in a bullfight.
entries.example_cn: 斗牛士在喇叭声中进入竞技场。
entries.example_en: The torero entered the arena to the sound of trumpets.

entries.definition_en: to cause emotional or mental suffering
entries.example_cn: 想到她的失败，他好几天都备受折磨。
entries.example_en: The thought of her failure tormented him for days.

entries.definition_en: to subject someone to torture
entries.example_cn: 士兵们拷问嫌疑人以获取情报。
entries.example_en: The soldiers tormented the suspect for information.

entries.definition_en: intense feelings of suffering; acute mental or physical pain
entries.example_cn: 他深受良心的煎熬。
entries.example_en: He suffered from a torment of guilt.

entries.definition_en: extreme mental distress
entries.example_cn: 争吵后她感到极度痛苦。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep torment after the argument.

entries.definition_en: unbearable physical pain
entries.example_cn: 伤口给他带来了巨大的痛苦。
entries.example_en: The wound caused him great torment.

entries.definition_cn: 令人极度恼怒或痛苦的事物
entries.definition_en: a source of intense annoyance or distress
entries.example_cn: 持续不断的噪音让他极度恼怒。
entries.example_en: The constant noise was a torment to him.

entries.definition_en: to treat someone cruelly
entries.example_cn: 绑架者残酷地折磨了囚犯。
entries.example_en: The captors tormented the prisoner.

entries.definition_en: a severe affliction or source of suffering
entries.example_cn: 瘟疫给这座城市带来了巨大的苦难。
entries.example_en: The plague was a great torment to the city.

entries.definition_cn: 遭受剧烈痛苦的，尤指精神痛苦的
entries.definition_en: experiencing intense pain, especially mental pain
entries.example_cn: 他因过去的错误而备受良心谴责，痛苦不堪。
entries.example_en: He was tormented by guilt over his past mistakes.

entries.definition_cn: 受噩梦或不合理恐惧折磨的
entries.definition_en: tormented or harassed by nightmares or unreasonable fears
entries.example_cn: 那个孩子每晚都被噩梦折磨得睡不着。
entries.example_en: The child was tormented by nightmares every night.

entries.definition_en: a person who causes pain or suffering to others
entries.example_cn: 故事中的反派是一个无情的折磨者，从不施以怜悯。
entries.example_en: The villain in the story was a relentless tormenter who never showed mercy.

entries.definition_en: a stage flat at either side of a stage that blocks the audience’s view of the wings
entries.example_cn: 舞台工作人员重新摆放挡景板，以免观众看到演员。
entries.example_en: The stagehands repositioned the tormenter to keep the actors out of the audience’s view.

entries.definition_cn: 折磨人或使人痛苦的人、动物或事物
entries.definition_en: a person, animal, or thing that causes suffering
entries.example_cn: 建筑工地持续不断的噪音让居民十分痛苦。
entries.example_en: The constant noise from the construction site was a real tormentor for the residents.

entries.definition_cn: 舞台两侧用来遮挡侧幕后区的窄幕或侧翼板之一
entries.definition_en: one of a pair of narrow curtains or flats at the sides of a stage that hide the wings
entries.example_cn: 舞台设计使用了两块侧翼板来遮挡侧幕后区。
entries.example_en: The stage design used two tormentors to hide the wings.

entries.definition_cn: 撕裂的；边缘参差不齐的
entries.definition_en: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.example_cn: 那块边缘参差不齐的布料很难缝回去。
entries.example_en: The torn fabric was difficult to sew back together.

entries.definition_cn: 在相互冲突的选择之间左右为难的
entries.definition_en: unable to decide between competing options
entries.example_cn: 她在接受这份工作和留在家里之间左右为难。
entries.example_en: She was torn between accepting the offer and staying home.

entries.definition_en: a violent windstorm with a funnel-shaped cloud extending to the ground
entries.example_cn: 龙卷风给这个城镇造成了广泛的破坏。
entries.example_en: The tornado caused widespread damage to the town.

entries.definition_cn: 可卡因（一种高度成瘾的、纯化的、可吸食的可卡因形式）
entries.definition_en: a highly addictive, purified form of cocaine that is smoked
entries.example_cn: 这种毒品在某些犯罪圈子里被称为“龙卷风”。
entries.example_en: The drug is known as 'tornado' in some criminal circles.

entries.definition_en: a shrub or small tree native to the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico with spirally twisted pods
entries.example_cn: 植物学家识别出生长在干旱沙漠地区的扭结豆灌木。
entries.example_en: The botanist identified the rare tornillo growing in the arid desert region.

entries.definition_cn: 与火山活动有关的低频地震事件
entries.definition_en: a low-frequency seismic event associated with volcanic activity
entries.example_cn: 地震学家记录到火山下方发生了一系列低频地震事件。
entries.example_en: The seismologists recorded a series of tornillos beneath the volcano.

entries.definition_en: a doughnut-shaped object enclosed by a torus
entries.example_cn: 磁场被限制在环面体内。
entries.example_en: The magnetic field is contained within the toroid.

entries.definition_en: a ring-shaped surface generated by rotating a circle around an axis that does not intersect the circle
entries.example_cn: 环面是由一个圆绕其外部轴旋转形成的。
entries.example_en: A toroid is formed by rotating a circle around an external axis.

entries.definition_en: having the shape of a toroid (a doughnut shape)
entries.example_cn: 磁场线围绕核心形成环状图案。
entries.example_en: The magnetic field lines form a toroidal pattern around the core.

entries.definition_cn: 一种武器，由长圆柱形自航水下弹体组成，接触目标时即引爆
entries.definition_en: armament consisting of a long cylindrical self-propelled underwater projectile that detonates on contact with a target
entries.example_cn: 驱逐舰向潜艇发射了一枚鱼雷。
entries.example_en: The destroyer launched a torpedo at the submarine.

entries.definition_cn: 一种用长条硬面包纵向切开，夹入肉、奶酪（以及番茄、洋葱、生菜和调味品）制成的大三明治；美国不同地区名称各异
entries.definition_en: a large sandwich made of a long crusty roll split lengthwise and filled with meats and cheese (and tomato and onion and lettuce and condiments); different names are used in different sections of the United States
entries.example_cn: 他午餐点了一份大三明治。
entries.example_en: He ordered a torpedo for lunch.

entries.definition_cn: 电鳐目中一种行动迟缓的底栖鳐鱼，身体呈圆形，头部两侧有能产生强电流放电的发电器官
entries.definition_en: any sluggish bottom-dwelling ray of the order Torpediniformes having a rounded body and electric organs on each side of the head capable of emitting strong electric discharges
entries.example_cn: 潜水员看到一条电鳐在珊瑚礁附近游动。
entries.example_en: The diver saw a torpedo swimming near the coral reef.

entries.definition_cn: 一种在油井（或气井）中引爆以启动或增加石油（或天然气）流量的爆炸装置
entries.definition_en: an explosive device that is set off in an oil well (or a gas well) to start or to increase the flow of oil (or gas)
entries.example_cn: 该公司使用爆炸装置重启了枯竭的油井。
entries.example_en: The company used a torpedo to restart the dry well.

entries.definition_cn: 一种放置在铁路轨道上的小型爆炸装置，当火车压过时即引爆；爆炸声警告司机前方有危险
entries.definition_en: a small explosive device that is placed on a railroad track and fires when a train runs over it; the sound of the explosion warns the engineer of danger ahead
entries.example_cn: 司机听到了爆炸声，于是减速慢行。
entries.example_en: The engineer heard the torpedo and slowed down.

entries.definition_en: attack or hit with torpedoes
entries.example_cn: 潜艇用鱼雷击中了敌舰。
entries.example_en: The submarine torpedoed the enemy ship.

entries.definition_cn: 一种小型烟花，由击发帽和用纸包裹的碎石组成；用力扔向硬表面时会爆炸
entries.definition_en: a small firework that consists of a percussion cap and some gravel wrapped in paper; explodes when thrown forcefully against a hard surface
entries.example_cn: 孩子们在后院玩这种小型烟花。
entries.example_en: Children played with torpedoes in the backyard.

entries.definition_en: a professional killer who uses a gun
entries.example_cn: 警方怀疑这名男子是一名受雇的杀手。
entries.example_en: The police suspect the man is a hired torpedo.

entries.definition_en: slow and apathetic
entries.example_cn: 这位迟钝的学生几乎懒得举手回答老师的问题。
entries.example_en: The torpid student barely lifted a finger to answer the teacher's questions.

entries.definition_en: in a state of biological rest or suspended animation
entries.example_cn: 许多爬行动物在冬季进入蛰伏状态以保存能量。
entries.example_en: Many reptiles become torpid during the winter months to conserve energy.

entries.definition_en: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy
entries.example_cn: 热浪导致全城一片萎靡不振。
entries.example_en: The heatwave caused a general torpor in the city.

entries.definition_en: a state of reduced activity and responsiveness, sometimes resembling hibernation
entries.example_cn: 这条蛇在冬天进入了蛰伏状态。
entries.example_en: The snake fell into a torpor during the winter.

entries.definition_en: a force that causes rotation or twisting around an axis
entries.example_cn: 引擎产生的扭矩足以拉动重型卡车爬上陡坡。
entries.example_en: The engine produces enough torque to pull the heavy truck up the hill.

entries.definition_cn: 对某物施加扭矩使其旋转
entries.definition_en: to make something rotate by applying torque
entries.example_cn: 电动机使转轴旋转，从而带动叶片。
entries.example_en: The motor torques the shaft to turn the blades.

entries.definition_en: a unit of pressure equal to 0.001316 atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 真空室内的压力是以托为单位测量的。
entries.example_en: The pressure inside the vacuum chamber was measured in torr.

entries.definition_en: a powerful and rapid flow of water or other liquid
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，一股洪流从山上冲下来。
entries.example_en: A torrent of water rushed down the mountain after the storm.

entries.definition_en: a very heavy fall of rain
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨带来了一场倾盆大雨，淹没了街道。
entries.example_en: The storm brought a torrent of rain that flooded the streets.

entries.definition_en: a very large and overwhelming number or amount of something
entries.example_cn: 演唱会结束后，她收到了来自粉丝的大量电子邮件。
entries.example_en: She received a torrent of emails from fans after the concert.

entries.definition_en: falling or flowing heavily or in large quantities
entries.example_cn: 暴雨整夜倾盆而下。
entries.example_en: Torrential rain fell throughout the night.

entries.definition_en: resembling a torrent in force and abundance
entries.example_cn: 歌手唱完后，爆发出如潮的掌声。
entries.example_en: A torrential applause broke out when the singer finished.

entries.definition_en: relating to or resulting from the action of a torrent
entries.example_cn: 大雨过后，河流变得汹涌澎湃。
entries.example_en: The river became torrential after the heavy rains.

entries.definition_en: extremely hot and dry
entries.example_cn: 炎热的夏日让沙漠景观在热浪中闪烁。
entries.example_en: The torrid summer days made the desert landscape shimmer in the heat.

entries.definition_en: characterized by intense, ardent emotion, especially sexual love
entries.example_cn: 这部小说描写了两位主人公之间热烈的爱情场面。
entries.example_en: The novel contains a torrid love scene between the two protagonists.

entries.definition_cn: 情绪激昂且精力充沛的
entries.definition_en: emotionally charged and vigorously energetic
entries.example_cn: 那场情绪激昂的辩论持续了数小时，双方都进行了激烈的争论。
entries.example_en: The torrid debate lasted for hours with passionate arguments on both sides.

entries.definition_en: a twisting force applied to an object
entries.example_cn: 工程师计算了桥梁所能承受的扭转力。
entries.example_en: The engineer calculated the torsion the bridge could withstand.

entries.definition_en: the state of being twisted
entries.example_cn: 这件雕塑的金属框架呈现出严重的扭曲状态。
entries.example_en: The sculpture showed severe torsion in its metal frame.

entries.definition_en: the part of the body between the neck and the hips
entries.example_cn: 这座雕像只展示了那个男人健壮的躯干。
entries.example_en: The statue showed only the man's muscular torso.

entries.definition_en: (law) any wrongdoing for which an action for damages may be brought
entries.example_cn: 原告就疏忽侵权行为提起了诉讼。
entries.example_en: The plaintiff filed a lawsuit for the tort of negligence.

entries.definition_en: a rich cake, typically covered with cream, fruit, or nuts
entries.example_cn: 我们端上了巧克力托特蛋糕作为甜点。
entries.example_en: We served a chocolate torte for dessert.

entries.definition_en: small ring-shaped stuffed pasta
entries.example_cn: 我们要了番茄酱配的小圆环状馅面。
entries.example_en: We ordered tortellini with a tomato sauce.

entries.definition_en: a person who has committed a civil wrong (tort)
entries.example_cn: 法院命令侵权人向受害者支付赔偿金。
entries.example_en: The court ordered the tortfeasor to pay damages to the victim.

entries.definition_en: a condition where the head leans to one side due to contracted neck muscles
entries.example_cn: 医生在颈部检查后诊断出孩子患有斜颈。
entries.example_en: The doctor diagnosed the child with torticollis after the neck examination.

entries.definition_en: a thin flat cake made from cornmeal or wheat flour
entries.example_cn: 她把豆子和奶酪放在一张温热的玉米饼上。
entries.example_en: She served the beans and cheese on a warm tortilla.

entries.definition_en: A Spanish omelet made with eggs, potatoes, and onions.
entries.example_cn: 我们点了一份加土豆和洋葱的西班牙土豆煎蛋饼。
entries.example_en: We ordered a Spanish tortilla with potatoes and onions.

entries.definition_en: relating to or involving a civil wrong that causes harm
entries.example_cn: 律师争辩说该公司的行为属于侵权，应赔偿损失。
entries.example_en: The lawyer argued that the company's actions were tortious and liable for damages.

entries.definition_en: usually herbivorous land turtles having clawed elephant-like limbs; worldwide in arid areas except Australia and Antarctica
entries.example_cn: 那只慢吞吞的陆龟稳步穿过干燥的沙漠沙地。
entries.example_en: The slow tortoise moved steadily across the dry desert sand.

entries.definition_en: a cat with black, cream, and yellowish markings
entries.example_cn: 我们从收容所领养了一只玳瑁猫。
entries.example_en: We adopted a tortoiseshell cat from the shelter.

entries.definition_en: the mottled horny substance found on the shell of some turtles
entries.example_cn: 这顶帽子是用一块玳瑁壳做的。
entries.example_en: The hat was made from a piece of tortoiseshell.

entries.definition_en: a brilliantly colored butterfly whose larvae feed on nettles
entries.example_cn: 蛱蝶在花丛中翩翩起舞。
entries.example_en: The tortoiseshell butterfly fluttered across the garden.

entries.definition_cn: 柑橘卷蛾（幼虫生活在橙子中）
entries.definition_en: a California moth whose larvae live in oranges
entries.example_cn: 加州农民正在努力控制其柑橘园中的柑橘卷蛾种群。
entries.example_en: Farmers in California are struggling to control the tortrix population in their orange groves.

entries.definition_cn: 印度茶咖啡蛾（侵害茶树和咖啡植物）
entries.definition_en: a small Indian moth that infests tea and coffee plants
entries.example_cn: 这种印度茶咖啡蛾对当地的咖啡收成造成了严重损害。
entries.example_en: The tortrix has caused significant damage to the local coffee harvest.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being twisted and winding in shape
entries.example_cn: 这条河的弯曲度使得航行变得困难。
entries.example_en: The tortuosity of the river made navigation difficult.

entries.definition_en: highly complex, intricate, and sometimes devious
entries.example_cn: 这部小说错综复杂的情节让读者直到最后都在猜测。
entries.example_en: The tortuous plot of the novel kept readers guessing until the end.

entries.definition_en: marked by repeated turns and bends
entries.example_cn: 穿过森林的弯曲多折的小径让我们走了好几个小时。
entries.example_en: The tortuous path through the forest took us hours to complete.

entries.definition_en: indirect and difficult to understand
entries.example_cn: 他拐弯抹角地解释让人很难理解他的真实意图。
entries.example_en: His tortuous explanation made it difficult to understand his true intentions.

entries.definition_en: in a way that has many twists and turns
entries.example_cn: 这条小径曲折地穿过茂密的森林。
entries.example_en: The path wound tortuously through the dense forest.

entries.definition_cn: 迂回复杂地；拐弯抹角地
entries.definition_en: in an excessively complicated or indirect manner
entries.example_cn: 他把复杂的规则解释得过于迂回复杂。
entries.example_en: He explained the complex rules in an excessively tortuous way.

entries.definition_en: the deliberate infliction of suffering to force information or confession
entries.example_cn: 酷刑是非法且不人道的。
entries.example_en: Torture is illegal and inhumane.

entries.definition_cn: 极其令人痛苦或难受的经历；折磨
entries.definition_en: an extremely unpleasant or distressing experience
entries.example_cn: 等待裁决简直是一种折磨。
entries.example_en: Waiting for the verdict was pure torture.

entries.definition_cn: 强烈的痛苦或剧烈的疼痛
entries.definition_en: intense feelings of suffering or acute pain
entries.example_cn: 事故后，连呼吸对他来说都是一种折磨。
entries.example_en: After the accident, even breathing was torture.

entries.definition_en: extreme mental distress or anguish
entries.example_cn: 争吵后，她感到深深的痛苦。
entries.example_en: She felt a deep sense of torture after the argument.

entries.definition_en: to subject someone to torture
entries.example_cn: 囚犯被折磨以获取情报。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was tortured for information.

entries.definition_en: to torment someone emotionally or mentally
entries.example_cn: 不断的批评折磨着他的心灵。
entries.example_en: The constant criticism tortured his mind.

entries.definition_cn: 极其令人难受或痛苦的经历或处境
entries.definition_en: an extremely unpleasant experience or situation
entries.example_cn: 等待延误的航班简直是一种折磨。
entries.example_en: Waiting for the delayed flight was torture.

entries.definition_en: experiencing intense physical or mental suffering
entries.example_cn: 她因不断担心家人的安全而感到痛苦不堪。
entries.example_en: She felt tortured by the constant worry about her family's safety.

entries.definition_en: a person who inflicts severe pain on others
entries.example_cn: 折磨者使用了各种方法来获取信息。
entries.example_en: The torturer used various methods to extract information.

entries.definition_en: extremely painful
entries.example_cn: 她忍受了数小时的剧痛。
entries.example_en: She spent hours in torturing pain.

entries.definition_en: the deliberate infliction of physical or mental suffering to force a confession
entries.example_cn: 警方被指控对嫌疑人实施酷刑。
entries.example_en: The police were accused of torturing the suspect.

entries.definition_en: extremely painful
entries.example_cn: 这段极度痛苦的旅程花了三天才走完。
entries.example_en: The torturous journey took three days to complete.

entries.definition_en: in a way that causes extreme physical or mental pain
entries.example_cn: 这名囚犯在招供前遭受了极其痛苦的折磨。
entries.example_en: The prisoner was tortured torturously before he confessed.

entries.definition_en: a ring-shaped surface created by rotating a circle around an axis that does not touch the circle
entries.example_cn: 这位建筑师设计了一座建筑，其中央支撑是一个巨大的环面。
entries.example_en: The architect designed a building featuring a massive torus as its central support.

entries.definition_en: a large convex molding, typically semicircular, at the base of a column
entries.example_cn: 修复团队仔细清理了神庙石柱上的古老圆凸线脚。
entries.example_en: The restoration team carefully cleaned the ancient torus on the temple columns.

entries.definition_en: silly or pretentious talk or writing
entries.example_cn: 别再说胡话了，听我说。
entries.example_en: Stop talking tosh and listen to what I am saying.

entries.definition_en: to throw or toss with a light motion
entries.example_cn: 他轻轻地把球抛给队友。
entries.example_en: He tossed the ball gently to his teammate.

entries.definition_en: to throw carelessly
entries.example_cn: 不要把垃圾乱扔在地上。
entries.example_en: Don't toss your trash on the ground.

entries.definition_en: to throw lightly to see which side comes up
entries.example_cn: 她把硬币抛向空中并接住。
entries.example_en: She tossed the coin in the air and caught it.

entries.definition_en: to throw or cast away
entries.example_cn: 他决定把旧家具扔进河里。
entries.example_en: He decided to toss the old furniture into the river.

entries.definition_en: the act of flipping a coin to make a decision
entries.example_cn: 我们通过抛硬币来决定。
entries.example_en: We decided by a toss of a coin.

entries.definition_en: the act of throwing the ball to another member of your team in sports
entries.example_cn: 四分卫完美地将球传给了接球手。
entries.example_en: The quarterback made a perfect toss to the receiver.

entries.definition_en: to move or stir about violently
entries.example_cn: 巨浪在风暴中使船剧烈翻腾。
entries.example_en: The waves tossed the boat around in the storm.

entries.definition_en: an abrupt movement
entries.example_cn: 汽车驶过坑洼时突然颠簸了一下。
entries.example_en: The car gave a sudden toss as it hit the pothole.

entries.definition_cn: 两个选择同样有吸引力或两个结果同样可能的局面
entries.definition_en: a situation in which two choices are equally attractive or two outcomes are equally likely
entries.example_cn: 选举结果在统计完所有选票前仍难以预料。
entries.example_en: The election result remains a toss-up until the final votes are counted.

entries.definition_en: one who tosses or throws something
entries.example_cn: 投掷者准确地把球扔给了外野手。
entries.example_en: The tosser threw the ball accurately to the outfielder.

entries.definition_cn: 手淫者的粗俗、侮辱性称呼，主要见于英国、爱尔兰及其他英联邦国家
entries.definition_en: a derogatory, vulgar term, chiefly in the UK, Ireland, and other Commonwealth countries, for a person who masturbates
entries.example_cn: 这部电影包含冒犯性语言，其中包括使用“tosser”一词。
entries.example_en: The movie contains offensive language, including the use of the word tosser.

entries.definition_cn: 胜负或结果难分上下的局面；五五开的局面
entries.definition_en: a situation in which two outcomes or choices seem equally likely
entries.example_cn: 在统计选票之前，选举的最终结果仍难以预料。
entries.example_en: The final result of the election remains a tossup until the votes are counted.

entries.definition_en: a flat tortilla with various fillings piled on it
entries.example_cn: 我们午餐点了夹豆和奶酪的烤玉米饼。
entries.example_en: We ordered a tostada with beans and cheese for lunch.

entries.definition_en: a crisp flat tortilla
entries.example_cn: 她在旁边配上了莎莎酱，端上了脆烤玉米饼。
entries.example_en: She served the tostada with salsa on the side.

entries.definition_en: a small amount (especially of a drink)
entries.example_cn: 晚餐时我只喝一小杯葡萄酒。
entries.example_en: I'll just have a tot of wine with dinner.

entries.definition_cn: 刚开始学走路的小孩子
entries.definition_en: a young child who is just beginning to walk
entries.example_cn: 那个幼儿拉着妈妈的裙子，在房间里蹒跚学步。
entries.example_en: The tot toddled around the room, pulling on his mother's dress.

entries.definition_en: determine the sum of
entries.example_cn: 收银员在收据上计算了总金额。
entries.example_en: The cashier totted up the total on the receipt.

entries.definition_en: the complete amount of something
entries.example_cn: 这次旅行的总费用是五百美元。
entries.example_en: The total cost of the trip was five hundred dollars.

entries.definition_en: the result of adding a group of numbers
entries.example_cn: 测试分数的总数非常高。
entries.example_en: The total of the test scores was very high.

entries.definition_en: including everything; complete
entries.example_cn: 在做决定之前，我们需要考虑全部情况。
entries.example_en: We need to consider the total situation before deciding.

entries.definition_en: complete in every way; absolute
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨给村庄造成了彻底的破坏。
entries.example_en: The storm caused total destruction to the village.

entries.definition_en: to add numbers together to find the sum
entries.example_cn: 请计算页面左侧数字的总和。
entries.example_en: Please total the figures on the left side of the page.

entries.definition_en: to calculate the sum of numbers
entries.example_cn: 收银员会在用餐结束时为您结账。
entries.example_en: The cashier will total your bill at the end of the meal.

entries.definition_en: to damage something so badly it cannot be fixed
entries.example_cn: 这场事故把卡车彻底撞毁了。
entries.example_en: The crash totaled the truck.

entries.definition_en: completely destroyed or demolished, especially in an accident
entries.example_cn: 那辆车在严重的碰撞中全毁了。
entries.example_en: The car was totaled in the severe collision.

entries.definition_cn: 记录彩池投注、计算并显示赔率以及出票的计算机化系统；总彩池机
entries.definition_en: a computerized system that records parimutuel bets, calculates and displays odds, and produces tickets
entries.example_cn: 总彩池机瞬间计算出了赛马的赔率。
entries.example_en: The totalisator calculated the odds for the horse race instantly.

usage.label: UK
usage.pattern: British usage; source w46282r0 explicitly labels the term UK.

entries.definition_en: an ideology or system asserting total, unrestricted power, especially for the state
entries.example_cn: 这份政治宣言批评了现代国家中极权主义的兴起。
entries.example_en: The political manifesto criticized the rise of totalism in modern states.

entries.definition_en: Characterized by a government with absolute and centralized control.
entries.example_cn: 那个极权政权压制了所有的政治反对派。
entries.example_en: The totalitarian regime suppressed all political opposition.

entries.definition_en: Relating to the principles of totalitarianism where the state regulates all areas of life.
entries.example_cn: 这种极权主义意识形态要求公民绝对服从。
entries.example_en: The totalitarian ideology demanded total conformity from its citizens.

entries.definition_en: A person who supports or follows totalitarian principles or government.
entries.example_cn: 那位极权主义者认为国家应该控制生活的方方面面。
entries.example_en: The totalitarian believed that the state should control every aspect of life.

entries.definition_cn: 主张国家或政府拥有绝对且不受限制权力的意识形态或信念
entries.definition_en: an ideology or belief that the state or government should have complete and unlimited power
entries.example_cn: 他的政治观点倾向于绝对政府权力论。
entries.example_en: His political views leaned towards totalitarianism.

entries.definition_cn: 极权统治；极权主义政体
entries.definition_en: a totalitarian system of government in which a dictator or state exercises absolute power
entries.example_cn: 该国几十年来一直处于严格的极权统治之下。
entries.example_en: The country was under a strict totalitarian regime for decades.

entries.definition_en: an aggregate quantity obtained by addition
entries.example_cn: 捐赠的总额超过了一百万美元。
entries.example_en: The totality of the donations exceeded one million dollars.

entries.definition_en: the state of being complete and without exception
entries.example_cn: 证据的整体性证明了他的清白。
entries.example_en: The totality of the evidence proved his innocence.

entries.definition_cn: 日食或月食达到全食的阶段
entries.definition_en: the phase of an eclipse when it is total
entries.example_cn: 科学家在一座偏远岛屿上观测了日食的全食阶段。
entries.example_en: Scientists observed the totality of the eclipse from a remote island.

entries.definition_en: a computer system that records bets and distributes the total winnings to the winners
entries.example_cn: 赛马场使用总彩池机来计算赛马的赔款。
entries.example_en: The racecourse uses a totalizator to calculate the payouts for the horse race.

entries.definition_en: to calculate or record the total amount of something
entries.example_cn: 会计将在月底对费用进行总计。
entries.example_en: The accountant will totalize the expenses at the end of the month.

entries.definition_cn: 把某事物视为或表述为普遍的、包罗一切的
entries.definition_en: to treat or present something as universal or comprehensive
entries.example_cn: 这篇文章把一个多元社群的经历一概而论。
entries.example_en: The essay totalizes the experiences of a diverse community.

entries.definition_en: completely demolished
entries.example_cn: 那辆车在车祸中完全损毁，现在只剩下一堆废铁。
entries.example_en: The car was totally demolished in the crash and is now just a totalled wreck.

entries.definition_en: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent; Completely or entirely
entries.example_cn: 风暴完全摧毁了屋顶。
entries.example_en: The storm totally destroyed the roof.

entries.definition_cn: 一种珍贵的新西兰树木，其坚硬的红褐色木材用于建筑和造船
entries.definition_en: a valuable New Zealand tree with hard reddish wood used for building
entries.example_cn: 码头是用从当地森林采伐的耐用totara木材建造的。
entries.example_en: The wharf was constructed from durable totara timber harvested from the local forest.

entries.definition_en: a large bag or basket with handles for carrying things
entries.example_cn: 她用一个大手提袋装着杂货。
entries.example_en: She carried her groceries in a large tote.

entries.definition_cn: 携带或搬运（通常指重物或大件物品）
entries.definition_en: to carry or bear, often something heavy or bulky
entries.example_cn: 他不得不费力地把那些重箱子搬上楼梯。
entries.example_en: He had to tote the heavy boxes up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: an object like an animal or plant that serves as a symbol for a family or clan
entries.example_cn: 熊是这个古老氏族的象征物。
entries.example_en: The bear was the totem of the ancient clan.

entries.definition_en: a group of people who consider themselves related to a specific object or animal
entries.example_cn: 这个图腾部落的成员不得食用图腾动物的肉。
entries.example_en: Members of the totem were forbidden to eat the flesh of the totem animal.

entries.definition_en: serving as or relating to a totem or totemism
entries.example_cn: 图腾符号被画在木杆上。
entries.example_en: The totemic symbols were painted on the wooden poles.

entries.definition_en: the belief that a group of people shares a kinship with a common totem
entries.example_cn: 人类学家研究图腾崇拜以了解早期的社会结构。
entries.example_en: Anthropologists study totemism to understand early social structures.

entries.definition_en: a person whose job involves carrying things
entries.example_cn: 搬运工们把沉重的箱子搬上了楼梯。
entries.example_en: The toters moved the heavy boxes up the stairs.

entries.definition_en: having the ability to develop into any type of cell
entries.example_cn: 受精卵具有全能性，可以发育成一个完整的生物体。
entries.example_en: The zygote is totipotent and can form a complete organism.

entries.definition_en: to move without being stable, as if threatening to fall
entries.example_cn: 老人走过结冰的小路时开始摇晃不稳。
entries.example_en: The old man began to totter as he walked across the icy path.

entries.definition_en: to walk unsteadily, with short steps
entries.example_cn: 长途徒步后，她不得不步履蹒跚地回到车上。
entries.example_en: After the long hike, she had to totter back to the car.

entries.definition_en: be on the brink of collapse
entries.example_cn: 那座老木桥在重压下开始摇摇欲坠。
entries.example_en: The old wooden bridge began to totter under the heavy load.

entries.definition_en: unsteady in gait as from infirmity or old age
entries.example_cn: 那位老人步履蹒跚地走下楼梯。
entries.example_en: The old man walked down the stairs with a tottering gait.

entries.definition_en: (of structures or institutions) having lost stability; failing or on the point of collapse
entries.example_cn: 经济在通货膨胀的重压下摇摇欲坠。
entries.example_en: The economy is tottering under the weight of inflation.

entries.definition_en: a brilliantly colored fruit-eating bird of tropical America with a very large, thin-walled beak
entries.example_cn: 巨嘴鸟用它的大嘴敲开坚果。
entries.example_en: The toucan used its large beak to crack open nuts.

entries.definition_en: to make physical contact with something
entries.example_cn: 请不要触摸热炉子。
entries.example_en: Please do not touch the hot stove.

entries.definition_en: to feel something using the sense of touch
entries.example_cn: 她摸了摸布料，看它是否柔软。
entries.example_en: She touched the fabric to see if it was soft.

entries.definition_en: to affect someone's emotions
entries.example_cn: 这个故事深深打动了我。
entries.example_en: The story touched me deeply.

entries.definition_cn: 触碰；触摸（尤指用手或手指）
entries.definition_en: an act of touching, especially with the hand or finger
entries.example_cn: 在人群中，我突然感到有人碰了一下我的肩膀。
entries.example_en: In the crowd, I suddenly felt a touch on my shoulder.

entries.definition_en: the sense of feeling things by contact
entries.example_cn: 盲人依靠触觉。
entries.example_en: Blind people rely on their sense of touch.

entries.definition_en: a slight sign of a quality
entries.example_cn: 他的声音里带着一丝悲伤。
entries.example_en: There was a touch of sadness in his voice.

entries.definition_en: to be relevant to a subject
entries.example_cn: 这一章涉及战争的历史。
entries.example_en: This chapter touches on the history of the war.

entries.definition_en: a distinctive style or manner
entries.example_cn: 这幅画有一种独特的风格。
entries.example_en: The painting has a unique touch.

entries.definition_en: fraught with danger; uncertain and likely to fail
entries.example_cn: 这次救援行动形势危急。
entries.example_en: The rescue mission was a touch-and-go situation.

entries.definition_cn: 一种北美一年生植物，通常开黄色或橙色花，主要生长在潮湿且偏酸性的土壤中
entries.definition_en: a North American annual plant with usually yellow or orange flowers that grows chiefly on wet, rather acid soil
entries.example_cn: 这种凤仙花开着鲜艳的橙色花朵。
entries.example_en: The touch-me-not has bright orange flowers.

entries.definition_cn: 一种地中海藤本植物，其果实受触碰时会猛烈弹出种子和汁液
entries.definition_en: a Mediterranean vine whose fruit expels seeds and juice violently when touched
entries.example_cn: 你触碰这种喷瓜藤时，它会射出种子。
entries.example_en: The touch-me-not vine shoots its seeds when you touch it.

entries.definition_cn: 一种热带亚灌木，长有刺，其小叶受触碰时会折叠
entries.definition_en: a tropical subshrub with thorns and leaflets that fold when touched
entries.example_cn: 这种含羞草灌木在夜间会折叠叶子。
entries.example_en: The touch-me-not shrub folds its leaves at night.

entries.definition_en: to type quickly without looking at the keyboard
entries.example_cn: 她练习了几个月后就能快速盲打了。
entries.example_en: She can touch-type very fast after practicing for months.

entries.definition_en: a skilled typist who types without looking at the keyboard
entries.example_cn: 作为一名专业的盲打打字员，她可以不看手就能高速打字。
entries.example_en: As a professional touch-typist, she can type at high speed without glancing at her hands.

entries.definition_en: able to be perceived by the senses, especially by the sense of touch
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家创作了一座雕塑，它不仅视觉引人注目，而且可以触摸。
entries.example_en: The artist created a sculpture that was not only visually striking but also touchable.

entries.definition_cn: 触回球：美式橄榄球中开球或弃踢球从端区后方出界，或接球队在本方端区获得球权的判定
entries.definition_en: a play in American football in which a kickoff or punt goes out through the back of the end zone, or the receiving team gains possession in its own end zone
entries.example_cn: 开球飞入端区，形成触回球，老鹰队在本方20码线获得球权。
entries.example_en: The kickoff sailed into the end zone for a touchback, giving the Eagles possession on the 20-yard line.

entries.definition_cn: 美式或加拿大式橄榄球中，球员将球带入、接住或在对方达阵区内抢回球而得的分
entries.definition_en: a score in American or Canadian football made when a player carries, catches, or recovers the ball in the opponent's end zone
entries.example_cn: 接球员在达阵区接住传球，完成了达阵。
entries.example_en: The receiver caught the pass in the end zone for a touchdown.

entries.definition_en: the act of an airplane landing on the ground
entries.example_cn: 飞行员宣布着陆平稳。
entries.example_en: The pilot announced a smooth touchdown.

entries.definition_en: feeling or showing strong emotion, such as sadness or pity
entries.example_cn: 她对他的善举深受感动。
entries.example_en: She was deeply touched by his kind gesture.

entries.definition_en: having come into contact
entries.example_cn: 湿油漆被粗心的人用手碰到了。
entries.example_en: The wet paint was touched by a careless hand.

entries.definition_en: slightly crazy or mentally unstable
entries.example_cn: 他有点疯，以为自己能飞。
entries.example_en: He is a bit touched; he thinks he can fly.

entries.definition_en: a person who causes or allows a part of their body to come into contact with someone or something
entries.example_cn: 接触者轻轻拍了拍孩子的肩膀以示安慰。
entries.example_en: The toucher gently patted the child's shoulder to comfort them.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being easily irritated or offended
entries.example_cn: 他的易怒使得很难公开讨论项目的问题。
entries.example_en: His touchiness made it difficult to discuss the project's problems openly.

entries.definition_cn: 令人感伤、怜悯或感动的
entries.definition_en: causing sadness, pity, or tender emotion
entries.example_cn: 她发表了一篇关于童年的感人演讲。
entries.example_en: She gave a touching speech about her childhood.

entries.definition_en: the event of something coming in contact with the body
entries.example_cn: 触摸热炉子导致被烫伤。
entries.example_en: The touching of the hot stove caused a burn.

entries.definition_en: the act of putting two things together with no space between them
entries.example_cn: 两面墙的紧贴没有留下缝隙。
entries.example_en: The touching of the two walls left no gap.

entries.definition_en: in a manner that evokes deep emotion or pity
entries.example_cn: 她感人地讲述了自己的童年回忆。
entries.example_en: She spoke touchingly about her childhood memories.

entries.definition_en: either of the sidelines in soccer or rugby
entries.example_cn: 当球越过边线时，裁判吹响了哨子。
entries.example_en: The referee blew the whistle as the ball crossed the touchline.

entries.definition_en: a computer display that enables the user to interact with the computer by touching areas on the screen
entries.example_cn: 这款新平板电脑具有灵敏的触摸屏，便于导航。
entries.example_en: The new tablet features a responsive touchscreen for easy navigation.

entries.definition_en: a standard or criterion used to judge the quality or value of something
entries.example_cn: 诚实是良好品格的衡量标准。
entries.example_en: Honesty is the touchstone of good character.

entries.definition_cn: 通过在其上摩擦留下痕迹来检验金或其他贵金属合金质量的石头
entries.definition_en: a stone used to test the quality of gold or other precious-metal alloys by rubbing them against it
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商将合金在试金石上摩擦，以检验其纯度。
entries.example_en: The jeweler rubbed the alloy against a touchstone to test its purity.

entries.definition_en: dry, decayed wood used as tinder to start a fire
entries.example_cn: 他收集干燥的引火木来生火露营。
entries.example_en: He gathered dry touchwood to build a fire for the camp.

entries.definition_en: easily offended or annoyed
entries.example_cn: 别提他的年龄了，他对此非常敏感。
entries.example_en: Don't mention his age; he is very touchy about it.

entries.definition_en: difficult to handle or manage
entries.example_cn: 谈判非常棘手，需要高超的技巧。
entries.example_en: The negotiations were touchy and required great skill.

entries.definition_cn: 过分亲昵的；爱搞身体接触的
entries.definition_en: showing affection through frequent physical contact, often excessively or in an unwelcome way
entries.example_cn: 有人指控这位经理对女员工过分亲昵。
entries.example_en: The manager was accused of being too touchy-feely with his female employees.

entries.definition_cn: （通常含贬义）诉诸情感、同情或浪漫而非理性的
entries.definition_en: (derogatory, usually) appealing to emotion, sympathy, or romance rather than reason
entries.example_cn: 这部电影充斥着煽情的浪漫元素，却缺乏令人信服的情节。
entries.example_en: The film was full of touchy-feely romance and lacked a convincing plot.

entries.definition_cn: （通常含贬义）凭直觉或情感而非理性思考的
entries.definition_en: (derogatory, usually) relying on intuition or emotion rather than rational thought
entries.example_cn: 他更看重清晰的证据，而不是感性而缺乏理性的想法。
entries.example_en: He preferred clear evidence to touchy-feely ideas.

entries.definition_en: very difficult; severely testing stamina or resolution
entries.example_cn: 期末考试是一个巨大的挑战。
entries.example_en: The final exam was a tough challenge.

entries.definition_en: substantially made or constructed
entries.example_cn: 这座桥是用坚固的钢材建造的。
entries.example_en: The bridge is made of tough steel.

entries.definition_en: physically toughened
entries.example_cn: 那位强健的士兵熬过了严冬。
entries.example_en: The tough soldier survived the harsh winter.

entries.definition_en: strong-minded and not easily affected by emotion or sentiment
entries.example_cn: 他是个无情的人，从不示弱。
entries.example_en: He is a tough man who never shows weakness.

entries.definition_cn: 粗野的；蛮横的；无法无天的
entries.definition_en: rough, rowdy, or lawless
entries.example_cn: 该地区以暴力帮派而闻名。
entries.example_en: The area was known for its tough gangs.

entries.definition_en: an aggressive and violent young criminal
entries.example_cn: 那个暴徒袭击了店主。
entries.example_en: The tough attacked the shopkeeper.

entries.definition_en: a cruel and brutal fellow
entries.example_cn: 他们害怕那个街区里的恶棍。
entries.example_en: They feared the tough in the neighborhood.

entries.definition_en: someone who learned to fight in the streets rather than being formally trained in boxing
entries.example_cn: 那个街头拳手在巷子里勇敢地搏斗。
entries.example_en: The tough fought bravely in the alley.

entries.definition_en: dealing with facts or difficulties in a realistic and determined way
entries.example_cn: 那位务实坚定的经理拒绝无视预算削减。
entries.example_en: The tough-minded manager refused to ignore the budget cuts.

entries.definition_en: having a relatively tough outer covering
entries.example_cn: 外皮坚硬的仙人掌能在沙漠中生存。
entries.example_en: The tough-skinned cactus can survive in the desert.

entries.definition_en: insensitive to criticism
entries.example_cn: 他对批评不敏感，从不让负面评论困扰他。
entries.example_en: He is tough-skinned and never lets negative comments bother him.

entries.definition_en: to make something stronger, harder, or more resistant to damage
entries.example_cn: 严酷的冬季天气使钢梁变得更加强韧。
entries.example_en: The harsh winter weather toughened the steel beams.

entries.definition_en: a particularly difficult or baffling question or problem
entries.example_cn: 最后的考试题目对大多数学生来说真是个棘手的问题。
entries.example_en: The final exam question was a real toughie for most of the students.

entries.definition_cn: 强悍的人，尤指暴徒或恶霸
entries.definition_en: a tough person, especially a thug or bully
entries.example_cn: 警方正在追捕一名袭击店主的恶霸。
entries.example_en: The police were hunting for a toughie who had attacked the shopkeeper.

entries.definition_cn: 强壮而坚韧的人或事物
entries.definition_en: a strong and resilient person or thing
entries.example_cn: 这些坚韧的植物可以在没有水的情况下存活数周。
entries.example_en: These toughies can survive for weeks without water.

entries.definition_en: In a tough or forceful manner.
entries.example_cn: 这些通知措辞强硬。
entries.example_en: The notices were toughly worded.

entries.definition_cn: 忍耐艰难、痛苦或困境的能力；坚韧
entries.definition_en: the ability to endure hardship, pain, or difficult conditions
entries.example_cn: 球队在比赛最后几分钟展现了巨大的韧性。
entries.example_en: The team showed great toughness during the final minutes of the match.

entries.definition_en: the property of being big and strong
entries.example_cn: 摔跤手的强壮体格给评委留下了深刻印象。
entries.example_en: The wrestler's toughness impressed the judges.

entries.definition_en: the elasticity and hardness of a metal object; its ability to absorb considerable energy before cracking
entries.example_cn: 工程师测试了用于桥梁建设的钢材的韧性。
entries.example_en: Engineers tested the toughness of the steel used in the bridge construction.

entries.definition_en: impressive difficulty
entries.example_cn: 考试的难度让许多学生感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: The toughness of the exam surprised many students.

entries.definition_en: a small hairpiece worn to cover partial baldness
entries.example_cn: 他戴了一顶假发片来遮盖他稀疏的头发。
entries.example_en: He wore a toupee to hide his thinning hair.

entries.definition_en: a journey through or around a particular place or area
entries.example_cn: 他们去游览了这座古城。
entries.example_en: They went on a tour of the ancient city.

entries.definition_en: a time period for working (after which you will be relieved by someone else)
entries.example_cn: 这位护士正在值夜班。
entries.example_en: The nurse is on a night tour.

entries.definition_en: a period of time spent in military service
entries.example_cn: 他完成了在军队的服役期。
entries.example_en: He completed his tour in the army.

entries.definition_en: to make a tour of a certain place
entries.example_cn: 导游将带我们参观博物馆。
entries.example_en: The guide will tour the museum with us.

entries.definition_en: someone who travels for pleasure
entries.example_cn: 这家酒店为国际游客提供服务。
entries.example_en: The hotel caters to international tourers.

entries.definition_en: a large open car seating four with a folding top
entries.example_cn: 他开着他的古董敞篷轿车沿着海岸公路行驶。
entries.example_en: He drove his vintage tourer along the coastal road.

entries.definition_en: a bicycle designed for long-distance touring
entries.example_cn: 她骑旅行自行车进行长途骑行。
entries.example_en: She uses a tourer for long-distance rides.

entries.definition_en: the business of providing services to tourists
entries.example_cn: 当地经济严重依赖旅游业。
entries.example_en: The local economy relies heavily on tourism.

entries.definition_en: someone who travels for pleasure
entries.example_cn: 夏天这座城市挤满了游客。
entries.example_en: The city is full of tourists during the summer.

entries.definition_en: visited by large crowds of tourists
entries.example_cn: 假期里我们避开了主广场，因为那里游客太多。
entries.example_en: We avoided the main square because it was too touristy during the holidays.

entries.definition_en: a mineral that is a complex borosilicate and hydroxide of aluminum containing iron, magnesium, calcium, lithium, and sodium; it is usually black but occurs in transparent colored forms used as gemstones
entries.example_cn: 珠宝商将电气石切割成璀璨的宝石。
entries.example_en: The jeweler cut the tourmaline into a brilliant gemstone.

entries.definition_en: a sporting competition where players compete in a series of games to determine the winner
entries.example_cn: 网球锦标赛将于下个月举行。
entries.example_en: The tennis tournament will take place next month.

entries.definition_cn: （历史）骑士为争夺奖品而进行的一系列马上比武
entries.definition_en: (historical) a series of jousts between knights competing for a prize
entries.example_cn: 中世纪的比武大会展示了全副武装的骑士进行马上比武。
entries.example_en: The medieval tournament featured knights jousting in full armor.

entries.definition_en: a thick steak cut from the beef tenderloin
entries.example_cn: 厨师为晚餐客人准备了精致的菲力牛排。
entries.example_en: The chef prepared delicate tournedos for the dinner guests.

entries.definition_en: a sporting competition involving a series of games to determine a winner
entries.example_cn: 这场国际象棋锦标赛吸引了来自全国各地的选手。
entries.example_en: The chess tourney attracted players from all over the country.

entries.definition_en: to engage in a sporting competition
entries.example_cn: 他们决定参加当地的篮球联赛。
entries.example_en: They decided to tourney in the local basketball league.

entries.definition_en: a bandage that stops the flow of blood from an artery by applying pressure
entries.example_cn: 医护人员用止血带止住了出血。
entries.example_en: The medic applied a tourniquet to stop the bleeding.

entries.definition_en: to disarrange or rumple something
entries.example_cn: 风吹乱了她头发。
entries.example_en: The wind tousled her hair.

entries.definition_cn: 弄乱或拨乱某物（尤指头发）的动作
entries.definition_en: The act of ruffling or disarranging something, especially hair.
entries.example_cn: 她调皮地把他的头发揉乱了。
entries.example_en: She gave his hair a playful tousle.

entries.definition_en: in disarray; extremely disorderly
entries.example_cn: 她从暴风雨中醒来，头发凌乱不堪。
entries.example_en: She woke up with her hair tousled from the storm.

entries.definition_en: to advertise something in strongly positive terms
entries.example_cn: 许多评论家极力推销这部电影，称其为年度最佳影片。
entries.example_en: The movie was touted as the best film of the year by many critics.

entries.definition_en: to show off
entries.example_cn: 他试图向朋友们炫耀他的新车。
entries.example_en: He tried to tout his new car to his friends.

entries.definition_en: someone who buys tickets to resell them at a profit
entries.example_cn: 体育场里挤满了试图以高价出售门票的票贩子。
entries.example_en: The stadium was full of touts trying to sell tickets at high prices.

entries.definition_en: someone who advertises for customers in a brazen way
entries.example_cn: 一个拉客者在机场接近游客，提供虚假的旅游团。
entries.example_en: A tout approached the tourists at the airport offering fake tours.

entries.definition_cn: 赌马顾问；赛马信息贩子
entries.definition_en: a person who sells advice about gambling or speculation, especially at a racetrack
entries.example_cn: 赛马场的一名信息贩子兜售关于哪匹马可能获胜的建议。
entries.example_en: A tout at the racetrack sold advice about which horse was likely to win.

entries.definition_en: a comrade, particularly in the context of Russian communism
entries.example_cn: 工人们在开始轮班前互相称呼对方为“同志”。
entries.example_en: The workers greeted each other as tovarich before starting their shift.

entries.definition_en: drag behind
entries.example_cn: 我们将不得不把你的船拖到码头。
entries.example_en: We will have to tow your boat to the marina.

entries.definition_en: the act of hauling something (as a vehicle) by means of a hitch or rope
entries.example_cn: 卡车不得不把抛锚的汽车拖到最近的修理厂。
entries.example_en: The truck had to tow the broken-down car to the nearest garage.

entries.definition_en: the act of pulling a vehicle or object using a rope or hitch
entries.example_cn: 船上的船员对受损船只进行了拖曳。
entries.example_en: The ship's crew performed the towage of the disabled vessel.

entries.definition_en: in the direction of
entries.example_cn: 她走向门口。
entries.example_en: She walked toward the door.

entries.definition_en: in relation to someone or something
entries.example_cn: 你对他有什么看法？
entries.example_en: What are your feelings toward him?

entries.definition_en: located close to; near a time or place
entries.example_cn: 会议安排在月底。
entries.example_en: The meeting is scheduled toward the end of the month.

entries.definition_en: for the purpose of attaining an aim
entries.example_cn: 他们努力工作以实现目标。
entries.example_en: They worked hard toward their goal.

entries.definition_en: approaching, coming near; impending
entries.example_cn: 冬天即将来临。
entries.example_en: Winter is toward.

entries.definition_en: yielding, pliant; docile; ready to learn
entries.example_cn: 这孩子学新词很顺从。
entries.example_en: The child was toward in learning new words.

entries.definition_en: in the direction of something
entries.example_cn: 她走向出口。
entries.example_en: She walked towards the exit.

entries.definition_en: in the direction of something
entries.example_cn: 风朝大海吹去。
entries.example_en: The wind blew towards the sea.

entries.definition_cn: 临近的；正在准备中的；即将发生的（古旧用法）
entries.definition_en: near at hand or in preparation; about to happen (archaic)
entries.example_cn: 我们正准备一场微不足道而可笑的宴会。
entries.example_en: We have a trifling foolish banquet towards.

entries.definition_en: a powerful small boat designed to pull or push larger ships
entries.example_cn: 那艘拖船帮助那艘大型货船驶出了浅水区。
entries.example_en: The towboat helped the large cargo ship out of the shallow water.

entries.definition_en: a rectangular piece of cloth used for drying or wiping
entries.example_cn: 请带一条毛巾去游泳池。
entries.example_en: Please bring a towel to the pool.

entries.definition_en: to dry something with a towel
entries.example_cn: 淋浴后她用毛巾擦了脸。
entries.example_en: She towelled her face after the shower.

entries.definition_en: fabric made of linen or cotton used for making towels
entries.example_cn: 这家工厂专门生产用于豪华浴巾的高质量毛巾布。
entries.example_en: The factory specializes in high-quality toweling for luxury bath towels.

entries.definition_en: a fabric made of linen or cotton used for making towels
entries.example_cn: 客房为客人配备了新鲜的毛巾布。
entries.example_en: The hotel room was equipped with fresh towelling for the guests.

entries.definition_en: to appear very large or dominant
entries.example_cn: 这座摩天大楼高耸于周围的建筑之上。
entries.example_en: The skyscraper towers over the surrounding buildings.

entries.definition_en: extremely tall; standing much higher than other things
entries.example_cn: 那座高耸的摩天大楼主宰了城市的天际线。
entries.example_en: The towering skyscraper dominated the city skyline.

entries.definition_en: having hair that is very light in color, almost white
entries.example_cn: 那个浅金色头发的孩子在深色背景下格外显眼。
entries.example_en: The towheaded child stood out against the dark background.

entries.definition_en: any of several American sparrows of the genera Pipilo and Melozone
entries.example_cn: 这只唧鹀在清晨大声鸣叫。
entries.example_en: The towhee sang loudly in the morning.

entries.definition_en: a rope used to pull a ship or boat
entries.example_cn: 拖船使用粗重的拖缆将受损船只拖至安全地带。
entries.example_en: The tugboat used a heavy towline to pull the disabled vessel to safety.

entries.definition_en: an urban area with a fixed boundary that is smaller than a city
entries.example_cn: 我们开车去最近的城镇采购物资。
entries.example_en: We drove to the nearest town for supplies.

entries.definition_en: the people living in a municipality smaller than a city
entries.example_cn: 这个城镇以其友好的居民而闻名。
entries.example_en: The town is known for its friendly people.

entries.definition_en: an administrative division of a county
entries.example_cn: 他当选为该城镇的市长。
entries.example_en: He was elected mayor of the town.

entries.definition_en: a person from or living in a particular town
entries.example_cn: 作为一名城镇居民，他更喜欢公共交通而非乡村生活。
entries.example_en: As a towner, he prefers the convenience of public transport over the countryside.

entries.definition_cn: 与大学无关的大学城居民
entries.definition_en: a person who lives in a college town but is not a student or faculty member
entries.example_cn: 作为一名当地的非学院居民，我经常看着学生们在假期离开。
entries.example_en: As a local townie, I often watch the students leave for the holidays.

usage.label: UK, US
usage.pattern: a person living in a university area unaffiliated with it

entries.definition_en: a person who lives in the same town as the speaker
entries.example_cn: 在社区中心遇到一位同镇人真好。
entries.example_en: It was nice to meet a fellow townie at the community center.

entries.definition_en: people who live in a town
entries.example_cn: 城镇居民聚集在广场上庆祝节日。
entries.example_en: The townsfolk gathered in the square to celebrate the festival.

entries.definition_cn: （尤指加拿大或美国的）县下行政区
entries.definition_en: an administrative subdivision of a county, especially in Canada or the United States
entries.example_cn: 为了管理不断增长的人口，建立了新的行政区。
entries.example_en: The new township was established to manage the growing population.

entries.definition_en: a male resident of a town or city
entries.example_cn: 这位市民自愿帮忙清理公园。
entries.example_en: The townsman volunteered to help clean up the park.

entries.definition_en: a male person from the same town as yourself
entries.example_cn: 作为一名自豪的同乡，他支持当地的足球队。
entries.example_en: As a proud townsman, he supported the local football team.

entries.definition_en: a resident of a town
entries.example_cn: 这位城镇居民参加了当地议会会议。
entries.example_en: The townsperson attended the local council meeting.

entries.definition_cn: 大学城居民（非学院成员）
entries.definition_en: a person who lives in a college town but is not a member of the college
entries.example_cn: 这位大学城居民每天早上走过校园大门。
entries.example_en: The towny walked past the campus gates every morning.

entries.definition_cn: 运河或河流旁供动物拉船行走的小路
entries.definition_en: a path alongside a canal or river used by animals to tow boats
entries.example_cn: 马匹沿着小路行走，拉着驳船穿过运河。
entries.example_en: Horses walked along the towpath pulling the barges through the canal.

entries.definition_en: a condition where the blood is poisoned by bacterial toxins
entries.example_cn: 患者因感染导致严重的毒血症被送进医院。
entries.example_en: The patient was admitted to the hospital with severe toxemia caused by an infection.

entries.definition_en: a pregnancy complication involving high blood pressure and protein in the urine
entries.example_cn: 医生警告说，未治疗的妊娠毒血症对母婴都可能很危险。
entries.example_en: The doctor warned that untreated toxemia could be dangerous for both mother and baby.

entries.definition_cn: 极其负面的；有害的（比喻）
entries.definition_en: Severely negative or harmful, especially in its effects on people or situations.
entries.example_cn: 这家公司给员工造成了有害的工作环境。
entries.example_en: The company created a toxic environment for its employees.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to or caused by a toxin or poison
entries.example_cn: 该工厂因向河流排放有毒废物而被罚款。
entries.example_en: The factory was fined for releasing toxic waste into the river.

entries.definition_en: a substance that causes harm, illness, or death to living organisms
entries.example_cn: 政府禁止在农产品中使用这种有毒物质。
entries.example_en: The government banned the use of this toxicant in agricultural products.

entries.definition_en: having the qualities or effects of a poison
entries.example_cn: 有毒气体使几个人立刻病倒了。
entries.example_en: The toxicant fumes caused several people to fall ill immediately.

entries.definition_en: the quality or degree of being poisonous
entries.example_cn: 该化学物质的毒性已在实验动物身上进行了测试。
entries.example_en: The toxicity of the chemical was tested on laboratory animals.

entries.definition_en: extreme harmfulness or deadliness
entries.example_cn: 局势的致命性使得谈判和平条约变得不可能。
entries.example_en: The toxicity of the situation made it impossible to negotiate a peace treaty.

entries.definition_en: relating to the study of poisons and their effects
entries.example_cn: 土壤的毒理学分析显示重金属含量很高。
entries.example_en: The toxicologic analysis of the soil revealed high levels of heavy metals.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to toxicology
entries.example_cn: 毒理学分析证实了毒物的存在。
entries.example_en: The toxicological analysis confirmed the presence of the poison.

entries.definition_en: a scientist who studies the nature and effects of poisons and their treatment
entries.example_cn: 毒理学家分析了样本以确定死因。
entries.example_en: The toxicologist analyzed the sample to determine the cause of death.

entries.definition_en: the branch of pharmacology concerned with the nature, effects, detection, and treatment of poisons and poisoning
entries.example_cn: 医生咨询了一位毒理学专家以确定中毒的原因。
entries.example_en: The doctor consulted a toxicology expert to determine the cause of the poisoning.

entries.definition_en: a poisonous substance produced during the metabolism and growth of certain microorganisms and some higher plant and animal species
entries.example_cn: 蛇咬将一种强效毒素释放到受害者的血液中。
entries.example_en: The snakebite released a powerful toxin into the victim's bloodstream.

entries.definition_en: a weakened form of a bacterial toxin used in vaccines to stimulate the immune system without causing disease
entries.example_cn: 破伤风类毒素是许多儿童免疫计划中的关键组成部分。
entries.example_en: The tetanus toxoid is a key component of many childhood immunization schedules.

entries.definition_cn: 由刚地弓形虫引起的感染，主要影响猫科动物，也可感染包括人在内的其他哺乳动物
entries.definition_en: an infection caused by the parasite Toxoplasma gondii, primarily affecting cats but also other mammals, including humans
entries.example_cn: 建议孕妇避免接触猫砂，以防感染弓形虫病。
entries.example_en: Pregnant women are advised to avoid contact with cat litter to prevent toxoplasmosis.

entries.definition_en: an object designed for play
entries.example_cn: 孩子玩了一个新玩具。
entries.example_en: The child played with a new toy.

entries.definition_cn: 非功能性的仿制品；玩具（常作定语）
entries.definition_en: a nonfunctional replica of something, often used attributively
entries.example_cn: 这辆模型车是真实车辆的玩具版。
entries.example_en: The model car is a toy version of the real vehicle.

entries.definition_cn: 被视为供消遣、无关紧要或非必需的装置；玩意儿
entries.definition_en: a gadget regarded as an amusing, frivolous, or nonessential device
entries.example_cn: 他把最新款智能手机当成昂贵的玩意儿。
entries.example_en: He treats the latest smartphone as an expensive toy.

entries.definition_en: to treat someone or something casually, carelessly, or manipulatively
entries.example_cn: 她玩弄了他的感情。
entries.example_en: She toyed with his feelings.

entries.definition_cn: 心不在焉地摆弄或把玩某物
entries.definition_en: to handle or fiddle with something absent-mindedly
entries.example_cn: 她摆弄着口袋里的钥匙。
entries.example_en: She toyed with the keys in her pocket.

entries.definition_en: to treat something as a game rather than seriously
entries.example_cn: 他们把建造房子的想法当作儿戏。
entries.example_en: They toyed with the concept of building a house.

usage.label: toy with + noun
usage.pattern: w03273r4 supports the construction for casual consideration.

entries.definition_en: a small-scale copy of a person or thing
entries.example_cn: 博物馆展示了一座古代雕像的微缩模型。
entries.example_en: The museum displays a toy of the ancient statue.

entries.definition_en: a breed of very small dog kept as a pet
entries.example_cn: 玩具贵宾犬是一种受欢迎的宠物。
entries.example_en: The toy poodle is a popular pet.

entries.definition_en: the act of playing with or treating something lightly
entries.example_cn: 他反复拿辞职的想法开玩笑，让同事们很恼火。
entries.example_en: His toying with the idea of resigning frustrated his colleagues.

entries.definition_cn: 一种原产于美国太平洋沿岸的观赏常绿灌木，开大朵白花，结红色浆果状果实
entries.definition_en: an ornamental evergreen shrub native to the Pacific coast of the United States with large white flowers and red berrylike fruits
entries.example_cn: 这种灌木在深秋时节结出红色的浆果，为景观增添了鲜艳的色彩。
entries.example_en: The toyon shrub adds vibrant color to the landscape with its red berries in late autumn.

entries.definition_en: a shop that sells toys
entries.example_cn: 我们在街角的玩具店买了一个新洋娃娃。
entries.example_en: We bought a new doll at the toyshop on the corner.

entries.definition_en: nonsense sounds made while singing or humming
entries.example_cn: 孩子们唱了一首带有衬词的快乐歌曲。
entries.example_en: The children sang a happy song with a tra-la refrain.

entries.definition_en: a set of nonsensical syllables used while humming a refrain
entries.example_cn: 孩子们跟着歌曲的曲调唱起了“特拉拉拉”。
entries.example_en: The children sang 'tra-la-la' to the tune of the song.

entries.definition_en: of or relating to trabeculae
entries.example_cn: 医生检查了患者扫描结果中的小梁骨结构。
entries.example_en: The doctor examined the trabecular bone structure in the patient's scan.

entries.definition_en: follow, discover, or ascertain the course of development of something
entries.example_cn: 警方正试图追踪被盗的款项。
entries.example_en: Police are trying to trace the stolen money.

entries.definition_en: follow the trail of a person or thing
entries.example_cn: 侦探在城市里穷追不舍地追捕嫌疑人。
entries.example_en: The detective traced the suspect across the city.
