entries.example_en: A whisper of wind rustled the leaves.

entries.definition_en: a person who speaks in a very low voice
entries.example_cn: 低语者凑近耳朵分享秘密。
entries.example_en: The whisperer leaned close to the ear to share the secret.

entries.definition_en: the act of speaking very softly without vibrating the vocal cords
entries.example_cn: 她的耳语声很轻，我几乎听不见。
entries.example_en: Her whispering was so quiet that I could barely hear it.

entries.definition_en: a light noise, like the noise of silk clothing or leaves blowing in the wind
entries.example_cn: 风穿过树林发出的沙沙声令人舒缓。
entries.example_en: The whispering of the wind through the trees was soothing.

entries.definition_en: making a low continuous indistinct sound
entries.example_cn: 公告发布时，窃窃私语的人群声音越来越大。
entries.example_en: The whispering crowd grew louder as the announcement was made.

entries.definition_en: a card game for four players in two partnerships where points are scored for tricks won over six
entries.example_cn: 他们晚上在壁炉旁玩惠斯特牌戏。
entries.example_en: They spent the evening playing whist by the fireplace.

entries.definition_en: to make a high-pitched whistling sound with your mouth
entries.example_cn: 她边走边吹着一支欢快的曲子。
entries.example_en: She whistled a cheerful tune while walking home.

entries.definition_en: to move quickly making a whistling sound
entries.example_cn: 箭从他耳边呼啸而过。
entries.example_en: The arrow whistled past his ear.

entries.definition_en: to send, signal, or call by whistling
entries.example_cn: 他吹口哨把狗召了回来。
entries.example_en: He whistled the dog back.

entries.definition_en: a high-pitched sound made by air or steam moving quickly through a small opening
entries.example_cn: 火车的汽笛声非常响亮。
entries.example_en: The whistle of the train was very loud.

entries.definition_en: a small instrument that makes a whistling sound when you blow into it
entries.example_cn: 他为孩子们的游戏买了一个塑料口哨。
entries.example_en: He bought a plastic whistle for the children's game.

entries.definition_en: the act of using a whistle to signal or summon someone
entries.example_cn: 裁判吹哨结束了比赛。
entries.example_en: The referee blew the whistle to end the match.

entries.definition_en: to express something by whistling
entries.example_cn: 他们在体育场用口哨唱了国歌。
entries.example_en: They whistled the national anthem at the stadium.

entries.definition_en: a device that produces a loud shrill sound by forcing air or steam against an edge
entries.example_cn: 船的汽笛发出了警告声。
entries.example_en: The ship's whistle sounded the warning.

entries.definition_en: a person who reveals illegal or unethical activities within an organization
entries.example_cn: 这位告密者提供的证据促成了公司的调查。
entries.example_en: The whistle-blower provided evidence that led to the company's investigation.

entries.definition_en: an informant who exposes wrongdoing within an organization in the hope of stopping it
entries.example_cn: 这位吹哨人向当局揭露了公司的非法行为。
entries.example_en: The whistleblower revealed the company's illegal practices to the authorities.

entries.definition_en: someone who makes a loud high sound
entries.example_cn: 那个吹口哨的人吹了一段曲子来向队伍发出信号。
entries.example_en: The whistler blew a tune to signal the team.

entries.definition_en: a whistling marmot (Marmota caligata)
entries.example_cn: 我们在岩石平台上发现了一只哨声旱獭。
entries.example_en: We spotted a whistler resting on the rocky ledge.

entries.definition_en: a goldeneye, a diving duck of the genus Bucephala
entries.example_cn: 白额潜鸭潜入冰冷的水中捕鱼。
entries.example_en: The whistler dove into the icy water to catch fish.

entries.definition_cn: 啸鹟属或相关属的一种澳大拉西亚啸鸟
entries.definition_en: an Australasian whistler bird of the genera Pachycephala or Coracornis
entries.example_cn: 啸鸭在森林中唱出了清脆的歌。
entries.example_en: The whistler sang a clear song in the forest.

entries.definition_en: tour the country in order to solicit votes for an election
entries.example_cn: 这位候选人下周将巡回竞选整个州。
entries.example_en: The candidate will whistlestop the entire state next week.

entries.definition_en: the action of making a musical sound with your lips to imitate a song or tune
entries.example_cn: 他花了一下午坐在长椅上，吹着一首欢快的曲子。
entries.example_en: He spent the afternoon sitting on the bench, whistling a cheerful tune.

entries.definition_en: the act of using a whistle to send a signal, such as calling someone over
entries.example_cn: 裁判忙着吹哨开始和停止比赛。
entries.example_en: The referee was busy whistling to start and stop the match.

entries.definition_en: a high-pitched sound produced by air moving quickly through a narrow opening or by something moving fast
entries.example_cn: 风很大，穿过树林时发出了呼啸声。
entries.example_en: The wind was so strong that it created a loud whistling sound through the trees.

entries.definition_en: a tiny or scarcely detectable amount
entries.example_cn: 没有任何证据支持他的说法。
entries.example_en: There was not a whit of evidence to support his claim.

entries.definition_en: having the color that is the lightest and has no hue
entries.example_cn: 她穿着一件白色的连衣裙。
entries.example_en: She is wearing a white dress.

entries.definition_en: of or belonging to a group of people with light skin
entries.example_cn: 白人在一些国家的人口占很大比例。
entries.example_en: White people make up a large part of the population in some countries.

entries.definition_en: the color that is the lightest and has no hue
entries.example_cn: 房间以白色装饰。
entries.example_en: The room was decorated in white.

entries.definition_en: the clear liquid part of an egg
entries.example_cn: 鸡蛋的蛋白适合用来烘焙。
entries.example_en: The white of the egg is good for baking.

entries.definition_en: the lighter pieces in a board game
entries.example_cn: 轮到白棋走了。
entries.example_en: It is white's turn to move.

entries.definition_en: to make white; to whiten or bleach
entries.example_cn: 工人们用石灰把墙刷白了。
entries.example_en: The workers whited the walls with lime.

entries.definition_en: free from moral blemish or impurity
entries.example_cn: 她的品格像雪一样纯洁。
entries.example_en: Her character is as white as snow.

entries.definition_cn: 白色裤子（尤指法兰绒、华达呢或粗花呢等面料的）
entries.definition_en: white trousers, especially those made of flannel, gabardine, tweed, or similar cloth
entries.example_cn: 他穿着白裤子去参加婚礼。
entries.example_en: He wore his whites to the wedding.

entries.definition_cn: 白人中产阶级生活方式的；传统而保守的
entries.definition_en: relating to a conventional, often conservative white middle-class lifestyle or outlook
entries.example_cn: 这本杂志常因其传统保守的白人中产阶级价值观而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The magazine is often criticized for its white-bread values.

entries.definition_en: relating to professional or clerical work that is paid by salary
entries.example_cn: 她从事会计工作，这是一份白领工作。
entries.example_en: She works in a white-collar job as an accountant.

entries.definition_en: having grey or white hair, showing signs of age
entries.example_cn: 那位白发苍苍的老人讲述了过去的故事。
entries.example_en: The white-haired elder told stories of the old days.

entries.definition_en: favorite
entries.example_cn: 那只白毛狗是家人最喜爱的伴侣。
entries.example_en: The white-haired dog was the family's favorite companion.

entries.definition_en: glowing white due to extreme heat
entries.example_cn: 金属在火中变得白炽。
entries.example_en: The metal became white-hot in the fire.

entries.definition_en: intensely zealous or fervid
entries.example_cn: 人群因兴奋而极度狂热。
entries.example_en: The crowd was white-hot with excitement.

entries.definition_cn: 因大雾、大雪或大雨而变得模糊不清
entries.definition_en: to become obscured so that visibility is lost because of heavy fog, snow, or rain
entries.example_cn: 在大雪中，司机的视线开始变得白茫茫一片。
entries.example_en: The driver's vision began to white out in the heavy snow.

entries.definition_cn: 美国非正式用语，与美国传统精英阶层或保守派的机构、公司或律师事务所有关的
entries.definition_en: U.S. informal, associated with an established, traditionally elite or conservative U.S. institution, company, or law firm
entries.example_cn: 这家精英律师事务所处理了这起轰动一时的案件。
entries.example_en: The white-shoe firm handled the high-profile case.

entries.definition_en: requiring men to wear white ties and tailcoats
entries.example_cn: 那场正式晚宴是要求穿白领结的场合。
entries.example_en: The formal dinner was a white-tie event.

entries.definition_en: small fish, especially herring, that are often eaten whole after cooking
entries.example_cn: 我们把白鲱鱼裹上面糊炸着吃，当作小吃。
entries.example_en: We fried the whitebait in batter for a light snack.

entries.definition_en: the young of certain fish, such as herring or sprat, used as food
entries.example_cn: 白鲱鱼是许多沿海地区的传统美食。
entries.example_en: Whitebait is a traditional delicacy in many coastal regions.

entries.definition_en: a wave that is blown by the wind so its crest is broken and appears white
entries.example_cn: 随着风势增大，船只在白浪上颠簸。
entries.example_en: The boat bounced over the whitecaps as the wind picked up.

entries.definition_en: a clown whose face is painted white
entries.example_cn: 当白脸小丑进入马戏团帐篷时，孩子们欢呼起来。
entries.example_en: The children cheered when the whiteface clown entered the circus tent.

entries.definition_en: a breed of hardy English cattle raised in the United States
entries.example_cn: 美国中部的农民经常饲养白脸牛以获取牛肉。
entries.example_en: Farmers in the Midwest often raise whiteface cattle for their meat.

entries.definition_cn: 使脸部呈白色的化妆；白脸妆。
entries.definition_en: Makeup used to make the face appear white.
entries.example_cn: 哑剧演员上台前化了白脸妆。
entries.example_en: The mime applied whiteface before going on stage.

entries.definition_cn: 北半球冷湖中银色的鲱鱼状淡水食用鱼
entries.definition_en: a silvery herring-like freshwater food fish found in cold lakes of the Northern Hemisphere
entries.example_cn: 他们在冰冷的北方湖泊中钓到了一条大白鱼。
entries.example_en: They caught a large whitefish swimming in the icy northern lake.

entries.definition_cn: 北半球冷湖中鲑鱼或鳟鱼状冷水鱼的肉
entries.definition_en: the flesh of salmon-like or trout-like cold-water fish found in Northern Hemisphere lakes
entries.example_cn: 白鱼肉是传统斯堪的纳维亚菜肴中的流行食材。
entries.example_en: Whitefish is a popular ingredient in traditional Scandinavian cuisine.

entries.definition_cn: 非鲱鱼的食用咸水鱼或贝类
entries.definition_en: a market fish that is an edible saltwater fish or shellfish, excluding herring
entries.example_cn: 厨师为海鲜拼盘挑选了一条新鲜的白鱼。
entries.example_en: The chef selected a fresh whitefish for the seafood platter.

entries.definition_en: to fish for whitefish
entries.example_cn: 晚饭后，他们去湖上捕捞白鱼。
entries.example_en: They went whitefishing on the lake after supper.

entries.definition_en: a tiny insect that feeds on plant sap
entries.example_cn: 粉虱的侵害损害了番茄植株。
entries.example_en: The whitefly infestation damaged the tomato plants.

entries.definition_en: a small whitish plug clogging a pore of the skin
entries.example_cn: 她涂抹了一种特殊药膏来治疗她的白头粉刺。
entries.example_en: She applied a special cream to treat her whiteheads.

entries.definition_en: to become white or make something white
entries.example_cn: 随着风暴加剧，雪开始将大地染成白色。
entries.example_en: The snow began to whiten the landscape as the storm intensified.

entries.definition_en: a substance used to make something white or whiter
entries.example_cn: 洗衣液中含有漂白剂，以保持衣物洁白。
entries.example_en: The laundry detergent contains a whitener to keep clothes bright.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being the lightest color, having no hue
entries.example_cn: 雪的白色刺得徒步者睁不开眼。
entries.example_en: The whiteness of the snow blinded the hikers.

entries.definition_en: having a light or pale complexion
entries.example_cn: 她白皙的肤色与黑土形成了鲜明对比。
entries.example_en: The whiteness of her skin contrasted with the dark soil.

entries.definition_en: the state of being free from sin or moral corruption
entries.example_cn: 她灵魂的纯洁在她慷慨的行为中显而易见。
entries.example_en: Her whiteness of soul was evident in her generous actions.

entries.definition_en: the process of becoming or making something lighter in color
entries.example_cn: 雪变白后，群山显得更加雄伟。
entries.example_en: The whitening of the snow made the mountains look even more majestic.

entries.definition_en: an arctic condition where clouds and snow create a uniform whiteness, making objects hard to see
entries.example_cn: 飞行员们因突然出现的白茫而不得不提前降落。
entries.example_en: The pilots had to land early due to a sudden whiteout.

entries.definition_cn: 使（视线）因浓雾、降雪或暴雨而完全受阻
entries.definition_en: to make visibility impossible or severely reduced with heavy fog, snow, or rain
entries.example_cn: 大雪很快使道路完全无法看清。
entries.example_en: The heavy snow quickly whited out the road.

entries.definition_en: to cover something with liquid correction fluid
entries.example_cn: 她用涂改液涂掉试卷上的错误，然后写下了正确答案。
entries.example_en: She whited out the mistake on her exam paper and wrote the correct answer.

entries.definition_en: a common North American deer with a white underside on its tail
entries.example_cn: 我们在森林里发现了一只白尾鹿。
entries.example_en: We spotted a whitetail deer in the forest.

entries.definition_cn: 单柱山楂；一种原产于欧洲、西北非和西亚的带刺灌木或小乔木
entries.definition_en: Crataegus monogyna, a thorny shrub or small tree native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia
entries.example_cn: 花园里的单柱山楂篱笆为许多鸟类提供了庇护。
entries.example_en: The whitethorn hedge provided shelter for many birds in the garden.

entries.definition_en: a common Old World warbler (Sylvia communis) with greyish-brown plumage and a white throat and underparts
entries.example_cn: 迁徙期间，我们看到几只白喉林莺飞过沼泽。
entries.example_en: During migration, we saw several whitethroats flying over the marsh.

entries.definition_en: a small Old World warbler similar to the greater whitethroat but smaller
entries.example_cn: 鸟类学家发现一只白喉林莺栖息在老橡树上。
entries.example_en: The ornithologist spotted a whitethroat perched on the old oak tree.

entries.definition_en: a North American sparrow with a white throat patch and a black-and-white striped crown
entries.example_cn: 花园里的白喉带鹀在清晨大声鸣唱。
entries.example_en: The whitethroat in the garden was singing loudly in the morning.

entries.definition_cn: 掩盖过失、错误或不当行为
entries.definition_en: cover up a misdemeanor, fault, or error
entries.example_cn: 这项调查被指责掩盖了腐败丑闻。
entries.example_en: The investigation was accused of whitewashing the corruption scandal.

entries.definition_cn: 通过敷衍的调查或有偏见的资料呈现来为……开脱
entries.definition_en: exonerate by means of a perfunctory investigation or through biased presentation of data
entries.example_cn: 批评人士认为，该调查为官员的不当行为开脱。
entries.example_en: Critics argued that the inquiry whitewashed the officials' misconduct.

entries.definition_en: cover with whitewash
entries.example_cn: 他们在夏季节日之前用石灰浆粉刷了栅栏。
entries.example_en: They whitewashed the fence before the summer festival.

entries.definition_cn: 一种虚伪或欺骗性的澄清，试图掩盖缺点和缺陷
entries.definition_en: a specious or deceptive clearing that attempts to gloss over failings and defects
entries.example_cn: 这份报告不过是掩盖公司失败的一种虚伪澄清。
entries.example_en: The report was nothing more than a whitewash of the company's failures.

entries.definition_cn: 一场使失败者一分未得的惨败
entries.definition_en: a defeat in which the losing person or team fails to score
entries.example_cn: 球队在决赛中遭遇了5比0的零封惨败。
entries.example_en: The team suffered a 5–0 whitewash in the final.

entries.definition_cn: 石灰和浆糊的水溶液；用于使墙壁和其他表面变白
entries.definition_en: wash consisting of lime and size in water; used for whitening walls and other surfaces
entries.example_cn: 那座老房子涂了一层厚厚的石灰浆。
entries.example_en: The old house was painted with a thick layer of whitewash.

entries.definition_cn: 掩盖、忽视或淡化争议或丑闻的
entries.definition_en: presented in a way that hides, ignores, or minimizes controversy or scandal
entries.example_cn: 这份报告掩盖并淡化了公司的财务问题。
entries.example_en: The report gave a whitewashed account of the company's financial problems.

entries.definition_en: covered with a mixture of lime and water used for painting walls
entries.example_cn: 那座老农舍有着涂白石灰的墙壁和茅草屋顶。
entries.example_en: The old cottage had whitewashed walls and a thatched roof.

entries.definition_cn: 因种族漂白而被塑造成白人形象或显得更白的
entries.definition_en: portrayed as white or made to appear whiter through racial whitewashing
entries.example_cn: 这部电影因将一位非白人历史人物漂白成白人形象而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The film was criticized for its whitewashed portrayal of a nonwhite historical figure.

entries.definition_en: water that is foamy and turbulent, such as in rapids or waterfalls
entries.example_cn: 漂流者兴奋地冲过白浪激流。
entries.example_en: The rafters bounced over the whitewater with excitement.

entries.definition_cn: 郁金香树的质地轻、易加工的木材，用于家具和贴面
entries.definition_en: lightweight, easily worked wood of a tulip tree, used for furniture and veneer
entries.example_cn: 这张古董桌是用优质的白木制成的。
entries.example_en: The antique table was crafted from fine whitewood.

entries.definition_cn: 尚未完成最终美术设计的弹珠台原型
entries.definition_en: a prototype pinball table without its final artwork
entries.example_cn: 设计看起来令人满意后，这台未完成美术设计的弹珠台原型会接上线，使其可以进行游戏。
entries.example_en: When the design seems satisfactory, the whitewood is wired to make it playable.

entries.definition_cn: 对白人的冒犯性俚语称呼
entries.definition_en: an offensive slang term for a white person
entries.example_cn: 指南指出，whitey 是对白人的冒犯性蔑称。
entries.example_en: The guide identifies whitey as an offensive slur for a white person.

entries.definition_cn: 欧洲鳕形鱼（一种类似鳕鱼的鱼）的鱼肉
entries.definition_en: the flesh of the European whiting, a cod-like fish of the North Atlantic
entries.example_cn: 欧洲鳕形鱼的鱼肉是传统欧洲鱼派中很受欢迎的食材。
entries.example_en: Whiting is a popular ingredient in traditional European fish pies.

entries.definition_cn: 北美沿海某些细长海产食用鱼的鱼肉
entries.definition_en: the flesh of certain slender marine food fishes of North American coastal waters
entries.example_cn: 这家餐厅供应在海岸附近捕获的新鲜鱼肉。
entries.example_en: The restaurant serves fresh whiting caught off the coast.

entries.definition_cn: 欧洲鳕形鱼（一种类似鳕鱼的北大西洋食用鱼）
entries.definition_en: the European whiting, a cod-like food fish of the North Atlantic
entries.example_cn: 烹饪时，欧洲鳕形鱼常被用作鳕鱼的替代品。
entries.example_en: Whiting is often used as a substitute for cod in cooking.

entries.definition_cn: 北美沿海水域的几种海产食用鱼
entries.definition_en: any of several marine food fishes of North American coastal waters
entries.example_cn: 当地渔民常在春季捕获这种鱼。
entries.example_en: Local fishermen often catch whiting in the spring.

entries.definition_en: a food fish of the family Sillaginidae (smelt-whitings)
entries.example_cn: 鱚科的鱼类因其细腻的风味和口感而备受珍视。
entries.example_en: Whiting species in the family Sillaginidae are valued for their delicate flavor and texture.

entries.definition_cn: 北美大西洋沿岸的一种鱼
entries.definition_en: a fish found off the Atlantic coast of North America
entries.example_cn: 近年来，这种鱼的种群数量有所增加。
entries.example_en: The whiting population has increased in recent years.

entries.definition_en: having a color that tends toward white
entries.example_cn: 那张旧纸泛白。
entries.example_en: The old paper has a whitish tint.

entries.definition_en: having a color similar to milk; opaque white
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨来临前，天空变成了乳白色。
entries.example_en: The sky turned a whitish color before the storm.

entries.definition_en: a purulent infection at the end of a finger or toe in the area surrounding the nail
entries.example_cn: 医生用抗生素治疗了他的甲沟脓疱。
entries.example_en: The doctor treated his whitlow with antibiotics.

entries.definition_en: cut small bits or pare shavings from
entries.example_cn: 她坐在火炉旁，将一块木头削成了一只小鸟。
entries.example_en: She sat by the fire and whittled a piece of wood into a small bird.

entries.definition_cn: 逐步减少或消除（债务等）
entries.definition_en: to reduce or gradually eliminate something, such as a debt
entries.example_cn: 这家公司通过出售闲置房产逐步减少债务。
entries.example_en: The company is whittling down its debt by selling unused properties.

entries.definition_en: someone who is dazzlingly skilled in any field
entries.example_cn: 她是数学方面的专家。
entries.example_en: She is a real whiz at mathematics.

entries.definition_en: a buzzing or hissing sound as of something traveling rapidly through the air
entries.example_cn: 门打开时，一阵嗖嗖的风声传来。
entries.example_en: There was a whiz of wind as the door opened.

entries.definition_en: make a soft swishing sound
entries.example_cn: 箭从他耳边嗖嗖地飞过。
entries.example_en: The arrow whizzed past his ear.

entries.definition_cn: 聪明能干且事业发展迅速的年轻人
entries.definition_en: a clever or successful young person whose career progresses rapidly
entries.example_cn: 公司聘请了一位事业飞速发展的年轻人来领导新项目。
entries.example_en: The company hired a whiz-kid to lead the new project.

entries.definition_en: a small high-velocity shell that makes a whizzing sound before exploding
entries.example_cn: 士兵们听到啸叫弹呼啸而过，随后击中目标。
entries.example_en: The soldiers heard the whizbang whizz past before it hit the target.

entries.definition_en: a firecracker that makes a whizzing sound followed by a loud explosion
entries.example_cn: 孩子们点燃了啸叫爆竹，然后迅速跑开。
entries.example_en: Children lit the whizbang and ran away quickly.

entries.definition_en: move along very quickly
entries.example_cn: 那辆车在高速公路上飞驰，超速行驶。
entries.example_en: The car whizzed down the highway, breaking the speed limit.

entries.definition_en: make a soft swishing sound
entries.example_cn: 他躲闪时，箭从他耳边嗖嗖地飞过。
entries.example_en: The arrow whizzed past his ear as he dodged.

entries.definition_en: someone who is dazzlingly skilled in any field
entries.example_cn: 这位年轻科学家是量子物理方面的天才。
entries.example_en: The young scientist is a whizz at quantum physics.

entries.definition_en: used to ask about a person's identity
entries.example_cn: 那个男人是谁？
entries.example_en: Who is that man?

entries.definition_cn: 用于引导以人为先行词且 who 在从句中作主语的关系从句
entries.definition_en: used to introduce a relative clause with a person as its antecedent, where who is the subject
entries.example_cn: 住在隔壁的那个人是一名医生。
entries.example_en: The man who lives next door is a doctor.

entries.definition_en: whoever; the person or people who
entries.example_cn: 谁努力，谁通常就会成功。
entries.example_en: Who works hard usually succeeds.

entries.definition_cn: 用于指代集体名词（如乐队或球队）的代词
entries.definition_en: Used with names of collective nouns for groups of people, such as musical groups or sports teams.
entries.example_cn: 披头士乐队是谁？
entries.example_en: Who are the Beatles?

entries.definition_en: a person who is being talked about or asked about
entries.example_cn: 我不知道门口是谁。
entries.example_en: I don't know who is at the door.

entries.definition_cn: （方言）谁的；用于名词前询问所属关系
entries.definition_en: a dialectal form of whose, used before a noun to ask about possession
entries.example_cn: 刚才响的是谁的电话？
entries.example_en: Who phone just rang?

entries.definition_cn: 侦探故事（小说、戏剧或电影）
entries.definition_en: a mystery story about a crime, usually murder, where the reader tries to guess who the criminal is
entries.example_cn: 这部侦探小说让我们一直猜到最后才揭晓谜底。
entries.example_en: The whodunit kept us guessing until the very last page.

entries.definition_en: The person that (no matter who).
entries.example_cn: 无论谁赢得选举，都将面临艰难的决定。
entries.example_en: Whoever wins the election will face tough decisions.

entries.definition_en: Any person or persons that.
entries.example_cn: 任何违反规则的人都将受到惩罚。
entries.example_en: Whoever breaks the rules will be punished.

entries.definition_en: Regardless of the person or persons that.
entries.example_cn: 无论你问谁，都会告诉你同样的故事。
entries.example_en: Whoever you ask will tell you the same story.

entries.definition_en: Any person or persons.
entries.example_cn: 无论谁负责，都必须站出来。
entries.example_en: Whoever is responsible must come forward.

entries.definition_cn: who 的强调形式，用于疑问句
entries.definition_en: An emphatic form of who, used in questions.
entries.example_cn: 究竟是谁想出了那个愚蠢的主意？
entries.example_en: Whoever thought up that stupid idea?

entries.definition_en: including all components without exception; being one unit or constituting the full amount or extent or duration; complete
entries.example_cn: 她一个人吃掉了整个蛋糕。
entries.example_en: She ate the whole cake by herself.

entries.definition_en: acting together as a single unit.
entries.example_cn: 全队团结一致赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: The team worked as a whole to win the game.

entries.definition_en: not injured or harmed
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，这座建筑仍然完好无损。
entries.example_en: The building remained whole after the storm.

entries.definition_en: all of something including all its component elements or parts
entries.example_cn: 在做决定之前，我们需要考虑整体。
entries.example_en: We need to consider the whole before making a decision.

entries.definition_en: an assemblage of parts that is regarded as a single entity
entries.example_cn: 这辆车是由许多部件组成的复杂整体。
entries.example_en: The car is a complex whole made of many parts.

entries.definition_en: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent; Completely or entirely
entries.example_cn: 她把整块蛋糕完整地吃了下去。
entries.example_en: She ate the cake whole.

entries.definition_en: restored to good health.
entries.example_cn: 休息了一周后，他又感觉恢复了健康。
entries.example_en: After a week of rest, he felt whole again.

entries.definition_cn: （兄弟姐妹）同父同母的；不是同父异母或同母异父的
entries.definition_en: (of siblings) having the same biological parents; not half siblings
entries.example_cn: 他们是同父同母的兄弟姐妹，不是同父异母或同母异父的兄弟姐妹。
entries.example_en: They are whole siblings, not half siblings.

entries.definition_en: with unconditional and enthusiastic devotion
entries.example_cn: 她全心全意地支持这个慈善项目。
entries.example_en: She gave whole-souled support to the charity project.

entries.definition_en: made from wheat that includes the entire grain
entries.example_cn: 我们早餐吃全麦面包。
entries.example_en: We eat whole-wheat bread for breakfast.

entries.definition_en: showing unconditional and enthusiastic devotion
entries.example_cn: 她全心全意地欢迎新客人。
entries.example_en: She gave a wholehearted welcome to the new guests.

entries.definition_en: without reserve or reservation; completely
entries.example_cn: 她全心全意地支持这一新举措。
entries.example_en: She wholeheartedly supported the new initiative.

entries.definition_en: made from whole wheat, including the bran
entries.example_cn: 她更喜欢全麦面包，因为它更有营养。
entries.example_en: She prefers wholemeal bread for its nutritional value.

entries.definition_en: the state of being complete and undivided
entries.example_cn: 这位艺术家试图在一幅画中捕捉到整个景观的完整性。
entries.example_en: The artist sought to capture the wholeness of the landscape in a single painting.

entries.definition_en: a state of being in excellent health
entries.example_cn: 经过几个月的康复，她恢复了健康，重返工作岗位。
entries.example_en: After months of recovery, she regained her wholeness and returned to work.

entries.definition_en: to sell goods in large quantities to merchants
entries.example_cn: 他们决定将库存批发给当地经销商。
entries.example_en: They decided to wholesale their inventory to a local distributor.

entries.definition_en: the business of selling goods in large quantities to merchants for resale
entries.example_cn: 这家公司专门从事电子产品批发。
entries.example_en: The company specializes in the wholesale of electronics.

entries.definition_en: at a wholesale price
entries.example_cn: 如果你订购大量物品，可以按批发价购买这些商品。
entries.example_en: You can buy these items wholesale if you order a large quantity.

entries.definition_cn: （比喻）不加区别地；不加选择地
entries.definition_en: figuratively, indiscriminately; without regard to distinctions
entries.example_cn: 未经核实，虚假说法被不加区别地接受了。
entries.example_en: False claims were accepted wholesale without checking the facts.

entries.definition_en: ignoring distinctions or details; indiscriminate
entries.example_cn: 政府对反对党发起了不加区别的猛烈攻击。
entries.example_en: The government launched a wholesale attack on the opposition party.

entries.definition_en: someone who buys large quantities of goods and resells to merchants rather than to the ultimate customers
entries.example_cn: 这位批发商为当地的杂货店供应新鲜农产品。
entries.example_en: The wholesaler supplies fresh produce to local grocery stores.

entries.definition_en: promoting physical health and well-being
entries.example_cn: 健康的饮食有助于预防疾病。
entries.example_en: A wholesome diet can help prevent illness.

entries.definition_cn: 有益身心健康的；健全的
entries.definition_en: promoting moral or mental well-being; sound and healthy
entries.example_cn: 这本书为应对逆境提供了有益身心的建议。
entries.example_en: The book offers wholesome advice for dealing with adversity.

entries.definition_en: in a wholesome manner
entries.example_cn: 孩子们被鼓励健康地在户外玩耍。
entries.example_en: The children were encouraged to play outdoors wholesomely.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being beneficial and generally good for your health
entries.example_cn: 这种饮食的有益健康性有助于儿童茁壮成长。
entries.example_en: The wholesomeness of this diet helps children grow strong.

entries.definition_en: completely or entirely; to a full extent
entries.example_cn: 该项目完全由私人捐款资助。
entries.example_en: The project was wholly funded by private donations.

entries.definition_en: used to refer to a previously mentioned person or people
entries.example_cn: 我昨天见过的那位经理非常和蔼。
entries.example_en: The manager, whom I met yesterday, is very kind.

entries.definition_en: used to ask about a person or people
entries.example_cn: 你邀请了谁参加聚会？
entries.example_en: Whom did you invite to the party?

usage.label: formal interrogative; object of a verb or preposition; patterns: verb + whom; preposition + whom

entries.definition_en: used in formal contexts to refer to the person(s) in question
entries.example_cn: 没有我们可以完全信任的人。
entries.example_en: There is no one whom we can trust completely.

entries.definition_cn: （用于指代集体名词，如乐队或球队）
entries.definition_en: used with names of collective nouns referring to groups of people
entries.example_cn: 披头士乐队被许多人认为是最伟大的乐队，他们影响了摇滚乐。
entries.example_en: The Beatles, whom many consider the greatest band, influenced rock music.

entries.definition_en: to defeat someone or something by a very large margin
entries.example_cn: 主队在决赛中以压倒性优势击败了对手。
entries.example_en: The home team whomped their rivals in the final match.

entries.definition_en: to hit someone or something with your hand
entries.example_cn: 他挥开苍蝇，然后用手拍死了蚊子。
entries.example_en: He whipped the fly away and then whomp-ed the mosquito.

entries.definition_en: a loud hooting cry of exultation or excitement
entries.example_cn: 当球队得分时，人群发出了一声巨大的欢呼。
entries.example_en: The crowd let out a loud whoop when the team scored.

entries.definition_en: noisy and boisterous revelry
entries.example_cn: 派对充满了喧闹的狂欢，音乐震耳欲聋，人们尽情跳舞。
entries.example_en: The party was full of whoopee with loud music and dancing.

entries.definition_cn: 一种常见的旧大陆天鹅，以其独特的叫声闻名
entries.definition_en: a common Old World swan noted for its whooping call
entries.example_cn: 这种天鹅经常在湖面上优雅地滑行。
entries.example_en: The whooper swan is often seen gliding gracefully on the lake.

entries.definition_cn: 大声欢呼或发出呼喊声的人或动物
entries.definition_en: a person or animal that whoops
entries.example_cn: 发出呼喊声的动物的叫声在山谷中回荡。
entries.example_en: The whooper's loud cry echoed across the valley.

entries.definition_cn: 一种罕见的北美鹤，羽毛黑白相间，叫声如喇叭
entries.definition_en: a rare North American crane with black-and-white plumage and a trumpeting call
entries.example_cn: 黎明时分，有人在湿地看到了一只这种鹤在飞翔。
entries.example_en: The whooper was spotted flying over the wetlands at dawn.

entries.definition_cn: 带着呼啸声快速移动或掠过
entries.definition_en: Move or pass quickly with a whooshing sound.
entries.example_cn: 箭从他耳边呼啸而过。
entries.example_en: The arrow whooshed past his ear.

entries.definition_en: Make a whooshing or breathy sound.
entries.example_cn: 翅膀在风中发出呼啸声。
entries.example_en: The wings whooshed in the wind.

entries.definition_en: gush or squirt out
entries.example_cn: 水从破裂的管道中喷涌而出。
entries.example_en: Water whooshed out of the broken pipe.

entries.definition_en: the noise produced by the sudden rush of a fluid
entries.example_cn: 火车经过时，隧道里响起了巨大的呼啸声。
entries.example_en: A loud whoosh echoed through the tunnel as the train passed.

entries.definition_en: to strike with great force
entries.example_cn: 拳击手用一记有力的右勾拳猛击对手。
entries.example_en: The boxer whopped his opponent with a powerful right hook.

entries.definition_en: to hit hard
entries.example_cn: 他用球拍将球重重地打在墙上。
entries.example_en: He whopped the ball against the wall with his racket.

entries.definition_en: something especially big or impressive of its kind
entries.example_cn: 那场风暴真是惊人，风速超过每小时 100 英里。
entries.example_en: The storm was a whopper, with winds reaching over 100 miles per hour.

entries.definition_en: a gross untruth; a blatant lie
entries.example_cn: 他撒了一个弥天大谎，连朋友都不信。
entries.example_en: He told such a whopper that even his friends didn't believe him.

entries.definition_en: very large (used informally)
entries.example_cn: 我们在餐厅的晚餐账单高得惊人。
entries.example_en: We had a whopping bill for the restaurant dinner.

entries.definition_en: to an extreme degree
entries.example_cn: 这个项目取得了巨大的成功，超出了所有人的预期。
entries.example_en: The project was a whopping success, exceeding all expectations.

entries.definition_cn: 对以发生性关系换取金钱的女性所用的强烈贬损、冒犯性称呼
entries.definition_en: a strongly derogatory and offensive term for a woman who has sexual intercourse for money
entries.example_cn: 指南警告说，whore 是对卖淫女性的强烈贬损性称呼。
entries.example_en: The guide warns that whore is a strongly derogatory term for a woman who sells sex.

entries.definition_en: to work as a prostitute
entries.example_cn: 她从未想过为了钱而出卖自己。
entries.example_en: She never wanted to whore herself out for money.

entries.definition_en: to compromise one's morals for money or gain
entries.example_cn: 他拒绝为了政治权力而出卖自己的原则。
entries.example_en: He refused to whore out his principles for political power.

entries.definition_en: to engage the services of a prostitute
entries.example_cn: 他因在该市的红灯区嫖妓而闻名。
entries.example_en: He was known to whore around in the city's red-light district.

entries.definition_en: the practice of offering sexual intercourse for money (archaic and derogatory)
entries.example_cn: 这部历史文献用 whoredom 指卖淫行为。
entries.example_en: The historical text used whoredom for the practice of selling sex.

entries.definition_en: a building where prostitutes work
entries.example_cn: 警方突袭了街角那家臭名昭著的妓院。
entries.example_en: The police raided the notorious whorehouse on the corner.

entries.definition_en: a pimp who procures whores
entries.example_cn: 该皮条客因组织非法卖淫团伙被捕。
entries.example_en: The whoremonger was arrested for organizing illegal prostitution rings.

entries.definition_en: a prostitute's customer
entries.example_cn: 那个嫖客在妓院付费寻欢。
entries.example_en: The whoremonger paid for sex at the brothel.

usage.label: vulgar; Ireland, UK
usage.pattern: Source w51166r0 supplies these register and regional labels.

entries.definition_en: an insulting term of address, literally referring to a son of a whore
entries.example_cn: 别叫我混蛋，听我说。
entries.example_en: Stop calling me a whoreson and listen to what I say.

entries.definition_en: the illegitimate offspring of unmarried parents
entries.example_cn: 历史上，“whoreson”一词被用来描述私生子。
entries.example_en: The term 'whoreson' was used historically to describe an illegitimate child.

usage.label: archaic; derogatory
usage.pattern: historical term for an illegitimate child

entries.definition_en: a lock of hair arranged in a spiral or curl
entries.example_cn: 她小心地将那一卷头发盘在头上。
entries.example_en: She carefully arranged the whorl of hair around her head.

entries.definition_en: a round shape formed by a series of concentric circles, such as leaves or petals
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子呈轮生排列，环绕着茎生长。
entries.example_en: The leaves of the plant grow in a whorl around the stem.

entries.definition_en: a structure consisting of something wound in a continuous series of loops
entries.example_cn: 蜗牛的壳具有复杂的螺旋结构图案。
entries.example_en: The shell of the snail features a complex whorl pattern.

entries.definition_en: forming one or more whorls, especially of leaves around a stem
entries.example_cn: 这种植物的叶子呈轮生状，沿着茎干呈圆形生长。
entries.example_en: The plant has whorled leaves growing in circles along the stem.

entries.definition_en: arranged in the shape of a coil
entries.example_cn: 花瓣围绕中心呈螺旋状排列。
entries.example_en: The petals of the flower are whorled around the center.

entries.definition_en: used to show that something belongs to a person or thing already mentioned
entries.example_cn: 那辆车的车主报了警。
entries.example_en: The man whose car was stolen called the police.

entries.definition_en: used to ask about the person or thing that something belongs to
entries.example_cn: 桌上的这本书是谁的？
entries.example_en: Whose book is this on the table?

entries.definition_en: used to show that something belongs to a thing already mentioned
entries.example_cn: 屋顶受损的那栋房子需要修理。
entries.example_en: The house whose roof was damaged needs repair.

entries.definition_en: used to ask about the people or things that something belongs to
entries.example_cn: 这些钥匙是谁的？
entries.example_en: Whose are these keys?

entries.definition_cn: 用于询问某事的原因或理由
entries.definition_en: used to ask for the reason or cause of something
entries.example_cn: 天空为什么是蓝色的？
entries.example_en: Why is the sky blue?

entries.definition_en: the reason or cause for something
entries.example_cn: 我不了解这种情况的原因和理由。
entries.example_en: I don't know the whys and wherefores of the situation.

entries.definition_cn: 一种黑白相间的非洲织布鸟；雄鸟在繁殖期长出醒目的下垂长尾羽
entries.definition_en: a mostly black-and-white African weaverbird; the male develops distinctive drooping long tail feathers during the breeding season
entries.example_cn: 维达织布鸟是一种黑白相间的非洲织布鸟，雄鸟在繁殖期会长出长尾羽。
entries.example_en: The whydah is a mostly black-and-white African weaverbird whose male develops long tail feathers during the breeding season.

entries.definition_cn: 蜡烛或油灯中通过毛细作用将燃料引向火焰的绳状物
entries.definition_en: a cord in a candle or lamp that draws fuel up into the flame
entries.example_cn: 她修剪了灯芯，使油灯烧得更亮。
entries.example_en: She trimmed the wick to make the lamp burn brighter.

entries.definition_cn: 靠毛细作用输送液体的绳状物
entries.definition_en: a piece of cord that conveys liquid by capillary action
entries.example_cn: 蜡烛里的灯芯烧到了底部。
entries.example_en: The wick in the candle was burnt down to the bottom.

entries.definition_en: morally bad in principle or practice
entries.example_cn: 这个故事警告人们贪婪会带来邪恶的后果。
entries.example_en: The story warns against the wicked consequences of greed.

entries.definition_en: extremely bad or unpleasant in degree or quality
entries.example_cn: 天气一夜之间变得极其寒冷。
entries.example_en: The weather turned wicked cold overnight.

entries.definition_en: having committed unrighteous acts
entries.example_cn: 在传说中，那个作恶多端的国王最终被人民推翻。
entries.example_en: In the legend, the wicked king was eventually overthrown by the people.

entries.definition_en: naughtily or annoyingly playful
entries.example_cn: 孩子们对老师恶作剧了一番。
entries.example_en: The children played a wicked prank on their teacher.

entries.definition_cn: 令人厌恶的；引起反感的
entries.definition_en: highly offensive; arousing aversion or disgust
entries.example_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人极度厌恶，无法忍受。
entries.example_en: The smell of the rotten food was wicked and unbearable.

entries.definition_en: in a wicked or evil manner
entries.example_cn: 那个恶棍邪恶地嘲笑他的受害者。
entries.example_en: The villain wickedly laughed at his victims.

entries.definition_en: behavior that is morally wrong or evil
entries.example_cn: 他行为的邪恶震惊了所有人。
entries.example_en: The wickedness of his actions shocked everyone.

entries.definition_en: the state or quality of being wicked
entries.example_cn: 他心中深感邪恶。
entries.example_en: He felt a deep sense of wickedness in his heart.

entries.definition_cn: 道德或精神价值的缺失
entries.definition_en: a complete lack of moral or spiritual principles
entries.example_cn: 这部小说探讨了一个没有良知的社会的道德缺失。
entries.example_en: The novel explores the wickedness of a society without conscience.

entries.definition_en: the state of being separated from God
entries.example_cn: 这个故事描述了人类背离神性的疏远状态。
entries.example_en: The story describes the wickedness of man turning away from the divine.

entries.definition_cn: 令人感官或情感上厌恶的性质
entries.definition_en: the quality of being disgusting to the senses or emotions
entries.example_cn: 那股令人作呕的气味让人无法待在房间里。
entries.example_en: The wickedness of the smell made it impossible to stay in the room.

entries.definition_en: work made of interlaced slender branches, such as willow branches
entries.example_cn: 他们坐在花园里舒适的藤椅上。
entries.example_en: They sat on a comfortable wicker chair in the garden.

entries.definition_en: slender flexible branches or twigs, especially of willow or canes, used for making baskets
entries.example_cn: 这个篮子是用天然的柳条编织而成的。
entries.example_en: The basket was woven from natural wicker.

entries.definition_en: objects made by weaving together thin strips of wood or reeds
entries.example_cn: 花园里的家具是由耐用的柳条编织品制成的，可以经受阳光的照射。
entries.example_en: The garden furniture was made of durable wickerwork that could withstand the sun.

entries.definition_cn: 用柳条编织物品的工艺
entries.definition_en: the craft of making things from wicker
entries.example_cn: 她跟祖母学会了柳条编织工艺。
entries.example_en: She learned the craft of wickerwork from her grandmother.

entries.definition_en: a set of three stumps with crosspieces used in the sport of cricket
entries.example_cn: 击球手将球高高击过板球门。
entries.example_en: The batsman hit the ball high over the wicket.

entries.definition_en: a small gate or door, often part of a larger door
entries.example_cn: 他们通过主门上的小门进入了花园。
entries.example_en: They entered the garden through the wicket in the main gate.

entries.definition_en: a small opening in a door used for conducting business
entries.example_cn: 邮递员把信从门上的小窗递了进去。
entries.example_en: The postman handed the letter through the wicket.

entries.definition_en: a small arch used in the game of croquet
entries.example_cn: 她小心地将球滚过槌球门。
entries.example_en: She carefully rolled the ball through the wicket.

entries.definition_cn: 北美洲西南部一些印第安半游牧民族使用的、以垫席或树枝覆盖框架搭成的圆顶小屋
entries.definition_en: a domed hut made from a frame covered with matting or brush, used by some semi-nomadic Native American peoples, especially in the southwestern United States
entries.example_cn: 旅行者在沙漠附近一座传统的圆顶小屋里过夜。
entries.example_en: The travelers spent the night in a traditional wickiup near the desert.

entries.definition_en: having a large distance from one side to the other
entries.example_cn: 这条河很宽。
entries.example_en: The river is very wide.

entries.definition_en: covering a large range of topics or areas
entries.example_cn: 她的兴趣范围很广。
entries.example_en: She has a wide range of interests.

entries.definition_en: very large in size or scope
entries.example_cn: 他们住在该国一个广阔的地区。
entries.example_en: They live in a wide area of the country.

entries.definition_en: (of eyes) fully open
entries.example_cn: 她睁大眼睛盯着他。
entries.example_en: She stared at him with wide eyes.

entries.definition_en: completely; fully
entries.example_cn: 门完全敞开着。
entries.example_en: The door was wide open.

entries.definition_en: with a large space between things
entries.example_cn: 这些房子相距很远。
entries.example_en: The houses are set wide apart.

entries.definition_en: not hitting the intended target
entries.example_cn: 箭射偏了，没中靶心。
entries.example_en: The arrow went wide of the mark.

entries.definition_en: to a great distance or range
entries.example_cn: 搜索在森林中远远地展开。
entries.example_en: The search went wide across the forest.

entries.definition_cn: 广角的；与广角镜头有关的
entries.definition_en: of or relating to a lens with a wide angle of view
entries.example_cn: 摄影师使用广角镜头拍摄了整个风景。
entries.example_en: The photographer used a wide-angle lens to capture the entire landscape.

entries.definition_en: fully awake
entries.example_cn: 完全清醒的孩子们跑出去玩了。
entries.example_en: The wide-awake children ran out to play.

entries.definition_en: fully alert and watchful
entries.example_cn: 警觉的警卫仔细监视着周边。
entries.example_en: The wide-awake guard watched the perimeter carefully.

entries.definition_en: a large commercial aircraft with a wide fuselage, typically with two aisles
entries.example_cn: 我们乘坐宽体客机跨越了海洋。
entries.example_en: We flew on a wide-body aircraft to cross the ocean.

entries.definition_cn: （燃料）由沸点范围很宽的烃组成的，含煤油型和汽油型成分的
entries.definition_en: of a fuel composed of hydrocarbons with a wide range of boiling points, including kerosene- and gasoline-type components
entries.example_cn: Jet B 是一种宽馏程燃料，含有煤油型和汽油型成分。
entries.example_en: Jet B is a wide-cut fuel containing both kerosene- and gasoline-type components.

entries.definition_en: having eyes fully open
entries.example_cn: 她睁大眼睛，震惊地看着那条新闻。
entries.example_en: She looked at the news with wide-eyed shock.

entries.definition_en: showing childlike innocence and belief
entries.example_cn: 那个天真烂漫的孩子盯着魔术表演看。
entries.example_en: The wide-eyed child stared at the magic show.

entries.definition_en: covering a large number of different subjects or areas
entries.example_cn: 委员会就新政策举行了广泛的讨论。
entries.example_en: The committee held wide-ranging discussions on the new policy.

entries.definition_en: covering a large variety of different things
entries.example_cn: 该博物馆收藏了来自不同文化的包罗万象的艺术品。
entries.example_en: The museum offers a wide-ranging collection of art from different cultures.

entries.definition_en: operating over a wide range of frequencies
entries.example_cn: 这台新型收音机是一个宽带设备，能够调谐多个频道。
entries.example_en: The new radio receiver is a wideband device capable of tuning across multiple channels.

entries.definition_en: to a great extent or over a large area
entries.example_cn: 关于这一发现的报道广为流传。
entries.example_en: The news about the discovery was widely reported.

entries.definition_cn: 相距甚远地；间隔很大地
entries.definition_en: with much space or distance between things
entries.example_cn: 田里的树木被种得相距甚远。
entries.example_en: The trees were planted widely apart in the field.

entries.definition_en: to become broader or wider
entries.example_cn: 河流在接近大海时变宽了。
entries.example_en: The river widens as it approaches the sea.

entries.definition_en: to make something wider
entries.example_cn: 他们决定加宽道路以减少交通堵塞。
entries.example_en: They decided to widen the road to reduce traffic jams.

entries.definition_en: to extend the scope, range, or area of something
entries.example_cn: 公司计划明年扩大其市场范围。
entries.example_en: The company plans to widen its market reach next year.

entries.definition_en: to make clothes larger by cutting and sewing
entries.example_cn: 我需要把这件夹克的袖子改宽。
entries.example_en: I need to widen the sleeves of this jacket.

entries.definition_en: the process of becoming wider
entries.example_cn: 河流的变宽导致山谷发生洪水。
entries.example_en: The widening of the river caused flooding in the valley.

entries.definition_en: the action of making something wider
entries.example_cn: 走廊的加宽将提高安全性。
entries.example_en: The widening of the corridor will improve safety.

entries.definition_en: a section of a road that has been made wider to allow cars to pass or park
entries.example_cn: 驾驶员进入高速公路加宽路段时应小心。
entries.example_en: Drivers should be careful when entering the widening on the highway.

entries.definition_en: widely circulated or diffused
entries.example_cn: 这起事故的消息在全国范围内广泛传播。
entries.example_en: The news of the accident was widespread across the country.

entries.definition_en: distributed over a considerable extent
entries.example_cn: 森林大火对周边地区造成了广泛的破坏。
entries.example_en: The forest fire caused widespread damage to the surrounding area.

entries.definition_en: a type of freshwater duck found in Eurasia and northern Africa, related to mallards and teals
entries.example_cn: 赤颈鸭低飞掠过芦苇丛，然后降落。
entries.example_en: The widgeon flew low over the reeds before landing.

entries.definition_cn: 某物（名称被遗忘或未知）
entries.definition_en: something unspecified whose name is either forgotten or not known
entries.example_cn: 我需要找到那个用来修补漏水的东西。
entries.example_en: I need to find that widget I used to fix the leak.

entries.definition_en: a device or control that is very useful for a particular job
entries.example_cn: 这个新装置让调节温度变得更加容易。
entries.example_en: The new widget makes it easier to adjust the temperature.

entries.definition_cn: 计算机应用程序图形用户界面中供用户操作的组件，如按钮或文本框
entries.definition_en: a component of a computer application's graphical user interface that a user interacts with, such as a button or text box
entries.example_cn: 点击这个控件以打开设置菜单。
entries.example_en: Click the widget to open the settings menu.

entries.definition_en: a woman whose husband has died, especially one who has not married again
entries.example_cn: 丈夫去世后，她做了多年的寡妇。
entries.example_en: After her husband passed away, she remained a widow for many years.

entries.definition_en: to cause someone to lose their spouse
entries.example_cn: 那场事故使三名妇女成了寡妇，她们的丈夫都遇难了。
entries.example_en: The accident widowed three women who lost their husbands.

entries.definition_en: single because of the death of one's spouse
entries.example_cn: 丈夫去世后，她守寡了许多年。
entries.example_en: After her husband passed away, she remained widowed for many years.

entries.definition_en: a man whose wife has died, especially one who has not married again
entries.example_cn: 妻子去世后，他做了很多年的鳏夫。
entries.example_en: After his wife passed away, he remained a widower for many years.

entries.definition_en: the period of time when a woman is a widow
entries.example_cn: 她在寡居期间环游了世界。
entries.example_en: She spent her widowhood traveling the world.

entries.definition_en: the state of being a widow who has not remarried
entries.example_cn: 她在未再嫁的寡妇身份中度过了二十年，之后才遇到了第二任丈夫。
entries.example_en: Her widowhood lasted for twenty years before she met her second husband.

entries.definition_en: the extent of something from side to side
entries.example_cn: 走廊的宽度不足以让两个人交错通过。
entries.example_en: The width of the hallway is not enough for two people to pass each other.

entries.definition_cn: 熟练地使用（武器或工具）
entries.definition_en: to handle or use a weapon or tool skillfully
entries.example_cn: 她知道如何有效地挥剑。
entries.example_en: She knows how to wield a sword effectively.

entries.definition_en: to have and exercise power or authority
entries.example_cn: 新经理将对部门拥有重大影响力。
entries.example_en: The new manager will wield significant influence over the department.

entries.definition_en: easy to handle, use, or manage
entries.example_cn: 这款新软件专为技术经验较少的用户设计，易于操控。
entries.example_en: The new software is designed to be wieldy even for users with little technical experience.

entries.definition_en: a smooth-textured sausage of minced beef or pork, usually smoked
entries.example_cn: 他中午在面包卷上放了一根热狗肠。
entries.example_en: He put a wiener on a bread roll for lunch.

entries.definition_en: a married woman; a man's partner in marriage
entries.example_cn: 我的妻子喜欢做晚饭。
entries.example_en: My wife loves cooking dinner.

entries.definition_en: befitting or characteristic of a wife
entries.example_cn: 她以对家庭的贤妻般的奉献而闻名。
entries.example_en: She was known for her wifely devotion to her family.

entries.definition_en: a hairpiece covering the head, made of real or synthetic hair
entries.example_cn: 她戴假发去参加化妆舞会。
entries.example_en: She wore a wig to the costume party.

entries.definition_en: a scolding (British slang)
entries.example_cn: 老师因为学生迟到而训斥了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave the student a wig for being late.

entries.definition_en: a type of freshwater duck found in Eurasia and northern Africa, related to mallards and teals
entries.example_cn: 当船靠近芦苇丛时，斑嘴鸭飞走了。
entries.example_en: The wigeon took flight as the boat approached the reeds.

entries.definition_en: wearing a wig
entries.example_cn: 这位演员为了扮演国王而戴上了假发。
entries.example_en: The actor was wigged for the role of the king.

entries.definition_en: a scolding
entries.example_cn: 老师因他迟到而严厉地训斥了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher gave him a severe wigging for being late.

entries.definition_en: move to and fro
entries.example_cn: 她扭动手指表示她还活着。
entries.example_en: She wiggled her fingers to show she was still alive.

entries.definition_en: the act of wiggling
entries.example_cn: 婴儿在睡梦中扭动了一下。
entries.example_en: The baby gave a little wiggle in his sleep.

entries.definition_en: a person who cannot stay still, especially a child
entries.example_cn: 老师让那个坐不住的孩子在课上安静地坐着。
entries.example_en: The teacher asked the wiggler to sit quietly during the lesson.

entries.definition_en: the larva of a mosquito
entries.example_cn: 蚊幼虫生活在死水中。
entries.example_en: Mosquito wigglers live in stagnant water.

entries.definition_en: a terrestrial worm used as bait that burrows into soil
entries.example_cn: 渔夫抓了一条蚯蚓用作鱼饵。
entries.example_en: The fisherman caught a wiggler to use as bait.

entries.definition_cn: 用于制造业（尤其是金属加工）中定位工件中心或边缘的工具。
entries.definition_en: A tool used in manufacturing, especially metalworking, to locate the center or edge of a workpiece.
entries.example_cn: 机械师用找边器定位金属工件的边缘。
entries.example_en: The machinist used a wiggler to locate the edge of the metal workpiece.

entries.definition_cn: 使带电粒子束在加速器中沿弯曲路径运行的磁铁。
entries.definition_en: A magnet that makes a beam of charged particles follow a curved path in an accelerator.
entries.example_cn: 这台加速器使用偏转磁铁使带电粒子束弯曲。
entries.example_en: The accelerator uses a wiggler to bend the beam of charged particles.

entries.definition_en: curved or curving in and out
entries.example_cn: 穿过森林的蜿蜒小径很难辨认。
entries.example_en: The wiggly path through the forest was difficult to follow.

entries.definition_cn: 以扭曲、蛇形或蠕虫状的方式移动
entries.definition_en: moving in a twisting or snake-like or wormlike fashion
entries.example_cn: 蛇在热沙上以蛇形蜿蜒移动。
entries.example_en: The snake moved wiggly across the hot sand.

entries.definition_en: a living being
entries.example_cn: 这片古老的森林是许多奇异生物的家园。
entries.example_en: The ancient forest was home to many strange wights.

entries.definition_en: a malevolent or haunting spirit
entries.example_cn: 传说有一个恶灵在废弃的城堡里游荡。
entries.example_en: Legend says a wight haunts the abandoned castle.

entries.definition_en: a person who makes and sells wigs
entries.example_cn: 这位假发制作者花了几个小时为历史剧制作了一顶逼真的假发。
entries.example_en: The wigmaker spent hours crafting a realistic wig for the historical play.

entries.definition_cn: 用旗语或灯光按特定代码发信号
entries.definition_en: to signal by or as if by waving a flag or light according to a code
entries.example_cn: 他们向大本营发信号，表明自己的位置。
entries.example_en: They wigwagged back to the base camp to indicate their location.

entries.definition_cn: 用旗语或灯光按特定代码发信号
entries.definition_en: to send a signal by waving a flag or a light in a specific code
entries.example_cn: 水手向过往的船只发出了求救信号。
entries.example_en: The sailor wigwagged a distress signal to the passing ship.

usage.label: US; historical
usage.pattern: signal by waving a flag to and fro

entries.definition_cn: 轻轻地左右或来回摆动
entries.definition_en: to move gently from side to side or back and forth
entries.example_cn: 树枝在风中轻轻地来回摆动。
entries.example_en: The branches wigwagged in the wind.

entries.definition_cn: 一种圆顶形或拱形的土著美洲人棚屋，通常覆盖树皮或兽皮
entries.definition_en: a Native American lodge that is often oval-shaped and covered with bark or animal hides
entries.example_cn: 旅行者在穿越森林期间住在传统的圆顶帐篷里。
entries.example_en: The travelers stayed in a traditional wigwam during their journey through the forest.

entries.definition_en: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated
entries.example_cn: 狼是生活在山里的野生动物。
entries.example_en: The wolves are wild animals that live in the mountains.

entries.definition_en: marked by extreme lack of restraint or control
entries.example_cn: 当乐队开始演奏时，人群变得狂乱起来。
entries.example_en: The crowd became wild when the band started playing.

entries.definition_en: in a state of extreme emotion
entries.example_cn: 当她赢得奖品时，她欣喜若狂。
entries.example_en: She was wild with joy when she won the prize.

entries.definition_en: in a wild or undomesticated manner
entries.example_cn: 马群在平原上野蛮地奔跑。
entries.example_en: The horses ran wild across the plain.

entries.definition_en: in an uncontrolled and rampant manner
entries.example_cn: 谣言在镇上疯狂传播。
entries.example_en: Rumors spread wildly through the town.

entries.definition_en: a primitive state untouched by civilization
entries.example_cn: 故事描述了人类到来之前森林的原始状态。
entries.example_en: The story describes the wild state of the forest before humans arrived.

entries.definition_cn: 偏离预定方向很远的；偏离目标的
entries.definition_en: deviating widely from an intended course
entries.example_cn: 这一枪打偏了，没有击中目标。
entries.example_en: The shot was wild and missed the target.

entries.definition_en: a wild and uninhabited area left in its natural condition
entries.example_cn: 他们花了一周时间探索北方的荒野。
entries.example_en: They spent the weekend exploring the wilds of the north.

entries.definition_en: having a glaring expression suggesting madness or terror
entries.example_cn: 那个目光惊恐的男人冲进房间，大喊大叫。
entries.example_en: The wild-eyed man ran into the room shouting in apparent terror.

entries.definition_en: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.example_cn: 他那个不切实际的、想不花钱环游世界的计划被驳回了。
entries.example_en: His wild-eyed plan to travel the world without money was dismissed.

entries.definition_en: a small or medium-sized cat living in the wild
entries.example_cn: 我们在河边的草丛中发现了一只躲藏的野猫。
entries.example_en: We spotted a wildcat hiding in the tall grass near the river.

entries.definition_en: an exploratory oil well drilled in an area not known to be an oil field
entries.example_cn: 公司决定在偏远的沙漠地区钻一口探井。
entries.example_en: The company decided to drill a wildcat well in the remote desert region.

entries.definition_cn: 暴躁易怒或性欲旺盛的人
entries.definition_en: a violent, easily angered, or sexually vigorous person
entries.example_cn: 大家都知道他脾气暴躁，像一只野猫。
entries.example_en: Everyone knew him as a wildcat, quick to anger.

entries.definition_cn: 通常含贬义的；不规范或不正当经营的
entries.definition_en: usually derogatory: operating outside standard or legitimate business practices
entries.example_cn: 这家银行因其不规范的贷款业务而受到批评。
entries.example_en: The bank was criticized for its wildcat lending practices.

entries.definition_en: without official authorization
entries.example_cn: 工人们进行了未经授权的罢工，因为他们没有被允许就此事进行投票。
entries.example_en: The workers went on a wildcat strike because they were not allowed to vote on the issue.

entries.definition_en: drilled speculatively in an area not known to be productive
entries.example_cn: 地质学家将新钻的井标记为勘探项目。
entries.example_en: The geologists labeled the new borehole as a wildcat project.

entries.definition_en: an oilman who drills exploratory wells in territory not known to be an oil field
entries.example_cn: 这位石油勘探者冒着一切风险在沙漠中寻找石油。
entries.example_en: The wildcatter risked everything to find oil in the desert.

entries.definition_en: a large African antelope with horns like an ox and a long tufted tail
entries.example_cn: 角马成群结队地穿越大草原进行迁徙。
entries.example_en: The wildebeest migrated across the savanna in large herds.

entries.definition_en: a wild and uninhabited area left in its natural condition
entries.example_cn: 他们驱车穿过荒野，到达了那座偏僻的小屋。
entries.example_en: They drove through the wilderness to reach the remote cabin.

entries.definition_cn: 纷繁杂乱的一大堆事物
entries.definition_en: a bewildering profusion
entries.example_cn: 花园里繁花似锦，令人眼花缭乱。
entries.example_en: The garden was a wilderness of blooming flowers.

entries.definition_en: a state of disfavor
entries.example_cn: 这位政治家落选后发现自己陷入了政治上的失势境地。
entries.example_en: The politician found himself in the political wilderness after losing the election.

usage.label: in the wilderness
usage.pattern: political situation of being out of office or favor; source w08543r6.

entries.definition_en: a rapidly spreading fire, especially one occurring in a wildland area
entries.example_cn: 那场森林大火摧毁了山谷中的数百栋房屋。
entries.example_en: The wildfire destroyed hundreds of homes in the valley.

entries.definition_en: wild or uncultivated flowering plant
entries.example_cn: 春天的田野里开满了五颜六色的野花。
entries.example_en: The meadow was filled with colorful wildflowers in the spring.

entries.definition_en: any wild bird hunted as game, especially ducks, geese, or swans
entries.example_cn: 猎人用刚捕获的野禽做了一顿饭。
entries.example_en: The hunter prepared a meal from freshly caught wildfowl.

entries.definition_cn: 野生植物（尤指野苹果树）
entries.definition_en: a wild plant that grows without being cultivated, such as a wild apple tree
entries.example_cn: 秋天，森林里充满了野苹果树的香气。
entries.example_en: The forest was filled with the scent of wilding apples in autumn.

entries.definition_cn: 暴力骚乱（通常指一群年轻人随机实施暴力行为）
entries.definition_en: an outrageous and violent rampage, typically involving a group of young people committing random acts of violence
entries.example_cn: 社区对昨晚那场暴力骚乱感到震惊。
entries.example_en: The community was horrified by the random violence of the wilding last night.

entries.definition_en: all living animals and plants that are not domesticated
entries.example_cn: 这个公园是当地野生动物的庇护所。
entries.example_en: The park is a sanctuary for local wildlife.

entries.definition_en: to an extreme or greatly exaggerated degree
entries.example_cn: 最近几个月价格急剧上涨。
entries.example_en: The prices have risen wildly in recent months.

entries.definition_en: in an uncontrolled or unrestrained manner
entries.example_cn: 当球队得分时，人群欢呼雀跃。
entries.example_en: The crowd cheered wildly when the team scored.

entries.definition_en: with violent and uncontrollable passion
entries.example_cn: 她扯着嗓子狂乱地歌唱。
entries.example_en: She sang wildly at the top of her voice.

entries.definition_en: the property of being wild or turbulent
entries.example_cn: 风暴的狂野性质使得旅行变得不可能。
entries.example_en: The wildness of the storm made it impossible to travel.

entries.definition_en: an unruly disposition to do as one pleases
entries.example_cn: 他的任性常常导致与父母的冲突。
entries.example_en: His wildness often led to conflicts with his parents.

entries.definition_cn: 野蛮或荒芜的自然状态
entries.definition_en: an intractably barbarous or uncultivated state of nature
entries.example_cn: 探险家们描述了那片未开发丛林的野蛮与荒芜。
entries.example_en: The explorers described the wildness of the uncharted jungle.

entries.definition_en: an intense or uncontrolled quality of emotion
entries.example_cn: 她反应中的强烈和失控让房间里的所有人都感到惊讶。
entries.example_en: The wildness of her reaction surprised everyone in the room.

entries.definition_en: a trick or stratagem used to deceive or entice someone
entries.example_cn: 推销员用欺骗手段说服那位老人买下了那块昂贵的表。
entries.example_en: The salesman used a wile to convince the old man to buy the expensive watch.

entries.definition_en: done by design
entries.example_cn: 这是一起故意的破坏行为。
entries.example_en: It was a wilful act of destruction.

entries.definition_en: habitually disposed to disobedience and opposition
entries.example_cn: 这个惯于违抗的孩子拒绝遵守任何规则。
entries.example_en: The wilful child refused to follow any rules.

entries.definition_en: in a deliberate and stubborn way
entries.example_cn: 他故意无视警告标志。
entries.example_en: He wilfully ignored the warning signs.

entries.definition_en: the habit of being disobedient and lacking discipline
entries.example_cn: 老师因该学生拒绝遵守规则的任性行为而惩罚了他。
entries.example_en: The teacher punished the student for his wilfulness in refusing to follow the rules.

entries.definition_en: the quality of being shrewd and skilled in deception
entries.example_cn: 侦探看出了小偷藏匿证据时的狡猾。
entries.example_en: The detective recognized the thief’s wiliness in hiding the evidence.

entries.definition_cn: 凭意志促使；竭力使发生
entries.definition_en: To try to cause something to happen by force of will.
entries.example_cn: 她努力凭意志让自己保持镇定。
entries.example_en: She willed herself to remain calm.

entries.definition_en: to decree or ordain something
entries.example_cn: 国王下令必须遵守这项法律。
entries.example_en: The king willed that the law be obeyed.

entries.definition_en: to leave property by will after death
entries.example_cn: 她把房子遗赠给了女儿。
entries.example_en: She will her house to her daughter.

entries.definition_en: the ability to make conscious choices and decisions
entries.example_cn: 你必须用你的意志去成功。
entries.example_en: You must use your will to succeed.

entries.definition_en: a fixed and persistent intent or purpose
entries.example_cn: 她获胜的决心很强。
entries.example_en: Her will to win is strong.

entries.definition_en: a legal document about property after death
entries.example_cn: 他去年写了遗嘱。
entries.example_en: He wrote his will last year.

entries.definition_en: a pale light sometimes seen at night over marshy ground
entries.example_cn: 旅行者们看到沼泽上方闪烁着鬼火。
entries.example_en: The travelers saw a will-o'-the-wisp flickering above the marsh.

entries.definition_cn: 虚幻或难以实现的目标
entries.definition_en: an illusory or unattainable goal
entries.example_cn: 不要追逐轻易成功的幻影。
entries.example_en: Don't chase the will-o'-the-wisp of easy success.

entries.definition_cn: 北美东部和墨西哥湾沿岸的大型滨鸟；半蹼鹬
entries.definition_en: a large shorebird found on the eastern and Gulf Coasts of North America
entries.example_cn: 我们在沙滩上看到了一只半蹼鹬。
entries.example_en: We spotted a willet standing on the sandy beach.

entries.definition_en: done deliberately and on purpose
entries.example_cn: 这是一起故意的破坏行为。
entries.example_en: It was a willful act of destruction.

entries.definition_en: habitually disobedient and oppositional
entries.example_cn: 这个任性的孩子拒绝遵守任何规则。
entries.example_en: The willful child refused to follow any rules.

entries.definition_en: in a deliberate and determined manner
entries.example_cn: 他故意无视路上的警告标志。
entries.example_en: He willfully ignored the warning signs on the road.

entries.definition_en: the habit of refusing to obey rules or show discipline
entries.example_cn: 老师不得不处理学生们的任性行为。
entries.example_en: The teacher had to deal with the willfulness of the students.

entries.definition_en: feelings of uneasiness or fear
entries.example_cn: 那片黑暗的森林让他感到不安。
entries.example_en: The dark forest gave him the willies.

usage.label: colloquial; plural-only
usage.pattern: Used in the plural: give someone the willies.

entries.definition_en: disposed or inclined toward
entries.example_cn: 她愿意帮助朋友完成这个项目。
entries.example_en: She was willing to help her friend with the project.

entries.definition_en: not brought about by coercion or force
entries.example_cn: 志愿者们自愿支持这个项目。
entries.example_en: The volunteers gave their willing support to the project.

entries.definition_en: the act of making a choice
entries.example_cn: 他做出选择的意愿显而易见。
entries.example_en: His willing choice was evident.

entries.definition_en: in a willing manner
entries.example_cn: 她乐意地帮助邻居搬家。
entries.example_en: She willingly helped her neighbor move house.

entries.definition_cn: 意愿；乐意做某事的状态
entries.definition_en: the state of being willing or ready to do something
entries.example_cn: 她乐于助人的态度使项目取得了成功。
entries.example_en: Her willingness to help made the project successful.

entries.definition_en: any of numerous deciduous trees and shrubs of the genus Salix
entries.example_cn: 河边的柳树在夏天提供了阴凉。
entries.example_en: The willow tree by the river provided shade in the summer.

entries.definition_en: a textile machine having a system of revolving spikes for opening and cleaning raw textile fibers
entries.example_cn: 工厂安装了一台新的开棉机来处理棉花。
entries.example_en: The factory installed a new willow to process the cotton.

entries.definition_en: slender and graceful in appearance
entries.example_cn: 她身材纤细优雅，在人群中格外引人注目。
entries.example_en: She had a willowy figure that made her stand out in the crowd.

entries.definition_en: the ability to control your own behavior and resist temptation
entries.example_cn: 戒烟需要极大的意志力。
entries.example_en: It took great willpower to quit smoking.

entries.definition_en: in a random manner
entries.example_cn: 该项目随意完成，没有明确的计划。
entries.example_en: The project was completed willy-nilly, with no clear plan.

entries.definition_en: without having a choice
entries.example_cn: 我们不得不接受这些条款。
entries.example_en: We had to accept the terms willy-nilly.

entries.definition_en: become limp
entries.example_cn: 没有水，这些花很快就枯萎了。
entries.example_en: The flowers wilted quickly without water.

entries.definition_en: lose strength
entries.example_cn: 跑完马拉松后，他觉得在炎热中会力竭。
entries.example_en: After running the marathon, he felt like he would wilt under the heat.

entries.definition_en: the act or state of wilting
entries.example_cn: 生菜的萎蔫是由于缺水造成的。
entries.example_en: The wilt of the lettuce was caused by a lack of water.

entries.definition_en: any plant disease characterized by drooping and shriveling; usually caused by parasites attacking the roots
entries.example_cn: 花园里玫瑰的突然枯萎是由真菌感染引起的。
entries.example_en: The sudden wilt in the garden roses was caused by a fungal infection.

entries.definition_en: limp because of heat, lack of water, or disease
entries.example_cn: 花园里所有的花都枯萎了，看起来很难过。
entries.example_en: The garden looked sad with all the wilted flowers.

entries.definition_en: lacking energy or willpower
entries.example_cn: 长途旅行后，他感到完全无精打采。
entries.example_en: After the long journey, he felt completely wilted.

entries.definition_en: the state of becoming limp or drooping due to lack of water or heat
entries.example_cn: 高温导致花朵在几小时内就枯萎了。
entries.example_en: The heat caused the flowers to suffer from wilting within hours.

entries.definition_en: clever at deceiving or tricking others
entries.example_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸设法逃出了猎人的陷阱。
entries.example_en: The wily fox managed to escape the hunter's trap.

entries.definition_en: hand tool for boring holes
entries.example_cn: 木匠用手钻在木梁上钻孔。
entries.example_en: The carpenter used a wimble to bore holes in the wooden beam.

entries.definition_cn: 用手钻钻孔或刺穿某物
entries.definition_en: to bore or pierce something with a wimble
entries.example_cn: 木匠用手钻在木梁上钻了一个孔。
entries.example_en: The carpenter wimbled a hole through the wooden beam.

entries.definition_en: a piece of cloth worn over the head and around the neck and ears by medieval women
entries.example_cn: 这幅画描绘了一位戴着白色头巾的修女。
entries.example_en: The painting depicts a nun wearing a white wimple.

entries.definition_en: weak, indecisive, or cowardly
entries.example_cn: 他太懦弱了，不敢对抗那个恶霸。
entries.example_en: He was too wimpy to stand up to the bully.

entries.definition_en: be the winner in a contest or competition
entries.example_cn: 她设法在逆境中赢得了比赛。
entries.example_en: She managed to win the race against all odds.

entries.definition_en: win something through one's efforts
entries.example_cn: 他们努力工作以赢得那份合同。
entries.example_en: They worked hard to win the contract.

entries.definition_en: acquire or deserve by one's efforts or actions
entries.example_cn: 她通过自己的敬业赢得了同事们的尊重。
entries.example_en: She won the respect of her colleagues through her dedication.

entries.definition_en: obtain advantages, such as points, etc.
entries.example_cn: 她在决赛中赢得了三分。
entries.example_en: She won three points in the final game.

entries.definition_en: a victory in a race or competition
entries.example_cn: 球队在最后一场比赛后庆祝他们的胜利。
entries.example_en: The team celebrated their win after the final match.

entries.definition_en: something won, especially money
entries.example_cn: 他用他的彩票奖金买了一辆新车。
entries.example_en: He used his lottery win to buy a new car.

entries.definition_en: attain success or reach a desired goal
entries.example_cn: 这个项目对整个社区来说是一个成功。
entries.example_en: The project was a win for the entire community.

entries.definition_en: benefiting both or all parties involved
entries.example_cn: 我们在贸易协议上达成了双赢的共识。
entries.example_en: We reached a win-win agreement on the trade deal.

entries.definition_en: a situation that benefits both or all parties
entries.example_cn: 这种合作对两家公司来说都是双赢的局面。
entries.example_en: This partnership offers a win-win for both companies.

entries.definition_en: to draw back suddenly, as if from fear or pain
entries.example_cn: 听到巨大的噪音，她吓得缩了一下。
entries.example_en: She winced at the loud noise.

entries.definition_cn: 因疼痛或不适而不由自主地皱眉或做出痛苦表情
entries.definition_en: to make an involuntary facial expression of pain or distress
entries.example_cn: 听到演员糟糕的发音，观众不适地皱起了眉。
entries.example_en: The audience winced at the actor's terrible pronunciation.

entries.definition_en: a facial expression showing sudden pain
entries.example_cn: 当针头触碰到他的皮肤时，他痛苦地皱了一下眉。
entries.example_en: He gave a wince of pain when the needle touched his skin.

entries.definition_cn: 对突然疼痛的反射反应
entries.definition_en: a reflex response to sudden pain
entries.example_cn: 他感到一阵剧痛顺着腿向上窜。
entries.example_en: He felt a wince of pain shoot up his leg.

entries.definition_en: a machine with a crank and cable used for lifting heavy objects
entries.example_cn: 他们用绞盘把船拉上岸。
entries.example_en: They used a winch to pull the boat up the beach.

entries.definition_en: to pull or lift something using a winch
entries.example_cn: 船员用绞盘把沉重的箱子吊上卡车。
entries.example_en: The crew winched the heavy crate onto the truck.

entries.definition_en: air moving in the atmosphere
entries.example_cn: 北风刮得很猛。
entries.example_en: The wind was blowing strongly from the north.

entries.definition_en: air blown by a machine or person
entries.example_cn: 风扇产生了一股凉爽的气流。
entries.example_en: The fan creates a cool wind.

entries.definition_en: the ability to breathe easily
entries.example_cn: 跑上山后，我喘不过气了。
entries.example_en: After running up the hill, I lost my wind.

entries.definition_en: a tendency or direction of change
entries.example_cn: 公司有一股变革的趋势。
entries.example_en: There is a wind of change in the company.

entries.definition_en: a turn or bend in a path
entries.example_cn: 这条路有很多弯道。
entries.example_en: The road has many bends.

entries.definition_en: to wrap something around another object
entries.example_cn: 请把电线缠绕在卷轴上。
entries.example_en: Please wind the cord around the spool.

entries.definition_cn: 向管乐器或号角吹气使其发声
entries.definition_en: to blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound
entries.example_cn: 这位音乐家吹响号角发出召唤。
entries.example_en: The musician winds his horn to sound the call.

entries.definition_en: news or information spread by word of mouth
entries.example_cn: 关于新经理的到来有很多流言。
entries.example_en: There is a lot of wind about the new manager's arrival.

entries.definition_en: the end or conclusion of something
entries.example_cn: 会议的结束出乎意料地简短。
entries.example_en: The wind-up of the meeting was surprisingly short.

entries.definition_en: the punch line of a joke or comedy routine
entries.example_cn: 喜剧演员的包袱让观众哄堂大笑。
entries.example_en: The comedian's wind-up made the audience laugh out loud.

entries.definition_en: a humorous attempt to fool somebody; a practical joke
entries.example_cn: 他捉弄朋友，把他的钥匙藏了起来。
entries.example_en: He played a wind-up on his friend by hiding his keys.

entries.definition_en: the phase of making a pitch where the pitcher moves his or her arm backwards before throwing the ball
entries.example_cn: 击球手仔细注视着投手引臂的动作。
entries.example_en: The batter watched the pitcher's wind-up carefully.

entries.definition_cn: 示意表演者快结束的圆形手势
entries.definition_en: a circular hand gesture used to signal a performer to finish quickly
entries.example_cn: 导演做了一个手势示意演员尽快结束这场戏。
entries.example_en: The director gave a wind-up to the actor to wrap up the scene.

entries.definition_cn: 需要上发条才能运转的
entries.definition_en: needing to be wound up in order to function
entries.example_cn: 这台老式发条钟需要定期上发条。
entries.example_en: This old wind-up clock needs to be wound regularly.

entries.definition_en: the force that slows down a moving object due to air resistance
entries.example_cn: 空气阻力影响了子弹在空气中飞行时的速度。
entries.example_en: The windage affected the speed of the bullet as it traveled through the air.

entries.definition_en: exposure to the wind
entries.example_cn: 船长调整了帆以减少船体的受风面。
entries.example_en: The captain adjusted the sails to reduce the windage on the vessel.

entries.definition_cn: 枪械或弓的瞄准具的水平调节
entries.definition_en: horizontal adjustment of the sight of a firearm or bow
entries.example_cn: 射手调节了步枪瞄准具的水平偏移。
entries.example_en: The shooter adjusted the windage of the rifle sight.

entries.definition_cn: 枪膛口径与弹丸直径之间的差值
entries.definition_en: the difference in diameter between a firearm's bore and its shot or projectile
entries.example_cn: 过大的膛隙会使弹丸在枪膛中松动。
entries.example_en: Excessive windage allowed the shot to move loosely in the firearm's bore.

entries.definition_en: a person who talks at length, especially pompously or tediously
entries.example_cn: 别像个饶舌的人那样，听我说。
entries.example_en: Stop acting like a windbag and listen to what I have to say.

entries.definition_cn: 被风吹走的；随风飘散的
entries.definition_en: carried or scattered by the wind
entries.example_cn: 暴风雨过后，随风飘散的树叶覆盖了小路。
entries.example_en: Windblown leaves covered the path after the storm.

entries.definition_en: having hair that has been blown into a disheveled state by the wind
entries.example_cn: 她沿海岸骑车后到达时，头发被风吹得凌乱不堪。
entries.example_en: She arrived with windblown hair after cycling along the coast.

entries.definition_cn: 受风塑造的（尤指树木因常年风向而形成的形状）
entries.definition_en: growing in a shape determined by the prevailing winds, especially of trees
entries.example_cn: 山坡上受风塑造的树木因常年向东吹风而严重倾斜。
entries.example_en: The windblown trees on the hillside leaned heavily to the east.

entries.definition_en: a hedge or fence made of trees to reduce wind force and soil erosion
entries.example_cn: 农民们建造了一道防风林来保护他们的作物免受强冬风的影响。
entries.example_en: The farmers built a windbreak to protect their crops from the strong winter winds.

entries.definition_cn: 防风、防小雨的轻便外套
entries.definition_en: a lightweight outer coat designed to resist wind and light rain
entries.example_cn: 她穿上防风外套以保护自己免受强风侵袭。
entries.example_en: She put on her windbreaker to protect herself from the strong wind.

entries.definition_en: redness and irritation of the skin caused by exposure to high-velocity wind
entries.example_cn: 在跨越开阔海洋航行后，他的脸上遭受了严重的风吹伤。
entries.example_en: After sailing across the open ocean, he suffered severe windburn on his face.

entries.definition_cn: 植物因寒冷多风、叶片干燥而受到的损伤
entries.definition_en: damage to a plant caused by cold, windy conditions that dry out its leaves
entries.example_cn: 在那段异常寒冷多风的天气里，幼树受到了风害。
entries.example_en: The young trees suffered windburn during the unusually cold, windy spell.

entries.definition_en: a heavy jacket designed to protect against wind
entries.example_cn: 他穿上防风夹克，然后走出寒冷的微风中。
entries.example_en: He put on his windcheater before stepping out into the cold breeze.

entries.definition_cn: 气喘吁吁的；上气不接下气的
entries.definition_en: out of breath, especially after exertion
entries.example_cn: 跑上山后，她已经上气不接下气。
entries.example_en: After running up the hill, she was completely winded.

entries.definition_en: a mechanical device used to wind a spring-driven mechanism, like a clock
entries.example_cn: 他用上发条装置收紧了古董钟里的发条。
entries.example_en: He used the winder to tighten the spring in the antique clock.

entries.definition_en: a mechanical device around which something can be wound
entries.example_cn: 在拉上去之前，绳子被固定在绕线装置上。
entries.example_en: The rope was secured to the winder before being pulled up.

entries.definition_en: a person who winds a mechanism, such as a clock or winch
entries.example_cn: 工厂雇佣了一名上发条工来操作大型绞盘。
entries.example_en: The factory hired a winder to operate the large winch.

entries.definition_en: a sudden happening that brings good fortune, such as a sudden opportunity to make money
entries.example_cn: 中彩票对这个家庭来说是一笔真正的意外之财。
entries.example_en: Winning the lottery was a real windfall for the family.

entries.definition_en: fruit that has fallen from a tree
entries.example_cn: 孩子们从地上捡起了落下的果实。
entries.example_en: The children gathered the windfall from the ground.

entries.definition_cn: 银莲花属的一种林地植物，花朵美丽，叶片分裂
entries.definition_en: a woodland plant of the genus Anemone with beautiful flowers and divided leaves
entries.example_cn: 银莲花在森林潮湿的树荫下繁茂地开花。
entries.example_en: The windflower bloomed profusely in the damp shade of the forest.

entries.definition_en: having many turns and bends
entries.example_cn: 我们沿着蜿蜒的小路爬山。
entries.example_en: We followed the winding path up the mountain.

entries.definition_en: describing a path that has many turns and bends
entries.example_cn: 这条曲折的道路提供了山谷的景色。
entries.example_en: The winding road offered a scenic view of the valley.

entries.definition_en: the action of twisting or turning something around
entries.example_cn: 绳子绕在柱子上的缠绕过程很小心。
entries.example_en: The winding of the rope around the post was done carefully.

entries.definition_en: a burial garment in which a corpse is wrapped
entries.example_cn: 牧师将裹尸布折叠起来，包裹住尸体。
entries.example_en: The priest folded the winding-sheet around the body.

entries.definition_en: a large sailing ship
entries.example_cn: 这艘大型帆船在风的全力推动下驶过海洋。
entries.example_en: The windjammer sailed across the ocean under the full power of the wind.

entries.definition_en: a device with a crank used to wind a rope or cable
entries.example_cn: 水手们使用绞盘升起锚。
entries.example_en: The sailors used the windlass to raise the anchor.

entries.definition_en: having no wind or very little wind
entries.example_cn: 那是一个炎热无风的日子，非常适合帆船运动。
entries.example_en: It was a hot, windless day perfect for sailing.

entries.definition_en: a mill powered by the wind
entries.example_cn: 那座古老的风车在蓝天下高高耸立。
